text_masked: Have stayed twice at the Westin Grand Central - this used to be the New York Helmsley Hotel in Midtown East. The first time I stayed here, it was just at the beginning of the renovation and I had some issues checking in and with room, but those were related to the conversion. The second time, I stayed in August 2012 - I was there the day they re-launched the Westin. Pros: Great Westin rooms, Heavenly Bed, good amenities and service. Cons: no restaurant and bar when I stayed there (check with the Hotel), and the location is a little boring if you're looking for NYC excitement. All-in-all, decent hotel if it's the right area, and has all the Westin/SPG perks.

Stayed here at the Rodeway Inn for one night since my girlfriend was sworn in (citizenship naturalization) the next morning at the Los Angeles Convention Center. We enjoyed the king suite (room 104), especially for the total price of $124.73. Not bad for being a little over a mile from the convention center. The room was clean with a microwave and refrigerator, and the bed was comfortable. The water was hot when we took a shower in the morning. The suite had a separate room in it with a couch, chair and big screen TV. Since it is downtown Los Angeles, the location is not ritzy. But we felt safe since the property (besides the driveway entrance) was entirely surrounded by a high metal fence. The continental breakfast was very basic, which is not suprising given the price of this hotel. In other words, "you get what you pay for" applies here. When we checked out in the morning, the kind gentleman behind the counter graciously made a couple of copies for us at no charge. All the staff at this location were friendly and courteous. As a point of information, it took five minutes to drive from this hotel to the convention center at 8:00 a.m. We paid $10.00 for all day parking a couple blocks from the convention center. Be aware that the closer you get to the convention center, the higher the price for parking!

My wife and I stayed here for a few days after a pretty rough month. I contacted the hotel to see if a few things could be arranged for us, and Kristana came through in the biggest of ways! She was great to deal with, and got everything we wanted done to perfection. I wish we would have had more time to stay at this hotel, but we would definitely stay here again when we are in San Diego!

Double caution - I booked two rooms through get-a-room.com (where I had previously had a good experience) and told them that I needed one room with a walk out shower for my 85 year old mother who was traveling with us. She is not handicapped or in a wheel chair, just can't maneuver in and out of a bath tub. They do have rooms with a walk out shower, but you would think that either Marrakech or get-a-room could have told me that not only does the hotel not have an elevator, but you need to climb two long flight of stairs just to get to the lobby to check in! And, the day we checked in, one of those rooms wasn't available on the lobby level so it would have meant even more stairs! Rather than just trying to sell rooms, one or the other should have cared enough to actually listen to the client's needs. Not acceptable. 
I agree with the traveler who characterized this as an upgraded hostel - small rooms (some REALLY small and dark/cave-like), noisy halls, no amenities, etc. A couple of positive notes: I found the rooms clean enough, but the highest marks go to the staff - professional, polite - bell staff in particular could not have been more helpful. Too bad whoever took the call from get-a-room originally couldn't have mentioned that an 85 year old woman may have some issues with their many flights of steps.
I made the mistake of not reading Tripadvisor in advance - that won't happen again!

I agree with some of the other reviewers that suggest that you won't hate this hotel - but doubt you'll love it either. Perhaps we got off to a bad start as despite being a member of their loyalty program and entitled to a room upgrade and my only request being for a quiet room we were put in a room on a low floor on the busy street side - we had a terrible night with the noise - it was almost as if the window was open. That said the next day the staff handled our request for a quieter room (on the back side of the hotel) well and I would recommend you push this point if you don't like a noisy room. The rooms are adequate if a little small and a bit tired and the whole place has a dated feel to it. Thankfully we managed to book a deal that reduced the onsite parking to half price of $19 a day but at $38 it could be a factor for some.
We had 2 rooms and had an incident where we came home in the late afternoon to one of our rooms being unlocked, with the door catch propping it open. The manager was most apologetic but it could have been a real issue if someone had decided to make their way in there for whatever reason.
On the plus side the staff were helpful, the hotel is well located and we enjoyed our time in the onsite bar that has meals available. Check your invoice though as we were billed for calls we hadn't made. There is also an onsite self serve laundry which was most welcome.
In summary if you get a great deal give it a try - but we'll probably be staying elsewhere next time.

title_masked: Happy Birthday weekend at the Omni!
text_masked: Booked a last-minute room thru hotwire for the weekend to celebrate my 40th birthday. Online the Omni is rated as a 4.5 star hotel, I would definitely give this hotel a strong 4 star rating overall (If their hot tub repair was complete i would agree with the 4.5). Anywho, my dear fiancee contacted the hotel and told them it was my b-day and these lovely people responded in such a kind way; there was champagne on ice and a sweet treat left for me (It was a nice start to my birthday weekend)! The staff was very professional and friendly. The rooms were superbly clean,the sheets were soft and the mattresses were very comfortable. I called down to ask for additional hypoallergenic pillows and they were delivered within 5 minutes, I showed the housekeeper a spot on the top sheet (a hot dryer burned them?) and she changed it right away. the mattresses passed my "bedbug" inspection (I pull sheets back and check mattress and boxspring,wall and headboard this is a must!),the corners around the room were not dusty, the caulking around the tub and fixtures was clean and fresh (no mold), the floors were vacuumed daily, furniture dust free, the toiletries and towels were decent quality and restored daily,the bathroom floors and fixtures sparkled, and turndown service was offered every night (although no chocolate or mint left...lol). We could not hear our neighbors through the walls, which was awesome. the only noise we heard was thru the front door occasionally when someone walked by. Needless to say I'm a neat freak and the cleanliness, comfort and attention to detail here was awesome, I stay in many hotels and I can honestly say that I felt as comfortable here as I do in my own home, which is rare. we had the breakfast buffet at the hotel restaurant 676 which was very reasonable and delicious. valet parking was a bit high but it is to be expected, they brought our car up very quickly and they would literally swarm us to insure we safely got into our vehicle as the street can be busy at times. I would return to this hotel in a heartbeat and recommend it to anyone whether your traveling for business or pleasure

During a recent family trip to the northwest, my goal was to save the best for the last. Since the best in this case was also the most expensive hotel on our stay, we could only afford one night at the Hotel 1000. To be fair, the hotel staff and service at the Hotel 1000 was the best of all the places we stayed at during out vacation. Cudos to Keith at that front desk for making our dinner reservations and also somehow working in complimentary appetizers for us! The cookies and milk at bed time was also a nice touch. However, while the service was good, I still can't justify the $430 we paid for a room that looked out to the wall of the building next door. During our vacation, we stayed at other nearby hotels in Seattle with a room as nice, if not nicer for almost $140 cheaper. Based on this, I would not recommend the 1000 unless you manage to get an awesome room deal somewhere or have money to burn.

The location was great as it was close to all. Be careful, whenever you ask someone, they say it is a 15 minute walk. It is a little longer than that, but still walkable. The service was outstanding. The staff went out of their way to help!. The rooms were spacious and comfortable. I know you don't book rooms based on amenities, but it was nice that they had toothpaste in the rooms (thoughtful!!). We stayed on business, so the room rate was good, but the prices on the food, drink, etc are on the higher side. It was great to have a bar and restaurant right in the hotel. Would stay here again.

We has a very difficult time getting our room booked through hotels.com. We waited in the hotel lobby for 2.5 hours waiting on our confirmation to come through. We were pretty upset. The bartender Zachery and the lady at the first desk Brittney were very helpful. They understood the frustration and helped us out any way that they could. Once hotels.com finally corrected their mistake, we were able to enjoy our room and beautiful hotel. I will stay here again because of the friendly staff. I just will never use hotels.com again.

I stayed in a room on the front side of the hotel on the second floor. It was a nice, clean, and comfortable room but was very noisy. The train station next door meant that late at night and early in the morning you could hear the train and the announcements. The radiator in the bathroom made lots of noises through the night as well. My room was small, but well furnished. I am not a light sleeper and was very tired the week that I stayed here so all the noise didn't bother me too much, but this is something to keep in mind if noise keeps you awake.

I gave this hotel a 5 star rating, because you can leave your car here for 14 nights!! for the price of a one night stay $99.00, in covered parking...That is incredible, since airports charge you about $10-$15 a day. Sure you can get an off site parking place for cheaper than the airport, but it's so nice having the shuttle straight back to your hotel, especially if your staying there on your return leg. The neighborhood is not great, don't go to the bowling alley next door...scary. If you're going there soon...ask for a renovated room, unexpectedly very nice. The pool is in the middle of this U-shaped property and it's not heated, The fitness room looked good. The staff was fabulous!! The hotel is literally 5 minutes form the airport. If you do like to party and have time, go straight down 4th street to downtown. We went out for pizza at the 4th street pizza. It was Saturday night and there was a club on every corner that was hopping. We're too old for clubbing ; ) but. if you're still into that, it looked like a fun place to party. Minus the gang looking element, but you're going to find that in any environment like that. Great place to just park, sleep and fly~

Pleasantly suprised by hotel, was bit dubious owning to what we paid for 3 nights, but excellent value for money. Reception staff were pleasant and helpful. Free wireless connection and free computer with printer in lobby (used for online check in). Complementry breakfast was good with cereal, fruit and danish pastries. Rooms were fine, with no cleanliness issues or other problems except sliding wardrobe door which didn't want to slide. Coffee machine in room with coffee provided.
Excellent location right next to the old town with free parking.
Would stay there again if going back to San Diego.

title_masked: A few pointers to keep in mind
text_masked:
First, we got a terrific deal on the room at L'Enfant and the room was fabulous, wish we could have stayed three or four nights to get full enjoyment. We had a corner room on the nearly topmost floor with view of Potomac--however, on a weekend the food court (fast food places) may be closed so other than the two restaurants IN the hotel, other eating places are a haul--be prepared.
Second, if you have a deal on the parking as we did, you must take your first ticket from self-park to the desk so they can program your room card and let you swipe in and out of garage, HOWEVER, when entering garage, use the LEFT most ramp, it has the swiper, not the right hand side. No one told me that so I wound up with an additional self-park ticket. Other than that you can use the Metro in the Promenade level to go anywhere. Oh, TV was not necessarily visible form the bed placed where it was in a cabinet directly in front of a sofa.

We stayed 5 nights at the hotel and I could not fault their service. The room was stunning, the bed amazingly comfortable, the bathroom lovely and the staff extremely helpful, polite and friendly! It was centrally located especially if using the subway. Fairly close to Times Square too. Will hopefully be going back to NY next year and will definitely stay again. The Wheeltapper Bar was convenient for that morning coffee, and sports - if that's your thing - and the staff welcoming! Thank you for making my first stay in NY amazing!

I want to thank the US Grant staff for such a memorable birthday. My girlfriends and I stayed
there in August and the staff made us feel welcomed and special. We have traveled together 
and stayed at many luxury hotels but their service & friendliness has made for a better experience than anywhere else we've stayed. We loved the rooms and the plush bedding. We enjoyed their very hip lounge but did not get a chance to check out their award winning art gallery. Thanks for a wonderful memory. We are still raving about it!
The Fantastic Four

Myself & my Daughter stayed for 5 nights and loved it, the free cookies & tea/coffee went down a storm with her :) staff were great, spoke with Rory a couple of times asking directions and how best to get to places, nothing was too much trouble. just across the way from union square, cable car stops almost outside the door, a few blocks up from powell st station... easy walk with a wheeled case. wallgreens few doors away incase you need anything, liquor store round the corner if you want a couple of beers to take back. Ate at Sears next door among other places and found the Steak amazing :) rooms spotlessly cleaned everyday (thank you room attendent enjoy the mintballs) if i went back to san francisco without any question this is where i would want to stay. thank you for a great stay.

Stayed here for four nights from September 3 -7, 2012 for our first visit to Chicago. We were very pleased with the hotel and the location was great. Everything was within walking distance. We had a corner room on the 9th floor and it was clean, bright and modern. I don't understand other comments that the rooms were dark and dated, unless the hotel is under renovation, which I saw no indication of. The breakfast was good and the cocktails in the evening were great (thought I do have to say a few of the nights, the snacks at the evening cocktails were definitely a bit on the cheap side e.g.: stale popcorn). For those who complained that the lines at breakfast and evening cocktails were long -- this should be expected when there is free food and booze. The line for evening cocktails moved fairly quickly, but if you wanted the fresh-made omelette in the morning, it did take a while. The only thing that really annoyed me was the fact that WiFi cost $15 per day. We did not bother to get it, even though we brought a laptop, but in this day and age no hotel should charge for WiFi. Overall a great hotel and would definitely stay here again and recommend to anyone travelling to Chicago.

title_masked: Good place to stay in downtown Ft. Worth
text_masked: My wife was in Dallas for training for her new job so I drove out Memorial Day weekend to see her and have some fun. Everyone recommended going to Ft. Worth to the Stockyards but the cab fare from our hotel in Hurst was going to be very expensive so I used my Marriott points to get a room at the Courtyard downtown. It is an older hotel that has been renovated so the rooms are small but are very nice. The staff was very helpful in telling us what to see and where to go and getting us cabs. The hotel is very convenient to walk to Sundance Square and just enjoy the awesome downtown Ft. Worth area. We ended up staying another night and really enjoyed our stay. Not fancy but definitely a good place to land in Ft. Worth.

I should preface this review by saying that I am a complete hotel snob. It takes a LOT to impress me. I travel often for business and I'm lucky to have parents who worked in advertising and took us on travel. I'm also from NY originally, so that says a lot. :)
My girlfriend was visiting LA for the first time and we wanted to have the full Hollywood experience. We decided to book a hotel and spend the night partying at some fun places on the Boulevard. But how to choose a place? I called several hotels and was so unimpressed by the insanely high rates and their horrible attitudes.
The tone of my Roosevelt experience was set by Janie when I first called [NAME]. She was so genuinely kind and interested in my trip - who does that? She didn't treat me like just another guest, she made me feel valued even as a first timer. She helped us secure a room and even offered suggestions for restaurants/parties in the area - including the incredible Roosevelt pool party that I'd been to before and loved. :)
When we arrived at the hotel, valet was smooth and easy. And the woman at the front desk didn't look down at our straight-from-the-beach attire. In fact - she even offered to upgrade our room at no cost! From a boring king deluxe to... a cabana suite. A POOLSIDE CABANA SUITE.
Yeah. Cabana suite upgrade. SERIOUSLY? This stuff doesn't happen in real life. 
It was every bit as gorgeous in person as it was in my dreams. Spotlessly clean, comfy bedroom, huge dining/sitting room, outdoor lounge with firepit and the sickest waterfall shower I've ever experienced (sorry, W Hotel). I would marry that shower if it let me.
We spent our whole time at the Saturday pool party with our sliding door open. Combine this with a sick DJ? We didn't want to sleep, ever. The crowd was good, the bartenders were on point, and we met lots of new people. Pretty much all locals too - it wasn't a tourist spot. The staff was awesome too and let us chill outside until past 2AM. And then we sat by our firepit for another two hours. On Sunday we just hung out by the pool and blissed out. I can't say enough good things about that pool both daytime and night time.
I do have to emphasize how impressed we were by the staff. Every whim you have is catered to. We wanted our firepit lit? Done in five minutes by maintenance. Bartenders? Attentive and whipping out flawless cocktails within minutes. Room service? 20 minutes. Valet? 10 minutes. At peak checkout time. And everyone had a smile about them. It was like Disneyland with style. 
We ordered room service for every meal so we didn't have to leave the room. They were incredibly fast (even on a Saturday night) and everything was hot and fresh. The baked eggs were my favorite of our many meals, but my BFF was impressed by their large seasonal fruit plate. You know how they're usually skimpy and all cantaloupe? They had a million berries and lots of other options. Yeah... she needed to try my grilled cheese with short rib.
It was such a perfect trip, a perfect experience, perfect girls weekend, perfect everything. You will not find a better value or experience in Hollywood - or anywhere really. Everyone we encountered had similar experiences with the wonderful staff and spacious rooms - even those in the tower.
I've spent the last two weeks touting the Roosevelt to every single person I've encountered. I'm going to be a loyal Thompson hotel girl for life. I've already booked a room there for my birthday in December. :)

THe hotel it self was fine, help was good. We left our Ipad when we checked out and call the next day. IT took the hotel 5 calls on my part and 11 days before we got it back. They charged me shipping even thou we checked out a whole day early. Which I feel is the cheap way to go as we had paid for two nights and only stayed one night and checked out before 12pm. THey could have sold that room over again. 
Marye Newfield

My mother and I booked a once in a life time trip to New York, and were suffiecently impressed with the hotels website when booking.
On arrival, we were disappointed to see how different the website and real life version where. The hotel is 'tired', and the only saving grace was the fantastic conceirge- 'Michael' who was kind, incredibly helpful and gave fantastic recommendations.
The peak of the disappointment, was during the night before my birthday at 3:30am in the morning 4 very drunk and loud men started banging on our door (which was intimidating for 2 women on their own) and being sick outside the door. The next morning, when we reported this to reception, the receptionist made it very clear that the hotel didn't care about what had happened. The mess was cleaned up- eventually, but the hotel room and corridor stank of vomit for the next 3 days, which made us in turn feel ill. Although some staff at the hotel were lovely (the cleaners for example), the receptionists were rude and made it very clear that they were not there to help you. 
A disappointing stay in a hotel that looked so promising.

We are a couple in our early 30's that booked through Hotwire on a friend's recommendation and Hotel Fusion is what we got. After booking, we read reviews and instantly regretted using Hotwire but we didn't have a choice so we rolled with it and hoped for the best. 
We stayed at Fusion Jan 10, 11 & 12. This was our first trip to SF and this was also our 10 year anniversary. We had let the hotel know ahead of time that we'd prefer a 4th or 5th floor room (based on reviews) and that we'd be arriving late (11pm-ish). We were assured our request would be honoured. Upon arrival, we were told our room on the 4th floor was given away (despite the room was already paid in full a month in advance) so we were given a room on the 3rd floor with a room with a king size bed and plenty of room, which was nice. But seeing as the room was on the 3rd floor, overlooked Ellis Street and the nightclub below, we were subjected to being woken up 3-5 times a night because of street noise from the nightclub - and we were there mid-week (Tues, Wed, Thurs)!!! We are really easy going but when you just want to sleep due to a busy day of sight-seeing and jet jag, the noise was excessive and we were relieved we only booked this hotel 3 nights. I can't imagine staying there on a Fri & Sat. 
The positives are that it's an ideal location for shopping, public transportation, restaurants, landmarks, etc. The room was clean and a decent size. There is a continental breakfast that is just okay so we didn't bother. I did see instant oatmeal, oranges, apples, lots of pastries and coffee/tea/orange juice/apple juice.
We didn't use the fitness centre but there really isn't much in there.
I wouldn't recommend this hotel to couples, families or for business - it's just too loud. Possibly a student break crowd?
We loved SF but would look somewhere else to stay.

Chose this primarily for location 8 blocks to Moscone West for WWDC. Easy to get to hotel from the BART getting off at Powell Street station (4 block walk to the hotel). Hotel is in a great location about 1 block from Union Square. Rooms are small but comfortable. I could also hear street noise from the 6th floor but used ear plugs so noise wasn't an issue for me. Front desk staff and conceirge were very helpful arranging taxi's and giving directions to Fisherman's wharf using the Powell St. trolley. There is no air conditioning but it wasn't required for my stay in early June. There is no restaurant in the hotel but Lois's Diner is right next store for breakfast. Rooms are clean and given that rooms were getting booked up for WWDC, I was quite happy with the room.

title_masked: Great value in NYC. Close to everything Broadway
text_masked: Surprisingly quiet for downtown. Very close to everything Broadway. I took the kids (9 & 11) for a walk to Times Square and around to Rockefeller Centre and it was close. Close to 50th Subway stop too. Great breakfast but you have to get there before 7:30 to avoid the crowds. Free coffee/tea/hot chocolate 24 hours. Wi-fi is plug in and really fast. Room was clean and apparently large for NYC. Beds were comfortable and lovely bedding.

title_masked: Cozy + modern spot in Soho that is very SF-like
text_masked: I booked the James for a one night stay since we were headed to dinner around the corner and I just wanted to be able to do a quick walk to the Lani Kai bar. The James offers California style comforts in the middle of NYC. There is a rooftop pool bar with a view that is stunning, even complete with Burning man photography decorating the walls. The lobby area is gorgeous with stocked drinks and food at all times of the day. We even had breakfast at Burke's Kitchen the next morning and it was delish. I would stay here again anytime, also worth noting are the cool glass wall in the bathroom with a moving art screen.

I was one of three rooms there to celebrate my daughter's bachelorette weekend.
The hotel was very clean and always felt safe & secure. The personnel were very
helpful and nice. We had a great time : )

Great hotel and been updated, Four Seasons service. Try to get a higher floor to eliminate street noise. A view of the lake is nice. Perfect location within walking distance of good restuarants, great shopping and site seeing

After so many positive reviews of this hotel there's not much left to say. With that said, here's my 2 cents worth. The Homewood Suites is very comfortable within walking distance to attractions and restaurants. There's a friendly, helpful front desk staff. The breakfast buffet is plentiful and is kept well stocked. If your stay is on a weekday the hotel offers a dinner buffet and complimentary wine and beer. Clean, comfortable rooms and very affordable rates for D.C. I'd stay here again in a minute.

I got a free 2 night stay here by a promotional deal so we did not have to pay. Upon entering the lobby, it was truly grand when it was built in 79 but is now very very outdated. It was one of the most grand lobbies I ever seen but the decor was very 70s and in desperate need of updating. They are advertising as under remodeling as Wyndham hotel chain just bought this old Holiday Inn. The remodeling seems to be just some basic fixtures installed by staff, not professionals. We had a remodeled room. Whoever hung the towel racks must have downed a bottle of whiskey first. It was so crooked it was comical!!
The place was clean but the overwhelming smell of old mustiness was not pleasant. The entire place, in the rooms and the hallways just smelled like the inside of an antique store. Not completely foul but just not pleasant. They were playing this horrific pop noise that teenagers call music all through the very large facility. That needs to cease as an older crowd was always present. There were dozens of conference rooms, all busy with business people. 
Everything was clean. Service was very good when we needed anything. Staff was very good and friendly. There is a nice restaurant in the lobby. We did not eat there but some one told us it was very good. Breakfast is all you can eat buffet $6.95 but a menu is available too. Entry to the facility is tricky due to the disastrous construction going on the highway. Overall experience was ok. New carpeting throughout would likely rid that old smell and this place would be awesome. New carpeting may well be in the future plans.

What a brilliant place to stay for a woman travelling on her own! I made this place my home for a week on a recent business trip to the US from Melbourne Australia. This is an excellently located, well priced and welcoming hotel. The staff were always extremely helpful and friendly. Good amenities and a nice, quiet, safe place to stay.

I live in San Francisco and my family was visiting and we needed an overflow place to sleep in the neighborhood. I was blown away by the attention to detail and overall comforts of home detail in the rooms. The staff, Oscar and Tiffany was were super friendly and accommodating. I will recommend this unique motel to everyone . It is a unique gem in San Francisco.

title_masked: The best place to stay in Houston!
text_masked: This was our second visit to Hotel Granduca and we expected it to be excellent and it was! The staff is gracious and welcoming, the hotel is a little slice of Italy in Texas! Gorgeous hotel down to the last detail with fabulous bed linens. Fitness center was great, not as sterile as some can be. The staff in the beautiful lobby bar is top notch, pleasant and professional. The pool area serene and perfect for alfresco cocktails at sunset. We will certainly select this hotel again when Houston is the destination.

Granted, this Marriott property is across the street from a convention center so it doesn't try to be anything other than efficient. It is. But geez. A plainer white box I have never seen. And in a famously colorful town, too. One bar, one in-a-hurry restaurant, no theme, no flair, no attempt to be anything other than a place to lay a weary head. This is the kind of place you stay at because you have to, not because you want to.

The location was good- we were closest to the White House. They sell bus tickets onsite for Big Bus Tours, a hop on hop off tour. 
Loved the dinners Monday-Thurs and the breakfast buffet had waffles, eggs, bacon, cereal, fruit, yogurt, and much more.
A really good place to stay- would recommend to anyone- rooms were quiet and front desk was helpful.

Hotel is in great location. Very nice and clean. Used indoor pool and workout facility; both are well-maintained. Parking in nearby garage was $30 per day or even more expensive by the hour so we chose to walk all over city instead of moving car and paying hourly fee. Hotel offers valet parking for $40 per day plus tips/taxes. Food court adjacent to hotel with lots of choices; everything closes at 8:00 or earlier. We paid $450 for 2nts - simple room with two double beds. Seemed high but we split with another couple to make it affordable. Haven't stayed in another nearby location so I don't have any other accommodations for comparison.

Awesome and clean hotel. Nice rooms and very inexpensive. Closest to IU hospital and Riley's hospital for kids? It was very quiet and a short ride. They are very kind and helpful. Great value for the price would stay again.

I booked a King Spa Premier Suite two months in advance for mine and my wife's anniversary. When we got to the room, I noticed that the bathroom did not match the pictures I had seen nor the descriptions from the website. My wife called the front desk to make sure we got the right room and was promptly assured we were. After looking at their website once again, I knew it was not the right room so I decided to call guest services and explain why. I read the exact description from their website and was told that ours was different because it was handicap accessible. I told them that the floors were not Italian Marble and no stand up separate shower. Also, I had requested a higher floor way in advance and was put on the very bottom floor with terrible views. I am a Kimpton InTouch member and was not expecting this type of service from a hotel rate so highly. Word of advice to all who plan to stay here....make sure you get what you pay for.

title_masked: What a surprise! A gorgeous Hotel.
text_masked:
. This Hotel is a beautiful and the check in process was smooth and quick they were very attentive and helpful and kind. 
 I believe the girl who checked us in her name was [NAME]. So friendly and seemingly genuinely so, it didn't appear it was just because it was the job. I was surprised when we went to our room because it was just so luxurious feeling. It was a beautiful, well decorated Room. It was a convenient location, close to downtown. We were able to catch the Hotel Shuttle to a local place we went too, got a cab back. I honestly considered just ordering in and not going that is how nice the Hotel is. 
Spent some time at the bar, great drinks, and I thought reasonably priced too. 
 A couple of draw backs, very small and quickly corrected except for one. The TV didn't work when we got there so we called down, within 5 minutes someone was there and he was extremely friendly also. (The TV was unplugged didn't think to check that) We didn't have a room service menu. However this was quickly corrected when we called down. Room service breakfast didn’t have the usual condiments with the breakfast (ketchup for the potatoes, hot sauce for the eggs, no preserves or Jelly for the bread, no water with breakfast) However the food was good. 
The most disappointing thing was I booked the room because of the Jacuzzi tub. It didn't work, however I didn't know it didn't work until I was in it taking a bath so I couldn't very well call for service on it. I was very disappointed though. I would make sure upon booking that it is working. Also it appeared the floors in the bathroom could have used a better cleaning, but everything else was spotless.

title_masked: beautiful lobby but very thin walls- too noisy!
text_masked: This hotel was very expensive usually but we got a deal so decided to splurge. It is located on Nobb Hill, near all the action of down town shopping and great for walking most places if you like hiking (hills are steep and hard on knees). That being said, we were disappointed in the stay mostly because the walls were so thin that we heard music and talking in the room next door as well as talking in the hall all hours of the night, and sirens driving by the window in the am hours. For such a top rated (by trip advisor) hotel we expected better! Bedding was very nice except maids did not change sheets and we stayed for 3 days! We ate at the famed Tango Room for $100 plus dollars for 2 and didnt think that was anything special either.

the always reliable Georgetown Inn continues to succeed. New management is sprucing the place up while many of the old staff remain to make the stay personal and personable. The Keurig coffee makers are a great addition to the rooms.

title_masked: Really nice hotel - the rooms are loosing a bit of their cache, but it's still very nice.
text_masked: I've stayed here before so I was looking forward to returning. The check-in was a breeze. The front desk staff were friendly and efficient. The room service food (French Onion Soup & Mini Greens salad) were absolutely perfect. The swimming pool was nice, but it is in need of an up-grade. It's not the cleanest pool in the world and they don't enforce any kind of diaper policy - so kids in saggy diapers are in there all the time. Also, there is a $10 fee for using the pool. Normas restaurant had lovely food, but the service was a bit contrived. The host was arrogant. Also I sat for 20 minutes before anyone offered me coffee or juice. It took another 45 minutes to get my food and coffee. I was just starting the food when the waiter slapped down the bill and told me he would take the payment. I thought that was a bit much. On the other hand, the bar there is lovely ... sort of The Russian Tea Room meets Amman, Jordan ... with friendly, beautiful wait staff.

This perfectly placed and beautiful hotel was exactly what we were looking for! The staff was very attentive (although an alternative to calling down for ice would be nice) and made sure that we had everything we needed both in the hotel and on our days exploring the city.
By NYC standards, the room was huge and we were thrilled to be able to stay in one room rather than two! I also can't say enough about the lounge area - Well, except that I wish we had more time to spend there!
Thank you so much for making our trip special - Looking forward to coming back again soon!

title_masked: One of my best vacations ever.
text_masked: I have stayed at many hotels in my life & this resort surpasses them all. The parking was very convenient. We had a great garden view on the main level which gave us easy access to the main hotel & pool. On my daughters birthday the pool attendant surprised her pool side with a courtsey piece of chocolate cheese cake. The business center was very helpful with helping me print etickets to Sea World & parasailing events. The location is in walking distance to the beach, Belmont Park & a host of restaurants. We definitly will go back again in the future.

Stayed for one night on business on a quick fly in fly out. This hotel desperately needs renovation to meet minimal business standards. Room while maintained as best as possible has old decor, a 25 in tube TV which had a terrible picture and since my room was on the top floor there had been a roof leak and the repair job was obvious. The conciege lounge was well run and the attendant was very professional and nice. She helped people with their requests and kept everything well stocked. Overall the service was very good, they just need a better facility. Wifi signal was weak and spotty in my room as well, I use only and iPad while traveling and went to 3G for a better signal.
After meetings the first day I checked out the sports bar. It was dead, no one there at all, just TVs and a bartender. I opted for room service. Food was good and server was prompt and again professional.The only staff person who was questionable was the front desk. The young man obviously grew up in the inner city. While dressed impeccably his use of slang and accent would probably be near impossible for many travelers to understand. I thought he was funny but I could see why some may be offended.
After a recent stay at another Renaissance property in Mobile which was great I thought I would try again. Bad choice this time. Will probably go back to mid range newer business hotels than this type of "full service".

My husband and I booked one of the smaller suites here for a long weekend in March of 2011 and really enjoyed the hotel... But when we returned for a long weekend recently — staying in a standard room this time — it was a huge disappointment. 
Here's what sucked:
1. We got booked into an ADA-compliant room. Nothing says "romantic weekend" like hand rails all over the place #sarcasm. We'd also reserved a room with a king bed. No dice. We got a queen. We asked to be switched, and they told us they could only switch us for the second night of our stay... not worth packing everything up and moving, we thought, so we stayed — although what if a person who needed an ADA room had wanted to stay there??
2. NO SAFE in the room. I've never encountered this before at a "nice" hotel, and it made me very nervous to have to leave my valuables in a dresser drawer all weekend.
3. When my husband called to express our frustrations with these issues, he asked if they could comp our wi-fi, which is $14/day otherwise. He got bumped to a manager who said he'd take care of it... When we went to check out, though, the charges were on our bill. Good thing we checked! Even when we referenced the manager's name and said he'd assured us we'd be comped, we still had to argue with them to get the charges removed.
4. The bathroom. This was not only a royal pain in the [--], but a humongous safety hazard. Since we were in a handicapped room, the shower floor was just part of the regular floor, so a wheelchair can roll in. But when they built the place, they must have done a crappy job laying the drain, because the drain was no lower than the rest of the floor. I came out of the shower the first time and discovered a lake of water — a good 1/4 inch deep — all across the floor, soaking the toiletries case and makeup bag I'd put on the floor. We had to mop the floor up every time after showering, and the floor was still wet and VERY slippery. 
5. There are two elevators serving our half of the hotel. Our first full day there, one of them broke. This meant there was ONE elevator to serve dozens of rooms. The elevator was still broken when we checked out.
6. TV didn't work. We found this out our final evening there... at that point, we were so frustrated we didn't even bother to ask someone to fix it — plus we were headed out to dinner and didn't want to wait around for a technician.
Now, to be fair, here's what didn't suck: 
1. Bed was comfy. 
2. We requested and received a late check-out without any trouble.
After staying here the first time, I recommended this hotel to several friends. I'm now embarrassed at the thought that they may have had experiences like this one. I plan to tell everyone about this total bust of a booking and warn them to avoid this hotel — or, at the very least, the standard rooms — in the future.
Small room but comfy bed, clean bathroom, great staff, quiet, nice outdoor patio with firepits and seasonal chairs, close to the Metro. Internet special of $129.00 was a steal

Stayed at the Omni Parker House Hotel for a long weekend getaway in July. It's in an excellent location for all downtown Boston attractions. Just a 5 minute walk from Boston Commons and 15 minutes to the harbour. Staff was very friendly and rooms were clean. Couldn't ask for much more!!

Beautiful Joel with terrific staff. They're professional, polite and will do anything to keep clients happy. The hotel has a nice restaurant and bar with outdoor seating. It's centrally located near all attractions. They have good coffee, but there's a Starbucks right across the street if that's your preference.

This is thee closest hotel to LAX, I even saw people walking from the airport to the hotel entrance with their bags. It sits parallel to one of the runways so if you like to watch the planes land and take off, request a room like I did. The rooms are spacious but, they definitely need a refurbishment. Check in was a breeze and there are many amenities to take advantage of...the free wi-fi is great.

Out of town Wedding so entire Family booked here. We had +10 rooms. They worked with us for a group rate, The staff was great, accomodating. The Hotel was very clean and nice setting. Great size pool and rooms were roomy with a microwave and refregerator in all. It was a good nights sleep. Noise levels did not carry thru walls. Walking distance to Old Town. Free breakfast every morning. Would stay again!
Best of all, I left my gold chain with gold & diamond charm in room, called next day and they had it!!
Great Choice the bride's family chose!

Nice old hotel, with recent renovation. Great UWS location in a real residential neighborhood with nearby grocery stores, etc. for a more "authentic" sense of NYC. Helpful concierge, front desk staff and doormen. Maids were efficient and unobtrusive. Rooms, though small as is typical in NYC, are spotless, well equipped and beds and linens are luxurious. All rooms air-conditioned. Free wi-fi. Restaurant right downstairs and many others close by. Duane Read drugstore directly across the street has wonderful selection of snack foods, drinks and fresh fruit. They had an elevator problem during my stay, with one out of order for three days, leaving only one operating. This was inconvenient. Overall, a very pleasant experience.

Hotel was clean but definitely needs some sprucing up. The staff was the best part! Very friendly, prompt and helpful! The restaurant was too expensive to consider an option. There are plenty of nearby places to choose from, but the area made me think twice about wanting to walk to many of them alone.

title_masked: Keep a Copy of EVERY Receipt
text_masked:
I recently attended the Philadelphia Stop of the Professional Bull Riders tour in Philadelphia. The Holiday Inn was the "event" hotel (partnered with the fan club,) so I booked a room. 
The complex of venues (football stadium, baseball stadium and indoor arena) with this hotel is very convenient. Everything is within reasonable walking distance. Additionally, within this complex is what I like to call a "sports bar mosh pit," where you can (just) drink, enjoy finger food or sit down for a reasonably nice meal. 
After the PBR event my wife and I went to the lounge at the Holiday Inn for a drink. I signed the drinks to my room account and left a cash tip. At check-out, I found the bartender had added a sizeable tip to my room tab. Unfortunately I did not keep my copy of the bill.
All efforts at check-out and for days afterward to rectify this were futile. Interestingly, at another restaurant in this complex, I was told they were prohibited from adding tips to transactions being paid-for with plastic. That should have been a clue.
The hotel was okay. Just make sure you keep a copy of every receipt to protect yourself from what happened to me. And don't rely on the hotel to "make it right."

Chelsea Pines is like our second home. We go there since 2005 once a year because it's really a pleasure to stay there. The location is really wonderful, the best to know Chelsea, Meatpacking, Village and close to the High Line. The subway is out of the hotel and in the 8th Ave there are a lot of very nice shops and restaurants. The staff of Chelsea Pines is really the kindest and friendliest we ever met and they do all the efforts they can to make our stay in the hotel comfortable and enjoyable. The rooms, inspired to the movie stars of the past, are really nice and comfortable. So, see you next year!

Comfortable rooms and friendly staff. The shuttle drivers were excellent, although we sometimes had to wait over an hour for them to arrive. Dirty carpets on fourth floor due to renovation work - it made the area look dirty, although it was tidy. Breakfast buffet not very appetising and closed at 9am despite the brochure saying breakfast was served until 10. It's not very convenient to get Downtown - a shuttle bus then public transport, but the buses are reliable. Overall a good experience and we would return because of the friendly staff.

title_masked: Great location with old school NYC charm!
text_masked: Lets get something straight...this is a mid range hotel and not high end nor do they claim they are. Most people with complaints here are probably expecting the Penninsula at mid-range prices. Newsflash...hotels in NYC are expensive! If you are staying here, even for $250-300/night you are still paying for a mid range hotel. I have stayed here numerous times for business trips and have never experienced anything that was so negative that it would prompt me to waste my time writing a review. Now, I have experienced a room with an old/musty smell...also had a room that was not properly cleaned...but guess what?? I PICKED UP THE PHONE and changed my room! That's all it takes. Their staff is more than helpful and have always resolved any issues for me. The rooms are fine....the beds are comfortable and clean. The location cannot be beat and in my opinion you cant get a better deal. This review is from someone that has stayed here a total of 17 times!

The hotel is quite old, the elevator is small and narrow, facilities are just so so, however, it really has a perfect location! Walking distance to Michigan Ave and Navy Pier. 
There Arevsome fancy restaurants very nearby.

We stayed just one night at the intercontinental on a quick trip down to see a show. I booked through hotwire so got the room under $400 for a saturday night, was a good deal for that weekend. I was pleased with the front desk, very warm and friendly welcome. Our room was not ready yet so we went to lunch, and had a message that we were all set to check in before we finished eating. Hotel is easy walk to time square, but I suggest walking the other direction for a great selection of restaurants in easy reach. I am pretty pregnant and this location was good because I could walk short distances easily, and there was always a cab available for whenever I needed to go more than a few blocks. The room was a good size for New York, certainly bigger than I expected from previous stays in the area. Well appointed for a 4 star hotel, bed was comfortable, everything was clean and orderly. But I need to talk about the bathroom, because that is where this hotel stood out, in my opinion. Bathroom is NYC hotels arent always the best. This was more like something you would see in Las Vegas, to be honest. It was not huge but certainly larger than average, and very well designed. Glass tiled walk-in with a rain shower... I love rain showers. There was a hand-held too if you want that. No tub, but this shower was worth the loss :) Nice amenities in the bath too, good products that were good sized, plus a little box of the extras you sometimes need to ask for (sewing kit, q-tips, showercap, etc). We did have breakfast at the hotel but I wouldnt repeat that, it was very expensive for what it was. Good, but pricey, and there are so many options so close by... if I am paying $22 for my eggs I expect my waiter to keep my water glass full, at least. Overall I would stay here again.

The area has all types of shopping and dining. The Hotel has everything you need on a more intimate level. A restaurant with a full service bar. Rooms seem larger than the Marriott I stayed in a couple of exits away and all new furnishings at the Sheraton. Nice large desk with a comfortable lounge chair. Great bed!
10 minutes to the beach and close enough to the city. You are less than 5 minutes away from every imaginable chain restaurant.

title_masked: We love New York and Eastgate Tower
text_masked: My husband and I just spent 5 nights at the Eastgate Tower. It was our first trip to NYC and we weren't disappointed. We used public transit to travel from LaGuardia airport to Grand Central Terminal and then it was an easy walk to our hotel. Melange Green and Gourmet, an excellent take-out spot is just down 39th st, near 3rd Ave, as is a very nice grocery store, D'Agostina. Our suite was spacious, clean and comfortable. The staff are very friendly. The hotel is in a very quiet neighbourhood, yet is within walking distance of many sites and very close to transit. We will definitely return to Eastgate Tower for our next vacation to New York city.

The trip started with my son's dream trip from Virginia to see his long time favorite NFL team, the San Diego Chargers on Monday Night Football. I explained to the person I spoke with in reservations my desire to make this a special trip for him. She worked with me to leverage my past stays, etc, etc to get into a room that perfectly suited our needs. We stayed on the club floor, completely worth the Starwood Points upgrade, and enjoyed a great breakfast with a great view each morning and evening.
The staff at the hotel was exceptional and my new friend in reservations had passed along that this was a special occasion. The hotel staff went out of their way to make our stay great.
I can't say enough about what a great hotel this is for it's proximity to the Gas Lamp District, the beaches and the airport. It was also easy to get to and from the game at Qualcomm. Not as convenient as Hotel Circle, but FAR nicer and more relaxing. You can get by without a car, but I highly recommend getting one(Mustang Convertible was great1) as it will cost about the same as taxis and you can do much more in a day. Warning. Parking is $22 day at the hotel and a little inconvenient when the hotel is full, but manageable.
Thanks to the staff at the Sheraton for taking such good care of us.
Next time Chagers, don't blow a 24-0 lead at the half.

This is the second time we have stayed here, the last a year ago and went back as the location for us is great, really close to Pike Place Market and down the hill to downtown - walking back up is not so good but walking in Seattle just involves hills! Close to bus stops (free bus system in central areas). The rooms we have had have all been clean with comfy beds and nice bathrooms. The staff are really helpful and very knowledgeable about eating, drinking and sight seeing places. The wifi wasn't very good in the room but fine in the lobby and free.

I stayed here 2 nights - travelling with 3 dogs. The hotel was very clean (no strange odors, no bugs) and quiet. The front desk staff were very attentive and courteous and gave me a free snack and water bottle when I checked in. The room came with a microwave and refridgerator. An excellent La Quinta- A++++

First the staff... Ariel, Maria, Cathy, the Big Guy in the Evening and even Wayne were all super great team that provide quality service.
The hotel... Very clean all areas, close to subway, Times Square, Fashion District, and Broadway
The Room... Clean, Comfy, Clean VERY CLEAN... 
Free Wifi and Free Breakfast 
Safety... I am a mother travelling with a teen daughter and I felt very safe at night walking back to the hotel.
We stayed 10/2012

So the first few nights were ok, then around the third day I started getting bites. At first I thought it might have been something on the street but when I started recieving more and more then I realized that it was Bed Bugs. By the time I got home my skin was swollen and red. I called the hotel to tell them but they hung up on me. So, if you dont want your house infested (had to spray mine) then I would not stay here. Just wanted to warn everyone before they went through the same hardship that i did.

The hotel is surrounded by other chain hotels - next time I would check one of those. Reception was very pleasant, room is spacious and quiet. Internet was not working, I was told it must be my fault because no one else had complained. I took the laptop downstairs and was able to connect - turns out the room is almost out of range. There were no towels in the room, when I called down I was told to come down and collect the towels myself. The rate was good (we use the tourist couple books) but there are a number of other hotels in the same range or cheaper that would be as good as if not better. Pool is nice but small, ditto exercise room.

Stayed here for the first 3 nights of our honeymoon in May this year. Arrived mid afternoon after a tiring flight from Manchester. Reception staff very friendly and made us feel right at home. Got to our room quickly and after a few minutes were surprised by a delivery of prosecco to celebrate the start of the honeymoon! The location is really good, it's about a 15 yard walk to times square itself. The room was lovely, not the largest but very clean and in good condition. The breakfasts were good, coffee, tea and pastries with fruit and yogurt which set us up for the day. THe free wine and nibbles in the evening was also great. All in all a lovely hotel and a great start to the honeymoon.

title_masked: First rate, by far one of the best in DC
text_masked:
I don't need many words; great hotel, amazing staff, modern rooms and the perfect location. One word....GO
Actually, TA won't print w/o more words. We have stayed here 4 years in a row and we have loved every stay. Truly one of the best in DC. OK TA did I meet the 200 character minimum???

title_masked: Pleasantly surprised at the low price
text_masked: Stayed a Saturday night. Hotel is located right off of Hwy 59 and between a Denny's and office buildings. Front desk was polite, fast and helpful. Room description said that microwave and fridge were available on request (and for a fee) so didn't bother, but when I got to the room they were both there and I was not charged. Ac/heater worked great. Room was very clean! Bathroom was small but served it's purpose eventhough the shower pressure was lacking...no huge deal. Bed was comfortable. Had 2 nightstands and a desk with chair. Tv was fine. Pool looked small but clean. Having Denny's right next door was nice since the breakfast at the hotel was bare minimum. Overall, clean, safe and had an unbeatable price. Will stay again.

title_masked: Shabby room but amazing location and staff
text_masked:
The lobby of the hotel is lovely and the location is amazing, a few minutes walk from Union Square, the cable car turn around, metro etc. You're really near a Westfield shopping centre and have food places and bars just a couple of doors down from the hotel.
We knew the hotel was being refurbished but i did expect a little more from the actual room decor - the bathroom door didn't close properly and the lock didn't work due to it being forced open at some point and just not repaired. The paintwork in the room was a bit shabby and had been patched up on a number of places in the room.
There was a mirror across the whole wall behind the tv/table and for some reason a painting stuck on the mirror in the middle of it (? hiding a crack maybe?). The air con unit outside our room was a little off-putting but some ear plugs soon sorted that out.
The staff were lovely and couldn't have been more helpful and so despite the shabby look of the room, i woul stay at this hotel again as a few bits of peeling paint here and there is not really an issue for me. The location and friendlness of the staff far ouweighed any asthetic issues.

title_masked: Fantastic Hotel in a great location
text_masked: We have stopped in New York many times and The Crosby Street Hotel is our favourite hotel. The location is superb for shopping in SoHo. Little Italy and China Town are easily within walking distance. The hotel itself is like a home from home with fantastic decor and features. Great bar and really friendly staff. I would recommend this place for anyone looking for a well run and stylish boutique hotel. Ivor and Joanne Allchurch. Worcestershire UK

title_masked: Very good hotel and perfect location
text_masked: We enjoyed the Orchard Garden very much; very good location for turists, walking distance from about everywhere, shoppings, cable car, buses and more. The rooms are fine, but I would choose the double instead the king room. Staff was very pleasant and helpfull, giving us an early check-in after a looooong trip, wich was great. The streets near Union Square are a little scary by night, but not the hotel street, a few steps from Chinatown gate. I also recomend Cafe de la Presse, right across the street.

I stayed from Friday April 27 to sunday April 29 2012. First things, i booked the hotel under comfort inn and suites, to come to find out the hotel switched names, so we pasted the hotel at first. I called the number to verify it was the former comfort inn and the lady on the phone said yes. I then asked her what garage to park in since there are several on the block. She proceeded to be rude, then hung up on me! Once we got parked, we had to carry all our luggage a block in downtown chicago on the street. Trying to check in took OVER 20 mintues. No employees there knew how to work the computers or what they were doing, i told them the woman on the phone hung up on me, and they didnt even respond with an apology or anything. Tons of constructions, construction worker in the lobby and breakfast area. Dust everywhere. Workers have loud radios they listen to. Our room was VERY small but an updated one. No mini fridge, no drawers, not even a clock in the room which was odd. Plus theres a glowing kiss print on the bathroom mirror you cant turn off that glows under the door at night. My boyfriend checked us out, while i was still packing. Once I returned the parking pass later on, the first desk woman told me my bf already got the receipt, i asked him and he said no. She acted like i was lying to her, and got an attitute about it because she obviously didnt know how to work the computers to print it out. Finally about 5 minutes later, she realized it was on the counter! with no apology or anything she just handed it to me, no "thanks for coming" or "have a great day". Staff was SO rude and needed training BEFORE the hotel was ready for business extremely disappointed.

title_masked: Good hotel, great location, expensive amenities
text_masked: I stayed here with a group of friends October 2012. We had two rooms and a suite on the 7th floor. Hotel was very clean and welcoming, pool and hot tub area were very clean. We picked this location because we were going to a concert at The Trocadero which is about a two minute walk from the hotel. They nickel and dime you on parking, which is $33 ($37 if you want it added to your room) and the only breakfast option is a $16 cooked to order breakfast in the upstairs restaurant. Skip the pricey breakfast and go next door to the Reading Terminal Market which is a famous Philly landmark and you can get anything you want and it will only cost you about $5.

title_masked: That was an excellent present for my birthday
text_masked: I was looking for hotels in NYC for my vacation for my birthday.I found Sofitel on very very reasonable price and the hotel is amazing.The location couldnt be more perfect and the service was outstanding.The view from the room was nice,the rooms was renovated and new,nice and clean.Great experience I will visit this hotel again.

My wife and I stayed here back in early spring. We were a little intimidated by the size at first. But after settling into our room and the subsequent small tours of the property, we were like old pros. :). Our room was a newer remodel so no complaints there. We can understand other folks complaints about sub par rooms etc. This resort is rather large w/many different rooms. I can see them not being able to remodel all the rooms yet. 
The pools are great and the grotto area just outside the resort (maybe 45 feet) was fun. Our only complaints would be that parking can be a chore because of the hills. (not as steep as they appear on their website,however). Something that should be fixed is we were not told that their Mexican themed restaurant just below us would be closed our entire stay. When making reservations make sure you ask if there are any conventions or proms scheduled during your planned stay. Noise was not a factor but room availability and parking could be scarce. Ask for a remodeled room. If you are fine taking elevators, having to walk longer distances than most hotels, having to look at area maps your first two days it is worth it. 
One more major complaint : the spa offered discount massages. They were terrible. Our experiences were far from satisfactory. We were told we had to pay first (no, no in that industry) our massages were not only faster (time wise) than what we were told our masseuses were both late. No apology was offered to my wife. We cannot recommend the spa because of our experiences. We always enjoy the spas wherever we vacation.....

title_masked: Excellent choice if wanting to be near to Universal Studios
text_masked: We stayed here for 3 nights (2 adults and a teenager) in a standard room with 2 queen beds. The room was well equipped with hair dryer and toiletries but no fridge. Breakfast was included in the room rate. It has a small fitness room and an outdoor pool with bar area (I believe it also has an indoor pool but we didn't use it). Our room had a fairly nice view over the rear of the property and pool area. There was plenty of parking and also valet parking which was more expensive. I think parking was around $15 a day. The buffet breakfast was good with a choice of hot and cold items. The main advantage of this hotel is that it is walking distance (10 mins) to Universal Studios and Universal City walk. There is also easy access to Hollywood via the metro. The hotel arranged a tour of LA for us and the company sent a minibus to collect us. The hotel can arrange a variety of tours and excursions and the concierge staff are very helpful. This is a really nice place to stay if visiting Universal and/or Hollywood with friendly and helpful staff. All in all a very positive experience. Would stay here again.

title_masked: Bad service... Too expensive for what you get.
text_masked: I stayed at this hotel after booking on hotels.com for a 2 night stay in early August. The rooms were relatively clean (although we did have some dirt stained towels in one of the rooms). We chose this hotel because breakfast was included in the room charge and it was a more central location but that did not substantiate the cost of the room. We could have stayed at a much nicer hotel for the price we paid. The first night that we stayed there, the hotel lost power and it did not come back on until almost noon the next day. They did not have hot breakfast (which is what we paid for) until very late in the morning. They sent us to the neighboring property to use the pool. There was no internet. What makes matters worse, they said they would contact us to provide some type of good will credit as a courtesy for the inconvenience. They did not contact us. We had to contact them and when we did the Sales Manager at the hotel, instead of being hospitable, was very argumentative, denied ever having a power loss, and concluded the conversation by hanging up on me while I was mid-sentence. Unbelievable, is all I can say. I am not usually a complainer however this experience made me pipe up. It was ridiculous. Steer clear of this hotel, you can stay at the Hilton for the same price.

After twenty four hours of travel I crashed here for a night recently. The whole experience was terrific. Picked up by a cheerful bus driver from the terminal (long story...I think it is a very easy walk but it was late and I was tired and I couldn't find/see the signs and the airport help desk assured me I needed the bus), friendly check in, large quiet room, excellent light meal late at night in the foyer restaurant..what more can I say? Oh yeah, the check out was a snap, and the internet worked well both in room and at the guest terminals in the foyer

When my girl friends and I were in Chicago for Lollapalooza last week we wanted a hotel that was a) close to Grant Park b) cool, safe, clean and had a boutique vibe c) was going to offer us luxury after long days in the hot summer Chicago sun.
Our choice? The Allerton Hotel Chicago on Magnificent Mile and it was truly magnificent.
The Allerton Hotel Chicago recently had a multi-million-dollar renovation to match the dynamic downtown setting on the Magnificent Mile. Every element of the engaging redesign reflects a contemporary and sophisticated, yet residential, feel. Luxuriate in sleek, modern rooms and suites appointed with every conceivable comfort, along with a few surprises. Dine in the chic, trendy M Avenue Restaurant. For meetings, weddings, and special events, their venues have been stunningly modernized to stage signature gatherings. 
The historic configuration of the hotel ensures a memorable experience in each of the hotel’s 443 luxuriously appointed guest rooms and 84 suites.
We took the train from the Midway airport to the hotel – it took less than 30 minutes and was an easy and non complicated ride. The check in was easy upon our arrival and we were able to leave our bags with the bell men whilst we set off to explore the city. 
When we finally did settle into our rooms, we found the space to be warm, inviting, clean, with new carpeting; sweeping panoramic views of the Chicago skyline, majestic cathedral ceilings, the rooms were free of any weird odours and emanated an elegance right out of Domino Magazine. I was impressed.
I loved the heavenly beds, the puffy and yet firm pillows, the powerful shower heads and soap sets, the pale blues and marshmallow shades in the rooms were soothing and serene, the padded white punctuated headboard felt like I was staying in a South Beach hotel suite, the abundance of towels and huge TV monitors which played HBO series (a blessing for a girl who doesn’t have cable at home) along with loads of other great entertainment channels made me feel like I was staying in a palace.
I liked that the Allerton Hotel was not a ‘party’ hotel but more a professional and mature space. This was huge when we came back after a 10-12 hour day. Relaxation was key and is what we got for the 6 days we stayed at the Allerton Hotel.
In the morning if you need a quick caffeine fix - you can venture down to the 2nd floor where from the hours of 6 a.m. – 11 a.m. you can have a lovely cup of Joe on the house. The coffee was indeed very yummy.
I loved the overall aesthetic of the hotel. This is a listed building and it is lovingly maintained. From the brickwork, exquisitely decorated rooms, hallways and common spaces, always helpful staff and overall architecture I definitely felt like we were staying in a building full of history and interesting stories. I felt instantly comfortable and very much at home.
After long days at Lollapalooza and trekking around Chicago, I really appreciated coming back to the Allerton Hotel Chicago and kicking back on my King Size bed.
I heard a few complaints from fellow guests about the elevators – ok, fair enough they are small. But this hotel was built in 1922 so the elevators speak to a time where North American elevators weren’t built to the size of sitting rooms. Personally, we never had to wait long for an elevator and to be frank I thought the elevators harkened to times of old and had a European feel.
Bring on Lollapalooza 2013! ;)

title_masked: There are better options for the same money in New York-- go to the Warwick!
text_masked:
Hi there,
I never ever write reviews for anything just because I am always skeptical about the outlook of people who give scathing reviews and wonder if the glowing reviews are written by hotel staff/ affiliates. However, my experience at the Millenium has been so terrible it deserves a review. I have been in New York for a few days over the past couple of weeks. So, I have stayed in a number of mid-range priced hotels-- the Warwick, the Westin near times square and now the Millenium. The Millenium is by far the worst I have ever seen. 
I checked in at 7pm following my flight, and my room was not yet ready. Apparently, the room wasn't clean yet. So, I ask how long the room will take to be ready. The man at the desk responds that they are extremely short staffed and no one has the guts to tell the managers for fear of losing their jobs but that they are doing the best they can. He then throws drinks coupons at me, and asks me to wait. I proceed to the bar and have one drink and a salad. This takes about an hour. My room still isn't ready. I head back to the bar where I chat with other clientele who like me, have their bags and no room. 
At 9:30pm I am told my room is ready and that I am being upgraded to the Premier Tower. My room is on an extremely low level and backs up to an alley. So, I can hear all the LOUD sounds of the city and all the rooms when I step inside my room. I then notice that the bed is dirty, sheets are thrown all over, and the bathroom smells funky. This was the beginning of my stay. I will never stay there again, and will tell everyone I know to go to the Warwick. It is cheaper, cleaner and quieter. It is a better hotel. This hotel was the absolute pits--- please avoid at all costs and do not book your clients there!

Chose this hotel for a week-long business trip to Houston as it was the most economical downtown option. Due to a booking glitch, I ended up taking a junior suite instead of a standard room.
What I liked: Convenient location - 5 mins walk to the convention center & Toyota Center, and 10-15 mins walk to Minute Maid Park as well as most downtown shopping and eating places. Helpful and friendly staff. Spacious and quiet rooms with good facilities (fridge, microwave), cleaned daily. Standard breakfast for HIE but nice touch with the milk and cookies every afternoon. Small pool - good for kids.
What could be improved (if possible): Area around the hotel was very isolated after dark. Hotel looked dated in some areas (elevators, exterior). No in-room safe. Public transportation a little sparse and unpredictable, especially on weekends. Carpet felt a little damp when I arrived, not sure if that was due to a recent cleaning.

After staying in many Sheratons around the world, this one was abit dissapointing. The hotel itself is old, that cant be helped. The lobby is very nice and vibrant and the staff are helpful. The rooms are on the smaller side, but are clean and have comfortable beds. The hallways are abit dark, and the pool area looks abit "Motel" style. We booked the club lounge, which had a nice breakfast, and nice variety of hot and cold snacks in the evening. Only downfall is there is nothing to offer between the breakfast and the evening. Would be nice to see some coffee or biscuits on offer throughout the day. It does have sheraton qualities, but it is more a "Four Points" style in my opinion. It is very convenient to Universal Studios and shuttles run all day to Citywalk. If there again, id stay at the Hilton next door.

I am in NYC several times a month for cultural events, but living only 45 minutes away, it is a real splurge to stay overnight. I'm a fan of the Marriot, whenever I travel, so I was not disappointed with this one! EVERTHING is always top notch, the service is superb, the rooms breathtaking (yes, you definitely should spring for the Times Square view!). If I have a complaint, it would be the mattress was not the same comfort level of others I've had in the past. And it goes without saying, the location is great. And I love the elevator system they have worked out. This was my second stay here and I will do it again....and again.....and again!

To start off I am usually not a big complainer. I typically understand and tolerate limitations of a hotel property. Here is my story posted on Facebook back in April 2012. 'Hilton San Francisco Financial District do not stay here if you are adverse to noise. I am on the 25th floor of a 27 floor bldg. I hear road noise as if I was on street level. I was talking with Teresa this morning on cell and had her on speaker and got a call from security that the next door neighbor in 2523 was thinking there was a fight in my room. I called downstairs around 8:30 to understand how loud was loud so I could be more considerate of my neighbors. I was transferred from person to person and then got the guy that says, "just came on at 7...loud is loud" and laughed and hung up...I then called back to help desk and they keep hanging up on me. Finally a lady who is suppose to be the manager calls and tells me this is a wooden structure and sound travels. She apologized for all the other things that took place. BTW, I have a great view of Alcatraz and the bay from my room and China town is right here. Take the good with the bad. The great thing is the Comptel Spring show is about 12 blocks away and will take me 20 minutes to walk there. So I will get some walking up and down the hills here in San Fran....' After all this the hotel did give me a nice fruit and cheese plate when I came back late the night before departure.

The hotel, although the lobby is under construction (it's not like you're sleeping there), was great! The staff was very friendly and helpful. The room wasn't the biggest, but it was up to date, very comfortable and CLEAN! It's around the corner from Big Nick's (an awesome greasy spoon), a block away from the Subway (get the week long pass!), "Stand Up New York" (a great stand up club) and a short walk away from the Museum of Natural History. 
This trip was a quick getaway after getting married, and both my wife and I enjoyed our stay at the Belleclaire. We'll be back when we can!
(In the review, we didn't check out the pool or restaurant, nor do we know if they had one, hence the "average" rating.

title_masked: Great after a long haul flight and for a long layover
text_masked:
We arrived at LAX at 7am and we called from the airport at 8am... they the shuttle and we were all checked in and showered and tucked into bed by 9am....this was absolutely fabulous after a 14 hr flight with NO sleep.....although close to LAX, there was little noise.
The hotel was an older style with only 2 stories. The room was clean and the bed comfortable and had a nice pool to cool off in or rest beside. 
Anyone needing a break after a long haul flight this place offers a cheap day rate of $49 ....I would definitely recommend it.

I have stayed at this hotel on a couple of occassions. It is really cheap on the weekends, really expensive on the weekdays, and consistenly good. The breakfast buffet is usually hot and fresh. The rooms are always clean and the staff is friendly. Although it's never over-the-top, I appreciate always meeting my high expectations.

This hotel is in an ideal location (Corner of H/14). I could walk to all of the sites I was interested in: Holocaust Museum, Smithsonian Museums, White House, etc etc. It was also very close to a Starbucks, Cosi and CVS Pharmacy (was cheaper to buy snacks/water here then in the lobby store).
The rooms are small but this was fine since the location was great. The maids were great. The room was always neat and clean when I came back. There was a few stains in the bathroom that were there when I got there and there when I left that were a bit gross (blood on mirror for example). I am in hotels too often that I often bring a little thing of Clorox wipes and wipe what I know I will be touching in the room (yes you can call me anal but that's okay). 
When I first checked in I was put in a room behind the elevators. I returned to the front desk and was promptly put in another room. 
The bell hops/concierge was very helpful and knowledgeable. 
There was free WIFI everywhere in the hotel... huge incentive to book here again! 
So with all good things come some bad...
1. The female bartender (I cannot recall her name) was good at service. However, I heard her talking loudly about patrons of the hotel in a negative manner (for one example, a guest had come down to the lobby in an unflattering outfit. The bartender went on and on about how people need to look in a mirror once in a while and just because they sell tube tops doesn't mean you should wear them.) I also heard her disparaging fellow employees. (I guess she use to be the manager/boss of a co-worker. She regretted giving this woman/co-worker such a good recommendation because now she is stuck working with her again.) 
As a guest/patron of the hotel, I was wondering what was being said about me when I walked away from the bar. It was just unpleasant and unprofessional.
2. The Grist Mill's menu is very limited and cannot handle special requests. I just wanted a bowl of pasta and was told that was not available. I asked if the pasta dish on the menu that had shrimp in it could be served minus the shrimp... well we could switch it out for chicken but it has to have on of those in it... um ok.

My third stay at this property in the past five years. Always satisfied with SPG properties and the Sheraton Chicago is no exception. Very nice hotel, comfortable rooms and beds, and excellent staff. Terrific location too. Would be my first choice in Chicago if you are staying downtown. Highly recommend..

title_masked: Fantastic Hotel at a great price
text_masked:
Can't say anything negative about the hotel. It was the first time I have stayed in New York and I was a bit worried that the hotel looked a little bit out of the way. I couldn't have been more wrong. It is ideally placed near to Penn Station, which is just a 5 min walk or very short subway journey away.
