The subway up to Central Park or down to South Ferry is right on the door step. The upmarket shops of Chelsea are nearby, as is the Highline which was a lovely walk on a warm afternoon.
I walked to and from Times Square area on an evening, and went in a couple of the local bars. I felt completely at ease at all times and enjoyed the experience of seeing NY at night.
The hotel room I had was very spacious, spotless and had all the facilities I required, including free Wi-Fi. All the staff were courteous and helpful. 
I would recommend this hotel to anyone wanting a competively priced, well positioned and customer friendly place to stay in NY.

The hotel from the outside is very impressive, inside it was very spacious and blew me away. I had a room on the 7th floor,but they do have lifts. The receptionists were helpful. A valet took our bags upto the room, and I recommend you give him a tip as they really do work hard to make your arrival smooth.The room itself was massive. I looked at the 2 double beds and saw how tidy and comfortable they both were. The TV was great and the mini bar had a good selection of drinks and snacks. The Bathroom was something else,Luxurious, it was so big, it had a shower, toilet and bath but separated in different small rooms. So I was really happy. I had a play and stay package which mean't you could have a go in the casino, well worth doing this. This Hotel has various restaurants to suit everyone and the portions are Big. Highly recommended. I stayed here so I could visit the Motown Museum with my Family and it wasn't too far away. I also had a view of the bridge to Canada!

the prperty is above average but the hotel stands out because of its staff ! From Angelica at the front desk ,to Genevee at the Zocca bar, and of course you cant go wrong with a reccomendation from Sandra at the concierge desk and my exit was was handled efficienlty by joe Fonseca all in all 5 star service!!!

title_masked: Nice location. Not worth the money!
text_masked: This hotel in any other location would be less than half the price. It is average at best, they just seem to missing the little things that a true $300/night hotel would offer. No mini bar, had an ocean front room, but only the second floor so a great a view of the battleship, and a cruise ship. The beds and sheets are not one would expect. The service in the restaurant bar is poor. If you want to stay on the wharf, it's a great spot, but for less money you could move up the hill and have a better view of the bay.

title_masked: Dont ever stay at this hotel!
text_masked: I thought that it had ben renovated and was up to par, especially for the prices they charge....my room smelled like smoke, the tv remote didnt work, only 1 lamp worked, the bed looked like it was just slept in, then to top it all off once I got that straight, when I woke up the next moring I had been bitten by something all over my back, whatever bit me made me sick as hell I was throwing up,fever and my pressure went up had to go to the ER, so beware they arent clean and have insects that will attack you at night, Ill never ever go there again or refer anyone! they need to be shut down and deep cleaned throughly!!!!!! They nasty as hell, should only charge 25 per damn room!!!!

Ricky was warm, friendly & pleasant to deal with. My daughter & I were traveling with friends on a college visit and he found a way to check us in at the same time and on the same floor in minutes in spite of first finding out that we were on separate floors and only one room was ready. Because of his diligence and attention to customer service we were able to get to our college visit on time.

The hotel is not expensive and in the city center, I booked it during my trip all around the USA thinking it was a good deal.
When we arrived we realized that that area, even if very central, is one of the most dangerous in S. Francisco.
The hotel and rooms are very basic but they seemed clean, the staff was nice.
The problem is that the area is full of homeless, prostitutes, alchool and drug addicted people that keep on stopping you asking for money (at least this is what happened to us).
However, the part we disliked the most is that elevators that bring you to the rooms floors are on the street, even if they work only with the magnetic room card we didn't feel safe, anybody could potentuially and easily access your room's door, moreover, during our (1 night) stay someone went into the car park and broke the glass of a hotel guest car (car park entrance is open on the street as well).
So my opinion is: there is nothing bad against the rooms or the staff, but if you are a tourist, which means walking with money, camera etc etc this is not the right place to stay in S.Francisco. After one night we left and went too Fisherman's wharf, even if it is very touristic, it is safe and we enjoyed our stay without any worry.

This is my third time in New York City and I had an amazing experience every time. This is my first time at a 5-star hotel and it was tremendous.
The service was impeccable. I could not be happier with The Peninsula.
From the start, the staff are very friendly and helpful. From the bell boy who chatted us up to the concierge who spoke French for your convenience. Everyone smiled and greeted us. The spectacular staircase entry to the beautiful, spacious rooms. Love is certainly in the details. Everything you need is in your room: stationary items, a sewing kit, jogging route, plush slippers, free newspaper delivery, A/C control panel, mood lighting AND music in the bathroom. And on and on. Strangely, no coffee maker. There's complimentary coffee at the pool. 
The breakfast restaurant was near-perfect. We were forgotten about on the first day because we were in the other room, not the main room. Second day, my eggs were not prepared correctly. Wouldn't be a big issue if it weren't for the 5-star rating. They apologized repeatedly and comped my meal. I do think $9 for a cup of coffee is pretty steep. No matter, through Expedia, we got a $90 breakfast credit per room, per day. Great value.
I will be back in September.

I stayed at Yotel NY for 3 nights in June 2012. Above all else, the hotel certainly is interesting. It's design and operation is very unique, from the lack of receptionists (you check in and out yourself using computer kiosks) to the odd purple lighting found throughout the entire hotel. From a comfort standpoint, the bed was quite hard, and the placement of the central A/C vent was positioned such that it blew directly onto my face when sleeping. Both of those were negatives in my opinion. Also, the room rates are pretty out of control at this place, considering how far west the hotel is (it's a good 10 minute walk to the nearest subway stop). I would not stay here again unless the rate was a fantastic deal and there were no other more convenient options.

Stayed here 3 nights 22nd floor, not much I can add that has'nt been said except that we found the large Shaws store just across the road very handy for meals if you don't want to pay for expensive restaurant or room service food.
This is a good tourist choice hotel not too far from the city sights, the bell staff were very friendly and knowledgeable.
The hotel is connected by a walkway right to the shopping mall across the street and the Boston duck tours are just outside.
Wireless Internet was available free in the lobby but in this class of hotel should be available free or minimal cost for guests in the rooms.
I would stay here again

It's a great location with great views of the city/Lake Michigan. The lobby is really nice, but seems a little stuffy. The staff is wonderful and the rooms are comfortable (aside from the tiny bathrooms). We enjoyed our visit.

title_masked: Not great - no a/c when wanted!
text_masked: I went with my mom this week - the hotel is very shabby, the furniture in our room seriously needs to get put out to pasture. What's more, the room was so hot when we got in - so we go to the thermostat and put it down and start the fan and figure by the time we get back from dinner it'll be fine. We get back from dinner and it's even warmer! We call down and they tell us that they have turned off the a/c because they're turning on the heat for the winter months. So we get no a/c! So the girl tells us to open our windows in order to get fresh air - which open out onto the *very busy* parkway full of cars, honking, ambulances, and police. No matter how late it is, there's the noise! What the hell kind of hotel is this!? I live in Canada and none of our hotels prevent us from having a cool room if we would like it no matter what time of the year! This is ridiculous and so is this hotel. I had come here based on reviews and that it was supposed to be a worthy establishment - not.ever.coming.again.

The front desk staff and the restaurant provide Excellent Service. This hotel is steps from Pike Place- In an Outstanding location. The Lovely Room was spacious, sparkling, comfy and had a great view (#705). There were Coupons Galore (2 $20 coupons for the restaurant/ 2 cocktail coupons) so it was a really good value. We would absolutely stay here again when in Seattle.

title_masked: Nice Hotel near Ohio State Univ
text_masked:
This was a nice hotel. Very clean. Only thing that appeared to be dirty was the dust ruffle on the bed. I didn't hear any noise. About 3 miles from main OSU campus. Indoor pool was nice and water clear, but they need to clean the tile at the water level- quite a bit of build up there. Breakfast was average- but some of us don't like cheese in our eggs. Beds were average. Pillows were marked for Firm or Soft
My only critiques would be: parking lot is small- if you're pulling a trailer, you will have to detach or park somewhere nearby. 
We reserved a room for 4 yet the towel setup was for 3- I find this pretty common. The reservation is for four, everything is ready to go when I check in. Why not the extra towels- so I make a trip to the desk.
I would definitely stay here again. And probably will.

title_masked: Not What I Expected and the Neighboorhood....
text_masked:
A series of issues......
1. Neighborhood: I thought I stayed here before, but don't remember it being this bad. I wanted to stay around Penn and Port Authority to be in walking distance to both, but when I walked from Penn Station to the hotel, it got worse and worse as I got close. Your neighbors at the hotel are 2 porn shops and the NY Parole Office.
2. The Little Things: first when I checked in they told me that there would be a Welcome Letter in the room with the internet access code in it. There was no letter. (at least internet is complimentary)
3. I turned on the TV and there was no picture - "no signal" floating around the screen for two hours until it came on.
4. There was no room service menu - one had to be sent up. (delay delay). When I called for room service they said they were too busy and could they call back in 10 minutes. 20 minutes later they called. I ordered food and asked what sodas they had. I ordered the Sprite. 10 minutes later they called back - no Sprite!
5. No real lobby - I should have remembered this, but I was planning to meet colleagues and interview some candidates in the hotel lobby but there was none. (also embarrassed about asking them to meet me in this neighborhood). I was able to use the bistro in the back but it was just a little awkward.
6. My favorite - the room got pretty warm in the evening so i went to the AC/heating unit on the wall and opened the little door. Inside there was a little sign that instructed you to use the wall unit. I went to the wall unit and there was nothing lit on the LED display. I pushed all the buttons more than once and could not get anything to work. I pried the unit off the wall (made to be able to do this) to check to see if there was a loose wire, and guess what? There were no wires connecting anything to anything! So unless this was a wireless unit that still did not work, it was a total sham and illusion that the customer had control of room temperature. I ended up opening the window which was pretty noisy!
The people were great, nice and friendly, but there are far too many options in NYC to bring me back to this hotel.

title_masked: Jewel of San Antonio - Slightly Faded
text_masked: In over 20 years of booking rooms, we last stayed at the Fairmount on September 13 - 16, 2012. We truly enjoy the quiet, the ambience, the antique furniture and plush furnishings. Staff are very helpful and very accommodating. Yes, it is a bit frayed and worn, but warmer and more inviting than the mega boxes. Will definitely stay again and hope that renovations to update are in the works.

The bed are incredible!!!everything in the room is new and top quality.the service is amazing,also for staying in san francisco it was amazing to get free parking. breakfat was simple but sufficent.we will definitely go back!!!

I have stayed at this hotel twice this past year for business. When the reservations were first made I was a bit apprehensive because while it is close to Times Square, it is not in my opinion in one of the most desirable locations in the city. I have to say, that I was so incredibly impressed with this hotel and its amenities. First and foremost, the rooms are so nice and clean and brand new! The beds and pillows to die for! I was there for 3 nights and slept like a baby. Couldn't even hear the noise outside. The halls are small but yet you don't feel like your room is too close to your neighbor. For someone travelling alone, hotel hallways creep me out a bit but not this one. You feel extremely safe at this hotel. The location is good, close to Times Square but nothing fancy. I like the proximity to 5th Avenue and the shopping. The personnel at this hotel are the greatest. I liked having the hotel for breakfast meetings but I must say don't waste your time there for breakfast. Service is slow and they run out of stuff and keep you waiting. There are alot of great breakfast options along Broadway and 5th Avenue. If you are driving into the city, make sure that you park on W32nd Street and Broadway because this is the discount lot for this hotel. My recommendation would be to drop off your luggage at the hotel and then drive to the parking garage. There is always plenty of room in front of the hotel to unload. I had to go inside and get a front desk person because the cops gave me a hard time but the personnel came outside and it was not a problem. Great hotel, would highly recommend it. My husband and son stayed there this year when they went to see a Rangers game and the location is perfect!

My mother and I stayed at the Hotel Giraffe for the first time in June. In our opinion, we thought the hotel was GREAT. The location was convenient. It was quite warm when we visited the city so there was always iced water w/ lemons ready for us to drink in the lobby. This was quite nice!
Also, there is complimentary breakfast which we thoroughly appreciated. There was turn down service at night and small chocolates were left which were a delight to us. 
I recommend this hotel and certainly will return to this hotel when it comes time to visit my relatives again.

Stayed at the Carlton Inn based on reviews, location and price and wasn't disappointed. Stayed one night before flight from Midway; airport is about a five minute drive away.
Room was rather large and even though we were facing Archer Street, it wasn't too loud. Sheets were a bit scratchy. Enjoyed the use of free wireless Internet.
Staff was friendly and helpful; had a list of restaurants that delivered readily available. One thing I noticed was the number of staff; unlike many reasonably priced hotels that are run with minimal staff, there were a good number of staff available for assistance.

Enjoyed this hotel.....I loved the walk-in shower! It was very nice and clean! The bed was soft and comfortable. Really good location too! The walk to Independence Hall is not too long, only about twenty minutes. The only complaint is that our room had scotch tape on the wall. It looks like the wall had a crack in it and they used scotch tape to hide/fix it. Wasn't really a big deal, but I'm surprised that they fixed it that way. Overall, a good hotel and very clean.

The location and price of the hotel was perfect for the marathon. The rooms look like they've been recently updated and were very clean. The breakfast was very good and plenty of it. Marathon morning they provided an early breakfast for the runners which was perfect! Great stay and we highly recommend it - especially for marathon weekend.

title_masked: Good hotel in a great location!
text_masked:
Got this hotel via Priceline, but could have booked direct for $5 more. Smallish room, but that's New York. Great location! Subway stop on the corner. Walking distance to many attractions. Room was clean and quiet. Ordered a refrigerator, which they brought up quickly. Bed comfortable. Everything worked. Plenty of outlets and flat screen tv. 
Lobby average. There was a bar with people hanging out at all hours, but we didn't use it.
No coffee maker in room, but plenty of coffee shops nearby.
Security at night by elevators was appreciated.
All in all, we recommend and would return.
The room was small but it was in a great location and the staff were very helpful. We could walk to public transportation, Quincy Matket and the north end.

title_masked: A Great Stay in an Amazing Location
text_masked: There are 3 keys to this amazing hotel - the beds are incredibly comfortable, the location is perfect for those looking to spend time in Boystown/Lakeview, and the staff are second to none. My decision to say here (and not earn rewards pts) was a gamble, but I won on this one. I will definately be telling my friends about this place and returning here in the future.

As several other reviewers have stated, the rooms are a bit on the small side but other than this we had no complaints whatsoever. The location of the hotel is excellent with the empire state building being just across the road and lots of other attractions easily within walking distance providing you are reasonably fit. There is also a subway station only a 5 minute walk away.
The hotel itself is very clean and the rooms are visited every day. All the staff we encountered were friendly and helpful and the rooms amenities were excellent. All told we would have no hesitation recommending this hotel to anyone.

I love the hotel, I had an amazing time visiting my husband while he is in tech school at Lackland Air Force Base...Although the guest are very rude and loud, I had to change rooms because of loud guest on my floor(2nd) and guest jumping and playing around on top of me on the 3rd floor. It was 11:30pm, I really needed to get rest after a long drive.. I moved to the 1st floor and it was very peaceful then. However, I did try to look over the noises from 8pm from when they started until I could not take anymore. My first guestroom was not very clean the second was very clean.

I've stayed twice at the Fairmont San Jose, once in each tower. The location is perfect for business travel: just 10-15min from the airport, centrally located downtown with tons of restaurants, bars, movie theater, museums, all within walking distance. The lobby in the main tower is great for meeting coworkers for a drink. The rooms are spacious, clean, comfortable - quite adequate for business travel. The rooms in the second tower are newer and quieter. I see in other reviews that people had problems with the service (particularly check-in) - I had none of these issues - check-in and check-out were uneventful. The parking and breakfast is quite expensive so beware. You can have a good breakfast at a much cheaper price at several of the coffee shops or restaurants close by. The only reason that I didn't give it an Excellent rating is that it doesn't have anything that really stands out compared to some of the other large hotels in the area.

title_masked: Good hotel, slightly dated but good
text_masked: stayed here in may, good hotel, rooms are good, lobby dated. cafe downstairs was good, bellboy was awesome. good location

This was our first time staying at a Hyatt in a few years and we would certainly stay at this hotel again. Due to the train schedule, we arrived before the stated check in time. To our surprise, we were given a room immediately. I call myself a "hotel fool" because I check every thing in a room before we decide if it is acceptable. I had no complaints or concerns whatsoever. This is a huge property and very busy; however, every aspect of service we encountered from the bellmen, front desk, gift shop, general workers, housekeeping and concierge exemplified their slogan of "exceptional stay". We never had to wait more than a minute for the elevator. I had an unusual request due to my negligence and it was handled seamlessly. 
The location was great for walking to the places we wanted to go in the city and the bus we needed was right across the street from the hotel.
We were celebrating our 42nd wedding anniversary and had a wonderful time.

We were assigned a room on the 18th floor, I noticed it was only several feet way from the main elevator corridor. Previous experiences lead me to believe all rooms near any elevators can be arena's for loud talking and coarse conversation.
 Of course I made my way back down to the registration desk pleading for alternative room. The staff at front desk were apologetic and accommodating. I recognize 911 as a national disaster. But our room in 911 was very quiet, clean, and pleasant... 
There are two city bus stops across the street from the Renaissance Hotel. Keep in mind most buses are free within the downtown area of Seattle. Taking a local bus can be adventurous in this upbeat city with a diverse moving crowd. Overall, because of the friendliness and kind staff at the Renaissance, my wife and I would consider coming back here again.

title_masked: Wonderful Location... Not so great food
text_masked:
The hotel was well kept and had very nice furnishings. The rooms were as described and met the needs of my visit. The hotel location is convenient to COSI, the Palace Theatre, good for a stroll on the Scioto Mile.... all within walking distance. We were given complimentary breakfast which the food was fair, but slightly bland. The staff preparing the food in the breakfast restaurant area were quite pleasant to encounter (smiling, asking about food quality, etc), however I wish I could say the same for the wait staff including the host & hostess. The wait staff as well as host/hostess were not friendly, didn't smile, were not courteous in the least. My first thought was "these folks must really hate their job". It was disappointing considering what wonderful and helpful staff that were present in most every other area of this location
Would I stay there again? ABSOLUTELY but next time I will seek breakfast elsewhere.

Drury Inn's always are better than the rest with the free food at dinner, vouchers for free adult beverages, a popcorn machine, and fountain drinks in the evening. This Drury was very new, and the exactly the same as another one in Des Moines I've written about. It has an elegant lobby, nice large open breakfast area with more food than I've seen in a continental breakfast, nice rooms as usual with stone counter tops, large bathrooms, big flat screen tv, and comfortable bed and pillows. (I stayed in a room with two queens). The location is right next to the interstate, but there was hardly any traffic noise. It must be well insulated. The area is nice and safe with some good restaurants around.

title_masked: Not that great for the price
text_masked: We stayed at the Grand Hyatt for a work trip. The hotel lobby and restaurants are nice however the rooms are old and out dated. The toilette looks like a toilette you would see in a locker room and there is really nothing too exciting about the rooms. The customer service is average at best and they do not go the extra mile for the customers. I will not stay there again unless is paid for by my company. The few good things about it is that you can get to the metro from the hotel without having to go outside and there is a starbucks on location. Other than that everything is over prized and under performs.

Hard to beat this location. The staff was always friendly and helpful. WiFi connection was a little slow/weak in the room. The Indian Restaurant right across the street, Kastoori Grill, was absolutely wonderful, which would be a good reason I would stay there again - just to have easy access.
A little on the expensive side but I would stay there again.

title_masked: Four Days with my daughter in the Big Apple
text_masked: My first visit to NYC. The hotel had great character, in a good location, a short walk between two major subway lines. Staff were helpful and friendly, room was clean and bed was very comfortable. We enjoyed the surrounding neighbourhood, close to Central Park. I will go back and would recommend it to friends.

title_masked: Great Energy and a Great Stay
text_masked:
I stayed at the Aloft Tapestry Park for 7 nights in May 2012. I love staying at Aloft hotels because they typically provide consistently good service and value. This is a newer Aloft which was just built a couple years ago. This Aloft is built a little different than others that I've stayed at, but still follows the same concept and has a fun and exciting atmosphere.
Aloft rooms are on the smaller side, yet they feel open by the way they are designed (built in desk, built in closet space, wall mounted tv, tall ceilings, etc). I absolutely love the showers and the sliding door used to separate the bathrooms. Each room has a mini fridge, built in safe, free wifi, coffee maker, and a 42" wall mounted tv. The platform beds are not necessarily the most comfortable beds in the hotel world, but they are slightly better than average, especially for a mid priced chain. This Aloft seems to have upgraded pillows compared to others I've stayed at which helps. 
The lobby and shared spaces set the Aloft apart from other hotels. This place definitely markets to a younger crowd and I'm all for that, you won't find any floral print wall paper here! The lobby is fun and hip with the WXYZ bar, pool table, snack area, and plenty of couches and chairs for hanging out. Their outdoor patio features more sitting areas and there is an outdoor pool built off to the side. The fitness center is fantastic with free weights, several cardio machines, and a weight machine. 
The service is great and the manager Scott is dedicated to make sure all my needs were met during my stay. 
I can't wait to return the next time I'm in town.

This is a great little hotel to stay in Chicago. The rooms are huge, bathrooms as well, and very nicely decorated. The staff is very friendly, we didn't meet a single staff member which did not at least smile and nod, which made us feel very welcome. Darren helped us with our bags and gave us a full introduction to our room, which was very much appreciated. The Wifi is free and very fast, and they even have a tv which also serves as computer (Mac) in your room. The location is superb, just off the magnificent mile and in easy walking distance of all the important sites. Definitely staying here again on my next stay in Chicago.

title_masked: Excellent location just off the freeway, maintenance has slipped.
text_masked: We stayed at this property 2 years ago and the hotel has fallen in terms of maintenance, we asked for a light to be replaced and it did not happen. The room was poorly maintained and the breakfast was not up to a best western plus standard!

title_masked: Great staff, nice rooms, easy access to airport
text_masked:
I stayed here for business and when I arrived (late, after 5 hour drive through the edge of a hurricane), there was a problem with my reservation not being direct billed to my company. I immediately cringed inside because I knew this could lead to an hour of hanging around the lobby waiting for it to be straightened out. 
To my surprise, the young lady at check-in was very nice and gave me my room anyway. She said she would straighten it out and if there was any problem "she knew where to find me." I really, really appreciated that because this has happened to me in other hotels and it was always a nightmare. I was soaking wet just from walking in from the car and I just wanted to get settled. I wish I had gotten her name so I could compliment her.
The room was very nice...clean, modern, spacious. And the bed was super comfy.
The location is great if you are flying out or have business near the airport.

I stayed at the Roosevelt for five nights in mid May 2012 with two other family members. After reading some of the bad reviews, we were quite nervous, but to be honest, it was one of few reasonably priced hotels in Manhattan that didn't have shared bathrooms (if you're just starting your search....many do....beware). 
The Check in process was quick and easy. We were given a choice of what floor we wanted to be on even (we chose the highest possible). The room was great, much better than we were expecting. We booked the superior (one size up from the cozy but one size down from the deluxe) and it wasn't the most spacious of hotel rooms I've ever stayed in, but it was BY NO MEANS the smallest. There was plenty of room to walk around. It was very clean....there were signs of age (it is a classic hotel from the 1920s) for example the corners of the wallpaper had some faded colors, and the AC looked like an older unit but worked fine. Everything was spotless, however. The beds were extremely comfortable (doubles, not queens) and provided a good night's sleep. The bathroom, while small, was also very clean and the shower was nice, although it had low water pressure (low flow shower head). Housekeeping did a nice job daily, and the staff was always friendly and accommodating. The doormen were not the most attentive (they didn't open the doors...) but that's my only complaint. The lobby (which smelled of warm cinnamon) was beautiful, as well. 
The location CAN'T be beat. You are literally right next to Grand Central. Tip: If it's cold or rainy, walk through the MetLife building to access Grand Central instead of walking the whole block to go through the main doors. There are numerous places to eat in the station in the dining concourse, as well. Take the S into Times Square which is a 50 second ride, or walk the 10 minutes on your own. You are in a prime midtown location...right next to the Chrysler Building also, which makes it easy to find the hotel if you ever feel lost.
Room was great, clean, good service, good location....not much not to like. The price can't be beat, and you're staying in a piece of history! Mad Men fans will enjoy the experience even more :) 
I cannot recommend this hotel highly enough for families/couples/etc looking to enjoy the city and not spend a fortune on the hotel room. You will not regret staying at the Roosevelt.
This was a great experience in a city I was not familiar with. The staff was very friendly and helpful. The hotel was very clean. The breakfast was excellent. I give it five stars!

This place is fantastic. Both concierges, Eden and TK, made this such an enjoyable experience and made planning our 'escape' so much easier. Not only were they able to pick up tickets for us (and helped us avoid lines) for multiple highly popular attractions around the city, they were also happy to provide excellent restaurant recommendations and took the time to provide the highest level of service to each person hoping to have their attention. Didn't do room service cause we aren't high rollers. Elevators, lobby decor etc. were very cool and they played pretty decent music for the most part. For a t-shirt and jeans kind of person, this was too rich for my blood. But we loved it. Just had a wonderful time in Chicago and this was a fantastic location to call home base. That being said, we like to walk - and don't mind walking 20/30 mins to get to another neighborhood.

Stayed for a week in May 2012. We were lucky enough to have a very spacious room on the 7th floor - bed was huge and very comfortable.
Staff were unobtrusive, polite, and always available to give assistance.
Location is excellent - just off Michigan Avenue, where you can jump on the red open-top double decker bus that runs a regular route between the Museum Campus in the south and the John Hancock Center in the north (you can hop off at or near many of the main sights).
Fresh coffee each morning in ther lobby was a nice touch - a real fortification for each busy day! 
The pool and jacuzzi on the 5th floor were also welcome. Chicago feels like home to me, and this hotel proved to be a big part of the attraction - can't wait for my next trip!

I have been staying at this hotel for over 15 years and it is one of the best large hotels in NYC for business and family. Even though it is one of the larger hotels that you will find, I completed the check-in process in less than 2 minutes. The rooms are consistently clean and modern, and you can not beat the location. The hotel is close enough to everything in mid-town but yet just outside of the craziness of Times Square. The hotel is just one block from the subway and it is easy to head West to the Lincoln Tunnel when it is time to leave.
The breakfast is good if you are getting it as part of your room charge. If not, you should head over to 7th or 8th Avenue as you can find some great breakfast places for less money.

title_masked: Happy New Year's Day at the Doubletree
text_masked:
We were very happy with our choice of place to stay after the flight from Philadelphia. It was so easy to call from the airport for our shuttle, which arrived within a few minutes. The hotel is set back from the street and is offsite from the airport, although quite close. Dinner in the restaurant was excellent and very quiet that evening. On January 2nd we asked about getting a rental car to get up to the condo we had rented, and the shuttle driver recommended an off-airport rental agency to which he drove us after his airport run.
Physically, the facility was very satisfactory. Wanted to get into the pool, which looked great, but we had to move on. Staff were all very pleasant. It was a great start to the New Year!

Rooms are small but well put together lots of cools stuff push button draps, TV behind the mirror in the bathroom, full body shower electric "do not disturb" sign. Storage looks very limited but they put drawers under the bed that really helped out. Lobby was cool with the fish tank loud at night with live shows and the busy bar area spilling out into the lobby. Would stay here again!

Our stay was part of a "night on the town" package that included valet parking and a voucher towards a meal at nearby restaurants and as such represented good value - the hotel frequently has such offers on their website.
Access is easy and the valet parking convenient. Check-in was very smooth and professional.
For an older, downtown, hotel our room wasn't a bad size with separate sitting area apart from the bed space. Decor was generally in good order and both the bed and linens were of high quality. The room was very quiet even though we were only steps from the elevator, and there was no street noise at all.
Slight niggles: some nooks and crannies suggested that cleaning hadn't been quite as thorough as one might hope - dust on top of a few less commonly seen horizontal surfaces. The tea/coffee service was incomplete with several choices of sugar and sweetener but no creamer.
The bar was packed to the gills on a Saturday evening and we had no chance to try their martini selection. The food vouchers did not include the hotels own restaurant, so we had breakfast elsewhere and had no chance to try the kitchen.
All in all a pleasant and comfortable stay, with a particular nod to helpful and professional desk staff.

title_masked: Typically expensive, but a comfortable place to sleep
text_masked:
The Kimberly is in a fantastic area of NYC, around the corner from the Astoria, a couple of blocks from Grand Central and 5th Avenue. The lobby is tiny and cramped, and as this is the only area for free wifi and it was slow, I barely took advantage of it, opting instead for the super fast, free McDs around the corner!
Checking in was professionally handled and fast, and the room was 4C facing...um...well, another building and some A/C machinery. Having said that, the alternative was a tall office block opposite the front of the building with the addition of street noise and honking taxis, so I settled for this as it gave me a good night's sleep!
The top floor lounge offers a great view, but it's always packed and is quite a small area. But it's very popular and a good spot for a party. Didn't eat at the hotel as nothing was included, but the room was big and clean, with superb beds, Microwave, fridge, minibar, nice bathroom, large wall mounted TV and a gimmicky HP control desk for finding out stuff/hotel info. This was placed in front of the TV and blocked the screen, and it didn't work - what's wrong with a good old fashioned hotel guide book eh?!!!
A good night's sleep. Pricey, but that's NY for you.

My wife and I stayed for a week. Check in was efficient and friendly. The room was clean and comfortable and the view (we had a Times Square view) was superb. The air con worked well and the room was quiet. The bar staff were friendly and the cocktails good. The terrace in the early evenings was excellent with great views. For the duration of our stay we had no negatives whatsoever. The hotel was also very well situated with the numerous restaurants of Hell's Kitchen a short walk away.
 For the price/star rating this must be an excellent choice.

title_masked: Flies in the bathroom, mold on the ceiling - and no heat!!
text_masked:
Things didn't start off well at Hotel Verite. I made my reservation through Booking.com. When I arrived at the hotel, the woman at the front desk reported that they'd 'just received the fax' from the booking site. The fax? What is this, 1993? Shouldn't this be done by, you know, computer?
Apparently, the room that I'd booked for two nights was only available for one night. The front desk lady tried to convince me to take the room for one night, then switch to another room the next night. I allowed as how I'd prefer one room for two nights, as that's what I'd booked. After several minutes she simply offered me the second night's room for both nights. "Why didn't you just give me that in the first place?" I inquired. "That room is larger - the room you reserved is smaller." This was at 6:30 in the evening. Perhaps they were waiting for someone to make a last minute, one-night reservation for the larger room...but it struck me as just poor customer service.
So, 'upgraded' to the larger room, I settled in. I went to the bathroom, and noticed some sort of fly on the mirror. Oh, and there's another by the sink. And another on the shower curtain. I'm not one to make a fuss, so I killed four of the insects and went on about my business. However, the flies (or whatever they were) seemed to return in groups of three or four throughout my stay.
It wasn't until I was in bed that night that I noticed the dripping noise from the floor above...and the water damage to a corner of the ceiling...and the black mold growing there. Of course I reported all this to the front desk, and they were very polite and apologetic, and even sent someone up to look, but apparently there was nothing to be done.
All of which would have been more or less harmless, had it not been in the low teens in NYC last night. The room had no heat. I got back to the hotel around 9pm and reported the heat problem. Then again around 11pm when it wasn't any better. Then around 5am when the cold woke me up, despite assurances that they'd fixed the problem. I finally decided to get out, shower somewhere warmer (the gym) and take my leave of the Hotel Verite. They were kind enough to credit me for the heat-less night...but I cannot recommend this hotel to others.
Two stars because the staff was always polite and generally seemed to be trying to help - just with very little success.

I rely on trip advisor when booking hotels and chose the Hotel 1000 based upon reviews. I'm so glad I did. This was the best service of any hotel I have ever stayed at. The rooms were absoutely beautiful, although my view wasn't great (roof and skyscrapers) but who cared. The hotel couldn't have been more conveniently located in downtown Seattle. We walked up one way to Pike's Market and the other way into the old town. I've stayed at 5 star hotels before but this one beats them all. I'd like to say that the front desk (Alice) and the concierge and valet service excelled in their jobs! We traveled with my former boss now retired from the practice of law and he and his wife also agreed this was one of the nicest hotels they have been to. Denny Fitzpatrick, the manager should be very proud of this hotel! And thanks again for the nice birthday and anniversary treats!

Surely the best feature of this hotel is the perfect location. Close to dozens of restaurants, theaters, metro, everything you could need. The lobby was under renovation and was always a bit crowded. The Hotem has over 1300 rooms and elevators and common areas are always crowded. The staff is very friendly and helpful. My room (2031) was actually quite small. My parents were in an adjoining room, in the same category but a little bigger. They charge a $ 14 fee for the use of wifi internet. I never use it.
In summary:
PROS:
- Location, location, location.
- Friendly staff
CONS:
- Small rooms (I think it is common for NYC)
- Crowded lobby.

We stayed at this hotel for Thanksgiving. It was very quiet and clean. Valet is too expensive so we parked on the street. There is a charge in the rooms for internet but it is complimentary on the lobby floor. Only think i didn't like hair dry was too dirty ( I am sure it was not only our room). I took a picture of it and showed to the front desk agent ( I dont know his name because he didn't have a name tag) He told me he would have someone take a look at it but nobody ever changed or cleaned it. But overall it is a nice place to stay.

Our stay was nothing less than CLASSY! The hotel is amazing, very clean and very personable and friendly staff! I booked through expedia and got a great rate, I was a little skeptical because some of the other reviews said that it was a timely check in process and so on... Totally not the case! We arrived about an hour early and within minutes was given our room key and permission to enter early! We had an amazing view, spacious room (corner rooms are def the way to go). From our king size amazingly heavenly bed we got fantastic views of the heart of boston. The prudential center was right out our window! We were celebrating my husband's 30th and it was a great choice! Very busy but still very relaxing, just as I would describe Boston! The hotel's restaurant's were pretty exspensive and a little to over the top so we took a stroll through the skywalks which are connected from the hotel all the way to a few blocks away! We ate breakfast and lunch at The Cheesecake Factory at the Prudential and it was delicious. There is so many nearby attractions and very conveinant shopping, even Shaws was step's away! This was great, I didnt have to buy 4.00 waters... I just went and grabbed a few 1.00 waters at Shaws! I love the night scene! All in All it was an amazing stay, amazing room, amazing service, and very fun! We can't wait to go back! So worth it! Thank You Westin Copley for making my husbands 30th Birthday getaway so special! P.s the heavenly shower and bed are both so very heavenly especially waking up to the scenery we did, totally felt like a mini pent house! <3

This was a quick trip to Seattle and we needed a hotel close to the action but not too close. We were in town for a show at the 5th Avenue Theater. The Vintage Hotel was perfect! Awesome greeting at the front door, front desk right on the spot!! We arrived at the wine reception, we declined because I don't drink. Just as we were settling into our room chocolates and sparkling water on a lovely tray showed up. Now that is class!!!! We were traveling with our small dog Cody Coyote and he was most appreciated with a welcome package as well. We will definitely stay here the future for sure. The restaurant down stairs is also top notch and accommodated dietary needs superbly. Fun and restful stay. Did I mention St Patrick's day? Everywhere else it was noisy but not here, we slept like babies.

The Empire Hotel is in a great location. Right across the street from Lincoln Center. 
The rooms were warm modern and comfortable. A little small but that's what New York City hotels are unless you double the price. But the staff is worth twice the price.
From the doormen to the front desk to the maids. All friendly and helpfull above and beyond what you would expect.
Made a comment about something that really didn't bother me but bother others. It was fixed almost before the phone was on the hook and they even gave me free breakfast for pointing it out.
Who asked? But it was nice to recieve.
Go enjoy.

I have a wonderful experience there. Unfortunately, I left some very expensive items, two chanel blazers, several blouses, a few other blazers, and a dress. I wasn't thinking clearly and was in a rush when I checked out of the hotel. Once it dawned on me in the middle of a conference I was attending, I called security right away. Office Coleman was incredible and called me back within 20 minutes to assure me they had my items secured. The hotel thought they should take them and he knew they were mine so he kept them for me and overnighted them to my house! My experience was great thanks to him!
Everything was perfect about this hotel. Staff, room comfort, location, price - everything!! I couldn't fault anything about it. Well done!

My husband and I decided to travel to Baltimore for a couples weekend. The hotel was really nice...location was awesome...but the true stand out was the staff! Everyone was extremely friendly and helpful...they made us feel right at home. I don't think you can beat a balcony overlooking the inner harbor...plus the quick shuttle to Fells Point was great too. We can't wait to go back!

I did a bit of research before booking in here, and I certainly was not disappointed. The room (and shower) was good, clean and well maintained. The complimentary wine tasting each evening was excellent and it gave us a chance to mingle with other guests and chat about our experiences.Its situated near to the waterfront/ Pier 39 and very handy for trips etc. Anja at the front desk was welcoming when we booked in, as were the other staff when we needed assistance. If you are considering booking here for your holiday, you can rest assured that its a good place to stay. I can't really think of a criticism. A complimentary bottle of water for a weary traveller would have been nice, and $3 for those provided did seem a bit excessive (especially when the supermarket across the street sells them cheaper) but hey..they are in this business to make a proft and thats Ok. Its a minor gripe when you consider they are handing out glasses of wine for free. Stay at the Tuscan, you wont be disappointed

Only a few minutes from downtown or from Seaworld.
The hotel was clean, the staff was friendly, and the price was right!

We fell in love with Kimpton when we stayed in Portland, Oregon and were so excited to stay at the chain while in Baltimore. The hotel is lovely. Rooms are clean, modern, and comfortable. The hotel staff were friendly and helpful. Our kids each received a welcome goody bag on arrival, a big thrill for them. The hotel is in easy walking distance to the inner harbor. 
We were a little disappointed to find that the evening reception definitely had an adult vibe. As Kimpton is usually very kid friendly, we were expecting the kid friendly evening reception that we experienced while in portland. (They had a Wii set up for the kids, painting, snacks, popsicles, lemonade, etc.) The only thing available for kids at Monaco Baltimore was water. And they had candles lit everywhere!! Not a good thing with kids ages 2 and 4! 
Overall, our experience was good, but would have been better had we not been traveling with our children.

Ultra Luxury accommodations in one of the best locations in NYC. Steps away from Central Park and off of Park Avenue, the warm welcome and impeccable service is noteworthy. We were upgraded to a suite which was bigger than most apartments in the city. I don't know how they kept fresh ice in our ice bucket. The toiletries were custom produced and a combination of citrus I had never smelled before. The bar is also a great stop for a drink while waiting for friends. I loved the complimentary nut tray, very nice touch. Pricey, but worth the splurge.

title_masked: great place at an awesome value
text_masked: the rooms (all are suites) are huge, with spacious bathrooms, comfortable beds, sitting area, the hotel has a nice restaurant, great location and amazingly friendly and attentive staff, and at 60% or less of the price of other similar options in Detriot

I stayed at this hotel for a business conference. The common areas and banquet hall are lovely and relaxing with a beautiful courtyard. The hotel catering was excellent. The hotel offers a very generous complimentary continental breakfast that was tasty to boot. All of the staff was helpful and attentive. The rooms themselves are well styled and pretty comfortable. The bed was fairly comfortable and the linens smelled very fresh.
BUT the walls are very thin. Not only could I hear people's conversations in the hallway like they were in the room with me, I could even hear the closet doors slamming in other rooms. In addition, Santana Row is very lively until the wee hours, and I could hear everything taking place on the street from the 6th floor. One other nit-pick was the bathroom in my room. There was no place to hang my bath towel and there was no exhaust fan. In addition, the water in both the sink and shower was either scalding or cold.
All in all, I would come to this hotel for another business function but not on my own dime.

The George is a great place to stay. I have stayed in many DC hotels and this one ranks very high. I often choose this Kimpton because of its proximity to Union Station which makes it a good place to pop in. If I am lucky, I can squeeze in a martini and some lobster bisque between train layovers. The staff are always top drawer and it is a quiet place to stay. An added bonus is that it is near to the monuments so it makes for a good place to run/walk. Will, of course, come back

The only good thing I can say about this hotel is the location is ideal.
We are Marriott Elite members and have stayed in Marriott Hotels around the world, 
the staff in this hotel were the most rude and arrogant I have ever had the misfortune to meet.
We booked the one bedroom suite 12 months ago requesting a high floor and quiet room because we would be driving 10 hours from Las Vegas to San Francisco that day, we even phoned the hotel to confrim this.
On arrival there was no valet parking, there were no trollies for all our bags, I unloaded and parked the car, when I returned the valet was taking keys from another guest, apparently space was available the other valet was mistaken, no apology!
My wife the informed me she was offerred no assistance with all our bags.
The room we required had been allocated to another client , we were given a room on the first floor overlooking the street and the waste bins, which were collected at 4-30am. 
When I asked the desk clerk for an alternative room, his response was that none were available, his attitude was we had a room, then he stated if we wished to check out he would only charge us half the room rate.
I advised him that we would check out first thing in the morning.
The room was noisy all night and even with ear plugs we were unable to sleep due to the waste collection and the traffic.
I would add that the morning staff were much more helpful and polite and the deputy manager was full of apologies.
The hotel is basic and very tired, it is in need of a complete facelift and it is not good value for money.
Fortunately we were able to obtain a bay view room at the ARGONAUT HOTEL, just around the corner, which was fabulous and in a differrent class, with polite staff that could not do enough for you.
For a small difference in price I would advise all to stay at a proper hotel the ARGONAUT.

We had a short stay at the Embassy Suites, LAX, North. The staff was very helpful with the reservations due to changes in the flights. We were delayed by cancelations. They were flexible with our time arriving. Everyone was friendly and helpful. The hotel was clean and comfortable. The room was large and comfortable. We did not notice significant airport noise. The shuttle to and from the airport was easy and convienent. The buses were large and there was plenty of room for luggage. There is a shuttle one block away to Manahattan Beach for sights of the ocean and shopping/food. Very pleased with the hotel, and the staff. They were very helpful.

I recently stayed at the Marriott for a hearing aid convention that I intended with my boss and one of my coworkers. Everyone there was very friendly and the food at the restaurant was excellent! Henry the bell hop did an exceptional job and was always there to lend a hand. The rooms were nice and clean. They have a beautifully landscaped outdoor area with a fountain and tables with umbrellas. I highly recommend this hotel!

We are a family of four and stayed there for 5 nights. The room smelled a little funky but when speaking with housekeeping they offered to ozone the room and clean the carpets...no more funky smell. I really though that was great of them to do. We booked through Priceline so got a fantastic deal and they managed to have two interconnecting rooms for us. I thought the service was very good The lobby is a little noisy and 'cool' but didn't bother us much. yes the elevators are small, yes the rooms are small but this is NYC folks...you really shouldn't be spending any time in your rooms anyway. Get out and see the city. The area was great and we all felt very safe - it was quite convenient to the subway. Minuses: The mini bar is a rip off and there is no room for your food in the small fridge.

The Marrakech is an upbeat place to stay in a great location. A lot of young people were staying there and it was a perfect place for a night in New York. The staff is exceptional and room was clean and quiet.

title_masked: Cool place but not a 'great' hotel.
text_masked:
Location is great, directly opposite the Chinese Theatre on Hollywood Boulevard. The Tropicana pool bar is world famous and cool, if not a little disappointing (it is quite literally a pool bar and nothing more).
Hotel service was off-hand and impersonal. Not impolite but also not welcoming. Room was bland and cold. It's also quite a noisy hotel, perhaps because of location but also I think because the last renovation was poorly executed. You can hear noise from the corridor and adjoining rooms.
On the plus side, the food was good throughout. Breakfast in "25 degrees" was delicious, especially the house scrambled eggs.!

title_masked: our family trip to the Martha Stewart Show
text_masked: We stayed at this hotel when my niece appeared on the Martha Stewart Show. The front desk attendant, Luidin, was very professional,helpful and somehow had the ability to put us at ease. Every time he saw us he gave us a warm smile. The room was small but comfortable. Our request to have rooms near one another was honored. All staff were polite and attentive. We would definitely stay again. We found the location near subway and within walking distance of Penn Station.

In the things that matter this hotel provides: rooms & public areas were clean; the breakfast was varied and plentiful, the staff was friendly, and the price was definitely right!
The middle rating is entirely for aesthetics/decor: lobby is spartan, doorways behind counter look like they are covered by shower curtains, pool area is rather industrial, rooms are on the small side, and furniture and carpets have seen better days. There was, at some point, an attempt to update room decor, ie bedding and pictures. Although the furniture was a bit beat up is was all clean, no stains. The pool is small & there is no hot tub. 
If you are used to luxury hotels this is not for you. If you are on a budget and looking for a decent place to stay, this is for you.

Stayed 3 nights at the Peninsula Chicago celebrating our anniversary. First class all the way.
This hotel lobby is actually on the 5th floor, which makes the hotel quiet and intimate. The Bar located on the 5th floor is the perfect size. Dark and cozy, well decorated with attentive service. Our accomdation was in the Executive Suite, which has a little over 700 square feet. It was awesome, with a separate living area, separate dressing area, and separate bedroom. Lots of technology in the lighting which was fantastic. The whirlpool tub had a large picture window overlooking the city. The room has everything you would ever ask for. When we arrived, we were escorted to our room by the desk clerk. Upon arrival in our suite, we were greeted with a bottle of Champagne, compliments of the Manager, along with chocolate covered strawberries. Nice not to be nickled and dimed as wireless internet was complimentary along with the morning newspaper, not to mention the coffee bar located in the lobby. There is nothing not to love about this hotel. I am repeating myself, but their Bar is about the classiest I have seen. First Class A Plus. Their website also is outstanding. It provides a wonderful view into their accomodations including photos and floor plans for all accomodation choices. My Continental (now United) Presidential Credit Card allows me to ask for a free upgrade, so I simply booked a King Deluxe Room and was upgraded to the next level of rooms, which was the Executive Suite. I really appreciate the information on their website regarding the accomodations. This is a can't miss hotel if you are looking for something romantic and intimate. The locations is also outstanding for shopping and dining.

I hosted a bachelorette party at this hotel in one of their luxury suites. The hotel exceeded my expectations in everyway. The staff was extremely accomodating with all my requests. Kevin at the front desk was expecially helpful and friendly at check in. He had lots of great recommendations! The suite is one the best two room suites I've ever utilized. The master bath was fabulous. It had a very large shower, large soaking tub, separate toilet area, and two large vanities. My only complaint was the restaurant service. We waited for 25 minutes before receiving service and when I complained no one appologized. They just shrugged it off like its normal to take an hour and half for breakfast. The food was delicous though so if you are not in a hurry I'd highly recommend it.

title_masked: Sister time at the Days Inn Chicago on Diversey and Clark
text_masked: We sisters got together from points east, west and south and had a great time. HUGE thank you to Neal (Jackson--not sure) for getting us the same room for all 5 nights. WHen I initially reserved, we could only get Wed, Thur and Sun (Chicago marathon weekend so was busy). However Neal kept his promise and kept me informed as he was able to add the Friday and Saturday nights for us over the next few weeks. His efforts really added to the ease and comfort and fun for us sisters! BIG thank you! Yes we will be back--besides the comfort, we love the shoe store across the street and we have family within walking distance. thank you. OJS

The Grand Hyatt is situated on the main street of downtown Seattle. It is a ten minute walk from Pike's Market. It is a five minute walk from Westlake Station - a shopping mall and the station for the light rail to/from the airport. The room has a wonderful, clean, large bathroom and the room we stayed in was of good size, quiet, with comfortable beds.
The price was better than other hotels and was an excellent choice for our two night stay.

Inexpensive but ultimately not ery satisfactory, this Hojo is on the Hotel Circle so not a bad location but vey hilly uneven lot, tiny pool and at the end of the day grubby and in ned of paint and cleaning and updating.

We enjoy the Upper East Side. The Wales is well-located for museums, shops, and lovely restaurants. Sarah Beth's Kitchen is terrific. Our room was small, but when we arrived there was no information cards, no menus or waste baskets. With only two elevators, it took a while to get downstairs from the upper floors. The public rooms were nice - coffee and tea available and a nice place to sit. What we noticed, however was that it often took more than one request to get something done. At that price range, they could do better. Yet, the place is charming and the rooms are quiet, something that is not often the case in Manhattan. Excellent for couples or solo.

If you're in Chicago, you have to stay at the Hotel Monaco. Excellent ambiance, decor and great staff. With our group of girls, the location was great for shopping , site seeing and restaurants. 
Fabulous!

my friend and i booked here because it was cheep and central. we then read the reviews on here and where terrified. needles to say this hotel is excellent the location is so perfect its untrue. bed was lovely and comfy (no bugs) for the price we paid we where so happy it has everything u need for a fantastic stay in new york. ok decor is a bit shabby but here it is simple u get what u pay for and this is more then value for money. ab come on ur in the big apple who wants to stay in a room or gives a crap that the carpet is old . its clean it central and new york is so great ull be so tierd from jet lag and sight seing u wont care less that the bed side table looks like it came from the antiquies road show. this place is ace its so fantastic value its untrue. oh and our room was toasty and warm. an just waking up everyday and being able to throw on any clothes an get a quick mourning cuppa whilst soaking up all the mourning atmosphere from the magnificent times sq on ur door step is priceless.

Literary nature is a vibration, and this hotel has it. Successful artists need to associate with others in the same field. I needed a speech from Elizabethan England. The head of the staff gave it to me online and twice in print! These are good people and the facilities are truly luxurious. Great location!

This is my first time ever staying at a Candlewood Suites Hotel. Well I stayed here only for one night and let me tell you. I enjoyed my stay and I would stay here again if I ever had the chance. Close to shopping at the Galleria Mall and other shops.

My family and I booked this hotel prior to 2 week trip and returned to find that the rate had gone up 20.00 with an explanation that it was the 4th of July weekend. The place was nearly deserted except for one wing that contained weekly and monthly guests of dubious character. The parking lot was dark and the neighborhood only seen during the day was very frightening at night. The room was in bad repair:missing light bulbs, inoperable remote and we were placed next to a large loud family who shot off fireworks during the night. Exhausted from our trip and being late, we felt it necessary to ride it through. We had never had a problem with a Days Inn before or since. I wrote to the corporate headquarters stating that this hotel was a blight on their reputation and complained about the last minute rate hike. I did receive a refund and a note of apology however it is over six years later and the reviews are still mostly terrible. 
Since I had to choose a date, I chose the latest. i feel my review validates the opinions of most that have been written since 2004 and want to warn people against staying here.

Stayed in room #910. Very first thing I noticed, when entered the room late afternoon was, how dark the room was. Then I realized no wonder why, the window of the room was tiny and even that tiny window was mostly covered by the decoration drapes. Asked for an other room but according to the front desk all the double rooms were like mine. This bad design meant that even on a beautiful sunny day when I was in the room the lights needed to be on.
I was the only guest in the room so it was enough for me but I can't imagine how 3 or 4 people would have space.
The air conditioning unit only worked on fan speed or off. The position of the A/C unit was so bad, it blew the air on the bed. Luckily, I didn't have to use that bed, but can imagine that if I had had to I would have got a cold and a headache. Also, the A/C unit kept on turning on and off and there was no way to keep it turned on which was annoying at night.
The cold water pressure was constantly changing; in the shower it resulted in really hot water or cold one.
Apart from these, clearly architectural, mechanical and design problems everything else was very pleasant. Great staff at the front desk and housekeeping, fast and reliable complimentary internet, nice bedding, nice interior. 
Location might not be the best (not much going on in the hood) but the North End or Quincy Market are just a few-min walk away, so, it's not that bad at all.
Overall good stay, especially for the discounted price I got.

I've stayed here twice. Both times I had an overnight layover. First time was in March 2011, I used my Hilton points for the room. Second time was last night, courtesy of United voucher. Yep, I've never actually paid cash to stay here. That said, if United Airlines hadn't put me up her, I would have stayed and payed the (exorbitant) price. The location is great; If you take the outdoor route to the United terminal you can walk to the security line in two minutes. That gives you extra time to sleep.
My room was nicely appointed, bed very comfortable, upgraded to room with nice TV with integrated A/V system. I got free internet and breakfast as a result of being Hilton Diamond. I walked to the terminal in two minutes. This is as good as it gets. As a previous reviewer pointed out, this hotel is why he/she stays at Hiltons. I agree.
Future reviewers - please stop griping about the price. If you want to stay at the airport at a major international airport like Ohare, you have to pay the price. If you want to save money, I'm sure there are other reasonable options if you take a shuttle to/from the airport. It comes down to how you value your time. As a business traveler, the extra 45 minutes I get back from staying on the airport grounds is invaluable to me.
In summary - stay here and pay the price. It is worth it.

Poor is the best way to describe an excessively expensive hotel. The only good thing is that it is near the hospitals and harvard medical school. Staff was poor, room was poor, one would think a 5th floor view of Boston would be great, but my view is of a stairwell, so no sunshine in my room for a week. The hallway smells like baby poo or vomit. I received a room with the wrong number of beds and when I called the desk they told me they were full. I am also next to the staff lounge so I get to hear them all hours of day and night, the walls are very thin. No pool and no exercise rooms.
This was extremely disappointing.

Well 21 years of marriage deserves a well deserved night out at a luxury hotel. We arrived at the hotel and was offered a suite upgrade. The suites were very well appointed, and enjoyed throughly. Down comforters, nice bathroom ammentities, and flat panel tv's everywhere. 
We started the day with spa services and a couples massage which was EXCELLENT and needed. The staff was always more than helpful and we really enjoyed our stay. 
A premium hotel commands premium pricing, but the name says it all. We had a great time?

title_masked: closest aiport hotel, clean, well worth the $
text_masked:
We stayed for a few nights and thought that the hotel was well worth what we paid on Priceline. Though the room services prices are steep, parking costs $20, and internet is another $10 PER DEVICE, the $85 we paid for the room was a great deal. Room was spacious, well lit, nicely furnished. The pool/outdoor area was very impressive, esp for an airport hotel. I was very surprised how large it was, both the heated pool and the hottub, and the free towels were nice.
It is probably the closest hotel to the airport. It would probably be easier to walk across the pedestrian bridge through the train station than drive, although we never did. Parking is a bit of a hassle if you are on the far end of the property. In order to park your car there and avoid walking what seems like miles through the entire property to get to your room, you have to drive through the parking garage and come out the other side. No easy way to access the other end of the parking lot. 
There isn’t much you can walk to except other airport hotels and a 7-Eleven across the street. If you want food, you’ll have to have a car or take the bus which is also just across the street.
We were charged double for internet but this error was easily corrected with one quick call, without delay or argument. That was the extent of our interaction with the staff because we had no problems during our stay.

Nice hotel for the price. I was driving from Vegas to Cali for a quick weekend trip and with gas prices going up I wanted something reasonable. $79.00 per night with taxes total was $90.82 for one night. I stayed in the traditional two Queens room which was quite spacious. Clean room & bathroom. I was missing coffee cups went to the front desk to let them know and they took care of it right away. Didn't eat at the restaurant on the premises as with most hotels it was a little pricey. Went around the corner to Denny's. For what I would have paid for a bottle of beer from the restaurant got a 6 pack from a 711 around the corner for $1.49 more. Parking was $20.00 but the next morning when I got up a little piece of paper under my door $0.00 for parking, nice!

This hotel is great if you are in Phoenix for an event at the convention center. It is a quick walk to the convention center from the hotel. The hotel rooms were well appointed with comfortable furnishings and excellent bed linens. The food inthe restaurant and the in room dining was excellent quality. I would caution against ordering room service breakfast if you are on a schedule. I ordered two mornings in a row and it was late both days. You would be better off going down to the restaurant if you can. Downtown Phoenix really has nohing to recommend it other than the convention center and sports arenas. There is not shopping nearby and few restaurants other than those in the hotels. However, if you are in downtown Phoenix for a convention or for business- this hotel is a good choice

title_masked: Great hotel, very modern. Equates to a higher-end Westin
text_masked:
This is an excellent hotel. Not perfect - not amazing, but certainly excellent. I usually frequent Westin Hotels and this one is like a Westin, but nicer. It's certainly worthy of its 4 star rating.
The location is good depending on your plans. If you want to do the tourist activities, you're far from the hilly streets, trolley line, wharf, Lombard street, Full-House park, etc. Instead, you're in the SOMA district which is south of Downtown, but near the convention centers and ballpark. The area is questionably fringy. There are homeless everywhere. I was confronted on more than a few ocassions. Not a pleasant experience but I put them in their place. They're a bit agressive in the area perhaps due to the large mall next door. The Whole Foods market is within walking distance - if you're interested. We found the best food places about a mile to the West in the Mission district.
The lobby, common areas, and room were very well maintained and wonderfully appointed. The hotel was quiet, roomy, and comfortable. Nothing really to complain about. The gym had high-end, newer equipment (Precor) and was well maintained. The pool was small and full of children. My wife went to the spa and found it very nice. Check the Intercontinental website for spa specials.
Parking cost was high, but we were there over the weekend and found street parking. There's also a parking garage a half-block away for half the cost of valet. Call me crazy, but I'm not a valet person. At this hotel, I noticed folks were waiting for their vehicles for longer than it took me to walk next door and get into my car. Once again, I find it petty and cheap for a hotel of this caliber to charge for internet.

We were there the weekend that the NATO conference was going on. A bunch of Secret Service people were staying at the Dana too. Friendly and helpful staff. We had a great room, walked everywhere and we decided that the Dana is our hotel when we are in Chicago.

First of all, I will not go back to this hotel for something that seems very small but is extremely frustrating... They have 20 floors, 4 elevators, and a LOT of guests... which means it can take literally 30 minutes to get to your room (count on at least 10). 
Before I go any further: The bedding made me break out in hives! I was so itchy I could hardly sleep. This has never happened to me before. My boyfriend didn't have an issue, but I wouldn't trust it...
The rooms look nice but are very small (and I upgraded to a corner room, which was supposed to be bigger; I can't even imagine how small the others are). Speaking of which, this corner room was supposed to have a "partial view of the Capitol building." It was very partial... we had to smush our faces against the wall to see it!
There were a lot of corners that were cut. For example: No bathtub, the "full bath amenities" didn't even include hand soap, only enough caffeinated coffee for one cup, television wasn't digital, only two bath towels, etc. 
The garage is hard to navigate and the parking staff are anything but friendly.
All these things seem very small but for the price it surely adds up to make for one very aggravating visit...
It IS a nice location and the rooms are modern and clean. However, with so many choices of hotels around why stay at one that takes so long to get to your room (plus everything else I mentioned)

This is a nice hotel, very updated and good location to the airport but it was a weird night with all the noises. It's close to the airport and all so it was a restless night. I wasn't too thrilled that they put a hold on my credit card when my company had paid for the room, as they did not do this to all my coworkers.

title_masked: Very Expensive Hotel and Great Location
text_masked:
No major complaints about the Long Wharf Marriott, except our room assignment. In fairness to the hotel though, we checked in quite early and were given the option of taking room 158, or waiting for a different room.
The view was hardly inspiring given the rave reviews I'd read on here about the location. Frankly our view sucked, as you can see by the pictures, but we didn't spend much time in the room.
That said, it's a solid, even above average, Marriott experience. Only weird thing was the way the bathroom door opened, more like a dish cupboard door, rather than a room door.
Breakfast was included in our rate for about $429 a night, which by the time you added in taxes, it came closer to $479.
But the location was perfect for Fanieul Hall and the Greenway experience. 
For those of you traveling to or from Logan Airport, the hotel is right above the Aquarium stop and it's about a 10 minute ride (or less) from the airport on the subway.
Nice pool and a great view there of Boston Harbor. There is a nice reading area near checkin, which was stocked with wonderful books.
Because of the hotel's expense, we only did one night there and then 2 nights at the Back Bay Hilton, which I've also reviewed.
If you can afford this hotel, you'll be happy. It's a bustling, quality experience that one comes to expect from Marriott. Everyone we encountered at the hotel was really nice.
Bottom line: expensive and good, but doubt I'd splurge again.

title_masked: If this is your last resort, sleep in your car
text_masked:
I have never seen a hotel room as small as the double room. There is about 2 feet between the foot of the beds and the opposite wall. The room had a mirror in the bathroom and one inside the closet door. The bathroom is tiny.
One of the desk clerks was so rude. I can't figure out how he keeps his job.

My husband travels each week for business and this particular week I decided to travel olong with him. He is on a limited per diem and watches his bills accordingly. This was a FANTASTIC hotel. Breakefast was great, nice selection of teas (Yeah!) very clen and the beds were very comfortable.

This hotel has the best staff in chicago. They smile and welcome you every time you walk in the door! They helped us out with information about the city and even got me into a top hair stylist when I couldn't get my hair just right for my son's wedding. The rooms are spacious, well and spotless. They made us very comfortable and treated us as if we were their very own family. Thank you staff at the Silversmith for taking such wonderful care of us.

We visited Seattle for a couple of days and stayed at the Homewood Suites by Hilton. The hotel is centrally located and it was about a 10 - 15 minute walk to Pikes Market. The shopping was just around the corner. The suites were clean and well designed for a downtown hotel. We were in a one bedroom king suite. The bed was very comfortable. The kitchen was well equipped as well. Each morning they offered a breakfast buffet. One morning they even had make-it-yourself Belgium waffles with sausage and bacon. The front desk staff was very friendly and helpful when we showed up and the the bedding configuration was not what Hotels.com had confirmed with us. Hotels.com mis-represented the bedding configuration at the hotel. I would not book with Hotels.com again as they really do not know what the bedding configuration is in each hotel. However, I would definitely recommend this hotel for a family or business.

For the money, this was a great hotel. Clean, fairly cheap (for NYC) and very near subways. Cabs easy to get in the area - we even hailed one at 6:30 am on a Saturday morning for a ride to a 7:00 am Swim Practice. Rooms a bit small, but I would definitely recommend to friends.

Our visit was for business in late October. We arrived late in the evening and were upgraded to a suite with balcony facing the water/marina as the promised king bed was not available in the Tower. All staff were consistently helpful and considerate. The weather was very comfortable, sunny during the day, with only one night of Santa Ana winds. The hotel complex has a very good restaurant/bar, and the chef prepared excellent options for all our meeting meals. Staff working in our building were always hospitable, friendly and offered to assist us with anything we might need. We would stay here again but a with a car, as this area is walking distance only to a park and another hotel; however, for anything else one must drive, take a cab, take a shuttle or one of the rental bicycles.
