The only real downside is, if arriving late, always eat beforehand. The hours for dining venues are shorter than during the busy season (this includes an Einsteins on the premises) and there were no vending machines. We were charged for movies we did not see but that was immediately removed from our bill at check-out. Very convenient to Sea World. Excellent exercise center right on the water.

The hotel is very posh and modern. We loved the auto curtains and bathroom facilities. I felt like we were in a clean and futuristic hotel. the balcony was so cute, had a little picnic table with a great view of the city. ah if only we had more time. I would love for more hotels like the joule to be around when i visit different places. hotel service was wonderful. parking is a bit expensive but what do you expect in downtown... we did find a parking garage a couple of blocks on elm street. it looked closed but we pushed the ticket and open sesame! parking was $10/day. jackpot.

title_masked: Know what to expect for a great stay
text_masked:
This hotel-inn totally filled my need for an inexpensive but comfortable place to stay during my business trip.
I would certainly recommend it if you would overlook a couple of issues which could be important to some, so you decide for yourself.
First the good: The room was clearly recently renovated. The beds and sheets were fit for a four star hotel. This is one of the most important things in a hotel and they got that covered.
You get a big LCD TV with dozens of channels and movies all free! If you like to hang around inside you are spoiled for choice. Another point there.
Housekeeping was good. The room was equipped with a coffee maker, iron and ironing board and another detail that is often overlooked but is important in this age of personal electronic devices: plenty of sockets. There were no less than twelve available sockets in the room (I actually counted them) pretty convenient. Obviously 24h aircondition to battle the desert heat and plenty of free ice.
Also free wifi with strong signal everywhere plus a computer with printer available to all who hadn't brought a laptop along.
Breakfast was complete. There were boiled eggs, pancakes, muffins, bagels, fruit, juice, the list goes on, it was all there. I didn't much like the coffee though and this spoiled what would be a perfect self service breakfast.
Service was always fast and courteous. The persons at the front desk were always smiling and quick to respond to our enquiries.
Parking is plentyful and conveniently close to the rooms, especially the ground floor rooms which was just what we needed. The pines were providing a much welcome shade in the morning when we were driving off.
There was a security guard and I believe electronic surveillance (more on that below)
Finally there is a pool (plus whirlpool and kiddie pool), a small air conditioned exercise room as well as plenty of public space around the pool and a vending machine which can be handy although there was a seven eleven next to the hotel for anything we needed around the clock.
The not so good: Obviously in no way the hotel's fault, the quests were not jet setters, mostly travelers staying a night or two. Some would get a bit rowdy.
A couple arguing very loudly in the lawn ended up with the police arriving to break it up. A party of two families would jump in the pool slightly drunk throwing in the sun chairs too. In the days of our stay we saw the police at least three times in the premises and the parking lot.
Also the hotel security would shoo away what I believe were trespassers using a loudspeaker in the small hours of the night which woke me up on two separate occasions. However I must emphasize that the area around the hotel seemed very safe and we never felt uncomfortable or threatened in any way.
Another issue was the condition of the pool which had muddy water and downright dirty with floating bugs.
The day we arrived there was a sandstorm which would account for some of the dirt in the water and in the bottom of the pool. In fact footprints were visible in the shallow part of the pool.
Upon mentioning it to the front desk they agreed that the pool was not clear enough and they would take care of it on Monday morning (we arrived during a weekend). Indeed the next day I saw some employees working on the pool but there was no visible improvement eventually. This was a pity because in the 45 degrees heat I would use the pool every day.
All things considered I would stay there again.

I travel a lot, at least every other week, all over the country. My company's Denver office is in Cherry Creek. I always try to stay at the JW when I'm here. Besides being conveniently located to office in the incredibly hip CC area, the service and rooms are just spectacular. All the staff, and particularly the front desk and concierge lounge. Ken Trumball is the consummate front desk associate - we connected on my first visit and he always remembers me and engages in discussion. He introduces me to co-workers, and then THEY remember me. Really, it is those little things that make a difference. Workout room is among best I have ever seen, and the bar is awesome. Only gripe - the business office computers. They are slower than the 286 processor one I had in college.

I love this Hyatt which is relatively new. I have stayed there 4 times recently for work and once for personal. The staff are very friendly and the rooms are great. The restaurant is excellent Great location as well. You can sometimes get discounted rates if you book on line and prepay for the room. I would highly recommend the hotel especially compared to some of the older hotel properties in the same area.

title_masked: Great location, bar and burger joint
text_masked:
This is the fourth time that I have stayed here on business and it is a most fabulous hotel. I have been upgraded twice to a junior suite, which was spacious and cool. It is always pristine and the staff who service the rooms are very friendly and accommodating. 
The breakfast/ brunch has one of the best menus that I have seen. I have eaten the Eggs Benedict with porcini mushroom sauce and the rock lobster and grilled asparagus omelet. Both were amazing, but be aware that potion size is BIG. Unfortunately only 30% of bookings are reserved for hotel guests, which did not impress. However, after some strong words, I got a reservation at a convenient time. Waiting time on a weekend is generally 45-60 minutes, so it is worth booking ahead. 
The hidden burger joint by the reception does amazing burgers. Look for the neon burger sign or the queue of people waiting to get inside. 
The bar is perfect for an evening drink before hitting the town, star spotting is not uncommon. I have seen Matt Dillion casually stroll through.

We came to Austin to visit family and had a great stay at this hotel. The staff was extremely nice and accommodating. The buffet breakfast was excellent with a very nice variety of choices. Coffee & apples are always available, and there is even chocolate at the registration desk. Our room was cleaned daily; it was extremely quiet, even though it faced the road. The location was convenient to everything with easy access to the highway, and the price was quite reasonable. All in all, a very pleasant stay. We will definitely be back to the Arboretum Hampton!!!

We had our annual conference at The Madison this year. The experience was legendary and with the help of the very accomodating and professional staff we have now raised the bar for all future events. Rooms remodel was well done!!!!! Meeting space for all our breakout sessions was right on target. Service throughout the conference was exceptional. Food and creative presentations all were impressive.

After checking into the Hotel and getting unpacked i went out to scout the area, have dinner and finish paperwork. When I climbed into the bed at 11:00 pm, I found the stink of body odor on the pillowcases and sheets were terrible. I had to sleep on bath towels. When I went to the office to complain to Mr [NAME], I found his mother working the desk who could not speak a word of english.

we try to stay in Kimpton hotels whenever possible. This was a week-long family vacation to the DC area. Overall, a nice hotel, would probably return.
PROS
as an in-touch member, love the comp wi-fi
large room and bathroom. Nice offer of upgrading to a larger room/room type for a nominal fee
location: close to the Metro, nice area strolling and shopping
friendly customer service
CONS
No bellmen were available to assist us with our luggage when we arrived, they were around, just not at the front door or available to assist with luggage
Person checking us in, was unaware of the "luggage promotion"- he made a copy of my boarding pass, then called me back 15 minutes later to say the hotel was honoring this- training of new staff
For persons with accessibility challanges, the front lobby and steps to get to the front desk is awkward. The side ramp is not easily viewable
Unless you ask for it, you won't receive an in-room coffee maker
Upon check-in, we received a notification from our credit card company, asking to confirm the charges placed (hotel needs to identify itself as the hotel Palomar to the credit card companies

title_masked: A Favorite Every Time I Visit NYC
text_masked: Have stayed at the Michelangelo twice, most recently in April 2012. The hotel is a boutique facility that has a superb and accommodating staff. It is located on 51st and 7th Avenue just outside of "official" Times Square. This particular corner is fairly quiet but close enough to the theater district to attend shows or eat at some of the fine restaurants. The rooms are always extremely adequate and spotless. We have stayed at many of the smaller boutique hotels in NYC but this is out favorite. We will be back again in 2013. Price is about what you expect to pay in the big city.

title_masked: Country Inns San Antonio very good
text_masked: This Country Inns is not the typical architecture and is very sleek and modern. The rooms and furnishings are excellent and the hotel is very comfortable. Well worth the price.

Is in a reasonable location for walking down the hill to the harbour. Short taxi ride to the Saloon and Stinking Rose. A 20 minute walk on a nice evening.
Thehotel itself is clean and convenient with free parking. I recommend.

This hotel is a hidden gem in Austin, and we were pleasantly surprised. Extremely clean, very modern, and not at all what you remember La Quinta being like in the past. Good breakfast with bacon, waffles, yogurt, pastries, etc. The staff was exceptionally friendly and made it enjoyable. They told us it was a franchised property and that the owner is very meticulous. It was obvious--the place was spotless! Our friends turned up their noses when we told them we were at the La Quinta, but that's ok. It's better than lots of the Marriotts and Hyatts where we've stayed. Our room on the 3rd floor backed to a green space and tall live oak trees. We loved it. 
At the intersection of 183, 620 and 45. Easy access to anything in the city and Lake Travis, and off the beaten path if you want something quiet. It's close to, but isolated from, the highways.
There is an empty mini-fridge in the room without all the usual alcohol and overpriced items. We made a 15 minute trip to the store and stocked it with drinks and snacks. There's also a microwave in the room if you need one.

title_masked: Ripoff prices, terrible food, bug in bed, door falling apart
text_masked:
Had a horrible stay here this past weekend. To start with, we were ripped off at a non-refundable rate of $500 a night for our room during the US Grand Prix. While we were there, someone walked into the hotel asking the room rate. They were quoted $250/night and immediately left saying, "No way!" Yet we were paying twice that rate. Their normal rate is $99/night for that room.
When we arrived, the toilet was stuffed up. The bathroom door had amateurishly applied paneling on it which was falling off. There was also a HEPA air cleaner sitting in our room. Why? Was it to mask the odor of a corpse from a previous stay, or mold? In any case, it was very suspicious to say the least.
The free breakfast was horrible. My wife and I tried the eggs and they tasted like egg substitute. We stuck to yogurt from then on.
The windows in our room had this ugly dirty film on the outside like they hadn't been cleaned for a very long time.
The worst part was the bug I killed on the sheets. I think it was too big to be a bed bug (although the billboard that you pass from a bed bug exterminating company down the street from the hotel was a little disconcerting.)
There is a tremendous amount of construction going on around the hotel on the street it's on, and it's quite a pain to get too also.
All in all, a place I will never go back to. Caveat emptor.

title_masked: Nice hotel in the middle of airport traffic
text_masked:
I stayed here for business - about 10 days. The streets outside are very busy, but the hotel is large, nice and has a great pool/open green area within the building grounds.
The food is great as well.

Did a weekend getaway for our anniversary for our first time at The GDM. The hotel lives up to the reputation. Wasn't able to play golf due to tendonitis but they gave me a rain check. Grounds and pools are beautiful. Had lunch at the adult pool and I must say it was the best poolside service we've had anywhere. At most resorts, pool oriented dining is 2nd class at best. Not here. We had a smoothie, salad and cocktails. Our service and food was as good as a nice restaurant. Spent the day shopping locally and then dinner at the Amaya. Again, the food and service was impecable. Looking forward to returning and trying Addison.

This hotel was perfectly situated for all our sightseeing of New York,it was very clean and the breakfast was worth the $9 extra charged.I would recommend this hotel and would stay there again.You are within walking distance of quite a few attractions ,but i would advise if you are going to visit the empier state building pre book you fast track tickets it saves you 2 hours of queing.

I travel a lot on business. I rely on Trip Advisor for much needed guidance. In the past year I have stayed at Holiday Inn Express hotels about 50 nights. This hotel is about on average with the other Holiday Inn Express properties I visit. The difference was the location and the staff. The hotel itself is about two blocks off Hollywood Blvd. Once knows for being an seedy neighborhood, today Hollywood is a tourist district much like Times Square in New York.
The staff at the hotel is warm and friendly, welcoming you back to the hotel each time you leave and come back. They are very helpful with local attraction information. The hotel location is terrific. The hotel itself is about 4 years old and has the usual amenities. The hotel was clean and neat, breakfast was much like all other Holiday Inn Express locations, not sure why some reviewers felt the breakfast as anything special at this location, but it was neat and clean.
The pool and pool area are very limited, but they do have a pool. What the hotel may lack in sparkle or glitz, the staff makes up for it with true hospitality.

Headed through L.A. last week and decided to shake things up and try a different property. Was definitely disappointed. I paid more for the room than I would have at my usual hotel and got a smaller room. The front desk staff was very friendly and helpful. The overall decor of the hotel was dark and in need of refurbishing. The elevator had funky lighting and the hallway leading to the room showed its age. The room was dark and small, with the king bed filling up the room. The bed though was very comfortable. The bathroom was average. Towels were very thin but there was great water pressure. Tried out the lounge and the bartender was very friendly and attentive. The flatbread, however, fell flat as it was very soggy. There is free wifi in the lounge which was nice and a computer for printing boarding passes near the front desk. The hotel is across the street from the car rental lots so is very convenient for those renting cars.

title_masked: Awesome experience and worth every penny!!!
text_masked: My husband and I spent 3 nights in a Top of the Brown room for his birthday. This was an outstanding experience from the get-go. Valet and doorman were very quick - from car to room in under 10 minutes. They were all ready for us at the front desk with 2 glasses of champagne - easiest check in I have ever had. The hotel itself is gorgeous. Lots of dark wood and beautiful decor. Our room was very spacious and the bathroom was plenty big with an oversized tub to soak in and a separate shower that will accomodate 2. The only drawback for the entire weekend was the bed. We found it very hard and had a very difficult time sleeping. But, back to the positives. The lobby is not to be ignored. They have an afternoon tea that is cute, but I think we will skip this next time. It appears to be more of an adventure for women to get together and talk or for little girls to get to be grown up. They were fun to watch, but this is quite a pricey adventure for just tea.Don't miss happy hour in the lobby. It is great and very relaxing. The lobby is just a gorgeous place to hang out. We ate breakfast both mornings in Elyington's and the food and service were incredible. The sunday brunch is like nothing I have ever seen - definitely make a reservation and give it a try. The hotel is in downtown Denver and is easy to get to from I-70. It is only a block or so away from an outside mall that has lots of shopping, restaurants and a theatre. One of the best things about the hotel was their outstanding staff. Megan at the front desk was absolutely on the ball and helped me with everything I needed. I have never encountered a more friendly front desk staff. Another impressive person that we met was Lee, who drives the complimentary car. He is totally awesome and I would recommend that you take advantage of his service when you get there. Not to be forgotten is Mariana in the lobby. She waited on us for both happy hour and afternoon tea. She is a classy and friendly young woman who made the experiences very enjoyable. I highly recommend this hotel. It is old, but has been beautifully restored and is worth every penny you spend. We will be going back next year for sure/

... this time with a group of colleagues from office. much better - maybe because roof top bars were closed? will persevere based on this experience. had a better size room. Enjoyed cocktails and snacks in street level bar. The ice rink out front fun - but not ready for skating, which was a shame. Will be back

As it has been each time I've stayed here, the hotel itself was clean and comfortable. My issue is that when I arrived, I stated to the valet that I wanted only to run up for five minutes then would be back down. The valet recommended that I take the town car to the show I was seeing at the Toyota Center. I stated that I would inquire at the main desk and decide from there. The lady at the desk assured me that the driver would be able to deliver us to/retrieve us from our venue. The driver assured us of the same and we agreed on a meeting point. He stated to call and ask for him after the show. My daughter and I called as we were walking out of the Toyota Center and was told this "I recommend you call a cab because there's no one here to get you". There were no explanations or apologies made and no offer to look up a number. It's almost impossible to get a cab on the street and two calls to a cab company produced no better luck. They said they'd send someone but made no guarantees. An hour later, as the crowd cleared out and we could still not get a cab, we found a bicycle cab who finally agreed on a dollar amount to return us to the hotel. This cost me $50 dollars and was more stressful than I can express--on a street corner in Houston with a child and frantic about how we'd get back to the room.

My husband and I stayed at this hotel past weekend. It was wonderful. We have stayed in the big hotels before, but the Sanctuary is small and very intimate. We felt very comfortable the moment we stepped inside. The staff was very nice and extremely helpful. The manager suggested a wonderful little Italian restaurant that was perfect. The rooms are small but well appointed and clean. Very comfortable bed. We went up to the rooftop bar and had a good time. The hotel is in a perfect location. It is down the block from Times Square and the Theater District. We went in to see Wicked and only walked 3 blocks. We definitely will stay there again!

Loved the rate of the hotel and were pleasantly surprised at how clean the room was. One problem we did have was the tv in our room was very grainy, when reporting this to the office they had the manager bring us a new tv! This was great becasue we didn't even have to move. Thank you for your warm service!

Great place, very well trained and helpful staff - restaurant outstanding for food and service! An experience to remember; my husband could not have chosen a better place to celebrate our 20th Anniversary.

I was in DC for some business meetings and chose the W because I could walk to a few of the appointments. The location couldn't have been better. When I checked in, the front desk agent was very friendly. She asked for my SPG status and then helped find a nice view for me. Nice touch. The doorman was great, every time I walked in and out, he was engaged and helpful. Confirmed my directions a couple times as well, really good service.
My room was pretty small, not sure if that's standard, but definitely one fo the smaller Starwood rooms I've ever been in. The desk was useable for laptops and the internet speed was fast. The bathroom was fairly large compared to the rest of the room. The closet was not designed well as you have to stand in front of the toilet to open it. Very strange, definitely a design flaw as there is nowhere to put your suitcase when unpacking except back around the corner in the bedroom. Shower was a good size.
Overall, it was a great stay, if you can past the small room. If not for that, it would have been a 5.

This Hotel ticks almost all the boxes and I rate it as "Very Good". I have just returned from a 7 night stay so can speak to most issues 'others' have raised. When I studied the hotel reviews prior to deciding on Diva I found most if not all Poor or terrible ratings were actually quite pathetic and a number by people full of their own self importance.
I requested an Executive Room for my partner and I just for extra room and found this to be perfect. I wanted a room facing the street not a alleyway or building wall and near the top floor. We got a room on the top floor which is the 7th. The Executive rooms a spacious, modern and had a lounge suite which could have been folded out for a third bed.
For us the much talked about lifts (2) worked the whole time and not an issue.
Front Office/Receptoin staff were very helpul and pleasant.
Housekeeping and daily room servicing was very good. Very Very comfy beds.
The thing that prospective guests need to decide is that although this hotel is not the subject of any protest, the Hotel Frank, which is about 100mtrs down the street is. Daily protests, starting at 7am, means you are woken by protestors chanting using loudhailers. These protestor regroup about 3pm obviously to try and deter guests arriving to check in at the Hotel Frank. On at least 2 nights loud hailers were used till about 10pm.(I think the protestors must have restrictions that they cant start before 7am and can go no later than 10pm)
These protests have been going for over 6 months and there appears to be no sign of a resolution. I cant believe that the Local Authority and Business Groups allow these people to disrupt such a large area - Hotel Diva and so many other businesses/restaurants and hotels have to suffer for the actions of others. 
We enjoyed the hotel and the excellent close proximaty to Union Square and shopping. We chose not to move to a room at the rear of the hotel or away from the street but I dont think this would have blocked out the loudhailers.
Yes - we would stay here again having now experienced the circumstances as outlined for ourselves. Maybe others would as well, maybe not - hopefully this gives you a clearer overview.

title_masked: Spacious Room, quiet and helpful staff.
text_masked: We arrived to what we thought was way out of the downtown, but as we became comfortable with the transit system it was very convenient. A bus is just across the street and goes by all the main transfer points. We had a 7 day CTA pass and went everywhere. Staff was helpful in giving us directions. Chicagoans are the nicest and most helpful people of any city I have ever visited!

Seek and thou shalt find a deal. We had a conference at the Hyatt by the Capitol but many of us stayed here for price. Turned out to be a nice hotel. It is about 1/2 mile from the metro so some us us walked others took a cab. For the savings, we could have taken a limo and still been ahead. Rooms were clean and updated. It is a few blocks from the 99% camp, but they are harmless and it is avoidable. The bar was a bit pricey so we went to other places nearby.

This was a wonderful hotel in the heart of all the action in Seattle. You are literally right in Pike's Market. I am from Wichita, KS and this hotel was superb. The staff was very professional and friendly, they definitely take customer service to a whole new level. Landon is a great member of the Inn at the Market team. I can't wait to visit Seattle again and stay with you guys!!

We booked our room over June 2nd- 3rd 2012....graduation weekend. My daughter celebrated her 5th grade promotion to Middle School @ Towneplace Suites by Marriot..and I must say that it was GREAT!!!!!! Justin @ the Front Desk went above and beyond for us! We bbq'd poolside as the girls splashed away!! When we called for extra pillows @ MIDNIGHT for our pillow fight..we were promptly served and with a SMILE!! As a single mother with two children and 6 kids as guests for the party...the staff was friendly, SUPER HELPFUL, the room and property were clean,cute and quaint. The young lady that worked the breakfast shift on sunday was so patient and kind with us..the food was hot, the fruit was fresh and tthe coffee was DEEE---LIISHH!!
THANK YOU ALL SO MUCH FOR A WONDERFUL STAY!!!!!!!!

Stayed here for a conference. We nornammlt stay at the Westin but this year the conference was at the Marriott. Nice rooms that were recently updated.
Ask for a room with a vew of the Charles River.
Also walk down to Newbury street for excellent shopping and places to eat.

This was a "shot in the dark" reservation. It turned out better than we could have imagined. Not only did we have a front-row seat of the Marathon event at the 25-mile mark, but the facilities and MOSTLTY the Staff are exceptional! They made our stay memorable! We'll be back!

title_masked: Home Away from Home - Great Stay !
text_masked:
Hands down, best hotel experience I have had for quite some time ! Checking in was very pleasant with a friendly, smiling staff who treated me more than just a room number. I felt they really appreciated me staying with them. They asked and offered many suggestions to make the best of my stay away from home. 
The room was extremely spacious and new looking with the business area privately divided from the bedroom area with a very beautiful frosted glass divider that helped me to focus on business first and then relax watching the game on the cozy bed. Very comfortable bed/pillow as I fell asleep with the TV running which never happens at home. 
The second night I actually spent time in the lobby initially reading a book and then out of the blue got invited to some barbeque with others who also were staying at the hotel. Got to try some good Houston bbq with some newly made friends watching football in the breakfast area. Come to find out a regular at the hotel helped make the bbq happen for all us strangers. Very thoughtful in helping those that travel alot feel like home as eating out can get old for some of us business travelers. 
I'm coming back to the Comfort Suites West Energy every time I visit Houston and plan to tell my colleagues back home !

We picked this hotel based on the Trip Advisor ratings and it lived up to expectations. The room was nice and clean and the staff were very friendly. Right behind the hotel are shops and restaurants which are very convenient.
The weekend we were there, the hotel was hosting a SciFi convention, and the hotel had designated a couple of floors as party floors. We were on a non-party floor, and were told at check-in that if we had an issues with noise to just contact reception and they would resolve it, but we had no issues.
Due to the convention, parking was at a premium and we were reluctant to move the car once we found a parking spot. 
The only irritant for me was the air conditioner in the room - it was very loud whenever it switched on and woke me several times during the night.
Overall nice hotel, nice area and I would stay there again.

Reserved this hotel via Priceline -- excellent price! Hotel stay was an excellent experience from the friendly folks at the front desk to the excellent housekeeping staff. View of the Baltimore Harbor was beautiful. Room was clean, beds were comfortable, bathroom was adequately stocked with more than enough towels and washcloths. Sunday breakfast buffet was pricey ($25) but it was good. The Water Taxi stop was at the corner of the hotel & the harbor. Loved the free bus that took you everywhere worth visiting (Charm Bus). We ate at some of the restaurants on the harbor -- Phillips was our favorite -- crab cakes are to die for!!! While I'm not a huge fan of Baltimore (city), I'd return to experience this hotel again and the great seafood.

We loved it! I met my husband for the weekend while he was on business for two weeks. We love staying in B & B's and this felt like one. The room was clean and appeared to be recently updated. The TV and wireless internet worked great. The staff was pleasant and very helpful. We wanted to eat locally and had dinner at a wonderful Italian restaurant, Pizzicotto. Sunday morning we walked to the Farmer's Market, stuffed ourselves with samples and bought food for a picnic lunch! We walked the neighborhood and enjoyed being away from all the tourist attractions. However, we were just minutes away from Third Street Promenade and the Santa Monica Pier. We would definitely stay here again!

title_masked: Good quality and better than most
text_masked:
I am a frequent business traveller and have stayed in many NYC hotels including the Hampton Inns and related Hilton properties. Very courteous front desk. Rooms are spacious (for NYC) clean with friendly and welcoming staff. Mix of tourists and business folks. One minor issue was the AC unit needed adjustment from the engineering staff...very quick and good humored. And, there was a minor flood at my front door...the carpet was soaked - I do hope it was water!!
Other than that I would stay again and recommend the hotel.

title_masked: So glad I chose Marriott Marquis
text_masked: I must say that this forum assisted me in making many choices and took the guesswork out of a lot of things. I found the hotel perfect for what I wanted, to me location is everything and I loved being right in Times Square. I'd walk for miles and would see the lights approaching and know I was nearly 'home'. I found the staff really helpful, that is reception on the ground floor. front desk and concierge. Because of the cost I chose not to access the internet in my room and happily sat in the lobby most evenings to do my surfing and people watch. My room was very comfortable, especially the bed, and was serviced promptly every day. Sure the hotel is expensive, but what isn't in NYC, to me it was value for money and wouldn't hesitate to return in the future. Really liked having two Starbucks in the hotel, loved the elevators (I knew exactly how to work them thanks to this forum) and enjoyed 'The View' on the last night. I was on the 45th floor and enjoyed my view of Times Square, also a clock (above the 1740 building) which flashed both celcius then fahrenheit temperatures and the time, was awesome. Was my first visit to the Big Apple and I certainly hope it won't be the last.

First visit to San Francisco back in April of 2012. It was a mother daughter trip with my 13 year old. I found the Joie de Vivre chain online and thought it seemed interesting. We almost stayed at Hotel Tomo in Japantown, but Hotel Rex kept beckoning and I'm glad. 
The staff was wonderful. Free glass of wine in the evenings. Clean room, wonderful service and friendly housekeeping staff. Rooms were small, but that's no matter. The lounge was perfect. Dave the bartender was lovely, as well as the regulars at the bar. They had a movie night one night and it was so fun. The food was also delish. I highly recommend this hotel to everyone. The friendly service was well worth it. The vibe was so San Fran and the location was perfect.

We recently spent 3 nights at the Travel Inn and we were very pleased with our stay. Our room as clean, the beds were comfortable and the room was big enought that we did not feell crowded...our son stayed with us and there was plenty of room for three...There was a little noise from 42nd street but we always travel with ear plugs so we had no problems..you will have noise no matter where you are in New York City
The only thing that happend was the fire alarm went off at 6am the one morning when a guest thought it would be funny to pull the alarm...
The room was always cleaned as soon as we left each morning. We left one morning for only an hour and when we came back the room was already cleaned, I have stayed at the "Big name hotels" and have had to waite hours to get the room cleaned.
The "free" parking was a huge plus...they even let us leave our car there the day we checked out since we still had things to do past our check out time.. I would stay here again.

Location - excellent downtown location just off Michigan Ave. Walking distance to the Navy Pier (20 min), Millenium Park (20 min) and just minutes from endless shopping and eating options. 
Room - clean...and stayed clean the entire stay despite the 3 of us being a little messy with our clutter and snacks. There was a king sized bed and a comfortable sofabed (believe it or not!). The room was fairly small and our 8th floor view was of the roof (nothing scenic) but at least it was quiet.
Facilties - did not get to take advantage of the gym or pool. But did frequent the Starbucks attached to the Hotel often.
Staff - loved the front desk people. They were super friendly and helpful when we asked for directions, info regarding airport shuttle, good steakhouses, etc. As well, the valet guys were also very friendly. It did sometimes take more than 15 min to get the car but I guess that can't be helped.
Value - excellent for this ideal downtown location. We had a car rental and considering overnight parking is almost half the cost of the room, this part doesn't seem worth it. But it seems this is the going rate everywhere.

Beautiful hotel near many Chicago attractions. Wonderful staff. Nice clean rooms. My only disappointment was they did not have in room coffee makers. Was happy to get a smoking room. Would stay there again

title_masked: Kwame is the best front desk staff member I have ever met!
text_masked: You will be talen care of-- not just checked in, but looked out for! We had a rough trip marred by a terribly destructive thunderstorm and Kwame (and the support staff) took excellent care of us! It alleviated so much stress and we were able to find a room at a tough time AND get 5-star service, respectful & courteous treatment at Westin. This was remarkable given the stress on all local DC area hotels-- all were booked full of displaced homeowners and tenants and travelers. And despite all the challenges, we were very well taken care of. Kwame (front desk/weekend) even stayed past his overnight shift duties to try to ensure that we had a place to stay when we were displaced from our original hotel! And he assisted our business group planner when our meetings were going to be hampered by inclement weather. He was remarkable and dedicated, helpful and concerned for all the guests' wellbeing. Even from the moment I walked into the hotel and one of the guests was crying from an unrelated incident (I guess they had a bad evening out), he was consoling her! Amazingly thoughtful. Who knew a business trip would uncover a hidden gem of Georgetown. And of course, our rooms were amazing, clean, comfortable and due to my inadvertent "loss of my cell phone" back on the other coast, the hotel provided me an evening pf complimentary internet so i could complete some work on my ipad. Thanks, Westin Team! (spearheaded by one amazingly hardworking man!)

title_masked: Enjoyed all that the Hyatt Regency had to offer...right on the River Walk!
text_masked: Attended a business conference in this beautiful property and enjoyed every minute. The hotel is at a wonderful location right on the River Walk and the staff could not have been friendlier. Would definitely return for a business trip or family trip again!

title_masked: Even though it's an Econo lodge
text_masked:
They could do better. I just left another review about getting what you pay for in this chain, but this place doesn't even deliver that. Just bad. Bathroom door didn't close right, Emergency exit door (also opens to the public, so anyone could come in out without going through the lobby) was propped open, maybe to provide some much needed circulation, I'm not sure. First room they assigned me was a smoking room, I booked and confirmed non smoking at check in. In the morning, the desk clerk is also running the continental breakfast, but getting caught up on bookings and receipts seem to take precedence. So as things run out, you have to constantly get her attention at the desk and wait for her to brew more coffee, get more food, (from quite a distance evidently), and such. Plus, all it takes is one hungry family and everything is empty again.
 So, naw. Even for the lowest bar of motel chains, this place doesn't cut it.

title_masked: Excellent room for a Concert Goer
text_masked: If you would like to walk out of your hotel room and be in the parking lot of Bojangle's Coliseum this is the place to be. The room was exactly what we needed and I was pleasantly surprised of how nice the room looked. Is it 2012 furniture? no try more like late 90's but I don't need a room to look at - I just need a clean place to stay. The room even had a mini fridge and microwave. If you are a family and have kids and do not want to be disturbed you make want to check the concert listing first but I personally didn't mind a bit of noise and I would say by midnight it was quiet. The price was only $70 and I'll stay here for every show now!!!

If you are looking for a very clean hotel, look no further. This is definitely one of the cleanest hotels I have stayed in! I was on a 2 week vacation with my family and we stayed at 7 different hotels. This was definitely one of the best! The hotel was spotless, the staff was constantly cleaning. The hotel had complimentary breakfast, which was different everyday, and they were constantly replenishing the food and cleaning the area. I have never seen such a large staff, and not only were they constantly cleaning but they were very friendly too! My compliments to this hotel and their staff!

The hotel is nice, and has a wonderful view of the river, but is still very noisy due to traffic no matter where you are at. Our room was tiny, but had a balcony overlooking the water. The bathroom was again, tiny, and we had double beds in a room that would barely comfortably fit a King. The desk chair backed right up to the second bed and if someone were sitting there, they would need to move to go out to the balcony. Breakfast was decent, but we got it for free. The staff was really nice at breakfast and were eager to get you eggs the way you'd like, and whichever drink you'd like. A lot was included with the buffet, and the food was delicious. There was no fridge or microwave in my room, and none of the rooms in the entire hotel have a safe. Parking was easy because you parked underneath and rode an elevator up. However, not much is in downtown as far as decent restaurants and places like Walmart. Those are about 10 miles away. If you get this room for a very low price and are only staying a few days by yourself, it is probably a decent place. However, I will not be returning again due to the location and small rooms.

title_masked: Was everything I wanted and more!!
text_masked:
We stayed 4 nights at Holiday Inn Lackland last week so we could be near the Airforce base for our son's graduation. It was an awesome stay! Here's what we loved:
1. From the hotel, it's about a 5-10 minute drive to the base.
2. Nice pool area though we never got in the pool.
3. Free hot breakfast every morning and it was delicious!
4. Housekeeping did a nice job.
5. Rooms were clean; beds and pillows extremely comfortable
6. It was nice to relax in their little bar/lounge in the evenings. (Special hi to Johnny, our bartender during our stay! )
7. All personnel treated us exceptionally!
8. Their restaurant had decent, well priced food.
9. Noise level was great even though I felt bad as our door shut hard so hopefully that didn't bother too many people.
10. It was nice and comforting to be surrounded by other families of Air force graduates going through the same thing as we were.

title_masked: Central location makes all the difference
text_masked: My wife and I thoroughly enjoyed our one night stay at the Hyatt Regency Boston. We wanted a hotel that would allow us to easily walk to the key downtown locations and this hotel fit the bill. It's a vey short hop from the Downtown Crossing Chauncy St. exit and a short walk to the Boston Commons and Chinatown. We had a 19th floor King bed room overlooking the State House (extra $10) and the view was very nice. The room itself was spacious and well furnished and equiped. Internet costs extra but we had our own Verizon Mifi, so didn't have to use the hotel Internet. We stayed away from the fridge since it's meant for the drinks to be purchased instead of for your personal drinks. The free in room coffee was nice though. Oh yes, the bed and the shower were also excellent. The staff were all very friendly and helpful (we were granted a late checkout). The key negative for this hotel to us was that it was a nightmare trying to find it when driving since our GPS kept losing connection due to the tall buildings and narrow and one way streets. Tip: if you are driving, make sure you know how to navigate it's maze of one way streets ahead of time. The parking lot entry and access to the elevator that brings you to the 3rd floor Lobby is on Chauncy Street. We will definitely stay here again.

We loved our stay at Rodeway inn. Service is great. Manager is very friendly and helpful. Room is clean and comfortable. Location was good. Hotel is close to restaurants and groceries.We will be back.

Stayed here on the 4th of July. A nice old hotel that's in a great location. We stayed in the old building in a standard room and while small it was very well put together. I am told the rooms in the tower wing are much larger. The room was spotless and had a great HD tv which was good to watch after a long day walking up and down the hills of SF. We got a great deal on Price Line so I wasn't expecting much and was pleasantly surprised. The hotel is only a short walk to the BART and the cable car stops outside. There are loads of shops nearby being on union square. The staff were friendly and very knowledgeable of the local area. Would stay here again.

The Surrey Hotel will forever be my hotel of choice in NYC. I will not try anything else because I know I’m setting myself up for disappointment. The Surrey did more than exceed my expectations. I was travelling to NYC on a girl’s weekend in celebration of my 40th and it was a memorable experience the minute we walked in. The hotel upgraded us to a suite, pure luxury – our home away from home for 3 days! The location is ideal. Walking distance from Central Park, great shopping and close enough to all the NYC action you may want without being in the middle of it which would become noisy and annoying after a few hours.

title_masked: Nice new Courtyard, convenient location and nice staff
text_masked:
I stayed here for 6 nights for business, and I'm glad I chose this Courtyard property. Frequent Courtyard business travelers will appreciate that this is the "newest" version of Courtyard, with the Bistro, updated lobby, new rooms, and new bathroom layout. Parking was free and ample, and property was easy to find and not to far from lots of restaurants, next door to a grocery store and a Starbucks. 
My room was really nice - super clean, and had a balcony. Plenty of power outlets, very clean bathroom, no issues whatsoever. Flat panel TV with all of the good channels and no issues with WiFi. Servers in the Bistro were very chipper, efficient, and friendly. 
I would definitely stay here again.

title_masked: What happened to the Westin experience?
text_masked:
My husband and I checked in here on Sunday, and while some parts of our stay have been quite good-- the bed, the personal service from the front desk and outside staff-- there are some things that are just lacking. 
The 'Business Center'? A crock. Absolute crock. I had a package delivered to the hotel, and they told us up front there would be a handling charge. That's completely acceptable. However, they never notified me that the package had arrived- as they stated they would. I had to go asking for it. And the handling charge? Nearly NINE DOLLARS. NINE.DOLLARS. 
I need to send something out again, and when I stopped by to ask if I could print the FREE return label, the guy said they normally charge $1.50 for it, but since it was just one page, I could just print for free. That's literally the best experience I've had here. When I asked if this postage paid label, for the box, that is a FEDEX label (of which this business center proudly displays their sign) I was told that again, there would be ANOTHER handling fee of NINE DOLLARS. 
I'm sorry, what hotel am I in? WHERE is the luxury and service that has epitomized every Westin my husband and I have ever stayed in? Before we moved overseas, we were Starwood Preferred, we stayed in these hotels so often. But it appears that this Westin (dare I say all Westin's?) has forgotten everything that made them an incredible hotel. 
Moving on to the bathroom. The bathtub is so shallow, that I can't take a proper bath. Really? Thanks for the two shower heads, but I'd much prefer to be able to enjoy a soak in the tub. That, by the way, doesn't even cover the tops of my thighs, it's so shallow (and I'm 145lbs, at 5'8"). 
Unfortunately, we are staying here for another 5 days, as my husband is attending a conference here. In that time, I fully expect to find some other ridiculous charge that will keep this rating at poor.
I should mention that when we first arrived in Boston, we stayed at a Hampton Inn. You know what? Their service was FAR SUPERIOR to that of this hotel. The business center was actually free, they didn't nickel and dime you for stupid crap ($1.50 to print ONE sheet of paper, and $6.00 for an hour of computer usage?!) and wouldn't have charged me nine dollars to send a package.

title_masked: absolutely central location and friendly staff
text_masked: What is the difference between al those nearly similar looking hotels? The staff and their service. I got a friendly and personal welcome, my room was somewhat clean (which improved after the first night, so that I left a tip for the housekeeping at the end). The bathroom was also clean, you really missed nothing, and everything was working perfect (dryer, fridge, microwave etc.). You may have a breakfast on 10th floor with an average buffet but a good cooking station with fresh made omelettes. One of the servers was very friendly, the other ones average, but really better than in other hotels. At checkout it was quick and woithout any complaints. The hotel itself is situated central to a SEPTA station, the convention center, and you may reach Chestnut and Walnut Streets as well as the historic ares within 15-20 minutes by footwalk, the must-see foodmarket is in the same block. The only complaint I had to the location was that the entrance area is dark, dirty and not inviting

We (3 adults, related) were in Boston for 3 days of sight-seeing, looking for a not-too-expensive place to stay. This hotel is good value-- for Boston. We ended up sharing a room. It was a little tight-- the best they could give us was a room with 2 double beds. They said it was a fire hazard to have an extra cot in the room, so we made due. We bought the package that includes breakfast and wireless internet service. Staff were friendly, helpful, and we liked the location-- a very short walk to a "T" stop, which we found convenient. Breakfast was excellent, although it involved waiting in line to place our order, so don't be in a hurry if you want breakfast or coffee. You walk into their little store and order it as carry-out, giving them your coupon, or paying for it. Then eat it in a section of their lobby set up for dining In the pet peeves department: hotels that do not offer free coffee for guests in the lobby in the morning. All in all, we enjoyed our stay at this hotel and would stay there again.

title_masked: Great location and service, just more than a bit pricey
text_masked:
We stayed here at the end of September 2012. Our vacation to San Francisco was kind of a bucket list item - we pored over the trip advisor reviews and decided to blow the budget at the Omni. It's a great location - handy to the cable cars, Embarcadero, Fisherman's Wharf, Chinatown and more. The service is pretty stellar - as it should be at these prices. The daily housekeeping was truly top notch. When we booked we joined the Omni rewards program - definitely do that - inital perks are maybe not huge but special - each morning we had a complimentary pot of coffee delivered to our door at the precise time we had indicated on the form that's left out each night. Delicious coffee by the way. Lex the concierge was very helpful as was all the front desk staff.
Bob's Bar off the lobby was always busy and hopping - the restaurant not as much - they should think about swapping the locations - there were frequently no tables or bar stools available at the bar but the restaurant wasn't nearly as busy. Bar service is available in the lobby which was fine but could get chilly whenever the front doors opened.
We had breakfast once at the Bob's restaurant - it was ok, not great, definitely not great for the price. We had light bites at Bob's a couple of times - we'd recommend the tenderloin sliders.
The Omni for us was almost a budget buster but we really loved the location - it was a special treat and we have no regrets.

My wife and I just stayed 2 fantastic nights at this hotel and only 2 blocks from the Capital Building. The rooms were spacious and clean .The rooms were recently remodeled with a huge granite bathroom and were provided with all the amenities needed for a great stay. The staff was very accommodating and I was upgraded to a room with a view of the Capital which I had requested.The lobby was beautifully decorated for the holidays and the size was overwhelming with views of the restaurant and cocktail lounge.
 We will be staying there again on our next visit to DC.

For a pricey hotel, the only appreciably upscale part of this hotel was the downtown location. Pretty convenient to all city sites. Other than than however I felt like I was staying at a Holiday Inn. Rooms were rather bland, mattresses were not up to the Hyatt standard, hair dryer in bathroom wouldn't work, shower curtain coming off its rings, $25 charge for moving things around in the fridge, one little in room coffee, and the list goes on. Don't get me wrong, things were tolerable, but not what I would expect from the flagship Hyatt in Boston. It would appear that the hotel is under extensive renovation, and it may be going on for a while. As mentioned in other reviews there is an entry at the ground floor (at parking level), which requires an elevator to bring you up to the lobby level, where you get off and switch to another elevator to get to your room. Sunday brunch at the Hyatt, which can often be an event, was again something I might expect at a lesser hotel. If I was going to return to Boston, I likely wouldn't use this hotel again, based mainly on what you get for the price.

When we checked in after a long flight, was surprised that the hotel wanted to take such a large amount on our credit card for items such as room bar, or meals. However when we expressed our surprise, this was reduced.
The room was very comfortable, best hotel bed we have ever used.
Staff extremely helpful and accommodating. Excellent location for all the tourist attractions. Bought a 7 day CTA pass and used the local transport which is incredably easy. Loved the city and being able to walk to the beach was fantastic.
Room was cleaned every day, and towels changed regularly.
Would recommend this hotel, and when we return to Chicago, plan on staying there again.

title_masked: Rethinking of reserving this hotel (especially via hotwire.com) !!!
text_masked:
I was ordered this hotel through hotwire.com one month in advance and fully paid it.
I got a confirmation from hotwire and the hotel.
Suprisingly, when I had arrived to the hotel there were no available rooms and I got a room in a lousy hostel on the other side of the street.
To make the long story short, i paid 140$ per night, got hotel which is cost 66$ per night.
Hotwire were willing to refund me with a redicilus amount of 25$.
I would not recommend having no buiseness with both horwire.com and this hotel !!!

The woman manager at the front desk on Sunday 09/09/12 came out to personally greet us and kindly gave us a view of Time Square at no additional cost. My sister and I came out from Los Angeles for the weekend and were staying in Brooklyn. We moved over to this hotel and were beyond satisfied with the location and the great customer service of the hotel. The rooms were very new and clean and our view was the icing on the cake. Thank you to those that helped us...I can't remember their names because I misplaced the manager's business card but whoever was on staff that Sunday and helped us check in...a special thank you to you :)

title_masked: An exceptional hotel with excellent customer service!
text_masked: Our stay at The Standard Hotel was fantastic in every way! The staff was friendly, courteous, and very professional. They made us feel very welcomed from the moment we arrived and went out of their way to make sure that all our needs were met. It was quite obvious that customer service is of the utmost importance to this hotel. Our room had a fantastic view and was immaculate. Our dinner at the hotel's restaurant was an outstanding dining experience with delicious food and great service! We loved the hotel's location and never had to worry about a taxi being available when we needed one. We highly recommend The Standard Hotel!

Spent one night at this property. It was one of the nicest Marriott hotels I've stayed in. Room was flawless, clean, very well appointed. Staff was helpful, polite, professional and helpful. Bed was big and very comfortable. I've stayed in many hotels in Chicago and this is the nicest one I've stayed in. I'm changing my future stays in Chicago to this hotel, I've found my new home. Anyone finding flaws with this property would be very, very picky.

title_masked: Hotel Service Near Perfect / Restaurant Service Perfectly Awful
text_masked:
My wife and I were traveling to Chicago for a family function, and were staying in the northern suburbs. just prior to our trip we received a Groupon offer for a night at The Dana with a $25 dining credit at Argent the hotel's new restaurant. We decided to purchase the Groupon and spend the last night of our trip (after the family function had concluded) at The Dana. Since we we're just going to be traveling across town, it was July 4th, and it was going to be 102 out, we asked when making the reservation if we could arrange for an early check-in, we were quite happy to be told we could check-in at 11 am, and sure enough upon our arrival, there was no problem with checking so early.
Overall the property is a very nice boutique hotel with loft-style rooms (hardwood floors, concrete ceilings and walls). When we purchased the Groupon offer, the regular king suites were no longer so I opted for the corner-suite upgrade which proved a wise choice. The floor to ceiling windows along two walls provided a fantastic vista of Chicago. The area around the hotel is a mix of residential, commercial, and tourist. The location is considered "River North" and it is on the border of the tourist area with many hotels 
The room features a room length counter/desk with a work area, an iPod/iPhone dock (the Zeppelin sound-system), a 37" flat-screen HDTV (with HD programming), 2 cordless phone handsets, an incredibly comfortable bed with very comfy pillows, a loveseat built for two, a small mini-bar fridge (with red and white wine selections). The closet contained 2 bathrobes and slippers (and a tall but shallow room-safe). The bathroom was extremely large with upscale toiletries, a mirror that had a lighted frame surrounding it, and a gigantic shower with an overhead waterfall showerhead and a separate shower wand. oddly enough, the shower wall in common with the room is clear glass (with a curtain on teh bedroom side) which means that if you forget to close the curtain all the way you can see directly into not just the shower but the toilet area as well.
When we arrived at the hotel, we were immediately greeted by the doorman, TJ, who was helpful, conversational, knowledgeable and friendly. Over the course of our stay, every encounter with him was pleasant, and he appeared to take a genuine interest in our well-being. We were checked-in by Terri, a guest-services associate, and she too, was an absolute delight to deal with. She too was incredibly friendly and helpful.
Our bellman, Christopher was helpful, friendly, and informative, he voluntarily showed us the locations of the emergency exits (a first for us in ANY hotel!), gave us tips about the climate control and window-shades in our corner-suite, and provided a number of other helpful tips about our room and the hotel.
Unfortunately I was unable to plug my iPhopne4 into the Zeppelin docking system, since the adapter on the Zeppelin didn't fit the phone's connector properly. As the majority of iPhones and iPod touches use the same connector as the iPhone 4/4s, I would imagine this is a common problem, a conversion adaptor would be a nice touch.
After such magnificent service from the hotel staff upon our arrival, our waiter "Erik H" at Argent was an incredible disappointment. I spoke to the hostess after our meal and informed her of Erik's lack of any interest in serving us. The hostess' reaction, lead my wife and me to believe that this was not surprising to her. He needs to be told that just because a table is not ordering alcoholic beverages does not mean that they deserve lesser service. He was rude, inefficient, and made my wife and me fell absolutely uncomfortable. One particular "highlight" of his service was when he brought two popovers to our table (after a busboy had previously brought us one). Erik began to tell us that, "these are our popovers..." when I told him I knew what they were because we had already been served one, he took the two he was bringing us away. There is no excuse for such poor service in such a fine restaurant as Argent. Our food was fantastic, but the service nearly overshadowed the positive aspects of our meal.
After dinner we went up to the rooftop bar ("Vertigo") for drinks and to watch the fireworks over Chicago. The view from the rooftop is quite breathtaking, and our server at the bar was as attentive and polite as could be. Overall the bar had a modern but not overly trendy feel. I'd have been interested to see what it's like on a weekend night.
On Thursday morning, , my wife and I were left to take our own bags downstairs after waiting more than 30 minutes for a bellman upon checking-out. I called down to the desk twice to get the status of a bellman, and the person on the other end of the line was obviously frustrated and embarrassed by the lapse in service, but unable to deliver a bellman to our room in a timely manner. We should have been informed if assistance is in such short supply during pre-check-out time hours. As we had been so impressed upon check-in, this didn't bother us as much as it might have if our other encounters with everyone on the hotel staff hadn't been so pleasant.
One other issue was that another room down the hall from us had ordered room-service sometime before our arrival on Wednesday, and the dirty dishes and trays remained outside their room past our check-out on Thursday, a little disturbing.
Overall, our experience was positive, and the corner suite is truly gorgeous. With a bit of smoothing out the rough-ends, this hotel would have been absolutely perfect,

Ms [NAME], the Sales Manager, shined bright by providing exemplary service to our large group before, during, and after our recent stay at the Sheraton Brookhollow. Having organized numerous events over the years, I have never had such a pleasant experience experience working with a Sales Manager as I did working with Ms [NAME]. She consistently went above and beyond the call of duty to meet or exceed our unique group's needs in a timely and efficient manner. The experience relieved a great deal of stress and work from my own personal workload in terms of organizing our event and I look forward to coordinating with Ms [NAME] and the Sheraton Brookhollow in the future. 
I can confidently say that this was the experience of all of our event guests as evidenced by our internal feedback questionnaire. Ms [NAME]'s name was hailed numerous times by participants who interacted with her and as an event organizer this is the highest praise possible, to know that the participants needs are met in a friendly and efficient manner. 
However, I would also like to point out that the pleasurable experience was not limited to Ms [NAME] but the entire Sheraton Brookhollow staff. Multiple positive comments were mentioned regarding the Bar, Restaurant, Registration, and Housekeeping staff. 
It's nice to stay in a great newly remodeled facility and know that your friends and family will be comfortable and well taken care of.
We very much looks forward to working with the Sheraton Brookhollow in the future!

This is an older hotel with little architectural or decorative interest, but it seems to be well-run and served us just fine for three nights. Our standard room was remarkably spacious, well-equipped, clean and comfortable, though dull. I learned the hard way that the electrical outlets on the front of the desk (clearly designed for laptops and chargers) were non-functional. No noise problems on the 15th floor.
The food and service at their Daily Grill restaurant (located next door in the mall) was excellent, breakfast especially. All the hotel staff I dealt with were courteous and helpful. There are many good restaurants nearby in the mall and in the surrounding neighborhood.
Their business center makes it quick and easy to print your boarding passes at no charge, even in the middle of the night.
Please ignore my detailed ratings, as my only choices were "terrible" or "excellent", at least on my browser.

We stayed at the Felix for a week during an architectural pilgrimage to Chicago. It's very convenient to Chicago's terrific public transportation system, two blocks to the subway and 2 steps to the bus lines. There is a building that looks under construction next door but when we asked, fearing drilling and construction noise ruining early mornings, it appears the construction has been idled for several years by the recession so it was lovely quiet while we were there.
 Rooms are clean, though tiny. Adequate for business travel and if you are not expecting a resort experience. One negative, the near total lack of closet and drawer space. Hint: look for drawer at foot of bed. Great example why minimalism is an OK aesthetic choice but highly impractical. Strangely, while the hotel brags about its Eco-friendly features (it's even LEEDS certified) they replaced all linens and towels every day, hardly the most environmentally sensitive policy.
Staff are very friendly and welcoming. They get 5 stars.
Small lobby and free coffee in AM.
Best surprise however? The restaurant, Elate. We had 2 great meals there and the chocolate Pot de Creme is not to be missed.
Overall, I would stay there again, especially if we could get a competitive rate by Priceline or other means. Not luxurious but highly acceptable. And the Pot de Creme!

Reservations: easy and great price through the TripAdvisor website.
Check-in: efficient, accurate, and very warm and friendly.
Room: spacious and quiet, with superb bath towels and linens, very comfortable beds, and a nicely appointed bathroom with excellent bath products. Nice flat screen TV. FREE internet!
Breakfast and Wine and Cheese Reception: free and just fantastic. Much more than your typical hotel continental breakfast, with bagels, cereal, pastries, yogurt, fresh fruit, coffee, tea, and juices. Lovely wine and cheese evening reception.
Check-out: fast, efficient, and friendly.
This is an awesome hotel with a great location just off of Park Avenue.

My husband and I drove down to do a little sightseeing last week and stayed at this hotel. It was very nice and only about a block from Chinatown. Lots of restaurants close by and a very nice area. I don't think I've ever been to a cleaner city!! We walked everywhere from the hotel. Granted my feet did feel like they were going to fall off but that's more because we were trying to see everything in a day!! Walked as far as the Lincoln Memorial which would have taken about 20 minutes if we had walked straight there!! Awesome trip!! Very nice, comfortable hotel. A little construction noises in the morning, but there is construction going on all over the city so I'm sure it would have been heard anywhere!!

Proximity to Times Square is a major plus. Staff was very helpful and it was quite refreshing for even the maids to say good morning each day as you passed. Room was clean and beds were good. Biggest complaint is lack of outlets in room. Whether for iron or laptop, good luck. But, this is a common complaint in most hotels as only a few seem to recognize that need. Bar was good and had a good selection. Breakfast was good, but pricey. Fitness room was okay, but some of the equipment was down.

Stayed here a couple of nights in mid May 2012. This is an old building that has been well renovated and has a lot of old style atmosphere rather than aluminum and plastic found in newer hotels. We had a corner room that was large with a sofa, work desk, bureau, large LCD TV and King Bed. We did not notice any noise other than sirens that you hear even in the most sound-proof hotel. Large bathroom and all rooms were clean. Service was good and you get a cookie at check-in. Hotel is well situated near Pioneer Square and a short walk to Pike's Market. Would stay here again

Very large, comfortable room. Comfortable bed, decent furniture, big window letting in lots of light. Very much a large corporate chain, all the rooms pretty much identical (benchmarked against colleagues' who were staying with me), though that said I had an end-of-corridor room which had an even larger bathroom appropriate for people with mobility issues. Long corridors straight out of The Shining. Location is where a map will show you - work out if that is appropriate for your stay. It is indeed right on the mall, which has plentiful shopping, cafes, an ice rink etc. Smallish bar on first floor with good service. Ate late(ish) at Oceanaire and had good seafood (was able to compare 3 or 4 different types of US oysters as a starter) but reluctant, bad service from a waiter who clearly was annoyed that we were keeping him from going home (we arrived well within the time that the restaurant stated it was open). We were sanguine about this but it would have ruined the dinner had it been something we'd been particularly looking forward to. Lobby staff, however, were great and all in all couldn't fault it. Good value, too.

Huge hotel with bustling lobby. Nothing really wrong with the hotel, but nothing special about it either. Hotel has kind of a crowded, congested feel. Location is OK. The Starbucks in the lobby had huge lines in the morning.

title_masked: Lovely hotel at an attractive rate
text_masked: My husband and I attended a convention at the last minute. We used an online service to find a hotel near the Convention Center and checked Days Inn on TripAdvisor. We liked everything about it: large, clean double room, parking nextdoor, exceptionally friendly and helpful staff, and the cost was half of what our colleagues paid at a nearby hotel. Three days before the date we booked there was a 20% off special posted online, which made our stay an even better bargain.

title_masked: Got The Room at a Great Price!
text_masked:
I stay in NYC a lot since I live on Long Island. This hotel was a great price so I couldn't resist staying there. I would actually give it 3.5 stars because there were many things I liked about it. The room was very clean. The bed was very comfy as were the pillows. The desk staff, as well as the concierge, were polite and helpful. The location is great and in a good neighborhood.
 The only thing I didn't like was that the room they gave us had a lot of imperfections. If it wasn't for the great price these imperfections would have been quite bothersome. For one thing, the heater made an awful sound all throughout the night. Parts of the room were worn and in need of an update. The television worked intermittently due to a weak signal. I'm thinking the room price was so low because of these imperfections. Read other reviews to compare. Overall, I would stay there again at that price.

My flight was cancelled today due to a major weather system moving in. As soon as I got the message from my airline, I asked my wife to search online for a hotel close to my last meeting of the day. She came up with this one. I stay in the city probably 5 or 6 nights each month and had never considered this place. Boy - have I been missing out. Truly extraordinary, friendly and helpful service at the front desk. Great room (king). Remarkably low rate (for mid-town Manhattan any way). Good room service food that's reasonably priced. Comfortable bed. Modern. Clean. I have finally found my must-go-to hotel in NYC.

The proprietor of this location owes a huge apology not just to the guests, but also to the staff. I have rarely stayed at a place where everyone was as keen as these people to make sure I was happy.
It is also in a fantastic location: four blocks from the convention center. An easy walk to the National Mall or public transportation.
But here's the let down: the rooms. OK, they're small. Not a deal breaker. But they're dismal. I couldn't tell if the carpet and bedding were old, or just not well kept. The wallpaper was scarred, peeling, and bubbling - not just in the bathroom, but the main room, too. The paint on the bathroom ceiling was bubbling: the sign of painted over mold. Then there's the smell. The first day it just seemed stale. But as the days progressed, my room had a growing sense of damp. A colleague had an even worse odor in his room. Another oddity was the placement of the hair dryer - right over the sink. One last oddity - a lamp on the desk wouldn't work and i assumed it was the bulb. Investigating a couple of days later, I discovered that it wasn't plugged in ... as there was no outlet anywhere near the lamp.
The positives ... the bed was very comfortable. And the lounge/dining area in the basement was well decorated.
The pictures on the hotel's website were obviously taken the day the renovations were completed - however many years ago that was. This could be an excellent place to stay. But it isn't.

This place is in a GREAT location. Fisherman's Wharf, the F-Train and a Cable car line are all within walking distance. 
The staff are friendly and helpful. I never opened a door or carried a heavy bag. The evening wine/pizza reception is a nice touch and the staff are so friendly.
Because of the location, the view we had was of the Wharf and was great, although with the view we also got some noise from the road and the bus stop across the street. Not all rooms will have a view of the wharf though. 
We did not have a car, but found it easy to get from the Amtrak to the F-train to the hotel with our luggage and then back without issue. Buy a Muni pass, it is sooo worth it.
My only complaint besides the noise of the street was the size/cost of the room. We reserved a King Suite for 3-4 people assuming it would be 2 rooms or a room with some separation. It was a room with a King bed and a couch that makes into a bed. Thankfully we only had 2 people in the room after all and even with that it was tight with all of our luggage etc. So if you have more than 2 people you might want to get 2 rooms, but they are pricey, but worth it for the location.

title_masked: Never have to leave the property
text_masked:
We had a fantastic stay of nine days in early February. It was very quiet, for most of the trip we felt like we had the place to ourselves. Friday & Saturday nights were a bit noisier as there was a business conference being held, but there were no problems.
The staff are all very friendly, smiling and waving and saying hello. 
We were upgraded to a beachfront room, and it was so nice to walk out the door and down to the water. Our toddler loved building sandcastles just in front of the room. Other highlights for him were feeding the ducks that hang around on the pond (and they sell little packages of duck food in the island market), climbing the lookout tower, going swimming in the main (heated) pool, and roasting marshmallows on one of the fires they have.
As parents, we appreciated the onsite laundry (which was located by a pool, so you can go swimming while your clothes are washing), the good housekeeping staff who were accommodating to our child's naptimes, and the feeling of quiet & safety. I felt no hesitation wandering around the resort after dark.
The food at Baleen was good, we ate there every day as the Barefoot was closed for renovations The staff were understanding about having a child in tow, and promptly brought to go containers, and supplied us with the extras (ketchup & peanut butter) that toddlers appreciate. 
We had an awesome stay, I'm sure I'm forgetting things but can't say enough good things about this resort.

I live in Houston and I took my daughter for a 2 day getaway to San Antonio and we stayed at the utterly beautiful, stylish, comfortable Hotel Havana. Liz Lambert is a genius with design! The hotel is warm, cozy, gorgeous with all the amenities you could want with a great personal touch - does not feel like a hotel, more like someone's beautiful home. It does not feel like Texas, actually does not even feel like the US. I feel like I am transported into a space that reminds me of a cross between somewhere in Paris and India... The Ocho Lounge has these incredible chandeliers with teal blue and yellow velvet couches....I would go back to SA just to stay at the Havana!

The Omni Hotel in San Francisco is a good hotel with great service by the staff. The rooms are certainly adequate and comparable to other similar hotels, but not wonderful. The same with the food options, but what makes this hotel really good is the service provided by the staff. They are friendly, helpful and go out of their way to make your stay enjoyable. Given today's difficulty in getting good service I would take a good service experience over a more luxurious room anytime.
Very comfortable,clean,nice bathroom. The view and proximity to Seaport area was so worth the price. Across parking lot to the T station. Walking distance to Cruise Terminal.
Great Hotel. If it wasnt for the construction going on next door I would have given the highest raiting. Walk to the Capitol!

Booked 4 nights from Aug 02 at this Hotel through travelocity and at great price. We are from Toronto and this was are first visit to NYC. The Hotel is very easy to get to from JFK airport, take the air train to Jamaica subway station and then the subway to 53rd and 6th and you are right around the corner from the Hotel, took maybe 60 minutes in total. Are room was on the 14th floor street side, very roomy and came with a fridge and a whirl pool bath. Great room, the staff very helpful and the bed was very comfortable. I would not hesitate to book this Hotel again. You are within a 5 minute walk to time square, how much more could you ask for. Get the New York City pass with hop on and off bus, you will love the attractions that come with the pass. Anybody that complains about this Hotel and staff have issues.

This is a special gem in a sea of choices!! We were very satisfied with our room (#116) and the location of this motel. I cannot say enough about the experience of our 4 days here. There is a convenience store right outside for any needs, the Cafe Lombard across the street and on the bus route (buy a muni pass). We parked our car and it stayed there for 4 days!! All in all the experience was exceptional and if you want a clean hotel to meet your standard needs, you will not be disappointed. Friends were at the Wharf Inn and we felt very lucky with our choice of motels. It was much quieter, cleaner, updated, etc. yet a quick walk to Fisherman's Wharf, Lombard Street, Coit Tower, the cable cars, etc!! The manager has been at the motel for 23 years and it is managed very well. Enjoy!!

Nigal checked us in and was, in essence, our first contact with Monaco Baltimore. He was genuinely welcoming and efficient with the check-in process. He was also insightful when it came to providing us with helpful hints on where to go and what to see in Baltimore. He set the stage for a highly pleasant stay at Monaco Baltimore.

First time in Philly and loved staying at the hotel. Service was excellent! Staff was eager to please and for an older hotel, we had a nice size room. Went up to the top floor for drinks Friday eve, but there was no room to sit. We were disappointed but realized this was a very happening place. The only down part was breakfast this past Sunday. The food left alot to be desired for $20 a person plus tip. It was buffet style but still...definately not worth the money. Will definately stay there again. Eat at Ralphs in the Italian district and you won't be sorry. The food was delish. The other place we ate was Butcher and Singer...you are looking at $200 plus easy for a couple.
