Beautiful place with awesome service/food. The location of this hotel was really good as well for being in an area where you will walk most of the time.

Wasn't overwhelmed upon first impression. The location and room was drab. When I checked in there was no chair or mini-fridge in the room. Upon request the staff did not hesitate to deliver them. The staff was freindly and responsive. The bed was comfy and the room was quiet. It was a great place to sleep. A big plus was the YMCA adjacent to the hotel. Another plus was the short distance from the hotel to the "T", only 50 meters away.

title_masked: Good Hotel, surroundings are weird but not that bad.
text_masked:
This was our first trip to SF, the first impression was bad because the neighborhood does not look so good. But when you identify your surrounding then you find you're close to a lot of convenient places and paying a lot less than in Union Sq. You are at walking distance to Civic Center and Market Street. BART is also close.
Staff was a mix of unfriendly and friendly people (mostly unfriendly). Rooms were clean but the bed was too hard and uncomfortable. Restaurant serves a nice buffet with good choices of food.
We rented a car to visit Sacramento but the price for parking at the hotel was very very high.

When I got "home" to my room at the Eastgate I settled in for the week. I had a beautiful view (25B is the best room of the many I've been in there) and the kitchen saved me money on meals. But the best part of my trip was housekeeping. No matter how busy I was, when I got "home" my room was beautifully clean and orderly with extra touches like folding my scarf and draping over the back of the chair. I felt completely taken care of at the Eastgate with tips on grocery stores and commuting advice. Carol was the first desk person I encountered but the rest of the staff is just as friendly. It's nice to be told hello when you come back from a hard day! It's the only hotel for me from now on.

Stayed at the Doubletree in Center City Phila Jan 5 and 6, 2012. Updated rooms. Right in the heart of the city. Ask for rooms that face Broad street and are high up so that you can see the Broad Street evening illuminations of City Hall and the Large Buildings along Broad Street. Friendly staff, good lounge downstairs. Close to the best restaurants in town. Plenty of parking. Across the street from the Academy of Music and the Kimmel Center.

We arrived on a Sat and checked out on Tuesday. Our room was in the renovated section on the 20th floor at the back of the hotel. We had absolutely no noise from anyone nor from traffic, even with the freeway right below us. The room was modern and with all conveniences. A motion detection night light underneath the night stand came on when you get out of the bed and was a nice touch. The huge window coverings were opened and closed by electric panel. A mini fridge was convenient. We found all personnel most helpful and eager to please. We did not use the restaurants there, except for the coffee shop and found it to be convenient for snacks , etc. We used the Super Shuttle to and from DFW, so no experience with the parking facility. With the convenience of the city in walking distance, we enjoyed it very much. Would stay again!

I had a wonderful stay at this hotel. I was very impressed! The room was magnificent. I love the granite design in the bathroom and the photos in the sitting room. This has been a very comfortable place to spend the last few day. 
The hotel has great character! Much of this is driven by the splendid art in the small lobby, out front, and next door. 
Lastly, I would like to comment on the staff. Everyone has been so nice and polite. The woman at the front desk, when I arrived, made the hotel feel warm and inviting.
I liked the fact that it was a very short walk to Grand Central.
I will be back on my next trip to NYC.

Wonderful staff and service, great being offered bottled water, given, for us, the temperature was up there. Clean rooms, easy access, good location, i.e. we visited Tempe to meet family from Pheonix, and easy access to the highways.

The Millennium Hotel has a perfect location for those who want to be in the heart of the city's theater district. Our room was on the 33rd floor and commanded a great view. The room was not huge but not tiny either. It was comfortable, and the air conditioning worked very well during the hot, humid days of late August. The staff were all pleasant and courteous, and the hotel was very clean. The rooms are not cheap, but neither is anything else in that location! We easily walked to theaters and restaurants, and I was happy to find a Starbucks right next door! I would stay here again on future trips to NYC.

title_masked: Great hotel and location when visiting Chicago
text_masked: We stayed here in early October. The hotel has a great location for seeing the sites of Chicago. Close access to Millenium Park, the Art Institute, Field Museum and Shopping. Our room was large, modern and had a great view of the park. There are lots of great restaurants nearby and the restaurant in the hotel was also very good. Staff service was excellent. My only issue is that wifi was an extra cost. This is where we will stay whenever we visit Chicago.

title_masked: I would stay here again and again
text_masked: A gem of a hotel located near Seattle Univerisity and Pill Hill. I stayed here alone for two nights, and loved it. The staff were very warm and generous. A glass of wine was waiting at check in, hand the rooms were clean, well appointed, and the beds comfortable. It is an old hotel, so the elevator is small (which is charming) and the plumbing a little slow to bring up the hot water (which is a shame as they must waste a lot of water.) They have a restaurant which I did not go to because it was more a meat lovers place. But the lounge was quiet and comfortable. I sat by the fire and ordered wine and read and just had a wonderful time all by myself.

We came to The Dana in San Diego from Marysvale, UT. Our son is stationed in San Diego was getting married. The hotel was perfect! Right across from Marina Village where the reception was. The suite had an amazing view and was perfect for entertaining guests between the wedding and reception.

Increadable! The service I received from check in to check out was out of this world!
We checked in early and not only was the room ready it was stunning! 
We had the most amazing concierge help us with a dinner booking (where I proposed)- on arrival we were given champeyne that had been arranged by the concierge- How crazy is that!
All of our internet charges were wiped clean and we also received a free breakfast. Stunning pool too! This hotel knows exactly how to treat people and I will sell this property to all of my clients =)

We drove past this hotel for years before we realized that it is a full size resort. This Hilton has it all--a variety of room types, great dining, great shopping, a gorgeous swimming pool, its own marina, beach volleyball, a full spa, tennis courts, lots of free activities--and it is all right on the beach. It is also within a 5-10 minute drive from the airport, downtown and Old Town. We were surprised to learn that this property is 50 years old this year--it has been upgraded and so well tended that it seems much newer.
Service is also spectacular. Ask for TC at the front desk if she is available.
Minor complaint #1--$32/day to park your car is absurd for anywhere in San Diego, but especially when there is free parking on the street in front of the property, in a relatively safe area. Minor complaint #2--WiFi is free but service is weak, which explains the gathering of people with laptops in the main lobby every day.
No hotel property is perfect, but this one comes close. We rented a waverunner and followed a pod of dolphins just 200' off the hotel marina, at slow speed of course so we wouldn't disturb them. You can't beat that.

We stayed at the Bentley for 5 nights and it was a big disappointment ! Arriving late evening we were informed on check in that the hotel was overbooked and we were given a smaller room with queen bed instead of the king bed we had explicitly asked for at the reservation stage ! Moreover, the explanation was given by the receptionist after being informed that we had booked through the hotels.com website and not directly through their site.. ! We requested for a room change right away and were informed after much whispering amongst the staff that we would have to stay out for the night and cud be given a change if we left our room keys with them in the morning .. Subsequently though we left the room key and a message with reception the next day, we were not given a room change as the message was not conveyed during ther day shift change! Finally, after putting our foot down on living out of a suitcase yet another night ( not to forget our feet hanging off the bed as we are tall!) and raising a ruckus, we were given a room change magically ! The hotel s average, quite jaded and honestly, needs a makeover in customer service being in the hospitality business. Last but not the least, did see another guy having the same problem as us at check in so definitely, not a one off experience.

title_masked: Excellent customer service plus usual hyatt quality
text_masked: Awesome experience the moment you walk in the door. Warm, genuine greetings from doorman to reception, to restaurant and housekeeping. Management extremely apologetic for a very minor issue regarding keys. Even got a small gift to say sorry which was not necessary. Room, gym, restaurant, check in and out experience all excellent. Gym was very good considering it was a hotel gym. I was offered lots of extras which i did not ask for including free breakfasts, wifi/internet in room, one ironing a day, US phone calls. Great location.

title_masked: It seems that the low rate attracts guests with unpleasant behavior
text_masked:
Room was quiet and of good size.
The mattress was uncomfortable.
There were stains on a towel.
The washing machines and driers are free.
No breakfast.
The other guests at that hotel are probably not exactly well educated. We had to wait an hour and 20 minutes for a guest to take his cloths out of the drier (after his cloths were dry already) in order to take our cloths out of the washer and put them in the drier.
We had to wait 30 minutes for a luggage cart, although the guest that was using it knew we need it and knew we were waiting for it.
The printer at the business center was out of order, so was the phone there.
The door of one of the rooms on ground floor next to the elevator was pemanently open and the guest there were watching every person that passed or used the elevator, it was more than strange.
At front desk the workers were friendly, but it's not enough.

New generation of Fairfields with good service from friendly staff. Fitness room is nothing special but they have an arrangement with a gym that is quite nice and less than 2 minutes away. Will stay here again.

My only complaint about my entire experience was the cost of parking...but, I recognize that parking is at a premium in D.C. so I willingly paid it. 
The staff was wonderful, efficient, and friendly. My room was awesome and it was supplied with everything I could possibly have needed. I love that it's a historic hotel...it had that old-fashioned charm that I adore.
The hotel is so well located! It's in the nicest part of D.C. and is so close to the Metro and several great restaurants and attractions. 
I had a great stay and hope to return soon!

title_masked: Not the best of the Drury properties
text_masked: Several family members stayed at this Drury Inn in June. Upon checking out, we were unable to get a receipt and had a PDF file emailed to us. I am a fan of the Drury properties, but this location has not kept up and modernized. As another reviewer indicated, there is a problem with rooms smelling like smoke. I don't know if it was once a smoking room or not, but the smell still lingered. Since a family member lives close by, the hotel selections are limited in this area and we've stayed in just about all of them. But he indicated he would be looking for another hoted for family visits. I was disappointed as I'm generally happy with the Drury Inn brand.

We got two adjoining rooms at the Marriott. One was a double/double and the other was a king. Lots of space to work, room safe, honor bar, large bathroom with separate tub and shower and granite throughout. King room had a sofa bed as well. DVD player and large flat screen TV.
The restaurant downstairs was excellent (ask for the couch potatoes) and service was great. 
Valet parking was expensive (there is no self park option) but the valets were very helpful offering water and would print out directions to wherever you wanted to go.
The Cherry Creek area is great with large number of restaurants and stores within 6 blocks of the hotel. There is also a great mall across the street.
Used the gym which had a number of cardio machines, free weights and one multi station. Towels, fruit, water and headphones are provided.
Staff was great throughout and highly recommend the hotel. Going back in April and will definitely stay here again.

title_masked: Huge Room, Great Location, Curiously Small Bathroom
text_masked:
MileNorth (formerly Affinia) is located on Superior & Michigan, next door to a Gino's East, and just down the street from the Magnificent Mile. The hotel is well-located to the bus lines, restaurants, stores, sights (a block or two from the Water Tower), and shopping. The only negative about the location is that the hotel is also located right next to a hospital, so you occasionally hear ambulances coming in and out.
The hotel room is gigantic. At the entrance of the room is a desk/office area, with steps leading down into a living room/couch, with the queen size bed tucked in the back corner. We liked that the bed was tucked away from the hotel door, as this minimized any noise from any other guests who were out in the hallway. The only negative about the room is, for the large size of the room, the bathroom was curiously tiny. You would have a hard time having more than one person in the bathroom at a time. As a point of comparison, our friends were staying at Hotel 71 across the river, and the bathroom at Hotel 71 was large - you could probably fit 4-5 people in there comfortably. However, this is a minor complaint, as it was only me and my wife staying at MileNorth, whereas our friends at Hotel 71 were 4 women who had to share one bathroom.
The staff was also very friendly - from the front desk staff, the porters, as well as the cleaning crew.
Overall, we enjoyed our stay at MileNorth and would recommend it to others.

This is a great place to stay not only is the service, food, and room great it has great history. Marriott converted this historic landmark which was a bank built in the late 1920's. The rooms, very comfortable and modern, were originally the bank offices. Don't forget to ask the Bellman for a tour and lecture about the building history plus get a tour of the old vault in the basement.

title_masked: Good value for money hotel in downtown San Francisco
text_masked:
We had a lovely cosy room. It was clean and everything you really need in a room - clean towels provided everyday, tea/coffee-making facilities, television, telephone. Only small niggle would be not having enough clothes hangers (we only had 5 hangers between us!)
Front-desk reception staff worked in a professional manner and were generally friendly and helpful. One member of staff in particular, Gaby Gonzalez was very helpful and went that 'extra mile' with fantastic customer care and service.
Fantastic location right in the centre of lots of shops (Macy's, Nordstrom, Westfield Shopping Center, Bloomingdales) and so many different types of eateries. You are spoilt for choice!
The hotel is also within easy reach of transport to touristic attractions and San Francisco Airport: the Powell-Mason Cable Car, MUNI Metro and BART Metro.

We arrived after a weekend of hiking in the mountains, and were happy to sink into one of the most comfortable beds we have ever found in a hotel. I don't know what they top their mattresses with, but it was a very luxurious rest. The location is great if you need a downtown hotel. It would have been nice to have a pool, but otherwise we had a great experience. The front desk staff was friendly, and the room was very clean.

I had opportunity to stay at this property from February 9 -February 11, 2012. I arrived downtown just before noon and called as I was on my way to see if I could check in before my 1230 meeting. The operator and then desk clerk was very helpful in getting me in my room early. The food at the reception on Friday night I attend was fabulous, everyone was very nice and the complementary shoe polishing service was impeccable and definitely recommended. The only down fall like most Marriott properties is they charge for Internet access. That said there is a Starbucks connected to hotel which does not and I always enjoy Starbucks on breaks.

We stayed in one of the larger suites and were very satisfied. There is a large kitchenette, a huge dining table and just tons and tons of space which is nice since we were with a large family group. The adobe fireplace is also a nice feature. Overall a good deal for such a nice room. 
The pools are great, there are many and lots of hot tubs too. In the winter there is never a problem with crowding, although once we visited here in the summer and it was much too crowded to enjoy at the main pool area. Unfortunately the water slide was broken during our stay, which was a huge disappointment to the younger children we were travelling with. They kept saying it would be ready the next day, so that was annoying. 
We had lunch at the poolside bar/cafe a few times and it was not very good for the price, but the service was nice and friendly. Plus, you can't put a price on sipping a smoothie in a hot tub in 80 degree weather at the end of November.
The one thing that really bothered me was the lack of free wi-fi. They really should just include wifi in the price. If they raised room rates by $5 and stopped charging for wi-fi I would be infinitely happier. 
Also, we used to love watching the movies offered in room, but they have recently gotten rid of them so that is annoying.

If you'd like to stay in a walkable area of Philly and know you're in a special city, stay in the Club Quarters. Built in the 1920s, it's an interesting and groovy building which bears no resemblence to the millions of chain hotel rooms that all look the same. The rooms are small, but unless you plan to spend your entire visit inside a bedroom, it's a perfectly fine place to shower, sleep, and do some work (rooms have ample desk space, wifi, and lighting). The price is amazing for Center City Philadelphia and the location is safe and filled with shopping, restaurants, and public transportation. I will absolutely stay there again!
Great location in the heart of UCLA. Excellent food and drinks also located in between Santa Monica and Hollywood.

title_masked: Comfy beds, good location and firemen!
text_masked:
This hotel is just fine. Booked it last minute while in the area for a funeral. Was allowed to check in at 11:00 a.m. That morning the hotel was welcoming the "Association of fire fighters'" *hubba hubba*! In their honor the hotel treated guests to complimentary pretzels, soda pop, water and fruit. It was a great welcome to Philly. Thank you Sheraton! Advice to management: If you do this sort of thing regularly guests are willing to forgive little mishaps. It absolutely helped me have a more pleasant stay. 
We booked a regular room and we got a decent view of the city. The best part of the room was the bed it was fantastic! Comfy pillows (lots of them). Most importantly the room was clean. The hotel itself is okay it's not fancy but its not bad at all. Great place to stay if you're in the area to sleep.
I took advantage of being in the city and had some fantastic *good eats* I had dinner at Morimoto and it was delicious. The Franklin Institute is awesome within a 5 minute walk and is currently exhibiting - The dead sea scrolls. Mutter museum was excellent exhibiting lots of medical oddities also walking distance.
I bumped my rating due to the complimentary treats it was such a nice welcome!

My girlfriend and I stayed at the Menger Hotel on Aug 6-8, 2012. Upon arriving to the hotel, the valet told us that parking was $28. I didn't realize that that was the rate per day. When we got the car back it was obvious that the car was parked in uncovered parking with all the dust on the car. Also, upon entering the room we noticed right away the musty smell and dust everywhere. The carpet was old, full of stains, and was wrinkling off of the floor. The room was tiny, as the King size bed took up almost all of the room. The TV was surplus from the early ninety's, and the furniture was just plain old. The bathroom had broken tile, a shower curtain that was stained and too short for the tub as if it had been washed a thousand times. The whole hotel was dusty and dirty. The lobby had dust balls visible beneath the antique furniture, and lights bulbs were out. I'm from San Antonio, and know the area, but I was curious if the the disk clerk would offer some suggestions for breakfast. "Oh the restaurant here has a very good breakfast." "Well, we wanted to sit outside and enjoy the weather," I said. "We also have table in the garden area." We took his advice and had breakfast amongst the maintenance workers working on the fountain area. A bottle of water "Fiji" cost $8 dollars if opened in the room. Really! Do yourself a favor and don't stay at the Menger. Instead, walk through the lobby to look at the memorabilia and save your money. The place sucks!

This hotel is a great value for the money!
Hotel staff was extremely helpful and courteous.
Room came with a fridge, and microwave, a rarity at this price range.
Room was large and clean.
For breakfast the biscuits and gravy were great, would have liked some fresh fruit but definitely don't expect it for the price of the room. 
Only complaint was that the queen bed hurt my back a little but switched to a king bed and it was great.
If I paid $100 + for the stay I woulda given it 3 stars, but for this price it's 5 stars!

One night stay for a wedding being held at this hotel. Staff was friendly. Although a few phone calls produced some frustration about an early check in time, when we arrived our room was ready and the front desk staff was very accommodating. The room was very sleek. The lighting was very hard to work ... high tech and confusing. The configuration of the bathroom made it nearly impossible to open the shower door and have the bathroom door open at the same time. The design of the sink in the bathroom is terrible...you end up with water all over the counter. Pricey.

always love the hampton inns , this one had a very good review , our room was smaller (no microwave nor refrig and pool area very small and not shaded (101 degree weather ) large opened breakfast area and computer space did not see many of their staff as in other inns but all were friendly and helpful ! hotel was clean and fresh per usual no real complains ! (we used hotels.com and got great rates on room ! )
we were attending a family b/day party so we were happy to drive up to ft worth from houston and have a clean and decent place to stay including morning breakfast. The next day we toured the city a bit, stockyards and the cowgirl museum, shopped and even got to go to a Sam Moons which is a great place for costume jewelry, handbags etc at reasonable prices .
it was a long ride back and forth but rented a car locally thru enterprise car rental and again a great rate and that was well worth it ! 
we will always recommend the hampton inn and now will include enterprise car rentals as another one of our favorites that we can count on !

title_masked: Good place to stay in New York
text_masked: Very good location , close to Central Park , nice walk to time square with lots of places to eat along the way. Staff was very helpful in any questions we had as was first time in New York Room was large, very clean and quiet.

title_masked: Im here now.. I got lost in our suite
text_masked:
I never stayed in a suite like this! this place is amazing and beautiful and so clean! The concierge was so helpful booking us things to do. I have a kulrig coffee pot and a fridge where I put a small hallf and half, the tv has an apple connection, and I'm typing this review from the sofa in my living room of our room on a wireless keyboard! all the things I have in my own home.. really I have NOTHING bad to say, and if you read any of my other reviews over the years, I can usually find SOMETHING to say! ok.. no ice machines...you have to call and they bring you a beautiful silver plated one filled with ice...is that bad? well my husband thought so.. he DOES always find something to complain about! lol 
Oh, and did I mention its 2 blocks or so from John hancock and the mag. mile!

title_masked: A good hotel with great amenities
text_masked:
I stayed here for one night on Thanksgiving Eve. This hotel has some great staff working here! The security guard on duty (Elroy) was even making sure I was having a good stay. The bartender made sure that all of my needs were met and the food here is really good! 
If you have access to the concierge lounge, it is one of the better ones I have been to. I am addicted to the latte machine at this place. The front desk staff was always accommodating and they were very knowledgeable of Marriott procedures. I will stay here again.
The parking lot is very confusing and I had to ask how to actually get back to the hotel. This parking lot is shared with other offices. Depending on times the elevators can be packed. One of the elevators was down for maintenance so I am sure that slowed some things down a bit. Overall I enjoyed every bit of this hotel. 
The only thing I can advise to travelers is the location. Even though this is listed as the Galleria area it is one of the hotels that is furthest from the mall. You will have to walk through a couple intersections if you are bold enough.

Recently had an event at the Westin Downtown in Denver for a group of about 190. We had a wonderful experience. The food was delicious and the service was even better. Had a great experience working with Kim S, our catering services manager. We used this hotel in 2009--and I was pleased to see that many of the staff members are still there! Must be a wonderful place to work... often hotels have a lot of turn over. Several others that made our visit spectacular were James T and Anthony. Appreciated all of their help!

title_masked: Best Hotel Experience I've ever had
text_masked: My stay was unbelievable, and excellent in every way. From the moment we stepped through the front door, we were treated so well. Andaz 5th Avenue is THE hotel to stay in while in NYC. You cannot beat the hospitality, views, modern and high tech rooms, and comfortable stay. Thanks to the Andaz team for such a great experience.

Stayed at this hotel in the past and it was always shabby. They have renovated it and the rooms are much nicer. Public spaces are better as well. Worth re-trying if you were disappointed in previous stays.

Stayed with a friend we had been to Graceland for her 50th Birthday treat. i stayed at this hotel 8yrs ago with my husband for my 50th Birthday, the hotel is lovely and very grand ! I love evrything about the hotel the beds are the most comfortable i have ever slept in. We made use of the swimming pool and hot tub.
My only compaint is that there are no tea making facilities in the room ( had i remembered i would have taken my travel kettle ! ) If you are english and like your tea do take your own tea bags as the tea at hotel is disgusting, we bought some tea bags and just got a cup of hot water from the Deli and made our own.
The hotel is ideally situated for a stroll to Beale street. we also took the Riverside Loop tram ride which was well worth the Dollar it cost.

I was visiting the VA hospital over on the westside, realized I needed a hotel and just looked online. This was so cheap I figured it'd be a dangerous rip...what a happy mistake! Its right off of downtown, the staff is friendly, and lots of young travelers and all friendly to me...yes, the rooms are a bit awkward...it's old! But yesterday morning while reading the LA times a guy sat at the piano and played a jazz tune...that is too damned cool for words...I'm hooked!

title_masked: Great stay, staff and location!!! Lovely property
text_masked:
Le Meridiem Parker combines classic elements and also modern desing and facilities. They have a fancy bar and a great burger place at the same enviroment. It's worthy to pay the fee for the pool, this is one of the greatest views you will have from the city and you can lay at the sun looking to the city and the Central Park.
Viviana and Stefanie from the Front Desk were so nice!! They were very friendly, smart and made me feel comfortable and definetely made my stay much enjoyable.
By the way, they are just few steps from Central Parl and some block from Times Square!!
I definetely recommend it.
Rodrigo Casanova

title_masked: Good location, would recommend to others!
text_masked:
We had reserved the rooms with the non-refundable rate which was pretty cheap for the room/ area. I don't think I would pay more for the room than what I did. It is right across from Union Station, a few blocks from the capitol building and slight walk from other attractions. We stayed for 4 nights and had it's ups and downs, but over all worth it. The construction next door woke us up promptly at 7am each morning. The staff was very friendly, although we were held back 2 hours our first day as I ordered a wheel chair for my grandmother that was sitting at the hotel, and even though I informed the staff, they were not aware it was there until we got a hold of the actual company who said they had delivered it at 9am (well before we checked in). 
The Dubliner restaurant associated with the hotel had great food and reasonable prices. The doorman was also great at getting us a taxi that was cheaper than when we hailed ones on the streets. We parked our car ourselves. The hotel charged $43 a night for valet parking where you can take your car in and out. We didn't use our car while we were there so we parked it around the block in Capitol Parking for $20 a night. I was told by a taxi driver this is the same lot they would valet park your car in anyway.
Note the rooms are small, the beds are pretty high up, my grandma used a step stool they provided, and the shower heads are pretty low. My husband, who is 5'8" had issues washing his face and hair. Also, I'm not sure how many rooms actually have a view of the street, but both our rooms, on different sides of the building, overlooked an alley. 
Overall, for the price we paid, I would consider staying here again and recommend it to others.

Stayed for 3 nights before touring New England...Only had a standard room but everything clean, smart and well thought out...Yes, the bathrooms are on the small size but nothing to complain about..Used the Pub downstairs for a drink and twice to eat late at night..food was really nice...above all else the staff at the hotel are all so friendly, never encountered anyone who didn't have a smile and a helping hand...first class.!! 
Had breakfast in the hotel only once...fine food but the price is typical big city price..plenty of restaurants nearby but not many open for breakfast...
Overall...Well done Lenox..!!

We stayed at this hotel for a one-night/one day visit to NYC. We chose the area as we wanted to be close to both Central Park and Times Square. This property was within walking distance of both locations. As I paid for the room through a bidding website, I was very pleased with the price I paid for the room/location. Well under posted rates. 
The property is older and the room size was what I would have expected in NYC...quite small but well appointed. Bed was very comfortable. We did not use any of the facilites or dining rooms at the hotel. 
Not much else to say...nothing fantastic and nothing terrible to say about this Sheraton...
If you found this review helpful, please let me know below! Thanks!

Stayed their super bowl weekend . $1980.00 
For 3 nights ... I somewhat understand with super bowl n all . What I can't understand is the hotel is a pig sty . My first room had a leak in bathroom ceiling with mold . We switched to anther room n it was a little better . TV in both room gets about 10 channels , no sports n is fuzzy . My room was never vacuumed in 3 days . Had 2 towels . Place should b shut down ... If your not getting paid to stay then your getting robbed . I'm not exaggerating ... I have been driven to write 2 reviews in my life n this is #2 . I don't want anyone to get duped like I did .

The location was excellent, central to both theaters and subway transportation. Hotel was quiet, clean, and the staff was friendly and quite helpful. Have been to NYC often, this was the best of all hotel e periences.

title_masked: Great help at a challenging time
text_masked: I needed a convenient hotel while my husband was in the hospital and The Inn at Longwood Medical certainly met that need. What I had not expected was the level of service, cleanliness and helpfulness I found. From the Front Desk staff to the management, I felt welcome and important. Even with a challenge with room keys, the staff was patient and extremely helpful. Everyone made this part of my stay easy and comfortable during a difficult time.

title_masked: Be careful where your room is located
text_masked:
Spent three night here while in town on business. The hotel was clean and comfortable, and the bedding was comfortable, the soap in all choice hotels lately reminds me of old type Lava soap.....it leaves a lot to be disired. The pillows at the chain are universally terrible, but you know and expect that at a choice hotel.
I was in a group of about 30 people who had 15 rooms. The hotel is tight up against an interstate and the folks who were lucky enough to get a room away from the interstate slept well, others were not as lucky. Breakfast was typical and the lady functioning as the breakfast hostess refused to acknowledg anyone or engage anyone.

Good value good location good parking older but renovated, go to hotel web site they also have other,s if this is not available, book in advance, do not eat at hotel go to 9th ave lots of choice, walking distance to time square
great hotel, came to town for the marathon,staff was friendly and helpful

We stayed here for the first time the other night, and we will absolutely be returning. The staff was warm, friendly, and genuinely seemed like nice people. This is a nice contrast to some of the other places I've stayed in SoHo. The neighborhood is great, and the hotel has a nice modern/industrial vibe that is still warm and inviting. One nice touch: the room had a working window. It was 60 degrees when we were there, and being able to open a window and let in some air was fantastic. I'm already looking into returning in the summer.

Because of its nightlife scene and general hipness, this hotel may have some appeal for some. I stayed for two nights in December on business, trying to keep costs down. I was on the 5th floor, no bar noise. However, the general noise of people in the hallway penetrated the room and made it difficult to sleep. Even as NYC hotels go, the room (on an alley side) was very small, with a small queen bed barely fitting. The bathroom was efficiently designed, but very small. Although I found nothing really gross, it was clear that maintenance was lacking. Unless they love each other very much and are rather small, I don't see how two people fit in this room.
Its midtown location is very good, and its an easy walk to 8th and 9th streets to find fun and moderately priced food. I gave it an average rating because the staff were very friendly and efficient.

Nice and clean,. Simple layout and reasonably priced. 
Decor is a little dated but the rooms have Comfortable beds and the location is handy to everything. 
Staff were very friendly and helpful. 
It is within walking distance of the Book Depository and we were able to leave our car there while we explored.

title_masked: There are lots of other choices if you want to sleep at night.
text_masked: I have previously stayed at The Benjamin because of it's convenience to the theater district, no cab necessary, a nice walk to the shows. And it is located close to shopping. A bit far from the Met but still walkable. But this visit convinced me to look elsewhere for a hotel. The employees were all friendly and helpful. The problems lies in the accommodations. The rooms are poorly decorated with boring beige older style heavy furniture. The carpets have dirty spots on them, and have not been spot cleaned so not enough attention to detail. The kitchen area in the suites had a dirty cup left in the clean cup area. The rooms are dim, not enough light. And if you stay in an exterior suite or a room facing Lexington Ave or 50th Street, you won't sleep all night. They kept saying that the windows are soundproofed but no one who works there has obviously tried to spend a night sleeping there. On the 6th floor you can hear laughter from the street below in the middle of the night as well as sirens, honking horns and construction noise. It was terrible. They changed our suite the next day to one on an interior facing area on the 14th floor and that one was quieter. The bathrooms are a big problem. They are tiny, one sink with very little space for toiletries. If you have the toilet seat lid up, something from the small area above it can easily fall into the toilet. The tub is small and incredibly slippery. BE WARNED--THERE ARE NO GRAB BARS IN THE TUB/SHOWER! Anyone of any age will have a terrible time getting in and out of the tub. The best lighting in the suite however was in the bathroom. But there isn't a vent in the bathroom so the room gets all steamed up. The National Restaurant downstairs is open for breakfast, lunch and dinner and was popular.

title_masked: An Oasis of Calm and Serenity in the Big City
text_masked:
Staff was extremely helpful and very courteous. I had a couple of issues that were resolved well but two things had not been resolved. I did not get a newspaper each day, and did not have any turndown service on the second night. I arrived for the CB at 9:30am only to find nothing left but yogurt. Second day the bagels were stale. In addition, turndown service did not include tidy up - garbage not removed, glasses not replaced. I did ask about the turndown service, but I recieved no response to my query. I did love the location, the room was fabulous and the people were terrific. Loved the rooftop terrace as an oasis of serenity! Could have been a little cleaner up there.....no garbage can provided so folks just left their garbage. I will consider the hotel again, as these issues are easily fixed and not a deal breaker for me --- a request was sent for my feedback and I am looking forward to see if these issues are resolved for the future. 
I would definately consider booking this hotel again, the rooms, while small, are well organized, comfortable and very clean. I had the neighbourhood corner and it was truly lovely! Well appointed, huge tv - lacking a lot of tv stations though for NYC. Nice electronic amenities, free bikes and skateboards although I am not one to take my life into my hands and bike around NYC!! Traffic is a disaster at all hours. The neighbourhood is very safe - I walked alone at 1 pm at night and did not feel uncomfortable. Serviced by many subway stops, tons of amazing restaurants - this property could not be more well located to see the heartbeat of NYC! 
A new addition is "Happy Hour" at 6 - 8 pm - I missed it on Staurday as I had to leave early for dinner and the theatre, and it is not available on Sundays. 
Check out the fabulous little organic wine shop across the street - don't miss the great eats and night life in the LES - try Stanton Social --- trendy but really good!

Went for a long weekend and selected this hotel based on other reviews and for it's proximity to the museums we planned to visit. On arrival were given a free upgrade to the top (39th) floor. The room had a beautiful view of St. Patrick's Cathedral and was spacious and clean. We loved the view at night and enjoyed happy hour each evening in our comfortable chairs facing the city lights. The room had robes, slippers, a safe, large flat screen and plenty of storage. Staff was wonderful- requests were filled quickly. The Frick and Met were within 20 blocks and easily walked if you wish. At the end of the day, the taxi home was about 10 dollars. We found a great deli - Oxford Cafe around the corner on Lexington. We would definitely stay again and recommend to our friends.

Stayed at the Radisson the night before an early morning flight out of LAX. They had the most reasonable price of the nearby hotels for the Park and Fly package for the night we needed. We had a nice dinner in their restaurant. The waiter, Felipe, was very helpful about explaining the sizes of the various meals and offering tips for a not too heavy dinner.
The room was clean, comfortable, and well-soundproofed. Not sure if we programmed the sleep-by number bed correctly since there are no instructions. It wasn't bad but I wouldn't buy one after sleeping on the one we did. 
 As mentioned in other reviews, the shuttle leaves the hotel every half-hour on the hour. That worked well. But they advise you that you now have to call the shuttle when you arrive at the airport and need a ride back to the hotel. We did that and then watched hotel shuttle after hotel shuttle drive by as we waited for the Radisson LAX shuttle to arrive. It finally did but they need to work on getting their shuttles to come by more often since it is frustrating after you've had a long day to see all the other hotel shuttles go by while you are waiting for theirs. The valets were quick to retrieve our car from the parking garage and gave good instructions for the best way to get back to the freeway.

I have stayed at this hotel 4 times. We stay here mainly for nights out in Broadripple. It is about a $15 cab ride from Broadripple, and the front desk will call the cab for you! The cab is always there within 10-15 minutes even on busy nights such as Halloween and New Years. Last time we got a coupon from the front desk for the cab company and got 15% off our ride! :) The staff is always very friendly, and the check in and check out process is easy. The rooms are clean! I have stayed in the studio rooms (1 bed, a pull out sofa, and a kitchen) and the double rooms (2 beds in seperate rooms with doors that shut and lock, a pull out sofa, and a kitchen) and they were both great, and worth the money! I love the kitchens. We have brought food to cook, you can bring drinks and they stay cold, or you can heat up leftovers after a night out! The hotel has always been quiet when we stayed here as well. The breakfast in the morning is pretty good. It isn't the most spectacular, and the lobby is small, but its decent. They have frozen waflles, bagles, muffins, danishes, fruit, cereal, and oatmeal. They also have a little snack bar that is there all the time that you can buy things from! The ONLY problem I have with this hotel is their pet policy, and even that isn't that bad. The last time we stayed here, we brought our dog with us because we didn't have anyone to watch him overnight. I was glad that the hotel accepted pets. I think that is great! However, it is a $50 non-refundable charge regardless of how long your pet will be staying. That is a GREAT deal if you're going to be there a week or longer. However, for just one night it is a little pricey. I know I could have probably boarded him for less, but we like to take him with us so we paid it. I just wish there was a better deal for 1 night. Maybe you could get your money back, or half of it if the dog didn't tear anything up. Or maybe it could just be a little cheaper? Other than that, no problems at all! Stay here if you're looking for a nice hotel that is close to everything, but feels tucked away and quiet!

I really enjoyed my stay at the Parc 55! The location is fantastic with many excellent restaurants, shopping and the convention center within a short walking distance. The hotel staff were friendly and very helpful! The only issues I had include one afternoon where it was almost 5 pm before my room was serviced, and the Wi-Fi signal in my room was weak and spotty.

Great location right on the Riverwalk. Nice, modern decor, but it's not cheezy or over done. Still has a warm feel to it both inside and out. Had dinner and breakfast at the hotel restaurant on-site, "Citrus". Both were very good. So were the drinks. Nice terrace to sit outside if the weather is right. There is a Starbuck's only one block away to boot! Staff was friendly and on point. We used the hotels spa service. Both my wife and I got an hour massage and they were great.
Only three things I didn't like, but weren't a huge deal: (1) The overall look and feel of the rooms are great, but the bathtubs have been forgotten. Don't get me wrong, they're look new and are fine, but the shower/tub area is plain and doesn't go with the rest of it... which calls out for some glass and/or stone or something... not a plain white tub with an entry level faucet. (the rest of the bathroom is nice though). (2) I couldn't valet park because I have a lifted truck that wont fit in the parking garage the valets use... so I had to park a couple blocks away on a pay lot. Not the end of the world, but kind of PITA for anyone who chooses not to valet for whatever reason. (3) No pool on site.
Regardless, we'll be back.

title_masked: Posh little hotel, Best for couples... but young families may wish to be near the National Mall
text_masked:
If my husband and I return to DC, we will stay at the Hotel George. With young kids, however, we will opt to be closer to the Mall. It is a bit of a distance and drive to get to the main areas, and this is a sweet little swanky hotel that caters to an upscale crowd on business. If you do bring kids here, you will still have a great time, but for convenience... its just easier to be closer to the tourist spots if you are squeezing in nap and snack times in your schedule.
The service was excellent. The front desk was extremely helpful. The valet/bell man was very cordial and efficient. The rooms were clean and comfortable. You MUST stop by Bistro Bis while here. No complaints... Hotel George is an excellent choice for business or a romantic weekend in the Capital.

I have stayed at this location on multiple occations and have always found it to meet my needs perfectly. Ideally located, clean and comfortable - this hotel is a good combination of quality and value. Most importantly, however, is the excellent service that I have received at this hotel. Both the front desk and hotel management went out of their way to accomodate a change I had to make in my reservation - even though it was my issue that required the change.
It is easy to see that the staff at this location truly care about their hotel guests. And at the end of the day - what more could you ask for?
I will definitely be back!

This was my first trip to NYC in forty years, and we wanted to be close to theaters but not too close to lots of noise and lights. This hotel was perfect. It is within easy walking distance to everything in the theater district as well as museums and shopping and the subway. The rooms were very nice, clean, and comfortable. The beds at Hampton Inn are always comfortable, and these were no exception. I also like for a room to be cool and dark for sleeping, which our room was. Except for one night, the hotel was also very quiet. Unfortunately, some young men decided to have a party in the room next to us one night, and the noise at 2:00 a.m. woke me up; however, I called the front desk and they sent security to the room, which took care of it. The only thing I would not recommend is the breakfast. We only ate the breakfast on the last day, and even though it's free, I have had better breakfasts at other Hampton Inns. Otherwise, I would highly recommend this hotel for a great place to stay in New York City.

I stayed at this hotel for 4 days/3 nights to attend a conference. Suffice it to say, I was happy when it came time to leave. There is no question that the hotel public areas are beautiful, providing opulence, elegance, and first-class presentation. However, that is where the impressiveness ends. My colleague and I both suffered similar experiences, experiences that are not consistent with the first-class expense and expectation associated with this hotel. First, when we arrived, one elevator door was broken, leaving only one elevator to serve one side of this immense hotel. It took three tries before there was enough room for us and our luggage to get on the car, as conference attendees were on and riding up from lower levels. Unfortunately, that became the problem throughout the stay: not enough elevator service to satisfactorily provide transport for the sheer number of people in the hotel. Getting on the elevator on its first pass was a rare joy - but not really a joy. The elevators, though regal because of wood paneling, are not well ventilated (which makes riding like a sardine with other passengers a less than pleasant experience), and are not well lit (rather than providing "mood lighting," they are just down-right dark). It became a joke among many passengers. If you are claustrophobic or actually are here for business and need to get somewhere within a reasonable period of time, these elevators make it an unwanted experience. Room service is a joke. While the food is excellent and the people who bring it are professional and pleasant, DO NOT order room service if you have anything planned for that day. It just never comes. I ordered ice cream and coffee at 10:30 pm one evening, was promised it would be up in 10-15 minutes, and it arrived 1 hour and 20 minutes later! The same level of (slow) service was afforded on all other room service orders I made (one lunch, one dinner, and one breakfast)- they never arrive when promised, consistently take well more than an hour to arrive (even during non-peak dining hours), and make it absolutely impossible to be able to eat and still have enough time to get to whatever meetings you have planned. Other things happened, too, that, though little, were problems that should not be had in a first-class establishment: one lamp knob was broken, forcing me to have to use one of my make-up appliances to turn it so I could turn it on, the batteries in my TV remote were nearly dead (I got up to change the channel or turn on/off the TV each time), and the iron was cheap and small and dribbled water constantly (ruined a shirt). If you come here for business, bring your own iron - while mine did not work well, my colleague's iron had uncontrollable heat settings (again, cheap irons), resulting in her burning (and ruining) one of her suits. While at the conference, we also were in need of help with something associated with the conference. The manager (?banquet manager?) said he would look into it, thought he may not be able to help, but would be back and definitely would let us know either way - he never returned. The bellmen and doormen are variably helpful - some are absolutely delightful, others hate their jobs and the people they are serving. The host ignored me and my business compatriates on two occasions, making us stand and wait to be seated without even acknowledging our presence (in a near empty restaurant for about 5-10 minutes each time). I do want to add, though, that, once seated, the wait staff themselves in the restaurant are excellent (must give credit where credit is due!). The front desk staff is excellent as well, being attentive, friendly, and impeccably professional. But, the elevators, the always late room service, the broken lamp and dead remote, the disinterested management level individual, the (often) unhelpful bell/door men, and the various other little things (all too numerous to mention - again, it all adds up after awhile) bespeak a hotel that may look grand, but definitely is not. If you want to see the best part of the hotel (foyer, restaurant, ballrooms), then walk in the front door and look around. Then, turn around and stay somewhere else - there are plenty of other hotels in the area with better amenities and service, many of which that will also, despite their superior offerings, actually cost less, too! It was disappointing.

I booked a one night stay for my 25th birthday night and I can not say anything horrible about the hotel. The location is superb and has easy access to the subway to get downtown. When we checked in the woman at the desk made sure that we felt comfortable and when we asked for a room with a view she gave us one. The rooms and hotel smelled wonderful and the rooms were beautifully decorated. The one complaint is the elevators were quite busy and sometimes had to wait a little for them but that wasnt really a big deal for my group. It was an amazing stay and I would definitely stay here again. The woman at the desk also offered us late check out since she knew we were going to be up late which I thought was really nice.

I was in San Diego with some friends running the half marathon and stayed here. It was a beautiful property with great amenities. What really stood out was the service, especially from Nate who was our bartender one night and our bell hop the next. He was super friendly and attentive without being over bearing and was sure to fill all of our needs. My friends and I had actually been having a conversation about how service levels have slipped below par at most places, but Nate gave us hope again!!

I was on a business trip to different cities in August. Hotels in Charlotte were very busy due to the Democrats convention. Sugar creek is not the best area in Charlotte, but I thought to give a try to Days Inn hotel. Unexpectedly, the hotel is very well maintained, nice lobby, clean room with comfy matress. Breakfast was great and the staff was very caring

We stayed at the Hyatt House for a long weekend getaway from Phoenix. My husband and I checked in on a Sunday and out on a Wednesday. I was very pleased with this hotel. I did get a deal thru Priceline so it was very reasonable and free parking and breakfast made it even better! The check in process was quick and easy and the gal at the front desk was very friendly. Checking out was the same except it was a young man instead and he was very pleasant as well. The breakfast was different every morning and they leave a schedule in your room telling you what they will be serving each day. They were even making omelets to order one morning. It was very good and there is a nice outdoor area that you can eat breakfast at, as well as the restaurant area inside. The pool was small and in the center of the hotel so very shady for the most part. My only complaint (and it’s not a big deal) would be that they should have the bar inside the restaurant open during the day. So if you want some drinks while out by the pool there is a place to get them. I guess they are open for breakfast and not again until 5pm. It was within reasonable driving distance to most things in San Diego/LaJolla area. I would say it took us about 15 min to drive to downtown LaJolla.

I stayed in this hotel for a week from 26th of April 2012. I loved the location. Just in the center of the shopping streets Mignificent Mile, Oak street, Rush street etc with many high fashionable shops and good restos. The Hankook tower just the next building to the hotel, with fantastic view. It is 5-7 minutes driving to Millenium Park. Apart from this, they lack a bit customer care service. The bellman was not there to help with the luggage when I was chcking off. It was pity that I couldn't indicate the hotel address for online shopping. The lady at the reception said that it is not allowed and she can not help me. Overall I recommend this hotel whether you are on a business trip or considering vacations. P.S. The italian resto downstairs is awesome

2nd year in a row staying here. Finished the race and were almost late for 11 check- out, but the desk staff was nice & accomodating and gave us some extra time with no problem. 
The staff is wonderful and the location great for a lot of activities close to the lake.
The hotel is old, but quaint & very clean. Beds are comfy.
There are also many good restaurants within walking distance.

title_masked: Very disappointed from check-in to check-out
text_masked:
We have stayed at Embassy Suites in other cities and have always been very happy, so when planning a trip to visit family in Philly, we decided to try this Embassy Suites. I have also never written a negative review, but felt that our experience warranted it. When we arrived, the two double beds that I had reserved were not available and we three adults were placed in a King room. My daughter slept on the sleep sofa, which is probably fine for children, but was very uncomfortable for her, resulting in complaints of back pain throughout the trip. 
The room itself was fairly clean, but lots of candy wrappers under the sleep sofa, plaster bits around on the rug in both rooms, and some kind of splatter on the walls and lampshade of the main sitting room. I discovered that the plaster was from series of large patches on the wall of the bedroom. That was the view from the bed. The lampshade next to the patched wall also had been crushed. Little things, but felt like I was in a slum. 
 Although we had reserved and paid for three adults, the room was set up for two so we had to seek out glasses and towels each day. The breakfast hosts on all mornings were short tempered (and appeared to be overworked.) The buffet itself could have been ok, but the kitchen obviously had difficulty keeping up with the demand. We waited about 45 minutes for just some oatmeal one morning, and finally gave up and left to buy breakfast elsewhere. There was plenty of bread for toast, cold cereal, muffins, but hard to get healthier options like bagels, fresh fruit, or hot cereal. Coffee ran out 3/3 mornings also. On the mornings that we had a little extra time, we waited but were still not able to get our simple preferences. On the morning that we had to be out by a designated time, we settled for dry cereal and toast. 
The hotel was very busy and the staff was generally courteous, although if we mentioned any of our concerns, the response was " We have a large group here today." Evidently it was so busy that we often waited 10 to 15 minutes for an elevator up and a couple of times chose to walk down rather than wait. Additionally, the air conditioner/heat unit was incredibly loud, so we had to turn it on for a while, shut it off to sleep, wake up hot, turn it on to cool, then off to sleep. At check out, we were charged for an extra night of parking and after waiting for breakfast, found it irritating to have to wait to resolve the overcharge. We did stop a the manager's reception one night where they served unlimited drinks, potato chips and bags of chex mix. It was nice, although a couple of free drinks and chips certainly does not make up for the inconveniences. The only saving grace for us for this facility was that the location is very good.

title_masked: Old world charm overlooking the White House
text_masked:
The Hay Adams has an old world charm to it. Attentive and generous in its service, we were blessed with a room overlooking the White House.
The room was small but enough for 2 nights. The bathroom could do with a little modernisation as it was a tight fit for 2 to move in at the same time.
There is obviously a lot of history associated with this hotel. It's not a hotel for everyone, but if you like the charm of yesteryear with modern service you will enjoy it.
We ate in the hotel restaurant 2 nights and it was both affordable with quality service and food.

I am currently checked into the Doubletree Denver. I must admit...when I first pulled up I wasn't sure. I had checked the TripAdvisor comments and that was what encouraged me to keep going. As SOON as I walked in I was warmly greeted by an incredible staff. My front desk check in could not have been more welcoming. This location seems to be a VERY genuinely happy place to work. I even rode the elevator up with a staff person delivering room service and she was almost singing... :)
I agree. The property is absolutely older but well maintained. The hallways are very dimly lit. And the linens have certainly run their course. However, the rooms are adequate. I am on business travel and know that I can always count on Doubletree for consistency. I am not disappointed in that regard.
I also agree the restaurant is a bit pricey...but no worries. There is certainly food within an 8 minute radius.

title_masked: Luxury hotel, Great Location and Quiet
text_masked:
The hotel has a simple Japanese elegance with beautiful flower arrangements throughout the common spaces in the hotel. We arrived in the early morning and had asked for an early check in and the staff had a room ready for us at 9 am no waiting just a pleasant greeting and "we have been expecting you". 
The location is within walking distance of all things in midtown, Grand Central 2 blocks away, Rockefeller Center a 10 minute walk. The rooms are large for NYC standards, nice size bathroom and closet area. The hotel is Japanese, so no coffee in the room but there is a teapot and tea. There is not an iron or ironing board in the room but one was brought within 5 minutes of calling the front desk.
The most astounding thing I can say about this hotel is how quiet it is. We saw people all over the hotel but when you are in your room you can not hear any street noise, hallway noise, people talking or doors closing. I asked the front desk and they said they had soundproofing to create a peaceful experience and they get 5 stars for that!!! Great experience and will stay there next time I go to NYC.

We stayed two nights at the Palomar. The facility is typical Kimpton offbeat chic with the only drawback the relative smallness of the room. The service and attitude of the staff is what really sets this property apart. Everyone is exceptionally friendly and helpful and are adept at graciousness. The location is very good and near all the attractions and many of the better restaurants. The staff here make this one of the better places we have stayedand an excellent choice for Philadelphia.

Got married at Gracelands and so decided to book 4 rooms for the family and guests. The location of Beale Street is EXACTLY where it is, with all the noise that goes with it! I had a room with a balcony on a corner which faced slightly away from Beale but the music plays until 2-4 Am so you get to hear it all. Others had rooms facing away from Beale and only just heard the music.
All of the staff were extremely helpful and could not do enough for us when we asked for anything. Ringing cabs, giving extra room items, special orders for breakfast (which was always yummy), advice on destinations and tourist spots........so very helpful.
Little extras, like having tea, coffee and biscuits available in the lounge all night as well as an on-site small convinence room made the stay great. A bottle of champagne in my room on the wedding night was much appreciated too. 
Thanks Hampton Inn, we will always treasure our stay and promote you guys whenever anyone asks.

title_masked: Good room, above average gym, opening hours gym a bit short
text_masked:
Stayed here for three days. Room is good, with good desk, free Internet, very good bathroom and in the middle of the old town. Old city coffee one block away, and close to the historical buildings.
Gym has enough machines and they're in good shape. There's also a pool, but did not use it.
Only downside for me, traveling for business and jet lagged, was that the gym opens first at 6 AM on weekdays and 8 AM (!!) on Saturdays. Also closes relatively early at 8 pm. That's just way too late for opening and too early for closing if you have to work.

title_masked: Fantastic Service! The Most Comfortable Beds EVER!!
text_masked: I am a Production Manager for a major network television show. I housed about 30 crew and cast in the Eventi for about 3 weeks while shooting in NYC. We also set up our production and technical offices there as well. Before stepping foot in the Eventi, I was nervous that, because they are very upscale, my crew would feel out of place or would somehow be treated less than kindly because we were constantly hauling gear thru their exquisite lobby. My negative preconception couldn't have been further from the truth. From the moment we arrived, we were treated like family. It only took only a day or so before most of the staff knew us by our first names. The rooms were immaculate and the beds were super comfy. Almost everyone on my crew mentioned to me at one point or another how they were going to invest in down bedding once they get home because they've never slept this well in there lives. The location was great too. But the real key to this hotel's success is the management team's desire to please their guests. There positive attitude and friendly demeanor is reflected well in their fantastic staff. If you are a production shooting in NYC, I highly recommend checking out the Eventi. Underground garage parking for your production minivans is a big plus too. Very reasonably priced monthly passes that give you in and out privileges. For those of you in production, you know how important this is.

title_masked: Pretty good hotel, but check your bill carefully
text_masked:
This is a fairly nice motel-type place. The room was reasonably large, and reasonably clean. Parking lot was small. Location is nothing exceptional -- despite the name it is not really near the Convention Center. Free Wifi worked well. When I arrived I was warned the aircon was not working in my room, which was not a problem in early January. (My room was quiet, even when I opened the window to take advantage of the cool evening air.)
But the customer service.....ooooooo! On checkout I was presented with a bill about $80 over what was confirmed on my online reservation. When I informed the front desk staff of the error, they looked up the reservation, hemmed and hawed, and said I had to present them with a printed copy of my confirmation. I SHOWED them the confirmation email on my computer, but they demanded a printed copy before they would honor the quoted rate. I then had to go to their business center, log in by webmail, and print off a copy of the confirmation -- all to get the rate that the company had promised me. So in essence, THEY made a mistake and made ME spend a half an hour to clear it up. Not acceptable.
the room was missing toilet paper, bath towels, many of the lights did not work, the trim was falling off of the walls, etc.

title_masked: Many positive aspects, but looking a bit tired now
text_masked: This was my second stay at the Pod and among its many positive elements are its location - it's easy to get to pretty much any part of Manhattan, the customer service ethos among its excellent people and the value you get for your money. However, the place is beginning to look a little tired and would benefit hugely from even a minor spruce up. The one thing to remember is that it is designed to be a place to sleep - a base while you're seeing NY. It isn't a boutique spa hotel, the rooms aren't terribly relaxing and it is, quite rightly, a question of function over form, to one degree or another. The rooms are small, but the name rather gives that away, does it not? Overall, it's a great place to base yourself while exploring NY, but it's never going to be a W or a Sofitel. So do your research, if you're looking for a convenient, clean, easy-going place to stay while you're getting the most out of an extraordinary city, you won't go far wrong with the Pod.

We stayed here for the San Francisco Marathon events, everyone was so helpful and accommodating! Everything we asked for was taken care of! The room was clean, comfortable and relaxing. 
If the concierge was a little better, would have gone with 5 stars.

title_masked: "Gem" Hotel? I say not: Worst Hotel Ever
text_masked:
This is by far the worst hotel I have seen in NYC. I had a reservation at the Gem - Midtown West property. Walking up to the front door, they had multiple trash bags on the curb along with old rolled up carpet. Not a good first impression. 
Checking in, the room they gave me was literally in the basement – as in you go to the elevator, hit the “B” button, and you go down. In the basement they have only one hotel room. To get to the room you have to walk past all the cleaning supplies, staff changing area, staff break room, and a shower facility (I’m assuming the shower was for staff, but I did not dare ask the real purpose). The basement room window provided a view of the staff smoking area.
The room was so small a two foot midget would have been claustrophobic sleeping there. Literally I could not pull out the chair from under the desk because it hit the bed. Standing in the room / cube, I heard a dripping sound. I looked up at the ceiling above the bed and noticed a long brown strip caused by water damage from above – this solved the mystery of why the carpet was out on the curb. At this point I knew that my presence in that room would be short lived.
I picked up the phone in the room to call the front desk to ask if they had a different room but the phone did not work. I took the elevator from the basement back up to the reception area to beg for a different room – no luck. On the verge of panic, I started weighing my options: 1) sleep standing up, fully clothed in the basement room, 2) find a bench in Central Park, or 3) locate a bar that is open 24 hours and tie one on. Since I cannot sleep standing up, option 1 was out. I went back to the room, got my suitcase. Walking through the lobby, the receptionist (who was a nice guy) even admitted it gets “a little scary” down there in the basement. With a strong shiver going down my spine, I bid him and the hotel a good day and walked out the front door.
By the grace of God a friend of mine was able to call in a favor and got me a room at a different hotel. The benches in Central Park and the hangover caused by a 24 hour drinking binge will have to wait for the next person sleeping in the basement of the Gem Hotel.

title_masked: Some rooms are small if on govt rate
text_masked:
We stayed for 10 days at the government rate (which is not cheap) before moving overseas and they gave us an itty bitty room. Luckily we are not giant people, but with all of our bags it was a challenge.
Otherwise - hotel was nice, stayed cool even in a DC heatwave and had good wifi / TV channel selection - very central.

title_masked: Average hotel, but very good location
text_masked:
Many others have said it before and I wish I had taken a little more time to read the reviews rather than just going off the overall rating. One person here said that it was hotel pricing for motel quality (nail on the head); another said that there were stains and dated furnishings such as carpets and curtains (very true, some even had holes in them); and someone here even mentioned they were given early check-in free of charge - yes, we also got that as well. There were no bugs, thank goodness; there was no way of adjusting the temperature in the room; our shower/tub combination consisted of a window ledge inward (so water collected onto it and stagnant) and bad water pressure. Interesting view, as we had a corner on the 10th floor... that looked straight into another room on the opposite corner (you can probably see our room in many of the exterior photos). Another thing that irked me was the elevators closest to us were not available for usage for the public - there were three of them, yet they were all for staff... AND, somehow, being eight rooms away in the hallway, I could hear someone blow-drying their hair as if I was standing right next to them.
Location is great; employees are helpful and quite cheerful, especially the bell-hop/valet guy that chatted us up and kept complaining about his own valet group to us/other customers, making it an interesting wait; and again, free-of-charge early check-in. Overall....average.

This hotel is stylish and practical. I had an excellent stay, and look forward to returning. From the hotel I walked to Second City comedy club, the Lincoln Park Zoo, and the Chicago History Museum. My room had a view of Lake Michigan. Top reasons to return: the rooftop bar, and bicycle rentals.

If there is one thing fab about this hotel then it must be its location. Connected to the Hynes Convention Centre and the various retail / commercial buildings that make up the Copley Place, this hotel has easy access to whatever you want in terms of shopping and dining options. 
Newbury street known for its chic shops and eateries is not too far. In fact nothing is too far away including 2 subway stations. 
The rooms are ordinary by my standards and the bathrooms OK to meet a 3 star rating. But the huge lobby is a great hang out space especially with an in house Starbucks outlet and free wifi. 
It does not pretend to be anything more than a property that sees a very high check-in check-out on a daily basis on account of the market it services. The housekeeping and other services gave me no reason for complain.

title_masked: Real good for a motel on the highway
text_masked: The staff we're really friendly on arrival even though we were just staying there a night and basically passing through. The rooms were huge which is always nice after you've been travelling for a while. There was lots of parking available, both under cover and open and a nice pool. For me the nicest part was the sleep quality, which was surprisingly good given you're right on the highway. I would suggest that you'd need a car to get around from there though.
The hotel was very nice, However, it is located in a dodgy part of the city, If I was going back again I would choose a hotel closer to fisherman's Wharf maybe!

title_masked: A little tired - but great staff!
text_masked: An older Hampton Inn but not too bad and conveniently located to business and shops. The pros: The woman who checked me in was very pleasant, cheery, and helpful! The breakfast was the usual Hampton fare, but prepared well - and the woman setting it up was also quite cheerful at 6 AM ! The cons: It took forever to get the TV working with this new DISH set up - I had to go re-program the channels. The walls are paper thin and I had to listen to my neighbors loud TV and conversations next door well into the night (which is why I always carry ear plugs).

title_masked: Enjoying staying in the Magnolia. Thought the breakfast was a lovely surprise. I would definitely stay there again.
text_masked: Thought the Magnolia was an attractive Hotel. Love the location, downtown. Thought the room was very clean. Really enjoyed the breakfast that came with our room at no extra charge.

This is one of the most sparkling clean and modern Courtyards I have stayed in. The rooms are larger than typical with great amenities. Large pool, huge hot tub, small excercise room, full breakfast, lobby bar, and a well stocked Market combined with an efficient and friendly staff made our 4 night stay pleasurable and comfortable. We had two rooms and they were equally immaculate.I recommend this hotel to anyone visiting Jacksonville.

We saw a great deal through SniqueAway and decided to take advantage of it. We went with a King Premier room. This is a beautiful boutique hotel, very close to Times Square. The bell staff and front desk staff were extremely friendly and accommodating. This is a pet-friendly hotel, and there were a couple of nice doggies asleep behind the front desk. In addition, there was a "welcome" bowl of dog food in the front entryway, awaiting some canine guests who were due to arrive. Our room was gorgeous - exactly as pictured on their website, and quite large for a hotel room in New York City. The furnishings are modern, everything very clean, the king bed nice and comfy. The shower was powerful! Really powerful! They had free WiFi in the room, which was a nice plus. There was also the all-important safe for storing valuables that we didn't want to take with us. The only thing missing was a coffee maker, but we requested one, and had one brought to our room within minutes. The hotel location was excellent - just a minute's walk to Times Square. And 2 blocks down W. 46th Street is "Restaurant Row," a wonderful area with a vast variety of restaurants. All in all, a lovely hotel in a great area. Highly recommended.

We were a family of four travelling for medical reasons. Poor sleep was due to a large group of college students who partied from room to room for hours 2 nights in a row. We had difficulty contacting the front desk regarding the problem. However after mentioning it while filling out Quality's survey the manager promptly apologized and refunded part of our stay; which was outstanding customer service. Breakfast was excellent, rooms were clean and they provided a free shuttle to the hospital for us. Easy walk to space needle and then take monorail into town or walk a short distance to catch a bus in the free ride zone. Would definitely stay again.

title_masked: A Clean Room With An Amazing View
text_masked:
After a long flight from Dublin to San Francisco (via Paris), the need for a clean, quiet room of one's own is paramount and this is exactly what I found at the Dakota Hotel on a recent visit. It had all of the Olde World charms of a San Franciscan hostelry with none of the disappointments often to be found in such places. 
I slept like a baby during my stay and woke early each morning to a magnificent view of the city and a powerful, hot shower. The staff were always on hand to help me and a first-time visitor to the city - which I wasn't - would be provided with even more assistance and suggestions. Not only that but the hotel offers entertainment every evening from music to cheese and wine tastings. 
I adored it there and was heartbroken to leave. Finding good accommodation in Downtown SF can be a tricky affair. The only reservation I'd have in recommending The Dakota Hotel, is that my room will be gone the next time (soon, I hope) I pay a visit.

I stayed in this hotel last week and had a great experience. This is the first time i stayed there since the rooms were upgraded. Not only was the staff extremely professional and kind but the overall experience was more than i expected. I would recommend this hotel to any traveler especially those on a budget and who travel with family. It is centrally located and close to pretty much everything you need and want to see. The rooms are new and the beds are extremely comfortable. Some of these posts I disagree with wholeheartedly.
