I have stayed at many DC hotels throughout the year and the rooms, the cleanliness and service at this hotel rivals all others.

We wanted to stay downtown because we thought it would be easier for us to get around if we were there, but couldn't find a place at the time for less that $180 so we opted for this. We were a little concerned because it is out, but didn't need to be. The room was actually a suite with a little sitting area which we would not have had downtown and the location was great. Access to downtown was very easy and parking downtown was not a problem. Good location to consider to cut your lodgingcosts. Many restuarants in the area. The breakfast area is very small and had to navigate. parking at the motel is free.

title_masked: Serves it's Purpose...and that's a compliment.
text_masked:
I have stayed at this airport hotel a number of times, mainly because my office is literally across the street. So I just get the airport shuttle service and walk to work when working in Phoenix, and don't need to rent a car. I've always enjoyed my stays at the hotel; it's a holiday inn express and nothing fancy, but the staff is always friendly and great and it just provides you everything you really need when staying at an airport hotel. Some notes:
-Free WIFI (although if you stay in rooms at the end of the hallways you will get a really weak signal and will probably need to use the wired option)
-Elevator (only one in the place and it takes forever; I would request a room on the 1st floor or 2nd, as there are stairs in the main lobby to take you right up there. Avoid the elevator)
-Free breakfast and a happy hour every evening during the week if you are a member of the hotel rewards program (they give you 2 cards for 2 free drinks, I believe)
-Free parking
-Not much to eat in walking distance (the Hilton next door has a restaurant which is decent and this is what provides the holiday inn room service; there is a waffle house in front of the hotel, but it houses possibly the greasiest food I've ever eaten....that's about all your options within walking distance).
-Good TVs with a bunch of channels offered.
-Free Shuttle Airport Service (the drivers are really friendly; leaving the hotel is every 30 mins and I've always had good luck with that. But picking you up at the airport is a different story - they usually take forever! You have to call them to pick you up, so I recommend doing it while waiting for your bag or when you get off the plane if you just have a carry-on.)
Overall, cheap rates for large rooms. You get great service and a lot of free features as well. I'd recommend it if you stay in the Phoenix airport area.
hotel was just nasty an not clean at all smell like an old furneral home staff rude an not helpful at all

Stayed here for 3 nights on a business trip and enjoyed the stay, the staff was very friendly and helpful. I especially enjoyed the Managers reception on Wednesday night and playing Wii bowling with Manager Alex Settlemire. He had arranged food and refreshments for the event and it was a fun way to spend our last night at the hotel. Extremely clean room and have recommended to my co-workers to stay here when we're in the area.

title_masked: Franklin P "Nice room and courteous staff"
text_masked: I stayed at this hotel with my wife so we have a date night. The hotel is located within walking distance to the entire theatre district and most shops. when I checked in it was done efficiently and quickly. One employee Bill Persaud helped out tremendously and went above and beyond his duties and helped me out. I would stay here again!

This was a fairly decent property, we ended up with the room on the main floor directly beside the public toilets, the room was clean the bathroom fan made a ton of noise and the room air conditioner did not work as well as it should have to keep the room at a comfortable temp for over night sleeping especially for those of us from Canada. 
Breakfast was not bad a nice selection of items, and the toaster even worked.
We enjoyed an hour in the hotel pool,just before dark, it was very pleasant; We did not try the hot tub.. there was no need.
Biggest negative was asking at the front desk for suggestions of things to do and being told that they had no idea really of things to do in Austin, managment would do well to keep a list with some of the attractions at the front desk, The next day we encountered a triathlon blocking most of the downtown area. Finding our way around was a tad challenging but made our way over to the Long horn stadium, found gourdough ,so those would be some suggestions for out of towners...

I stayed at this hotel at the for one night at end of October (just before Sandy). My room was unclean-- hairs in the tub (!)-- unknown splotches on the wall and bits of stuff on the floor. The bathroom was also poorly laid out for non-obvious space saving constraints, e.g., the toilet handle was underneath the sink and very hard to reach-- but the main bedroom was big. My room was also cold-- they only had the air conditioner running throughout the hotel even though legally they had been required to turn over to heat two weeks previously. The plus side was that when I complained upon checkout the staff were very nice and commiserated with me, and took a bit off my bill for my troubles. I ordered room service for both dinner and breakfast and the staff who brought it to me were also very friendly.

the room was nice, not what expected, but when having to attend a conference being able to stay in the same hotel is a plus. The bed was very comfortable, the bathroom nice with normal items provided. There were 2 robes provided in the room for those that like that amenity. We did not eat any meals in the restaurant, and after our one lunch that was provided with the conference, I'm very glad that we didn't. The food served for our luncheon was terrible.
There is a Starbuck's in the hotel and they have very good breakfast sandwich's. 
We stopped by the bar one evening and our drinks were terrible. The service was very lacking and this is not a place I would ever recommend to anyone.
We did spend most of our off time in the West end section where there are some very good restaurants. This is probably a convention/ seminar/ conference hotel.
we did travel for business, and felt this hotel was a bit sub par for the prices

I second the nice staff reviews - they are great. The location is excellent as well. 
The hotel itself is good but dated and in need of a renovation. It's not as nice as the other Kimpton properties I've stayed at. My room was on the small side (reminded me of hotel rooms in New York), but for the price I got, it was reasonable.

I missed my flight so I stayed 01 overnight. Very kind driver for the shuttle airport-hotel and v.v. Very quick, professional and polite person at the check in, internet access code was provided without even asking for it, room was very clean, very comfortable bed. Noise from the aircrafts was acceptable. Breakfast next morning - a pleasant surprise! Will definitely stay there again!

Extremely dissapointing. Room was dirty, toilet was leaking when we arrived, hair in the shower and a used razor. The sheets felt like some sort of latex mixture.. not soft at all. Woke around 2am to shouting in the hallway. The service was good but the hotel was a huge dissapointment. Location great.

The hotel still has the new smell. The room was quiet, large, clean, and comfortable. Good work area. Near the airport with a shuttle. The entire hotel was very clean. Just regular breakfast items.
Easy check-in and out. Great value for the price of the room.

title_masked: Great location, really nice but noisy
text_masked: I stayed at Affinia Manhattan in 2008 before it got renovated. At that time, I thought it was a really good hotel for its location. I just got back from another trip in NYC and I must say that the renovations really makes it like a brand new hotel. Don't get me wrong: they didn't rebuilt it. It's still a little noisy on the lower floors. So if there's any availability on the higher floors, do not hesitate. The location is perfect: close to Times Square, the subway and both NJ Transit and Amtrak stations are across the street.

title_masked: Made for a great start to our vacation
text_masked:
After a lot of delibration while planning our first hotel for our 3 week vacation in California, we opted for the Parc 55 for location, reviews and the reasonable rates. We were not disappointed on arrival. As a family of 4 (two adults and 10 and 12 year old boys) we needed a room with two doubles minimum and also chose the club rooms which was an excellent chose, as they are on the higher floors with great views and also this gives access to the Club lounge on the 31st Floor with a superb complimentary continental style breakfast (the Granola is made for the hotel specaily and is the best i have tasted) and also evening snacks and an honesty bar 
 (The meatballs were great). The club lounge can get a little crowded for breakfast, but you just have to pick your times. The hotel room was clean, roomy enough for our family with a good size bathroom.
 Another tip is to join the Wyndham Loyalty scheme which gives free WiFi in. We used an iPad and the speed was very good
The hotel is a short walk from Union Sq, Westfield Shopping Centre, trolley bus terminus. Its a great location to explore central SF, shopping and as a general base to do the SF sights. Far better as a base than Fishermans Wharf, in our opinion.
We did read the comments on the homeless, etc, but this is all over SF and at no time did not we feel threatened - You just have to be sensible and keep your wits about you as most other big cities.
Overall we had a great experience at this hotel and have already recommended to family who are planning a trip to America next year

title_masked: Great location; smaller more intimate hotel
text_masked: I really enjoyed staying downtown at this particular Hilton. The staff was exceptional, the restaurant food very good and lots of nice restaurants and sights to see within walking distance including a large mall with Macys. Parking is a bit steep - I think $38 per day but everyone is steep. Hilton still has the best beds and pillows in my POV.

Had an excellent stay at holiday inn express at 5th avenue staff very helpful, rooms very clean & tidy breakfast was very good, location perfect ,hard to say anything negative the only one drawback was that it states in the room description that there is a safe there is no safe in the room & when we asked for a safety deposit box the staff said there wasn't one available but they would notify us when one became available, we did not get a safety deposit box for our entire stay & had carry our passport & valuable items etc. with us at all times which made us quite wary especially in a city like New York it may be something the management should look at.
 as a regular traveler it is something i look for when i am booking any hotel.
however it did not spoil my stay very pleased with the hotel would definately return & recommend to friends.

title_masked: Austin lacking in service, breakfast and location
text_masked: This motel is new and the rooms are big and comfortable. However, the staff seems really incompetent and rude. The breakfast service was awful, you had to ask for everything and still the waffle machine was out of service every time, there were no bagels and the juices and the coffee were extremely diluted. It was a short ride to Austin downtown, where there is not that much to see or to do. Skip this place. Best Western, how about an Audit about this place?

title_masked: Good price, good location, quiet, clean
text_masked: I stayed in a triple room (double and single bed) on the 7th floor for $160 night. The hotel was a very cool, funky old Victorian. It was completely clean. The beds were comfortable. We never had to wait for a bathroom. The floor space in the room was TIGHT. The street was very quiet - we never heard traffic noise. The Gramercy Cafe is the corner of 17th and 3rd - great place for a cheap breakfast! About five blocks from Union Square with lots of budget eating options.

title_masked: Marriott Marquis in Times Square is convenient and quiet
text_masked: I stayed on the 17th floor facing Times Square. Great views of the new years eve ball and Good Morning America show each morning. Location is right on Times Square and very convenient to the subway yet the hotel is really quiet. Beware though, the room service prices are astronomically high. I know room service is pricey but $21 for a waffle (just a waffle) is just exorbitant, even for room service.

Stayed here recently -the hotel was booked to full capacity. I called housekeeping for extra towels and the housekeeping staff member arrived at my door in less than 5 minutes. Also, there was a problem with the temperature in the room and I called the front desk to notify them of the issue and a facilities staff member was at my door less than 15 minutes later. I could not believe it. Every hotel staff member that I encountered: front desk, concierge, bellhop, and housekeeping- each person was friendly, and helpful. I used to stay at another nearby hotel each year, but I will only stay at this hotel from now on. It is clean, and well-staffed and maintained. Beds comfy.

Stayed for three nights while work was being done on my nearby condo. Excellent North Michigan Ave. location. Comfortable beds with quality linens and duvet, excellent A/C small bathrooms with shower in tub. If you don't plan on spending anytime in your room other than sleep this older, non chain hotel is for you. Very friendly staff, and while elevators are small there never seems to be much of a wait, quiet hallways and no street noise in our queen room. Good prices are available on line. It is old but clean and was very well done. If you like a room that is a bit quirky rather than cookie cutter these rooms are for you. Had room service for breakfast one morning outrageously priced and not that good. Local breakfast spots, Pancake House and Tempo are much better value and a whole lot tastier.

title_masked: super fun at an ultra hip hotel
text_masked: I came out for a work thing and got to stay at the Blu Aqua Chicago. We had so much fun we almost for got we were working! The hotel is beautiful, the service amazing, and food/ wine phenomenal, I can't say enough good things!

We were looking for a good Washington DC hotel and couldn't be happier with our decision to stay at the State Plaza. The price was very good and the room was huge, newly renovated and the bathroom was absolutely beautiful. We've stayed in many "suite" hotels with less room and it was very nice to be able to spread out and be comfortable getting ready for our many excursions. The location of the hotel was also great. Just a few blocks from the Washington Mall, we walked to many of the monuments and several of the Smithsonian Museums. The staff at the State Plaza also helped us get discounted tickets to the Kennedy Center and we were able to have a very pleasant walk to the show.

The XV Beacon is a perfectly located, very comfortable and beautifully designed boutique hotel. 
Staff is competent and polite, but unenthusiastic, which I was told is just the Boston way. As an European it was actually refreshing to stay in a US hotel where the staff doesn't jump at you constantly with smiles and greetings. 
The lobby is quite small, but very nicely appointed. The elevators are old, a bit noisy and slow. I absolutely adored the rooms, beautifully designed and lit, with lovely boiserie, very elegant classic contemporary furniture, and a fireplace! I believe I got one of the smallest rooms, but it was still rather spacious. The bathroom was small, perhaps too small for two people to use it simultaneously. 
The hallways, gorgeous as the rest of the property, had a very strong smell of food. I complained about that, but the issue was not addressed. It's probably a permanent problem, and a very off-putting one in my opinion.
The restaurant is a very nice venue. We had our thanksgiving lunch there and it was great. 
We also took advantage of the hotel Lexus to drop us of at a restaurant once, but we were offered the hotel car almost every time we left. This is such a nice and rare amenity, it really makes up for any shortcomings the property might have.
Hotels for me are all about comfort, design, service and location, and the XV Beacon delivers an excellent performance in most domains. I highly recommend it, and will surely return.

title_masked: OK Hilton, have stayed at better ones
text_masked:
Rooms are a bit smaller than regular Hilton, but nice. 
I stayed at the 8th floor that has a nice courtyard (pretty weird having a little park outside your window)
Front desk person wasn't too helpful, but in general stay was ok. 
Breakfast is very good and the location is excellent: just a short walk to Inner Harbor and to the great restaurants in the area.
Hotel was pretty crowded, as it was graduation week at Hopkins and the start of Memorial Day Weekend.

title_masked: I found it high on style, low on service...
text_masked:
The ground floor is the best thing about the hotel - the entrance from the street is very pretty with the ivy, and the ground floor restaurant is beautiful. It was hopping the two nights I was there, so busy in fact that it didn't work as a hotel restaurant in my opinion as it wasn't the type of place to stop and relax at the end of the evening. 
Check in is on the 2nd floor. Basically that means you bypass the lobby as you come and go and they're short-staffed on the ground floor so there's not a sense of welcoming as you return to the hotel.
Rooms were nice enough - small as others have noted, in stark white and royal blue. Very modern. Hallways are a bit dark but not too much so.
Worst part of my stay was leaving. We had checked bags and wanted to pick them up at the end of the work day, only to find that no-one was around. The bellhop was busy running other people's luggage out and flagging down taxis, and while the floor manager was there and was aware of our situation, he made no attempt to pull our bags for us. So we waited 10-15 minutes to leave. Odd.
Oh, and second worst part is the noise from adjacent rooms. The blow dryer was used in the room next to me both mornings at 5 a.m. Seriously, the first day I thought someone was in my room it was so noisy.
So no, I wouldn't recommend it.

Decided to take a chance on a Bloomspot offer for three nights at thie 'boutique' Times Square hotel, though the offer turned out not to be that much better than booking directly. The property itself is definitely different from most Times Square or mid town hotels, with a small one person reception desk at the end of a narrow lobby and tow adjacent buildings with the rooms. The building my room was in required one steep flight of exterior stairs and another narrow curvy flight of internal stairs. Quaint like a an old New Orleans apt but not at all accessible. The room was a decent size for NYC with an exposed brick wall and fireplace facade. The lighting was a problem with the only choice between very bright recessed overhead lights or a very dim desk lamp. No desk area for working but the bathroom was a good size shower.

title_masked: Due to Hurricane Sandy we had no heat or electricity in our...
text_masked: Due to Hurricane Sandy we had no heat or electricity in our home for 2 weeks. We live on Long Island in New York. We were very happy to get a hotel room since every hotel we called or visited in our area had no electricity or was booked solid. We were happy to have warm beds to sleep in.

title_masked: Home Away From Home and Wonderful
text_masked:
Recently we travelled to San Diego and Anaheim, CA. We flew into LAX picked up a car from Midway Car Rental (great prices) and drove to San Diego. The hotel was approx six miles from downtown San Diego and while we had to get into the car and drive it was well worth it for us.
We travelled with my husband, myself, daughter (13) and one of my best friends who needed some privacy due to medical needs yet needed to be affordable as I was paying for the trip.
We rented a two bedroom loft unit. The property is laid out like townhouses with several units together. The loft units were up one flight of stairs (no elevators). We walked in there was a living room with fireplace, flat screen tv, sofa bed/chair. There was a breakfast bar with four seats and a kitchen with stove, microwave, dishwasher, garbage disposal and refridgerator. A couple of nights we were so tired we drove to the grocery store (about 1 mile away) and I cooked dinner int the room. Breakfast consisted of fruit, yogurt, four kinds of cereal, coffee, tea, toaster where you could make bagels and toast. There were two waffle makers to make your own waffles and then a chafing dish with eggs/sausage or bacon and muffins. Plenty to eat and a good variety although it was pretty much the same every day. I had waffles with strawberry sauce every morning and was never disappointed. There was an outdoor pool and hot tub but in April it tended to be on the cool side (we had to buy fleece jackets) so we did not use the pool. I would stay here again anytime. Clean, lovely and very up to date and the proximity to the highway to downtown was almost across the street. Great Property, great for families and those who just want some extra room or privacy.

Took a weekend trip to NYC and stayed here, would recommend it to all. Easy walk (3 blocks) to Penn Station and close to good food & drink options. Fairly new hotel (opened Jan. 2012) so everything nice. Rooms are the typical NYC small, but well planned and efficient. Great shower and room amenities. We had a fantastic view of the Empire State Building out our window! Favorite characteristic is the narrow design that results in only 8 rooms per floor. Cuts down on the "in & out" noise. Why oh why can't somebody come up with hotel doors that close quitely??? Pleaseant & helpful staff - never used the exercise room of small bar off of the lobby.....

title_masked: Great new hotel close to everything!
text_masked: We stayed here for 3 nights this past weekend. I loved the decor and everyone was VERY friendly and helpful. The only complaint I had was that the shower pressure was terrible. The front desk staff was great. I am glad that I did a package deal with valet parking included as it was $25/day if you had to pay. Free breakfast in the morning was tasty and typical hotel fare. Our room had a nice view of Sports Authority Field at Mile High.

My wife and I recently stayed at the Hampton Inn Majestic and let me just say it was the smoothest, most enjoyable stay...the location for this hotel is right next to the Blue Line (O'Hare Airport Line), one block from the Red Line (All of the attractions) and about a ten minute walk to the Union Station Train Station (which we had to use also)...there are also many great restaurants (Trattoria No #10, Geno's Pizza, Girl & The Goat...to name just a few) that are very close...but enough on convenience the front doormen were great, the front desk was great, the room was clean, spacious and great...they have a Broadway-like show in the same building and free breakfast every morning that was "way" better than expected...Overall if you need to be downtown and don't want to pay and arm & leg and want to be perfectly located (did I mention 3 blocks to Millennium Park) This is where you want to stay!!!

My sister and I spent five days at the Jane Hotel in Greenwich Village, New York in July 2012. Looking decidedly ordinary from the street, we were delighted upon entering the expansive lobby as though the clock has been turned back to the 20's. Tiled mosaic floors and dark wood panelling, ornate lighting with original filaments, palms in tubs and subtle lighting all lent to a warm ambience of a bygone era. Jane has its own French-Moroccan style restaurant featuring many objects d'art and serving reasonably priced food with a French flavour.
The rooms run off narrow corridors, which are carpeted and have the wood panelling at shoulder height. Warm yellow wall lamps light the corridors. 
We started off in the bunk rooms which are very compact to say the least, consisting of bunk beds with a tv screen at the end of each and a very narrow strip next to them. Rooms come with bottles of water, glasses, towels, robes and air-conditioning. The air-con was noisy but necessary on the hot July days but we were exhausted from all our walking, so slept through it OK. The rooms are designed along the lines of a ships cabins and are ideal for back packers or those with light luggage.
The smaller rooms don't have private bathrooms, instead we shared common showers and toilets which also featured two hair dryers. The area was always spotlessly clean and tidy.and was not a problem sharing with the opposite sex.
We also upgraded to a Captains cabin which was sumptuous. We shared a queen bed, and the room also housed an antique sideboard, wardrobe and small table and chairs. We had our own bathroom,, featuring the black and white mosaic floors and walls, a huge bath and complimentary robes, soap, shampoo, conditioner and body lotion. This room also had French doors opening on to our own balcony, replete with outdoor furniture and plants.
Our beds were very comfortable, the pillows and bed linen were very clean and crisp. The Jane Hotel is excellent value for money, immaculately clean, the staff are helpful and polite and we highly recommend it for travellers who want to stay in the delightful and famous Greenwich Village.

Beautiful views of the space needle - especially at night so if you like photography ask for a room with a view. The staff are great and the local restuarant is excellent.
Secure parking is a plus. Free wi-fi - my only issue was waking at 4 am to do a conference call and I could not find the internet password - called down to the front desk and the man on duty would not give it to me - he insisited I come down to get it in person - I tried to convince him that at 4 am I was not dressed but he claimed it was policy that guests come down to collect the password at the desk ....so I got dressed and went downstairs to get it.
Ridiculous and I was seriously irritated ! 
Anyway I spoke with the day staff and they seemed shocked - that is not hotel policy! 
Keep the code safe!

The hotel is near the Theater District and this is very useful if you want to go crazy and see all the plays, musicals and the crowd at the Times Square. I stayed in a very good bedroom, clean, but simple. The bathroom is shared, but I was lucky because I have a bathroom next door and it was always available. There were many bathrooms and one kitchen. The building is a little old, there was a computer and free wifi at the lobby. The access to the internet was not free. There were nice restaurant nearby.
O hotel fica perto do distrito de teatro e isto é muito util se voce quer enlouquecer e assistir a todas as peças, musicais e o povo que fica perambulando pela Times Square. Eu fiquei num quarto muito bom, limpo, mas simples. O banheiro é compartilhado, mas eu tive sorte porque eu tinha um banheiro bem ao lado e estava sempre livre. Havia muitos banheiros e uma cozinha por andar. O predio é antigo, tinha computador e wifi gratis no lobby. O acesso à internet não era de graça. Havia restaurantes bons por perto.

Just a shout out to the front desk and everyone who helped make my stay and that of my co-workers a truly enjoyable experience. Both myself and my colleague are platinum members and the hotel went out of their way to insure an enjoyable stay. Special thanks to Nelson Massini at the spg desk. He's a great personal welcome to this large but yet really nice hotel

The hotel was beautiful!! The staff and service was above and beyond! Bellman-PAUL moonlights as an Elvis impersonator on the side and serenaded us with "Love me Tender"! OUTSTANDING! Showers are wonderful-bed and pillows extremely comfortable-best sleep ever!! Attended meeting at hotel and food was excellent, staff very attentive-Augustine was amazing in banquets!! Paula and Jim in Sales and Catering did a fantastic job!! Couldnt have been any better!!! Definately will be back-referring all my friends and family when visiting Dallas to stay at the Adolphus!!!!!

My husband and I stayed here for 3 nights as part of our honeymoon. The hotel is conveniently located just a short walk from Union Sqaure and we received a couple of great restaurant recommendations from the front desk. The room was large and very clean. I liked the decor and the overall feeling of the hotel and wouldn't hesitate to recommend this place to my family and friends. Also, front desk were great in helping us arrange a shuttle transfer back to the airport with a local company who picks up guests from the hotel on the last stop before heading to the airport - means you don't have to drive around for an hour picking everybody else up first! Was only about USD30 for both of us which was cheaper than a taxi - thanks Hotel Vertigo!!

I have stayed in Brexton 2 weeks.It was a very comfartable stay that I realy felt at home. First of all very professional staff, very good and safe location, VERY CLEAN and nicely renovated and refurbished building.....After having awfull one week 5 star hotel experience it was a real paradise....starting from manager to house keeping staf, very friendly, helpful staff.....they love their job and what they are doing....once again congredulations to management.....Nice breakfast room ,very good continental breakfast.......not only the rooms everywhere of hotel is very clean....As a location it is very convenient...it is in the heart of Mount Vernon which is very nice, safe and historical area in Baltimore....very close to Penn station that you can walk....also only 50 meters away from bus stop that with Charm City Circuler Line you can easly reach to Inner Harbor,Little Italy and Fells Point without paying any cent......Very suffıcant , quick ,excellant concierge service far beyond 5 stars hotel....... Once again many thanks to Paul Masai (General Manager), Melody,Ebani,Esther,Milton and Maria that they made my stay in Baltimore unforgteble......My final advice to visitors don't think twice to stay in Hotel Brexton , just stay and enjoy it......Mrs [NAME]ğlu

title_masked: A very different experience for me
text_masked:
We had a 12 night stay at this hotel in Sept 2012 and it was very different to the reviews we had read for this place. 
Our experience:
1. money STOLEN
2. dirty rooms - previous guests rubbish was still under the curtain separating the bathroom and bed area
3. 'gallery' facilities were often broken - coffee machine didn't work, no cups
As for the stolen money, I do admit fault that we didn't lock it in the safe (learnt from another review where money was stolen from the safe) nor in our luggage, but it wasn't exactly left out for all to see. LIving in a hotel for 12 nights, you tend to put things away in drawers and shelfs. The money i had was tucked away and you really had to go thru our possessions to get to it.
If housekeeping was that thorough, makes you think huh. The thought of someone going thru all your stuff while you put trust in their professionalism.
So 'mission control' was no help, they just hand you over to the security team and even when i gave feedback to them, I was pretty much ignored.
It's not all negative thou, the security team are doing their best, interviewing staff and updating us.
It wasn't a lot of money and I dont expect to hear from them again but it's a downer on the whole experience. Up to you what you make of this review.

I really like this hotel. I've been here two times and I will probably come back. It's a design hotel, with very spacious rooms and a great bed, I think one of the best beds I've ever sleep in. Totally recommended.

We live in the Galveston area, but enjoy the occasional trip to another Texas tourist gem, San Antonio. We love the missions along with the food and find the trip an easy one. 
A nice hotel with quality rooms and amenities always makes the trip enjoyable and our stay at the Grand Hyatt on this trip was spot on. 
Next door to the convention center the hotel is very busy, but the lobby is large enough to handle the crowds without feeling crowded. The decor was lovely with beautiful glass work in many different forms. The well appointed room met our every expectation and had a great view of Hemisfair Park from 22 floors up. The room was also spotlessly clean which is always a big positive. Our bellmen both in and out were extremely courteous and quick to serve. 
We did visit the pool which was the source of our only real complaint. The water in the pool was extremely cloudy, much more so than I would expect from a hotel of this quality. However the poolside cocktail service made up for it, with friendly servers who always made sure our beverages were full. 
I see complaints about parking, but having visited San Antonio many times I know what to expect so the $33/night charge for in/out privileges was not out of line with others. They were also very quick with retrieving our vehicle when needed having ample staff on hand to deal with demand. 
All in all the Grand Hyatt is a wonderful property, and one I would recommend to others.

The location is great. Just a half a block away from Broadway and less than that from 6th Avenue. 
If you are looking ofr a luxury hotel that you will spend a lot of time in, this isn't the place for you. The rooms are good size but basic. The bed was comfortavble and the room and bathroon was clean. The barhroom looked like it had just had the walls redone and a new sink and tub installed. Fruniture was sparse and consisted of two bedside tables, a table with two chairs, and a low 4-drawer chest that suitcases could be placed on. It had a HD TV mounted on the wall. The closet was narrow and I had to hang clothes turned a bit because it wasn't deep enough to fit the width of the hanger. The hotel is a bit dated and the room needed some fixing mainly in the way of painting. If you want a hotel that is just for crashing at night after spending the day in the city, this hotel fits the bill and is (at least when I booked it) reasonably priced. 
If you need a place to keep your luggage either before or after your stay thay has self-serve lockers for $5 per 24 hours that will easily hold 1 full sized suitcase plus three roll-aboards.
Our room was on the 11th floor and our friends were on the 6th floor. We both would stay here again.

I am at the hotel right now and I have to say its the smallest room/bathroom I have ever been in and I travel every week. When I entered the room, I was very surprised at how small the room was and I am supposed to automatically get an "upgraded room" at check in given my status with Marriott. In this room, there was only enough space for ONE person to walk around the bed without hitting the dresser on the left of the bed, the desk at the bottom of the bed, and the air condition unit on the right side of the bed. Dont let the armoire door hit you in the face! The bathroom was even worse. there is a small shower(no bath tub), next to a small sink, next to the toilet and the toilet barely has enough room to sit given the location of the toilet paper uolder. Again, there's only enough room for one person to stand in front of the sink. if you bend your head over the sink to say wash your face, the top of your head hits the protruding mirror box. Once you start washing your face, water splatters all over your body, and feet. There's no avoiding getting wet all over. There's just no wiggle room! Now, don't get me wrong. I am not a complainer but I felt claustrophobic the whole time I was there. This was the first trip, that I will be glad to be checking out of the room at the end of the trip. The bed was comfortable and that was the only good thing about our room. There is no access to ice, & you have to call for it every night. The lobby is very nice. The rest of the hotel is very nice. The staff is very nice and helpful. I will not be going back to this hotel when I travel back to New York.

I got this hotel at an excellent Name-Your-Own-Price on Priceline. Typically, I would not stay in the Financial District when visiting NYC, as it is a bit out of the way of where I usually like to spend time and work while in town. BUT, I am glad I did! This is by far the nicest hotel I have stayed at in NYC. I have used the Hampton Inn and others there, but the Doubletree had very clean, modern and newly-renovated, comfortable rooms with very plush beds and modern features in the bathrooms and bedroom area. The staff were all very nice and very helpful. For those in other reviews that have said the rooms are small, I beg to differ. The rooms are of comparable size for NYC, where rooms are always small. Others also complained about the elevators being slow, but I had no issue whatsoever. And even though it is in Lower Manhattan and a bit off the beaten path, it is very convenient to the R or 1 lines of the subway, and just a few extra minutes on the subway and you can be wherever you need to be in the City. For the price and the quality of this hotel, it was definitely worth it!

title_masked: Almost never disappoints as a Five Star Property
text_masked:
When I want to go to the City I always book at the Ritz,Battery Park. This is done via my AX Platinium Travel service and includes plenty of added value including the $100 food and beverage credit. Other hotels offer the spa credit but there are only so many treatments if you go there every 2-3 weeks. The food credit is ideal.
Whenever nicer rooms are available I get an upgrade and prefer a junior suite rather than looking at Lady Liberty which is the tourist's choice for an upgrade.
Parking is expensive at $60 so it would not hurt to walk a couple of blocks if I wasn't so darn lazy.
The restaurant food isn't anything special but convenient but a little overpriced.
Bed linens and comfort is great.
Nightly rates vary quite a bit so it is a good idea to be careful when making reservations if you are flexible

Myself and my husband stayed in this hotel for 5 nights (8-12 November) and I cannot fault it at all. Everyone was so friendly and helpful. The room was perfect for two people (the bed was enormous), we had a complimentary buffet breakfast every morning which came in so handy as we were on a budget and there was free wifi. The location of the hotel was perfect as it was close to Empire State Building, Times Square an $8 taxi ride to Rockafella Centre. All in all we will definitely be using this hotel again when we visit.

title_masked: Hotel needs to be maintained properly
text_masked:
This is my first review of a poor for a hotel. I had called the hotel before I booked because I was traveling with children. They advised the double bed suite because it was roomier with a kitchenette with microwave and fridge. I paid 30% more and we took that room. 
When we arrived at about 9pm, the room was nice enough, but NO microwave and a mini-fridge sitting on the counter. I went to the front desk. The fellow said he was alone !? but would try to get one. I explained that we were a family with kids and a baby and would not be able to eat without the microwave and suggested he simply transfer one from an empty room. The microwave never arrived. The kids and us ate cold TV dinners.
A little before 11pm my wife put the kids in the bath. Problem - NO hot water. They suggested we let the water run. That did not work. In the meantime the desk persons shift was over and a new fellow came and gave us keys to other rooms to try to find hot water.
The rooms for several floors above us were empty and we found one which did have hot water but no water coming out of the kitchenette sink! Now we had a microwave too in this one, so we figured we can manage here and took the room, transferring the kids and our luggage at about midnight. 
The next day we had no room service don't know why and Saturday evening ONLY boiling hot water came out of the faucets, nothing else. I almost burned myself. When I asked the front desk how they could rent such rooms he just shrugged and said "to tell you the truth I don't know". If not for the guys honesty and friendliness I would have raised a greater ruckus.
The staff told me there was this ongoing problem with the number X09 and X10 room lines going all the way up. 
A friend of ours on the twelfth floor in one of the cheaper single bedded rooms told us he had a great stay without problems, so PLEASE check your room before you unpack.
The bedding was ok, unremarkable, though the covers were lumpy. The hotel was clean in all its areas. Our coffee was never replaced during the stay. Toiletries were replaced.
The location though not that close to the inner harbor has a charm of its own. As for parking we found over night street parking and parked near the harbor during the day as the hotels rates came to near $35 a day for parking.
This hotel really has alot of potential, but they have to invest in maintenance and consistency.

Stayed in Denver one night after spending a few days in Boulder and this hotel was about the ONLY thing good about our single night trip to the "Mile High City." Everything about it was superb...the room was flawless, especially the bathroom!! The service is really top notch, as you would come to expect from a place like this. If you have to stay in Denver, this place is amazing...but I would choose to stay in the mountains every time.

I recently was in Denver for a conference which was held at this hotel. I must say that it gives Hilton a run for its money! I loved it. I travel frequently, and it is rare to find a hotel that I can give a 5 star rating. The room was well furnished, and clean. The amenities are nice. I ordered room service often, and every single meal was wonderful. The filet was cooked exactly as I requested, and the presentation was nice. Housekeeping was a plus here. Every meal (including those at my conference) was superb. They went above & beyond to please. I truly felt like a valued guest, and was called by my name each time I called downstairs. The hotel is conveniently located in downtown, with shopping within walking distance. My room was quiet and I never heard any noise from adjoining rooms.

title_masked: Great Hotel – Will definitely be back!
text_masked:
For someone who travels a lot I was looking for a special place to get away for a couple of nights with my husband to celebrate our anniversary. We were not let down! The staff was exceptional, kind and welcoming, they even knew why we were there, congratulating us as we arrived and a treat waiting for us in the room! 
Thanks.

title_masked: More than served its purpose for me
text_masked: Needed a place to stay downtown near my office when we had a snow storm hit the city, and this place served its purpose perfectly! I was able to check in well before check-in time and got a nice room on the 21st floor. The room was nice and clean and very well appointed. The location is great too. You can easily walk to anywhere you need to get to in downtown in minutes. I'll definitely stay here again!

I have stayed, in many, many Hotels in and around the San Diego area, and I was pleased to find this County Inn.
The staff is exceptional. And, that includes all of the Reception, Housekeeping, as well as the Restaurant and Bar personnel at this Best Value, and exceptional Hotel. The location (adjoining the Qualcom headquarters area) in a superb location, allowing one to "dart" in, out and around San Diego and North County. 
Rooms are well appointed, and exceptionally clean. The breakfast buffet is very well prepared and presented. And, then there are the fresh baked, Otis Spunkmeyer cookies in the reception area at 5PM, as well as complimentary coffee and fresh fruit throughout the day and evening. . 
The overall hospitality is contiguous.

Read all the reviews prior to going. We golfed, went to baseball games, shopped and relaxed. 
The golf course was in great shape. The rooms were well maintained and the staff were excellent, very helpful and obliging. I would highly recommend it. We didn't travel with kids, but the waterpark and evening activities for the youth would be great for young families.

The hotel is very nice, the lobby area is very elegant. The personnel is quite polite and always smiling and willing to help you.
Check in-Check out: so we arrived to SF @ 10.30am, and we were at the hotel by 11.15am. The only dissapointing thing of our entire stay was the check in time, 4pm, we found this very unconvenient as even thought they can keep your bags, you cannot get into your room until that time. The check out is at 2pm, which is great.
Rooms: clean, comfortable. The bathroom a little small and the closet which is right by the sink.
Cost/Value: 250$ per night is a bit expensive for what you get in other places.
Overall, I would stay there again...ahhh one more thing: keep in mind that this hotel is walking uphill from the Union Square, very very steep!!!...so we had to take taxis constantly; which are not really expensive in SF.

The Baltimore Marriott Waterfront is the best hotel in downtown Baltimore by far! Located right on the Baltimore waterfront, the hotel is in walking distance from downtown and famous Baltimore attractions. Great rooms and service!

We just returned from San Diego after staying for 4 days at the Inn at the Park (formerly Park Avenue Suites). I was hesitant because of the mixed reviews, but after stepping through the door of our King Bed Suite, Room 608, I was entranced. The room had not been remodeled yet, and I was so very glad to stay before the historical aspects are forever removed. I LOVED all the 80+ year old built-in shelving in the dressing room, and the kitchen is a history buff's dream: etched glass cupboard doors, a built-in "pantry" cupboard with grates for air flow, and, my favorite--an antique built-in Kelvinator mini-fridge (non-working). See my posted picture. The bathtub was huge and deep with a rainfall showerhead; the bed was comfortable (small square pillows were not). 
Our room was right off the elevator and across from the bottom of the (steep) stairs to the morning continental breakfast on the 7th floor, and although there was a party upstairs on the 1st night of our stay, the only time we could hear anything was when the people were leaving down the stairs.
If you are a ghost hunter (this place appears to ooze with spirits), do not mind that the lack of air conditioning (we found it non-necessary surprisingly), like a 1930-40's atmosphere, and want to be within walking distance of Balboa Park and Hillcrest (a tad further but walkable), then Inn at the Park is for you.

Was there on business from August 19th thru August 28th. This hotel's got just about everything one would expect from a Holiday Inn Express.
The front desk staff are very kind and courteous and helpful. I only stopped by for breakfast one time and found it to be very well done- good selection, and a nice ambiance in which to enjoy it.
Housekeeping was great and timely and did a fine job. The condition of the room was somewhat poor. The carpet was dirty and musty and the room had an odor, but it wasnt' overwhelming. The furniture was somewhat "beat up". Many surfaces had water marks and scuffs. The dresser drawers weren't fitting into the slots correctly and some of the bottoms of the drawers were falling out. The granite near the coffee pot and sink area had burn marks/stains. The bathroom was a good size with a large sink/vanity area, however the bathtub was tiny considering the large size of the bathroom. Water pressure was good and I always had hot water when needed.
Most of the "in-room" movies were over $10, so skip that. There was only one washer and dryer and I had to wait a good bit for use of the appliances. 
The bed was very comfortable and I slept very well. The bed was very clean. The AC didn't have a digital display, so I had to guess on the tempurature setting.

title_masked: Not far from the DART line
text_masked: We stayed in this hotel because of the close proximity to Love Field. The price was right as well. What made the experience a good one was the willingness of the staff to shuttle us to and from the airport but also to and from the DART line. The room was clean but the beds are small (double) but we knew that in advance and we made our choice. Not much surrounding the hotel that you can or would want to walk to but we had the transit available to take us to the things we really wanted to see in Dallas and Arlington. Overall a great value and would stay again.

We stayed for 8 nights at the beginning of April and I must say that everything was perfect. From arrival to departure, the service as consistent and impeccable. The room was beautiful and had a stunning view, the bathroom was super clean and spacious. And the location is unbeatable. We will definitely be coming back.

My first stay at Red Roof Inn and first things first the price was excellent and the bed was supremely comfortable. I just felt the hotel was in need of some maintenance as in a few things needed doing: There was no smoke detector in my room i could see into the roof and the wires hanging there, the metal shower handle fell to pieces in the morning and just missed my toes! Two lights were not working. the a/c clunked through the night as it roared into life when the room warmed up. The front desk ladies and drivers were all very pleasant. When i reached Houston Airport there was no way to call the hotel as they were not listed on the boards but the first driver said the name was called something else, so all in all confusing and if you do not have a local phone (as i did not) then not sure how you would get to the hotel using the free shuttle, by luck a small van pulled up as i was waiting and i jumped in. On balance i reflect on the price and the free wifi, free airport transfer and comfy bed make this a very doable stay near the airport, just hope someone in Maintenance gets to fixing the broken things i found and i suspect may also be in other rooms.

We went to San Francisco (from Texas) for a couple of concerts. Cova did NOT dissapoint. Lobby is small but very nice and inviting. I like the fact that you needed your keycard to use the elevator. Gave a good sense of security. Despite the location being in the Tenderloin, we had no problems walking back from The Warfield at 2am. Easily walkable location. The room was spacious and comfortable. The rooftop deck gives breathtaking views of the city. Totally recommend this place.

We booked Legacy throught HOTWIRE - so had no idea what it was until we accepted their terms etc! Wow - we were happy - nice location, nice condo and nice golf course - handy location to malls and groceries or anything else for that matter - nice grounds and easy to go for walk in the evening in surrounding neighbourhood - staff were all exceptional. Restaurant at the course is very tasty too! Did not use the spa facililites - I thought were a little pricey?? Did check out the pool area and common use areas all looked nice. Would rebook and stay if we could get the hotwire price - which was considerably lower than booking the resort directly. It is also adjacent to another golf course called "the Raven".

title_masked: Three night stay June 2012 - more than happy!
text_masked:
I booked the New York Barclay for a trip celebrating my wife's 40th. First impressions were good, the doorman was welcoming (as you'd expect!) and the lobby looks classy and sets the tone of the hotel. The staff were helpfull and us checking in three hours early wasn't a problem (check in isn't supposed to be until 3pm).
The room was clean and tidy, I'd booked a Deluxe King room and I believe it's slightly bigger than most rooms in NY. As others have mentioned, some appliances are not ultra modern, but why worry about the TV not being flat screen HD? How much time do you spend in the room watching telly when you're on holiday!!
The bar was expensive, but that wasn't unexpected but you're within walking distance of a number of restaurants. We didn't find any bars nearby, they were mostly restaurants, but some did also have a separate bar area if you just wanted a drink.
We had breakfast in 'Raffles' which was a three minute walk from the hotel. I'd booked the room only option and breakfast in the hotel was expensive.
I agree with other reviews that you're not far from most tourist attractions but away from the busiest areas. It's not quiet, where is in New York, but the traffic noise certainly didn't disturb us at night. The doorman whistling for cabs faded to background noise too.
In all we had a very pleasant stay and I'd be happy to go there again. I liked the fact that if you fly with BA you can check in online and print your boarding passes for your return flight in the 'business section' of the hotel (just through the lobby on the left) free of charge.

We stayed in the Beverly Garland for 2 nights while we went to Universal Studios in Hollywood. Check in was very swift and the person was very efficient and nice. We had reserved a "kids suite". I was a little nervous when she said we were going to be on the first floor. That turned out to be great. The highway noise that some have complained about here was negligible. We could barely hear it if we were really quiet. I think the trees and shrubs helped us out. The room was nice. Flat screen TVs in the main bedroom and the kids room. The only downside of the room was the bathroom. It was really tiny and a bit dated. We had breakfast at the restaurant and it was very good. We spend one late afternoon at the pool and it was really nice. The towels were constantly being refreshed, the pool bartender was super friendly and helpful and my daughter loved the noodles and watching the movie. We took the shuttle to Universal and at 6:15pm was waiting to take the one back. It did not show up. Finally at around 6:45 I called the hotel and they said it had broken down. They said to take a cab and they would reimburse us (which they did). A bit of inconvenience but nothing they could control.

title_masked: Very nice hotel at a reasonable price, prime location
text_masked: This is a very nicely appointed and clean hotel in a prime area of the San Fernando Valley, right in the middle of Warner Center. We had a beautiful view of Warner Center from the 8th floor. The staff was professional, courteous, and attentive especially the woman (Asian gal, whoever she was) who managed the front desk and checked us out around 11:00 on Sunday, 12/16. The hotel lobby and lounge are warm, open and inviting. The hotel appears to be very well maintained. Across the street is a very nice mall and PF Chang's (a favorite). There are many other restaurants and lounges dotting the area.

title_masked: Needs to get with the times
text_masked:
We stayed at the Waldorf last January, mostly holiday part conference (at the Hilton). The Waldorf's draw is it's history - period. Apart from that it's just a large hotel catering largely to conventions, still dining out on its cache of being famous. Get real, Waldorf - $15 per day for internet access? We had a junior suite, which was generously sized, but the bathroom is in serious need of updating - it looked old, tired and grubby. I liked the proximity to Grand Central, but apart from that it's in a pretty quiet area.
Probably the best aspect of our room - between the neighbouring buildings we could peek out and see the Chrysler building - nice!

title_masked: perfect place for a baseball weekend
text_masked: Planned a visit down to San Diego to catch a Padres baseball game for opening weekend and this was the perfect place to stay. It is a stone's throw from the ball park and from the 9th floor roof bar, you can watch the game, which we did the night we got there. From pulling up to the valet (the only option at the hotel) to leaving the next day after spending the day at Petco Park for an afternoon game, we were treated so well by the staff at the Indigo. The hotel is filled with bright colors, lots of natural light, the rooms are beautiful with hardwood floors, colorful bedding, tasteful but funky furniture. The location is perfect, again right by the ball park but also good walking distance from the Gaslamp district, the embarcardero, and Seaport Village.

This is one of those hotels that is a diamond in the rough. It is under construction and has been taken over by someone who knows what they are doing..hopefully. Our room a junior suite was on the 5th floor facing a building and looking the the AC so we asked for another and at $450 a night I was hopeful we would get one.... After a few hours we were upgraded to the Cassa Suite which was a wonderful huge room with nice views, The staff was very impressive and the cleaning staff did an amazing job folding the clothes and truly cleaning the entire room. GREAT job Cassa! This hotel should be rated in the top 30 and with the new owners this will be one of the best places to stay in Times square...get it while it is still affordable because it will get expensive!
Stay there every week on buissness and I must say it is GREAT.. The area around the hotel is super with lots of places to eat. I wish they had cheeper parking.. 26.00 is a bit much..

My daughter and I stayed here for a girls week-end. We felt very safe there. The staff was the friendliest and most helpful I have ever encountered. The room was small like you often find in large cities. However the bathroom was quite large and there was a large walk in closet. The closet was nice for storing all of our stuff out of sight and out of the way. The bed was one of the most comfortable I have slept in anywhere. There was a small amount of hallway noise, but no noise from the other rooms.
This hotel is a nice location and I would recommend it as a great place to stay in New York City.

We stayed there over the weekend and it was an ok stay. Loved the lobby. The room was very nice. Bed very comfortable. The only thing I have to complain about is that it took about 20 minutes to get checked in, couldn't find a front desk clerk.

title_masked: Modern boutique hotel with all the Marriott amenities and so much more
text_masked: We had an amazing experience at the JW Marriott Denver Cherry Creek and we HIGHLY recommend this hotel to visitors to the Denver area. Excellent customer service begins the moment you arrive at the JW Marriott - the valet service is wonderful, guests are encouraged to relax and let the valet and bell staff worry about your bags and your vehicle. You have easy access to valet vehicles, but it doesn't even matter, because so many great restaurants and shops are walking distance from the hotel. Cherry Creek Mall, dozens of restaurants, coffee shops, and boutiques are moments away and the neighborhood is safe and welcoming. This is an amazing place to stay. Every JW Marriott staffperson is knowledgable about the area and can help you decide where to go for breakfast, lunch, dinner, or a snack. Visit the JW Marriott - you won't be disappointed.

title_masked: Gorgeous Hotel but Choose Your Room Wisely
text_masked:
This is a beautiful hotel. The lobby has old-world grandeur and is a very happening place on the weekend. The rooms are decorated in a style both elegant and fun. The bath amenities are high quality. It’s one of the few hotels that have good lighting and mirrors in beautifully refurbished bathrooms and generous closet space. The staff is amazingly friendly – even the cleaning staff smiles and greets you in the hallway. The whole place has a “whistle while you work” attitude. The bellmen are efficient and highly motivated and, curiously, were calling us by name after only one night. The same bellman takes your bags from your room, down into the lobby and out the door and hails a cab – one tip, not three like in many hotels.
But do not under any circumstances accept a room close to the elevator lobby. You will hear the whoosh of the elevators all night. After the first night spent with a pillow over my head, they moved us to another room far away from the elevators and gave us a complimentary upgrade. I actually liked the bathroom in the first room better (a king) than the smaller bathroom in the junior suite. We didn’t need a suite, but we would have been proud to host a gathering in the parlor area – it was gorgeous and had plenty of seating, its own powder room, refrigerator, bar and large TV.
If mobility is a problem, you need to ask how far from the elevator your room is. This place is enormous and the hallways are very, very long. I felt like I needed to leave a trail of breadcrumbs from the elevator. 
Parking fees are crazy. At $42/night to self-park, we opted for taking cabs rather than renting a car. You need to have at least two cab company phone numbers in your phone. The concierge and bell services will not call a cab for you off-premises, which was a bit disappointing considering they were extremely accommodating in every other way.
I will definitely stay here again, but will be insistent upon a quiet room with a larger bathroom.

title_masked: Great place to stay, and great value
text_masked: The staff was very friendly and hospitable. I arrived late and they helped me find a place to eat a late dinner. The room was small, but it was fine. It was very clean and decorated simply but nicely. Perfect for business travel. I would definitely stay there again.

Stayed here for 3 nights, the price was superb. This hotel was probably built in the 60's. Everything looks tired including the TV and the heater. The heater was probably nearing the end of its life as it's not heating up the room properly. Breakfast is good. Pool is great, we did took a plunge. The pool is outside our room and it is not heated. The landscaping is awesome. There's a free shuttle to airport. Denny's is a few steps away (their shrimp was so small, quite unbecoming for an American dishes) and there's a Taco Bell a few blocks away. The parking is behind the hotel and it's free. Car rental is like 2 minutes walk from the hotel. Overall, it's more that what we bargain for. Will stay here again if we visit Lax another time.

Clean, easy access to freeway, staff friendly and helpful!!! Highly recommend this hotel. The AC was not working called down to front desk within a few minutes someone came up to rest the unit. Excellent service, I will return and recommend to everyone.

I stayed here for a second time this weekend. I love coming here because the grounds & gardens are so beautiful and makes you feel like you are away on an island. This time we had a different style room in the garden area but I liked it just as much as the tower rooms. The seating outside our room was really nice and perfect for reading. Overall, good stay, delicious breakfast inTrellises and super accommodating staff. Oh, and thanks to Jennifer for the gift basket. That really made our day.
This hotel was warm, and the staff were friendly. At $107 a night, it meets the typical expectations of a Hyatt...clean, new, and a little pricey. However, it is worth it!

We enjoyed our recent stay at the Westin Boston Waterfront. As first time visitors to Boston we liked the location which is somewhat removed from the congestion of the city centre. The hotel is also a stop for the Boston Old Town Trolley Tour. The trolley stops right outside the lobby every 15 - 20 minutes as part of the seaport loop which connects to the tour's main hub at Long Wharf, the Boston Harbour Cruises and the New England Aquarium. While the hotel is billed as "waterfront" it is three blocks west of the water. It's about a 10 minute walk to the restaurants on Seaport Blvd. It is also close to the cruise ship dock so it's a good choice for those passengers embarking or disembarking. 
The staff were all very friendly and helpful, a nice surprise for such a large hotel. Our room was small but comfortable with those heavenly Westin beds. We reserved a "deluxe" room which means that it is at the east end of the hotel and offers a panoramic view of the waterfront. There are only a few rooms on each floor with this type of view. Our room had only one upholstered chair (along with a desk chair) so I spoke with the concierge Steve Wadkins. He had another chair delivered to our room that evening. We had room service our first night which included very good clam chowder. We had the buffet breakfast at the hotel both mornings. There was the choice of a lesser priced continental buffet, a nice option. Parking was about $30 a night.
While some travelers may find this hotel somewhat isolated it was good fit for us. After a busy day of sightseeing in the city it was a nice, quiet place to rest and relax.
John and Pamela
Ottawa, Canada

I stayed at Trump Chicago shortly after it first opened and moved rooms within the hotel due to a few problems. I had not planned on giving the hotel a second chance but I am so glad I did! The service at this hotel is the best service I have ever experienced, far and wide over decades of travel. The hotel worked with me prior to my visit to assist me with my guests who were on a very special status in the USA by calling me, and when we arrived encouraged me to take a different kind of room offered to me at a bit of a discount. A bell staff overheard a problem, quietly asked if the hotel could assist, and over the next two days the hotel worked on my problem with another hotel, solved it, in fact taking over the issue so I could be free. Service was perfect in providing the things we needed in a suite such as unfolding the sleeper sofa and sheeting it very promptly and again in returning it to sofa status. Spa service and the spa was much, much better on the second visit as well, and if you enjoy a good gym and plush locker room supplied with scrubs, oils, fancy showers this is for you. Room service food arrived hot, perfect, quickly and was set up on a table beautifully. River view rooms and suites offer the best views of beautiful Chicago as does the restaurant which I also liked much better on the second visit. There is only one thing I do not enjoy about Trump Hotel Chicago and that is the lobby, and lobby life. I prefer the kind of hotel that has a huge lobby for people watching and for that I would stay at the Palmer House Chicago, another great hotel, but the Trump is more modern, quieter, the gym a bit better (though Palmer House gym is far better than the average hotel gym) and has better service. This last 4 day stay

If you are a business traveler, or used to Hilton standards (or any other decent hotel), find somewhere else. This hotel is a joke. 
The rooms are clean and large, but absolutely nothing special. That is the only redeeming quality for this hotel. There is no WiFi in the hotel rooms, even though two different front desk clerks informed me otherwise. I had to have some special adapter sent to my room just to access WiFi in my room (which intermittently works). If that wasn't bad enough the wired connection that is available in the room is not near a desk, or any other convenient work station (it is in the corner of the living room). 
After resolving the internet issues I attempted to order room service - this was an exercise in futility. It took four phone calls and about 10 minutes just to get through to room service. Took forever to arrive and the food was barely palatable. 
Every employee I dealt with was apathetic and overall unhelpful. When I asked for a comment card I was not provided with one. The pool and health center is mediocre. Do yourself a favor and forgo the frustration this property is likely to cause you. There are too many other hotels in the area. This hotel should be embarrassed to call itself a Hilton.

My husband and I took our 2 young children to Chicago this weekend and we stayed at the W Hotel - Lake Shore (booked through Hotwire.com). A pleasant stay - the location was ideal (we had a great view of Navy Pier), and our 2 double bed room was comfy for our family. Unfortunately, the lack of attention to the details were immediately apparent: the room had poor ventilation (windows were condensed with steam from the shower for most of the weekend) and had a faint smell of cigarette smoke, there was not directory in regards to room/hotel amenities, the condition of the pool was not ideal (pool water was salty and the pool area smelled faintly of formaldehyde) and the TV monitors in the exercise room had poor reception. Obviously, this was a deal on Hotwire, so for what we paid, what we got was above average, but I would never pay full price for this hotel after our weekend.

Very busy location yet quiet inside. Picked for the perks alone (included full breakfast, happy hour, free parking, indoor pool/hot tub). Our suite was spacious, staff was kind, helpful, and location was an easy drive to anywhere. If at an upscale, glitzy hotel we'd pay sooo much more for less just to say we stayed there. Instead we picked value over glam, and had more money to spend doing stuff in the city than paying for a place to park/sleep. Will return again.

Room smelled, the carpet was wet in some portions of the room. I opened the window and paint chipped and cracked and went everywhere. The box of tissues in the bathroom was wet!?
This is a classic hotel and could be nice if they were to work on the upkeep and updates. They probably have some very nice rooms - but this one was bad and I've heard from other folks staying with me that the rooms were old and smelled.
Disappointing.

title_masked: Wonderful Property with Great Staff; Very Convenient to Universal Studios
text_masked: We stayed here for two nights in March 2012. The hotel is very nice and the staff offer outstanding service. The hotel is about a 5 minute walk to Universal Studios, which is a great attraction if you like movies and entertainment. Check-in was fast and efficient. The rooms are over-sized with good views of the local area. The room was clean, and the bathroom was quite spacious. We got good recommendations from staff on local restaurants. Parking is convenient and covered. I definitely would stay here again- great property!

We visited for three nights at the beginning of September. First impressions were of a standard, non-descript hotel on a city street corner. The reception staff were polite but far from welcoming and offered the minimum of information. There were no porters (at any time) and we even had to ask how to find the lift. The room was OK, looking into the central courtyard which, from other comments, was a good thing. Certainly the room wasn't overlooked and the courtyard was tidy. Otherwise it was adequate if basic. At breakfast, staff were again surly and unwelcoming. The concierge was clearly unhappy at being disturbed from her screen and uninformative.Similarly, there was no one to call a cab on departure. The high spot was the wine reception each evening but, apart from that, don't bother if you're looking for service.

title_masked: Clean and Spacious Rooms. Friendly Staff. Excellent Location.
text_masked:
This hotel offered everything we wanted; clean and spacious rooms, very helpful staff and perfect central location in San Diego. It's also very close to a lot of great restaurants and Fashion Valley Mall. The hotel is also very close to the light rail station to take the train to Old Town or Downtown.
We stayed here two nights in January and the always felt welcome. As a HHonors member, this hotel provided excellent delivery of the HHonors benefits, including breakfast for all in the room, internet, water and of course fabulous cookies. Would certainly stay here again as it meets the Hilton standard for hotel quality.

This is really pretty picky to mention, but the elevator service in the hotel is really a bit of a problem. During our visit, only one elevator was operating most of the time. You really had to add an extra 10 minutes to any planned meeting times! 
Elevators aside, The Blakely is outstanding. Spacious, comfortable rooms, well decorated and comfortably appointed; modern plumbing and bathrooms; free wifi internet access with really good bandwidth; breakfast included; wonderful Midtown location on (by Manhattan standards) a quiet street. Back in the "picky" department, the bath towels will soft and fluffy could have been a bit larger. 
The staff was universally thoughtful, responsive and available. I had left my iPhone in my room when I checked out. By the time reached the ground floor and before I had missed it, housekeeping had found it, called the front desk and brought it to me!

My partner and I stayed here for 3 nights in October and was really pleased with our choice. It's quite overwhelming with the choice in San Francisco and we wanted something with character which this place certainly had. The staff were exceptional, always helpful and cheerful no matter what time of day. They have recently opened a restaurant which we didn't get to try but had a drink in the bar, they had a great selection of all types of drinks and again the staff were really friendly. As for location it's not in the centre of the hussle and bussle but we didn't want this anyway, there is a bus stop right near the hotel which the hop on hop off bus tours stop at but if your not shy of walking which we weren't it was only a 20 minute / half hour walk to the centre. There are also several restaurants and bars just round the corner from the hotel too. The rooms were very clean with really comfy beds, kitchen facilities and TV. We couldn't have asked for any more and highly recommend this hotel to anyone. If you have a booking to see and opera - even better!

We stayed at this hotel for one night on a Saturday. We got a great deal on price line. I saw when we booked on price line that we were assigned a smoking room. I called right away to have it switched to nonsmoking and the lady on the phone said she switched it. When we got to the hotel we parked in the parking structure. It was $39 for a 24 hour period. (not too bad for Chicago) When we checked in the man at the front desk said that we had a smoking room. I told him that I called and had the lady at reservations switch it for us. He said that since we booked it on price line we had to take a smoking room and there were not any non smoking rooms available. Ok fine. When we got off the elevator the hallway stunk like cigarette smoke really bad and so did the room. Some of the previous reviews said the the smoking reviews didn't smell too bad. Ours however did. The room was ok. The chair in our room was full of stains and the flooring was coming up. We got a king sized bed and it was very comfortable. We went to Chicago to shop and see a few sights. It was within walking distance to a lot of stuff (mag mile, Navy Pier and millennium park) and was off the main streets with all the hustle and bustle. I would return to this hotel again if I got a good deal on price line again. However, I would have been disappointed if I would have paid full price ($150+) for the room.

The hotel is very modern. Reception lady was so friendly and helpful. She pointed out all the nice restaurants and places to visit on the map and explained to us the easiest way to get around the city. The bed and pillow were very comfy. Our room was on the top floor, with nice view of the bay. 
We booked the hotel for one night at an expensive rate a few month before our trip. My sister in law booked the same hotel last minute and paid half of what we paid. Wifi and internet were not included in the stay. You have to pay a daily usage rate.

title_masked: You get what you pay for
text_masked: I was visiting family so I wanted to find a hotel close to the lower valley. Since I wasn't going to spend much time in the room I opted to select a cheaper hotel. I really don't care about the brand name I just want a clean, comfortable, convenient and safe hotel. With this hotel I got what I paid for. It wasn't the fanciest, no frills or thrills which is fine however the hotel is in serious need of renovation. It's old and you can tell. The overall room was decent; it could've been cleaner. I had several issues during my stay and had to call the front desk numerous times. I will say that the front desk was very responsive in addressing my issues which was nice. Near the night stand it smelled moldy like the carpet had gotten wet and never dried. The first night I opened up a drawer to put my clothes in it and there was a pizza box in it. Several times during my stay the T.V. signal kept going out. At one point I received a call back advising the technician was gone for the day so they couldn't send someone to fix my T.V. They did offer to move me to another room. Fortunately I was able to get the T.V. to work on my own and declined the offer but it was nice they offere. The blow dryer didn't work so I had to call again to have someone come fix it. The morning that I checked out I got up really early to take a shower for my 6 am flight. The water was ice cold and didn't warm up until I was ready to get out. The bed was pretty comfortable. I would stay at this hotel again if it was a last resort however it wouldn't be my first choice. There is a Denny's next to it which is convenient for meals. The hotel is pretty close to I-10 but I didn't hear the traffic since my room wasn't facing the interstate.

Stayed at this hotel in September of this year. The staff are second to none, two male members of staff were on duty when I checked in & they were both first class, I was made to feel so welcome by both of them.
The rooms were a little on the small side, but they were very clean & had everything in them that I needed during my stay. The bed was very comfortable & the sheets were always fresh & clean.
If I were to go back to San Francisco, I would defiantly stay at this hotel again.

title_masked: Noisy, poor service - missed wake up call
text_masked:
The hotel is on Union Square, so it's expected to be noisy, but because there is no air conditioning, you have to sleep with the windows open, and the noise is terrible, even at the back of the hotel. Also, the walls are very thin, so you hear every little noise in the rooms around you. We were on the uppermost floor, and the noise was still so bad that we could barely sleep. The beds are also very noisy. If your sleep mate moves the slightest bit in the night, the bed creaks terribly.
We had a very early flight out of San Francisco and requested a 3:40am wake up call, but never got the wake up call, so if you're staying here, be sure to use the wake up call as a back up only.
The front desk clerk was very nice to us, which made up for the bell boy's bad attitude.

Got this hotel on Hotwire at a 30% discount. Although hotel is listed as on the "Riverwalk", it is at least 3 very confusing blocks to get to the touristy Riverwalk area. Even with 2 maps in hand, we both got lost walking down the first 2 blocks of this deserted end of the Riverwalk, go back up to the street, ask a police office on how to get back down the main Riverwalk area. So if you want to stay in the Riverwalk area, don't book here.
This hotel also has the rudest & most un-professional valet staff. Both the morning & evening crews were horrible. Their uncaring attitude were extremely unsettling.
