Even at $28 for valet parking & $24 for self-parking in lot across the street, it's not worth it. They ran out of valet parking spaces in the evening & you're on your own to find your own parking. 
Rooms were nice & comfy, but rest of hotel seems old & dated.
Would not recommend this hotel for a relaxing family vacation.

Hotel is nice enough. Good rate for a decent and clean room. Breakfast is LQ standard. Elevator was filthy, floor littered with peanut shells and M&Ms.
I would have given this place a 4 if the catalytic converter hadn't been cut out of our car while we slept. Looking through trip advisor, it seems that LQ has a crime problem in this city. We went out of our way to empty the fully packed car because of that, only to have someone remove a section of the exhaust.
Won't be comin back, Indy.

Great service--front desk person came down to greet us because he noted when we were coming in. Rooms clean and comfortable, but a little noisy.
Location very convenient to theaters, Art Institute and mag mile.
Parking fee is steep--$42 per night.
Overall a very nice experience.

We came here for a small family event, sort of a reunion. We picked the Waldorf because it has an important place in my family's history. We were disappointed with how the hotel is maintained, very disappointed with the indifferent service. On the plus side, the rooms and baths are large. The location is amazing. This wonderful old place deserves better care.

title_masked: Convenient, up to date and well run
text_masked:
Spent one night here visiting friends who were attending a conference. Impressions:
- very convenient to the convention center - just a short walk across the street.
- the GasLamp district is also a short walk away. 
- solid, well trained staff. Lines never lasted long during check-in and check-out and they take the time to step out from behind the counter to direct you to the elevators. 
- if you are on an upper floor, there are awesome views of the Bay, even if you are on the side of the hotel with the Dole Foods shipping terminal, as long as you are on an upper floor.
- we were on the top floor, and there was a corporate event in one of their meeting rooms on that floor, and it was very loud from 8 to 10 PM, so if you plan to hit the hay early, make sure you are away from the elevator lobby area.
- our room was very clean and comfortable.
- we would stay here again.

We went for a five days stay and we decided to give a chance to Harlem, as it is not a central place to stay. This is the only negative aspect of this Hotel. We were very surprised with the way confort and informal ambience may go together. The rooms are clean, beds are great, don´t expected to have a closet to put your things. There are no drawers but who needs it anyway! People are professional and very friendly. Girls at the front desk are always available to help you. The are no cuisine but it is possible to get a quick meal by serving ourselves from a self.
It seems it is one of the few hotels dog friendly.

title_masked: Comfortable and great location, but a bit tough around the edges
text_masked:
We stayed in the Club Quarters and found it a fine place to stay in Manhattan. It is located a block away from Rockefeller Center, a block or two from two subway lines, and a half mile to both Times Square and Central Park. 
Our room was typically cozy for midtown but was more than sufficient for our needs. Everything was quite clean. The bed was a little on the soft side, but it got the job done.
My only complaints would be very minor. The tiny lobby gets uncomfortably crowded and chaotic around key checkin and checkout times. The elevators can be very, very slow. The computers they provide at the "business center" (which is really just a shelf adjacent to the bar) are achingly slow, and every printer I tried was out of toner (so we were unable to print boarding passes). And our room could've been quieter--we heard every time the ice machine down the hall dropped ice and every time a person purchased snacks or beverages from the vending machines. 
On the positive side, the service was excellent. We called to move forward our arrival date by a couple of dates and were told it was done, but when we arrived we found no reservation awaiting us. Dean at the front desk solved the problem quickly. We had questions about the area and found the staff helpful.
I'd recommend Club Quarters, but with a little more polish this could be a five-star hotel.

We stayed for 4 nights up on the Hill, room 301. We had a fantastic time here, the rooms were comfortable and clean, and the staff were amazing, really super helpful and polite and happy. The pool on the hill is great, we spent a few days lazing by the pool and were pretty much the only people using it. The views from the top of the hill, from the apartment and the pool are nothing short of spectacular. The rooms may be a tiny bit tired, and could do with a paint, but we didn't care about that at all. The location is perfect, a 5 minute walk from reception to Hollywood Boulevard. This place has two hotels, the Hollywood Hills Hotel, up the hill, and down the bottom of the hill The Magic Castle Hotel. If you want spectacular views and an awesome pool then head up the top. We can't recommend this place highly enough, we'll be back.

My husband and I took our two teenagers to Boston for the week during July 4th and really enjoyed staying at the Hilton Financial District hotel. We stayed in a king suite which was very spacious, clean and comfortable. The concierge staff was amazing, especially John. They set up our New England Aquarium visit and Whale Watching cruise - absolutely wonderful experience. They also set us up with trolley tickets and told us all the great places to take our kids. Oh, the best part, they helped us find a perfect spot away from the crazy crowds to watch the fireworks on the fourth! Had the most amazing vacation ever!! Highly recommend!!!

title_masked: Good place for overnight before flight
text_masked: This is a great hotel for those flying out of CLT and do not have a car. The shuttle is a well run clock and time to the airport is short. There are a couple of restaurants nearby, Cracker Barrel next door. Staff is helpful and friendly. The property improves every time I stay there. It is an older property, recently painted and most room doors open to the outside. More than adequate for an overnight stay.

title_masked: Don't stay here until the protests stop
text_masked:
My mum and I stayed here in June 2012.
PROS:
Great location, friendly staff, nice rooms (although the bathroom is bigger than the rest of the room, and the windows provide NO sound barrier to the street outside).
CONS:
The hotel is undergoing some kind of ownership change or something - in any case, every morning at 7am protestors stand outside and form a picket line for one hour. On top of the awful noise that they make, they actually harrassed me and made me feel really uncomfortable and unsafe when I was trying to load my car with our luggage.

We stayed at the Warwick for just 2 days at the start of our extended trip and found the rooms excellent and the hotel was central for everything. The hop on hop off bus stopped just outside it so you couldn't get better than that. Would recommend

First time to Chicago would recommend Embassy Suites Downtown. Lovely comfortable beds, brilliant breakfast, friendly and helpful staff. Perfect location for 7 day family holiday would have no hesitation in booking again.

We stayed for three nights at the Palomar in Westwood (Los Angeles). There's a very friendly feel to the hotel--they are pet friendly, and quite a few guests bring their dogs, which adds to a homey, welcoming atmosphere. The lobby has free coffee in the morning, water and iced tea during the day, and wine from 5 to 6 pm. We were traveling with my niece, so we got a king suite, which worked well; there are sliding doors between the bedroom and the living room (which has a queen sized sofa bed.) The king suites have a huge bathroom. The view of the city was fabulous. There was also a nice exercise room that we used every day. My only complaint is that the dining room was VERY dark. But all in all, a nice hotel, well located, clean, with helpful staff.

This hotel is in one of the best locations in lower manhattan. There are great bars, restaurants and shops flanking it on both sides as well as trains very nearby. The vibe is super cool and hip. The rooms are small but modern. The beds are insanely comfortable. Also note this is a pet friendly hotel. We are staying here due to being displaced from Sandy and they helped us out with the rate. Also complimentary wifi and a really nice breakfast spread. Wonderful hotel in a great location. Staying here also gives you access to the NY Health and Racquet Club across the street. I wouldn't say this is a kid friendly hotel as it seems to cater to a younger crowd. My husband dog and I were very comfortable though.

this place stinks like 60 year old mildew warmed over with cigarette smoke. i was scared the whole time i was there; could not sleep. heard screaming foul language throughout the night. the only thing i didn't see was the yellow crime tape. the pictures on this website are misleading. doors feel like they are made out of balsa wood. bed was disgusting. bathroom was nasty. i should have paid attention to the reviews. i made the awful mistake of bringing my family here. never again.

title_masked: I like this hotel alot. Very clean rooms, easy access, great service
text_masked: Overall excellent hotel. Clean rooms, comfortable beds, great service. There is a nice sushi place within walking distance of the hotel. Parking is easily accessible if choose not to use the valet. Plenty of elevators that work very quickly. A+ , highly recommended.

Always a good experience at the Marriott, but the location of this hotel is superb. We got a promo on which included breakfast buffet, so it was good value for our money. Close to Pike Place Market, within walking distance, the Seattle Aquarium, shopping. And right across the street from the harbour. Beautiful spot.

title_masked: Great Value, Comfortable Rooms, Friendly Staff
text_masked:
We have stayed 4 or 5 times at Days Inn Inner Harbor and been more than happy every time. Recently the rooms were renovated, though frankly we were happy the way they were. They are spatious and well-equipped. Refrigerator and micro-wave make a big difference to us, and the Wi-Fi is free. 
The staff are both friendly and helpful.
Parking is available at an additional charge at a public garage that is attached to the hotel. No need to go outside in bad weather. Bill the parking to the hotel rather than paying the garage directly and you can go in and out without additional charge.
The hotel is not in the midst of everything, but it's easy walking distance from the harbor, the ballpark, and the business district.
The price has always been lower here than any comparable hotel in Baltimore. A really great value.

This is an older property that has been kept relatively clean. Could use some updates (had 90s vintage TV, hallways smelled a little old), but was fine for a night. Received a fine price via Priceline. Not luxury, but not luxury money, so you get what you pay for. Not walkable to any eateries, but that is typical for the region. Staff were nice and breakfast was fine. For one night, it was nothing to complain about.

title_masked: Great value, big rooms, pull out sofa
text_masked: I was very pleased with the rooms, and the price. I traveled with my 2 children, aged 11 and 14, and was able to get 2 queen beds with a pull out couch, so we each had our own bed. The hotel was clean, staff friendly, elevators worked well, no waiting. The view is nice, and it's convenient to subway, and many attractions in NY.

we have just returned from 5 days at Hotel Monaco. It is in a beautifully restored historical building and is quite lovely. The rooms are small, nothing spectacular really but the location is fantastic. It is located right across the street from the Verizen Center, so very easy to attend hockey or basketball games if that is of interest. It is also across from the subway (under the verizon center) making it very convenient for almost everything.
It is within walking distance of the mall, so access to all of the smithsonians and monuments is easy. The National Portrait gallery is also right across the street, the spy museum is next door...you get the idea. Lots of restaurants and bars nearby.
It is expensive, but worth it because of the location. The beds were very comfortable and I loved the bedding. The people were nice enough.

We were three female friends in our 50´s visiting New York for a few days. We had booked a room for three persons, with two delux beds, promised to be big enough for two friends to share. When we arrived they gave us a room with two 120 cm beds, not enough to share, and we had to change to a dubble room with one extra bed. The explanation was that the rooms mentioned in the booking did not any more exist, it had changed after a renovation. The extra bed was defenitely not suitable for anyone above 10 years old and we ended up booking one more room and paid 789 USD for that room. The rate for the first room remained the same as in the original booking, for three persons in two deluxe beds. Our stay in Belvedere Hotel ended up very expensive.
The staff was nice but we had very little to do with them. The elevator was a problem, not always enough for all guests going up and down. The room were average but ok. The location great but there arre so many hotels in this area to choose between.

I really have nothing bad to say about this hotel. It was a gorgeous lobby, clean rooms, and helpful staff. My friends and I enjoyed the breakfast buffet... but there could sometimes be a long line :-)

So we are coming to Houston to see my step son this weekend but not only that it is going to be a get away for my Birthday...My Birthday is Feb 12th but I will be unable to take anytime off of work for my birthday so this trip is a gift to myslef. I finally get to spend time with my husband and our 3 kids. The kids are so excited about staying at the hotel and I just wanted to say that Thanks to all the great reviews it has made my selection of Hotels easier. I look so forward to staying at this hotel.....See you ES on [TEL]. Have a blessed day..Tiffaney Aberle

We held a two day customer training event at this facility. The banquet staff and food quality was on par with other hotels we've used in the 4 star category. The hotel is well appointed and the location is lovely overlooking the naval canal. Sleeping rooms are comfy and super clean. It was an outstanding facility for our meeting and we will return again. I recommend this hotel highly for all of your most important meetings and events. A+!

The 2-Room Riverview suite on the 9th floor was EXCEPTIONAL!!! The light next to the bed didn't work but the beautiful view more than made up for it. I was surprised that the hotel staff was unaware of a sold out Annual Marathon for the benefit of the areas largest Children's Hospital but, not everyone is in to fitness ; - )

Upon checkout I asked Lara if I could mail a package from the hotel. She replied that it was not a problem. I gave her the box, shipping information, and account number. She arranged to prepare the box for shipping and asked if it was ok to ship by a certain carrier as she passed by it on her way home! Box arrived safe and sound. Thank you Lara. I will be sure to return to the Crowne Plaza Brookhollow my next trip to Houston!

One of the reasons I booked this Comfort Inn is because of the wonderful service I had at the Comfort Inn in Oakland. Maybe these people need to talk to Oakland. We went to breakfast at 9:10 and were told we couldn't get anything to eat. I talked to the manager and showed him the flyer in the room saying breakfast went until 9:30 (their flyer) and he said it was an old form and the breakfast ended at 9:00. I said I based my coming down to breakfast according to their information and booked the Inn because they served breakfast. While bickering with him, the woman cleaning up the breakfast area let someone else in to grab a few pre-packaged pastries. They did let us eat a few of the breakfast items. I will say, if you are white, you won't be treated as nicely as if you are not. The front desk people weren't very friendly either.

Had a great stay at the hotel. Rooms small but very clean.The staff were very efficient and courteous. The AC was a bit noisy. Very convenient to subways - very central. World trade centre within walking distance.Great cafe next door which served fabulous coffee. Great experience and would definately come back.

title_masked: ok hotel rooms were decent area not so great
text_masked: The hotel is located across the street from ground zero, noisy construction was really annoying at 7 am when i was trying to sleep in.. There is no internet in the rooms, and in the lobby it was like 20$ for internet, just plain ludicrous. The rooms were okay, nothing special, decent size and mostly clean.

title_masked: A wonderful, classy hotel in a fantastic city
text_masked: We stayed for four nights in the Hotel and would recommend it to anyone. A fantastic location and a beautiful Hotel. The Hotel still has real character- it is like stepping back in time. Everything from the lobby, to the restaurants, to the rooms have real style and were well maintained. We enjoyed the food in both Murals and Randolphs and found it good value for money (huge portions!) Very friendly, helpful and professional staff.
We stayed in the new suite for our party. It was great and the balcony and view was amazing!

I stayed at the airport Marriott for three days while attending a conference at the hotel. I arrived at the airport about 8 PM, very tired after a 6 hour trip from L. A. Signs to walk to the hotel from the airport were clearly marked. It took about 7-10 minutes from terminal E to terminal B where the hotel is located. 
Check in was a breeze--very courteous. I asked for a quiet room on a high floor and was very pleased with my king room on the 11th floor. I ordered room service for dinner, which was amazingly quick and delicious. The bed was comfortable, and the linens were lustrous and soft. Very comfy sleep. Spacious and very clean bathroom. I heard no noise from the airport or from adjacent rooms. The hotel catered a good continental breakfast for the conference and a delicious lunch with many vegetarian entrees. Dinner at the hotel restaurant was fine. Not gourmet or fancy, but fine. I had the tomato soup and the quinua dish, with a glass of white wine. Service was friendly and fast.
Only a couple of quibbles: the pool was too cold. Perhaps the heater wasn't working while I was there. The pool and jacuzzi area were very pleasant, and I swam in spite of the chilly water. The jacuzzi was quite hot. The only other issue I had was that on the last morning, housekeeping had forgotten to leave paper cups for in-room coffee. I used a glass instead. 
The absence of wifi in my room was not inconvenient for me, as I could check my email and internet via my phone service on iphone and ipad. 
I booked with the hotel directly, and got a AAA rate of $111 per night, which I thought was a good deal for the amenities, convenience and friendly staff. Usually I book on Price line, but I wanted to stay at this hotel specifically because of the conference. I would stay here again if i needed to be near the airport.

title_masked: Great hotel, easy walk to broadway shows
text_masked: Nice hotel, clean and comfortable. Had a reading light problem and it was fixed the next day. The concierge was not real helpful. We asked her to get us a taxi for an early flight, and she said, "this is New York City and there will be taxi's lined up in the morning.". Of course they weren't, and we had to walk down around the corner and hail one. The first day we asked for help with some shows and we felt like we were bothering her. Other than that can't complain. Really great location.

I stayed at this hotel because it is where my seminar was held. What a great location! It's 5-10 minutes from SeaTac airport so I was able to take a later flight in to Seattle and an earlier flight back home. With it so close, you'd expect to be in the middle of everything, but it's like an oasis! The beautiful hotel grounds border wetlands and I enjoyed a lovely evening walk. The only downside to this was that I didn't need to use the beautiful fitness room. It was fun to see the chef's garden as well. The facility is beautiful and the rooms are very nice. If I'd have thought of it, I would have checked the pillows before I went to bed & requested others - mine were a bit hard. There's a nice living room in each building - with 24-hour snacks (yogurt, string cheese, fruit, candy) and chilled, bottled water - how thoughtful!

title_masked: Don't waste your hard earned money on this place.
text_masked: We spent 3 nights. The rooms were small and layout of the building was confusing. Rooms seemed clean when we arrived but we had to request clean towels each day. The second day they didn't clean at all. Check-in was very slow. We booked 4 months in advance and didn't get the room with 2 queens we had requested. There are a lot of hotels in downtown Seattle. We'll pick a different one next time.

Billy in Security was a huge help during our stay at the Hilton San Diego Resort. He took the time to help me fill out paperwork so I could ship my luggage at the end of our say. I appreciate the time he took to help me....great service. Thank you Billy!

The Hotel is incredible. It has that feeling of living in The city not a Hotel feel about it.And to have an address like 5 ave.that would be nice. The Staff was helpful from the front door to your room.The room was huge compared to most hotel rooms in the city. The decor. is very nice and very clean. Fresh flowers were waiting and a box of chocolates. Had an incredible time. I will be back!

My family and I stayed at the Hyatt on Wacker Dr. on March 27, 2012. We were excited about the great price we got for your 4-star hotel through priceline. Unfortunately, we were not impressed. In the past, we have stayed at the Hyatt in downtown San Diego for spring break on the Marina, but chose to stay closer to home this year. The room was not clean to our standards when we arrived, even though we paid for an upgrade. We asked for it to be cleaned while we were sight seeing and were assured it would be looked after. Upon our return, nothing had been moved in the room to re-clean including the tea my sons had made prior to our excursion so I can only assume, it wasn't even checked as promised. We only had 3 towels for the 4 of us and had to call for more. They were promptly delivered but room service took 40 + minutes to deliver us a knife and corkscrew we essentially paid for because we felt compelled to tip even though we had to call and ask for it twice! The curtains were dirty and frayed by the vacuuming, the bed skirt had a foreign stain on it, the honor bar/fridge was gouged and dirty, too! The mirror was dirty and the beds appeared to have been jumped on - not neat and tidy at all....There were boxes of trash in the hall and an old refrigerator or two as well. Very disappointing to say the least. I have buyer's remorse and wish we had just taken the train home and stayed in our own beds! We were compensated for our upgrade - $20.00 but given the price of parking, taxes, and etc. at this point I wouldn't recommend this Hyatt to anyone. My husband travels and uses his Hyatt business travel points quite often and also expected better from your 4-star hotel. 
I felt compelled to let you know how unhappy we were with your facility.

As a former 12 year resident of Dallas, I know where to go, and where to avoid.
When my trip to Dallas was being planned, the Warwick Melrose was my hotel of choice.
From the charming structure, with all it's lovely architectural details, to the fantastic location & welcoming staff - once I arrived I knew I had made the right decision.
My room was spotless, comfortable, and tastefully decorated. My special instructions for breakfast by room service were followed without fail. The staff made me feel welcomed, important, and accommodated my every request, cheerfully. Even sending a housekeeper to steam my shirt at the last minute, before I scurried away to host a very special dinner.
The property maintains a very nice SUV, which gladly dropped me off, as well as picked me up, several times around town during my stay; an immense convenience. 
I travel often, always staying in the finest hotels, and would stay no where else. The Warwick Melrose is my hotel of choice in Dallas. And that's saying a lot, in a city with so many upscale properties to chose from.

We stayed at the Hotel Edison the first week of April and couldn't have been happier. We had a junior suite with plenty of room. The room was nicely furnished and super clean. We had a corner room with a great view of Times Square on the 18th floor. The location of the hotel couldn't have been better. We felt like we were in the middle of the action with all kinds of activites, theaters and sights within walking distance. The subway was only a short walk away. The only complaint that we had was that we would have liked a bigger bathroom with three gals! The staff was very helpful from the front desk to the doorman giving advice--- Highly recommend the hotel to all.

I have stayed at the Extended Stay America of Houston - Westchase for two and a half months now, and I could not be happier with my experience. The Hotel employees have made me feel at home and several have become friends of mine. The Hotel employees are extremely friendly, accomadating, and helpful with anything you need. The Hotel is very clean and well kept, not to mention it is in a great location.

Charming boutique hotel in a great neighborhood! Pillows, bed, rain shower head, and robes were better than I've had at more expensive hotels. View was meh and suite layout was odd but overall it was a lovely stay.

We picked this hotel since we had tickets to three games at Fenway. Our last experience in Boston was that it can be difficult to get a cab back to the main hotel area. This location was perfect - a six minute walk to the game. You can see Fenway from some of the hotel windows. 
Hotel is top notch - lovely rooms, great service. Very clean, all the amenities. 
My only negative comment is that room service (provided by Eastern Standard - a very good restaurant in the hotel) and the menu is a bit limited after 11 pm. We also liked the oyster bar restaurant. 
Overall a very good stay although I'm not quite sure why it's the top rated hotel in Boston - if we weren't going to baseball, we would have thought it was a bit out of the way! However, it is only a five or ten minute walk to Newbury Street. 
We would stay again - especially if we were going to multiple baseball games.

We stayed at this property mainly due to its proximity to the Verizon Center because wwe were in town for a Washington Caps hockey game. We found the entire Penn Quarter (the name of that whole area) to be filled with great restaurants, bars, shops, close to subway, across the street from the Spy Museum. The hotel was clean, the staff friendly; they even offered cookies and hot chocolate every afternoon!

title_masked: Ideal location - great for a large corporate hotel
text_masked: I was in San Antonio for a conference this month - and the Westin was the location of the conference. The hotel was extremely busy - but all of the staff was attentive, professional and courteous. Much of the Riverwalk is very busy, noisy, and touristy. But the Westin is located on a tranquil part of it. At the river level is the bar and the restaurant Zocca. As of this writing, Zocca is the #1 restaurant on TripAdvisor. I can only vouch for their breakfasts (you have a choice of an extensive breakfast buffet or you can order off the menu) and the lunch. Both were very nice, but I did not eat dinner at Zocca. The bar at the Westin is also very nice - and it's very relaxing to have an drink at the outdoor patio and watch people and boats along the Riverwalk. My room was quiet - and the perfect size - with a large bed, extra chairs, and a desk. The maid service was great. I really have no complaints. I prefer smaller boutique-type hotels. But this hotel is definitely a cut ABOVE the usual chain, corporate hotel. I'm glad I stayed there!

We chose this property in a package deal(hotel, flight, car rental) was good buy. We were in room 171 a floor level room king bed with very generous size shower (no bathtub) with a nice patio and our view looks south across SD bay. From our room to the bays edge is about 150 ft or less. The onsite resturant menu is varied and food is quality, staff all were very very friendly and treated us very well. There is some noise from the helicopters and occasional jets the leave the naval base across the bay, as this is a major navy base area and security is noted, however the flights are not constant like a major airport, which U can hear the jets take off from SD Intl AP somewhat but that noise is somewhat muffled. We really enjoyed the nice cool temps (60s night, 70s daytime) as compared to our home in Texas near fort worth. Some inconvienent issues: the wall swithches that control the bathroom lights the overhead fan are all on timers. Not a problem for lights but we would fell a bit more comfort with a over fan on all night. The AC unit is mounted high, (over 65inches) therefore U cannot read the controls, U can see them and guess what mode U are in IE heat, AC and temp up or down. we loved the patio sit early in am drink coffee or a meal anytime. The gulls did not seem to land and bother us like we saw them do everywhere else around the bay. There are many resturants less than a mile. We think we would stay here again as we have family in Calif, (I grew up here in Pacific Beach on a surfboard)

Room was dark
Beds weren't very comfortable
Very low water pressure in shower
Clean room
Great staff
After a long day of work, I was helped extensively by the individuals at the front desk and treated nicely by Rocket at the bar. One of the better trips I have had in a long time.

Our biggest surprise was how much fun it felt to be in that neighbourhood. The hotel is on 3 different bus routes to downtown and only 1.5 blocks to the L and only a few blocks from Lakeshore to get onto the main roads. Very convenient on all fronts even though slightly further north than we might first have wanted to stay.
The hotel is spotless, lovely lovely clean rooms, great duvet and super comfortable beds. Service was excellent. Parking at $24 seems expensive until you realise that is what it would cost if you parked on the street and fed the meters... the hotel isn't making parking a profit centre!
Breakfast was very nice and served in a breakfast room. The drinks are all in one corner and that makes it a little chaotic. Most clientele seem to be younger and full of energy. We were there for the Springsteen concert and met many clients a little older and full of energy!! It is walking distance to Wrigley Field and Lincoln Park and the zoo.
We stayed 3 nights and it felt like home - we call that a home-run because so few budget hotels can make that feeling happen. More boutique than budget.. lucky us!
Only downside was the room a/c unit. It was loud and pointed at the bed... it needed a thermostat on the wall so that it didn't need to be on all night. We lined up the chair and spare pillows between the unit and the bed and that helped keep me (it was my side of the bed) out of the cold air stream.

Stayed for 2 nights in the Renaissance Seattle in March. Requested for a quiet room and we did not get any disturbance from the traffic noises. We did get disturbed by our neighbours next door blasting loud music during 1 night and i called up the front desk immediately. Very pleased that the music was stopped shortly afterwards. The staff during our check-in and check-out was nice and friendly. This hotel is walkable to Downtown and Pike Place market but beware of steep hills! Rooms were huge and beds were comfortable to sleep in. Overall i would recommend this hotel in Seattle and i will choose to stay here again when i return to Seattle!

Where to begin... All I have to say was this was absolutely the worst hotel experience I have ever had and will NEVER recommend this hotel to anyone!!! I came with my daughter's high school group for the Thanksgiving Day parade. When we arrived, Stephanie at the front desk, was not friendly at all!!! She seemed "put out" by having to do her job and deal with a group. Secondly, which was not as big of a deal we had specifically requested a King size room. The teacher told me that had contacted the hotel and they confirmed a king room for us. Obviously it did not happen. Then you had one elevator working to accommodate a sold out hotel!!!! Seriously- that is completely unacceptable. We stayed in room 817. Lets see- the room smelled of bleach, we got "baby pillows" on our bed, the were cigarette burns on the comforters, the sheets were stained, we had to sleep on top of the comforters, the ice box lid had been used as an ashtray, the housekeeping shoved 4 tissues in the tissue box, had an almost empty roll of toilet paper(no spare), the air conditioner worked when it felt like it, and the ice-machine was out so I had to go to the 6th floor and get ice there where all the construction was going on. Another room on that floor that actually had 4 high school students in it, had not been vacuumed and had white and purple pills on the floor!!!!!!! Are you kidding me????? Finally we asked the girl at the front desk how to get to Sonny's and she sent us walking in the opposite direction. Finally breakfast was just gross!!! The orange juice had crystals in it!!!! We had to stop on our way to the parade to get coffee and a bagel!
I have stayed at Days Inn, La Quinta's, etc so I am not a hotel snob! However while you may be doing renovations you still need to keep in mind that you have paying customers staying there and should not be treated like we were. You company should be embarrassed that people are staying in these conditions!!!!!

Stayed 4 nights in early May: huge room, nice views, great spa/pool/gym. The concierge and bellboys are very helpful. Everything works in this hotel! Safe location, convenient for Russian Hill and Nob Hill as well as access to places tourists go. (The Cathedral opposite is really worth entering too.) Would definitely return here. I couldn't speak highly enough of it.

title_masked: Great comfortable hotel in North Hollywood
text_masked: I really enjoyed this hotel very much. Very very comfortable, very quiet. It's easy access to buy foods, eat out .... I look forward to coming back to Sportsman's Lodge hotel soon.
We enjoyed our stay at the Westin. Our room was very nice with a great king bed. Staff were very nice and helpful. Good location near airport. Would stay again and recommend to family. Thanks Westin.

I stayed here with a friend while we vacationed in Phoenix. The hotel is spartan, but very clean and a good value. It was within walking distance to many activities and restaurants in downtown Phoenix. My only complaint was that the "breakfast" seemed more like a pre-breakfast snack to me (donut or apple and coffee) and wasn't available until 7 (we were up at 6 sometimes). We also had our windows open at night and heard the rabble across the parking lot most nights.

The location is very convenient to Broadway and Time Square. If your room faces the street be prepared for excessive noise. There is no access to coffee/tea or vending machines on site. Many of the rooms are extremely small. The staff are very friendly

We arrived in Chicago after a awful red eye flight on Spirit airlines at 7am. We took the Blue Line from O'Hare to the Clinton stop which dropped us off right at the hotel. While the hotel is pretty much surrounded by construction and a parking lot, the inside of the building took you away from the hustle and bustle that was outside. The exterior is not much to look at but the inside is clean and the staff was friendly. One particular staff, Bianca, saw how exhausted we were and did everything she could to get us into a room as soon as possible so that we could take a nap. She was amazing. We had a nice experience at this hotel. One suggestion...if you are a light sleeper, bring ear plugs. Each side of the hotel is on busy streets and if you are in an end room, you might be disturbed.

We stayed here while travelling for a wedding in Dallas. The first thing we saw upon arrival, a table of free cookies and hot apple cider! I don't know if it was because we had traveled all day, or if it because I'm 8 months pregnant, but that was enough for my high rating! 
We ate at the restaurant for dinner, where I had some of the best bass in my life, and ordered the room service for breakfast which was also good! ( expensive, but we were not paying ... maybe my rating would be lower if I saw the bill!) 
The gym is 24 hours which was great for me, as I get up quite early to workout. The pool had literally no one at it while we were there, which might be because we're from Canada and it was Dec... maybe it was too cold for people. 
Service was always good and the staff were friendly.

title_masked: Great for a night or two!!
text_masked: The Hyatt Regency is a great hotel if you plan only a short stay. We stayed for 7 nights and although the room was excellent, a good gym, nice pool and the staff very good, the little things that can make a difference were missing. We stayed friday to friday and were disappointed to find on friday,the main bar was shut at 10.30pm, on saturday it shut at 11.00pm even though there were plenty of guests requesting its services. From Sunday until we left it did not open again and the only bar available was in the on site restuarant! You may wonder why the fuss, well what the tourist guides and hotel info do not tell you is that although Downtown Houston has lots of restuarants and bars is that the majority shut by 9pm as they cater for the demands of the business people who work downtown during the day! After a day sightseeing and driving its nice too relax in the late evening at the bar and have a quiet drink or two with your travel campanions.There are other districts, but that means a taxi or long walk which we did, but after a long day you sometimes just want to stay local and relax. Another disappointment was that this hotel charges $9.95 a day for Wifi access which considering where it is and the type of client they target is quite unbelieveable, also be aware the cheapest charge for a days parking here is $15.00, valet parking is $30.00!! To sum up, a perfect place to stay for a night or two but no more and only for a business person certainly not for a family.

My wife and I stayed for our anniversary. We asked for a high floor room and we were given a beautiful corner room on the 33rd floor with a view overlooking downtown. We watched the fireworks right from our room. The executive lounge was great for breakfast, beverages, & snacks throughout the day. We had lunch at the sports bar restaurant off the lobby and slept peacefully on Marriott's signature bedding. What a wonderful weekend trip thanks to the JW Marriott!

Wow! I stayed at the Chatwal on October 6th for 1 night for a day trip visit to New York. I was greeted with exceptional service and smiles, from the doorman to the front desk attendant to the butler. I loved this hotel. The location is great, just a block from the main area of Times Square. When I checked into my room, I just walked around it in awe. It had a very chic modern feel with ample closets, huge tv, and bathroom mirror tv (that actually scared me at first), and a heated toilet seat! The bathroom is unbelievable. 
The bar was lovely with great attendants. The food was delicious at the bar and also room service. I was very grateful of the room upgrade (I'm a SPG member). 
I really must say that this hotel blew me away, and I can't wait to return, and I've stayed at The Ritz-Carlton, Park Plaza, Four Seasons, and other top-star hotels, but this took the cake. BEAUTIFUL. BEAUTIFUL. BEAUTIFUL. A MUST STAY.

title_masked: If you can stay here you must!!!
text_masked: What a fabulous hotel!! My family and I loved it here. The attention to detail is just unbelievable, and the personalized service. If you are considering any other hotel in Boston check our the Four Seasons before you book. The rate we paid here was the same as we would have paid at many other lesser hotels, thanks to a promo rate the Four Seasons was running. The location is great right at the public gardens and so close to everything! You can easily walk to many things or make use of their complimentary car sevice, which we did for a trip up to Fenway. The conceirge can help with all kinds of things and made some great reccomendations. Everyone of the staff is so friendly and helpful... what a great feeling that was. I can't say enough about this hotel what a beautiful place with great, great service.

Didn't have reservations for three women made six months in advance. small room no sofa a rollaway 15 dollars a day. hotel shows it's age. the noise of the frig was louder than the train that runs next door. the two star restuarant charges five star prices. some of the staff are friendly. There are plenty of taxis and walk to many points of interest but this is a business district. there is a mc donalds and cvs in the block. count your change at the mc donalds. there was only the view of the train tracks and an alley from room 573. the pool is seasonal. there is a gym and a laundry. weather permitting you can sit outside. some times there is entertainment but what we heard was really bad. I did not chose this hotel. I tend to prefer an upscale venue that is part of the vacation destination. but for the price it is better than a motel but not much. it was clean. there were many international school groups and families There is a deli that is only open early in the morning. there is a very busy star bucks attached.

title_masked: Perfectly located, Wonderful staff, Beautifully hotel!
text_masked:
First and foremost, the hotel was beautiful - very well appointed and quaint, which made a nice place go "home" to all week. The suite was very spacious. It was easily accessible to everywhere we wanted to go - very ideally located! The staff was also extremely helpful and kind.
My fiancé and I have been shopping for a new bed and we actually reached out to hotel management to find out the "make/model" of the bed they have in their rooms as it was one agreeably the most comfortable sleep we'd both had in quite some time.

I was a patient at MD Anderson medicla center and had major surgery and then had to go back for 6 weeks of raditaion.I stayed here both times.I was treated very well by everyone.Starting with the Director of Sales Shirley Perry she was wonderful.I felt very comfortable and well taken care of.They helped when I needed help and prayed when I needed prayers!.I will need to return in July and in Spetember and I plan to stay here both times I come back.I wanted to take a few minutes to recognize each member of the staff I came in contact with.
Aziz,Maria and Corey were the desk clerks,did all that needed to be done to take care of guests.Harold ,Kevin and Elmer were the shuttle drivers I relied on heavily to get to my appointments on time.they took me and picked me up everyday for my radiation. Manuel in houskeeping did a very good job as well as Patel the yard man.I appreciate their kindness and caring for me during my long stay that totaled about 2 1/2 months.I will recommend this hotel to anyone I know that is visiting Houston or MD Anderson.I am thankful to have found such a nice place to stay during a difficult time.

This hotel is very nice. It was close to all of my interests which makes it nice really handy. The personal we encountered were all very well trained and friendly. We did not eat there but the restaurant looked inviting. I would recommend staying there.

title_masked: Repeat guest, what keeps us coming back....
text_masked:
We recently stayed at the Sofitel for a family weekend trip to Philadelphia. We stayed there several times in the past and find it hard to consider other hotels in the general area.
The location is perfect for us. We like to travel on foot during our time in the city and the Sofitel is in a great location for sightseeing during the day and dining at night.
We enjoy the bar for after dinner drinks and people watching through the large windows. Travelling with a child, it is nice to have a place off to the side to relax after dinner but before bedtime. 
Breakfast is fantastic with fresh squeezed oj and super strong coffee. Breakfast was included in our room rate and we had the option of the buffet or ordering off the menu. I picked the buffet both days while my husband and son ordered off the menu. The buffet has European offerings such as cheeses, cured meats, fresh baked goods as well as American classics.
The staff shines at the Sofitel. Little things like bringing our son hot chocolate with our coffee service and a real glass (not a goofy plastic kid’s cup) for his club soda make a huge impression. It is a good feeling when the younger members of the family are treated like valued guests. 
Our room was on the 14th floor on the odd numbered side of the hall. The location was very quiet and we didn’t hear any street noise. Our request for a room with a view of Liberty Place was honored.
The beds were very comfortable and the quality of the linens and pillows was very good.
We had a superior room with a king bed for this trip and it was large enough. 
My only area of improvement that I would suggest is a sprucing up of the guest rooms, the finishes are starting to show some wear and tear.

title_masked: Some touches of Old San Antonio but overrated
text_masked: The room overlooking the Riverwalk with a small walkout balcony was kind of nice but not a suite advertised. The service was definately mediocre at best. The bed was very comfortable. The worst part was finding a sticky piece of candy stuck to the extra pillow. The location is good but anything on the Riverwalk is more or less similar. There are certainly nicer top properties, but there is cetain charm to the place.

Had a girls night out to shop at the Galleria, dine and spend the night. The rooms and bathrooms were spacious and updated. If you are booking try going directly through the hotel versus a travel website as I was able to book for about 100.00 less by calling the hotel and booked over the phone.

title_masked: $200 a night with a clogged bathtab
text_masked:
service is a major issue needless to mention the feeling when you would like to take a shower with no hot water and a clogged bathtab all for $200 a night way to go Westin :(
Service is another but an AMAZING few individuals the rest of the staff have a lot to learn....When living in the air there are only few things that matters,
...

This was a surprise to be so close to the airport and not hear the constant noise of the planes.
Beautiful grounds, wonderful beds and a gratis breakfast added to our stay. Great place if you need to be close to the airport; if not, you must have a rental car to get around. Very close to I-5, so it will take about 20 minutes to get downtown.The Southcenter mall is within 5 minutes of the lodge and offers a wide selection of stores and restaurants.

I usually stay at the Grand Hyatt when I'm in San Francisco. It's location is great, just one block from Union Square, but the rooms overlook the square itself. The rooms are good size and their recent renovation has improved the hotel. One of the best parts of the hotel is their restaurant/bar, which is on the 36th floor and gives you a wonderful view of the city. 
The staff is very friendly and accommodating. I've never been to the breakfast buffet, but have ordered room service for breakfast many times. Food is good and they are generally quick to bring it up. 
You won't go wrong staying at the Grand Hyatt.

As a business traveler, I know finding a property that will meet my familiy's needs is always a challenge. Upon visiting the Four Seasons Hotel Austin, it is clear that we have found our new weekend getaway. Our weekend began with Marlon's friendly greeting and suggestions for the weekend. Every suggestion was right on target! Our room was perfection and the views second to none. The kids loved playing on the lawn outside while my wife and I enjoyed a spectacular lunch on the veranda. The staff could not have done one more thing to make our trip anymore perfect. Thank you to everyone for making our vacation such a success!

Location - great, a few blocks from Penn station. 
Lobby - small, not much area to sit and meet with people. No bar.
Breakfast - continental breakfast. Muffins, hard boiled eggs, cereal. COFFEE. Nothing Earth shattering, but very nice considering it was included.
Room - Clean. Small - but that is standard in NYC. King bed room was fine for two guests. We did get a room with a view of the Empire State building - beautiful! 
Stayed in many hotels in this neighborhood, this is nicer than the Four Points and nicer than the Double Tree.

Everyone at the hotel was friendly and helpful, but Ester was amazing! She could not have been more helpful. She made us feel very much at home, yet very pampered. Thanks for making our vacation such a memorable experience!!!

title_masked: Oh no, its a conference centre
text_masked: This hotel was a disappointment as we did not realise it was a conference centre hotel. The lounge/bar area was full of delegates waiting for Crabby Hour and buying merchandise relating to their conference. The bar was unmanned. We did eat in McCormick and Schmuks which was excellent. We will not be returning.

title_masked: Overlook the location and you'll like this...
text_masked: Let's face it, you don't come here for the area ambiance, but it is certainly convenient to the airport. As you reach your room you will find wide hallways, clean carpeting, pleasant decor and, likewise, once you enter your room you will find the same. It's clean, the beds are very comfy pillow tops with nice, puffy duvet covers and plenty of pillows. We were only here for one night, arriving late and needing to leave early. The gentleman at the front desk informed us breakfast was available at 6:15AM and he said if we needed it earlier (which we did) just to call him in the AM and he would open up the breakfast room so we could at least have some coffee, juice and cereal before we departed. That was SO nice of him to do!! The wireless worked fine. Parking will likely mean you need to leave your key at the front desk because most spots are 2 deep. Perfectly fine motel.

title_masked: my stay at the hotel carter from may 9th-may11
text_masked: I really don't know what people are complaining about. I stayed at the Hotel Carter from May 9th till May 11th in room 2020 with my son and we had a very nice stay. The room was very nice, and the bed had clean bed linen and a warm blanket. The tv even though it had only local channels worked. The bathroom was nice and clean and we had a nice size closet. We were close to everything in times square, and we even took the subway train to union square. There was no noise at all while we were there. I would definately go back to this hotel again

I just completed a 5 night stay. I was in town for a conference. The hotel is located right next to the convention center. Everyone was great. The Bar Rojo and Grand Club staff were amazing. They truly made me feel welcome. The gym was very nice. Not too crowded. I also enjoyed the pool deck. They are adding a bar to it so it should be very nice once done. I cannot wait to return.

An awful experience. :-\ 
I actually had to book two hotels this trip because of downtown Chicago being sold out. I just came from a CHEAPER stay at the Conrad Hotel, that was probably 10-20 times better than this hotel. 
This hotel is extremely dated. There are stains on the carpet, scratches on the walls, poor sound proofing, small bathrooms (those who say they are bigger must not have been to many hotels recently) and a weird layout. While not the most uncommon in Chicago, you have to enter through one bank of elevators, go to the lobby on level two, and then proceed to another set of elevators to reach the rooms. Also not entirely uncommon, but still crazy, is a 50.00+ rate for valet. 
I have honestly, though, never paid such a price (329.00 per night) for such a poor quality room with a CRT TELEVISION. I honestly did not even know that they made these anymore, or if they did, that they were still functioning. Most of the channels on the TV received incredibly poor reception. Numerous complaints were not received well and I only received a response of, "Sir, these issues are completely out of my control until the hotel is remodeled." Um... okay. But you can't do anything to make it right? Not even, say, offer free internet, since you have to pay 10.00 for that, too? 
That's okay, Hyatt. Luckily, I was able to hop onto the FREE internet from the neighboring Fairfield Inn by Marriott.

This is the third time I've stayed here for business. It has all the basics: fitness, pool, bar. Granted this is not high end, but very comfortable and something for every travelor. Always a pleasant stay here that I appreciate.

My husband and I love this hotel. This is our spot for "staycations". Anytime there is a function in downtown Phoenix - we stay here. The rooms are cozy and the Hotel has so much character. The rooftop pool is our favorite place to hang. The staff is awesome. They gave me a nice discount just for being a repeat customer.
Hotel San Carlos will always be "our place".

I stayed at the Langham from May 17th to May the 22nd of 2012. I was in the area to attend 2 College Graduations and had an excellent stay at this hotel. I loved the room, the central location and the staff were all superb. Due to my hectic schedule, I was unable to enjoy the amenities and had to pass on the morning newspaper deliveries. I can easily recommend this classy hotel to friends and family. All the staff stood out and both Dan's and Keith are great. I will be back.

title_masked: Best Hotel near the University of Pennsylvania
text_masked:
We travel frequently to Penn and the Sheraton is always our first choice of places to stay. The hotel has been refurbished several times and the rooms are always well appointed and comfortable. The room views are outstanding. On one side the beautiful Penn campus is in full view in all its glory from Franklin Field to the Vet school. On the other side is Drexel. 
The staff is especially friendly and helpful. We go so often this is our "home away from home." Brenda in reservations is attuned to campus events and other happenings and does her best to fit you in if at all possible. This is different from other hotels with national and impersonal reservation systems.
 We tried the Inn at Penn once because it was hosting our event and were sorely disappointed. It is plush, but rooms are smaller and most views are of the sides of other buildings.

What a grand experience at the Arizona Biltmore. Luxurious ans well appointed. On property cafe and restaurant selection. Plenty of sitting spaces and groupings to enjoy conversation with friends. So glad to have experienced this unique property

title_masked: Many issues: Do not book the hotel through third party.
text_masked:
I stayed at Westin, Chicago River North for 4 nights for a business trip. I had booked the hotel through a third party website. We were a part of a conference delegates. The check in was fine. However, there were many issues subsequently. I was told that there is no free internet although the conference lodging information mentioned free internet in the room at this hotel. When asked for a clarification, the front desk told me that since the room was booked through a third party, this offer was not available to me. My other colleagues, who stayed at the other Westin, less than a mile away were offered free internet while they had also booked through a third party. So, I guess this hotel follows its own rules.
The quality of the beds was not up to the mark of other Westin properties and these were easily the worst beds of any business hotels I have stayed at. The refrigerator was not working well. The shower knobs in the bathroom rusted and only one of the two heads of "heavenly showers was working" and the water pressure was extremely poor. I expressed these concerns at the end of my stay to the check out desk. Finally at the end of this all, I see extra charge on my credit card without even an invoice sent to me. I have no idea what these charges are for. The restaurant was decent but serves their Egg-Benedict with fish instead of bacon.Who does that? I would not recommend the hotel, especially if you are booking it through third party. And it is not worth the price offered on the hotel website.
The rooms are beautiful ...bright ...and up to date. The staff is always friendly and very professional. I stay here when ever possible.
This property is great for the family, close to Seattle.Center. Staff is friendly and accommodating. They also have free breakfast every morning with lots to choose from.

title_masked: Need a good value SEATAC Hotel, this is it!
text_masked:
One of the best complimentary breakfast spreads I have encountered. Terrific. Lots of choices. Hot and cold. 
Clean affordable rooms. Only a couple minutes by shuttle from the airport.
Staff are very friendly.

We enjoyed the comfort of the hotel and its support. We made use of the dining/bar & room service for our meals & entertainment and were very pleased. The desk service and information center along with the doorman and van availability were resources that were extremely helpfull for our four day stay. The pool and exercise room are excellent and well maintained. .

This hotel is very conveniently located. We took the train into NYC and easily walked with luggage the few blocks to the hotel. Rooms are small (Hey, remember, this is NYC!), but comfortable and clean. Typical Hampton Inn complimentary breakfast offered lots of choices and a good start to a busy day.

This is a good quality budget motel that we chose after reading Trip Advisor reviews. There were three of us so we had 2 king beds and a very spacious room. It really was a little too far from Beale St as we did not have a car ( $13 taxi ride) but for the price it was ok. Airconditioning was very noisy. The friendliest person was the house maid who was extremely helpful with local knowledge.

title_masked: Nice overall with a couple issues
text_masked:
Good: This hotel has a great location on Union Square, which is walkable to the Moscone Center and lots of the SF things to do. Nice rooms, very spacious with good housekeeping. Clock Bar was nice, and the service was prompt, even though they were busy.
BAD: I was disappointed in the check-in. Waiting in line a long time, over twenty minutes, only to be told there were no rooms available at that time. It was 2pm so slightly before check-in time, but was still frustrated that they wasted my time. Was awoken by disgruntled unions picketing and yelling on a bull horn at 7am, which was even more frustrating. Slow and full elevators were very common.
It's a convention hotel so I get that they had a big group while I was there. Good to know for the future.

Based on the other reviews I chose Andaz from a list of 10 other hotels offered by our corporate travel agency. And I wasn't sorry one little bit. The staff was welcoming and very ayentive, the room convenient and relaxing. The semi-transparent door and window to the show didn't bothered and my daughter so it was not a big deal at all. Free snacks and non-alcoholic drinks also added to our pleasure. We stayed there only one night as later we were moved to another hotel closer to my office but I would prefer to stay in this nice hotel situated n the relatively quiet area and get to the office by metro that is comveniently located. So, we were very sorry that it was only a one night out of 6 in New York. The room was booked to me but they let my daugter stay without any additional payment and it was a nice surprise. By the way there was some movie shoting just outside the hotel at the day of our stay and it was very entertaining to watch.

Just completed a three night stay at Affinia 50 with my wife and two teenage sons (ages 19 and 17) and would definitely recommend. Everyone we dealt with from the hotel staff, including front desk, housekeeping, concierge, doorman, etc. were extremely friendly and helpful. Any request we made (extra pillows, towels, etc) was handled very promptly and positively. We chose a junior suite with two queen beds with a separate living area with sofa sleeper and were amazed at the size of the room when we walked in. There was more than enough space for us all to spread out during the limited time we spent in the room. The beds were comfortable, bathroom was adequate size with a great shower, and the kitchen was handy. My wife is very picky about hotel cleanliness and this met her high standards. Nice big flat screen TVs in both rooms for late night or early morning viewing. I'm an early riser and particularly enjoyed the second floor lounge area in the mornings for free coffee, newspaper and wireless internet while letting the family sleep in a little. I do recommend skipping the continental breakfast and taking the short half block walk to either Ess-a-Bagel or the NY Luncheonette for a great breakfast. The hotel location was great and in easy walking distance of 5th Ave shopping, Rockefeller Center, Grand Central Terminal, Central Park, and Times Square. Subway access was very convenient and easy. To be complete and add balance, our only concern with the hotel was with traffic noise but it really didn't bother any of us substantially. All in all, Affinia 50 exceeded our expecations in every way and we would definitely stay again.

title_masked: Close to the Rock, functional and clean hotel
text_masked: Have stayed at this hotel a few times in the last year. Check-in and check-out were easy. Most recently had a standard queen bed room which was more spacious than their club-size room. I liked the second window that was overlooking the west side of the property. The additional sunlight was great. The bed wasn't as good as the ones at nearby Hilton or Sheraton, but still alright. There's a self-serve water bottling station on every other floor. Location of the hotel was unbeatable - Rockefeller Center, 5th Avenue, Central Park and Time Square all within walking distance. There was road construction going on the 51st street, and it was very loud and this was going on through past midnight! I think this will continue for another 2 to 3 weeks. Maybe choosing a room facing north will be less affected.

My wife and I stayed here for 5 days. Great service, exceptional people running this hotel -- from the concierge, to the front desk, to the housekeeping and all the way to its manager. 
Although we stayed in a room on the 3rd floor facing the street, we slept pretty well and did not find the room noisy at all. The park suite was wonderfully appointed. One thing that impressed me was how the hotel tried to be ecologically responsible, not just the run of the mill save detergent by saving your towel to save the environment thing, it was something much more than that. The hotel went all out in involving itself in being truly a green hotel.
complimentary wine tasting in the late afternoon and hot drinks in the morning were wonderful services. Areas in the hotel worth visiting and enjoying are the walking/jogging track in the 3rd floor, which I use for quiet time by sitting and reading a book. The lobby with the fireplace is a favorite too.
The location of this hotel is difficult to beat, it is near everything--10 minute walk to the ferry building, its also near china town, near union square, near market street, near public transportation stations too!
It has a wonderful Japanese restaurant as well worth visiting, or if you are tired, you can order in and eat in the comfort of your room

Bonus! We were able to use a TripAdvisor $20 food/drink coupon for the Magnolia to offset the $25 valet parking fee. The rooms are well sized, and the shower has enough room to swing a dead cat. A couple of the elevators were out of use, so waiting for one elevator was a bit lengthy as everyone was checking out on Sunday, as was the wait for the valet to retrieve cars. However, with free breakfast (french toast, potatoes, cereal, oatmeal, coffee, juice) , no complaints here. A Starbucks is conveniently located next door, and there is free Wifi in the rooms. Location is great, only about a mile from the American Airlines Center to see a Stars or Mavs game. Valet was very pleasant, even with the rush. We will likely return here.

Location is Wonderful! walking distance to many must see sights of New York. Staff was great and very friendly. Rooms were small but we didnt spend much time in them. The bar down stairs was convenient. Lots of choices for food conveniently located within a few block radius. 
About a 30min / $65 cab ride to JFK (we hit very little traffic on our ride)

I stayed at the Boston Harbor a few weeks ago, as a colleague booked it first and I choose to stay near him rather than book at a separate hotel. My first room was so loud that it seemed like the elevator control room was in my hotel room. There were constant sounds of people talking in the corridors, and even a dog barking away around 1 or 2am. I got about 3 hours of sleep that night. I got moved to the 'quieter' tower. I was taking a conference call from the room around 3pm and could literally hear the jangling keys and rustling of a garbage bag by one of the housekeepers walking by. I then checked out and moved next door to the Intercontinental. I would never re-book at this hotel until they figure out some sound attenuation. It's sad, because it is classic Boston with beautiful views and good restaurants, and a stellar location. I have stayed at the Liberty, Intercontinental, Ritz, Beacon XV and W and have not had any sound issues to this extent, and I have spent roughly 25 nights in hotel rooms in Boston over the last 8 months.

title_masked: Covnenient location, classic hotel, but not worth it
text_masked:
I got this room using Hilton points so it was worth it in that respect, but if I had to pay the $400+ they were looking for a room on the same night, I would not have been to pleased. It wouldn't be my first choice in Chicago as there are several other nicer hotels for the same money. I was stuck here due to the Chicago Marathon going on the same weekend. Such is life.
As for the hotel, it is old and classic. It's great looking in a great location with an impressive lobby. So they get points for that. The negatives: long check-in lines. There are many rooms in this hotel but they don't have the check-in staff to keep up with it. Also the walls are paper thin. I had a terrible night's sleep here due to that. You could hear doors slamming all night long along with rude people (not the hotel's fault) shouting all night in the hallways as they come home drunk. While the hotel cannot control its people, they can have better doors/walls something. You can hear someone sneeze next door and for some reason our toilet would run for a second every 5 minutes or so. 
The rooms are small, but that is to be expected. If you're one who likes to enjoy their hotel while on vacation and spread out in the room, I wouldn't stay here. If you're here for a night and want to be in a hotel that is very convenient and right outside a red line subway stop, then this is it. 
I wouldn't stay here again unless I had to, long story short.

Great hotel,so many people to help you with everything you need or need to know,they have people for everything and are only to glad to help.Rooms are fantastic and big,cleaned to a high standard.In the evening there is security at the lifts and you have to show your keycard to even get in the elevator.A personal limmo to the airport was only 75d well worth it,yes we did try the airport shuttle but the looney driver has put us off doing that again.The famous Tic Toc diner has a walk through to the hotel and is open 24h.The Empire State Building is just a 5 min walk away,this hotel is very well located and near to all the top sights,Times Square, 10 min walk.
Book and pay for your show tickets online from the theater,you can print them off at home and just show them at the box office when you go this will save you a lot of time queueing for ages trying to get cheap tickets with not good seats.
Be prepared to tip a lot,the whole place relies on them,you usualy get a choice of between,15,18 or 20% on top of the bill.Three of us where there for 5 days and we tipped around 150d in various places, but hey if your going NYC you´ll be taking a few bob anyway.If you rearly want to see as much as possible then do as much walking as you can,tour busses are OK but you need to be on the ground to take it all in.
Happy Holidays and get booking now,you´ll have the time of your life,we did,Oh,it was our daughters 21st birthday present.

First off, our stay here was not without its problems. We had two situations that could have been holiday wreckers - but the very things that make this hotel such and awesome experience: the people, the service and the drop-dead fabulous property saved the day.
There's something very reassuring about a provider who acknowledges when there's an issue, doesn't try to fudge it and then works overtime to make it right.
We enjoyed a wonderful 10 days here, all up, in the Clocktower room. The complimentary breakfast was basic but a God send, budget wise. We also made the most of the free evening Happy Hour and met some lovely people.
The rooms here are enormous and beautifully furnished. Twice daily housekeeping, evening turn down, plush robes and lovely amenities give the place a real luxury hotel feel - but with all the benefits of a plush holiday apartment with all the amenities.
Loved it all and we'll definitely be back.

I travel to Memphis several times a month for business and stay at this hotel all the time. The staff treats each guest like family members. The hotel has recently been remodeled and has a very modern vibe. The rooms are all large and the beds are very comfortable. You will not be sorry if you choose this place.

The people running this hotel could not be nicer. Even the appearance of the room once in it is not unpleasant. The price (early November 2012) was around $85 with tax, so reasonable in my opinion. I picked it because I was familiar with the prosperity of the shopping just east of Beltway 8 and all of the Katy exits further west. But it's like everything around Wilcrest, all the way down to Westheimer, has been forgotten. It's a very old building, and kind of depressing. Every step you take you are looking at something that is scarred, torn, cracked, or run-down. It's just a little part of Houston that is not for those wanting that new and safe feeling.

title_masked: You can't exist on name alone.
text_masked:
I found a place on Earth where the laws of physics cease to exist: room 3322 at the Fairmont Chicago. Let me explain. Upon check in my room was hot. I hate being hot. I cannot sleep when I'm hot. I'm irritable when I'm hot. The outside temps while I was in Chicago were upper 40s to lower 50s during the day and upper 30s to lower 40s at night. Why was the room so hot??? I found the thermostat on the wall. You can adjust the temp down or up and the fan speed down or up. I turn the temp down to 60 (lowest it will go) and the fan speed to high. This resulted in a tiny little trickle of air dribbling out of a tiny vent in the wall that looked like it was about to fall out. This was clearly not going to cool the room off. Suprisingly, the room had two windows that cracked open at the bottom around 5 inches. I opened both of them. It's cold outside. The wind is blowing fiercely. Surely my room will be cold in no time. Nope, it barely made a dent. What in the world is going on? I felt like I was the victim of a practical joke. 
Moving on... 
Hotel managers need to understand that people care more about being able to control their room temp than whether or not the soap came from some boutique where rich people would shop. 
Hotel managers also need to understand that putting a gross, scratchy coverlet and boudoir pillows upholstered in gross, scratchy material on the bed is a waste of time. They get thrown on the floor, and they never get washed. People want a nice, CLEAN bed. 
Overall, the room was nicely designed in modern, low key decor. The bathroom was nice, appointed in marble. Seperate shower and tub. Although, i did find a clump of hair in the bath tub that was not mine because I didn't take a bath, and I don't have any hair on my body that was that long or that color. If I'm dropping $300 on a room, I better not find anyone else's hair in the room. I know the cleaning staff has to be very thorough to accomplish this, but what the hell? It's the Fairmont right? It's $300 a night right? That's a freakin car payment. Clean the rooms!
You ever notice how the higher the room rate, the more you have to pay out of pocket for simple stuff. I'm paying several hundred dollars a night and you can't float me a cup of coffee and a stale doughnut??? Hell, $60-100 a night hotels give you a damn buffet in the morning or at least a cup of coffee and some breads. It's not the highest quality, but it's hot and contains caffeine. I've stayed in a $700 a night hotel, and they had a very nice, free breakfast including fresh yogurt and berries. Maybe the middle ground is where you get screwed, or maybe it's stingy ownership? 
Hotel feel: They're attempting to be as hip as possible while still being low key. The result is one of the darkest hotels I've ever been in. The lobby was lit like a club, and they even played some sort of ambient yet upbeat techno in the mornings I guess to get people pumped for the day. I don't know. The rooms were also very dark. You could turn on every light in your room, and it would still look someone turned on a couple of weak lamps. I don't like pooping in the dark.
Location: boring. There is a CVS across the street, which is nice if you can't afford a $5 mini bar Coke. It is one block north of Millennium Park, one block east of Michigan and one block south of the Chicago River and Whacker, but it felt so removed from the action. I'd much rather be on Michigan or around the corner from Michigan or on the river. I guess I'm being picky, but there are tons of hotels in Chicago that have much better locations and are probably much less expensive.
My view was nice, The room faced east so you could see Lake Michigan and a nice little park that bordered the University of Chicago. I would have preferred a south facing room to see the museum campus and Michigan Ave. I've never really considered Lake Michigan around Chicago very pretty.
Overall, you can spend this much and do much better IMHO. Do you research. Don't swoon over the Fairmont name. At least not at this location.

title_masked: Cold water and lack of proper parking spots
text_masked:
I stayed in the room and was never sure what temperature the water would be. Sometimes it would be hot and get hotter. Sometimes it would go from hot to cold, all in the same shower. That problem is enough to make me not want to return. 
Also, the parking spaces were in short supply and were physically short. Because the spots were so small, cars and trucks were over lines both sideways and lengthwise. Denver has SUV's and this lot made no provision for them. I did not have a big SUV but I could only park in the back with my passenger getting out to help though I even had a rear view camera.

Just completed our 4th or 5th stay at this hotel. I host a small group of 15-20 here every six months. Since staying here the first time our group won't even discuss going anywhere else. The convenience of flying in and connecting to the hotel is great but it is the quality of the property, the staff and the amenities that make it outstanding. The rooms are modern, clean and comfortable with huge well insulated windows that give you a great view of the runways without the noise. The food in the main dining restaurant The Met is outstanding. The meeting rooms are large, bright and comfortable. Finally, the staff is outstanding in every way from front desk, to bell staff to banquet and AV. Be sure and ask the concierge for a pass to use the first class screening line when it's time for your flight.

Went to San Francisco for an athletic event. We couldn't believe our luck at the location. A few steps to Dragon Gate to Chinatown,, we were able to eat well and sight see on foot. The beds were like clouds. We really liked the Eco aspect of the hotel, and how quiet it was in the midst of bustling San Francisco. I am planning to stay here again when I come to San Francisco, or just make an excuse to come back.

We had stayed at a chain motel prior to our stay at Old Town Inn. It was a wonderful surprise and makes you realize that independent motels can and do provide better service. I booked here after reading the reviews and although I couldn't book online, a phone call provided me with a choice of rooms. I chose a room on the 2nd floor that had a kitchenette. It was quiet. You never heard anyone going by or from the upper floor. The staff, before and during our stay, were extremely friendly and helpful. The room was clean and quiet and had everything we needed throughout our stay. I've never stayed at a motel that provided real china and silverware for the continental breakfast! That area was always clean and well stocked and we always found a table even though the motel was sold out. The pool area was also clean and very pretty with all the flowers and shrubs.
We were able to walk to Old Town or take the trolley to the downtown area. We used the trolley to go to a Padres game and it was so much better than dealing with parking! It was close to everywhere we wanted to go. It is in an industrial neighborhood but I never felt uncomfortable. It's well lite and a charming motel. I would definitely stay here again if I was in the area.

title_masked: Classic Stay that resembles Ritz in London
text_masked: This hotel is known for its reputation from the past. Still a very nice hotel, lots of renovation done in the past years. Rooms are nice, especially suite 1936. Furniture is French 1800 / 1850 style, very heavy. Room service was very good, you would like the demotic control in the room. It was my 3rd stay at this hotel, usually we go to the Oak Room but now closed. Your restaurant options are very limited. Hotel bad had a good band, and serving a good variety of drinks. Expensive but a must for one time stay in NY. Location not the best but good.

Attended a 4 day corporate retreat - we slept, met and ate at the Doubletree in addition to some outings that were coordinated with the help of the sales and event staff.
