Rooms were some of the cleanest I have seen in a long time. Banquet server Eileen (hope that is her right name) was amazing and professional and very caring. The front desk staff were great - always professional and super helpful. The transportation arrangements went GREAT! I recommend the Doubletree for sure.

Stayed this past week for my sisters graduation. What a great area. I was able to walk around the city and city park (the commons) and get a cool feel of the city. Weather was awesome, went to the pool and was amazed by the deck. Full panoramic view of the city. Rooms were very nice and you can tell this is a brand new hotel. Coming From NYC and staying at hotels there, this was in same league. (Red Sox/Yankees)
I had a great time and everyone was friendly and helpfull.

title_masked: Customer Service is Alive and Well in Denver
text_masked:
I stayed here at the Residence Inn for three nights in May, the customer service was awesome. Kennisha at the front desk went way above and beyond to make my stay so great!
The suites are clean and well maintained, the service impeccable. You will love the location, close to everything. I definitely recommend the Residence Inn in Denver!

title_masked: Great place to Stay on a Budget.
text_masked:
2nd time for this property. I was attending CEDIA show in Indianapolis. Picked me up at airport promptly. I had a package sent to the Hotel and it was there when I arrived, no hassle. Staff friendly, room clean, pool and hot tub a bonus. Free breakfast was surprising. Beds comfortable. 
Excellent value overall.

Arriving at the Fairmont, you first find doormen in 1920 swank garb. Cool! Inside the lobby, you get the feel that I can best describe as "old California opulence." There is a light grandness, not the East Coast or Midwest dark woods grandness. Lots of light colors and light marble.
The front desk could have been a little better staffed, but the wait wasn't too long.
The room, however, was incredible. It was almost as big as the first apartment my wife and I rented out of college when we lived (in all places to compare) in Palo Alto, only a bit up the road. Lots more light marble. A separate make-up room and an almost walk-in closet. A separate water closet. A bath tub separate from a glass enclosed shower. The only small sad detail was the water fixtures were clearly dated and worn by abrasive cleaner.
(Important to note: on leaving, I checked with the front desk: this was a STANDARD room)
Upon returning to the hotel after supper at Maggiano's Little Italy (review to come), there was an incredible jazz quartet playing in the lobby. There was an enthusiastic audience gathered. I was sad that I was still on East Coast time and needed to get to bed... I would have loved to stay and listen.
I was granted a late checkout which was efficient and non-eventful.
Every staff I spoke to was articulate and courteous. 
Other reviewers have noted that there are PLENTY of eating options near by. I can saw that that was my observation as well.
Kudos to the Fairmont and their staff. It is a pleasure to write a review of a great place to stay and recommend.

I've stayed in a lot of fancy hotels before, but there is something special about the Adolphus. At 100 years old it has all of the charm of an old European hotel and all of the modern comforts of a mega-chain 5-star. The staff were all super helpful. 
Only complaints were that the elevators were a bit small (or charming) and slow, and the TV system had so many options I couldn't figure out how to just watch "regular" TV. But with complimentary WiFi, I had all the entertainment and productivity that I needed!

title_masked: If it looks like a duck, smells like a duck...
text_masked:
5 star=Ritz
4 star=Marriott
3 to 3.5 stars=Affinia Gardens
Room size was huge for any hotel, anywhere. 
Decor was extremely dated. Wall paper was old. Carpet was old. Bathrooms need to be recaulked. However, if you are looking for a value and need space, then this is perfect. 
Great location, and very quiet. 
Best Bell Desk. Helpful and friendly.

This was the starting point for a family trip with people flying in from different locales. It had what I was looking for: free shuttle from airport, free parking, and free breakfast. I signed up for the Club Carlson card and got on the promotion through the end of the year that is stay one night and get one free at any of their hotels. So it was a great value and a nice hotel.

This is a very good little hotel. The rooms were not huge but comfortable. The beds were comfortable and the rooms were clean. There was a nice restaurant in the place. It is close to Pike Market and the mono rail to Space Needle. Sadly this place may be replaced by some Amazon.com office towers.

the rooms are well equipped, very clean and quite new.
location is very convenient, across the street is the seattle center and the space needle is 10 minutes walk away
behind the hotel there are cafes, restaurantes and a safeway supermarket.

My sons and I were traveling back from a baseball tournament in coral springs and stopped here at midnight. I didn't notice much at first glance except that there was a guard sitting in the lobby. I should have left at that point. I thought perhaps he was staying there. I was so tired I simply got the key to our room. We had to park in back and take an old elevator to the third floor. You then walk on an outside cat walk to get to the room. It is more of a motel style. The pool looked dirty with an empty pizza box floating in it. The room itself although old, didn't look dirty. We were in bed for about 45 mins when we heard what could have been firecrackers, although it had just rained when we got there. My son felt it was gunshots. I said I would call the front desk to find out what was going on. The phone had no dial tone. We instantly packed up and checked out. Guard was still in the lobby when I left.

Hotel is next to Rockefeller center and close to Times square. Very close to buses and subways.
Rooms are great. Very clean. Very good service and help with recommendations to restaurants and directions. Separate access to fitness room and living room with free use of computers.

Not much to say but that it's dated like other users have already said, dirty carpets and torn furniture. Location is probably the only good point. Staff is friendly but doesn't compensate for the dirty rooms. Saw the housekeeping come in and "clean" the room in 10 minutes, changed sheets as requested, did a quick bathroom run around, sprayed a disinfectant and left. No vacuum or dusting. Carpets feel dirty to walk on and I wonder why the management cannot get it steam cleaned after each guest leaves if it cannot be replaced. Curtains seemed like they haven't been washed in months. Bathrooms are dated and during my stay no one cleaned the bath tub once. Overall I liked the staff for most part but I wouldnt recommend this hotel for more than an overnight stay.

title_masked: THIS IS THE WORST HOTEL STAY EVER
text_masked:
DO NOT STAY HERE...
We asked for a weekly rate in July of 2012 as we are moving out of town. My children and I were given a room that looked like it hadn't been vacuumed in weeks, the faucet leaked, the shower leaked, and the outlets didn't even work correctly. No one has stayed on the opposite side all week probably because its condemned. The paint is peeling from the ceiling of the walk-ways. My kids were with me and both said they would rather have gone camping. Keep driving. With in 3 miles there are a host of other choices....
A very friendly hotel especially for extended stays. I was recently there for 5 days and when you would walk in the door you would be greeted with Welcome Home. A very nice touch.

title_masked: Outstanding Hotel near shopping and restaurants
text_masked: This is one of the nicest Doubletrees around...besides their great cookies, this Doubletree has a special floor for Hilton hhonors members and an Exeuctive Lounge on the top floor for gold/platnimum member with wonserful breakfas ( eggs benidict when we stayed)t and evening snacks and drinks. Wow!

Overall this was a good stay. The hotel is in a great location. You can see it is dated and a little worn in the common areas such as the halls, elevator, lobby, etc. The service was great. The room was spacious, clean, and updated. The bed was comfortable My only complaint was the wake up call that I received 15 minutes late. Thankfully I only use wakeup calls as a backup. The indian restaurant directly across the street..mmmmmm.

title_masked: Just what I was hoping for!
text_masked: Stayed here just last night - needed a place to stay on my drive home from Tampa to Pgh, and got just what I had hoped for .. great price, nice room, very quiet, good nights sleep. I'll be back to stay here on my next return trip from Florida!

Girlfriend and I stayed here in September of 2012. We really liked it here.
Got there super early because we took the redeye in from the west coast. Showed up around 10 in the morning, fully expecting just dropping off our bags and wandering the city in a stupor until check in time. Much to our surprise the hotel had our room ready! It wasn't a high floor, which is the only reason they lose a point in this review. 
The East Side Marriott was super convenient to everything. Easy cab ride to Broadway shows, walking distance to everything, a quick and very entertaining cab ride to little Italy/SOHO. 
Room was clean every day when we got back. The shower was clean, the room stayed cool with the AC on, and we never had a problem getting a cab to go anywhere we wanted to go.
On check out they let us stash our bags so we could go explore the city for the last few hours we had left. They also hooked us up with a car service to the airport, which if you're going to JFK this is the only way to go. $65, including tolls, tips, and the car. Well worth the extra $8 it would cost over the shuttle service.
Over all very happy. Would absolutely stay there again, but next time on a higher floor!

From the Front Door (where the helpful and polite bellmen assist), to Check-in, and into our room, everything went very smoothly. Each day, once we completed our sightseeing, shopping, and dinner, we had a "nightcap" in the CityScape Bar; not only was the view spectacular, the Bar staff were terrific with their product and service. Last, we had a good breakfast in the restaurant each morning; again, the staff attitude and their abilities made our dining experience positive. I gave this hotel a full rating because we thought our stay there met our expectations. 
The only improvement I would suggest is installing new air conditioning units. I realize this would be expensive. However, when the Chicago heat is sizzling hot and the AC unit is rattling, our hotel room would have been a perfect oasis from the heat if there was a higher functioning unit in our room. 
Thank-you again, Chicago - Mart Plaza!

We stayed at the Kensington Park Hotel At Union Square for 3 nights in mid October. The hotel is in a great location, which is why we selected it and based on other reviews. The hotel, overall, has "character", which we enjoyed, but could benefit from some upgrading. The room we had was small, the bath was small as well. There was no fridge or safe, no dresser for storing clothes, no comfortable chair to sit and read other than a small desk/chair. Lighting was very bad, it was difficult to find things in my suitcase. There is no air conditioning. I am *always* freezing, and did not think this would be a problem, but we had over 80 degree weather the first day there and the room was so hot it was uncomfortable. Opening the window let in even more street noise, and with the trolley and construction going on, it was noisy. The windows, even when closed, are not very sound proof, so the noise was a problem even though we were on the 11th floor.

My wife and I stayed here last week because she had a convention to attend early the next morning. It is right across the street from the convention center and Water Gardens, so you can't get much closer if you are looking for something close by. 
When we called to reserve the room, they quoted my wife $369/night! This hotel is not even close to worth that price. It's very dated and the rooms are what you'd see in any budget hotel. So we complained about the price. Then suddenly, they had a room available for $169. I hate how hotels do that. Always ask for a lower price, because usually you'll get it. I can't stress enough that this hotel is not work $300/night, not even close. But if you can get them close to $100, you'll probably feel OK about it. 
Check in was fast, valet is expensive. Self parking is also expensive. We ate dinner in the hotel restaurant. The food was pretty good, but the service was very slow. The waitress was friendly enough, but she hardly even came by, and we had to keep reminding her of this we needed because she'd forget....ketchup, more water, salsa, etc. Seriously, every single time, she forgot until we reminded her again. I would understand if they were busy, but there were probably about 8 people in the entire restaurant, and most of them were just sitting at the bar, so she didn't even have to handle them. 
If you just need a place to sleep while you go out into the town, or the convention center during the day, it's an OK place. If you want to stay at a nice hotel, I would pick one of the other, nicer ones downtown.

I spent a week here on a business trip. The best thing about the hotel is the location. You are only a few blocks away from several subway stations. In addition, the hotel staff is very friendly and make you feel at home. On the down side, the hotel is very small and the rooms are tiny. For such a small room, there were not hooks to hang your coat or other stuff up. I would suggest to management that they add a few hooks in the entry way to the hall. There is a small wardrobe to hang clothes, but no dresser which I found annoying. The fitness room consists of one elyptical machine and one treadmill, so don't count on having a "gym" to work out in. Overall, a nice place to stay.

Overall, it was a fairly good stay. This is a very modern, trendy place... therefore, if you're not a modern person it might be the place for you. We checked in late, and the bar area was very loud, with lots of people, looking like they were having fun. However the hotel staff was courteous and professional. Our room was modern, but went with style instead of functionality. Someone mentioned issues with the lights and shower doors. However, the room was very spacious. We had a problem with hot water. We also had a problem with a few drunk customers early in the morning. One banged on our door around 4 a.m., and had the wrong room 
But the location was great and close to friends. Would I choose to stay here again? Probably not. But if you're looking for a trendy place with an interesting feel, this might be for you.

The rooms were okay, decent size and beds were fine. quiet rooms and convenient for getting around the larger SD area. I have had better breakfast selections at different la quintas, a lot better. The night manager seemed short of staff and clean rooms but he took care of us and was nice.
The hotel was OK, we stayed in the "new" tower which is a renoation of the old tower. Bath rooms are small. Service is extremely slow. Breakfast is very poor.

Hotel staff was quite friendly, helpful and attentive. The correct room was available on our arrival, and the room seemed clean, bright, and well appointed. It was also a fairly spacious room. Even though it was close to the elevator, the room was quiet. My father, my brother and I shared a room with two "doubles" (felt like queen-size) and a pullout couch.
The room has a small wet bar which includes a sink, a refrigerator, a microwave (stored underneath, oddly) and a two-cup coffee maker (which was inoperative on our arrival but quickly replaced). The thermostat is near the window in the pullout-couch room, and had to be turned up to nearly 80F to achieve a comfortable temperature - a design/installation flaw the maintenance person assured me. Also, between the two rooms are double doors with ball catches at the top. One door did not have this catch - maintenance informed me they did not have the part to fix it. Not a huge deal but a little odd.
The only somewhat major drawback was my brother reported (as have others) that the pullout was very uncomfortable. I cannot personally report on it as I did not sleep there. (Hey, I was paying for the room, I was sleeping in a real bed!) The doubles were really quite comfortable, on the other hand. Wired Internet didn't seem to work (the modem had been unplugged from power, but even plugged in it wouldn't connect). WiFi/Internet access wasn't free anyway. At a downtown Hilton in a major city, having to pay for Internet access is unreasonable. (On the plus side, I discovered the 4G-LTE signal was powerful and the one-time low-cost tethering program works well.)
Another very over-the-top expense was parking. We had taken a cab to the hotel, but when family came to visit they found there is no nearby parking and the valet costs $35.00 for between 2-6 hours. (I think it was $27.00 for 0-2 hours and something like $50 for beyond 6 hours.) The family lives in town and said the cost was beyond the pale.
Returning to the positives, there is an unsurprisingly expensive coffee shop which has a few snacks and serves Starbucks coffees. There is also a restaurant which I will review here as well, which is really quite good.

My husband and I stayed here for a San Diego Padres game. I would like to start with the positives. The hotel is gorgeous and is very centrally located to exactly what we wanted to do. The room was beautiful, bed was comfortable, and the shower was great. The Gas Lamp district is one street over and it was fantastic. The baseball park is a short 15-20 minute easy walk from the hotel. Now, for the unfortunate negative issues we had. The staff was not friendly or helpful, we had a dead bug on our pillow, and housekeeping never came to make up our room. I thought with a hotel of this caliber that the housekeeping staff would have their system down. We were gone from 8 am to 1 pm and the room had not been made up. I called down to the front desk and Steven said he would send someone up. We decided to wait in the lobby so the housekeeping people didn't have to work over us. We stayed down in the lobby for an hour and 20 minutes. We get back to the room and still no one had cleaned the room. Very unprofessional! This is such a grand and wonderful place, but they really need to get their act together. We would probably not stay here again, which is such a shame because I would have easily given this hotel a 5 stars if not for the issues. Happy Traveling!

title_masked: Feet did not touch the floor
text_masked: Great location but crappy hotel. Parking is outrageous but common for SF. I didn't mind the area. It was a two minute walk to my conference. Very accessible to Wharf and other sights, but the hotel interior was a mess. It seemed clean, but it was dingy and musty. I will never stay there again because I need a higher standard.

Stayed here earlier this month for five nights over Easter break. Room is spacious,, a little dated, but clean. Great location in a quieter part of the city. Plenty of restaurants nearby, didn't even try the cafe in the hotel. Shower pressure is a nice change from California's water saving shower heads.

The staff is extremely friendly and the concierge (Sara) helped us with tickets to a show. The room was a decent size for NYC and was well maintained. only issue was the lack of cold water for a couple of hours one day. Great experience. Thanks!

We have stayed in hundreds of hotels, our decision to stay here on June 27 was one of the finest reservations we have ever made. If you have the opportunity to stay at the Distrikt, you really must; it is truly a superb property! It distances itself from the other hotels by virtue of it's staff - from the initial "hello" of the doorman, to the "thank you" of the garage attendant, your experience at the Distrikt is a rare pleasure.

Was able to get a good deal on rates at the Helmsley Park Lane...right across the street from Central Park and close to some great NYC sites. As to the room...it was great, large and well appointed...clean, comfortable...and good air conditioning!
The staff, from the front desk to housekeeping was polite and knowledgable.
I would definitely go back and recommend to others.

I was very happy with my stay at the Hilton New York Fashion District hotel. At night it was quiet enough to get a good night's sleep. The staff was very helpfull and friendly. I plan on returning to the hotel in the summer.

This hotel is beautiful, the perfect location to hit all of downtown Denver's hot spots and the staff is amazing! My only complaint is that housekeeping had not been in by 3...we wanted a siesta before another round of downtown and dinner and had to wait another hour for someone to show after we called.
Other than that tiny glitch, the bartenders are FABulous, Quiera at the pool bar might be the nicest wait person I've ever met..and the bellhops, concierge etc. go out of their way to meet every need. I will definately stay again.

My sisters and I stayed here the night before our cruise was to leave for the Bahamas. This was a nice hotel with excellent service. Malcolm the manager was very pleasant and friendly and wanted to ensure that your stay was enjoyable. They offer a free shuttle to the cruise port and you can park your car there for the length of your cruise. They have a fenced in parking area that is secure. The shuttle drivers are THE BEST! They are very friendly and eager to please. I couldn't say I have ever been treated better. Unfortunately our cruise was cancelled on cruise day due to Hurricane Sandy.

The Hyatt is ideally located in the heart of Philadelphia's Historic Area and on the banks of the Delaware River. Honestly, I reserved our rooms on the basis of a low bid on a "name your price" web. But am I thankful we got this beautiful, comfortable and user friendly hotel. First the folks at check in did not treat me less than a full paying customer. They helped me find two rooms on the same floor. I took the $20 upgrade for a water view......and it was the best $20 I spent all weekend. Out of my window I could see the battleship New Jersey, Dewey' s flagship the Olympia, a WWII sub, and a two masted square rigger......PLUS all the river traffic. The hotel was hospitable, the beds were extra comfortable, the dining room fine. I recommend this hotel. Our guests from England were awestruck.

title_masked: Excellent location, great service and amenities
text_masked: Our stay here was in conjunction with a cruise package which we purchased prior to sailing to Alaska. It was a great value, which included parking for the week we were away, breakfast the morning of our departure, and shuttle service to the pier. Upon our return, we stayed an additional three nights and were not disappointed. The customer service at the front desk is outstanding, particularly the service and help we received from Nikki. She answered our questions about the area, gave great tips on attractions, and arranged for us to even check in earlier than planned. The hotel is relatively new and well appointed. The room was large and very comfortable, with a great bed. Parking in Seattle is a nightmare and extremely expensive, but the hotel's parking rate was half that of their neighbors. Parking is very safe, in an underground secured parking garage. The hotel operates a "fireside cafe" downstairs with reasonable prices for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. Room service is also available, as is a guest laundry. The only downside was no spa or pool, which would have been welcomed after a long day of walking and sightseeing. The location is very convenient, with a nice walk to the Space Needle and the monorail system.

title_masked: Another Great experience at Chelsea Pines!
text_masked: Just had another great experience at the Chelsea Pines Inn last month. As an X-New Yorker I really appreciate having a place to stay where I feel at home and not like a tourist. The location is great! It is nestled between the hip Meat Packing District, The West Villiage, and Chelsea. The subway is on the corner and connects you to the whole city. The rooms have fun Vintage Movie Star themes and are always clean and well maintained. The staff members are very friendly and well informed of the goings on around town. Chelsea Pines is a great place to stay and feel at home in New York City.

The hotel is about 5 minutes walk from the BART stop at Market/Montgomery. We were welcomed warmly at check-in & this service was consistent throughout our 12 night stay. All the staff were friendly, helpful & professional - as with other reviewers, the towel origami is fun, not sure if the elephant or snail was our favourite! Our 7th floor room overlooked Grant Avenue and we didn't have any noise problems, despite it being a busy road. We slept with the window shut to make sure we weren't disturbed but the ceiling fan kept us cool & was left on all night as it was completely silent. The room itself was clean & a good size for us, extra pillows were provided within 10 minutes of being requested. We made use of the safe in the room & there was always a good supply of toiletries & lots of towels. There are lots of places nearby for meals, Starbucks is handily 3 doors away from the hotel & opens early morning. I made good use of the complimentary Wifi when awake at all hours in the night due to the time difference from the UK & had a good connection always. The receptionist was happy to keep our cases safely after check-out so we could go shopping one last time! I booked this hotel as part of package with a British Airways flight through Ebookers & would recommend it to anyone.

title_masked: Clean and Close to Times Sq / Theatre District
text_masked: Stayed 6 nights at this hotel. It is about a 10 minute walk to Times Sq and many theatres which made the location very convenient for us. The hotel is about 4 years old and we found it to be quite clean. The rooms are fairly small especially with two adult children staying with us. The rooms were cleaned well every day. We stayed on a lower floor - no view. Would suggest a higher floor would give a good view - the hotel is about 30 stories. For an additional fee we had breakfast included. The hotel cost while expensive compared to any other place, it was less expensive than many hotels in the area. (We booked through booking.com). There is free wi-fi. The breakfast buffet was better than the average hotel buffet. The restaurant was clean and staff courteous HOWEVER the last morning there my daughter found a hair in her omlette. No apology was offered by the server. This was the only bad experience in an otherwise good hotel experience.

The staff and manager were very rude to me and my wife. Everything in the rooms are very old and dated. There are bugs crawling around, water leaking from ceiling. The manager is realy bad. We will never stay at this place again.

It is easy to find a 5-star hotel that meets expectations. But, sometimes circumstances don't allow us to stay in luxury hotels! For reasons of cost (it was graduation week in NY, and hotel rates had doubled an tripled - no joke), and location, our TripAdvisor research took us to Astor on the Park. Yes, we did have a view of Central Park - and great access to the park. We ended up spending free time between graduation activities, exploring it for hours! The lobby is small, dark and worn. But, the greeting at reception was warm and we were able to check into our room hours before the official check-in time.
The room was smallish and worn out. BUT, the bed was a king and very comfortable. The washroom was mainly updated, and very nice. The shower was great. The whole place was clean. Is it luxurious? No. Did it provide us with everything we needed? Yes! Thanks, Astor!

title_masked: Great hotel at a great price.
text_masked: It was clean, comfortable, and the staff was friendly. Right off I-10 so driving to Six Flags or Downtown San Antonio is a breeze. Breakfast was plentiful and delicious. Will definitely stay here again when I visit again next March.

I have stayed here many times and I like the hotel, although it does appear to be falling apart rather quickly (there are sheet rock cracks throughout the rooms and hotel). The breakfast is very good and the size of the rooms are nice. The beds are not comfortable - they sag and are uneven. My biggest complaint about this hotel is that I called the front desk about 10 times from 3 a.m. to 6:45 a.m. and no one answered. So I went down to the lobby and no one was staffing the front desk....but some shady characters were coming in to the hotel and the doors were wide open. The desk clerk emerged at 7 a.m. when breakfast started...he had been sleeping in a room near the desk.

We stayed here 5 nights in March. We had a nice Club level room which was spacious and well-appointed. The bathroom is big! The Club hostess was very welcoming and personable. Lobby and bar can get crazy in the evenings - we had to wade through the mob to get to the dining room. The dining room is very stylish. Dinner in the restaurant was excellent - it's nice to see a celebrity restaurant where the celebrity chef is actually in the kitchen. Mr [NAME] was there all evening and stopped by tables to check on guests. Nice touch. We will be back!

We looked at several places to meet our needs for our brief stay in Seattle and Cedarbrook fit the bill. The location is so close to the airport and transportation but yet you feel like you are in a wooded retreat rather than an airport hotel. The grounds are beautiful, the staff is very pleasant and the rooms are spacious. The "living room" is a wonderful surprise. Each building has it and is equipped with water, chips, lots of candy, ice cream, cheese and yogurt. When you have the mid-day or late night munchies, you have this all at your disposal and it's at no charge. We went downtown for the day and were driven to the train and it took a matter of a few minutes. When we returned and called again, we were picked up within a minute as well. The continental breakfast was wonderful. Lots of choices and there was something for everyone. Fruit, oatmeal with toppings, assortments of cereals, pastries, breads, muffins, etc. They even offer 3 different kids of milk. If traveling to Seattle and you don't stay at this hotel, you are a fool!!!

My husband and I ended up staying at this particular hotel during a vacation in Austin as had difficulty finding any room availability closer to the city. The hotel was very clean and the staff was excellent. I needed assistance downloading tickets for a show one evening. Since the public pc would not allow a download, the manager on duty offered to let me use his computer in his office. He didn't even raise an eyebrow. Very funny, very courteous. The only thing that would keep me from staying there again was the location as you have to deal with enormous traffic if you want to be in downtown Austin. Otherwise, we had a very positive experience.

This hotel was in a terrbile part of town, the room & hallways stunk from smoke (and we were in a non-smoking room). The front desk was enclosed in glass, bullet-proof is what it looked like. Put it this way, we slept with the lights on because there was less of a chance that the roaches would come out. We arrived at the hotel very late, so we had no choice but to sleep there.

Be aware. If you are going during a weekday thinking it wont be busy, ask if there are any groups scheduled for that day. We checked in on a Monday and had the park almost to ourselves. We woke up Tuesday morning to find four school buses parked outside and about 200 kids from the local synagogue day camp. The counselors spent no time monitoring the campers as they laid deluge to the place. In addition, there was no consistency with the life guards. Our 48 inch tall daughter was allowed to go down the slides for two hours before a guard measured her for the second time and said she was too short, by 1/2 an inch of the minimum 48 inches. We argued with the supervisors and eventually gave up. She must have grown a 1/2 inch overnight because the next day, they let her use the slides all day! My pregnant wife had her legs in the Jacuzzi the first day then was told she couldn't do it the second day?! Otherwise, we were satisfied with our stay, just dont expect a whole lot. The hotel is outdated. The rooms are small, very imperfect. The staff is young and inexperienced.

This hotel came highly recommended by my sister and said it was the only place to stay in Boston. The staff, Ashley and Meghan at the front desk and Justin the Concierge were outstanding. We queried Ashley as what we might do the next day and after a delicious dinner in the City Table restaurant we returned to our room to find an envelope prepared by Justin. He had printed out Mapquest directions for our Harvard visit and a personalized letter telling us his favorite restaurant, Barkley's (best burgers ever) and not to be missed exhibits in the Natural Science building (glass flowers).
We had a marvelous day sightseeing because of his recommendations. That evening as we sat by the fire awaiting the arrival of a group of friends he received a call they had "overshot" Boston and he helped them with driving directions to get them back to the hotel. Upon their arrival he had a special treat for them that was much appreciated.
Location was perfect and we walked over to the Back Bay station for our continuing trip to Mystic. 
We have been fortunate to travel worldwide and have never experienced the warmth and professionalism we were shown here. These employees truly enjoy their jobs and made this a very special trip for us. Thanks Lenox...we'll be back!

I chose "name your own price" on Priceline and got the room for under $90. It is rated a 3.5*. The location is great. It's walking distance to restaurants and if you really don't mind walking, you can walk down to the historic sites. If not, a cab ride is only about $7. It's very close to many restaurants and bars so there are choices for everyone. I didn't like the size of the rooms. They may be only as big as a cruise ship room (if that). I felt there was no room to move around. The rooms were also so thin, I could hear conversations taking place next door. Maybe it was just my timing because I swear that my floor was the gathering area for everyone going out to party over the weekend; as a result, I could hear the conversations of people congregating in the hall. The overall service (front desk, valet) was good.

This hotel was our saviour during Hurricane Sandy! After our flight home was cancelled and we had to evacuate the East Village apartment we were staying in we quickly made a booking for one night through Priceline. Despite the chaos of people trying to check in and out they were super professional and even allowed us the check-in early. We then found out our flight had been cancelled again and we would need 2 additional nights. They had no problem accomodating us, and gave us an even lower rate than we had obtained on Priceline!
The rooms were a decent size (by NYC standards) and we never felt too cramped even though we were 4 people to a room. We were lucky that this hotel was in an area that never lost power, and the free wi-fi allowed us to keep people up-to-date on our situation. The room aslo came equipped with a microwave, coffeemaker and a fridge which was very convenient for keeping our "hurricane supplies" (aka wine/beer) cold.
Although the location is not my cup of tea (i am more an East Village kind of girl), if you are looking for a midtown hotel within walking distance of the Empire State Building, Times Square, Bryant Park, Hell's Kitchen, etc than I would have no hesitations recommending this hotel.

Just stayed there for a conference and enjoyed it very much. It is a very large resort with a lot of walking. They do have golf carts and are very nice about coming to pick you up and take you where you need to go. However, even with that there is still a lot of walking depending on where you room is. I would definitely stay there again, but I would be more careful about where my room is located. The resort might want to think about having a wheelchair available for guests.

title_masked: Aging Boston Landmark only Economy Plus
text_masked:
Was a guest for four night's at Boston's Park Plaza Hotel as a part of a large group. This is an independent hotel and I suspect business travelers stay here only because of the excellent location. For frequent business travelers, there is little else to recommend here.
Front of house staff were friendly and helpful without exception. They made an early check-in happen on the spot. Critically, the beds are comfortable and the linen, pillows and duvets were of good quality and well maintained. Though the rooms are 'historic' and fairly worn, everything was serviceable. There aren't enough plugs in the room and the mediocre WiFi was expensive and charged per device (!). The toiletries were basic and the plastic cups in plastic wrap had a decidedly "Motel 6" feel. The single cup coffee maker was nice, but failing to provide real cream for the coffee was annoying. Again, a plastic packet with powdered creamer doesn't feel like an upscale hotel amenity. My frustration was compounded by the fact that there wasn't free coffee to-go in the lobby. It seems that this hotel adopted some business practices of their lower priced competitors while maintaining the "nickle and dime you" techniques of some 5 stars.
The concierge desk in the lobby is large and visible. It is staffed for much of the day. However, though the staff was friendly, they provided inaccurate directions and didn't have a jogging map.
The valet parking is impossibly expensive ($42 bucks for in-and-out service) and you would be better served to use the pay and display meter and risk a $25 dollar ticket. Its literally cheaper. 
The day before we departed, our room was not cleaned. When I got home at 8:00 PM and asked for service, they merely brought extra towels and left without explanation.

title_masked: Trump SOHO best location and service in New York!
text_masked:
Want to share my excellent hotel experience at the Trump Soho Hotel this past weekend.
The location is superb - perfect shopping really close by as well as smashing good restaurants such as Balthazar and Barolo. 
I got an excellent impression of the hotel from the very first minute as the doormen was so pleasant and professional. They were always smiling and i got the impression they put much pride and joy in their work.
Also want to complement the hotel having strawberries and champagne during check in - very nice treat! 
The hotel in general was really chic and clean and the beds were so wonderful it was like sleeping on a cloud! 
All in all this is by far the best hotel experience I have had, and I work with travel myself – so I have some experience!
So go and enjoy the Trump Soho like I did :)

This is the second time I have stayed at this hotel. Although it is not right downtown, a cab fare is a meer $10 or so. From start to finish, staff are very friendly and always helpful. Tried out the bar attached to the hotel for the first time. I was treated like I was a local! Rooms at this hotel are clean. After a long flight to get to Chicago, I was surprised to learn that I was the "guest of the day". Nice touch Marriott! Always a pleasure to stay at this hotel. It has some personality unlike some of the expensive faceless hotels downtown. Thanks to the staff for an enjoyable stay.

Attended a conference here and stayed for the first time. This is a superb hotel and you would easily pay well over $500/visit in NY for a similar accomodation. The room I stayed in was the Deluxe King. As I approach I notice that the Do Not Disturb is a light that is activated just inside the room - no hanging a card on the door handle. There is also a motion activated light as you walk in so no groping for light switches as you enter a strange room at night. The bathroom is spacious with a nightlight! The bed was very comfortable and the room has a phone by the bed and one on the credenza. There is a Bose radio that is already wired to take your iPod. My only negative was that the water pressure is weak. They give you an alternate hand wand that mitigates this somewhat. The shower has very nice chrome dispensers for shampoo and conditioners (I think) in the event you need them. I live out of my bag but there was plenty of closet and drawer space.
Now the fun part. I got to my room at night and the view over the harbor and distant (as in no noise) airport was just stunning. The Boston Harbor is between the Hotel and the airport and I sat for hours taking in this gorgeous view in the dark. Huge tankers clink by in the dark. At 11:00 I ordered dinner and for a great price ($40 with tax/tip) I had a shrimp sciampi dinner with a glass of wine. The food was outstanding, including the breakfast buffet (not included).
This is a first class facility for conferences but I recommend it for personal stay. It's a brief cab or walk to the Boston sites. Parking is available. I'm going back with my wife and will stay in a similar room. You will not be disappointed.

We were told our room, based on the hotel's agreement with Priceline, had one full size bed for two adults. We called [NAME] and were told we were guaranteed a room for two, so one full size bed qualified. We had to upgrade for $20/night for a queen size bed. Maybe 30 years ago, two adults expected to sleep on a full size bed, but this is not the expectation today, especially in a 3 1/2 ** hotel. The queen size bed was very comfortable; the room was clean. However, the queen bed barely fit in the room, leaving very little space to walk around the bed. Worst was having to pay extra for a queen size bed!! Once we did, the bed barely fit in the room space. THIS WAS NOT A 3 1/2 STAR EXPERIENCE.
wonderful hotel, well located, excellent service, great restaurant and spa

title_masked: Nothing fancy - tiny rooms - great location
text_masked: Stayed here with 2 kids in twin room. There was no room to move with luggage and 2 beds in room. We joked that only one person was allowed to move/stand at a time in the room. Having said that the rooms are practical and recently refurbished. Not fancy but clean and tidy and worked well. Hotel location is great if you want to be in the middle of the NYC action. Blockout blinds worked a treat and kept the room dark so we could sleep in. No excessive noise fro streat - no noise from adjoining rooms so was in fact a nice quiet room. Staff were all helpful and friendly too which was a bonus.

title_masked: Price ok for such a great location
text_masked:
New York is an expensive place to stay unfortunately, and Manhattan is even worse with their prices. Last time when I was in New York, I stayed in a hotel just across the Lincoln Tunnel, to save money, but this time we wanted to stay in the heart of Manhattan. And after a long search, I found the Belvedere, which was just 2 or 3 blocks from Times Square, and even affordable for a 4 days stay. Check-Inn was fast and not complicated, only the woman-receptionist wasn't really friendly, but that was the only unfriendly person we've came across in the hotel. The rooms were big enough, we even had a small kitchen, so if you're in mood of a midnight micro-wave burritto after a Musical , perfect !! The only thing , I hated in that hotel were their elevators, it's a big hotel, and they have only 2 elevators, so they were always crowded, very slow, stopped at nearly every floor etc etc. 
Internet is not for free, but we were lucky to get a free wifisignal from the restaurant just next to the hotel,so try to get a room to the side of the restaurant, slow connection, but free, because internet is as in much hotels to expensive.
So, I can recommend this hotel, the location is perfect for musicals, for times square, Rockefeller Plaza , price was ok, I would definitely go back. I just hope they find a solution with those elevators...

The Loews Philadelphia knows what they are doing and lives up to its reputation as a stylish, boutique hotel while maintain excellent customer service. From the moment you pull up to the curb, each employee warmly attends to you. Every last employee makes you feel like you are on vacation. I highly recommend this hotel!

Spent 2 nights in this lovely hotel, the room was clean and plenty big enough, check in was a breeze and very quick, customer service in this hotel was outstanding, nothing was to much trouble, valet parking was fast and efficient 11/10 I can't fault anything about our stay!! :)

The Four Seasons in NYC deserves FIVE stars. It is a fabulous location, the rooms are spacious, dining is delicious, the view spectacular and the bathroom the best ever.
Walk to Fifth Avenue and Central Park, enjoy a gorgeous room with every comfort, eat in the lovely restaurant and bar, see the park and the amazing skyline from your room as you press a button to open the drapes from bed, and spend lots of time in the amazing shower with the powerful shower head and a soaking tub that fills in a moment as you pamper yourself with fabulous toiletries and soft bath sheets.
I want go back, NOW!

title_masked: Plan on staying in this area? This is the Hotel for You!
text_masked:
Visiting from Raleigh,NC this was our first time staying here and it was a most pleasant stay far above my expectations. From the Front Desk on down to the friendly smile of the our Housekeeper in the morning, everyone has that warm down to earth personality where you can feel their welcome to you as a guest. Even the Maintenance gentlemen greeted you with a hello. Very rare in most hotels.
If you decide to stay here you have to try to book a Suite for it is spacious,comfortable and very nicely decorated. You have a large dining table if you decide to have room service and the decor is nice to go along. The swimming pool is fairly large and well maintained where you can relax in the sun and enjoy your swim in clean crystal clear water.
The Breakfast Buffet ( reasonably priced) is great for you are not subjected to just scrambled eggs, as here they will make you omlettes and eggs of your choice freshly made. Spacious dining area also. We ordered room service and the food I ordered ( Salmon) could not have been better in a fancy restaurant. I usually don't order a seafood dish in a hotel in relation to it being fresh,but this was perfect. So you will not be disappointed if you are just heading in and just want to relax and have a meal here. The Chefs (also very friendly) are very good cooks in my book.
There are other hotels in this area and we did stay at one close by a year ago, but that was never going to be a repeat for this is the place to stay Easy access and close to I-95 you don't have a way to go to get back driving to your destinations. Almost forgot..Sleep member beds for your pleasure at night.
Very good job Radisson! See you next year!

title_masked: Spent 6 nights, could have stayed longer
text_masked:
So I chose this hotel because of the location--close to Union Square, close to Moscone convention center--and being a Starwood member, had heard that the Market St. Westin was slightly more consistently nice than the Westin on Union Square, which is more of a "historic" building. 
Staff: was excellent; requested a high floor, which I didn't necessarily get (17 of 30something), but it was high enough. Requested a king away from the elevator, which I did get. Used the concierge a couple times, who were very helpful. Needed a 6 passenger cab for transport to the airport, which was easily arranged with the doorman (though plan ahead). Cleaning staff were all friendly.
Room: considering the price, $311/night, I've stayed in nicer rooms at that price. Bathroom was pretty small. Had a large king bed, which was extremely comfortable. Full sized desk as well as another chair next to the bed. Large flat screen TV was nice, but due to the shape of the room, was kind of in an awkward position to watch from bed. Room had plenty of plugs for cell/laptop/iPad chargers. Closet was a little small, as well as the storage for clothes (for those of us who like to unpack). Not a huge fan of the Westin brand toiletries--but that's the same at all their hotels (W stuff is much better). The room I had was a pretty nice location; very end of the hall, almost a corner-type room, with a view of the bay. It was right next to the ice machine, but I NEVER heard it. 
Food: didn't eat in the hotel a single time, though friends who did use the restaurant said it was very good.
Misc: The gym is average. Not very large. At one time, there were 10+ people there, and it was way too crowded. I did see signs about Westin clients being able to use the gym at the Four Seasons, but I didn't investigate this. It should be noted, the elevators were extremely fast. The hotel was crowded, there are tons of rooms, yet I never felt I had to wait for an elevator.
Overall, the place was clean, staff was awesome and accommodating, and the Westin bed is very nice to sleep in when spending such a long time in a hotel room. I would give the hotel a 5 star rating if the rooms were a little larger and maybe more extravagant, considering the price.

Stayed at the nyma for 13 nights in late October - including during hurricane Sandy. The location of the hotel on 32nd and 5th is perfect, close to a lot of attractions in Midtown (empire state building, Macy's, Times Square, Bryant park, etc) and has easy access to several subway lines. The hotel staff were friendly and efficient. We were on the 7th floor in room 705 - a double double room. It had an average view but the room was quite big, with a closet, a large chest of draws, a writing table and fridge/microwave/coffee maker. As we had a long stay we unpacked our suitcases and stowed them away in a corner. The bathroom was functional, and had enough bench/storage space for two ladies to put all their stuff. The beds were soft and comfortable. The only issue I had was the air conditioning was too hot for me, and not being able to open the window meant the room became stuffy with the air con off - I guess I'm used the the fresh air of Australia! The complimentary breakfast was ok, not a great deal of variety, but enough to get you going in the morning. As I drink soy milk, I purchased my own and took it with me to the breakfast room to have cereal. It was just as easy to go to one of the many local diners for breakfast, some of which had espresso coffee (heaven!). The lift is a bit slow, but i didn't find it a problem - I'm not in a rush when I'm on holidays. During the hurricane, the staff were helpful, the hotel was safe and had power. Even the maid staff stayed at the hotel to ensure our rooms were still serviced. Our maid on the 7th floor was lovely. All in all, I'd definitely stay at the nyma again

I found this hotel to be a brilliant stopover on our way from New Zealand to the UK. The staff were very helpful and lovely. The rooms were clean and tidy if a little worn and dated. The pool was clean with lots of towels and the kids spent a good couple of hours getting rid of pent up energy. The restaurant The Daily Grill was great - family friendly, nice food and reasonably quick.
Definitely recommend

title_masked: Perfect location and close to everything you need
text_masked: I got a deal on this hotel and did expect it to be a nice as it was. The hotel was nice, rooms large and very clean. This was the perfect location, we were near the T, aquarium, harbor, Quincy market, north end, nothing is really more than 2 miles away. There are great pubs near by as well so you can grab something quick to eat. There is a 24 hour market near by so you can get something quick to drink if you don't want the 24 hour coffee available in the hotel.

I've been staying at this hotel for a trade show, forever. The rooms are always clean and comfortable. The noise level is what you're used to from a Marriott. The staff is always very friendly and helpful. The location of this hotel isn't close to anything. I usually rent a car or use a car service, but this year I took a cab downtown to meet friends. The cab ride took forever and cost about 40.00. This wouldn't be much of an issue if there were places to go around the hotel, but there isn't anything but fast food and a CVS. The hotel and the staff are great, but make sure you have some sort of transportation if you want to explore Indy.
Pretty rooms, delicious breakfast, and absolutely loony service some of the time, but I'd still stand by my "excellent" raiting. I love that the windows open!

title_masked: The Hotel Highlight of our New England Trip!
text_masked:
Just got back from our week stay in the New England and could not wait to review this place. 
The only sad thing about this place was that it was our first hotel stay of the trip and set the bar way too high for any other New England hotel to match. We took the red eye flight in from Los Angeles so when we landed at Logan at 5am we were zombies. It's really easy to get here from Logan via the "T". All you have to do is take the Silver Line to the South Station and it's a short walk up Atlantic (We wish we knew this when we first got there). 
Knowing that our hotel check in wasn't until 4pm we wondered over to the hotel to simply check our bags and wonder around town. The front desk was extremely gracious by seeing if there was something they could do to help us out and gave us our 4pm check in at 7am! 
Once we got to our room we were quite impressed with the size of it. It was very spacious and very comfortable. I've read some of the reviews about the style being old fashioned or outdated in this hotel but after checking it out it wasn't old fashion. It was a bit more turn of the century and Art-Deco in it's design. Sure it wasn't one of the modern design places like the Intercontinental a few places over but I come from LA where every hotel looks like that. The Boston Harbor Hotel gave me a little more of a New England Feel and for that I am very grateful. 
When we finally crashed on the bed we laid down of one of the softest most comfortable mattresses we've ever slept on in our lives. It was like sleeping on a cloud. 
I took advantage of the Fitness Center and was very impressed with it. I loved the salt water pool and was impressed with the locker room which had a sauna and amenities for me to shower, shave and start my day. 
The hotel also sits on the harbor with a beautiful boardwalk at it's back door. 
This hotel was truly the hotel highlight of our trip and cannot express how pleased we were with our experience. No other hotel was able to live up to this hotels experience. If you have the dough to shell out for a little luxury, make the Boston Harbor Hotel your choice. We're so glad we did!

We had a short stay here with friends visiting from out of state. We wanted something close to Sea World that was comfortable and affordable. This hotel was exactly that! The rooms were nice (small but updated), the staff was friendly and helpful and the grounds were pretty. We enjoyed sitting out on the community patio area at night, sipping wine and enjoying the warm evening weather. There is a TGIF's VERY close by that we had dinner at one night (great menu and prices) and a Denny's just down the road (we had breakfast here). Also, an AM/PM mart a block away, which was nice for loading up on water/drinks/snacks. 
Great little hotel. Would stay here again!

After we checked in at the Embassy, we remembered that once years ago when the kids were young, they cried when we left the hotel because they wanted to live there they had enjoyed it so much. Although this time we did not use the pool, we once again enjoyed the Saturday night manager's reception (great place to meet up with friends before going to dinner) and Sunday brunch. This time we had a room with 2 Queen beds in the main bedroom, our guest said the sofa bed was comfortable. NO problems whatsoever with the room. Staff was really friendly and welcoming, when we arrived we were immediately directed to a parking spot on the street in front of the hotel which was free all weekend. Location is easy for Metro access and for walking to Dupont Circle and nearby restaurants. There is a restaurant attached to the hotel (Italian) which friends told me was quite good but we only used it for late night drinks since we were in a sushi mood.

title_masked: Quiet and spacious near GW and Georgetown
text_masked: I never knew that this place existed, and you pretty much thing it is a luxury condo or apartment building when you drive up to it because there is no fanfare or landscaping or large flashy sign to alert you that it is a hotel, but that's just fine after all if you want a quiet unassumiong place that is comfortable with nice amenities for a reasonable mprice in a great neighborhood near to a lot of things, My room included a sleeper couch, for my twin daughters, who were here for a GW event. We were all comfortable and had a good stay. The housekeeping people were accommodating, and the room was modern and functional and large enough for all of us. They have a small gym and a pool that I didn't know about until I was there--I'm sure to use it next time! Their restaurant is highly rated, and accross the circle is a burgers and shakes joint that has interesting and unusual flavors for their shakes. The neighborhhod has many dining options, and it is an easy walk to Georgetown where Georgetown Cupcakes is! This place is recommended.

My husband and I stayed here for 6 nights and was put in a room that faced the front of the hotel, for 2 of those nights we put up with the noise level from the constant traffic and bin trucks between 3-4am. We asked at the front desk if we could be moved to a quieter room, the staff were more then helpful and was informed, we will be moved by the afternoon. There is a fridge and a coffee machine and the room was kept very clean. All in all a very enjoyable stay.

title_masked: Friendly boutique, convenient to downtown market & shopping
text_masked: This is a modestly priced boutique. The best part was the super-friendly helpful staff. Room was basic but very comfortable. Great shower! It is walking distance from Pike place market and lots of great shopping and restaurants. Nearby is Top Pot Doughnut and Icon Grill.

title_masked: Feel at home in the Big City
text_masked: We just adore this hotel. From the smiley greeting to the lovely rooms, we feel right at home. Kudos to all the staff who really care.

I hated this hotel. My room smelled humidity. The air condition is so loud. The area around the hotel is dodgy and far from a subway stop (15 minutes walking). The hotel and the rooms badly need renovation. Old furniture. Comfy bed. The cover and blanket always seemed wet because of the humidity in the room. So noisy because of the construction site in front of the hotel that starts around 6 am !!! hotel reception employees were ok. Some better than others, but not that friendly. Breakfast is average. Overall it is not horrible, but for the price i would not recommend it.

This Hotel was situated on the other side of town they don't tell you about. It was somewhat close to the "hood" and was not as close to the city center and you do have a view of capitol Hill...on the other side. It was a 5 minute walk to the train station, however it was near the washington nationals ballpark and there was a lot of construction around. You have to pay $15.00 extra for a mini fridge and a microwave....each, but we were told the suites have them. The lobby was black, white and red 60s retro and seemed clean. The room was clean and there were 2 bottles of water offerred, but you have to pay for them. $4 each. The bathroom had no fan and there is no airconditioner in the room. They do have heating in the rooms, however it was hard to adjust as once you turn it on it was too warm so we had to shut it off. When the wind hit the windows it sounded as though a bird hit it..each time. I was unable to use the shower as the water pressure didn't reach all the way to the shower head so I had to use the bath pipe. I would've paid the extra 10-15 dollars per night to stay closer to the center of D.C. It was ok but I don't think I would stay there again.

title_masked: Great hotel with great staff Thank you
text_masked: Had a great stay seemed like an oasis in the middle of busy LA . The bar and Culina restaurant are fabulous . I definitely suggest checking them out .The staff are always attentive and there for your needs.

I visit SF 3-4 times a year and always go to the Palace hotel - service is very friendly, rooms are big and very clean. excellent king size bed. room service is good, location is very good, with all the best places close by. only down size is that the WiFi does not work well. but all in all highly recommended.

title_masked: A very good hotel and amazing staff
text_masked:
I stayed here off and on for more than a month and the staff was extremely helpful and friendly.
The hotel is in perfect condition. The rooms are nice and the beds are very comfortable. Wish all Residence Inns were this quality.
I enjoyed my stay and will stay again when in the area. Everyone was very nice and helpful. For the cost a great place to stay.

This hotel is one of the nicest Sheraton's i've been to, it has many restaurants on the property and close to the airport. I travel for business so its super convenient. I'm a sStarwood platinum member, and the club lounge is the nicest I've been to. The 5pm cocktail/snacks were great and Anthony the server was great.

We stayed here this past weekend while in town for a Broncos game. It was an excellent deal at $89 per night with a clean and spacious room. The highlight of this hotel is by far the delicious spread that was prepared each morning for breakfast. In all the times I've traveled I've never seen a hotel provide such a vast amount of options for breakfast. 
The only down side is this hotel is a short drive from Denver, but if you count the price of the room plus the delicious breakfast each morning you are saving money in the long run. The hotel staff was very friendly and even let us have a late checkout, to grab a quick shower after hiking Red Rocks, before catching our flight. We will stay here again!

title_masked: Nice hotel, but a bit underwhelming
text_masked: Not in the best location, and no room service after 11. The lobby is pretty, and the rooms are nice.

I booked this for one night through hotwire, and got a great rate. The location is great and easy to get on and off the interstate in both directions; and that don’t happen often in down town Dallas. The staff was friendly, the rooms were good the bedroom was a little small but the bathroom and front room were spacious. TV, iron, refrigerator, and other amenities in the room were all up-to-date or new. Will use again.

This is a great location just minutes away from the piers and cable cars, but it was over priced for what it was. Parking was $40 per day in addition to the room rate and breakfast was also extra. The staff were friendly enough and the rooms clean and what you would expect from Holiday Inn, but our room was not ready when we arrived and the consierge was amost just plain rude. A pleasant enough hotel in a great location, but not sure if we would stay again because of the price.

Stayed at here for 3 nights with my kids and my dog. Very clean and comfortable rooms, they gave me a room near the stairs so it was very convenient for me to take my dog out for walks. My only complaint would be breakfast buffet is a little pricey, and would recommend more wait staff available.

We stayed as a surprise for my husband's 40th and I emailed in advance to ask if there was anything they could do to make the occasion special - when we arrived they had upgraded us to a gorgeous and stylish suite. The staff was gracious, generous and genuinely friendly. We loved the hotel, loved our stay, loved Tribeca and thanks to the wonderful staff at the Smyth it was truly a special occasion and a weekend we will never forget.

title_masked: Another Great Stay at The Edgewater
text_masked: Due to a business trip to Seattle, I returned to The Edgewater for my second stay and was not disappointed. Room was very clean, staff was very friendly and helpful with any questions I had. I stayed on the city side again, but I enjoy the great view of the Space Needle from that side. It is a great location on the water and convenient to everything downtown. I took advantage of their complimentary shuttle to take me into the downtown area. The shuttle is handy if you want to go anywhere within a few miles of the hotel. Overall, another great stay at The Edgewater.

Chose to stay here a second time and once again felt that the hotel staff showcased true southern hospitality. All were friendly and helpful, plus my room on the concierge level was huge and quiet. I had lovely views of the lake, which has a running/walking path around it. Great salads in lobby bar, nice breakfast in concierge.

We were lucky with a good deal at somewhere we wouldn't normally afford. We really enjoyed our stay. A cool burger joint, the beautiful bar/cafe and great pool, though u need to pay extra for it. Staff generally friendly. We like it as it was beautiful but not stuffy. Room was a good size with a great view.

This isn't three star. You will feel 5star hotel. Seriously I got discounted price from Hotwire but they don't treat you like that like other hotels. Rooms was awesome. Nice and clean. Staff was really nice. And amenities was good. Beds are comfortable too. Definitely I will stay to this hotel if I will come back to San Diego. :-)

Great customer service from the night audit attendant, Tom. Great location easy to get anywhere from hotel. Nice and cozy rooms. Gives you a sense of historic pride knowing the history of the area and hotel. I would recommend this hotel to all!

We thoroughly enjoyed our stay recently. The rooms were wonderful and the staff was pleasant and bent over backward to be helpful.
The location of the hotel makes it easy to walk up Michigan or head to Rush street for some restaurant/bar browsing. We enjoy the location and the price was much less than other hotels in the area.
The only downside was the NoMI bar - the location is great and the drinks were well done. But the service is lacking - we waited over 20 minutes for one set of drinks. Many better places to choose.

I stay here nearly every time I visit the Valley of the Sun. I'm always very happy with the prompt shuttle to and from the airport. The location is close enough to downtown and Tempe. Great spot for Spring Training as it's right by the Angels facility. I was also very glad to have a mini-fridge in the room to place my beer. I was even more delighted when I found out they have free beer on tap (bluemoon too!) and food during the evenings. The staff was excellent as well. Dineh at the front desk was very helpful and courteous. The desert view is decent and makes the relaxing jacuzzi even better.

There's a lot to like about the Crowne Plaza. We arrive from Hawaii after midnight. The shuttle, as promised, was prompt with a phone call. The shuttle to the airport was equally on the ball - a very short wait, drivers extremely friendly and helpful. Despite its proximity to the airport, noise was not a problem. Also: light rail line across the street was great - a short ride to the Heard Museum downtown, then, also, another short ride to Tempe for food and drinks.

The hotel is in a rough part of town but the customer serevice is good. They serve a very nice breakfast and the Hostess Georgia Rios is very proud of her meal. She is cheerful and really tries to go above and beyond.
The only complaint I have is the first day I checked in I reported a burned out light bulb. It took 2 days and 2 reminders to get it replaced.

This is the perfect place to stay in the Gold Coast area of Chicago. The service was excellent and the hotel is absolutely beautiful. The Waldorf Astoria has the most wonderful staff and amenities! The staff went beyond what is expected and made our trip to Chicago perfect.

I stayed at this hotel w/a Road Scholar tour, and found it quite nice. I liked the character of the 1930s-style building. The room was very large, w/2 bathrooms and 2 closets. The beds were quite comfortable, and everything worked. The staff was friendly and helpful. The location was just perfect: blocks from the Empire State Building, the Theater District, Times Square, etc. The hotel coffee in the conference rooms was dreadful, but there was a Starbucks right across the street, so all was well.

Enjoyed our stay again at the Holiday Inn Express, warm, friendly professional staff , bellhop and waitresses. The room was clean, comfortable and attractive. A metal bedframe is a must for my Family to travel using a hoyer lift. Thanks again for providing this essential piece. The parking garage was attached to the hotel. The historic attractions were walking/rolling distance away from the hotel. Enjoyed our stay!

This hotel is great value for money and in the best location in San Francisco. Cable cars run straight past the hotel, steps away from shops like Forever 21, H&M and the Westfield Shopping Centre. Plenty of places to eat within a block of the hotel... And free breakfast :) We stayed in a Family Room and had no problems at all. Free WIFI a bonus! Reception staff are more than happy to help... Would recommend this hotel to anyone visiting San Fran :)

The hotel NEEDS rennovation...the carpets were filthy, the sitting area in the lobby has head stains on the furniture, and the bar seats are uncomfortable and worn out. Stayed there for 5 nights, and only ONE TIME did a doorman hold a door open for us. The Bartenders at night were rude, did not seem to care, and at times were overwhelmed. Would not stay here again...as Taylor Swift says....ever, ever.

title_masked: Great location but not easy to stay in and navigate
text_masked:
The location is great-right in the heart of Denver. The issue is if you get 'stuck' in the Tower side-you are not conveniently located and going back and forth takes considerable walking. The front desk staff is extremely accomodating. The one exception to exceptional service was Suzanne in the gift shop. She was rude-dismissive and should not be in a customer facing role. I had presents to buy-but with her attitude-I just went into the city and spent the funds. 
If you stay here-call ahead and ask to be in the Plaza-not the Tower side. The rooms are spacious and clean-the beds are comfy and the large plasma TV is great! Avoid the gift store at all costs unless you want to be treated horribly and dismissed as an inconvience for stopping by.... The front desk staff is kind and will help you out-kudos to them!

My husband & I spent one night here & wish we could have stayed longer. From checking in to checking out everything was perfect. The staff was polite, helpful & friendly. We were greeted with a glass of wine which was an unexpected surprise. The room was clean & comfy. The bed was comfortable. There was free parking behind the hotel & we also had a fantastic complimentary breakfast in the hotel restaurant. I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone looking for luxury in an inn type setting.

Wonderful!!
I stayed here with my husband,Nov, 10th 2012.(Were both in our 30's). I had such an amazing stay at this hotel!The location as others have written is Amazing! A 5 min walk from MSG, Penn station, and walking distance from times square and all shopping. I booked my room with Tom, who was so great over the phone that I was considering going somewhere else(for financial reasons) and he won me over. Unfortunately, I did not get to meet him in person, but he had the Best customer service skills! Upon arrival, I was instantly checked in. The staff was knowledgable, and extremely helpful. The room(ROOM 1111) was beautiful(nice color scheme), comfortable, clean, and had all the amenities that a basic hotel should have. Blow dryer, iphone dock, alarm, iron, safety box, cofee maker...etc. The bed was SUPER comfortable. Air conditioner worked perfectly. Noise level was okay, although I think the walls might be a bit thin...but didn't bother us. We enjoyed drinks at the 14th floor bar that they have and it was great. There's an area that you can sit with friends and have drinks and enjoy the view of the empire state building. They had heated lamps which was great to be able to sit out there and be comfortable. We checked out at 12:30 the next day and check out was easy and smooth. They held our bags in a room so that we could enjoy nyc for the day. When we returned for our bags in the evening, it was efficient, and easy. I enjoyed my stay so much that I became a rewards member. The front desk told me I was staying in a renovated room, so I can't comment on other rooms, but I loved my stay. I WILL Stay here again, and I recommend it to anyone. Even thought of getting someone a stay as a gift card. The front-staff was excellent but I did not encounter housekeeping. Reminder, I only stayed one night. They have free wi fi which worked just OKAY in the room, but great in the lobby for some reason. Also, free breakfast which I can't comment on because we slept in and it was only until 10am. But it was nice to know that it is available. Im not super picky, but it was clean, comfortable, no bed bugs, and just perfect for me! In NYC all you need is somewhere to rest your head anyway, since there's always so much to do. The shower was pretty nice too! Paid $267 total with my AAA discount which was great for a holiday weekend!

This hotel is a gem, with a fabulous staff. My wife and I picked the hotel because of its proximity to GWU Medical Center, where our son was having surgery. The staff was responsive to our every request, including providing an extension cord so our son could power his computer following his successful operation. Our room was large, and the kitchenette allowed us to purchase food from a nearby Whole Foods so we could have meals early and late following long days at the hospital. The fresh coffee beans, grinder and pot were added treats. We enthusiastically recommend the One Washington Circle Hotel to everyone.

Enjoyed a lovely 3 night stay at this hotel during our trip to New york. The room was very comfortable, particularly the bed.
We were on the 20th floor, not the best view in the hotel but OK.
Room sizes are very good for new York where rooms are traditionally small.
We didn’t eat in the hotel so cant comment on this.
The reception service was fine if a little slow when we were checking in.
The bellboys called us a cab very efficiently when we were leaving.
The hotel is in a great location right on Times square so veery easy to get out and about in the middle of Manhattan.
For a hotel in the centre of town the room was very quiet and we could sleep easily and didn’t hear any outside noise.

Spotless room, execellent bed, good towels, freindly professional staff, great location, easy to get the subway and a cab. These folk went out of thier way to be helpful. I spend a lot nights out of town and this was a superior experience.

When we arrived at the hotel we were told our room was not ready. Check in provided my wife and I with vouchers to obtain a free drink at the JSix bar. At the bar we were served by Angelo and on taking his advice we ate a bar meal which my wife and I both enjoyed. We returned to check in to find that our booking for a Master Suite corner room could not be honoured. We were both very unhappy with this - so you may take this in to consideration when making your choice.
The Front Office manager has since provided a response as to why the room was unavailable for the first night of a five night stay. 
Dining out on our first night we returned to the hotel at 22.00 and went to the Loungesix bar for a nightcap we were told the bar was closed and when we tried the JSix bar we were told that this was also closed. Not the kind of hotel service I would have expected for the Thursday night prior to the Labor Day holiday weekend.
We dined in the JSix Restaurant on two occasions and I have to say the food, wine and service were excellent. My wife particularly enjoyed the dish of Double Cut Niman Ranch Pork Chop with duckfat potatoes, garlic yellow beans, grain mustard jus. My wife rated this as the best pork chop she has tasted.
For dog lovers a nice touch is the name board welcoming the dogs staying at the hotel should you wish to bring your dog.
Overall once we received the type of room we had booked then the quality of room cleanliness and service was very good.

Small room but expert use of space. It was clean--my most important concern--and the staff was very very friendly and helpful. A relatively good deal in LA.
Two observations: Bathroom door doesn't quite close (not an issue with the door, but that "sliding door" trend I have noticed in some hotels.)
Second, which was more of a big deal and which I should have pointed out to management--bath towels smell like food which makes me think that the napkins are washed with bath towels. I didn't eat at the hotel, so I didn't have to worry too much about that, but quite frankly, that would probably make me think twice about eating in the hotel restaurant.

I stayed for three nights to do some shopping before returning to Australia. Check in was easy and fast. The room was a good size, nice and clean and the bed comfortable. I had a room overlooking the airport and although it was not a bad view watching the planes taking off and landing, the plane noise was quite disturbing at night. Definitely could do with further sound proofing. Would have been nice to have a fridge in the room. The food in the restaurant and bar were reasonable. You can catch the Ocean Express Trolley bus to downtown Manhattan Beach, Manhattan Village Shopping Center and Plaza El Segundo shopping center or the Big Blue Bus to Santa Monica and Venice Beach just outside the hotel. Manhattan Beach has a lovely vibe. Really good shopping along the 3rd Street Promenade in Santa Monica. There nothing much immediately around the hotel. Hotel has a frequent free shuttle to the airport.

We experienced difficulties with our reservations prior to arrival. George was fantastic in helping and correcting it. Completely de-stressed what could have been a headache. I had occasion to meet him in person on my trip and he was just as courteous, helpful, and professional in person as he had been on the phone. Terrific employee, great asset to Hilton and to its guests.
Tom

title_masked: Nice, pretty and clean, just don't sleep over the lounge
text_masked: We love visiting Manhattan, and were excited to find a reasonably priced hotel in Midtown. The Flatiron is relatively new, so some small quirks (room card didn't work at first,etc.) but the management and staff were responsive. Good morning coffee a block or two away at Stumptown or the Birch Cafe! We loved our corner suite, which worked fine for two adults and a quiet teenager. The lobby aquarium is pretty cool, too.
