Our only complaint was that the lobby lounge music is very noticeable at night when you're on the third floor. We'll be happy to go back to the Flatiron, but will reserve a room a little higher up. Not sure what this hotel wants to be, yet. Internet a little slow, so not business travel. No pool, so not good for young kids. Worked for us, though.

The nicest hotel we stayed in during a month in the USA.
Our spacious room was a suite rather than a bedroom. Very well furnished, bright & comfortable. In the heat of Phoenix we didn't want to leave it!
The hotel doesn't have a restaurant. Guests eat in the lobby which can get a bit crowded but you can always take thing back to your room as we did at one point. There is a small room off the lobby where breakfast, which is included in the room price, is available to assemble. The simple food was fresh & appetising.
A limited range of food is available from a counter next to the Reception desk. There are also sandwiches & cakes. My only slight complaint is that the Reception staff take the orders for food so there is a conflict in their roles at busy times.

title_masked: Average hotel in a great city
text_masked: We stayed here over the Thanksgiving holiday. The location is excellent and their concierge desk was very helpful. Even though we had made our reservations directly with the hotel, we were not offered an upgrade and we were given a room that was obviously not yet remodeled. The carpet was old and looked dirty, there were spots of sticky stuff on the tables and the bathroom needed a makeover. I expected small and the room was actually bigger than anticipated, but there was no place to put your own things in the bathroom except on the floor. All of the pillows (three, for two of us?) were mushy and provided no support. On our second night we had to call the front desk and ask them to have the other guests take their children into their rooms rather than letting them run and scream in the hallways - and this was after 11:00PM. I have to give them credit, they took care of it right away. We've stayed at other hotels in Manhattan with excellent locations that took a little more care of us, and we will likely not return to the Park Central.

I enjoyed my stay at the Regency Suites. The hotel is clean and everything works . The people are very nice, helpful and pleasant. They offer continental breakfast in the morning lobby.
They have DVD player in room for your own dvd's. 
The hotel is modern and the rooms are a nice size.
I felt safe and comfortable here. 
This is 7 miles from the Houston Bush Airport. 
Some of the bad reviews here must be old and the place is now under new management.

We picked the Palomar based on past reviews, and it was satisfactory overall, but I am surprised it holds the top spot on tripadvisor. Of course, I am really picky and particular, especially when it comes to service and cleanliness.
The location is lively-- both inside the hotel and the neighborhood. We liked that there were good restaurants within easy walking distance. But, the walls were thin-- we could hear doors opening and closing, the guests on both sides peeing and flushing the toilet, and showering. :( I really don't want to hear other people peeing. Especially at $350/night plus $50 tax = $400 night.
I am a really clean person, so I notice when things are not clean. In our King Spa Room, I noticed some mold in the shower and stains on the wallpaper, and the grout on the floor could use a good scrubbing. But the sink and mirrors were clean. The tub was ok, a little peeling but we didn't use it.
During our stay, service was not outstanding as other reviewers have raved about. There was not a smile when we checked in late, and no help with the door or luggage. Isn't the front desk supposed to at least pretend they would like to welcome you? 
The pictures submitted by guests are accurate-- the spa room was spacious and the walk in closet was huge. I don't know about the smaller rooms though, they look really cramped in the photos.
Decor is like in the pictures, and that is personal preference. It's not really my style, but we managed. A lot of animal print (carpet, blankets, robes, etc.)
The metro is a couple blocks away, but we walked or took taxis. 
Urbana was enjoyable for dinner-- the bread was really good, and the service was excellent. Room service for breakfast was fast; late night not as fast.
We usually stay at the Ritz Carlton, which is really clean and has really top notch service, so perhaps we've been spoiled and our expectations for the Palomar were too high.

CLEAN! Friendly staff. Great location with local markets around the corner. Room was small but clean. Anyways, all you need is a bed and shower. BTW-the bed was the most comfortable I've ever slept in! Quiet-lobby construction was not an issue. I would definitely stay again.

title_masked: Perfect start to a road trip
text_masked: From the airport pickup to the buffet breakfast, everything about our stay was excellent. Helpful, friendly staff, fantastic suite room, good value for money - would definitely recommend. Shame about the flash floods we brought along with us!
We decided to stay at this hotel prior to a conference at the Westin. The price was very good. Location was great. Staff was very helpful and very kind.

The room was very nice and the hotel was near to the monorail near the Space Needle which took us quickly downtown. The trip we took on the ducks was fantastic. Staff was very helpful especially with a taxi to a restaurant for dinner.

title_masked: Great place to stay with outstanding service
text_masked:
I recently stayed at Parc 55 while attending a 3-day workshop and had the most amazing stay.
It was surprisingly located right in the heart of the city (Union Square). The entire staff was amazing and over-the-top friendly & courteous including the conceige team & housekeeping team. 
The hotel has a free gym but what we really stood out was the fact that they provide special running maps for the outside adventure seekers which specifies different routes and the respective sightseeing and distance. 
The room had a fresh feel so I'm confident that teh housekeeping manager does a good job in monitoring the respective rooms.
What I found a pleasant surprise was that they provided daily complementary bottle water. In a day of age where everyone is increasing prices and decreasing services; PARC 55 offers many services.
I will definitely visit again since I didn't have enough time to explore the city and Napa Valley being stuck indoors at the convention.
Finally; the beds were very comfortable and gave me a great night sleep!
Great Job PARC 55 Team!!!
Tip: though it rains in S.F. a lot; you don't need to bring an umbrella as the hotel provides complementary daily umbrellas.

The good things about this place is that :
1. It is only a few blocks from the Transport
2. Near eating areas
3. Close to hop on and hop off sightseeing bus stop
The downside is:
1. Noisy rooms - you can hear the background noise from the airconditioning/ventilation machines from nearby buildings on the rooftop

I don't understand some reviewers. Marina Inn offers a decent room per usd 100/120 the night in a very nice location in SF. Close to the buses and 10 minutes walking to Fisherman Wharf. And that is a fantastic deal. Ok, the breakfast is not so good. But with the money you have saved you can have breakfast anywhere you want.
The staff was very helpfull and the overall experiencie was perfect for me.
Try to ask a room facing Octavia St. It's gonna be quieter.
The only problem is that the Hotel has no parking. Is tough to find a place in this area. Three blocks away there is a parking. The maximum you will pay there is 22 usd per day.

The staff at this hotel are simply outstanding. Everyone who we came in contact with, without fail, had a nice greeting every day. Even coming back afer just running across the street for a sandwich, we received a, "Welcome back!" I was on Club Level and the breakfast had both hot and cold choices. The late afternoon also had hot appetizers as well as fruits, cheese and crackers, red and white wine. The rooms are updated, albeit on the smaller side...but, it doesn't matter because you are never in your room anyway. Housekeeping was impeccable. It was within walking distance to the White House and all other major sites. The neighborhood is safe and there are restaurant choices very close. I would absolutely stay here again. I really can't say enough about the quality of the staff. Every single person working there truly seemed to like their job and it showed in how genuinely friendly everyone was. I'm sure you can get bigger rooms that are closer to the sites, but I think you would be hardpressed to get the same level of service anywhere else. I'll take a smaller room for wonderful people any day. LOVED our stay!

I stayed here both in 2011 (when it was still the Cooper Square hotel) and in 2012 (after it changed to the Standard). Overall, the hotel retains the high quality and service that I appreciate. However, I do have to say that the hotel has become slightly less personal and the feeling you get is less cozy. The hotel definitely feels less like a "hidden gem" and the hipster element has definitely discovered this hotel after the switch to the Standard hotel group. 
Pros: 
- Amazing location. The hotel is in the middle of everything (midway between Union Square, Washington Square, SoHo -- and only one block from St Marks Square and the LES), yet Cooper Square is quiet and calm. 
- Friendly staff who go out of their way to help you. Friendly but not intrusive. Hip but not annoyingly hipster. Just right. 
- Well-appointed and thoughtfully designed & furnished rooms that are new and clean. The bed is very comfortable. I liked the sauna function in the shower. 
- Free Internet Wifi. 
Cons:

- A bit expensive for the room size, especially without breakfast. 
- The heat/AC settings fluctuate randomly, so the room veers from too hot to too cold and back.

title_masked: Very nice people and good service
text_masked: I stay at this hotel at least once a week on my business trips. I really like this hotel because I feel welcomed and the rooms are very nice. Also havea a great breakfast bar.

We booked directly with the hotel. Having been recommended this hotel and viewing the reviews on TA we had quite high expectations. Happily these were met, the staff were welcoming and friendly we had a room on the 32nd floor. Although our room was not ready when we got there we left our bags and headed out into the bright lights of NYC, The room is huge with a fully serviced kitchen including a full size fridge. title_masked: Hazzle free policy a real joke
text_masked: This is the 3rd time we stay in the hotel. This time we were given one of the older rooms, not refurbished yet. We didn't care much about that , but what really made us mad was they didn't make our room on our 2nd night. They didn't make the bed, change towels or cleaned our trash bin. When we requested to abide by the "Hazzle free" policy in which they shoud reinburse you in case there is any kind of hazzle, the "Customer service specialist" just said we're sorry we cannot reinburse you for the night because the stay had been made through expedia, but that I should call expedia to ask for a 10% discount... that's really a joke. Will deffinitely not stay here again. THe only thing we chose this place was location which is close to the riverwalk but you can choose a comfort inn which is around the corner. We stayed in this hotel for two days It's an excellent choice if you want to stay near the airport. The breakfast was almost the best we ever had. Rooms were spacious, very good beds. Staff very helpful. No complaints at all! So we definitely will stay here again!!

We needed to stay close to O'Hare Airport as we were catching an early morning flight. There is no close hotel to the airport than the O'Hare Hilton. Very nice place to stay.Very nice room with just the right amenities for you to sleep comfortably and get on your way early without further transportation to the terminal.
Friendly staff, close restaurant and great views of the airplanes taking off if you book a higher room. Reasonable rates, as well. Would definitely stay again if flyting out of O'Hare.

We arrived on WED June13,12 rooms were ready but not very clean.One bed had hair on it doorknob to connecting door was loose mildew in bathroom ceiling, not to mention that the beds were very small furniture outdated...I reported to front desk I beleive his name was [NAME] that the tub faucet drips and water does not turn completely off,also I left a note in room for hsk to report it never got fixed.We were there with our church youth trip I work in a hotel and I look for the cleanliness @EVERY hotel I stay in the hair dryers were full of dirt and hair seems as though room had not been stayed in a while it was on the 20th floor room 2001 maint/hsk need to do a General cleaning of rooms this is unacceptable for a full service hotel the area is nice but rooms are not what you expect when you walk in....we stayed 4nights

This is a real hotel, nice big clean rooms with all the facilities for the Business man,a Pool and business centre, fitness centre and get this, this has to be a first in the world /world
Free yes free washing and drying laundry room, Customer service is here.
Only one draw back its located in limbo land a total new area. The nearest shops are about 3 miles away so you need a car or taxi. This is suited to arriving from the airpot or leaving and yes they have a shuttle. If you have a car Auroa is about 8 miles away with a big shopping centre.
Warning Denver is a big city and going anywhere is a tirip, it is very well spread out.
Breakfast is very good.

This is THE place to stay in Houston, especially if you are undergoing medical treatment, which was the case with me. I checked into the hotel on Nov.18, and from that moment on, I was treated like royalty. Thank you all so much for making a medical appt. more tolerable.
My room (suite, actually) was spotlessly clean and comfortable. The bed was great, and I especially enjoyed the variety of pillows. Bath area was good, and the water pressure was perfect.
While there, I ate in the restaurant twice, and had good meals. First for dinner, and the food, while pretty basic, was good. The breakfast buffet is fantastic, with variety of meats, eggs, etc. Good coffee, too.
I used the shuttle service to go to my Dr. appt, and the driver did a wonderful job of getting me there, and picking me up again. They also have shuttle service available to go to some of the shopping areas, such as Rice Village and the Galleria.

title_masked: Best way to spend a Bday!
text_masked:
The W alone is an amazing property to stay at but the W Lakeshore beat any expectations that I had.
From the moment we walked in the door Diana at the front desk was so welcoming and sweet. She did not hesitate to assign us to such a beautiful room with a remarkable view. :) Thank you Diana.
The trip only got better as we met Ashley at the Concierge desk! Ashley, you are an absolute Asset to the W Lakeshore. Being a Concierge at a Hilton in Fort Lauderdale Fl. I know what guest expect from the Concierge desk and Ashley went far beyond the call of duty! She recommended the best places to go and the best way to spend my 23rd birthday! Ashley, thank you for the surprise gifts awaiting our arrival back to our hotel room. You made Chicago and my birthday that much better! I will definitely be returning. ;)

The Touchstone is just that. It is a touchstone for you to leave your bags ...and later go to sleep while in San Francisco. It is not a destination hotel. I booked it here because I spend very little time in a hotel and the price was really excellent for San Fran. 
My room was really small. In fact, one of the concerns i had was that it didn't even have a full length mirror. Probably wouldn't fit! It was very clean but definitely could use a coat of paint. Lots of scrapes and marks on the walls. Bathroom was tiny but shower was hot and so no complaints there.
Bed was super comfortable and the first night i slept great. I had read reviews about the noise but quite honestly, noise doesn't usually bother me. The telling factor was the ear plugs provided in the room. The second night there was a "drum concert" on the street with people banging garbage cans. This lasted over two hours. I realize this is not the hotel's fault but it is something to consider if you don't have the luxury of sleeping in and need a full night's sleep.
Free wi-fi is provided in the rooms but was not in service my second day. Diner adjoined to hotel was pretty good and i enjoyed the 25% discount. 
My overall opinion of this hotel is it is Average and that's not bad. It's good if you are a tourist and just need a place to shower and sleep.

For Starters
The public areas look great and the designers really got this right. 
They took the old Trump Hyatt Gold gaudy glitz and buried it.In its place is a world class dramatic lobby of today and tomorrow that clearly is in keeping with more of the Grand Hyatt architecture and design tradition more so of Hyatt International standards. 
Check in Reception 
Excellent and highly hospitable with can do anything attitude 
The new and inspired club lounge inside and out is simply sensational looking.
It ranks up there with the slickest looking executive lounges I have seen anywhere in the world. In nice weather they even have an outdoor deck to enjoy the offerings outdoors. Brilliant! The silly dead butterflies on display seem odd to me inside the lounge and I'll assume some decorator’s weird idea of what would go well in the new lounge. 
The club is now located on the 16th floor (previously the 31rst floor) and only there did they do really do a hard renovation to the hallways and immediate areas entering the club. It’s a welcome refresh. It would have been cool to follow through on every floor.....Relocating the lounge on the 31rst floor was a good idea as the elevators are poor and take a considerably long time to get up to that floor. Especially when the hotel has high occupancy.
The hotels elevators are looking worse for wear and they are the same small cramped elevators. One would hope they are slated for replacement or refurbishment.
The club lounge closes for breakfast at 9:30 AM in the morning
For those of us coming from other time zones especially International guests this seems uncaring and insensitive. The breakfast is satisfactory however the hotel should pay more attention to baking quality and variety of offerings as the previously did in the past. Evening offerings are now very minimal also compared to years past. The beverage selection is outstanding
Accommodations’
The folks at check in couldn’t have been more hospitable and welcoming
They upgraded me to a nice jr suite as a Hyatt Diamond long time guest
Unfortunately it was very noisy on a mid level floor facing 42nd street. I liked my room otherwise. The caring good folks here yet upgraded me further to a quieter larger suite where I had a wonderful one night stay overall after moving.
I really appreciated the small refrigerator that they now have in every room!
The unexpected upside here to the new rooms is though the bed is a platform (not a fan of such beds typically) it appears Hyatt has indeed found a mattress that can disguise how firm the platform bed really is. One gets a satisfactory enough night’s sleep. Housekeeping overall needs a little more attention to detail. It seems that they are rushed to finish their duties leaving some small unattended concerns. Mind you it’s still in the acceptable range
The Grand Hyatt New York Executive Club lounge was in years past the Gold standard of club lounge offerings they do need to step up their game less on presentation which is excellent and more on substance. It would bring me back more frequently.
Let’s hope for more continued improvement certainly the hotel has been made more desirable.My thanks to the hotel for recognizing Gold Passport members.
This is where the hotel still shines Guest Program recognition.
The Hyatt may not be the best choice in town but it still remains on my very possible list every time I come into town depending on rate which frequently can be wildly overpriced. The Grand Hyatt is dependable overall and the location can’t be beat. 
Experiences will widely vary due to size of property and a very different array of room types.
While it’s far from a great renovation it’s an adequate one and a hotel after many years is now looking better. The hotels management has changed a number of times over the course of the years. What's great about the hotel is Hyatt finds some remarkable individuals that always seem to care about the customer with or without issues that can arise.
Even though challenges remain at this hotel at times I continue to return thanks to the caring team that helps you to forget this is a large convention hotel with 31 floors and over 1000 plus rooms. 
Just think how hard it must be to manage all guest expectations.
They do reasonably well despite the service bumps along the road.
Thank You Grand Hyatt for many years of caring service at the end of the day and taking good care of me!
Kudos too for being interactive with your customers/customer service online and off!
We can be a hard bunch to please :)

title_masked: Lovely area, nice clean rooms but for price can get better else where.$325 night & no room coffee maker? not good enough
text_masked:
We stayed at the doubletree for 6 nights and paid approx $325 a night for 2 double beds. This is my 6th visit to New York.
I will start with my first impressions of the Doubletree Metropolitan which is a friendly welcome outside of the hotel by the door staff, then when we checked in we were ' welcomed' to the doubletree by the receptionist however this was done with no smile what so ever. The receptionist made no small talk such as how was your flight? or told us any hotel information about wifi etc only what room/floor we were on.
I believe that when you check-in you are to be given a choice of water or a cookie, we were not given this option and was given the cookie.
I requested a room on a high floor on my booking reservation however I was given a room on the 3rd floor. When I asked for another on a higher floor I was given the 11th which was appreciated however my 'special request' for a higher floor was clearly never even looked at.
We was pleased with the room size it was very spacious and clean. We had 2 doublebeds and they were very comfortable. Bathroom was a reasonable/ average size for NY standards but didn't appear to have had been refurbished.
I believe the whole hotel has recently had a refurb but I wouldn't say I noticed in the room it just looked like average decore.
On entering our room it was exceptionally cold, we had attempted to follow the instructions given to increase the room temperature however found this to be complicated so I called and asked for the maintenance to come to the room to assist us.
3 phone calls to the care line, 1 visit to reception and over a 2 hours wait we finally had the maintenance in our room and told us how to work it. The instructions to use it are incorrect without the maintenance guy showing us we would have never had figured it out. Having to wait 2 hours and make 3 phone calls AND a trip to reception was unacceptable, in other hotels I have never had to wait longer than 20mins for assistance and given this is not a particularly large hotel in comparison with others I am not sure why I was waiting so long?
Each day the housekeeping staff said good morning and were always very friendly. They also did a great job each day maintaining the cleanliness of our room. They are a credit to the hotel so much more than the reception staff in my personal experience.
The staff in the lobby would also wish us a good morning however the reception staff did not and any interactions we had with them were not done in a welcoming or friendly way.
Our room key stopped working twice on our stay; I believe this to be an issue with the hotel, an issue which has not yet to be rectified. On both occasions when getting a new key card from reception there was no apology given either time and on one occasion I found the receptionist to be quite rude when showing her my key card and room number instead of apologising for the key not working and asking for ID she simply said ' well I don't know who you are I've never seen you before as I didn't check you in so I will need to see identification' 
It comes up time and time again on here, there is no tea/coffee maker in the room which is crazy in this day and for the price you pay for this hotel it is expected and totally unacceptable not to have them. Even if they compromised and instead of in the rooms had tea and coffee available for guests in reception each morning so you could at least come down and bring a coffee up to your room, but nope nothing! 
I asked one of the staff why there was no tea/coffee maker and was informed it was due to the time and upkeep which for the price guests pay, size of hotel and for the 4star it has ( also being a part of the Hilton chain) is a pathetic excuse! To save money more like....... so much for the customer comes first. 
Finally I was aware that to check bags on check-out they charge $1 a bag/case however what I was not aware of was that it is $1 to check-in each bag and then another $1 each when picking bag up. So for 3 hours we had left our bags at hotel before returning and leaving for the airport and the total cost of this was $12.
The hotel is well located and in a really lovely area of NY however at the price they are charging there are other hotels in the area which for the same price or less you would get more for your money or if you manage to get a good deal much less than what we paid which was $325 a night.

title_masked: Loved the assistance from the Front Desk
text_masked: We arrived very late- night flight from California and were really challenged by the one way streets in downtown Chicago- not to mention that Wacker Drive has an east,west,north and south version. Emiguela was our front desk hostess and she made it feel better. Got us into a nice room and promised us a better one the next day. Gave us some great tips on "Word of the month." I have stayed here three times in the last month. I do business in Dallas. I find the service by the staff to be above average, but the hotel rooms need improvement. My desk chair looked kind of ratty and worn. The decor pillows need to be revamped or taken out of the rooms. Daily cleaning is somewhat minimal, but I am not a messy person. The area around the hotel is suspect and the police are frequently making arrests. It gets lots of tourists and the price seems to fit the lower end budget. The bar is nice and always a friendly person to serve you. The clientele is really a mixed crowd. I've stayed at other crown plazas and really had a comfortable stay. This hotel needs some work in the rooms. On the weekend nights, the hotel bar turns into a nightclub which I can't stand. The crowd gets pretty lit and they are not Dallas's finest. Not a pretty site. I'm looking for another hotel to stay at to have a more subdued but comfortable stay.

title_masked: Convenient, friendly staff, a little dated
text_masked: This hotel is a half a block from the red-line Tufts station and just a few blocks from the other lines. Also a nice walk to Boston Commons or other downtown areas. Our room was clean, but the furniture was showing some wear. The staff at the front desk were exceptionally helpful. The omlette-maker in the restaurant buffet enjoys his work and it shows. The Starbucks off the lobby is about the same level as our local Safeway starbucks.

We stayed in this property over a long weekend and found the hotel to be a very good all around selection. 
Let me begin with the positives, and the top marks belong to its location to Time Square and the Broadway district. You can see and do anything with in an easy walk of 4 blocks. You have a variety of places to eat, shop, and be entertained, and you don't need a cab. The room appeared clean and after we asked for linens for the fold away couch they made effort to keep that area clean and neat each day. We got to the city at 1:30 and we were allowed to check into our rooms early which helped us get a jump start on our trip. The Concierge was very helpful and made excellent suggestions when we were planning our trips into different areas of town. There is a Starbucks right next door for your morning coffee!
The suite that we stayed in was dated, and the wifi was terrible. The bedding was not the quality that you normally find for the price of the room, and the mattress felt like a rock. I was very disappointed in the sleep quality, but we did so much walking that we were worn out by the time we got back to the hotel and passed out it did not matter. 
They could certainly upgrade the bedding and the mattresses, but the location goes a long way to make this a very good option to see NYC.

The Hotel Pennsylvania is a great hotel well positioned in Midtown Manhattan for those visiting NY. The Penn 5000 room was large and had all conveniences required. The hotel has a charm about it and may need to look at upgrading the rooms over the next few years. The room while comfortable needed a new paint job as walls and doors were scuffed in places. Other than that, l can recommend the Hotel Penn to any traveller.

This hotel is right off Hwy 8 and near lots of great places. You can hit the Mission Valley Mall during the day, and go out in Hillcrest for dinner at night! We didn't have breakfast or use the spa at the hotel, that is the only reason I marked it as average.

For those less familiar with Manhattan, the lodging options are overwhelming. With so many choices, it should be easy to find a myriad of properties that suit any number of requirements. But for me, it was a struggle to find the perfect location, level of amenities, and acceptable price point for a recent 4-day trip w/ my hubby. 
I ruled out the overpriced hipster boutiques, the stuffy landmarks, the dinosaur properties, the tourist-laden chains, and the too-good-to-be true rates in less desirable parts of town. After that, I wasn't left with nearly as many options as you'd think.
Then I found the listing for the San Carlos. I loved that they're one of the very last independently owned hotels in NYC, catered to a European clientele (which usually means non-fussy rooms, immaculately clean spaces, and competent staff), and the Manhattan East location; the area was convenient to RCMH where we were seeing 2 nights of concerts. The fact the rooms looked large vs the price and came w/ mini fridges and microwaves (somewhat unusual for Manhattan) sealed the deal. But looking good on paper doesn't mean in reality it will pan out.
I'd made my reservation months in advance, over the phone, for a certain room type that the young lady I spoke to had 100% guaranteed. When I called week-of to confirm my reservation, I was told there was a possibility I might not be able to get the room type I'd been promised. Irked, I referenced the original reservation but they explained sometimes these things happen. True, but I hung up the phone and considered rebooking elsewhere; the phone rang back moments later and the young lady I originally spoke to apologized, said they would upgrade me at no fee and get me what I needed no matter what, and really acted as if she valued my business. I'd expect this from a 5 star property, but at a under $300 a night spot, it was refreshing. Customer service is a dying art. The staff at the San Carlos is old school, in the best possible, most refreshing way. 
Upon arrival, an easy cab ride from Penn Station, the lobby was sparkling, the bellman exceptional, and the check-in flawless. It's not the fanciest place, more suited for the upscale business traveler (though I spied many families too) but the cleanliness, a huge factor for me, absolutely perfect. And my room, a King, was HUGE. Not huge just by NYC standards, huge by any hotel standard. 
The view from our particular room wasn't much to see, but windows that actually open in both the room and bathroom were a bonus. The amenities were lovely, towels and robe divinely soft, the bed linens super comfy, and a pant press a blast from the past. The room was modern, simple, understated, private, quiet, and cozy. Everything worked too. Which should go without saying but unfortunately is often not the case in any class of hotel. The real silverware, plates, and glasses provided were a great compliment to the microwave and fridge.
 Did I mention that housekeeping is outstanding? In my years of travel, I've never seen more competent housecleaning. 
My interaction with the staff was easy peasy. Items I needed were sent up immediately, dinner spots/phone numbers provided, and I was always greeted with a smile. I dreaded check out because it meant our experience was over. I literally had zero complaints during my entire stay except that the Indian restaurant next door (that serves as the San Carlos' complimentary breakfast serving area and then offers their own menu for limited room service too), is simply not up to par with the rest of the hotel.  If 24 hour American cuisine room service is a make it or break it deal for you, that's about the only reason I'd consider finding a different hotel. Seeing as Manhattan has every food conceivable, most of it deliverable, I easily overlook this.
Quiet rooms, pleasant interiors/halls, a great business center/overflow lobby, elevators that were kept constantly cleaned (check the Ritz for smudges, lol), and staff that valued my business means that next I'm in NYC I'm making a beeline right back here. Sure, there's more glamorous or hip spots, but for the level of service vs price and comfort, there's a reason this is a hidden gem amongst your hundreds of NYC hotels. Part of me doesn't want the secret to get out.

title_masked: Chic Hotel in Gas Lamp district
text_masked: We stayed 3 nights in this hotel staff were great. The room was very nice and comfortable. Located in trendy Gas Lamp district. Great for hip younger crowd who like go clubbing in the evening. Lots of restaurants and bars nearby. Horton Plaza is in walking distance with stores, movies etc. Pro's -morning coffee and evening wine tasting Cons -If you drive or rent a car it costs $40 a day for parking. Sign up for their loyalty program before you go to be able to have Wi Fi free and you get other perks.

This is the third time we have choose to stay in the Sohotel. The staff is very polite and gentle, and ready to do for you what ever you need. The rooms are big and comfortable, and very clean. 
In spite of that, the WI-FI was working very slowly, or didn't work at all in the rooms. Another thing which be must considered is that the street sounds and noise is strongly heard in the room, a whole day long. 
We absolutely will come again.

Ir was the second time that usted the hotel. The serviles completes, the perplejo vera nice . The rooms Have many things that help me a live vera good in my das there. The point most low was the breakfast, but is in relativo sin to prize. 
It is ideal for trips alone or bussines or shopping. I like it more the Quinta In in Fort Laudarle. This is most modern.

After a long summer of working in the hospitality industry my boyfriend and I decided we needed to get away for a night. Found the perfect deal on Hotwire for a 4.5 star hotel in the Back Bay/Copley Place area of Boston for one night. Purchased the hotel and found out it was the Westin. Upon check in we were placed in a King room compared to the two doubles we originally thought we booked. The room was on the 18th floor and located in the corner, it had windows all around with a panoramic view of the city (and in the distance, Fenway Park, which we found out later). Also in the room was a flat screen tv, individual coffee make with Starbucks coffee, in-room safe, and a mini bar (with the normal prices). The bed was "heavenly" which Westin is known for. Bathroom was nice with a magnifying vanity mirror and towel rack that was located on the wall of the shower. The complimentary bottle of water was perfect after a long day. Not knowing the area as well as others, we decided to speak with the Conceirge for suggestions on dinner. Since we did not know what we wanted she gave us a map and suggested we walk Newbury Street for ideas. Finally we decided that we wanted steak and she recommended Abe & Louie's, perfect recommendaton. All in all the hotel was in a beautiful location (also attached to the shopping at the Prudential Center) and had perfect accommodations for our quick getaway.

We enjoyed our stay a the Bay Club Hotel. Overall, it was a good experience. The rooms and hotel are clean and the staff is very friendly and helpful. They offer a buffet-style complimentary breakfast which was "ok". We ate breakfast 2 days there, but after we went out for breakfast. The fitness room over looks the marina, but honestly we enjoyed walking/jogging along the bay much better. The equipment is a bit outdated. We discovered after the first full day there, that you have to call the front desk to arrange your room to be serviced, but after that was pleasantly surprised when they came in thereafter on a daily basis without the phone call. All in all a good experience and we will definately stay again.

title_masked: My Weekend at the Empire Hotel
text_masked: This is my first stay at the Empire, although I have eaten at the fabulous Ed's Chowder House several times before performances at Lincoln Center. The location is perfect. We walked in Central Park, shopped at Columbus Circle, and the Met was a quick stroll across the street. The room was very minimalist but comfortable. The staff really makes this hotel special. Thanks to Romeo and everyone else who helped make our stay so pleasant. The Empire will be my New York home away from home from now on.

I stayed at the Revere with my nine year old twins who are seasoned travelers. The staff was lovely. A complimentary dessert was sent to my children the first night along with a complimentary breakfast.
The room was beautiful and roomly. It was also close to Boston Common and the T. What more could you ask for?

title_masked: Perfect Place to Stay to See Events in Downtown Houston!!
text_masked: My daughter and I attended a Paul McCartney concert a couple of weeks ago in Houston at Minute Maid Park. The Hilton Americas Hotel is located in downtown Houston and was the perfect place to stay because its within walking distance of the ball park! We parked our car in the Hilton parking garage which was complimentary and we walked to a nice restaurant downtown for dinner and then to the ballpark for the concert. No problems with traffic or parking! The hotel and room was very nice and I got it with Hilton Honors points so you couldn't beat it! We had a wonderful stay with no hassles and it was the perfect hotel to stay in to see an event downtown!

title_masked: Perfect location, amazing service and comfy bed!
text_masked: This Ritz is great. It is located in Water Tower Place, which is a great location for shopping. Very close to amazing restaurants. The service is outstanding. Beds and pillows are what you would expect from a luxury hotel. I did not get a chance to experience their spa, but I plan to on my next visit. They accomodated me with a late check out (2pm!) which was great. Randy at the reception desk was friendly, welcoming and very informative.

Each morning, I awoke to bug bites. On the last night of a four night stay, I woke up around 1am and had to get out of bed. I was covered in bites. I notified the front desk who advised I would have to wait for the manager who would arrive around 8am. The general manager never did contact me. After I arrived home, I still did not hear from the hotel.

We reserved 2 rooms this weekend. From the time we stepped through the door our service was great. I left my watch in my room and called after I realized it. They federal expressed my watch to my home! It is an old hotel but very well kept. Location is great.

title_masked: Trendy, good location, but you have to pay for WiFi
text_masked: stayed here for a conference taking place down the street so picked it for convenience. Rooms as I understand it are small in NYC - was upgraded to the one above cozy i think (called wonderful?) upon check-in and room size was fine for me although I cant imagine what kind of shoe box i would have had if not 'upgraded'! A/C is quite loud but you get used to it and i didnt spend much time in my 'Cozy' room anyway. Room a little worn but nothing to really cause concern as was clean. No bath tub if you want one (I prefer showers anyway). Great supply of Body products each day - not topped up but new individual products given. Not sure about the breakfast as ate at the conference. Lounge bar area is where you pickup free wifi but expectation to purchase a drink or two. Otherwise pay about $15 for the in-room wifi per day. Bar next door always seemed to be buzzing each evening. Staff are polite, helpful, especially the concierge lady who recommended a french restaurant about 10mins walk from the hotel - Matisse (? cant quite remember) which was pleasant. If you're looking for a place to crash and a good location (subway very close, grand central station down the road) - this is fine but can be more expensive than other hotels yet not as brilliant as the price tag may suggest.

i thoroughly enjoyed my room at extended stay, the staff were extremely polite and helpful. what really got me was that every morning, there was fresh coffee alongside bagels and muffins just waiting for guests in the lobby. my only grievance is that they do not have kat 5 cables/ethernet cables for there guests. Me, having stayed at extended stays before, was expecting them too. i brought my x-box along and thank goodness i brought a wireless adapter because it would be useless, plus the fact that when i first plugged in my laptop i realized why... they want to charge extra for a highspeed connection!!! i was thoroughly disappointed. the other extended stays all have been able to provide me with ethernet cords so far for free without trying to get extra money. that majorly disappointed me. sry extended but you need to change that. id rather pay 10$ more to stay somewhere that can provide me an ethernet cord and not try to rip me off $3 dollars a day for highspeed WIRELESS internet, what a joke. wireless only gets so fast. other than that the features and ammenities where great and the staff friendly and helpful.

I was in town for a hardware show and this was one of the hotels that was recommended. We were approximately 4-6 blocks south of the heart of the shopping on Michigan avenue. I really enjoyed this property, the lobby was very contemporary in decor and clean. My room was a corner room which had a view on two sides which was very nice. The bedding was very comfortable and lots of pillows. The bathroom was rather large and was equipped with a large bath tub, and a shower. The lobby bar had a nice open air feel with great service. I was not a fan of the bar stools though, not very comfy at all. We did not eat on property, there was a wonderful breakfast place down the street, "Wildberry's" that had a coffee bar and inside that we ate at every morning, and 1 block east on Michigan ave. was a nice diner "Sweetwater" that had lots of draft beers, and great sandwiches and salads. Right next door to the property was a drug store that came in handy for bottled waters, and anything you might have forgotten. Next time I'm in Chicago I will try and stay here again if the rates are what I consider reasonable to the competition.

We travelled as a family to New York for my 2 sons to run their first marathon so dissapointment was rife when it was cancelled just 36 hours before it was due to run.
Staying at the Doubletree Inn Times Square however made up for some of that. The rooms were spotless and well equiped, and the sitting room gave space for everyone to spread out and also afforded privacy.
We found the staff attentive, polite and they quickly repsponded to calls when our toilet refused to stop filling!- it was fixed immediately and was fine after that.
Warm chocolate chip cookies on demand was a great afternoon treat, and the position of the hotel meant all the glitz and glamour of Times Square was right on the doorstep.
Only negative was the bar - bit of an afterthought as just by reception and felt more like a holding room for the lifts.- so get your drinks elsewhere.
Overall a great place to stay and I would do so again- despite the high cost - but it is New York right?

Stayed here for 2nights, free parking which was great. The room was comfy and clean. Got the Tour Bus from outside the Hotel which took us all around the City. Area was safe and we found some great bars and restaurants. Breakfast was a little bit cramped in the reception area which did not matter as you could take your drinks and food to your room, Staff were very friendly and helpful. Would recommend this Hotel .

Wonderful hotel, great location, great staff you can stay here for any occasion: Business, vacations or for a quick getaway!
Two thumbs up ! Spectacular rooms, modern installations, they have it all. A little bit pricey but hey.. you know what they say, you get for what you pay for
I will definitely come back to the W location

Everything you'd expect from a modern hotel. Great service. Large and comfortable rooms. Staff were happy to help. Room service was a real treat and I liked the healthy options menu.
One of the two elevators wasn't working while I was there. I didn't mind waiting but I thought it was really cheeky to put up a sign asking you to "participate in their wellbeing initiative by taking the stairs." It's not a wellbeing initiative, your lift is broken. But I guess you don't spend time DC if you don't have a high tolerance for bull**it.
Would happily stay there again though.

We don't usually stay at Radissons because of the cost. However, the hotel prices in Phoenix (at least in September 2012) were so affordable, we went with this upgrade. We had been traveling in Arizona and needed a place to stay near the airport before flying out in the morning.
The staff were very nice. There was help available to bring up suitcases if we wanted it, but they let us borrow their suitcase cart and do it ourselves. Someone brought up a small portable crib and set it up for our child. In the morning, the breakfast staff let us feed our three year old off of our two orders of breakfast buffet rather than pay $14.95 for her, too. (Don't worry, she hardly eats anything compared to an adult.)
The outside pool was beautiful--very up to date and modern, and the hot tub was the largest one I had ever seen. It was too hot for me as a pregnant woman to sit in, but hubby enjoyed it. Unfortunately, the pool itself was VERY chilly. We swam at night, but the day had been in the mid-90s. I guess the pool is in the shade in the afternoon, which might be why it was so cold. It was definitely not heated, as the hotel information had stated. 
The room was updated, pleasantly decorated, and mid-sized. The desk in the king bed room was huge--the biggest I've ever seen in a hotel room. If you needed to work, you could easily spread out and get a lot done. The bed was a sleep number bed and was extremely comfortable with nice quality sheets. 
Negatives: under the curtain at the window, the wallpaper was peeling off the walls, probably due to to a leak from outside. The tub/shower was also not as sparklingly clean as I expect in a hotel. I saw some mold growth and hairs.
When we checked out, we ran into an awkward moment with a staff worker. She said since we had registered through a travel site, she did not have a receipt to give us for the night's stay. Since we had given the hotel our credit card number for incidentals, we just wanted a receipt saying we had no incidentals. The staff person refused to do this. I imagine the manager would have been willing to work with us on it, but we forgot to ask for him or her. 
Overall, we were pleased with the stay and would stay there again.

title_masked: Fantastic Place in Clinton (Hell's Kitchen) New York City
text_masked: I brought my daughter and her friend to New York for their 16th birthdays and based on the amazing reviews I had read here and the low price (compared to other places in NYC) chose to stay here. I even got a great unsolicited recommendation from a friend back home when she found out we were going to NYC. An excellent choice! Right from the moment we arrived it was welcoming, comfortable, and professional without being stuffy. All the staff were friendly and helpful. The rooms were roomy (pardon the pun) and the bathroom was a very nice size. The housekeeping was spectacular. It was close or central to pretty much everything we wanted to see and do. I highly recommend staying at the Distrikt Hotel and would stay again.

We stayed the first night up the street at the Holiday Inn - that was a disaster as previously reviewed. This hotel is just up the street and close to the bay. You can easily walk downtown to the Gas Lamp restaurants or the the big shopping mall - 5 short city blocks away, or you can walk to the Midway museum and the harbour cruises in 5 minutes. You have to valet park your vehicle - which is ok since you walk most places and can get your vehicle quite quickly if you need it. The hotel has a nice free breakfast in the morning and a happy hour with free drinks in the evening. My only complaint is that it does not free WIFI internet - although if you ask they will give you a complimentary few free hours or you can use one of the 3 free terminals in the lobby ( although they can all be occupied at certain times).
For the money this as the best hotel on the San Diego waterfront IMO.

title_masked: Older style in a very traditional setup
text_masked: This hotel is well located in an older building with some old facilities with very traditional looking rooms, I could not find why I did not feel at home during my stay but now I know, there is NO ambience here.

Easter weekend was our first trip to Boston and we had the pleasure of staying at the Hotel Commonwealth! The staff was friendly and helpful. The room was large, clean and had an excellent view of Fenway Park. It's located right next door to the "T" so transportation was easy! I would recommend this hotel to anyone traveling to Boston!

Spent four nights while at a conference, and couldn't have asked for anything more. Clean, friendly, helpful. Great views, comfortable bed, great restaurants. My favorite feature might just have been how I could get from the Westin to the shops to the conference center -- all by walking indoors! Everything was connected!! Sure helped on one of those dreary rainy days. Maybe the concierge was my favorite feature--always more helpful than I expected. Maybe it was the restaurant/bar? Good sports, good food. Couldn't have been better.

My wife and I stayed at the hotel teh weekend of Jan 14-15. Booked though hotels tonight for $105 total including taxes. First impression was only "Wow!" I don't think I've ever stayed at such a chic place before. 
The lobby has a modenist design with chairs and couches spread though out. The carpets have a great design with soundwaves printed on them. Each floor is named after a musician and has a great mural of them on a wall and has a case with some memorbilia as well.
We were given a 19th floor room which was impeccably clean. The room had a great vibe with sleek stylish funiture and comfortable queen bed. The little reading lights above the bed were a nice touch. I like to read at night and my wife is a light sleeper and they didn't bother her at all. 
The same chic vibe continued to the bathroom with modern fixtures and lighting. It was a shower only with no tub which is fine for my wife and I. The shampoo and shower gels were particularly good. So, good that my wife went down to the Hard Rock Shop and puchased a full sized shower gel for home. The only drawback to the room in general was the shower couldn't be closed all the way. It had a half plane of glass that couldn't be closed so it was off putting but by no means a reason not to stay there again. If anything it was that I just wasn't used to the design.
A note about parking. Valet is $50 a night and there is limited self parking that's about a half block away and $35 a night. Now, this is standard for Chicago and while high it's something that you'd have to pay no matter where you stay.
Overall, I would definitely stay here again. The rooms are swank with nice music touches all around. A great hotel and I will certainly be staying here again on my next trip to Chicago.

Stayed at this hotel for one night while visiting Napa and San Fran. Loved this hotel. Very clean and modern. Very lively lobbby. This hotel is also pet friendly which is why we chose this hotel in the first place.

I just spent a wonderful night at the Hotel Sorella, Sat. March 24th. Service was wonderful and the rooms are very nice. I asked for a room on a high floor facing away from the citycentre activities and I'm glad I did! We didn't hear a thing and it made for a great night's sleep! The beds are very comfortable and decorated nicely. The room had plenty of pillows, towels and 2 bathrobes. We are from Katy so this was a mini staycation after having dinner at Eddy V's and sipping wine at the tasting room. We also visited the bar at the MonaLisa and they had a live band that was AWESOME!

We were so tired of Tgiving traffic that we decided at the last minute to spend the night in Dallas before continuing on home. I am so glad we did. The hotel staff were readily accommodating and very healpful, friendly and professional. This location is perfect for us - close to my son and close to everything downtown. 
An historic building that has been restored and updated - lovely eclectic decor, nice art work. Our room had an amazing view of the Dallas skyline and a huge TV...but most importantly an incredibly comfortable HUGE bed. An excellent rooftop pool area (gorgeous views and an infinity pool) with a great bar. The bar staff made us up some truly tasty cocktails and we met a lot of fun people. We had a couple of small plates that were also really good. We would have eaten there - I wanted to try some interesting things on the menu but we had heard such great things about the place across the street that we just had to go. 
It was just such a nice experience - everyone was friendly and professional. We will stay there every time we're in Dallas - I am really looking forward to going back.

I stayed here with my mother for my son's BMT graduation from Lackland. 5 minutes from base. We had a queen suite, with tv, free wifi, mini fridge and microwave. It was more than adequate for our needs as we left before dawn and returned after dark each day we were there. The place was clean, comfortable beds changed each day, fresh towels and wash cloths daily, I did laundry twice while there as they have a washer and two driers available to guests. Staff was friendly and helpful. If I ever have to go back to San Antonio, I will stay here again. If you are looking for amenities this isn't your place, if you are looking for a comfortable, clean and friendly place to stay, this is a great value.

title_masked: Nice rooms but a bit tiny, good location in Downtown Seattle.
text_masked: I'm a Hhonors Gold member. We booked a room on the executive level with two double beds. The view was a side view looking north, you could see some of the Puget Sound Bay if you look to the left. I traveled with my family, there were 5 of us with four full sized luggages and carry-on. Needless to say we were pretty cramped, but we did expect that coming in. The rooms were kind of tiny, but it would be ideal for 1-4 people. The bathroom has a walk-in sink and three way mirror, with the toilet and bathtub separated by a door. The toilet a high efficiency/water saver flusher. Very efficient and quick. Room service was excellent, as you would expect at any Hilton. The executive sky lounge on the top floor had excellent food and the view was great. We went for both 5 pm complimentary snacks and breakfast buffet. Got to mention this: The smoked northwest pacific salmon was to die for! (if you're into smoked fish) The hotel is about a 10-15 minute walk away from the Pike Place Market. As for the garage below the hotel: If you rent a car, try to get a smaller sized car. The garage is a little cramped and the parking spots are small. The garage might be difficult to drive through for some people, especially if you have a full sized SUV.

To whom it may concern-I recently spent two nights at your hotel, September 8-10. I was very disappointed with our room. I did extensive research and decided that my wife and I would have a second honeymoon at the Brown Palace. Here is what I thought I was getting as per your website:
Signature room. A king or two queen beds with plush bedding, a rich wood armoire, a walk-in closet—this spacious room with high ceilings invites you to spread out and relax. Marvel at the expansive bathroom featuring double marble sinks, a makeup mirror, and a deluxe corner glass shower with rain showerhead. With a flat-screen HDTV, iPod docking station, WiFi and personal Keurig coffee maker
Room 739 does not have the "double marble sinks, deluxe corner glass shower with rainhead or walk in closet" as your website stated above. Very disappointed with this, this is not the room your site suggests and not what I reserved.
Other items that were not there. Only had one robe instead of two for the guests. Exhaust fan in bathroom didn't work.
I would expect for the money we would have had a better stay. Spent $700 on the room and another $700 on food, wifi, parking and the spa. Don't feel I got my $1,400 worth of this place. Will not be returning.

Just got back from a business trip to San Francisco. Our conference was at the Hilton, Union Square. I was pleasantly surprised by the cleanliness of the hotel. It didn't feel old and outdated. There are plenty of places within walking distance to go and eat. You can walk to China Town.

Good location if your going to the convention centre. I was not. Here for a week I found the area quite and uncomfortable: near he greyhound terminal and a church that takes in drug addicts it doesn't exactly paint a great picture of Philly.
Breakfast is free, but to be honest I wouldn't pay for that slop (my colleagues and I ended up going to Reading Terminal for breakfast). The bar is quite depressing at night.
The rooms are big, however and they are clean (although I found it disturbing that the hotel mad a point of advertising the fact they washed the sheets for new guests - I would hope this was standard practice and nothing to feel the need to advertise so much).
May be coming back to the city on business next year, but definitely won't be staying here again.

The Best Western airport is a good place to stay if you fly in and are going on a cruise.They provide transportation both from the aiport and the cruise terminal.Staff is very nice and helpful.Will stay again.

title_masked: Great Hotel and Amazing Views from the top
text_masked: We stayed here in August 12 during a 3 day stay in San Fran. The hotel is huge and well located in SF. It took us 25mins from the airport, and it's a 5 min walk to Union Sq. You can catch a cable car to Fishermans wharf or try walking. It's a half hour walk and takes you through the scenic side of SF. The view bar is the jewel in the crown for this hotel, with great views over SF from the 34th floor. The hotel has free wifi in the lobby and in the view bar, great for uploading your pics of the view on your Facebook. wifi in rooms is chargeable. We didn't try the dining options apart from the food in the view bar. the staff are all very attentive and helpful. the waitress in the View bar organised off-menu options for our kids. The concierge even organised Alcatraz tickets when all of the sites were reporting 'sold out'. I would recommend this hotel and would def stay again.

Hotel was great, the location for those going to Qualcomm HQ is perfect and walking distance. The hotel is modern with everything you need for a very reasonable price. For those looking for a holiday this is not the place and far from the beach but for business great. Breakfast was great and all you need. Coffee, Tea and cookies can be found in the lobby 24 hours a day for free. Rooms are large and with everything you need.

I formerly lived nearby, and have driven by the MarQueen hundreds of times, and I really wanted to love the place.
The exterior and lobby are gorgeous, and the hallways have a warm-and-cozy air, but our room didn't feel nearly as inviting unfortunately. It was large, but it felt cold. The furnishings were more 1990's-Bombay-Company than antique; an update wouldn't mean giving up old world charm, and I think it's time. Bed was jiggly, sheets were old, and the burgundy coverlet was flat and dated. (The one single thing that would have improved the room, a LOT: new, fresh linens.)
In the bath, they've done a fine job with old plumbing, but I had to bend-double to reach the faucet while avoiding smacking my head on the wobbly glass shelf. And while the fixtures were clean, the walls are so textured that dust and mildew are gaining ground, and little things like the wainscoting/frames/hairdryer-plug were coated with dust.
We had reserved a King room, but after opening our door to two queen beds and a trip downstairs to clarify, we were told they had oversold them. The clerk was breezily apologetic but it was kind of a bummer. We also weren't asked at check-out how our stay was, and I think it's just good policy to ask. Either way, I have to admit I was ready to go. (I'm sorry, MarQueen!)

We stayed for 1 night in Cova and were very pleased with this modern hotel. The only slight disadvantage is that the direct neighborhood is somewhat less appealing, with more beggars and homeless people than elsewhere in this part of the town. 
The staff was very friendly and helpful. The room was perfect. Breakfast on the 8th floor was much better than in most comparable hotels! 
We liked the service with the shuttle bus that can bring you to spots such as Fisherman's Wharf and the convenient shuttle to the airport. 
The large car rentals on O'Farrell street are within walking distance. 
When we ever return to SF we certainly will consider to go back to this pleasant hotel. 
In our opinion, the overall balance between costs and quality is excellent.

This was a fabulous, relatively cheap (for Chicago), hotel! Perfect location-the redline is just a stone throw away, and walking distance to Michigan Ave and the theater district. We stayed here on the coldest weekend of the year for the auto show, and the staff was always pleasant, even the poor valet and doorman outside in the bitter cold! The wine reception (a Kimpton standard, I think, because they had it at the San Francisco Kimpton I previously stayed) is a nice touch- the cocktail area with fireplace was packed. At check-in, we also got a "Raid the Minibar" voucher which was fun for drinks while getting dressed for the evening. As for the room, it was funky and unexpected, in a very good way. One of the nicest touches was the Etro bath products- though it is quite unfortunate because I can't seem to find them online to buy them now that I'm addicted to the musk scent! Overall, a great hotel. I'd suggest parking your car (and yes, the $50/night is standard in Chicago), and explore!

The hotel is located in a good location for a visit to san francisco,CA as a tourist.
It's appears safe around the area and has free parking with limited parking on lobby level.Elevetor is centrally located on lobby/parking level with luggage carriers and room key access for the elevators at the lobby location making it safer access to the hotel.There is some sight seeing brochures and maps in the lobby with a small seating area.
The room was very nice and clean and well appointed with flat screen tv(approx. 42"),with round table with chairs and bay window view and climate(ac unit) underneath this area of the window.The climate control was on the wall near the bathroom.The window did open at this level making it precarious for children to be around with the window open though.A modern alarm/radio clock was on night stand besides bed.Plenty of pillows for the bed of which was king size and firm mattress made it very comfortable sleeping on.
The bathroom was roomy and had a heat lamp as opposed to exhaust fan and nice showerhead and plenty of soap dishes in tub with supplied shower cap and soap,shampoo,conditioner.A coffee maker with ice bucket and hot and cold cups provided along with coffee/tea I think also.A ice machine and drink machine only is on this level at elevator.
Furnishing were clean and modern and overall very nice!
I don't remember seeing a hotel directory though in the room of amenities,etc.A phone was availabe but didn't need one like most unless need to call the front desk which never had a reason to since the room was well appointed with everything.
I definitely will consider staying again at this property of their other properties.It's pricey for the area($98/nt weekday and $140/nt. weekend but hey this is san francisco,CA).
We stay there each time we are in Indianapolis. Love everything about it. Particularly impressed with Dawn's friendliness..

title_masked: A Lot of Love and Attention
text_masked: We wish to say that they were kind, friendly, prompt and clean. From extra towels without asking, great shower, comfortable bed, clean, great in-bed breakfast, quiet, welcome letter, coffee and tea corner, plus water and juice, upon entering. Good size rooms, location was great, answered questions quickly. One extra piece for me was the chocolates on the desk, when checking in. Loved it! Great bar and rest. on the first floor. Elegant!

We were in week three of gluten free, casein free dieting for my wife when we arrived at the hotel. The next morning when we went to breakfast we asked for the chef as recommended by the books we had read. Chef Jeff Foresman promptly arrived at our table and after a short conversation he advised that Sous Chef Michael Ruiz had a son that was on a gluten free diet and could better serve us. Michael was absolutely fantastic and immediately put our fears to rest. Wendy was able to eat things that she enjoyed and were satisfying. We were quite nevous about the trip but Michael was our savior. In addtion every single staff person we encountered, from the maids to the Concierge, was genuinely friendly and helpful and contributed to one of the finest hotels stays we have ever had.
Don & Wendy Armacost, Stilwell, Kansas

This is a great hotel for the price. The rooms and hotel look exactly like the internet photos. Often times we are mislead by fraudulent photos but this hotel was on point. The beds were so comfortable. The rooms were very spacious and clean..The only thing that needs improvement is the breakfast menu. Other than that it was great!

Okay, so this isn't the newest place in the world and if you're looking for a Hiltonesque place to stay you'll want to look elsewhere, but I find this place acceptable for the money. I've stayed here twice. They have a nice courtyard with lots of lush palm trees that surround a nice pool. All rooms--I think--have a patio or deck that overlook this. Its relaxing to just sit out and enjoy the beautiful surroudings even if you don't want to swim. they also have a free breakfast that outdoes what other hotel/motels will usually do--in my experience anyways. It includes waffles, eggs, cold cereal, coffee and juice, muffins, engilsh muffins, etc. Just be sure you get there early. It was busy the two days we were there and the first morning there wasn't much left. these two aspects, the courtyard and breakfast, was enough to allow me and my friend to overlook its other shortcomings and stay there more than once. The rooms definately need some refurbishing. They are very nice and plenty spacious and include a fridge, but there are problems. Opening the sliding door that leads to the patio will give your muscles a workout and there was a nasty stain surrounding the bathtub drain. My roommate tried taking a shower and said he couldn't regulate the water temp and thus it was too hot to stand in. The tv was old, but worked fine. the beds are firm which some may or may not like. Overall, I enjoyed my stay and may choose to stay there in the future.
I'd also like to mention that its a decent location. Their are restaurants and groceries near by and its just off the 405.

We just spent 3 nights at the Muse with our family to celebrate my mother-in-law's 87th birthday. We are Kimpton afficionados (honestly, where else can you get such great ambiance and service for the money?), but she had never stayed at a Kimpton hotel. She did not know what to expect, but was so thrilled with the quality of the hotel and the beauty of the decor, as well as the wonderful, caring staff. She did not expect it to be so nice for the value we received. The hotel was beautiful, had a great location near Times Square and the Theater District and the service was even better than expected. All of our needs and wants were attended to, and the staff truly went out of their way to assist everyone in our party in every way they could, particularly my elderly mother-in-law and my disabled husband. The staff treated them with genuine concern, caring and respect, which is priceless. Overall - beautiful, great value for New York, great location. I would highly recommend the Muse and other Kimpton hotels!

The Hotel was very nice overall and the staff was extremely friendly. My only two points that I found a bit disappointed in was that they advertise for romance packages (which we did not purchase) but yet their "garden tub" was barely big enough to fit even one person and we are not very tall people (5'5"??). The other point would be that there was a nice IPod player in the room for some music but everytime the air conditioner came on you could not hear the music. The fan for the AC was very loud in my opinion.
Other than these couple of points the room was very comfortable and had some nice amenities.

The hotel is very conveniently located just a couple of blocks from Times Square. The front desk staff was very friendly and helpful. The breakfast area is located in the basement which I thought was strange. The rooms are nice looking, but very small. The cleaning crew didn’t do a good job of keeping our room clean or providing us with enough towels. They do provide complimentary water in the rooms. I didn’t have a major problem with anything while I was there, but I wouldn’t stay there again.

My husband and I visited Philly on vacation and were pleasantly surprised by the Latham. Terrific location for walking the city with vibrant Rittenhouse Square 1 block away. Spacious room with a nice view and very comfortable king bed. Personable staff ready to help with sight-seeing and dining tips, lots of restaurant options within easy walking distance from breakfast bakeries to raw oyster bars. Definitely earned our recommendation!

We arrived at the hotel around 10:00 with a 3:00 check-in. They accomodated us with no problem and that was FANTASTIC... it allowed us to get a headstart on our vacation. The room was also a great deal going through the HYATT travel service.

Hotel Monaco is an excellent hotel! Spotlessly clean, the room was beautifully decorated, well appointed, the bed was very comfortable. The service was truly excelellent. I travel frequently, and I can say with confidence that the service here is among the best, from the bellmen, to the concierge, front desk, and housekeeping; all were exceptionally helpful and friendly. The front desk staff know the area well and gave great tips for entertainment and getting around town. It was our anniversary weekend, and the staff surprised us with a complimentary bottle of champagne chilling in our room. A truly wonderful weekend, and I would highly recommend the hotel. Oh, and if you wish, you can ask for a goldfish to keep you company in your room. A quirky, fun little extra that we enjoyed.

We read very negative things about this hotel, but our guide told us it's all you'll need. We actually enjoyed our stay in Hotel Pennsylvania. We were staying at the 16th floor, the backside, it was quiet. Your room will be cleaned every day. The bathroom looks old, but the shower was working. We had more than enough space to store our luggage. The location is very great. Next to Penn Station so very easy to explore the city. It's an 15 min walk to Times Square.

This hotel is fantastic and the only negative points to call them that way would be the cost of parking and the location, but, like everything in life, depends for who.
I chose this hotel knowing it is located in Fishermans Wharf which for many may be convenient and for many others not. You need to know where you want to be and then choose the hotel.
In some other visits I have stayed in central SF, near Union Square, you name it. Hyatt, Intercontinental, Chancellor, etc all of the great and centrally located. But for this quick stop I had what I needed.
The hotel is very well located in Fishermans Wharf, which is no more than 15 minute walking from Embarcadero, the end of Market Street. I love FW and I enjoy my Cioppino at Sabellas Tower. Knowing where I was going to dine the decission was easy.
Hotel is well located, the building does not make justice to the rooms which are spacious, very clean, big and nice appointed. No complaints whatsoever. Bed very comfortable. Breakfast quite good and if you want to go for more you pay an extra 5-6 USD and you get what you want.
Went for a run from the hotel to Bay Bridge and way back; fantastic.
Parking is a problem, mainly because being that touristic its expensive. But, very near the Argonaut hotel you have some streets and parking spots where is free of charge to leave the car overnight. If not just park it in front of the hotel and "insert coin".
If I go back to SF and I dont mind staying 15 minutes from Union Square I would pick this hotel again. Yes or Yes.

Our group stayed at this hotel during Labor Day weekend for three nights. We had a deluxe suite, which had a small kitchenette area. We found a great rate of about $119 a night, given the slow weekend. Also, the free wi-fi was key and definitely separated the hotel from the other hotels in the area which charge for it. The rooms were clean and updated, and generally looked the same as the pictures online shows, however, the hotel shows its age more than the pictures let on. The lobby looks a little on the dated side and the hallways look kind of aged as well. As far as location, the hotel is about a 7-10 minute walk to the heart of Dupont Circle in a more residential neighborhood. Its about a 10 minute walk to the Metro stop. i thought the place would be closer to the square, so keep that in mind when booking. 
Overall, we enjoyed the stay, but it was a bit further away from the main part of Dupont than we liked, but for what we paid, the inconvenience was probably worth it.

title_masked: clean & comfy with very minor drawbacks
text_masked:
Reservations process was easy online - I had a great $101/night AAA rate which included tax/fees. The front desk staff was always helpful and knowledgable. This is one of the area's few free airport shuttles, very convenient but does, as mentioned by others, have some night hours limitations. The room was really clean with a functional layout, comfortable bed, microwave and refrigerator, desk, sofa, and convenient electrical outlets at both the desk and at bedside tables. Although I could hear some airplane noise it was a distant drone and did not bother me at all. 
The breakfast was not included in the cost of the room and seemed expensive for a fairly limited food selection, particularly the "continental" offering which is often free at this level of accommodation. Breakfast area service was adequate. Getting to this lodging is still a little confusing and although I did see the lighted sign driving in from one direction I think it would be helpful to add more signage driving in from the gas station side of the hotel.
I had a great 3 night weekend stay in early November and will definitely stay there again when I travel to Austin.

title_masked: the best Holiday Inn I have stayed at - more like a good Embassy Suites
text_masked: This was by far the best Holiday Inn I have stayed at. The rooms are suites very much like the Embassy Suites properties although slightly smaller. The bathroom entrance is from the bedroom rather than in between the bedroom and living room. But otherwise they are very similar. My room upon arrival had some AC problems so they quickly moved me to another room where everything worked. There is a restaurant on the premises that is pretty decent and the prices are quite good. There is a little shop that sells the usual sundries one might want for the room. Ample parking out in front of the hotel. The places seems very well run and the staff was quite professional. The room was very quiet and everything was in good working order - except perhaps the hairdryer which worked but was falling apart - and I reported it to the front desk. I would definitely stay here again. The place far exceeding my expectations for a Holiday Inn. I'd even rank it high compared to several Embassy Suites I have stayed at in the last few years.

I was extremely disappointed at the overall condition of the the property, including the rooms, elevators, conference rooms. When I do stay at the ICGHs, I usually stay at Holiday-Inn express and boy what a difference between the two. I was in town with a large group for a conference for 5 days. You can tell they are not use to large groups as they couldnt handle the demand. The rooms are decent, but time for remodeling! The elevators are barely functioning, taking 5 minutes to get to you once you called it. Granted there are about 4 elevators! The walls are thin! I heard everything next door, above me and outside! Stay away from rooms on the 14th floor because the ball rooms are above, God help you if they are having a night event! The conference rooms are large but needs rennovation. I am not sure why we were not provided with a microphone while using the conference room. The conference rooms are located next to a kitchen!!!!!! So imagine my horror when we heard the garbage disposal and dishes against each other! They have several shuttles, but I dont think they adverstise it! I was told they use them only for pilots! so not cool! Honestly I dont think i will stay here again. On the positive side, it is in a great location. If you are looking for a quick one night stay then I would say go ahead! The staff is great!

title_masked: First time to fly by myself
text_masked: This was my first trip to fly and out of a big city by myself. Microtel Philly took care of all of my needs. I stayed there the night before my flight to Phoenix.
