I woke up in a clean hotel room and was fed a light breakfast, shuttled to the airport and taken to the appropriate terminal. I also parked my car at Microtel for about 7 dollars a day. The shuttle drivers were beyond courteous and caring! When I got back March 23rd around 11pm in Philly from my flight, I called the very easy shuttle number on a card the front desk gave me and they were there in a matter of moments to pick me up. Mike the van driver was very energetic and friendly!! He even asked if I had anything to eat before I checked in to the hotel. The first night I stayed at Microtel the room was very clean and smelled clean. The night I got in late the room had an urine smell. That was the only bad thing I experienced. I wish the rooms had refrigerators and microwaves in the room. I had to go to the lobby to cook my dinner at midnight after a long flight. the price for the rooms were great for what I needed the room for...a room to stay in the night before a flight and a room for me when I returned late to Philly. I felt safe at this property as well. I am flying back to Phoenix in November along with my husband and it will be his first trip as well and first time to stay in Philly. We picked microtel to stay the day before our flight and the night we return again!! I love the shuttle service and on site parking while away on our trip. don't need to worry about anything...Microtel will do it all for us!!

Stayed here four consecutive nights on my first visit to this property and have nothing but good things to say. The staff was very friendly and efficient. My junior suite was clean, comfortable and spacious (and had two TVs); bed was comfortable; shower had more than adequate water pressure. Liked the breakfast buffet, too. Would definitely stay here again.

title_masked: Great hotel in central Denver location. Minutes away from I-25.
text_masked:
The hotel is 20 minutes away from DIA. There is currently road construction so it may take longer. The hotel staff is great and the facilities good. I found the rooms comparable to other brands like the Hilton. The hotel is not new and is showing its age. The walls between rooms are not fully insulated against noise. I had adjoining rooms, one side was quiet the other not so much due to rowdy neighbors. My son had a room on the 11th floor and he had to put up with noise from a dance floor above.
The food service is excellent. Morning brunch for about $14 with made to order omelets and waffles and a variety of side dishes. Staff was excellent. Parking fee applies.
Location great for shopping and dining.

title_masked: Nooooooo! Do not ruin your stay in New York
text_masked: I stayed here with my friend as a short notice quick shopping trip. We stayed here for 2 unfortunate nights. We were given a double room with one double bed for us to share, (luckily my friend and I have had to do this before so therefore we were ok with this although not very suitable). The room was much below standard it resembled a hostel. The bathroom was clean but extremely basic with the bare minimum. The hotel was full so they were unable to move us as that weekend was a very busy one in New York. The next day we complained as we had a terrible night as all through the night we kept hearing banging and all sorts of noise, we were able to move rooms. We were given a double room but again very basic. The hotel was very small so therefore there was no breakfast or food at all, there was a cafe next door that was linked to the hotel. On the first day we had breakfast there it's a very basic and local cafe so we planned on having breakfast there again the next day. Big mistake. We turned up for breakfast and ordered the same meal as the day before, as the waiter bought my food over I noticed a long hair strapped across my omelette and under my toast, to my hurry I called the waiter over and advised him of this, he was very apologetic and told me that he would get the chef to make me a fresh meal. I felt sick and refused to eat anything else. A very horrid experience.

We stayed in Chelsea Lodge for about a week at the end of October/start of November. It just happened to be the week that the hurricane & subsequent blackout occurred!
That aside though; the place itself was great. Clean rooms, friendly staff always willing to give advise or have a little chat on the stoop. Local amenities were grand. There is a subway just around the corner on 8th (wasn't operating when we were there though). Most things are in walking distance anyway.
Check in & check out was hassle free.
I'd highly recommend Chelsea Lodge for anyone who is going to New York City.

Initially put off by the lack of a view from some rooms, but soon won over by helpful, friendly hotel staff and convenient location (proximity to Times Sq & Rockerfeller), zen-arty decor/style (see pic attached of poster from restaurant).
The lifts worked, the trendy rooftop bar (10th floor) is fun, and the cold buffet breakfast is more than adequate, even for me!

The Casablanca totally deserves it's No.1 position on Trip. I booked direct and from my first enquiry through to check out the staff at The Casablanca were professional, helpful and cheerful, nothing was too much trouble and they took pleasure in making our stay a pleasurable one.The hotel was spotlessly clean, Rick's Cafe provided a fresh and plentiful breakfast with a good choice of breads, pastries, cereals and fruits, the 24/7 refreshments were great and the cheese and wine reception was a lovely touch. Rooms were tastefully decorated, the bed was comfy, housekeeping was excellent, bathroom was classy and the shower was big with a powerful and hot water supply. Reception staff were fantastic and they along with all staff should be congratulated on representing the hotel so well. Well Done guys!

A recent stay at this hotel was so nice. Great part of Memphis and walking distance to Beale Street. So much to do. Rooms were not large but very elegantly appointed. Staff was very attentive including the wait staff. The whole duck parade is more of a production than I understood and was worth the investment of time. The rooftop provided a great view of the Mississippi but the seating was not comfortable. A bar up there with some nicer furniture sure would make it nicer. It is a great "splurge" type of hotel - you will remember your stay there.

This resort was just what we needed. It was incredibly family friendly. Stayed there about 5 nights & just really enjoyed it. I think my son enjoyed relaxing in front of the nightly outside movie after a long hot day, as much as any part of our trip. We felt very much at home. We didn't particularly love the food at the buffet, but that was a minor down fall. It was convenient though.

We had a meeting at the WHO regional office of America and block booking was made for us. The hotel was clean, most receptions are nice except one guy with black curly short hair who does not allow anyone to have even 1 hr late check out while all other recptions listen to the reason for the request and tried to allow to help the travellers who have very late flight.
the jotel is very clean, the house keeping could not speak English but very helpful. They also cleaned the dishes for us.
it is very close to all the Washington Monument. you can walk to the museum if you are good at walking.

I was in town for a conference Mr [NAME] went above and beyond to make sure I was taken care of. His smile and assistance was greatly appreciated. There was 2 events going at the same time. He was everywhere also the set up with food in the atrium was nice. Kathy and Daz where very accommodating.

My family and I were very excited for our New Years Eve trip to NYC. I love Exhale and sushi both which are located here. The kids were thrilled; they love the city and when I told them I reserved Wii for the room they couldn't wait. These things mean a lot to a kid. It finally did arrived at 6:30 on our last night of our 4 night stay with dead batteries and with only one controller despite telling the front desk we had 2 kids. It took about 40 minutes and 2 maintenance visits to get up and running. The fact that the room had peeling wallpaper, frayed carpets, and no towels in the bathroom was just icing on the cake. Each morning we awoke to the smell of cigarette smoke (on a nonsmoking floor) and no promised daily newspaper. On 2 of the 4 nights the room wasn't cleaned until 5 PM. Honestly I hate complaining but it actually became comical. On January 2nd the room next door had a loud party until 4 AM! The hotel is very unlike other the sister Park Ave location which seems much nicer. So much for luxury.

This is something like my 6th stay at this property. I was lucky and received a room on the 20th floor (room 2018) with a view over the river. Beautiful view. The room, while smallish, was well furnished and had an extremely comfortable bed. The only complaint I have is that it seemed the main water pipe for the floors above me ran right through my room, any time anyone took a shower, I had to turn the volume up on the tv. Since I wasn't in the room that often I really didn't mind. The recpetion was, as always warm and welcoming. I did feel for the people on the front desk on Saturday morning, because the check out line stretched to about 20-25 people most of the morning. The location is perfect, attached to the Prudential Center. Convenient to T stations and easy walking to Newberry and Boylston Streets. The staff is helpful and the hotel seems to really work hard for each guest.

title_masked: Updated, very accessible and has good facilities
text_masked: We stayed here and did a tradeshow in INDY. Getting to downtown was very convenient and it also sits right next to highways. The hotel has a nice 24hrs coffee shop and that is very very convenient. The rooms are reasonable updated and they have digital channels on their LCD televisions. If you get a room in the far back, it makes more sense to park in the back as its is a very long property.

title_masked: Next time will try harder to find somewhere else
text_masked: This was a short notice booking and hence was extremely expensive for a one night stay. The reception staff were most unhelpful with one small request that I had. There was no sense that they were going to assist me with it at all.The rooms are clean but are like a shoe box. That's to be expected in big cities but not at the price that I paid for the room. I thought the bathrooms were very dated and common area carpets were old and grimy. I felt ripped off.

I stayed at the Omni because we were seeing a play across the street. They really care about their customers and went out of their way to make us feel special. The moment we checked in it was efficient, personable and just great. I would 100% stay here again and recommend it!

title_masked: A beautiful hotel with paper thin walls and dishonest employees.
text_masked:
First of all the valet mentioned there was no parking anywhere close by and our ONLY option was to valet. Upon entering, I asked the receptionist if there where any discount membership and/or for the most cost effective rates. After checking in I discovered online that there was a AAA discount...the receptionist never mentioned this. Going outside we took a stroll <20min after checking in and there where vacant parking garages everywhere...the valet never mentioned this. I asked to speak to the manager first thing in the morning and was told I would be reached...it never happened. 
For Hotel Contessa to step it up a notch, it needs to practice integrity. I'd much rather recommend a hotel that give a complete enjoyable experience, shady characters excluded.

Just up the block from the Walters Art Museum, the Wyndham offers pricey valet parking, but parking is free on the street on weekends or at the Walters lot if you're out early or $10 if you're not. Our room was spacious and clean, faced the Washington monument, with a wet bar, coffeemaker and mini fridge behind closed doors. The mattress was comfy and abundant pillows in various sizes made for relaxing TV time. A switch near the bed controls a do not disturb light in the hall, and on the other side of the bed a power strip accommodates a bevy of electronic accessories. The bathroom is lined with marble tile, with a city view from the commode. The water in the shower and sink takes a while to warm up, but it will get there, and there is a heated towel rack.

Older, updated property. Rooms are small and sometimes oddly laid out as can happen in these buildings. Bathrooms are small, beds were comfy pillow tops and the pillows were actually comfortable. Strongest asset is the staff. Parking is a challenge, as they have curbside valet, but very little area to turn in and unload...the valets work it out for you professionally and swiftly. Front desk staff were superb--especially Robert! We were traveling with my sister-in-law who uses a cane to walk with a hip ailment. During check-in, Robert saw her and asked if a room with a walk in shower would be needed (as we hadn't reserved one). We realized that made sense, and Robert managed to rearrange rooms to better suit our needs. Later, he was a de-facto concierge, providing us with information on night life in the area and directions to it. Outstanding job, Robert.
The restaurant is an Il Forniaio, a respectable brand which provided a standard I.F. dinner. Breakfast needs work...cold potatoes, over medium eggs with whites not cooked, etc. Original Joe's down the block may be a better choice (http://www.originaljoes.com/index.htm).
Overall, the hotel is good, clean and updated. The staff make it shine. The food can be improved.
JR in Sacramento

From the moment we arrived, we realized that the staff was going to go above and beyond in every way possible. We were greeted in the front carport and asked if we were interested in valet parking. We said yes, our bags were removed from the car and we were shown into the lobby. We got to the front desk where a friendly clerk asked if we wanted a king suite or a double queen suite. We went to our king suite and found a lovely sitting room with large flat screen TV and, appropriately, Spanish styled furniture, then on to the dressing area with beautifully appointed bath, large counter with coffee fixings and mini bar for those who would choose to use it . Beyond that area was the bedroom with our very comfortable king bed and another large flat screen TV. The bed area was private and had a door to close it off from the sitting area where one could use the sofa sleeper. 
After a full day of sightseeing and enjoying the Riverwalk in San Antonio, we returned to our hotel and enjoyed the beautiful evening on the patio outside the lower level bar. The patio is right on the water and we sat and watched the boat cruises go past for awhile. We soon returned to our room and had a very comfortable and quiet night's sleep.
We checked out in the morning and found Natalie, another very well-trained desk assistant to help us. While we waited, the bellhop kindly asked if he could order our car to brought over. Every part of our experience at the Hotel Contessa was pleasant and we recommend the hotel and will stay there again when we return to San Antonio. Hotel Contessa is in a very convenient part of San Antonio, within walking distance of nearly all of the major attractions. You will not be disappointed if you stay there!

title_masked: Don't love the name,but the hotel is great!
text_masked:
Recently stayed at this establishment for one night. We were very pleasantly surprised to find a very nice facility with well appointed, and decorated rooms. The street that the hotel is on has free street parking available in the usual New York fashion (you have to move your car twice during the week for one hour or so), and we were able to secure a place right outside the hotel - literally. 
Lovely staff and an excellent espresso machine (Cimbali) at the buffet breakfast just topped it off. Would return.

title_masked: very great place to stay in los angeles area
text_masked: my fist stay here at the holiday inn express since it was the ramada limited alot of improvements very clean room parking was great the staff was friendly and also the breakfast bar is free every day i love my stay at this hotel me and my friends will be back soon thank you holiday inn express .

title_masked: Review from a 1st time visitor to NYC
text_masked:
As it says in the title, this was my first trip to NYC so I literally booked this hotel because it was #1 on Trip Advisor and I was clueless about anything in NYC. 
We drove in from Philly and used the Myers parking. The hotel will validate parking and it a pretty big discount at $25 a day. However, all over the hotels website it says "self parking". This is not a self parking garage. The attendant will take your car. I was unprepared for this!! So I just wanted to note it here to help anyone else. 
We arrived at around 11 am. We were unable to get into our room early. We had a king bed room and it was adorable. I loved it. The room and hotel were very clean. My air conditioner worked great. We cranked it to 67 degrees so Im sure it was working hard, but the room was nice and cool when we got back in from the 90+ degree weather. The drinks/snacks in Ricks cafe were awesome. I hadnt planned on ever eating there, but it really was high quality and convienent. 
There are ice buckets in the room, but you have to call the front desk to get ice. That was a little odd. 
The only real negative was that I booked the room under Expedia. Two nights was $722 dollars. All paid well in advance. When I got home from the hotel, there was almost 1100 dollars in pending charges on my credit card. I was shocked!! This seems EXTREMELY excessive, so much so that I had to call to confirm that they were indeed just pending charges. I did not read anywhere on expedia that this would happen and I am guessing that it was because I booked through that site, but wow. If you have a small credit line please beware. That was a huge shocker. 
Now on to the AMAZING aspects of this hotel. It is the greatest hotel location I can imagine. You can go out and about and easily stop back in for bathroom, dropping off bags, etc. It was so close to public transportation and all the happenings. The location alone is worth the cost. 
My room was completely silent. I have no idea how seeing as how it is so close to the mania going on outside. In fact, the morning I checked out there was a huge storm. I walked outside and said "It rained?!?!?!" I had no idea. Amazing. 
So next time I will book through the hotels site to avoid those insane pending charges. And I will definitely be back. Seriously, the location can not be beat.

Having stayed in lots of conference hotels, I was happily surprised to find that the fit and finish of the room itself was actually quite lovely. The bathroom was the biggest positive surprise, in that it was exceptionally spacious, with a large soaking tub and separate, glass-walled shower. There was lots of hot water with good pressure, even though were were on an upper floor. 
The view of the Space Needle was an added bonus, although obviously only visible from one side of the hotel. 
We had a mildly complicated check-out bill, but the front desk staff had it all organized, exactly to our specifications, within moments. And the workout room was a treat, with individual televisions in the cardio equipment, and a refrigerator with chilled towels. It was quite motivating!
Overall, our stay was lovely and I would stay there again.

title_masked: A Good Value but Nothing Special
text_masked: The price was great...the location too. The room was spacious and the beds comfortable. I felt like the linen, TV, and ambience was very poor....even though clean the place felt "grimy" to me. We had to ask for washcloths - only one was given on one day and none the next. The employees were very nice. I see below that I am to rate the continental breakfast...was there one? We were never told there was.

My son and I recently stayed at Inn at the Opera and it is an older hotel but the charm is exceptional and I appreciated the fabulous service we received. Every staff person was attentive and kind. Evita went above and beyond by providing us detailed transportation information so we could easily navigate our way through the city. The rooms are clean, and comfortable. We staye d in the OPERA room and appreciated the size. It was a nice surprise to have a basket of goodies and water waiting for us -complimentary. I will be back with all my family to enjoy this fabulous city during the summer and will certainly stay here. The restaurant was being renovated during this trip but they did a nice job with providing complimentary breakfast in the lobby. Charming hotel, exceptional staff, nice value, location super easy for navigating.

The Good
- Great location 
- Lobby has great character
- Friendly staff
- Comfortable bed
- Complimentary continental breakfast (muffins and coffee) and free WiFi
The Not So Good
- Our room had such a strong smell of bleach that I started to get a little light-headed a few minutes after we entered and we couldn't open the window to air it out so we asked for another room. A housekeeper was very pleasant and apologetic.
- The 2nd room was bigger than the first but was tiny and didn't have a dresser, (drawers were under the bed), no desk or 2nd bedside table so we had to use an ironing board to put things on.
- Stuffy (and it was winter when we were there)
- The only table in our room was a small one attached to a chair (like in college) which wasn't suitable as we needed a desk for work. The housekeeper was kind enough to offer to bring us a table but it was the size of a TV table and was dirty and worn.
- Very little counter space in the bathroom.
- Staff could have been more knowledgeable with regard to directions for how to get to/from the airport, what restaurants to recommend and so on.

title_masked: A brilliant hotel, excellant service, spotlessly clean, most helpful staff!
text_masked: This hotel far exceeded my expectations having read some reviews! The bedrooms may not be the biggest but were spotlessly clean and had everything you needed for a most comfortable stay. Breakfast was a feast each morning with helpful staff busily keeping everything replenished. Each person at reception acknowledged all guests as they passed by and the duty manager clearly visable checking guests were happy. A most enjoyable stay which will shared with friends and family, and visisted again next year by myself

This downtown hotel is in close walking distance of the COBO Center and other downtown attractions. Friendly staff, comfortable rooms, good hot breakfast daily and a separate bar/restaurant next door, (Big City Grille)
Too many smokers allowed at the entrance of the hotel makes a bad impression. Television stations did not match the in-room guide so you surf the channels forever to find your desired show.
Overall, a worthwhile hotel when staying in downtown Detroit.

I stayed at the Hyatt House for 4 nights in May for a business trip. I have stayed at several hotels in Uptown Charlotte but this is now my favorite. For the money, it certainly has the most in-room ammenities. I especially love the mini-kitchen. The rooms are spacious, like a studio apartment. This is really nice if you're staying for several days. Love the full-size refigerator and freezer. The beds are like sleeping on a cloud they are so comfortable. The breakfast is very good and the food in the bar is excellent and very reasonably priced. The location is very close to the Epicenter and many restaurants within walking distance. Everyone I interacted with was very friendly and you could tell they have a customer focus at this hotel. I will definitely stay here next time I'm in Charlotte and will recommend it to my co-workers.

Every president since Truman has stayed here. I can see why. Security is tight here. Beautiful lobby especially when the Christmas tree is up & gingerbread house. Nicely updated to blend modern with classic styles. Room was terrific but, could use some updating, with nice view of the lake & Buckingham fountain. Staff was very nice. Clean lap pool & spas next to the real gym! Good views for working out. Good soups & coffee at Snaxs. Only complaint: someone was smoking in a nearby room. It's worth a visit even if you don't stay in the hotel.
All factors of the stay were quite acceptable. The 3 pm check in time was very inconvenient. More flexibility would go a long way towards another stay at this hotel.

Unbelievable! People were waiting in a huge line for breakfast. Tables took for ever to be cleaned, food all over the floor, no service what so ever... and when we asked at the reception if somebody from management could have a look at the disaster, we were told "... so sorry, but on weekends we don't have management on site..., you should write something on tripadvisor..." Well, here you are, if you don't want to manage, please leave it to somebody that wants to do so! The staff tried, but without guidance and training they never had a chance......

The location is FANTASTIC. Easily accessible to Grand Central (10 min walk), all of the Rockefeller Center attractions, Times Square etc. Take advantage of the restaurant at Club Quarters next door; we had great (and relatively inexpensive) cocktails and appetizers on the veranda. 
I found the room a little small (especially since I had booked a Superior room to accommodate 3 females) but we weren't in the room much so it was fine. Note that some superior rooms come with a pull-out (what I had expected) and some come with a rollaway (what we got). 
Check in was a little confusing; it's not very clearly marked but you can self-check from one of the kiosks. I'd recommend it since waiting for the attendant didn't net anything in terms of additional information or room options.

We spend 2 nights in the Casablanca. Was greeted by a doorman who took our luggage to hold until room was ready. Bags taken to the room for us. Complimentary wine and cheese every night and breakfast was fantastic in the morning. Delicious coffee. The hotel is clean and very well staffed! Loved every minute of our time there!

I stayed here for 4 nights with my husband and son. The location worked well for our family, but the room was run down and had an odd smell - something like a mix of chemicals and deodorizer with an undertone of stinky socks. The wallpaper was peeling under the window and there was a black streak of soot on the ceiling in front of the A/C duct. Breakfast was busy, with lines for everything, but the food - and most importantly, the coffee - was ok. Nothing special, serve yourself. I felt it was a bit overpriced for what it was, but I guess the location made up for it. No free Internet, except in the lobby. Small, crowded pool. Slow service and very busy front desk.

title_masked: Good Location, Small Rooms, Wi-fi issue in rooms
text_masked:
Was on a business trip in Feb 2012, stayed here with a few of my colleagues. The location is great as its 2 mins from Union Square, good resturants around one was right across the hotel and had excellent breakfast menu. 
The staff at the hotel is friendly and helpful. The hotel is an old building with the charm, but the rooms I felt were small and the bathrooms even smaller. I had a room with double bed that looekd over the Powell street. Being on the 4th floor and facing the main road I could hear street sounds through the night. 
Also, has wi-fi connectivity issues in the room. There was no wired connection for internet and with no wi-fi signal, had to keep going down to the lobby to check my mails. There's tea and coffee served at the lobby in the mornings if you need a cuppa as there is no tea making facility available in the room.

title_masked: Three days in a clean (small) room
text_masked:
Really good.
It is the only both cheap and clean place I've ever found in Manhattan! Excellent location and frindly environment. 
The bathroom was the only drawback, it was too small but, you know, in NYC it's cool.
I preferred the private bathroom formula that is more expensive but let you have your own privacy.

title_masked: A home away from home...consistently exceeds my expectations
text_masked: This review is long overdue, after a dozen+ stays at Chambers Hotel. I can't say enough good things about this hotel and its staff and I'm already looking forward to my next visit. Chambers offers an unmatched experience if you're looking for seclusion and serenity in the middle of a concrete jungle. The accommodating staff come without any of the pretentiousness you often get at other top hotels. The luxurious, art-adorned rooms are a generous size by NY standards, making one wish this was their very own pied-a-terre in New York City.

The first experience was great...the last two were horrible. I travel for work and know we all have bad days...I get it...but I realize this hotel has spiraled out of control. The management has lost control and it is apparent. 
The staff is all new and nobody has any training. 
Please seek anything else but here. If you think sleeping in the airport is a horrible idea, trust me when I tell you that it is better than staying at the Comfort Suites DIA. The owner is unreasonable and is the only person allowed to make a decision. She treats you like a terrorist and is less than personable.
Right in the middle of everything we wanted to get to. It is well presented, and very clean and great value. Have already returned, and will do so again!
I stay at this Hilton garden as often as possible. I work in NYC and this hotel is very convenient. The service is great and very accommodating. I also like to use the fitness center.

We visited New York City on a spur of the moment day trip. We were only there for 24 hrs and Carmelo made the trip! My biggest concern prior to arriving was unloading on the road outside the hotel with two small children and lots of luggage! 
It was busy when we arrived and Carmelo greeted us with the biggest smile and told us it would just be a few more moments until he was finished with the prior guest. My anxiety quickly diminished. Carmelo was more than patient as he helped us unload all our stuff. He was interactive with not only us but our children and made us all feel very welcome. 
Cramming New York City into 24 hrs is impossible but we wanted to make the most of our quick trip. Carmelo is very knowledgable with the area and was quick to lead us in the right direction. Whether it was to Central Park, Time Square, a shoe store opened at 8am for aching feet, or the best food in our area, Carmelo knows the way!
Thank you Carmelo for showing us such great hospitality in such a short time. We are already planning our next trip (longer this time) to New York!!

We stayed here for two nights and the hotel was really nice, it was modern & clean.
It was a 10 minute walk to the nearest Metro and it was only a short ride to be at the centre of all the attractions.
The bed was really comfortable.
The hotel offers coffee in the morning and complimentary wine in the reception daily which is a really nice touch, it really makes the stay feel special.
We didn't know at the time but we were staying whilst the Washington Gay Pride was on so the hotel and surrounding area was very busy but it gave the area a really great festival vibe.
I would recommend this hotel to others and if I was to return to Washington DC I would stay here again.

I LOVE the Kimpton Chain. Each Hotel is "Their own", with their own feel. Even though there are other Monaco's in other Cities, Each one is special, and a unique experience. This Monaco is truly great. Staff was great, Room was great! I upgraded my room to the two person tub.... Fantastic. Whenever i travel for fun to cities, and I am not looking to be cheap, The Kimptons are the first I research. Excellent Place Monaco Denver! Highly recommend, and would stay here in downtown Denver in a heartbeat.... FYI: Digging the crazy leather stirrup chairs in the lobby....Please note, did not have time to try out any other Amenities the hotel has to offer.....Missed the free wine hour due to dinner.

For the intersection of room quality, location, and price, it would be hard to beat this place in Chicago. The hotel is right off the Magnificent Mile, but on a small one-way street that keeps traffic minimized. Service was prompt and attentive.

title_masked: Great hotel and awesome customer service!!
text_masked:
I am an employee at a Hilton in Tucson, AZ and stayed at this property for a night so I could go to a Diamondbacks game. I have to say that the service I received here was some of the best I've received anywhere - and staying as an employee, you don't usually expect that.
The grounds are beautiful, well-kept, and inviting. I'm sad I couldn't stay for more than the one night so I could enjoy the pool. The restaurant had just opened when I arrived, but I did have a drink (which was great!) and spent a few minutes talking with the bartender (Mitch, I think) and the guest service agent (Travis).
Travis is one of the best front office employees I've ever met at a hotel and believe he deserves lots of recognition. Every time I saw him, he was going out of his way to help a guest and always had a smile on his face. I'd also like to thank the van driver (Angel, I believe his name was) for his hospitality and conversation with me when he took me to the Lightrail station before the baseball game. You have really great employees here.
The room was beautiful. I was upgraded to a suite (sooo appreciated!). The towels were huge and fluffy. The room was clean and smelled great. They use Bath & Body Works amenities in the bathrooms. The bed, as usual for Hilton Garden Inns, was fantastic. I had a stove top in my room, too, which I didn't use, but was nice to see.
I'll be back many more times this year, hopefully, when I come to Phoenix. I had such a great time! Thank you.

I traveled with the NFL team that I work with which may be the reason for the extra exceptional service. The friendliness of the staff was amazing. 
Wireless Internet was spotty. Pools were all around the resort.
If you're coming to play golf, make sure it's available as it was closed to get the grounds ready for busy season during my mid-October stay.

title_masked: Best beds of any hotel chain
text_masked:
I visit Indy regularly, 5 times or more a year. This used to be my favorite place to stay but the hotel was dated and the rooms were starting to show too much wear and tear. Recently the rooms were updated as well as the lobby. 
I can't compare rooms from my past stays because I would normally stay in a suite. The suite side of the hotel has been converted to apartments for lease - bummer. My room was larger than average king with a sofa. The remodel is beautiful - lovely decor. The bed and bedding are absolutely heavenly. I can always be assured a good night sleep in a Sheraton bed. One more perk is the direct access to the mall. The mall is in the midst of a remodel but there was a clear path to Cheesecake factory. 
One negative - internet fees. The minimum option is a 2 day rate at $18.95 - even if you are a Starwood member. Although, when I inquired about a discount for members, the front desk immediately removed the charge - very considerate. Looks like I'll be staying at the Sheraton again for my Indy trips.

title_masked: Texas Friendly People and Nice Hotel
text_masked: I always stay at this hotel now that I return to this area frequently. I love the staff and the room set up. It is ideal for one night stays or much longer. This is the best hotel I have stayed in for the price paid.

My husband and I recently stayed at the Dupont Circle Hotel. We booked our vacation on short notice to celebrate my husband's birthday and found this hotel through Hotwire. The hotel was very centrally located with a nice selection of bars and restaurants in the area. It was also very close to the Metro. We were given a room with two double beds the first night due to lack of available rooms and our third party booking but were switched to a King room the following morning. We did run into a snag partway through our trip but the hotel dealt with the issue very quickly and effectively. We had a problem with our room. While it was being looked after, we were offered drinks at the hotel bar and were later provided with dinner at the hotel restaurant where we had a lovely meal. Mistakes can sometimes happen but I think the mark of good service is in part how quickly and effectively a service provider deals with that mistake. In our case, the hotel staff, particularly the manager of guest relations, Ms [NAME], was cordial, gracious and made sure we were well looked after. Overall, I have nothing but good things to say about this hotel and would have no hesitation booking a further stay here if we return to DC.

This is a relatively new facility and it is very decent for a business stay. The lobby is pleasant, more modern design than most HI's, There is decent sized bar area which is well stocked, but which closes relatively early, 10pm I believe.
The workout room is small, 2 treadmills and 1 cross trainer machine (All Star Trac and new) with 2 TVs. If you're not there early, chances are the machines will be in use. The pool is small but good enough.
I had a room with a nice spa bathtub which worked well. The room itself was decent sized, had a coffee maker and small refrigerator, and comfortable work space, 
I was disappointed in the reception, the woman at the desk seemed utterly uninterested that I was staying there (I did get a bag with chips, water and some candy as a Priority Club member), and the lobby smelled funky, like mold. The younger attendant on duty the following morning was much more pleasant but every time I went to the counter, she was in the office behind the reception area.
The business center has two computers, both of which were very slow. Since this is a new facility, I would have expected better computers. Still, I was able to print out my boarding pass with no problem.
There are more than enough restaurants nearby (Texas Roadhouse, Outback, etc.) if you have a car (5 minute or less drive). Only Cracker Barrel is in walking distance.
I'd stay again. I was expecting better for a new facility, but I've no major complaints. 
And regarding the reviewer who said items were stolen; I had enough items worthwhile stealing laid out when I was not there. Everything was in perfect order when I got back. If there was a problem, I'm certain it's been eliminated.

title_masked: Not a 4 star in my opinion
text_masked:
I was disappointed.
The furnishings and room are sumptiously decorated, and there is a TV in the mirror of the bathroom - and I can't complain about the sheets or attress. The room was laughably small - but that's true of NYC in general. Only a Queen bed, which is too small for the two of us. 
But, the towels were ratty - I've added a photo. The thermostat has a blue screen which is right at the sleeper's eye - a no-no for good sleep. The hotel information notebook had no pages, and when we asked for them, never receved them.
There is a nightclub on the first floor. It certainly looks popular and has live music. BUT, we were in room 301 which is RIGHT above the nightclub. Nightclub = nightmare when you want to sleep.

This new Hilton is excellent for anyone having business in NYC's Fashion district. Rooms are good size for this part of Manhattan with all the usual amenities. 
Staff was very friendly and helpful. The on-site restaurant and bar is nice and dinner entrees are affordable. There are also local area restaurants that are good and in easy walking distance. The concierge recommended an Italian place on 7th avenue that was also very good and reasonable. 
We walked easily up to 42nd St/Times Square along 5th Ave. 
I would definitely recommend this hotel.

Just got back from a long birthday weekend in Baltimore. My girlfriend booked a room at the Sleep inn and the price was very reasonable. This was our first trip to Baltimore so we really didnt know what to expect. The area around the hotel isnt the greatest. It is located one street away from what is known as the "block" which is a row of strip clubs. My girlfriend was a little uncomfortable when we ended up walking through the block while trying to find the harbor. Although the hotel is right next door to the police station and it wasnt an issue during the day we made sure to take a cab back at night. The hotel was clean, bed was comfortable, room was modern looking and it was a great value. 15$ a night for parking kind of blows but it is what it is. The inner harbor of Baltimore is awesome. We live an hour from Philly and NY so we know what the city is all about but Baltimore has a style of its own. The water taxi for 12$ an adult gets you unlimited rides all day long (until 11pm on the weekends) and you get a bunch of coupons to use at the locals bars for buy one get one beers and discounts on food. If it wasnt for the water taxi we would have never found the Dog Watch Tavern in Fells Point. Awesome bar ( I am still dreaming about their old bay honey wings) in an awesome town. Make sure you eat at Mama's on the half shell in Canton and Amichis in Little Italy(ten minute walk from hotel). Overall great stay. Save the money and stay at this hotel. It doesnt have a view of the harbor but your a 10 minute walk away.

I stayed here for one night on a business trip. I had a lot of downtime, so I spent two days exploring the city from the Sheraton's awesome, super-central location. Everything is within walking distance; shopping, great restaurants, Pikes Place Market, etc. The rooms are great, and all of them offer city views. In my opinion the best thing about this hotel is the staff - who are all the friendliest people I have encountered. Each one seemed happy and ready to help you out. I would definitely stay here again on my next trip to Seattle!

title_masked: everything I've come to love about the W....
text_masked: ....I found in this hotel. Our room was located directly next to the elevator. I panicked at first, but it was super quiet and we never heard a sound! It was clean and comfortable with a beautiful view of the harbor. The surrounding neighborhood is quiet at night, but it was perfect for us. We were still able to be out late at night, enjoy wonderful pizza right around the corner, and had easy access to public transportation. We arrived home just today, and I can't wait to stay here again!

The hotel is always good in almost ever respect and the the service is really exceptional for New York, particularly from the butlers. The bigger grand luxe rooms are well worth the higher price, if you prefer more space.
The only downside is that the room tarriff can be quite high, even by NYC standards. Fortunately, I was able to avail of the special offer for this month - pay for two nights and the third night was almost free!

I just stayed with a friend and was so happy that we were able to check-in 4 hours early. The room was clean, beds comfortable and breakfast was perfectly fine and included in the price. It's great to stay in a hotel where the people are nice too. Our room was streetside, 3rd floor. Noise from the street was a bit loud. The only big downside was that there was only a pedestal sink in the bathroom, but that might be because we had a handicapped room.

Stayed one night after disembarking from cruise and en route home. Were dropped off at the airport after a land tour with the cruise. Pickup by the hotel from the airport was so easy - just called from a phone in the designated area outside the airport and the van came within 5 mins! Rooms are dated but clean and even offered two types of pillows! Nice business office where we could check in online and print out our e-tickets (free of charge!). Close to the light rail terminal that brought us right into town. Going back to the airport pass midnight was also a breeze.

I must agree with the taxi driver that drove me from the airport to this hotel. It is the best hotel in Los Angeles. Well, at least in its price range. The staff is very professional and polite. It has the best location in Hollywood. The room is spacious and clean. Excellent.

title_masked: Terrible Service, Terrible Billing, Terrible Experience
text_masked:
Booked correctly, got confirmed but was put into a different room because they send someone else to my room. I had to chase people to move from the two twin bed room to the king bed one that I reserved and that happened after I begged for it and late in the afternoon. I was offered with "a breakfast" to compensate for all the misunderstandings but, they ended up charging it to my corporate card.
Not a good choice if you're attending AdTech or if a corporate client. Stay at the W or other more serious option.

Just spent three days in the OMNI Park West. Rooms are roomy and clean. Staff was very polite and helpful. A bit out of the way but they have a great restaurant and bar on premises. Plenty of restaurants and shopping within a short drive. Would recommend this hotel.

It´s a simple hotel, perfect to have a shower and sleep. It's clean, comfortable and offers a small breakfast (coffee, juice and muffins), which was fairly enough for us. The price is a good advantage if you are just looking for a place to rest comfortably at night. Other positive detail is the price of the valet, which was cheaper than others.
The one thing we didn't like that much was the location. During the day it was good, it's really near Market street and bus stops so there's no problem to access it. However, at night we were a bit cautious walking around, but nothing too dangerous (what we read online was worse than what it was in reality). You just have to be alert and avoid certain areas.
There is a bar nearby and we could hear some music, but it didn't bother.

title_masked: A good hotel for a few nights
text_masked:
I stayed at this hotel for one night. The hotel is close to the airport and has their own transit bus. 
The hotel has large and clean rooms. There are free WIFI, but not wireless. The wireless WIFI is only i the reception.
The breakfast is basic.
There are some fastfood restaurants in walking distance.
If ypu want to have a room for a night, close to the airport - the hotel is good.

I travel to Chicago about five times a year for business. I almost always extend the stay and bring my husband and daughter along for a mini-vacation. My first experience was over the phone with a cust. service rep regarding my stay and the charges. The rep was so rude, I got off the phone and emailed the hotel directly regarding her attitude. The hotel quickly responded with a very nice apology and an upgrade that I was not expecting. What started off bad, turned into one of the best hotel experiences we have had to date. I have stayed at many different hotels on and around Michigan Avenue. The Sheraton has quickly become my favorite. The staff is friendly, the hotel is clean and the location is top notch. The view we had of the river was spectacular. We walked to Michigan Ave and to the Navy Pier. My work was the the Merchandise Mart and was a very short ($5) taxi ride over.-- And I could have walked had it not been raining on and off that day. I do wish the burger joint in the hotel had a kids menu...a $12 burger for a three year old seems very expensive- but that is not really something the hotel can control. We loved how friendly everyone was to our daughter. They made her feel like a little rock star. 
Thank you Sheraton for a great stay.
My wife and I had a very pleasant stay at the Courtyard by Marriott in Charlotte on our way to Hilton Head, SC. The hotel is nice and the hotel staff is very friendly.

This is a biased review as I place a lot of emphisis on peace and quiet which at an airport hotel may be a bit much to ask for but as such I would rate this hotel with 2 stars. My 6th floor room must have been renovated as it was current, clean and comfortable as opposed to some of the other reviewers coments.The staff was very friendly and professional. My complaint is the constant whine from the rooftop HVAC fans and as I write this, I can hear every word of my neighbors TV and not because it's too amplified, last night I could hear the other adjacent neighbor's conversations like they were in my room. The desk offered to move me to another room but as they indicated they were all the same in this regard, I declined to bother. As I am here for a 2 day class and need to study in the evenings this has been a real downer which will not be repeated, at least not here.

Location: Good.
Atmosphere: Upscale
Staff: Happy, professional and exceptionally helpful.
Rooms: Tired, average.
Amenities: Ordinary
Cost: Very Expensive and extra charge for Wifi!
This seems to be a hotel mostly populated with people from Conventions who are probably being subsidized. Those making reservations individually are paying for the breaks others are getting. So, $300+ room charge, and everything is extra including WiFi. 
We've stayed in much nicer Westin properties other locations.

title_masked: little gem in the big apple
text_masked:
just got back from our first trip to New York when we stayed at the Metro Hotel. Although the comfortable and well-appointed rooms are very small (we were lucky enough to be upgraded), the location of the hotel and the friendly efficient staff more than made up for this. Let's face it - you don't go to New York to spend time in your hotel room. The hotel is so central that we were able to walk to the Empire State Building, which is literally within spitting distance, Macy's - just at the end of the street, Times Square, Broadway, Fifth Avenue and Central Park. If you want to use the subway, it's only a few yards away from thr hotel too. 
The continental breakfasts offered are more than adequate and the tea / coffee available 24hrs a day was much appreciated.
i would certainly recommend the Metro to anyone looking to visit New York and who, like me, isn't too keen on high rise hotels (the Metro has 12 floors). If / when we go back, the Metro will certainly be our first choice.

When you travel thousands of miles to a different culture with different systems, you could not get better than the Sheraton on Dalton Street. We arrived and were offered an upgrade for $30 per night from traditional to club. For the first 2 nights the club was unavailable, but when we did move room (which took no time) we were further upgraded to a Club Suite at no charge. The staff made us feel as if we really did belong in the Hotel, they were friendly without being pushy at all. The rooms were both very clean and the decor is precise and without clutter (we had previously spend a week at the over-rated Waldorf=Astoria in New York). You can easily afford to eat and drink at the Sheraton. So many hotels have luxurious public spaces and poor rooms. Not the Sheraton. The Club level allows you access to free drinks (cans of pop etc) throughout the day. The best breakfast is to be had down in the Apropos area as the Club is only toast, cakes, porridge etc - no scrambled eggs or bacon or sausages. Club also gives you free drinks (soft) and appetisers in the lounge area each evening 6-8pm. The portions are vast and you wont need an evening meal! Alternatively 'go green' and you collect $5 per night you decline housekeeping - fish & chips is only $15 so you can easily collect enough for a free meal. We have stayed in many hotels - all 4 or 5 star and this is the best. We actually spent our money on doing things we liked!

title_masked: Great hotel with a view and location in Seattle.
text_masked: Great hotel within walking distance of the popular Seattle downtown sites.Hotel is clean modern and with great staff.Get a room with a Lake Union view and not on the freeway side.The breakfast is great with a great variety.Valet parking cost $22+taxes.You get free access to the 24Hour fitness across the street

We went to a downtown concert and made a staycation night of it by getting a room at the Courtyard. It was tremendously convenient. We walked to Harry and Izzy's for dinner and then took in the show. Walking across the street afterwards was a treat and made the concert so much more enjoyable. The room was nice, new, and had a great view of downtown. Staff was super friendly and took great care of us, including chocolate covered strawberries to help us celebrate our anniversary. Very nice touch. I would do it again in a heartbeat and recommend it to out of towners as well as locals who need a night away.

title_masked: Good Base to work In Phoenix
text_masked:
I had a room over looking the pool and it was great. I made me feel I was in a resort. The staff was great. Mila and Laura was fantastic. The manager was greeting all the guests at breakfast and they did care about how it was. The little boy at breakfast just learning to feed himself reminded me of my grandaughters feeding themself, cute. 
I will stay again!!!

First of all this hotel is first rate with a great location and even better staff. Here is one example. On a recent visit to this hotel we were visiting San Diego to drop off our kid at college. We had our SUV loaded with all the typical stuff one takes to go live in a dorm room. We arrived in San Diego on a Friday and the move-in day was Saturday. I had planned to move a lot of the stuff we had packed into our hotel room for the night for safekeeping. Instead, the valet who greeted us, Roman, suggested that since the valet lot was very close to the hotel entrance and very secure, we might consider leaving it all in the vehicle overnight. This was a huge help and I noticed he even parked it in a spot that was in plain sight of the staff at the front entrance. It also turns out that valet parking was only a few dollars more than self parking. Everything was just as he said. We had no problems and he saved us a lot of trouble. I looked for him the next day to thank him but missed him. THANK YOU Roman! The rest of the staff we encountered were also very helpful and friendly. Kudos to the team at the Hyatt Regency Mission Bay!

I recently stayed here for a night while travelling on business. The hotel was very nice and I had no problem. It is not super fancy or luxurious, but it is a good business suite style hotel. The room size was good, I did not have any noise issues, and the staff was very polite. The bathroom is a little cramped... but not too bad.

My Wife and I were celebrating our 20th anniversary and decided on Boston. The Back Bay Hotel was perfect. In the center of most everything, so walking to dinner and shopping was close and convienent, perfect. 
 The person that made the entire trip for us was Heather at the hotel. Her suggestions were spot on and the contacts she has in town to get us into very busy restaurants at a moments notice was superb. Tickets to the Sox / Yankees game.....no problem, Grill 23 saturday night at 8pm......no problem, Heather found out we were celebrating our anniversary and sent a bottle of champaign with chocolates to our room for us to enjoy.
 If your ever in Boston and need some guidence and a beautiful hotel to stay in you can't beat the Back Bay Hotel and make sure you ask for Heather.

The Nine Zero has a great location, nice view, and an interesting contemporary decor. We got a clean and spacious corner room (805). They offer a happy hour with surprisingly pretty good wine @ 5pm. The room temperature did not go lower than 72 even though the thermostat would go down to 62. My guess is that the a/c does not have the adequate capacity for the room. Bed and pillows are fine (could be better), perhaps is about time to get new ones. Not too bad but if you want a cool room to sleep this particular one would not do it. We had breakfast at their restaurant one morning and the food was simply ok. Spent $38 for breakfast for ONE person including tax and tip! We did not have a car so did not have to worry about parking. If you are thinking about renting a car in Boston, think again, it is almost impossible to find a parking spot without paying a fortune. I would definitely stay here again and skip their restaurant.

Was a little nervous when I walked in and saw the mid-1980's color and fabric scheme. 
But what it lacked in contemporary "cool", it more than made up for it with good, classic, service. Everyone was polite, things worked as they should, the maids said "hello sir" in the hallways, the gym was well serviced, clean and tidy.
The room service people were jovial, the food was good, the room was cleaned quickly and on time. The internet didn't need any codes - it just worked.
All in all, an extremely well run hotel. And I'm not going to take a star off for the fact that the color schemes really are for really old people; but I forgive them because I'm probably not their primary demographic - and they NAILED everything else.

title_masked: Pleasant 2 night stay at the Hilton Garden Inn
text_masked:
We stayed here for two nights on the last leg of our honeymoon from the 15th-17th September 2012 and it was very pleasant.
Rooms and decor basic but comfortable and the 2 employees on the Reception desk Anthony Pham and Helena were lovely, helpful and friendly ( especially on our checking out day).

Good service - held room even though checked in at 2am after being at US Open all night. 
Good location - short walking distance to Grand Central, Times Square and others. 
Good value - used points, and as of the time of this review, still a category 4 hotel. Hope it stays that way, although heard rumors it may be reclassified as the hotel has only been open for a short time.
Good room - upgraded to corner suite, and provided pull out couch upon request. 
Good lounge - free juice, coffee, fruit and pastries every morning. 
Good concierge - good recommendation for food and good instructions.
Good decor - clearly a newer hotel with a nice contemporary feel.
Good bed/bedroom - comfortable bed
Overall, good experience. Would certainly go again even though had three small issues (elevator was down two separate times; shower temp fluctuated slightly every shower, was billed $10 for mini bar use even though never used [Hyatt agreed to reverse charges]).

I had a class trip to a convention held at the Palmer House. Despite the fact that I was there for a night, I enjoyed this big hotel and its amenities, all except the wireless, which might not have been a big problem if we weren't 3 assigned to one room. I didn't give it 5 stars because I was only there for one night, and I didn't get to experience everything. The staff however was great and very accommodating and the hotel was luxurious and opulent. The second con was that the roll out bed was very old looking and the bathrooms were tiny, other than that, my stay here was comfortable.

I am a Marriott Rewards Elite level. I reserved 2 nights at the Courtyard for the start of my son's honeymoon cruise because of all the great reviews about location and service. We were not disappointed as everything lived up to prior billings and more. When I mentioned the honeymoon to the hotel staff and asked if there was anything that could be done to make it special (like a water view), little did I know that they would go above and beyond and provide a top floor suite! Wow! Son and wife were so suprised. They appreciated all the smiles they were provided as well. Everything was great. Thanks so much!

We stayed here for 4 night with 2 adults and 3 kids ( 15, 16 and 17 years old). We had a suite and it was really big, especially for NY standards. The beds were great. The hotel looked a bit old but the rooms were very clean. The people at the reception were very helpful.
The subway station was just around the corner and a pizzeria ( great pizza!!) and small grocery shop were next to the hotel. Central park was a 5 minute walk just as Broadway. The price was really good for New York, we would definitely go there again!

We stayed 3 nights with our 20 months daughter. The hotel is ok, clean, but considering the high price paid, the room and bathroom were small and nothing special about them. The soundproofing of the rooms is bad, we could hear the people next door and in the corridor at night. The service is good though and the location is great, walking distance to everything. I recommend The Thinking Cup for breakfast, a short walk from the hotel. Next time in Boston, we will try another hotel in the same area.

Stayed here from Feb 28, 2012 to March 2, 2012 for business and found it to be ok. The rooms are dated but clean. We were told that this Hotel has been sold and that the new owners will be doing renovations. Had a problem with the sink in the bathroom and when it was brought to the attention at the front desk it was handled immediately. Friendly staff, knowledgeable and willing to help. 
The subway is located across the street which was really convenient for us. Their is Limo Service service located at the front lobby and the Head Bell Boy even got us a rental car for a great price. The Hotel is located about 20 mins from The Walk of Fame, The Kodak Theater and Downtown La (La Live).
Overall we found it to be a very pleasant experience.

We spent the night here on our way to and from Hawaii. We found this to be a very nice hotel. It had several shuttle vans and provided free transportation to/from the airport. There are not many restaurants nearby, but the driver offered to take us somewhere. Instead, we walked to the taco stand right down the street - it was really good. I would definitely stay here again.

title_masked: Ink 48 Is Great - stay there when in nyc!
text_masked:
At first, I thought the location was too far off the beaten path. But it's a great location, easy access to all parts of town.
The rooms are nice. I stayed at the Hudson and the rooms were soooo small it was ridiculous for $200. The Kimpton rooms are nice, clean and large enough for two people. The prices are typically reasonable.
The staff is amazing. Very friendly and upbeat. They aren't so hip that you feel intimidated. They make you feel welcome. The hotel also welcomes dogs which is nice.

title_masked: Great Boutique Hotel for the Family
text_masked: We spent 3 nights at The Muse Hotel in Times Square and it was a great stay for my husband and 2 year old toddler. I'm a Kimpton In Touch member (love the raid the bar credit and pet friendly attitude) and have always enjoyed their properties. I made reservations in March and there was a deal if you stayed 3 nights or more. Thanks to Tripadvisor, I asked that we be put in a room away from the construction side and they put us in a great corner room on the 9th floor off the elevators. We could see the lights of TimeSquare from our beds (the blinds were great and blocked them out when it was time to sleep). The front desk receptionist was great when we got there since our room wasn't ready yet and stored some fruit & food in their minifridge at the front desk. The hotel is incredibly quiet given that it's between 6th and 7th near Times Square (closer to 6th Ave) and it was great being able to get on and off the subway and be walking distance to the Rockerfeller Center. It was also very nice to have a bathtub to use to give our 2 year old baths. The room was very spacious - we had an Executive Double Double Room and there was plenty of room in it for our 2 year old to run around in. The only thing I didn't really like was how close the hotel room door was to one of the double beds. You literally could reach up from the bed and open the door and there was enough room to have moved the one bed over slightly since there was space in the corner of the room where there was a very fun zebra print chair.

We spent 5 nights at the Staybridge just after the Easter weekend and whilst I can't fault our 2 rooms (a King and a twin queen) for space and cleanliness the hotel struggled with the number of visitors at this peak time. 
With over 30 floors of rooms the 3 elevators really struggled at peak times and the wait from the top floors was considerable. 
The included breakfast buffet was the usual Staybridge offering, however every morning the buffet area was over capacity even with the use of the bar for additional seating. Additionally half of the buffet seating is at low lounge like tables and chairs which are not really suitable for eating at.
You could make up a tray to take back to your room but then by the time you had waited for the elevator and been squashed inside I am not sure how appetising your breakfast would be.
Location is a couple of blocks from Times Square and you do have to walk past the parole office but I didn't feel any more vulnerable than on other streets. The bus station is opposite and you can access the subway from there so it is very convenient. 
Would I stay here again, yes but not on a peak holiday.

title_masked: Nice hotel but bad Internet availability
text_masked: This was an attractive hotel in a good location. the room was attractive and comfortable, except for the small pillows which seems to be a chain-wide problem. The one thing that keeps me from giving this hotel a better rating is the problems we had with the Internet. The hotel advertises free wifi, but we had constant trouble connecting in our room eventhough we had the router right next to the conputer. We called for help and they came and said that is just the way it is and even the desk has trouble off and on. I was able to get our boarding passes using the computer in the lobby, though it had connection problems as well. So, if you are depending on Internet access, I would not stay at this hotel. Otherwise, it is nice room with a pool and nearby shopping and restaurants and a movie theater. We would not return unless we knew they had upgraded their internet service.

title_masked: Good value, great location, very nice rooms
text_masked:
We just stayed in the Whitcomb hotel for a few nights. 
We booked it thru hotwire, so we didn't actually choose it, so when we arrived there it was a nice surprise!
We paid something like 90 usd. and for San Francisco prices it was super good value.
The room was big, the bed was perfect, and we had 2 sets of pillow each. 
The room was big, we had a big bed, a big changing room, a spacious (not very nicely decorated) bathroom, a large TV, and TWO set of tables with chairs and sofas. 
The mayor con was that the room was old, and the window was blocked by a air-con's tube, so there was no light. The hot water was not hot, but warm.
Overall it was a nice stay. I recommend it.

We stayed at this property for an extended date night "staycation" to go dining and shopping at the Domain. It's extremely convenient to walk to restaurants, bars and enjoy yourself in an upscale urban area without downtown hassles of parking and taxis. The hotel is clean, modern and hip. We had a decent size room, which was a little larger because it was a handicapped accessible room. Got a good rate through AAA and we enjoyed ourselves.

We just returned to the GTA from 4 days in Chicago where we met my Brother and his family who arrived from Winnipeg. We had been planning to meet here for some time and as my niece and nephew (ages 5 and 6) were going to be there we wanted to stay somewhere central so we could easily see all the things we wanted to. I did a TON of research and to be honest in reading some of the reviews about the sheraton downtown I agonized a bit about whether or not to book this hotel. In the end the location seemed to be what we wanted (this was our first trip to chicago so the terrain was not familiar) so I booked. Let me say the Sheraton met and exceeded my expectations!! Let me start by saying that yes, there are some signs of age in the hallways and rooms as this is clearly not a brand new hotel but the rooms were in good repair, most importantly CLEAN and the beds were some of the most comfortable we have had in any hotel anywhere. The few signs of age were just not that noticable unless you were hunting for flaws and certainly in no way impacted our stay. The check-in was flawless the front desk staff helpful, polite and genuine. The concierge was truly helpful. Guest services bent over backwards!! The lobby was impeccably decorated and the servers in the lobby bar were friendly and engaging! The location is absolutely top notch and you will not be disappointed as you can easily walk to Navy Pier, Millenium Park and Magnificent Mile even with kids. You have access to the double decker literally right outside the lobby and the water taxi is right at the hotel to go Shedd aquarium and the Field museum. We used the pool every day with the kids and it was lovely. The equipment in the gym was modern and in good order. Plenty of towels. You could hear a bit of noise from the hall during the day but it did not honestly affect us at all. In reviewing some of the complaints now that I have returned I can tell you that in my experience if you have any issues, tell someone at the hotel and they WILL make it right. Chicago was a WONDERFUL city and if you don't have a wonderful time staying in Chicago and at this hotel I think you may have unrealistic expectations of travel. Thanks you Chicago and thanks to all the great people at the Sheraton. We will be back soon!!

Everything was top notch. This great hotel had excellent service and ameneties. The rooms and hotel was very clean. The only draw back to me would be the spa an pool area needs to be updated, tho it's hard to say anything negitve when everything else was outstanding.

I've stayed 6 nights at Distrikt hotel with my sister. When we arrived from a pretty exhausting trip (customs at JFK was horrible), we were welcomed by very friendly, helpful staff. They really made us feel like home, gave us good information on the neighbourhood and restaurants etc. The man who helped us with our luggage was also super friendly. And this through out our entire stay. Times Square is a few minutes walk, across the street you have Port Authority bus station (also to and from the airports), at the end of the street you can take the subway and you're close to the big variety of restaurants of 9th Avenue. If I visit NY again, maybe I would prefer a hotel which is in a more quiet neigbourhood but for people who don't mind to stay in the middle of the hussle and bussle, this hotel is perfect. The rooms are very nice, clean and we didn't have any noise from the streets (we stayed at the 7th floor).
Too bad the elevator didn't work very well. You had to waive your roomcard before pushing the button but the waiving didn't really work every time so the elevator took us to the 20th floor and up several times. Nice to meet new people in an elevator, not so nice when you arrive at the hotel exhausted and just wanting to get to your room. We booked breakfast buffet in advance but this was a big mistake. I would really recommend going somewhere else to have breakfast, or maybe order breakfast from the menu, maybe that's better than the buffet. 
I would really recommend this hotel to everyone who's looking for a great place to stay, with friendly staff who go the extra mile for their guests.

This is one of our favorite hotels! Rancho Bernardo makes us feel at home. . . the ambiance reflects a fine balance of comfort and elegance, set in a serene and natural surrounding. All the staff are extremely friendly and greet you as if you have always been living there, giving you a sense of belonging. We were particularly well taken care of by your Front Desk Supervisor, Kyle Mitchell, who patiently assisted us with last minute changes to our room reservations.
Thank you, Mr [NAME] (General Manager) and all your staff for continuing to make our experience at the Rancho Bernardo the bestest ever!
We will be back very soon. . ..

title_masked: This is one of the finest hotels EVER!
text_masked: I just can not say enough positive things about this hotel. Your stay will be worth every single penny. The service is impeccable (this is my favorite thing about the hotel), the rooms incredibly clean and comfortable and the location is PERFECT! We come to Dallas at least twice a year and I sometimes hesitate on if I want to spend that much money on a hotel but I have now decided this is my go-to hotel for Dallas. It really doesn't get any better than this. The only hotel experience that I have had that rivals this hotel was the Ritz Carlton in Grand Cayman - and they are a resort!! But the quality service is the exact same. I absolutely love this hotel!

title_masked: Terrific property, location, and helpful staff
text_masked: Here for business last week, and must say, it's one of the best Choice Hotel properties I've ever stayed at. Only 6 (very walkable) blocks to the inner harbor area, and pretty easy access to the interstate. Its a very new property, hopefully they keep it like that! Staff member "Lou" provided excellent service and was extremely helpful, and gave me excellent instructions for a jog to inner harbor and driving directions to I-95.

We went to NYC for a long weekend, to enjoy a few Broadway shows. This hotel is 1 to 1.5 miles from the theater district (depending upon which theater) and is a reasonable walk. Note: A cab ride to the theater is only about $7 + tip, if you don't want to walk. The subway (E train) is right across the street and will get you very close to your theater, too.
Pros: VERY large rooms by NYC standards.
 VERY clean rooms and bathrooms.
 Very friendly hotel employees.
 A quiet hotel. Much quieter than being near Times Square. We were on the 23rd floor.
 Very reasonable rates for NYC. We booked months ahead of time. $237/night.
 Free use of computers in their business center, which was never busy.
 Subway station is very close to the hotel.
 A good CVS/Walgreens type store is right next to the hotel.
Cons: No large beautiful lobby, if that means anything to you. We couldn't care less about that.
 That's it!!!
Note: This property is a typical 3-star Courtyard Marriott. If you're looking for the Four Seasons, this isn't it. 
We could not have been more happy with this hotel. Kudos to the management of this property!

title_masked: Convenient Location, Clean Room, Comfortable Bed
text_masked:
My daughter and I travelled to New York for a visit to the Big Apple. We chose the Doubletree Metropolitan based on previous reviews and the upgrades made to the hotel. 
The hotel has had a makeover, the lobby is clean and modern on check in and they present you with yummy chocolate chip cookies upon arrival. The carpets look relatively new and are fairly clean. We noticed the hotel gets a lot of traffic at the elevators and at peak times you can wait several cars and minutes before you can squeeze into one of them. 
The room was a decent size with two double beds and a LCD style tv and had a safe for personal belongings. Our room was furnished with a desk, a couple of chairs, a desk and several modern style lamps. Although the carpet was newer we had a rip in ours - not sure how this would have occurred but it was noticeable. 
The bathroom was a reasonable size with shower/tub and single sink with decent counter space for toiletries, etc. The one thing we noticed was that the bathroom didn't have a fan so after a shower it took some time for the mirror to defog. The towels were replaced regularly and the bed was comfy with 4 pillows per bed - soft and firm depending on your preference. The room was cleaned daily and the beds made each day as well. 
You can hear doors closing in the morning and evening when people leave/return - it's a bit of annoyance when you're in bed and trying to fall asleep. As well, we could hear the sound of water from above - running and toilet being flushed. 
If you're looking for a very quiet hotel where you can't hear your neighbours at all - this isn't it. 
The hotel is very conveniently located to the subway system as there are stops across the street and another block away depending on which route you're taking. We found this to be very convenient as we explored much of the city by subway. 
There is free wi-fi in the lobby so you able to connect to the Internet if you don't want to pay the fee for access from your room. 
There are many restaurants and food outlets nearby so you don't have to travel far for meals or snacks/refreshments. 
I'd stay here again based on convenience of location and overall cleanliness.

title_masked: Phenomenal service and stay to make for the perfect get away!
text_masked: We wanted to get away from Dallas for the weekend and decided to stay at the DoubleTree Suites by Hilton - Austin for the weekend prior to Halloween. Despite being a busy weekend for the hotel, we had exceptional service from every staff member we came into contact with, our rooms were cozy and well kept, cookies were warm upon arrival and the card in our room was personalized beyond the typically found generic ones from GMs. Also the proximity to 6th street, UT, the Capital building, and the museum made this the perfect hotel for our stay. We will certainly stay here again and recommend it to all of our friends and family visiting the area. Thank you!

title_masked: Andaz 5th Ave is Excellent Hotel in NYC!!!
text_masked:
We visit NYC several times a year, Andaz 5th Ave is our home away when we are in NYC. We had a corner suites with beautiful views, love the foot bath especially after a long walk all day long :)
Love the coffee bar and breakfast at The Shop was so good, make sure you order Chef Vence's specialty Lemon Poppy Seeds pancakes it is so delicious and please do say hello to chef Vence, he is a great chef.
The staff on this hotel is very friendly and yet professional, always ask if we need anything over drink and wine while waiting for room to be ready or waiting for friend to pick us.
We are looking forward to get back to this hotel.

I recently attended a conference at the beautiful Renaissance Austin Hotel and spent three nights there. The rooms were clean, in well working order, and appropriately furnished; they are, however, starting to show some wear. The common areas are excellent for conferences, the conference rooms are well equipped, and the staff are extremely helpful, efficient, and friendly. Every member of the staff with whom I came into contact was very professional and expressed a genuine concern for my comfort as a guest. The coffee packs in the room traditionally have one regular and one decaf; when I asked for additional regular packs they readily gave them to me without charge. Parking is free unless you use valet parking, which I recommend during inclement weather. WiFi is not free. I would be inclined to return to this hotel the next time I am in Austin.

Great stay at the W San Fran. Was especially pleased with the level of customer service from the concierge desk. Had three nights in SF and wanted three good restaurant and they nailed all three. For the record, we requested trendy restaurants with an energetic vibe. 25 Lusk, Ozumo, and Kokkari were all excellent. Pleasant and attentive service from our concierge Amy Owens and another whose name I don't know. All reservations were done the day or two before. I also thought food at Living room bar was better than expected as well.

We had a one night stay prior to flying back to New Zealand. We stayed on the 9th floor, room 911.
I can't fault the place. 
Check in was prompt & polite and all questions awswered (we had many!)
