Internet access was super easy, fast and reliable
Our room was smaller than where we'd previous stayed (especially the bathroom area) but we and all of our luggage (7 suitcases in total) managed to squeeze in.
The room was quiet, immaculately clean and although the beds are smaller than used to, we all found them & the pillows fresh & comfortable.
There weren't enough towels in our room to accommodate of family, a phone call had someone with extra towels at our door within 5 minutes. Love it.
The breakfast area was clean & spacious and well designed. The food itself was more than adequate.
The shuttle was very reliable both in and out of LAX, and the driver friendly and helpful.
Maybe we timed in right, but we had no hassle with the lift, despite one being out-of-action.
Perhaps, the best thing about this hotel was the SECURE and well-managed luggage storage so we could go and explore LA prior to our night time departure. In addition, prior to flight - there was sufficient semi-private space to reorganise our luggage (shopping) in the lobby. Also the restrooms in the lobby were ideal for getting changed/freshened up ready for our flight - they were spacious and clean.
A big thumbs up from us. My husband is planning on changing his usual LAX hotel to this one in future.

Great hotel. Large,clean,stylish and comfortable rooms. Helpful happy staff. Included breakfasts were very tasty. The bar on an evening served very good food. My son enjoyed the small pool, very pleasant after a busy day sightseeing. The guest laundry was a really useful addition to facilities.Great location for any of the sporting events. A very smart hotel which made you feel welcome.

Stayed for 2 nights at Gaslamp Marriott. Beautiful hotel in downtown/GasLamp district. Short walk to convention centr and Hilton where the conference was. Concierge lounge was very nice and attendants were stellar. Room was spacious and clean. Close (walking distance) to any number of good restaurants. Nice fitness area with great view over the city.

title_masked: Weird vibe from front desk, small rooms
text_masked: We stayed with a bunch of friends for a little SF holiday eating, drinking and shopping. One of our group booked the rooms through an online booking service. It seems that whenever I've done this they treat you like the unwanted customer. The attitude of the young man who checked us in was odd-Our rooms weren't ready (after check in time) until pushed, then suddenly they're ready, etc. I never use online booking sites anymore because of this common problem. You can usually match the site's price directly with the hotel and if not, just ask. Our rooms were nice enough but small, which is not unusual in SF. Bathroom so small only one of us could even stand in it at a time. No coffee in the room which really bugs me. 40- for coffee for four of us? The building is really beautiful and we've enjoyed the Starlight Room many times in the past. Unfortunately this year there was a private event and we couldn't get in. That was a disappointment. I would choose another hotel near Union Square, there are MANY other, better choices.
I was in NY for a very brief business trip. I got in late, but had a great quiet room to relax in. Very close to my meeting. Staff very friendly and helpful. Will definitely be back.

Recently spent a long weekend at Rancho Bernardo and was so impressed by everything - decor of common areas, landscaping, room decor, Aveda products and wonderful staff. Hotel has two restaurants and a cafe. We dined in the more casual restaurant which has an indoor section,indoor bar and an outdoor setting with fire place, bar and overlooks the property. Food was reasonably priced for hotel restaurant - giving option of either off the menu or buffet. Breakfast buffet was plentiful and constantly replenished. The dinner buffet can be a great deal depending on the night. I would recommend checking out the buffet before deciding whether or not to order off the menu. Overall - wonderful place.

I asked my wife to join me on this business trip and so 2 months in advance reserved a 1 bedroom suite when she said yes! The day before we arrived i was called by the manager to tell me the suite would not be available because a big client was staying longer. When I questioned this reasoning (I've wanted to overstay before and been told the room was rented) she said "don"t you know about fracking in Texas?" and offered me a lesser room at the same price as available on the website as consolation, huh?Should have been my clue. The hotel is fine, an average LQ Inn and Suites in a good location and like all, reasonably priced. The fact that there were 60 hardworking guys who drug mud in each night (unless they hosed it off on the walk at the entrance) isn''t their fault. Overall I can almost never complain about a LQ. They are good value. But this managers attitude seemed to be focused on revenue and not the promise made when I reserved the room. When I said "Why is the room online for reservation if it does not mean it is available?". She said "I don't know". Sometimes when you get busy you forget that busienss is a two way street. This was a fail in the customer interaction department. Things happen, but you don't transfer the burden of your emergency onto your customer if there is a way to avoid it.

Huge, perfectly decorated and appointed rooms with amazing views, ideal location, genuinely courteous and help staff, warm and elegant public spaces, great bar with excellent wine list, great breakfast and a much improved restaurant. My pick for Chicago, always.

title_masked: Suited my purposes for one night
text_masked:
My wife and I came down for St Patty's for one night on points. The first bone to pick is 15$ for self parking, or 18$ for valet. Pretty pricey for Memphis. The Holiday Inn on Union is only 10$. The hotel is fine overall. Valet took our car and a porter helped us with our bags all the way to the room. If you don't feel like tipping then carry your own bags. I wouldn't say it was in need of any serious updating. The price you're paying for this room is 1) It's a Crowne 2) location -- There is a Holiday Inn Express farther up Union about 2mi from this that is half the price. There is a free shuttle here which we used once to get down to Beale. The other time we just grabbed a cab which park on the street right outside waiting for passengers (note: the cabs will dock you an addl
3$ fee for travel around downtown) as the shuttle was not readily avilable and have people already waiting on it. If neither of those are aviaible, the trolley is behind the Marriott across the screet and runs to around Beale street every 10 minutes or so, and cost something like 1.50 each way, or you can get a pass. The room was fine and clean. No refrigerator but we didn't request a room with one. Typical Crowne amenites. I'm Platinum (I'm going to miss that status) so we got a coupon for free breakfast on Sunday. It was typical buffet stuff - scrambled eggs sitting in a milky sauce, biscuits and gravy, bacon, etc., all sitting in those silver warming domes. We just stopped in to get some juice to drink. Here's the real kicker though.. our 'free' breakfast would have cost 32$!!! We had to sign the receipt and I was floored at the price. It's no wonder there were very few people there (probobly only those who got it free). There is a restaurant on site but I don't know if they cook a 'real' breakfast or not. There was free coffee near the business center in the morning. There is a bar there with a few beers on tap (one is Yuengling) and some alcohol (limited selction, not a 'full' bar).
Checkin/out were both smooth with no problems. We were in an even numbered room on the 6th floor opposite the freeway, so we had no sound concerns.
All in all, I'd really only stay here again if I was not able to get in the Holiday Inn on Union. I've stayed there many times, and even though it's a little outdated, the proximity to Beale more than makes up for it.

title_masked: Great location, Phenomenal roof bar view, Great deal
text_masked: Great location right across from Rockefeller Center. Amazing view from private access roof bar overlooking Radio City Music Hall, Rockefeller Center, and St. Patrick's Cathedral. All at very low prices for Manhattan, especially for Midtown. Rooms are small, but well designed. Tiny bathroom with only a standing shower, no tub, but new, nicely designed fixtures and clean. Free Wi-Fi. Free dispenser near elevators to fill empty water bottles provided with filtered water to take to your room or with you for the day.

Had to opportunity to hit Chicago and this hotel was part of the package...from WestJet..included four nights at the hotel and air. Hotel is a bit older but totally renovated and remodeled. Loved it. A little upgrade to view the lake was very nice. Rooms very clean...your basic hotel room. Staff very friendly and professional and knowledgeable as to the sights, etc...all very helpful. and most of all, the hotel was located right in the middle of the action, well maybe a little bit south of it, but everything we did was within walking distance. I would totally recommend this hotel for a stay in the city. Close to all amenities.

title_masked: Excellent location in the heart of Times Square in New York City
text_masked: Accommodating staff, comfortable lounge, excellent for mixing business meetings with NYC entertainment. On W44th Street and walking distance to midtown Manhattan attractions - Broadway shows and restaurants, Rockefeller Center, St. Patrick’s Cathedral, Madison Square Garden, etc…

When one travels a lot, I get kind of sick of the cookie cutter hotels, this one has an old world charm yet it has the upscale feel which for its location would be expected. Service is good, rooms are upgraded, sheets and comforter good quality, a well stocked mini-bar. The bell hops very friendly and helpful. The location is fabulous, walking distance to all of the area shopping and restaurants. I would stay again without hesitation. Enjoy Chicago!

Pleasantly surprise by the experience and good service. Cordial employees and pleasant service. Extremely clean rooms and atmosphere, w were surprise about the breakfast that was included in the rate.
Great location just blocks away from inner harbor. Asked for late checkout, as was no problem. Overall best service we had in the entire trip in Baltimore.

Location, Location, Location..... this hotel was in a perfect spot. So close to Times Square, 5th Ave. and just about everything I needed to do/see on my (too short) visit. Room was very clean and modern. I loved the shower, and the bed was crazy comfortable. The room even came with it's own iPad for ordering room service, check out, etc....
This would be the perfect hotel for a romantic getaway, and room even came stocked for just such an occasion, but since I was there for business, I didn't get to take advantage! 
The lobby was very dark and at first I didn't even see the registration desk, but once I figured it out, no problems. And the staff was sooo nice, even suggesting places for me to take my clients for a photoshoot. 
Would I stay there again, absolutely.

Booked multiple rooms here for a wedding. I left all of the paper work at home but the staff was friendly and accomodating. There was a mix up with one of the reservations that they were quickly able to work out.They could not have been nicer! Rooms on the lower floors had a view of Marina City parking garage. I asked for and recieved a room higher up with a view of the river. Rooms were spacious, decor bohemian. My only complaint was lack of counter/storage space by the sink in the very large bathroom. The bar/club in the lobby is beyond gaudy. It was a very happening place but lacked adequate number of waitstaff and bar tenders.Took 35 minutes to get a drink. Our post wedding party left and went to another bar. Booked on lastminutetravel for a rate of $132. Would stay here again.

The location for us was excellent since we did not have a car. Target and other shopping next door. The subway entrance was very close but the hotel also provided a shuttle to an from the subway entrance. Breakfast was excellent with a lot of choices. In the evening, had cookies, coffee, hot tea and cocoa that we enjoyed even though it was June, the weather was cool and rainy during our trip. The front desk was friendly and helpful. Room was very clean and housekeeping was also friendly.

title_masked: My adopted home in New York
text_masked:
Just returned from a three night stay at The Lucerne. I was not disappointed! I discovered this hotel a few years ago and now consider it my home away from home when I visit New York. It is close to the Subway as well as Central Park and Riverside Drive. In addition to the restaurant attached to the hotel, there are quite a few restaurants nearby. It has a great neighborhood feel. 
The hotel staff, especially the Doormen and Housekeeping were so accommodating. I lover my room (a suite with a separate sitting area and small fridg). 
I can't wait to go back.

The COAA Spring Leadership Conference was held @ the Westin. We were hosted on the 3rd floor which was perfect for our group. Meals were great as was audio-visual. My room was excellent and the Green program incentive helped pay for my breakfast on my last day. I enjoyed a staff recommended dinner and breakfast in the 2nd Floor bistro, and found the food gourmet quality. The staff was not only professional and friendly; they went out of their way to provide walking maps and information on local attractions. They were having fun and their attitude was infectious.
I recommend the hotel for business travel. The free internet allows you to keep in contact with your company and the 3 story Galleria, provides a wonderful escape for you or those traveling with you.

My wife and I stayed at the Millennium this past weekend for a night out in the city. We did not stay in the hotel very much but enjoyed the time we were there. The hotel is in a great location. We drove to a parking deck in NJ near the PATH train and took the train in from there. I say this because if you are a Jersey person the train station at Harrison on the PATH line has a great safe parking deck that will cost you $11 for 12 hour instead of the $60 the hotel charges. The hotel is a quick walk from the PATH station and a ton of subway lines. We saw a play had dinner, hung out at a few bars in the village and had a wonderful bed a few minutes away in the Hilton. The view was amazing. We were right above the eastern edge of the World Trade Center site. I was worried that there would be noise from construction but there was nothing but that great view of the site, memorial and NYC skyline. We stayed on a Saturday in mid march, reserved on the Hilton website and paid a $189 AAA rate. With tax it came to about 220. The room was pretty small but the bed was so very comfortable. No complaints what so ever. We were given the option to pay $20 more when we reserved for a room away from the WTC site. I was tempted but glad I didn't. As I said there was no noise and I would have missed the view.

The overall hotel is modern with a cool vibe. The rooms are clean and have Bliss spa products. The gym is small but well appointed with the newer fitness machines.
Room service was very prompt, but overall food quality was adequate. Oatmeal for breakfast touted sour cherries, but was served with marachino ones. Roasted tomatoes were barely touched by oven heat, and the sausages were sliced in half and dried out. For the price of the menu items, the chefs in the kitchen need to step-it-up.
If you're looking to be near the Gaslamp district...look for a closer hotel, this one's a mile walk away.

title_masked: Extraordinary customer service: they make things right
text_masked: This was my 2nd stay in the past year; I specifically returned here, and encouraged 6 other people to also book at this hotel rather than the Hilton because of my 1st experience. I was concerned that I had made an error when the Club room I'd specifically booked was not available and instead we were placed 11 floors below the Club. There were a few bumps along the way, but every staff, again this trip, "made it right". I'm not kidding - they didn't have to go ask anyone, they just made decisions to please us. From Esteve and Olga on the front desk to Renee in the Club Lounge, they are genuine, professional, customer-focused folks! I'll definitely return -- and, based on my recent stays at Sheratons & other SPG hotels, we are looking to go to Boston the end of August and stay at an SPG again!

My girlfriend and I recently stayed here for 3 nights as a part of our cross country road trip. I left the hotel feeling very conflicted regarding what rating to give it. On the one hand, the hotel met all of the basic criteria I look for when selecting a hotel. On the other hand, it lacked things that hotels I have given 4 or 5 stars to. I wish I could could give 3.5 stars here on trip advisor, as that is what this hotel deserves. Allow me to explain. 
First off, if you are looking for a hotel that is in the heart of San Diego, this is not the place for you... you are at least 15 to 20 minutes away from locations like La Jolla and downtown. This was good for my girlfriend and I, as we rented a convertible while in San Diego and wanted to have some nice drives so we could really appreciate it, but for someone who wants to be in the thick of things, I'd suggest staying either closer to the beach in Del Mar itself, or closer to town. The hotel itself was conveniently located near the highway, and had plenty of free parking, including a secure garage which I appreciated. The rooms were clean, the breakfast was plentiful and situated in a nice large room, and the Internet was complimentary. These are all pretty basic things I look for when picking a hotel; free internet and parking and a nice clean room, so I want to give this place 4 stars, but I simply feel like it falls short of the 4 star distinction. The Internet was painfully slow, there are no fridges or microwaves in the room, the pillows are very small, and the hotel itself simply failed to inspire any strong positive emotions from me in the way that other hotels have on my trip thus far. 
I really wish I could give this place 3.5 stars because that's really what it deserves. It's a suitable hotel, the price was reasonable, and if you don't mind a short drive, it's in an ideal location. I'd even stay here again, as it was a good price, but would hope to see a few minor improvements made to the hotel.

Hotel was beyond awesome. First the hotel team from the front desk to the housekeeping were the nicest most caring people I have met and I travel a lot! We normally stay elsewhere during our market trips in Dallas but could not get reservations for the time we needed to be there. Candlewood worked us in and then made us feel like family. The hotel shuttle was the most accomidating transportation and the drivers were wonderful. All future trips will be booked at Candlewood. Special thanks to Senedu - your entire team rocks!!!!!
The room was clean and very close to Sea World. The only thing that I didn't like was that the beds were very uncomfortable. Other wise the room was good

We loved all the W experience. It's my 4th time staying with w ant I love it. 
The rooms are cool and cozy. Bathrooms are very good with nice amenities 
The service was great. The concierge is there to provide with all your needs, even if he has to go all over to help you he does. Front desk also great. 
Perfectly located. Around the corner from MOMA, and in front of the Yerba buena complex. 
Parking sisterm works well, a little expensive, but. San Francisco parking is not
Cheap. Walking distance from union square an chinatown , without being inside the noise there 
Highly recommend. Will stay there next time in SF

Both my wife and I have been to Hollywood before but this was our first time together. Neither of us had stayed at the Roosevelt before. There is a valet service, but we found it convenient to park in the structure across the street as we had only one bag. The hotel is beautiful and the staff was extremely friendly and accommodating. We were upgraded to a very nice suite on the 11th floor. I used to travel every week for a living for years, so I'm a bit of a hotel snob and I've had my fair share of complimentary upgrades. But this upgrade was totally unexpected as I have no status with this hotel of course. Within the first few minutes of getting into our beautiful room which had a nice partition between the work area and the sleeping area, I found my previously irritable and travel weary wife suddenly in lingerie, on a beautiful bed, iPod in docking station and ... So Anyway, yes great hotel, great service, great staff, great accommodations. I highly recommend it!

I have stayed at this hotel several times. On my most recent visit, the construction next door was deafening and so I specifically asked about it when I checked in. The fairly unfriendly person at the desk said that it no longer was a problem. Still, I was stunned when I went to my room, only to discover that it sat directly on top of the construction site. I went back to check in and an only slightly more friendly staff member changed me to the other side of the building. And neither room was Starwood Preferred (I'm Gold status), even though the hotel seemed far from fully occupied. Even though the hotel's location is very good, I'd rather stay somewhere where the staff seems to value my repeat business.

This place used to be great....yes the TV's were old and the elevators slow but service was always phenominal. The Manager used to be in the lobby talking to people and the employees seemed to care. Now, the building is run down, the bar and loby is disgusting and worn out, the rooms are beat up and nobody is smiling. Everything in the building is worn out. The employees are there to only pick up a paycheck! Noone helps you anymore. They look at you like you are bothering them. I asked to speak to the General Manager twice and both times I was told he is unavailable. Obviously, something changed and the peple there just dont care. I wouldn't $100 let alone $400 to stay here again. Whoever is there now really needs to reevaluate what they are doing. I will be staying at the London from now on.

title_masked: THE ST. ANTHONY RIVERWALK WYNDHAM HOTEL SAN ANTONIO TX
text_masked: My husbad, 3 year old son, 9 year old daughter, and myself spent 2 nights in the St. Anthony Riverwalk Wyndham hotel. We arrived on August 11th and checked out August 13th. This hotel is overpriced!! The only nice place in this hotel is the lobby. When we arrived to our room there were stains on the carpet and I'm not talking about little stains-they were huge. There was no microwave, or refrigerator. I had to ask for a refrigerator and it was a piece of crap! The beds were very noisy and not comfortable at all. Don't even get me started on the television, it was an old box television. The bathrooms were dirty. The toilets weren't cleaned correctly since there were stains on the bowls, and the hair dryer had hairs stuck to it!! I wouldn't recommend this hotel to anyone!! Oh and when we checked in the receptionist told us that they had free breakfast, IT WAS A BIG LIE! My daughter and husband went to eat breakfast Sunday morning. My husband and daughter agreed that the food was cold and nasty. On top of bad food my husband had to pay $20 for breakfast. Don't let the lobby fool you. I would NEVER stay at this hotel again!!!!!

We booked this hotel through a third party vendor and were very pleased with the accommodations. The staff (from valet to front desk) were as friendly as could be. The room was spacious and sheets were super soft (surprising for a poly/cotton blend). There was even a private balcony off our room. The hotel gym was excellent. There were 5 cardio machines, free weights, and a couple of other weight resistance machines. The view from the gym is also amazing.
Things to know: we stayed in an even numbered room (room *02) and the view was of the parking lot. If you choose to valet, the fee is $26 per day. Internet access is also a separate charge. However, there are package specials that you can find directly through the hotel's website. Depending on the package you choose, some of these costs might already be included. The ceilings in the room are not very high. The location is great. You can walk to all of the top restaurants from the hotel. And, there's a heated roof top pool.
Overall, we were happy with this hotel and highly recommend it.

title_masked: Good value hotel in a safe part of town!
text_masked:
We ( 4 girls !) stayed for 4 nights after a long drive from Sierra, so this hotel was a good rest stop for some very tired bodies. 
Location : At Grant avenue, in Chinatown area. About 5 minutes walk from Union Square. 
Room quality : Comfy mattress, decent ensuite bathroom, room was big enough. Very comfy overall. Feels very very clean! This is the cutest part, the chambermaid would actually craft the a towel into an animal ( eg, snail, fish etc ) and place it on your pillow! :-)
Lobby : Comes with a Pc terminal ( You need to pay for using it though) , printer, coffee faciities and a vending machine for snacks and chocolates.
Front desk : Very helpful and obliging.
Price : we paid about US$100 per night for a Queen bed room/ non smoking.
Shuttle : It was US$15 per person to get onto a shuttle that goes straight to the airport.
Safety : It felt very safe as front desk was in operations all the time, and the main door was locked after 10pm. We were given front main door keys to unlock the door. But of course recept would auto-open the door when they see us. The neighborhood was free from vagabonds and weirdos. Mainly just tourists and residents. 
Overall : Highly recommended for folks on a budget!

title_masked: Nice, clean property centrally located in North Phoenix
text_masked: I am a local but stayed here one-night to save myself a drive back up to North Phoenix the next morning. It is a very clean, conveniently located hotel. It had an indoor and outdoor pool area, a nice restaurant for breakfast, and WiFi. I chose this hotel because I received a great corporate rate and it was slightly better than most overnight business trip hotels I stay at. The only downside I would comment on my trip was the $4 pint beers in the empty bar. Probably why the bar was empty, but that's not a huge detraction for me anyway. Overall, nice place to stage from in PHX.

title_masked: Great Views and Location, Good Service, Fair Food
text_masked:
Just spent a great Labor Day weekend at this hotel. Our family of four had a room with views of the entire length of Times Square and beyond from the 26th floor. I can't imagine any other hotel has better views. The suite was reasonably large (don't expect huge spaces anywhere in New York) and clean, as well as surprisingly quiet at night. It's great fun to be able to watch the Times Square melee from the quiet and comfort of your room once you've finished your battle on the street.
Aside from Times Square, the Doubletree is also within walking distance of Rockefeller Center, MoMA, Central Park and, of course, the Theater District.
Service was friendly and helpful and express checkout is available. 
The only thing a little lacking was the restaurant, Gingers. Granted, we only ate breakfast there, but it is certainly nothing to write home about. The food was passable, but usually not very warm, and there seemed to be a definite push for customers to buy the over-priced buffet. Our family was mainly interested in getting breakfast as quick and easily as possible so we could "get out on the town," with no intention of ever eating dinner in the hotel regardless of how good it could have been. With that in mind, Gingers filled the billed adequately, but nothing more. 
We will definitely stay here again on our next visit to New York.

title_masked: Magnificent Trip on the Magnificent Mile!
text_masked: I stayed at The Drake for almost a week, hosting a conference. The staff I encountered from the time I dropped off the rental car at the front of the hotel for valet parking when I arrived until the morning I left the hotel, were OUTSTANDING and ALWAYS willing to go out of their way to help you! Even the staff who helped me with my event, went above and beyond! The rooms were larger than I expected; with a very large bathroom, 2 large closets, with a personal coded safe, desk and chair, credenza with TV, side chairs, stocked refrigerator and snacks. I can not forget the fluffly pillows and the comfy king bed. I felt like I was sleeping on a cloud! Catering went out of their way for our events, even when we had more people show up than had registered. The location was perfect to visit the shops on the Magnificent Mile and the Navy Pier. I would highly recommend the hotel to anyone on a personal or business trip!

title_masked: Favorite Hotel in Santa Monica/Venice area
text_masked: This is by far my favorite hotel to stay in while in LA on business. The area is so close to everything and the beach is right there! It is a great size, not too big or overwhelming so it makes check in very easy. Everything you need in the area is walking distance so it is easy to find your own favorite places. The staff is great very helpful, make you feel right at home and completely unpretentious. Great restaurant Barlo inside with such delicious local food. The rooms have been recently renovated are very clean and have super comfortable beds. The bar upstairs is great too with beautiful sunsets and the staff supplys blankets when it is cold. JUST LOVE IT!!

We had a group here for the weekend (4 rooms total) for the Seattle Rock N Roll marathon. It was the perfect location because it was so close to the Space Needle (and therefore close to the start & finish line) and the amenities around. The staff were very friendly and helpful. We really appreciated the free shuttle service (which we didn't even know about until we were about to walk to Pike Place in the pouring rain & it was offered) that was able to drop us off and pick us up wherever we liked in the city. The breakfast is decent - hot food (including waffles!)
Beds were comfortable and the rooms are clean & we felt the value was excellent.

It was altogether a great experience staying at The Chelsea Pines. It was a very personal service with real care in helping us with ideas of where to go and what to do. It was our 10th wedding anniversary and a lovely bunch of white roses was delivered to our room from the owners. If we return to New York we have no doubt we would stay there again.

We stayed at The Beacon for a week (one couple + 1 18 yr old). The Beacon offers small apartments (suites) with a bedroom (with cable TV), bathroom, kitchenette and living area (with cable TV) with sofabed. This was perfect for us. The Beacon is very well located: close to central park, close to the subway station (73rd Street) and plenty of decent restaurants in the neighborhood. The front desk staff is very helpful as is the doorman. For breakfast you can go to the "Viand" which is in the same building as the hotel or you can go to a few diners within a few blocks.

title_masked: Cosy little hotel, great location and staff, though noisy
text_masked: Stayed here one night, the hotel is small, but nice and cosy. The staff is very friendly and service minded, the rooms are small but clean and have all you need for a city break. My room faced 5th Ave and it was very noisy during the night, actually quite disturbing. The location is great with a view at the Empire State building, up and close! If you don't need much space and can handle the city noise, this is a good hotel.

Wonderful hotel with excellent location. Very nice service. We had the fortune to get a corner room at the top floor with glass from floor to ceiling. Really nice view. The sleeping comfort was very high and the room intreior was very nice. Clearly recomend!

The Talbott is located close to the magnificent mile and lots of shopping. Also, close to some of the main attractions and stops for the Hop On Hop Off tour bus. A variety of restaurants are within walking distance. Service at the hotel was very good and the concierges (especially Gene) made excellent recommendations for restaurants and getting around the city. Rooms are very clean and comfortable. All staff was pleasant and accommodating.

This is our fourth summer in a row staying at this hotel (I reviewed it earlier here on TripAdvisor), and I'm happy to say it just keeps getting better. 
The rooms are just as clean and comfortable as last time (for those of you complaining about size, please remember you're in a major city and size is at a premium - they're more than adequate!), and weren't lacking for anything. Even the views were very pleasant.
The staff is terrific here, too - not only are you greeted as if you're an old friend, but any of our questions or requests (extra shampoo, directions, etc.) were met with genuine friendliness and specific attention.
It really is a great hotel, and the location can't be beat - one block off of Michigan Avenue, so close enough to everything without having "everything" (and "everything's" accompanying noise) right out your front door. We'll be back.

Met by Monique Madison - 
the Premier Consierge, what a lovely lady. Nothing was a bother to Monique, from early check-in to late-check-out. The breakfasts were lovely, the cocktail bar in the evenings first class - especially when waited on by Nyshraf, what a great fellow, very obliging. The rooms on a high floor were large by NYC standards, and a bonus if you don't like aircon you can open the two windows for fresh air. Lovely huge bed and very comfortable. Finally after a hug and kiss from Monique we left our lovely hotel but we will be back..................................soon, look out Monique!!

Very Clean hotel, beds are comfortable, very spacious rooms. Right in times square, staff was very helpful and friendly. We asked where we could find a vending machine with water, and complimentary was brought right up to our room. Left note for cleaning staff for extra supplies and we recevied our requests for the rest of stay no problem. Excellent service, however no fridge or microwave.

I love it being at Hudson! Even the room was small, also it was really beautiful, confortable and well desgined. The service was really good and it was great having places in the hotel to hang around or just have a drink like the sky terrace and the lybrary. I had just two problemas during the time I was there (15 days). I couldn't connect the wifi at my bed, so I had to go near the door to use the internet. Also, the room was noisy and I kept hering other guests leaving their rooms and several noises coming from the street (57th).

I've stayed at the hotel several times......the new rooms are wonderful. Bed is also great! The lobby is getting remodeled and I'm sure will be nice as well. Just be warned if you park your car it can cost up to $49 per night!!

We arrived early and were welcomed without delay. 
Our first stay was on the 3rd floor in the nonsmoking area. We could smell cig. smoke from down the hall. The room was clean and the bathroom was complete with basic amenities. Great T.V. service
The second stay was on the 5th floor. Along with the basic amenities we had a hair drier, mini-fridge/microwave and great (flat screen) T.V. The maid service ,room cleaning, was not as good as the first stay. It was superficial. The bathroom very clean. 
The shuttle service to anyplace within 5+ miles was great for drop off and pick up.
A little trouble figuring out the thermostat. Would be nice to have a window that opens.
The quality of the breakfast buffet was low for the price.
The pool and spa was clean as well as the exercise room.
Yes, We would stay there again.

This Red Roof Inn is really inexpensive, and the gal at the reception is a sweetie. Amanda! That's her name, one of the other reviewers noticed what a nice person she was, too. She was genuinely interested in the customers, probably because she hasn't been at the front desk but since April. We customers are a dicey lot.
Remind me to return the ice bucket the next time I am at a Red Roof Inn; the manager gave me one because I had come downstairs without the one that came with the room, and it ended up in the travel cooler.
The Red Roof Inn Phoenix West is a little hard to get to. Even though it's right by the freeway, you have to get off early and navigate the various road fragments that are left when a freeway charges through town. In this case the map applications seem to work.

I'm not used to stay in fancy hotels, but when I was in Boston with my University attending a conference, we chose to stay there. The rooms were great, with a big bathroom. Very clean and tidy. Helpful staff, that don't mind showing you directions to wherever you need to go. Close to the Arlington subway station and Boylston St. It'a a bit expensive for young travelers, but for business people it's ideal.

The light switch at the sink area was defective. The lights would only turn on 100% about 1/4 of the time we were in the room after the first couple of days. Sometimes it would go out after working properly. Other times it would not turn on at all or only a very dim light in one panel. I called the desk four times about the problem. The problem was not resolved. Only after the 4th call did a maintenance person show up...and he was unable to repair the problem. We did not want to change rooms because our daughter was in the room next to us and we had too much personal belongings to want to move it all.

title_masked: very clean safe and nice and great customer service
text_masked: great cozy bed to sleep in, a nice roof top pool and great customer service.

Attended a business meeting at this Suite, which was a perfect venue for an extended stay. Kitchenette is not well stocked, but usable. Grocery and shopping within close driving distance. Breakfast and dinner included in stay. Suites were perfect. Good hotel, I would recommend for all types of travelers and families.

Staff was very friendly. The room was a cut above a tradtional Holiday Inn. Their breakfast buffet was expensive - $15. Their restaurant, Dine, had zero atmosphere, although some of the menu items were appealing. We opted to eat elsewhere each night. The hotel, being situated on the border of Greek Town made it easy. Their valet parking was OUTRAGEOUS: $36.50 PER DAY!!!! The only thing that made it seem reasonable, after being there for a few days,, was the parking in the self-park lots: $28 for about 4 hours. All in all, we would return. Our TomTom GPS said "you have reached your destination", but in reality, because of the 1 way streets, we were about 3 blocks away. Only entrance is on Halstead St. Don't miss Pan Hellenic Pastry Shop - it's awesome!

Clean enough. Rooms are somewhat dated. I stayed two night 2/15 - 2/16. The noise from he room above was worthy of complaint but the " guy" obviulsy didnt want the confrontation...so I called up to the room. The next day same noise. This time a lady dealt with it and they quietened down. Small pool and jacuzzi. Ok. Nothing special. The little shop they ahve is WAY expensive. There is a 7 Eleven across the road and they too were WAY expensive. I live in Denver and was staying while some work was being done on the apartment. So knowing 7 Eleven prices in town..wow...watch out. They have you cornered. It's an Ok hotel but nothing special. One night stay would be enough. Village Inn close by and their prices seemed ok.

Stayed one night here before picking up our cruise to Alaska. Having read all the reviews I was very much looking forward to checking this place out.
Being a sucker for water views I always try to get a water view room if it’s in my budget. This time I splurged, even though I wasn’t wanting to spend quite that much. I’m glad I did. 
Location: Could not ask for a better location if you want to be near it all and able to simply walk out of your hotel and enjoy downtown Seattle. Pike Street market, Post Alley and the waterfront are all right within walking distance.
Check-in/Staff: The staff was polite and helpful. As soon as we pulled up the bellman helped to load our luggage on a cart and escorted us to the entrance. We arrived at 1:00 so I didn’t expect a room to be ready, and it was not. They completed our check in and told us they would call when the room was ready. We decided to check our luggage with the bellman. I first pulled out some warmer clothes and changed in the ladies room. They gave us directions to the waterfront so I could get my much anticipated Ivar’s fish and chowder. We walked around for a while and then wandered back to the hotel. Our room was ready when we got there. We were given our keys and the bellman quickly loaded up our luggage and brought it to us.
The room was comfortable and clean. We were greeted with a piece of some sort of dessert and a note wishing us well on our anniversary. The view of the market and waterfront was wonderful. The roof top deck looked very nice as well, although we didn’t use it. The bed was comfortable. I have a problem with feathers so when I called they quickly brought me some non-feather pillows for the bed. My only gripe about the room itself would be the pedestal sink in the bathroom. It really didn't give a lady much space to work when applying make-up, etc. 
Great night of sleep. Never heard any noise from the street or market below or from any other guests. 
We ordered room service for breakfast. This is probably my only complaint. Apparently they messed up my husbands order (an omelets) and had to remake it. Mean while my breakfast (French toast) got cold. By the time our food arrived, mine was so cold the butter wouldn’t even melt. My mocha was good though.
Check out was smooth and easy. We called to have the bellman come up and get our luggage which he did on time and off we went.
I would most definitely recommend this hotel to anyone not worried about budget that wants to be near the action of downtown and the waterfront. Giving it 4 stars only because of the room service issue. I didn't complain but think they should have realized that the one meal would be ruined while they remade the other.

This is a fantastic traditional townhouse hotel - dark wood, paintings, books and and palms - two minutes from Union Square. The staff were very friendly and helpful. There's a lovely library bar downstairs where residents are offered a free glass of wine in the evening, which means people congregate there and there's a really good atmostphere, that you don't often get in town hotels. The room was spacious and comfortable, and well decorated. I'll definitely stay there again when I visit San Francisco.

The hotel was pretty shabby, but it was clean. Noisy, since it is near the interstate and train tracks, but it was convenient to the business I was visiting. The hot breakfast daily was so-so, but hey, it was free (and more than just donuts and juice -- eggs, hashbrowns, ham/sausage, fruit, waffle iron, yogurt, cereals, pastries, and supposedly an omelette station -- though no one ever offered to make me an omelette and I'm sure they were hoping I didn't ask!). Shuttle will take you within 5 mile radius of hotel, though you need to schedule ahead and you might have to wait awhile on your pickup at the other end. It's a rough neighborhood, so I wouldn't expect to be able to go out for a jog.

title_masked: Chic, cool & sexy with Latin vibe
text_masked: I stayed at the Hotel Americano for 5 nights and loved it! I would definitely stay there again. It is a very stylish & chic boutique hotel located next to art galleries, bars, restaurants & night clubs in Chelsea. I loved the sleek, minimalist interior. The rooms are impeccable, if a little small. Don't expect a whole lot of storage space, particularly not in the bathroom! I liked the futon which I felt was very comfortable, as well as the view from our room, which was located on the 8th floor. The room is bright, and has a funky interior with cool, artsy pieces of furniture. The best part of the hotel was definitely the rooftop "La Piscine" with the pool, where you can get cocktails at night and amazing views of the city. The pool itself is very small and not really meant for "proper" swimming, but a nice luxury to have on a hot summer's day for a quick dip. Most of the staff is very friendly, professional and courteous (although there were one or two snooty ones). There is always good music playing, usually bossa nova or some other lounge-music, which suits the place perfectly. We also had brunch at the hotel on Sunday, when they had a flamenco / bossa nova band playing soothing music, perfect to overcome a killer-hangover. The brunch was spectacular, if a little on the pricey side. However I feel you cannot put a price-tag on comfort, and this place really is worth every penny in my opinion. For me it was a very pleasurable experience and I would return in a heartbeat!

Stayed for 6 nights with a friend and loved the Staybridge. 
Well located to most attractions without being slap bang in Time Square madness. Great selection of bars and eateries on 9th Avenue only 100m away. Snobs might find the location slightly "seedy" with a few Sex shops and the probation office nearby. But this is NY and I love to mix it with the locals!!!
The room was well appointed and reasonable size by NY standards. Staff were excellent and very accomodating. The hotel has a free buffet breakfast each day and on Tues, Wed, Thurs free tappas and drinks(beer, wine etc) from 5-7pm. If your stay here and love to shop for interesting gifts, make sure to check out Hell's Kitchens Flea Markets on Sat & Sun down on 39th St and for excellent beers and bar food go to Shorty's Sports bar just around the corner on 9th near 42nd. Ask for Ron, he'll look after you!

We arrived on Friday night of Baltimore Grand Prix weekend, and were delighted that Robert Bready reached out and offered every assistance he could to make us feel like we were receiving the Ambassador experience we used to have when Intercontinental owned this hotel.last year. He provided the kind of service usually only found in small elite hotels, and we were grateful to feel like we were still at our Baltimore home away from home.

We stayed in Chicago at the Raffaello Hotel in February. It is a very beautiful smaller hotel. It is very close to all of the best restaurants and shopping. Our suite was beautiful and clean. The bathroom is a little small but we loved the living room.I would highly recommend staying here.

title_masked: We have always loved it, but want to love it more.
text_masked:
As I say above, we have always loved the Canterbury and will probably continue to stay there. (We will check out the Conrad though, right down the street.) It has a great location and service, just like the other reviews mentioned. The feel is cozy and unique. Doormen are spectactular. 
However, we like it so much and our expectations are so high, that the smallest things are irritating. The plastic cups are silly. The front desk could be as nice as the concierge and doormen. On our last visit, we were awoken twice by drunk people running around the 6th floor on a Saturday night at 2am. Really, at the Cantebury?
Hotel is always clean when I visit. Been there 4 times and enjoy staying. Nice comfortable beds and nice tv . The staff is always helpful and courteous. I recommend this hotel.

I booked the hotel through hotwire as a hiding the name deal for a 3.5 stars hotel. When I finally saw the hotel name, I was quite disappointed. Best Western should be just 2 or 2.5 stars.
Anyway, the hotel is a typical best western. The staff at the front desk is very nice though. The free breakfast is the same as in other best western. The free WIFI is extremely slow and sometimes it doesn't work.
What I personally don't like is the location in lower east town. It might be convenient for people interested in the fish market. For people like me wants to use NYC public transportation, the hotel is about 15 min walk to the subway station. I would like to stay in Mid-town next time when I travel to NYC.

We stayed at the 4 Points Seatle on Saturday, Sept. 15, 2012 on our way to Olympic National Park. I was surprised at how ordinary the room was considering the premium pricing but I guess that is to be expected in a metro setting.
There is a courtyard that ajoins the bar off the main lobby. Many of the rooms balconies face this courtyard. The night that we were there a table of very loud and obnoxious drunks partied in the courtyard until 3:15 am. I was very disappointed that Sheraton management took no actions to break-up the party at a reasonable hour.
Needless to say, my wife and I were Sleepless in Seattle and will not be frequenting this location again.

Just got back from a 6 night stay at the London N.Y.C. It was excellent and all our requests were accommodated.
Stayed in a suite on the 35th floor which had very good views. The suites are so spacious and the bathrooms and showers first class. Housekeeping brilliant with a constant supply of clean white towels. The beds are soooooo comfy and just what you need after a day around New York!!
We ate at the Maze on our first night which was also excellent and very good service. 
If there was one thing I could say it is that there could have been more seating area in the bar and lobby area. 
The staff were very helpful and the concierge recommended a great steak restaurant - Del Frisco's- which was nearby.....we went there 3 times!
Spotlessly clean in all areas. 
The Hotel is centrally located and handy for everywhere...2 blocks from Radio City and the Rock. 5\10 mins walk to Times Square.
We had a great time and would recommend London N.Y.C to anyone and we would definately stay ther again.

We stayed here in March for a long weekend getaway during the Centennial Cherry Blossom Festival. It is walking distance to museums and monuments. The lobby is amazing and filled with cherry blossoms which is nice as the real trees we came to see were bare due to the increment weather a couple of days before our arrival. The staff and Concierge was wonderful and helpful. Our room was clean and quiet.

We stayed here while touring the area. We loved the pool area, it was like a little hideaway form city life outside.
We were promptly greeted by friendly staff and given our room with no extra charge even though we were about 2 hours early! 
Loved the turn down service. Very nice to come back after a day of walking all over the city to find water bottles in room for us :O) 
The room was very clean and comfortable.
We dined twice in restaurant and had very good food and service both times.
We will definately rebook here next time in area.

The hotel is beautiful from the outside and costs a lot so you would expect to get a very nice room. It was problems from the very beginning. We booked a room with a king sized bed and only received a queen. Very surprised that they honored the request and did end up moving us to a room with a king sized bed. The only good thing about this room is the bed though. It is on the street and very noisy. I can hear people outside hailing cabs and deliveries being made. Not the ideal sleeping conditions. The walls are paper thin and you can hear EVERYTHING! Plus...No bathtub. Only a very very small shower with a previous customers hair in it. GROSS! The shower head is so low you have to crouch to get underneath it. Would not stay at this hotel again.

I just returned from a mini-vacation here with my girlfriend and we were both very impressed with the Monaco. We checked in during their "wine hour" and Foster helped get us each a glass of wine before we even had our room keys! 
We had a river view room at it was very cool. They have window seats large enough to lay down in and they look right down the Chicago river. The bed was comfortable and we did not hear too much street noise. 
The Monaco is located in the perfect spot. Even though it was a little chilly for us, we were able to walk to most of the restaurants/stores we wanted to visit.
Rich the concierge helped us navigate our way through Chicago. He sent us to Lou Malnati's for some deep dish pizza and and amazing Italian dinner at La Scarola (that review is coming up next). Nick at the front desk was also able to help me find a liquor store and all the bellman were very friendly!
We are planning on making a return trip to Chicago this summer and we are definitely staying at the Monaco!

We moved to The London NYC after spending 2 nights at another very pricey hotel in New York which we were very unhappy with.
From the moment we entered the lobby we were delighted. The staff were very helpful and friendly always.The concierge staff couldn't do enough for us, the wait staff in the Restaraunt were always very pleasant and courteous.
We were a family with 3 older teenagers so were delighted to find such a large apartment .
The rooma were always cleaned, the gym was fabulous, and we thought value for money, the whole place was well worth it.
Will definitely be back.

I was under the impression when I rented the room that all the rooms are river front. They are not even close. Maybe if you rent the penthouse you can see the river.You have to walk about 100 yards to get to the river. All the brochures show nice river front views. The landing of Jacksonville is supposed to be this premier spot. Far from that. Its just a run down shopping mall with a few poor looking restaurants. The rooms are not spacious as described. Our cable in the room kept freezing up and we were told we had to just deal with it until the next day when the cable company could come. The pool had no lounge chairs as brochure pictured. Staff was nice overall. I feel as though I got dooped for the price.

very clean, very nice staff, the location is very central.............
would definetly stay again..................went with four other girlfriends, had 
a fantastic time......hotel was within walking distance to shopping and times square
and many great restaurants.........allthough new york city taxi's are everywhere.

This hotel has wonderful history and definitely has or had tremendous potential. Having been in the hotel business for years, however, your first impression is very important and the staff all should go through training in how to treat guests. Both the front desk (if you can find it) and the restaurant staff except for the hostesses that were helping us were simply not trained very well or just didn't get it. The noise level at dinner and at breakfast destroy any ambiance that is definitely there but has been lost when your wait staff is clearing tables and just throwing the dishes in black tubs. 
Cost is relative but this is a reasonable place to stay in DC because of the proximity to key locations and Dupont Circle has its own charm apart from the Mall and the ongoing security madness that has occurred since 9/11. Parking could be a real challenge and don't expect any help from the staff at the Tabard, but the Topaz staff were outstanding and we are thankful for that. 
I've read most of the reviews and I don't think "charming" is the word I would use - I've been to many B&B's throughout the United States and this one needs an overhaul from management. Quirky/ different is wonderful, but when all is said and reviewed, you come back to service with a smile and this is not a happy staff - and that goes back to management with a capital M. 
Dinner was well presented and was good. Breakfast for a guest is okay - nothing out of the ordinary but adequate. However, at one point, I really wanted to just stand and ask everyone to take a deep breath and lower their voice one decimal so that everyone in the room could hear one another, or use something on the walls to absorb the sound.
Bathroom is a funky experience, and we had warm water, but we were thankful to be in room 5 and not have to negotiate the steps. Lighting is definitely limited and having coffee available in your room would be a "nice touch" or something for the early morning risers in the lounge area. 
Overall, some very simple cosmetic work could be done and you would truly have a quaint, charming B&B which would be very unique to Washington.

This hotel was beautifullly presented, nice atmsphere. Room was a a bit cramped for 2 adults and 2 children, the bathroom was small. The beds were nice and it was made up each day. The house keeping had to be reminded to leave tea & coffee and we had to request shampoos. We ate in the resturant, which was nice, however and they had a kids menu which was fine. We did feel it did not have a lot of choices. Staff were very friendly. Unfortunately the bell boys get upset if you do not tip them over $10, which for a family is just stupid, obviously we are going to have more bags. When we tipped the bell boy, he refused to put our bags into the cab, the guy on the front door had to chat to him about it all very unsavoury!!

I stay in hotels 3 nights every week. This is the the most filthy hotel I have stayed in for years!! Bathroom and bedroom had stains on the walls. Shower had streaks down the walls and needed to be cleaned before I could use it. Coffee maker was unusable due to a missing filter. Alarm clock did not work and was not replaced by the front desk. I've stayed in roadside motels that were cleaner and better than this place.
Avoid this hotel at all costs!!

title_masked: Black Mold in Bathtub/no towels at checkin
text_masked: I traveled 3 hours, checked in, unloaded our bags and left to work. Came back to the room late at night to find there were NO towels in the room and mold "black" in the tub. (i took pics). We went to the front desk and was told that they were out of towels so I asked why they allowed me to check in if they could not service us properly. The unconcerned lady told me the office is closed and the manager is gone for the day. I had to go to work 4 hours later and had no time to look for other lodging and assumed they'd at least put towels in my room before i returned. I tried several times to call during the day with NO Answer. then again we returned near midnight. The room was not serviced AT ALL AND STILL NO TOWELS! I went back to the front desk and was told the same as before. After cursing this same woman out I grabbed my bags and looked for another hotel in the middle of the night. Oh. and the carpet had a faint stink of urine. Only reason I booked this room is because they had a full fridge that i needed for the food i needed to store. Save your money even if it is cheap its NOT WORTH THE FILTH AND DISRESPECT THESE PEOPLE SHOW.

We stayed at this hotel for a business meeting. The first room we checked into was a weirdly laid out room in the corner of the building that faced Mason St. There was no tub, just a shower, but acres of floor space. Everything was hunky-dorey until 5 am when the trash trucks started picking up outside our window and we never got a wink of sleep after that. The windows are all single pane and so not terribly noise-reducing. Or energy efficient.
We asked the front desk to move us and they couldn't have been more helpful or understanding. We moved to the "spa" side of the building (we overlooked the neighboring health club) and were able to sleep. We even got a tub!
We never ate at the hotel becuase within a one block area there were lots of diners/restaurants/shops to grab a bite. We did enjoy some drinks at the bar where John took great care of us in the evenings.
While my husband slaved away in his business meetings, I went all over town and explored. The hotel is nicely located for shopping at Union Square, Chinatown, or the financial district. You could also hop on a bus tour (discounted tickets are available from the concierge) and see more of the city. I felt safe walking in those areas, but DO NOT GO to the Tenderloin District. The homeless are brazen enough in the Union Square, Chinatown, Financial District, and Fisherman's Wharf, but even the tour busses announce that tourists should not go to the Tenderloin.
All in all I would recommend this hotel because it was clean, roomy, moderately priced, and ideally located. Just don't stay on the Mason Street side unless you hate sleeping after 5am.

We arrived late at night and walked in to a check-in area that had been completely flooded. There were fans running everywhere and water damage on the ceilings and walls. The computers didn't work at the front desk and they had to work from a computer in the back office. I only mention this because with these conditions,it would have been understandable if the two women behind the front desk had been unfriendly, but it was just the opposite. They were so nice and checked us in as quickly as possible.
The room was nice and clean. Breakfast was okay. Plenty of choices, but we got to breakfast kind of late . The biscuits were hard and the fruit seemed old. I'm sure it would have been better if we had arrived to breakfast earlier. 
I'd definitely stay here again.

Loved that it was in the center of L.A. with so much to see close by. Everyone at the hotel is very helpful and nice. Eager to help, to answer questions, or if we needed directions. The hotel is very nice, the room was comfortable and clean. Loved the cafe downstairs, and their super great brunch. We only had a problem with our card keys on one night which they were not opening our room and we did have to be very persistent to get help with this but, it was done and we were sent a voucher for free brunch and spa. I would defintely go back to this hotel.

Went to Comerica Park on July 4 for a Tiger game. This hotel was a nice stay for our family. We booked the wetbar suite and had plenty of room. Two double beds and a pull out couch with a ton of space (except the bathroom). The hotel staff was fast and efficient. I know that people hate the valet parking, but this is a downtown hotel and $18 dollars a day is WAY cheaper that alot of other downtown hotels. We didn't use the pool or get breakfast so I don't have an opinion on them. The city of Detroit seems to be trying to get it act together, but there are still some very problematic areas that we walked past on our way to the ballpark. Boarded up buildings, graffitti, homeless people are still a big problem. We personally had no problems, but if you are worried about it, the people mover is just a couple blocks away. We would definitely stay here again.
Great location and convienient to everything.

My son and I stayed here during Austin Comic Con due mainly to the location. The hotel is directly across the street from the Convention center and in the middle of downtown, so the location is ideal.
The rooms are clean and comfortable, but nothing extra ordinary. The housekeeping was very late in the afternoon, so plan on that. We wanted to rest during the afternoon after spending the morning at the convention center, but left when housekeeping arrived. Water pressure and hot water were fine.
We tried the local hotel restaurant the first night (Champions) and it was average. They have a nice bar with TVs, so it would make a good spot to drink and watch a game, but not for food. Luckily there are a ton of restaurants downtown, so you have a lot of choices for lunch and dinner. As for breakfast, there is a Starbucks attached to the hotel, so we had coffee and breakfast sandwiches there.

title_masked: Great experience at the new Hilton
text_masked: Hosted a company customer appreciation Christmas party at the new Hilton. Our party room and our party food options were great although the pasta bar stove set of the fire alarm emptying out the hotel for a few minutes. If you do an event there make sure you plan a pasta station becasue it was the bomb! Staff was great and very attentive but the hotel let the luncheon before us run over an hour from when they were supposed to be done which delayed our setup. Hotel has been open less that two months so you can expect a few minor issues. Hotel rooms were very nice and comfortable. Great beds! Atrium area was beautiful with nice views of the lobby, restaurant and the bar area which were all very upscale. Food in the restaurant was french style based. Many might struggle with the limited menu, high price and its french cuisine but what we ate was better than expected and the atmosphere was very nice. Hotel location is great within walking distance of numerous restaurants and bars. Plenty of elevators so there is no waiting. We will definitely be back!

I wanted to make my husband's 60th birthday special, and after much research, chose a stay at the Drake hotel as our celebration headquarters. From the time we first made our reservation, to the moment we checked out, we were treated as cherished guests. The hotel is gorgeous and immaculate! Used to the generic, cookie cutter big chains, what a wonderful treat it was to explore the hotel and learn of its history. The pride in their work and their place of employment is evident in every staff member we encountered. The hotel's location is perfect for exploring the city, and its proximity to the beauty of the lake (our room had an amazing view!) is awe-inspiring for Chicago natives and tourists alike. For us, there where will be no other place we'll stay when we treat ourselves to another getaway in our beautiful city. Special thanks to Melissa Neigebauer and Hotel Manager, Stevan Gruvberger for your help in making our stay, and my husband's birthday, extra amazing :>

It was hot and humid when I arrived. The last thing I wanted was a crappy hotel and dirty room. Well... This hotel surpassed my expectations. The front desk was helpful. Got my key to my room swiftly without any hassle. The room itself had a large bed with a mini kitchen with a microwave and pretty sweet "office" desk where you can put down your work and laptop. I only stayed here for 2 nights but would not have minded if I stayed a bit longer. Hotels in Houston are expensive and this was definitely in my budget.

title_masked: Good Value on the Mag Mile
text_masked: The Knickerbocker is one of Chicago's grand historical hotels, now manged by the global Millennium franchise. The rooms are on the small side but completely refreshed and baths are sleek and modern. I had a Jr Suite for 4 nights which has the bed in a separate alcove behind the sitting -TV area, but there is another TV across from the bed, compact but functional space. The location is excellent, across the street from another Chicago landmark The Drake, 1/2 block to Michigan Ave, maybe 5 mins to Hancock Center and Water Tower Place. Nice lobby bar. The Restaurant across from the bar looks under-used, and may need to be re-concepted. Front desk staff consistently courteous and helpful.

We'll add our kudos to the other reviews. The room was clean, comfortable, and quiet. We stayed in 309, which is in the back of the hotel. This room has a nice entry space with plenty of storage space, making the room itself clutter-free.
The location was in a great, pretty neighborhood with easy access to the metro and within walking distance to numerous restaurants.
We also thought the staff were wonderful, particularly Michael and Fernando. They greeted us warmly coming and going, but were never overly chatty--a geat balance of hospitality.
We hope this was the first of many trips to D.C., and would love to return to the Madera.

I stayed at the St. Anthony for a wedding, and I'd be remiss not to give the staff their due. EVERYONE, from valets to the front desk to housekeeping to bartenders to servers were completely on their game and exceptionally friendly. Not only were we always greeted with a smile, but the greetings always felt genuine.
The facilities themselves were okay. I'd give the St. Anthony five stars for charm, especially in the lobby and common areas, but but probably three or less for the upkeep of the rooms themselves. I suspect may travelers may consider old world charm a quaint selling when it comes to decor but not when it comes to the functionality of the bathrooms, etc. Our room was quaint, but the bathroom could use some updates. The old plumbing and wiring were just, well, old. The hair dryer repeatedly tripped the breaker, and the sink had little water pressure (the shower not bad, surprisingly). Plus, towel racks were missing. The bathrooms were just a little run down. Not dingy or anything, just in need of a little TLC.
Those nits aside, I'd stay there again. It's priced fairly. The bed was very comfortable. It's a short walk from just about all the sights in downtown San Antonio. The ambiance is nice, and the staff more than compensated for the very few gripes I found with the place.

This is a great hotel. People are correct that the lobby is tiny and unimpressive however how much time do you really spend in a hotel lobby? I'd rather have a bigger room than a huge lobby. My room was a great size and very clean and comfortable. I could control the temperature of the room and make it as cold as I want when I slept. Granted most hotels have thermostats you can control in the rooms but in my experience they only work about 50% of the time. The staff is very friendly and helpful. My one complaint is I set out the door hanger for breakfast delivery before I went to bed, and when I got up in the morning and went to get my paper it was still there. No one picked it up that night so no breakfast for me. I mentioned it to the staff when I checked out and they were very apologetic. Also the temperature in the cardio room seems inconsistent. I went down one evening to work out and it was freezing in the room and I went down another day and the room was like a sauna. The location of the hotel was perfect for me, away from the Times Square madness but within walking distance of a lot. Overall this is a great hotel and I would definitely stay here again. I travel to NY quite a bit for work and this could easily become my preferred hotel.

Exceptional service, clean rooms, friendly staff, in the heart of the gas lamp district and walking distance to everything. Expensive, but you get what you pay for. Valet parking fee is really high at $40/day. But I would definitely stay here again.
Stayed here because I found this to be the best price in the Marriott chain. Close to all transportation and close to time square. Good staff, neat room!

Great service, lovely rooms, excellent service, everything you would expect from a hotel.
Avoid the bar though, the drinks are really expensive.... Get out and about and sample everything NYC has to offer.

So it turns out the ice machine on our floor was broken and had a really loud and constant beeping. Sound isolation is really poor so we barely got any sleep. The manager wasn't there and the person at the counter basically said there was nothing he could do about it (I even suggested to unplug it and he said that was not possible). He didn't even offer to switch us to a different room! We checked out at 5am after no sleep at all and the manager was supposed to give me a call to apologize and offer us a refund. He never did. Wrote to Hilton and got no response either. Very unprofessional, stay away.

Had 3 nights stayed in this hotel and I would say I like it and will be back. The room is spacious, clean and the one I had, faced to the swimming pool. The bed was comfortable and I can smell the fresh and clean of the linen.The air condition was too cold I had to shut it off. The Metro is right at the lower level of the hotel and there is a food court and some stores. It is close to major attractions, very convenient.

Overall the location is nice by the airport but not to noisy. In the past week I have had 3 different bug varieties in my room. My bathtub hardware makes a screeching noise when showering and the tub stopper does not work so there is no peaceful bathing option. After all of that I would say my biggest complaint is the internet. I travel on business so working at night is necessary. The internet is so slow that this page (yes I am still a guest at this hotel) took 10 minutes to load, I timed it!! My blackberry loads faster. So I just wanted to let all business travelers know that if the internet is important do not stay here, or next door and the other marriott property because they share the same internet connection.

This is a lovely little hotel, not too posh but has everything you need. The room was very small and basic with a tiny balcony with not much of a view but the pool area was nice and the shuttle bus and on site shop were useful. The restaurant on site wasnt that good however as the staff didnt refil the breakfast buffett for ages and the staff werent very tentative to us.

Having just spent 6 days with 3 girlfriends at your hotel, i must say what a fantastic time we all had, your hotel is clean, well run and the staff we so very friendly and helpful. The lady on the concierge desk went out of her way to help and direct us, and everyone on the front desk always spoke and wished us a good day with a cheery smile, (and its little things like that that make your holiday even more enjoyable) the saff at breakfast time were always happy and welcoming (great start to the day). All in all your hotel made our holiday that so much more enjoyable thank you so much, and when we return again or if anyone asks i will deffinatley be advising a stay with you. thanks again
Kath, England

I am from England but now live in California and I love this cosy place. We were upgraded upon arrival to a large king room with a fireplace and flat screen tv. In addition to the bathroom there was a dressing room with a vanity area sink and closet, and another separate area with a fridge, wet bar and tea/coffee making facilities. The fridge contained complementary water bottles and sodas. Our room was at the back and was quiet. The windows etc are old but it adds to the charm. There is tea/coffee and home baked cookies available most of the day and we enjoyed the 5pm wine and snacks, so nice after a busy day sightseeing. Wine was of a good quality and snacks were different each day. A pasta dish, cheese and biscuits, and cake one day and vegetables, dip and apple cake the next. Enjoyed talking with other travelers and there are plenty of interesting items on display around the hotel. Breakfast buffet was nice. The two guys at the front desk were nice and friendly, the female not so much. Parking is difficult, as with most of San Francisco, the first day we arrived was a Sunday so we did free street parking but had to move the car 7am Monday morning. We found the least expensive undercover parking lot was a city one a few blocks away. We spent a total of $28 on parking rather than $32 + tax valet per night.

I was expecting a nice but older hotel. This hotel might have been around for a long time but it sure doesn't feel like it. The bed was very comfortable, there was a nice flat screen HD tv, and I had a nice view. The room service was prompt and friendly. When I went out and bought a bottle of wine ( a local grocery store really had a nice selection) the front desk even got me a wine glass and cork screw. How nice is that? The restaurant's food is good and if you like Pan-Asian food the bar's happy-hour is something you should try.

My Boyfriend & I stayed One Night here and was it was Great. I mentioned it was unplanned, because we rented the night before (usually bad experiences when booking less than a day in advance). Great location, close to the metro. When we arrived our room was not ready yet, so the man gave us tags for our luggage and said we could wait at the hotel or get a bite to eat; We did across the street at Bread and Butter! The lift worked (rest time took stairs, much quicker). We stayed in a Standard room. Queen bed, table, chair, dresser, iron, ironing board. Then there is the bathroom, and the only thing I disliked was the size of the shower!! SOOO SMALL! So so small. Other than that, perfect for the night. Very friendly staff!! Smooth checkout. No problems. Hope to return on the next trip!
Not far from Times Square, but not too pricey. New place, with a staff who is trying to establish a reputation as helpful and knowledgeable.

The staff at this hotel were quite nice & friendly as well as professional, except for the restaurant staff who appeared to have been brought in off of the streets to work without any proper or professional training at all. 
The cost for the room, an enlarged corner King room, was way over priced for what the room provided one. The size of the room was okay but the king bed was anything but comfortable despite the hotel website claim that the bed was their latest ultimate comfort offering. And the pillows were not comfortable at all with regards to sleeping on.
The room was in immediate need of updating and upgrading as there were worn carpet, wallpaper in the bathroom that had once had something else attached but since removed and the colors were rather bland. The desk was way too small for trying to do any kind of business work on and the room lacked counter space in it despite the size of the room possibly accomodating more practical furniture along the walls. The couch was cheap generic and uncomfortable to sit on for more than a half hour at a time, if that long. The entry way lighting was dimly lit and the light switch was across the room from the door. The clothes closet in the entry way was small and lacked clothes hangers. The lighting in the bathroom was very poor. The combination shower/tub was okay but the shower curtain did not cover the curved shower rod thus when taking a shower water would go out on the floor. The toiletries offered in the bathroom was of inferior quality and offering than other upscale competing hotels. The bath towels were quite nice but the wash cloths and hand towels were not of the same quality. As requested there was a very small refrigerator in the room though it was quite small and more suitable for a very small dorm room at a inexpensive college than this hotel chain. And the staff simply placed the mini refrigerator on the floor thus one had to practically sit down on the floor to get into the refrigerator each time. The microwave oven provided was also equally small and cheap or low quality. The flat screen TV was very nice size but offered very few channels and had a problem with buffering the receipt of programs from whatever service the hotel was using at the time. The wireless internet service, which is not free, was only perhaps a 3 on a scale of 1 to 10 with 1 being the lowest, as the service or signal kept getting lost every few minutes or so on any device one attempted to use it with within the room. Valet parking was exceptional at the hotel as each individual working in Valet very professional and friendly and polite. 
Overall the room was way overpriced. What was priced between $240 and $300 a night should in reality been only maybe $100 for what one received from this hotel but due to its location they were able to demand and receive much higher.
And do not choose the offered meal plan at this hotel as the food is not worth it and the staff in the restaurant act more like you are intruding if you do choose to dine there.

title_masked: Excellent loaction, attractive design, small rooms
text_masked:
