The location of this hotel is excellent, right across from the Boston Commons and the freedom trail, and very convenient to public transportation. 
The rooms are very attractive, but quite small. The beds were comfortable, and the airconditioning welcome. The room comes with free wi-fi, a big plus in my book, and a wine reception in the early evening. The staff was helpful.

Stayed here over Easter with husband and 2 teenage daughters on the 14th floor. Very clean room and plenty of hot water. Great location as only a short walk to Empire State and about 15-20 mins stroll to Times Square. Got breakfast inc. in room rate which was great not having to find somewhere to eat early in the morning. Plenty of Frosties, fruit, croissants, scrambled egg on toast, etc. All good, and the ladies waiting on the tables were lovely, serving huge glasses of OJ. If you are a light sleeper, take ear plugs because the horn blowing goes on at all times. Also, the florists in the road where the hotel is start to set up early in the morning. Looks beautiful when you wake up and look down at all the flowers. The only grumble was with the air con unit. It's under the window sill and is very noisy when it fires up in the middle of the night. Apart from that, it's all you need ... Clean room, hot water, fresh towels every day and a good location and they don't mind looking after your suitcases for a couple of hours after you've checked out. PS: to the Manager ... the windows on the 14th floor could do with a clean :)

Just great as usual! We've just been there for the second time and we just love this place. Nice furniture, amazing view on the Empire State building, excellent situation in Manhattan, very nice and helpful people at the front desk, lively Hall. I you wanna "feel" NY stay there!
I would however not recommend this place for "elderly" people who might neither feel so "comfy" nor at ease there.

I spent 2 nights and really didn't expect anything more than an okay Hilton. I found everything from my arrival to my departure better than I expected. Alex at reception was warm, welcoming, and helpful throughout my stay. I found everyone friendly and helpful, the conceige was better than many 5 star hotels I have stayed at. My room was quiet, clean and the bed was extemely comfotable. The staff was helpful with several special requests. It was quick and easy to navigate to airport terminals and public transpotation into the city. I would stay here again and would reccommend it for a 1 or 2 night stay in Chicago. For an airport hotel I would give it 5 stars.

title_masked: a good hotel in a great location
text_masked: older hotel room. If I was going to be spending more time in the room, I would prefer a more up dated room.

title_masked: Great location and very helpful staff.
text_masked: I stay here when I go to Tiger games because of the convenience. I can just park my car, walk to Comerica Park in about 10 minutes, then walk back after the game to have a fresh start in the morning. The breakfast was excellent and had a lot of variety. The staff was very friendly and nice, and extremely helpful when my sister who was visiting parked her car in a garage nearby that closed earlier than she thought. They were able to find keys to the garage and get her out so she could get home. The room was comfortable and clean, and the valet parking was not exorbitant (only $20 a night, and many hotels charge at least $30 a night, so no reason to grumble). Easy access to I-75 by driving right down Michigan Avenue and taking a few turns around the ballpark to get home, too.

I've stayed at some trendy hotels (Hudson Hotel, NYC; The James Hotel, Chicago, etc.) but rarely have they also been relaxing and comfortable as well. The Blackstone is all that. The first thing I noticed when I got to my room was there was a tv in the mirror in the bathroom. How baller is that? I also noticed that there was no bathtub, just a shower stall, so I called the front desk and asked if they had any rooms with bathtubs because I loves me a bath after a long day. They set me up with a corner room overlooking Michigan Ave., the Buckingham Fountain, and Navy Pier. It's been a delight watching the sun rise and set from my desk.
The only reason I'm not giving this hotel 5 stars is because the hotel's location is not ideal for me. It's a beautiful view, but I prefer staying in River North or Streeterville where there's more movie theaters, stores, and restaurants. This would be ideal for tourist who want to go to Millennium Park, the Art Institute, Shedd Aquarium, Soldier's Field, and the Field Museum.
I was quite pleased for the quality and value though; I booked the hotel about 2 months ahead of time and got a rate of $189.

The staff is very friendly, the hotel is clean, modern and very nice. The room was very large, the bathroom was clean and had great towels. The bar had good food, the pool area was clean and inviting. The trolley was right across the street, we took it around town. We have a student at SDSU and this hotel was close by and near new and modern stores and restaurants.... We will definitely be back.

Had a great time! Hotel is centrally located to all the hot spots downtown! Our room was clean& housekeeping was on top of everything! It took less than 3 minutes to get a bucket of ice! Not bad for a sold out hotel! 
My only complaint was/is the elevator! Way slow! If your there & hotel is all booked-up, give your self a few extra minutes to leave. Or take the stairs as I did! Only happened to me once-but I heard fellow hotel guest complaining that it was an ongoing issue!

Very disappointing for a Ritz-Carlton. It's not a horrible hotel, but for the price, there are many better options. They need to spiff up the place for those who are willing to spend $300/night including parking. Shower in the handicapped room (the only king left when we checked in) was old and broken and caused a large puddle of water to accumulate on the floor. Also, we had to ask three times for shaving cream in the morning, not good since we had to get going for a meeting. The staff was very nice, but we will not stay there again.

title_masked: Clean, quiet but missing a few ammenities
text_masked: A co-worker and I shared a room at the Hyatt for a week while attending a conference at the hotel. Our room was on the 26th floor, so I never experienced any of the noise issues commented on by other reviewers. The hotel staff was very friendly, fitness room was great, but crowded. Don't plan on eating anywhere in the hotel if you're on a budget. There are plenty of restaurants within walking distance for lunch, but this area of town seems to roll up the carpets after 7pm. You can avoid the panhandlers by using the network of tunnels accessible from the hotel. There you will find plenty of food at much more reasonable prices. Our room would have been complete if it had a fan (white noise helps drown out my roommates snores) and a mini fridge. Otherwise it was a pleasant stay.

title_masked: Great Location, One of the Better Hotels in JAX
text_masked:
Jacksonville "proper" is limited in nice hotels, but this is a very nice location and nicer than most Sheratons (SPG property). There's also a little lake behind the property that adds some kind of view from their bar/restaurant.
The restaurant is actually very good. It's kind of a bar/restaurant area. Full bar, tends to get a little noisy at night. The bartenders aren't rude, just not interested. It's really a business hotel, so it closes early. The restaurant food is good - fresh, great waitstaff. American menu. However, note: for breakfast, they have a buffet that's a little pricey - around $16 with tip. You can get a menu and just get eggs, bacon, toast, etc...for a little less $$, but it's not obvious. You also have to fairly aggressively ask for any drink other than coffee or juice. Room service is available, too, which is nice. 
The rooms are really nice: clean, roomy, and we had a view of the lake/pond. I keep looking for gators (there's a sign there that says they could be there), but I have yet to see one other than at the zoo! The rooms also have a great, very large work desk that has all the plugs you need. WiFi signal is very good, too. It was a little noisy as I think they were doing outside repairs, and we were next to the housekeeping room.
There's a heated indoor pool, too. Very clean. Also a nice, small gym with a couple of treadmills and free weights.
In the lobby, there's a great kiosk of large-monitor computers free to use as a guest, with a printer for work/boarding passes, etc...there was never a line to use them, so we actually used them to look up places to visit while there.
Staff is VERY friendly and helpful. Overall, great hotel.

title_masked: dont stay here if you want to use the swimming pool
text_masked:
We booked this hotel specifically because it had a swimming pool. After days of travelling our children (aged 10 and 13) were really looking forward to a swim. We went to the health suite full of expectataion. The water looked dirty - it was cloudy and you could not see the bottom. We tried to convice ourselves it was fine - but as we stood by the side a huge clump of hair with debris sitting on top floated by. My daughter commented that it looked like vomit - and that was it...Absolutely disgusting. None of us could face going in. We complained - but the staff at a hotel this size really didnt seem bothered.
The room was fine. But there are lots of hotels in Seattle with identical standard rooms. But few with pools. Dont stay here if you have any intention of going in the pool or expect a "personal caring" service. Big disappointment. Who would have thought a 4 star hotel would fail so badly on cleanliness. This must also apply to the rooms - in that we found the previous occupants purse down by the side of the bed.

title_masked: Third time was as good as the first two
text_masked: We like this hotel because it feels like home, we always get good service and have never had anything to complain about. We will be back.

The worst hotel I've ever stayed at. I usually laugh at some of the reviews you read, where people book a budget hotel and then write a bad review because it doesn't offer superfluous services/facilities or because the decoration is basic or the furniture outdated. Therefore, I'm a bit sceptical and try to read between the lines. When visiting a city, as I spend all day out and about, I prefer to save money on the hotel and spend it eating out or shopping or on attractions or whatever. Consequently, all I need from the hotel is a clean place to sleep, have a shower and leave my stuff, I'm really not too fussy. 
Before booking the Carter, I read several reviews and thought it would meet the criteria. People are usually more critical and demanding than I am, and despite that, reviews in general were OK. Although the location is great and initially it seems like a good price (it turns out it's actually expensive for what you get), it's not worth it. A terrible pungent smell down the corridor and all the way into the room, which was disgusting. The carpet was filthy, covered with what previous guests had left, definitely hadn't been vacuumed for months, and as if all that wasn't enough, just a few minutes after entering the room we saw a DEAD MOUSE lying on the floor. We left.
I've stayed at many budget hotels in different places and of course they're usually basic, but adequate taking into account what I'd paid. I'd never seen anything like this. If you want to stay somewhere central, you need to pay out a bit more, otherwise you risk ending up at a place that's a public health hazard. If you're on a tight budget, you're better off staying somewhere a bit further away from the centre, as public transport works well and taxis aren't even that expensive.

title_masked: Average. Depends what you are looking for.
text_masked:
This is a hard one to write. If someone had recommended this place to me, I would have wondered what they were smo***, I mean thinking. It really, really depends what you are looking for. New and fancy? NO. Clean and sparkly? NO. Cool and funky? NO. Huge room? Yes. Huge bathroom? Not even close. Good price? Yes. Decor from the 70s? Formica counters? Couch from 1965? Yes.
They are friendly here. The service is very good. The elevators are scary. The carpet is in bad shape. The bathroom floor is 1" mosaic tile. The lighting is not bad. The desk is adequate. The room is HUGE for New York. The area is interesting, and safe, and fairly centrally located. The price is fair.
Hope this helps.

A good central motel, with good size parking spaces. In a really central location, this is really good value, and the rooms are large with plenty of storage space. The hairdryer in the bathroom works well. The room and the property in general was clean. Breakfast was limited to muffins, pastries, juice and coffee, along with some fruit.

title_masked: Good location for food and public transport
text_masked:
The Fisherman's Wharf area is the tourist hot spot of the city. The Sheraton hotel itself is a bit dated on the inside so don't stay here if you are expecting Westin-like quality. I was fortunate enough to get the Presidential Suite twice and that was huge, but the rest of the rooms are very average. The best feature of this hotel is the location. The F-train stop is right outside the hotel and Fisherman's Wharf is a block away. Three blocks away is the famous Buena Vista Cafe which is famous for Irish Coffee. About four blocks away is Ghirardelli Square...chocolate heaven. There is also a cupcake store there that has gluten-free cupcakes. 
There is valet parking here and an option paid garage across the street. This hotel is also across the street from a Safeway grocery store and a block from a Trader Joe's. This hotel is also within walking distance to the awesome North Beach area (Italian District).

title_masked: Great boutique hotel in the heart of Pike's Market
text_masked: This little hotel may be a bit on the expensive side but it's well worth the price for its location, just steps from Pike's Market. It's staff were, without exception, friendly and helpful. The hotel has a large viewing balcony on the fifth floor overlooking the market and Puget Sound. You can bring your own food and drink onto the balcony so even if you opt for a city view room, you can still enjoy the evening sunset view of the bay. Because the hotel in on a hill side, the city rooms do not provide much in the way of a view, as you're mostly just looking at the building across the street, but we didn't mind as the city view rooms were less expensive and we were so tired from walking all day that we basically crashed when we got back to our room each night.

title_masked: Service is lame and they charge for everything
text_masked:
The service is lame, housekeeper tried to come into the room without knocking!!!!!!!!!!!!! I asked for a weight scale, their answer is of course "no, we don't have one" and hung up on me.
Parking is ridiculous expensive, and they even charge me for 5USD for every package sign up.
This is a terrible place and I'll never go there ever again.

I'm just getting back from a weekend stay here... I was VERY disappointed this hotel was very average nothing special what so ever. Valet took forever to bring the car every time, once we ended up catching a cab because we waited over 20 mins... Staff was by far the worst it took 30 min + to get extra towels & wash clothes, the manager on Sat morning was rude and unwilling to help with my problem he needs to step down & be a bellman instead... I felt as though he treated me down because I was there on a discounted rate... To make a long story short I only stayed here because of the discounted rate I usually stay across the street at the Lowes where I get much better service, respect & a much finer room and dinning option... I will never stay at this hotel again if they payed me to...

I stayed for a week in October 2012 for work. I usually stay at the Vitale but prices were crazy this particular week so I found the Galleria Park, which is I believe to be a nicer hotel hotel under the same company. Like someone said, it is a nice hotel with some historic charm. The room I stayed in was very small, but did not lack in any of the basic necessities and it was clean. The bathroom is where you can notice the place is a bit old but it was not dirty or anything. Free coffee/tea in the am and free wine from 530 to 630 which is pretty cool. The location is great, lots of great places to eat and drink within walking distance. The staff is very friendly too. There is a nice little walking courtyard that has some charm. It is for walking, it would probably take 20 laps to do a mile so don't plan on using it for jogging. The fitness room has a couple machines and some weights, the bare minimum. I have a 24 Fitness pass which is on the same block so I didn't need the gym at the hotel, but keep it in mind, very small. The free wi-if was pretty slow.

We stayed for one night before an onward journey to New York having travelled from San Francisco. Check in was quick and efficient and handled by friendly staff. The hotel is perfectly placed for access to the various museums and Soldier Field and is a few paces away from the bus stop for the 'Hop on hop off' trolley bus tour. The hotel is perfectly adequate for a short stay, however I do agree that it may be in need of a little updating to the decor.

Perfect location, amazing views and impeccable customer service. This was our first stay at a Trump property but will definately not be our last. I expected the hotel to be beautiful - and it was, but it is also well executed. It is designed in a thoughtful, utilitarian way that still feels luxurious. From the copper sink in the bar area to the amazing shower next to the soaker tub with amazing views this hotel make you feel like a VIP. The ability to lay on the bed as you gaze at the incredible skylines of SoHo, uptown and downtown while controlling every aspect of your room via remote control is so conveniently modern. The property feels anything but sterile and cold; however, due to the warmth and hospitality of the employees. From the doormen who remember you after the first time to the concierge who can get reservations in a moments notice, everyone is personable and kind.

Our one night stay was a great experience at Yotel! With a good price, good location and cool vibe this hotel exceeded our expectations. Our Queen cabin was clean and comfortable. While small it was nicely designed giving sufficient storage. The bathroom,divided by only glass and curtain, was an unusual design that at times did not allow for the privacy that we might have preferred. None the less it was functional and adequate. Body wash/shampoo was delightful. The slide out bed was quite comfortable and when retracted allowed the small room to have a more spacious feel. Cruise ship designers should make a note of some of Yotel's design elements! A Sunday brunch was in full swing when we arrived and looked like a fun event for a hip young crowd. Altho we stood out as both too old and too square to fit in it was fun to observe the group. The coffee and muffin breakfast the next morning were a nice extra. We will definitely stay here again.

We recently stayed in this hotel for 6 nights. The room was clean and well maintained. All public areas of the hotel, lobby, pool area, etc. were also clean and well maintained. The breakfast was very good, including scrambled eggs and a breakfast meat, usually ham or sausage, as well as toast, cereals, pastries, etc. The food selection was efficiently replenished as necessary, and the area was kept very clean.
Front desk staff were very friendly, and helpful with any questions we had.
We would definitely stay at this hotel again.

This is a very spacious SpringHill Suites with all the usual amenities. Staff were courteous. Very convenient to the airport and would stay here again without hesitation. Breakfast was ample and the usual fare.

A great hotel in Chicago central that is convenient to shopping, restaurants and theaters. The staff was friendly and helpful. Especially nice is the continental breakfast located on each floor; no fighting the crowds for your croissant.

The Central location is great, easy for midtown, shopping and getting to restaurants. The rooms are functional but small and there is little room on the desk to work. The place is a little too cool for a business visitor but run efficiently and rooms are well isolated so you don't hear noises from the street. The bar

Stayed here for a friends wedding so I received a great group rate for a suite. Probably wouldn't have wanted to pay full price for the room but it was a good room for what we paid. We had a wonderful housekeeper during our stay who took great care of our room even though it got pretty messy with friends in and out during our stay. Had great times in the hotel bar. All the staff I encountered were great. Our room was on the club level so we took advantage of the free breakfast and evening drinks.

I travel on business to Washington DC numerous times a year and I found this hotel to be a great value for the location as well as the excellent hospitality from the staff i would definitely recommend. One of the 1st places I check availability on when traveling to DC.

title_masked: Not impressed by the sleep comfort bed.
text_masked:
We checked in and were provided the room of our choice. We found the room to be very quiet, despite its close proximity to the IND airport. The hotel appeared less than half full so a parking spot was of no concern to us. 
I did find some displeasure with the comfort level of the bed and could not get it adjusted to suit me. I woke up with a sore back as a result. 
We awoke the following morning ready for breakfast and realized we were not given the breakfast vouchers we had purchased. We stopped by the front desk and explained the situation and were provided the vouchers with an apology and a smile.
The balance of the stay went without an issue.
Thank you

We stayed Saturday night in Rm 1127 and while the room was very clean and relatively new looking, I was surprised how much of it looked unfinished or not right. The beds had holes cut in the headboards which appeared to be for bedside lights, instead they had table and floor lamps. The table lamp took up all the space on the bedside table, the clock radio took what little other space that was left. The desk where you would normally put your laptop to work also had a lamp on it, and while it did not take all the space up on the desk it did take the only plug available to plug in the laptop. Apparently there was to be a flat screen TV on a wall as evidenced by the wall mount for the TV, instead on the only other flat surface was an old 25 inch CRT style TV and the wiring for it stretched across the wall to it from the wall mount. The place where the old style TV should have been placed was left empty and unfinished. The coffeemaker did not appear to work so i tried to figure out where it was plugged in and realized that the plug was trapped behind the empty TV cabinet and would not reach a power source. Lets see what else. There was not any information provided by the hotel in the room about checkout or anything else for that matter, no paper, pen, nearby restaurants room service etc... Apparently there was supposed to be some form of continental breakfast, but when I came down at 8am there was none that I could see. I asked the concierge about Ellis Island tours and she had no idea and just pointed to the brochure rack for information. I had my laptop and could find that sort of information on it, what I hoped for was knowledge that only a competent concierge could provide. Finally, when I dropped off my room keys I was presented with a second charge receipt to sign. I refused stating that I had already been charged for the room the night before and had checked my account online to see that it had been debited. She tried to convince me that this was something entirely different at which point I mentioned that I had stayed in hotels before and never been asked to sign a receipt twice. She was still insistent, so I mentioned that if they wanted my Trip Advisor review to have even an average rating that she might want to rethink this type of trick. She then grumbled and gave me a copy for my records. Apparently the first floor of the hotel is made up of apartments and when I came back later that evening the front lobby and street was filled with the families that live there, just a little odd. Lastly, as I came out of the bathroom in the morning I saw a cockroach scurry under one of the beds. So check your bags before you bring them into your home, no need to have any other residents moving in.

This hotel has just undergone a complete renovation! New furniture, bathroom with granite and gorgeous tile, new huge flat screen tv, love the colors they used so beachy and cool. The location of this hotel is perfect, my room had an ocean view it's set a short block from the beach. Your are within walking distance of tons of restaurants and shops and the pier. Great staff was so helpful with everything!

title_masked: Good place to stay flying in and out of Philadelphia
text_masked: The price is high sometimes but every once and a while you can get a good deal. The food is very good and the service is good.

I stayed at the hotel for 12 days since I was on holidays to visit a friend. The hotel was very clean and the sheets/towels were changed daily. The room was very comfortable with a very nice bed plus couch and desk so I could work easily. Toilet/shower also was kept very clean.
The fridge and the microwave oven were also incredibly useful for me.
Overall a very good experience.

Great hotel for business around the financial district. Although there is not much to do around the hotel at night you can expect a typical Hilton experience at this hotel, which in my opinion is very good. The rooms face the new towers and water behind which provide an awesome view at any time. Rooms are spacious, clean and very comfortable beds. There is a subway stop right outside the entrance which will take you uptown if needed. Would not rate higher because (a) telephone was out of service in my bedroom and although I reported it, it still did not get fixed and (b) was surprised at the lack of HD channels on the TV for a hotel of this type.

title_masked: This is not a four star hotel
text_masked: Even that I had a pre-paid reservation, the reward for arriving at the hotel at 10:00 pm, was a micro room for my wife and myself, and even that they changed us next day to a regular room, nobody said "sorry for the inconvinience". The other bad notice, it´s their breakfast buffet, make yourself a favor and go somewhere else, instead of paying $25 dlls. for cold food.

title_masked: Not me and, if you dig a modern sensibility, probably not you
text_masked:
Look, my go-to hotel in Chicago is the James. Was this better? No...and let me explain. 
It's more traditional, old school and, um, upper 1%-er. You can tell by the Wall Street Journals lining the crystal chandelier lit hallways in the AM. 
The lobby is awkward. There is no bar or activity in the lobby area. The restaurant/bar are on the second level. The bar, in particular, is small, dark and odd. The rooms are large and nice, but so what? This is my parent's hotel. It's just much too old school traditional for my taste. Back to the my go-to...

I stayed at the Washington Court for four nights for a conference. The hotel website stated that renovations has been completed recently (last couple of years), but it already looked dated. The room was clean, and the bed had very new sheets. It was clear that there had been changes to the room with new tv and furniture. The bathroom was another story. 
The meeting/public bathrooms were not cleaned regularly. It is hard to keep up when several hundred people are using them a day, but there should have been arrangements for that, such as more staff. The front desk staff were very courteous.
The hotel's only restaurant served healthy and tasty food. I didn't try the breakfast buffet, so cannot speak about it. The a la carte menu provided a lot of choices. However, the preparation of a dish changed everyday in size or ingredients, which was a little odd.
The hotel location was convenient to go to sites on Capitol Hill but not convenient for other locales. There are limited choices for restaurants in the area. There are several homeless shelters within a few blocks of the hotel, which made walking around at night feel dangerous. I would not recommend walking at night.
Georgetown was a $15-20 cab ride from the hotel so could become pricey if done often.

title_masked: Needs some updating but still very good option
text_masked:
This is the second time I stayed here and from the first time I visited (2004) it seems they have not updated much. Rooms lack some maintenance on the doors and furniture yet the bathroom is ample and very functional.
Service is great when taking orders and always kind and courteous but sometimes when ordering food, they made their own decisions and change some ingredients on the dishes, nevertheless the quality of the food its outstanding.
Location its unbeatable but they can work on getting a better organization at the motor lobby as sometimes getting on/off transportation had to take place on third row on the street!
Glad to see some celebrities like Federer and Bruce Willis at the lobby. This tells you that it has not loosen its charm at all and I still recommend staying there.

We stayed for a week at this hotel my room was on floor 22 my son's on 4th floor.
Booking in was uneventful and we were treated very well
The Bell boys are amazing and cater for your every need from carrying luggage, storing it, getting a cab etc. My room on the 22nd floor was light and bright, very effective air con and plenty big enough for one or two for that matter. The en suite clean with brilliant shower.
My sons room on the 4th floor had different layout, different air con system but still very nice.
He felt he perhaps picked up a bit more noise being lower down. The maid service was also very friendly. The room was cleaned thoroughly every day My son paid for Wi-Fi which was good.
There is a gift shop attached also accessible from the road as well Here you can book your shuttle, theatre tickets or whatever. The cafe also attached and also accessible from the road is very nice with a typical breakfast menu as well as meals served all day. All of the staff here are pleasant and attentive. We only had breakfast here so cannot comment other than the breakfasts were fine.

title_masked: Great Location, Small Rooms, Good Choice for Starwood Members
text_masked:
I stay here solely because my office is on 125 west 56th street- that's literally across the street, doesnt get any closer than that.
elevators are slow, you'll find that you will need to wait for the elevator at the lobby and when you are trying to come down. i was on the 19th floor. 
Price is not cheap, again I stay here for work, i wouldnt actually pay face value for a personal trip as i found the rooms to be old and small. i dont like how the shower head does not have a removable shower head, the water pressure is low. the cleanliness is great, housekpeeping are very considerate, change soap bars every other day. 
location is a big plus, a block away from 5th avenue and right next to 6/7. 
dont really have much else to say, i feel the hotel is pretty neutral, nothing great, nothing horrible, but at prices north of $350/nt for a basic room, i do expect more.
food is not cheap, room service, etc - eating at norma's is expensive and three is always a wait. 
i like how they have nice 55" led tvs in the room, but the selection of channels is not great, i expected more espn channels, there was only 1.

We booked for 3 nights to enjoy T'giving Parade from balcony and see family. View was great, but heater was so loud that at night, we'd turn it off completely. The breakfast would have been fine had we been only 2 of 100, but the set up was far too tight for hungry hordes--not enough tables, not enough food, jockeying for beverages, underdone bacon, unmonitored food supplies, dirty tables. We felt like rats in ship's hold, fighting for the same crumb, opting out for last morning. Elevator waits were long, followed by sardine-in-can experience. Actual suite was very nice, although all noise on floor lobby was audible. Staff was nice but overwhelmed.

The Boston Park Plaza hotel is an old Boston Landmark. The hotel was opened in 1927 as " The Statler Hotel. " The Statler was a Boston tradition for generations - a large hotel that catered to business & recreation travelers.
Overall - the hotel is great - a real Boston institution with a very rich history.
* Rooms - adaquate - some of the rooms are quite small by today's standards. When making reservations, ask questions about the rooms - especially about the size & amenties.
* The hotel is very well maintained & very clean - no issues what-so-ever.
* The single room that I had on my most recent - April 2012 - visit was very small. The queen sized bed consumed the room. I was on the 7th floor.
* Service - overall very good - typical major urban hotel service. This hotel handles alot of convention & meetings - hotel staff responsive & helpful.
* Restaurants - several excellent restaurants on site. Standard level of service - acceptable.
* Location - perfect - very central & in a very good area, Very close to everything - including the Arlington Street T stop. Boston Public Garden & Back Bay very close by. Newbury Street only a couple of blocks away. Great location for walking around Boston.
Suggestions - do your homework, research the room availablity & sizes. In addition, check out the online sites for special packages - rates vary. There are frequent rate specials.

title_masked: Big rooms in a tired hotel
text_masked:
I was disappointed in this hotel. Start with the lobby. Staff was not unfriendly but not going out of their way to be helpful either. No comfortable place to sit if waiting for someone. 
The room with adjoining living room was large but dingy. Overly draped with curtains that could have used a good vacuuming. Sheets don't tuck in the mattress.... Bathroom very small with not enough room to put items for two people and the same complaint about the closet. 
The service in the restaurant was excellent - too bad I can't say the same about the food. Dinner the first night and one breakfast and never again.

I stayed here last weekend and was totally wow'ed by the hotel overall. My room looked out onto the Riverwalk and had a little patio area with a table and 2 chairs. The people working there were helpful and friendly. Valet was quick, check in was easy and the rooms were beyond compare! Would totally go back in a heartbeat as well as recommend it to all my friends!

We spent our honeymoon on Ink48 hotel. We arrived the 3rd of september 2012 and stayed for 6 nights. 
Actually we didn't use the hotel's facilities very much. But we got everything we hoped for and more. 
We had seen what kind of great views over Manhattan the hotel offers on their website. So prior to our arrival, we wrote the hotel and asked for the highest floor possible with the best view and let them know we were on our honeymoon. When we checked in we were placed on the 15th floor (just beneath the roof top bar) with an amazing view facing the Manhattan skyline.
When we entered our room (1504) there was a card from the concierge with the best wishes and a bottle of Brut and fresh fruit (see the picture). Thank U very much :-)
The room was spacious and had a seperate shower room and a big bath tub in the living room. The bed was very nice and the furniture adequate. There was a big flat screen TV. 
Our room was made spotlessly clean every day. And the staff even came late afternoon to role down curtains, hang our the bathrobes out and make the room comfortable. 
The only negative thing about our hotel room was the fact that it was a little drafty. Standing in front of the front door you can easily feel the draft on your feet from outside the room. Having said that, it didn't bother us, because of the warm weather. But it could annoying at wintertime.
We didn't use the hotel's resteaurant so we can't comment on that. Neither did we use the free wine hour each day, where you can meet with the other travellers over a free glass of wine. 
But we used the roof top bar. Besides the bar it offers amazing views almost 360 degrees. You have a perfect view to the Hudson River and an even more perfect view over midtown Manhattan. 
The hotel is located at the 48th street on the 11th avenue. We used 10 min. to walk to Times Square. The neighbourhood seems a little "desert" for Manhattan. We used the 48th street the first night to get to Times Square. It's a rather dark street. I'm sure it's an ok neighbourhood, but still we chose to use the much bigger 42nd street the rest of the days to get to midtown Manhattan. 
It's not a cheap hotel. But hotel prices in NYC are generally high. 
The day before we left, we asked the reception staff if it was possible to check out an hour later (1 pm.). No problem at all. 
Btw if you come from Newark Airport, it's a rather expensive taxi bill you get since the taxi crosses the stateline to New Jersey. 
You can take the Newark Express bus, which operates between Newark Airport and Port Authority Bus Terminal on the 42nd street. It's 16 dollars a person. You can also take a shuttle bus which 17 dollars a person. We took the shuttle bus when we arrived (it drives you directly to your hotel) and the Airport express bus back to the airport to avoid to much driving around picking other people up before going to the airport. 
We are very satisfied with our stay. The staff conducted very professionally and friendly. We will definately recommend this fine hotel in a great city.
Cheers from Denmark
Camilla & Kim

In September 2012, my wife, 19 year old daughter, and I stayed here 13 nights. On the first night we experienced our first fire alarm ever, which was triggered by a hotel employee. By the 5th day, the linen hadn't been changed - although a card in the hotel indicates that linen will changed every 3rd day. On the 9th day, we returned late in the evening to discover that the room hadn't been cleaned at all. For a total of 13 nights, the linen was changed 3 times - 2 of these were only by our request. In addition, every single day - including the first evening - there was a piece of toilet paper on the bathroom floor, next to the tub. None of the cleaners discovered or removed it - which left us wondering how intense the cleaning actually was performed.
The room was lacking overhead lighting and a full-length mirror - much needed utilities when travelling with 2 women.
Noise from the adjoining room, with kids bouncing off the wall. We could hear toilet noises in the middle of the night from a room from the floor above.
Also on the first evening, someone tried to steal the plates off our rented car. We informed the security guard - who is always parked only near the front entrance; he suggest we report it to the front desk; the front desk attendant seemed totally disinterested.
Best thing about this hotel is the free cookies given out at the front desk - delicious, though surely fattening - but worth every calorie.
The hotel is located near a ghetto-type area. We actually had to purchase gas one evening nearby and saw drugs being dealt from a gas station. We left in a hurry.

The Westin Beale Street is at a fantastic location, right next to the FedEx Forum, and around the corner from all of the bars and music venues on Beale Street. We stayed here for one night on a recent trip that took us through the area. The hotel was well maintained, and our room was clean and comfortable. 
My only complaint was that the parking (at a garage next door if you don't want to use the Valet) was $20/day, which seemed a little steep for self-parking. 
Additionally, the front desk patched through a call to our room at 6am, which was meant for a different guest with the same last name as us, it was very confusing and a little unsettling, as the person on the line was calling from overseas, and didn't seem to understand that we weren't who they were looking for. When I called the front desk to understand what had happened they were not very nice or apologetic about it, and basically said that they just did their job. 
If we went back to Memphis, we'd likely stay here again, although I thought the price was a little high for a mid-week one night stay.

title_masked: Great location, great value, great hotel
text_masked: I loved spending a weekend here in December! Can't beat the location, the hotel is fairly new so everything is still clean and fresh. Check-in was easy, we avoided the $22 valet by parking in the $5 public lot across the street, no big deal at all. The hotel seems very aware of sustainability, however I do wish the showers could be a little hotter! Loved our corner room with a view (much less expensive than other Uptown hotels) with it's mini kitchen, modern decor, flatscreen tv, wifi, comfy bed, and clean bathroom. There was street noise, but not more than any other city hotel. Once of the best features was the complimentary breakfast, which wasn't gourmet, but includes made to order omelets and a variety of other selections - one of the best hotel breakfasts I've had. Would definitely recommend and stay there again (plus it is a clean pet friendly hotel - a rarity!).

This is our third stay at Ink48. The staff is friendly and go out of their way to make sure our stay is perfect. The rooms are comfortable and the vibe is not pretentious. Our dog loved her stay and received a lot of attention from fellow guests as she passed through the lobby.
Excellent nights sleep. Clean room throughout! Plenty of guest towels and they were very soft and fluffy! Room service was EXCELLENT! I will stay again ... hands down!

We stayed here when booked in with our package deal after the cruise from southampton to new york. the hotel is lovely and rooms are big and spacious and kept clean. however as it has many conference rooms it was noisy during the day, but this did not carry on through the night thank goodnes. the only thing missing was tea/coffe making facilities - you either had to go downstairs to the restaurant (which closed at 5.30pm) or call room service. Or alternatively go to one of the many facilities near by.

I have been to San Francisco many times, but never stayed in this area of town. It is very convenient to Union Square and the Financial District, assuming you are lucky to get nice weather. It isn't 5 star luxury pampering/spa, but it is clean, comfortable and conveniently located to many attractions. We also walked through Chinatown, and if that is an area you will be spending a lot of time in, definitely stay in this hotel. The hotel staff was beyond friendly and helpful. They run a very disciplined process from check in, movie rental, maid service, valet and check out. The rooftop deck was an added bonus and the only thing better would have been a pool for the kids. My only complaint was the valet service took 30 minutes each time we asked for the car. They informed me of this when I checked in, but I forgot every time and when we wanted to get out and go, we had to wait.

title_masked: Nice hotel, Updated Rooms, Lacks Central Location
text_masked: This is a great place to stay if you need to be at U Penn. Otherwise, stay somewhere else. Be warned that there may be no one here or there may be noisy students here. Service is very professional and the rooms are nicely updated and comfortable.

This hotel is worth staying at. The employees were always friendly and helpful. Rooms were very clean and updated. The elevator took some getting used to, but after a few days it was a great system.I think all hotels should use this technology.

Went there on business from November 25-27. Found black hair in my bed before even sleeping in it. I am blonde, so definitely not mine. This was followed by hair in the shower. The hotel rooms have absolutely no view. Both windows faced brick walls. The lighting is horrible in the room, so there is no chance of reading a book or anything in bed. The mini-fridge in the room sounds like a vacuum, so I ended up unplugging it. The attached restaurant to the hotel called [NAME] was absolutely horrible. My food was ice cold. (not fun eating cold eggs!) The next day I had a flight to catch...showed up 35 mins early and 40 mins later I still did not have my food. I had to cancel my order and leave. Just overall not a good experience. The front desk was friendly, concierge lady was very nice as well as the bell boys. The hotel rooms and experience were terrible. NEVER AGAIN!!

title_masked: Lovely hotel that is pet friendly!
text_masked:
Just returned from a two night stay at The Liaison. We had a great time. Each staff member is so attentive and strives to give the best possible service. Special kudos go to Pricilla Pack for rectifying a situation in a wonderful way PLUS she always seemed to find us to make sure all was ok. Our pup was so relaxed in the hotel. The 3rd floor is the pet floor. At first I thought it wouldn't be a great flooor after reading all the other posts concerning an upper location. I didn't find this the case at all. Our room was extremely quiet. (except for a few youngsters next door that were having a great vacation!) We heard no street sounds or other noises. The rooftop pool and bar are nice. Yes, it can be a little crowded however, it is mostly families enjoying the pool. Overall, I appreciate their attentiveness to service and their special touches. The place was packed our first night yet we never felt overwhelmed. Our pup was albe to enjoy dinner with us outside and also able to share a few drinks with us in the lobby bar....now..how cool is that!!!
ps- also, we had a wonderful maid. She made sure our room was clean and tidy. KIudos to her!

I can't get past the idea that no matter what you pay for a hotel it should be clean. This one was not. Not the room, not the breakfast room and not the common area near the lobby. Since we had a very early morning flight we had not choice but to stay in our room but I slept in my clothes on top of the bedclothes. I'd forfeit the Internet and breakfast for a clean room. Note that when we complained the manager very quickly came up to the room and offered us a discount since the housekeeping staff was gone fro the day. Bottom line, someone has taken there eye off the cleanliness ball at this hotel. If that matters to you, I'd suggest finding another place near the airport.

We've stayed at the Homewood Suites in downtown Chicago before, this visit being just as pleasant as the first. The rooms are what you'd expect yet very clean. I am suffer from allergies yet have not had any difficulty at this Homewood Suites and how many hotels can you make that claim? A wonderful staff makes this hotel successful along with a terrific location in the loop. We walked or took public transportation everywhere we went. The hotel provides a tasty breakfast and quite a nice dinner along with beer and wine. There is also a fitness center with a great city view and a pool. The only negative is the cost of parking, $42 a night but the hotel makes up for the cost with their amenities.

My daughter and I decided to get away from Orange County to the heart of the Big City. I am a Hilton Honors member, and used my points to pay for the room. When I arrived, I could see that the hotel was a tall, narrow old brick building that had been tastefully renovated.
I had to wheedle the parking structure staff next door because they have a "no motorcyles" rule, but they gave in and found my a quiet dorner of the underground structure to tuck my bike into. They even showed me a "secret" always-open street door, so that I could access my motorcycle easily!
As other reviewers have commented, the doorman and staff were very pleasant and helpful upon my entering the Checkers. I got my key, peeked into the small lounge, and went up to my room number 410.
The room was a bit small, but I like cozy room sizes. There is a nice fridge, large LCD TV, king sized bed, armoire, desk, and ample lighting. I wasn't too worried about the details of the accomodations, as my daughter and I planned to eat out, do the town (on foot), and enjoy the Checker's rooftop pool and spa. By the way, to room was spotless and smelled very fresh.
We ate dinner that night at the Octopus Japanese Restaurant, right across the street from the hotel. It was pricey, but the service was very good and the food excellent.
After dinner, we returned to the Checkers, made drinks, and went up on the roof and jumped in the cool pool and luxuriated as we gazed at the tall buildings surrounding us. We also lazed in the clean spa. We stayed in the rooftop spa about an hour past its closing time, then security showed up and asked us very kindly to come back and enjoy the spa tomorrow. 
Overall, our stay was very nice.

Spent two nights here. It's clean and convenient to the inner harbor. The staff was friendly and helpful. The room was not luxurious, but the bathroom seemed very updated and had a really good shower. The room service was great for breakfast (although I see their restaurant did not get very high reviews from others). I would recommend this for business or a couple wanting to visit the inner harbor for a getaway.

This is my home away from home. Front desk staff is great, especially Tim. He recognizes me when I come in and assures that my every need and desire is met. They always acknowledge my Priority Club status and thank me for my continued support. Bar and restaraunt staff are great too. Best tasting food of any hotel I've stayed at recently. Even do special requests with pleasure. Highly recommend this property for your business or pleasure travels.

make sure you book an executive suite which is a two room suite
separated by french doors...elegant older furnishings...hotel staff
is quite friendly and accomodating.
perfect views of puget sound from upper floors.
nice bar but pricey.
would be nice if they added a fairmont gold club floor at this location.
love the complimentary shoe shine service and free internet for presidents club members

I recently spent one night here for business and it was very nice. Extremely helpful staff, clean well appointed room and excellent location. Would definitely recommend it. Rooms are all easy to access and no playing parking lot roulette to be near the right door.

We arrived as a group of 7 and they were able to have us on the same floor which was perfect. The location is walking distance from Times Square and various other hot spots. Rooms and bathrooms were always spotless. Concierge Desk always helpful. Would stay here again.

The location of this hotel is terrific. Access to the hotel via public transport was easy via the CTA orange train line, and then a bus or a walk for half a mile. We had a contemporary room with a queen bed and I'd recommend this room for a single traveller only. The bathroom is a tiny box, I could touch opposing walls at the simultaneously. There is no exhaust fan in the bathroom, and the 2 tiny glass shelves were already full. You cannot have the bathroom door open and then open the main door, they block each other. The arconditioner, whilst doing a very reasonable job at keeping the heat level down, is old and wall mounted underneath the window blowing air straight up meaning you can't close the blockout blinds because then the cold air blows up behind the curtains! The bed was comfortable, but the sheets felt like they were almost plastic or been starched to death and are strangely noisy when you move around. As for the in room wireless, I tried connecting 4 times and kept being told that my billing address didn't match AVS records, so I was unable to connect via wifi, and the 3G coverage for my iPad 2 on AT&T was thin. The lobby in the hotel is very modern and has 30 minute sessions of free wifi for free for guests. The elevators are fairly slow and I found myself taking the fire stairs once. The furnishings, location and price all amount to a good offering in theory, but I find the size of the room and space let's it down dismally. Perhaps we'll stay here again but in a larger room.

Good location but this is the only plus point. The hotel rooms are very old and the bathroom horrible. One advise : choose an other hotel. For the price you will find a lot better even in the same location.

title_masked: Close to Central Park, the river and the subway to downtown
text_masked: The location was fabulous and felt very safe. Each room has a kitchenette (including a bagel toaster) and there is a supermarket / cafe across the road. We were given a list of restaurants close by and hotel staff were happy to recommend one depending on our mood. There is a coin operated laundry in the hotel. We walked through the Park to the Guggenheim and in the opposite direction to the river where we had great hamburgers at Pier i cafe. The subway is close by and is great value - next time we will buy a weekly ticket. The Peter Woytuk on Broadway sculptures start at the subway station on 72nd and the 'Hens' are in front of the Beacon. We will stay at the Beacon again.

The hotel was very clean and well kept, the staff at the front desk were very helpful. It is easily within walking distance to 5th, Empire state building, broadway, Times square, NY city hop on hop off bus, Intrepid with river cruise, Odditorium, Tassauds and much more. Thankyou for making my stay in New York so easy....

title_masked: Very clean, quiet hotel close to restaurants and shops in Chinatown
text_masked:
My wife and I stayed here for five nights in September 2012. Our room had two huge and very comfortable beds, was very well-appointed with a large flat screen TV, tea and coffee making facilities, a bar fridge and free wifi and had a view of Columbus Park and the new World Trade Centre (within walking distance), and the whole hotel was spotlessly clean. There is a free computer and printer in the lobby, but you have to use it while standing. They give you vouchers for free breakfast a few doors down the street; most of the food there is fried, but you can have fresh fruit instead of the fried stuff. 
We loved the location facing a park in Chinatown, popular for tai chi and board games and also with the homeless people. The area is densely populated but the street is quite narrow and only one-way so there is not much traffic and we got a good night's sleep. There are lots of small grocery shops and restaurants nearby, and it's fun to explore this area with its mostly aged Chinese residents. It's a bit of a time warp, and we had to walk out to Canal Street to buy the New York Times. The subway on Canal Street is 5-10 minutes walk away. There are no taxis passing by, so you have to walk about 100m to the end of the street to hail one.

I booked this hotel based on reviews and nightly rate. The hotel was nice and comfortable and the room was clean and quiet. The free breakfast was average with what most other hotels offer. I stayed for 2 nights and was very impressed.

With a privileged location, between the 5th Avenue and Broadway, is a good option for those who will make tourism. The room is small, but clean and comfortable. Is a simple hotel for a reasonable price.

Very nice outdoor area. Arrived late, but there was some sunlight left and the courtyard was pretty and peaceful. The pool isindoors in its own pool house with outdoor lounge chairs facing the pool. Well kept garden and pots. Many rooms had balcony's overlooking courtyard. I did not notice any noise from airport in the courtyard.
Lobby was modern. There is a business area, booths and a snack bar with wine and beer. It was buzzing with activity. 
Room was fine, typical Courtyard. Staff were great, very friendly. Free internet. Flat screen TV. Granite in bathroom. Free coffee in lobby. The free shuttle to the airport stops at all 3 Marriott properties, so plan accordingly. 
Early am (4 am) I could hear the planes taking off, but a colleague on the same side of building did not hear anything.

My daughter found this boutique hotel on line when I was having trouble getting reservations for hotels in Phila. It was just wonderful. The innkeeper and staff were friendly and accommodating. The rooms & bathrooms are small but tastefully furnished and up-to-date. There was a very satisfying continental breakfast served in a delightful room--with "real" dishes and silverware! We were able to leave our luggage there after check-out and picked it up after our day of activity. There was a parking garage a few blocks away and we received a discounted price there from the hotel. There was a small gym and computers in the basement level. It is well located in the city.--walkable to many places, but cabs were readily available. We would definitely return--& observed that there were many return patrons at the hotel. They offered a AAA discount on the rooms.

Great alternative to pricier hotels downtown. Plentiful breakfast included as well as Mon-Thurs light meal and happy hour.
Suites with kitchen allow for dining in options as well.
Great stay for the week!
Great Italian restaurant next door at the Hotel Monaco.

title_masked: Disappointing, but got what I paid for.
text_masked:
Stayed here for five nights in March 2012. The receptionists were generally nice, but the girl at the bar across the hall (which I believe was run by the adjoining restaurant rather than the hotel) kept making fun of my accent until I told her off (at which point she started crying). I had very little contact with the staff otherwise, and there were no baggage handlers, so I took my own bag to my room (but, as I am British, this was pretty much the norm). My room was positioned as such that I was awoken every morning at 3 O'Clock by refuse collectors and delivery lorries. Bed was not particularly soft (but I had just come from a much more expensive hotel in New York, so this may just be by comparison). That said, I don't remember having much difficulty sleeping (until around 3am, that is). Good choice of television channels, and the free WiFi was a very useful inclusion. Bathroom could have used a lick of paint, but everything was functional. Not overly keen on the location, either; the hotel appears to be literally round the corner (on the same block) as a homeless shelter so the final street of my walk to the hotel occasionally seemed like a gauntlet of loiterers of some kind. Aside from Union Square Park, it wasn't very centrally-located (admittedly, there's not a lot they can do about that). I had previously read good things about the Fish and Farm seafood restaurant located on-site, but being a vegetarian and a lone traveller I didn't really look into it. Most hotels have 'business centres' for internet access; this one did, but instead of computers, they had iPads! Brilliant. Extra points for that.
In all, I would not stay here again, personally. Should you wish to stay here, you may save money, but be prepared to get what you pay for (or not get what you don't). It's not the Ritz, but hey, at least it doesn't pretend to be.

title_masked: excellent room, shuttle did not arrive
text_masked:
After a long 11 hour flight we went to the shuttle pick up spot out side the airport and waited and waited all the other hotels shuttles came and we scrutinised all the signs for the crowne plaza and nothing.So after nearly 45 minutes we had to get a taxi and even after arriving at the hotel people were waiting for the return shuttle to pick them up and we finally saw one and nothing of that colour went past us so don't know what happened that day.
check in was very slow so we eventually got a nice room but it was on the airport side to had quite a bit of aircraft noise, it was a lovely room otherwise and could not fault it, thats why we gave the rating of 4 stars, had to get a taxi next morning as we just could not rely on shuttle after the previous experience
to go to the car rental pick up.We also got a very good price through our agent.

Stayed with my wife and 1 year old. Beds were comfortable. They provided a good crib. There is convenient access to the highways. Room was quiet although i felt that it was on the smaller side. Brunch was included in the room and was adequate but not great They were not able to provide us with a portable fridge the first night but we were able to keep milk in their main fridge and made staff bring it up. They were able to get us a fridge on the second night.

good location, great service, continental b-fast included lots of fresh fruit,bagels, toast, cream cheese, cottage cheese boiled eggs and more. the room was not as nice. we had a 1 bedroom deluxe and had 4 people While it would have been good for 2, for 4 it was a little tight. only 3 chairs and hideabed couch for seating...couch was not up to shell standards. tvs small. non functional radiators didn't look nice.

I found the staff, location, accommodations, and restaurants excellent at the Intercontinental hotel to be top notch.The shuttle rides were extremely valuable and the drivers were extremely polite, helpful, and respectful. I appreciated that.
Caution trying to walk anywhere - like in Vegas you would be taking a great risk of getting run down. If you don't like roundabouts - don't rent a car in Dallas.

I stayed here recently on business, and it was quite disappointing. The room was fine and the price was quite good for Boston, so it may be OK with some travelers. Here are the issues I had with it:
1. Small, cramped bathroom with very little "horizontal space" to lay out shaving materials and toiletries.
2. The door to the room did not latch automatically. It was one of those old style doors where the resident could put a suit to be cleaned inside the door from inside the room, and the staff could collect/return the cleaning by accessing the compartment from the outside. That feature had been disabled, but the heavy, bulky door was awkward and did not shut properly. At least once I returned to the room to find that all I had to do was push to enter. This is definitely not cool.
3. Service in the restaurant/bar area was non-existant. Even after I asked if it was table-service or self-service it was at least 10 minutes before I could place an order, and after waiting 15-20 minutes over my empty plate, I decided not to order a drink refill. It took over 10 minutes (after I finally found someone to ask) before I got the bill. I was sorely tempted to just leave and let them find me.
4. To top it all off, there was no hot water for my shower on the morning of check-out. It seems that "engineering needed to restart the boilers". I have no idea whether this was planned maintenance or emergency response, but the complete lack of helpfulness by the staff was "disappointing". Being told to "wait 30-60 minutes and try again" was also not too helpful, since I had business meetings to attend.
My advice? The price makes this tempting, but be sure you know what you are getting in for.

Great location for a hotel, that can't be denied, however a hotel cannot sell itself purely on that. First impression of the building was fantastic, beautiful art deco features, gorgeous public areas. greeting by reception staff was friendly but unhelpful. Our room wasn't ready despite our arriving at the check in time of 3pm. The man on the desk then told us he couldn't give us an estimated time that it would be ready because if he did and we returned and it still wasn't ready it would give us cause for complaint! We were left in limbo with our hand luggage to wander in the local area and get a drink from a local diner after travelling for 19 hours. An hour later room still not ready, then some confusion as he realised this room wasn't going to be cleaned until late evening, tried to allocate us another room, also not ready, told to wait in reception and he would come to us as soon as ready. Another hour passed, asked another member of reception staff who found a room that was ready and finally gave us this one at 5pm! Room had lovely art deco features, fantastic views but despite a recent refurbishment it was shabby. Tile paint peeling off in the bathroom and an ineffectual shower. Tiny wardobe space and no drink making facillities.
Concierge very unhelpful when enquiring about how to get 911 memorial garden passes, she was more interested to try and sell tickets for a boat trip which included passes than helping us with the enquiry. 2 lovely irish lady guests in the business centre helped us get online and we booked passes within 3 minutes, something the concierge could easily have done or advised where and how we could do this. Stay if you want to gaze out of the window all day. Other hotels are just as central and probably will provide more facillities and better service. Disappointed.

We stayed at the Beverley Hills Crowne Plaza as part of a quick stop over in LA on our way to a wedding. We wanted to go to Universal etc so our agent recommended this as a reasonable location with child friendly facilities. 
When we arrived I was a little taken aback by the location and the outside - it does not really seem close to anywhere and is in a residential area with not many things around. The building itself is a tired 70s style faceless block. We wandered about on the first morning but quickly concurred that we probably needed to get cabs to Santa Monica, Universal etc and the tourist attractions as there did not seem to be much to visit around us. 
The rooms were okay - quite decent sized beds (we had two doubles) and clean and well laid out if a bit tired. The communal areas are similarly a bit past their best. We were tired after travelling and opted for the in house restaurant which was large but virtually empty. The decor is a bit jaded like the rest of the hotel but the food and service were good and the meals reasonably priced. There is an in house Starbucks so reasonable coffee and the breakfasts are also served there - buffet style, plentiful and varied. 
I ordered the in house car service to take us to Universal next day as we had a 10am meeting point for a VIP tour so I did not want to leave it to chance with a taxi. This was a bit of a disaster as they seem to have overbooked the service and so our 9.00am car never appeared and eventually at 9.30am we were asked to join another couple in a minibus! The driver drove like mad to get us to our appointed time of 10am for the VIP tour, but we were still late in getting to the gate etc which was a pain having sorted everything out the night before. The driver also charged us more than we were advised because he was not coming back for us. Perhaps we were just unlucky, but the organisation of the driver service seemed a bit haphazard with lots of people waiting for pre ordered cars whilst taxis were pulling up regularly!
There is a nice outdoor pool which is a welcome respite at the end of a busy day and is a nice extra. 
When I looked at our reservation afterwards, this hotel is at the cheaper end of the others we stayed in whilst in the US and I would say this is reflected in their offer. If you are after a basic 2/3 star hotel for a quick stop off this would probably work for you but I would happily have paid for something a bit more modern and upgraded.

Talk about style, comfort, and absolute value.....Hotel commonwealth was perfect. We(my fiance and I) stayed a couple weeks ago for the weekend and loved it! The location was perfects since we wanted to be able to walk to most attractions and being one block away from Fenway park made even better. As for our room, we had the deluxe suite on the top floor that looked out over the city. It was awesome to have vaulted ceilings in a hotel room...made us feel extra special the whole weekend. Service was absolutely great as well...I forgot a toothbrush and the front desk had one at the door within minutes of my request. Oh and yes, the room even has a doorbell that any of your guests can ring to get you out of the most comfortable bed ive slept in, in a long time! Perfect place for a perfect weekend.

Picked this property because of value (2BD RM 2BT ADA AARP Disc.) but by far the best run desk and housekeeping/maintenance coordination we've seen in a long time. The new Manager (Michael) inherited an excellent staff and property where our expectations were far exceeded.

Okay, so we knew this was a golf course attraction hotel which was fine as this was a business trip for Mr. A. The grounds were lovely when seated in the dining/bar area. Not so much when entering our hotel room. This unit seemed to be neglected since (maybe) it sits so far away from the rest of the hotel. The room itself was clean but that's about it. Seemed rather old school & dull to me ... especially for California standards. Small patio with 2 chairs & a little table and cobwebs. Maybe they don't take much pride in something that they don't have to look at???? 
Dinner was ok. Not great, just average. Our dinner service was great! Yikes, back to the check in service ... she was average (like average for a motel 6) but not for what I thought would be a fancy smancy hotel. 
I would not recommend unless you are a huge golfing fan. This hotel is situated in a housing development with nothing of interest close by. Thank goodness we had family close enough to drive to, otherwise I would have been bored out of my mind staying here for 2 nights.

It was a nice hotel. Comfortable beds and nice showers. The breakfast wasnt great but it was ok. They need to fix the waffle maker. Overall it was a great hotel for the price paid. This hotel wasnt my first choice nor will it ever be but I wouldnt mind staying here again.

Our family stayed at this hotel because the hotel we usually stay at for Labor Day weekend was fully booked. However there was a couple downfalls to this hotel; there was holes in the blankets, not the best internet connection, the TV wouldn't work, and to be able to use the pool you had to buy swim caps. But don't get me wrong the location was amazing as well as the view. The hotel was clean and well serviced. They also are missing on some amenities like toiletries, but exceed in others like a free DVD rental system, free use of bathrobes, free internet, free breakfast, free use of gym, and free use of play station. Overall I would say this is a great hotel!

The hotel is walking distance from the Alamo and the river walk. It is a 15 minute walk through non-scenic parts of San Antonio.
The room was very large and well appointed. The cooling unit was very loud and not very efficient e.g. it runs all the time just to keep the room comfortable.
There is no room safe, and the safe at the front desk is not big enough to store a laptop.
The complimentary breakfast was acceptable.
You will pay for parking although they will not tell you until you see the bill on you last morning. There is limited street parking.

I choose this hotel primarily for its location, I wish I had done more research as I didn't enjoy my stay at this hotel. The entrance and lobby aren't positioned well and certainly aren't as sleek as portrayed on the website. Even though the hotel was kind enough to give me an upgrade to a larger room, the room was small. The heating did not function properly and had a bad odour, a real let down in the dead of winter. I did not enjoy my stay and will not be visiting this establishment again.

title_masked: Nice hotel in a great location
text_masked: I checked into the new Holiday Inn on 31st Street this morning around 10:00 a.m. The hotel is between 5th and 6th Avenues. The front desk staff was very nice and accomodating. The hotel only opened in February 2012. The rooms are still brand new and are well decorated. The 20 story hotel was newly constructed on a vacant lot. There is a subway stop close by. I took it down to Times Square, had dinner at 47th and 8th and then walked back. My room is on the 11th floor and has a great view of the Empire State Building. The room is very quiet. I would recommend this hotel to anyone traveling to NYC for business or pleasure.

Stayed in hotel for a night.
Great service, great room.
Very good location
Food in Blue Tavern just perfect.
Will recommend this hotel
Strongly believe this is best 5 star hotel for you money
Hope to come back soon

title_masked: An Historic Beauty in need of a facelift
text_masked:
Spectaculiar Hotel, amazing Lobby. The duck show was the highlight of our stay, lobby bar is gorgeous as are parts of the hotel. Service was impeccable. Food and cocktails very forgettable. The highlight of the stay was the famous ducks walking through the lobby.
I would suggest visiting if in area for duck show, but never for an overnight stay. We checked out early...that should say enough.

Just perfect, wonderful helpful friendly staff ,very comfortable quiet rooms ,free wi fi , good location for food shopping and tours, all in all one of the nicest hotels I have ever stayed at , would recommend to anyone

This is the third time I have stated at this Embassy Suites in Chicago for New Years. Everything is convenient for a safe and enjoyable stay. Check in was quick, room is immaculate, bedding is wonderful. The safety precautions in place for a big night for a lot of out-of-towners make it a great place for singles as well as families. Extended check-out is greatly appreciated in view of many people being out to the wee hours. Location is great.

My husband, sons, ages 11, 13, 15, and I just returned from a 4 night stay at The Lenox Hotel. We had a fabulous room with 2 queens and a cot, plus a sofa and desk. We were thrilled to be able to be together with plenty of room. Our room was beautiful and extremely comfortable and clean. The staff is very friendly and attentive and the location is fantastic! We walked to the theater district to see Blue Man Group, we walked to Fenway for a game, we walked to the Charles river and the Common. On a rainy day we took the bus to the MIT museum (our least favorite "event"),, which was very convenient. On another day we used the "T", which is also nearby and convenient. Taxis can take only 4 passengers, so that wasn't a travel option for us. Our car was valeted by the Lenox staff for 4 days. We used it twice (to visit Boston College and Tufts) and the staff at The Lenox made it very easy to come and go with our car. My sons were in love with The Lenox from the moment we stepped inside. They were each given little stuffed animals and cookies. They also loved the little chocolates. We loved the morning coffee and bananas in the lobby. There was water in our mini fridge, and no extra charges for these amenities. We look forward to returning!!

title_masked: nice but you need to be rich to eat in the hotel
text_masked: The best aspects of the hotel are its position in new york and the very friendly staff.The room was a little dated but adequate. My main problem was the cost of eating in the hotel.My party consisted of two granparents and two teenage grandchildren.We arrived before the room was ready and had travelled from washington so a meal was in order. We went to the Peacock restaurant which was located just by the lobby.My grandson ordered burger and fries 32 dollars.The real stunner was when we went for breakfast in Oscars. No prices displayed and only buffet breakfast available.The breakfast was good and plenty of choice but no better than the one I had in the Omni shoreham in washington for 23 dollars.The bill came for breakfast in oscars at the waldorf 191 dollars for 4,acost of 44 dollars plus tax.

I recently stayed at the Omni to attend a large business conference. This is a very nice property. Brand new, clean with great amenities. My room on the tenth floor had a great veiw of the downtown skyline. The room was spacious, the bed was comfortable and the bathroom was very nice. I really liked the t.v. that was in the mirror of the bathroom. I've seen those on DIY type shows so this was the first time I have seen it in person. Very cool feature. I managed to get a work out in and the exercise facility was just right. The pool area is quite spectacular with an awesome infinity pool and again, a great view of the skyline. I ate dinner twice at the sports bar located on first floor. Great sports bar with massive HD tv's everywhere. Excellent place to watch sports, have a beer and eat a burger. Food was good but not spectacular. They have two other restraunts on site but I can't comment on them as I did not eat there. Overall, a very good stay and I would recommend this hotel to others.

This is my fourth stay at this same location. Each time I have found the rooms to be exceptionally clean and the linens appear to be new. It's true that the bathrooms are quite small but how much time does anyone really need to spend in there? The beds are very comfortable and I've had a king, a queen and a double all of which were comfy. The only problem I've ever encountered was a non cooling refrigerator and that was just once. I didn't complain as I had no use for it that trip anyway. Now this hotel is located right next to a busy interstate so you are going to hear some road noise but it never prevented me from getting a good nights rest. The breakfast they provide is right in line for the price you pay, muffins, bagels, cold cereal and waffles and I've always taken a muffin to go. They also will provide extra coffee packets for the coffee maker in your room, just ask, they are happy to oblige. There are several well known eateries in close proximity. Honestly you are not going to find a better hotel for the money, believe me I've looked, and I will continue to give them my business. You should too.

We only stayed here for one night, but I actually really liked this hotel! They had a lot of great perks, which we, unfortunately, couldn't enjoy. 
A previous review mentioned that valet was $40 a night; however, when we gave the valet our car, they even suggested the parking lot across the street because it was cheaper. However, we just parked there because it was convenient. We thought it was nice that they suggested this though. Expected the high price being from Chicago. Pretty standard. 
Offered wine tasting, which I thought was neat. Too bad we don't like wine! 
Everyone was SO nice! Forgot toothpaste - no problem because the front desk gave us some for free! Needed our car at 3:40 AM - no problem - ready to go for us. 
The room was small, especially the bathroom; however, I loved the feel of the hotel. Everything was brand new. 
I would stay here again!

Great bang for your buck! Room was very spacious, and the beds were comfortable. Breakfast was limited and the usual fair but enough to get started. The only downside is that they advertise free parking but there are limited spots so if you're later you have to find parking nearby and may end up paying. You can walk to all of the main tourist areas.

title_masked: Nice... But No More Than 3 Stars
text_masked:
When I entered the Fairmont Olympic hotel, my first thought was "wow, this place has some class!"
