On the way to our room, we visited the fitness center, which again was very well kept, well designed and lovely. Unfortunately, that's where the great experience stopped. Our room was musty, and was definately in need of some updates. Carpet seemed old, bedding was torn in places, and wallpaper was stripping. Shower water was normally lukewarm. We were so taken by the exterior and lobby of the hotel- but that was it. 
While this hotel has a lot going for it (GREAT service, good amenities), but we felt like we could have gotten more for our money by staying in a nearby 3/4 star hotel.

We stayed at this hotel looking for a relaxing place....got the complete opposite....1).there is no refrigerator for your things...just a weight sensitive refrigerator you cant touch without getting charged. 2)I had a room for 2 people and each of us drove and the valet would not let me park both cars without a charge and asked me to park in the casino and walk the bridge over when my agreement had stated valet was free. 3) We were going to go to the casino and had taken the bridge from the hotel to get there...at security we had been hand picked to have IDs swiped when many others before us had just had theirs looked at or not even looked at all. my 32 year old friend's ID was damaged unknowingly on the magnetic strip and did not take in the machine and they man denied us entrance to the casino. then when presented with other ID he told my friend no because he was holding up the line. 4) we had tried to get late check out and were told it was not possible until ihad asked on the 5th try at the front desk personally. 5) We wanted to get some things out of our car and were told there was 'no in and out privileges' because the 'big wigs' were in the main entrance. 6) 2 men in suits decided to confront an upset gambler who lost $1000s right in front our room and try and offer him credit for a night but gave us a dirty look and ignored us when we asked them to move somewhere else with this transaction. 7) as we were leaving the hotel my friend had realized he left his work shoes in the room right in front of the sink and called lost and found....left a message and no return call. then he had called again and talked to the manager saying he was going to come back for the shoes and they told him not to come and he would get a call back. finding this unacceptable we went to the hotel to get his shoes back. At the front desk my friend was told he needed to get me because my name was on the room. as i had left the car in the valet area, the valet was yelling at me for leaving my car all the way in a non obstructive area and when i told him i was resolving a quick lost and found issue he told me to park somewhere else. The lady at the front desk then said the shoes were not in the room or in lost in found and she insulted us saying we had them in our luggage after my friend spent and hour searching the car and clearly need these shoes (only having sandals now) for work later that evening. when filling out paper work for lost and found the front desk lady also said if the shoes were found 'we might not be able to release them over the mail for security reasons with out ID at the front desk' even though we live 5 hours away and they are just shoes which were described exactly and the room was noted. This was the most stressful stay we have ever had and upsetting because there was extra time between work for us and we had picked this hotel to relax and enjoy for once instead of a 2-3 star hotel and we were treated worse and left scarred from the visit. my friend is still missing his shoes and we have called every day for 3 days now about these issues and not one person has called us back!

title_masked: Cool Hotel in great area of Chicago
text_masked:
Great location on the river north side of the city. Only had on eproblem with service which was corrected. We arrived in the city for a convention around 930 am and our room wasnt ready(understandably), but the front desk clerk had a bellman check our luggage in and off we went to work. When we returned around 430pm, our room was ready and the bags were up within 5 minutes. 
The room was nice and large for a Chicago hotel. Very nice bar area with sink and fridge. The in-room coffee was not very desirable....hot water kettle and instant coffee( not even Starbucks which this was is good instant coffee). The queen size bed was very soft( we prefer a firmer mattress). The bathroom was nice and modern. Step-in bath/shower combo. The full size shampoo/conditioner/body wash was very nice! The entire hotel was very clean.
The service issue I spoke of earlier in the review was a call I out in for some ice to be delivered. hey dont have ice machines- delivery or at turn down service only. Waited 40 minutes and never received the ice. After calling downstairs again, the ice was delivered within 5 minutes by what looked like a chef.
Loved the art around the hotel-including outside our window on the opposite wall. Still wonder if and what was on our side of the bldg.
Excellent doorman service, housekeeping and front desk clerks.
Would stay here again if I got the same priceline deal.

Great location just a few blocks from Michigan Avenue, and a couple more blocks to a subway station. Staff was very friendly and helpful. The only issue we had was with our television in our room but the staff found a solution to fix it quickly. Will look at this hotel the next time I stay in Chicago

Great hotel, easy walking distance to many restaurants and has a great workout facility. The concierge is amazing. Rosie will take care you, always has a smile, and welcomes you in. All the staff in the concierge and front desk are great. Excellent hotel, I spend over 40 nights/year here, and won't stay anywhere else when I am in the area.

Just had a fantastic but brief stay at the Smyth Tribeca after running the NYC Half Marathon over the w/end. Sebastian, the Desk Manager assisted with an early check-in after the race & gave us a complimentary upgrade to a room with a tub to soak my weary bones, which was very much appreciated. The room was spacious & very nicely appointed with Kiehls amenities in the bathroom. The bed was very comfortable & was complimented by high quality linens, so we slept very soundly. Overall a great downtown hotel!

Stayed there with my wife this July, and loved the experience, but invest time trying to get a decent rate. It is a small hotel, with not much of a lobby at all, but rooms are quite nice, and importantly, quiet. This is to be appreciated,a s NY is a noisy and crowded place, and you need your quiet time sometimes.
Breakfast is of superior quality ingredients, but I would not consider it especially tasty. Choices are more in the healthy side.
Very friendly service at check in, concierge and breakfast room; great location on Fifth Avenue. 
The Peninsula will never disappoint you, just try to get a good deal.

title_masked: Perfect location and very nice bar
text_masked: Wonderful location and nice big rooms. The bar is excellent, I highly recommend their cocktails! Only a negative thing: short dark hairs in the bathroom, I have long blonde hair so not quite mine : (

Next door was a major construction site, but regardless, the Hampton Inn Madison SG offers a good location, clean rooms and bathrooms and friendly service. Nothing exceptional, but equally nothing worth complaining about. Would gladly stay there again.

The entire staff was very friendly and extremely accommodating to our group. Everyone we encountered went out of their way to make our stay comfortable and enjoyable from check-in to the gift shop, to the amazing sous chef and serving staff. Would definitely stay again!

title_masked: Older hotel, good location, rooms a little cramped, internet connection sketchy
text_masked: Stayed at the Omni while in Boston for a seminar/training course being held at the hotel. The common areas of the hotel are impressive and give you a feeling of what the hotel must have been like at the turn of the 20th Century. The staff was friendly and helpful even though the hotel was incredibly busy during my stay. My room was nice and well appointed, and the bed was very comfortable. My only two negative comments come from the size of the bathroom (tiny) and the wireless internet connection. Being away from the office for the week meant that I was trying to check-in occasionally via my laptop. However, the wifi in the hotel was horrible. Between the computer and my phone I was never sure if I would get a connection, or whether I would have to restart them to get them to connect. Additionally, the cell reception while in the lower levels of the hotel was horrible. Not something the Omni can really change, just be aware of it.

This hotel was a great experience! The staff was super friendly, especially at the front desk! Nick (i think that was his name) helped us find some great dinning options and became our go to person during the 2 days at the hotel. I would not think twice about staying at this hotel again!! We even had a gold fish in our room and played Wii in the lobby!!
Pay for the upgraded room! its worth it!!!

The staff is very good and sweet while still being very professional. breakast huge and super delicious. old style luxury but i found bit heavy in style for new york and some placees needs better maintnance e.g. wallpaper peeling, humidity on the bathroom wall etc. 
The bed was queen size and very confortable.

I turned to this hotel due to an online article by Huffington Post titled "In Search for NYC's best boutique hotel". Then I read reviews on multiple sites and compared. Here's my assessment: this is not a luxury hotel nor will you find cavernous rooms with wasted space. I think it is appropriately labelled boutique, but it's not a Kimpton. Hallways are narrow. My room was impeccably clean, most of the floor is clear of carpet. Decor is unique with clean, simple lines (think IKEA) but the furniture was solid. Bed was very comfortable. We were out in a flash. The air conditioning is a window unit, with which we had no issues. I was on 11 th floor and we could hear distant street noise. I've never stayed in NY hotel where you couldn't hear some street noise. Even at 18 th floor of Hilton you can hear the garbage collection, so bring your earplugs if any noise is an issue. I thought we were the only ones on the floor. It was that quiet. If you want space to walk around the room, make sure you book a larger room (like Madison King). Location, wow, cannot be beat! Staff, helpful and friendly. Drop your bag off before check in and after check out to continue enjoying NY. Value for the $$, A plus! I'll be back!!

Excellent facilty, easy access to transport, shops , wonderful staff that go out of their way to help in anyway possible. Very clean. Excellent ***** breakfast provided. Shuttle service provided by Jeff on application. Generally fantastic place to stay.

I have stayed frequently at the Hilton at Logan which is perfect for catching an early flight out. The hotel is clean and contemporary. The rooms and bathroom are small but work well. The health club and small indoor pool is nice except the steam room and sauna are now closed (not ADA I was told). This is unfortunate as this was a great part of the stay in the past. We had dinner at the hotel and the food was surprisingly good; however it was expensive and the portion small. Parking at the hotel is expensive so we usually drop our rental car off prior to checking in. There are some very good inexpensive Italian restaurants (Spinelli’s for takeout, Javelli) in East Boston which is nearby. The hotel is convenient and clean, however not really that near Boston itself – so if Boston is the focus of your trip stay in the city.

Here's the thing with the Balwdin, you are in San Francisco to have fun and soak in a fantastic city. You aren't here to relax and have some "me" time. If you want that, to go Napa. The Baldwin seems to run with this attitude in mind: you probably won't spend too much time in your hotel, all you really need is a place to sleep.
The rooms and the lobby are wee and a little outdated. Rumor has it they are fixing it. The heating system was a little fiddly but my other half and I managed to figure out how to control the temperature. The bathtub is tiny but we shower anyways. The lack of hair dryer was a little concerning at first, but I just embraced my inner Chakka Kahn and rolled with it.
It's close to the main gates in Chinatown and a boatload of shopping. The view from the room was neat and I felt safe the entire time I was there. The only thing that woke me up was the world's noisiest trash truck at about 5:30 one morning, but I nodded back off. It was close to the Bay to Breakers starting line which is what we wanted, so it worked out just fine. The staff was friendly and helpful.
I think I'd stay here again, but there are other areas in the city that might pique my interest more due to not spending enough time there this time around. If I don't stay here, it's not because I don't like it.

This hotel has become a second home for us- because the staff is amazing. We have been here several times as a couple, and before we were a couple. The hotel greets us by name, the room is ready and- given we have a 2 year old - is ready for him. How the entire staff knows our name, and our son's name is genius. The lobby is beautiful, great flowers, but not overstated. The bar has an amazing house red Zinfandel, and has a patio to enjoy a cigar. The restaurant is classic Italian, and Sunday brunch makes you feel as if you are sinning. The rooms are comfortable, quiet, and connected.

We love the location of this hotel. It is near everything, but far enough away to not be overwhelmed with the craziness. Domenic at the Concierge desk was fantastic helping us with reservations and solving a problem we had with a local gift shop. We highly recommend staying here.

3 Australian travellers shared a 2 room suite. The beds were very comfortable, made up with crisp, clean linen. The sofa bed was also very comfortable. The kitchenette was well supplied with glasses, crockery etc. and included a fridge and microwave. The bathroom is small but adequate and clean. We had a fantastic view looking onto Times Square. The location is wonderful, subway and train station across the street. All the staff we dealt with were helpful and courteous, Maureen at the tourist desk was particularly helpful and always cheerful. PS we also got free Wifi for the week of our stay. Super!
Just back from a weeks stay in this hotel and cannot fault the place! The room was excellent (a 2 queen bed room), staff were very helpful and courteous and the location is brilliant.

I had a groupon for the hotel. It's an old hotel, which isn't a bad thing, but there's just stuff to get used to..small bathroom, few outlets, small elevator, room doesn't have a coffee maker. It's in a good location. It's a fine hotel. They offer coffee & tea service in the morning. The staff was very accommodating.

When we checked in and went to our room the bellman noticed the toilet was running and arranged for a new room at his suggestion ie we did not have to complain......the bellman suggested it upon his inspection. I am in the retail business for many tears and know how important such behavior by a employee can be to the "can do" immage of the company they represent at their point of contact with the customer who in this case was me. I have found that lactions like the bellman's can make a huge difference to the customer.

title_masked: Accomodating and close to some good restaurants
text_masked:
The Hotel was very warm and charming inside. Not a lot of front desk staff but the ones who were there hustled and bustled to get things done. One of the doorman didn't seem very helpful when I asked him about a local restaurant, and I couldn't find the concierge, but the front desk staff stepped right in and helped me get set in the right direction.
Rooms are comfortable, clean and very contemporary feeling. I'd recommend a room facing the street and not the facing the interior enclosed "pit". 
Area surrounding the hotel was busy with construction, but I never once was disturbed by noise. Other than that the neighborhood is very safe and relatively quiet.
Ideal convenient place to stay if you are attending something at The Convention Center.

title_masked: Good alternative for the Philly airport
text_masked: The rooms were clean and quiet, however the mattress is soft and the pillows were uncomfortable. You can see signs of wear and tear with chipped tiles and cracks in the fiberglass shower. The hotel is located in front of a Ruby Tuesday and very convenient. The staff was friendly on check in. The breakfast was included and offered the normal fare with make your own waffles, etc.

I booked a pretty good deal with my Starwood points. They let us check in early and check out late, really making the most of our quick 2 night trip. Room was very comfortable with a great view. Front desk was pleasant and the complimentary Acura ride service was extremely handy and helped us save money on cabs. Location has easy access to all forms of public transportation. We took the BART to and from SFO and bought a 3-day MUNI pass to get around the city. Plenty of buses/streetcars to catch all within walking distance of this property. 4 stars for having overpriced, not included WIFI.

My family and I stayed here during a TCU football game. We are Hilton Gold members and picked this hotel because they had one of the very best reservation agents ever - Kate - who was able to reserve us connecting rooms (King to two doubles). When traveling with kids, having connecting rooms can make or break a trip. Kate went above and beyond during the reservation process and not only remembered us at check-in but confirmed that everything she promised was delivered. I give her an A+! The hotel is in a great location downtown (a 10 minute drive to TCU) and one block from our favorite restaurant in Ft. Worth, Grace. The lobby is very impressive. The rooms were recently updated but showed signs of what used to be.

We stayed at this hotel on May 18-20th for our daughter's graduation at UT. It's just a few miles from downtown, but there are restaurants and lots of shopping around it. just off the highway and convenient to all areas. We liked the suite. The hotel is dated but many areas have been refurbished and all looks clean and nice. The suites are comfortable, and include a kitchen with all the utensils you need. We were 3 in the room and it wasn't crowded. Our friends and family stayed there as well and we were told that their rooms had a different layout and were not as nice, however clean. I loved being nestled among greenery and trees. Staff was very helpful, and the included breakfast had a variety. This hotel also serves appetizers in the evening during the week, along with beer and wine. In all, I was pleased with this property. We paid a very good rate as well. Something like $115.00 for the suite. I recommend it.

I'm not a particularly hard sleeper, and I never heard any trains, though I did notice the ear plugs on the nightstand and thought that was odd. Like most Hampton Inns, the accommodations were comfortable and clean but nothing special. I didn't feel that the service here was particularly great. No one was rude, but they didn't go above and beyond either. The "gym" had 1 elliptical-type machine, 1 kind of scary treadmill, and 1 recumbent bike. I'm 5'3" and thought I might hit my head on the ceiling while I was on the treadmill.

This hotel is not bad for its location - the very noisy times sq does successfully get blocked out once inside and the rooms are surprisingly normal (ie not typically small ny size) which is a positive. Check in etc efficient and the hotel is clearly a Hilton - ie it runs like an average to good hotel should. Other than that it's all pretty much as you would expect for the chain. The reception entrance is a rather gloomy kind of lower level thing and the wine at the bar is not to write home about but for a business trip and a need to be downtown central, it's fine. If you are looking for anything special, there are of course far better places .

The entire experience enhanced our vacation. There is plenty of parking, checking in was easy, our request for a high floor room was met, our room had plenty of space to spread out in, and we love the layout of the Embassy Suites how you have 2 TVS and the bedroom seperated with a door. Bathroom was rather large, maid service was excellent, and front desk staff was helpful. 
My husband loved using the desk table for his laptop and the entire family loved the pool and the hot tub. All areas of this hotel were very clean, including the pool area.
Breakfast and the snacks offered in the evening was average-nothing special, but certainly acceptable. My only complaint was, there was no coffee out unless you purchased from the Starbucks shop in the lobby.

I spent four nights here while attending a conference at the convention center. The hotel has a nice lobby, bar, and gift shop. I had a king room and it was a comfortable size. Decor was updated and tastefully done. I stayed in from 540 and it was a LLOOOONNNGGG walk from the elevator. Wifi was an extra cost, but free in the lobby.

My husband, 4 children and myself stayed here 1 night before our trip to Michigan. This hotel was perfect. It accomodated all 6 of us nicely (2 queen beds and a queen pull out coach, and very spacious eating area), the price was very reasonable, it was close to everything we wanted to see, and the staff was EXTREMLY NICE! We had no problem at all with noise from the nearby firehouse as others have stated. We did not hear any sirens at all in the middle of the night. The hotel was very clean and the room looked brand new. The beds were very nice. We will be back here the next time we are in Chicago!

I thought the Intercontinental New Orleans was bad but thi s one is worst.
It is old , tired and dirty ..
I am an ambassador Platinum member with Intercontinental and our suite was so dirty it was unbelievable .
Save your money and stay under a bridge it is cleaner

title_masked: Excellent location, excellent staff, excellent ammenities
text_masked: We needed a place near the northwest side of the city for a medical conference at a hospital and wanted to make a family weekend trip out of it. The beds were a bit firm for my preference, but that truly is my only negative comment and it really is a personal preference. The pool and pool area were excellent...the kids loved the indoor pool.We spend hours in there! And dried off outside by the fireplace on the patio. We love having a full kitchen even though we did not use it to the fullest potential, but having the cabinet space is GREAT with a family! Breakfast buffet is amazing! Never had so many choices for breakfast and the Texas shaped waffles were a hoot for the kids! The hot items changed each morning we were there, so plenty of options. The locaion is amazing being so close to the mall, shopping, restaurants, entertainment and the area felt secure. The staff was super friendly, very accomodating no matter the circumstances or request.

I'm currently living here with my long time boyfriend, he attends Tulsa Welding school. It is awful. While there are a handful of roudy boys here from the school we are not included in that, we stay in our room, aren't loud, never disrespectful. Apparently I'm not allowed out past 9, I can't even go smoke a cigarette outside (They complain when we smoke in our rooms, even though we have a smoking room) Often times I don't even get off work until after 9, say I wanted to grill some chicken? Nope. Not allowed. Stay in your room. They threatened to call the cops if I didn't put out my cigarette and go inside, now I understand that they have to keep the place safe but I was just smoking a cigarette. What the hell? Most of the tenets here are Tulsa students, which is where their income comes from, they don't do anything for us, they don't clean our rooms, they don't give us towels or toilet paper, and that's fine, but when I pay 600+ a month for rent I expect not to be treated like I'm 15. I do not reccomend this hotel/motel for anyone. I haven't seen hookers, to my knowledge there hasn't been terrible fights, not since I've been here at least. So why are they being so terrible?

title_masked: Service was great but hotel was extremely noisy & very poor internet service. Walls very thin. Heard every step & flush.
text_masked:
Hotel was very neat, clean & great service but, in dire need of upgrade in insulation. Very noisy, heard every flush, steps & words from other guests in other rooms. If you are a light sleeper & in need of rest this is not the hotel for you. Front desk suggested booking a room on the 3rd floor so as not to have people above you. 
Don't buy the internet service don't work 50% of the time.
Beautiful grounds & great service.

I just checked out of this hotel -had two rooms for two nights- and I can't say enough about how nicely we were treated. Malia checked us in and was so accomodating on room types and making sure we had everything we needed. We were tired and ordered room service. The order came up to our room and it was perfect! The next morning, I met Sharby in the dining room for breakfast. She was great! The made to order omelet station and fresh fruit on the buffet is very good. The second night we slept fantastic and were happy that the room had great a/c since it was hot outside. This is wonderful location for shopping, close to I-25 and everything that you might need.

According to the hotel.. they say it's a 4-star hotel.
Maybe it's because it's NYC but it's a 3-Star at the most.
The room was tiny which is okay to me.. but interior lacked. 
Great location though.
Staff was friendly enough.
However I didn't like the housekeeping.. there were long hairs on bathroom floors not just a few.

If there was a way to rate 3.5 I would. The hotel has a nicely renovated lobby with the lounge theme found elsewhere, nice cafe area, self service computers and free coffee (breakfast is not included). It does not appear that the renovations have continued upstairs to the rooms. My room was nice, but had a dated appearance. The hallways have that DC Federalist style with wallpapers, carpets, generally nice but a bit worn. Staff was doing touch-ups while I was there - like repainting the trim around the elevator doors. The room was very small and had good furniture but the mattress was very old and soft, it hurt my back. The bathroom is tiny and with a pedestal sink so there is no counter space. The closet was tiny and there was really no place for me to place my rolling suitcase in a flat position to pack/unpack. The door to my room did not close tightly, wide enough gap to allow bright light to shine in all night - it also meant I could hear all the commotion in the hallway, screaming child running around until midnight everyday (I think my parents always had me in bed hours earlier, even when on Holiday...) An update on the wifi - it appears to be complete throughout the hotel and works well in rooms and common areas. The staff is very friendly and seemed eager to please. I think they are trying to make the best of their situation. Overall this hotel is mostly good, I just hope the guest rooms get an update like you find in newer Courtyards, this place could be real gem in the Courtyard family. There is parking on site for $29/night, which is typical of DC prices. On-street parking is available in the neighborhood but the regulations are tough - 2 hour limits until 8:30pm and then starting again at 6:30am.

Just back from family holiday, stayed 4 nights in Marriott in San Francisco, Long line at check in desk when we arrived, but moved very quickly, check instaff very friendly.
Room was spotless , cleaned daily & plenty of fresh towels every day.
Hotel very central to alot of big name shops such as maceys, Barnabys etc.Well worth visit to Visitors dept to get your dicount voucher in macys.
Would recommend Mels Drive In for breakfast, only 5 mins walk from hotel.
Would recommend this busy hotel to family & friends

We enjoyed three nights at the hotel. The staff, food and location are excelllent. We took a 10 minute water taxi ride from the airport directily to the hotel that provided fantastic views of the Boston skyline. Our room had a beautiful view of the harbor. The restaurant recommedations we received from the concierge were excellent. All of the staff were very friendly and gave us welcome suggestions for the best way to travel to the places we wanted to visit (JFK Museum, Newbury St., North end, etc.). Because of the downtown location, a car was not necessary.

I stayed here for a meeting at the Moscone Center, so the location was great...only a 5-10 minute walk away. Check-in was quick, and even though I arrived at noon, my room was ready. My bag was in my room 5 minutes after I was...very quick bell service. The exercise facility is certainly adequate, though not glamorous, and is open 24/7. The wireless service was extremely slow. When I checked in, the clerk noted that even though the rooms state that there is a charge for wireless, I would not be billed. It was a good thing...slower than dial up, and I ended up using my phone tether over 3G, which was faster. The rooms are clean and simple, bathrooms the same. The restaurant service was excellent, though food not really a value. The "Grab and Go" breakfast of bagels, yogurt, coffee, fruit, etc. was a good idea, but it ought to start earlier than 6:30.

Loved our stay at the Marriott Marquis. Big hotel so busy but rooms clean and comfortable and location terrific. Very close to transport (BART, Muni, cable cars) and easy walking distance with our two small kids to MOMA, Yerba Buena Gardens (and playground), shopping, Chinatown etc. Super-easy transport to Exploratorium, Cal Academy and wharf areas. The kids loved the hotel lifts and swimming pool. We liked the nearby shopping and many places open for breakfast super-early (hotel breakfast starts at 6.30am, Mel's Diner and Denny's around the corner even earlier). Gym also looked good and has some spa treatments available. Window opposite carousel at Yerba Buena has great kids snack options for reasonable prices. Would also recommend Sushi Rocks for dinner.

This hotel has a very convenient location if you are doing the "tourist thing" in NYC. It is near Times Square, the Empire State building, and close to the subway. It is very clean, and the rooms are modern. They are small, but most NYC rooms are. They have granite in the bathroom, and actually have a tub in addition to a shower. They have a full breakfast buffet every morning with hot and cold dishes, which saves a lot of money. The staff was very helpful, with some great suggestions for us. I highly recommend this hotel as a very nice choice when traveling on a budget. They even gave us ear plugs in case we were sensitive to city noise.

As anyone knows driving in Ny is no easy task! Trying to find the hotel you're looking for that doesn't have a sign or a bellman outside is a challenge you don't need! The room itself was fine however our main complaint was the noise in the middle of the night. The walls are paper thin and our neigbors woke us @ 1:30 am. We were not able to fall back to sleep which left us very tired for the next day. While management asked them to quiet down, the damage was done and the hotel did nothing to compensate us. Addtitionally, they left out cookies on a plate which weren't wrapped or covered. I find that to be unsanitary. There also was no blow dryer which I believe is a staple in most hotels. The location was not great. Definitely off the beaten path.

My husband and I live in the Chicago suburbs. We needed a quick one night get away to feel like cool 20 somethings we are and not the tired old 20 somethings we felt like after dealing with a teething two year old for a week. 
PUBLIC is very cool. It's an Ian Schraeger hotel (Delano, Mondrian, etc) so it trendy and the decor is amazing. The lobby very chic, all nuetral colors with a very cool vibe. The service was great. Everyone is very friendly. However being an older hotel, the bathrooms are SMALL. This hotel is the old Ambassador East, a very famous place in the 30's and 40's. The location is very unique, not a lot of hotels in the area. So if you are looking to get away from the tourist on Mich Ave, this is perfect. It's in a great neighborhood, surrounded by the old money of Astor and Lake Shore.
We had drinks at the Pump Room. Loved the people watching. The bar itself is very cool, it's illuminated beautifully. Seemed to be a really popular place to be. 
The only complaint I have is the people above seemed to jumping around or moving furniture at 7:00am. Which totally isnt the hotels fault, but annoying when it's your one morning in 2 years to sleep in. Minus that, would defintely go back.

title_masked: Great service, mixed review on room
text_masked: Staff were very friendly, and the room was clean. The room, however had stained carpet, and the curtains were tattered and and holes in it. (I also found the art work didn't match the contemporary furniture, but thats just my opinion.) While I'm sure that my room wasn't typical, all rooms should meet the same high standard associated with the Hilton brand, and I couldn't recommend it to anyone expecting a consistent high level of quality.

I went on a business trip to Washington, DC a couple of months ago. Initially I had hard time finding suitable accommodation (due to a short notice). All hotels with free Wi-fi and close proximity to Crystal City were extremely expensive. I decided to look for alternative options for corporate housing and found Executive Apartments. Their website looked a bit outdated and it put me off a bit; however, once the booking was made online and I stayed in a fully furnished corporate apartment (I've never rented a short stay apartment before), I must admit that the quality of service was stellar! I was so pleased with my stay that I actually decided to leave a review here. Thank you!

We just stayed at the Indianapolis Marriott North this weekend for a wedding. Our room was on the 8th floor, had a room with 2 double beds, and looked north over the suburban area. The room and bathroom had more space than a typical hotel room and had plenty of room for the four of us and our luggage. The beds and pillows were comfortable. We paid $10 per day extra to have Internet access but this included all the devices used in our room and was worth the add-on for us. The hotel had a pool and exercise room but we did not have time to use those. The hotel lobby was attractive and all the staff we encountered was accommodating, friendly, and appeared happy to assist when asked. We did not have to wait more than a second or two for an elevator and it quickly transported us to and from. The wedding reception we attended was held at the Marriott. The ballroom looked great and the serving staff did a wonderful job getting food in and out without interfering with the festivities taking place. They were quick and efficient when drink requests were made and it made for a great evening. We enjoyed our weekend and would definitely stay there again if we were in that area.

I loved the location and the hotel. The service was terrific. The only thing I did not like too much was the food at the main restaurant. I would definitely recommend this resort if you are in Austin.

The location is what makes this location such a terrific spot to stay for a visit to San Fran. We found wonderful pricing on line for a last minute get away. The hotel is located right at the cable car stop and about 1 block from the local tram and busline too. You can buy a transporation pass for all three modes about 1 block from the doors of the hotel. Great shopping and dining in the area. The hotel offers a model continental breakfast of coffee, juice and pastry - enough to get you up and running in the morning. Apparently they also offer a complimentary wine reception Monday through Thursday. Sadly, we were there outside of those days so missed out but I'm sure it's a nice treat. Rooms are modest, smaller but comfortable. Service a the front desk was very friendly and prompt. They do offer valet parking for around $33 per evening if you have a car.

title_masked: Good location but could use some updating.
text_masked:
We had a decent stay at the Bedford. The location is very good and the staff was nice. The rooms are very plain and very dated. We had a suite. The twin beds in the bedroom were very hard and uncomfortable. There were three full size pull out sofa beds in the living room. So, you could sleep quite a few people if you wanted to. There was a little kitchenette that had a small fridge and stove top with a coffee maker and tea kettle, plates and silverware. The bathroom was small but it was updated and there was plenty of hot water. 
I'm not sure if I would stay there again but it worked for us for this trip, it just wasn't very comfortable.

stayed here for a couple of days at a legislative conference. The hotel is massive and can accomodate as large of a event as you need. $305 a night for a weekday was a little much to me. Flat screens in room, spacious bathroom, but in the end, it was basic. air did not work very well in room at all. Hot

We stayed at this hotel because my husband was attending a conference here which made it very convenient for him. After reading the reviews I wasn't sure what to expect. I called ahead and requested an early check in which didn't seem to be a problem. We got to the hotel around 1:30 and checked right in.....that was nice since check in is 4pm. 
The room was ok but every thing looked old and worn. The bathroom was clean but again was worn. The bed was ok to sleep on. I always check for bed bugs and was surprised when I looked at the mattress and it was a pillowtop which looked fairly new......there were no signs of bed bugs. There was only one additional pillow in the room and we could have used another one. The next morning my husband saw the maid in the hallway and asked for another pillow.....we never got it! 
There was NO coffee maker in the room! This is one of the reasons I am giving them a 3 star rating. We also didn't get much sleep. The hotel was very noisy! People slamming doors all night long and even though we were on the 42nd floor you could still hear the traffice from the street. 
I had breakfast at the hotel restaurant....it was good but very pricy! I found the concierge to be very friendly and helpful. She gave me a map and a lot of pointers for the places I wanted to go while my husband was at his conference. 
Since this is right in Times Square it is very conveniently located. You can get to any major place from here whether you walk or ride.
Check out was very smooth and we left our suitcases with the bellman for the day which he put in the back room and not off to the side like some of the reviews I read. 
I can't complain too much because we only paid $159 per night which is very cheap for NYC. If you can't get a good rate then I would suggest staying somewhere else. I think this was a nice hotel at one point but definitely needs major updating to be the 4 star hotel it claims.

Days Inn??? Who woulda thunk it...I was so sceptical that before I would stay I wanted to see the rooms....The brown hallways did little to boost my confidence but the newly renovated rooms left me with no questions...The rooms are California yellow, marble bathrooms and brandnew everything throughout the room...there was no question but to check-in....Once the door was shut it was a private bit of heaven, so much so, I tried to change my flight to stay a few more days....The room was clean, quiet and just had a great feel...The Days Inn??? Yep....OK..its not downtown D.C. but for the price (anything $100 or less) the neighborhood has whatever you need including a great Italian Restaurant attached that does room service....imagine that ......When you want to go downtown its a bus or cab ride in short order...in the meantime, there's a Starbucks, CVS, 7-Eleven and a Bruger King in stone's throw....Oh yea if you've got a car..its free parking...no where in the D.C. area is there free parking..In fact no where in the Tri-State area of D.C. is there free parking except outside the beltway oh...and the Marriott at Pookshill...for my money the Days Inn is way better than that particular Marriott....As for the pics submitted by others, the first room pics I saw were spot on but the entry way was not exactly as is showing... the tiny gift shop is not all that but the CVS and Walgreen's has all you might need or want in that respect...I'd also recommend asking for a room in the front of the hotel on the high floors at the end of the hall way street side so you can use the front elevator instead of the back open the curtain and windows without an audience and miss any early morning traffic noise during rush hour.......Free internet is good since the hotel's computers are good only for prinitng flight tickets that's about it unless your in a pinch...Great value if you get it for under $100 bucks a night no questions asked ....

You have to go watch the ducks...the place is just a stand by. We have continued for several years to stop in on our way north and we just wouldn't miss it for the world . Clean respectible establishment

When we checked in, we were given a 2nd floor room. I told the clerk we had requested 1st floor on our reservations.. His reply "I don't assign the rooms". Still he was more polite than the rest of the clerks during our stay who didn't even acknowledge you when you walked by. Their showers are crazy, we had to ask directions to use. Clerk said "everyone has trouble with them" Then why don't you post instructions? Regular rooms have no refrig. although there is a place for them in the dresser. I would rather have a fridg than the microwave. We came back to the room after 4 pm and the room was still not even made up. VERY noise from interstate traffic. In order to change channels on tv from the bed, you had to hold your arm up to get the remote beam to hit the cable box or the channels wouldn't change. The reason we chose CIS is because we had such a good experience in St Petersburg CIS, but this one is making us think twice.

Well, on the plus side, the hotel was only 3-4 blocks from the philadelphia museum, and on the down side, slightly dingy, dark with rude check in guy. The price was better directly on the best western site than on travel sites. Good enough place to stay while in philly if you're main aim is to see the museum. Free parking was a definite bonus, and the rest of the staff were sweet as pie in the city of brotherly love.

Based on recommendations from friends, this was our first stay in a Kimpton hotel. We thoroughly enjoyed it. Kimpton renovated the old Bismark Hotel in what is now the Chicago Loop theater district. It is a perfect, walkable location for access to the Loop theaters as well as the Art Institute, Millennium Park, and other south-of-the-river attractions. The hotel is just plain fun from the contemporary geometric decor, to the tiger striped bath robes, to the very popular wine hour (free wine!) in the beautiful lobby. There were so many touches that differentiated our experience from the typical cookie cutter hotel experience. The staff was very helpful. Room and bed were very comfortable with nice nice linens. And the price was the same or less than typical Chicago hotels, for example the Marriott. Both restaurants, one more of a bar setting, the other fine dining Italian, are quite good. We will definitely return to Kimpton.

My Husband and I stayed at this hotel with our daughter and granddaughter both in their late teens and it was the perfect location from which to see the city.We were within 4minutes walk to times square and 6 minutes from central park.We could also walk to loads of other attractions really easily,ie: 5th avenue,The Rockafella Centre,Radio City, Grand central terminal,and we were also in the heart of Theatre land,so all in all this made our stay perfect!
 There was a great argentinian restaurant practically opposite and just down the side street next to the hotel a lovely Italian restaurant. 
 The hotel itself was very clean and the staff lovely.The rooms were big and linen and towels changed daily.Downstairs in the lobby they had hot drinks available free, day and night,which was great after a day or evening out.We were also able to use internet in the lobby free and this was really useful as we were able to print up all our return flight tickets! A godsend. If there were any negatives it would only be the cooked breakfast which was very rubbery!!, but there was plenty of choose of other cold items cereals, fresh fruit, bagels,pastries etc so that made up for it. Hopefully we will return one day!.

When booking hotels I picked this one based on its location - and I feel that it turned out to be a great choice. It is a few blocks' walk away from most of the top tourist destinations in downtown Seattle, such as the Seattle Monorail, Macy's, Pike Place Public Market, etc.
The rooms are also fairly spacious for a major city in the USA - I am comparing this to NYC (maybe not such a good city to compare with). More importantly - the toilet was pretty spacious.
The hotel has a 'welcome drink' (strawberry and lime-flavoured water) every afternoon for all guests - more particularly for those who are checking-in, but free for anyone in the lobby.
Of course, there is free wifi - both in the lobby and the rooms. It is definitely fast - a big bonus.
The staff were really helpful when I was there - in terms of giving suggestions of good food to check out in the area, solving a problem of unresponsive room cards, and transportation to the SeaTac airport.
While this hotel may seem a little pricey, it is definitely more value for money compared to other 'brand-name' downtown hotels which are further from the waterfront.

You will most likely get a better deal if you call reservations. They pieced together a custom made package for me which I wouldn't have been able to do otherwise. This was a surprise weekend that I booked for my husband and I. We checked in on Thursday night (Thanksgiving), entered our room and it was pretty nice at first glance. The towels in the bathroom are rough as heck, nothing luxurious about them. Pillows are too soft, the couch in the Bayside Jr. Suite has no support. Even though it was clean, the tub didn't look clean. You may run into an insect every now and then, from either the patio door being open for a moment, the front door, or who knows.
This place is so overpriced and will nickel and dime you to death. 
I had a package for the next day of spa services which was amazing! Both of us truly needed a day of relaxation. The people were very nice and professional. I have however had better nail jobs, by Saturday one of my nails had chipped polished. We had 30 minutes of jacuzzi time in a private area and I asked that lunch be served at that time as well, which came right on time after our massages. 
*Some of you may think that I'm being picky (and I could really care less) but for some reviews like this help and for the money you shell out to this place, you should know before you go.
Dinner was superb at the Baileen restaurant. We both ordered the Fillet & Lobster tail. The lobster tail was so flavorful, fillet cooked to perfection! 
Saturday was simply a do nothing catch up on sleep day. But we purchased items at the marketplace to use one of the pits outside our suite for a bonfire. Items were once again overpriced but loved sitting outside with the fire overlooking the water. 
Sunday we will be checking out. Overall it was a cool experience but for the price I expected more. I do think the rooms need a facelift.

title_masked: Superb hotel, good rates, clean, comfortable, exceptional service.
text_masked: We usually try and stay almost exclusively at Marriott properties because they are universally excellent and we liike to collect their points, but we're glad we made this exception. This is a teriffic property with lovely rooms and exceptional staff.

The accommodation was just average. Nothing to rave about or to write home to. Basically a place to sleep and rest. The room we were in (314) was facing the road, so very noisy first thing in the morning with garbage trucks and work vehicles. The noise level at night was ok. We were out all day so cannot comment what the noise level is during the day. Try to get a room facing away from the road and on a high floor to avoid the noise in the morning. Room size was acceptable. But the bathroom felt a bit small.
Buffet breakfast was acceptable. Nothing special.
Staff members at the hotel were pleasant enough. Valet parking was convenient. Would try to stay somewhere else when we return to San Diego.

Nice hotel. Complementary muffins/scones and coffee at breakfast time, fruit in the afternoon and wine, cheese and crackers at night! Modern room. Not very spacious but big enough. Nicely located in Soho, practically next to a subway station. Quite a busy boulevard right next to it (avenue of the Americas, 6th avenue) which does produce some noise, especially during the daytime! Cleanliness was average.

title_masked: Great value and great for families
text_masked: We went to San Diego with our two children (9) & (5), to do the regular visits (Seaworld & Zoo). This was our first time at the Sommerset Suites, but it will definately not be our last. The property is located nicely about ten minutes from Seaworld and about five minutes from the Zoo. We had a one bedroom suite which contained two queen beds in the bedroom, and a sleeper sofa in the living area, a small kitchen area with stove/oven, fridge/freezer, and microwave. The hotel is located directly across from a hospital which at times can be a little noisy but not bad at all. Shopping is available nearby, and the staff was friendly and willing to help in any way possible. The morning breakfast was great, and for the price...this place is a great great value. We will be back for sure!

If you're a history buff or enjoy the atmosphere of by-gone eras, then you'll enjoy The Waldorf Astoria. The location is fabulous and very central to many of the "must see" sights. Our room was large and had been redone at some point, but the carpet is old, the sofa was old, and the room decor was very "grandma-ish". The price point is high but what isn't in NYC these days? The buffet breakfast was good, but certainly not worth the price, but then again, it's NYC. Would I stay there again - no - I would be just as happy in a more modern hotel in a smaller room, that was less of a tourist sight in itself.

Had a great family weekend at this property while attending a soccer tournament at the nearby Starfire Complex. Our 2 bedroom, 2 bath suite was very clean and spacious. The beds were very comfortable. Free hot breakfast had a good variety of items to choose from. The property has a decent size outdoor pool, basketball court and runing path. Quiet location, yet close to freeways, Southcenter Mall and Seatac Airport. Highly recommendable!

We loved this hotel. Everything is first class. We could stay forever.
Beautiful: rooms, grounds, common areas. Restaurants excellent.
Service outstanding.

We have visited San Diego twice but quite a few years ago. We couldn't locate the hotel we stayed at the last 2 trips and started to view hotels in the area that looked like the previous hotel. The Crown Plaza seemed similiar in look and the rates were very good. This trip started on the right foot from the beginning with making our reservations through their hotel. The reservationist was so helpful. We decided not to rent a car without knowing how close or far we were from the hotel. Much to our surprise the hotel had a free shuttle service to/from Old Town, Train Center and the Fashion Valley Mall. I cannot tell you how many times we used the shuttle to and from each of these forementioned places a day. The guys were just the greatest! Housekeeping was exceptional. Our room was cleaned early after we left and when we need extra towels etc someone arrived right away with the items. We only ate breakfast at the hotel and we highly suggest the french toast made with corn flakes. The front desk was extremely helpful and nice at all times. I cannot say enough of our stay which was largely due to the complete staff at the Crown Plaza. Kudos to everyone and Thank you!!!

I stayed here recently for one night. We got upgraded from a wonderful king room to a spectacular room. If you are used to nice hotels, the W in Seattle is disappointing. It gets the job done, but I won't stay there again. The room was okay, and big, but the bathroom could have been in any 3 star hotel and had some cleaning / maintenance issues. A the towels were like sand paper. The lobby is small and has a strange layout, and in the morning they have "breakfast" there which makes it even worse. The hotel parking costs $37 and fills up fast, there is a parking lot nearby (self-park) that they do not validate against. Internet is $17/day. The experience was not helped by a party happening in the adjoining room which went on all night including flighting, yelling and copulating, which I suppose that could happen in any hotel. The hotel staff was very agressive trying to get into clean the rooms in the morning. The lobby bar is loungey (douchy) and the restaurant served some delcious seafood, but I would not seek it out as a destination. The location of the hotel is very good, right down town. All in all, it wasn't horrible, but I like to enjoy my hotels and I will definitely seek another one in Seattle next time.

My husband and I stayed in this hotel for 4 nights in June and found it exceeded our expectations. I had reviewed this on Tripadvisor before booking and was not disappointed. It was very modern and exceptionally clean throughout. The staff were friendly, helpful and efficient. Our room was spacious with a very comfortable king size bed, good sized bathroom and a kitchenette with everything you could need. It was kept very clean every day by the chambermaid. Everything in the room was new and modern and we had a view of the Empire State building from our window. The hotel provides a breakfast each morning and although this was more or less the same each day, it was more than adequate and the dining area was kept very clean. Some people had complained in other reviews about waiting for the lift, but we didn't have any problems whatsoever and the lift was extremely fast (we were on the 26th floor). The location of the hotel was very good, being on W 40 Avenue and only 2 blocks away from all the main buildings in Times Square. I cannot say one bad thing about this hotel and would recommend it to anyone.

We have stayed here three times and whilst this time was better it is an average place to stay. The doormen are very good, but the hotel was having a lot of work done and although it was ma clear, it was very loud during the day, but whos in the hotel in the day, so no worries. All said its just ok really, good location for FW, bridge and the rock. The cable cars are so busy and over the past seven years we have seen them get much busier so go early they are for me the best way to see and feel the city.

This hotel was THE WORST hotel I have ever stepped foot in. It was absolutely disgusting. There are bed bugs, and no sheets on the bed. There was mold growing on the ceiling right above the bed and you could see that it was falling down on to the pillows. There were DC rats running all over the place. I was honestly afraid for my health in that place. The room was AWFUL. The front desk person Alex was rude, unhelpful and totally untrustworthy. I am totally DISGUSTED with this hotel and I cant believe it hasn't been condemned. I will be reporting this to the BBB.

I recently stayed at this Westin enjoyed my stay. The only real negative, and not a big one at that, is that it is starting to show its age. Doors are very heavy and make quite a bit of noise when one lets it slam shut. The big plus is the staff. I got to know the bartenders very well and they went out of their way to make me feel comfortable. A big shout out to Jamie, Elizabeth, and Nikki.

We stayed in this hotel for one night on January 12. The service was excellent. The room was very nice and spacious. The bathroom had a large sink area and a lighted make-up mirror which I always appreciate. Room service was prompt and very good. The lobby bar has very good food. I would stay here again when visiting Dallas.

I travel to Los Angeles for business once or twice a quarter and always book the Omni if available. Absolute first choice for LA hotels. The staff and service is excellent, always willing to go the extra mile.
In my two most recent trips (April and May 2012), I have had flawless experiences. The express check-in option is a great feature, allowing an easy entrance without a wait in line. Everybody who stays here should be a member of their loyalty program, which offers great perks such as pressing services and a complimentary morning beverage. I can't say enough about the service.
The rooms are large, and the king beds are excellent - soft enough, but not so much that you just roll into the middle of the bed. I know mattress choice is very different for everybody, but I consider these a close second to the one I have at home for comfort level. The separate shower/bathtub is great.
The rooms aren't cheap, but they are a great value for the level of service and the amenities you receive.

Convenient location, just a block and a half (uphill) from the University light rail station. This is the 3rd Kimpton hotel I’ve stayed at and I am completely hooked on the brand. Consistently wonderful service and terrific rooms. This was my first time with a kid in tow at a Kimpton and I was very pleased by the attention given to him. At check-in, while I dealt with the very friendly staff, the child in our group was invited to open the lobby toy chest and choose a free toy. We were provided with a kid’s activity booklet and bag of fun items. The booklet included a trivia quiz about the hotel and, upon completion, we called down to room service to claim the free milk and cookies offered as a prize. Delicious! We also requested one of the hotel’s goldfish and a large bowl with a cute little fish was promptly delivered for our enjoyment. Also enjoyed the complimentary social hour with free wine for the adults and free soda for the kid. Our room featured 2 beds and was absolutely huge! It offered modern furniture and fixtures with plenty of space left over. Beds were huge and comfy. Alarm clock featured an iPod docking station. Bathroom was nicely sized and offered a great shower, featuring wonderful, scented Caswell-Massey soap/shampoo. A terrific stay, as always, from Kimpton! Onsite restaurant was terrific for lunch the next day. Hotel is a quick cab or light rail ride from Safeco Field and not far from the major Seattle attractions. Loved the hotel, the staff, everything about Hotel Monaco. Definitely recommended!

We couldn't have loved this hotel more. The staff was helpful and welcoming, the location was fantastic. I've already recommended this hotel to someone who will be going to Philadelphia soon. We will be back.

Great hotel with excellent restaurant attached (Custon House). Rooms are clean and service is very good. Location a little off the beaten path (South Dearborn), but within walking distance of office and a number of decent bars and other restaurants. I travel to Chicago at least 6 times/year and try to stay here everytime.

Just left a 2 night stay at St Giles. Everything was great, we called the day before for an early check in. We were there super early and dropped off our bags so we could walk around and they called once the room was ready which was great. The room was HUGE, much bigger than any other place we had stayed in before in NYC. Didn't make it to he bar but seemed cool. Walking distance to almost everything.

At 2am in the morning an alarm went off in the hotel. My wife called front desk and they told us to stay in the room. After a few minutes it went off again. This time we left the room and went to the lobby. A few minutes later the firemen arrived and disregarded the alarm. According to the hotel staff, there was some dust in the smoke detector. How come the front desk guy told us to stay in the room while knowing nothing about what was going on? How come there is dust in the smoke detector that can activate the alarm? This cannot happen in a serious hotel. Of course, it ruined our night. After complaninig with the front desk lady the next morning and asking to be reimbused, she ironically smiled and said: that is not gonna happen. I'm still waiting a call/email/letter with an apology and a reimbursment. Not sure if it is gonna happen at all.
The rooms are old dated and quite dark but the bathrooms are ok. Location is good but there are many other options for the same price in the area.

I was very pleased with my experience at Wingate. It was only one exit away from Mayo Clinic exit. The staff was very pleasant and helpful. Knowing I had an appointment at Mayo, upon the maintainence dept arriving, he immediately came and unlocked the safe so I could store my laptop while at Mayo. The housekeeping staff was also very helpful. Even though I did not need any housekeeping services, they happily emplied my trash and provided new towels even though I told her that I could reuse them. The housekeeping staff was so friendly even asking how I was making out with my Mayo clinic appointments. I really appreciated that since I was alone for the trip. If ever coming to Mayo again, I would definitely stay at Wingate.

the hotel was very good for our long weekend in manhatten. The location was perfectt in the middle of Manhattan 5-10 minutes to 5th Avenue , Empire State Building, Time Square ect. The room was small but very clean and good enaugh for us. About the noice outside the sleep quality is not very good, but who cares...NY never sleeps :) The Americana Inn is a good choise for sightseeing in New York./Manhattan.

My self and ex-girlfriend stayed here in March-
We found the hotel to be in a brilliant location, located just off 5ave (If your looking for shopping) and also a very short walk to times square and other Mid-town attractions (With links obviously to all the others) 
First impressions were great - Arrived via cab from JFK (only $51 + tips) Welcomed warmly by the door man, and our bags were taken by the bell hop (Tipped). The lobby of the hotel is pretty spectacular, very grand! Check-in took a matter of minutes, all staff friendly and happy to help. 
The room (on the 3rd floor) was dated and small (Manhattan rooms are typically small) however, the room as very clean! The view looked out onto the hotels roof/services area - a little unimpressed by this. The bed was very big, apparently we booked a 'Cosy queen' however the bed turned out to be a 'Superior king' - very comfortable, with plenty of pillows. The room was fitted out with A/C and or heater - very noisy to say the least, we only used this when we weren't in the room! All facilities in the bathroom worked a treat, all very clean also. The room also came with iron, ironing board, suitcase props and also plenty of space and hangers to hang shirts dresses etc... 
The room was kept clean everyday by the brilliant maids, all towels were changed everyday without fail, and the bed was always made as if fresh. - Always very friendly when passing in the halls (Goodmorning, Goodevening etc...) 
The concierge at the hotel seemed to be very helpful, pointed us in the right direction a few times, and gave us information about airport delays and transfer times at different points of the day.
The hotel bar was quite expensive, however served a wide selection of beverages including morning Starbucks coffee! (not that we needed them too with the 100's of other Starbucks on every corner!) 
The hotel Gym - we didn't use however we did have a look and the facilities did look impressive (Small gym with the usual equipment) 
Food/room services- we didn't bother with either, however prices weren't to bad, food always looked goof also. 
Checking out- We checked out just before 12pm, again staff very happy to help and wished us a safe flight back to the UK. Gave our bags to the bell hop for safe keeping until our departure time - Bell hop was very snotty at our $10 tip for 2 bags! 
Door man flagged us a cab back to JFK ($51 + Tips) and we were on our way home. 
- Overall this was a very nice hotel to stay in. Previously in October I had stayed in the Hilton Garden Inn just off Times Square (Much more modern). 
Services was always good, except for the last encounter with the bell hop! 
Room was brilliant, clean and big enough for what we needed it for. 
Location was excellent also, as are most Mid town hotels boasting the Times Square location.
Would defiantly stay here again!
(Bare in mind that if your visiting NY for sight seeing, 85% of the time your not going to be in your room! - If you are your not doing it right! ;) ) 
Andy.

need more accommodations for smokers...smoking areas etc...Also if there is a $150 cleaning fee for smoking in the room than it should be more clear to offer smokers rooms on the first floor near an exit...or some other alternative

title_masked: Nice hotel for a long stay
text_masked:
Stayed here for 2 nights end of September. I have stayed at HS's before, and all are large rooms, small kitchens, most seem to have a ceiling fan. Great for a long stay. ONLY concern with this chain, as they are like small apartments, they seem to be constructed as such. Thin walls, and can hear the guy walking above your room with the squeaky floors. Thats just being picky though.
This hotel, like most had free breakfast. (very similar to a Hampton Inn in quality), and nightly free food and drinks (bud, bud light and red or white wine). This is free as well. Keep in mind, its FREE, so don't expect fine dining. I was here on business, but without a car. You can read in other reviews and its true, there is NOTHING in walking distance to eat here. SO, the free nightly food and drink had to do. It was not horrible, just like I said, free food.
Most of the staff was nice and attentive. Nice business center, internet seemed par. Not a bad location, just wish I had a car to go out at night.

title_masked: Family trip to Chicago - Labor Holiday weekend
text_masked: We had a great time. Outstanding location, close to many attractions including Millenium Park and the Magnificent mile. Enjoyed the complimentary wifi on our portable devices. Swimming pool was out one night but we were given the opportunity to go to another hotel cross the street. Staff was friendly, room was clean and comfy. Overall our stay was enjoyable.

My wife and I were very much looking forward to staying at the hotel due to the big hype it gets everywhere.
We were rather unimpressed.
The rooms are very small and the bathrooms even smaller.
The staff, although fairly friendly, have a very rushed attitude. This helps in receiving assistance quickly, but you never feel calm and relaxed. There are always lines of people waiting for checkin, bag storage, drinks, everywhere. This is probably the reason the staff seem so rushed, but I like a relaxed feel when I get to my hotel.
If you enjoy returning to a calm and soothing atmosphere after a long day of shopping or sightseeing, this is not the place for you.
The other thing you'll notice at the elevators, is a bunch of people waiting to take their own luggage to their rooms.
I don't know why, but I couldn't find anyone to take our bags up.
At a hotel of this level (and price), I expect that as a given. I shouldn't even have to ask.
Finally I was there for my birthday and noted that on the reservation. Upon checking in the clerk wished me a happy birthday and that was it. No card in the room or anything else to make you feel special. 
It's the little things that make the difference. The Empire seems to skip over the little things all the time. (Probably to assist the lines of people you find everwhere).
At this price, I wouldn't recommend the hotel.
You can do much better in New York.

title_masked: Leaking bathroom and no refund for cancelation
text_masked:
I cannot recommend this hotel. We stayed and prepaid 4 nights (3 persons). We had to leave one day earlier than planned. We received no refund, allthough we immediately announced this upon arrival. Our bathroom was leaking water and we had to change room. Breakfast is even worse than continental breakfast. The boiled eggs are one week old on ice. Smelly :-(
We will avoid this next time --- a pity! Only full beds available (No Queensize, nor kingsize.)

title_masked: Reliable Marriott, Staff Like Clockwork, Not Exactly Time Square
text_masked: This is a no bells and whistles Marriott. My daughter and I went to visit Columbia University in late August. The hotel is easy walking distance from the subway. We walked from 34th from the Megabus stop. This hotel is totally the reliable Marriott that I have come to know and love. No real bells and whistles. Breakfast is included. Nothing to write home about. I agree with other writers that the microwaved (gray) sausages are a bit of a turn off. All plastic cutlery. Humph. Plastic cutlery definitely a deeply seated pet peeve of mine. The foot print of this hotel is tiny. 8 rooms crammed per floor. The lobby is a postage stamp. The breakfast area tiny and my daughter and I had trouble sitting together for breakfast. We were there on a Friday and had to get an early start. Every other tourist staying there had to get an early start too. The room was tiny but reliably comfy, clean and since since we are Elite and had a room on a high floor (30?), we had a beautiful view of the Empire State Building. If we would have been lower down, we would have been admiring the NY State Depart of Corrections, Parole Office. The hotel is located on a side street with shady video stores) and the rooftop club attracts the scantily clad crowd. The elevators were rocket speed. This was a pleasant surprise given the number of floors. There is a cab stand, less than a block away. This worked out since we had to get up to Morningside Heights. Finally, and most notably for this particular trip, we had to leave our baggage behind so we would not have to drag it all over NY and a college campus. Marriott staff was ready at the elevators and outside breakfast area to quickly and efficiently issue tickets for any guests checking out and storing bags. We returned later in the afternoon to collect our bags and experienced the same efficient service in getting our bags back and we didn't have one minute to spare to get the bags and catch our Megabus back to Baltimore. No complaints. This hotel is in the Time Square vicinity. I think its a bit of a stretch to say it is in Time Square.

The location is perfect if you want to be away from the craziness of Time Square, just walking distance to Central Park which was fantastic to enjoy each morning with a cup of coffee in hand. As for the hotel itself the rooms are very small but the charm of the old creaking oak floors to your room takes you back in time, in a good way. Bathrooms have been all updated with stone and nice hardware and does not seem out-dated in my opinion. The area of where the hotel is located is very safe whether traveling with a companion or by yourself like I was when visiting NYC. And if you are coming to see the Macy's Parade, than this is an ideal location because the start of the parade begins just two blocks away but make sure to find a good spot early (05:30 to be exact!)

Loved the decor of the room. Easy to access public transportation. Great rate. Breakfast was included, only issue was we had to go outside to get to the public restaurant. No big deal we didnt have the kids, if we had the kids with us would have been more of an issue. 
Great hotel all in all!!

title_masked: decent rooms with decent service and excellent food
text_masked: This is well located in the middle of Manhattan and a safe neighborhood. the food in the bar is wonderful - do try the lobster appetizers. the rooms are quite large for this part of town and the staff friendly for New Yorkers.

this is hotel is at a good location ,i really enjoyed my stay and the rooms are comfortable...just the batroom need a bit of renovations ,so thumbs up for this hotel.
If you drive ,the 24hr parking is just across the street and good rates too if you pay online and there is an asian restuarant past the lobby and another the italian across the street which is very good.
Broadway if this is your thing ,well i couldn't get enough of it because its just a few minutes from the hotel

I stayed five days at this hotel for a conference. What a mistake. The hotel is very old, with tiny rooms that are not comfortable. You almost have no blankets on the bed, certainly no comforter. The hotel is extremely noisy. I stayed there over Saint Patrick's day weekend for the convention and there was a block party outside. When I complained that we should have been informed of this planed event I was told I should have known about it. How am I supposed to know where a block party is going to be held in San Diego when I live on the east coast? 
Additionally, I booked well in advance and requested a room high up, which they said they normally do for guests staying for several days, I was placed on the second floor. Right next to all the noise. 
Additionally, my flight was canceled so I was a day delayed getting into the hotel and I was told I would have to pay for the entire night even though I wouldn't be there and it was out of my control, no discount, no I'm sorry that is unfortunate, just I was told that is our policy even though I was staying for four more nights. 
I would never stay here again. Spend a little more and stay next to the convention center.

Stayed here for a combined business and leisure purpose. Hotel location btw 44 and 7 is just perfect. Downstairs you will find the shake shack hamburger restaurant with probably the best burgers in NY. The hotel has a very good and friendly staff + extra bonus for Vicky at the front desk. Breakfast was also very good and recommendable. In room you had all the stuff you would need both for leisure and business, a special bonus for the huge bed which was definitely XXXL-size. The warm water in the shower took a while to come. I would definitely go back here any time.

Let me start this review by stating that I am not the target demographic that aspires to this hip hotel brand. I lucked out (or so I thought) purchasing a room for myself for a weekend in Chicago. I did not choose the W-Lakeshore, I purchased it blind through Hotwire and was enticed after learning it was a 4-star hotel and I had received an amazing deal. After staying here for the last 2 nights, I cannot recommend this hotel and in fact, have stayed at far better 2 and 3 star hotels.
My biggest gripe with the room was the connecting doors between rooms. I was awoken at 4 AM by incredibly ignorant, drunk and loud morons from the room next door. After banging on the adjoining door and asking them to keep it down, I finally called security. While I understand that being situated near unruly hotel guests is unfortunate luck, I am surprised that a 4-star hotel would have this feature in their guest rooms. The rooms design also leaves much to be desired as the bathroom sliding door and windows do not retain heat well from the shower- a definite plus for colder Chicago AMs, when you step out of the shower. Additionally, the shades covering the windows do not do a very good job of blocking out the light, so an early wake-up was my bonus for staying in such a chic botique hotel room. 
Two other things really made me feel that the W-Lakeshore was nickel and diming their customers. The first was being given a complimentary plastic water bottle on arrival into the room. I also saw two other bottles of water in the room as well, but when I read the tags on the other bottles I realized that these were $2 each. I imagine some W Marketing genius decided that this was a great way to "increase value" at the hotel. I call that deceptive and gouging. The other nickle-and-dime move is the hotel charging fees for WiFi use. What's the matter Starwood, the room rate isn't enough for you? I've stayed at 2 and 3-star hotels that gave me free WiFi- plus I even got a chocolate chip cookie...for free. 
So in conclusion- W-Lakeshore bad; W-group- I don't see the value in your brand, but perhaps that's the point, I'm just not cool enough to get it.
We have stayed in many hotels in NYC including the best reviewed and highest priced. The overall experience at the Carlyle is superior to any of them.

Stayed here the end of April for 4 nights. Had some concerns about staying here because of reviews, but booked because couldn't beat the free parking. It was a a pleasant surprise, front desk very friendly right from check-in, let us check-in early and even though our room wasn't ready, the cleaning staff came to our room and got it ready for us immediately. Our room was a great size, bigger than most NYC hotel rooms and the microwave and a fridge was a nice bonus. Bathroom was clean and very good size. Hotel staff did a great job cleaning our room everyday and there were NO BEDBUGS which is a problem in some NYC hotels. Hotel location is great. Right on 42nd St. and very close to theatres. Three blocks to the subway station and an underground walkway leading right to Times Square. People have complained that there is a train track behind the hotel and a police and fire station across the street. Have to say this wasn't really an issue for us. Hotel parking was also good - well monitored and very secure. 
Overall a great experience and we already have another stay at this hotel booked for July.

title_masked: For the price and location? It's EXCELLENT
text_masked:
I liked this place. It was clean and very well-located, if a little rundown. Understand that it's undergoing some renovations and I think I got an un-renovated room but it was still clean and comfortable.
I had no problems sleeping though my window was next to some exhaust... So, there were fumes from cooking for a while but it didn't disturb me that much. I was just a bit surprised that the room didn't have AC. Oh well.
Nonetheless, the location is amazing. It's literally 5 min walk from the quirky Hayes Valley neighbourhood. The trolley stop is literally in front of the hotel. You'll find that the F Trolley goes EVERYWHERE that a tourist probably wants to go. The metro is less than 5 min walk. Super convenient.
Will definitely stay here again but will ask for a room that's been renovated, with AC and not next to an exhaust :)

I had a two night stay in the Hyatt Regency Embarcadero. I used Supershuttle from the airport which takes about 15-20 mins depending on drop-offs. The hotel itself is situated in the Embarcadero area of downtown, right beside the Bay Bridge. Basically it is in the region of everything downtown. Be advised that this is a huge Conference style hotel. Do not expect a boutique type atmosphere for your stay.
