However I was checked in by a very friendly Ruth who upon seeing me at any other time during my stay remembered me by name (a nice touch in such a large busy hotel). I upgraded from a standard room to a Club room for $75 per night. Well worth it. The Club Lounge has incredible views over SF bay, as well as an excellent supply and selection of food and drink. The atrium lobby is very impressive, as is it's sister hotel in Atlanta. I sat in the atrium frequently just to watch what was going on around me and people watch. A very satisfying experience as there is so much activity going on around you. My room(1616) had a spectactular view of the Bay Bridge and was immaculately clean. I slept extremely well both nights in a very comfy bed. The only difficulty I had was getting a taxi outside the hotel on the first night of my stay. The queue was long and there were very few taxis around. I would have been better off booking a town car. In-room internet was $9.95 for 24 hours and was super fast. It's complimentary in the Club Lounge. I wish I had more time in SF but the Hyatt Regency was perfect for what I needed. I would have no hesitation in recommending this hotel.

I was a female travelling alone for four days and the hotel was in a great location. The two blocks to the 103rd street station are a pleasure to walk and always safe - locals on the upper west side were always friendly, including the young African American guys who run the convenience store across the street.
Downstairs is clean and comfortable, with free wifi. Would prefer Wifi in rooms, and the TVs are always on very loudly. Not much by way of socialising as I've seen in other places, so guests don't tend to mingle much. If you're looking to make friends, I'd suggest staying elsewhere. The hotel does have a lift though, which may hostels don't and the staff are always helpful and friendly. 5-10 minute walk to Central Park. If you want somewhere to hang out for a drink and something to eat, Amsterdam Ave between 82nd and 86th has a bunch of bars and restaurants.

A fine place to stay, the Club Quarters friendly staff, convenient location and above all town car service has made the difference of where one stays for business. As you know, good repoir inevitably develops when there is trust and convenience over the years. A vital synergistic approach to business, and pleasure for that matter, has been well cared for; the least of which is price and comfort. The result: a pleaseant experience, good food, and energetic ambiance that promotes vital readiness for tomorrows business today.

Since I "blindly" booked my one night stay via Priceline, I wasn't sure which hotel or what kind of room I was going to get. Well, Priceline booked me to stay at this hotel. After reading the positive and negative reviews, I wasn't quite sure what to expect. Since I couldn't make the 3pm check-in time, I definitely wasn't sure what kind of room I was going to get. During my early Friday evening check-in, I was pleasantly surprised to find only one other person ahead of me in line. Liliana, one of the friendliest customer service reps. ever, cheerfully answered all of my questions and concerns. I requested a room in a certain area and she gave it to me with no problems. I was SO surprised when I opened the door to my room! My senses--especially smell and sight--were pleasantly greeted with a gorgeously remodeled room and no annoying smells--thanks to Romelia. :) I love everything about this room and bathroom! The grounds are beautiful, and I really enjoyed taking a night swim in one of the hotel's heated pool. I wish that I had enough money to stay one more night! Thanks again, Liliana, for giving me such a great room. God blessed me through you!

title_masked: Very spacious room and good location
text_masked: We stayed in the main building and our room was huge! (room 351), it was basically two rooms separated with a door, sharing a bathroom, each with its own flat screen... very comfortable! The view was not pretty at all (facing the courtyard full of AC equipment) but the size of the room compensated for this inconvenience. The hotel charges for the internet, but if you enroll their loyalty program and you give your "President's Club number" they will drop those charges (and a few others, like charges for local calls) and you have complimentary access to the health club. A problem is that they don't have coffee makers in the rooms, though they said they are working on that and that soon they will be available. I do recommend this hotel, it's classy, comfy and well located.

A wonderful place to stay. We shared a suite which gave us a lounge and place to relax - although we didn't have much time to do that! We enjoyed the breakfasts and the 5pm drinks and hors d'oevres. Lovely service.

140 is just a minute's walk from Back Bay station and about 10-15 minutes from Boston Common. The rooms are small but very comfortable, with free wi-fi and a good-quality TV, coffee/tea-making facilities. The staff are great, very helpful and friendly. We had a great time and I would recommend this hotel to anyone.
The only (small) downside was that the air conditioner was pretty loud.

Better than your average SpringHills brand. Decorated in a European boutique style, only open for a month, it still had the newthe staff bent over backwards to please. Well thought out rooms, ours was a king. They do need to move the long mirror from next to the window, you can not get in to see your self there. Great view of the city from the 5th floor at night.

title_masked: JW Indy Hotel is my sanctuary after a tough day
text_masked:
I used to stay at a number of hotels in Indy when I stayed there but recently I have taken to staying at the JW Marriot and I cannot compliment them enough. The Staff are all very, very helpful.. The Lobby staff and check in staff are super friendly and are just what you need after a tough all day meeting.
The Bars in the Lobby are both great places to hangout and though Indy has some nice restaurants, the folks at the JW make it hard not to just stay in for the night in their bars and restaurants. 
Finally the Exec floor lounge up on 31 is the cherry on the top of this delicious cake. They are very, very supportive of your business needs.. I nip up there each night for a low fat yoghurt and a diet coke and they always greet you with a warm welcome.
If your coming to Indy for whatever reason, make the JW your base :)

title_masked: Recent stay a little disappointing. Bathrooms showing some age.
text_masked:
No bellmen on duty when I arrived. Head valet watched me unload my bags but never offered to help. Easy check in but a little hard to find my room alone. Tracked down a housekeeper to find an ice machine. Carpets & corridors show some wear - I was on the 10th floor of the main bldg.
Big room, triple-sheeted king bed w/nice linen but bed was too hard. Prefer Westin beds. Separate tub & shower stall, but the small shower has no place to put toiletries except a tiny aluminum built-in soap dish, so had to put shampoo, razor, etc on the floor & stoop for it. Adjustable spray but dripped for a very long time after shut off. Terry robes, bath sheet + towels. TV ok but premium channels cost extra. Safe in closet. Energy conserving light bulbs not great for grooming in bath or vanity area. Hi-intensity gooseneck reading lights on each side of headboard. 
More street noise than I expected. Homeless encampments in the park across the street.
Good workout room with lots of machinery, clean. Fast elevators. 
No food service in bar after 11pm on Saturdays. Slow room service. Better dining available outside the hotel. Courteous staff. I'd give this 3 & 1/2 stars, but not up to standards of other Fairmont properties. Within arms reach of the shower floor, things weren't very clean. 
For $200+ per night, I expected a bit more. Internet access is $13.95 per 24 hrs, but join the Presidents' Club& get it free.

title_masked: Looked great on the web, but...
text_masked:
I don't know if my experience was typical or not, but I was very surprised by what I found when I checked in. I had just spent a day at a convention and was ready for a night's rest. They guy at the desk was friendly and helpful, but the ROOM WAS A DISASTER for me. When I opened the door and walked in, I was struck by the very strong smell of some kind of perfume or incense. I quickly located the source. There was a small globe on the desk with a reservoir of scent on the top of it and it was plugged into the wall power outlet so that the liquid could was heated up to spread the smell. I never asked for this amenity! My guess was that some or all of their rooms were formerly smoking rooms and that they routinely turned on the perfume/incense machine to hide the smell of cigarette smoke. I was tired, so I decided to unplug the machine and open a window to clear the air. To my amazement I found that there were no openable windows in the room. I tried to stick it out for a while (the bed was nice), but eventually I started getting such a headache that I went down to the front desk and asked to be moved to a room with windows that open. They were nice about it, and the person even offered to make sure that someone unplugged the perfume/incense machine before I got to the room. This led me to believe that perhaps ALL their rooms are equipped with electric perfume machines!
Anyway I found the replacement room indeed had a window that I could open, so I was able to clear the air (it did smell a lot like cigarette smoke after the perfume smell was removed). This second room had FLUORESCENT bedside lamps, so I felt like I was in an office. The only normal light in the whole room was the desk lamp, and it was burned out. I made two attempts to get them to fix this burned-out light (telling them each morning at the desk that I'd like the light to work) and failed on both of these attempts. Finally on the third attempt, I just unscrewed the burned out bulb, took it down to the desk, and asked that they get me a replacement bulb so that I could replace it myself. 
In summary, what was on the web about this hotel gave me no warning 
(1) existence of an electric perfume machiine in each room which is turned on by default
(2) rooms with windows that do not open
(3) mostly fluorescent lighting in rooms
(4) slipshod service when you need a burned-out light replaced in your room

I've recently spent a longer time in NYC during the July 4th week and had the pleasure of staying at the Crosby St Hotel. The staff was very friendly and accommodating, that what you would expect from a first class hotel.
The hotel is perfectly located in soho. Shops and subway stations are all located steps away. 
I really enjoy that there is a great little fitness studio on the property! 
The rooms were spacious for NYC standards and were meticulously cleaned everyday by housekeeping. 
The Crosby Street hotel makes my visit to NYC that much more enjoyable everytime I'm visiting!

This is a hotel I would highly recommend. On my first visit I was advised 'get a cheap hotel, you will be out and about so much it wont matter', this is true, to a degree, but after a long day out a comfy bed is a must and the Sheeraton does not dissapoint. To be fair, I had a high room with goood views, the decor was recenty refurbished and the hotel looked spotless. The King size beds are magnificent and don't listen to people who say just get a cheap hotel, just get a comfy bed! As other reviews will testiffy, the location of this hotel is second to none, 53rd and 7th offers everything on your doorstep.
One of my favourite aspects of the hotel is the busy bustling lobby. This is what New York hotels should be like, a haven of life. New York hotels are generally functional and you will always pay for location, the Sheraton offers more than location and dismisssive reviews leave me wondering what they were not getting here!
 If I had one complaint it is in the length of time it takes to get checked in. It seems there are queues every day to get to reception and I dont know why this is seemingly always so slow. 
Once passed this obstacle New York is waiting for you at the front door. 
I've stayed here twice and will do so again, I'm not super picky but I like clean and smart and comfy in a good location and this delivers in spades. Like I was told, you wont see too much of your hotel room if your doing New York right but what I did see of it was great. 
I will stay here again and I can't offer a better review than that.

I really enjoyed my stay at the Pacific Shores Inn. Clean Rooms which were much larger than the norm. Beach is literally less than 30 seconds away. Great restaurants in the area and the weather was beautiful. What more can you say. Next time Im in the area, Ill be staying there for sure!

Due to my business i choose this hotel and i am totally satisfied with the location.Everything is done in 1 day and hotel get the credit due to the location.Thanks for staff also for the amenity sent to my room.
J

One would think that they were in a luxury hotel at 3 star rates.Service and staff are excellent.Very good and well equipped business center.Late afternoon comp cookies fresh baked and sweet rolls in the AM.Convenient location.

My husband and I stayed at Le Parker Meridien for a two nights recently. We had a nice price due to priceline. I was not overly impressed with this hotel though. Everything was nice, but there was no luxury in it. There were extra charges for using the gym, or the pool, a view was extra, staying in a higher level room was extra, etc. That being said, the room was clean and nice. The location was fantastic, we walked through Central Park each day we were there, were able to walk to both the Met and the Natural History Museum and found the subway very conveniently located as well. Just don't expect anything special from the accomodations... they are small and extremely basic.

The hotel has a good location for walking to the Market and even to the Riverwalk however, it needs some updating or rather just some basic touch ups is really all. Paint peeling, dripping faucet and window unit installed pretty damn crappy!! The hotel staff was very nice and welcoming but they seem to be letting this place go to waste.... it's doable but I stayed in La Quinta around the corner and it seemed to be much nicer and closer : )

I just loved your hotel, but was not enthralled with the room itself. VERY small bathroom and super narrow hallway leading into the room. It was fine for just me, but i had to change hotels once my husband arrived (no bigger rooms were available at that time), because it would have been very uncomfortable for the of us to be in that room. Our kids stayed in a Business size room, which I will ask for next time. loved the breakfast, very nice hotel. Super location!

I stayed here on a recent business trip and had a great overall experience. The front desk staff was very friendly and I had a corner king room with a great view of the space needle and the waterfront (although obstructed by other buildings). The location is within a short walk of Pike Place Market and all of the downtown shopping. There are also many restaurants nearby. There was a mini fridge in the room with two bottles of complimentary water that was restocked daily and Aveda amenities. My one complaint is that the elevator took a long time, every time. There appeared to be a large convention in-house, so that was probably the cause of the slowness, but it was still frustrating.

The hotel is very well located near Times Square, but far enough away to give a reprieve from some of the crowds and noise. It is surrounded by numerous small restaurants, spanning Brazilian to Italian and Thai food, so as a guest you will never go for lack of dining selection. The concierge and reception staff are friendly and helpful. Rooms are moderately sized but clean, well-lit, and the walls and windows are very sound proof. Having said that, they could use some upgrades. The safe utilized an actual key, the room was not equipped with a minibar, and the fridge was not even plugged-in. The standard tray of coffee-maker and tea selection was provided. No complementary water bottles were provided, or available for purchase in the room. 
Our only real gripe with the hotel was the awful beds. The mattresses and pillows were extra-firm, so we all suffered from stiff-backs and necks, as well as lack of restful sleep by the end of our 5 day stay. 
Overall, this was a good hotel choice in the Times Square area, and we would stay here again -- but hopeful of a change in beds for a better nights sleep next time.

I'm a frequent traveler and NY is one of my regular spots. I would not consider staying at any other hotel in NY since I have it all at The Bryant Park Hotel. It makes a big difference when the staff recognizes you and makes the effort to know your name. Everyone is exceptionally friendly and service-oriented. I have stayed in many different rooms at The Bryant Park Hotel and one room is just as good as the next. Having a bright and quiet room are both important to me; having an open space around the hotel--the Park itself--is also refreshing. It goes without saying that the rooms have great amenities and they are comfortable and clean. Also, many hotels in NY are traditional and stuffy; Bryant Park is the complete opposite. It's contemporary and has a bright open feel. Again, The Bryant Park Hotel meets all my criteria and more! I thank the team at Bryant Park Hotel for making my experience so great. Bryant Park is my home away from home.

Had to be in SD for a wedding and we decided to give this hotel a try (first time here). We had a great room in the main tower, facing the fireworks. Room was well appointed and clean. Housekeepers were really nice, always offering assistance and asking if we needed more towels (gotta love that). The pool was the best part by far! Three pools with two water slides made for a fun day at the pool (sadly we only had time for one day). Great place for families and easy access to Sea world (they have a water taxi to the park). Mission Beach is a quick 10 minute walk. We will be back to this hotel!

Ok first of all my boyfriend and I are in wheelchairs and we travelled from Amherst Massachusetts to Baltimore via Peter pan buslines. You can see the hotel when you walk out of the bus station. (for us this is a big plus). Mike was there to check us in. He was awesome We had asked for a room with a roll in shower. Nice bathroom plenty of room for the chair. We we got to our room there was a big chaise lounge in the room. There was no room for me to park my chair and charge it. I understand that they don't always sell that room as a handicapped acessible room. I called down to the desk and asked them to move the chaise lounge out of the room. there was someone there within 5 minutes of me calling. Housekeeping did a wonderful job. We were there for an Oriole game and didn't know how to walk to the stadium malcolm walked us as far as the train tracks which was very nice. 
Yesterday when we were leaving we were running very late. we had a lunchbox with us and Bella packed us a breakfast of fruit water and cinnimon rolls to eat on the bus with us. which was very nice. 
the two biggest problems that i see is there are a group of homless men that wash people's windows very close to the property. not a big deal to me, but i can understand why people would feel uncomfortable. and the next biggest thig for us is they do have a shuttle that you can request to pick you up from the ballgame. it is not accessible to people in wheelchairs. I feel that they charge you for use of the shuttle in the price of the room. (which was very reasonable.) but the shuttle should be accessible to all. overall i give this place a 9 out of ten.

title_masked: Be careful if you're a light sleeper
text_masked:
I've been here now for 3 nights, and be careful coming here if you're a light sleeper. 
Along with the other reviews, it does feel dated. Dim, narrow hallways. The rooms are OK, but are very small. I just came here after 4 nights at the JW Marriott in San Antonio which is incredible, and maybe isn't the fairest comparison.
Every morning, at 7 there is construction next door, and I don't mean just a hammer. Trucks, back up beepers, the whole deal. If they have ear plugs for you, it's a sign. I can also hear noise from two doors down and someone above me. And there goes a police car...... I know it's in the middle of the city, but the windows are filthy and single pane, and they let in a lot of noise. I don't think they've been cleaned in a year, it would help a ton with the overall feel if you hand a clean look at the great view.

I always enjoy Kimpton Properties. The lobby is spectacular. All of the staff is friendly and helpful. Their service is top notch. When I checked in, the desk clerk made sure that a cab would be waiting for me at 3am in the morning so that I could get to the airport in time. My only complaint was my room. Since I checked in early, I was in a Handicap room with walk in shower. There was hardly ANY water pressure and the finishes in the WC were not to usual standards (no towel bar). The WALLS were VERY thin and I could hear "everything" going on next door. The room also had NO view and the blinds did not work correctly.
A perfect boutique hotel. I stayed for almost 10 days and had a great time. Right sized room for single occupancy. Very central but away from hustle bustle . Will stay again.

The hotel location is really good, right behind the Capitol and next to the union station.
The staff was amazing, helped us with parking location and some directions. Especially an attendand called [NAME], she was very helpfull during our stay on Washington.
The hotel is very clean and organized, and the accomodations is fantastic.
Could not have a better place to stay in DC.

title_masked: Great location for eating, shopping and business
text_masked: Great location for shopping at Copley Mall and Prudential Center Mall - - both connected via a skywalk which is great if the weather is bad. Had a fantastic view of Boston from the 36th floor. Enjoyed most meals and drinks in the Hotel except for a walk to the 'Legal Fish' in Prudential Center Mall. Very nice large Lobby Area with plenty of sitting space. Very comfortable beds and a great T.V. No fridge in the room. Close by Subway stops.

title_masked: Hotel is a bit out of the way for a short break
text_masked: This hotel is on the shore of the Hudson river. We got a Statue of Liberty room which had a good view. Battery Park is a bit out of the way for getting around if you are only in New York for a short break. However it is very close if you are wanting to do the Statue of Liberty, Ellis Island, 9/11 Memorial and Wall Street. The hotel itself is okay. It mainly serves business clients. We opted for a club room so we could use the club lounge. But the club lounge was very disappointing. The food was not that great and drinks options were minimal. Two bottles of wine were left out in the evening. The soft drinks ranged from coke, lemonade or water. The coffee machine was out of order. I really don't think it was worth the extra money. We had a meal in the restaurant and as it was restaurant week we did have some reasonable choices and the food was good. We decided to go to the main restaurant for breakfast the next morning instead of the club lounge but they seemed to be taking ages to get people seated. In fact one group of 4 walked out. After waiting ourselves to be seated we thought that they were not quick enough bearing in mind you wanted to get out and about to see things. So we left too and found a coffee shop a short walk away. One thing we noticed about this area and in fact the whole of New York was how much scaffolding there was around which detracted from the buildings. Also everywhere there were piles of rubbish on the pavements. I am not sure if this was just at the time we went but I would struggle to recommend going back to this area.

My hubby and I travel to Chicago annually and stayed here at the recommendation of our friends for the first time this past weekend. 
we took an early flight and were allowed to pre check in (8 a.m.) and our room was ready by noon. they upgraded us to a corner suite which over looked the Chicago river. The bed and linens were wonderful!! 
I have no complaints about the hotel employees and felt like they really tried to make our stay as enjoyable as possible. I have only two things that I didn't like:
*lighting in the room was horrible, especially the bathroom. they do have a make up mirror but the room was soo dark! this could easily be fixed and i'm over it :)
*two drinks at the bar in the lobby (bacardi coke and a grey goose gimlet) were 27.00. I understand we are in Chicago but it just seemed excessive. the bartender was very nice and the bar was welcoming. other than that, i have nothing at all to say that isn't 100% positive!
it may be worth noting that i've stayed in the Four Seasons, Hotel Palomar, and Hotel Sax while visiting chicago. I would say the Westin is my new favorite along with Palomar. 
we'll be back !

title_masked: My stay in Chicago couldn't have been better!
text_masked:
Thanks to all the positive reviews in Tripadvisor I chose the Talbott Hotel for my stay in Chicago. I am not a big fan of anonymous international hotel chains and what I found at the Talbott Hotel was exactly what I had been looking for!
Such beautiful decorations during Christmas time, a fire burning in the cosy lounges, very friendly staff, great location within walking distance to all the department stores, shops and restaurants. My room was very comfortable, spacious and I enjoyed my favorite Molton Brown amenities. Bath robes were provided, but the only thing I really missed were a pair of slippers that usually go with them! Next time I won't forget to pack my own.
I didn't have breakfast at the hotel but went across the road to "The Godess and Grocer" for some freshly pressed orange juice and a toasted breakfast bagel. A wonderful delicatessen with a wide range of delicious choices. I took it back to my room to enjoy it with the free coffee from the Keurig coffee maker.
Next time I come to Chicago I will definitely stay there again!!!

I can not say enough good things about the service. Erin, a concierge, handled some requests for me before I arrived and exceeded my expectations. As a result, I went to her about dinner reservations.She reserved exactly the type of restaraunt I wanted.
The rest of the staff handled everything professionally and with polish as well.
Compared to other New York hotels I have stayed in, the bedroom and bath were spacious and comfortable.
We did not eat at the Hotel, so I can not comment. But, my wife wanted coffee after the lobby service was removed and, before she could say more, a staff person went to the kitchen and got her a fresh cup.
I have stayed in more than a few nice hotels. However, this is now one of my favorites.

We had planned a three night stay for a convention. I was appalled at this location. I've stayed at La Quinta before and never had an experience like this.
I'll start with the positive. The staff was helpful and very friendly.
The rest was awful. There was mold in the bathroom. I walked to get ice in my socks and came back with black bottomed feet. The ice machine wasn't working. The room smelled musty. There were no toiletries offered in the bathrooms despite the price. The whole place made me feel grungy. This was our second room. The first one smelled heavily of cigarettes, despite being a non-smoking room. The front desk informed me that they 'don't have control of people who smoke in the rooms.' I was nauseous when I left and had trouble breathing. I would definitely NOT recommend this place. 
We were able to find alternate accommodations fortunately.

title_masked: Giana and Melissa at the Bar
text_masked: Two wonderful, engaging bartenders made a stay at the Westin for a business conference all the more enjoyable. When travelling solo for work, it is always comforting to be able to sit at the hotel bar and feel welcome. Even though the bar was buzzing they both always made time to make sure I was doing well.

My wife and stayed at this hotel for two nights and were very impressed with it. The room was on the ground floor and was very spacious and comfortable. The restaurant was very good and the staff were keen to please us. The food was well presented and reasonably priced as were the drinks.
The hotel is a little remote although there is a steak house restaurant about five minutes walk away. Other than that you will need transport to get anywhere else. The hotel is positioned about a fifteen minute drive away from the main part of San Diego.
I would be happy to recommend this holiday for couples and there appeared to be a large contingent of people on a medical convention staying at the same time we were there.

3 days recently and nothing could ever incite me to stay in this hotel in the future. The good? An exceptionally well appointed fitness room, but there's simply nothing else to say. Dated rooms, marginally comfortable beds and awful lighting. The food our group was served was reprehensible and a number of them took ill, and by that I mean nearly twenty. The hotel is difficult to navigate and just seems chaotic and generally a mess operationally. The worst? The two female bartenders in Mix, the hotel bar were unequivocally the surliest and most god awful I've ever seen. It baffles me how Starwood, a group I respect and whose properties I enjoy, could allow their staff to treat guests with such ambivalence. 
A plethora of other hotels in Denver, don't waste your time with this one.....

After reading many reviews we choose Palomar Washington to stay while visiting our son & our daughter-in-law. 
We were disappointed in the friendliness of staff and rarely got a door opened by a doorman--we realized with the storm it caused additional problems but we never felt that glad you stayed with us--and we stayed 5 nights. Our room was fine-had LOTS of problems with the room keys-
We have Palomar Philadelphia to compare to and the DC hotel doesn't even come close. We felt like family at the Palomar Philadelphia and not even acknowledged in DC.
Our first morning we went to the hotel restaurant -got seated immediately--not that busy and after 5 minutes of waiting for wait staff to come we left--i'm sorry but you have experience in this field-that is why we chose this hotel-we will not come again.

We took the Limo Liner from Boston and were dropped on the sidewalk outside the hotel. The Hilton was very central, and we walked almost everywhere. Central Park was only a few blocks away in one direction, Times Square in the other. Rockafeller Center was just around the corner. 
The staff was unfailingly helpful, and cheerful. We were greeted by everyone from housekeeping to the front desk. 
Though we are not handicapped, we were given a handicapped room and frankly we enjoyed the extra room and the ease of the walk in shower. We were on the 14th floor and there was no noise from the street. 
The room appeared newly re-done and was very comfortable. We have never stayed here before but could not have chosen a better hotel. This time of year the room was $239.00 per night, reasonable for NYC.

This used to be the Radisson but has been completely remodeled and has a contemporary feel. We stayed in room 1007 which is fairly large and filled with light, but it doesn't have much of a view. The beds are very comfortable. The bathroom is on the small side but ok. The skoah products were so good, I would have gone to find the store if we had time. The concierge (Sargent?) was very helpful and provided us with detailed instructions on public transportation to the arboretum - a great place to visit away from the city.
Wifi is free and fast enough for web browsing, etc, but the room is not set up for wired internet connection, so if you need a faster connection than the wifi for work, you may have some trouble. We didn't check to see if they had a business center for this purpose. Anyhow, this is much better than most other Boston hotels that charge daily for internet access.
The hotel is close to theaters and is within easy walking distance of the Boston Common and the public garden. You could reach Copley place within 15 minutes or so. A Legal Sea Foods restaurant is right across the street and there are many restaurants within a short walk. We didn't eat at their restaurant, Rustic Kitchen, which has interesting decor. All in all, the Revere is a good value and nice "new" hotel and we wouldn't hesitate to recommend it.

We love the firmdale brand, so chose to stay for my wife's 40th Birthday for 5 nights.
From the moment we arrived the personal touch and experiances made our stay a dream.
We have both travelled to NYC many times and hardend global traverlers, if you want and deserve a treat, then enter the world of Crosby street.
The front staff and conceirge made our stay, Room upgrades, champagne, cup cakes, personal cards, flowers, all on the house! 
I had my heart set on a special restaurant, no luck booking from UK, the conceirge suprised us both on the eveing of my wifes Birthday with a reservation to the restaurant! amazing and extremely thoughtfull.
The bar area is chilled, best drinks and service and bar interior in town, you can hear yourself think and unwind after a day on your feet, the breakfast is superb, try the full english! again serviced with perfection in peice and quite.
The Hotel is very quiet, sleep quality outstanding for NYC, you will not beat this.
Thankyou, Thankyou all at Crosby street, the value you give is extrodinary and rare.

Bonnie is the best breakfast chef. She makes your day with her cheerful attitude.
 The room is very cozy and it is easy to get anywhere in San Antonio you need to get to whether watching the UIW Cardinals play football or shopping or enjoying the famous river walk.

The room was large and clean and the beds were comfortable. It appeared to me that this is a older facility - the ceiling was damaged, the wall paper was curled and the carpet in the hallways was threadbare and separating at the seams.According to the certificate of inspection in the elevator, it had not been inspected in 10 years. There was undercover parking but it was not big enough for all the guests. The computer in the business center was the slowest one I've used since my Apple IIE. Althought not elegant, it was an adequate facility for our needs in spite of all these other issues.

title_masked: definintely a good choice for family
text_masked: we stayed here for 3 nights and it very enjoyable. Rooms were super roomy and clean. The breakfast is nice and has many options, but if you are in a hurry it won't work for you. We weren't and it worked for us. The location is nice. Walking is easy to good places to eat. Michigan Ave is a couple blocks toward lake. Taxi to museums runs you about $10. You do hear some sirens so if that is problematic for sleeping, you will need a taller hotel.

I and several colleagues stayed at the Andaz for a week-long business trip, and it speaks volumes for the experience that not one person in the group of frequent business travellers had a single complaint, and instead most had praise and made sure we were booked here for our next trip. That never happens! The staff is very helpful (although someone did try to check us in again every single time we came in with rolling briefcases!), but it is the overall atmosphere and approach that makes it a nice change from your typical hotel. There is more of a boutique/living room feel to the lobby, and guests have lots of places to sit and enjoy the complementary wine in the evenings while clearing emails or catching up. It is very inviting, as is the bar on the concourse level. The rooms feel more like an apartment to me than a hotel room, and were very comfortable. The Respire rooms are great if you have allergies - I was put in one after merely asking for foam pillows, and it actually made a big difference for me. For the rates charged in NY, it is nice to see a hotel including soft drinks and snacks in your room at no charge, along with wireless. If you have any reason to stay downtown, the Andaz is a great choice for business or leisure, and is close to the subway - I was able to easily get to midtown for a business dinner by hopping the subway, although you do have to allow about 30 minutes. Great hotel, we'll be back.

Oh my goodness! What a wonderful hotel! We loved it so much! I have been to NYC more than 20 times, but this was my husband's first time. I really wanted it to be special and it was! From the time we checked in, everything was 100% perfect! The staff, and I mean every single one, was so nice, accommodating and so helpful! A special shout out to Cara for helping us on restaurants and our 4th of July plans! We loved getting to know everyone! The tea in the lobby was fabulous! The apple computers in the lobby were a great touch, the free wifi was so nice to have!! Other hotels barge $10 per day!!!our room was immaculate and very roomy for a NYC room!! The bed was so yummy and comfortable and the AC worked great! The bathroom was great and the shower was extra great....great water pressure! We loved, loved, loved the shampoo, etc...
Whenever we needed ice, it was there in a flash! And when we tipped, the sweet guys were so grateful!!! I ordered breakfast one morning and it was wonderful! Best hot chocolate I have ever had! Beats Starbucks!!! We were so sad to leave today and one home, but we will definitely be staying at Distrikt Hotel every time now!! Please, everyone, take my advise!! This hotel is great for the money, fabulous room, staff, close to everywhere.....
Thank you sooooooo very much, staff, for making our stay the best ever!!

title_masked: Right next to the mall, easy access, some restaurants walking distance
text_masked: This was booked through our company travel organizer, who managed to get a decent deal. Free breakfast with bananas, apples, scrambled eggs, fried potatoes, meat patties, yoghurt, cut fruit (changed daily: melon, pineapple), wafflemaker, toast, juices. Some fruit was available 24h which was a very nice touch. The manager's reception had decent food and drinks, yet there were surprisingly few guests. Two internet PCs in the lobby, one with printer for getting boarding passes. Hotel has no shuttle to the airport, supershuttle is about 25$ to/from IAH, ample free parking. Limited restaurants in safe walking distance, as well as the Willowbrook mall. Bed comfortable, AC worked well (with some constant low frequency background hum), everything clean. Good work desk with quality adjustable chair. Triple AAA rate provides some savings, best if you have a corporate deal directly. Would come back here again. Bonus: they provided free tickets to the race course, just ask at the front desk.

fitzpatricks hotel was a home away from home to us. friendly staff clean and warm rooms very comfy beds, clean towels nice size esp for NYC , the staff were so nice and helped us with our directions . a really lovely hotel and we loved the irish bar attached to the hotel.

title_masked: Good Location, not worth the price
text_masked: My husband and I decided to take a weekend trip in Memphis. We chose this hotel because of its location to Beale St and access to the Trolly. The rooms are nice and clean. However, for the price of the room, I expected better service. First, they do not prorate the parking. We arrived at 8pm and had to valet park because the self park was full. Despite arriving so late, we were still charged a full day for parking. The hotel does not offer a continental breakfast. Our first morning, we received good service and decent food. On the second morning, we ate the breakfast buffet. The server did not even visit our table. We each fixed our plate (separately) and then had to stop a server to ask for drinks. When he returned he only poured drinks for my husband. I had to ask him to return to pour my coffee. We then had to flag down another server to ask for our check when we were done. The food was luke warm and definitely not at a safe temperature. The scrambled eggs were very runny, like they weren't done. The hotel has an indoor pool, but it is not heated and was so cold we couldn't even swim in it. At the end of the trip, we decided that it would have been better to book a room at a mid-rate hotel and drive to all the attractions. The convenience of the location to downtown and the trolly was not worth the price of the hotel.

In Dallas for a soccer tournament. Has very comfortable beds. Staff goes out of their way to make your stay comfortable. Stay on the lower floors as the upper floors tend to get hotter. The extras are with in walking distance of many resturants. Laundry mat at Park street only 5 minute drive. Many stores close by. A nice work out center on second floor. Several computers in the business center. Will stay on my return visits.

We were amazed at the extremely high standard at the Waldorf! We travel a lot and have become very blase with so called 5-6 star hotels but Waldorf has restored our faith in hotels! Two turndowns a day is the exception at other hotels but here was the norm!And the concierges were outstanding with their knowledge!And the position was the best in Chicago!

Great hotel location in Chelsea. The hotel only had two elevators but they were pretty quick and I never had to wait very long for them. The hotel has a small courtyard outside the lobby that does a nice job of separating the entry from the street. 
The Lobby was pretty small, but the staff was excellent and friendly. They were able to check me in quickly and were nice enough to give me a late check out time.
For the price the room was excellent, especially so in NYC. You won't be having parties in these rooms but they are not cramped at all. Beds were nice and comfortable. Bottled water, coffee and tea were complimentary. 
The bathroom was nice though a bit standard with a little weak hot water pressure, but I still had a nice hot relaxing shower.
The hotel does offer complimentary internet, but in my 8th floor room it was pretty slow. Tethering 3G internet from my phone was faster.
I'll defiantly look there again next time I'm up in NYC.

We've stayed at the Library Hotel several times over the past few years and it has never disappointed.
We returned this November (twice, as I had a business trip to Charleston - for the Librarians Conference), in the wake of the hurricane that split New York in two and... had our best trip ever.
The staff are the best we've ever experienced (and we're well seasoned travellers), the location is great and the rooms are spotless (as well as being beautifully decorated - and with the most surprising and amusing selection of books, themed to the room.)
The best thing of all though is how friendly the hotel feels - after a days work or pleasure on really feels as if one is "coming home" - so unlike the run of the mill corporate hotel.
There are a great selection of cocktails at the top floor bar as well!
Many thanks to Timothy, Billy and all the Librarians who made our trip such a good one!

The hotel is conveniently located just south of Market Street within easy walking distance of Union Square shopping as well as many transit options - BART, Muni, cable cars etc. It makes a very convenient base for a leisure visit to explore all that San Francisco has to offer. With that said, this is really more of a business oriented property with many meetings and events held in the property's conference facilities. I chose this hotel over the Stanford Court (also a Marriott property) because the concierge lounge was open on the weekend. Note that many concierge lounge locations are not open on weekends, so you should take that into account for leisure travel. Many travelers complain about the cost of parking at most downtown hotel locations. As I mentioned, this hotel is very conveniently located near a variety of public transit options and San Francisco is relatively easy to navigate without a car so leave the car at home if that is an option. For day trips to outlying areas, you can retrieve and return a rental car from a number of downtown locations.

We stayed for 2 nights in June. The room was very clean and recently remodeled so it was a pleasure to stay here. Our room was on the front of the hotel overlooking the lake and the park across the street. The staff was courteous and helpful. The elevators were a little slow occasionally. The most annoying thing about this hotel was something that is common among hotels of this class - they charge $12.99/day for WIFI! After paying $279/night for the room and $55/night to park a car you would think that the least they could do is give you free WIFI but that is not the case. The room was nice, the bathroom was beautiful and the view was spectacular. The hotel is very close to the Art Institute and the Field Museum is walking distance. Chicago is fun to visit and the restaurants are great. We enjoyed a fabulous breakfast at Yolk about 5 blocks south of the hotel. The concierge can give you a pass to go to the front of the line if there is a wait at the restaurant. We enjoyed our stay at the Blackstone.

I travel to New York quite often, typically twice per year. The Helmsley Park Lane is one of my favorite hotels. If you get a high room with a park view, I am not sure if there is a more magnificent site in all of New York. Yet, in comparison to other hotels located on Central Park South, the room rates are relatively reasonable (with emphasis on the word "relatively," this is New York after all - Compare what the Trump or the Ritz Carlton charges for park views). The HPL has gone through some extensive renovation, so I would suggest that any potential guest request specifically a "renovated room" with a "park view." This is a must. The hotel is not a long walk from the theater district, also the subway is just a couple of blocks away. There are many areas you can stay at in New York, but I prefer visiting the theater district and not staying there (too many tourists and crowds, noise), the calmer peaceful view of Central Park gives one some distance from the hustle and bustle. Also, at different times of the year, the Park is a winter wonderland or a lush green forest. Absolutely magnificent. The service at the hotel is typical NY brusque but absolutely efficient and thorough, and I have always found that the concierge at the Helmsley can get me into shows and the best restaurants. Harry's Bar has friendly bartenders, sports on the television, a great place for a night cap. The restaurant on the 2nd Floor looks directly out on Central Park with large glass windows on the world.

This Hotel is top notch. The room is very nice and the bed is extremely comfortable, the pool is indoors and it’s a little stuffy when you first walk in. They have a nice patio off of the pool area over looking Houston. Minute Maid Park, Toyota stadium and the convention center are within walking distance. This hotel is well worth the money, even the valet parking.

We stayed at the Desert Ridge Canyon Villas for a week in April. Room # 2834. We had a great stay with our two young children. I don't have the energy to go into detail about our stay due to my lack of sleep and loss of patience. We believe we brought home bed bugs from there. My husband was getting bit during our stay but we figured it was mosquitos or spiders. It can take up to several months after you stay at a place to realize you brought home a problem. We've been dealing with our new problem for a month now. The hotel called me back within 30min after I called and said they checked and found nothing? Not convinced. Really...would a hotel like this really admit to it anyway?!? So traveler beware! BTW...this was our first family trip in 2 years. We do not travel. I've never even thought about bed bugs and no one around us has ever had them either.

This property is just fantastic! Before we arrived, I contacted the hotel with questions about how to get around in the city. They got right back to me with directions and even offered to drive me to locations that were within a few miles of the hotel. The location turned out to be within walking distance to so many of San Diego's great attractions.
The staff was exceptionally friendly and welcoming. Our room was lovely and very comfortable. Coffee and tea was set up for guests in the morning, lemon or delicious cucumber water was out for us later in the day, and then a wine hour in the evening.
I felt at home here in this wonderful hotel in such a beautiful city. Sad to leave!

My sisters and I meet every December in San Francisco for plays, walking tours and shopping. We have stayed at the Cornell for the last 15 years, and it is always wonderful. It is a quick walk to Union Square, Chinatown, theaters and the financial district. Parking and breakfast in the delightful restaurant downstairs is included. This year they have added a small cafe for free coffee and tea which is the perfect meeting place. The hotel is decorated beautifully with different French artists honored on each floor. The hoted seems to get better every year!

title_masked: This is an excellent airport hotel !
text_masked:
I have been coming to this hotel on and off for years now. It is conveniently located adjacent to LAX airport and offers a free shuttle bus to and from the airport. All of the airport hotels that I know of, including this one, use a third party shuttle bus service (blue colored bus with a scrolling LED banner on the front with hotel names). This is important to know, because if you are looking for a shuttle bus that is branded with the Crowne Plaza logo's in its sides you will be looking forever.
Without question this is a very good hotel. The staff is friendly and very helpful. Check in and out has always been fast and the complimentary airport shuttle picks up and drops off about every 20 minutes. The hotel has a very good restaurant, a Starbucks Coffee shop, and a bar with live music on some nights. The food in the restaurant has consistently been very good to excellent. The assorted pasta salads on their food bar, and fresh fruits and vegetables in general, have been some of the freshest I have eaten anywhere. 
Being a Platinum level Priority Club member I usually get offered a room on the club lounge floor. Or at a minimum when there were no rooms available on the club floor I have been given access to the lounge. 
The lounge has both a mini breakfast and a lite dinner available. Breakfast includes fresh fruit, coffee and juices, cereal and oat meal, assorted breads and baked goods, and usually something like an Egg McMuffin or similar hot item. In the evening there is also fresh fruit, soft drinks and beer/wine, a cold vegetable plate, chips, plus some type of a hot dish - recently there were quesadillas. If on a tight budget and have access to the lounge one can save a lot of money by eating breakfast and dinner there. However the hotel's restaurant prices are not bad, and the food is uniformly very good.
The rooms themselves are large, clean, and well maintained. Beds are comfortable. The bathrooms have always been very clean and modern. The hotel is currently undergoing a renovation with everything scheduled to be completed by early 2013.
The one down side is that with this hotel being adjacent to LAX's runways it can get rather noisy if your room is on the airport side. If this is a concern ask for a room on the off airport side, it will make a big difference.

My husband and I stayed at the intercontinental for our 1st anniversary and it was great. The room was gorgous and the view was amazing. I book my room with a staff member named [NAME] and she was great, she got us a great room and suprised us with champage and chocolate covered strawberries to make our experiance that much more special. I would highly recommend this hotel.

title_masked: Great location at a good price
text_masked: The Comfort Inn has a great location and a good price. I attended a conference at the nearby Sheridan, about 2 blocks away. As compared to the conference price at the Sheridan, I paid $30.00 a night less, got free wi-fi, and the hotel offered a great breakfast. The hotel is located about 2 blocks from the 16th street pedestrian mall. The front office staff is very friendly and accommodating, and the use of the business center was free. It also is easy to get in and out of the hotel, as opposed to having to wind your way past multiple stores to get out.
We had a last minute rate...99 for 1 night before return to Venezuela. Great location! Clean and Large room. No breakfast

Found this hotel to be clean, quiet, with a very helpful and compliant staff. The beds and linens were wonderful and I would recommend it to anyone visiting NYC, As a former New Yorker, I return to the city almost every year and certainly would stay here again.

The "new" Algonquin is a treat indeed. This famous old beauty of literature and art has been reborn as an efficient, modern hotel that still retains its charm. The rooms are large enough with all new everything. The design may not appeal to all - but for us it did. The bath was smallish but with beautifully done. Morning coffee is free and good; a 24hr coffee center also has Keurig machines 24/7. Internet was good - real newspapers exist if you prefer. The lobby is filled with people chatting, having drinks or reading nearly all day. 
It is close to Times Square but not too close and the walk to Rockefellor Center and other mid town shopping and eating is easy.
It may not be for everyone but if you like beautiful old hotels with modern efficiency you'll like this.

title_masked: Nice Hotel, Great rooms, Excellent service
text_masked: We stayed here in the summer of 2012 and were very happy with the rooms. The rooms were roomy and the beds very comfortable. The service was excellent even though we were there at a very busy time. Very clean and comfortable. We would definitely stay here again.

This was our first stay at the Magnolia in Dallas. We’ve stayed at the Magnolia in Houston several times and could not resist the opportunity to try the Dallas property while there celebrating a birthday in late August. We had a “Guest Room” on the 26th floor (no. 2691) facing to the west with a view of Reunion Tower. The room was very spacious as was the bathroom with its separate tub and shower arrangement. The mattress and bedding were extremely comfortable. We had the opportunity to enjoy the complimentary evening glass of wine as well as a hot breakfast the next morning. The Dallas Magnolia location in Downtown was perfect for our needs as it was only a bit over two blocks to the nearest DART (Dallas Area Rapid Transit) train stop located on Pacific Ave. Though a few blocks further; it was also convenient for catching the free trolley service to the Uptown area of Dallas. To sum it up, the Magnolia never lets us down.

I very recently stayed in this hotel. I was looking forward to it based on the reviews. When I got there I found it was situated in a beautiful part of town and surrounded by fantastic restaurants. I walked into my room which was spacious and appeared a little old but well kept. I was there for three nights. After a very long day at work, i came back to find that my room was not serviced after the first night. I asked them to service it at 7 pm when i was leaving for dinner. Rather, room service woke me up from a nap at 6:00 pm and then again at 6:30 pm. I asked them repeatedly to please come at 7 when I leave. I went and came back from dinner and the room still was not serviced . . . siiigh. Forgot about it. I woke up and found that on closer inspection in the bathroom, there were these disgusting stains in the toilet like it had never been properly cleaned. I then found toenail clippings on the floor next to the chaise. They were not mine! I was thoroughly disgusted. That night, a large group of very drunk guys (part of a wedding) were roomed next to me and they continually tried to open the door which connects the two rooms. All in all, the visit was not up to the standard it has set for itself as a luxury hotel. Maybe closer to a 2 or 3 star hotel. I'm glad I was compensated (by my job) for my stay in this hotel.

We stayed at this hotel and was quite nice and not too long to drive into downtown Phoenix.
The rooms are clean, and the each day the rooms are serviced to a good standard. There is a breakfast on each morning which was a pleasant suprise and an added bonus.
The T.V's in the rooms could be updated with flat screens, but this is only a minor issue. Also the air condition units were the noisiest out of 7 hotels so far on this vacation.
The only negative experience was from a visiting junior baseball team who kept banging on doors at gone midnight with no concern for other guests, which I hoped the front desk staff would have dealt with but took care of this myself.
Other than that quite a pleasant stay and would use again if I visit Phoenix.

title_masked: Great location, staff couldn't do enough, superb service
text_masked: Stayed for 4 nights just over a week ago, cannot praise the Ritz Carlton enough, due in main to the brilliant , amiable and friendly way in which EVERY member of their staff went about their job. From the girl on reception who recommended I buy a telephone card, to the girl in the Spa who brought a set of hair straighteners up to our room once my wife realised she had left hers back in the UK, to the waitress downstairs in the main lobby bar who only served us once the day before, but greeted us like long lost friends the next day whilst we were waiting to go out. A great location, right on the Magnificent Mile, all the main shops within 5 minutes and an open top bus tour stop across the road. I have stayed in a number of hotels in different countries around Europe and the US, but I can safely say that this hotel tops the lot, and the next time I visit Chicago I would definitely stay here again. Room was great, loads of room, good air con, huge bed , comfy mattress, my wife actually has a bad back , and the next morning commented on how good a nights sleep she had, pulled the sheets back and checked the make of the mattress to see if we could get hold of one when we got home. Sometimes when writing a review , it is always helpful to put down what you liked least about a certain experience, sorry, but I can't, the whole Ritz Carlton experience was a joy , and to be honest the staff should be very proud of the job they do here, because they made our stay an extremely enjoyable one.

title_masked: Cheap, nice room in the middle of everything
text_masked: This hotel has great service and the room was clean and comfy. It is located right by Pratt Strett and it was 20 dollars cheaper per night than any other hotel in the Inner Harbor. Parking is reasonable as well at 23 bucks a day. You don't find much better than that in downtown Bmore. My only complaints are that there is no free breakfast and the hotel bar/restaurant closes at 10, which is too early. Thanks for a nice stay!

We decided to splurge at this property and get a suite. It was sweet alright! Two FULL bathrooms that were to die for! Almost a tad Vegas-y...looks like Teresa Guiduice could have been on the decorating team. LOL Very Italian villa like...but a nice contrast to most other hotels. The place exudes class. The attention to detail is amazing. Best example of attention to detail: when they would clean our room, they would wind up all the cords to our chargers, hairdryers, curling iron etc and tie it with a gold ribbon. So neat! I can't neglect to mention what they place on your pillow at night with turndown service....chocolate dipped Oreos!!!! Again, amazing! Our suite looked over the adult pool and hot tub. Looked amazing but never got to stick a toe in as I was with my children every moment of the visit...with the exception of the night they went to the kids camp...which by the way is very cool! My kids are veterans to resort kids camps and they thought this one was a 10. My children are 8/10. Pool was a bit of a haul from our room but we didn't mind. Grounds are lovely so the walk was not a problem.
Have to mention that the pool service was horrible the first day(Friday). Such a bummer. Luckily it turned around the next two days. 
Really hard to find much bad to say. We will definitely be back!

title_masked: Luxury in the heart of Seattle
text_masked:
We were lucky enough to score Hotel Monaco on Hotwire and since we had stayed at a Kimpton hotel in Atlanta we knew we were in for a nice treat! First off, I love the location of this hotel, it is in the heart of downtown and 1 block from a large bus stop. We were able to catch buses to many locations without having to transfer (score)! The lobby has some beautiful chandeliers and nice comfy chairs and couches. Our room wasn't ready when we checked in, but we were given a compliment upgrade to a higher floor which was definitely appreciated.
The rooms here are not your run of the mill hotel rooms, and thank goodness they are not! In my opinion, they are trendy, hip, modern, and beautiful. Our bed had a funky grey and white wall paper behind it, which was so cool. There were two lamps beside the bed that were cut in half lengthwise so they didn't jut out super far. There was an adorable little shelf in front of the window, in which you could totally sit down and read a book if you wanted to (I've always wanted one of these). They had cute white wooden shutters and our view was of the architectural marvel, the Seattle library. The bathroom was also very nice and had a cool sliding door.
We were very comfortable here for the 3 nights that we stayed. I was a little annoyed that they didn't offer free internet and I had to become a Kimpton member to get the free wifi, but we are staying in another Kimpton in Portland so really not a huge deal. The staff at the front desk were very kind, but some of the other staff members were cold. I know they also offer two cool amenities that we did not take advantage of, you can have a goldfish delivered to your room and they have a complimentary wine hour, very inventive and fun. Overall, this hotel has a fantastic location and the rooms are modern but comfortable and decorated in a fun way. I would stay here again without hesitation.

title_masked: A Wonderful hotel to stay in when visiting Boston
text_masked: I have stayed in the Westin Copley Place on more than once when visiting Boston. The location is great, easy to walk to the many sights, restaurants and shopping. The hotel rooms are spacious and beautiful. The staff could not be more helpful.

title_masked: Good location, nice rooms, a bit noisy
text_masked:
Fantastic location for exploring San Francisco, and not as manky as the neighborhood where the other two SF Hilton's are. The onsite restaurant was a bit of a surprise--- much better than the usual hotel restaurant fare and while it's a bit pricey to dine in the hotel, it's on par with hotel dining anywhere. Beds are comfortable and the room was perfectly clean. All staff was helpful, friendly and professional. 
The only negative was that, like many older hotels, there's a fair bit of hallway noise (I can deal with street noise in an urban setting), and their big event space attracts lots of large groups which can translate to noisy neighbors, but one call to the front desk usually gets things calmed down.
Executive lounge was comfortable, well-appointed but a bit small for the size of the hotel so time your visit accordingly.
Great views from the lounge and from our room!
Overall we were happy with our stay and will be happy to stay again.

My recent Distrikt stay of 4/12 - 4/16 couldn't have been better. The rooms were on the 18th floor which overlooked the city. The staff at check in were friendly and efficient. Gave us dining recommendations. Assisted with cabs. Rooms were very clean. Beds were very comfortable. A/C was nice and cold.
You will not be disappointed.

I had stayed at this hotel last week for four nights and the only complaint that I have is the size of the rooms and showers but the location is great, staff was very friendly, hotel was clean and the hotel restaurant was very good.... Overall, I had a very good experience and would stay here again if the price was right.

title_masked: Buyer beware of customer satisfaction policies
text_masked:
I'll be as fair as I can. Lovely lobby, great location. We're currently staying for the week, but thought to get our warning out early to potentially save other people their hard-earned money.
The other reviews are accurate - small rooms, loud AC... we were prepared for this. We were not prepared for mattresses with no box springs (just wood supports = extremely hard beds), lumpy pillows like rolled up socks, and *vibration* of the bed from the loud permanent AC, which is inches from your head, given the size of these rooms, and earplugs don't stop this. Unfortunately, the warning to those considering a "boutique" hotel is that, unlike any other hotel you may have stayed at, payment is NOT due at checkout, and you cannot simply leave and go elsewhere if you are unsatisfied. From their website, carefully buried, emphasis theirs, not mine:
Cancellation Policy:
Cancellation and/or Changes must be received by The Washington Jefferson Hotel by NOON hotel time at least 72 hours prior to arrival. No Refunds, No Changes and No Cancellations. FULL PAYMENT AT TIME OF BOOKING. .
Reservations must be made with a valid credit card or the hotel will not confirm. 
So, if you don't like your room, your stay, or your trip, go jump. Whaddya want? We'll take your money first, and then nuts to you! This is New York!
Read the fine print, folks.

A great atmosphere inside and out! Rooms are spacious, modern, and clean! Staff is wonderful and you can tell they love their jobs! Close to shopping, great dining and easily accessible to downtown. Will definitely return on our next visit to the area!

I booked through Hotwire at a rate of $60 per night. My wife and I were traveling with our three young children (oldest is 8) for quick weekend getaway. It was perfect for our family: close to Dallas attractions we were visiting, great pool, welcoming staff. No complaints and couldn't beat the price.
Had I paid full price, I might express some reservation about the hotel's age and slight need of a facelift. Still, it's not enough to keep me from recommending it.

Like many other trip advisor reviewers my "review" began the moment we arrived. I am glad I waited a few days until I commented because the hotel did grow on me a bit. 
For one the location is great. Easily within walking distance to many things including the Magnificent Mile, Starbucks, Corner Bakery, a small grocery store, Millenium Park, Wildberry's Pancakes and the River.
Rooms are surprisingly small and the bathrooms are really poor even though they are new in design. There is no counter space and zero storage space so your toothbrushes, etc are dangling on to the sink ledge. 
We upgraded our room for the view which we really did enjoy and while it was an extra $20 it was worth it. 
Gym is decent but sadly there is no pool. They do have many services on location such as hair salon, dry cleaners and store. Parking is pricey at $50+ overnight.
This is a very large hotel spread between 2 towers. We stayed in the West tower due to our view upgrade which meant that you have little interaction with the main hotel & restaurants. They do nothing to lure you over to the other tower & thats a missed opportunity for them I believe. Most times that we crossed through our lobby in the west tower there was not even a single person from the hotel to greet us or assist us. That made us question the safety issue even though there were no problems for us and you do need your room key to enter the elevator after 10:30pm.
We had great sound proofing & really thought this to be a huge benefit of the hotel until our last night when we had a couple of lovebirds rent the room next to us with a less than sound proof adjoining door.
We expected more from this hotel & with so many hotels to choose from we were somewhat disappointed. I think when you are choosing to stay in a hotel over a holiday to some degree you want to feel welcomed, wanted & important. 
**I also want to mention that we checked with the front desk staff on Thanksgiving dinner upon our check-in 3 days prior to the day and they were "not sure" if a Thanksgiving meal was even being offered.

This hotel is in a great location - close to Prudential Center, food, other shopping and bars. The staff was super friendly and attentive. We spent a few hours up at the rooftop pool - it was really fun. Drinks were a little pricey but we were on a long weekend vacation so what the heck! The sheets on the bed were to die for!! We would definitely return.

title_masked: The best thing about this hotel?...location...
text_masked: and the front desk staff. The hotel is nice...very modern and cool looking. But as a guest you get the sense that the hotel management rely too heavily on these facts and do very little else to make this an outstanding hotel. It is a W, so with that comes a few givens: nice showers, spa amenities, cool lounge. But this was hardly the best W of the chain. Not terrible, but nothing "special", which is surprising for a big city like Boston.

We had a great stay at the Allerton and didn't experience any of the issues other reviewers have mentioned. The room was nice and big enough (likely because we got upgraded from a queen to a king room), the location was perfect, and hotel staff were fine. It would have been great to have a coffee maker in the room, but that's a small complaint in the scheme of things. We'd definitely stay there again.

spent 5 nights in this hotel in august great hotel with really nice modern rooms and a great pool. close to san diego down town and beaches several places to eat nearby. the only downside was the 16 dollars a night parking fee but would recommend this hotel.

title_masked: Awesome Stay ! Brings back some old memories too
text_masked: Used to go to The Ohio State University for college and the apartment I used to stay is in close proximity. This HIE never used to exist then (I asked the lady at front and she said they built this in 2010). There are so many hotels nearby and this place is so close to the University, Downtown and the stadium for games. Coming back to the hotel, the rooms are so neat and clean. I got this huge room, elegant looking with excellent painting on the wall. The TV's were new and flat screen. Took care of rooms every day, clean bathrooms, huge space for dresses. Did not get a chance to try their breakfast, but expecting a typical HIE station (not sure though). There are so many food options nearby (literally walking distance); like Subway, McD, Burger King, a Kebab place and Canes (Chicken fingers place, awesome one!). Grocery store 'Kroger' is also few minutes walk from this place. There is public transportation right in front of the hotel that can take you to the University and other nearby places. Since it is a University town, the public transportation is pretty decent. This place is awesome and will come back and stay here if I ever get a chance to go back to Columbus.

Stayed here for work in November, 2012 for one night.
.
While I was a little alarmed at the size of the room and the space to navigate, I was very pleased with the courtesy of the staff and the design of the hotel.
.
My only complaint is about the bathroom door. It did not exactly give a lot of privacy. I understand why they used pocket doors, but it was slightly uncomfortable to be there with a colleague.
.
My colleague and I had the chance to enjoy the rooftop bar, it was very lovely. It was unseasonably warm in New York and the atmosphere was very nice.
.
The beds were very comfortable and after having neck pain for almost a month in my own bed, I was pleased to wake up and not have neck pain after my sleep. The pillows were clearly just what my body was looking for.
.
Two thumbs up!

On many occasions I have had the luck to surprise my wife for what ever reason it happened to be. Sometimes just because I love her. It was our 21st anniversary and I wanted to do something really special. I had been to the Magnolia Hotel a couple of times just to hear some jazz bands play. I thought then that the Hotel was very nice and quaint. I made several trips to the Hotel and talked to the front desk who was extremely helpful. I knew that I was going to need rooms for my children and their spouses as well as a couple for some close friends that didn't need to be driving late at night and of course something for my wife and self. They set me up with the marketing department who understood what I wanted to do. The Hotel is a very nice boutique hotel that is warm and friendly. They have a comp wine/beer happy hour every evening followed later that evening with delicious milk and cookies prior to bed time. The rooms and suites are very reasonable (especially on weekends). I didn't want to do this party in just a meeting or ball room. The hotel had adjoining the Restaurant a room that they called the "LIBRARY". It was above average in size with stocked bookcases surrounding the room and a large table in the center. Not wanting to do a sit down dinner for 40 they suggested doing a appetizer style serving. This worked great, I had fajita's, premium nachos, cheese/fruit platters (wonderful), specialty dip trays and gumbo (I didn't think everyone would want this so I only bought for 10......it was fantastic). Along with this was coffee, tea and water. I opted to have a cash bar from the bar for those that wanted something else. Those that were left came up to our suite afterwards for into the mourning conversation.
You could not ask for a better price for what they offered for a suite. With full kitchen. Not to mention the great comp breakfast in the mourning. They have a small pool and hot tub on the roof just past the fully equipped gym. Being as this is on the 23 floor roof and is basically cement needless to say it was fairly hot to the foot and back on the chairs.
On Thursday before the stay on Friday the Hotel sent my wife's boss an invitation for a free two night stay (he was in on the surprise) which he offered to us because (wink wink) they couldn't stay. The trap is now set and off we go on Friday for our weekend stay. After checking in 4 of our friends showed up and the Hotel carried us to III FORKS steak house. Afterwards they picked us up and carried us to the Alley to see "BLACK COFFEE", then picked us up and returned us to the Hotel. Everyone always smiling.

title_masked: Great central spot in the Windy City
text_masked: We spent a week in this hotel and had a wonderful time. Friendly and helpful staff. Breakfast was standard for Hampton and always enjoyed. Room was large and quiet on the 12th floor. If you want to be in the Loop this is it as the Blue EL is half a block west and the Red El is half a block east, and the buses on State street take you just about anywhere.

title_masked: One of the best hotel experiences
text_masked: Fantastic boutique hotel with quality service. The rooms seemed new and I'd definitely recommend this hotel to a friend.

Stayed for 2 nights in the W Hotel DC, check-in was very professional and offered me a choice of rooms due to my platinum status. However, on second night there was music until 1:30am in the bar upstairs that I could hear in my room. Called the concierge repeatedly and they said "this is the W experience". The concierge was rude and dismissive. They're more concerned with their bar guests experience than their business travellers sleep on a Thursday night.
Not staying here again.

This is my review on Memphis and Nashville we travelled as 2 couples celebrating my sister in laws special birthday from 17th September to the 25th, we stayed at the Holiday Inn Select Downtown Memphis, our 1st reaction when we arrived at the hotel was that it was a bit dated but then when you realise why you are in Memphis you are almost going back in time, the room was a nice size bathroom little bit small but ok.
The staff there are excellent willing to help you in anyway, the night security man was pretty cool he would allow us to bring a beer from Beale street and sit in the lounge area of reception, the hotel does food but we didn't eat there, the bar was pretty good reasonably priced for a bud in fact most of the bars in Beale street charge the same $3.50 remember the tip. 
The reason we booked this hotel was that it was close to Beale street as the receptionist told me it takes 5 minutes to get there and 25 minutes to swagger home....
Sun studios is on the same street as the hotel approx 20 minute walk, turn left outside the hotel and you will get there, this is worth going to see especially if you're into Elvis or Johnny Cash we went on our 1st morning the weather was great and so was sun studios you will learn a great deal.
Now Beale street is worth a mention if you have never heard of it it is basically about Blues, Booze and BBQ some many places to drink, eat and party our favourite place was the Blues City Cafe which do the meanest ribs what totally melt in your mouth, they own the corner so even when the bar is shut down, they are open on the corner you can even have a take away, we did Ribs, chicken and catfish all very good washed down with a bud(burp) lite, supposedly they even deliver world wide.
The main reason for going to Memphis was obviously to go and see Gracelands we did this on my sister in laws birthday, now the hotel will book this for you for $44 you will be picked up at a certain time and dropped back at a certain time, now i have travelled from the UK i don't want to be rushed so we made our own way there taxi $30 then we took the VIP package at $70 dollars per person, this allows you to go into Gracelands as many times as you like unlike the other tour plus you get to see some other things like Lisa Marie talking about her dad. 
What can i say about Gracelands very tranquil and i would rate 20/10 we loved every minute of it we arrived just before 11am and left after 5pm by the end of this i was all Elvis upped!!! We even signed our names near the gates make sure you take a permanent marker!!!
The next day we were going to Nashville and staying at the Best Western Plus Music Row about 20 minutes walk away from Broadway, now 1st of all nice hotel but NO bar, room was nice the weather was very hot as we were staying for 2 nights on bed and breakfast terms i was quite looking forward to breakfast, ok the only good thing for me personally was that you can make your own waffles, now paper plates and plastic knives n forks for a BEST WESTERN PLUS different standards in UK!!!!! what i ate was, well not quite sure whether it was meant to be a slab of omelette or scrambled egg anyway wasn't very nice for me.
Now i will give you a little advice if you fancy going to Nashville and your not driving book the Mega bus in the Uk cost us 4 adults just over £5 return serious it is a 4 hour journey with wi-fi and toilet on board, not too busy but if you book like we did 1 month before you will get a brilliant deal, they also do a pit stop for a McDonalds and a stretch of legs.
