Nightlife in Nashville is on the main strip called BROADWAY beer here varies from pub to pub from $4=$6 plus dont forget to tip even the bands want a tip, music in Memphis blues fantastic, music in Nashville country now i'm not a great lover of country i like Johnny Cash but very good nevertheless, even in the short time we were in Nashville we even met the Kings of Leon who were getting a walk of fame award. All in all Nashville was excellent....
Back to Memphis on Saturday for another party on Beale street we were not dissapointed and so was the Sunday, opposite the Holiday Inn Select there is the famous Peabody Hotel if you know anything about this hotel it is about the ducks marching to the lift ....have your camera ready!!!
On the Sunday we went to the civil rights museum where Martin Luther King was shot and killed at the Lorraine motel this is very interesting but also very sad, worth a visit get the tram down it's only $1 make sure you have the right note..
The only downside to Memphis was that there is too many beggars, all quite friendly just asking for food as it's the law NOT to give them money as you can get arrested as well as them....
ALL IN ALL WE HAD A FANTASTIC TIME IN MEMPHIS & NASHVILLE AND RECOMMEND TO ANYONE FROM THE AGE OF 21 AND UP.....ENJOY

This was a tremendously disappointing trip to the Admiral Fell Inn. Let me start by saying that we stayed at the Admiral Fell last summer and loved it. It was quaint, in a nice part of town, well kept, and super nice visit. So, when we had to go to Baltimore again this summer for my step-daughter's graduation we booked five rooms at the Admiral Fell for ourselves and various family members. This year's room was not nearly as charming as last year's. The carpet was dirty. The bathroom door did not close. The sheets, and especially the pillow cases were pilled and rough. I actually checked to make sure there was actually a pillow case on the pillow. When we checked in there was only one person working, and he was dealing with a pretty hysterical guest who could not get her car out of the garage (it was flooded, and oh by the way, our valet is off). The valet was off? Really? He then turned to us and said he hoped we found parking because there was no valet on duty. Sigh. Nice start. He did find out for the hysterical guest that her car was on the third floor and was safe, not like the cars on the first floor, like another guest's BMW that was under 2 feet of water. Okay, more. Not once when any of us in any of our five reserved rooms called the from desk, was there anyone there to answer. My in-law's toilet broke, and my father-in-law had to go down to the front desk (as we were getting home from the movies), and he had to wait for someone to show up at the front desk, explaining that his toilet was not working, and why was no one answering the phone at the desk. The guy at the front desk said, "well, I have been trying to get someone without a reservation checked in all night. I will have someone look at your toilet." It was about 10:00 p.m. and he asked, "when?" Front desk man answered in a clipped tone, "Tonight." Really? You have an 83 year old man standing in front of you and that is your answer. When asked if there was a manager on duty the answer was, "no." Nice customer service. We did find out as the toilet was being fixed a bit later that there is one person who works as the handyman for three local hotels. Finally, the noise is untenable! The hotel was not crazy noisy last year. This year it was insanely noisy! There is a bar or something next door with live music, police activity, etc. It felt like they were in our room and we are on the fourth floor. It was just... not good. Not coming back.

We stayed at Night Hotel for our 20th anniversary and it was our first trip without our two children. The location is perfect and the hotel is very trendy. Staff are extremely friendly and helpful. Rooms are on the smaller size, but then again we are used to having an extra bed in the room. We did not eat at the hotel but did have drinks where atmosphere is great and the employees were great too!

I stayed at the Bristol for one night while on a business trip in May. 
The room was quiet. The bed was comfortable. The room and bathroom were clean. Connecting with the WiFi was easy. The bill was accurate. 
The staff were friendly. I didn't eat or drink there. The location was convenient for the train station and the Gas Lamp (I didn't have a car).
I would definitely stay there again.

title_masked: Comfy place to spreadout and chill for the weekend
text_masked:
Did a 2 night getaway for the weekend and decided to stay at the Sheraton since we never have been there and both Westins and the W seem to have construction going on right now. Self parking was different; it's a structure in the building and doesn't start until you spiral up to level 7, but get yourself to level 11 and take the elevator to level 12 for check-in. Valet at the street was helpful and courteous. Check in desk was very friendly and got us our club upgrade we wanted. We ended up at the top floor and on the end so I think we got lucky with a quiet room and a nice view. The room was suite setup which made it roomy for us staying the 2 days and we were able to chill in the room and spread out a little. You can definitely here your neighbors when they were in the hallway but we heard nobody from other rooms.
We visited the workout room it had various cardio and one weight center, no free weights. It was very small but did provide what we both needed. Indoor pool we didn't use, but some other folks were enjoying it one morning. 
We enjoyed the breakfast buffet and the lounge both days. Cook to order omelets and all the normal hot and cold breakfast items. Fruit was awesome.
Self - Parking was $24 a day and it was in and out all day which we did use a couple of times, but most of the time we just walked through Gaslamp district.

I travel to the medical center on an annual basis and this hotel continues to provide me with the best of service and comfort. The staff is very accommodating and friendly. The breakfast staff works hard to please the guests. The shuttle drivers go "the extra mile" in more ways than one! And the front desk personnel are very willing to help and answer questions about the area. I will be staying here again next year. By the way, they do have a medical rate available which helps with the expense.

title_masked: Small but clean, comfortable and so close to Times Square!
text_masked:
The room was small, yes. However the fact that you are literally right on Times Square makes up for it! It was very clean and as a single female travelling on my own, it was perfect for me to use as a safe and comfortable base to see New York. 
The free wifi was also a great plus - I was able to work remotely with no problems at all!
Also the bed was very comfortable.
Checkout was 12pm and it was also great that they minded my bags after I checked out for only $1 per bag.

Just got back from a weekend at this resort. This place was chosen by my husband's employer for incentive/awards weekend for the top so many employees and their wives. When my husband checked in at the front desk, they told him there was a mix up on the rooms. We were assigned a horrible tiny room which we promptly complained to the front deskl. We should've been assigned one of the lagoom front bungalows. Apparently the place was full for the weekend and after so many phone calls between the manager and the employer's person in charge of this event, we were supposedly upgraded to a room with a "lanai." Upgrade? Lanai was strewn with dead leaves and the patio furnitures were filthy with mold on them. We complained to the manager again and they moved us to "another upgrade" but this time, no lanai but still filthy patio furnitures, now facing the road. At least this room was slightly larger and had a couch. But the bathroom sink had a huge crack in it, no air ventilation in the bathroom and the a/c could barely keep up with the hot afternoon sun pounding on the windows and the door. The maid never showed up to make the bed or give us fresh towels until almost 4:30 in the afternoon the following day. At that time, we were in the room resting and didn't want to be bothered with her taking out the trash or making the bed. We just told her to give us fresh towels. When we went to do express checkout, the gal said we owed them over $100 in room charges. They charge for parking for you to park in your designated space next to the bungalow!!! And we didn't even drive there; we caught a ride with another couple!!!. Another charge was an erroneous bill that we didn't even charge at the bar and grill!!!

This hotel is just 1-2 blocks off the main mall. The room is spacious and comfortable. The staff are friendly and were able to help me hook up the TV to my laptop so that I can have more screen space for my work. The gym is nice too. However, wifi is not complementary in the room.
No complaints staff was nice rooms were clean fine for our family

title_masked: An Upper West Side, NY Treasure
text_masked: This hotel was the cleanest hotel I have ever stayed in. It was easy to get to local attractions. The staff was extremely friendly and never stopped smiling, even during construction going on. The room was beautiful but quaint. We had plenty of room even with two adults and two children. They only charged us $45 for overnite parking and they kept our car for 26 hours with no additional cost. All I can say is a total amazing experience!!!

title_masked: Lost its Swagger - Just a Convention Hotel
text_masked: Back in the day, this hotel hosted presidents and Hollywood functions. It never was the Four Seasons or Peninsula, but it delivered a quality product, and its design and lobby became an iconic (if not dated) part of the hotel world in Los Angeles. I started staying here in the 1990s when it was part of the Starwood/Westin chain.... now, it's a Hyatt. While I've stayed at a few decent ones in that chain (Beaver Creek and Chicago's Park Hyatt), this hotel is now a crowded and tired shadow of its former self. For one thing, they've obviously cornered the market on giant conventions of middle-aged, suburban women from middle America. In three of my last four random stays over the past 5 years, I have encountered 3 different estrogen conventions - 1)a dubious looking talent agency casting call for teen girl models and actresses 2) a scrap-booking convention (not joking), and now, a children's book writer convention. You'd think the hotel would ramp-up its staff to handle the giant crowds, but they only had 2 people working the front desk and some people had to wait hours for their rooms. The elevators and common areas were all cramped with loud, excited women with name tags. When I came back from an evening out, an entire side of the building's elevators had broken down as well. I always used to look forward to using their gym/spa (now an Equinox Club) but the harried person at the front desk told me that it costs an additional $20 a day from the price of the room. I guess they figure since they're turned the hotel in a Vegas-style convention hotel, they may as well start charging Vegas prices. My room seems to have the same furniture, paint job, artwork and carpet that I remember from 20 years ago - with the exception of a flat-screen TV. I stopped counting all the scuff marks and paint chips in the room and patio because there were so many and it was just depressing. Even worse, they've taken the bathrobes out of the rooms - I guess they figure their typical customer now wouldn't miss them. I don't want to sound like a snob, and I truly feel lucky that work (usually) puts me up in really nice hotels. But I no longer consider staying here a perk. It's more of a problem. The only positives are that they didn't get rid of some of the nice staff who were here in old days - and somehow, they're managing to still be friendly, despite working for such a worse a hotel. Despite being full, room-service was prompt and good (except the toast was clearly some cheap store=bought bread). Instead of feeling like I was staying at a classy joint, I felt like my plane landed in Vegas instead of Los Angeles, and that my taxi took me to Circus Circus instead of the Century Plaza.

title_masked: Close to Everything, but in a Quiet Area
text_masked: We booked this hotel after hearing of it through a Southwest Airlines email and were very satisfied. Unlike what other reviewers stated, the elevator was just fine and worked faster than the one at my office. The room was super clean. Large, flat screen TV worked great. Amazing shower with great water pressure. It's a two minute walk to the Magnificent Mile and three blocks from the Red Line subway to get everywhere else. It was our first time to Chicago and we had a great time. The Raffaello was a perfect anniversary trip hotel. I'd highly recommend looking online and calling the hotel directly (what I did) for lower rates than what is on their site.

Overall, we had a great experience at this hotel. Here's what you should expect.
Pros:
•Attractive lobby with nice seating area
•Very nice staff
•Lively lobby bar
•Comfortable, minimalist rooms - those who prefer more traditional luxury will not appreciate it
•Very convenient to The Domain shopping area, within walking distance
•On site restaurant
•Free self-parking
Cons:
•Other than The Domain shopping and restaurants, there is nothing to walk to. This hotel is squarely in a suburban area.
•Expensive, given the area it is located in
•Restaurant service is slow
westin lax was a great value with good service and ammenities would definetely stay again

The Inn at Sunset Cliifs is a wonderful, aptly named little hotel looking out over the Pacific near the coastal area of Ocean Beach. The folks here are kind, helpful and pleasant. My girlfriend and I stayed here for two days during a west coast vacation and this was by far our favorite place. I actually chose the Inn as the location to propose to my then girlfriend and now fiancee, and the staff was extremely helpful in assisting me anything to setup the proposal (and Leo even took pictures for me! Thanks!). Sunsets here are truly breathtaking and all of the comfortable seating allows for a wonderful spot to read, relax and take it all in.
The rooms are small, but clean and very decent. The bathroom was updated and shower excellent. The bed we found to be a little too firm (on the verge of hard) for our liking, but this was our only "con". You'll find coffee in the morning and several helpful suggestions of places to grab breakfast in OB (Check out Shores, their omelets were excellent). This is a 15 drive to downtown or less than that to the Zoo.
The rooms may be slightly more expensive than other places in the area, but i think the combination of location and service outweigh the slight cost, which is still completely reasonable. We plan to stay here again on our next trip through San Diego.

My wife and I attended 3 broadway shows in 3 days and found the Wyngate location to be convenient (within walking distance and the subways are close by) and comfortable. The room was comfortable and we used our Wyndham Rewards points to book it. The front desk staff were most helpful and a lot of fun. We will be back and try the free breakfast next time (other reviews said it was good).

title_masked: Great staff, clean modern rooms - recommend this hotel
text_masked:
We stayed here after a driving vacation to see colleges in Boston before flying home. The location is right next to the UMass stadium & near the JFK Library, a few minutes from downtown. Easy to get to but we definitely needed the GPS to navigate Boston's exits getting here. The lobby is large and modern with many cozy seating areas, free wireless access, a bar, and a deli located right off the lobby.
The staff was friendly, professional and provided clear direct answers to questions. I love Doubletree's custom of their warm cookie check-in greeting! Overnight parking was in a gated lot behind the hotel. 
Our room was on a higher floor overlooking the parking lot, the bay and Logan airport. There was very little noise from the planes in the room. Our room had 2 doubles, which was roomy enough for our family of 4. It had a desk with internet access, a small fridge & double cup coffee maker. The bathroom had a tub/shower & the standard amenities. 
The shuttle driver took us to a nearby restaurant which was convenient. 
One tip: The business center computers were 1970s slow due to video gamers gumming up the servers. Let the staff know. Once they were alerted to the issue, they dealt with it right away & offered their personal computers so that I could check-in for our flights while the servers rebooted. Kudos for making sure customers needs were met efficiently. 
Recommend staying here. Very nice hotel with a good location to get around Boston either by car or mass transit, & great helpful staff. Also very economical when comparing prices compare total costs including coffee, parking, internet access. We saved lots by staying here!

This hotel was really good. The hotel was hip and it was close to everything we wanted...restaurants, Central Park, 5th Ave shopping, bars and Broadway. We love walking in the city and didn't need a cab for anything.
We would come back again in a minute and wish our stay was longer than the two nights we stayed!!

title_masked: Great Hotel, Great Service, Great Location
text_masked:
Stayed here for a short business trip and found the staff to be extremely friendly and willing to attend to your every need. It has a very modern vibe and the rooms are clean and well appointed with granite baths, one touch shades, and comfy beds. Was placed on a smoking floor and they moved me as soon as I asked for a change. I asked for a bottle of bubble bath and returned from dinner to find a full bath drawn for me--now that's service. Excellent location on Magnificent Mile and walking distance to everything.
 I would have given it 5 stars, but due to time constraints I did not experience Nomi restaurant, the spa or the fitness center. Would absolutely stay here again!

Our father's day was an unexpected stay..We were visiting San Diego for the day happend to drive by Paradise Point and decided to spend the night because we knew the stay would be both great and fun from our previous 4th of July week last year..Need less to say again fantastic...
Thank you so much, Julie,Thom and Ron (front desk) for another wonderful experience
at Paradise Point..
See you all again next month..July 4th...

title_masked: Best overnight retreat for a party of one!
text_masked: If your looking for a quick get away, pampering and exercise included then this is the place. Don't let the location fool you, stuffy and pretentious are not their style. The staff make you feel at home. Start with a massage at Trellis, ask for a recommendation, not all massuses are alike. Have lunch at Olivette, the Tres Leches or Chocolate lava desserts are decadent. Pair with any alchohol infused coffee beverage. Relax in The Bar, order a drink, dessert and read your book, that's right a bar so quiet you can read there! When your traveling solo this is a plus. Take a walk early morning on the outdoor track. Then take a yoga class with their exceptional instructors. The Tension Body wrap is a great way to end the stay. Room service was prompt and food was good. Four rating instead of five was only because the bed sheets were not soft and a former military must have made the bed, and the rug in the room was dated. But minor details! I live in Houston, wanted a getaway weekend that was not pricey or awkard for being solo, but polished! Got it!

Good value for the price you pay. We were visiting Sea World, the motel was around 10-15 minute drive, but worth the drive for the savings. The beds were more comfortable than other motels we've stayed in. We didn't get their free breakfast in time, so we ordered tacos from the restaurant around the back of the parking lot, which I recommend! 12 taco pack for $12. The pool was nice & maintained well. All the workers including security were friendly.

Victor at the concierge desk helped make this wonderful trip to Chicago even better. He started my day off on a happy note, greeting me as I wondered over to Starbucks. He made several perfect suggestions about things to do, how to navigate, and how to find the best prices. It was a treat and Victor made it all the better. Thank you!

We come to LA on business twice a month and find the convenience, value and service sets them apart from any other options in the LAX area. 
Newly renovated rooms are a plus. Highly recommend for the busy traveler like us looking for a business-freindly hotel with lots of extras.

I read the reviews before booking, being a Hilton diamond member I had certain expectations, which this hotel did not deliver. Besides that they are in a middle of renovations, the whole hotel was upside down,calling front desk-half hour on hold, going to breakfast- half hour waiting for a table..parking fees are outrageous, at least five times greater than other Hilton hotels. Very dissapointed!

Stayed for two weekend nights and everything was great. Typical Courtyard with redone lobby. Everything was clean. Very handy location off I805 and close to I5. Good place to stay if touring San Diego as Parking Is Free here.

This hotel is very-well kept. The onsite restaurant has reasonable rates and good-quality food. I enjoyed breakfast and lunch as well. The location is convenient to the convention center, has an adjacent parking garage, and is within hiking distance of major shopping, dining, and attraction centers. The bed was comfortable, the room was very clean. One of the nice touches: bottled water and snack waiting in the room at arrival. The staff was very knowledgeable about the local area and always pleasant. Rob, one of the security staff was able to direct me to some of the best (cheapest that is) parking near one of the shopping areas I wanted to go to. It is fairly higher priced than competitors a few miles further out, but more than worth it for the convenience, security, and comfort.

This hotel was terrible value for money. They charge something like 300+ US$. They give you a tiny cubby hole of a room. The room does not have any closet so you are forced to live out of a suitcase. The aircon controls are fake – everything is controlled centrally so you may alternately freeze and sweat. When I came back from dinner on the first night, I found that the AC was not working. On calling reception, I got some ‘We’ll take care of it’ sort of reply. After 15 minutes, I went downstairs to complain and the reception said that the ‘AC Maintenance’ person was busy and would shortly be putting the AC on – 15 minutes to put on an AC switch??? They also do not have a breakfast area – ostensibly because ‘there are many restaurants’ in the area. While the hotel and the room was relatively clean, that is the only positive. I should have checked the ratings on Tripadvisor instead of looking solely at Expedia. I would not recommend this hotel to anybody, no matter how desperate.
A.K.Mondal
Mumbai

Travelled here on business last week and then extended our stay through weekend with my husband. My second time here. You cannot beat this location - what a view and excellent vantage point to take in the best of chicago!. Rooms are beautiful and loved the large bathroom. Beds and pillows are great - I slept so well!!
I ran each morning along the river and lake - what a great way to start the day!
The staff at the desk were very helpful and accommodating. We loved sitting outside Hoyt's and on Saturday, they had a live band...great touch!! 
First choice for my next stay!!

I attended a conference at this hotel. My room on the 23rd floor was spacious and had a fabulous view of the city and the river. The price seemed reasonable for such a great location. The bed was comfortable and the room was quiet. The public spaces of the hotel are also very nice. My only complaint is that the banquet food was simply awful. It was worse than a cheap cafeteria. All around the room I could see people picking at their tasteless, overcooked pasta on the first day and their soggy, heavy eggplant parmesan on the second day. So by all means stay here, but think twice about having your wedding or catered meeting here.

Extremely modern and comfortable. I thought the value for money was outstanding. The location isn't close to downtown but the area around the hotel is much nicer than downtown in any case. The restaurant may be a little overprices but is very nice and the bar / pool areas are beautiful. Highly reccomended.

I stayed at La Quinta on business and while it was absolutely fine, I did expect a little bit more. The things that disappointed me were the lack of minibar, lack of tea/coffee making facilities, lack of wardrobe and lack of bathtub. Also, the bed covers did not seem to properly fit my bed - when tucked in at the bottom they came up well short of the pillows - when I yanked them up so I would be covered up to my neck, they failed to cover my feet! Weird. For me, these are basics that I expect. There is room service of a sort, but it is provided by an external restaurant so my order was pretty cold by the time it reached me.
On the plus side the complimentary breakfast has a good selection, the location is great and all the staff I encountered were friendly and helpful.

Check-in was very slow. I had received an email that breakfast was on them, but found out since we had a "special" rate, that we didn't qualify for the free breakfast.
While the location was great, the staff was less than friendly. The rooms were very outdated. We had a deluxe room, so size was fine for 2 people. Mold in the bathroom. Very few outlets for chargers. Mattress was less than comfortable which you need in New York after being up and out early and coming back late.
Ate at the Edison Cafe -- a little pricey and they only take cash. Food was alright. Only 1 waitress was the least bit friendly.
Would we stay there again, I doubt it.

Beautiful rooms with spacious bathrooms. Housekeeping service is fast, efficient and practically invisible. Concierge desk is very helpful at arranging everything from finding a restaurant for dinner to arranging a day trip to the mountains. The restaurant is one of the best places for a steak dinner.

title_masked: NOT a 4 Star Plus Hotel Experience
text_masked:
My daughter and granddaughter and I selected this hotel for our 2 night stay in Chicago. We wanted a 4 star + hotel on Michigan Ave. in order to enjoy museums, shopping and restaurants. 
We had a nice trip, but also had several issues during our stay that left us disappointed.
Therefore, I do NOT feel that I received fair value for the cost of the room. I have no complaints about the cleanliness or appearance of the room, and the staff was quite accommodating, however here are the expectations that were NOT met.
The bathroom is smaller than expected with only 1 sink.
I hoped for a make up mirror in a 4 + star hotel.
I hoped to be provided with 2 complimentary cups of coffee available with the coffee maker when there are 2 adults in the room (with lids?).
I hoped for a closet that is not filled with a dresser meaning there is no room for shoes, an empty suitcase or clothes that hang lower than 30 inches..
I hoped for a complimentary paper on weekday mornings.
I hoped that the ice machine on the floor would be in working working order.
I hoped for an uncrowded inviting lobby area with ample seating. 
I think the front desk could have been more amply staffed, perhaps so that I would not have had to wait in line for 15 minutes to collect my keys after an early registration, especially with a tired 6 year old.
I was disappointed that wine glasses were nowhere to be found in the room when wine is available in the mini bar. I don't want to have to have to make a call and wait for glassware to be delivered. 
Most 4 star + hotels have cotton balls, cue tips, a shower cap and a shoe buff in the bathroom amenities.
I prefer Queen size beds NOT doubles in a twin room.
I expect that if I am paying $328/night before taxes that internet access would not be an additional $18/day.
I usually stay at Hyatts, Omnis, Westins and Marriotts and an occasional Four Seasons, and thought that the Intercontinental would be comparable. I am sorry to say it is not so in my estimation.

title_masked: Nice Hotel just outside of downtown
text_masked:
Stayed here for a conference (stayed at the smaller hotel but there is also a sheraton tower main hotel too). had a nice room facing the marina. the rooms are huge and have a balcony. the hotel either faces the bay or the marina/airport both views are nice. hotel is very clean though a little old. cab ride to the gas lamp district was $15 so not too bad. breakfast was very good and I had that included in rate. hotel bar was tiny, would recommend walking to the main tower hotel as they had a lobby bar and one in their restaurant. staff was very professional and helpful. there is an outdoor pool, but it was a bit chilly to use that. there are a couple of delis within walking distance and valet parking for the rental.
overall very nice stay.

Love that the history of the building is preserved. We were in a deluxe 2 room suite. I loved the terrace and over-sized jacuzzi tub. The room amenities were as stated and it was very clean - huge closet. The valet parking sounds expensive, but I think it's a must for the area. It was convenient to have the car when we wanted it, and to know it was secure otherwise. The Quickstart breakfast was good. On the hot side, they had pancakes, sausage, eggs, sawmill gravy and biscuits, potatoes. I'd prefer bacon to sausage, but the food was good and always warm. They also had bagels, cereal, etc. We stopped in for one of the free drinks during the Kickback one evening and could have made a meal, but opted to eat on the Riverwalk. The only issue is we were in the San Fernando Tower and had to follow a maze and take 2 elevators to get to our room. The Riverwalk access is great - even though the city is currently working on the sidewalk to that area and you have to either get a river taxi or walk up street side.

This is a clean friendly place. I was very stressed about Southwest losing our luggage! The overnight desk guy, Michael, talked to me a bit and calmed me. All the desk help was very kind to us. The breakfast was what you would expect. It was out very early. The pool looked inviting.

title_masked: the way 5 star service should be
text_masked:
I have stayed at a number of hotels in new york from the major chains to boutiques - downtown, midtown, etc., but this hotel understand what it means to be a 5 star property. The room was fantastic, with nice views of soho, nice use of space, and with focus on green initiatives (glass water bottle filled every evening - economical to me and the hotel - I was just as Swissotel in Chicago - $8 for a bottle of water). 
The biggest reason I will look stay at this property again is the Service, from the reception desk, concierge, room service, cleaning team, etc - they were courteous and friendly. I felt like i would meet any one of them at a lounge in new york. Morgan took the cake for helping us with restaurants, making recommendations, and helping us. It is well worth spending a few dollars more at St. James - you get a lot more.

title_masked: Great price, great rooms, great location, great staff
text_masked:
Stayed here for 3 nights in June. Staff were always, always friendly and chatty, from the front desk to the cleaners.
We were on honeymoon and arrived to some congratulatory cheesecake and a hand written card which was a cute touch. The room was adequate (felt small coming from Vegas but it wasn't!) and clean and cleaned promptly each day. The products in the bathroom were nice too.
The coffee in the room and lobby were welcome. I have to say the bed was so comfy it was hard to drag ourselves out of it!
The location was excellent, we weren't fussed about Times Square once we'd been once, so we loved that of you turn left out of the hotel we came across some great bars and Hell's kitchen. If you went up 9th Avenue there are some great local bars and restaurants from any cuisine you can think of. It felt a lot more 'gritty' and real NY up this way, much better than going to the usual tourist traps near Times Square. There's also tons of 99c pizza slice places for a late night snack! We loved the Albert Hall tavern pub for good beers and pit stops on 39th and 9th.
We had a few drinks in the bar at the hotel was pleasant but always really really quiet.
Would stay here again without a doubt.

Nice, pleasant location, with many nearby restaurants, ample parking. We liked the fact that there is a small restaurant for light meals, including made-to-order breakfasts, and a cold beer or glass of wine. Very casual lobby with an HDTV in a side area. There is a nice center courtyard, which was a god-send for visiting teen hockey teams and their families, complete with comfortable lounge seating and open gas fireplaces.

title_masked: The Four Season Hotel, Seattle WA
text_masked: The Four Season Hotel in Seattle or other cities is a must for atleast one night of your vacation. And a super bonus is if you can stay longer. The service is outstanding and that matches your surroundings. The suites are a little pricey but well worth it.

Truly enjoyed my stay this September during a work conference. Excellent food at the dinner, breakfast and lunch provided. Most impressive was the service of the valet, bellhop & banquet staff. Clive (bellhop) took the time to review my agenda with me, giving me the floors for each meeting and banquet room to save me time. Very courteous staff!

title_masked: Stopover in Seattle before Alaska cruise.
text_masked: Three day stopover in Seattle prior to cruise to Alaska - this Best Western hotel was ideal. Easy free transfer from airport via shuttle bus. Easy getting in to Seattle via same hotel shuttle bus back to airport light railway station - day return to downtown for a few dollars. Room was clean, comfortable and well equipped. Staff were very friendly and helpful. Substantial breakfast (included in room price) could last you all day! Evening meal - not much choice but good. Hotel staff arranged bus to cruise terminal for 20 doillars each.

Stayed in the Dana hotel for 3 nights, and had a great stay. The corner rooms are fantastic, with great views, and great amenities. I'd definitely stay at the Dana again. The corridors are a bit dark, and the interior rooms as well, but request a corner room, and you will be very happy. I didn't give it a 5 star rating, as the first room that I was given keys to hadn't been cleaned, and there was still someone occupying the room when I walked in. The hotel staff gave me an equivalent room, and all was fine.

title_masked: More than a Pearl, it is a GEM!
text_masked: I have stayed in dift areas of Manhattan, but decided on the Times Square area to be close to Broadway shows. I decided on the Pearl based on the reviews here, and I was totally satisfied. The service, the location, the room, the nice touches (like a bottle of champagne for our anniversary) exceeded my expectations. I would highly recommend this hotel. Kudos to management!

title_masked: Charm and great service at your fingertips
text_masked:
It had been several years since I last visited Seattle. This week, I had the opportunity to return and wanted something other than a large chain hotel. I set out on my quest by reviewing what other tripadvisor reviewers had to say about local offerings.
I came across excellent reviews for The Sorrento Hotel and decided to give it a try. Since the purpose of this trip was a business trip with my boss (and I just recently started my job), I was nervous about staying at a non-chain hotel. I'm happy to report that I had nothing to be nervous about!
The aesthetics of the hotel were exactly what I was looking for! It had a cozy, yet refined, "feel" to it. Guests are greeted by a gorgeous lobby with big, comfortable chairs - both cloth and leather, and a fireplace. It very much reminded me of a "smoking room" with rich textures and colors. The only thing missing was a hound at the side of the chair!
In addition to the common areas of the hotel, the rooms feature a lot of little amenities that made me feel welcome... a teapot, french press for coffee, complimentary WiFi, and a a comfy robe to name a few. The bed welcomed me... I literally sank into the soft interior. So comfortable that the hotel sells the components to recreate the experience at home!
All-in-all, I was very pleased with my stay and look forward to my return. Special kudos go to the following employees that provided excellent service: Shantelle, Chris, Jackie, Rob and Bryn.

I didn't really know what to expect when I arrived at The Paramount, but what I got was excellent. Initially I was a bit concerned on arrival due to the busy nature of the lobby and the signs of building work, but I shouldn't have worried because neither were an issue.
My only problem came on the first night, the AC in my room was not working, however after reporting it to the front desk I was assigned a different room straight away so the problem was handled extremely well and very quickly.
The best thing about the hotel though is how close it is to everything you could possibly need, I was in and out all day and the central location made this a lot easier.
My room was spacious (renovated queen size), which was a pleasant surprise after reading some of the comments on here, it was more than big enough for 1 person and would also be absolutely fine for 2. I didn't try the food, but the bar was extremely comfortable and well stocked, it was maybe a bit expensive, but what would you expect from a hotel bar?
I expect to be back in the City again a couple of times next year and will definitely be booking again, highly recommended!

We moved out of NYC four years ago to a nearby suburb and decided to treat ourselves with a night in the city with our two kids (ages 9 and 12). One The Ave is where we'd booked friends and relatives when they had come for a visit so we decided to try it ourselves. It was a great decision. The room was spotless, the beds were comfortable and the staff couldn't have been any nicer. And you can't beat the neighborhood!

title_masked: Fantastic Hotel - Beware of the Trains
text_masked:
I'll start off by saying the hotel is fantastic. I'm here for 8 days on business travel and the amenities are awesome. The room is modern, updated and very comfortable. Little things like the peephole cover, a door that doesn't allow light in the bottom, and curtains that are truly light blocking are a rare thing to find. I'm only giving it 4 stars because of the abundance of noise that exists here in downtown San Diego, which is no fault of the hotel itself. I just wish I would have read a review that mentioned this - I might have reconsidered my stay downtown and gone to Torrey Pines. It almost isn't worth it to be close to so many amazing things downtown for the degraded sleep quality.
If you end up with a room facing the city.. beware of the trains. BEWARE of the TRAINS. They are loud, annoying and don't stop. Ever. 1 in the morning and a freight train blasting it's horn for 10 minutes? This will happen. The freight trains are the worst. The trolleys aren't so bad, but the crossing gate bells are worse than the trolleys. If you're a light sleeper this could be your own personal nightmare.
So.. the hotel is awesome. I highly recommend the 40th floor. Best views in the city for sunset. As for sleep quality? Bring earplugs.

title_masked: Walked to everything. Breakfast and nightly social was nice. Rooms cozy. Will return.
text_masked: There was no pool that I saw but everything was amazing! No complaints here. The bellhops/valet were very attentive. Very quiet. Everyone had a smile on their faces and it made for a great stay! The cookies were definitely a plus! =) Rooms were cleaned. Room service didn't bug you if you put out that sign.

We had a great visit to the Palomar over Thanksgiving with our dog. If you travel with a dog, you know it can hard to find a decent hotel that will accept your pooch. Palomar, on the other hand, has a water station by the front door with a chalkboard greeting all its canine visitors by name. They provide a doggy goody bag when you check in with food, water, treats and poo bags. There is a wonderful neighborhood right behind the hotel for great walks, and a patch of grass close enough to the door for quick late-night visit. Our handsome hound mix loved it, but it probably helped that we couldn't walk 10 feet without admirers giving stopping to pet him.
More generally, the staff was very courteous and responsive. The valets and bellmen were quick and polite and helpful. The location was convenient for us. The rooms were clean and had a modern urban flair -- and there was plenty of room. The bed was firm and restful. We had an ADA room (maybe due to the dog), and the shower was a roll-in affair with a fold-down seat and hand-washer.
Overall, we felt like it was a super value for a very nice hotel. We look forward to going back.

title_masked: never too late to say "stay there"
text_masked:
This is my 2nd try to write a revue, dont know what happened to the 1st.
Great hotel, our favorite for the price on our 7 week holiday. Spent 4 nights there and thought it was always great to come "home to". The location is fantastic and the complimentary tea, coffee, cookies and apples great. The room was not large but very well catered for with bathroom toileteries and a jar of lollies and always welcoming. The front desk staff were very helpful and friendly always. We had a couple of lovely breakfasts in the Restaurant and the staff there were also helpful and friendly, especially the man, sorry have forgotten your name.
If thinking of staying in San Francisco than this is the place to stay.

I found a great rate on this suite hotel for my family while visiting San Diego. It is a little out of the way if you want to be more central to the Zoo, Sea World, etc, located in a business district, but the rooms are nice and clean, spacious for families, excellent free breakfast, free Internet and parking, something that is hard to find in hotels around here! heated outdoor pool and great front desk staff. They were out of cribs when I arrived and come bedtime my toddler was running around the room and I was not happy! The staff was very helpful in my moment of desperation and a crib was found! Stay was great, highly recommend!

title_masked: In the neighbourhood of walk of fame
text_masked:
No frills, tiny window check - it had us worried; the room however was clean, comfortable with two large queen sized beds and free WiFi that instantly connected to our delight! New to us Indians was the concept of the wash basin being out of the bathroom, it worked very well though!
We missed our morning cuppa in the room (spoilt by the Indian hospitality industry).
A big one in favour of this hotel/Inn was its proximity to the Hollywood Boulevard and array of convenience stores located around it: a Seven-Eleven; laundromat; Burger King and even a McDonald's. Bus stop just outside the hotel was helpful as could be and the barely seen Front desk person was extremely efficient in calling in a cab.

title_masked: One of my favorite places to stay!
text_masked: My family has stayed at this location several times and I would highly recommend it. This hotel understands customer service and that the little things count. Every employee is friendly and helpful and willing to help any guest. We love eating at the restaurant and really love the daily happy hour! The rooms are comfortable and clean. The location is close to Dupont Circle, the train, and several restaurants.

Stayed there during a convention this past July and thought I was staying at a hotel in europe. My room was very small and the desk was not very ergonomic. My bathroom was small and the sink was clogged and it took a few minutes to drain.
I had lunch there and the food was very good.
The location can't be beat and the staff were all very friendly.

We stayed at this hotel for 3 nights. Good clean and fresh hotel with a pool (though small but adequate) and gym. Although there is no coffee/tea facilities in the rooms the hotel offers complimentary fresh coffee and pastries as a take away each morning, this is an excellent benefit but unfortunately they didn't inform us so we missed out on the first morning. The hotel is located opposite the Beverly Centre which is a large Shopping Centre and there is a bus stop outside which takes you to Rodeo Drive area. Easy access to The Grove and Farmers market too which are really nice. Speak with the concierge for bus timetables as they were very helpful.

title_masked: Ok, but wouldn't stay again for the price
text_masked:
A decent location pretty close to a subway station and walking distance from mosr downtown sites and Brooklyn Bridge. Soho a bit quiet for me on an evening, but not far from other more interesting bits of the city,
Rooms pretty small and not very clean- looked like someone had stood on the bed to close window as there was dirt on it when I arrived and under beds very dusty. But decent sized bed and I slept well.
 Service fine without being outstanding

My husband and I recently took our very first trip to NYC.....after being so over-whelmed, trying to decide on a hotel, we picked Hotel Azure. MANY wonderful things about this hotel that I need to point out....Great location, close to subway, and China town!!!! Hotel was super clean, very quiet and the staff at the front desk were SO nice and helpful!!! Also the price was so great!! A must stay for any visit!! (It is very small though!) But I hear that is the norm for NYC. Overall a FABULOUS hotel and would definitely choose again!!

My daughter and I (and our puppy) visited the US GRANT during the last week of August. We had an amazing time there! The room was perfection, but the aspect of the property that we most appreciated was the warm, welcoming, and incredibly accommodating staff at the hotel. From the valets, to the bell men, to the front desk staff - all were so very nice. My daughter is 6 and even she said to me, "Mommy, everyone is so nice here!" She, like me, didn't want to leave when our day of checkout arrived. Thank you for a great trip! We'll definitely be back soon!

My daughters 18 and 20 and I took a vacation in Seattle recently. We stayed at the Mayflower for 4 nights on their Sunny Side up Package. We stayed in a Deluxe Queen Suite. Our room had two bathrooms, two queen beds and a sitting room. It was spotlessly clean. The staff, Bell Man, Front Desk, Concierge, Room Service, House Cleaners, Waiters, and Waitresses were all so friendly and helpful. They all spoke very clear English which I appreciate. The Mayflower is connected to the Westlake Center Mall where the Monorail starts. The train ride from the airport to the hotel was very convenient and the walk was only one block after DE boarding the train. The hotel is a very good location for shopping and enjoying Pike’s Market. The food was good and the room service was excellent. I will stay here again. The price was top dollar but well worth every penny. We also felt very safe. EM

I have stayed several times over the last 6 yrs, never had a problem, staff always very friendly, and if something was wrong with my room they moved me. The airport shuttle is wonderful, and usually never have a very long wait for it at the airport or hotel. I always book here first, as I know the room will be clean, and comfortable.

Room was great and staff were lovely especially the concierges! Great location. Would not pay for wifi from the hotel we paid the charge for one night ($20 I think) and it was so ridiculously slow we could barely use it - just get a coffee a day from Starbucks right next door which has free wifi

It appears that the concerns that I read about last February via Trip Advisor have been addressed. We had a good stay! No complaints from my company party of six people, four rooms. Hotel was clean, front desk staff very helpful. Location was great. 15 to 20 minute walk to convention center which is absolutely fine in San Diego. However, we did have option of free transportation via bus. Not sure if hotel or convention supplied the bus but guessing the convention did so. I would stay here again, no question! Every staff member that we encountered was pleasant and helpful. Anyone who travels much these days understands that customer service seems like a dying priority in the business world. The management and staff of this hotel should be congratulated.

When we first pulled up here I was intimidated but from the guy working in the garage to the the person working the front desk service was exceptional. The bed was so soft, the blankets were made of down, there was a freakin Keurig!! :) The room was so lovely. Now I know some people on here are sticklers for certain details so yes there was a crack in the toilet that was just a problem cosmetically. Also there was a bus stop outside so I heard it all night. These things didn't bother me at all-to be in a historic, immaculate hotel I realize that it wont be as quiet as the Hilton. But the Hilton lacks character and the Dunhill has plenty. We will return!!! Oh and GREAT location so close to so many great places to eat.

HORRIBLE!!!!!
Personal cold! rooms like horror movies! ants in the room, bath rusty, crumbling walls, broken lights........ do not go!!!!!!

I stayed at the Westin St. Francis for 3 nights in July with my daughter. By joining their Starwood program, I got an upgrade to the 29th floor, which had a fabulous view over the city. (I think this is a newer part of the hotel.) The glass elevator rides on the outside of the building that went up to our room were quite exhilarating--although my daughter (who suffers from vertigo) couldn't bear to look through the windows as we went up and down! Our room was very spacious, the beds were extremely comfortable, and the room had everything we needed. The bathroom was also a good size, and the shower was fabulous! 
I was very impressed with the friendliness of the front desk staff. Everyone I came into contact with at the hotel, from the porters to the concierge staff to the wait staff in the bar, were professional, courteous and helpful. And the location couldn't be better. You're right on Union Square, and just steps away from excellent shopping, and some of the best restaurants on the West Coast. If you're just staying in the city and not planning to head further afield, you don't need a car. The cable car, bus stops and BART are all on your doorstep. I would definitely stay here again! We loved our stay here.

title_masked: Enjoyed our stay at the Westin
text_masked: Overall a good clean hotel conveniently located in downtown San Diego. Rooms are on the small side but clean and comfortable. Hotel is within walking distance to the piers, and a short drive/taxi ride away from the airport and other attractions in the area. Front desk staff and parking attendants were pleasant and provided good prompt service. Lobby café staff left a lot to be desired when it comes to customer friendliness. Disappointed with the overpriced daily parking fees as well as the fact that there is a daily fee for wi-fi.

title_masked: Historic hotel but the glory has faded
text_masked:
Arrival experience: Arrived early afternoon on a Sunday. Courteous and professional front desk staff.
Room (general): the rooms are fairy spacious. The furniture is very worn (see photo of end table) and not high quality. Overall, the paint, drywall, and general quality of the finish out is poor. For example, caulking is smeared near the bathtub, very poor drywall work is obvious throughout, and the carpet was stained. The paint is dark throughout the hotel, possibly in an attempt to conceal very poor finishing. Furthermore, the hotel is dirty. I walked onto an elevator twice hours apart and the floor was covered in dirt. Also, the blinds in my room (1007) were falling apart on one window (see photo). Small LCD TV.
Bathroom: Spacious bathroom, but the plumbing is old and makes a ton of noise. 
Bed: Decent bed but the bedspread was dirty (see photo).
Houskeeping: Leave a modest tip to ensure basic service such as changing the liner in the ice bin and replenishing soaps.
Restaurants: I did not eat at the restaurant, but the morning breakfast buffet was good. 
Bar: The free happy hour at the bar was pathetic. The only free options were cheap wine (options of Chardonnay and Cab) and Bud on draft.
Grounds: small public area in front of hotel (see photo from room looking down)
Pool: none 
Gym: Medium to small gym with your routine workout machines like exercise bikes, treadmills, etc. The water cooler in the workout room was extremely slow at dispensing water. 
Parking: Efficient valet staff. At arrival, 2 valets waited at the curb and immediately assisted me. 
Misc: Other: The first night the smoke detector woke me up beeping; not a fun way to begin an intense work week. I brought this to the attention of the staff, and the problem did not arise again. The free wi-fi was frustrating. The front desk provided code cards for my phone and tablet. One card was invalid immediately. The other stopped working after a couple of days. The elevators are slow and make a creaking noise. The interiors of the elevators have seen better days; they need to be refinished. 
Overall, I love the history of the building, but history is not enough to generate customer loyalty. I would never stay here again because it’s dirty and worn out. Maybe a chain like Hyatt, Hilton, or Marriott could turn the place around?

I only have one word to describe this hotel..AWESOME.Rooms are so clean, The staff is very friendly; my favorite person is Yari Ramirez ( Reservation Supervisor) she was so helpful when I asked her that I want to surprise my husband for out 10th anniversary. She really surprised me. Thank you YARI RAMIREZ you make our day so special. 
Howard & Silvia Perez

We are a family of 4 and stayed at Hotel George for 2 nights. The staff were professional and very helpful. The room was fine for two adults and two smaller children. Overall the room was clean and comfortable, however, I do think there could be more care in the vacuuming of the carpet edges - lots of dust pile up.
We would stay there again.

I recently took my wife and inlaws (who are visiting from S. America ) on aweek trip to Philadelphia. We booked the Rittenhouse hrough a recommendation by Amex travel. I would not normally book such an expensive hotel ( I usually stay at Westin, Kimpton type hotels which are very nice) but i will have to say The Rittenhouse proves you get what you pay for! This is the best hotel i have ever stayed in anywhere in the world! The service is exemplary and everyone is very friendly. When i saw pictures of the hotel i thought i might be getting out of my league but everyone treated us in the friendliest of manner. I can tell everyone there seems to love there job.I generally dont take advantage of concierge services much but the concierge department headed by Frank Marandino is just out of this world!! Even my housekeeper Mary J made a point to write a personal note each day thanking us for our stay. WOW I will never be able to stay in other hotel in Philadelphia (finances willing) again. I will always compare the service at other hotels i stay in to The Rittenhouse and i doubt i will ever find one as good. Besides the rooms are huge and it is in a wonderful location. I would move in if i win the powerball..hahaha

title_masked: Fantastic location but rooms in need of refurbishment
text_masked: I stayed at this hotel for a recent conference in Chicago. The hotel has a wonderful location - right on the river and close to restaurants, shops and attractions. I could see both the river and Lake Michigan from my hotel room. The common/public areas were great - modern, clean and well-maintained. The service was good on check-in/out. However, the guest rooms were quite small and dated. There were also a few telling signs that the rooms were in need of refurbishment e.g., peeling wallpaper. We had a faulty exhaust fan and our bathroom sink did not drain properly. We made several requests to maintenance, and although they did send someone up to "have a look", that's as far as it went. I'm not sure if I would stay here again. The location was fantastic - but not so sure about the room quality.

The hotel is beautiful and the rooms are nice, but the AC and especially the toilet flushing were SO loud that you couldn't sleep. I've stayed there before and it wasn't this bad last time, but the inconsistency shouldn't be there. The marble in the lobby doesn't matter when the toilet and AC are keeping you up. That having been said, the staff is very very helpful and even let me put my ice packs in thir freezer.

We enjoyed our stay. The hotel is lively, but also very quiet at night when guests are sleeping. I wasn't awakened by noise once in five nights. The mattresses are extremely comfortable. The corners of the platform beds, making contact with shins, not so much.
The bathroom could have been bigger, but there was a shelf under the sink for holding toiletries. A full-length mirror would be a good addition. 
This hotel is hip/trendy rather than high-end luxurious, but has a good location and the staff is very helpful and attentive.
We had quite a few family members staying at the hotel for a wedding, and everyone had positive things to say. The evening happy hour was a hit!

stayed recently on business as all other hotels were booked. Had been here before for rooftop bar and enjoyed it. easy checkin and room was corner king. Room was hot on checkin as large windows were unshaded and blinds were up. A/C worked hard to get it to 70 by nightfall. 2nd floor has some street noise but I always use earplugs which worked fine. free sodas and juice from in-room minibar is a nice touch. bathroom was large with no tub, which I prefer. breakfast is on the roof and somewhat overpriced...in response to my question about buffet or ala carte offerings, my high school waiter actually explained how a menu worked...much to the amusement of my business colleagues. evenings on the roof is a whole different thing...on thursdays and saturdays in SD, folks do the club thing. Interestingly, fridays are pretty tame. anyway, thursday night, roof was packed...did bottle service in order to sit down somewhere and bill was around $600 for 8 of us. I have to say the service was beyond excellent and the club staff is amazing. Views from roof are incredible and of course, the weather is always nice. I'd stay here again, but prefer the Marriott at the Marina for the money.

title_masked: A Little Hotel North of Ft Worth
text_masked: The room had a charming arrangement with a unique chaise lounge next to the window that was perfect for relaxing while watching television. Breakfast included fresh, hot waffles and friendly greetings from fellow travelers. The hotel staff were helpful and polite and the price was reasonable. There was a nice little fitness room with a treadmill and weight machine. The elevator made it easy to bring luggage to the room, but why not take the stairs once moved in? (For a healthy heart!)

title_masked: Great location for going out and eating.
text_masked: My friends and I stayed here for a long weekend. The front desk staff was very helpful and friendly. The location is especially great for 20 and 30 somethings looking to go out at night b/c many great restaurants and bars are located w/in walking distance. It is a 10 minute walk from the Dupont circle metro station as well. The beds were comfortable and the only downside is the bathroom space. We had a room w/ 2 double beds which I would expect to have at least 2 sinks or one sink w/ a larger counter space. There really was not adequate counter space for 2-3 people staying in the room for toiletries. Aside from this we all enjoyed our stay. Free afternoon wine helped too!

When we first stayed here two years ago we thought this was a great location and a great value for the price. The rooms were awesome too! Now that we have continued to stay here it has become worse. The rooms are looking runned down, carpet smell, room smell, things are falling apart in the room. My next stay will not be at this location any more!

Very interesting hotel at 10 mns from Time Square and 5mns from the Subway, well located!
Nice service, very polite and open minded personal. 
Everything you need to enjoy your stay in New York

Concur with other reviews...clean, great location, good price, NO amenities. One thing I wanted to emphasize was that the rooms are SMALL. At least 301, which was a tiny bedroom, connected to a tiny sitting room by a really tiny bathroom. My sister and I are both pretty small (under 5'6" and thin) and there was no place in either room where we could walk past each other without turning sideways. Not awful for us, but my 6'2" husband would have been very cramped. Some of the pictures seem to show other rooms that are larger, so maybe you could call ahead to ask for one of the "larger rooms".

Stayed at the Hilton Manhattan East over Thanksgiving and will not stay there again.
This "boutique" style hotel does not do the Hilton brand any favors. 
There is a lot of potential here that is just not realized.
Kimpton does a much better job with a property like this and I'd like to see just what they'd do here. Anything is better than what Hilton is doing.
Needless to say, I would not recommend this hotel.

I have stayed at this hotel a few years back when it was the Ramada and now recently as the Seattle Pacific.. The location is excellent, within walking distance to the Space Needle. The hotel coulod use a remodel as the outside looks a little worn, but the inside was clean and quiet. I must have arrived at peak arrival time because there was a line at the front desk when I got there but the receptionist got through the line rather quickly. The rooms were clean and comfortable enough. If you are looking for a good location, decent price, but don't need a fancy hotel room, then this is for you.

We love this hotel! It is in an excellent location. It has excellent accommodations and amenities. Beyond that, the staff is one of the most attentive and helpful teams I have ever encountered. From the bellman to the front desk, from the concierge to the maid service, Guest Relations at this hotel are par excellent. Their Guest Relations manager provides remarkable service and faciliates an award-worthy staff.

title_masked: Run and run fast the other direction!!
text_masked: This hotel is out dated. The room smell of mildew and the carpet is so nasty that I wouldn't walk barefoot. The mattress made me itch. The toilet wouldn't flush properly and the tub is stain. House keeping did not clean our room. When I call to speak to the manager about housekeeping he wouldn't take my call. I heard him tell the desk clerk to try to help me, he was busy with other things. I guess hotel guest are not important enough for him. I paid $239.00 per night! It's walking distance to reliant stadium thus the reason i made reservations at this hotel. If you are thinking about staying at this hotel room I caution you. Find somewhere else as your health is at risk.

Stayed for 2 nights in May 2012. This property is more like an inn/motel than a hotel. The room was spacious, the King bed was comfortable, the bathroom was clean, and lots of amenities. Even if the property is fronting the freeway, it was quiet and secured. Free parking, free wi-fi, free coffee/coffee maker, microwave, mini ref, and best of all free shuttle to seaworld. It is also very near a huge mall where you can eat and shop and for us, catch a late night movie. 
This was a very good deal for the accommodations, very comfortable and pleasant experience for my first visit to San Diego.

It was my first time at the Muse. The occasion was my annual father & son weekend. My son, who's thirteen was welcomed by the hotel and it's staff.
The room was very large (for NYC), clean, the shower had good pressure and our beds were also quite comfortable.
The hotel is part of the Kimpton chain (it's a sister property to the Nine Zero in Boston, pls see my review). It's on 46st Street and the taxi arriving from 7th/Broadway can't turn left on the street. I would say that's the biggest issue, since the taxi will either leave on the corner or have to go 2 avenues further to come down 46st and leave you at the front door. Either way, that's a hassle. 
On the plus side, this location offered us the chance to go to Time Square by feet and be amazed by the scenery at night.
I will go back the NYC and stay at a Kimpton, but I will probable stay at another of their properties, simply because I like other neighborhoods. But if you want to be close to Time Square and Broadway, it's a very good choice. Over the years I've stayed at the Millenium, the Sofitel, the Marriot and the Royalton, all in the same areas. All things considered, my favorites were the Muse and the Sofitel.

title_masked: 4th business trip in NY, here is best
text_masked:
Very advanced concept hotel.
Pros:Reasonable price, Nice location, free wifi, free breakfast, free coffee on same floor,Excellent crew, Nice and big terrace(NewYorker is gathering at night), Clean room, good business facilities(Meeting),Lovely japanese concept pictures.
Cons:Small for 2 people, open bathroom

title_masked: Great hotel at an affordable price
text_masked: I always stay at BW Executel and find the staff to be very kind and helpful. It has occurred to me that the staff members must be quite happy to be working there so the management seems to be doing something right. The complementary breakfast is excellent and the pool/ hot tub are a great way to relax while traveling. The only reason I did not give it the highest ranking is that the shuttle service from the airport is not always very convenient and I have waited for quite a long time on a few occasions. On the way to the airport, it is perfect. I really feel comfortable at this hotel and would recommend it to anyone.

The hotel was in a perfect location. Easy walk to just about everything and located where I felt safe doing so. The staff were wonderful. Small glitch upon check-in, I requested twin beds and apparently when you book a "standard" room you get a full, queen or twins, despite what you ask for. I got twin beds the next day. The rooms are extremely small, but I was expecting that. I really feel that the space could have been utilized better. A dresser in the room instead of a desk. A shelf or two in the bathroom. A small night stand/table between the twin beds. Beds could be a bit softer. I would stay there again, but maybe after I get with their design team to fix up those small rooms!

This Hotel is in an excellent location at one end of the Gaslamp District which means you are surrounded by unlimited dining and shopping options. We ate one breakfast at Mary Ann's which is located inside the Hotel and it was very good (little on the expensive side). And on the next few days, we found a great Coffee house that served up excellent (and healthy) breakfast options called [NAME] (Take 5th to Market Street and then go left). The pool on the 4th floor is very cool to check out and the lounge up there is great. We stopped off at the concierge desk several times and got great advice and/or discount passes to places were were visiting (Midway Museum / Zoo). Other nights we ended up eating at Osetra (Concierge recommendation) which had great seafood options and then the Palm (great steaks). And since its a Hard Rock, the music is playing everywhere you go.

title_masked: Large bustling hotel in a prime location...
text_masked:
The hotel is located smack dab in the middle of Times Square. As someone who used to live in NYC, I used to avoid T.S. at all costs because of how crazy busy it is, but for tourists, this is a great place to be. I was there for business attending a 3 day conference at the hotel. The hotel runs like a well oiled machine for such a busy large hotel with multiple conferences and events going on. 
The lobby is very large with lots of places to sit and meet people. Check-in was smooth, my room was a large and comfortable to typical Marriott standards and had a great view of T.S. The hotel had a nice Starbucks/gift/snack shop in the lobby which made it convenient to grab something quick before heading to the conference, not needing to step outside. Many elevator banks meant getting to and from the room and down to the street a breeze. 
Nothing veryy personal about this hotel, since there are so many people coming and going, but overall a consistent Marriott experience.

Cracking stay at the Manhattan Soho. I really don't see the point in paying so much more to stay nearer the midtown area when you are only a couple of subway stops from everything. The staff were exceptional- friendly professional and helpful. The breakfast was great- kept you going for hours and a wide choice and variety both hot and cold. Lovely clean rooms- No smaller than my bedroom at home. Sparkling bathroom. LOVELY shower. Great tv. My only grumble- and I think this probably only applies to the room we were in- was that due to being directly under the air vents on the roof it sounded like we were in a wind tunnel- and I never managed to quite get used to this. Had we been on a lower floor we would not have got this- but no doubt there would have been noise from the street instead. I would definately recommend, and for the sake of a 29 dollar subway card I don't regret not being "nearer the centre" for a moment.

title_masked: A little outdated for the price
text_masked: The stay was pleasant but if you are going to the Riverwalk this is not a good location. We were there for business and stayed two nights. The Hotel is a little outdated. Nothing outstanding about the staff, they were cordial. The Room was clean but the bed was a little soft and pillows were the smaller than standard size. It was o.k. but I think I could find something nicer for the price next time. This hotel is right off the freeway and by plenty of Restaurants.

We arrived to NY early and we were able to drop our bags off at the hotel and check out the area. We asked for a quieter room location but were told it is a city and there really aren't rooms that are better than others for noise. However, they tried to put us on a higher floor. The room was very modern and we were impressed by its appearance and detail. The air temperature in the room was a little messed up. We couldn't get much heat and we were able to get a portable heater. Then it got hot outside and we needed colder air but it was still a little warm. It was noisy at times - especially because there is a fire department very close. We could also hear the elevator at times. The hotel is in a great location as it is walking distance to theatres and Times Square. It is a short walk from the subway. There is a Food Emporium just down the street for food to go and there is a grocery store below. There is also a small grocery store even closer for smaller items. Our room had a small kitchenette. It was not stocked with any utensils or dishes - just a microwave, fridge and coffee maker (with coffee packets). We ate at one of the restaurants on the street of the Belvedere and had a great time. Great people and service. We would stay at this hotel again.

Perfect location, very comfy, quite, safe and a nice staff. As with all luxury hotels, the front desk is polite, helpful & just a touch snobby. However, the doormen, restaurant staff and ESPECIALLY the housekeeping staff were are genuinely friendly. Highly recommend. Will stay again.

This is a first rate hotel. We had a suite. Air coin was excellent. Poll was just right and a great spa bath. Breakfast was all you could expect apart from coffe from thermos type dispensers. Staff helful. Great atrrium with bar. Very clean. In fact whilst we only stayed one day could not fault it. Would have liked to have stayed longer.

title_masked: Does what it says on the tin!
text_masked:
Enjoyed a four night family break in New York staying at this hotel. Got an excellent price through LastMinute.com and, like others, arrived with mixed feelings following the very mixed reviews.
Thoroughly enjoyed the stay. The hotel is quite central, although away from the 'city-tour' bus stops, but on the right side of Manhattan for JFK airport. Our rooms on 11th floor were of reasonable size with excellent bathrooms, good storage, individual room cooling / heating (very noisy) TV and mini-bar. We all felt that an in-room safe would be much more useful.
The rooms were in good decorative order, as were the hallways.
As with other contributors, we used the Moonstruck Diner across the road for breakfast. Excellent food, large quantities and free-flowing coffee at very reasonable prices.
Final tip. Happy hour in hotel's bar from 5pm to 7pm every evening!

title_masked: The Ballantyne Hotel and Lodge is a Beautiful, Luxury Hotel
text_masked:
My husband and I stayed at the Ballantyne Hotel and Lodge for one night in February. I was very impressed with the facility, and highly recommend the hotel. I do not have one complaint about my stay. The artwork in the hotel is lovely, and it really gives the hotel a personal touch.
The rooms are traditional, and finely appointed. The bathroom was beautiful, and luxurious. 
The spa is outstanding. It is a gorgeous facility. The restaurant was divine. Our food was delicious. We ate there for both breakfast and dinner. 
We were staying at the hotel on a rainy, cold weekend so it was nice to have everything we needed in the hotel, and not have to get out in the weather. We were seeking solitude away from our young children, and the hotel provided that amenity with perfection. I think the hotel would also be great for families. The pool looks beautiful.

title_masked: Brilliant Location - just a few minor quibbles
text_masked:
Stayed in the dream hotel from 24th to 27th August for my wifes 40th birthday.
The location was excellent, just blocks from Time Square and Central Park.
We had a King Room which was of a good size, bed was very comfortable to lie on but not so great for sleeping. The bathroom also of good standard except the toilet kept running and we had to turn the water supply off and on each use rather than listen to it.
Had a look at the roof top bar are which was lovely with fantastic views although seemed to be a very exclusive venue with doormen outside the hotel with a door and a lift cordened off for those who were on the guestlist!!! You had to prebook to go - guest or not?? Does not mention this on their website. And also no mention of the dress code!!
Staff at reception where mainly helpful and pleasant and most of the concierge/bellboys epect for one (Issaac) who had a big chip on his shoulder, no need for the rudeness or ignorance.
On the first night we received 2 oranges on our pillows, do not get the concept of this, would much have preferred the bottle of wine in the bucket that we have normally received while staying away over my wifes birthday, but unfortunately on this special occassion there was no special treatment in sight at the dream hotel where I have read previously that this was the for a previous guest.
Overall we had a great time in NYC, Dream Hotel was a great base and would recommend it to anyone who gets it on a deal, would definately stay in this area again.
always a pleasure to stay here. clean rooms, easy access to freeway, fine gym and great staff!

title_masked: Very Nice but Some Teething Problems
text_masked:
The hotel opened in November 2011. It has a great location, downtown Chicago, across from the Fairmont.
The facilities are new, of course, and it has everything.
Staff are friendly and helpful. 
Their computer system needs a bit of work though. We booked for three nights, and when we arrived were told our checkout was the next day. We re-confirmed for three nights, but got a bill the first night indicating we were checking out the next day. We got that straightened out for one room, but a couple of others had the problem every day.
That said, I'd stay there again.

We spent 5 nights and had our honeymoon in new york as well as our wedding in central park.it was perfect.hotel food excellent,comfy clean beds,easy access to city as prime location.we didnt realise the new york giants were going to be playing and the only negative comment is because of this as the service in the bar the evening of the game was horrendous,we found it difficult to get a drink and the bar closed at 1130pm a bit too early for our liking.the guests in the hotel appeared to be forgotten about and the emphasis was on the game.But apart from this we did enjoy our stay and will definitely come again.

A girlfriend and I went to Chicago for fun and I chose the Doubletree for its price and location. I couldn't have been more happy with my choice! It's only 3 blocks from Michigan Ave or the river, and 4 blocks from Navy Pier. The room was great, the bathroom clean and updated. Concierge (Diane) was extremely helpful and doled out discount coupons for every museum & attraction that I asked about. The front desk couldn't have been more efficient; they even had our room ready 4 hours before check in! We didn't use the restaurant but did patronize Einstein's bagels which is in the lobby. The lobby bar was nice. My only complaints are that the refrigerator is packed with honor drinks so there was no place to put our own items, and there is no free wifi in the rooms (just in the lobby). I will definitely return!
A great place to stay for our 3 night stay in NYC. The staff was superb and housekeeping exceptional. The park across from the hotel was perfect for our Starbucks.

title_masked: Good hotel, but primitive facilities for smokers.
text_masked:
This is a large, fairly grand hotel in a central location. There is an on-site American grill restaurant which serves good, reasonably priced food and wine. The staff are friendly and helpful. Rooms are large and the air handling is quiet. Extra SPG points are available if you forego housekeeping.
However, I would advise against paying the extra for a club floor room, as the club floor lounge does not provide complimentary alcoholic drinks. Breakfast is available there, which is OK, but the evening hors d'oeurvres are not very exciting.
Also, the two smoking areas are pretty primitive - at the front edge of the hotel, under cover, but with only a small wall to sit on. It is chilly if the wind blows.

This is a nice elegant hotel for a weekend in NYC. We were upgraded to a Superior Guest room which was spacious. We had requested a few things pre-arrival which was not there, but as soon as they where reminded everything was quickly there. However it is not suitable for businesstravellers. Their wifi is very very slow.
