They have a business center where you can pay for high speed(??) internet, but then one can just as well work from a cafe close by with proper wifi...Breakfast is great with really nice fresh high quality bagels, muffins, croissant and a choice to order grenola youghurt or oatmeal with lots of fresh berries. They did not inform us of this the first days as staff was not very attentive to us early birds. They open for breakfast at 6.30 but are not really ready before 7.00. We were there for a week and this happened every morning. Some of the staff came in really late and sometimes the kitchen was not ready. But it tasted great!! The gym and the elevators have aerosol airfresheners-can you imagine someone spaying hairspay in your mouth when you are running?? No, right? Please remove those!! We also noticed that the doormen in this hotel got really agressive when several other guests did not want them to take care of their luggage. This is so unnessesary!! Take it with a smile when the guest wants to carry their small suitcase and do not want to pay 4 dollars for the service. This could be an excellent hotel with more serviceminded and attentive staff.

title_masked: Unpleasant area, unprofessional staff, but free wifi!
text_masked:
For a day trip I generally would not care about my stay since I am not in the room but from the start i did not have a pleasant experience. The location is not ideal= BAD neighborhood, not THAT close to the subway and the subway only has TWO lines. 
On to the room: Scratched and dirty lamps, DIRTY mattress
Bathroom: DIRTY toilet. and no bathroom air ventilation? 
LASTLY FRONT DESK: not helpful, not hospitable, no agent was professionally responsive except for the asian guy in the morning checkout

Hotel is in a really great place. We were upgraded to the 38th floor with views of Times Square. Very nice. We asked for a refrigerator which they provided. The room was decent size for New York City. Bathroom was a little small. Not a lot of counter space. Easy access to everything (Subway, train, bus). The staff was friendly and helpful. We definitively stay at this hotel again.

$100 a night for a room at a place called [NAME]-Lodge may seem a little steep, but when you consider that it's located in downtown Memphis, and an easy walk to (and stumble back from) Beale Street, it turns out it really is economical.
The rooms were clean, and comfortable, if a little worn. The elevator was a bit dicey, but not so much that it was unusable. The staff was helpful, and efficient. Parking was cheap, and secure. I'd stay here again on a short trip.

I've stayed here several times, usually with my husband, and this time we had three kids with us. They are very active and curious and they loved the hotel. The room was spacious and comfortable, the staff are really courteous and helpful, there's always a big bowl of apples and oranges in the lobby so the kids could go down and grab one at any time. Also, it is great that the subway is right around the corner so we could come and go easily.

The only nice thing I can find to say about this property is the staff are quite nice. Other then that - the work 'yuk' comes to mind. The room was so small I could barely squeeze between the end of the bed and the dresser. The carpet was tatty, not terribly clean, and the room smelled moldy. The bathroom was exactly as wide as the tub, and exactly as deep as the tub and the toilet. Which ran. The walls are paper thin and I could hear walking, talking, and flushing all night the one night I stayed there. It's cheap, so it's always full, but it's so loud and so old. I even had a first floor room at the end of the last building away from the street traffic and it was still loud. And the 'free internet' is there ... barely. I was there for a trade show and had to work, but ended up using my phone's hot spot, the hotel's internet was so slow. 
I checked out after one night and went across the freeway to the other Comfort Inn and Suites on Hotel Circle Place. Fabulous, wonderful, clean, and still very cheap!

We telephoned/asked for the price given over the internet/were given another (higher) price over the telephone. We were stranded due to Hurricane Sandy and did not know our way around/have transportataion, so we took the room for four days. The room was dark and promised balcony non existent. On the night of the concert, the band gave the crowd more than their monies worth. One of the front desk staff seemed really wary of my spouse and we wondered what that was about. We paid in cash and that was a problem as well. We will not stay there again.

Hard to tell where to start. First the bad news... worn out lamp shades, nasty carpeting. Sure needs work that hotel. Then all the good news over two stays in the hotel.
My wife and I were waiting in the lobby - not happily either - since our room was not ready. A gentleman caught our eye - walked over and said "you look unhappy" how can I help. He got us checked in immediately, took our luggage up to the room. We were missing towels (laundry problems) - he brought those too along with two glasses of wine and a sincere apology. Not sure who he was until we met him at the Admiral's reception down in the bar. He is / was the General Manager. And...he made pickles! Lot's of them! And we loved them! Seems there were done as a promotion for the hotel that was once a vinegar factory. The next day - and for the next two days - we saw him in the lobby at breakfast chatting with everyone and in the lobby at night as he directed guests to area attractions and outstanding restaurants. (Our favorite and we hear his too was the Thames Street Oyster House.) Leaving after the first visit we were searching for a taxi and out the door and down the street he went until he flagged one down.
Our second visit (my wife is a JH patient) was just as kind and memorable. Still bad carpet and shades, still needing a good upgrade but..still very inviting and caring. We missed the manager on the first day of this last visit but he left a note in our room and caught up with us as we checked out. We will be back and, hope to see him again soon. 
Another bad note though - the pickles are gone! Bring the back the pickles - probably the best ones I have ever eaten (better that my wife's and even she agrees). Very seriously it is the staff and the manager who made these two stressful trips so much better for us. I hope he lasts there. Our hospital contact sadly let us know that the history of the property does not bode well for it's managers.

I stayed here June 23,2012 to July 20, 2012...almost a month. I travel for a living AND work nights. Housekeeping was FANTASTIC on accomodating my schedule. Beautiful property. Back patio and pool are probably the nicest Ive seen. Cushioned open air seating with fire pit. Covered pagoda style seating with BBQ grills. 
Clean, comfortable and ALL staff were friendly and courteous. I particularly want to call out the Director of Sales Lynette Deihl. I travel with a group and she was particularly helpful in securing our accomodations. The most surprising aspect came when I casually mentioned to her that my group would be moving on to our next city. The next morning in my email I had a list of Staybridge Suites in the area we were travelling to, specific room types for my groups needs, prices and short reviews. Her email closed with "Let me know..and I will make the arrangements". WOW!
If your travelling to the Stone Oak area in San Antonio as a group, an individual, or a couple, I HIGHLY reccomend this hotel and Lynette. Awesome customer service.

My husband had a business trip to Philadelphia and this is the hotel they use. Very nice, clean and great location. Breakfast buffet was excellent. Walking distance of many sights.
Only big negative is parking. $44 a day when you factor in tax. There is a parking deck located across the street that is $27 a day.

We stayed here for 2 nights at the end of September at the end of our 3 weeks tour of the West Coast. 
We paid around 600 dollars for 2 nights, a little pricey, however it's in the heart of Hollywood blvd. 
Reception staff were young, friendly and very professional. Check in was smooth and we were upgraded to a superior queen with 2 beds instead of 1. 
Room was a little on the small side, bathroom was nice and roomy and nicely done. Bags were brought up to the room not long after I got there. Mini bar ridiculously expensive, 10 dollars for a bottle of water! Coffee machine in room only took the 3 dollar coffee filter from the mini bar. Room a little worn, bed comfy and clean. In room safe and cupboard to hang clothes. Air con worked well and not too noisy. 
Pool area was the place to be seen. Live dj during day, who I might add couldn't dj very well! Pool parties until 2am. Drinks pricey, 15 dollars for 2 non alcoholic juice drinks! Reservations for sun beds needed. The crowd were young and trendy.
Reception area and lobbies around the hotels were nice, dark wood and grey colours. Several events took place while we were there, so quite busy.
Expensive to park, 33 dollars a night. You can park over the road for 20 dollars. Also 15 dollars a day for wifi, per device!
Location was central to Hollywood attractions. Theatre across the street, tour buses depart nearby to sunset blvd, Santa Monica and Beverley hills. Right on the walk of fame.
Overall good stay, I'd recommend staying here, however you don't get a lot for your money, but its Hollywood!

Stayed here while on a business trip. Lovely hotel with modern colors and textures throughout. The Domain, where the hotel is located, is a swanky shopping/eating area. Tiffany, Louis Vuitton, Free People, Anthropologie, and Neiman-Marcus are steps away.
The hotel lobby is awash in granite, chrome, sharp right angles and velvety-veloured sofas. They have also paid someone to create musical wallpaper for the lobby: mood-evoking music meant to complement the decor. 
My hotel room was 328. The bed was fantastic except for the pillows, which absolutely sucked. The "heavenly bed" is phenomenal, really it is. Climate-control system functioned perfectly. Furniture (side chair, task chair) was very pretty but super-uncomfortable.
Bathroom is huge. Huge walk-in shower with glass doors. If you have read any of my previous hotel reviews, you already know how I detest rainfall shower heads. I am happy to report that this shower had a Speakman showerhead with multiple settings.
All this attention to detail....and then I noticed the room service menu. 
It contained eleven...ELEVEN....spelling errors. Serious things, such as "blackeberry", "Shiner Boch", "jalepenos", and "buerre blanc". How, how, HOW can a place that has created a specific soundtrack for its lobby not run the spell-checker for its in-room menus? I called [NAME] customer service at once. They instructed me to turn in the menu to the manager, which I did...with the errors circled and correct spellings added. 
Later that evening, I wanted room service but had no menu, so I called to have one brought up. It was an entirely different menu. Different font, different food choices, different entirely. I am not stupid enough to think that the hotel fixed and reprinted their in-room menus in one day, but being given an entirely new menu was a little bizarre. And there were typos on it as well!
According to the little paper on the back of the door of my room, the rate for my room was $699 per night. At that price, you would think some attention might be paid to the printed materials in the room.
I'd like to give this place 5 stars but I just cannot forgive the menu debacle.
Great location good value just found some staff not as helpfull as others but would recommend this place to anyone

We stayed four nights in November 2012 at the SF Grand Hyatt located in Union Square. The Union Square area is convenient and feels relatively safe for tourists. Lots to do and see there as well. The recent room rennovations were excellent! Everything was new and fresh. The desk staff and concierge were helpful to me and my guests. When we were there they were in the process of completing rennovations on the lobby and restaurant. We were told this via email in advance so that this was not a surprise. My only disappointment was that the restaurant on site where I took the group for lunch was buffet only. This would have been fine but they ran out of food right away and the food they had was disappointing. Small complaint for a lovely property!

title_masked: Perfect Hotel in the perfect location
text_masked:
First the location is just amazing and the legendary service of Kimpton Hotels is once again well alive in Philadelphia. For our second week on the East coat after driving from New York to New England we decided to go visit Philadelphia and reserved at the Palomar. We were not dissapointed by either the hotel or the sites. 
Our next stop is Atlantic City before going back to New York and heading home.
You can go wrong booking at the Palomar

Stayed here for four nights in August alone and would rate it as one of the best hotels I've been lucky enough to stay in. There are probably more luxurious hotels to be had but given the levels of cleanliness and customer service, coupled with the location make this a real find. Main points:
- very friendly and helpful staff
- the rooms are large and very clean. I was upgraded as a result of being a Kimpton member (which is well worth doing) so was very happy
- good restaurant and bar area with a great free continental breakfast
- a great free drinks hour at five giving you the opportunity to met other guests or just drink for free on your own
- free wireless and a $10 mini bar
- great location in a really vibrant area and a few blocks away from a metro. You can also walk to the mall in around 30 minutes
- it can be a little noisy outside if you're facing the street but I didn't have a huge problem with this
- I didn't visit the pool and didn't see any dogs so can't comment on either
All in all, if I were to visit DC again (which I plan to do) I would definitely stay here. I would also look to stay in ny Kimpton hotel in the US on future visits.

title_masked: Super cool spot at Venice Beach
text_masked: I travel a lot! So I had to share this gem in Venice Beach. Hotel Erwin has one of the sweetest roof bars, blankets are provided if there's a chill and the drinks are classically made, some with an updated twist. My room was cozy with a very comfortable bed, a roomy bathroom was smartly designed with a fantastic sink and superb showerhead. My room overlooked the beach where I could sit outside and drink my morning coffee, or dine at a little table for two set in the room. Attention to detail was certainly on the minds of those that revitalized this historic hotel. Loved all the Larry Bell watercolours scattered throughout the hotel.

title_masked: Very nice rooms, accessible by public transit, above average rates.
text_masked:
Stayed here as a business traveler for four (4) consecutive weekdays.
Overall: Would recommend to others, but be prepared to pay for what you get.
Positives: (in no particular order)
+ Very clean rooms, turndown service, complimentary robe use in hotel room
+ Right next to Silver Line public transit, walking distance to downtown area
+ Complimentary in-room wireless and LAN internet access
+ Access to small refrigerator for keeping items cold
+ Decent restaurant choices for individuals or groups around the waterfront area
+ 7-Eleven convenience store right outside the north entrance of hotel
+ Tips are "included" as hotel policy (i.e. no need to leave tips for services)
Negatives:
- Above average rates ($274 w/discount + $42 tax per night as of October 2012) for king bed
- Bit of walking distance to travel to downtown/north end area

title_masked: great location, good value for money
text_masked:
The hotel is well situated in New York.
The rooms are clean and not that small for NYC. They were also quite comfortable but a little old fashioned. The beds were comfortable, the bathroom big and seemed new/renovated.The air conditioning was ancient and noisy but it worked (thank god)
Breakfast was included, it was nothing to write home about but we could eat bagels and pastries.
Staff was very nice and helpful
would recommend to a friend

Stayed in this hotel for 6 nights. Our room was clean and spacious (suite). The bed was extremely comfy, and the blanket was nice and warm! The street was very quiet, didn't hear a peep in the evenings. The staff was friendly and attentive especially the housekeeping (super kind and polite people). The location was great, everything we needed was very near and the subways were very close. The only complaint which is minor in my opinion, is the hot water took several minutes to get up to our room, but once it did it was piping hot!
Would highly recommend this hotel!

title_masked: Very nice stay at Hilton in Fashion District
text_masked: We had a quick trip into New York for a Christmas party and stayed at the Fashion Distract Hilton. Very close to everything, hip & cool hotel vibe, friendly staff, nice clean rooms even though little on the small size, fast elevators but having to scan your key first was ignoring (forgot and we where up to 22nd then gradually got back down), love the valet parking for its location and Rare restaurant had good burgers but service tad slow. Would stay again.

title_masked: Not the best part of town
text_masked:
Walking down First Street is not a pleasant experience due to the homeless and the unpleasant smells. Did not feel safe during the day, took a taxi back when it started getting dark. Since parking is not easy downtown, I had expected to be able to walk most places easily due to the location. Would not recommend.
The hotel is okay, not great.

We stayed here the night before our early departure. The room met our needs for the short stay. The bed was comfortable, but it wasn't one of those adjustable mattresses that HGI's have at other locations. The bathroom was clean.
We were able to leave our car here for free ($5 per day after 5 days), then take the shuttle to the airport at 4:30 a.m. When we got back to Columbus, I called for the shuttle from the luggage claim area. It was waiting for us by the time we got out to the pick-up area.

Antonio V. went out of his way to make sure our meal service was excellent. Fuedosa and Oscar Del Cid also assisted with our meal. The service and food was perfect. We had six people for the business lunch. It had been a long day but this staff served us well. They were very service oriented. The facility was clean and the buffet was good and at a great value.

We stayed here for 5 nights during April 2012. Paying in advance resulted in a good discount on the room rate. The rooms were nicely furnished and spacious. The hotel seemed fairly new; everything was in good shape. The staff was very helpful. Breakfast was good, but unchanging, i.e., same menu every day. No pool, but you can use the pool at the nearby Holiday Inn. The hotel was literally two blocks from Fisherman's Wharf, and also two blocks from public transportation (cable car, trolley, and bus). The $27 transit pass for a week was a good deal. Without the pass, a cable car ride is $6.00 one way, so it pays for itself pretty quickly.

title_masked: Good hotel, though a bit pricey
text_masked:
We stayed here, even with high prices (close to $300 for a regular room) because my wife was attending a conference there. The good: Very comfortable beds (my wife has grown to really like the beds in Hilton beds, which are not found in sister properties such as Double Tree or Hampton Inn). We got a room on the 19th floor with a great view of Telegraph Hill and San Francisco Bay (didn't mind time I had to spend on our PC since I had the great view). The restaurant was surprisingly good, especially the wild halibut and salmon. There are free PCs and you can have something printed at the concierge desk. The concierge was very helpful. When we had something faxed to us we were able to get it right away. The hotel is near public transportation. And close to several reasonably-priced restaurants in Chinatown. If you like Tai-Chi you can probably join groups in a plaza across the street. We walked to restaurants and shops on Market Street. Fairly short walk to the trolley that went to Fisherman's Wharf and a bus that went to the Golden Gate Bridge. Hotel is almost next door to the iconic Transamerica pyramid building (which has a small grove of redwoods, in case you can't make it to Muir Woods). It is a bit far from BART if you use that system to get to SFO or Oakland airport. 
The not-so-good: Wi-Fi is $10. The four elevators were woefully inadequate for a hotel of this size (they seem to be underghoing renovation, but unless the number of elevators is increased I don't see this avoiding delays up to several minutes or more at peak times). Parking costs, which we thankfully did not have to pay, are obscene. As mentioned, the room rates are high. The building is far from new and, frankly, rather ugly from the outside. The room was comfortable, though not large. Breakfast is not included in the rate (a Chinese restaurant next door has American breakfasts for about $4-5),

The hotel itself is cute, very compact, perfect for a night in the city. It's very clean, which is a super plus. Also the staff is amazing, super helpful, and very friendly. For this reason alone I would stay here again!

title_masked: Club Quarters - Great price, good stay
text_masked: We had an overnight stay at the Club Quarters, Philadelphia. The hotel is clean and accommodating. They are doing some upgrades to the elevators, so there can be a little bit of a wait. Our room was on the 12th floor. It was nice with a comfortable bed. The best feature was that it had skylights that open! It was too cold to open them, but I want to request the room in the summer, it would be beautiful under the stars.

My husband surprised me with an anniversary weekend at Mokara, and it was amazing! The hotel is beautiful and well-appointed. The staff were all very responsive and service oriented - they all remembered our names. The beds are very comfortable and the pool top terrace with cafe is lovely. The spa was very nice but a a little over-priced. The hotel was in the middle of the hustle-and-bustle of downtown San Antonio on the Riverwalk, but when we were in the hotel, it was like a quiet, secluded getaway. If you are looking to splurge a little for a romantic place to pamper your sweetie, this is it!

title_masked: Good location, but hotel too busy to care.
text_masked: I checked in around 7pm for a 4 night stay during a conference I was attending at the same venue. Upon arriving, I notice a very musty odor. I called the desk immediately and was told there was nothing they could do as the hotel was full. I understand. Before going to sleep I turn the AC to 68. I have a sleepless night because the AC is apparently broken. My room is no where near 68. I had three more nights of that because the hotel was full. I would only take off one star for these issues because they are room specific... HOWEVER... the internet service (costs $15/day) was spotty and at times completely down. The service line they tell you to call is endless ringing and no one ever answers. I even called guest services for the issues, and all they did was transfer me to the same line even though I told them no one was answering. For a hotel that sells itself as a conference center this is completely **unacceptable**. The satellite television had issues with reception (would cut out and switch to "searching for satellites") and I had unpleasantly slow service with room service as well.

We stayed for 4 nights while attending a convention. The motel was convenient because a bus ran directly downtown from in front of the motel. (Entrance to I-85 was also close.)
The room was very nice, with a refrigerator and microwave, as well as a fast internet connection. The motel was far enough off the street that we did not hear the traffic noise from the busy intersection nearby.
Also liked that there were healthy choices offered at breakfast, such as yogurt, fresh fruit, and low fat milk, as well as bagels and waffles.

We've stayed at the Palomar twice and have enjoyed great service and a very nice room each time. The hotel room is spacious,modern and attractive, and the staff goes out of their way to be of service. They offer a complimentary glass of wine in the early evening and people gather in the lobby to chat and enjoy it. From the bellboy to the parking valets, service is accomodating, and rendered with a smile. The hotel is also pet friendly, which creates a homier atmosphere than your typical big city hotel.

title_masked: Nice stay, average amenities, good value
text_masked: I stay here occasionally with my sons when they need be in the area for athletic events. The best things about the Radisson CK are the location, and proximity to very good food, such as Donna's for dinner, and a little cafe in the courtyard (don't remember the name, but is not part of the hotel) which has very good breakfast, including amazing homemade muffins. The hotel also does a nice job of putting out complementary coffee, granola bars, and fruit, very early in the morning. The lobby is very nice for some early quiet time until 6 am when they have a "policy" to turn on the TVs, even though no one is there - I asked them to wait until I left, which they did, but told me that was their policy - why do hotels think we want noise so early in the morning? The front desk staff were extremely nice and accommodating, but the roll-out bed they gave us (we tried 2) was in very poor condition. Nevertheless we will continue to stay here because of the location and relatively cheap price.

title_masked: Great Hotel for traveling on an a budget.
text_masked: I have now stayed at the Comfort Inn Downtown twice (previously in November 2009), and both times it has proved fantastic. It has a great location to be able to reach many of the main attractions of Memphis either by walking or by the trolley that only costs a dollar. The rooms are clean and comfortable and the staff is friendly. It also has a continental breakfast, which I always love. It is nothing too fancy but its a great way to start a day of sightseeing.

title_masked: Great Hotel Great Staff Great Rate!!
text_masked: What a Hotel !! Real nice Staff especially Amy she was super!! So was Doug very helpful!! I will stay here again! Great Location to the Airport and shutttle service! Very impressed with this Hotel so much to offer and great rate! The best in the area! Very clean rooms! Only thing limited T.V. Channels! Overall super place to stay!!
I found the room very clean and fresh, the bed was very comfortable! The evening social hour was a nice touch and the host, Stephanie was nice!

The staff at this hotel are friendly and helpful. The rooms are clean, updated and stylish. There is free wifi (something you don't always get these days!). And the best part is the location. The hotel is situated one block from the main shopping/food area in the University District. Also, the hotel is situated very conveniently to the I-5 and all of the main neighborhoods (my husband were in Seattle house hunting so we drove all over). Although it is not a massive chain hotel, they have a surprising number of amenities for a small boutique hotel (e.g., restaurant, bar, attached coffee shop - Tully's yum!, and a small gym). Overall, it's a great hotel and I would recommend it to others wanting to stay in the University District.

We went for the "Sailabration" tall ships extravaganza over the June 16-17 weekend. We got a harbor view room on the 10th floor which proved to be a ringside seat for watching much of the festivities. The lobby and entire hotel was very clean and stayed that way despite the throngs of people that were staying there. Our room was spacious, clean and very comfortable. The bed was great for my wife (she prefers a very firm mattress), a little firm for me, but still very comfortable.
 The staff was friendly and despite the crush of people, they were very efficient and patient in handling room assignments and answering questions about the events going on. We arrived fairly early on Saturday morning (I was hoping for a lucky empty room as we had an early lunch engagement) and our receptionist diligently tried to fulfill our early check-in request, but no luck. Left our bags and went sightseeing. They dutifully called when our room was ready, and we were thrilled with the view and overall excellent amenities of the room. I really like the Aveda shampoo! 
 The great view of the Inner Harbor and the proximity to all the Inner Harbor activities is a real plus. We could leave the car and walk easily to anything (National Aquarium, restaurants, Constellation, et. al.) We were able to watch the Blue Angels show from our room and had a great view...especially excellent as all the other venues were packed and some pretty much inaccessible.
 The workout area isn't huge but there were four or so of each: ellipticals, treadmills, stationary bikes. Enough weight machines for an effective workout. Superior to most hotel fitness areas. Once again, it was clean and with a pleasant attendant.
 The downsides were the elevators being so crowded and slow, and the room was noisy from exterior sounds of the Harbor festivities. Once the activities were over, the room was quiet and we both slept well. So I think you can attribute the minuses to the very high activity level of the special weekend.
 Overall, this an excellent hotel for Inner Harbor activities or a football or baseball game as everything is easily walkable. Clean, luxurious and friendly are keys to a great place to stay and the Renaissance delivers.

You talk about great location, right over the bridge first exit and you are there. They have a shuttle that will take you down on Beale St(1.5 miles) from the hotel. Rooms are okay,all you do is sleep in them. They are doing some remodeling.The bed was very comfortable. We will stay again.

I recently enjoyed a five-night stay here. The hotel staff was friendly and helpful. Lena at the front desk handled a room change for me after my first night effortlessly. Rooms are clean and comfortable, although the first room I had was quite small. Although it could use some updating, everything was well maintained.
I really enjoyed the indoor pool and spa, which was clean and had towels and a changing area (I hate traipsing through hotel halls in a wet swimsuit!). The hotel was also very quiet.

title_masked: Outstanding service and comfortable place to stay
text_masked: My sister and I recently stayed here during a 5 day stay in LA. The rooms are very comfortable and clean. The service staff was wonderful, friendly and very helpful. Little Tokyo is in walking distance and a great place to find great food. If you are looking into doing some sightseeing and trying to figure out how to get there (Hollywood sights, Universal Studios, etc.), here are my top 3 options. First choice is taking the Metro. It's cheap and convenient. Second choice, take the taxi from the hotel. Ask first about prices as they my vary from one taxi company to another. Also, remember, LA traffic is terrible so the meter could be running for awhile. We took a taxi from Universal back to the hotel. The driver gave us an estimate of about $35. We got stuck on the highway a long time but at the end, honored that estimate! Third option for sightseeing. About three block or so from the hotel is the Hop-On-Hope Off tour company. Great way to see the sights. One more thing about transportation from the hotel. I don't recommend taking their town car that is available at the hotel. It is extremely expensive and could cost you as much as $100 for round trip transportation to Universal Studios! Overall, super hotel, good food at their restaurant downstairs as well as a beautiful little Japanese garden at their facility.

Big conference oriented hotel, with a great location if you want to be near the Capitol, union station, and east end of the Mall. Clean rooms, comfortable beds. Appeared to be people using wifi in the lobby, but we never managed to get on in room. Valet parking is available - but be aware that it's $45 a night (though they did say this include in and out if you need it). Quick return of car on check out if you use their text for your car feature. Room set up was a little disappointing - no table or light on 1 side of bed, alarm clock/ihome was missing power cord, and no in-room safe. Location was great for our needs - walked to a concert at Nationals stadium (about 1 mile south) and took a great run on the Mall Saturday morning (about 3 miles round trip to the Washington Monument from the hotel). Breakfast is good, but hard to say the buffet is worth $21 - there's a starbucks around the corner that would probably be a better bet. There is surprisingly little choice in restaurants right near the hotel - so plan to venture more than a few blocks to eat.
This hotel has a great location-close to major freeway. Restaurants are around. Hotel is very neat and clean. Staffs are polite, nice, and very helful. Price is affordable-value... I will comeback!!

title_masked: Nice hotel, decent pool, friendly staff, decent location
text_masked: Stayed here with my husband and two kids for a weekend in Seattle (acting like local tourists). It is located in the northern end of downtown, but walkable to everything. The pool is nice and warm (as compared with the Sheraton pool last year that was too cool for even the kids). I was pleasantly with the rooms - they were roomy and nicely updated. Lots of treadmills, stationary bikes, and ellipticals in the gym.

I was recently in Chicago on business and, due to a very large convention, was having difficulty finding a hotel. At the last minute I spoke to someone at the Sheraton and they were able to accomodate me. The hotel is very conveniently located near Michigan Avenue. The staff was very friendly and helpful, even though they were extremely busy with the convention attendees. The public areas were very attractive and there was a very good restaurant that was accessible from the lobby.

We were looking to staying at the Hilton Garden Inn in Times Square but it was booked, and I'm actually glad for it. Everything was in walking distance even though it was blisteringly cold, our view of the empire state building was cool. It's what you would expect for a mid-range hotel, one cool feature was we could adjust the firmness of the beds. We had 2 rooms and it would've been nice if we were on the same floor but understandable. Skip breakfast here unless you have a voucher as its expensive for what you get or aren't used to eating a lot for breakfast. For 5 people it was $95, we could've gone else where in the vicinity for better and cheaper.

title_masked: Excellent hotel evoking the political spirit of Washington DC
text_masked:
We had one of the newly renovated suites on the top floor. Gorgeously decorated but the one next to the lift shaft is noisy. We were moved to one further away and it was perfect. 
This is now one of my top hotels in the world - great atmosphere, fantastic concierge service, beautiful room with spectacular views of the Washington monument and the Treasury building, ideal location - 3 minutes walk to the White House and 5 minutes to the Smithsonian. The reception areas are so historic, visitors not staying at the hotel come in to look. 
Take a seat at the bar during the week and eavsdrop on the fascinating political conversations going on.Perfect!

We have been coming here for short visits for 10 years, and have never failed to enjoy the incomparable views, rooms and wonderful amenities at the resort. Perfect place to enjoy the best of San Diego- the weather, the numerous bay activities just steps from your room, Sea World, the San Diego Zoo, downtown, etc. The pool area is perfect for families with clean restrooms and delicious food easily accesible from the deck area. We have always found the service to be excellent as well; on our visit last weekend, we were greeted warmly and helped to our room by Jeffrey. He was genuine, professional and most of all, helpful with everything we needed! Thanks for a great visit!

title_masked: Rooms are very old and dirty
text_masked:
At first glance the hotel is nice looking. My company booked this hotel so I didn't have a choice. After talking with some colleagues they had said their rooms were nice enough but a few had bad opinions of the room quality. I had to take pictures for them to believe it.
Cons.
The paint was peeling off of the ceiling. The wall paper was peeling off and was stained in places. The door jam has been painted multiple times and was peeling in spots. There was something disgusting stuck in the textured wall paper in the bathroom. The caulk in the shower was stained and looked to be installed by a 5 year old. the screws in the vent in the shower were falling out. The vanity was scraped and very worn. The light switch had dirt/dust lodged inside of it.
Pros.
The bed was comfortable and the water pressure in the shower was very good.

title_masked: As good as it gets at ANY price! (And the price was great!)
text_masked: Sunita, Steve, the breakfast chef, the maids and the rest of the staff at the Baymont Inn and Suites close to Love Airport in Dallas, Texas have it figured out: 1) have a clean (indoors and out), well-decorated and appointed, complete and perfectly functioning hotel, 2) take care of inadvertent problems quickly and with a positive go-out-of-our-way approach, 3) put the customers above everything else, 4) make them feel welcomed, at home and not wanting to leave, and 5) DO ALL THIS WITH SMILES AND CONSTANT, PLEASANT ATTITUDES, WITH HONEST WORDS AND ACTIONS TO SHOW THEM THAT THEY ARE INTERESTED IN YOU AS CUSTOMERS AND AS PEOPLE! If you can trust a stranger, TRUST ME, this place is the best I have ever stayed in, and the staff is the best I have ever had the pleasure of serving me. Did not want to leave. I live in Nebraska and will definitely stay here when and if I should visit Dallas again, as long as Sunita is running the show! AND IF ANNNNNYBODY SHOULD WRITE A COMPLAINT ABOUT THIS PLACE, I WILL BE SHOCKED!!! When I read all the reviews about it which were all positive, I wondered if my feelings would match all the 4.5 and 5.0 glowing ratings and reviews. They did not. They EXCEEDED everything I read!!!!!!!!! Thanks, Sunita! My wife, Taekwondoe son of ours and I hope to see you all again someday!!!

I've been staying at this location for over 20 years. The staff are friendly, courteous, knowledgable, and progfessional. They promptly respond to all of my requests. I've been staying there so long, many of the staff know me by name. General Manager Fidel Caballero is the epitome of professionalism.

title_masked: Good hotel, friendly staff, clean room, and convenient location
text_masked:
First impression & Starbucks: 
I booked a room for me, a girl friend, and her daughter for Sept 28 - Oct. 1, 2012. I arrived at this hotel one day earlier than them at 0930 on 9/28/12. The hotel lobby was very clean and welcoming with the entrance facing the corner literally of Republic and Queen Anne. The staff member, Kelsey, was very friendly and helpful. The only thing that annoyed me was their 4PM check in. They kept saying they would try to see if they can check me in earlier, but I didn't get a room until 4pm exactly - good thing Starbucks was just down stairs to keep me busy with work during that day as I was so tired from only two hours of sleep the night before and from my flight, that I had no choice but to wait and use my laptop at Starbucks - even after I went out on a mission to search for Kerry Park. Having Starbucks downstairs was very helpful every morning for a great cup of coffee and free Wi-fi.
Room:
Room was a decent size. Very clean!! The kitchenette feature with a microwave was very helpful for my friend and I to heat up some oatmeal and make hot tea in the mornings. Our room was on the 4th floor, #423. The windows faced the roof of the building next door with a slight view of the Space Needle to the left. It did not get hot during our stay, but only stuffy during the night and morning even with the window slightly open. Luckily all three of us were small enough to fit on the queen size bed. To get a rolling bed was $15 per night, and we opted out of it and stuck with the single queen size bed instead. Quiet floor and room location even with windows open.
Bathroom was very clean. I noticed they clean the tub very well and replaced all the mini toiletries every morning - they smell good, too!
Roof:
AMAZING view both during the day and night!!!!! Too bad their other roof entry gets in the way of the view for picture taking, but it was still a great sight, nonetheless. The roof was empty for the most part when I was visiting. Several reclining chairs lined up, allowing several visitors to relax at the same time. The hotel only has one elevator that goes to the roof which got annoying after a while since we had to wait for it to come back up and/or wait for other people to get off.
Overall, this hotel was great. I would go back and stay here (if the pricing is good next time) since it is nearby Seattle Center/Mono rail and the Space Needle were less than 8 minutes away, walking distance. A lot of great restaurants, varying in all types of Ethnic foods. The bus stop was just right across the street of the hotel as well! 
Hotel cost for three nights, 2 adults+1 child was $333.

title_masked: No AC; shuttle service was horrible
text_masked: We stayed here to take the shuttle to a Carnival cruise; the hotel was full, room had no AC. The guy working gave us the incorrect time to the shuttle so ended up having to wait until the 2nd one came. On the return, we had to wait almost an hour waiting on a couple who decided to be the last ones off the ship; even though the shuttle was full we still had to wait on the last two, so there needs to be a deadline of when the shuttle will depart from the ship. This place was a place to sleep/shower... and that was it. On the plus, it was an easy elevator ride up one flight and the door opened to the room.

I stayed here August 24 & 25, and was here for a business meeting. I have stayed at many different hotels in Austin over many years and this one is the best! I will always stay here next time I need to be in Austin. The staff at the front desk were friendly and professional. My room was immaculate and comfy. The free breakfast each morning has a lot of choices and very good - both hot & cold choices. The morning of the 26th, around 9am, an alarm went off but stopped within 10 seconds. I was on the 6th floor and walked down the stairs to eat breakfast. Within 20 minutes, the elevators were working again, and the staff quickly got them running again. The alarm was due to a pipe in the laundry room....hey, these things happen. While I stayed here, the staff at the front desk were friendly each time I came in & out the building. There is a Burger King next door, and across the Mopac expressway is the Arbor Walk shopping center with more choices to eat, as well as shops.

title_masked: A relaxing experience with the best of both worlds
text_masked: I have stayed at the Bay Club every time I come to San Diego. It is so peaceful - only 2 stories, wonderful rooms and beds, great breakfast, bar and pool. You can have a room that faces the bay or the marina. In the morning and/or evening before you take advantage of the fabulous city, take a long stroll along the bay and watch the wildlife and the activities of Pt. Loma.

title_masked: Convenient to Macy's, SOHO, Empire State Bldg
text_masked: Very comfortable hotel rooms with Frette linens, great rainfall shower heads, perfect for business travel. Convenient to Macy's, subway, SOHO bars and restaurants, and the Empire State Building. Perfect for business travelers.

title_masked: Great location for conventions and sporting events
text_masked:
Visited the hotel in November, had a nice room overlooking the park. Room was clean, well appointed and smelled fresh. the bathroom was also clean, including the Tub / Shower area. Had access to the concierge lounge for evening snacks and morning light breakfast. The lounge is open on the weekends and it is quite large. Many areas to relax and meet in. 
Overall a great stay. Did not eat at any restaurants in the hotel but just a few short blocks is a variety of restaurants now

OK, I generally don't write these things, but in this case, I am compelled to thank the entire staff of the Hotel Palomar in Dallas. My son had pretty major surgery on his knee and, as a student at nearby Southern Methodist University, needed a few days of care before starting second semester classes. We have stayed at the Palomar before and loved it, but this time, we needed a little more help. We needed to move to a different room in the middle of the night. We needed two huge buckets of ice three times daily to keep the ice machine on his knee working. We needed every person, housekeeper, waiter, or other staff, to tap lightly on the door so as to not wake the patient. We needed prescriptions filled, and other items from the local CVS. We needed trips to my son's dorm room to pick up clothing and sundries. We needed middle of the night trips for other items and errands. Most of all, we needed compassionate and understanding folks to change the hotel room into a private hospital room. 
In no particular order, I wish to personally thank the general manager, Andrew Wright, for gifts and conveniences offered to my family. I wish to thank Kristy and Beverly at the front desk for helping me find the right room a couple of times, sending toothbrushes, a large garbage bag with rubber bands to my son could keep the bad leg dry while showering, delivering numerous other items and coordinating other support staff for my every request. I wish to thank Darin and Nick for setting up balloons and other stuff I really can't talk about to cheer up my son, not to mention the constant ice delivery at all times of the day and night. And finally to Michael who helped coordinate all of these efforts. The room was kept spotless thanks to the efforts of two really sweet housekeepers who coordinated the cleaning of the room while we were at dinner, and managed to do this while moving two machines necessary for the physical therapy on that knee.
In summary, if it sounds like I'm stroking this hotel and the folks who helped me with me stay, I am. They deserve accolades, and did all that I asked and more to make this last difficult week as enjoyable as possible. I'd stay here anytime - these guys never got lost like folks in so many huge properties.
Best,
Dan Stratton

Just got back from our three night stay at Hilton Palacio del Rio. This was our second visit to the San Antonio Riverwalk and our first time staying right there where all the action is. I found this hotel to be very clean and the staff super nice and friendly. You can see that the hotel has been renovated and the colors and style etc were really nice. 
Our first night we stayed on the 7th floor in a river view room which was handicapped accessible. we did not need this room type and after the first night we moved to a city side room. Our reasons were that the riverside was very noisy with compressor units and many people around very late into the evening. also the bathroom was really large which took up precious space in the rest of the room. so after dinner the first night we stopped by the front desk and requested a possible room change--the manager was very nice and said to stop by in the morning around 11 and there would be another room for us to switch to on a higher floor and in the front per our request. and oh yes--here are two free breakfast coupons for you for the inconvenience of not have another room available right now! This was Memorial Weekend and they were totally booked..this was above and beyond and we truly appreciated it! The next morning they did indeed have another room for us on the floor/location we requested. All in all a wonderful stay and visit with our son who is in the Air Force (six years and counting!) San Antonio is a very proud city and the people are really friendly and nice. Also very loyal to their basketball team--Spurs won first game of playoffs and every single auto/truck/train drove around the city for hours until about 2am honking horns etc....should be a real loud time if they win the series!

Front desk is very friendly and helpful. We had a city view and the room was very clean and comfortable. Absolutely the nicest and most comfortable bed we've ever slept on! There was a coffee maker in the room (great coffee!), bathroom was large and clean, even had a lighted magnifying mirror. It was my husbands birhday and there was a bottle of wine waiting in the room when we checked in, that was a nice surprise. Pikes Place Market is right there and it's a short walk to the monorail for going to the Space Needle. This was our first time in Seattle and only had two nights so we wanted to be close to everything we might want to see. The rooms were a little expensive, but all the hotels in Seattle are not very cheap...and we saved money by not having to rent a car and didn't waste our precious time getting to where we wanted. The old saying that you get what you pay for applies here. The hotel was full so we weren't able to ask to see a waterfront room, so can't comment if the additional cost would be worth it, but the roof top deck was nice.

This hotel was extremently comfortable, and convenient to the beautiful marketplace. Free parking, offered a full delicious breakfast. The pool was very nice, and all of the staff were excellent, and helpful. The marketplace was only a few blocks, within walking distance (approx. 10-15min).

The room was a nice size. Had an very nice desk. Coffee maker in the room. Only bad thing was the refrigerator was too full of expensive items and not able to be used for anything else.
Very comfortable bed.
Great location.

title_masked: Ok for the price but avoid the 14th floor!
text_masked: We stayed here for two nights in Memphis as it is just around the corner from Beale Street. The hotel is very dated and really needs an upgrade. However the staff are lovely - we ordered room service and it was prompt and a bargain price. Unfortunately on our second night we were prevented from sleeping because there was a wedding happening on the floor above. We stayed on the 14th floor and it was a Saturday night. The music was so loud that it was vibrating the ceiling and the cupboard was squeaking - we actually thought there was some serious couple action going on next door! But on further investigation it was the bass reverberating through the structure of the building from the music being played above. I complained to the reception, but was brushed off so then I complained to the Manager, who was apologetic and we did have some money knocked off our bill when we checked out. Location wise it is good but avoid the 14th floor at all costs unless you can sleep through anything!

Great Marriott quality at a good price. Rooms are a bit bigger than some in downtown Chicago, and the free breakfast makes feeding kids a breeze. Great location between Michigan Avenue and the lake. Close to excellent shopping and restaurants and within a short walk to State/Grand El stop on the Red Line for quick access to the Loop, Lincoln Park, Wrigley Field and U.S. Cellular Field.

I will start this review off by saying that since I live in NYC I don't stay in many of the city's hotels. I stayed in the city for a girls night out to celebrate a friend's bachelorette. 
Service - Checkin was a breeze and didn't take more than 5 minutes. During checkin I signed up for Hilton Honors and casually mentioned that I have a few friends coming to celebrate. I was pleasantly surprised when half a hour later there was a knock on my door with a complimentary bottle of champagne. 
Room- I got a jr king suite and the room was much more spacious than I expected. Full bedroom and ok living room. Our view from the bedroom was absolutely amazing. We had a full on view of the WTC memorial and tower. 
Decor - decor is ok but pretty bland compared to other places I've stayed in. 
Food - I cannot comment on as I didn't stay long enough in the hotel. However as a New Yorker I would recommend that anyone visiting from out of town go out and explore the city instead of room service as we have so much to offer for all budgets.

Everything about this hotel is satisfactory or a bit better as I expect from a large hotel chain. The rooms are comfortable and a good size. Shower was very powerful which was a pleasant surprise and all areas seemed clean. The neighbourhood the hotel is situated in however is not the best. In England we would call it 'seedy'. It was fine getting down to the tourist areas of Pier 39 by bus and picking up the tram so by day the location is good. For breakfast I went to Sam's Diner across the road which was great and ate much more cheaply and by the looks of the dining room at the hotel ate much fresher ingredients too.

title_masked: Good Stay at the Wheeler Mansion
text_masked: The mansion is beautifully restored and we loved the atmosphere during our stay in March 2012. Upon check-in, we would have apreciated a little more info on the hotel. For example, we were never told told about the time for breakfast or where it was located. All in all, the room was beautiful and the staff was very friendly and helpful. Would recommend to anyone looking for a charming B&B in Chicago.

title_masked: A really classy, classic hotel close to the convention center.
text_masked: We stayed at the Four Seasons recently for a meeting at the convention center. The location was convenient, the rooms well appointed and comfortable, and the level of friendly service exceptional. The hotel is located on the river with great access to a running and walking path and is walking distance to the music scene on 6th street and numerous good restaurants. It's not an inexpensive place to stay, but was an excellent bargain at the conference rate. Would highly recommend, it, it stands up to some of the best hotel stays I've experienced (primarily traveling to conferences).

title_masked: Unique hotel, Good sized rooms, and great service
text_masked:
My wife and i took a trip to Boston for Memorial Weekend. 
I reserved 2 nights at 225ish but wasn't sure what to expect from Liberty Hotel since it was our first time in Boston. 
The hotel had an interesting feel as it used to be a prison that was converted and extended. Service was excellent, the rooms were clean, and modern.

Just spent one evening at Granduca -- would have loved to stay longer and take advantage of the fitness room, pool, hot tub, etc. We stayed in a "Traditional Suite" (its name on Hotels.com), which the Granduca website calls a Junior Suite. It was truly posh! Beautiful sitting area and kitchen complete w/ granite counters, cookware, a lovely dining table, etc. I kept telling my husband we should build a vacation home that looks just like that! He said no -- we'll just return to Granduca!
Ristorante Cavour was great for lunch. The service was impeccable. Food was good (not great), but very enjoyable. Lovely atmosphere.

I stayed at this hotel as it was through part of my prize i won from Broadway Across America for a trip to the Tony's. It was an excellent hotel and as others have commented, the staff is top notch. The wine reception is a plus and being so close to Times Square without being right on top of it is wonderful as well. I too, joined the Kimpton In touch and it was nice to be able to have some water right there via the mini-bar. The room size and bathroom were very good for what I had anticipated in NYC. Will hopefully be able to return on my own dime as the extra night I paid for was way above my budget, even in NY. The beds were some of the best i've ever slept in hotel wise.

title_masked: Marriott Marquis, NYC, the place to be
text_masked:
It was a nice hotel, but not the best. The room wasn't as clean as I thought it would be. My clock was very dusty, see picture attached. There was a stain on my carpet. My ice bucket had melted ice from the last visitor(s). The elevators were a little confusing. It's hard to figure out which elevator you go on to get to the right floor.
Marriott Marquis was nice, especially its location. I'd come back if I could, but I would hope for a little better and/or cleaner room.

title_masked: Pleasant enough service, difficult for hotel to compete with others
text_masked:
Stayed for one night at the Indianapolis Hilton. The location is great, near all the major restaurants and sights in downtown Indy. It is very accessible by the freeway and there is plenty of nearby public parking if you don't want to pay the steep hotel parking fee.
The lobby is large, well-lit, and welcoming and there are two nice spots attached to the hotel for a nice meal or drink.
Check in is efficient and the staff is friendly.
The worst part of the hotel (and why I would probably choose another) is the room. Yes, the hotel is a little older, but my room on the 10th floor did not have a serious window. The room felt like a cell block because the only "window" was a piece of glass that was 1foot wide and maybe 8 ft high. The room felt dark, cold, and unwelcoming. I understand that some hotels in Manhattan may have small windows, but this room should be taken out of the rotation and used as a storage room. I can't comment on the other rooms because I didnt ask for a change, but I feel that if a customer is paying $190/night, he/she should not be put in a room such as this. Perhaps other rooms are nicer, but i didnt have one of those and my experience was soured.
While my room was non-smoking, there was a residual scent of tobacco in the room. The bathroom was dated (but clean) and there was a faint smell of mildew. 
Overall, the location is great, the service is fine, but I was disappointed in the actual room.

Very helpful and friendly staff.Ideal location in Philadelphia for sightseeing. Easy walking distance to Independence Hall & Liberty Bell. Room was a bit small but adequate especially as we were sightseeing every day. Breakfast was average but was complimentary.My wife liked the fact that she could made waffles for breakfast, nice touch. When I return to Philadelphia I will probably stay here again.

title_masked: Well-named; like home (if your Mom was a decent cook)
text_masked: Beautiful site, often-empty pool, handy to have supper provided, spacious suite, but most important is the friendly staff. Techno-savvy for those of us who aren't, knowledgeable about the area, never too busy to help you out. And they don't make you feel rushed if you want to linger an hour (or 2) in the dining room.

title_masked: Great property near Times Square! Good value!
text_masked: Nice, 3 star hotel convenient to Times Square, Penn Station and the bus terminal. Rooms are small but clean, big desk and flat screen hotel. I love this place as a business property being relatively close to my company's showroom and for getting around NYC and beyond. Thirty-two floors x 8 rooms per floor all close to the elevator but no elevator noise! This property has a lot of group activity so the free breakfast is a mob scene most mornings so hang a right out of the hotel, go up one block, cross the street and get a real breakfast if you want one at Teleon Cafe. Also, there is a roof top lounge that must be pretty nice (Sky Room) as every night I come back there is a "Saturday Night Fever" crowd waiting in line to go up. Also, the black bouncer guys are not real friendly and act like they're working the door at the Viper Room. Whatever. Still a very nice property overall.....I have already booked another stay for the end of next month.

title_masked: This is an excellent hotel in an excellent location
text_masked: I really enjoyed this hotel. It couldn't be in a better location. There are tons of things within walking distance and it is close to the train as well. My queen bed room was small, but everything was nice and up-to-date. There isn't really a restaurant in the hotel (just some breakfast basics at a little deli-type counter as far I could tell), but you are so close to restaurants within walking distance, who cares? I really liked the price I paid - good value for the money.

I just stayed in the W Union Square, for my semi-annual trip to help my NYU child move into residence. This hotel has become our home away from home, not only because of its proximity to the NYU and wonderful SOHO area of New York. We had arranged for a "mega" room because of all the luggage we had, and the room was great. We lucked into a corner room so we had two different views. The doormen were wonderful helping us with our luggage. The breakfast in Olives, the hotel restaurant was superb! The egg white omelet they make is amazing. The dinner was also great; I didn't feel like anything fancy and the chef was good enough to just give me pasta with tomato sauce, with no fuss at all! The staff were all wonderful, and very pleasant, even wishing my daughter good luck on her next semester. While we were here, an elevator broke down, but the staff were nice enough to let us use the staff elevator, for the one time we had to go up to the room before the elevator was fixed. 
The gym is small, but well equipped, even with a boxing area for those so inclined.
The rooms are a bit dark, but we don't notice it really because we don't stay in the hotel , because we came to be at the university, or explore this great city.
Thanks, W Union Square, for another pleasant visit. See you in the spring!

Pros:
-Everything was very clean.
-The beds were very comfy
-Check in and out was very easy
-Location is like four blocks from Pike's market
Cons:
-TV did not work very well, some channels were very fuzzy. I didn't know TVs were like that anymore! 
-I was there for a conference and the set up of the conference rooms was kind of weird.

Hats off to the staff of the Ritz Carlton in Battery Park. Sure it is away from alot of the typical NYC sites, but the staff, the property, the views are just unbeatable in Manhattan. We were greeted by name every where we went, got absolutely perfect dinner recommendations and the room was outstanding, very large, great beds, good rest after travelling from Singapore. The club lounge was well appointed and quiet too, made for a nice way to start our evenings with a cocktail. We will return!

We came here for my husbands review at MD Anderson. What a wonderful place this is!!! The room is great and can't complain about anything. The staff is awesome and always ready to go the extra mile for you.
We are very close to MD Anderson and also close to other places like places to shop. We had two days off, so drove to Galveston yesterday.
I would recommend this motel to anyone. After reading the other reviews that people have posted, I agree that the bathrooms are in a little need of updating, but nothing so bad that I would give them a bad rating.
The breakfast was great and the gal running it was sweet and very helpful. 
We will be coming back next week for my husbands surgery and this is where we plan to stay!!!
Thanks for providing a wonderful place and helpful people at a time when we are in need of them!!!!
Cheryl and Bill Raduenz

title_masked: Good hotel, nice view of city
text_masked: Needed a hotel at the last minute going to a conference. Everything was sold out and this wasn't too far away. Reasonable price too. Breakfast in restaurant at top of hotel had a great view of the city. Shuttle can take you to convention center or if you don't want to wait you can drive there in under 10 minutes.

I recently stayed here for 9 nights with my partner and overall was very impressed. For tourists to San Fran, the hotel could not be better located. It's right by Union Square so very close to all the shops and restaurants in the downtown area. It's also just down the road from the China Town area and well located for public transport (Powell St MUNI and BART stations are less than five minutes walkaway) so it really is a great base for exploring this fantastic city. 
The staff were friendly and generally helpful. I mentioned on check in that we were staying for my partner's 40th birthday and within ten minutes of arriving at our room, reception had sent up two cakes and a bottle of red wine. It was a lovely gesture! We were originally assigned a room on the 16th floor and it was a little noisy outside. When my partner mentioned this the following morning, we were switched to a room on a higher floor. This was perfectly quiet and of course, the views were much better! Our room was large and very clean. 
Make sure that you go to the bar on the 36th floor. The views are awesome and it's a lovely space to relax with a glass of wine after a hard day's sightseeing or shopping. 
The only downsides were that the hotel's lobby area was a bit cramped and chaotic but this was no doubt because that area of the hotel was in the middle of a renovation. Also there is no free WiFi, either in the rooms or reception. This is obviously a drawback in this day and age. But for this, the hotel would have received 5/5 from me. 
On the whole though, a great choice and I'd stay here again.

Had to spend a night in NYC and found this hotel on hotels.com for $109. There was 24 hour parking 2 blocks away for $38 but the hotel validated the parking ticket which provided an $8 discount. The hotel is in a great location, the rooms were clean, furnishing modern, the beds comfortable. The buffet breakfast was pretty standard hotel breakfast food, the bill came to $36 but we had prepaid for breakfast for $15 for 2 people. With breakfast and taxes the bill came to about $145, pretty good for a nice midtown hotel. I would definately stay there again.

I read many of the reviews on this place before I decided to still take the plunge - luckily for the most part it worked out for us. The location is good - we were able to walk to many of the places that we wanted to eat and drink at. When we checked in and I heard a had a room on the 2nd floor, I asked for one on a higher floor to which the replied not possible to both nights, I could try coming back to trade the next day - but bonus, I was upgraded to a junior suite which is at least from what I have read - bigger than alot of the other rooms. It was nice having a refrigerator in the room and the seperate day bed to keep our stuff on. Did have a tub with shower - but the stopper for the tub was not working properly. The staff for the most part was fine except for one woman which I wish I checked her name...otherwise they seemed nice and helped with directions. The valet service leaves a bit to be desired, it usually took longer than the 20 minutes we were advised and the one time I left my car to be put away - it was still there an hour and 20 minutes later. Did not even try the "breakfast". We did use our free drink coupons at InFusion and had some chicken satay - which was good. Also we did not go to the club. The hotel served it's purpose good location, good price......overall not the worst place I have stayed - just make sure you try to get a room away from the nightclub, we could slightly hear club thumping but wasn't too bad in room 223.

title_masked: The Holiday Inn Inner Harbor is a Homerun!
text_masked: We just recently stayed at the Holiday Inn Inner Harbor and it was terrific. The Location is absolutely fantastic and within a short walk of almost everything in the Inner Harbor area. We had tickets to the baseball game and you could actually see the inside of the stadium from the room. The room itself was really nice and very clean. The bedding was in great shape and the entire room was spotless. Everything in the room also worked perfectly including the wireless high speed connection so was able to use my IPAD. Service was great and the Front Desk very helpful in assiting us with dining suggestions as well as being very accommodating. Loved the coffe shop, Dotti's, right off the lobby...perfect start to the morning....The Holiday Inn Inner Harbor was a homerun in our book. JohnNYC

Chose the Palace as we were attending a wedding, with a reception that would be held in the Palace. Location is fantastic: across from St. Patricks Cathedral, Times Square and Central Park were just a short walk, Theatre District is also in walking distance, but taxis abound here.. The staff was available everywhere and extremely helpful. It would have been nice to brew a cup of coffee in the room, but that was the only thing missing.The room was large and the bed was very comfortable.

title_masked: Great location, very good staff, comfortable room
text_masked: Stayed here for a night and had a great time. The hotel is located right on the water and within walking distance to everything. We had a very comfortable room, beds are great. The bartender was friendly and fun to chat with. We did not use the pool this trip, but it is nice to have one. There is a T stop next door but truly you can walk to South Station, North Station and everything in between.

title_masked: JW Marriott San Antonio Hill Country Resort & Spa
text_masked:
Visited this property in June for a convention.
I was very impressed with the hotel as a whole. The rooms were really clean and well-decorated as you would expect from a JW Marriott property.
The restaurants and bars were really nice as well. The sports bar on the property was the coolest one I've ever seen in a Marriott, and was the center of activity at night.
I didn't get a chance to play golf or visit the water park, but I was told that both were very nice.
The only downside is that the hotel is not very close to downtown or the riverwalk, but you wouldn't stay here if that was the reason for your visit to San Antonio.
I would highly recommend this hotel.

Hotel is clean, sleek, and provides good service. The Omni is a quick walk to Congress and Sixth St nightlife without having to be in the thick of it. Two complaints: there was a lot of noise throughout the night/early morning coming from other guests. It was the first weekend of the UT football season, so lots of young alumni at the hotel. Secondly, the shower does not have a light in it and can be quite dark.

It's clean, downtown, nice sized room, has free parking, & great service; what else do you need? It might not have all the frills & thrills of a 5 star hotel, but for the location & a third the price, you can't beat it. We stayed there for 3 nights & it's within walking distance (yes, we walked everywhere) of numerous attractions, restaurants, & shopping. 
If you're looking for a nice hotel, without the need for all the extra frills, in downtown within walking distance of enjoying many of Chicago's attractions, don't discount this hotel. The free parking saves a lot of $$, along with the convenience of having the vehicle available whenever you want it. We will definitely stay here again.

Had breakfast at the hotel and everything was so delicious, and the staff was extremely nice, and made me feel right at home. Especially Chef Nati Moreno, thanks for making my family's experience wonderful.

title_masked: Waited All My Life to Stay Here
text_masked:
As a kid when our family visited San Diego, I would dream of staying at the Catamaran. It's charm mixed with location left me longing to stay there when we passed by. All these years later and I was thrilled when I could finally live out my Catamaran dream! 
It wasn't all I dreamed it would be, but it wasn't bad either. The room I had was rather small and my view was overlooking the road where trash and laundry leave the property. It was also noisy for that reason, as loads of carts rolled by for both trash and laundry pick-up. Dreams dashed on the room side, I did thoroughly enjoy the restaurant and sitting out on the patio overlooking Mission Bay. Although the hostess was talking on her cell phone when I stepped up to get a table, the rest of the wait staff were very nice/helpful. My first night there I wasn't feeling great so I tried to order hot tea from room service. Lets just say that hot tea is not their specialty. They only had one tea bag in stock and the water was definitely from the hot water faucet.
The hotel was booked with back to back to back to back wedding events. As I sat at lunch overlooking the bay, the staff were setting up for three different weddings on the lawn. The staff did a remarkable job for the volume of weddings, as all three were turned over within two hours to accommodate another two weddings. 
I'm glad I finally got to stay at the Catamaran as it was a nice property although the rooms seemed overpriced ($169 per night) for what I got. The location is amazing and the grounds of the hotel are beautiful. Would I return? I'll give it a "maybe" depending on if I got a better room rate next time around.

One of the best hotels I've visited in NYC. My Mom and I travel to NYC every couple of years and usually end up in 'closet' hotel rooms. This was much like you would find at a normal hotel. 2 beds, lots of room to walk around. Of course we end up spending more, about $300 a night over the weekend, which isn't bad for NY. Beds were clean, bathroom was clean. View was nice as well. Breakfast in the restaurant was almost $25 per person for the buffet and it broke down to $6 for an egg and toast. So the concierge told us to walk a block down the street and visit a diner, and the food was excellent, the place was packed, coffee was good and all for $10!! What a steal and real close to the hotel.

This was really the best hotel we could wish in NY. Close to Times square but still quit. We had a room on the 24th room with a nice view on the Empire State Building. The bed and bathroom were very comfertable. When we go back to NY we will take this hotel again, without any thinking!

I was a bit worried as I thought this was an older hotel in Seattle, but boy was I wrong! It was completely renovated and modern. The room was very big for city standards, and beautifully decorated. The lobby was comfortable and a hangout with a beautiful fireplace and comfortable seating. The staff was incredibly accomodating. The two restaurants attached were both great, and Lola had the best happy hour! The location was so perfect, right in the center of town. I highly recommend this hotel!

title_masked: Best Place to stay in NYC for work or fun
text_masked: This is a great hotel, the service is awesome, they make you feel welcomed. The staff are very helpful. The rooms are spacious and very comfortable. Some have balconies. The bathroom amenities are great. The location is very convenient. There is a lounge on the second floor perfect for meetings or working inbetween meetings. Very close to everything, many nearby dining options both inexpensive & culinary excellence.

We stayed three nights due to the good reviews. At arrival we needed the pin emailed by the hotel. Worked well. The location is really good for non-car-user. Every point of interest is reachable either by foot or via the rail. If you have a car look for another hotel as parking lots are very expensive. The room itself is small and there was ahorribly smell in our room. The heater was on without possibility to be switched off. Lovely in summer...... The bathroom is not a room but a small tiny chamber with hot or cold water. Nothing in between.
Be aware no elevator. So if you have heavy bags you have to put them over a narrow stairhouse. Not funny.
Next time I will stay at the motel which is in the same corner as the H. It has a parking lotvand a similar price.

We always go back here. You can't beat the location or friendliness of the staff. It is very central for everything you need downtown.
The rooms are a fair size and the hotel is peaceful. The evening free wine reception - with sangria - is a really nice touch.

title_masked: Decent Stay; Ask Twice If Accessibility is Needed
text_masked: Stayed here for a convention in July 2012. Lovely room and well kept; kudos to the cleaning staff. Location a bit isolated from stops in Dallas, but I didn't go for sightseeing. Wifi at $13/day? Seems really excessive and unnecessary. Had reports from friends regarding the hotel's accessibility options that the front desk was not helpful at all. Travelers may want to check out those options before booking.

title_masked: Cool hotel, good staff, nice amenities
text_masked:
Stayed in room #1407 for three nights. King bed, large room and bathroom for the city. The hotel’s design is on the stark side. I generally don’t like design hotels b/c they look cool but are rarely functional (the cooler the shower looks the more it leaks) – and there’s usually an air of snob. The Andaz is different – it’s a really good hybrid of chic and friendly. I was met immediately when I arrived – no real check-in desk, just a bunch of folks w. iPads. I was offered a drink and quickly checked in. Room 1407 is spacious. No view to speak of – but quiet and calm. The bed was good – a little firm, more along the lines of a European hotel bed than American. Great bedding and pillows. Lots of plugs for gadgets. There’s a full-length mirror – it pulls out from wall beside mini-fridge area. Small closet. Blackout shades to assure privacy and good sleep quality. Flat screen TV w. lots of channels – but most of the time I was there the satellite was iffy. Had three room service breakfasts – good food and fast service. I asked for a NY Times and rec’d gratis. Duane Reade (drug store) across the street. 
The only thing I really didn’t like about the room was poor lighting. It’s much too dark in the bathroom and area by the closet mirror. I dragged a freestanding lamp in to help but it was still much too dark. A lady needs her light to primp. 
The 1 & 2 lines are very close. Short walk to stock market, Trinity church, Century 21, South St. Seaport and Century 21. Wall St. is much livelier after hours than it used to be – but it’s still pretty quiet at night. 
Ate in the formal restaurant – very good food and service. Also had drinks and food at the bar. Good drink and the crab cake – while minute – was yummy. 
Pros
Quiet location, good for sleep
Good-sized room for NYC
Free Wi-Fi with good signal
Good work area
Free snacks & water – why don’t all hotels do this? 
Free coffee & lattes downstairs
Friendly staff
Good bedding & pillows
Strong shower strength, very large shower
Cons
Very poor lighting in bathroom and closet/mirror area
Satellite TV was in and out most of my stay

title_masked: Not so Clean and Problem after Problem
text_masked: I checked in which took what seemed forever. Got to my room used the toilet and it was clogged before I used it. So I spent the first 15 minutes plunging the toilet. The room was stuffy and smelled like pet urine. Then my room key didn't work. I left to run some errands got back to my room to find that my door was open. You had to pull it really hard to make sure it was closed. The room was dusty and looks like a blind person cleaned it. The microwave's turn table plate was missing. The shower had mold growing between the tiles. I don't think I would stay here or recommend this place to anyone.

title_masked: Great hotel in an excellent location
