text_masked: My mom and I stayed here for 4 nights in June while I attended a conference. This is a great property if your company will spring for it. Right across the street from the convention center, and within walking distance to many area attractions. Hotel was sparkling clean, and all staff very friendly and helpful. A tip for parking: choose self park. It's cheaper, and very convenient (directly underneath the hotel), and you have unlimited in and out privileges.

The Conrad is a nice hotel centrally located in downtown Chicago. Very convenient to Michigan Ave. The rooms are well appointed and the staff is professional. But if you are looking for a world class hotel, this isn't it.

Oh boy,
Unfortunately my family and I were placed at this hotel as a result of a priceline bid for a 4 star, this hotel is anything but a 4star. I'll reiterate the sentiment from other travellers here...the queen rooms are microscopic. My 6 year old son who has had a fair share of nights in hotels, as we travel fairly often, upon untering the room said ..."mom this room is ridiculous"..lol. hmmm (I wonder if he could spell ridiculous)
Simply getting from the bathroom to the bed involved thought so that you didn't knock your leg on the hard wooden frame of the bed, which we each did a couple of times. Requesting a different room was to no avail as the front desk staff informed us that they were fully booked (definitely believable as it was flower show weekend in Chicago), they were however willing to show another queen room, that unbelievably was smaller than the one we were in. I think my chuckle and expression conveyed the "ridiculousness" of the space and the hotel clerk informed me that this was a boutique hotel. As if to say the definition of a boutique hotel is one with very small rooms.
During our short one night stay, one of the maintenance staff tried to enter the room and then immediately apologized saying that she though that the room was unoccupied, later on that evening, closet hangars were brought to us when we didnt request them. The hubby and I had a good laugh...murphys law. The one service caveat was the doorman... excellent excellent excellent... he always seemed to appear out of nowhere to get the door or offer up a cab
Now on to the goodies: 
The location is about 5 blocks west of Michigan avenue, so not in the heart of the shopping district but close enough if you dont mind the walk. 
If you have children, Rainforest Cafe, McDonalds and a the super reasonable Barnelli's Pasta Place is within a couple of blocks south of the hotel. A couple blocks north of the hotel there is an "outside" parking lot that was less expensive than hotel parking.
There are restaurants everywhere on every corner near this hotel so, lots to eat. The hotel also had a restaurant that we did not really have an opportunity to try, so no comments there.
Anyway, for the business no-frills traveller or the crash and dash-budget conscious single... this could be your place (if the price is right). Not a place I would recommend for families, I'd look first towards Michigan Ave. 4 star hotels as on the non-event weekends rates are sometimes less than $100 per night.

The customer service at this hotel/motel is always extraordinary. This is the main reason that I return to this property. Front desk personel are always VERY helpful and courteous. Property is well kept and clean and safe. Kudos

We stayed at the Prescott during the end of May 2012. They offer a continental breakfast...just average, but free. They offer a wine hour from 5-6pm every night. The room was neat, clean and big enough. The staff was pleasant and helpful. The very best part was the location, just a block or so from Union Square. Would stay there again!

Stayed here for 2 nights in September while waiting for a cruise departure. Excellent location to the Freedom trail and other downtown Boston sights. Hotel does not have a courtesy car, but you can take a free airport bus to the Tube and the medical center station is right next door. Hotel was clean, but needed some cosmetic treatment in the bathroom.
I paid $199 plus tax per night for 2 king bed room using a corporate discount. Otherwise the rooms are over $300. Taxi to the cruise port from the hotel is about $12.
I did not eat at the hotel as there are several restaurants and fast food places within near walking distance. Check in was quick and staff was very friendly.

Great location, and the cheapest for having almost everything I need in walking distance. I travel for work, and with the travelodge I'm not only near transportation but also near sights I like to take my family to if they are visiting for the weekend. The door man also always gives me great suggestions for food and for the fastest way to get somewhere.

title_masked: Luxurious and comfortable but not for the noise sensitive
text_masked: I stayed at this hotel for a conference. My room was lovely, luxuriously fitted out as one would expect from a hotel of this standard. Overall, the service was great, the room very comfortable and very clean, the location to the conference and business centre of Austin excellent. Unfortunately I was disturbed most nights by the noise, despite using earplugs. The elevators are extremely noisy, so much so that I was told the staff stop one or two of them during the night if there are not too many people in the hotel. In addition to the frequent "clunk, clunk" of the lifts, there are huge airconditioning motors outside which make a low but constant drone. In all fairness, I didn't ask for a different room, I was too exhausted at first and then the hotel seemed pretty much full because of the conference. However, I would not stay here again because of noise. If you are going to stay here make sure you get a room away from the elevators.

Great choice for families wanting to be in walking distance to the harbor. We have 3 kids and found sleeping arrangements to be well planned out. The room was not tight and the front desk staff as well as the breakfast staff were friendly. The cons included some noise from local emergency vehicles and TV placement on a small side table making it difficult to view from the beds in the 2 bed/couch rooms. Would suggest looking for parking options before you go as valet is a bit pricey.

We stayed here during the 2012 Broad Street 10 Mile Run. 
We would have preferred to stay in downtown Philadelphia, but everything was booked. 
The hotel is modern and clean.
The front desk staff and phone operators made me feel that I was either annoying them or asking them to go beyond their duties when I asked for assistance.
The cost for the room was a bit more than it should have been for the overall experience, building, and neighborhood.

This hotel is has a great, quiet location and a welcome shuttle for the airport and seaport, plus area restaurants. All of the employees that we interacted with were very pleasant, with the exception noted later in this review. The hotel is in need of a good cleaning and better maintenance. We stayed there recently twice within a two week span, and the hallway carpets on 6th floor and 3rd floor were filthy with stains from spilled beverages. The tiles in the entry area near the fireplace were sticky with a spilled beverage that was not mopped up, and filth buildup along all corners and edges where walls meet the floors. There is peeling wallpaper all over, cobwebs above the curtains in both rooms we had, small cosmetic touch-ups needed throughout, leaking sink faucets around the handles. The brass interiors of the elevators were dull, discoloured, and graffitti scratched up. During the breakfast time, all of the thongs for various food items (muffins, bagels, English muffins, etc.) were placed in a single container near the food items; my wife and I witnessed many people who simply reached in the plastic bins with their hands to retrieve what they wanted. This could be prevented by leaving the thongs in each individual plastic bin. It would help if there was an employee who could hover in the area to do clean-ups as needed; tables in the area were always dirty. The worst part of our second stay was a housekeeping employee who knocked on our door 3 times between 8.30 and 10.00, and then called us at 10.15 to ask when we were checking out; checkout time is 11 a.m. Never in all of our years travelling have we been urged to vacate our room before checkout time.

title_masked: Back Again and Wish I Could Stay Here Every Time
text_masked:
Just everything is right; perfect location for me - midtown close to my customers and food; friendly/helpful staff without pretense, genuinely like to help and want you to enjoy your stay; great accommodations - still in great shape, comfortable, modern, all the technology you need.
What more can I say? If the price is right, this is my choice in Manhattan.

title_masked: The staff is the highlight, but the location is great too
text_masked: I spent six days at this property in June while in Seattle on business. The staff could not have been more accommodating - from the friendliness of the valet to the front desk to housekeeping -- they were genuinely welcoming and friendly. Brian, who is new to this hotel, went above and beyond in a very genuine way. He was very eager to help me with tips about where to go (the Crumpet shop -- wonderful!) and was just generally delightful. David, the GM, was attune and attentive. I had a small issue with the bartender in the restaurant (he just was not nice) and David handled it immediately and with grace. That was not a hotel staff member and was not at all representative of the overall hotel staff. My experience with the restaurant servers was great. The restaurant is excellent -- both food and service. The lobby of this property is not as spacious (think library) as the other two Kimptons in Seattle but the intimacy has a lovely boutique feel. I am a big fan of Kimptons and will chose this one again in Seattle.

title_masked: Great for work meetings, nice accomodations, great location downtown!
text_masked:
I recently booked a last minute work meeting at this hotel and the staff was wonderful to work with. They were very attentive and Travis F was most helpful. The meeting space was great and the hotel accomodations were quite nice. First time visit to downtown portland and was very pleased.
Beds were soft, rooms were spacious and clean, nice views from some rooms. Restaraunt and lobby bar in hotel as well as Startbucks onsite. 
There was a pool and fitness center but did not have time to see either. 
Easy to walk to many restaraunts and shops in the heart of downtown. Great location

title_masked: Just Like a Potemkin Village...A Facade
text_masked:
Vastly overrated. Quaint, semi-elegant entrance not remotely representative of your room and bathroom, especially if you're a [Discount Site] guest. Housekeeping routinely forgets to deliver a full set of towels (I had no towels whatsoever one night). Drains are chronically slow, ensuring that all the accumulated gunk from previous guests returns to haunt you as you shower. In addition to plumbing problems (water can switch from tepid to boiling in 10 ms.), you will encounter inpoerative lights and broken accessories (broken hook on bathroom door). Front desk always overstaffed when lobby is deserted and understaffed when busloads are checking in.
Last but not least, the prison cell sink, complete with no shelving or cabinet to place your toiletries.

We stayed 3 nights around July 4th to show the grandkids historic Philadelphia. We walked from the Hampton Inn to historic Philadelphia. A bit long, but not bad. Note that parking by the hotel is an extra fee, but the lot was secure. We did not move our car during the 3 days.
The hotel is large, but we did not feel over-run. the elevators were efficient and fast. The pool and exercise room were good. Breakfast was in true Hampton Inn fashion, very good.
Staff was friendly and accommodating.

Normally I would not choose a hotel near an airport due to noise. However, we had an early a.m. flight so decided to stay close by. The hotel was quiet, comfortable, clean, convenient and even had the football game on tv so my husband was excited to watch it.

We spent 3 nights here and booked this hotel with loyalty points. Our room was spacious and overall represented good value for the price. The reception staff were not overly helpful when we asked about leaving luggage. The refurbishment has still not been finished and as a result the bar and restaurant were totally lacking in atmosphere and very basic. The location was good and we were able to walk to most of the places that we wantedd to see. There were a lot of people visiting the adjacent hospital and not so many tourists. A good experience but not as good as we had hoped given that we thought that the works would have been finished by the time we were going.

this staff , and hotel is a gem in nyc! lovely lovely peopls, great rooms, great value- we love it and will highly recommend this hotel.locatioon is great, staff know all the best places to go, from top to bottoom , lovely stay

This was my first stay, I normally stay across the road but the rates were too high. I had a nice, clean room, large TV, and comfortable bed (evidently you can modify the hardness of the mattress but I couldn't tell the difference!) and my rate came with a great cooked breakfast, and the staff service in the breakfast area was the highlight of my stay.

title_masked: Certainly not up to Hilton's standards
text_masked: I know this is a large property with a large staff, but as a business traveler I would have to ask what in the world management is thinking to have an Embassy Suites in this state of mismanagement. Starting at the beginning, I booked a two-bedroom suite -- supposedly with a king in one-bedroom and two queens in the other bedroom, plus a small living area. Pretty simple, right. But when we arrived we were told that this hotel had no such rooms and our only choice was a two-bedroom suite with one king and a queen and sleeper sofa. But that was not the worst at this hotel: The garage, which was quite expensive to park in, had trash everywhere and the elevator looked dangerous and reaked of urine. It just felt creepy to go into. The stench was terrible. That should have told us something. The hallways were dark and depressing. The rooms were not all that bad although not what we booked. But when it came to the breakfast area, depressing took on a whole new meaning. There was nothing attractive about the breakfast -- even though we haver had great experiences at other Embassy Suites. And there was just not enough seating. You just felt like you were on a crouded subway in the middle of New York when someone stood up from their seat and there was a scramble. I would think that even a beginning hotel manager could see the filth, smell the mold and urine, and fix those things. If they can't. there must be somebody, somewhere who cares.

My husband and I recently stayed at this hotel for a quick one-night escape. What a pleasant experience! The hotel is very, very clean and beautifully decorated. It looks like it's been recently renovated. Our room was pretty small but was adorable and very well appointed. The added bonus was that at 5pm we were treated to a wine sampling. We relaxed in the lobby while we tried some great wine - and at no charge! The staff couldn't have been more helpful and accommodating! Looking forward to a reason to go back!

Well I shouldn’t say “surprising” I suppose, since Hilton has a good reputation, but I was blown away by how chic this hotel was! Our stay was fantastic! We needed a hotel close to our old neighborhood in Keller, as we were visiting our rental house so my husband and I selected the Hilton Garden Inn and were pleasantly surprised with its elegance, amazingly nice staff and SUPER comfortable beds. Seriously, the beds were some of the best I have ever stayed in, and we stay in a decent number of hotels. The lobby is very welcoming with dark décor, great lights, and wide open vaulted ceilings. The front desk checked us into our room in about 30 seconds and was very nice. The rooms are very well furnished (I LOVED the paint on the wall, very modern and fancily textured). Everything was very clean, the linens are all washable, including the duvet. I love that they have Neutrogena products as their standard toiletries. My only complaint about the room is that housekeeping didn’t do the most thorough job, as we did not get clean/new drinking glasses in our kitchenette area, but if that is our complaint, hey, it can’t be that terrible. My only other complaint about the hotel is the noise level, not of the staff or road, but of the guests, the hall noise pours easily into the bedrooms and we had some very unconscientious neighbors. But luckily that was only while they were checking out, the rest of the time it was fine. I would totally stay there again in a heartbeat and wish that all hotels were this classy and reasonably priced. Everyone we talked to was very nice, welcoming and competent. The place was not overly crowded. The breakfast had a great selection, the service staff at the restaurant was great! They even have a decent happy hour. The hotel is very close to the airport, Grapevine, and the Ft. Worth suburbs. I was impressed, nice work Hilton Garden Inn, we will surely see you again!

We stayed at the beautiful Standard hotel in East Village a week ago. We would like to share some feedback. It was a great experience. One of the best vacations/hotel stays ever. Fantastic room, great service, complimentary super-nice bikes etc etc. We had no complaints just a great deal of fun. We will definitely come back next time in NYC. We loved both the architecture and the interior design.
And my wife tried to steal the bed and put it in the cabin bag but fortunately it didn’t fit. :-)

I spent two nights at the Double Tree Market Center. I had to attend a conference at the Hilton Anatole, and that hotel was sold out, so I turned to the other convention hotel offering, the Doubletree. I had a room rate of $149/night. The Doubletree is an easy walk to the Hilton Anatole.
The cab fare from Love Field was about $20, which is reasonable. The Doubletree does not offer an airport shuttle. When I arrived at the hotel, I was immediately greeted. I also arrived at 10 a.m., which is much earlier than the usual check-in, but a room was available. I was even given a warm chocolate chip cookie.
My room had two double beds, a desk, a sitting chair, and a dresser unit with a microwave and refrigerator. The room was clean and comfortable, and I never heard any noise from other hotel guests. The hotel provides free Wi-fi, which worked fine for email and some light online work.
The hotel lobby has a bar, and there is a restaurant in the lobby as well, which also offers room service. I didn't eat or drink at either, but it was nice having an in-building option if I needed it.
For other dining options, there's a Dennys and a place called [NAME]'s Prime across the street. There are also restaurants in the other nearby hotels, which includes the Hilton Anatole, Sheraton, Courtyard and Fairfield Inn. A Days Inn and Best Western are also nearby.
The hotel has a business center with two computers and a printer. I also saw a fitness room. I could see the outdoor pool form my room. If you want a pool view get a room ending in 08 or 10, which directly overlook the pool. The even-numbered rooms face west, so if you don't want the morning sun shining in, get an even-numbered room. Also, the rooms ending in 14 and 16 are directly in front of the elevator.
The hotel is about two miles from the Dallas landmark Reunion Tower, which can be seen down Market Center Street.
I enjoyed my stay at the Doubletree. I give the hotel an overall score of 4 because I reserve a full 5 for truly outstanding experiences. I would stay here again. (CS)

A beautiful lobby brings you to an efficient, friendly, staff on your way to a clean and comfortable room in the middle of downtown. A block from 5th Avenue shopping or Grand Central. Food is reasonably priced for New York. The hotel is frequently used as a backdrop for the movie industry.
The rooms are small, but clean, with very comfortable beds and linens. I stay here frequently and it is a favorite.

title_masked: Ok if your in town for Baseball
text_masked: Parking is expensive, but you have no choice really. . . Rooms are ok, clean. They could have a better towels.They have done AWAY with room service but not disclosed when making reservation. Pool was small, had enough chlorine for a pool 4X the size, poor ventilation in area also. Beside the above observation it was just ok.

I booked this room on Priceline and got what I believe to be a great price for a central Washington location for a Saturday night stay. However, I selected a four star property on Priceline and in its current state, I would never rate this property with four stars. You can see that the lobby had a 80's mod vibe but that an attempt was made to update the decor. Did they succeed - I am not so sure. There is a Starbucks in the lobby as well as some type of bar/restaurant which I did not use. There is also supposed to be a very nice real gym that you can use but I did not get a chance to use it. The woman at the front desk was pleasant and helpful. There are some floors in the building that are undergoing renovation. I did not hear any construction noise but I was there on a Saturday night. 
I believe my room was on the 15th floor and the windows faced and interior atrium so I did not hear any street noise. The carpeting in the hallway and the room as well as the curtains were extremely dated looking in what I would describe as a colonial design. The room was somewhat updated with a large flatscreen TV and comfortable beds and nice bedding. The room was smallish. I was given a choice of 1 king bed or 2 full beds. I chose the later but I would have much preferred 2 queens as I was travelling with 2 teen sons. I called the front desk because the TV did not work and a man came with a new remote almost instantly and that solved the problem. It was difficult to position the curtains to block out the daylight but I overlapped them and used a chair to hold them and it worked pretty well and I did get a good night's sleep so I was happy. 
I valet parked my car and left it in the garage. This was expensive but that is what I would expect. There are many restaurants in walking distance in this neighborhood, which is known as Chinatown, but looks as though it is not as Chinese as it used to be. The convention center, Verizon Center, movie theaters are all within walking distance. I took a taxi to the Smithsonian but probably would have walked if it were a cooler day. 
In summary - I got a good night's sleep and that is all that really counts. Was this a beautiful property that I would want to hang-out at - not really.

title_masked: Good choice for a family trip to DC
text_masked:
Four of us came to DC for the week of July 4th. We have 2 children, a 6 year old and a 10 year old. This is a good choice for families because you get some extra space, not just a square room with a bed. We liked the full size refrigerator to put all our drinks. The stove is small but we did not cook. It was too hot in DC. The breakfast buffet that is included every morning is a hit with the kids but being that it was a holiday week - it was extremely crowded and chaotic during breakfast time. At one point they ran out of coffee and they were not to in a hurry to replace it. They also have a light,basic dinner Mon-Wed that we took advantage of also. Also very busy. The service at the hotel was just OK. I think they could be a little friendlier and a little more helpful. But again, it was a very busy week for them. 
This hotel is in a great location to tour the sites. This hotel is close to the Metro station and a short walk to the Mall. We chose this hotel in part because we had a short walk from the fireworks back to our hotel on July 4th. I also read other reviews and thought that there were no places to eat around here. Well there are plenty of casual, family friendly places I think. Next door is a decent pizza place that is open very late at night. McDonald's and Starbucks are a short walk away. Also it is easy to hop on the Metro and go a few short stops to some very good restaurants if you want something fancier.

We stayed at this hotel because of its location and great breakfast. It is not a eautiful hotel, but our room was. Very nice junior suite in tower one. View from 18 th floor was wonderful. Asian and American breakfast was out of this world!

We got married in Aug 2012 in NY and chose to stay at the Trump Soho
Great hotel in the heart of Soho
Treated very well by the hotel who provided some strawberrys to celebrate the occasion which was a nice touch.
Loved the tub overlooking Manhattan and the roof top pool. Staff were helpful and attentive
on the down side room was a small....... would've also liked to have been given the option to purchase an upgrade on check in
Overall though great hotel

title_masked: Nice hotel, nice staff, a few details need sorting out
text_masked: I booked a few rooms for a friend’s bachelor party. Let’s face it, after a crazy night on the town, you’re happy with just being able to rest your head somewhere. At check in each room was to be charged on a different card, but they ended up being charged on my card. After a few calls, everything was sorted out. The hotel in close/convenient to everything. Although the rooms were quiet, I was struck by how small the rooms seemed and especially how long it took for the coffee machine to produce a cup of coffee in the morning, WROAR!!!! The bathroom was very clean and the beds were meh comfortable. The night was a success as no one ended up in jail or divorced…If you’re staying in downtown, I’d say this place would be a nice choice. Valet may give you sticker shock, but you don’t really need a car if you’re staying at this hotel.

title_masked: Great place to stay for the value
text_masked: The staff was very helpful and friendly; always paying attention to detail. Rooms were very clean and quiet. Hotel was full due to the American Legion convention going on, but the place never appeared overwhelmed. Even the breakfast area was completely stocked, clean and organized. Though it was very busy, getting food and finding a place to sit was not an issue. Great place and will always stay there on my vistas to Indianapolis.

Our group travels to Chicago every August for Market Days and begins looking for good deals in the early part of the year. This year, the Congress was the winner in the deal department. The pictures and descriptions were very inviting, but I have realized that a photo can not offer the total story.
Upon check in the hotel appeared a bit worn out and dated. The structure had beautiful architectural elements but the decor did not support this. The furniture was modern and cheap which was a complete contrast to the gilded style of the tiled ceilings and carved woodwork. The hallways and bar areas were drab and dated as well. The display cases were full of advertising items but they were covered in dust and dirt. Not very appealing!.
The rooms were large with fantastic high ceilings but again, the decor was very dated and the furniture worn out. The bathrooms, while functional, had broken tile and sinks, slow draining faucets etc. I tried to look beyond these things and realize that this property was built in the late 1800's but it was very hard.
Upon check out, I inquired as to potential renovations and was told that "we do things as needed". I commented to the staff member that it was sad that the owners did not care about upgrading the property to breath life into what was once a stunning example of a hotel. She just shrugged her shoulders.
I do understand the size of the hotel would warrant a huge capital investment but some simple updates like new furniture, wallpaper, paint and lighting would at least bring some freshness to a tired old building.

title_masked: My GABF week staying at the Ramada
text_masked:
Sure our room key never worked and getting home between 12 and 2am meant we attempted to insert and remove the key about a dozen times before begrudgingly waiting for the elevator for 3-5 minutes to come to our floor (just take the stairs - you're in Denver, you could use the exercise), just to take us to the front desk so they could give us another key that would only work once. But honestly, the amount of money I paid for this room for a week, a very expensive week mind you (GABF stole all my money, with my direct permission of course), made me exceedingly happy considering how understaffed yet pleasant the hotel staff was. My roommate for the week was able to take the shuttle to and from downtown all week while I was working my life away drinking beer for a minimum of 12 hours a day. 
The location is just outside the hustle and bustle of downtown, which is actually nice, because at night, once you're done festing, all you want to do is a.) drunk-snack or b.) sleep. I had the best (vacation) sleep of my life at this hotel - no distractions (besides the dinging of the elevator at all hours of the night; our room was right next to it), no fancy linens or towels or mints on the pillows. This is a 'I need a good place to sleep shower and... well the other s- thing you do in your hotel room.' The drive to downtown during the weekday morning traffic took about 10-15 minutes tops, on the weekend, I can't really remember how long it took, but it was definitely less. 
I wouldn't recommend the restaurant mostly because I was terrified to go in there, we never ate the complimentary breakfast because there are far better options downtown. 
Our original room was on the 4th floor, but the 4th floor is half smoking and half non-smoking rooms - which means, most rooms on the 4th floor probably reek of cigarettes; I instantly requested a new room and within minutes the blonde front desk girl came upstairs and delivered new room keys to us herself. Our new room, didn't smell. It was awesome. My nose is terribly sensitive to cigarette smoke, so maybe if you aren't as sensitive the 4th floor won't bother you. 
The night club is obnoxious. I think Thursday-Saturday night it was blasting hip hop or hispanic music; I was too tired to notice. Fortunately, on the 3rd floor, I couldn't hear the music at all, but I'd imagine if your room was on the 1st or 2nd floor you'd have a different experience.
When I return to Denver, there's a good chance I'd pick this hotel again.

Yotel is a great concept with cabins that have everything you need very close to hand. The cabin has loads of power sockets to charge all the gadgets, great shower but was only very slightly let down by possibly the hardest bed mattress i have slept on. I love the little touches -- the automated check, the luggage robot, the 'crew' are great and the free muffins and coffee are a nice touch (the $9.99 breakfast special is very good). Plus the location is great just a couple of blocks from Time Square and close the water if you want a jogging route. Overall I would definitely recommend it. Would have got 5 star rating had it not been for the bed.

title_masked: Great location, step away from Times Square
text_masked:
We stayed at the hotel for approximately a week during new years. The hotel has a great location with times square a street away which was fantastic for new years eve (mind you with the mad rush after the ball dropped it must have taken us 20 minutes to walk back!), good service, especially at the travel information desk. The staff are very friendly. Some of the front desk staff were slightly abrupt. There was a wrong charge on the check out bill so check your bills thoroughly!
Hotel is clean and well maintained, I feel that in room dining was unecessarily expensive, 9 dollars for a bottle of water and 20 dollars for friens and a sandwich? I suppose thats what you get for staying at a 5star hotel. I learnt my lesson after that and found a duane pharmacy a block away. 
We stayed on the 18th floor, great room with a lovely view of the city. It was our first visit to the city and would definitely return! Absolutely loved it, possibly stay at another hotel next time just for variation.

Within a block or two of the main Fisherman's Wharf area, plus many shopping areas, a cable car stop, and many other SF attractions this hotel is great. It has all the amenities one expects of a big city hotel and very friendly and helpful staff. The rooms are a good size, although I would always like some more counter space in the bathrooms, and well outfitted. The breakfast buffet is extensive and great value; and there is a to-go bar to buy drinks and snacks.

I want to commend the hotel on the wonderful staff we encountered during our stay at the Marriott Waterfront. From Julia at the front desk, to the assorted valets working out front, everyone was friendly and attentive. When I requested rooms with a harbor view, I was informed of the upgrade fee. I declined the upgrade but Julia was able to provide us with rooms with a semi- marina and waterfront view. Just as nice. We stayed on the 15th floor and there was no vending machine available for me to get a bottle of water. It was 11pm and the deli had just closed so I went to the front desk to request a floor number where I could find a vending machine. The desk clerk-I am sorry I didn't get her name- asked me for my room number and had water delivered to us. Again, another touch of great customer service and going above and beyond. This stay was arranged through Priceline due to the greatly reduced price offered through them. No where in my experience the weekend did I feel like a "discount" customer.
When planning another trip to the Inner Harbor, I will be sure to include staying at the Waterfront Marriott. 
The in-house restaurant provide breakfast options from sit down service menu selections to walk out pastries and coffee in the deli section. 
It was just a short walk (approx. 1/2 mile) to the Aquarium and Pier 5 and just beyond to the HarborPlace shops and restaurants. There is a Water Taxi stop just outside the building to make getting around the harbor easier if you or the weather are not up for walking.

Morgan's was the 2nd hotel that we stayed in on our trip to New York.. And was such a fab find.... We arrived early for check in so we just left our bags and went for a walk.. On return the room wasn't ready we weren't really that bothered as we were able to sit and wait in the beautiful living room on the 19th floor and use the wifi.. Never had to wait long tho as the manager came and gave us a free up grade to a superior room! DELIGHTED.. 
Room was just beautiful big soft bed amazing double window that looked out on to the street spacious bath room. Room was spotless.. Just what we needed after a days traveling.. 
Morgan's is just the perfect location for everything in New York we walked every were taking in all the sights and of course perfect walking distance to walk back with All them shopping bags!! 
The breakfast in the morning was just what i needed and kept me going until I lunch time.. 
Over all we had a fantastic trip and Morgan's played a big part in that.. I will most deff be recommending this hotel to all my Irish friends..

title_masked: Great facility, rooms not as great
text_masked: I stayed here during a recent conference. The location of the hotel and the facility itself is amazing, made more memorable by a king and professional staff. Shopping, tourist attractions, all within walking distance. Despite the fact there were no noise problems, and that I had a magnificent view from the 42nd floor, I found the comfort of the room very difficult to maintain. I can usually sleep almost anywhere and spent 3 sleepless nights at the Marriott. The bathrooms are smallish, not a much of a problem in a major city, but in major need or renovation. Cracked ceilings and peeling paint are a good indication that it's time to revamp. Also, as a previous reviewer mentioned, the dryness of the room was very uncomfortable. That said, the hotel dining facilities are marvelous, if a bit pricey, workout facilities and pool are outstanding, and staff extraordinarily accommodating. Without conference pricing, the room would have run pretty high, so I'm not sure I'd stay here again without a pretty good discount/deal.

I stayed with my friends. This hotel is located in a great area and it has Little Italy/ China Town in a short distance walk (less than half mile). From the hotel you can get anywhere. The subway system is next to the hotel and the transportation system is quite accesible. The hotel breakfast is excellent, service and employees are extremely attentive and friendly. The room was clean, beds were comfortable and room service was excellent. I definitely will stay again!

Great room, great service, centrally located and the right price using Priceline! Stayed at this hotel before embarking on cruise to Alaska. Was able to see Space Needle, Glass Museum, Pike Street Market and the Klondike Museum. Great access to city bus transportation and Westlake Station.

Outstanding service . Although the location is not in the heart of Beverly Hills the hotel provides a courtesy car within 2 miles ,so even if you don't have a car you can shop and enjoy a lot of great restaurants,because there are a lot in the area,including Rodeo Drive!!!.
The rooms are not big but are confortable .The hotel decor is absolutely beautiful.Even being a city hotel there are a lot of green areas ,beautiful flowers everywhere inside and outside. The bar and the restaurant are amazing and good choice of food.It was really a wonderful experience and the best was really the outstanding staff.

I was really disappointed in this hotel. We were with a group and they initally did not place us near each other. Two members of our group had to request to move closer to us. Our group - 20 of us - had requested if breakfast could be early 1 month before we arrived, and they informed us that it would not be a problem, as we had to get to our event downtown by 7am. When we arrived, they were rather rude and said no that would not be happening. The rooms were very worn and out dated. It looked like it was straight from the 80's. There were couch and chair was saggy and had stains. The kitchen wasn't well stocked, a couple of plates and 2 forks, 2 mugs, and a pot. The paint was peeling from the porches on the upstairs units, and it was very slippery, no traction at all. Police patrolled this section alot, so I'm not sure if security is an issue. I know we did not feel safe. 
The good - it was clean.

This Marriott is in a great location. Within walking distance to the convention center, as well as the tourism. Close to Reading Market - which is a great spot for lunch. I found the front desk service to be excellent, but would only rate the housekeeping service at average. Our room wasn't serviced one of the days, and the housekeeper got a bit snippy at us saying we left the "do not disturb" marker on the door, which we didn't. One disappointment is with the hours of the concierge level. Only open on weekdays, and I just don't understand why Marriott does that in the US. Was there on business, and they should realize that many conferences do extend into the weekend. As a gold member, it would be nice to utilize this service over the weekend. The room was clean, but only average compared to other Marriott properties. We did eat in the restaurant - and the food was good and service was excellent, albeit slow. Still a good Marriott property for business.

The hotel is in a very convenient location near many restaurants and shopping. It was great being able to travel with our dogs. One problem was that the Leathernecks were having a convention, and their motorcycles were very loud. The people we met from the group were very nice, but I think I would have liked a warning from the hotel about the convention when I reserved. Also, the pool heater wasn't working. Lastly, I had to reserve a smoker room because there were no non-smoking available. I had forgotten how smoke gets so embedded in things. We bought air freshener and lit candles, but nothing helped. The room was smaller than I expected. It has a nice kitchen, but only one seat at the table, which didn't work well for the three of us.

Fabulous location, great room with an amazing view uptown and downtown. Concierge(s) were extremely helpful for restaurants, salons etc.
Neighborhood is excellent - so much within walking distance.
Will definitely stay here again

We upgraded to a huge suite so our daughter could stay one night on the couch. There was no vent of AC control in the bedroom so we could not close the door between the bedroom and the living room because it got hot so quickly. Our daughter froze on the sleeper sofa so we could get enough AC in the bedroom area. This is really crazy when you think about the price we paid and that we were uncomfortable. When I called down to the front desk to discuss I was told they had this complaint many times before but there was nothing they could do about it.

Located a half block from Times Square and Broadway where the hi-risers are located allowing people to sit and watch what is happening on Times Square. All kinds of places to eat are located nearby. You'll be right in the middle of the Theater District, West 47th. Subway station is close by on 50th and 7th. The hotel has old world charm. The rooms are clean and the staff provides great customer service. I had to change rooms because on the fifth floor I could hear the noise from a roof top air conditioner. They gave me the opportunity to preview two rooms and I changed to the 18th floor and had a corner room with long views including the river. I would stay again.

title_masked: Great location for doing business on the Hill
text_masked:
This is Hyatt "business" hotels are all about. Clean, efficient and well located on Capitol Hill. Downside is a single restaurant that "fits all" as well as open non bar/lounge. 
Rooms are Hyatt business hotel functional, up to date and more importantly Hyatt clean.\\

My fiancé and I decided to have a two day get away to Chicago, decided to stay at the Palomar, and we are happy we did. The staff was always on point, very courteous and professional. The concierge “Bobby” was able to help us plan out our weekend, with no regrets! We arrived Friday afternoon, and joined the free wine reception near the lobby from 5-7pm (it was very classy and gave us a chance to socialize with other people from all across the nation.) The following morning we had breakfast at the hotel’s restaurant “Sable Kitchen & Bar” where the staff and the meals really impressed us. The rooms were unique and comfortable. On Sundays check-out again the staff was helpful and had us leaving satisfied with our stay. Overall the Palomar was a great experience at an affordable price and can easily pass for a 5 star hotel.

title_masked: Low cost, clean, friendly boutique hotel in the heart of New York
text_masked: Less than 3 minutes from Time Square, surrounded by theatres, restaurants, diners and delicatessens, and a VERY reasonable price, this is a clean, modern hotel with FREE WiFi in the spacious rooms, an excellent Desires plan, and extremely helpful front-of-house staff. Plenty of well-placed power sockets, good room lighting, and hot powerful showers complete the perfect place to stay in New York. This will be my hotel of choice in New York from now on.

title_masked: Don't listen to the bad reviews!
text_masked:
I booked this hotel last year for my disabled mum and her two cousins. I have contacted the hotel a number of times to ensure that she had a suitable room. Each time, staff replied quickly.
They had a wonderful time and described the hotel as amazing. They had one of the new rooms and could not fault it at all.
Lots of people have described the rooms as small - this is new York and if you want a bigger room you will need to pay more!
, I do genuinely believe that the hotel has listened to comments from previous guests and taken criticism on board. Once all of the hotel has been updated it will be amongst the best in new York. I have been a frequent traveller to the big apple and I always stay in the iconic 5 star hotels but when I go next I will certainly give the Hudson a try.

title_masked: I will stay again at the W Austin!
text_masked: I recently returned from my weekend at W Austin with my wife where we celebrated our wedding anniversary--what a great time. I stay at the W Austin for business, and the staff and experience are always top notch. This was my first time staying for pure pleasure, and it was even better (which is what I wanted and hoped). We were always warmly greeted by staff members, enjoyed a show at Moody's Theatre and than the W Bar afterwards was a happening place. Our room was spacious and clean, just as I expected (and it always is that way). I am glad my son is attending University of Texas in the fall, we will stay at the W Austin.

Went to the LA Auto Show Dec 2012 and stayed at the Days Inn on Sunset Blvd. The room was so small you couldn't move without climbing over the bed and the bathroom was really small. The bathroom door blocked the use of the sink and the john. This room was way over priced.

We enjoy our trips to NYC and this hotel is right in the heart of the city!! The staff has always been friendly and rooms comfortable. We were met at the door by Quinton, he is very helpful and we appreciate his courtesy and professionalism. He acknowledged us anytime he saw us in the building. Walking distance to Rock of Ages and the subways. The comfy pillows are a bonus after a day of walking around the city. See you in the spring!!

Next to Times Square. Rooms were clean. We had two rooms: one was very small, one was small. The very small one didn't have a desk.Price was reasonable for the location. Elevators are really small and the lobby is tiny. But I don't regret as it was a great combination of price and location. They have a gym on the 2nd floor. Also, a computer with printer (need to pay to use) that came in handy to print out tickets to attractions. Overall, I would recommend it to others.

We stayed for one night in a suite. Very spacious, modern, and exceeded our expectation. What a pleasant stay. The location is excellent, upscale, green (for LA), and close to UCLA. Food by the pool was convenient and friendly, though there are many options within a 5 minute walk .

title_masked: Public spaces great; private rooms need upgrading
text_masked:
Loved the VERY comfortable bed and linens, and the bathroom with fluffy large towels and upscale amenities was wonderful. The public spaces, decorated in a kind of English-country-house way were nice, especially the bar which had very good couches and books on the walls (though upon closer inspection they seemed to have purchased these books from the Netherlands and other foreign countries for their bindings, since most of them were in Dutch or Danish).
However, our room which overlooked the harbor (wonderful view) looked like it had seen better days with peeling baseboards and carpet which was about 20 years old in a kind of hideous maroon design with large flowers, no artwork on walls except for 2 small prints, in other words, it just needed attention. Another curious feature was the fire system which blinked continually through the night, pretty annoying. At the high prices for the harbor view rooms, in my opinion the rooms should be spotless and very attractive, with NO major design flaws, or the desk staff should steer the high-paying customers to the rooms which have already been renovated.
We also want to note the accomodating staff who were all gracious, seemed to take pride in their work, and were anxious to share Baltimore with us. All in all, can't quite give the place 5 stars but with good management they can get there eventually...

Great place...simple and walking distance to times square
Liza is the best...let us know that is was dining week in nyc...and printed out a list of all the participating restaurants...ate a great meal, at a great price...Thanks
already planning the next nyc adventure...Spa week..yeah

Hotel is in an excellent location in midtown Manhattan. Service was really good in both the hotel and the pub and the hotel laid on a great birthday surprise as we were in NY celebrating my partner's 40th. Concierge was really helpful and knowledgeable. We were really surprised by the size and quality of the room given we were so central in the city. Whenever I've stayed in NYC in the past, the rooms have been poky and dark - here they were clean, spacious and didn't feel like a hotel room at all. Would definitely stay here again.

3 friend and I won a trip the dial a flight and this is where we stayed
Fab location (10min walk to times sq) rooms were very clean and modern
Used the rooftop bar that was lovely although cocktails were $18 
Staff were great,cannot wait to go back and would use this hotel again

We booked through Expedia. We were able to check in early without an issue at all. The location was convenient (walking distance to many bars/restaurants). The room was clean, quiet and modern. The lobby and hotel bar were fantastic, very impressive. Did not make use of the pool/workout facility but it was available and the rooftop pool offered views of the city. Valet service was $25/day (in-and-out with fast, polite service). The highlight was the breakfast. Full hot breakfast buffet...easily a $10-15/person value.

Was warmly greeted and checked in, quickly without any problems. Found the room spacious and great view of Thomas CIrcle. The decor was a bit mimialist for my taste but comfortable. Found everyone friendly and helpful,

I just returned from my first stay at the Peabody. Quirky, yes, but in a most entertaining way. Don't miss the Duck Parade! My room was expansive and most excellently appointed. In advance of my stay I had requested that all down filled pillows be removed from the room. Upon entering my room I was delighted to discover that my request had been granted - no reminder needed as is the case in all other hotels I have stayed in. The bathroom was on the small side; amenities were ample and the fixtures obviously new. The only negative was the 4:30am wake-up call thanks to either a fire drill or a false alarm. The staff is extremely helpful, personable and professional - from bellhops to front desk staff to housekeepers, all were a pleasure to deal with. On my first day I asked a staff member where I might find a cup of coffee; the gentleman was kind enough to walk me to the Peabody's most excellent deli. (Don't miss a trip to the deli - the pastries are worthy of any Parisian patisserie.) Breakfast buffet was included with my stay; the offerings were modest in variety but of very good quality.

We stayed here for 8 nights in March of this year for a trip centered around St Patricks Day. We wanted stay in or near the Lower east side/East village area. There arent many hotels in this area so this was the closest we could get at a reasonable price. 5-10 minutes walking brings you to countless dive bars and music venues which is exactly what we wanted. Home Sweet home and Welcome to the Johnsons would be two of the best we visited. 
Grand St Subway station is only 1 block north and serves the B&D trains. (Orange Line) You can get the J&Z trains (Brown line) from Bowery St which is about 4 blocks north. Also, Canal St Station is about 5 blocks west and the N, Q and 6 trains stop here. We got the train from JFK to Bowery St and walked the 4 blocks to the hotel. With two suitcases this was a bit awkward as the footpaths are quite uneven and crowded at the junctions but its not that far and we saved about $40 each way by not getting a taxi. We were first timers in NYC but being fairly seasoned travellers we werent fazed by the hustle and bustle in the chinatown area. 
The hotel itself was fine. Decent sized room with a nice big TV and very clean. Staff were very efficient and friendly and really seemed to care. There was a bit of a mixup when we were checking in but this was dealt with quickly and without fuss. Very quiet at night, we asked for a high floor so we would be further up from street level. I would recommend this hotel for travellers who want a nice, clean, safe hotel near the lower east side.

title_masked: Conference at Hilton Bayfront San Diego
text_masked: I was very pleased with the hotel. I went for the professional conference. It is located at the shoreline. I liked the pool, it's facing the ocean, but I didn' t like the view of the warehouses for ships or whatever it was. We had a wonderful time, the reception was outside in front of hotel. The hotel has a nice spa with the steam room. The view from the room was very nice.

Homewood Suites is a great little hotel. The staff - as has been mentioned - is super from the folks driving the courtesy shuttles to the reception staff to the cleaners to the food servers. The hotel picks you up at the airport, quickly checks you in, and goes the extra mile to ensure you have a great visit. The rooms are a good size and feature a kitchenette (the hotel will go to the grocery store for you; a Vons is about 1/2 mile away). Note: some of the suites have a separate bedroom and one combine the bedroom, kitchen, and living room (same size, just a wall separating the BR). The breakfast and dinners (served Mon-Thurs) are good; the morning waffle makers are a big hit. There is a small pool and small fitness areas (one per building). There are gas grilles and a nearby park with charcoal grills (bring your own charcoal). There are several restaurants next to the hotel. The location is good, but you will probably need a car. Overall a very good experience.

A year since my last visit and the status quo remains. In all respects an average property with the exception of the staff. Consistently above the norm from the front to room service. THEY are the reason I will return. People do make a difference.

title_masked: Could My Stay Have Been Better? Not Likely
text_masked:
Look. I call 'em as I see 'em. Last year, you may note my less than flattering review of the Westin St. Francis in San Francisco. For a high end hotel the service was not up to par, not only in what was delivered, but in HOW it was delivered.
Now. Regarding the Palmer House Hilton. Wonderful stay, beautiful hotel, excellent location in downtown Chicago. To begin with, our room was small but very clean and on the Executive Floor - which give you not only a nice morning continental breakfast, but with two dedicated elevators serving the two executive floors exclusively - nice touch.
Regarding service - perfect. From the desk clerks, to the wait staff, to the cleaning staff - I haven't been given so many smiling and sincere "hello's" and "good morning's" in any previous hotel experience. I don't know if the hotel was pumping in something in their air vents but the staff was very friendly and engaging almost without exception. I mean - the banquet cash bar tender greeted me with a great smile, talked to me about his life in Chicago and a brief stay in San Antonio (nice, but too hot in the summer).. the hotel is magnificent with a magnificant history - but it really was the people who made it stand out.
Lobby, as others have said, was stunning. The Potter's Lounge food was good, service was better. 
I can give a full two-thumbs up to this hotel, without reservation. Stay here - you won't be disappointed.

We arrived at the hotel and were given a room with a view but it had 2 double beds in it, not what my wife and I expected but we were tired from the day's travel so we stayed in it anyway. The next morning we inquired about the possibility of being moved to a room with a King bed and Tiffany at the front desk immediately acknowledged my Platinum status and told us to hold on and she would see what she could do. As it turns out, they were able to move us to a suite overlooking the Botanical Gardens and we could not have been happier. Awesome view, great hotel, top notch service and the pool area is one of the best I've seen anywhere. Lazy river and about 3 other pools to lounge at. We were planning on checking out on Saturday and driving around to see the sights but we were so impressed with the atmosphere that we opted for a 4pm late checkout and just hung out at the pool as well as got a spa treatment as well. The spa was also top notch and if you have the time we highly recommend it! Overall, would definitely recommend this property!

title_masked: Extremely poor and rude customer service
text_masked:
First of all the pool wasn't working and they act as if that's okay. Not for the price you pay!!!
The customer service is horrible. They have a shuttle service that take you within 5 miles of the hotel. So we wanted to go to the mall which is within range so when I call to ask they told me that they can't take me to the mall because the mall service runs every 3 hours and the next one is in 2 hours. So I asked the guy "You take guests within 5 miles of the hotel right?" and he answered "Yes but just not the mall." So I tell him if I find something close to the mall will you take me there "He was like yes" so I said "Can you just take me to the mall then?" and he was like sorry "We can't do that, mall shuttles run every 3 hours."
ARE YOU SERIOUS???? So I ended up looking up a restaurant half a mile away from the mall and going down to the shuttle desk. The guy I had just spoken to was there. I ask them to take the to the restaurant. He asked me if it was near the mall, I said yes, but you won't take me to the mall so...
Then he started being dumb was like well if you have asked me for a favor, I would have said yes. ARE YOU KIDDING ME?? You are a 4 star hotel!!! You should have been taught customer service and offered me a ride there when I asked over the phone.
Never staying here again.

title_masked: This is my rating AND I stayed in a renovated room!
text_masked:
The location is fantastic and that is where this ends. While you are waiting for your room you are sitting in an open area with hotel Nazis that watch it to make sure no luggage goes in there. They are nasty about telling the guests this. A simple sign could have sufficed. my 5 days stay - two rooms (yes I am a glutton for punishment) had the maid NEVER knocking and opened the room several times a day even when I was dressing. I called the Russian head of cleaning and the woman yelled at me telling me it was my fault for not locking it with a dead bolt. Are you kidding? REALLY. I complained to management who did nothing.
I was not treated as a guest but as an unwanted relative. The renovated rooms they make a big deal about because compared to the non renovated ones look like heaven. They suffice- if you like sleeping with no blanket. They charge you to watch your bags (another disaster). Every place in Times Square is nice and I will be choosing another one. Do not walk- run!

title_masked: Great budget hotel for a Sea World getaway!
text_masked: My family and I stayed here from July 8th - July 11th. This is a very good budget hotel for families going to Sea World. The staff is extremely professional, friendly, and very accommodating. The hotel has been opened for less than a year and is very clean. When looking for hotels, I was looking for one that shuttled to/from Sea World. This hotel charges only $10 per stay for the shuttle. Very few hotels in this area actually shuttle to Sea World. This amenity is great considering the shuttle drops/picks you up at the front entrance of Sea World. One of the shuttle drivers, Mike, provided a lot of information regarding the area, including places to eat and things to do. His professionalism and hospitality matches, if not exceeds what I expect at high end hotels. Overall, I felt this hotel was very good. I highly recommend this hotel for the budget minded family who wants to spend a few days to experience Sea World. Enjoy!

title_masked: Good Spot to explore Baltimore from.
text_masked: I had been to Baltimore before, so I knew the layout. I had some free night certificates and decided to do a baseball trip. This is a great location and facility for a Category 4 hotel in the Marriott system. I was suprised I could get that close to the Inner Harbor area. This hotel isn't right in Inner harbor, but has it's own array of upscale dining and shopping nearby. There is a water taxi shuttle about 5 min walk from hotel. You really only need the water taxi if you plan on going to Captain James landing or Ft. McHenry, the main part of the Inner Harbor district is an easy and pleasant 15-20min walk. I actually walked 2 round trips to Camden Yards, but I don't think most would want to do that. It's about a 30-45min walk, I was in full explorer mode. The pool is interesting, much smaller in person. There is a nice garden type observation deck that is perfect for a cup of coffee or evening drink. All of the staff that I encountered(mostly night shift) were great! I did not get to use the restaurant or bar in the hotel. They had a power outage due to storms that lasted several hours. They informed me when I returned from the game, then upon check out, told me they were crediting me 20,000 marriott points for the issue(looks like they actually reissued my free night coupon). I thought it was a nice gesture, considering I wasn't really inconvenienced at all. It' s good to see a company pro-actively getting ahead of a potential issue. I would stay here again and also reccomend to other travelers. The location of this hotel is better than the Fairield Inn Inner harbor. IF your comparing it to the waterfront Marriott, you can actually see each location from each other. If view and saying your "on the waterfront" aren't as important, then save the money and stay here.

This is an elegant and extremely customer oriented hotel with a spectacular location though if you plan to walk to too many places where good hiking shoes. The hills leading up or down from the hotel are a touch steep. The rooms are magnificently comfortable, the staff helpful and courteous, and the food in the Tonga Room was wonderful. The gym is also quite adequate. I would encourage you to join the Presidents Club of the hotel as it then gives free standard access to internet and to the gym. Ready access to Union Square shopping, and some lovely little cafes down the street for meals if you want to eat out of the hotel proper.

I stayed at this Hilton Garden Inn on business for 7 days, I spilled something on my bedspread and asked housekeeping in the hall to change my bedspread and top sheet. That was at 10am in the morning. That night when returning nothing was done. The front desk clerk brought me a blanket for the night. I told housekeeping again in the hall the next morning that I needed a bedspread and sheet and what happened the day before and I only had a blanket to use the night before. I returned after another 12 hr day and the room was cleaned but they only made my bed and left the blanket with no sheet or bedspread. I called the front desk and they said how sorry they were and housekeeping would be right up. 2 hours later and 2 trips and 1 phone call housekeeping showed up and took care of the problem. After talking to other employees they said housekeeping couldn't speak English and they probably didn't understand what I was telling them. Other then that shuttle was on time every day and hotel was nice, beds were comfortable.

Lovely hotel with hard wood floors. Sitting outside having a cocktail was a great way to unwind after a long day in the office. My only issue is that on my way to my room, I could hear someone taking a shower.

this hotel had many situations where i was disspointed. the staff have inconstancy in the process of serving guests. they offer different answers at different times. i was not satisfied with the overall stay.

The reviews led me to believe that this was a poor excuse for a Hilton. I strongly disagree.
Located a nice walk from Fisherman's Wharf this is a 3 star hotel. After a very easy check-in I spent 4 nights in room 274 and really enjoyed it. The carpet was clean but not new. The bathroom was a decent size and equipped with a very nice grade of toiletries.
Avoid rooms above the pool to avoid noise. I opened the windows (they only open about 5 inches) to enjoy fresh air.

My wife and I stayed here this past August on 2 occassions. We used the free shuttle service from the airport( about 15 minutes away).
Excellent facilities with up to date everything- free Wifi, flat screen TV, etc. 
Excellent hot/cold breakfast with large spacious room dedicated for the purpose.
Large indoor pool and business ctr just added to the experience.
Staff helpful and caring. housekeeping- 1st rate.
Would easily stay here again.

I found the Moore Hotel on TripAdvisor and was so pleased with the location and value! The staff I spoke to on the phone were incredibly helpful, Liz in particular. We stayed Friday and Saturday night two weekends in a row, with a kayaking/camping trip to San Juan Island during the week. Being two blocks from Pikes Place Market was the perfect location for sightseeing in Seattle. It was also only two blocks from Westlake Station so we were able to get to the hotel from SeaTac Airport for only $2.75 each. There are no "extras" at the Moore which I believe makes this a price that can't be beat. Open windows were adequate for a comfortable night sleep. One queen bed was just perfect for my husband and me. I was able to borrow a hair dryer from the front desk. 
Having read other reviews about noise on the street side, I requested and was given quiter rooms in the back. There was no view, and one room looked into a brick wall about 20 feet away, but there was adequate light and ventilation. 
Some people might find the footed bathtub/shower a little difficult as there was no place to set down the soap and caution should be used when entering and exiting in one big step over the side.

title_masked: Beautiful hotel, great location, but expect to pay more than the room cost
text_masked:
I have stayed here twice now, each time for weddings. This time I was here with my husband for 3 nights. My overall impression is that it is a very nice hotel, but I was ultimately really ticked off by the little things. 
Pros: 
- Comfortable beds
- Close to the White House and on top of a Metro stop
- Awesome (but EXPENSIVE) brunch - seriously though it's worth the price if you're hungry.
Cons:
- Incredibly dark rooms and bathrooms. You feel like you are taking a shower in a cave because there is no light in or near the shower. Doing your makeup or shaving is virtually impossible. I had to remove a lampshade and sit on the desk to get ready for the wedding. 
- Paying a hefty room rate and then getting nickled and dimed throughout the weekend.
----- Seriously? $10 to use the gym??? I really can't get over that.
----- I paid $10.99 for standard wifi and it was so slow that I could barely access anything I needed at the office. Apparently I was supposed to pay $13.99 for the Premium Wifi, if I actually wanted to do anything productive beyond checking the weather. 
----- All in all, my husband and I ended up spending (in 3 days) almost $200 on extras (2 brunches, a few drinks at the hotel bar on Friday night, internet and gym access).

This is a small chain of hotels in the Seattle area. We reserved a room for the weekend at the recommendation of an associate we were visiting. Great value for the money. The room was spacious and comfortable, the staff was exceedingly friendly and helpful, and the continental breakfast was one of the best we have had in a hotel. There is no restaurant, but the hotel is within easy walking distance to a number of fine restaurants.

very clean, nice staff and close to the federal bldg down the street. also very close to alot of different resturants. Only complaint is the elevators are so antiquated that I got scared that I would get stuck in them every time I got in them. Never did though.

Great location. Great staff. Beautiful accommodations. Our room, as well as all other areas of the hotel were very clean. Excellent selection of restaurants in the hotel and the surrounding area. Can't wait to return. Definitely would recommend this hotel.

For 2 consecutive days I did not get hot water in the morning and the rooms were smoky and made my stay quite uncomfortable. I travel regularly to memphis and this incident made me switch hotels to a different brand.

I've been to Chicago a number of times but this was my first time staying directly on the Magnificent Mile. The location was great and made getting around the city a cinch. The hotel itself is very interesting as it has a historic look but with a modern touch. Front desk staff was extremely helpful during check-in, and always answered any questions I had with a smile.The room I stayed in was very spacious and felt comfortable, with a really nice shower and a firm bed. The view was probably the best part of the room, as it overlooked the city and the river. I had a lot of really jealous friends during my stay! 
Breakfast at the Continental restaurant was great, as the servers were very responsive without being intrusive. I don't think my cup of coffee ever got below half empty before they freshened it up! For dinner on one of the nights I stayed I went with a few friends to the Michael Jordan's Steakhouse located in the hotel's lobby. The food was really fantastic, better than I'm used to having at all but the highest-end hotel restaurants. Overall, my stay was excellent and I would easily recommend IC Chicago to any visitor to the city. I know for sure that I'll be booking there again next time I come to town.

I am relocating to El Paso and was looking for an corporate apartment until my family can join me, but found everything I needed at Guest House suites so no need to commit to a lease term on an apartment. This hotel is perfect for my extended stay needs.

My daughter and I stayed here for one night on a combination business/pleasure trip and thoroughly enjoyed our stay. The staff were very friendly, from the front desk, to housekeeping, to the bartender. The room was spacious and the decor was fun. To make up for lack of outlets, there was a power strip for plugging in cell phones near the bed. The location is great, nice side street near shopping, restaurants, and transportation. The only disappointment was that our window view was of an alley/parking area but that was a minor issue and it was certainly quiet.

We stayed for 2 nights on what appeared to be a busy weekend in Boston. The location is a real plus as you are across the street from one of the cemeteries on the Freedom Trail and less than 15 minutes to the Long Wharf or North End. The Commons is right around the corner. I really can't say much else about the hotel other than the place was clean and service was fine. The concierge answered questions, but didn't offer much insight or options. In general, staff were professional. Would I go back? Only if I got a bargain rate.

title_masked: One of the Very Best Lodging Experiences I Have Had in a Long Time!
text_masked:
From driving into the very well lighted lot to the extremely cordial and helpful gentleman behind the desk, this entire stay was one of the very best! The hotel is beautiful and obviously well managed! One of the very biggest positives is that the housekeeping staff is quiet and there is no door slamming in this hotel!! Obviously management made the adjustments to the doors that even if you want to slam the doors, you can't! (That means so much to this late night traveler!) 
The hotel is immaculate and the staff is an added plus! If there was any slight negative, I went to have breakfast at 9:20 AM, which is served until 10 AM and there were no omelets and little bacon. And I saw no one overseeing the area. (Just a bit more attentiveness to breakfast bar)
Overall an extremely "special" stay and we will make this our hotel of choice whenever staying in the Denver area!

Everything was superb, from the time we arrived until our departure, three days later. The personnel at the hotel could not have been more friendly or accommodating. We had a large room with two queen beds overlooking 8th Avenue. The location was perfect for theater. restaurants and shopping. Incidentally, the restaurant within the hotel, Pigalle, is excellent.

title_masked: It made our trip to SEA wonderful!!!
text_masked: We had an activity filled weekend trip to Seattle planned - baseball, food and King Tut - and the Mayflower allowed us to have a great foundation for a busy and fun weekend running around downtown Seattle. It is a clean and well located hotel with a pleasant and helpful staff. Thank you Mayflower Park for making our visit just great!!

My husband and I come to Denver every year and stay at "The Grande Damme" for a professional course which is held in the hotel. We come for a week (usually coinciding with the Annual Champagne Cascade!) and simply cannot get enough of this beautiful hotel. Not only are the accomadations top-notch, but the hotel itself is so convenient: its restaurants are fabulous, its location is more than ideal (in the heart of downtown Denver, only a block away from the famous 16th street mall!), laundry services are super easy, fitness center is wonderful, the service is spot on, you name it! The hotel is built on an artesian spring, so even the water coming out of the tap -that you shower in- is like bottled water! So luxurious! And speaking of luxurious, please visit THE SPA when you're here. It's a day in heaven. Shai Albright (esthetician), as well as Haley and Ida were AMAZING! I did a facial, massage and body wrap and it was absolute perfection!

Very clean rooms, great view of river walk. The staff was great! Leslie Casey of guest reception made my day. After finally making it to San Antonio for vacation, my car was broken into. I was so upset because it cost me half of my day. When I was greated by Leslie, her friendly smile welcomed my family. She had all of the right answers and her dedication to her job showed what a true professional the Hyatt had employed. This is a great hotel to unwind in. I will be back!

We stayed at this hotel back in January for the Cotton Bowl. I booked several rooms as we had a large group of people going. When we arrived to the hotel it was under construction which was never mentioned anywhere. The lobby bar/restaurant were part of this construction. The first night I didn't sleep as the air conditioner made a horrible noise the entire night. It was really late when we had returned from dinner and drinks so I was not going to change rooms. The next morning I went to take a shower and it was freezing. The water never warmed up. It was quite the rude awakening after a horrible nights sleep. I went to the front desk shortly after to change rooms. The moved us to a different room and gave us a free breakfast for the inconvenience. Not really what I was looking for after not sleeping all night long and having an awful shower. 
The hotel has an atrium in the middle of it with a few shops and restaurants. This is where we would meet in the mornings since the lobby wasn't open. The hotel is walking distance to a few bars and restaurants. We took the tram and taxis everywhere. 
On Saturday night/Sunday morning the lobby/bar/breakfast restaurant finally opened but the staff seemed like they had forgotten how to do their jobs. The breakfast service was excrutiatingly slow. We had to ask twice for our ticket so we could pay. 
Hopefully they have it together now that it's been 5 months but I would not stay there again.

title_masked: Fantastic Hotel in a Wonderful City!
text_masked:
Visited NYC in February 2012 with my Boyfriend. Hotel staff where very friendly and welcoming, which was refreshing after a long and exhausting plane journey. Room was a good size, with all the latest mod-cons; flat screen TV, alarm with Ipod docking station, built in safe, free internet, hairdryer etc... I was unable to work the safe on arrival, i called down to reception and they tol me an engineer would be up to be as soon as possible. Within 60 seconds of making the call, an engineer was at my room to assist me, which demonstrates the excellent customer service that you recieve that this hotel.
Continental breakfast is outstanding with a vast array of cerials, bagels, muffins, fruit and more and we never struggled for anywhere to sit on a morning. 
Although it was too cold for the roof-top bar to be open when we visited in March, we did pop up there and it looked fantastic. You get the most fantasic view of the empire state ever, ad i would imagine that in the summer this terrace is lovely to sit and relax in. 
As for location- this could not be faulted at all. You are pretty much opposite Macy's and in the next block to the empire state. Times square is easily accessible on foot, taking no more tha 10 minutes to reach and the fFatiron and Madison Square Garden are also within easy walking distance. For the city that never sleeps- you can sleep soundly in this hotel and I would recommend to anyone who wants to visit NYC...!

We drove up from Miami for a business meeting in Jacksonville, and decided to stay at this Red Roof Inn. I was pleasantly surprised. Free high-speed WiFi was great. The room was spotless, and we had a full desk to work at in our room. Raphael at the front desk was extremely helpful. I asked him for a few choices to go to dinner and some entertainment. His recommendations were right on. The hotel is in an area surrounded by other high end hotels. We made the right choice picking this one. The rates were the most reasonable in the area and the hotel was better than we expected.

title_masked: Okay Hotel, But No Embassy Suites
text_masked: The hotel is okay, and offers some nice ameneites, but I most likely would not stay there again. I should have just stayed at my favorite place, The Embassy Suites. It is hard to offer a fair comparison if you are used to staying at high-end hotels, but overall the hotel was clean, the service was good. Be advised that the nightly rate was out of scope for the value of the room, and there are not a lot of good restaurants in the area.

My girlfriend had previously stayed at this hotel while visiting Philadelphia, but I had yet to have the opportunity to visit it. None the less, this past week we spent a night in the hotel and I found it to be very enjoyable. Everyone there was incredibly friendly, from the doorman to the staff to even other guests, everyone was friendly at this hotel. It isn't cheap to stay at this hotel, though for a hotel that is in the heart of downtown Philadelphia, it certainly could be much more expensive. The hotel is presented in a trendy, up to date fashion... very modern design, bordering on hipster. The room we stayed in was spacious, comfortable, and well equipped. The hotel is incredibly pet friendly, providing doggy beds and other items for our canine companions. A lone complaint would be just how long it took to receive the car from the valet, though the valet did give a warning that with the traffic, it could take some time.
