I certainly would not hold this minor detail against the hotel though, not their fault there was traffic.

My family stayed here Jan 6-8. The hotel was very clean and the room was great. We liked the extra sitting room, fridge, microwave, and flat screen tv. Breakfast buffet was above average for being complimentary. Employees were very nice and there is a shuttle if you want a ride to nearby attractions (not to airport though).

This hotel was great. Great service and staff. I would recommend this hotel to famliy and friends. The management is GREAT.....very convenient to hwy and close to resturants.he hotel was a good value.

At first I was a little skeptical as i thought a lot of the reviews were shills (a lot of first time reviewers giving high ratings) but I was pleasantly surprised. 
It's a nice boutique hotel that is In a great location. Lincoln park is across the street (as is the free zoo there as well). The beach is not too far either as is a 24hour Walgreens.There's a lot of different buses to get you uptown or downtown (Mag. Mile, the Bean etc). Gym is tiny as are the elevators but there are three elevators. 
Room is a bit tiny but is well furnished. It's got a flat screen tv, safe, free wifi. The bathroom is small with very limited counter space and needs more hooks. There's no mini-fridge but no big deal. The walls are thin and u can hear conversations fairly clearly among other sounds. Luckily our neighbors weren't too noisy. 
Overall we enjoyed our stay and had no complaints. We also scored a nice deal when we made our on-line booking (4th nigh was free) which was a bonus. The staff were friendly and the fact our neighbors were not too loud leads is to our 4 out of 5 rating (loud neighbors would've dropped to a 3).

title_masked: extemely good value, clean, well run and great staff
text_masked:
I purchased via Kayak/Hotwire and got fantastic price. I was apprehensive because the price seemed to be low for a quality hotel. I was very impressed with all aspects of this hotel. If you are paying your own expenses this is a fabulous buy.Ttwo rooms with nice outside fire pit to relax after a long day. The Fox news non stop at lobby bar is a bit much, but bartender was willing to change.
I travel 100+ days a year and this is one of the best deals I have seen.

I was pleasantly surprised on arrival at this property. It is quite new, modern, very clean and was an excellent value. The bed was very comfortable and the free breakfast choices were very good. I will return when in the area.

I have stayed here at least 4 times in the last 6 months and it is SO convenient to everything and reasonably priced. The rooms are nice size,quiet, and clean.The front desk is always pleasant and eager to please and if something isn't as promised they go out of their way to make it right. The Front Desk manager, Kerman, sent me an email apologizing when the staff took 2 hours to bring up a coffee maker to my room and promised an upgrade and better service on my next stay. In this day and age you don't often find this kind of customer appreciation! I intend to stay here on every visit to NYC ( my daughter lives in Manhattan) which will be often!!!

title_masked: A bar with rooms on top
text_masked:
The Clift is a nice hotel with friendly staff, clean and comfortable rooms in a good location on Geary and Taylor (near Union Sq). However it is also a series of rooms on top of a loud and dark bar that's full of prostitutes looking for business travellers. The music pumps throughout the whole ground floor, and it's difficult to relax and chill out when you're surrounded by fat and balding business travellers being fawned over by 20 year old hookers. The bar could be nice, but it's the customers who bring it down - if you want to feel depressed to the point you would welcome some righteous wrath of god type cleansing then sit in the Clift bar on a Saturday night.
The Clift could be good, but it just needs to decide whether it is a late night bar or a hotel. I've stayed here many times over the last few years for work (forced to because of business rates) and I've had enough. Never again.

This is an older hotel. My room (one queen bed) was small - barely enough room to walk around the bed. The wall-mounted a/c unit is right next to the bed (and your head), with limited control options; it's old and noisy (but then, so am I). It's not the kind of room where you want to linger & lounge. 
The property is squeezed in a crowded area of hotel circle. But the location was very handy. The rates were good. The bathroom was clean, and spacious enough. The water was hot, the amenities good (I hate that gooey super-sweet smelling shampoo). We were arriving late & leaving early, and needed a basic, predictable, inexpensive place to sleep. For that, it fit the bill.

Stayed here for a conference and the hotel accommodations and staff couldn't have been better. Inner courtyard is very pleasant with beautiful patio furniture and a fountain. Rooms were super clean and bedding very lush. TV was a bit hard to navigate but a call to the front desk produced very courteous and helpful staff. Henry, the Hotel Ambassador, was pleasant and took a personal interest in making sure each guest had an enjoyable stay. Given that I had a cold - he was always asking how I was doing which was very much appreciated.

We booked the hotel through quickbook, got a good deal and were very pleased with the hotel. The room was good/average, the bathroom was nice and clean and the location (being close to the Empire State Building and the Grand Central Station) was excellent. However we did find the wifi and the breakfast expensive.

Hotel with perfect location in center of Manhattan. Very friendly staff! Very large, spaceous rooms!
Extensive review will follow later!

I booked online with no problems. Finding the hotel we easy. The staff was very friendly and even provided a nice amenity for our anniversary. The decor was top-notch and the room was fabulous with a great view of Mt. Rainier. I would recommend this to any one desiring to stay in the UW district. Restaurant choices in the area not the greatest but its a U district. What do you want. Thanks for a great time.

I was in Chicago for a conference at the Swissotel and decided to stay at Blu Auqa instead of the Swiss. The hotel is connected to the Swiss and the Fairmont hotel via tunnel. I had a corner suite on the 15th floor facing Lake Michigan. Beautiful room and view. New and very nice - even had a balcony off the room - although too chilly to use. Hotel staff service was excellent. I booked the AAA rate which included breakfast in the restaurant - which was ok. Beware that they add a $4 tip to your room for the breakfast buffet - even though I left a cash tip on the table when I dined. I stayed several days and the waiter never bothered to tell me I was tipping twice. Wait staff at the buffet did not seem very motivated, unlike the front desk staff and others in the hotel. Regardless, it was an excellent place to stay and I will do so again next year. Much nicer and newer than the Swissotel - but just as convenient when attending a conference there thanks to the "Pedway".

For convenience it is great. Directly attached to Terminal B and with a shuttle service every 20 mins in the morning to all other terminals. It seems to be an older hotel despite the modern exterior. The staff were friendly, but every time I passed check-in there was a line - even at 4am! The room was very clean, but on the small side and the furniture and fittings looked a little past their best. The bed was comfortable and the room was quiet, in spite of facing onto a busy road. I ate at the restaurant. It is somewhat dark with a university boathouse theme. The hostess was absent from her podium a lot and I saw guests walk out after waiting too long, or going into the kitchen to find someone to seat them - not typical at a Marriott. The service was friendly, but also slow, and the food was fine, but nothing to write home about!
The bathroom was small but plenty of hot water and a great shower.
If you have an early or very late flight this is the most convenient choice and you will find a clean bed and friendly staff in a hotel that needs a somewhat improved infrastructure.

I have yet to write a review of a hotel, but the reason is I have never felt compelled to. My experience staying at the Sofitel after Hurricane Sandy knocked out power to our apartment was a breath of fresh air during a hectic and difficult time. Hours after I lost power (and water) I made dozens of calls to local hotels as I have a toddler daughter that I was eager to keep warm and safe. Many of these calls were met with brief negative responses. I understand it was a trying time but I will not forget some of the rude response I received. The desk at Sofitel was different. They welcomed me and my family warmly. Due to the length of the blackout we ended up staying at the Sofitel at length, five days in total and I have not one complaint about the experience. The room was clean and maintained with finesse the entire week (it was as beautiful and comfortable a room I have stayed at in New York City). The lobby and the restaurant were cozy, comfortable, and accommodating to even my 18 month old daughter (We have noticed this isnt always the case in a hotel as nice as this). But as good as the rooms and amenities were the service and the way my family was treated the entire stay is the true reason we will return (Within minutes of reaching our room a fridge was brought to us to store my daughters milk and other necessities!). I am thankful I chose Sofitel for my family during this difficult time.

A large group of friends stayed here for a recent long weekend in the windy city. It was a perfect choice. We chose the suites and it worked out perfectly for us. "Free parking" was what attracted us in the first place but we were thoroughly pleased with our entire experience. The front desk staff was always smiling and helpful (Wallace, the concierge, is a gem!). Rooms were very clean and comfortable. The hotel is within walking distance of numerous wonderful restaurants and we were able to catch the "hop on - hop off" double decker tour bus only 1 block away.
We enjoyed breakfast in the hotel restaurat where the meals were reasonable and to our entire group's liking (there were 9 of us).
We will definitely be returning to River North for our next stay in Chicago.

My husband and I recently spent our 1yr anniversary in our own hometown, and stayed at the Hilton. They upgraded us to a room with an amazing view of camden yards and there was complimentary breakfast and happy hour snacks in the executive lounge. It was a great location for all of the downtown attractions and you could easily walk to the inner harbor or the stadiums.

Stayed at the hotel for 5 nights with the family. Front desk and room attendants were all very welcoming and did their jobs exceptionally well.
Rooms were clean and the amenities were excellent; especially the frequent shuttle service to Inner Harbour and John Hopkins Hospital.
Breakfast buffet was good and ala carte service in the evening was very good.
A nice touch would have been concierge service.

Room was large, clean, comfortable and well appointed. I'm not a fan of the giant , mall-like atmosphere of the hotel and the lobby area but appreciated the amenities and overall comfort level of the room. Conveniently located close to a metro and you can easily walk to Adams Morgan for access to restaurants and bars from the hotel (as long as you don't mind about a 15 minute walk). Again, while not personally a fan of the property's general layout and design, I would stay here again as the rooms are clean and comfortable.

We orginally booked the Rennissance and although this was a great property the location of the Marriott Long Wharf was too tempting to not take. The staff was great...the rooms are a bit small, but again LOCATION LOCATION LOCATION! The food was great and I loved the hotel staff member that greeted you at the escalator every day. Finally the bellman are the best and you can trust their expert advise~The last words we heard as we left the property was, "You are a lucky man what a beautiful family." Its the simple things....Thank you guys!!!!

title_masked: Awesome hotel, close to so much!
text_masked:
One of my girlfriend's and I stayed at this hotel back in March, over the St. Patty's Day weekend. It was the first time in Boston for both of us so we did not know exactly what to expect. We had a blast! We ended up taking the subway from the airport to the hotel and it was super easy. When we arrived at the hotel, our room wasn't ready but we waited in the cozy Library. Once we got to our room, I was happy with the set up and cleanliness! The beds were comfty and the bathroom was spacious (being two girls, we had A LOT of products to put out but there was ample room for our stuff). 
The hotel staff was helpful, especially the doormen :) Being the St. Patrick's day weekend, there was a TON of noise and commotion out on the street, which was easily heard through our windows, even though they were closed. We didn't mind of course but for families looking to stay here at the same time of the year, I would suggest perhaps to request a room away from the busy streets if possible.
A couple MINOR negative points about the hotel, internet was expensive if you wanted to use it. But that is a small set back because there is always Starbucks down the street with wifi. Also, the hotel is (was) undergoing external restorations so at the early morning hours we could hear (and see) construction workers outside our window. We were on the 6th floor by the way. Not something they could control but the view wasn't pretty and we had to keep our blinds shut so no one could look in...slight downfall.
Other then that, I would highly recomment this hotel! It's extremely close to all the amazing things in Boston. We walked everywhere and those sites that weren't in walking distance (Harvard, Fenway) we took the subway, which is very close to the hotel. All in all, I would definitely go back and stay there again!
Thanks Hilton! :)

We were actually suppose to stay down the ways at the Radisson and then shipped off to this hotel by our convention which turned out to be the best thing at first i was upset then I got to interact with the staff after this problem and that in it self made my whole stay better. The rooms were great very nice and I enjoyed the two knights. Special thanks to Jessica and Mario ask for them they were a big help during my stay

title_masked: Great location, great value and friendly staff
text_masked:
Got a great deal through expedia. Enjoyed our stay in this well located hotel.
The room was well presented and clean, only undone by cleanliness of the window frames. The decor could do with an update, and unfortunately the early start to the on going roadworks outside meant we got an early wake up call most mornings. The windows could do with better sound proofing to stop the noise from outside encroaching.
The proximity to the cable network meant we had a great transportation connection to key parts of SF. Get a City Pass and it becomes a cheap travel option. One drawback is that the closeness of the cable cars also means you have to listen to it. At times it sounded as if we were living in the Windy City.
The staff were friendly and really helpful, and we really enjoyed the daily wine tasting. It was a great way to meet the other guests.
Wifi was fast and free. Used the nearby Cafe Roxanne for good breakfasts so didn't missing the the fact that the hotel doesn't have a kitchen. Didn't consider Masa's restaurant as a real part of the hotel - too upscale in comparison to the rest of the place.
And no, we couldn't smell the musty odour that some others have mentioned.
Overall a really good experience and yes we would consider going back.

Had a wonderful stay in a nice room at the Hilton Baltimore. It's close to many restaurants and not too far of a walk from the pier/wharf area. Front desk staff were very friendly. Disappointments: Lobby bar too expensive. Could not get a late checkout (only needed 1 hour). But most disappointing was the air conditioning. This was even after engineering checked it. So sleeping was not an option in a warm room. That may be preferred by others, but not me. By the way, even the engineering staff were friendly. They leave you a chocolate hammer for contacting them!! So, customer attention A+....air conditioning--C-

title_masked: Great location and very good service
text_masked:
We stayed here in late April 2012, We were returning to New York for pleasure and have been to the city several times before.
Location is just perfect as a tourist and you have access to the subway and Times square is a stone throw away (100m) max
The hotel is very dark, in fact nearly black in places, but it was lit very nicely giving a sense of french boudoir.
The room was nice and modern with an open plan view of the shower area, which is a large walk in made off glass. So really this hotel only really works for couples as privacy can only be had in the toilet !!! The room was small, with no real view outside to talk off, but hey we wanted somewhere to sleep, nothing else.
We had an added bonus of free breakfast, hot coffee and rolls, some cerials and muffins and juice. With some fruit. Very good for nothing but if you left it much after 8.30 it was a bit of a job to find a seat. 
The hotel had a bar area which closed at 11pm everynight ? very odd for a hotel but not a problem as you have loads of bars across the street.
Overall I really enjoyed the stay and its a great place for the tourist in New York.
Staff let us check out at 5pm on our last day as our return flight wasnt until 9pm, so very good service all round.

title_masked: Perfect location for catching an Orioles game!
text_masked: I stayed one night at the Radisson Plaza Lord Baltimore, and booked through Priceline. I was a bit worried after finding out where I'd be staying and reading the reviews but was pleasantly surprised when I got in. Check-in and check out were quick and easy, I had no trouble finding the hotel, rooms have sleep number beds, that DID work (read a lot of reviews saying many did not) and were surprisingly comfortable. I have always wanted to try one out, so that was a nice touch. I was given a room with only one queen bed, but there was only one of me staying, so that was fine. Carpeting had some weird reddish stains on it, and the bathroom was a bit outdated and had a window with shutters in the shower/tub area, strange, but it was fine. The hotel is about a .7 mile walk to Camden Yards, and I did not feel unsafe, even as a single female at night. I believe this hotel is a historic hotel, the building is old and charming, and while the rooms could use a little updating, I was very pleased with the price and the location. Exactly what I was looking for!

People keep going on about the size of the rooms, yes there are small but they are very nice and clean. Besides, how long do you really stay in the room. The small rooms have an added advantage - the A/C the rooms are the prefect temperature!
The staff are very helpful, the girl at the reception (Erica, I think) had lots of patients with my grumpy face after the 4hours in the airport, 7 hour flight and 2 hours in customs.
If I were to describe this hotel in one word I use 'Cool!'.
When I was there I only visited the bar once, it was very nice and chilled. But 9th Ave has all the night life you need, loads of great bars and restaurants!
So to sum up - the rooms are small but very nice, the staff are helpful. If you are travelling alone, on business or as a couple you'll have a great time and for a good price (given NYC prices) :)

This hotel was okay. No free wifi, no free breakfast, the room was clean and pretty spacious for NYC standards, and it was quiet, too, which was nice. The hallways were dank and dark and had an odd smell, maybe because the carpet looked old? I know that's being nit-picky, but, overall I don't think I would seek it out to stay there again bc of the no wifi/no free breakfast reasons. Front desk people were lovely, though!

Stayed 9 days in a deluxe suite. Loved our deluxe suite. Comfy beds, big living room with big flat screen tvs. Was a busy time for them but only breakfast was busy in the mornings. Elevators were never much of a wait even though they are fairly small. Bell man, door man, desk, housekeeping all great. Breakfast was a little small but was fine. We also ordered continental breakfast through room service which was part of our rate. Bathroom was big for new york which was great also. The only problem I had was the mini bar guy who kept insisting we took from the mini bar but we never did. He very rudely told me the computer know if you took or not because of the sensors. Ended up to be an error with their computer. Still he came everyday to say the same thing. Next time i will ak to have the minibar emptied. Not much of a lobby but we were always too busy to sit down. I really loved this hotel. Their suites are the same price as regular rooms in other hotels and service is top.

I booked this hotel for a couple of nights break in San Francisco and therefore location was important. I arrived by BART from the airport and the hotel was easy to find and a short walk from the station. It is located a couple of minutes from Union Square with its shops and the end of two of the cable car lines down to Fisherman's Wharf.
Check in was about as slick as it could have been and I was in my room in no time. Being a Philippe Starck designed hotel the communal areas are dark and funky. The hotel is designer throughout with many great features.
My room was a Superior room on an upper floor which meant that I got a view out over the city (not the greatest of views but at least I could see the sun go down). Being an older building the rooms were a good size and not overloaded with furniture. The room was well furnished and clean, the only downsides I would say is that there were no coffee making facilities and the sockets were few and in poor positions for using the desk. Minor points on balance.
The bathroom was small in comparison to the bedroom but well fitted and the amenities were good.
At night the ground floor of the hotel, with the Redwood Bar, turns into a trendy drinking joint, however, your room key allows you to jump the queue which is great if you're looking for some nightlife.
If your not then you have to stay in your room and I found that at 0200 when the bar closes the noise on the street is loud enough to hear on the upper floors.
All in all a great hotel, although at the weekends you do have to watch out for the "pretty people" who seem to walk straight through you with self importance.

When you check in, make sure to ask for a room away from the street side. I'm here for a week on business and my room is LOUD LOUD LOUD!! I can hear ALL the conversations at the sidewalk cafe below my room and it's 11:00 p.m. The honking cars are very unpleasant as well. My room is nice but I'm glad I have the room to myself because there is no privacy in the bathroom and/or shower. Very cool and modern but NOT a place for family. And I like a very dark room so again....ask for something away from the street because the street lights shine in my room and light it up. I didn't bother asking to move rooms because I was unpacked for the week and had toiletries, cosmetics, and clothes everywhere. Too much of a hassle to move and besides, one little Ambien tablet will solve the minor inconvenience of noise and light. Otherwise this is a very nice hotel and staff is very helpful and friendly.

We had a great time. The hotel is beautiful. Everyone was very helpful.
Send us some coupons.. :)
The sights are within easy walking distance and there are many good restaurants nearby. The restaurant and bar in the hotel were also very good.

title_masked: What a boutique hotel should be!
text_masked:
Where to start? The hip trendy decor? The nice room and bathroom size? The location? Let me start by saying this is one of the best hotel experiences in my life!
I traveled from the 17 til the 21st of October with a friend and my nephews (age 6 & 10). We arrived on a late flight from Panama, so a couple of weeks before the arrival, I sent the hotel an email to confirm the room (two queen beds) and to make sure there was no problem arriving at 2 a.m. I got a very quick response confirming both this things, so I can say my great experience began two weeks before I got into the hotel.
I arrived at 2 a.m. and had very fast and friendly check in process. Hassle free. Got to the room and it was SPOTLESS! Very nice size with two queen beds, a mini fridge, microwave (no forks or knives), with sink to clean up, a mini bar (for soft drinks and juices) and some snacks. Huge 50 inch SmartTv and even a couple of chairs and a table. The bathroom was also very nice. Loved the lipstick nightlight (gotta be there to understand)
The hotel is located near a lot of restaurants and stores. A few steps to the Grand Red Line Metro Station, and a 5 minute walk to Michigan Ave (The Miracle Mile). There are bus stops everywhere to go to Navy Pier o anywhere else (public transportation in Chicago is very good)
It had a very nice breakfast included in the room price. It consisted of waffles, quiches, toast, pastries, juices, milk, coffee, tea and hot chocolate. I also remember seeing fruits and yogurts. Great added value.
I would definitely will come back to this hotel while visiting Chicago. It has pluses all the way (and remember, I was traveling with kids, and the also LOVED the hotel)

My husband and I thoroughly enjoyed staying here for a convention at the Hynes Covention Center. It is a very short walk -- about 1 1/2 blocks. The room had adequate lighting, especially the bathroom. The room had a mini-fridge and a hair dryer, but no coffee maker. However, one can get coffee and hot water for tea in the lobby, just bring your own decaf tea. The breakfast was good, and we didn't mind having the same thing every morning (as we have the same thing every morning at home). There is an elevator, but it is a bit slow. It was a quiet place to stay. In fact, although we saw other guests at breakfast, we only shared the elevator once with one other person. We liked the fact that there were restaurants on the same street. We especially liked the lunch buffet at the nearby Kashmir Indian restaurant.

I was quite surprised by the great customer service at this hotel. Everything from just really friendly staff, to being very quick on requests for extra glasses, bottle openers, etc... even a bowl uncooked rice when we needed to dry out a wet iphone (at 2am).
Loved the happy hour too!

title_masked: Great stay, wished it was longer
text_masked: Took my daughter and a friend to the Crowne Plaza - to avoid a long drive between a 2 day volleyball tournament. We checked in pretty late, and check-in was quick and friendly. Room was comfortable and just right after a long day. We did not have time for the pool or breakfast, but my daughter liked it enough to ask if we could come back another time. 1st time booking with Hotwire, and it was a positive experience at the Crowne Plaza. Did not hear planes at all, and would stay there again.

title_masked: great location and staff, I would stay again
text_masked: From doorman to housekeeping, everyone was friendly and helpful. The room was well supplied, even with umbrella and flashlight. We were there during Hurricane Sandy, and staff stayed in the hotel so service was continued. There was a complimentary wine and cheese on a couple of afternoons. The metro is just a block away on Broadway, and the hotel is located mid way up Central park, close to the Natural History museum. After the storm we walked to TIme's Square,(there was no metro after the hurricane), it took an hour. Easy walking to to Lincoln centre. Revolving shower head with great water pressure, nice tub and bubble bath. Fluffy towels, and comfortable beds/pillows. No excess street noise noted, but traffic was reduced. The neighborhood has a variety of local restaurants.

If you want subtle elegance without the anonymous, standardized "hotel feel", comfort and absolute cleanliness, a sense of total safety, a great location two minutes' walk from the magnificent Central Sation and the impressive New York Public Library, about ten minutes from Time Square), excellent value for money, feeling you're in the centre of the centre of New York without the noise and stress...look no more! It's the Library hotel!
My special mention for the excellent (free all day long) espresso - it beats even some I've had in Italy!

Recently in Chicago for a conference, and my office put me up at the Almalfi. A bit of a mixed bag, the service was great, no issues there, but the room felt a lot like a tarted up Holiday Inn. Everything was a little cramped, except for the bathroom (which was large), but the space devoted to that, while nice, took away too much from the rest of the room.

My family and I stayed here for two nights in July. I called ahead on the day of our arrival to ask if we can have our two reserved rooms adjoining or as close to each other as possible. The gentelman who took my call, Milan, was so helpful that he even checked the floor to see if the two rooms he was holding for us were next to each other or across the hall from each other. That type of exceptional service is hard to come by these days. Both rooms we had (we were a family of 10) were impeccably neat and clean. The staff was always friendly and helpful. This hotel is also great walking distance to Georgetown and other sites. The continental breakfast was also a wonderful bonus. Only down sides: there is no pool and no restaurant on the premise.

We stayed at this hotel for a wedding. It is an older hotel, but seemed fairly well-maintained. The staff were friendly and attentive. I just wish they would add some background music in the lobby, it was too quiet.

title_masked: Great place to stay in Downtown
text_masked:
A nice, upscale hotel in downtown Seattle. It's expensive, being in downtown, and parking prices are a bit of a sticker shock. But the beds are way comfy, the rooms are pretty big and really clean. Maxwells' is a pricey but good place for breakfast (in hotel, second floor). The 28th floor lounge is quiet and has good views of the city. Again, food and drink is a little pricey. I choose to stay here as a one-night minivacation - a little luxury. Generally I eat dinner somewhere else around town and relax in the hotel (most rooms come with a bathrobe!). 
It's about three blocks from the waterfront and a good walk uphill. You can walk to restaurants on the piers and get your blood going on the walk back. 
Staff have always been friendly and outgoing, especially with recommendations on local places to eat (I mean LOCAL, little hole in the wall places you'd drive right by that are very well priced with fantastic food!). Will definitely stay there again.

I stayed at the Palomar in Chicago a few years back and enjoyed the Kimpton aesthetic (and evening hosted wine hour!). This stay was no different--the hotel has a convenient location more or less in the gaslamp (but not RIGHT over the bars so it was relatively quiet) and was walking distance to all the bars and restaurants in that area.
Pros: Clean, modern rooms. Comp. coffee/tea in the lobby in the morning and wine/beer at night. Cheap and tasty happy hour snacks in the attached bar/lounge. Free fast wi-fi and "raid the mini-bar" coupon if you join the (free) loyalty program (who wouldn't?) Staff were really nice, friendly, helpful.
Cons: Lovely but awkward shower--rain-style shower head and no door. Very stylish but also ended up getting water all over the bathroom if you weren't careful. Pool area was also lovely, but the pool was rather small and very shallow. (But then again, I wasn't really looking to swim laps.)

We stayed at the London and our experience was truly unforgettable.. The room was large and spacious. The view of the city was great. It is in a great location close to Time Square and many restaurants. Everyone that worked at the hotel was very helpful and ready to take care of any need we may have.After a long day of sight seeing we decided to have dinner in the hotel restaurant Maze.It was so convenient and we really enjoyed the food & atmosphere.

I've stayed at this property 4 times in the last 2 months and was not overly impressed.
On each of the first 3 stays I booked a rate that included breakfast and each time the front desk indicated that it was not included in my rate and only included it after I showed them the reservation details from the Marriott website which indicated breakfast was included. Even after getting them to correct this upon checkin I was still denied breakfast on one occassion even after the restaurant inquired with the front desk, so beware that you get everything included in your rate.
Other than my issues with the breakfast, the hotel is acceptable, but not exceptional.
The Good: Nice lobby area; staff was friendly; comfortable and nicely appointed rooms; great internet speeds
The Bad: HVAC is loud; try to get a room away from the main road (Tower Rd.) because road noise can be heard in the room; small fitness center; bathroom counter is small
Overall not a bad hotel, but I believe there are better alternatives in the area.

We wanted to spend a couple of days seeing the sites in Chicago. This hotel proved to be an excellent location at a good price. We love historic buildings transformed into nice places to stay. The doorman who greeted us was over the top friendly and helpful. He also served as concierge with great tips on restaurants, sites, in town transportation and more. He really made us feel at home. 
The room was small but very nice. The toiletries were quality, the bed was comfortable, the view was good (wish I was a few floors higher). They have a restaurant which seems to be nice, but we opted for neighborhood italian restaurants. Got a stuffed pizza about four blocks away that was fantastic. Greg the doorman advised we get some flavored popcorn at a place along the way as a snack while waiting for the pizza. It was great! 
There is a convenient pharmacy around the corner to buy day passes on the metro - definitely worth the money. The metro and buses are nearby as is the famous fountain, museums and Lake Michigan. The Magnificent Mile was a short bus ride away, as was Millenium Park. All in all this was a great jumping off point.

This hotel was very easy...
They have valet parking then they are very helpful at the front desk and it has very friendly staff!!
It is conveniently located and there are very good restaurants very close!
I will definitely stay there again!!!

Wow. Service is what this hotel is all about. Everyone is super friendly and looking forward to help you out with anything you need. The hotel is very nice indeed it has a bar which is always with some people on it but definitely not crowded. Breakfast is not the best but is very good indeed (scrambled eggs, bagels, bacon, sausages, french toast, fruit etc.) The restaurant terrace is really nice and the pool also is great. 
Be sure to ask at your arrival for a parking ticket that will last during your whole stay. Be sure as well to ask for internet or wifi, which it seems that if you ask for it you could get it as complimentary.
The rooms are not huge but very good space, lobby and corridors smell really good and clean. The bed is someway softer that harder and the pillows that I used were feathered... loved them. 
The bathroom has just the basic don't expect anything fancy here. And standard room do not have minibar and safe box. 
Perhaps the only downturn is that if you have a connecting room, you could hear loud neighbors and even their telephones ringing at night or when you are asleep.
Edwin was at the front desk all the time and was very helpful it was the only name I could learn during my stay! Good Work!

An absolutely fabulous boutique hotel in a perfect location for anyone visiting New York...It is beautifully outfitted with a contemporary feel to it...the attention to detail is wonderful, everyone is helpful, the view from the higher floors overseeing the City and Central Park is worth the extra money and all the rooms are really suites which in NYC is a rare welcome. The food and bar downstairs is really a happening place....everything about this hotel is 5* from the moment you walk in....everyone is helpful, a super concierge staff and front desk that is fast, and efficient...You won't be sorry....joanh

title_masked: What more could you ask for
text_masked:
This hotel is awesome. It is new and clean but its really the people that make it great. Everyone of the hotel employees was as friendly and helpful as they could be. I had no problems during my stay, but If I had, I feel like they would have been all over it and made it right (who knows... maybe not, but its the perception that counts). 
Breakfast was great and you just can't beat the happy hour.

I wanted to stay in mid-town because I had many business meetings in the area. I had found the Library Hotel on TripAdvisor. But, I have to say it exceeded my expectations. The staff is friendly, welcoming and knowledgeable 24/7. Included in your room is breakfast, wi fi and wine and cheese in the evening. I opted for the petite room and was a little worried that it would be too small - but it comes with a big bathroom with all the amenities. It was clean and comfortable - the TV was a little old and the reception not great - but everything else was fantastic. I stayed in the Poetry room and loved coming to the room at night and see the poetry books, very relaxing. They have room service and a restaurant with a great wine list. On the day I checked-out my flight didn't leave until later, so they held my bag and said I could continue to use the second floor room where they have newspapers, bathrooms and food. After my meetings, it allowed me to get some water and fresh fruit before I headed-off to the airport. I would definitely stay here again.

title_masked: Good place worth being off Time Square
text_masked: Convenient to theatre district, Hell's Kitchen and a good block away from Times Square (I tried to stay away from the more touristy places). Walked to the Javit's Center each day and really liked the lobby staff. The only thing I would improve would be asking the cleaning staff not to change the radio station each day! Will be back.

Recently we traveled to New York City and stayed at the Affinia Dumont Hotel on East 34th Street in Manhattan. We selected the hotel because of its Midtown East (Murray Hill) location — within easy walking distance of many of the City's sights and a host of excellent restaurants and shopping venues and close to subway stops, which allowed us to explore farther afield. We also chose the hotel because it offers suites, including fairly spacious living room, a separate bedroom and bath and a small, fully functional kitchen.
We were pleased with the service we received from the staff from the time we arrived and were greeted by bellman Juber and front desk staff members. This fine service continued throughout our stay, including our final three days when Superstorm Sandy hit the City and plunged lower Manhattan into darkness. 
Our concierge Gabby was especially helpful in arranging to cancel and get a refund for boat tour tickets advertised as nonrefundable. Front desk agent Paul, who lost his home and belongings in the storm, kept us apprised of the status of services in the hotel and City, despite his personal losses. Hotel general manager Alex Spektor was especially solicitous of us and of all of his guests during this trying period.
We look forward to returning in calmer weather.

We went in April and stayed in this hotel initially because it was well located, reasonably priced and got great reviews and we were not dissapointed. It is a very different hotel experience, not at all the usual formal and often stuffy reception you get, since it is very chilled out and the staff are more like good friends who can't do enough to help. This was a special occaison since I was proposing, so I had been emailing the hotel for a few weeks before we arrived for suggestions on making this extra special. Amanda coletta could not have been more helpful and I cannot praise her enough on what she did to help us. I would like to mention Joe also who was also a great laugh, not just because he kept filling my wine glass during the 'free' happy hour each evening in the reception.

I did not realize until very early in the morning that the window was broken and allowing a draft into the room. I called to complain and the hotel sent extra blankets, but would only offer me to change rooms. my daughter was asleep and i chose to stay in the room because we were leaving so early in the morning. the hotel did not offer any discounts or reimbursements to make my stay better. besides having a very noisy, very drafty room, the hotel was great. the location and price are perfect.

We were a bit nervous when we first arrived, as the hotel seemed to be on a main road, but it was really quiet, and the location was really convenient. It was a short drive from the gas lamp quarter and to other attractions. The rooms are clean and comfortable, and the breakfast was great. Parking is provided.

title_masked: I felt like I was in a horror movie
text_masked: Though this hotel didn't have cockroaches it looked like a roach motel! When we first walked in the hotel, I noticed that the plaster was cracked and coming off of the ceiling and walls! Check in is at 3:00, we arrived at 3:15 and our room was not ready! So of course I needed to use the restroom, the door had no lock and there were holes in the plaster and walls where I could see the lathe every where I looked and it was filthy!!! We finally get our room and take the creaky, creepy two person elevator, it opens up to a dark,dank hallway with dirty, stinky, stained carpet! It's an image I could imagine to be in a Steven King Novel!!! Our room was even worse! The head boards and lamp shades had a thick layer of dust and dirt, the lamp shades also had splattered soda, I'm guessing, on the inside! The bathroom was moldy and dirty with the only outlet for the room next to the shower wall! No towel hooks or anywhere to put your toiletry's. I was afraid to sleep in the bed for fear of bed bugs! There were only 8 fuzzy cable channels No air conditioning so we had to sleep with the window open and you could hear everything. And the customer service was lousy, no help at all!!! The owner should be embarrassed and ashamed at the condition of this hotel! It should be condemned!!! I would have changed hotels but their cancellation policy is ridiculous and I would have ended up paying for my three nights stay either way! I also have pictures which I will try and post later.

title_masked: Two star quality in a five star facility
text_masked:
Over the years, I have stayed in Hyatt hotels countless numbers of times. I have never in all those visits encountered so many unfavorable surprises at a Hyatt hotel as I did recently at this Chicago location. At $325 per night, the bed was a total disaster...I spent the first night tossing and turning due to the lack of back support, all the lumps and the loud squeaks. When I complained the next am to front desk, I was initially told that the whole hotel was furnished with "standard Hyatt beds" and there was little they could do to help me. After further discussions with the director of housekeeping, I was told that all mattresses are changed out on a yearly basis, but if someone before me was particularly "rough"on the mattress in my room, they could bring a new one up and exchange it. The new mattress was much better but still nowhere near the high comfort quality of the mattresses I find in lesser starrred chains such as Hampton Suites, Hilton Garden Inns, and Fairield Suites, 
Also of note, this is another hotel which has decided to "go green". Air conditioning automatically powers down to lower fan settings after running for a while. To get it restarted on high, we had to turn it off and on occassionally at the thermostat. The new toilets which they have installed do not flush with the industry standard 1.6 liter flushes for "greener models", but instead use on 1.3 liters per flush. This must save significant on the Hyatt's water useage and bill, but the toilets remain soiled after a flush and guests need to hand clean the toilet rim with toilet paper to avoid unsightly messes for the next user. The bathroom in our "Junior Suite" was so tiny only one person could possibly enter at a time, and it was equipped with a shower only and not a tub (even though the room descriptor did not mention this). The "suite" also had no separation between bed and the sitting area (which was two small couches and a desk at the foot of the bed.
Thed Hyatt employees were generally polite but it was interesting to see that no matter what number I called, the call always transferred first to the hotel operator and then i would have to wait several minutes for the front desk, housekeeping,concierge or valet to pick up on the call. I felt bad for the bellstand employee who took our luggage to the car. He had back problems and I had to lift the luggage into my car for him even though he was getting the tip.
There are many better choices for a fun weekend near the magnificent mile in Chicago.

Group of girlfriends stayed 4 nights at the Whitehall Hotel in July. The room was clean, beds were extremely comfortable and cleaning staff very accommodating (4 gals need lots of towels!) The hotel is very convenient to Michigan Ave, Rush & State Streets. We didn't need any transportation as we walked everywhere. As stated in other reviews, the elevator is small, but very speedy. Lobby is under construction and is quite small, but didn't affect our stay. Early morning whistling for taxis at the neighboring hotel was somewhat annoying. Had a problem with A/C, but figured out that if you shut the system down for a short period and then reset, it worked fine. No ice machine (which may have been due to the construction), but staff delivered it quickly when called. Concierge was very helpful when I needed help rescheduling flights and airport shuttle. I would definitely stay at the Whitehall again!

title_masked: Great weekend away with the girls!
text_masked:
This hotel more than met our needs for our girls weekend away! As soon as we got to the hotel (9:30am) they had a room ready for us and we didn't have to store our luggage. We were only on the 5th floor but that didn't bother us. We were there for the shopping, not the view from the hotel room. The room was spacious with two very comfy queen beds with plenty of pillows. Lots of drawers and hanging space in the closet. Flat screen television and iPod dock/alarm clock. Bathroom was very nice and refurbished. Excellent lighting that made us look tanned :)
The lobby was spacious and they had free internet use for hotel guests. Six large elevators to our East Tower left us rarely waiting for an elevator.
The breakfast buffet was unbelievable. We had paid $5 per day ahead of time to have breakfast every morning and we thought it would just be a continental one with some fruit, cereal, and pastries. We ended up eating the $23/person hot buffet every morning and were never charged extra. It was delicious, so much to choose from, who doesn't love a fresh omelet made just the way you like it? Make sure you pay ahead of time for the breakfast if you can! More than worth it!
We didn't have any extra charges from our room other than when we made 3 local calls ($1 each). We used our safe in the room and did not get charged extra like some people have mentioned.
The location was perfect! Its on East Wacker right down from Michigan Avenue! It was perfect. We were also right near the middle of the Signature Double Decker Bus tours. We could jump on at like 3 different spots within a short walk. 
The only negative was not having a small fridge in our room for bringing back leftovers or treats (particularly our cheesecake from the Cheesecake Factory). But regardless, I'd stay here again in a heartbeat.

I was impressed that the decor matched what I'd seen on the web. Very nice at government rates.
My room was dark when I arrived but the maintenance man responded pretty quickly and replaced three bulbs. The view was of the hotel in back of the Palomar, but I didn't expect a view paying per diem rates.
The bed was comfortable and the cleaning ladies did a nice job while I was at my conference every day.
So, why only average?
After settling in I went to the pool and saw "happy hour" signs all over the place. The "happy hour" must have been only in the main restaurant, because the pool bartender charged me $9.70 for a gin and tonic in a plastic cup (I realize the plastic is for safety, it's the price that made me unhappy.) I wouldn't have ordered another drink at that price, which was fine because the waitress didn't even look at me the whole time I was there.
The drink put me on guard, and investigating the main restaurant's (the Salt Box) menu I decided I'd be eating somewhere else. Even the breakfast menu was quite pricey.
The design of the bathroom was exotic over functional. The walk-in shower had no door or curtain, just a piece of glass on the shower end that didn't do a good job of keeping water off the floor. I have a slight handicap (foot drop) and was concerned about having no hand holds at all. Everything except a bar of soap was in toothpaste-like tubes that were pretty annoying with wet hands. The two towel racks were placed to require a trip outside the shower. The exhaust fan was missing or very weak. The door itself was a sliding frosted glass thing that again emphasized the exotic over the functional.
I didn't bother checking the prices for the snacks and drinks in the room. I bought a liter of pop at a nearby CVS and just had room in the 'fridge for it. Guest services said there was no ice machine, but sent up a valet with a big bucket of ice. I honestly forgot to tip him. The next night I asked for another bucket of ice and after half an hour called again. The valet came on the second call. I did tip him.
The room had no coffee maker.
The DirecTV connection was poor and most of the stations reverted to ads for pay movies.
The Wi-Fi was $10/day unless you signed up for their rewards program.
The comfortable bed made up for a lot, but unless you are unconcerned about money the only thing you'll want to do here is sleep.

This is a nice hotel but it is in desperate need of updating for a Grand Hyatt. It is a convention hotel and it well worn. You definitely want to ask for a renovated room, but doesn't mean that the room is top notch. The bathroom could of used a through cleaning because the floor seemed dirty. The room seemed to have dust all over it and I could not understand if it was from the linens or something else. The blackout curtain became stuck and after complaining about it 3 times, I just gave up asking them to fix it. I am a Hyatt Gold Member and love staying at Hyatt hotels. This is not as good as other Hyatt's I have stayed at. This hotel is definately not like other Grand Hyatts and I would say it should be classified a class lower than Grand.

I booked a quick getaway for my wife's birthday this past week-end. We always worry about picking the right hotel and spend way too much time reading reviews. You get excited about good reviews but start worrying about the bad ones.
We bit the bullet and booked the W hotel and were pleasantly surprised. Yes the room and bathroom are small but who cares? We were there to roam the city and not spend our time cooped up in the room. The studio was just right for us.
The hotek is very trendy and lively (loby & lounge) but when you get upstairs you can't hear a thing its as if you stepped into another world.
Everything was so cleand and tidy and the staff was attentice and helpful. Three people nust be commended, Jessie on the 16th floor was extremely nice and friendly. She was pleasant as was David the guest coordinator(?) stationed right by the elevators.
There was also the concierge (a pretty blonde) that was right on the money with all restaurant recommendations.
In my booking notes I had indicated that it was my wife's birthday and wanted to do something special for her. I even discussed it with the clerk when I was checking in. Something was lost in translation because nothing special was done. For that David and Jessie were both very apologetic and that ws appreciated.
The Hotel was central to all of the places that we wanted to visit and we will not hesitate to book them again.
Management must commend their workers for a job well done!!!!!

Let's just say that we (colleagues and I) only stayed here because the rooms in NYC were extremely expensive.
Let's start with some minor glitches; $15 for internet - should be free these days, there was no clock in the room, the bathroom was so small you had to move the wastebasket around to make room to use the shower, sink or the other things! You could practically touch all the walls from one spot. There was black mold on the ceiling of the shower as you can see in the pic.
Then I called the front desk to see why there was no room service menu. Oh, the restaurant was closed for renovations, so I had to stop working and walk out in the rain to go get food. Oh, and did they bother to mention when you were booking a room, that they were turning off the electricity for about 4 hours at midnight? The AC stayed on even though the room was hot, but no TV, and nothing charging my laptop or cell. Think about how fun the trip to the bathroom was in the pitch dark.
Also, the bed was awful and they use the "chicklett" pillows, you know, these half pillows that i don't get at all. Who likes half size pillows?
Then in the morning I am about to get in the shower, and there is no shampoo or conditioner. I call the guest services number and tell her. She says, "I will send some up" and hangs up on me. I waited 15 minutes and nothing. I had to shower without to make my appointment. By the time I left the room about 40 minutes later, it still did not arrive.
Don't get fooled like we did.

We arrived at the Marriott to learn that they would not honor a government rate because the hotel was fully booked. My husband had to literally argue with the manager to at least get one night at that rate. There was a $70 difference in the price! In addition, we are Marriott rewards' members which I guess means less than nothing. Our room was awful. Even the person who took our luggage to the room suggested we request a different room. That wasn't going to happen because supposedly they were fully booked. It was, needless to say, very disappointing to not be treated with courtesy by the front desk manager and to not be offered a different room. To add insult to injury, there was no self-parking available but the difference in the cost was only $2. The valet staff was wonderful. At least they represented what Marriott service should be.

title_masked: Great Hotel for the Business Traveler
text_masked:
I travel all over the country and spend about 15-20 days on the road per month. Many hotels pay lip service to taking care of the business traveler but few actually do. I have been to the Renaissance Dallas Hotel quite a few times and it is now my "go to" hotel of choice when I need to conduct work in the "Big D"
The main reason for continuing to give the Renaissance my business is their attention to detail. The restaurant is superb and their location is second to none. However the main reason they still keep receiving my patronage is the fact that they go out of their way to make sure your stay is comfortable and relaxed. The last time I stayed there a personal emergency came up that was really going to put me in a major bind. While on the concierge floor I had the pleasure of meeting Erin Dowell who could immediately tell that something was wrong. She asked if there was something she could do for me and boy did she deliver. Erin personally assisted me in arranging a few details and really went out of her way to make sure that I could focus on work and not have this trip go to waste. Above all else she is the reason I will continue to go back to this fine establishment. 
Big kudos to Erin and the rest of the Renaissance Dallas Hotel Staff. Thank you for going out of your way to make my stay on the road much more pleasurable.

title_masked: Great service and location but old tiny rooms detract from stay
text_masked:
Handlery is in a great central location to anything in San Francisco City. We found the staff very obliging and helpful. The grill next door with an internal access was a great venue for quality meals.
It is an old style hotel with small rooms with minimal space for luggage or relaxing. The room was basically clean but the bathroom was not so good with dust and peeling paint on the window frame. Wire reinforced glass windows on the sixth floor fortunately obscured the view of rusty roofs and brick walls. The room was noisy particularly from 7am when a union contract protest at a different hotel across the road got on their bull horns chanting anti employer slogans. Not the Handlery's fault but the rooms did little to diminish the noise (in fact we thought the protest was in our room on the sixth floor).

After living in River North for three years, I moved to Denver. My frequent returns to Chicago have given me the opportunity to experience lodging in the area. I booked the Acme during the second week of December. Location is probably best in Chicago. Staff very accommodating (even expecting my arrival!), quirky and fun decor, very quiet and comfortable room and bed, loved the chalkboard on the door. Great option for breakfast, coffee 24x7 (hot AND good); bar and small restaurant coming soon. Room well equipped with wet bar and microwave. I absolutely loved it, and have booked again for Christmas. If you want a flashy lobby, go to the big guys in the neighborhood, but why bother: you can just walk there from here. Top shelf!

I stayed here in June 2012 for nearly three weeks on a business trip. The hotel was selected and paid for by my employer, so I am really unable to comment on the value of the hotel compared to others available in San Francisco. The decor could have used a little freshening/cleaning (just signs wear and tear, like scuff marks on the walls). The room itself was clean, and the housekeeping staff were very friendly and accomodating throughout my stay (due to the duration of my stay, I had my room serviced only every other day). While I would have really liked to have a microwave in the room, which the hotel does not have an option for, there was a decent sized refrigerator. That, combined with the fact that there is a Whole Foods one block away, was very convenient for a long stay. Sleep quality was good- some street noise that was easily blocked with earplugs, but no real noise problems from adjacent rooms and the hallway. There were good transportation connections, to include the cable car, right outside the hotel. I mainly did a lot of walking for excercise, and if you can handle walking the hills, there are some nice restaurants in the neighborhood, especially on Hyde St. I gave this hotel only an "average" rating because although I was satisfied with my stay, I think that the location may be a bit less desirable for those who are visiting solely for tourist/vacation reasons. Also, although I found the location to be perfectly fine, there are some rough areas nearby if you walk the wrong way not knowing where you are going. This is common in any big city, but some people may find this a concern and prefer to stick to more "tourist friendly" areas.

title_masked: Great location, pricey and poor service
text_masked: The location was perfect because it was on the beach. We had several problems from the beginning. First when we booked our reservation they had a free continental breakfast which was why we booked at this hotel to begin with. I am not sure when, but they stopped providing the breakfast their customers. Next we called a few weeks before because my mother in law was going to be staying there as well and we were hoping to get ajoining rooms this way if my husband and I wanted to go out she could watch the kids by leaving the ajoining room door open. They told us that the hotel didn't have any, which we later found out was a lie. Then the first night we were there the A/C in my mother in law's room went out. We asked if there were any rooms on our floor that she could move to and they stated that there was nothing on our floor. We found out that there was no one on either side of us the first three days we were there, however, the front desk insisted that there was no room on our floor and that she would have to move to a completely different building. Overall the trip was decent, once we stopped asking for any kind of help from the front desk.

title_masked: More like a hostel than a hotel
text_masked:
This hotel was more like a Hostel, the rooms were small and a little shabby but adequate and were cleaned daily. A central kitchen on the 3rd floor means you can expect quite a bit of noise if you happen to be anywhere near there of on any stairwell. 
That said the place is cheap for San Francisco, we paid $85 a night for a double room.
Location is good. The best part for us was "Eric" the guy on the front desk who was really helpful. 
So if you can do without the creature comforts and are on a bit of a budget this place does what is says on the tin.

Do not be fooled by the Marriot name. The motel is NOT Marriot quality. As soon as we entered the room I realized the closet door was falling off the track. There were marks on the walls, dust on the ceilings from the vents, and the rooms were not updated. Wi-fi is $12.95 per 24 hour period when most hotels offer it free. It is clean, but NOT what I expected.

We have stayed here several times because of the hotel's proximity to medical facilities and it is such a welcome respite. The staff is just wonderful and always accommodating from the front desk to housekeeping. Their beds are just wonderful and I always sleep better than at home.
 I love the french press coffee in the rooms along with the extra thick towels and bathrobes. The furniture is starting to show wear a little, but is still comfortable.
 The fireside room is a wonderful place to unwind and the bar is a true classic that is hard to find these days with its warm, wood interior and always incredible bartenders and wait staff.
 This is my favorite hotel in Seattle.

We had family in last week and our house is just too small, so we made a weekend getaway out of it. We were able to secure a great rate online for this hotel. Rooms are CLEAN and very spacious. The beds were comfortable too. My family loved the pool. Free hot breakfast Sunday morning was good. We found staff to be helpful and friendly. We liked the area and found it to be quiet, but able to quickly get to all areas for dinner, shopping, etc.
Over from scary residence inn at 12:30 am and was in heaven...highly recommend..Marriott platinum member

We stayed here from the 12th to 16th September and loved this hotel. This was our first trip to San Francisco & we were unsure where to make our base. Fisherman's Wharf is a bit touristy with the usual cheesy souvenir shops but the hotel is located away from this section, at the end of the Wharf in a nice area next to the cable car turnaround, giving easy access to the rest of San Francisco. The rooms were very clean, spacious and well kept and had enough space for the 3 of us. The bathroom was big enough, shower in bath but all very modern and nice decor. The rooms were comfy, great beds, we would defiantly stay here again.

The rooms are small, bed comfortable, the bathroom shared, everything very clean. Had no difficulty getting into the bathroom each time I needed it. Two on the floor. Even though our room was next to the bathroom, we never heard any noise from there, maybe because the air conditioner was so loud. The elevator is tiny and slow. Don't bring a lot of luggage. We were pleased to find that there was free on street parking on the block from 6 pm Friday to 8 am Monday. When one of us sat in the desk chair, the other had to climb over the bed to move around. Very inexpensive and well worth it. Convenient to the place where my workshop was being held.

Hotel Penn. shudder. The first room we were given was reminiscent of a room where someone who had lost all hope would go to compound their misery. Opened the door, looked for the light switch but there was none. The only light was a lamp on the other side of the room which you had to stumble in the dark to get to. The dim, orange glow did nothing to improve the mood of despair that oozed from the room. The sink had a large crack and (of course) a flickering overhead light to add to the horror film atmosphere. We went back to reception and were 'upgraded' to a room with a light. It is quite a good move to put the bar so low with the first room that for 2 min we thought this room was ok. It wasn't. Dirty, grey sheets, damp on the walls and an old, flaky toilet seat. Couldn't find any power points and the thought of foraging around the darker places in the room to find them filled me with dread. We stayed in several hotels on that trip and this was by far the worst value for money. Not a pleasant experience

We spent a weekend there in the beginning of November. The room was clean, comfortable and well appointed and the bed was very comfortable. The staff was very friendly, including those that we met in the hallways and elevators. Our room did not have a refrigerator but it sounded as though you could request one.
The hotel seemed very busy (good for them) but it was also right after Hurricaine Sandy. What ever the reason, it was a very busy breakfast area. Food was mediocre at best but what do you want for "free". Overall, certainly a hotel we would return to. The location was great and within walking distance to several local attractions.

I searched and searched for a good hotel for a good price in a good location. I found a GREAT hotel at a very reasonable price in a Great location. The staff was excellent, attentive, prompt, courteous and most of all just very welcoming. Akesia (hope I spelled it right - sorry!) the concierge was UNBELIEVABLE!! She was spot on with directions, touring suggestions, dining suggestions and reservations. We were there to celebrate the 40th birthday of my wife and her twin sister and we all loved the attentive friendly ways she helped us out. While I suppose it wasn't too hard to figure out where a big guy from Georgia wanted to eat, Ben and Jacks Steakhouse on 5th (a top 5 steakhouse I have been to and I have been to a LOT) she sat with my wife and her sister and really listened to their wishes for their birthday dinner and picked out a place they REALLY loved! (The Blue Water Grill)
The location is a block away from The Empire State building and we felt like all the things we did were very easy to access (we are walking or taxi travelers in NYC)
 Everyone we encountered at Hotel Chandler, bellmen, front desk folks, cleaning staff - everyone - was exceedingly gracious and accommodating. We wouldn't think of staying anywhere else in future New York Trips! 
Thanks for the great stay!
Jeff and Michelle

We had a beautiful king room facing the Pacific ocean. It was everything I had hoped for.
Not to stuffy, although very clean, comfortable, beautiful views right from our room and friendly and professional staff. Parking was just $10.00 extra a night compared to other hotels was a deal. They had a salt water aquarium in the loby which was one of the best I've ever seen.
 O yes did I mention the comfy bed. There where good restaurants just around the corner. The beach was clean. I would love to visit again and will recommend it to my friends.

title_masked: A touch of class in a classy city
text_masked:
We stayed 6 nights last week in a tower room with a city view.
This is a very classy and historic hotel in a beautiful city. Each time you enter the lobby area you feel like Royalty and its worth gliding up and down the grand stair case a couple of times for full effect. 
We were very impressed by the standard of service given to all guests by all the staff [discrete, understated, helpful and friendly].
And, our observation was that this held up whether the guest be wealthy, famous, on business,or just ordinary folk like us who had saved hard and treated themselves to some thing a bit special. 
It was the understated service and old world elegance, with out it being pretentious or snobby that we appreciated - as a opposed to the staff being all over you. We did not get any "have a nice day" which can some times feel a bit false.
If you like flying with British Airways and Lufthansa and think Virgin Atlantic is over rated, then you will get it!
And it was the staff and the beautiful old worldliness of the Fairmont that made for a memorable stay.
We like the super comfortable bed and the big bathroom. It was spotless and house keeping were 1st class.
The room décor is old fashioned and a bit tired - but we thought it was part of the charm. Our window could have done with a visit from the window cleaner - that's our only gripe.
We had a couple of breakfasts, and an evening meal in the Laurel dining room as well as cocktails in the Tonga room. All pricey, but value in terms of quality, service and setting. The Tonga room is very kitsch.
The Fairmont is really handy for public transport - you can get every where on the cable cars - the 3 lines x outside the hotel. A tip, use the the hotel's garage entrance for the most convenient way of being in the right place to jump on and off the cars - we loved them and as long as you are in no great hurry - "when in Rome". We also used the No 1 bus which is handy and like the cable cars - saves your legs too. It's not for the distances involved - it's the climb - vertical. If you are going to use public transport and ride the cable cars to get about then buy a MUNI pass [1 day, 3 day or 7 day] a long with a MUNI map at the airport tourist information desk in arrivals. We paid $27, each for a 7 day pass and were $'s in by day one - a single cable care ride costs $6 other wise.
If and when we return to SF, we are now spoilt and will find it difficult to stay any where else.

title_masked: Maybe in other time was a good hotel
text_masked:
I read some reviews at tripadvisor so I decide to reserve at this place, since it was close to Broadway,
Hotel was pretty noisy, avoid to stay by 6th floor above they have their old aircondition machine, also you can hear next room conversations (and much more), carpet smells weird, we ask to change room but was full the place;
Beds are really old, clean but old, their staff is kind of rude, 
the good thing is the parking, and is close to Times square, plays and piers.
Elevator partially works, wifi is not free,
Maybe 30 years ago was a nice hotel, not now, quiet old;
for the price I paid I should move to another near by, I wont be here again.
I change the hotel to The New Yorker Hotel some blocks ahead (34th st) and I paid the same (13 usd more) but much much better.
is kind of one star hotel...
Pool is ok do not expect that much, but it is ok

The room (right on the beach) was great. The pool and hot tub were very nice. There were complementary beach unbrellas and boogie boards available for loan right by the door to the beach. All that was great, but the best thing was how accommodating and friendly the staff were. I highly recommend the Ocean Park Inn.

title_masked: Tourleader for DK Gislev-Group, Anna-Lise Jensen.
text_masked:
As a tour-leader for a danisk travel-agency I have stayed at Warwick Hotel many times throughout the last 3 years. I always stay there with groups from 14 to 35 persons.
And is is ALWAYS a pleasure to stay at the Warwick. Everything is prepared and ready upon arrival. The staff in the reseption and the door-men are so nice, smiling, helpfull and obliging.
The whole hotel is filled with a wonderfull atmosphere. The hall, the elevators, the corridors, the pictures on the walls and the rooms.I simply love every room I have ever stayed in. Every room is different but at the same time there is a common assent to all rooms - so coming into a room is like COMING HOME ! 
Breakfast - is fantastic and delicious ! If you can´t find something you like at the very well-stocked bufet, you must be very fussy about food..... And the retstaurant is beautifull. The big paintings on the walls is interesting entertainment if you are on your own. 
I give the hotel and the staff my very best recommendation.

We arrived on a Thursday and received great service for the entire weekend. Ellen was super-friendly and helpful at check-in. The amenities were top-notch, and all the services (valet and bell-hop) were quick. Breakfast was crowded and takes a bit of time in line, but it is a full buffet and omelet bar that is complimentary, so just get there early for a seat! The free manager's reception every night is adequate (free drinks and light snacks), and it is close to all the touristy stuff in the Capital. Rooms are clean and spacious. Nice experience!

I chose the hotel for its location, but was delighted with my choice. The room was spacious compared to other NYC rooms at the same price. It is nicely decorated (just like on the website) and everything smells and feels clean and new. Service was prompt and friendly, food well priced and generous in porton. I also enjoyed the complimentary touches - the walking kit, the pillow menu, the wine!
The only negative is the noise level in NY in general. Bring earplugs! Also walking shoes and big empty suitcase for shopping.

It's a short 10 minute drive to Hillcrest and about 15 minutes to LaJolla. 
This hotel was a bargain for San Diego. While the property itself is aged, they have done a very nice job keeping it up. The rooms were extremely clean. My only real negative feedback is the lack of SPG status acknowledgment.

Our only disappointment is we were only staying one night! Fantastic location - planned to walk to our conference in the morning, but it was raining and we were quickly assisted by the doorman in getting a taxi. The breakfast buffet (very unusual in D.C.) was outstanding. But the best thing about this hotel was the staff - from the guys at the front desk check-in to the breakfast staff - very friendly and helpful. We would go out of our way to stay here again.

Celebrated birthdays in NYC at the Trump Soho- couldnt have been happier! Love the Soho shopping and restaurants. What a beautiful hotel! Room was large and gorgeous! Bathrooms (we had a suite with two bathrooms) were fantastic. We loved staying in the Soho area and will definitely return to the Trump Soho on our next trip to New York!

I was very impressed with this hotel. I stayed for one short night because I was flying out of San Jose early the next morning. When I mentioned this to the woman at the front desk, she said she would prepare a breakfast bag for us the next morning since we would be checking out before breakfast. I didn't even have to ask her to do this! Wondering if she would be true to her word, she greeted us with a smile and gave us the breakfast bags. They weren't very elaborate, but I certainly appreciated her thoughtfulness.
On the whole, I found the hotel very clean and the bed very comfortable. I noticed the room had a small kitchen (sink, microwave, and refrigerator) While I wasn't there long enough to use the kitchen, it's certainly something that's nice to have in a hotel room.
Lastly, the parking is under the hotel and well lit. I felt very safe because of this. However I took the last space under the hotel, and it's conceivable that the following person would have to use the outdoor lot just next to the hotel.

All of the employees with whom we met showed a caring attitude and attentiveness. 
During our stay our son was hospitalized and we had to extend our stay. The hotel was full. Shantelle, the young woman at the desk, helped us extend our stay. If a room could not be found, we would have help looking for another hotel. How kind could a person be? We can not thank her enough for her kindness. 
We will remember the kindness and hospitality of the employees of the Sorrento.

The least attractive part of this hotel is the street on which it is located. The interior is an oasis--clean, attractive, modern. The breakfast was basic but free. Room busy but not unmanageable. Staff friendly and efficient. Excellent location for restaurants and attractions.

My experience at the Sheraton hotel was awesome, the staff members were very nice especially Tessa at the front desk. She was very professional and friendly at all times.Tessa went above and beyond to assure that our stay was magnificent. A true gem

I thought the rooms were in need of a facelift but they were big, clean and comfortable.The public areas were good and there was plenty of parking.
So it was functional but not that exciting.
I get the imression that that European Marriott's are more stylish than those in the US.

This was everything you'd expect from a high class hotel.Helpful staff, very nice, well appointed room and a bar and restaurant to match.The downside of course was that everything was priced accordingly as well. We'd opted for the pricier waterside rooms and ours on the 2nd floor was great apart from the cruise ship that docked next door on our last night. The rail-road to and from the docks ran down the other side of Alaskan Way and it might have made the rooms on the street side a little noisy. Typical of the pricier hotels there was a charge for internet access - how is it that budget hotels provide free internet access but the most expensive want to charge?

Stayed here for location which was probably the best thing about the hotel!
No tea or coffee making facilities in rooms; no water; bed sheets covered in yellow stains aliong with torn mattress coover. HAd to request to be changed twice!
Staff unhelpful. Not once did I get asked about my stay.
Food in bar in ridiculously expensive but cafe next door to hotel which is cheaper.
Noisy as on main street.
Corridors and other interior extremely dated and could have done with a clean; unclean carpets and stains on wall coverings.
And to top it off...you have to pay 4 dollars to store your luggage when checking out!
Would not reccommend this unfriendly hotel with unhelpful staff!

Stayed here a couple of months ago for a weekend getaway - rooms were clean, comfortable and spacious. Lobby was large and clean - Bell staff very helpful. Great location, easy to walk to restaurants on the pier and close to pike place. Would stay here again.

I have been using trip advisor for years, and think I am pretty good at deciphering what people have to say and making a decision based on what I have read. I feel totally mislead by positive reviews of this property.This is a prime example of a property that has rested on it's laurels purely bc of it's proximity to a college campus and is thus popular with students and families visiting.
