We were in Washington to tour Georgetown University, and wanted to stay somewhere close to the campus. The Georgetown Inn IS close to campus, but the convenience of its location does not merit a stay here. The property is totally run down- our room had one of the most outdated bathrooms I have seen in a long time, and the carpet in the room was torn out in places and frayed. The bathroom had a small shower and a chipped and old bidet. The promised entertainment system and CD player in our "suite" was an IPod dock. Except for a very helpful bellman, no one on the staff could answer any questions about local dining or even how to get a car to the airport. But the final straw was the lack of insulation between the rooms. As previously stated in another review, you could hear everything in the rooms on either side. And I mean everything. I finally called the front desk to complain when the party next door reached the point of not being able to hear the TV in our room. I would definitely pay more to stay somewhere nicer- and would give up the convenience of the location. And yes, we asked for other rooms and were told nothing else was available- and we didn't even get the room type that we had made reservations for- even though I had called to confirm the rooms the previous day. As a former flight attendant, I have stayed in many run down hotels. The Georgetown Inn ranks up there as pretty bad.

The hotel was pretty dilapidated. It was in a reasonable neighborhood - but the hotel was extremely noisy. Additionally we were using two hairdryers with the tv on and we blew a circuit and had to have maintenance come up to turn our power back on. When has that ever happened?!?!

Excellent guest service. From Clive the bellman to Robert the concierge, everyone at the front desk and in the halls where polite and attentive. I was recognized as a loyalty member and offered additional perks, which is the benefit of me racking up points with the same hotel company! The hotel was clean, decadent and the location was perfect. I would stay here any time I go to Chicago.

I fully recommend that you stay at the Waldorf. Historic, interesting, comfortable and luxurious.
The staff are highly professional throughout. The rooms are wonderful - we got an upgrade to a king bed double, and it was a truely lovely room. Furnished nicely, comfortable bed, functional bathroom and a useful sitting area to relax. The hotel bar is very nice (although somewhat expensive). We did not eat at the hotel or use the spa, so cannot comment on these areas. 
The Waldorf is in a perfect location for exploring the city, and is a landmark in itself. However, I understand that they are just starting to undertake refurbishments at the front of the hotel (June 2012), so check in advance whether or not this will impact your stay. My guess is not, given the professionalism of this hotel. Stay here. Do not hesitate.

We were in Columbus to compete in the state fair. Desk clerk was easy to work with. We were on the floor, with two queen beds. It was a very nice room with a nice chair and small couch, desk and chair, nice flatscreen, and good beds. Free wifi worked well. The bathroom was good, except I could not find a way to turn on the fan. There was one switch for the light, and that was it. I think there was a fan above the shower, but it was not running. I was a little worried about noise since it was closer to the airport, but it was not a problem. You could look out the window and see the planes landing, but the rooms were well soundproofed all around. The scenery on the east side is two water towers. The pool was tiny, not much bigger than the hot tub. The deepest was four feet. We always swim at hotels, but we skipped it this time. The breakfast was good. Most of the choices were carbs, but they were still good. You can make regualar or cinnamon waffles. Overall, we were very satisfied with this hotel, and recommend it.
Very expensive $150.00 a night could have stayed at the ritz carlton. I will be looking for another hotel in the area next year. $2.00 for a can of coke cola.

title_masked: Flawless stay at the Mondrian Soho
text_masked:
We loved this hotel. Walking in via the Crosby entrance, you feel like you've stepped into an oasis, leaving the streets of Soho to find yourself in a leafy entryway. The hotel itself is modern and beautifully designed. The rooms are bright and spotless, with great floor to ceiling windows. The location is also perfect, because the hotel is steps away from Broadway and everything Soho has to offer, but Crosby is an extremely quiet street.
We were staying to celebrate a special occasion and the hotel staff took great care of us. This was easily one of our best hotel stays ever.
I strongly recommend the Mondrian Soho.

there were bedbugs, terrible service, and incredibly dirty! :S i couldnt even stay there! THE WORST! they didnt want to give my money back! :S they stole it! and the beds are smaller than individual ones, its super old and in bad conditon. and you may not believe it but there were hairs taped on one wall, I SWEAR.

I stayed at the Washington Jefferson (for the first time) for an extended Labor Day weekend (Thursday through Monday). Though I was unfamiliar with the area, it turned out to be quite convenient to everything I was planning on doing. The staff were very courteous and friendly, and were gracious about answering my frequent questions on directions.
The main problem I had, however, was that the room I had faced the street. Apparently trash is emptied 24 hours a day in NYC - or so it sounded! VERY noisy street, and I was unable to sleep due to that and due to the wood blinds in the window, which did not block out the light. The window air conditioner worked fine, and didn't blow directly onto me so I was OK with it. So my advice would be to request a room not facing the street.
I had a single room, with a very comfortable bed and nice bathroom. Very clean. 
I will certainly consider the Washington Jefferson for another trip to NYC.

but I liked it alot! Fab location, lovely room, fun little step out balcony. The room was very sleek, and the hotel was quiet...I was on the 9th floor facing the front. I easily walked to museums, the theater, shopping. The things I missed were a safe in the room, coffee pot in the room, ice machine available to guests, but these are personal preferences. The bed and pillows were extremely comfortable. Food through room service very good. I had cocktails in the bar twice, and both times the service was very lacking, although there was plenty of staff. 
The front staff was very good, especially Deanna in reservations, and Chet, who took care of all kinds of miscellaneous items for me. Housekeeping was hit and miss....toiletries were not refreshed, and day 2 brought no TP. Lastly, I would be remiss if I didn't mention a little encounter with a bellman. I was going to the theater, and when he couldn't get a cab, (which was not a big problem) I said I'd walk, and could I use his Gotham umbrella. His response was that there was one in my room, and it was the only one he had. That is SO not the right response, and had I gone to my room it would have made me late for the play. Instead I walked in the rain, and came home with a raging cold. Perhaps the hotel could invest in some umbrellas at the front door.
Some hits, some misses, but all in all a nice hotel that just needs a little staff training.

We stayed at this hotel after spending a few days on the road in other hotels. The location of this hotel is great - and impressive. It is located right across the street from General Motors, has a station stop for the PeopleMover in the building, and almost directly across from the tunnel to Canada. We went to a Tiger game, and used the train to get there and back - very inexpensive and handy.
The hotel surprised me - considering GM is connected via walkway. It wasn't dirty, but it never felt clean and updated. The sheets and towels were so thin you could almost see through them - and I'm not exagerating. Walls were also thin - more than I needed to hear... Curtains were old, and the carpets were questionable. The hotel staff was nice, but average. I probably would not stay here again.

title_masked: Close to good restaurants and metro stations.
text_masked:
Location: One block from metro where you can access all lines so it is easy to go anywhere in the city without having to do a lot of switching trains. Easy walking distance to theaters. 7 block south and 1 avenue east to the center of Times Square (remember that streets are short walks, avenues longer). Easy walk to 47th Street (also known as Restaurant Row) in the Hell's Kitchen area where there are many great little restaurants. (Take a right out of the hotel. Walk to 47th. Turn right. Lots of quaint, good restaurants down this street.) About 8 streets south of the tip end of Central Park.
Cleanliness: Overall, the hotel is relatively clean. It is important to note that it is beginning to show some wear and it is time for the hotel to do some "deep" cleaning to keep things nice. There is no exhaust fan in the bathroom and this is a real problem. Mildew and mold are beginning to show on the ceiling, in the floor corners and along the tub/floor. The deadbolt on our room was broken and the alarm clock didn't work (although we didn't use it anyway). I told the front desk person about it when we checked out so they could be repaired before the next check in and she wasn't over appreciative that I let her know about it. For NYC, the room itself was a pretty good size, smaller than some I have stayed in, but much larger than others. The bathroom was small, but that is not a big deal to me.
Breakfast: Typical Hampton. Cereal, waffles, yogurt, boiled eggs, canned fruit, some type of cooked egg item, oatmeal, etc. As good as any Hampton and included in the room rate. They were very nice to even offer it the morning we checked in! Coffee, tea, hot cocoa in the lobby all day.
Concierge: This was the most disappointing part of this hotel. We experienced two different concierges during our visit. Neither had the personalities to do this job well. When I asked one where we could get good Chinese, she said there really wasn't any. She proceeded to open what looked like a travel guide, picked out a couple and wrote them on a piece of paper. So I asked about good sushi. Again, she couldn't give us any suggestions. A couple of days later I asked the other concierge to recommend his favorite rooftop bar. His response was, "I don't have one. They are just overpriced drinks." It was an absolutely gorgeous night out and we really didn't care if the drinks were expensive. We wanted the experience. He named the one rooftop bar he said he had been to, but said it really wasn't that good. So disappointed in these two. We stayed in a Hilton Garden Inn in the city several years ago and we still frequent the bars and restaurants recommended by the concierge there. The manager at this hotel really needs to reevaluate these positions. My low rating for service is strictly due to the concierge service.
So stay here, it's not a bad hotel, but download yelp on your phone so you can find great restaurants and bars.

title_masked: Exceptional Hotel in the Valley of the Sun
text_masked: Stayed at the Embassy Suites Phoenix-Scottsdale from 24-26 Jul 12 and found it to be an exceptional hotel. The room was very clean and spacious and I especially liked the jack-and-jiill doors from the living area to the bathroom and sink sections. The breakfast buffet was outstanding and the view of the golf course from the dining room was cool too. The employees all had a "service with a smile" attitude. Am looking forward to my next stay here in August!
Newly remodeled and clean. Excellent value for the money (with my ATPE discount). Bed and pillows were comfortable. Lounge chair was o.k.

We got to the Westin Gaslamp after a long drive and I was disappointed to find out that the room was not ready at 7 PM. I did mention that to the agent, who, in turn, spoke to the supervisor and we quickly got a room on the 12th floor, with a nice view toward the Bay. The room proved to be noisy due to the AC, so I asked for it to be changed. The change was done seamlessly while we were out and about and was also upgraded to a larger corner room. The quick response from the staff was much appreciated - hiccups can happen, but it is the manner in which they are being resolved that matters.
The rooms are newly renovated and have a fresh feel, in perfect agreement with one's expectation for a Westin. The area is very good, within walking distance from Gaslamp District, Seaport Village, USS Midway, Little Italy. 
The only negative aspect worth mentioning is the parking rate - only valet is available, at $32 / night. Coming from Vegas, where parking is free everywhere, I found it excessive to pay close to $100 for parking for a week-end, roughly the same amount I spent on gas for the drive from Vegas to San Diego and back.

I spent four nights at the Elysee during a business trip. I loved the hotel. Great service, comfortable and elegant rooms, the staff was incredibly helpful. The location is excellent. The front side rooms can a bit noisy at night. The back was quieter. Yet, I live in the country and there only hear the hooting on the owls at night, so I may be a bit oversensitive to city noise.

this was the cleanest hotel i have ever seen, the carpet was so clean i walked around in white sox for 4 hours. when i got home i couldn't tell which pair.
i fell while taking the cart to the car. every one was very helpful.

I have stayed at the Doubletree near the airport several times and have always felt it was a top notch property with first class service. The breakfast buffet is always great, fresh, and has so much to offer. the entire staff at this hotel truly understands what great customer service is.

title_masked: Nice hotel let down by back room staff
text_masked: My husband and I booked this hotel through Agoda.com which was a huge problem and somewhat soured what would have been a very positive experience. The hotel had our booking on file but no record of our prepayment. This was only apparent when we came to check out and were presented with a bill of over 400 dollars. Their solution was to charge our card the full amount while they looked into it. We had a sleepless night in our next location worrying that we had been scammed by a false booking site. All they had to do was phone Agoda directly as the details were on the hotel voucher but they only did this when we emailed them the next day informing them that we had instructed our credit card company to investigate a possible fraud. Agoda informed them that we had prepaid and the hotel then said they would refund the amount charged to our card less the extra resort fee and taxes. We still have not received an invoice for a breakdown of this and it appears that we have been overcharged for this but can't be sure. The hotel is lovely, great location, staff are very helpful apart from one younger man on the front desk who was the opposite of friendly. In spite of these positives I would be hesitant to recommend this hotel because of how they dealt with our issue, we were very reasonable throughout but we should not have been forced to leave the hotel without a satisfactory resolution to the problem, being made to feel that they thought we were trying to get one over on them and the worry of a possible fraud on our credit card.
We were in San antonio .Staff were very excellent and courteous .Would recommend this place .People at the desk were very helpful.

This hotel is fine for travelers who have an early morning flight out. That's exactly who this hotel is made for. It is very out-dated with small rooms and the rates are very high. But you pay for convenience and the location can't be beat when you have a 7 am flight the next morning. Not up to usual Marriott standards, but will get the job done.

While my room was adequate, the hotel public spaces were quite dreary and worn. At least two of the computers on the main floor to which I was directed to print out my boarding pass were not connected to the printer next to them. If there were athletic facilities, I never found them. There were no materials in the room on hotel services and amenities. The location is not so hot either, away from restaurants.

title_masked: In Desperate Need of an Updating
text_masked:
First the Good: 
 The staff was excellent. Everyone was pleasant and accommodating. The hotel was clean in the sense of day-to-day cleaning.
The Mediocre:
 The breakfast was not bad, not excellent, just middle of the road for an ES. The evening reception was not as good. Besides the drinks, just pretzels or tortilla chips and dip and/or salsa.
The Bad:
 The rooms, including the furniture, are very tired and need to be renewed. I saw two rooms and both had the smell of 'old carpet' no amount of cleaning can get that out. The furniture and carpet had very old stains. The cushioning/stuffing on the furniture is shot- I could feel the wooden frame by just softly pressing on the upholstery. The wooden chairs at the table wobbled so much I expected to crash to the floor. The color scheme- coral and dark green- went out of style 10 years ago. 
The pool area was very nice and clean but the chemicals were too strong- the following morning our eyes were still bloodshot. This might have been an anomaly and hopefully it's no like that all the time. 
I have been a loyal Hilton Diamond member for over 10 years, but unfortunately I have to say there are better options in the Jacksonville area than this hotel, although a good remodeling might change my mind.

The hotel is in a great location and connected to lots of shopping--this helps if it's cold or raining outside. It's also a very short walk to Newberry St. The front desk check-in was good because I didn't have to wait in line but our room was not ready until 5pm. The valet guys are not as friendly or as efficient as they should be for a Westin. They valet parking was $47 with in-out privileges but it always took 15 for the car to come whether it was busy or not. The room is nothing special with smaller than average bathroom but it was very clean and housekeeping was pleasant when I asked for more shampoo. I would stay here again because of the location!

We had a great stay at the Barclay over a long weekend. I got a gooddeal on Priceline and check in was a breeze. We had requested a king sized bed and when we tried to check in early at noon, the front desk staff told us that a king would be available at 3:00pm or we could check into a queen room right away. At that point, we just wanted to check in and freshen up so we took the queen and were happy that they gave us the choice!
I thought the room was large for NYC! There was a decent sized bathroom, full closet, queen sized bed, desk with chair, arm chair, ottoman, and a large unit with drawers, a refrigerator, and a huge flat screen on top and a mini Keurig! I had read some complaints about the bathroom, but I thought it was nice. There was a long shelf above the sink, which gave me plenty of room for all of my stuff. The Keurig was great! I usually never bother with in-room coffee makers, but the Keurig was so convenient. We were always stocked with two regular and two decaf K-cups, to go cups with lids, and little boxes filled with creamers, sugar and sweet & low packets, and spoons. It's the little things that make me happy!!
Everyone at the hotel was friendly and helpful. The location was great, there was so much we could walk to and it was so easy to grab a cab out front when we needed it. It may not be the most modern hotel, but I liked the old New York style. The hotel shows its age a little, but I think that's pretty typical for a hotel built in the 1920s! I think they've done a good job of keeping it updated. I would definitely stay here again if the price was right.

stayed at Royalton in a business trip last October - very well located with good service and clean and neat room (I've stayed in the std room, which is the most basic and quite liked, in comparison with tinny rooms in another hotels).

We stayed for two nights in May 2012. I was thoroughly impressed with this hotel. The rooms were very nice and comfortable, the staff (from the front desk, concierge, waiters, etc) were all delightful to deal with. While it is not directly in the downtown area, the hotel will take you anywhere you want to go within 2 miles of the hotel (except the cruise ports). And the food was delicious, both in the restaurant and also when we ordered room service. I would definitely recommend it, and if I am ever back in Seattle I will definitely stay there again.

title_masked: A lovely porter deserve to work with a better hotel!!
text_masked:
On our USA trip in May 2012, Last day before back to uk we decided to back to NY again just for one night so we wanted to stop at somewhere is affordable and in a convenient area on the other side of town that we've never been. Cosmopolitan was what you pay and what you get. My leg cramped from an activity that we did in Sanfransico so I couldn't walk very well especially on the steps, so arriving at the hotel with their lift was broken (only one lift at the hotel) ! It was a night mare!! Everyone had to walk up and down by the fire exit but I clound't manage for the steps at all. They said to us if we wanted to come back in an hour it should be ok, so we went out for some lunch nearby. We came back and nothing was sorted. All the staffs at reception tried the best to swapped our room on 2nd floor but i still needed a lift. We did understand but after a few hour we still didn't get to our room and they were still waiting for a guy to fix the lift. Bearing in mind we were only staying one night, and we couldnt get to our room after a long flight, we expected the issue to be dealt with better - especially considering the room rate wasn't cheap. We asked for the manager and were very disappointed with how he dealt with it. Yes it wasn't his fault the lift was broken but his approach was lethargic. We were paying top dollar for a room we couldn't get access to. He would not try find us alternate accommodation and was unwilling to discount the rate we were paying for the inconvenience of paying for a room not accessible!! We had three very simple questions we asked the manager which he could not answer. 1) why hasn't a hotel of that size & room numbers only got one lift? 2) what if we had already got the lift to the room before it broke? We would be contained! (health & safety?) 3) what about disabled guests? 
The manager offered us a free breakfast or cocktails. We left the next morning without accepting either. The room itself was small and dated but location was right for our requirements. We would not return to this hotel and would look for alternatives in the same area. One positive was the extremely helpful concierge/porter. On top of carrying every guests bag up and down the extremely steep stairs whilst the lift was broken (several hours), he always remained cheerful, insightful and did everything which embodies good customer service. He stood in the torrential rain with us in the middle of the road for nearly 25 minutes patiently trying to get a cab to the airport for us. Most taxis said no as it was shift changeover time and they didn't want the long journey so close to clock off time. Without him we would have struggled to get a cab and would've got dangerously close to missing our flight home. If the manager had the same commitment to customer service, our experience would've been significantly more enjoyable.

title_masked: Beautiful Hotel, Lovely Pool, Great Service!
text_masked:
I stayed here for two nights with my husband and two children, ages 6 & 10. We stayed a Friday and Saturday night in a suite (490 sq ft) which was quite nice as we had a king sized bed and had privacy doors to shut between our bedroom and the living room, where the kids slept on the pull out sofa. 
Everything in our room was elegant, good quality and comfortable... the lobby and Georgian dining room were gorgeous, and everything else (the stairs, the hallways etc) all continued the trend. 
Location was perfect. Here's what I wanted to know before I went, and could not find information about, so here it is. The hotel is:
2 blocks from a grocery store
2 blocks from 2 drugstores
Exactly 4 blocks down (on 5th Ave) from the monorail ($2.50/adult, $1 kids) that takes you straight to the Seattle Center (Space Needle, Science Center etc) 
Exactly 5 blocks from the entrance of Pike Place Market (2 blocks over to Pike Street, and 3 blocks down Pike Street). It's an easy walk.
Basically, it's EXACTLY in the heart of the retail core, with tons of restaurants, and entertainment within blocks. Also there's a town car that will take you to where you need to go at no charge, we got a ride once, but it's so fast to walk everywhere we just did that most of the time.
A great place to try eating, is at the cheesecake factory on Pike & 7th... AMAZING food...
The breakfast buffet was ok (nice fresh berries, fresh juice, the rest was basic sausage, eggs, potatoes, cereal... we got it as a part of the stay-cation and it was very convenient to eat there in the morning, but if you have energy to go out in the morning, there's many places you can eat that offer great buffets that I feel offer more for the $25/plate per adult the Fairmont charges for this breakfast buffet. Frankly, for that price and the quality of the rest of the accommodations, I was expecting something a little more gourmet. My little girl ordered the teddy bear pancakes though and she really loved them... I'd go once to try it out, and enjoy the lovely dining room, but keep your eyes open for other breakfast options as you're going around.
We loved the pool, which was perfect for the kids to play, and the large crystal clear hot tub (more like a hot pool) where we spent a lot of time. The pool area was well appointed and elegant, with skylights and palm trees giving a tropical feeling. There were constantly people polishing and tidying, making everything perfect. The bathroom in the pool/ health club area was BEAUTIFUL... everything you could want!
The staff were super helpful and eager to make everything perfect, they really put energy into answering our questions, taking care of small requests and going the extra mile... when one of the staff on our floor (8th floor) noticed we were heading to the pool and our son didn't have a bathrobe, she personally went and got one his size and brought it to the pool for us. I think her name was something like Zalenka, she was from Croatia... Anyhow, it takes energy and caring to notice something like that, and care enough to do something about it. I was very impressed!
Sleep quality was so so... the beds were beautifully made up with nice sheets and feather bed, and were comfortable and beautiful. The problem we had (no idea if this is common to all the beds, or just ours... of just ours because we're "bigger" people...) every time one of us turned over, the bed shook back and forth (as it was on a metal frame on wheels) and woke the other person up. If you're a bigger person and taking a queen or king bed, try lying down and seeing if the bed shimmies when the other person turns over... if so, call housekeeping and ask them to fix it! Basically, next time we go, we're getting 2 queens instead of a king... :-)
Bottom line is, hotel is beautiful, we loved it, and will absolutely be back next time we're in Seattle. For quality, service and location in downtown Seatte, we were very happy with the Fairmont Olympic.

I was in Chicago on a business trip and decided to try the intercontinental this time.
It is centrally located within walking distance to some of the best restauants and bars in the area.
I would highly recommend staying here.

Location was good for the sights to be seen. Great location near the Natural History Museum.Near by the national mall and the Capitol....The hotel staff was absolutely amazing! They were so friendly and very helpful
Good breakfast included in the price....

The location was great in that it was close to downtown as well as the airport. We stayed here before we flew out and it was a quick drive in the morning. 
The place was well maintained and very nice looking. The staff was helpful. Based on the sunburns, the kids enjoyed the pool for a decent amount of time. I liked the lobby and a variety of things for guests to do there. I always like it when hotels make that extra effort.
The rooms had a DVD player (and I think I was told that there were some DVDs in the lobby), frig, etc...
The breakfast had a good variety and was a good continental breakfast.
I'd stay here again and I recommend.

Stayed here for a business meeting and found location perfect. Hotel is located in a perfect place near public market, with many restaurants, and shops to walk around. The front desk was friendly, and easy to check-in. There is valet for your car. The room was clean, except for the carpet which was slightly worn, but bed comfortable. Wifi available. Small refrigerator provided. Free paper(s). Coffee machine in room, but around the hotel is the best coffee shops, bread, cookies & other stuff that you can send you wife, or husband to fetch for you. Best part is there is a great gym that you can get a pass (Seattle Athletic Club) that has a pool, basketball, racket ball and excellent gym equipment. There is also a nice roof view area to watch the market and sunset. Several restaurants in the hotel property, but many more outside that are great. This is not a luxury hotel, but a good place to stay. I would recommend this place to anyone visiting in Seattle.

The rooms are big & comfortable, and clean. I heard no street noise. The fridge & microwave were nice to have available, & the service was very helpful. No, it's not a fancy place, but it was very close to MCRD, and it met my needs just fine. I look forward to staying there next time I'm in San Diego.

Apparently there has been a re-branding, refurbishment going on at this hotel for the past many, many months. Either it didn't make it to our room, or the refurbishment was super-shoddy. Soon after walking into our room we found that one of the A/C units did not turn on. I was going to call the front desk to have it fixed, but the phone jack had not yet been re-wired. Just an ugly hole in the wall and an unplugged phone on the desk. The staff was very helpful and replaced the unit within a half hour, but did not fix the phone.
The bedroom blackout curtains were not big enough for the window, leaving a six-inch gap between the closed panels. Forgot the traveling clothes pins. Doh!
There was an electrical outlet in the bathroom that had no face plate. 
The kitchen sink had not stopper.
The toaster stank the room up like burnt plastic.
It was a suite for for people, but only two chairs at the dining table.
The ice machine in the freezer did not produce ice.
There is no breakfast provided. No dining room. Nada.

I stayed here since it had a good rate, great location, and is a historic hotel. While a really nice staff greets you, the rooms leave a bit to be desired. They're fine, just not as clean as they could be, and a bit worn looking. The exhaust vent in the bathroom hadn't been cleaned in weeks...maybe months. It took me five seconds to wipe it off with a wash cloth when I was done with a shower. That's something the hotel staff should do. It's not bad, but not anywhere good enough to make me want to go back.

We chose the Sheraton Fisherman's Wharf because of it's location and the mostly positive reviews. Was a bit concerned after first arriving. We arrived at the hotel about 10:00 a.m. and proceeded to the front desk to ask if we could get early check-in (knowing it was highly unlikely) and were told nothing was available, which was fine. At this same time, per the suggestions on here, I asked if we could get a fourth floor room facing the inner courtyard when we finally did check in. I was told they could not give us one of those rooms because they were reserved for the Sheraton "Gold Club Members." Felt a bit second class after a comment like that and wasn't sure what the rest of the stay would bring, however, besides the size of the bathroom in our room, it was the only negative thing I have to say. Amazingly enough, I don't know if the person made a note on our reservation after asking or not, but we were given a fourth floor, inner courtyard room. The hotel is nicely decorated, the staff was very courteous and helpful, the breakfast food was very good (despite being a buffet) and the location was absolutely perfect. The room was good sized, except for the bathroom, which was really too small. The bed was extremely comfortable, the room was nicely appointed and despite some of the other reviews, we did not have any problems with the temperature in our room. If/when we return to the bay area for more fun, I would not hesitate to return to the Sheraton.

title_masked: Very good 3 1/2 star hotel across from Penn Sta. & Mad.Sq.Garden
text_masked:
We just spent 2 nights here, on the 4th floor; after a lot of bidding, bid $201 for a Manhattan 3 star and got the extra half as well. It's on the west side of 7th Ave. between 30th and 31st street.I can't say the room was large but it certainly was not "teeny tiny" as one reviewer claimed, it was moderately sized as was the bathroom (no tub, but a nice shower). we had an iron and ironing board, closet with hangars (no, not the chintzy theft-proof kind; I appreciated that) and a good coffee machine with all the fixings and supplies for the two of us. The bed was fine, the pillows large and there were extra smaller pillows. We had a desk, and bed tables on both sides. No ice machine, but call 0 and you'll have a bucket of ice at your door quickly enough. There's a lot of street noise, but (as we discovered after the first night) there is an extra set of buffer curtains you can lower which are thick and block out both noise and unwanted light. Penn Station and Madison Square Garden are right across the street. Everything worked well. The rooms have individual thermostats, There's a health spa on the 4th floor but we never had time to use it. The lobby has an info desk with free maps, etc. The staff were very nice and helpful. One small thing: when you summon an elevator and the elevator door opens, you better move quickly as they close again right away. I checked out of curiosity and found if I'd gotten the room through one of the travel sites it would have been $258. 
Oh, and if you walk up a bit and around the corner onto 32nd street, you can catch an M4 bus which will take you up to 100th street, then across to and up Broadway. AND there's a $1 pizza place right there. The hotel's wifi isn't cheap, but don't wory - there's a Starbucks right across the street, and theirs works perfectly.
We never did use the downstairs bar, which looked like a fun lively place, or the restaurant. But we were told hotel guests get 20% off in the restaurant and 10% off at Macys. We would definitely stay there again.

SO very disappointed in this hotel. I admit I am really picky, and probably read 50 reviews, everyone said they enjoyed the hotel and that the rooms were well appointed, ask for a higher floor for quiet, ask for an upgrade, and they will treat you right. It is my 50th birthday today and I am kicking myself that I am staying at this dump-I'd rate it a 2.5 hotel. 
Rudy, was polite enough, and did his best to upgrade us with a terrace room, nice albeit the room was not ready at the 3pm time-so 4:00pm and we head up to the room and the cleaning staff had just begun cleaning, so we waited while they finished. The power went out, so they could not finish vacuuming. 
The state of this room is horrible (2114), old, furniture chipped & nicked, woodwork/doors chipped and the whole room needs paint. The carpet is disgusting, I have stayed in Holiday Inns nicer then this hotel. The bed is not comfortable, unless you like really firm beds, no pillow top etc. Average sheets, no central air/heat it is a unit in the room. 
The room is noisy, even on the 21st floor!!! You can hear your neighbors next door & above you.
When I called down to complain the front desk lady said I could upgrade to a "premier" room for 50$ more, I went and looked at it and it was decorated nicer, newer and more stylish, but the bed is the same. For a $100 more I could upgrade to a larger premier room, no thanks.
So very disappointed, I hope I can switch hotel tomorrow to the Hotel Intercontinental. Would never ever come back to this hotel. Stay at the Ritz or Setai. Bummer for my 50th!

This is a nice hotel, but it's more suited to families. As a business traveller I wanted to be close to the airport for an early morning departure and I expected a typical airport business hotel. The hotel is more of a resort and teaming with young kids. I changed rooms a few times as the road noise (not the airport) was very noisy. In the end I just put up with it.
The front desk manager was impatient & arrogant - next time I'll stay at the Hilton,Marina.

I have been staying at this place on an off for about two years when i was stationed at Ft Sam Houston. I stayed there on Jan 5th 2011 years later because i was familiar with the place. Bad move, I forgot my watch there and called from the airport and they confirmed they had found it. The manager asked me for my address and told me that they would ship it to my address but i would have to pay the shipping on arrival. It has been 10 months and no watch. When i call the manager alters his voice and says "the manager is not in today". However, i know his voice and am surprised at the low level he would go to keep my watch. Even if you stayed there for two months as i did and put money in their pocket these people have no sense of customer service and professionalism. There are much better hotels with comparable prices in the area; Motel 6. Their price is usually five dollars more but it is worth it; they are professional and have redone their rooms which are usually clean and don't smell like like the cab of an 18 wheeler. No offense to truckers. I would never stay there again even if it is very convenient for me.

title_masked: Lovely room and very attentive staff
text_masked: We stayed at the Hilton Garden Inn at 790 Eighth Avenue in NY to see Porgy and Bess. It was only a few blocks from the theatre. The first thing we noticed when we walked in is that there were all kinds of people offering to help. We used our HIlton Honors points to stay here. My husband called ahead and asked if we could have our room by 1:30 (we took a bus to NYC) because I have severall serious health problems and couldn't walk around the city all that time waiting until 3 or 4. They were very accomodating and our room was ready by 1:22. They got an A plus for that. Our room was spacious which surprised me. They have a concierge to help people on vacation. I was very impressed with everyone at the front desk. The place was extremely clean and very nicely appointed. Couldn't say enough nice things about it.

title_masked: HILTON REVIEW BY J. J. LACEY, JR./ LITTLE ROCK, AR
text_masked: As indicated by the rating above, we gave this hotel a rating that is very good. Being a retired school adminisrator from the south, my greatest drawback is that the daily room rate is somewhat expensive, but what is not in NYC. All of the staff encountered were knowledgeable, courtesy, and provided service with a smile. In particlular, I would liike to commend front-desk attendant Martha V. She was all that I just mentioned for the staff overall and then some. Hire more Marthas...

I sent in a review in May and the rating is not showing up properly for this hotel . The rating should have been excellent and only showed as a 1 vs a 5. 
Please correct this error on my review and repost. Thanks Dale Nelson

title_masked: Has everything you need but no bells and whistles
text_masked: Days Inn San An is a clean and spacious hotel. The hotel room we had was a one bedroom suite with a spacious living area and a separate bedroom. there is a small fridge and microwave and limited cable with two flatscreen TVs, one in the living room and the other in the bedroom. The continental and complementary breakfast is huge and delicious. I only wish they had soy milk, but no matter. It has cold cereals, hot scrambled eggs breakfast potatoes sausage and bacon, texas shaped waffles (so cute), yogurt, donuts, toast, peanut butter, jelly, honey, tea, and coffee. You also get two basic drinks during dinner time INCLUDED wtih your stay. Very basic hotel rooms, a bit worn but honestly who stays in their hotel room when visiting San An? If you ARE looking to stay in your room to relax find someplace nicer, but if you are here to enjoy San An Days Inn has everything you need.

I stayed in the Seaport Boston for a local trade exhibition - had a corner room with a view back over the conference and exhibition center, no view of the harbor which would be preferable.
This is a hotel that gets many things right - clean, comfortable, quiet. The room was of a reasonable size, the desk was adequate with a good number of power sockets, there is a Keurig coffee maker, room safe, free wi-fi. Bed is comfortable. Water provided was $2 for a small bottle and $4 for a slightly larger 'branded' bottle. The air-conditioning thermostat seemed somewhat unreliable. Breakfast is adequate with a buffet or a-la-carte choices. But it is not luxury, the entrance, foyer, facilities, style, the colors, quality of furniture and fittings were all pleasant but not striking, the area is ok, overall it was good as a business hotel. So no complaints but the price seemed at the high end for what you get. 
One thing that I hadn't seen before for a US hotel is the policy that tips are included, something they remind you of at check-in and every time you settle a check. It doesn't mean they are included in the prices, it means they add them to the check and there does not appear to be any discretionary aspect to this. 
As for the area from what I could see there was very little in the immediate vicinity. The hotel is close to the conference and exhibition center. There is a Morton's steak house across the road and the Legal Seafood restaurant a short walk away as well as a few other bars and restaurants. Otherwise the sites and activity is a longer walk or taxi ride away. 
Overall I liked staying here and it definitely met the needs of my visit which was business. If I was a tourist I would probably choose a different location.

title_masked: Great place to get the New York experience!
text_masked:
My daughter and I stayed here July 1-8. Though it was my third trip to NYC, it was my daughter's first. I wanted her to get the full experience, and not just the touristy places. I had looked all over the city for a decent place to stay, with two beds and a private bathroom, that wasn't going to break the bank. The MAve met all my demands. I lucked out on the rates, as they must have had a sale back when I looked in January. As soon as I saw the rates, I booked. Of course, if Trip Advisor had said it was a dive, I wouldn't have booked no matter how cheap it was. But everyone on here raved about it, and I can see why.
We had a Madison double, on the 11th floor. Although the room was fairly small, it was plenty big enough for the two of us, and it had everything we needed. We unpacked right away, and either hung our clothes or put them in the really large drawers, and then we could tuck our suitcases away to make more room. I really liked that they had a small safe, at no extra charge, and a laptop desk, and an ipod dock, and my daughter loved that they had FREE WIFI. The beds were very comfortable, and each had two comfortable pillows. We slept well every night. There was very little noise, as our room was high up and faced 27th street. Not a great view, but we weren't there for the view. 
The shower was good, with good pressure. Even though it was not a full door on the shower, we never had a problem with the floor getting wet. The shower head points straight down, so I'm not sure how you would get the floor flooded, unless the drain was blocked. 
We always felt safe at the hotel. The door does not always latch automatically, but the housekeeper knocked on our door on our first day and told us that, so we made sure that it was closed properly after that. When we would go outside for a cigarette, the front desk staff always greeted us, and the doorman was always there to open the door for us. Whenever we had a question for the staff, it was always answered politely and promptly. Other times, we would just chat with them, and they were always friendly. We were in our room once when the housekeeper was cleaning it, and she was always very friendly as well. Absolutely wonderful staff.
The location was incredible. Two blocks to the #6 subway, and three blocks to the N & R. We bought our Metro passes the first day, and definitely got our moneys worth. Also around the corner was Cafe 28, which is open all night and sells everything you might need. They also had hot buffet, and cooked to order sandwiches, and hot coffee. Also close by was a MacDonalds, Taco Bell, Dunkin Donuts, and a Duane Reade, and several banks if you needed those. When I was there previously, I stayed in midtown, closer to Central Park. This was way, way better for a location. Although there were not that many touristy things close by, there were more restaurants, more convenience stores, etc. It was more like the real New York, instead of the tourist New York. No matter the time of day, it was always busy around there, but with real New Yorkers, as opposed to tourists. We were also able to walk quite a bit. Union Square was only 14 blocks, and on the walk up 5th avenue was a lot of shopping. In the other direction, we were 6 blocks from the Empire State building and all the souvenir stores. 
I don't see myself going back to NYC any time in the near future, as I live so far from it, but to all of you reading this review, I would very definitely reccomend The MAve as your hotel. It has everything you need, with great location, great rates, and a wonderful staff. Oh, and check their website before you go to Expedia, etc, as that's where I found this incredible rate.
Have a great trip to this amazing city!

title_masked: Great Service/Excellent comfort- Poor ADA accomodations
text_masked: The service, comfort, and cleanliness was great, however, if you're traveling in a wheelchair I wouldn't recommend this hotel. The disabled parking and parking in general was very limited. The covered drop-off area doors were not wc accessible. I had to push my grandma outside and up a steep incline to a door that had to be held open. The ADA room was rather small and there wasn't a grab-bar in front of the sink. Othersise, it was alright. The beautiful decor, cleanliness, comfort of the bedding, and friendlieness of the staff made up for the problems, though, I wouldn't take my grandma their again due to the failings of accomodating someone in a WC. If I was going with my husband, I would stay again.

We stayed here for one night. It is in a great location and within walking distance to all the monuments and museums. The room was perfect, clean, and nice. The pool was great for the kids to swim in and the night we were there, there were a lot of people using it. There is a fitness center there as well, but we didn't utilize it. We didn't eat in the hotel, but headed out to an Irish bar which was very good. We would definitely stay here when we come back.

Losing light, power, telephone, then water during Hurricane Sandy meant this hotel's limited attractions faded fast. Its advantage is its location but with the elevators down other than the service elevator at the back of the hotel, it was no place to stay during the storm. So I left early but that didn't stop the hotel claiming for it all on my credit card. Not your fault there was a storm, St. Giles, but I think not nice to charge when nothing was operational.

It is rare when the staff at a hotel makes the experience but it did on a recent stay at the JW Marriott. EVERYONE I encountered was accommodating, pleasant and went out of their way to make sure that we were satisfied. Desk staff, bar tenders, catering staff, bellmen. I stay in a lot of hotels and can say that this really made the stay. Food was great, room was great, etc. but the real item that you recall is the quality of the staff. I guess the fact it stands out so is that it is not so commonly found these days in such a consistent manner.

I was at this hotel for business meetings. Everything was wonderful and the staff went above and beyond. The sleeping room was large and very clean. I had a balcony as well so it was nice to just sit outside and enjoy the weather. Would recommend this hotel to anyone.

This is a new hotel and the staff are really nice. Booked a 2 night stay online but wasn't aware of the extra $25 per night incidental charges until returning home and checked bank acct. They really need to tell customers this upon booking and again at check in. Very irresponsible for a hotel like this. Our bank acct. was on the verge of overdraft because of these unknown charges. Otherwise would stay here again. 2 King size beds and very large rooms. Pool was very cool but hottub was nice. Breakfast was great.

I will start with the good. The location at Water Tower Place is very good--especially if you want to spend time with daughters at American Girl. The service is very good as well. The staff was attentive and friendly as you would expect at a Ritz Carlton. Now the not so good. A recent Tripadvisor review stated the hotel had been "renovated". I have no idea what that person is talking about. No part of the hotel looked recently renovated to me. Yes, it was my first stay here, so I don't know what it used to look like. My guess is parts of the hotel were renovated about 10 years ago. My opinion is this hotel shows significant wear and is a little tired. Scuff marks, worn carpet, etc are visible. The bathroom in our suite was terrible-- my guess is the shower is at least 20 years old. Our cordless phone in the suite was broken--not a huge deal but in a hotel with standards (and prices) as high as this one it was an annoyance. Again, the staff was great, but in a city with a lot of GREAT hotels, this one is good, but not great. One last point, this is the only Ritz I am aware of that is not part of Marriott.

When I spend $700 a night for a room, I expect more quality. The rooms are nice -- contemporary and pleasing to the eye -- but upon closer inspection, cheap. Really? Plastic bathroom walls and a plastic sliding door to the bathroom? The furniture felt very IKEA-ish -- nice lines and modern, but cheap. And the lighting. OMG, don't get me started. I couldn't see a darn thing -- in the lobby, on the elevators, in my room. I'm not that old, but do require more than a 40 watt bulb once in a while. I felt like I was in a dream the whole time I was there -- not in a fantasy dream, but in a fog. And the fogged mirror behind the bed didn't help as it only made me feel more blind! 
Location is great for theater goers, but I won't stay in Times Square again -- way too much noise and way too many crowds. The staff was good -- did their best to get two rooms near each other (even though we made it very specifically clear that's what we wanted when we made the reservations) which required one to get upgraded to a corner room which they didn't charge us for. Amenities are okay -- bar was hopping Saturday night and dinner at the Blue Fin was okay (I wrote a separate Open Table review on that). Very touristy obviously.

title_masked: Very nice hotel, will stay again
text_masked: Have to come to Houston monthly for medical reasons and this time tried this hotel. Amenities in the room were awesome. Loved the easy access to electrical plug below beside light for charging cell phones. Bathroom was spacious and tub area was real nice. Love the balcony that opened up. I read this was a non smoking hotel and it even mentions it in the booklet in the room and a fine for smoking, however when we went to use the ice bucket the top of it wreaked of cigarette smoke. I do not smoke and have a lung condition so that smokey smell was not good. The a/c was hard to regulate and I got cold and had to find and extra blanket because thermostat wouldnt change. Bathroom floor looked like it didnt get mopped. Something red like spot on floor, I took towel and wiped it down.

title_masked: Modern, well run hotel, good location
text_masked:
rooms are on the smaller size, although my room had two double size beds, all very clean and modern, very quiet, I was near the top floor, great bathroom products, staff very friendly and helpful, breakfast was average, not much choice and nothing seemed very healthy.
I was happy you could open the windows a small way to let in some fresh air.
I received all benifits and was recognised as a Diamond member of the Hilton Hotel programme.
Good value if you stay outside peak periods (i.e New Year Eve).

title_masked: Rooms are small, noise, dirty carpet and run down furniture. Not worth it.
text_masked: When I arrived at the paramount I was not sure if they were remodeling or not, it is a little confusing. I was staying for a week in NY and got stuck in this hotel. Rigth on time square, I stayed on the last floor and even there the noise was a lot. When I opened my room what a surprise, the room is so small, the furniture is old, the chair was peeling, the bathroom is even smaller and there is no water pressure. The carpet of the room was dirty and old, the blanket was dirty as well, there were spots on my bed sheets. There are better hotels in the city for the same price as the Paramount. The restaurant waiter was very rude, when I ordered a Salmon with the sauce on the side he acted like I was asking for something so hard and gave me a hard time actually arguing with me. Do not waste your money, the hotel is really run down.

With in walking distance from penn station. I was little worried about walking to there with my two kids but it went fine, just a 5 to 7 min walk with our luggage for a 7 day cruise out of ny. We came early to go to my kids first yankee game and then thier 1st cruise. Pricing was good and the room was very clean but small compared to most hotels ( but i guess all hotels are small in ny city). Did have to call maintenance up because toliet would not flush and they came very quickly and fixed the problem. Breakfast in am was very good, alot to choose from and all included with room price which is always good. We stayed two nights and then when we checked out they helped us get a taxi to to cruise port.

title_masked: Average standards but poor for Holiday Inn Express
text_masked:
We regularly stay at Holiday Inn Express motels because they achieve a good standard.
This however was not the case with the Holiday Inn Express San Antonio North.
The rooms present fairly well although it is clear here that cleanliness and maintenance are not always the priority. The mirrored door of the main wardrobe needed repair, which had been attempted but it was an extremely poor effort and the door continued to sway open, unable to secure it in a closed position.
On arrival the room appeared clean and bed linen was fresh. We stayed 3 nights and conditions continued to deteriorate during the stay. Beds were not made and the room was not cleaned to the original standard. We also had to follow up with cleaning staff to request replenishment of standard in room refreshments.
Breakfast supplies kept running out to the frustration of guests and it was really sad to see that new staff were being interviewed in the dining room whilst guests were having breakfast.
The walls and doors do not prevent noise intrusion and plumbing is very poorly maintained.
The elevator is very noisy so request a room as far as possible away from the elevator.

My wife, Daughter and I stayed at the Ameritania during a weekend trip to New York City. We needed special accomodations for our daughter and they were promptly answered by the Manager, Erin Becker. She checked in with us the next day to assure everything was to our liking. Every individual we had contact with at the Ameritania was gracious and friendly, Mourad, the doorman even knew us by name. I would highly reccomend this Hotel to anyone traveling to the Time Square/Broadway area. Great location, Great Service, all around a delightful experience!
Angelica, was extreamly helpful in taking care of us with a last minute stay-over.

The staff was outstanding and sharp as a tack. The room was awe inspiring . Overall it left me feeling special. the concierge, waiters,bell staff and front desk staff all were top notch. I highly recommend this hotel

title_masked: Always a great stay at Springhill Suites
text_masked: We have stayed in 3 different Springhill Suites in the last month and all three were very nice. Most of them have recently been remodeled and everything is crisp and clean. The decor is beautiful. We stayed at the Springhill Suites in Austin earlier this month and everything was just as pictured. Very nice room with microwave, mini fridge, and wet bar. Nice to have a sink other than the bathroom sink! The colors and decor are contemporary. They also had a very nice patio area with lounge chairs and table that was shaded by many trees most of the afternoon which was very nice. The 24-hr Market is also very convenient. We were able to purchase a bottle of wine at 11:00 p.m. along with some snacks. The staff is very courteous. The breakfast was okay. One morning we had biscuits with ham and egg along with some pastries. Very good. We did not have any problems finding the hotel, but the turn into the hotel is IMMEDIATELY off the exit and could easily be missed..I definitely recommend this hotel.

Hotel is located in Del Mar; beautiful city on the beach to start with. Checked into the hotel on a weekend. The smiles from the front desk agents made my heart feel like I was home; along with it came the warm chocolate cookies and the speedy check in; took the front desk agent less than 2 minutes and we had the keys in out hands.
Our room had the pool view and my family was so happy. Went down to the pool with the kids and It was heated one. They even had towels at the pool. We had dinner at the hotel restaurant. The staff were extremely friendly and the manager was a very kind young man. The food tasted delicious and it sounded music to my ears for myself and my family. 
As we were checking out I was sad to leave but I made a promise to myself if I do come back this is the place that I would be staying at. THIS PLACE IS HEAVEN ON EARTH.

Ok, so the Japanese Anime theme is attractive, the rooms were neat and clean, and the staff were friendly. But I felt like something was missing...maybe quality? Maybe umph? As the event planner for a work conference in San Francisco, I had the backdoor experience of customer service. They anticipated us and I felt that a lot of the pleasantries were based on this. Based on the average price, I don't think the hotel meets its value. 
I felt the furniture in the room were cheap...Ikea-inspired. The bathrooms were very dark (I had a hard time taking a shower in the dull/dim lighting) and the layout was not ideal. I felt the common spaces looked worn down and they could be a little more creative-- after all, this is an "Anime-themed" hotel. The restaurant also fell flat. It felt dark, dingy and the food was not note-worthy. I didn't feel inspired to eat "fresh" sushi there...I was disappointed to learn that although located in the same building, they do not offer room service. Bah!
Would my son like this room? Certainly; well, maybe at first. Eventually you find that the only "cool" thing about the theme is the murals and you can't do much with a wall (not to mention, I wasn't really impressed with the wall art in my room). I think if they pumped up the "fun" more with some futuristic gadgets or 3D toys / Anime characters, this could be more interesting. To me, it mostly felt like a place to crash and nothing more. 
Outside, there isn't much happening (although you're in the center of Japantown) and it feels a little isolated but a block away, you can start to find some action and restaurant options. 
Technical:
There is an iPod dock/alarm clock (I appreciated that). I believe Wifi is complimentary...and I had a strong signal throughout my stay. The television had a few channel options, which was good. 
Overall, it wasn't bad or great. I don't think I'd spend my own money to stay here...I would be more interested in seeing what else San Francisco has to offer.

We stayed here for my husband's BMT graduation. We booked two rooms for the family. The first night, the toilet in the king room would not stop running, called management and they sent up two people to sorta stare at it/attempt to fix it (this is probably around 10pm). They couldn't fix it, so they moved me to a queen room. It was fixed the next night and they refunded me 11 dollars for the room difference. Breakfast good each morning, since the family was getting up at 4 each morning to get onto the base for ceremonies and such.

Relative to other Crowne Plazas worldwide, this is very similar. Staying 4 days on the 33rd exec floor it was a nice view for sure, and the location is excellent for walking to major tourist attractions. Room service is expensive as expected, but the food is of a higher than usual standard. I did not have a vehicle so cannot comment on parking.
Room for improvement: Definitely something up with the HVAC system. A 2 degree change would cause it to alternate between AC/Heating which led to some loud night time ventilation. I ended up switching it off so I could sleep. The lifts seem to be programmed obscurely and there can be long waits for lifts at peak times.

title_masked: A good pit-stop before international travel
text_masked: We had about 1.5 days to spend in the LA-area before our long trip overseas...so we decided to check out Universal Studios Hollywood. The hotel parking was reasonable (we self-parked, very easy). The property is older but well-maintained. Staff is friendly. Got a free-upgrade to executive level since I'm a HHonors member. We had an alcove room which was very well appointed and clean. Great views. Great shuttle service to Universal Studios/CityWalk OR just walk - only takes a few minutes. Breakfast was outsanding and was discounted for HHonors members. Overall great stay and worth the short drive from LAX.

I travelled here for work so I may have a little bias because I didn't pay for my room. However, my stay at this resort was excellent. I had a large room on the 4th floor on the main tower. The room was clean and while it does not feel like a ''modern'' hotel, it had all the amenities that I needed. The gym is large and had a lot of equipment. It was not included in the price however (5$ per day). The whole resort seemed well maintained. 
Service was great in all respect, nothing to complain about here.
I would agree that the value is certainly not the best, especially if you are not looking for a ''resort'' experience. However, since I had a flawless stay, it would be hard for me to give a bad review.

This hotel is really quite bad. Undoubtedly one of the worst ive stayed at. I was put on level 1, it potentially may be much better on higher levels as I've heard they may have been more recently renovated. The room was very small, which I can dealwith, but everything felt very worn and drab. The bed was not great and the hallway had a bad smell. It really felt quite creepy in the hallway and the community room felt like it had sat there suspended in time from the 60s. The positives -it is a budget hotel, it is in safe and quite location and close to central park and The people working in the hotel were all lovely and the clientele seemed decent even though you felt like you could be in the middle of the Bronx in the 80s.

We used a Groupon and were pleasantly surprised...one block from Inner Harbor. We had a one bedroom suite which was nice because my husband goes to bed earlier than me and I had a small living room area that I could read and watch tv without disturbing him...Employees were pleasant and breakfast that was included was more than we ever expected...it also had a microwave, coffee pot, small fridge and small sink....

I had a last minute overnight in the city, and somehow stumbled upon The Library Hotel. I absolutely loved it and would not hesitate to stay there again. The location is great - only a few blocks from Grand Central Station, Times Square, etc. During the check in process, I felt very well taken care of - the two people behind the desk were very pleasant and helpful, as was the doorman. The lobby was really neat (looked like a library). I was happy to hear about all of the complimentary amenities, as it seems everywhere you go in the city, things cost a ton. There were free passes to a local sports club, free complimentary breakfast (which was GOOD). The breakfast included coffees, teas, pastries, cereals, bagels, fresh fruit, eggs, etc. Free daily newspapers (several different publications). They offered free wine and cheese (and other snacks) from 5-8 pm each night. There were complimentary drinks and snacks in the library room all day. They had great free toiletries and free wireless service. They also had free DVD rentals, including the AFI top 100 films. I was wishing I could stay longer! They also had nice comfy beds, bathrobes, slippers and umbrellas in the room. My room happened to be rather small, but it was completely cozy, perfectly adequate for my needs with a really nice view of Madison Avenue. The fixtures were higher end - great bathroom. There was an assortment of snacks and alcohol in the room that you had to pay for, but there were free water bottles. I didn't think it was noisier than any other room I've stayed in in NYC. I believe the price was competitive and fair, and with all of the free amenities, I actually felt like I was getting a great deal! I would without a doubt stay here again, in fact - I can't wait to come back.

We stayed at the Hotel Monaco Chicago for five nights and loved it. We had stayed at a Kimpton Hotel in San Diego previously and this one was even better.
The room was great, with an extremely comfortable King size bed and antique style furniture. We asked for a quiet room on a pet-free floor and that was exactly what we got.
The hotel is in an ideal location, being walking distance from many tourist destinations and from a choice of restaurants. Chicago is both an interesting and amazing city to visit.
The staff were both welcoming and very helpful. I would not hesitate to recommend this hotel to anyone.

My trip to NY was for a short 'respite' break from caring and I was by myself for a while until my son joined me. The staff were so friendly, helpful and welcoming that I felt safe and comfortable being by myself. Ihave to admit that I chose this hotel not only for its excellent reviews but for one of the staff members - Charlie the cat who was delightful and very friendly once he realised he was in the presence of a mad cat woman! He knew which room I was in and would wait patiently outside until invited in.
This is the best place I have ever stayed in - the staff, the ambience, the comfortable suite; wonderful breakfasts and coffee; the yummy home-baked cakes and bread and a cat. I could have stayed forever!
Jay managed to book us some excellent seats for 'Jersey Boys' which was fantastic - exhilarating and fun.
At the end of each day, exhausted from sightseeing and art galleries, it was heaven to climb those stairs up to collapse on my extremely comfortable bed.
I would love to return to NY - I just hope there will be a vacancy at this charming hotel........

We stayed at this property from august 8 through 12, 2012. We chose it because we are members of the hilton rewards program, because it was centrally located, and because it a short cab ride to the NYC cruise ship terminal, where we went after our stay was complete.
We had two rooms: one a room with a king bed and one a room with two queens for our kids. Rooms were located on the 29th floor facing south with a view of the garment district and the empire state building. (A cityscape just like on TV!) Though I didn't ask for it, hotel staff took the trouble to make sure they were adjoining. I also appreciated that staff called up right after checkin to make sure accommodations were satisfactory. 
I am glad to say that our experience was very positive - from the univerally friendly attitude of all staff to the central location relative to the NYC attractions we wanted to visit, to the air conditioning that functioned well (very important as the city sweltered). Also as all the rooms are well above the 15th floor, very little of the urban noise filters through. 
Being in Time Square, there is every imaginable kind of restaurant and service nearby including an Applebees accessible from the hotel entrance where we ate breakfast nearly every day. Because of all the local dining options, restaurant facilities at the hotel itself seemed quite limited and we never used them. 
It's not cheap but that's par for the course in mid town NY. I knew that going in. Rates seem typical of other Time Square hotels. Anyone wanting cheap accommodations while visiting New York should consider New Jersey or Brooklyn. 
One minor quibble - didn't care much for what was to my mind a hard sell given to hotel guests for a hilton time share project on w 57th st under the initial guise of a "welcome package".

title_masked: My home away from home in SF
text_masked: I have stayed here 3 times on visits to San Francisco and thoroughly recommend it. Central (cable care runs past the door and adjacent to Union Square), friendly staff (say hello to Tom, the concierge). Very retro and you're not going to get a view, so don't expect your standard hotel room, but has all the modern facilties you need, including great free wifi. Happy hour wine tastings in the lobby and many people take their wine to the comfortable public lounge on each floor. Also make sure you visit Johnny Foley's bar a couple of blocks away for a couple of jars and a great feed (especially if your homesick for meals familiar to Brits and Aussies).

title_masked: Good modern property, Executive suite is large
text_masked:
stayed for business:
Pros:
- location, near times square, but fairly quiet rooms, (stayed on 16th)
- modern fixtures, flat screens, furniture, windows, etc
- good bathroom amenities and service offerings, free shoe shines, bathroom kits, razor, toothpaste etc
- hardwood in the entrance
- nice lounge
- free wine hour
- free wifi & raid the mini bar ($15) for members, wifi signal very strong
- pretty large room, executive suite, separate bedroom, living, entrance, like an apartment
- decent sized bathroom, modern finishes
- solid bed and pillows
- room service, food is decent, chicken sandwich/burger and pizza pretty good.
- good desk to work from
- clean, well serviced
Cons:
- black carpet (odd)
- couch is uncomfortable... *too* modern, basically no cushions (its really bad)
- asked to stay til 2pm, got the "we'll have to charge you" (i suppose since i paid for a suite i thought id get some leeway, perhaps it was a bad day... they didn't exactly elaborate why which didnt help the situation)
- tea/coffee is only downstairs in the AM, but i suppose you could request a coffeemaker (per signage)
- construction was going on, BUT it didnt bother me, sound didnt seem too loud.

title_masked: Decent hotel, not so good location
text_masked:
We recently stayed here for three nights, the rooms were clean and a good size, ours was on the upper floor facing out to the pool, it did get a little noisy at night but nothing too bad.
The staff were in the most part helpful, particularly Mike and Mariah. The only downside to the hotel is the area that it is in, lots of homeless people etc, however if you are sensible and get taxis back to the hotel after dark you should be fine. There is also parking available (off street) and a pool and a light breakfast each morning (muffins and hot drinks). It was pretty easy to walk to places like Union Square or the BART stop wasn't far (we managed to walk to the BART with suitcases in tow!)
If you are looking for a cheap and cheerful hotel in San Fran you should definitely consider this one!
new/nice property. great service, easily navigable, close to the stadium.

Son and I spent two nights here to start the year 2012. I was pleasantly surprised. The room was nice with two very comfy beds (the only more comfortable bed on our vacation trip was at Disney). The location (near the 101 and 405 freeways) was perfect for our needs.
The parking was the only problem. Unfortunately, we returned to the hotel after 9 p.m. on the evening of January 1 and the lot was completely full. Even the compact spots were over-stuffed with vehicles too large for them.

My one night stay at this hotel was very nice. I was on the 15th floor with incrediable views of downtown.
The room was very nice. It is large by city hotel standards. It has a large wardrobe closet in the hallway, a desk & 2 chairs, a coffee bar w/Nepresso (no charge). 
The bathroom was very nice. It had a soaking tub, seperate shower w/ a regular shower head & a rain head. 
The TV in the vanity mirror was nice, but a "low signal" kept it from being anything more than frustrating. Probably operator error, but come on it's a TV how hard should it be to use?
I ordered room service for dinner and breakfast. I must say that I was not impressed. Bummer, because usually Four Season meals are good anywhere, room, pool, restaurant. The service portion was absolutely terrific; which almost made up for the bad food. 
The following is just my pet peeve: In a downtown hotel why are they charging for wireless internet? If we were on an island or somewhere remote it would be much easier to take. 
Thank you for reading.

title_masked: Great time at a great property
text_masked: Beautiful grounds, friendly and helpful staff, good food, two hot tubs & pools, very clean rooms and great price, all adds up to a very good choice for vacationing in San Diego. You will probably need a car, it's not near downtown SD. Free shuttle to Sea World. Sure they have massage but we never had time for that, but we enjoyed the hot tubs. We had a great stay and recommend highly.

title_masked: Is it possible to give a lower rating than one?
text_masked:
The worst. Aside from problems I can live with (the room was as long as the bed and about 2 feet wider), here are the main complaints:
-Internet was barely functional.
-No elevator and I was on the 5th floor. Glad I only had a backpack!
-Both toilets on my floor were clogged. I didn't want to write the word "feces" in my review, but I feel like I have to.
-The bathrooms smelled like mold.
Thought I'd save a buck - never again!

title_masked: Ultimate convenience but could use an upgrade
text_masked:
To be fair, I'm an avid traveler for work and for non-work trips. In 2011, I spent nearly 6 months living in the Four Points in Soho, which is a newer hotel than this one in Chelsea. While the format and layout of this hotel is nearly identical to the one further downtown, I think that this hotel would benefit from some upgrades.
The best thing about this hotel is the location. I found that I could easily walk to most of destinations from here, and for those farther reaches, I could easily walk to the subway of choice. Easy to find, easy to access, and across the street from Whole Foods. Fantastic!
The carpets in the hotel should probably be replaced, and the room bathrooms could use some improvements. (They still have that white-tile-institutional feel.) The rooms are comfortable, though, with enough space to unpack and not feel squished (particularly in NYC where all hotel rooms are relatively small). Free wifi was a great perk. The mirrors in my room were cracked to bits and taped together to keep their shape -- probably should have been replaced long ago, and not a great impression.
Housekeeping was sporadic - for some reason, I had to remind them to clean my room. The following day they were knocking on the door at 10am, which is even before checkout time! From what I understand, some of the staff from the Soho hotel (who are AWESOME) are helping to revamp this one in Chelsea, so hopefully there will be overall improvements soon.

title_masked: Too bad it's the only Marriott property downtown
text_masked:
I've stayed at this hotel before but this was the first time in a couple of years. It is NOT again well.
Both the rooms and the common areas need some freshening up and TLC. Nothing big was wrong, but lots of little things. Drippy shower that wouldn't stop, badly bruised fruit, stale baked goods and cold, pre-formed eggs at breakfast, soft mattress, noisy elevators that we could hear in our room well down the hall, carpet and drapes starting to wear.
Also, even though this is a "suites" hotel, it's really not functional as one. The sink in essentially in the room, so that it's impossible to get ready in the morning but let another person sleep. It's made worse by a large mirror that reflects light right back at the bed.
Prefunctory front desk "service".
It wasn't a disaster, but I'm sure we can do better in Downtown Phoenix and won't be back.

The hotel staff and facility were great! Breakfast was what you would expect, fresh fruit, great waffles, nuts, meat, juices, biscuits & gravy, and much more. Our room was on the top floor north side with a great view of the city to the north. The room was extremely comfortable, well laid out. CVS is right next door, close enough that when it's raining hard you don't get too wet, even it you choose not to use one of the hotel's umbrellas. Elmer was great helping us with our car and luggage when we arrived. Would love to stay here again!

The first thing to mention is that the hotel looks NOTHING like it does on the website. They have obviously employed a photographer with a really wide angle lens and slipped him a few extra dollars. Its probably a good time to mention that the owners ought to look up the word 'boutique'. In fact it is better described as a hostel.. So let us continue with our review of Hostel Fusion..
Next we were given our room and found that not only was it dark and dingy but it overlooked a tiny courtyard making the room unbearably hot. Here's we we discovered there was no air conditioning..!! On the first night we were struggling to breathe in the tiny room by 3am so I went down to see about the possibility of borrowing a fan, oxygen mask or changing rooms. 
Next problem.. The Staff...!! Not only were they slow and incompetent but they gave the impression that customers were complaining about the same things daily.. In fact when we did complain they shrugged it off with 'I agree' It comes to something when the staff have no confidence in the place they work..
There is no real complaint about the breakfast as it is free which is great if you like cake and orange squash - (kids party anyone?) The strange thing is that it is served in a bedroom on the top floor which is a bit random..
