If after reading the reviews you do decide to pick this hotel the Italian opposite is okay and the Irish bar round the corner is fine for a drink. Apart from that everything is very spread out in San Francisco... For a decent meal head 10 mins down market street, avoiding the tramps, to Zuni Cafe...
Hotel Fusion???
More like Delusion....
I would prefer Alcatraz over this place...

title_masked: Great location and super excellent staff!
text_masked: Traveled here on business. Enjoyed the walk to the convention center each day. The return is up hill and good exercise. The hotel is located near a few nice restaurants and some shopping although it's necessary to walk a bit to get to more options. Food in restaurant was very well done.
The staff was very friendly and accommodating. It was clean and comfortable and we had a very nice weekend stay. Next time we will try the pool!

The Dana was a great hotel during my stay in Chicago. Great location, very friendly staff, my highlights were the rain showerheads in the bathroom, very comfortable beds, and the fact that the lounge with nightly music and great atmosphere is on the rooftop rather then near the lobby like at some other hotels I have stayed at. This way you don't hear the loud music thumping through the lobby area.
nice hotel in quiet area of jacksonville.$20 for taxi to city. quiet well run hotel ,no bar or restaurant but nice breakfast.

title_masked: Second stay; as great as before
text_masked:
People tell me this hotel is dated. I didn't notice it.
It is true that the exterior of the hotel is unexciting but the exterior is of interest only to passers-by. As a guest, you are only concerned with the interior. The property is maintained to the highest Four Seasons standards and is very well appointed.
Also, the views of Boston Common are beautiful if you're fortunate to get a room with that view.
For my second stay in 6 months, the experience was no different. At every level, this is one of the best hotels I have ever stayed in and Four Seasons does not get better than this anywhere.
Large luxurious rooms, lavish bathrooms with L'Occitane toiletries, wonderful service from all departments.
The Sunday Brunch at the Bristol Room was excellent.
Keep it up!

title_masked: All around great - one of the best hotels I've stayed in
text_masked: What a wonderful hotel! I was here for a conference and EVERY hotel employee I encountered was outstanding. The hotel is like a museum; grand and beautifully maintained. I stayed in a king room on the 30th floor of the Harbor Tower that was recently remodeled and had gorgeous views. The bed was quite comfortable and I loved the spa-like bathroom with the stall shower. My room was quiet, clean and had a small refrigerator, which was nice. The adult-only pool near the Kin spa was a dream, so relaxing and quiet with stunning views. I had lunch at Sally's one afternoon, the service and food were fantastic. The hotel is very conveniently located, 10 minutes from the airport, adjacent to the Seaport Village and within comfortable walking distance to Petco Park and the Gaslamp district. The gym is very nice (particularly the chilled, eucalyptus-scented towels post-workout). The concierge suggested I try the trolly tour of San Diego and it was a treat, I'd recommend it. In my opinion, you could skip the "Top of the Hyatt" bar on the 40th floor - the service was slow, it was very hot, and the drinks were rather expensive - that was the only negative experience in this hotel during my entire stay.

I usually stay at the 6th Ave Hilton for business, but since this was pleasure, I tried this Hilton and glad I did. We drove to the property and you have a choice of valet or self park up the street. Either way you are charged an additional $10 for in/out privledges. The hotel appears realtively new. Rooms very clean and typical NYC small but adequate. Staff was over the top in wanting to help you. Housekeeping would always stop you in the hallways with a smile and ask you if you were having a good stay. My wife and I prefer taking the subway all over Manhattan and the #1 train stop is at 7th and 28th (the hotel is on 26th just off 7th). We came back from Broadway shows late at night on both nights of our visit and we felt very safe walking from the subway back to the hotel. There is a great rooftop bar on the property as well. We will definitely be back.

We stayed here for only one night on the way to my son`s wedding in New Jersey!The hotel was a short walk from NY Penn station,around the corner from Empire State building & Macey`s.There was plenty of restaurants & Bars within walking distance or there is a metro station next to the hotel if you want to go further afield!The room was great & had everything you need for a comfortable stay,the bed was so comfortable & the walk in shower was nice & powerful.Would definitely stay here again & recommend this hotel for its great location.

Stayed here for pleasure while visiting family in the Vally. The location was terrific - really wasnt interested in Universal city - but its there if you are into it. The service was great - except at the pool if you order a lunch that has to be brought down from the kitchen (vegi burger or vegi sandwich) it took forever - the did feel bad and comped it. The room was spotless and everyone was helpful. I would definitely stay here again on my next trip to LA. Wish there was a spa! Stayed 2 weekends in a row!

I checked into this hotel due to my various stays in different Grand Hyatt in the world as I travel a lot and like to use different hotels. I was in the Interncontinental Hotel which is on a great location few minutes walk from the Times Square, although small rooms, but good service and excellent value for money, $500 per night. I opted to spend my last 2 days of New York in Grand Hyatt for it's location and got a suite for almost $700 a night. No Mini Bar, no Tea/Coffee making facility, the bathroom is smaller than what we would get in a bed and breakfast, i mean horrible. Not to mention the rudeness of the staff, MY GOD... the porter dropped bags outside the room for us to bring them in and waited outside so we can give him a tip, I mean . . . . I was wondering if we should order room service, they would tell us to come and fetch the food ourselves, you never know, what an attitude they have. My AC were not working, I called 3 times until the next day someone came to fix them. This is ridiculous for the money I paid and I would NEVER recommend this hotel to anyone. An old hotel renovated in a poor way.

First of all, I thought the room I was in, and the facility in general was very nice. It is a rather large and spread out hotel, so one may be forced to walk a lot to get from one place to another, especially to banquet facilities across the street. Older design I suppose, doesn't seem like its necessarily an efficient use of space. The location downtown is perfect, if downtown is where you want to be. Breakfast was included in my stay, and though it could have been more elaborate, such would have been lost on me; I thought it was just fine. Restaurant service was a little slow when busy, but within reason. I had a car to park, and I must say the parking facility was disorganized. But I had no problems. Elevators are ample in number, no long waits. I might would consider this facility a five star with one exception--the reservations team. I must have spoken by phone with them a dozen times and when I arrived they still hadn't gotten my reservation right. The problem: I was reserving two rooms, one for myself and one for a colleague. Our itinerary changed a couple of times necessitating call backs, and the experience was akin to banging one's head on the wall. I'll take credit for my part in communication breakdown, but it really wasn't complicated. A very capable and warm young Asian women straightened all out when I arrived. As for room service personnel, I had no interaction as I chose to go with their "eco plan" and not have my room prepared anew each day. Can't critique the price as I was participating in a conference with a special rate, which rate was reasonable. We did have a banquet and the food was enjoyable. I would return, but I might have someone else call in the reservation!

Visited in March 2012 and it was good value for New York. The lifts do drive you slightly crazy but the rooms and clean and big so plenty of room to move around. The breakfast was free and really good selection, just needs to be more space to eat it but for the price you can't complain. It's in a great location, really handy for everything. I think it depends on what kind of deal you get and we got a great one so happy to put up with the slow lifts!

My husband and I stayed at Barton Creek for 2 nights a couple weeks ago. The check in process was great and easy. Everyone was really nice, especially the valets! Our room was wonderful and the view was spectacular, a view of the hilly Fazio Foothills Golf Course! I couldn't believe we were in Texas! That view was awesome! My husband said that the Fazio Foothills were one of the best courses he had everbplayed! We ate at the wine bar that night. The servers were so nice and gracious! The food was wonderful! The next day we we got a couples massage. It was good but very pricey!!! Then I went to the pool. Oh my goodness, the staff at the pool serving drinks and food were the best! So accommodating! We really enjoyed our stay. We will definately go back!

title_masked: Beautiful hotel but what an disappointing service
text_masked:
Traveling from Norway and stayed here for one week.
This is a beautiful hotel, modern and sleek with very large room.
I have nothing bad to wright about the hotel and room itself it is al what you expect and more
The main problem with this hotel is the service. or lack of it.
Everything you want from ice cubes to other amenities you have to order room service, 
But when we have to wait 4 hours to get some ice cubes that is to long. Other time it takes 5 minutes. But we find out if you order room service early in the evening it is going to take ages but if you order it early night it takes only couple of minutes. The concierge would charge us up to 150 extra dollar for ordering Broadway ticket , that is way to expensive when British 5 star hotel do this for free. The refrigerator they told us will cost 27 dollar each night. But when i read the reviews here i just wonder if they treat people different because some payed 25 dollar each night for the refrigerator, and some get it for free. This is not good!! And to the end we where disturbed 3 times in 2 hours period the day we where checking out from 8 am wondering when we are checking out, Is that a way to treat the guest after a long stay?
But the hotel is perfect. With a perfect quiet place and plenty of good restaurants nearby such as pj clarks, Blu smoke and Harrys italian.

title_masked: Nice view, overpriced, no special access to the hotel club
text_masked:
Skip this hotel!!!
Pros:
- View is nice
- New interior
- Polite staff at front desk
Cons:
- Over priced 
- On a Saturday night I was denied access to the club at midnight and then 3am even though I was a hotel guest!!! Bouncer was rude and didn't let us in at all (two 30 something females)
- ZERO shower privacy, only a clear glass covering for all too see everything
- Stayed on the 14th floor and hear the club music from the 18th floor till 4am

I have to start with the location of the hotel. My family and I were placed in the Beach Building after I insisted on a room with a water view. It is just a very short walk, around the corner from the Holiday Inn main lobby. There is a Denny's in the lobby of the Beach Building. All around were Walgreen's, In & Out Burger, Starbucks, Muni F-Line stop, and of course Embarcadero street which is along the piers of Fisherman's Wharf. The location of the hotel is UNBEATABLE. When my family were tired or needed to go back to the room quickly from the Wharf or Ghiradelli square, it was a short and easy walk. Also, we just had to cross the street to get to the Muni- F-Line stop to take a ride to the Ferry building as a meeting place for some of the tours we were doing. Leaving in the morning and returning in the evening, we were essentially "going against the traffic" so we did not have to get on a crowded cable car. We went shopped at Walgreens 3 times to pick up some necessities. There was a parking garage and a parking lot for anyone who has a car. The best treat was being able to see two 4th of July fireworks shows going on simultaneously on the Wharf. While we watched everyone below fight for parking, lug around chairs, freezing in the wind, and using porta potties, we stood comfortably around the window of our room to watch spectacular fireworks from the left and the right. We could hear the music too. Rest of the time, noise was not too much of an issue since people left the area after dark and we left the room in the morning by the time it got busy again.
Check in was good. I was thanked for being a Platinum member and given a pouch of brand name sample grooming / toiletry products. My request for a high-floor room with a water view was met. Unfortunately everything else about the hotel was either average or below average. The room was not cleaned well upon check-in. There was a used bar of soap with hair hanging from it in the tub. The same type of hair was in the piece of fabric that laid across the end of the bed. There were used glasses in the room that just had the cover over them. After the the first day, consequent cleanings were decent. The bed was comfortable and there was plenty of hot water and good water pressure from the shower.
The building had 2 elevators but only one was working during our entire stay which meant long waits and crowded rides. On our last day, the only working elevator didn't work for a while so we had to climb stairs. Thank fully by the time we were leaving, the elevator was working so we did not have to drag our luggage down the stairs. 
I never saw a concierge or bell man on duty at all times even though there are concierge and bell man posts. I had to walk to the main building to talk to a concierge. Derron was very helpful. On our last day, there was a bell man (I wish I knew his name!) and he was kind enough to call Rodney, the driver to bring the house Town Car to take us to the airport for the same price as a taxi ($55). 
I was able to get a really good room rate of $129 plus taxes through the travel agency at my work so I am quite pleased with what I got since location was so important to me. 
My advice to travelers with families is to stay in a hotel in the Wharf area because you will find yourself coming to the area everyday to join up with tours or to visit. Even if you wanted to go to Union Square to shop, you can hop on the Muni. Great nearby places to eat: Castangola's (in front of hotel) for great clams, roasted garlic dungeness crab, and seafood cioppino; Sally's Fishwich at 43 1/2 Pier for fish sandwiches and garlic fries; and Sabella's stand for dungeness crab and bread bowl.

title_masked: ok for this price in Philly
text_masked: I stayed one night there with $124, ,which I think it is very pricy. I had a room with the river view and noisy street. Room is not very clean. The tub has some stains and I feel there are som bag in the other bed. Good thing is there are two beds in the room. A/C and street were so loud that I had to put earpluges to sleep. The view from my room is very beautiful and the staffs are very nice. Breakfast was okay.

We stayed 2 nights at the Seattle Marriott Renaissance Hotel. It's location is called "pike area" on Priceline but it is a little out of the way. Still, Pike Market is only about a 10-15 min. walk. We asked to stay on the west side of the hotel so that we would not be over the Interstate 5 Highway. This request was kindly accomodated, along with our request for 2 double beds and an upper-floor room. Front desk staff and conceigere were all helpful and professional. I see that people posted trouble with elevator--I have to say we did not have this problem (April 27 - 29). As for the room itself, it was fairly large and newly renovated. The bathroom, shower, and beds were all in good condition and there were nice touches such a Aveda products and complimentary newspapers etc. In the hotel lobby, Starbucks coffee is available in the coffee shop. Our only complaint was the self-parking fee--$30.00 and then $6.60 per night in tax. I queried this and was told that the parking tax is at 20% which I don't fully understand (hotel tax is 15%). Personally, I think they should just charge a rate that includes tax like all other parking garages so that there are no unexpected charges on check-out. Other than this, I can recommend this hotel as a comfortable, well-maintained hotel to stay in Seattle.

Your staff is uptight and think they can do no wrong. The customer is always right is not part of their training is obvious. They are unyeilding when it comes to breakfast. My daughter came in and arrivied at the hotel around 2 am she was very tired and is 5 months pregant. Was given a hard time checking in and in the morning got down at 9:32 am and they locked the doors. Again five months pregant still tired and now hungrey. Never again.

It is a great hotel for NY standards. Four of us were Confortable for a week. the location is central to everything. Missing laundry and free coffe throughout the day. Polite staff. It is Definitly a great choice and great value for money

Where do I begin? First off, my wife and I were given a room on the Northwest corner of the property. The sun was blazing and the outside temp was 114(F). The room AC was off and the room was extremely hot. There was also a unidentified stentch in the room. I turned on the AC to 68 degrees. Two hours later, the room was still hot and still smelled badly. I went to the office to exchange rooms. The young female associate there was very helpfull and gave us a room on the cooler side of the hotel. When we entered the room, the smell of cigarettes burned my sinuses. We went back to the office to get a non-smoking room. The associate told us that was a non-smoking room. She gave us another room. This room still smelled of cigarettes, but, was not as strong a smell. The AC cooled down the room quickly. Upon inspecting the room, we heard a cricket, found it, and killed it. It must have had a friend, which we could not find and kpt chirping all night. The furniture in the room was in bad shape. It looks like they bought it all at a thrift store or used on ebay. The bathroom tub was repainted and the paint was chipping off. All of the furniture had chip marks at the base. The plug beside the TV had way too many plugs used, without the use of a surge protector. A jumble of wires also lay between the bed and nightstand. The bed matress was very uncomfortable and both my wife and I woke up with sore necks. The bathroom was very small and had no way to be cooled. It remained very warm our entire stay. We like to leave the bathrrom light on as a nightlight, but it had a built in timer/motion sensor and kept turning off. The room widows had locks on them. There was no way to open the window. In case of fire, there was only the door; if blocked, would have to throw a chair through the window to get out. The chair in front of the computer desk was a cheap $5.00, straight back, metal framed kitchen chair. The bad smell was in all three rooms we had. The rooms could use a good carpet and curtain cleaning and bed spread change. That might help! The location was not the greatest. Except for a couple truckers, the hotel was mostly deserted that night. 
Positives: 
* The desk associate was friendly and accomodating (moved us twice).
* I could tell the room cleaners try hard to make the rooms nice (folded washcloth into a design, bed made neatly, etc.), but all the surface cleaning and sprays in the world won't remove the smells from those rooms.

I stayed at this hotel for one night the begining of March when I was going through Charlotte. I just needed a safe, clean hotel close to the intersate with interior corridors. 
All of my specifications were met during my stay. I had a non smoking room with one queen bed. The room and the bathroom were clean. 
The hotel is also close to the airport with a free courtesy shuttle. They offered the shuttle when I checked in but advised I did not need that service. Plus they offered to take you if they weren't busy to some of the local restaurants nearby.

I just stayed at the Holiday Inn and Suites by the airport in Denver. I got upgraded to a suite and the room was great. There was a sitting room, seperate bedroom, and a kitchenette. It was fresh and clean. The staff are great too. I would certainly stay here again. 
There is a enterprise car rental right in the lobby.

My husband and I stayed here for one night and I loved it! The front desk staff was so nice and helpful. The room was very clean and the beds were very comfortable. The room was very modern with newer furnishings and fixtures. We had a perfect view of Victory field and Lucas Oil Stadium. We were able to walk to the mall and it was a very easy walk to Victory field as well. The bathroom had Paul Mitchell shampoo and conditioner bottles and the shower had great water pressure. Our king room had a sofa as well. I would recommend this hotel! Close to shops and museums.

title_masked: Overpriced. No big deal for this frequent traveler to Boston.
text_masked: Rooms were cramped, bathroom tiny. Beds average, not the 5 star quality advertised. Poor drapery allowed sunlight in at top of panels that awoke us every morning. Tile grout had mold, hair on bathrrom floor, had to move rooms. Walls allowed all noise in. Large gap at bottom of room door entrance. Mediocre service: Front desk put me on telephone hold "to take a customer in line" when I called about non-working remote control (dead batteries); after waiting in lobby line to ask about drink coupons we never rc'd, the front desk staff asked me to step aside so they could take the next customer as my inquiry apparantly was taking too much time for them to figure out right then. Way over priced. Will not return. Will go back to the Sheraton Back Bay, 3 star, for larger rooms, similar beds, more ammenities/convenience on site, half the price. Giving Colonnade 2-3 Stars.

title_masked: Great location at a good value!
text_masked: I stayed at the Chancellor hotel while attending a convention at the Moscone Center over the weekend. The hotel is located just off Union Square so there is plenty to see and do right out the door. Our room was comfortable, but if you want a good view be sure to request it. Noise is an issue being that the Hotel is so close to the square, but I appreciated the various options that they offered to alleviate it if necessary (such as earplugs or a white noise generator). The only down side of our stay was that there was no internet access in our room because the network signal was too weak. We had to go to the lobby to get online. Besides the comfort and amenities, I was very impressed with the staff. The service from the moment we drove up to the time we checked out was top notch. Every employee was friendly and extremely helpful without being overbearing. Also, for being in the middle of S.F. the price was very affordable. I would definitely look into staying at this hotel again.

title_masked: Great start to our California holiday!
text_masked:
This is an excellent hotel, in a good location.
We stayed on the 19th floor and the views were awesome.
The room was very clean with everything we needed so no complaints here.
The bar/restaurant was very nice and reasonably priced too. The staff were very pleasant and helpful too.
Would definitely stay here again.

title_masked: Great hotel in a great city
text_masked:
We stayed in the drake for a few nights before flying back to Dublin. It is a very busy old hotel with great history attached to it. The location is brilliant right across the road from the lake and oak street beach and right in the middle of the shopping area. The whole hotel while old is very clean and the room was very comfortable and had character compared to most Hiltons. The bed and linens were lovely and the bathroom very spacious with nice toilettes. There is plenty going on with music in the palm court at night and nice bars in the hotel itself. Staff friendly and helpful. 
Lovely hotel in a great location.

OK, so terrible is a strong word. The location is excellent, from the proximity to the mall (a two-minute walk) to the underground mall (never hurts to have a Five Guys in your back pocket if you need a quick bite). However, the hotel is no longer the four-star property of years past and the breakfast buffet is truly terrible (thus the title). Also, the hotel's inability to confirm a crib and an inexplicable dearth of microwaves (we were only able to wrangle one of the last day of our stay) were unnecessary annoyances.

Ok I know I was warned that rooms would be small in NYC but not as small as we were given! room had no closet so could not hang any clothes up and it only had a half window which looked out on a brick wall, even with all the lights on it was dark and horrid. We complained to desk and in fairness were given an upgraded room which was bigger and very bright but the closet only had hanging rails about 3ft in length (not very good as I had maxi dresses to hang). The rooms were clean but very old and not value for money. The lobby is quite impressive but beware you could get a bad room. Didnt think this was the best of locations in NYC either but obviously location is an individual choice. Also did nt really rate the Tick Tock Diner much, it was ok for one night but compared to MacDonalds and the Pizza place directly across the street it was over priced! If you like old fashioned hotels this might appeal but I would choice modern over this hotel any day!

My cousin, best friend, and myself were in Austin for the the day and needed a inexpensive place to stay. 
Got into town around 830p, called the hotel and the front desk clerk was very patient and gave precise directions to the hotel. 
hotel was very easy to locate, and its location was ideal! literally 2 miles away from 6th street, and shared a parking lot with a gas station. 
check in was quick and easy, and we were pleasantly surprised to discover that our room and a fridge and microwave. never seen this inside a hotel room unless it had a kitchen in it!
complimentary breakfast was nothing special, but it was the deciding factor when we were choosing a hotel to stay at.
all in all it may not be the most glamorous but definitely a outstanding value.

The photographs of this hotel look great but it is not all that it is made out to be. The rooms are big and the beds are very comfortable but my room was a little bit shabby in places. I am not fussy so it didn't bother me but it is tired and could do with refreshing. The bathroom was fine but the shower did not have much power - more of a dribble than a jet! Lobby was a bit dark but fine. Staff were okay. The area is convenient for GSS and the main mid town sights but lacks atmosphere. This is an okay hotel in a handy location but I wouldn't return to this hotel or area of NY unless I got a cheap deal.

Stayed here for a one night treat whilst visiting friends in Houston. When we first arrived at 3.15pm we were told that only one of our two rooms was ready but that we could all use that and we would be called when the second room became available. We trotted off to the room and found that we were on the first floor and had no view at all. All that could be seen was a grassy slope up to the path to the car park. Not very impressive for $300 a night, particularly when the two bottles of water on the hospitality tray were $1 each.
We got into our swimmers and went off to the pool. Not a bed to be had unfortunately and we had to make do with a table and rather uncomfortable metal chairs. The drinks attendants were very nice and after a couple of drinks and a dip in the very nice pool the chairs didn't seem quite so hard.
We were called to be told that our second room was now ready and we headed back to reception. This was where we struck lucky. Someone had let our second first floor room go so we were offered two new rooms on the 6th floor. Much, much better. Both rooms had lovely views of the surrounding countryside and lo and behold free bottles of water!
We ate dinner in Brannon's Cafe and had a very nice meal. The service was a little slow but our server, Andrew, was so lovely that it really wasn't a problem. We ate in Brannon's again for breakfast, and although the buffet was very nice $105 did seem a little excessive for just 4 people. We also were not told that we could have ordered fresh waffles from our server as part of the buffet, this info came to us as we finished eating and overheard the folk on the next table enquiring exactly what the buffet included. Would have been helpful to have been told this from the outset.
The complementary late check out was very welcome as this allowed us to have a lounge at the pool for a couple of hours before we had to get ready for the off. As we got to the pool at 10.30 we also managed to bag some beds too!
All in all a very nice stay, though I think we may have felt differently had we not been elevated from the dungeon level.

HVAC in our room was LOUD, sounded like a jet flying overhead. We had some noisy neighbors across the hall, but they quieted down by 11 PM. Breakfast was a big disappointment because it was just "grab & go". Rooms were spacious and comfortable, we slept well.

Stay at the Canterbury for a convention in August 2012. Had an issue at check in with the hotel billing my American Express upfront. I can understand the $50.00 a day for " incidentals " but my credit card was billed for the full amount as well. Stayed at the Hyatt Orange County several months ago and was billed at the end of the stay. The Hyatt did hold several hundred dollars for incidentals as well. Curious why this " boutique " hotel required $1200.00 up front. When we got home the $250.00 for incidentals was refunded. Staff had no explanation for why I had to pay in advance. I did not have a bank or debit card but an American Express credit card. I have never experienced this with any other hotel or resort. Staff was very indifferent to my complaint which put a very bad taste in my mouth from the beginning. Will not be back or recommend this hotel.

Good location. Right across Staples Center and LA Live. People are friendly and helpful. Housekeeping was great! Concierge was very helpful. A must place to stay while in LA. No real breakfast though. But coffee/tea and pastries are served at the lobby every morning.

my husband has a serious medical problem, and he is being treated at Johns Hopkins.
they recommended Days Inn at the Inner Harbor and we were so glad they did.
we have stayed at Days Inner Inner harbor on each of our trips to Johns Hopkins and on every visit the staff was exceptional. they were kind enough to hold our room for our late arrival, since we were traveling . front desk staff was knowledgeable, kind, and couldn't do enough for us. 
Most of the time we dealt with Debbie at the front desk during the day shift. She was excellent and very efficient , and extremely helpful.
I would highly recommend Days Inn at the Inner Harbor, in Baltimore, MD to all of my friends and family.
also, I have to mention, we ate at Hopkins Grill in the hotel, the food was excellent along with the service and friendliness of the staff.
again, thank you everyone .

A great location and service to match, with helpful, polite staff throughout the hotel. Both of the restaurants have a lot of atmosphere and the food is great - especially the seafood. I was also impressed with the spacious, well equipped room and its view over the Red Sox stadium was a real bonus, making the trip even more memorable.
When I return to Boston, this wil certainly be my first choice.

Great location, great service, great ambience. Tres French. The feather bed mattress topper, combined with the high-thread count duvet, made for much better-than-usual hotel sleep experiences, which was wonderful. The bathroom was opulent...almost as big as the entire sleeping area (small, by American standards, but big enough), stocked with high end toiletries, a soaking tub, and a huge walk in shower. A couple of suggestions: 1. The towels are rough and scratchy. An easy problem to fix. 2. There are cards in the bathroom encouraging guests to conserve resources by re-using towels, but there is no where to hang them! In my opinion, the bump out for the bathroom window is the perfect spot for a couple of hooks. I'd definitely go back.

I had tickets to attend the Phila. Auto Show and was looking for a hotel that wasn't too expensive and was w/in walking distance to the show and to The Reading Terminal Market. Must say, this hotel met both criteria. We arrived early and was not sure if we could secure an early check-in. Not only was that possible, but the staff was extremely gracious and very helpful with basic information and directions. Upon entering our room, we were pleasantly surprised at its size and cleanliness. The only issue we had was some noisey neighbors who were quieted quickly after a call to the front desk. There is a charge for parking since you are staying midtown. The parking lot is located right next door to the hotel & you are allowed easy in and out access. Would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone for its convenient location to shopping, restaurants and value. The free breakfast is also a nice perk. Will stay here again on my next visit to Phila.
My husband's former colleagues had a reunion here, and the experience was pleasant. The hotel provided a hospitality room and reasonable rates, making the weekend enjoyable for all.

title_masked: Friendly Staff But Hotel is Poorly Maintained
text_masked:
Pros: The staff was super friendly -- I'll give them that. And the airport shuttle was convenient. Room was clean and the wifi worked well. 
Cons: Phone did not work; TV remote did not work (until I reprogrammed it): AC was weak and took 3 hours to cool down the room: and the elevator was out of service.
It's one thing to "lack" amenities, it's quite another when the amenities don't work. Was inexpensive so I guess I should not expect the Ritz. Would not stay there again.

title_masked: Spectacular golf resort, prepare for $$$ extras
text_masked: Visited with 24 women on a golf outing and loved La Cantera's scenery, professional golf staff and facilities. Didn't love the expense of the basics. Water bottle in lobby $3.50, Parking $20 seemed out of step for a rural setting, House wine by glass $11. Both golf courses are stunning and the pool area beautiful. But water and wine should not come with sticker shock. If you travel by car, especially with a family, bring your own.

Just steps from The Magnificent Mile, this hotel offers friendly, professional, and PROMPT service to guests. We had two requests during our overnight stay, and each time, a staff member was at our door within 10 minutes of our call. The room itself was large and well-cared-for. Bathroom lighting is pretty abysmal, though there is a plug-in lighted makeup mirror to mitigate some of the horror of trying to apply makeup in the main mirror. Our room overlooked the front of the hotel on Superior Street, which unfortunately faces the hospital directly across the street. The all-day/all-night sirens are somewhat disruptive. Between that and the aging mattress, I did not sleep as well as I would have liked.
All that said, I wouldn't shy away from staying here again if the price was right. There's a lot to be said for feeling as if my business is appreciated.

title_masked: quiet, spacious, well located for shopping
text_masked: We stayed there the 3 first days of July 2012 after a crossing from England with the Queen Mary and before going to Canada for the summer. We had a kind of mini suite giving on the back of the hotel. It was perfectly quiet which is unbelievable in NY. The room was big, clean and in good order. The bed was made up with a wool blanket as requested (instead of the usual unescapable duvet) we had two well functionning & well supplied bathrooms including showers with good water pressure, The air conditioning was precise and quiet. The drapes did their job of cutting the light from the outside. We slept well. Location perfect for shopping

title_masked: Great location, great staff, large room
text_masked:
My stay was made exta special because of a member of their staff Jenny who made my stay special!
Location next to Penn Station and MSQ Garden. Larger room then typical nyc room.

I stayed here over Labor Day weekend and though it was good I thought it was way overpriced for what I thought we would be getting. We had a bay side bungalow which basically was a one bedroom suite with a couch bed. The kitchen had no stove or microwave. We initially thought we'd just cook in the room but that idea quickly faded so we had to eat on property and it got to be pretty expensive. One morning I ordered a children's oatmeal and an adult oatmeal with 2 milks and it was $37.00!!! just for oatmeal! I was shocked to say the least. The pool is nice but the beach was pretty crummy and dirty. The grounds are beautiful with lovely landscaping but overall I was really let down and would not stay here again. There was also sand in the fold out bed so I guess they didn't wash the sheets b/w visitors which is disgusting. We didn't use the spa or the exercise equiptment or any rentals. We did go by water taxi to Sea World and the trip takes 15 minutes each way, though it's only 0.8 miles away. If I had to do it again I'd just go by regular taxi and not get stuck having to wait for the water taxi to take you back to the hotel. We waited 20 minutes and it had filled up so we had to wait another 30 minutes with a 2 and 4 year old...not fun.

title_masked: Lovely small hotel on the beach
text_masked: Great hotel right on Pacific Beach. Rooms were great and bikes were provided for free to cruise the beachside footpath. Rates were quite expensive but you're paying for the excellent location. We would have no hesitation staying here again if we return to San Diego and wanted to stay by the beach.

They did a pretty good job of fixing up this former office building. Great location and warm desk staff. Rooms were just great! Breakfast, given free was plentiful. Good view of William Penn from the top floors.

Eden made my mom and other family members feel like roalty. The rooms look absoloutly amazing. Very modern and confortable. All the staff were very friendly and most accomadating. The location is perfect. Around the corner is willis tower (Must see).

We spent 6 nights here in June, we were upgraded on check in to a larger room as we were celebrating my husbands birthday. Thought the room size was great, don't know how small the smaller rooms were but ours was a very good room. Staff were very friendly. Breakfast prices seemed very expensive so we ate out every day. Great base and situation for the subway and for walking. I would recommend this hotel.

title_masked: Good Value! Clean, Comfortable, and Located in the Cultural Heart of SoCal.
text_masked:
The purpose of our trip to Los Angeles was business combined with a bit of pleasure. We chose the Sheraton Los Angeles Downtown because of its location half-way between our meeting locations and the reasonable price for a three-nights stay.
Check-in was prompt and we found our room to be tastefully decorated, clean, and spacious. It was clear that our room had been updated. The hotel kindly provided us a refrigerator and microwave for a small nightly fee. The view was unspectacular (our room looked across the mall rooftop into another office building), but the windows afforded plenty of privacy and good sunlight.
The hotel's location is conveniently adjacent to Macy's Plaza, which is not the flashiest mall, but offers a Macy's Department store along with other mid-range shopping options and decent dining options. We went to dinner in the mall and had some very good steaks. If you have a car, and in LA who doesn't, you can easily drive to Downtown attractions (Walt Disney Concert Hall, Dodger Stadium, LA Live, Staples Center and the Convention Center) as well as University of Southern California, Los Angeles's West Side, Pasadena, and the South Bay.
My only complaint would be the cost and convenience of parking. We had to walk through the mall to access parking that was 32.00 per night. There are less expensive parking options nearby but they do not offer in/out privileges and typically have time restrictions.
I recommend this hotel if the location suits your needs. It is a good option for business travelers, families, friends, and solo travelers.

Construction happening; I didn't notice it much. My room was completely new--carpet, walls, etc and seemed very fresh. May be because I'm from the midwest, but I learned to avoid staff. The check-in staff was eager to use the phrase "not at that rate" when I asked for credit on my Hilton frequent stay account. Conceirge (male) told me to look "on-line" when I called down to ask about attraction in the area. Young woman who came in at 10:00am to the concierge desk was wonderful, polite, helpful.

title_masked: Consistently great service at this hotel
text_masked: I've stayed at this hotel a half dozen times. The cost is reasonble, the quality of the rooms is consistently high, the food is terrific, and the service is on a caliber with the finest hotels. The location could not be better and is in close proximity to most of the attractions in Fort Worth. We wouldn't stay anywhere else.

Spent 2 nights at this hotel, and was a bit worried about it given some of the reviews. I have to say we thought this hotel was great. 
First off, the location is perfect. Right smack in the middle of City Center. Loads of really good restaurants and shops in every direction. The hotel is quite lovely........very nice lobby, with most helpful front desk staff. They were right there for us with recommendations for restaurants, making reservations, calling cabs, they even called the Hop on Hop Off Tour Bus and arranged for us to be picked up in a van and driven to the site in Old City where the tours begin. ( I recommend this tour, by the way. Very imfromative and a great way to see the city and get your bearings). The room was small, I admit. However, the only real issue we had in that regard was the size of the bathroom. I didn't care that there was no tub, just a shower. The shower was a very good size. It's just that the overall size of the bathroom is just a little too small to be truly comfortable moving around etc. But other than that, the room was very clean, had nice furnishings, nice bedding, the bed was comfortable.....nothing wrong with it, it's just small. We had no intention of spending a lot of time in our romm, so for the purpose of our trip, it was not an issue.
I would recommend this hotel.

title_masked: Relaxing Hotel Still Near the Fun in San Diego
text_masked: Stayed at this hotel on a short business trip. Hotel is not new but is well-maintained. Reception staff were courteous and efficient. Hotel was busy when I was there. The hotel is tucked behind a shopping plaza with many stores and a wide variety of restaurants, and within a few minutes walking distance. The location is quieter than a downtown hotel, and relaxing. This Courtyard was very close to the San Diego Airport. Hotel offers a free 24 hour airport van. Call for a free pickup when arriving at the airport. Parking is free, My room was of standard size and had two queen-size beds. Public spaces in the hotel were pleasant. A bar adjacent to the lobby is open evenings. Hot food can be ordered from the hotel kitchen. A sit-down restaurant is across the aisle from the bar for a traditional dining experience. Prices are fair. Work out room had the standard aerobic equipment and some free weights, although the exercise room was larger than one normally sees in a hotel this size. Everything worked in my room. I was pleased with this hotel. I will look to return on future trips.

title_masked: excellent, quiet, great food and attentive service
text_masked: I stayed at the Inn recently--in October 2012. The two night stay was a pleasure in all ways. Quiet place. The windows opened onto a balcony...an unusual thing to find these days--fresh air in a hotel room. The service and attention from the front desk and others was wonderful. The room was enormous with an amazing whirlpool tub, and sustainable materials used throughout. The crab cakes were superb. This Inn is a remarkable place, and in an interesting area of the city with access to many points of interest. I will not hesitate to return there. Fantastic place.

We live in Fort Worth, TX and were looking for a quick, overnight, relaxing getaway. This is exactly what we got. We had no plans to venture out, we wanted to lay by the pool and have I mentioned, relax. We found this hotel to be extremely peaceful with the golf course and pool our back it was really beautiful. The lounge chairs were comfortable, pool temperature was perfect (cold but not freezing) and we enjoyed the hot tub as well. Tiny complaints: the towels were those small blue ones but if you use 2-3 they work. Another plus was that there is a multi-use tennis and basketball court so make sure you bring tennis shoes. The raquets that the front desk were kiddy rackets so if you really want to play tennis bring your own racket! Our room was clean, comfortable and nice looking. We were pleasantly surprised by this hotel and will likely stay here again when we want to RELAX!

I stayed here 2 weeks for work, and really enjoyed my stay. The staff is nice and goes above and beyond to make your stay comfortable. My hotelroom was very big, I received a free upgrade to a room on the 11th floor, the premium level. I opted to not get my room cleaned and received vouchers for the hotel restaurant in return. ($5 a day) The restaurant is great, I had breakfast every morning and the fruit is very fresh! The hotel is right next to the mall, which is very convenient. Loved my stay here!

We stay last weekend at this newly remodeled location. It is very nice! The staff are very friendly and the shuttle service to the airport is great. We did the park and fly and the price is the best we could find. Even though it is very close to the airport, it is super quiet.

we were there for the tow show and everyone at the hotel was so nice & helpful. you made our trip . we hope to come back next year. And the taxi driver you called for us , he was Great! Wendell Smith with At Your Service. Thanks

Let's start with the positive. Very nice staff, check in was great and the hotel is in a great location. Now the negative. This hotel is not for families or vacationers. The rooms are small, very little drawer space, and the bathrooms are so small that when you sit you cannot get to the toilet paper!! Half the sink is under a shelf so when you bend over the sink to wash your face you bump your head. We had a room with double beds and the housekeeping staff continually only left two towels even after we asked for more the first day. Our air did not cool so the hotel sent someone up. Their solution was to take off the air vent cover and leave it exposed so the air would flow better. They said they would move us the next day but then had no available rooms with double beds. The second night our lights would not turn off when we got ready to go to bed after a late night out. Once again they sent someone up and they couldn't get them off either. Their solution was to take out the four light bulbs in the ceiling so we could sleep. Both the air and the lights NEVER got fixed the entire time we stayed. We asked for compensation when we checked out but all the manager would do is give us enough points for a free night the next time. Not sure Hyatt will ever get our business again. There are a lot of better hotels in New York City to choose from so think twice before staying at the Grand Hyatt.

title_masked: About as good as they get!!
text_masked:
After reading some of the other reviews and some that were down right negative, we were very uneasy and we were assigned this hotel by Shrine International so had no choice. Well very much to our surprise we were extremely satisfied and all disbelief of of the what we may find were gone upon our registration. We found absolutely every aspect of our stay a wonderful experience, from registration friendliness, the Motor Lobby crew and bell-service were so friendly and helpful. Our room was kept very well with a very friendly housekeeping staff, and all of the necessary complimentary soaps, creams and shower items were always replaced during our stay. When we checked out the Motor lobby staff went over backwards to be so helpful and friendly. Our favorite thing about the service an hotel was the very close proximity to some of the best restaurants all within short walking distance. 
A very pleasant experience overall and to heck with those who have written some of the bad reviews, the must have went in with blind folders on!! We would use this hotel for our personal choice when there for pleasure with no questions. Shriners International picked a choice hotel for us this time. We have stayed at so many over the years I guess we can't count them too. This was a AAA +++ for us. Only one tip I would have for visitors, it is a shared parking and spaces are real tight for SUV type vehicles.If there are more than one to a couple spots you might have to exit out your back window! I would suggest doing the valet for the extra bucks and those guys are nothing but GR[TEL]. as well as great respect for your vehicle care. 
Harold E King

Stayed one night with my family. Was upgraded to a two bedroom suite (which was greatly appreciated since we had a 6 week old baby and a 6 year old). The lobby was beautiful, enjoyed our warm cookies, very warm reception at check in. The room was clean however it did seem like it hadn't been used in awhile. Could have used some freshening up. Also minor things like caulking, baseboards, tears in wallpaper were observed as well. Breakfast was a pretty good buffet. Eggs were runny but they also offered made to order omelets which were delicious. Regular assortment of cold and hot items on the buffet as well. Service was a little slow but friendly. Convenient location - within walking distance to the mall and several restaurants. We usually stay in the Renaissance across the street which we love but we normally don't have our children with us. This hotel was much better with kids. We enjoyed our stay and will return with our family next time we're in town.

title_masked: Great hotel let down by bad service
text_masked: My wife and I stayed here for a couple of days while visiting NYC. The location of the hotel is great, and the refurbishment is excellent, with a sensitive combination of modern amenities and retained period features—there is even an original fireplace in the fitness center! However, the hotel is let down by poor service. When we checked into our room, we found the TV was faulty, so we reported it the following morning, and were assured it would be taken care of. When we returned in the afternoon, the TV was still not fixed, so we reported it again, were assured again it would be taken care of, and yet, when we returned to the room that night, it was still not fixed, nor was there any evidence that it had even been looked at. Also, while there was a lounge for the use of Gold Elite members, this was open only on week days. It was good to stay here, not least because of the hotel's history, but next time we are visiting NYC, we will look elsewhere.

Stayed at the Sofitel for 2 weeks on business and enjoyed it completely. Rooms were sleek and modern and the bathroom was marble with both a shower and bath. The bed was on the soft side, but I found it terrific, as I did the huge TV. There are Keurig coffee makers in the rooms (plus complimentary bottled water) and also coffee/tea/fruit in the lobby early. 
The gym was respectable for a hotel gym and had a mix of cardio, weight machines and dumbells. One of the few drawbacks was the elevator : one needs to swipe one's key card to get to your floor, but they often malfunctioned. Of course, it's a good security measure but could be annoying. Since I did not pay for the room, I cannot judge if it was a good value.
The Rittenhouse square area was wonderful! Loved the park (farmer's market on Saturdays) and all the shops nearby. Marathon was a reliable favorite restaurant and Trader Joe's is walking distance. Another tip: the Palomar Hotel across the street had a happy hour from 10-11pm.

We stayed at The Argonaut for 3 nights at the time the Americas cup trials were going on. This meant that the whole area was a bit of a madhouse! Leaving that to one side, the nightly wine tasting also means that there are queues of residents waiting for their free wine which to my mind isn't worth bothering with. On the positive side,the staff are very friendly and nothing is too much trouble. Our room was okay but the bathroom was just like a cupboard. If you like to be in the heart of the tourist area then you'll probably like the location. The Mermaid kitchen is great for dinner and breakfast and there is a great bar next door called [NAME]. Probably wouldn't stay here again.

this place was fantastic, not to mention convenient to most attractions, stores, and freeways. it's comparable to being in a mini resort, without paying the resort prices. I don't think I can add on to what's already posted except I wished I would have stayed here longer!

Well kept, large corner room on 32 floor is the way to go. Super clean, great staff, best location . Expensive parking, but this is NYC. Surprisingly quiet for big city. Great bed and super large fluffy towels. Not your average highway motel.

The rooms were very shabby. Rugs snagged and spotty. The bed was on a metal frame that squeaked awful. The service at the bar was the worst. Girls in tiny black dresses that only waited on you if you were wearing a suit or dripping in diamonds. The Algonquin needs to hurry up and get renovated already!!

We have stayed twice at the Milford and you can't beat the value for an excellent location in Times Square. Room is clean and the bed is comfortable - all we needed. We did have a problem with a foul sewage like smell in the BR and when we complained we were provided another room without delay. We'd stay there again, for sure. It's not a luxury hotel so don't expect one.

We recently stayed at Best Western Apartments. The apartments were very roomy. The staff were very friendly. We only had one issue. We were in the penthouse and the water pump was right next to our room. The pump was so noisy that it kept me awake the first night. We talked to the staff the next day and they sorted the issue out. The breakfast is basic. We found the breakfast room crowded so we took our breakfast back to our room. The apartments are within walking distance to the City. There are lots of places to eat and enjoy within easy walking distance.

I always stay in Holiday Inn Express Sorrento Valley when I'm in San Diego, they always welcome me with a bag of goodies that at least make me feel good... All personnel is always very nice and I would like to give a special thank to Elisa Santos for all her help and as always she is very helpful, I really appreciate it.

title_masked: A very good hotel in Boston
text_masked:
I loved this hotel and very much appreciated the furniture and the beauty of it as well as a very set of attentive staff. In particular Yan Yan Chen the housekeeper was excellent and kept my room spotless every day.
The only thing that prevents me giving the highest rating to this hotel is the fact that the bathroom whilst super clean was quite small without a proper rainforest or walk in shower - I know many hotels in the US do not have that but I think an hotel charging over 250 bucks should have that to get an excellent rating. In addition i would expect room service to be 24 hours rather than till 11pm again for an excellent hotel, and I would also expect the internet to be better although the IT support were excellent.
 Location is great, and there are always taxis outside. The tv is very good and i particularly appreciate the HBO plus additional HBO stations. room service was good, laundry was good, and the writing paper and pens etc were a delight as well as the books about the hotel.

I had stayed at the Latham several years ago, and took advantage of their special pricing during renovation to see the Van Gogh exhibit at the Art Museum. The boutique hotel has a great location just off Rittenhouse Square. The room was larger than you would expect from an older property, and very comfortable. The staff was friendly and helpful.

This hotel is in a great location! It is within walking distance to many attractions. We were only there for 2 days so we didn't get to use all the hotel amenities, however, the hotel decor and the size of the room was excellent. We plan on going back to Baltimore and we will definitely stay at the Pier 5 Hotel.

we have been staying at marriott hotels for some time. however LA Marriott downtown was a huge disappointment. The rooms are shabby and in desperate need of renewal. Parking charges are 35 USD/night!!!!! no complimentary wireless (even in the lobby). no minibar in the rooms. executive lounge snacks are poor..We would never go back and never recommend. I am not sure we will ever stay at a Marriott facility again..

Stayed here for President's Day weekend for 2 nights. Had booked with points on Priority Club Website as I am a Platinum member. I called ahead to confirm my reservation - a King Executive floor room. When I arrived to check in, I was given a room on the 6th floor with 2 double beds. Went down to the front desk to change rooms and they gave me a King down the hall from the original room. After we had unpacked I decided to check out the Executive lounge which was supposed to be on the floor I was on. Much to my surprise, I discovered I was not on the Executive floor at all. Back down to the front desk and was offered to move AGAIN!!!. I refused as we had already settled into the room we were already in.Between the first room and the second room, the key machine stopped working, so they had to escort people to their rooms and let them in only to have to stop at the desk later or the next day for keys. After returning from dinner, I stopped by the front desk to retrieve my keycard and went upi to my room to bed. When trying to unlock my door the key did not work. Back down to the front desk AGAIN !!! They re did the keys and they finally worked. 
I do understand that things happen that are beyond the control of the management, but with the exception of one person at the front desk named [NAME], everyone else was very unapologetic and uncaring about these issues. I also had mentioned in the morning that my bathroom sink stopper was not oprable and could someone take a look at it. That evening when we returned form a complete day of sightseeing, it still was never addressed. I brought it to the attention of Valerie at the front desk, who offered to send someone up right away. Thank you Valerie.
Overall, the hotel is nice, clean and updated. The rooms are comfortable and beds cozy. The location is only about a 10-15 min drive into center city and there are alot of dining options within walking distance of the hotel. I don't know that I would stay here again because of the issues that I experienced, but it is an ok place with free parking.

Stayed here for a week in January. The location is great, a block off Michigan Avenue, so you have great access to the "Magnificent Mile" without the noise and bustle of being right on the strip. Excellent restaurants and shopping are nearby. The room was very clean and quiet. Best of all, the staff was uniformly pleasant and competent. I would definitely go back.

I stayed for the first time at the Homewood Suites-Westchase on a recent business trip to Houston. I was very impressed by the room! What a comfortable, easy-to-work-in suite! The room had a nice living room, kitchen, separate bedroom and bath. The breakfast in the morning, which was free, was excellent and had everything from fruit and cereal to eggs, sausages/other meat, pancakes, bagels, juices, coffee, toast, etc. The workout area was better than average, as was the pool and spa. The price was in line with other hotels, and maybe even a little less expensive. The location has many choices to eat and shop within a close distance. The front desk was very helpful in arranging taxis. I will be back!

We had a fantastic stay. Everyone of the staff we encountered were extremely helpful and friendly. The hotel is located right next to Petco Park and we attended the Dodger/Padre game. We were in walking distance of the Gaslamp District, which was very convenient for meals and entertainment. We will recommend this hotel to anyone planning a visit to San Diego.

title_masked: Our stay at TownePlace Suites Downtown was very pleasant!
text_masked: Our stay at TownePlace Suites Downtown was very pleasant! We arrived at a late hour and had some hitches but Victoria at your front desk went out of her way to make our stay enjoyable. It is people like her and her attitude towards customers that make us feel welcome. Even our dog Twinkie had a memorable birthday and enjoyed the attention she got.

title_masked: Too trendy for me, but fantastic location
text_masked: My family and I recently stayed at this property for 3 nights per my teenage daughter's request. She and I had stayed before, and she wanted to stay there again. Property is best suited for hip 20 somethings, not really the older or younger crowd. Lobby is very club like at night on the weekends. We happened to be in town during the Padres/Dodgers series and so there were a lot of drunk patrons around the common areas. A lot. We stayed in a suite which was fantastic. I'm not crazy about the almost see through shower and toilet room, but we made do. Having a balcony was really nice too as we could see Petco Park very well. Having Mary Jane's onsite was also really nice. Food was good, and was nice to just walk downstairs to eat, especially when it was late and we had just checked in. Location is key with this property. It's in the heart of the Gaslamp District which means stores, restaurants, and bars are within blocks. It was really nice to be able to walk rather than having to take a cab everywhere. It's also walking distance to Horton Plaza for shopping, Ralph's for groceries, and Seaport Village for a little of everything. Hotel staff were extremely helpful and nice. I would stay here again even though it made me feel really old.

title_masked: Excellent location, stay at the Towers!
text_masked: Beautifully located in the city centre! Fifth Street runs parallel to it, second street up, whilst Centre Park is 10 mins walk. If you stay in New York and you do not have too much time this is the area you should try to book. We were upgraded to a Suite in the Towers and had a fantastic time there, it is not cheap but you feel you are part of history. The breakfast lounge in the morning was always busy and the selection is not very extensive however, there was always a choice of good quality pastries, breads, cereals, yogurth, fresh fruit, and smoked salmon. if you like eating the Sunday Brunch is recommended.

Upon check in, we were upgraded to a Presidential Suite!! What a beautiful room. Fresh fruit and bottled sparkling water awaited us. Huge room for NYC standards and bathroom was so beautiful and clean. Excellent shower pressure and hot. Beds were very comfortable and even had evening turndown service that made up the sofa bed for my son. Room also had wet bar and multiple spacious closets. Would definately stay here again. Will not dissapoint!

Two issues that tell you all you need to know about this hotel
1. Daily internet access 16.95
2. Mini bar empty - small bottle of mineral water 12.95. Told room service I would complain. "Do what you need to do".
Possibly one of the worst hotels I have ever stayed in.

This location works well for me. The room was large by NYC standards. All very comfortable with good linens. With advanced purchase, I got the room for $180 - unbelievable. The staff is super friendly and helpful, all of them. The two cons - elevators can be a bit slow and they charge $14 for Internet. I know, I should not complain with that rate. They had a fan in my room, see a previous complaint from someone else. I would definitely stay here again.

I'll start with the positives, and there were many. Great location. Loved the layout of the room. Super quiet. Automated check in was easy and efficient. I wanted to love, love, love the place. BUT, when it came to the little things that were meant to make the Yotel unique-- felt they dropped the ball. The galley on our floor (19) was a disaster. The coffee machine was constantly breaking down, and I ended up emptying the very dirty, very wet disposal tray myself several times in an (unsuccessful) attempt to get it working. Spoke with several people who had also called down to "Mission Control" to report problems-- but it remained problematic for all three days of our stay. The desk's suggestion to use a galley on another floor was less than satisfactory. I don't want to have to go from floor to floor in my leisure wear to get a cup of coffee. On our last night of a special celebration weekend, we opted to avoid the hyper loud lounge and enjoy a bottle of champagne in our room. Unfortunately, the bar would not let us have a couple of wine or champagne glasses to take with us-- offering us only plastic cups (which we already had available in the bathroom of our room). Disappointing. I've never had a hotel refuse such a simple request. At the end of the day, it's the little things that make a big difference. Probably won't return.

Our room was clean and relatively large. It's well-maintained. The included breakfast is fair, though the hot line appeared to be a step up in quality over the pre-made buffet. Good location. You can walk to a lot of places. It's a bit annoying that you have to take 2 elevators to get in and out each time. With a family of 4, this is a great option and we'd probably stay here again. Our relatives stayed at the Omni, and said our room was bigger, for what it's worth. One really bad thing is that they charge for wifi and it didn't even work in the bedroom.

Stayed here for three nights. Check in and out was quick. The establishment is nice with a tower and multiple smaller units. We reserved 5 rooms and the tower rooms are definitely nicer than the one in the 500 unit we had. All the rooms had an outdoor balcony or a lanai. There's also a refrigerator and coffee maker in all the rooms. It took us awhile to find ours as it was in the closet. The maids were very friendly and kept our rooms clean. The community areas were being mopped all the time. They rent peddle carts for two or four and we ended up renting 2-2 people one and a 4-people one for $85 an hour. It was really fun and a great way to peddle along the water and get a little exercise. The hotel location was great as well. You can catch the Sea World fireworks every night at 10 pm from your balcony and most attractions and places are only about 10-15 minutes away. One down side is the $32.00 a night parking that they charge.

We had a wonderful mini getaway for our 18th anniversary. We were greeted by the front desk staff with smiles. Nate was awesome and upgraded our room for us and provided us with complimentary cocktails and a free appetizer. The clams were incredible! The room was comfortable and nothing is better than a Westin Dreambed. We came home from our evening out and found a bottle of wine and a sweet note from Nate for our anniversary. Thanks Westin for helping make our anniversary special. We had a minor problem with our bill since we used Starpoints for a free night and Gentlejoy graciously assisted us with the adjustment. I would highly recommend staying as this hotel.

title_masked: Terrible hotel and is by far the worst Marriott I have ever seen.
text_masked: Was the worst experience I have ever had a a Marriott. I have been going to Marriott's for over thirty years and I have never complained before but after sending us to three different rooms that was supposed to have a balcony when the first two did not while never even offering to help with our bags that we personally had to haul around and then when we get a room with a balcony it oversees an boarded up abandoned house that looked like homeless people were living in. The worst part is I used 50,000 Marriott points to stay in this wreck of a hotel.

My family (including 2 little ones) loved this place. Location is a block from the Riverwalk. The place was super clean, the staff was friendly, but the room setup was what we loved. Perfect layout if you have kids...including the sound curtain along the beds so that the kids can sleep while we made breakfast in the kitchen. Would highly recommend...and will certainly look to stay there again on my next trip.

title_masked: Great hotel is a great location
text_masked:
I stayed one night at this hotel with my three children. When we walked in to the sleek, modern and hip lobby, my 11-year old said "this is not a hotel for kids" with a big smile on her face. The staff was great, they had cookies waiting in the room for all of my kids and had given me an upgrade as a Starwood Gold Member. We were on the 54th floor, and while the noise was there, it was hardly noticeable. My kids were out like the lights down below on Broadway. 
The location was great, but Times Square was a very crowded place that was a little overwhelming to my younger kids. However, the hotel was an oasis of hip calm.

title_masked: Great location for a charming hotel
text_masked: My room had a nice view of the city. It had also been renovated. The beds were most comfortable. The staff from the bellman to the maintenance people were very friendly. Very comfortable room. Would love a bathrobe in the room.

title_masked: This ranks in my top 2 worst places I've stayed
text_masked:
I should have stuck with my gut instinct and asked to see our room before signing anything. The only thing that didn't make it my worst stay was at least the other people staying weren't loud. Outlet covers exposed, carpet that was soild to the point of making my socks dark and smelly. A non smoking room that likely was converted the day before.
Dryer sheets on the A/C unit to try to resolve the smell. A fresh painted ceiling without replacing the yellow 1970's smoke detector. A clogging toilet, a broke table, a non working remote, with a on/off switch on the tv busted to the point you had to stick your finger into the tv to get it to go on and off.
FLAT OUT DISGUSTING! Owners should be ashamed of themselves honestly.

We thoroughly enjoyed our stay at the Michelangelo! We have been to NYC several times before, but this was our first time at this hotel. We are a family of 4 (kids ages 14 & 10) and we stayed in a room with 2 queen beds (not a suite). The room and bathroom were twice the size of the rooms in other hotels we have stayed during previous trips to NYC. Everyone had plenty of room to spread out. The big walk-in closet was another pleasant surprise - it was perfect for storing all of our empty suitcases, shoes, and shopping bags, so our room never felt cluttered. The decor was elegant and the room was spotlessly clean. The beds and pillows were very comfortable. The location was perfect - very convenient to theaters, restaurants, shopping, etc. but well-removed from the chaos of Times Square. We will definitely be back!

Very comfy beds, great breakfast Buffett, wine in the late afternoon, and delicious cookies at bedtime too! Beautiful place, friendly helpful staff. Great location--I could walk to the convention center in just 12 minutes.

"Retreat" being the key word. The hotel upgraded us from a 2 bedroom to a 3 bedroom suite. The suite was luxurious, comfortable and clean and a great hang-out for old friends to gather. The staff was very accomodating--from the valet, to the front desk, to the housekeeping staff. All appeared to truly want to provide whatever was asked of them. The pool area is lovely--weather did not permit us to get in the pool but did not stop us from having cocktails on the veranda! Location was very nice and within walking distance from a superb wine bar. The hotel paid attention to details with art work/furniture, landscaping and amenities. Although cost of room on high side but when sharing the cost with friends, the luxury was well worth it. 
Only criticism to the hotel was the hallway on 3rd floor tended to have a musty/smoky smell. The room did not have a musty or smoky smell at all.

My husband and I stayed at this hotel for a week whilst on vacation in Austin. The staff were polite and incredibly helpful when asking advice about where to visit in the city. The room was spacious and very clean. The bed was comfy than our own at home. We would definitely stay here again if we manage to visit Austin in the future!

title_masked: This is a great find in NYC
text_masked: Sure there are way more luxurious hotels in Manhattan. They also cost five times as much. For the money, this is a terrific value: the location is stupendous----1/2 a block from Central Park, four blocks from Lincoln Center. The rooms are small but comfortable. And it's quiet (especially on the back). The breakfast is the usual American dreck. But who cares: you're in a wonderful location in New York for less than $200/night!

I start by saying a very good hotel is made great by it's staff. The Swissotel is no exception. I must thank Rhonda in particular. Above and beyond. With a sold out hotel of CPAs and soccer players we never felt rushed with our dozens of questions and requests. Thank you from your new Rhode Island friends! You made a great city all the more enoyable.
The location is ideal for getting around the city by walking, cab, bus or rail. The rooms were spotless and well kept, the hotel fresh and airy (note this hotel has great air circulation systems, not one area was stale or stuffy and the room hvac it great). The lobby bar staff were attentive on all shifts and everyone smiled.
Our friends attending the conference said all continued through to their meeting services. 
I do not know if it is standard practice or an ooops but not having top sheets between you and the duvet on the beds was a minor inconvienence and rectified relatively quickly with a phone call. 
We will return to this wondeful city and most certainly will stay with this hotel again.

title_masked: Amazing experience, felt like it was my home!
text_masked: I had to travel to DC for 2 months for work. I stayed at the Embassy Suites every week. The staff was very curtious and helpful. The manager Rachel, really helped our whole group out with reservations and really made it a pleasant experience for us. The whole experience from the great breakfast and managers reception to the excellent service made it feel like a home away from home. If I ever need to go back to DC again, I will for sure be staying there!

The Marriott Copley didn't have anything particularly exciting about it, but it was in a good location, the staff friendly, rooms small but clean. I stayed for one night and it was convenient to the Hynes Convention Center. Breakfast in the Champions restaurant was very good.

We've been doing winter getaways at the Sofitel Water Tower for three years. We recommend the Prestige Suite. Beautiful marble bath with a bedroom and a large living room. Wow! This chain is French and modern in decor. You are walking distance from Michigan Avenue.

We pulled up to the front entrance and my son in law said I don't know it looks pretty seedy. My husband said well were only here for 1 night before our cruise. So we go in and the desk person kept changing our rooms finally he put us in the very back of the motel. My husband and son in law carried our cargo carrier in my daughter and son in laws room because my son in law didn't feel it would be safe if left on the car. Then we went out for dinner we were gone about 1 and 1/2 hours. When we came back my husband and I went to our room and daughter and son in law went to theirs. A minute later they knocked on our door and said there key card didn't work and they had to go to the front desk to get it reset. To make a long story short when they got back in there room all of our stuff had been robbed. We called the police and were still fighting it out. Windham Corp. or Ramada are both claiming no responsibility. Not a safe place to stay. The cops told us it was an inside job !!!!

I stayed at the Embassey Suites near the convention center in Washington DC. I want to mention a certain housekeeper who worked on the 12th floor where I was staying. Her name Is Delitia ( not sure of spelling). Well she is the best PR person an hotel can have. I didn't feel well one day, and told her not to clean my room, just give me some clean towels, which she did. A short time later she knocks on the door and hands me some soup, a can of ginger ale and bottled water. I was so touched and just wanted the hotel to know what a wonderful person she is.

We really loved being at the Roosevelt. We were there for 2 nights with a special deal through Booking.com. If it wasn't for this special price, we would not have had the chance to book here. The room was really nice and the furniture, bed and tv were all of high standard. The only negative would be the tiny bathroom where there is nowhere to put your things and only one person can use at a time, but everything else was so good, and it's a historic building so it was easy to forgive this. I must admit the staff at checkin were excellent! The two young ladies greeted us with smiles and were very informative and we felt very comfortable. I would looooove to go back again.

title_masked: nice hotel - great concierge - ok location
text_masked:
The intercontinental is nice we had a great room on the 14th floor with a slightly smoggy view of downtown la and the distant hollywood sign. The room was nicely fitted out everything was in good condition the bed was extremely comfortable. The pool was great with a good hot tub on a terrace at 2nd floor level. 
The conceirge was great really enthusiastic and gave us really helpful tips and maps. 
The location is ok it is practically in fox studios but a drive away from everything else westfield is a short walk away which has some ok places to eat. 
My only issues with the hotel that someone in the room below if above was smoking (it is a non smoking hotel) and the smell was getting into our bathroom the front desk were helpful but weren't able to stop the problem. It also wasn't mentioned on our check out nor were we asked if we had a good stay he just wanted us to check out. This was the only issue we had with the service though.
