The lobby and communal areas could do with an update maybe more modern lighting the exterior is not a great example of I guess late 70s early 80s architecture but not much you can do about that. 
Overall a good place to stay a bit out of the madness of la but probably not really close enough to the sites for a tourist

We liked our room. We were told it was a suite. Didn't feel like one (no fridge/microwave), but we were told NYC rooms usually are small. Beautiful hotel. One moring, we could hear alot of people talking just outside our door...The hotel obviously rented out the 2 rooms next to us to a law firm doing interviews. We had chairs in the hallway for the lawyers that were waiting for their interviews...weird. Why not put them in a conference room. We stayed here a week. The ice machine that had a sign on it when we arrived (ice machine to be repaired immediately) was never fixed. Long wait for elevators. Great location. Walked alot. Customer service...very friendly. I think we would stay here again.

Janette McCary and Manuel exceeded my expectaions upon arrival as a SPG member,made me feel like a VIP as I checked in.Service is very important in this business and these employees have show it!!!! The room upon check in was huge and the linens were awesome.

Like several other reviewers, we took advantage of a Living Social special and got a great deal. We don't live too far from DC, but were looking to enjoy a nice Spring weekend in the city. It really is a nice place to stay - good service, nice (but not spacious) rooms. It was a great start to arrive at the hotel and take advantage of their complimentary wine "happy hour". The included breakfast was nice too, although they seemed to be a bit behind in making sure everything was available. It was a truly enjoyable stay - exceeded our expectations... really turned out to be a great value in the city.
One additional tip that might help people who are looking to stay here is that if you have a car... parking at the hotel is expensive. We had luck finding street parking and we left and came back to the hotel a few times. It's a bit of a roll of the dice, but might be a good way to save some $$$. If you aren't driving, keep in mind that the Dupont Circle Metro stop is a pretty healthy walk away. The hotel is a BIT removed, but we actually really liked the location on a nice side street. We also really enjoyed walking around, but that wouldn't have been as enjoyable in July and August in this area.

First of all got a great online rate for our stay in January. I am sure peak summer season that the prices will be more expensive. This is a great hotel right on Michigan Avenue. About a block to the Chicago river. Walking distance to many great sites including all the MIchigan Avenue shopping, Millennium Park, multiple restaurants and bars. A little bit of a hike to Grant Park and the museums but not bad. Public transportation is close by with the L , bus service etc.. Very easy train ride to from O'hare. The Clark/Lake train stop is very close by and you can walk it or grab a cab if you have multiple bags. The train ride cost 2.25 per person each way. A cab or car service will run you 55.00 plus tip each way. The front desk was polite and helpful. Our concierge Scott was A+. I had some places I already knew about but he was spot on with his recommendations. We had a king corner room. Not sure the size difference with other rooms but it was big enough for our two person stay. No noise problems at all. The housekeeping service was great with daily cleaning. I didn't use room service or the hotel bar or restaurants. But the bar looked like it would be fun and busy on a weekend. Again if you can get a good rate then I see no problem staying at the Hard Rock Hotel in Chicago.

Had a great stay. Really good restaurant next door too (wonderful seafood). Rooms are really nice and clean. Great service. Good breakfast in the other restaurant connected to the hotel. Perfect location if you are visiting Boston University.

great place to stay for business or personal. The staff was more than helpful. very clean. this property is in a very convienant location will stay there again i would recommend to friends or any business traveler doing business in the dallas -ft worth area

title_masked: Perfect Chelsea hotel for business travel to NYC
text_masked: This is the perfect hotel and location if doing business near the Flatiron/Chelsea area. It is located very close to a subway line which can get you uptown or downtown in reasonable effort. The hotels is very clean and the staff was excellent when I was there. The room surprisingly was a good size and the bathroom was in good shape and size as well. For the business traveller who frequents the city it was the perfect balance for cost/comfort and was well kept. There aren't a whole lot of restaurant options near by but for me it wasn't an issue as I used it mostly to sleep and clean up after a days work. The price can fluctuate however, and not always is this the cheapest option.

The staff was very helpful with directions and answers to questions. I really would not consider the accommodations a suite, more like a large bedroom. However, it was convenient, clean, and the beds were very comfortable. I felt very safe walking at night in this area. It was approximately four blocks from the metro and two blocks from the DC circulator bus to Union Station. A Walgreens and CVS were close by. It was within walking distance of restaurants as well as fast food places.

title_masked: The Red Lion A Notch Above The Other Hotels
text_masked: Visiting Seattle we decided upon staying at The Red Lion Seattle Airport. A friendly staff welcomed you into a beautiful lobby. Our room was very spacious, the large kingsize bed's mattress was sooo comfortable and I woke up refreshed and not stiff. So many nice amenities refrigerator and microwave in the room.Very clean bathroom, hair dryer, ironing board, terrycloth bathrobes. The room price included breakfast, I mean a chef cooked buffet that was delicious with lots of variety and again very friendly staff. You cannot go wrong choosing the Red Lion it has reasonable rates that include a delicious and delightful breakfast. To top it off they have airport shuttles right outside the lobby that leaves for the airport every few minutes. We have told our family and friends what a great hotel this is.

This was our first time at a Cambria Suites and we were impressed at the overall decor of the common areas and the guest rooms. The hotel is convienently located next to the Polaris mall and there are many great restaurants in the area. The room was very functional with a separate sitting area to relax and watch TV, and a well furnished bathroom with a large shower. The only problem with the room was with the king size bed next to the wall, I kept tripping over the air conditioning unit. The lobby was large with plenty of seating and laid out efficiently with a bar and restaurant. Overall it was a comfortable night stay at a reasonable price.

We knew what we were getting before we arrived here, so we weren't surprised
The location is fantastic, a 5 minute walk to times square and so many nice bars and restaurants on the doorstep, as well as a grocery store and fast food places. The price is also fantastic
However, to get the location for the price I guess something has to give, and the hotel is very dated. The furniture is obviously pretty old, and the aircon units could be 50 years old, very very noisy. I have also never known a hotel where they want to come in and clean at 8am, and also knock as they walk in the room! We were nearly caught out a couple of times!
One other negative for me was the wifi. This was the third hotel we stayed in on our trip, and the first to charge for wifi. I thought $35 for 5 days was very steep, especially seeing as was locked to 1 device! Not ideal when a couple has 2 smartphones and an iPad!
A positive though was the staff, very friendly and they couldn't do enough for you

While the hotel is in a great location and has views of the river a friendly and helpful staff . I found the bathroom to be disappointing . The original plumbing fixtures(25-30 yrs old) still exists and needs to be updated. The toilet in our room was not bolted down to the floor and rocked back and forth when you sat on it. The shower had 2 heads and both had weak pressure, Sink had a crack down the middle and the vanity was the lower height of the 80s making it difficult for a taller person to bend to the sink. 
We had room 718 . This is could be a great property if they spent some money in the bathrooms.

The Hilton Hotel at University Place was a good experience. My room was spacious and comfortable. The bathroom sink area had enough counter space to put out my shaving gear and I didn't have to work off of a toilet top. The lobby bar serves both food and drinks and the food choice is similar to the dining room. John, the bartender, does a good job and knows how to mix drinks. I didn't eat in the dining room except for breakfast and it was the usual fare. There are a lot of restaurant choices in walking distance of the hotel that are good. This is a good place to stay for business trips in the Charlotte area.

Our family stayed here for the USA National Volleyball Championships and it rates as one of the worst hotel experiences we have ever had! It took almost 40 minutes to check in as there was only one staff member at the desk - and she was RUDE! The entire staff was very unpleasant and not willing to accommodate their guests. Our room was very outdated, smelled and we found condom wrappers under the bed and behind the night stands. The laundry machines were out of order and you had to go searching for an ice machine that worked as most were out of order and no attempt was made to have them fixed during our 5-day stay. The housekeeping service does not have enough linens to supply the hotel so they come and take everything (they took our pillowcases, towels, shower curtains, etc.) and we had to go down to the front desk DAILY to get our towels back. The breakfast is in an old shutdown restaurant and after the first morning, we refused to eat there. There was little selection and you had to wait for everything! One can get a better breakfast out of a vending machine or from a convenience store. Lastly, we have had to refute charges on our credit card statement with our credit card company as the hotel is unwilling to rectify improper charges (we were charged for a night we did not stay). If this is the only hotel with rooms left in Columbus, I would chose to sleep in my car or a tent before staying here again.

Just returned from a stay in San Francisco and stayed at the Parc 55. This wasn't our initial hotel, our initial hotel was under going renovations, so we were offered this hotel instead. Checked out some reviews on here before we went and there were a bit negative, which didn't instill me with confidence. However, the hotel was fine. The staff were great, the hotel was clean and the rooms were just as good. The hotel is located about a five minute walk from Union Square and there is a cable car stop just round the corner from it, and I mean just round the corner, about a minutes walk. This stop is the end of the line so you get to see them turn the cable cars around ready to set off in the opposite direction. As a result you have a better chance of getting a standing space on the front of the car, as these go straight away so if your getting on at a later stop all of the standing spaces will be gone. We never ate in the hotel as there are so many places around to go to, however the bar is good. The staff bring your drinks to the table for you so you don't even have to go to the bar, RESULT!!!!!!!! San Francisco is a great place, if you go I would definately go to Alcatraz, the trip is fantastic. I would book before you go to make sure you get tickets as it's extremely popular. I would recommend buying a "CityPass" as well. This gives you entry to 6 attractions and lets you ride on the cable cars and trams for a period of 7 days. It costs about £40, but when you think a single ride on the cable cars costs 6 dollars each, which equates to about £3.70ish, it's well worth it. Not sure why anyone would write a negative comment about the Parc 55 as I thought it was fine. The hotel is also used by a number of airlines which must say something about the standards they set. If I ever go back to San Francisco I would certainly stay here again.

I have visited Chicago for the past few years at this time, December for the hustle and bustle of city life and the Christmas decorations etc. I again stayed at the top class Palmer House Hilton Hotel on 17 East Monroe and State Street. An excellent hotel within easy reach of Theatre Land and Macy's (formely Marshall Fields's) and all the downtown shopping etc. The foyer of this hotel is worth having a look at even if you are not staying there, the ceiling is a masterpiece. Its a huge lobby. I arrived at approximately 6.30pm and I had a quick run through reception and was given my room on the 11th. floor.The room was warm and cosy and very nicely decorated. It was at the back of the hotel and it was very very quiet. The bed was cosy and very comfortable. I had breakfast each morning and I must say it was great value for money. The full buffet breakfast including tax came to $23. It was a great breakfast. I found the staff very helpful and very courteous each time I visited the hotel. I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone visiting Chicago especially if it is their first time. It is beside almost evrything you would hope to see on a visit to the "Windy City"

Yea the elevators are small and slow sometimes. But it has a superb location. Complimentary breakfast and wifi makes the price unbeatable. The stuffs were very friendly and informative. Rooms are clean. definitely will go back.

This is our second stay at the Millenium in a year. Last year was bit of a bust. This year we were assigned a club room in the Premier section next to the main hotel. 
There is a seperate check-in area for this portion of the hotel. It is more European in style: sleek & contemporary. The room and bath were quite large. The room had lots of windows and a full length couch in the room. The bath had a nice soaking tub separate from the shower. Daily complimentary continental breakfast and happy hour on the mezzanine. This portion of the hotel is much quieter and more serene than the main hotel. The Mellennium is well located just a block off Broadway, smack dab in mid-town. 
My only complaint with this hotel is the cleanliness of the room - particularly the bathroom. The shower is small with sleek limestone tile. However, the caulking was peeling away and partially blackened with mold. The tile was badly stained as was the shower curtain. The vanity had a sleek glass top which highlighted the residue around the sink lip. Makes you wander what else is there. The couch had burn marks and I always wander about those decorative pillows! The platform bed was quite comfortable, but the bottom and top sheet refused to stay tucked.
This is a good hotel for the location and the price, but the cleanliness issue needs be resolved. 
We were a couple staying for business and personal.

We took our 5 month old on her first trip to Chicago and didn't want to bring her travel crib since we were flying. I had heard horror stories about the cribs hotels offer, so had low expectations. But the Westin was great, we told them at check-in that we needed a crib, and a beautiful Heavenly Crib was delivered to our room within 15 minutes. It was clean, safe, and stylish. My baby loved it and slept like a dream. They also gave us a handicap accessible room which was quite large, and it was easy to roll around the crib into the hallway or a quiet corner while she was sleeping so we could still keep the lights on and move around without disturbing her. The hotel overall was great, very clean and modern rooms, wonderful lobby and fantastic location!

A co-worker and I stayed at the hyatt for the Chicago Hairshow at McCormick Place. I couldnt have been more pleased with this hotel. They were able to store our luggage while we went to the show and called us when the room was ready. The bellman was cordial and informative. The people at the desk cheerful. The room was comfortable and inviting. The beds were very comfortable, the pillows awesome and the room spic and span clean. Hairdryer, coffeemaker. There was a gift shop as you walked in, also a convenience area to purchase coffee, juices, cereal and such on the run. I did not go to the bars or restaurants while I was there. The concerge suggested a great Mexican restaurant not far that was outstanding and only a short cab drive away. The hotel is centrally located, we went to Howl at the moon that evening which was great fun and Rosebud Trattoria for dinner. Perfection! Cant say enough about this great hotel. They treat you like a queen.

We stayed here one night over the veterans day weekend. Simply put - the rooms are old and filthy. There is no excuse for a hotel chain of this magnitude to allow the conditions of there hotel rooms to become like this. We went to three different rooms and all of the rooms had a yucky old wet mildew smell to them. The carpet was dirty, the beds were lumpy, the hallway carpet was dirty, and staff appeared unconcerned. And to put the nail in the proverbial coffin...We were offered free breakfast (which was a very nice gesture on the part of the morning manager), however, we couldnt get anyone to take our order in the restaurant they were no where to be found. Very dissappointing!

I found this hotel while researching for my trip to San Francisco. This deal was an absolute bargain, as we only paid about $100 per night, which included FREE parking. The hotel is walking distance to Fisherman's Wharf, Lombard St, Telegraph Hill, Chinatown and plenty of restaurants. I normally stay in main brand hotels while traveling on business, such as Hyatt or Marriott, and I was a little skeptical about staying here, but the beds were nice, flat-screen TV was nice, bathroom was just fine, and parking was free. I have to mention that twice, as most hotels charge $30-40 minimum on parking in Fisherman's Wharf or Union Square areas. I'd rate this hotel a 4.5 rating if I could.

title_masked: Great location and good value for the $$
text_masked:
We stayed here for 4 nights while exploring the Indianapolis area for pleasure. The hotel is located in a busy shopping and business area but tucked away in a quiet corner. There are numerous restaurants within a short drive and/or walking distance from the hotel along with the shopping mall accross the street.
I have somewhat mixed feelings about the hotel itself. The staff as mentioned before was very friendly and accommodating. Our room was not ready when we arrived at 4:30pm on a Saturday but the desk clerk brought me over to the room to check on its status where we found it in process of being cleaned. One of the manager's was helping clean the room and he was very apologetic. Fortunately it only took about 15 minutes before the room was ready. However after we got in the room and started to unpack we found one of the window sills covered in cigarette ashes and I had to go find the cleaning staff to come back. We later noticed that the sofa had not been vacuumed and noticeable areas of dusk on some of the tables. One of the 2 TV remotes was missing which never did get replaced during our stay.
Our room was large with 2 bedrooms, 1 bath, living room and full kitchen. Very nice layout and spacious but pretty basic with some signs of wear and tear in our room and overall the cleaning was not as good as it should be. The next day after being out all day we returned to the hotel around 4:30pm to find our room had still not be cleaned . We asked the cleaning staff down the hall about our room and they complained that they had many rooms yet to clean. We ended up going out for an early dinner so the room could be cleaned which was finally done when we arrived back around 7pm. The hotel was full the night before but was not full the next day, so I find no excuse why our room could not have been refreshed earlier in the day. I mentioned this to the manager at the desk the next morning and she was rather dismissive. Our room though was cleaned by mid-day the next day. 
The property feels more like a suburban apartment complex rather than a hotel. The breakfast was very basic with cereals and packaged muffins and only 2 tables in the small lobby where people can eat. We opted to go out and buy our own healthier breakfast items and eat in the room. 
All in all a good value for the money especially if you like more room to spread out and a full kitchen. Definitely not a luxury property.

title_masked: Don't let the name fool you
text_masked: This place is nowhere near Sea World. Its right off the interstate, among some old car dealerships. I think the hotel used to be an office building. Otherwise, the service was OK at best.

title_masked: Art Deco Cocoon in Grunge Broadway
text_masked: Cosy cocoon to cuddle in the most comfortable quilted bed, riding freely Amsterdam bicycles by the silver Hudson River, Sipping Singapore Slings on the roof terrace feeling like the Fitzgeralds for one evening, Bathing in Argan fragranced foamy bath after a day of saturated senses in Chelsea, homely tasty breakfast served by the sweetest and most attentive staff in the opulent art deco Veranda, it makes me all gooey inside just writting about it; just like the best chocolate souffle; there is never enough of it.

It was our youngest daughters 18th birthday and as a last family holiday (we reckon) we decided to go to New York for the week. We could not have chosen a better hotel to stay in. We were greeted by Shane, the General Manager, with a warm Irish welcome. That set the tone of the holiday in Fitzpatricks, we were made feel so much at home and nothing was too much bother. Special thanks to Chris , Jessica, Leo and Peter for making our trip so memorable. We will certainly be back!! Neil and Maria Quinn

From check-in to check-out the staff at 6 Columbus was top notch. The property reminded me of a stay in a boutique hotel in South Beach Miami. I booked with an internet travel site for a last minute deal, and was supposed to move to a different hotel for the last two days of my stay. I enjoyed the first night so much, I asked if they had availability to extend, and they did, so I cancelled the other stay. The location is amazing, at the top of W 58th just as you enter Columbus Circle. It was an easy walk to Times Sq/Broadway and Hell's Kitchen resturants, A subway stop is directly across the street. 
I was in a king room and did not find the room to be loud from street noise as I have in past NYC hotels. Also found the room size to be bigger than what I normally expect from NYC. Room was nicely decorated, not over the top with a good color scheme. The heated floor in the bathroom was a nice surprise. Be sure to check out the roof deck, it wasn't open for the season for service, but was open to sit and work from, it was a nice quiet "retreat" from a busy day of work. 
As others have mentioned the restaurant is supposed to be amazing, but it was full each night I wanted to try it. People waiting to go in did also rave about the food. 
The staff can truly make or break your experience, and as mentioned in the opening they were just amazing. Welcoming you back each time you returned, and consistently checking to make sure everything was top notch.
I'll be sure to return.

who'd expect a rotating restaurant in Indianapolis; great price fixed menu option; I had the halidbu twith lemon beurre blanc with crab - - TEN shoudl seel that toppign TY ITSELF!!!!
Great staff; felt very welcomed at dinner.
Hotel under construction, cavernous interior, not quite hit yet, but in the best location to get to the convention center. Nice enough room, delicious shower head and friendly room service. Good, peaceful sleep ..and thankfully a Pepsi property!

Got to stay at this hotel through Groupon! Great deal 2 nights, 2 breakfasts and 2 Museum Tickets. Was a great deal and would do it again. This hotel has a secret gem with the roof garden and lounge! Free coffee and tea 24 hours, free wifi and friendly staff. Very Nice!

We stayed at the Joule last weekend for my best friend's bachelorette party. The first thing that went wrong, is they told us that they werent going to allow us to bring in our own alcohol to the room, even after I had called and was told that was fine. They offered us a free bottle of champagne to be sent up to the room, which of course never showed up. The next day we were laying by the pool on the couch/bed things, and were told that people wanted to rent them for $200 so we had to get off. They ended up renting everything out there to people so there was NOWHERE else to sit unless you wanted to be in the pool. Don't charge me $400 for a room per night and then expect me to pay $200 to sit by the pool. ridiculous. We requested ice to ice down our cooler full of sodas and they said there was no ice machine so sent us up ONE bucket of ice. Don't think that did any good at all. When we ran out of toilet paper, we had to call twice to get some sent to us, and at which point they sent us ONE roll of toilet paper. The day we were leaving we asked that a luggage cart be sent up. We asked that it just be left outside our room so that we could load it as we go, but they arent allowed to do that- because they want us to tip them. all they want is MORE MONEY! The staff was very friendly, and I knew that it wasnt their fault that all of these policies had been put in place, but it's a customer-serving business people! So whoever did come up with all these rules needs to re think their policies! I will not stay there again- not worth paying that much money for having to obey such strict rules.

title_masked: Great Location! Wonderful Staff & Clean Hotel. Great Service.
text_masked: If you like casual dining and taking in a movie, this is the place for you. There is a Tinseltown Movie Complex right next door, as well as a fabulous restaurant, 7 Bridges Brewery. Also located within walking distance are several other casual restaurants, including Ale House, Hooters, The Tilted Kilt, The Mellow Mushroom, and T.G.I. Fridays. There are several fast food choices as well. The hotel was clean and the staff was very friendly and helpful. I would love to go back when the weather is warmer and take a swim in the small pool and relax in the sun. It is a lovely little setting. Will return ASAP!

title_masked: Nice stay at the Lakeway Resort and Spa
text_masked: We checked in on Friday 28 Sep 2012. We arrived a little earlier than the regular check in time of 4:00 pm and were allowed to check in early. The clerk at the desk was very efficient and friendly and the whole registration process probably took about 2 minutes. We had reserved a "hill side view" room with king size bed. The room was a nice size and clean. We had a nice deck however, I should have sprung for the "lake view room" as the "hill side view room" had a view of the parking lot. Not what I had pictured in my mind. The view of the lake is very pretty though. The free wireless internet is very slow. There was a flat screen tv which did not have a good picture and there were no high def channels. And there were only about maybe 15 channels. On Friday night when we returned to our room we found the the light over the bath room sink had burnt out. It was late so we did not request it to be fixed until Saturday morning. It was fixed upon our return on Saturday. The hot water handle on the bath room sink also leaked. We ate at Josie's restaurant for breakfast on Saturday morning. Thought the breakfast buffet was rather spendy for $14.95 and thought the food was just ok. On Sunday evening we ate at Josie's again and it was very good. I had the chicken fried steak which was excellent and my husband had the pork chop which was excellent as well. We did not utilize the spa services or the pool, or hot tub. I thought it was very quiet, the bed was comfortable and we slept very well. We did not use the concierge or the valet services. There is a very small gift shop which did not have anything in it that I could live without. We checked out on Monday morning and received very quick and efficient service once again. Everyone was very friendly at the resort. All in all, I enjoyed our stay at the Lakeway Resort and Spa. I would consider staying here again if the opportunity arises.

Hotel appears very new and spotless. The room was large with a full kitchen, sitting room and separate bedroom. Two large screen tv's and good work area. We were here for business and my wife was able to shut the door and go to sleep when I had to work late. Free breakfast in the morning was very good with hot foods, omelet bar and typical cold food selection. Location is great for downtown Charlotte. Would definetly recomend for anyone in the area. They offer valet parking, but cheaper to just park accross the street in open lots. Outdoor pool is nice feature if you want to be outside since most hotels in area seem to have only indoor pools.

Was there with my family from 3/1 till 3/3. Decent hotel, although room is small, we expected that, no complain. Everything is good, we had good time. Want to thank the housekeeping lady, Yong is her name? She was really helpful and friendly. We had a baby and she was very considerate and flexible with our time. She did everything very gently so that she would not wake the baby up. 
The toilet was clogged and we made a call to front desk. Help was sent up in less than 10 minutes and the technician solved it real fast. He is friendly and nice too. 
We requested a refrigerator to store baby food, and the fridge was sent promptly too. Great service.
The only drawback maybe is the location, I think the next door Adult DVD stores are a big eye sore. Other than that, it is great. Location is good - convenient.

Was here for 4 nights for a business conference. The weirdest thing about this place is that it is in a parking lot, off a highway with nothing nearby. The hotel has a free shuttle for a 5 mile radius and the only places it takes you are other strip malls. I had the feeling Dallas had become the land of the body snatchers.

The nearby options included the standard chains in Copley Square. Compared to these large impersonal, corporate hotels, the Eliot is more like a hotel in Paris. What you get is a hotel in an historical type building, set back in a real neighbourhood, on a tree lined street, nearby the trendy Back Bay area. While there may not be a fitness centre, tuck shop or large lobby, all one does is take ten steps outside and you have everything close by in the neighbourhood. Contrast this with Copley Square - escalators, 30 story towers, concrete everywhere, another mall containing all the same chain stores you know.
Both options are worthy, but the Eliot brings you closer to the feel of living in Boston. The choice is yours.

title_masked: As basic as hotels can come... and beware of the noise coming from the hallways
text_masked:
This hotel is really the bare bones minimum when it comes to in-room amenities. The bed is a decent size but it leaves almost no space for anything else. When I arrived in the room it smelled moldy so I needed to air out the room for over an hour before being tolerable. Also, the biggest problem with the room is that since the rooms are jampacked together, the door does not reduce outside noises. I was awoken at 8AM when the staff or other tenants were roaming the hallways or going in and out of rooms. Also, the doors basically slam shut after being opened so I was constantly hearing the doors opening and closing. 
The wifi and complimentary breakfast is nice but doesn't justify the disturbance. The only benefit to staying in this hotel is its relatively lower price and great location. There are several hotel choices nearby and I would probably stay elsewhere .............

We had booked two rooms for four people under one reservation. Found the hotel easily, and the location is excellent. However, when we got to the hotel, it turned out that the water had been turned off, and wouldn't be on for several hours; difficult, but no choice but to deal with it. The air conditioner in our room sounded like a 747 engine (sounds as though a bearing in the fan is going bad); we could stand it for one night, but any more than that would have driven us crazy. You could hear the window unit air conditioner from outside of our room standing in the hallway, it was that noisy. After running the water for minutes when we got back to the room, it continued to be brown. We used bottled water to brush our teeth. Finally, when we went to check out, they had added a $1.00 safe-usage fee to our bill. We complained, as we had never used the safe, and the charge was removed. On the second room, it turned out that my sister was overcharged in some confusion about overnight parking. Calls to the hotel have failed to get a returned call to straighten things out. We will look for another hotel next time in Baltimore.

We always stay here - price is on the higher end, but you do indeed get what you pay for. Compared to other hotels with comparable prices (or higher) I have to say this is the best I've ever been to. Great restaurants on the property as well.

title_masked: Great location in the heart of Chicago!
text_masked:
We've stayed in a lot of different hotels in Chicago, and this hotel is always a solid choice.
The good: a nice sized suite that was very comfortable for a family of four. Location is just a block off Michigan - close to hopping, restaurants, the beach. Price isn't bad for a suite in downtown Chicago.
The not so good: parking is outrageously priced, especially since we didn't use our car the whole time we were there. Lack of dining options at the hotel. There is one restaurant, and it was not terribly impressive. We had a bit of issue at the very end of our visit with left us with a pretty poor impression of the staff, with the exception of the director of security.
In general, it's a a pretty good choice for an affordable family stay in Chicago.

title_masked: I will be returning....If i get the chance
text_masked:
I just stayed here for a weekend with friends. Overall, the service was outstanding. Although this is a boutique hotel, they satisfy all of your needs and are efficient. We checked in at around 11pm. The front desk agent was great and checked us in very quickly. When we got up to the room, we were very happy to see the size of the room (we had the guestroom with a workout bike section). The bathroom is small but with the sink outside it functions better. Two queen beds, i home, 42 inch flat screen tv, separate desk area mini room- this room is all you can need for a weekend.
The location is tremendous- next to dupont circle. For younger crowds, there is all you could possibly want. For sightseeing it may be a little far. We took a cab to the national mall, which took around 15 minutes on a saturday. Nightlife is all around that area and many good restaurants of many cuisines to choose from. 
We did not visit the restaurant but it did seem full for breakfast and dinner. 
One other side bit: In the mid afternoon and early evenings they had a reception of some sort for the guests with free drinks in the lobby, which was a nice touch after a day of sightseeing. 
Why i am not giving it 4.5 or 5 stars:
I booked my room on expedia with the room type of 2 queen bed balcony. However, upon check in the agent informed me that room types are not guaranteed. He did seem to try and accomodate me when he could. He apologized and said he can offer me that room type for my second night there. I said no because of the hassle of repacking, etc. It was just a little frustrating to be expecting a nice balcony to wake up to and instead waking up to a view of the alleyway. 
Parking: Around that area, it seems difficult to find a spot on the street so we did the valet parking with the hotel. The price was a killer 41 plus tax! That seems a little high but i guess we chose to do it.

title_masked: If you want to be in the Times Square area, this is the place to stay!
text_masked: This is one of the nicest hotels due to the high level of friendly service offered by every employee that I dealt with. This hotel is located in the heart of Times Square putting you just steps from where the action is. Nice restaurant with an exceptional, although a bit pricey breakfast buffet. Nice, trendy bar overlooking Times Square, if you're into that, as well.

Here's a list of the BAD...
Staff, Room Service, Bar, Pool, Rooms are dirty and worn, Front Desk, Security, pretty much the entire hotel itself and everyone that worked there.
Good List...
Nothing, there's nothing good to say about this hotel. The balconies are pretty nice I guess. But I wouldn't pay what I paid just for a nice balcony.
Tips for management: Find new staff and renovate as soon as possible or go bankrupt. And management should probably be replaced because they are obviously not doing their job by hiring the right people or training them correct customer service etiquette. 
Word to the front desk employees: You work at a hotel, wake up, you are not any better than anyone else so stop treating people like you are.
Summary: Stay at the new Omni hotel in Dallas or Hotel Zaza don't stay here.

Check in was easy, and went smoothly. The manager, Susana, was very helpful and kind. Room service was prompt and accurate. The room was beautiful and clean, and the bed was very comfortable. Everything worked well. Front desk staff (a woman on the evening of 9/18), was rude when I called on one occasion (after being transferred 3 times and hung up on once), but did eventually get me what I needed.

Having stayed in a great many hotels in a great many locations, I was delightfully surprised by the thoughtful courtesy shown by Hotel Palomar staff when I stayed at their Westwood location. Not only were staff able to answer any question presented, they did so cheerfully. How lovely to be treated like a guest!

This is the best inexpensive hotel I have found in the Tempe / airport area. It’s certainly not fancy, but for the price it’s very nice. All the rooms are two-room suites that open onto an outdoor courtyard with a pool and sitting area. There are suites nicer and pricier than the one I had. The living room has a sleep sofa, overstuffed chair, dresser, large full-length mirror, large screen TV, and a bar with microwave, sink, and fridge. No dishes, by the way – it seems there should be at least some dishes. 
The bedroom area is as large as most hotel rooms in the area, with a dresser, large TV, sink, and free-standing wardrobe. There are four pillows per bed, two of which are clearly labeled “Firm” and two “Soft”. (As a lover of firm pillows, I really appreciate this.) As others have noted, the bathroom is teeny. If I were trying to sleep a family in this suite, or perhaps my spouse and another couple, the small bathroom would probably be an issue. But with just one person, no big deal. 
On the downside: When I arrived, the room was (ahem!) not fully supplied. No problem – until two days went by without being replenished. Housekeeping came promptly when I called.
I gave this hotel 4 stars. If the management and staff would “pick it up” just slightly, I’d gladly go to 5 stars. And I will be back. It’s nice. Really.

title_masked: A great hotel on Pacific Beach
text_masked: We stayed here Oct 14th after a stay at Disneyland and LegoLand. This hotel is extremly nice, and the hotel staff are very elpful and very courteous, attending to any of our needs. The location of this hotel is easy to find even though it is right on Pacific Beach. We drove here and arrived earlier than expected due to good traffic, the staff was more than helpful getting checked in early to our room, at 11:30am. We expected to have to store our surtcases and wonder if our room would be ready when we got back from LegoLand. It was nice to drop our stuff off in a beautiful room, and take a quick look see at the patio and pool area. Our first floor room had a partial ocean view and the patio let right out into the courtyard and pool area with easy access to the key carded back gate and pool area. The staff was more than helpful getting us a couple of beach chairs and boogie boards for my son and I. Plenty of towels for hte beach and a short walk down the stairs had us on the beach in less than 5 mnutes. The beds were excellent, but the bed frames were fully surrounding the bed, something that we did not expect, and took some getting used to in getting in and out of bed. The bathroom was very roomy and very clean with ample storage for your personal gear and bath towels for four people. We had a complimentary glass of wine the second night, and had a couple more drinks at the bar during happy hour. The bar serves as the breakfast eating area and is the only low point of the hotel. This hotel does not have a full service kitchen or bar, but makes an excellent Lon Island Iced Tea, the best I have tased in years. This hotels location allows a quick 15 minute walk into "town" or down the street to have some lunch. We went out for sushi for lunch and found lots of places and freindly people in Pacific Beach. Kind of makes me want to visit again and just do the beach thing, swim, boogie board and eat out, a great vacation. I would recommend this hotel to anyone wicshing to stay at Pacific Beach and checking out the local sites / eateries.

Charming Hotel - it is a bit older but has aged very well. The room was spacious and clean. No odd "hotel smells". They need more plug outlet's especially near the bed. I use my phone as my alarm and I have an iPod but there wasn't an open plug at all by the nightstand. The one plug on the lamp had the radio plugged into it --- very frustrating.
The bathtub was a plastic "fit over" piece on the original tub. So it felt and looked very cheap. The hotel staff was very nice and eager to help out with everything.
There is a restaurant in the lobby that serves french cuisine. 
The key to this hotel is it's location, location, location. It is right across from the Prudential Center Mall, the Cheescake Factory, PF Changs and a Seafood place -Legal Seafood- yummy.

I was in town for Gen Con and the Indy Fringe Fest, a good week and a half, and wanted some place comfortable and convenient to stay. This Super 8 fit the bill to a "T." The price was just right, especially considering just how much the other hotels in the area jacked up their prices for the MotoGP that same weekend. The location was good, too, what with the number of restaurants within a five-minute drive, as well as a Wal-Mart next door and quick access to 65 and 465. The free breakfast was pretty good, especially the waffles. (What can I say? I like waffles!) The hotel is very clean and well maintained by a staff that's friendly and very conscientious. When I called them months before, I asked how often they cleaned the rooms of longer-term guests. The lady told me every other day, but from the looks of my room, I'm guessing they cleaned it every day. This was very cool and very impressive, considering that the year before I had stayed at the nearby Motel 6 for about the same length of time and all they did was toss in some clean towels -- once. One thing that really surprised me was the mini-fridge in the room, a nice, clean, quiet fridge. I asked them about it and they said that, given just how long I was going to be staying with them, they put it in there at no extra charge. It was just too cool of them. I think my only ding on the place was the one day I had planned on sleeping in late, they called about 10am, asking if I wanted my room serviced that day; never mind that I had a Do Not Disturb sign on the door. Next time, I'll just mention it to the front desk.
I have every intention of staying with them again next year. Thanks again, Super 8 -- South Emerson! You're one of the best!

title_masked: Hotel Palomar - great hotel in downtown Phoenix
text_masked: I have been traveling to Phoenix on business on occasion for several years and have always stayed at the Hyatt when in downtown Phoenix. This week our group tried the Hotel Palomar, opened earlier this year - loved it! The staff was very welcoming and helpful, the wine hour from 5-6 is a great touch and the restaurant was great. Also very centrally located to other restaurants and venues in downtown Phoenix. Would highly recommend. Instead of breakfast in the hotel would recommend the Breakfast Club right next door - similar menu for half the price. And Gold's Gym is free for all hotel guests.

The hotl staff is wonderfull, the food in the Concierge lounge is the best I have had at any Marriott! Tuesday nights are the best when the Chef turns himself loose and gets creative. The hotel is convenient to all transportation, minutes away from the Hudson River walkay along Battery Park, and Tribeca is a short walk as well.

Awesome place! Perfect for my husband and I who were out most of the day exploring. Yes, the rooms are small but they are clean with a mini kitchen so you can do some of our own cooking/breakfast. You could also use the washing machines for free. We stayed for 2 weeks and didn’t mind the once a week cleaning. You can ask for fresh towels from reception. They also had DVD’s to watch free of charge which was fantastic. The free coffee down stairs was a life saver. I thought the location was excellent – just around the corner to Times Square and walking distance to the subway. Staff were friendly. Didnt hear any noise during our entire 2 week stay. Overall I have don’t have anything negative to say. Would recommend to family and friends.

There are a number of us from different companies who stay here regularly (most of us very picky). We stay because of the service. I have found the front desk always willing to help. On the 9th floor service area, Jennifer is extremely helpful. I stay here by choice and enjoy it and the staff is responsible for that.

Wow. GREAT hotel. I recently spent a night at Hotel Monaco with some friends as part of a girls night out/birthday celebration and I don't think I can stay in a "regular" hotel again. This place is extremely cool with funky/contemporary decor and is right in the heart of things however, we all know what makes one store or restaurant or hotel better than others...service. From the moment we drove up to the valet, we felt like stars. The valet and doormen, super nice. The front desk staff, super nice. We waited a little longer than expected for our rooms to be ready, so they upgraded us, super nice. The rooftop bar, again, super nice. But here was the real kicker for me...I left something of value in our hotel room and the housekeeping staff turned it in. SUPER NICE.
I can't rave enough about this hotel. It is new, so I hope it can keep up the good work!!!

The Rancho Bernardo Inn is just beautiful ! We had a wonderful room and it seemed like the amenities were endless - a spa, golf course, multiple pools, fountains galore, restaurants, gift shops and a coffee house. 
Evenings were a treat. We had happy hour and dinner al fresco at the Veranda which overlooks an impressive golfcourse. The Veranda also has an outdoor fireplace and all kinds of comfortable seating; we didn't want to leave ! Add in the lantern lighted paths and the serene sounds of trickling fountains which made it all enchanting. 
A short drive to beaches, wineries, mountains, downtown Gaslamp, San Diego harbor, Wild Animal Park, Zoo and Seaworld. Perfect for the family!

We selected the hotel as it was rated four star and it was our last night of a long trip and we had an early flight. First, the Sheraton employees were respectful, passionate and determined to please us from the front desk, to the ONE bell man to maintenance, but it stopped there. Again, the employees were great, its the executive management that's obviously incompentent. There was ONE overworked bellman and no carts available so we hauled all our bags manually to the first room (Note: in an alleged four star hotel). We entered and it literally smelled like somebody had thrown up in the room, which we believe was the case given the clients in a "conference" at the time that should have been in a "low rent" hotel as they were "low class" and known per an honest employee for wrecking the place. We went down and they moved us to another room which was acceptable, but still quite worn. The hotel showed considerable wear and tear on the walls, poor calk work, stained tile, stained carpet....etc. I'd honestly give it a 1 star and my family and I would sooner sleep in a snow storm without heat in a 65 VW van on I-95 rather than stay there again. Skip it, save $50 and stay at the Motel 6!

The staff is absolutely great, they are extremely friendly. They have shuttles to the airport and to the medical district. The pool is nice but there's no hot tub. You have to walk a little ways to the elevator. The rooms are also very nice as well. It's only downfall is it's location. If you are there for medical reasons it's a five minute drive. Also it's right on a busy street which is sometimes hard to pull out into. We've stayed there twice now. I would go again but it's easier to stay at hotels that are in walking distance of MD Anderson. Oh, also the zoo, bass pro and the galleria aren't all to far away either. Also great movie and game selection, with no rental charges.

Spent 3 days in The Big Apple. Stayed at the Paramount which is a half block off Times Square. Very convenient to theatres and museums. Walked to most events with relatively short taxi rides to others.
Hotel recently refurbished. Clean and vibrant place with reasonable rates for NY. Total cost for 3 nights $750. 
Room small, as in very, but nicely decorated with a few signs of it's old age on the door jams. Don't bring a large suitcase as the standard room won't accomodate two of you and two large suitcases very well! 
Handy breakfast spot off the lobby at Dean & Deluccas- again reasonable, for The City.

I've stayed in plenty of hotels...some worse, many better. This one is worth writing about. We arrived on the shuttle after waiting 25 minutes...and the hotel is less than 10 from the airport. Check in was really fast...but that euphoria was short-lived. The room had NO toilet paper on two holders. We later discovered no cups. Then my trip to the hot tub was a big disappointment as the water was pool-warm (maybe 85 degrees). The desk did knock off 5 bucks from our bill, so I was not too unhappy until I returned two days later. THIS time, one of the beds had dirty sheets (human hair and a stain on the sheet), and a broken drapery pull. The wait for a shuttle was over 40 minutes and when it did arrive, it was stuffed full and the driver was extremely rude (replying, "so?" when I said we had been waiting for over a half-hour). We were eventually picked up after 50 minutes. The building is starting to show its age, but the service is what is really poor.

Stayed for 4 nights. Very pleased with the location.Rooms are very small, but adequate. Also, all was very clean. Good beds. Pillows needed some help. Staff friendly. Very nice Library Bar. Would stay there again.

This hotel was absolutely filthy. The only thing decent about it is the location. The bed was horribly uncomfortable, the sheets were dingy and stained and I had to sleep with a jacket over the pillow. There was also a dirty and stained couch crammed in the corner that you couldn't sit on, the bathroom sink and taps looked like they had never been cleaned. There were several burnt out light bulbs and the shower head is so low it hit me in the shoulder blades and I am only 5'9". The owner was also very rude and check in took forever because he apparently has no interest in decent customer service. I would never recommend this hotel to anyone.

This hotel is directly across the street from the Galleria, and convenient to the major freeways. It has a modern feeling, with a very tasteful and pleasant lobby. My room was large, very large, with a separate living and working area with a sofa, coffee table and large television. There were connectors for all kinds of electronic devices, but all I used were the electrical outlets for my computer. The bed was very comfortable. 
My only gripes were minor: 1. My door was cracked and did not close easily, making me a little uncomfortable about the lock. This did not quite fit with the upscale tone of the hotel. 2. The workout room was just a small, too-warm, kind of dimly lit room, with no climate control available. Outdoor running routes were limited. 3. They did not have soy milk for my coffee in the morning.

This reasonably priced hotel is in a good location in the Loop, great for sightseeing. Our room was nicely decorated and comfortable. The breakfast was quite good and the pleasant breakfast room had big windows overlooking the street.
The hotel is close to the Blue Line train, with direct service to O'Hare airport.

As per a lot of other reviewers, we chose this hotel for an overnight stay between flights to/from LAX. This hotel was a great choice for our needs. 
Yes, we agree it is not 5-star, but it is comfortable and quiet. Easy pick-up from LAX using the wall phone at the terminal exit. Courteous drivers and easy check-in. Only mild problem was lugging bags up to the second floor. 
We also used the Denny's on site for a light lunch upon arrival and later, for dinner. Once again, not a winner but more than adequate. 
Our morning flight was too early to take advantage of the included breakfast, but no problem, the shuttle driver grabbed an assortment of pastries and fruit for all of his passengers. 
We not only recommend this hotel for an overnight stay, but will have no hesitation of staying there again.

We have stayed at this hotel a few times while traveling and never have been disappointed. Our check-in is always very fast and our rooms are always very neat and very clean. The breakfast is good and being in a large room you can relax as you eat .

I made a reservation at this hotel for myself, my husband and 2 yr old daughter, little did I know that the walls are paper thin ... you can hear the people next door having intercourse... There was no weather stripping on the doors or windows so all the traffic noise, and bugs got in. This was only the beginning, we stayed 6 nights, every night there was shouting on the staircases by our hotel door, drunken fools in the parking lot, and people with their t.v.'s blairing at 4 a.m., all which we complained about and recieved no help from the front desk. The room itself had torn and old comforters, stained walls and not very big at all. We have stayed on Hotel circle many times, and NEVER been so disappointed in a hotel as this last trip, I would never recommend this hotel to anyone, and even though you save a little money, it's not worth a goodnights sleep, and comfort... NEVER AGAIN!!!!

The location is perfect for the 16th St Mall or the Convention Center. Light rail right in front of the hotel and walking distance to all things downtown. Nice and clean, bright rooms and some of the most helpful and friendly employees ... at every level of staff! Had, of course a two room suite with a flat screen in the living room and one in the bedroom. Full bathroom, plus a sink and mirror in the area between bedrm & livrm. Nice view of downtown Denver from the room and excellent free breakfast each morning ... bacon, eggs, potatoes, fruit, toast, bagels etc. The price was comparible to all the other name hotels, maybe a little less, and well worth it. This is the place to stay!

just recently stay in this hotel not bad its close to nationals ball park just a couple blocks of walk near to navy yard metro rail not whole lot to see around besides the ball park the only thing that disappoint us i use there phone to local calls to order a food around that hotel then they charge us a local call on our bill with no warning after we check out they never told us,we just find out through my credit card bill ,i will think twice to stay here again:(

I came in to Houston at around 11pm with no place to stay. When I contacted Crowne Plaza Aurellia Gaskin answered the phone. I advised her of the situation I was in and despite the fact the hotel was basically at capacity she not only was able to find me a room but she also accommodated my girlfriend, her son and my dog!! I would recommend Crowne Plaza as the hotel itself is nice, but overall it’s the staff that truly makes the experience enjoyable. Employees such as Aurellia will keep me coming back to Crowne Plaza whenever I am in Houston, but even more so keep me loyal to Crowne plaza in general when I travel!!

Our family of four stayed in a room with 2 double beds over the March Break. The staff was very accommodating (free fridge), the room was very clean (housekeeping was wonderful!), and the location was unbeatable (15 minutes to the Mall). The concierge really knows his stuff. The lobby is very impressive too. Had an easy time walking to the museums and the train station -- which we did quite a bit over the course of a week. 
Charging for the internet at a nice hotel is ridiculous in my opinion; we had to walk over to the corner Starbucks for free wifi, but it isn't open in the evening. The parking fee of $45 really is too high, so we parked there the first night, then did free street parking for the weekend, followed by overnight parking at Union Station (15 minutes away). Moving the car like that turned out to be quite a hassle.
Washington is probably the cleanest city we've ever been to. So beautiful too with the magnolia trees blossoming. The buildings were so grand and the best part was that we didn't pay a cent for the museums or zoos. Museum of Natural History, Air and Space Museum, and the National Zoo are the best bets for little kids. National Art Gallery offers free audio tours, but is, not surprisingly, set up more for adults.
Fast food sources include Chipotle, Pot Belly's, McDonald's and more at Union Station. If you're near the American Indian Museum, go there for some top notch food rather than pay an arm and leg for sandwiches elsewhere. Also, if you're tempted to go to DC Cupcakes in Georgetown, be prepared to wait in a long lineup; we stopped off at Baked and Wired a few streets away instead.
Metro stations are spread out quite far from each other and it felt as if we were always at least a 10 minutes walk from everything (20 min. if you have the legs of a little kid to consider). We never did end up taking the circulator bus route, but I will next time around.

Looking for a 2 night stay near the Denver Airport, Baymont was a good choice.
There were plenty of restaurants in the area to choose from, and we were able to take a walk & feel safe.
Very nice place to stay.

I arrived at the Rodeway late at night- tired and not feeling very chipper. The gentleman at the desk was extremely pleasant and kind, and I just knew I had picked the right place. The room was spacious, clean, and quiet. It seems to be a family run operation, perhaps this is why it was such a great experience. Incredible value for the money, and I would definitely go back!

This Embassy is not built around an atrium so it is quieter. Nicely appointed rooms and very nice size bathroom. The decor gives a sense of luxury and the back of the hotel is on the riverwalk. The evening Manager's reception is well garnished and they make sure that it is stocked for the totality of the happy hour (unlike certain Embassy properties that serve the cheese tray once and that is it...).And the girls at the bar were really great as well as the wait staff. The reception desk people are neither here nor there. They essentially check you in...for that type of unpersonal service you could have a machine do it... on the reservation it was marked 2 adults I am standing in front of this guy with my husband that hands him his credit card and he still asks me if there is a second adult in the room?... There is a way to ask the question such as "I see you have reserved for 2 adults would you like 2 keys?" I do not think that English was his native language but if that is the case, then Management should at least ensure (for whatever slight role they may have in this position) that the way the language is used does not irritate the guest? It is well placed. The only reason I do not give this hotel an excellent rating is because to have very recently built a hotel this size and made a miniature pool is idiotic above all in the summer when everyone wants to cool off, you can't even get into the pool and there are not enough chairs. That was really disappointing for an otherwise really great property.

This is my 3rd stay at this property. As with the previous stays, the hotel is just brilliant. The staff is nice, courteous and helpful.
Location is perfect for Times Sq, transportation and pretty much everything else in NYC.
My room was on the 30th floor and I had views of the river on one side, the Empire State building on the other.
The breakfast is busy, but we didn't have any issues finding a seat after a few minutes.
Other reviewers complained about the elevators... Here is a tip for you: take the stairs! This will solve the obesity issue in the US. I just don't understand why people take an elevator to go down from the 2nd floor. 
And yes I took the stairs to go up 30 floors. Good workout!
Also, if you want to go down, press the arrow facing down... Want to go up? Guess what press the arrow facing up! So many people on all floors pressed both buttons so the elevators stop at most floors even on their way up...
Anyway, at the week end with a full hotel, I didn't have to wait more than a few minutes.
"Social hour" on most weekdays from 5 to 7 is great, wine, beer and appetizers are served downstairs.
This hotel is my favourite choice for a NYC stay.

Super locale, great service, fab-o hotel and the staff goes out of their way to be helpful. Rooms are clean, spacious and comfortable. While there, I used the small meeting rooms as well as the ballroom. Great layout. Plenty of places to eat nearby. Great locale to go sightseeing (although be prepared to tackle the steep hills).

title_masked: Homeless people and terrible internet service
text_masked:
My husband and I just finished our trip in CA which started in downtown San Diego. It was stamped with AAA approval which is who we booked it through, however, we were disappointed with the terrible internet connection. When we first arrived they said we should have a connection. It didn't work so my husband called the office and they said a maintenance man would be up to our room. He came while we were out and left a cable. The cable worked, however, it would be connected for a couple of minutes and then it would drop. This went on for the next two days. We checked out Sunday morning. Also on their description, online, it says "minimum of two nights" which we found out through the Best Western 1-800 number that this is not a requirement of Best Western. The room was small for the price, however, very clean. The TV is not a flat screen. The breakfast area is very tiny. The breakfast was of good quality. If you have never been to San Diego beware of the many homeless people. Obviously they are allowed to walk the streets all day and sleep on the sidewalks starting at 8:00p.m. They look in trashcans a lot. Very sad. The cabana area on the very top of the motel is cute and clean. The woman clerk was very nice, however, the man was a bit snippy when I asked if the internet problem was corrected.
Tom and Mary July 2012

The Marriot River Walk is located right on the San Antonio river walk. It is right across the street from the Marriot River Center. The two hotels are right next to each other. The M River Walk is the smaller of the two and it actually has some rooms with balconies and is not quite as busy and more relaxing that the Marriott River Center in my opinion. The rooms were clean and well kept. The room I had did have a very small toilet shower area although the entire room was quite large, To get into the shower you had to squeeze by the toilet and carefully shut a door to gain access to the shower. Other than that my stay was good, I had access to the club floor concierge lounge and the staff working there was excellent. Both hotels are right next to the River Center Mall and a very short walk to numerous restaurants so if you are traveling in from another location you will not in a car in this area.

title_masked: nice room and very friendly staff
text_masked: The hotel is situated close to 38 bus which drives you directly to the city centre. Staff (Brendan was very friendly) was in general very friendly, the breakfast room was crowded but the selection was limited but nice and fresh fruit salad. The diner next door was typically US and very very nice. The rooms were small but clean. Somehow the airconditioning was smelling weared and the windows could be opened but towards the noisy street and not to recommend. In all I can recommend the hotel for a short period (1 week max).

title_masked: Great hotel - highly recommend - stay here
text_masked:
I recently stayed at the Copley Square hotel. I was very impressed with the hotel and recommend it to anyone staying in Boston. The staff was one of the most helpful and kind group of people I have ever interacted with - they did all they could to make our stay great.
The room was perfect and the location was amazing.
I look forward to staying at the hotel in the future. It was perfect for individuals, couples, and families. Stay here!

I stayed at this hotel for a business trip and would not normally pay the higher price, but this hotel has it all! It is located conveniently off the Orange Line Wells/Quincy stop. There are many shops/restaurants nearby, and it is within walking distance to Michigan Avenue. The decor is fantastic, the rooms are some of the largest in Chicago, and the amenities are amazing. I actually had a street view room and was surprised how quiet it was. The hotel lobby/bar gets very loud at night, but once you are in your room, it is peace and quiet. I would definitely recommend this hotel if you have the extra budget. It is worth the experience.

Had a great overnight here this past weekend.....hotel is very convenient, small, quain, historic, elevator is slow...very slow it sucks, butall and all the hotel is cool. Small rooms but that's just Philly. You will enjoy it.

title_masked: The only reason to stay here is you can walk to Southcenter
text_masked:
I really expect more from a Hilton property. 
Pros:
This hotel only exists because of its convenience to Southcenter (there are only 2 within walking distance and this is the closest). We stayed here so my teenagers could walk over to Southcenter and shop on their own without me having to follow them around. We paid an extra $80 a night for this convenience.
Staff service was good.
Cons:
Beds - I expected the typical comfortable Hilton bed but we had old beds that you could hear the springs when you got up. Hard as a rock and very uncomfortable.
Noise level. The walls are paper thin if you stand next to the pocket door you can hear every word of the conversation next door. In our case a screaming baby and a large Asian family who spent every waking moment fighting and screaming at each other. Fortunately we didn't understand the language so no need for damage control with the kids.
The room wasn't as clean as I'd like. The coffee maker still had grounds from the last person and my socks were dirty from the carpet.
The hotel and rooms are very old and dated. I don't mind old but when everything is worn out or not functional it is unacceptable.
The living room furniture were very uncomfortable. Even just for having coffee and reading the paper in the morning.
No microwave, sorry but I think at this price and for a suite it should be standard.
Paying for internet, really? In this day and age? $10 per day.
No dresser. I like to unpack my clothing but there was no dresser, Just a table for the television. The TV was a flat screen but very small.
Food - pass on the restaurant. Cold, boring, hotel food. 
Towels - when you pre-book and list you are a family of four there should be four towels.
The pool is too small for laps and the hot tub was broken during our visit (all four days).

Stayed at the Rouge with my eldest daughter. We were in DC for the weekend. My daughter had been wanting to see the Capital for a while, so I took her with me on a business trip and stayed the weekend. We were in one of the rooms with a separate space with bunk beds and its own TV. We were given a game console to use in the room and the front desk presented my daughter with a stuffed animal. We went out that day and when we returned, the front desk had set up a fresh fruit plate for us. None of this was requested. I have never had a staff go so far and above my expectations. To this day, my daughter still lists the room as one of her favorite parts of the trip. I even slept in the bottom bunk while my daughter took the top bunk. Awesome trip, awesome room and a staff that we'll remember for a long, long time. The Rouge and Kimpton know how to treat guests. We were even given an itinerary on Saturday that had the museums and attractions we had mentioned wanting to see, circled and drawn with directional arrows, waiting for us on our first day of sightseeing. Again, just blown away by the service. Truly Exceptional.

we stay at this hotel every year. it is clean & the kids love the indoor pool. we did have a problem this year with the commode & refrigerator not working though. this is the second year we got stuck with a sqeaky mattress too. Also, I have concerns about the security system. The security monitoring system showed a 'fault' each time I visited the front desk and the side entrance was not secured.

Stayed for a 3 day weekend in Feb. The hotel was very nice, the lobby a little small, staff was helpful and friendly. We upgraded to a higher floor since this was my first time in NYC, the view was awesome, the Empire State Building was unbelievable!! The rooms were nice and newly remodeled. The shower was a little strange as the shower and bathroom floor have nothing seperating them, therefor the floor got a bit soaked after showers. The rooftop bar has a wonderful view and some great drinks. Sorry to say we didn't get a change to try Rare, the resturant in the hotel, but it was packed every night so that must mean it was fun. The location of the hotel was good, walking distance to ESB, The Rock and Time Square if you are up for it. Subway not far, nice park around the block. Definately would stay here again!

We stayed here in june, The hotel is very centrally located . Few blocks away from union square and china town.It had a decent size room which was clean. It had everything you need. coffee machine,safe etc.The staff at the reception were very friendly and helpful.The door man was very sweet too ,who helped us with directions.

I am so much looking forward to my next stay. If I were American and lived in the neighbourhood,
I would stay there every weekend ... I am simply in love with that gorgeous Hudson.

Taking my family here for a weekend, we are really happy to pick this hotel, walking distance to the fenway park, museum of fine arts. Close to back bay area which is a must see. The green line is about 10 mins walk. The rooms are clean and comfortable. The food court is connected to the hotel and my family loved it, so convinient with varieties for everyone. Highly recommend it.

We stayed at Hendersons Wharf Inn while visiting John Hopkins, which is close by. Such a quant neighborhhod with lots of shops and restaurants.Our cozy and comfortable room faced the wharf and the bedroom/bathroom was large with brick walls. While there is no restaurant in the inn, they had a lovely continental breakfast with hard-bioled eggs, fresh fruit, bagels, oatmeal, granola, nutbread, coffee, juices, etc. and a pretty courtyard so you could eat in/out. The staff were super friendly. Some nights they have a cocktail reception with an open bar! The parking was free in a secure but open lot. In sum it was charming and the historical setting made it an intersting place to stay. I would definitely stay here again and want to go back soon to see more.of historic and lively Baltimore

title_masked: Beds and pillows are a joke
text_masked: First off, the Marriott staff was very nice. Almost always are. Been a Marriott Rewards member since 1995. Lobby is very nicely updated. Staff was very helpful and appreciative for us staying. But that does not hide the fact that the bed was very uncomfortable. My wife thought she may develop curvature of the spine after one night. We seriously contemplated leaving after one night and driving home which was 455 miles away. Pillows? Take a pillowcase and throw in a couple of towels and that is what if felt like. Two of the four lamps in my room (143) were so lopsided I felt we were in the Titanic when it was sinking. I never drink hotel room coffee and I challenge anyone to want to drink a cup brewed with the coffee maker in this room. And the parking was confusing and never working correctly on the weekend.

My husband and I stayed at the JW Marriott for Gen Con and had a wonderful time. 
As soon as we pulled up to the front door, everyone outside was friendly and helpful. We had to wait a bit to check-in (maybe 5 to 7 min), but that is because of the mass of people checking in for the convention. I thought it was very nice that they were offering cookies while we waited. We didn't have lunch, so it was nice treat. Once it was our turn, check-in was quick and easy. We stayed in room 2618. The room was spacious, clean and up to date. I loved our view of the park. Also to note, we never did hear out neighbors; so we always got a good nights rest. Never had a problem with cleaning service; always had clean towels even though I always hung ours up to re-use. Used the gym once during our stay and there again I thought it was very nice; had a lot of choices. It too was spacious and clean. Felt like a real gym. Never did try any of the restaurants (Though the items on the menus looked good), since we were close to a lot of other great place around town. I did visit Starbucks a few times and was happy with their service. Also used the FedEx Store. We bought several games and could not get them all in our luggage. The gal was helpful and made sure everything was packed up. We'll see if we get our package on Wed like she promised. =) 
I know a few people complained about the cost of parking and/or having to pay for internet/WiFi, which I would agree with them, but I never used those services this time around. 
If we decide to go to this convention again, JW will be our #1 choice.

Loved our stay of 4 nights. All of the staff were super nice and friendly, especially the valets. I really appreciated the decor, especially the well appointed bathroom. Instead of the typical and useless tub/shower combo, they had a decent sized shower that two people could fit into. The granite topped vanity had nice big drawers to put things away in and the toilet was very nice. Great TV placment and very excellent sheets! I would highly reccomend a stay here.

I arrived at the hotel by taxi from Dulles which cost USD70. 
The check-in and greeting were excellent. I recall that 'Sharon' did an excellent job of checking me in and making sure i received the SPG benefits to which I was entitled.
The bed was comfortable and everything functional.
I did spend some time in the gym. The treadmill was good quality which I enjoyed.
All up, a pleasant stay, friendly and functional staff. I would stay here again.
I should add that the downtown location isn't excellent for tourists.

I am a Hilton Hhonors Diamond member, so I am sorta prejudiced toward Hilton properties, however I was still very impressed with the service and personnel. Location is fantastic to get around LA when you are vacationing with family. Even with hitting rush hour (it seems like it now is all day...) coming back from Hollywood to LAX, it was still 20 minutes. You were within 10-20 minutes of Venice, Santa Monica, downtown, Hollywood, etc. It's not set up for family in reality as you don't have a refrigerator to store leftovers or simple stuff for breakfast (Their fantastic restaurant Andiamo is rather expensive for family dining). You can pick up pastries and Starbucks at the Cafe or Bistro, but otherwise, walk one block to Carl's Jr for breakfast. Denny's is 3 blocks down. Many, many reasonable options abound nearby in Inglewood, Manhattan Beach, Hawthorne, etc, all within 10 minutes drive.They are still doing some remodeling so if you go relatively soon there is some work being done, however, I would definitely stay there again!

I recently stayed at the TownePlace Suites and had a wonderful experience. The hotel is updated and modern. Our room was very nice, clean and spacious. The kitchen was a nice add on that we didn't expect. The staff always treated us in a respectful way and were attentive to our needs from the moment we arrived until our departure. The location is perfect for the downtown area as it is right in the middle of everything. It is about 2 blocks from the Alamo and the Riverwalk. We also took the trolley/bus to Market Square as the stop is right outside the hotel. We couldn't have asked for a better place to have a quick get away. We will definitely return!

- got a good rate for the room
- good size room with TV, wifi 24 hrs, useful kitchenette, modern bathroom
- in house laundry is very convenient
- 5 min walk to shopping plaza that has Walmart Supercenter, Pizza outlet, KFC etc
- 8 min walk to Bank of America, Indian restaurants, AT&T store
- may other food, dine in, take out establishments within 10 min walk
- 3 miles to TIAA CREF location
- 1 mile to Hwy #85 (direct to airport)
- garbage disposal on every floor
- plenty of parking

This hotel was great for a weekend getaway!! It's a well lit two block walk to access the Riverwalk at Rivercenter. Very quiet, huge room, A/C works great, very comfortable bed (if you like firm). The water pressure in the shower is phenomenal, the showerhead is fantastic. The lobby is very nice, breakfast has a great selection. On-site parking lot is small (~20 spaces), but off-site parking is only a block away in a relatively secure city parking lot. I never saw any seedy looking folks milling about, no broken windows or such. Would highly recommend and will definitely stay again!

The word Suite is a joke and a bad one at best. The room I reserved was so small that the "opened the door and crawled across the bed" cliche applies. Their web site shows suites but their so called suites are 40% more expensive than their cracker barrell rooms. Place was clean but wi fi signal was almost non existent. Never again Wyndham for me.
enjoyed the city view from our balcony, the staff was very friendly and helpful. I loved the pool and spa area, the firepits were charming and so comfortable for chating and relaxing
