We stayed in late September for 4 nights. The location was great- easy to get on the subway to any direction but out of the hoopla so you can relax a bit. The hotel was clean and nicely decorated, all very up to date. The service was friendly and efficient. The morning breakfast (complete with newspapers!) was a nice option to grab on the way to museums, etc and the happy hour wine, snacks were great as well as cookies, tea and coffee available at all times.. We enjoyed walking in the neighborhood south from the hotel also. We were on the 6th floor and there was some street noise but did not interrupt our sleep at all- white noise. There was no noise from within the hotel- nice sound proofing. I would definitely stay here again.

title_masked: Nice location, unassuming hotel, small rooms...
text_masked:
My title really says it all. I liked this hotel, I didnt love it. The location was convenient to where we needed to be. We drove by it a few times before we realized that this was the hotel! The rooms were very clean and extremely small. Our particular room was no larger than a college dorm room. The bed literally took up the whole room. There was an equally small bathroom. Not what I like when I am staying in a hotel. The staff was very friendly and helpful and the only reason I didn't give this Hotel less stars. 
There is no room service and in fact, the only restaurant on property was closed for renovations. NOt at all convenient when you would like a cup of coffee etc. Parking is $55.00 overnight -which is about the going rate in the city to park overnight when staying at hotels. We parked and took cabs everywhere because if you take your car out of valet, your charged every time. 
Our room was on the 5th floor facing the front of the building. Not a great idea! We were awoken all night from the sounds of car horns, sirens, people yelling(yes people yelling) and the hooves of the horses of the Hansom cabs! When we were able to fall back to sleep we were then again awoken by the voices coming from the rooms next door through the the paper thin walls! You can hear everything people in the next rooms were saying as well as people walking in the halls! I am from New York, so noise isn't usually an issue for me....it was here!
Overall our stay was nice. The hotel it self is fine. It was just nice, nothing special. I know you can find other hotels, with more enmities at the same price. For me I rather pay more and get the luxuries I have come to expect at hotels.

I picked this hotel since the conference I was attending was also at this venue When you first walk into the hotel it seems very luxurious with lots of marble, huge ceilings, artwork etc, but my room in Harbor Tower was entirely the opposite. When we got to our room the first thing we noticed was a water stain on the ceiling, a mildew odor, and a very, very wet patch of carpet. We would have been OK with ignoring it if we hadn't had stained sheets when we attempted to get into our bed. The next morning my husband went to the front desk to complain about the wet carpet and he was simply told that there was construction happening on the floor above us and they had overbooked the hotel so there was nothing they could do. The mildew was starting worsen my allergies so the next morning I spoke with the concierge and she was very pleasant. She offered to comp us a night stay in the room as well as offer to send someone up to investigate and clean the patch of carpet, hopefully removing the mildew odor. No one came.
I came down again the next morning and pointed out a few extra things I found wrong in the room including someone else's hair still attached to the hair dryer, a mold/mildew spot in the corner of the bathroom, and the rusting door frame of the bathroom. Thankfully, despite being overbooked, they were at least able to relocate us (although I feel quite bad for the folks that ended up in our room that night). The second room was MUCH better and in Seaport Tower. It actually smelled clean, was clean, had dry carpet and it had a lovely view. With it being a corner room we had 3 windows to enjoy the view with. The remainder of our stay was better and the buffet at Lael's was quite delicious, but during the first 3 days of the stay, quality of the room and the construction noise occurring above the room left something to be desired. 
I am appreciative of the concessions that were made by the hotel in an attempt to right the situation, but despite the high touting of the renovated rooms, I would be hesitant to revisit them for another stay without a business reason to do so.

title_masked: Great location and little touches make for a nice stay
text_masked: This was a great hotel, very nice amenities; hot water comes on as soon as you turn it on; Illy coffee at the coffee shop; good service, very accommodating. Even though it's located right around the corner from Times Square, most rooms are high enough up and well enough sound-proofed that it's not a problem. Beds are wonderful, one of the most comfortable nights I've had in a hotel. The location is very convenient; although Times Square is quite crowded you can go around the other way and avoid it if you choose.

I stayed here for a business conference that was held in the hotel. The room and bed were very nice, and I arrived early enough to enjoy the outdoor pool and hot tub. The water temperature of the pool was very pleasant in late September. The breakfast was standard but good. I could hear some airplane noise in my room, but fortunately there aren't many flights at night. My only complaint is that the doors have large gaps that let in a significant amount of hallway light and noise. Everything else about my stay was perfect.

I was there for 6 days in March. I loved the water in the lobby which was just ice water mixed with strawberries and lemons. It was refreshing! I thought the rooms were a bit dark for my taste. Housekeeping left the room tidy each day and had chocolates on my pillow each night.

Booked this hotel via Orbits with a flight. This Hotel not directly on the Riverwalk but walkable distance. Good accommodations with the standard room. Nice to have a place that still allows a smoking room- so appreciated. Only the non-smokers complain anyway. Front desk good. Taxi service promt. Nice place-will stay again.

We easily walked from the Powell St. BART station (1/2 hour from the airport) and then enjoyed short hops on public transport to where-ever we wanted to go. For an old hotel, in this location, we were pleased with the amenities and service.

Excellent hotel! That's all I have to say. Staff was amazing from check in to check out. 
Parking at the hotel at $39 a night for self parking. Parking garage was clean and easy to find a spot. Parking attendant was very nice and helpful. The elevator wasn't attached to the hotel but wasn't far from the hotel entrance.
Check in was quick and easy. Since I was traveling w/my wife and child, we needed a room w/2 bed. This was the first hotel that I was able to find w/2 Queen beds instead of 2 Double bed. This was great. Even though they confirmed 2 Queen beds during check-in, they messed up and gave a King Suite. My wife and I loved this room and wanted to keep it but we needed to exchange for 2 Queens. They quickly fixed this issue for us.
Our room was spacious. Room had balcony which was nice. Rooms were recently updated. Bathrooms were updated and nicely done. Safe in the room. Sleep number beds. Big closet. Bar area w/coffee, water, ice bucket and wine bottle opener. Hotel also has free Wi-Fi which is great in my opinion. Our room was right next to the elevators and had NO issues w/noises after hours. I read some reviews on the AC/Heater unit being loud but I didn't think it was bad at all but then again, I can't sleep if its too quite.
The hotel lobby was small but done up nice. There is a pool which we saw but didn't use but looked nice. Off the pool was an outside balcony which is over the parking garage. Done up very nice and good views from here. The location of the hotel was great also. There was plenty of places to eat around the hotel and located one block from the Boston Common and Public Garden.
We also took advantage of the concierge desk. We dealt w/John Hallette both times who was amazing. He helped us navigate through the "T" (Boston's Subway) and also booked our tickets for the Duck Boat Tour. 
We will be back at this hotel again. This was truly a great place and staff was amazing. Thanks Revere!!
Pros:
Amazing Staff
Balcony Rooms
Location
Free wi-fi
On-site parking
Cons:
Elevators were slow
No refrigerators available

This is a relaxed and comfortable place to stay in upper Manhatten. Excellent value. The location is right across from Central Park and close to subway lines that get you quickly downtown. It felt a very safe place to stay. The staff were friendly and helpful and the downstairs lounge area was cosy with relaxed seating areas and tables so that you could talk to people if you wanted or just sit and read.
There was free wifi if you had your own computer and cheap access to the internet otherwise. We were lucky enough to get a free upgrade to a private room with ensuite which was lovely. Gorgeous comfy bed and nice sheets and a good bathroom with really hot water.
They don't do breakfast but there is a brilliant bagel place right across Broadway and lots of other eating places nearby. You can get tea and coffee and snacks downstairs.
I happened to be staying here with my daughter but I've have been very happy to stay here as a lone traveller.

title_masked: Great rooms, nice amenities, good for family or business
text_masked: I've stayed here twice now and both times really enjoyed the experience. Rooms are large (rare for SF), have great views and housekeeping is prompt and thorough. It's in the business/financial district so there is not much going on here at night. But during day, it's great as it is walking distance to China Town, Union Square and the Embarcadero. Really nice lounge for grabbing a drink by the fire and watching a game. Don't miss The Grove around the corner for breakfast.

If you are traveling to San Antonio, this is a must stay location. The location related to the city is perfect. The facility is one of the best my wife and I have visited. The staff is top shelf and their attention to detail and your satisfaction is their number one priority. I was most impresses with how the grounds were spotless and the surroundings, too include both golf courses, were so relaxing! 
Both Brannons and Francesca's service and menu was award winning. The Grill at the country club hosted a Beer Dinner our last eveninig and that was the icing on the cake.
The young staff is a blessing for our future! These young people are an inspiration for our future and should all be recogonized! 
Will be making a return trip

We where greeted by the clerk in the reception, and where given an upgrade to a corner suite. The room was very spacious, and had all what we could wish for. The bed was very good, and it gave us the best sleep we have had on this trip around the world. All the personnel we where in contact with from room-maid to the front desk service and concierge was smiling and gentle. The breakfast was great too. With a variety of food to enjoy from the buffe. The only downside that we could pick on was the other restaurants in the hotel. There where nothing special buy the food they offered. We had both lunch and dinner there. The location is great if you visit LA buy car, and most people do. Parking was easy. You could choose from vallet parking or self parking. We had self parking. The car rental companies are close by, so there is no problem in returning your rental car. And there is a shuttle bus to the airport, it only takes 10 minutes. Overall we recommend this hotel, and we will definitely stay here again.

title_masked: Bring the Wallet for this one
text_masked: Nice Hotel in the heart of Downtown Los Angeles the hotel is a city in itself. There are a couple of jewels to be found if you take a walk around. The staff won't tell you about them because they are leased and not a part of the Bonavenvure. The Suede bar is a good example, after spending $7.00 per beer and asking if there were any other pubs I was told no by the staff until I walked around a bit and found this. So keep your eyes open and there are a few other "leased" places to find.

I stayed at the Amalfi Hotel in Chicago recently as part of “Stay-cation” in the city I love so much. I chose the Amalfi because of its unbeatable location. We were within walking distance of some of my favorite restaurants, Michigan Avenue, Millennium Park, and a host of other Chicago attractions. 
Perks of the Amalfi also include a “Manager’s Reception” every day, which is basically a cocktail hour with finger foods. The signature cocktail, “Amalfitini” was TOO good. It was included in the room price, which is unheard of! There was also a wonderful breakfast on our floor in the morning, which was convenient! We were able to grab our food and eat in the luxury of our own room just down the hall! 
The staff at the Amalfi went above and beyond at every chance we gave them. Nick Ditter, Sales Manager, was so responsive and helpful in getting me a great room. The front door staff was incredibly cheerful, friendly, and fun to talk to! 
I would HIGHLY recommend the Amalfi Hotel to anyone visiting the Chicago area that wants to be downtown. It is truly unlike any hotel experience I’ve had!

The hotel is less than a mile from the airport and is great when you have to catch an early flight. The site is easy to find from the freeway and when you want to go to the airport, you just go out the front and turn right. If you have a high room facing the airport, you can see the planes take off and arriving. However, with the door shut, we could not hear them. The restaurant is part sports bar. That doesn't detract from it and the food was good. I am not pleased with what is apparently Doubletree, if not Hilton, policy about charging guests for the privilege of parking their own cars.

I was in Boston for one night and I am so glad I stayed here. The staff was excellent!! Everyone was so professional and it made me feel at home. The rooms were spotless, and all the public areas were immaculate. It is great to see such a big hotel being kept after so well.
I also ate in their restaurant, Connolley's. The food was fantastic and the service was great. All around this hotel certainly deserves a 5-rating. There is no other hotel I would rather stay in Boston than this one!

We checked-in here with no trouble at all as they have these clever check-in machines (as well as people behind a desk) that give you your room keys and everything. The room was super nice. The bed and pillows were extremely comfortable and room service was fantastic. We had partial views over Union Square which was nice. Probably one of the quietest hotels I have stayed at. Close to everything and far enough away from the Tenderloin area which is something I would recommend, especially for travelers who don't have an overwhelming amount of homelessness where they are from..........it was actually quite shocking the amount of homeless etc in San Francisco.

title_masked: Nice clean hotel close to the airport
text_masked: Staff was very friendly. Rooms were quiet for sleeping and had a view of the pool and palm trees.

title_masked: It's the Ritz - If can you afford it, stay here when in downtown Philly
text_masked:
The beginning was not as expected - I walk up with my small one-night bag and went in while several staff stood on the steps talking together - no attempt to open the door. Strange for the Ritz...
But, then it all switched:
- Lobby was beautiful - classic but modernized just enough
- Check-in was very professional and helpful
- I am Marriott preferred and got an upgrade to a suite without asking - very nice
- I got a call 5 minutes after I arrived asking if all was OK with the room - very nice
- The desk clerk and concierge were friendly to me as I left 10 minutes later for meetings
- The doormen (two of them) never again did not open doors everytime I came through them, so I assume the first time there must have been something that required their undivided attention
My room was expensive, but I was at a conference and the others hotels were full. If I could afford it again, I would stay here.
Also, another reviewer is correct, there are a few steps (4-5?) to get from the desk to the elevators. No way around them.

Stayed here for a business trip last week. Nice front desk staff, super small rooms. 
When I checked in I was told my King Bed request was not available. Keep in mind I booked this room 3 months prior to my arrival. When i walked into the room they provided, I seriously thought I was in a coat closet. One double bed and not even enough oxygen to breath!
I called the desk, said that room was not going to work, they switched me to a two double bed room. Better, but still so small. The ceiling in the bathroom was only 7', so you felt even more cramped in their. Every time a door in the hall closed it sounded like a freight train, thin walls, thin doors... like most hotels.
The hotel bar offered some great food, with the exception of a wilted dinner salad. Be warned, when you order a dinner salad, that is what you get. Wilted lettuce w/ a red onion slice on top. 
Not even close to what I would consider a good salad.
Everything else, including the service at the bar was great.
I stayed here because of the location and closeness to AMA (which is where my seminar was).
Great location if you are attending something at AMA.

title_masked: Character and history - brilliant for the price
text_masked: We would like to put 'superb for the price' in the scores - this hotel has loads of character, is quirky and prettily landscaped. The room was a good size, maybe decoration a bit tired and monocoloured (brown!) but perfectly clean, with an excellent bathroom. We had a room with interconnecting door which had a slight, very slight, gap, enough to hear the people next door but from about 10pm until we left the next morning they were silent - but that would have been a problem with inconsiderate neighbours. There is a complimentary airport shuttle bus but you have to ring for it, and complimentary 'continental' breakfast, but we went to Denny's next door for our first US breakfast this trip. Overall - we would certainly go back, maybe ask for a room without a connecting door. The hotel is close to the airport and is on a main road - but the road is well-disguised by the landscaping. The pool is a good length, we didn't have time to try it but would have liked to.

I took my daughter to NYC to celebrate her 18th Birthday, therefore I wanted a special hotel. Our travel agent sure chose the perfect hotel to make my babygirl feel very special! From the moment we walked in, Jimmy and Lauren made us feel like VIPs. While we were unpacking and getting situated, Jimmy came to our room with a special treat and birthday card personally signed by the whole staff for the birthday girl. So thoughtful! 
The location could not have been any more perfect. We were close and convenient to Times Square, the theaters, Central Park, Rockefeller Plaza,... everything! Sweet Brandon helped us choose the perfect restaurant for a celebration dinner after seeing a show on our first night in the city. He was so kind and eager to help to make our stay special.
Our room was spotless and gorgeous! Our view was not amazing, but hey, It's New York City - I wasn't expecting an "ocean view". We had a building and fire escape out our window, but again... it's the city! We were extremely pleased with our room. 
The breakfast was perfect. It had everything we could have wanted in the morning to start us off ready for our adventures in the city. I highly recommend The Sanctuary to anyone wanting to feel special. I've stayed in the chain hotels in NYC before, but nothing compares to this special little boutique hotel and the special staff running it!

Stayed here for St Patrick's day. Location is spot on.5th Avenue at end of street, 2 Min walk from Empire State Building, 6 min walk to Times square. Hotel was a little out dated but room was a good size and clean. We had a Queen sized room for 5 nights. looking on the floor lay out it was a good choice, as some of the rooms looked very small. There are no views with the rooms but didn't book it for this. There is a coffee/tea vending machine in lobby between 7.00am and 10.00am then 3.00pm and 7.00pm. Dunkin doughnuts on the corner with good priced and lovely breakfast bagels. we took breakfast back to hotel for the free teas/coffee. the bed was comfortable,only had a little window which looked onto back of building which made room very dark, not a problem. Would recommend and stay again.

Room was a decent size and clean. Upon entering the room, I checked the bathroom and it passed my expectations. It was so central to either walk or take the nearby subway. There were Korean restaurants nearby, which was a bonus at the end of the day, since dinner is a few steps away.
Complimentary breakfast was included, but mostly toast, bagels, doughnuts, coffee and juice. We didnt expect much as we got the reservation at a good price.

It was a good hotel - the only problem I noticed was that the vending machine / ice machine area looked like the floor had undergone an earthquake and was about to give way. As long as you stay away from there, you should be good. But our room was great, very comfortable. The breakfast was so-so - the eggs were nasty cafeteria-style fare, but the rest of the breakfast was good.

First the doors to the rooms are extremely low and small. I am not a tall or large person but I truly noticed it. 
Also while very resort like, being so close to the airport it was noisy. For a night before an early flight it was perfect but I would not spend a weeks vacation here.

I wrote a long detailed review it mysteriously disappeared. Oh well...summary. Rob and Kelly at front desk...fabulous. Great price for ridiculously huge posh room. no AC but nice breezes and fans. Fab bar below and restaurant above. Free breakfast doesn't have hot items but I loved it. I don't know how anyone could complain about the value. It IS a little spooky at nigh, old building and empty rooms under construction. We were upgraded without asking!!!! PLEASE upgrade us again! I want to go back sooooo bad. My new favorite hoteL!!!!

My hat is off to the General Manager, Amanda Hopkins and her staff. I had occasion to stay there recently while in San Antonio for a wedding. I found the layout of the room and the amenities in it to exceed my expectations. There was an apartment size refrigerator, an electric cook top and microwave, along with a desk and another table. The room was very clean and comfortable. The bed was bigger than most queen sized beds and was perfect. However, I was most impressed by the people that work here. Many properties offer a free breakfast but are just waiting to close it down at the appointed hour. Not at this place. They even provide a small bag for you to take something on the go. We sat for 45 minutes after closing and food was still out.My only caveat is to make sure you understand the Texas turnarounds and loops on the street layouts. This can cause confusion when using your GPS.

title_masked: Smells Terrible like a smokey bar room
text_masked: When I checked in to this hotel, the smell of smoke was so overwhelming, I should have turned around and gone home. I had pre paid, unfortuneately. I love marriotts, normally, and this was equal to a motel 6, except for the cost! No coffee offered in the lobby on a Sunday morning, no extra's at all. The view out of our window was apartments, the shabby low rent type. I was extremely disappointed as you can surely tell! Oh, did I mention that I am a smoker and even though, the stink was nauseating. BTW this was a Marriotts Courtyard Hotel, but there was NO courtyard. The residence inn across the lake looks like a courtyard but is actually a Residence Inn. My Bad for sure!

They say location is important, as indeed it is. The Lombardy is located on Pennsylvania Avenue about half a mile from the White House. Lot's of stores and restaurants around so plenty to see, although the hotel is in a quiet location which is good. Front office staff were excellent and so helpful. Breakfast was not included in the room price(unlike in Europe) and was average at best and also expensive.

Good value for money for NYC. Stayed with family 3 kids so swimming pool was welcome. Sauna was broken and Gym closes at 6 pm on Saturday, a pitty.
Wifi in guestroom is very very slow and needs a serious upgrade. No problem to pay as long as it meets the speed expectation.Ideal the fact that the hotel is located just inb front of bus station that takes you mid/downtown and no need to use the crowded and warm subways.
Concierge was very helpful in arranging an airport taxi/minivan.

Our travel agent managed to get us a good deal for just one night after a cruise that arrived early morning at pier 35. After the usual USA immigration delays, we arrived about 9:30am, but had requested our TA inform them of the early arrival.
The receptionist hardly batted an eyelid when we said that an email had been sent and had a room ready straightaway. The receptionist also supplied a temporary Starwood loyalty card as even though we have been Starwood members for a over a year, we never had a card. 
As others have said, the lifts are a bit slow and the hotel layout is a bit confusing until you have been to and from your room a couple of times. The room was advertised as for a Starwood prreferred guest, was clean and spacious, yet the beds were only doubles and not Queen or King, which is unusual.
Food in the coffee bar appeared a bit pricey, but there is a 711, Subway and other eateries close by.
Great location as the Hop On Hop Off bus office and terminus is less than 100 yards away and the waterfront not much further.
Piers 39 and 45 are within easy walking distance.
No refrigerator in the room is poor at this price and the rooms are not double glazed. Our room wasn't dark enough as the Roman blinds let in far too much light and there were lights outside.
At $25, we decided that breakfast was too expensive.
We parked our luggage and the pleasant concierge also booked our airport shuttle, which arrived on time at 6:15pm. We didn't use the pool but we did sit outside late afternoon until the shuttle pick up, in a sunny area primarily for smokers, adjacent to reception. There is an outdoor gas fire for each of the four seating areas which is pleasant enough. We weren't troubled by smoke drifting across either.
The important question as always, is "would we stay again". Given the ideal location, the answer would probably be yes.

I think Kings Inn Motel would be a more appropriate name, but semantics aside, the room was fine. However, I had a bit of trouble finding open electrical outlets to charge my phone and plug in my laptop. I made sure to ask for the WiFi password at the front desk, and had no trouble logging in and using the internet. 
However, the A/C in my room wasn't working! To be fair, I checked in around midnight, so I didn't call for maintenance. To my surprise, the room got quite cold through the night (the thermostat said 63 degrees), and the blankets weren't very thick. Suffice to say, I didn't sleep very well. When I mentioned it to the front desk the next morning, they said they weren't aware of A/C issues in the past, but that they'd take a look at it. Perhaps it was a one-time fluke, but either way, it was a rather poor way to prepare for my interview that day.

very good Stayed at this hotel this past weekend, and loved it! If you are looking for a spacious room right in the middle of times square, it's a great place to stay! ! The room had a queen sized bed , a living area with a second flat screen tv, wet bar, microwave, fridge, coffee make

As the title says, the cookies are the best part of this hotel. It is very nice and welcoming that they offer warm cookies to the guests. This hotel has just become a Doubletree, it was formely the Wyndham, so it is still going though some changes. The staff is very nice and friendly. The rooms are small but ok for NY city standards. The elevators take too long to come. There are three computers with free internet in the lobby and free wifi in the rooms.
It is very close to Penn station and a short walk to Times Square.
Overall it is a good choice.

The Washington Hilton is becoming my accommodation of choice in DC. I stayed here for 2 nights with a friend in late Feb 2012 and the service was terrific. I am a Hilton Gold member and was upgraded to the Exec floor, where even on weekends they served breakfast and early evening snacks (including hot food like chicken wings). The location is just a few blocks (walking distance) to Dupont Circle. I know the hotel doesn't have wireless in it's guest rooms (it has corded high speed internet)...but our room was right near the lounge so we were able to pick up wireless from the lounge. My only gripe is it looks like they raised the parking fees recently. It is very expensive to park here and given it's further away from downtown I would hope they would consider making their rates more reasonable. We ending up valeting and a few nights it was really busy and took over 20 mins to get the car, but this was my only gripe. I'll be back again to this historic hotel.

Third trip to Boston in less than two years. Booked the Commonwealth the first time account great reviews by other Red Sox Nation members. Despite its proximity to Fenway Park, the hotel is very quiet, both during and after games. The staff is friendly and helpful and more than willing to answer nearly any question sent their way. Complementary Champagne at check in was a welcome surprise after traveling 3/4 of the way across the country to get there.

title_masked: Expected better w/ the Hilton Name
text_masked:
I left a note w/ the front desk outlining the following.
The a/c was erratic, set at 68 but won't come till 71. then only one setting High and LOUD.
Spa was luke warm.
Bed was both comfortable, but at the same time to high for a handicapped person to get in w/o assistance.
Food at the restaurant was surprisingly good, tasty and HOT.
Try the couples retreat deal we thought we got a great value.
Staff was excellent, friendly and helpful.

My partner and I stayed one night at this hotel. The experience exceeded my expectations given the price of the room. I have stayed at other hotels in Seattle in this price range and BW was far superior. The woman who checked me in was very friendly. I arrived early and my room was not ready so she upgraded me to a suite! The hotel is a turn of the century building. The decor is consistent with the hotel's vintage and I found that very charming. The room was beautiful, spacious, and very clean. Modern bathroom fixtures, Neutrogena products, coffee maker, good lighting and free WiFi. We were asked if we wanted fresh towels in the early evening-a pleasant "extra" not common these days. The location of the hotel is perfect for tourists and is within walking distance of the Pier and most Seattle tourist destinations. Breakfast is included and was one of the best comp. breakfasts I have had lately. Great selection of hot and cold items and a large spacious dining room. Parking is an additional $20/night and the lot is about a 1 1/2 block walk from the hotel. There is "check in" parking at the hotel door however.Staff were very friendly and greeted us every time we entered and exited the hotel. They had good advice re restaurants and enquired if we were satisfied with everything when we checked out. I would highly recommend this hotel and will definitely stay here again.

This I have to say was one of the worst full service Marriotts I have ever experienced. First of all I have never seen a Marriott were the staff is so unfriendly or basically just absolute ignore you. You can barely even get a hello out of any employee. The hotel is very old and even though its probably been renovated it still shows signs of again and is poorly maintained. 
Location is ideal but beware of the noise. The sirens from the fire department on the next block are24/7. Plus a new hotel going up across the street means jack hammering that starts as early as 7am and does't stop till dark!!! 
The halls of the hotel are dark and dingy. the carpet was all coming up at the seams. Our room was the standard marriott furnishings. Scuffs all over the walls. The paint on the bathroom door was peeling off. The duvet covers on each of the beds weren't even the same. The carpet looked dirty and was coming up all along the edges. 
Pool was closed for repair my whole stay. There was no notice on the hotels webpage about a pool closure. only a piece of paper at the front desk. 
Overall I am disgusted that Marriott would even call this a four star Marriott. Seriously put some money into this place and train your staff how to be friendly!! Won't stay here ever again. There are way nicer Marriott properties within walking distance.

title_masked: A big thank you to a very professional team!
text_masked:
The Westin was reccomended to me by colleagues who have stayed their several times. I stayed for a week in March 2012 with my family in two connecting rooms. The week was to celebrate two landmark birthdays. Aware of this the hotel provided us with fantastic rooms, and some very thoughtful touches.
The rooms on th 37th floor were spacious and comfortable, well maintained (House Keeping is excellant) and kept very clean. We had great views up 43rd and 42nd Streets and over towards the Empire State Building.
Throughout the hotel the finishes are of a high standard and its all well maintained. The Express lifts are a big advantage when you are that high up!
The front desks were very efficent and helpful, be it checking us in, storing luggage, printing vouchers, providing directions or hailing a taxi, and i left feeling that everyone was very professional and effective.
Room service is also very efficient and the food is qood quality. 
The location is hard to beat, Times Square and Broadway on the doorstep, Empire State, Chrysler, Rockefellar, Grand Central, Central Park, Shopping, all within walking distance or short taxi ride. 
Some good quality delis on the doorstep open day and night if you need to keep eating on the move.
The subway is on the doorstep its the most cost effective and quickest way of getting Down Town.
We booked the hotel as part of a hotel and flight package with British Airways.

This ES is very nicely located, across from the Seaport Village. It has a very nice view of the Bay and the ships passing by. As always, the breakfast was very good with a nice variety of fare. We've stayed in many ES and this one by far had the best Happy Hour. The snacks were healthy and filling--the mixed drinks, beer and wine very good. The staff was very friendly and helpful.

title_masked: Another excellent stay in the Radisson Martinique
text_masked: I stayed in the Radisson Martinique with 6 Family Members for 5 nights during March. This was our 3rd stay at this Hotel and the next time I return to NYC I will definitely stay at this hotel again. Yes the rooms are small (but are spotlessly clean) but this seems to be the case in all Hotels in NYC but the Location more than makes up for this. The Subway is directly outside the front door, you are 2 Blocks from Macy's and walking distance to most of the other Sights.

I booked this on priceline, I wasn't looing for anyhting special so I figured it would be good enough. Not the case. Ive stayed in sone doosies, but this was probably the worst hotel I've stayed in. THere was a big spot in the ceiling that wasnt painted and was obvious that they had recently patched over a previous poor patch job. The bathroom was clean enough. The bed was ok, but squeaked everytime I moved. The carpet was filthy. My socks would stick to it as I walked around. Pretty gross.

To begin, the staff could not have been more friendly or helpful. I was pleasantly surprised as to the size of the room for the money. I Loved the ultra-modern / chic rooms and I did not want to take my robe off. Will probably purchase one my next visit which will be very soon. 
Had a great meal at Marble Lane, the steakhouse in the lobby as well. My server was great. 
Tom Brady

title_masked: Priceline and Expedia customers-beware of bait and switch- otherwise ok place to stay
text_masked:
I arrived at about 5:30 to check in and when I asked for a high floor room, I was told it was to be in the Park Central across the street. My mouth dropped open. They said that they had already booked all of my "class of room". Well, I have stayed at the Park Central as a Priceline customer once and it was the shabbiest darkest room I have stayed in except for the Days Inn on Broadway. I did not get upset. But I refused to leave, and started recounting my experience over there. (Some of these hotels save their worst rooms for Priceline customers.)
Finally they gave in and "upgraded" me. It was a lovely room- newly renovated but the size of a closet (or a New York Apt.) TINY. If this was an upgrade- still wondering what the other option was? The funniest part of the room was the shower curtain bar was so high that the shower curtain hung above the tub so the water just dribbled down. Someone was not thinking. I see more renovations in the future starting with the ceiling below. 
Furthering the second class citizen feel, the free internet listed on the hotel website is not available to Expedia or Priceline customers. I used Starbucks across the street. The window opened a little but even with the heat turned off, was still tropical in there. There was no coffeemaker or fridge (no room for either). 
And some poor exhausted Australians showed up after we went to bed, having been assigned our room. oops. Sorry mate if you got shipped across the street. 
Good location by the NR and by the park.

My 5th stay at the London NYC because its unique style, excellent service, and prime location cannot be matched in the city. I have experienced the hotel's many room offerings from the massive "apartment" to the intimate "double" and always felt my money was well spent. I look forward to a return visit later this summer

title_masked: Great location, Friendly Staff but needs improvement
text_masked: What this hotel lacks in luxury it makes up for with the extremely friendly and attentive staff. I love the location and the staff made us feel very welcome. Breakfast and in and out parking was included with our room, great deal. What I was not impressed with was the room cleanliness or size, the room was very dusty and the bathroom was in a word Dirty. I had to wipe the brown stains from the toilet seat, the room made me want to clean it. Not what you want to do on vacation. The rest of hotel common areas were the same. Dusty surfaces and smudge windows they need a serious spring cleaning. The gym was leaking water onto one of the exercise machine and down the wall. The beds not the most comfortable and the heating/AC very noisy.

title_masked: I don't think they really care
text_masked: Service and value mean a lot to me and cleanliness is where I draw the line. I know things can go wrong, I also know things can be fixed. When I let the staff know about issues in my room and leave for the rest of the day I expect them to be fixed when I return. I also expected they would care when I told them they were not. So much for my expectations. Maybe I'm just spoiled by hotels that care.

I read a few reviews on-line and this place was great. Local flavor by the truck loads plenty of small shops and eateries. Next time we go we will stay there again. Right across the street from the beach sunsets to die for. Everyone at the hotel was great and helpful. The only bad thing about the stay was our room was right at the stairwell other than that it was a perfect get away.

title_masked: Historic hotel; they need to play that up
text_masked: Business traveler, stayed just one night. 9th floor room, nice view, comfortable, quiet, attentive staff. I would stay here again but they need to give some attention to a couple items. 1) the buffet breakfast appears (I didn't go for it) to be really low-cost, heated up baked goods and typical awful eggs and meat on warm plates, nothing special, even though the dining room is elegant and historic. I can get that breakfast at a Courtyard. I walked around downtown SJ and found a number of much better choices; 2) This hotel has a fascinating history, but the staff and design seem to ignore that. Where are the old photos of this hotel in its prime? Movie stars and prominent politicians stayed here...show me the photos! Early photos of parties at the bar?...nothing. They have picture books in the lobby, not of wonderful days of old, but of silly modern weddings. YUCK! Who cares! The best part of this hotel is the write-up of its history hidden in the room notebook. The management here seems to want to ignore the wonderful history but the reality is its the absolute best feature of this place.

title_masked: Roomy but tired hotel in Murray Hill
text_masked: Rooms are extra large with small kitchens, big dining/living spaces and separate bedrooms available in the suites (at prices similar to the pod-like rooms you'll find in most other hotels). The location is slightly out of the way, adding a couple of extra blocks to Midtown, but still walking distance to all amenities. Rooms are clean, though a bit tired. Some attempts at updating have taken place but this is not a new hotel. None of the amenities of Affinia Hotels. That said, the staff was great, the price terrific. I'd stay here again. Perfect, too, for a long-term stay, because you'll have fridge, stove, microwave, dishwasher and basic kitchen equipment so you won't have to eat out all the time.

Sam L's review was right on the money. The hotel was close to Hollywood Blvd, we walked to the Hollywood/vine metro station (10 minute walk) and took the train to Universal Studios. On another day, we walked to Hollywood/Highland ave also (20/30 minute walk). The walk back to the hotel is a little harder because it is up hill after long days at the park and touring, it seemed extra far back to the hotel, so I probably wouldn't recommend it for little kids. We did walk back at night and it seemed a little dangerous with all the cars and crossing the streets. Hollywood has a huge amount of homeless people on the blvd at night. Many urinate on the sidewalks, so you have to watch out for the puddles. We had adjoining hotel rooms on the opposite side of the expressway and they were very compact and small. I thought they were clean and the beds were comfortable. The pool was tiny and didn't stay open very late (9:00 pm). That's probably so that it wouldn't disturb other guests, since it's surrounded by the hotel rooms. The parking is $15.00 with a valet. There is a great little donut shop right next door to the hotel that has an awesome breakfast burrito. It's really cheap too, compared to the diner, Cafe 101. The diner in the hotel is supposed to be famous. Scenes from the Gilmore girls and the movie Sex in the City were shot in the diner.

3 girls who wanted to stay downtown without spending a fortune! I am not a picky person when it comes to staying at a hotel as long as the rooms are nice. I think this hotel has a long way to go. It doesn't give the greatest impression on the outside. When we walked in the room was nice! We only slept there one night so my review is based on this. As the night progressed it got more and more moist. By morning the carpet felt dewy. And it was really noisy. Right next to Interstate. It is at a great location and has great potential. I just think it needs a little more work done.

We stayed in Serrano for 2 nights in end-September and paid about $210 (with taxes) per night. It is expensive, but then again, most well located hotels in SF are. It is a decent hotel, close to the shopping district and transport. During our stay, the hotel offered free coffee in the mornings and free drinks during happy hour in the lobby. The rooms are quite small but well maintained. The staff is friendly and helpful. The only downside to the hotel is that though the location is convenient, it is also very close to the homeless centre. This means that there are areas close to the hotel which should be avoided. (The concierge was good enough to tell us which areas we should avoid.) The check-in time is 3 PM, so if you plan to get in early, make sure you request for an early check-in well in advance.

title_masked: Great location, reasonable prices and have realistic expectations
text_masked: I have stayed here twice in the past 2 years, one time alone, once with my grandson.. Location is great -- Penn Station, subway & bus lines nearby & plethora of passing cabs makes getting around easy. Diner off the lobby is 24 hours. Restaurant in the hotel was acceptable to good. Rates are reasonable for NYC. The poor reviews given to this hotel may well be due to poorly considered expectations. Folks, this is an historic hotel and room sizes won't match bigger, newer ones but work well for two people. As for staff attitude ... I lived in the City years ago so was not expecting Mayberry. Reasonable questions asked in a respectful, polite manner were answered in kind, albeit with the classic NY lack of smiles & prolonged eye contact, which should not be taken personally. I will stay there on future trips.

The rooms were nice and clean. We did not have any problems but the this hotel felt like we have stepped in the 80s. It needs updating badly. The walls are really thin, we could hear footsteps outside and above.

The Strand Hotel has some great features. The front desk staff and bellmen were excellent. The concierge was ok. The housekeeping staff is their weakest link. The room we had in this hotel was rather small, but fine. The shower had "issues" because of a half-wall only, and it leaked onto the floor every time we took a shower, despite our best efforts to keep it dry. Breakfast was ridiculously expensive, and just ok. We also had dinner here and the food was very good. The only suggestion I would have is that they get rid of the "steak sauce" that was served with a very nice steak. The steak sauce was A1 from a bottle. After all that effort to make a nice steak, why not make a little sauce instead of pouring from a bottle. Or, serve it on the side for those that like it.

Very nice, clean, quiet room with beautiful view. Everyone on staff whom I encountered was knowledgeable, helpful and courteous. Excellent level of service from all. 
I ate dinner at an off-premises restaurant, so I can only comment on their breakfast and lunch offerings, both of which were more than satisfactory.
One word of caution: If you are driving to this property, make certain to input the complete address in your GPS. There are at least 6 streets in the area which start with "Ballantyne!"

title_masked: Great location but sketchy rooms and very noisy
text_masked: Stayed one night at the Tremont and tried to keep an open mind going into the property given the reviews are all over the map. Checked into a regular room with a king bed and immediately the street noise hit me even though we were up 10 stories. Even more weird was the complete lack of privacy with the room next door while separated by a connecting door that was locked with a thin single door did not diffuse any noise from the room next door. I could hear entire conversations going on with the couple next door and had to deal with their iphone blaring loud music. I was extremely uncomfortable making phone calls in my room in fear of eavesdropped or interfering with their personal time - I ended up going outside for all calls. The breakfast buffet not included in my rate was a major let down. Stone cold bagels and muffins with sparse cereal options was nothing to write home about. If you are planning on staying here, make sure you ask about the room situation or else you will extremely uncomfortable with the lack of privacy

We have stayed here before when it was the Adams Mark. And although there are signs of age money is being spent and renovations are being made. We did have a billing problem but with the help of David at the front desk all was cleared up before we left. I also recieved a call from Darla Wade an on-site manager. All in all a positive experience.

Stayed at Ink48 for 1 night to celebrate two birthdays, I had let Jeffery know of this before hand, as he had asked if there is anything he could do via email a day prior. A complimentary bottle of champaign had been delivered when we quickly stepped out to walk around the neighborhood right before dusk. (there were two giant cruise ships docked at this time). To our delight, we came back and found the champaign and a birthday card note. Pretty good Jeffery, that was a nice touch there. 
The room was pretty clean, we faced east towards manhattan as requested (among other things requested, all of which Jeffery was able to accomodate somehow). There were no noises of dogs anywhere to be found (dog friendly hotel). I like the hotel, I am really not dog friendly at all unfortunately. So I am really happy that there were no such sounds coming from anywhere as I would have surely complained to the front desk. I do not believe dogs should stay unattended, that's just asking for trouble.
We got haggled by the security guy that stands out in front of the roof top elevator in the downstairs lobby, he asked for our ID's when he should have just asked if we were hotel guests and if he could see our room keys. He gave my girl friend a hard time with her pasport. I would advise this guy to not be so serious, this is a hotel for adults, not a dive bar for kids. I would have gotten annoyed but I was too anxious to get upstairs.
One of the waitresses on the rooftop took the $20 I put down for a single vodka pineapple drink and kept the remaning money, I did not really have the energy to pursue the witch hunt to find this woman and tell her where is my change, but whatever. I considered that very rude, there is nothing the hotel can do about that other than to ensure they hire people who have integrity.
The PRINT restaurant was interesting, we never ended up scheduling dinner like Jeffrey had suggested a day prior in his email, but we tried to do so last minute and he ended up squeezing us in with just a 30minute wait time, bravo there. Food was pretty good, and the decor was great. 
All in all, I will be back in the spring time, the price is good and the customer service was excellent.

title_masked: So glad I wasn't on vacation
text_masked:
I stayed here for 5 days for a conference. While the stay wasn't horrible, I was very glad I wasn't paying rack rates out of my pocket for a vacation at this hotel. I wouldn't stay here again if that were the case.
Pros: Location, location, location. Close to the airport, downtown, North End, and lots of major sights within walking distance. Great dining nearby. Renovated interiors that make it feel a little bit like a Westin hotel (dark woods, modern furniture, clean lines). Overall food at the Waterline restaurant and served at the conference was good (especially the soups).
Cons: First of all, the NOISE. I was stuck on the lobby level facing the aquarium side of the hotel, right above the rent-a-bikes. Saturday night I could hear drunk people and cars until 3 am right outside my window, including three guys who thought it would be fun to ride bikes in circles, yelling and taking pictures. Walls are thin; you can hear people down the hallway talking as if they're right outside your door - not fun when they're coming back from the bars at 2:30 am like last night. There's a lot of construction still going on at the hotel on the lobby level as well. Furniture and fixtures lined my hallway, which the staff decided to open up and unbox/unwrap right outside my door on Sunday morning. Debris littered the hallway as a result. Monday morning, hammering started at 6:50 am; today, it started at 7:45 and finished at 8 am, at which point, loud vibrating machinery (like a sander or buffer) started and continued until I left the room around 9:30. Both days the construction noise woke me up and I couldn't sleep after that. There is NO warning that construction is taking place when you check in; no signage anywhere, and no note in the rooms that apologizes for the disruption. So if you really need peace and quiet and you have to stay here, make sure you get an appropriate room and DON'T book on a weekend when there are events and late-night party-goers out.
Also when I checked in, I went into the bathroom and found the handsoap already open and used, with the empty box sitting on the counter next to a used hand towel. There was water around the faucet and in the sink. I called to request housekeeping to come clean it up. Someone was bringing me a portable fridge for some medication I needed, and when he arrived with the fridge, he just handed me a bag with two bars of fresh soap (boxed) and extra shampoo, conditioner, and lotion. No one actually cleaned the bathroom, removed the towel or threw away the used soap, so I did it (ewww).

You can hardly beat this place for its location: a couple of blocks from the White House, in the middle of everything, close to restaurants and other attractions. In the midst of being totally remodeled, some floors still under construction. Room was nice, staff was friendly.

When I travel for business I'm easy to please. A clean room where I can shower, sleep and go to the bathroom is all I need. So it takes a lot for me to give a place a bad review.
The good: the guy who checked me in was very, very nice. The toilet, sheets and towels (paper thin) were clean. Free, good wi-fi signal.
The bad: The couch smelled so musty that I put a towel over it before sitting on it. I couldn't close the bathroom window because the latch was broken off. The shower was filthy and didn't drain; I stood ankle deep in water. If you're lucky enough to get the loosely-termed "suite" you can see the downtown skyline off in the distance, just over the adult video store. All of the other rooms look out on the boarded up motel across the street. The vinyl backing was falling off the curtains, which made for interesting light patterns on them in the morning. And a lampshade had these weird, old water stains. I'm only assured by the fact that the stains went all the way around that it wasn't something more ... bodily oriented. Overall the place was just ratty. I really liked the thick, one inch wide border of ancient dust that circumnavigated the entire room, right where the vacuum cleaner can't reach it. Also, the motel can't be blamed for this, but the traffic noise on Hwy. 99 is terribly loud. This is also the first time I've ever seen what can only be described as wilting plastic flowers.
I stayed here once before a couple of years ago in a non-smoking room that smelled like an ashtray. Buzzing refrigerator kept me up all night. Never wanted to stay again, but I didn't make the reservation this time and didn't recognize the name until I drove up to it. At which point my heart sank.
The room was cheap. $59 in Seattle awfully low, but you'll get what you pay for. I didn't give it one star because I've stayed in worse. (Nothing will ever beat that awful stay in the thankfully-now-closed Pacific Motor Inn in Springfield, Oregon!)

The longest part of my planing is always regarding hotels. It's hard to combine everything we want: great location, rooms that are clean, spacious, with plenty of amenities, nice service and of course, with reasonable prices.
I'd like to reinforce the "reasonable": that doesn't mean "cheap"- but value for the price.
I thought my experience with the Helmsley Park Lane was just that. Location is stupidly good - and as someone who works with technology, being 50 mts from the Apple Store is something you have to grab without asking.
The check-in experience was good - not great. I can't complain, though - I arrived too early. But they did allow me to get in earlier than usual. The service is fine - I really don't use it much - and the room I stayed in was worthy of its price. Spacious, wifi working fast, nice bathroom - great shower.
Overall it's something that's worth of what you're paying. And if you're looking for location, it's probably one of the best prices you'll get in the area.

We thoroughly enjoyed a recent postponed Valentines Day weekend in Seattle. Our stay at the Marriott Courtyard Pioneer Square was just what we had hoped for; nice hotel, clean and comfortable king sized bedroom, great location, friendly and informative staff, reasonably priced..

Visited this hotel last September. We were given our rooms within a couple of minutes along with a warm muffin which was well-appreciated after 13 hrs of traveling! Rooms are very spacious and beautifully decorated. 2 fridges ( one equipped with drinks etc and the other one left empty for your own use), microwave and coffee machine. The kids were to sleep on a sofa bed which wasn't too comfy so we asked for another mattress. This was brought up to our room in no time at all. The location of the hotel can't be any better; right in the heart of Times Square where there's something going on 24/7. Just one recommendation: don't have breakfast from the hotel. It's good but soooo expensive. If you walk 2 blocks uptown, there's Applebee's where you'll eat better at half the price.

My husband and I enjoyed our one night stay. Lobby and room were nice and clean, staff helpful and polite, complementary breakfast was good, quality of the sleep perfect ! This is a bit far from San Antonio main attractions, but we stayed here to be close to Tejas rodeo as they had a special offer for rodeo fans !

title_masked: Friendly service, nice rooms, reasonable hotel food and beverage
text_masked: We stayed here for two nights while visiting our daughter. This hotel must be stressing outstanding customer service because every staff member was very courteous and always asking how they could be of assistance. I felt like I was in a Four Seasons Hotel. The hotel is located a distance from the city center in a commercial district just off I-35. Free parking is a great plus at a Marriott. Our concierge level room was large and immaculately clean.The beds were comfortable and we got two nights of great sleep. We had breakfast in the restaurant and beverages at the bar and both were relatively inexpensive for a Marriott.

title_masked: Great location on the Colorado River close to lovely walks and within walking distance of the centre of Austin
text_masked:
Free parking, heated swimming pool, fitness centre, great service and great location - the Holiday Inn in Austin is a great place to stay to explore the Austin region.
We had the biggest room we have ever had in any hotel (Room 1140) with a microwave, decent size fridge and free wifi.
The multistorey car park next to the hotel is free with a lift straight into the hotel.
Great stay, if I was in Austin again, would definitely use the hotel again.
If there was one downside it was the air conditioning - when it was switched off there was still a low level droaning noise.
Oh and I forgot to mention the view from this huge room - full length window overlooking the river and the surrounding area - fantastic.

Got this room for an amazing rate through Priceline, so that we wouldn't have to travel over Snoqualmie Pass in the wee hours. As we left baggage claim at SeaTac at 12:51 a.m., we called the hotel to request the shuttle. The clerk said it would be 10 - 15 minutes, and to wait at Island One. We were at Island One within 3 minutes. We watched and waited and finally called the hotel. The clerk said the driver had been through there and didn't see us! SOOOO!?!?! We were the only couple waiting at Island One; we looked at each and every single shuttle that came through there! And so what if he really did pass through there? (We don't believe he did.) Why didn't he come BACK? Were they really going to just let their registered guests sit there and wait?! In the cold wet wee hours of SeaTac airport? Unbelievable! As for the room - the bed was pretty hard, the shower was good, everything was dated, but clean.

Let's get the easy stuff out of the way-the hotel was clean, modern and appears to have been recently renovated. Great for vacation but not for business travelers. It was a $30 cab ride to the convention center (I thought it was much closer and they will tell you on the phone that it's a short cab ride).
I checked in at night and the reception is not the hotel. You haveto go back outside to get to your room even for the tower. It's not well light and the signs were confusing. It's like your wandering around Jurasic Park. I finaly found the entrance to the tower. Now to find the bar...one of then is in the restuarant Red Marlin..a short hike through the jungle. My friend isnt there..he's in the pool bar..which also doesnt have an inside entrance. Back through the jungle. You can see the bar but you cant get to it. Now a locked gate (have to use your room key). Now the bar, but where's the door in all this glass. OK..now setttled. No soft drink machines on the floors, no coffee in the lobby. Breakfast is back at the Red Marlin..what??? OK..there's a Enstein Bagel shop..how do I get there? back through Jurasic Park..down the path..through the parking lot, Turn right up the path to the walkway.. Walk down 100 yards to the store. Get it?? I checked out heading for the Bayfront Hilton...everything's in one building..including the coffee.

We recently stayed at the Omni Parker House. We were able to check in early at 11am which was great.
The room was nice with a king size bed and nice size TV. The A/C worked well and the room wasn't too small. The bathroom was very small, but this wasn't a major issue.
The food that we had at the hotel was very good and the drinks were strong in the Last Hurrah Bar.
I would definitely recommend this hotel.

Just stayed in D.C. for less than 24 hours for business. This was actually the cheapest hotel I could find in the area. It was amazing!!! The room was great even though I only got to sleep in it for a few hours. When I went to work and came back at about 4am, there was still someone at the desk to greet me. Very friendly and great atmosphere. Had breakfast at the attached restaurant...was pricey but very good.

We picked this hotel for its proximity to LA Live. For the price we paid we were disappointed at how dated the rooms were. The room had a faint smell of old water although the room appeared clean. The beds, dresser and TV were the only furnishings that seemed to be updated in the last decade. The closet had old mirrored doors, the bathroom had a sink faucet from 1980 and overall had a time warp feel. The light switches were dated along with the lamps, phone and alarm clock. This hotel's only saving grace was its modern lobby which includes a restaurant, Starbucks, internet area and a small TV 'living room'. Also, another positive was the free parking across the street at a meter on a Sat night to Sunday.

Great Value in perfect location. Just next door to Times Square and just a few blocks away from Central Park.
On the downside was the roomsize, really small. But what do you expect at these prices in this location.

stayed for just 1 night in a jacuzzi double, large room with huge bath for 2. The decor is a bit dated, but clean and smart looking. There is free wifi, just ask for a code and the breakfast is included and there's a good choice of pasteries, waffles, eggs all fresh and tasty. The area is kind of trendy bars and the water front, its a very relaxed area and we ate at one of the bars, but there was also a really great ice cream place. The penn harbour area is nice, and we were there on Friday night and were treated to live music and a fire works display, it seemed to be on most weeks and there's a schedule for the summer worth checking out. Only about 5 minutes walk to all the historical sites that you could want in Philadelphia and there's a metro station 1 minute away. It's quiet, clean and friendly and would definitely go again.

The rooms are small but not as bad as some of the other European rooms I've been in! But its not as terrible as I thought it was going to be based on the other reviews. Yes, the bathroom is very very small. But the room itself is nicely arranged, the room is decent sized and its enough space for 1 perosn. I suggest you get a bigger room if there is more than 1 person! Location is fantastic! And the staff, from check in to conceriage to room service is great! Walls are slightly thin though so I could hear all the other unruly guests on their way back at 3am. The bar is also very nice. Very chic place to stay. Took me quite a while to fine it though.

title_masked: Too big to be treuly good
text_masked: It's not a bad hotel. My room was renovated not long ago, not so big as you could expect from 4 diamonds hotel, but I guess this is very common thing for NYC, especially in Manhattan. Still it was clean, cozy enough and everything was there. But being so big (51 floors) the hotel has breakfast room small enough even for a hotel of 300 rooms. I was told that many Americans prefer having breakfast outside, as it's much cheaper, but I guess those who had to queue some mornings didn't know about such an option, or were foreigners as myself. With around 1500 rooms they have usual number of staff at the lobby. So be ready to queue as well to check in and out or to ask concierge about restaurant you have an appointment at. Computers (6 or 8 of them) with free Internet are so popular that if you happen to be there without your lap top, you have to wake up at 6 a.m. and rush downstairs to find one or two free to use. Still the location is good, service is ok. Not bad but too big

title_masked: Incredible service in a perfect location
text_masked: We got a great rate for a weekend extension following a business trip at another hotel. The concierge, Shah, went to work before we arrived and continued to be amazingly helpful. His suggestions and directions worked out perfectly -- ask for him! The hotel is located by two cable car lines and an easy walk to great restaurants and neighborhood haunts. It was quiet and accommodating. We'd definitely choose it again!

I'm about to complete a six-night stay at the hotel with my wife and four-year old son. I have traveled around the world and have stayed at some very good hotels. What I have been blown away by at the Omni Parker House is the service and enthusiasm of the employees at the hotel. From the maids, to the bellmen, to the front desk, everyone went above and beyond.
For example, last night my son woke up late and was still hungry. He wanted pasta but had to settle for pizza since there wasn't any pasta available for room service (at least at 11:30 pm). The gentlemen who brought the food to us could not have been kinder to my family and threw in two extra bottled waters to make up for the lack of pasta. This is the kind of extra effort which sets the Omni Parker House apart from other hotels. The only other hotels that I've experienced this level of service are in Asia and the Middle East, and I was paying a lot more for those rooms than I am at the Omni Parker House.
In any event, my compliments go out to their incredible staff.

title_masked: Very nice hotel near the Convention Center
text_masked: This hotel is within easy walking distance to the Convention Center which makes it very convenient. We used this hotel as the main meeting facility for the American Society of Landscape Architects. The hotel provided great meals and the meeting rooms were large and spacious. I would definitely come to this hotel again if was in town for a convention. The restaurant was very nice and the food was excellent. The room that I had was on the corner, so I didn't have anyone next to me which was great. it was a bit annoying to have to use my room key on the elevator to get to my room, but after a while I got used to it. I did hear some of the other people in the meeting complain that they felt that the meeting rooms were too cold, but to me they were just right. One other thing that this hotel offered was a special $5.00 coupon to the restaurant if you chose not to have daily housekeeping. That was a nice feature and I took advantage of it. The only bad thing was that it was ONLY good in the restaurant and not the coffee bar which was unfortunate.

Loved this place! Located walking distance to MOMA, Shopping, Trump Tower with easy access to subways and other sights. Welcome champagne upon arrival. Excellent restaurants across the street. We took our kids and the room was quite spacious! The beds were super comfy! This place had a very futuristic feel which was really cool!

Truly first class. We searched tirelessly for a wedding reception venue and are so happy we chose the InterContinental and they're wedding team (Chris Schmidt). The location and facility speak for themselves, but the service we received exceeded our expectations, which were high. Guests couldn't stop complimenting the speed and quality of service, along with the food. Highly recommend!

title_masked: Great Hotel in Heart of NYC
text_masked: Our party of three - my mum, my sister and I spent 4 nights at the Casablance in mid March and we'd a fabulous stay! Our room was at the back of the hotel and very quiet so we'd great nights sleep after walking Manhatten, we'd two compact double beds in our room and they were very comfortable. All staff that we encountered were so friendly and helpful, lovely people! The inclusive breakfast was enjoyed and we took full advantage of Ricks Cafe, both on pitstops during the day and also after our evenings out. I was very impressed by the fact that we were encouaged to use Ricks while we waited for our taxi to the airport at 6pm, a lovely touch as once you check out in most hotels the only facility available is luggage storage. All in all a great hotel and we'll be back next time we're in NYC.

my husband and i spent 2 days at the drury and it was wonderful,room was spotless.we stayed on 8th floor which was great.i highly reccomend this place for families,the breakfast was awesome tons of choices.but i think what families will appreciate is the evening snacks.wow you can eat dinner here .free from great baked potatoes to salad.nachos and hotdogs.and every one is so helpful..the only negitive was the pools the rooftop pool was aweful green dingy lots of people were in it but i was not going to risk it.indoor pool next door was worse, when i stepped inside room the chlorine was so strong i almost got sick..you really could not breathe.and that was one of the reasons we picked the hotel was for pool ..but you are right on river and we never used our car we walked to alamo and all over.but i would come back ..

I think this Red Roof Inn have very mannerable workers that put fort and extra effort it pleasing you or getting you booking to your room which is a major plus. Nice rooms with much space in them that your not cramped up and your confrontable. Great prices for room that make it easier of my company book with you all instead of running around look for the best deals or the most cheapest room which can be a rude awaking sometime with the quality of the room, but make everything so easy and simple thank Reed Roof!!!!!

What a great hotel. The ambiance is fantastic, rooms are quaint, location is fantastic. Their Colonial Room restaurant is outstanding, with great food and service, and a lovely guitarist in the evening. History everywhere you look. Would definitely stay here again.

Easy walks to the Wharf and many sights. Parking is very expensive but you can get a 24h/parking deal just around the corner for half the price! Marriott is Marriott - it's a good one. Downside has been the concierge: Unbelievable that after 6 pm no one can make a reservation in a restaurant for you. But other than that: A good place and we would go again.

the hotel is very clean and the staff are helpful. the carpets throughout could do with renewing, and tea and coffee are only available in the lobby, the lobby is quite small and there is no bar. the location is very good, close to all transport and bars and restaurants and chinatown.There are lots of top stores nearby if you want to shop.

title_masked: Some good and some not so good
text_masked: This is an average hotel. Generally clean and generally maintained. Their is always a line at the elevators. For whatever reason they didn't have enough capacity. This is very noticeable as many people commented on it during my 4 day stay. The bathroom was not maintained as the bathtub didn't drain and the faucet leaked. The staff is somewhat friendly. The free breakfast coupon was a pleasant surprise. It allows for the breakfast buffet which is very good.

If you have work in the North area of the city, this is a great place to stay. Very efficient and helpful staff. Although the property is locted next to the highway, its very quiet. Several eating places close by too.

title_masked: Perfect for a family break in DC to see the sites.
text_masked: Not 5 star but perfect, roomy, big and great location. 5 of us 3 kids under 7 stayed there for 2 nights. We walked to the white house and museums easily each day, used the hotel pool and relaxed in our clean v spacious room. Only slight criticism was the kitchen was equipped in 70s but all worked perfectly and was clean. The kids loved it! We booked on Expedia $165 a night parking extra 46 a night.

title_masked: A little off the beaten path but hotel was otherwise great!
text_masked:
We booked a room at the TRYP Hotel Times Square South for a spur of the moment trip to NYC with our 3 young boys (5 of us total). The lodging was great - they upgraded us on arrival to a family room (we had booked a premium), which has bunk beds. That was fun for the little guys and the room was enormous! It had sleeping for 8 - bunk beds, pull out sofa, and two queen beds. It also had a bench and hook upon entry for back packs, coats, shoes, etc. which kept the clutter out of the rest of the room. Huge kitchen area with a sink and an extra mirror (made brushing teeth and getting ready faster), hotel staff was superb, and room was brand new.
We didn't eat breakfast in the hotel as it was close to 20.00 a person. Instead, the first day we went to the Skylight Diner (very good, excellent service and no wait) - it was around the corner on 9th Ave so less than a block away. The next day we ate at Andrew's Coffee Shop in the Herald Square area (7th and 35th maybe). Much busier but that place was run like a machine - super efficient. 
The blue line subway/penn station is at the end of the TRYP block. To get to the orange line (Rockefeller Center, etc), you need to walk a block or two.
The reason we stayed at this hotel was because of the room size (we have 5 and 3 are young so we didn't want two rooms), and proximity to the theater where we were seeing a show Friday night. It was easy to get to the show and to Radio City Music Hall (where we saw the Rockettes Saturday) from our hotel. It was less easy to get downtown for the Staten Island Ferry, Wall Street, Ground Zero, etc.
Not sure I would stay there again just because of the location but if you are traveling with a large group and don't want multiple rooms, it is a great option!

In August of 2012 I was the event planner for my company conference that took place at Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers.
Great location, friendly staff, over the top service from the front desk and good meeting space.

title_masked: Attitude and Cleanliness detract from what is pretty good
text_masked:
We booked into the Penthouse Suite which cost around $400 per night. 
When one books a penthouse, there is an expectation of better than average, but this is definitely not the case. 
One female staff member has a real attitude problem and she is quite rude and overbearing. Request was made for regular coffee where decaffeinated was provided and she argued the point regular coffee was provided and even after being shown what was provided, she continued her rudeness. She argued the heating was on when it was not, so a cold night was endured with no extra blankets provided and when asked why room service was not attended we were told guests cannot remain in their rooms when cleaning staff are present due to union rules, however we were not told of this prior. You just know she argued about this also. Staff were unable to return to clean the room as they were due to finish work for the day. I asked if there would be a rate reduction as no room service was provided. Her reply floored me. "You have plenty of money sir, you can afford it." Cleaning standards are very poor, a toddler finding scraps around edges of the carpet, which were stale food scraps.
Fittings of the Penthouse are tired and are overdue for replacement. Carpets are old and lifting and poorly cleaned.
I have stayed in the regular rooms of this hotel previously and they were to an acceptable standard, however this is not the case now.
The bedding is comfortable and the free parking is appreciated.

Stayed here for one night while in NYC on business and for a wee bit of R&R. They treated us right, with not the least bit of pretension, even on a discounted rate, and put us on the 31st floor with a view of the Empire State Building and a partial view of the Hudson. Rooms are small, and somewhat basic but tidy and clean with good beds and decent sized bathrooms with shower and quality toiletries. Generally the place has minimalist but tasteful and fun decor. There are 3 Apple computers in the lobby for guests to use and free wifi in the rooms. There are only 4-5 rooms on each floor. Didn't try the restaurant/bar but there is so much to try on 9th Avenue from pizza to ethnic food, don't miss that! If you're headed to the Theatre District and Times Square both are a short walk. We walked here from NY Penn Station after arriving on Amtrak. Definitely check out the Distrikt hotel, it deserves the great reviews its getting here.

We stayed for one night - the staff was super friendly and the location was great. Just a couple blocks from Grant Park. Price was okay I guess considering we were downtown but I know I've stayed at other hotels that to me seemed better for that same price. 
One of the 2 guest elevators was out of order so we used the freight elevator a lot. The room. Well, it was clean but because the whole room (trim, pipes, wiring, etc.) were all covered in texture spray, it made the room seem dirtier than I think it really was. The windows were frozen in time. Wouldn't open and wouldn't close - gap at the bottom of one window allowed cold air to flow in. Beds were hard and pillows were horrible. I was kept awake at night listening to the flushing of toilets. Nothing I couldn't deal with for one night but an extended stay will not be in my future.

it is a nice and cozy boutique hotel, friendly staff and very clean rooms. If you are staying on the weekends, it is very quiet neighbourhood at nights and not as convenient as midtown area.
