Food is good (only had breakfast), service fast and I really like Thomson Chain, next time I will try their other locations in NYC.

The Cassa is the perfect hotel for a stay in NYC. Centrally located (on 45th Street between 5th & 6th Avenue) it's ideal for a long weekend of shopping & sight seeing.
The staff were excellant - always available to help with friendly greetings. Housekeeping was top standard. Rooms were large for NYC (we were in Executive rooms) and bathrooms were large for NYC.
The restaurant wasn't opened at the time of our visit, so used the 10th floor terrace for a few drinks before heading out. The lack of a restaurant may be seen as an issue for some, but shouldn't be - your in NYC and there are places a plenty to eat & drink

title_masked: Potentially great but flawed in the execution
text_masked:
Booked for three nights in a London Suite, November 27th-30th, based largely on TA reviews. On the good side the hotel is excellently located for our mission to experience New York in the holiday season, go to plays and the Rockettes, watch the tree lights come on and wine and dine with friends. There are also no negatives about the actual building, eg the London Suites are spacious and well appointed.
On the bad side there just seemed to be something organizationally lacking in this hotel. 
Issues noted in no particular order:-
Room service slow to dreadfully slow. When you call for a pot of coffee and they say "25" minutes and 50 minutes later the coffee is still in room service you lose confidence. When the hot water is announced to be switched off from 10pm - 8am for the first two nights but you find that it still takes 40 minutes to get a hot shower on the third night you lose more confidence. When it takes more than 30 minutes to get a drink at a table in the trendy London Bar that's frustrating. When you spend more than $1,300 on dinner for 4 at Gordon Ramsay and then "enjoy" the after dinner ambiance of the London Bar with people being asked to leave for throwing drinks and others allowed to stay even though they are dropping the F bomb loudly and often it makes you wonder why you didn't just go to the Pub across the street. The feeling in the bar that night, November 28th. was that the manager was out of town and nobody else knew how to control the problem drinkers. Still some very personable employees but someone really needs to manage this place if it is going to live up to it's potential.

This property is an old building that is well located if you are going to the Redbirds or a basketball game. Quick walk to either. Neighborhood not pristine, but that is true across most of downtown Memphis. Facility is clearly tired, but it is more interesting than the typical side of the highway new box style Residence or Fairfield Inn. The staff are nice and seem to be busting it for guests. The bellman and the night manager found us a spot to park a Suburban with a roof box that would not fit in the garage. 
The room we had was good sized. The common area for breakfast reflected the classic nature of the lobby and the breakfast was good.

We spent 3 nights here and loved it! The hotel is beautifully updated. Loved that it was a historic structure---actually the old Boston P.D. Had a room on the 6th floor and didn't notice any noise there. Staff was pleasant; no problems encountered during our stay. We used bookit.com and had a noticeable discount on the room rate. It was very reasonable for a Boston hotel that has such a great location. We walked to the Pru, up and down Boylston and Newberry Street, through the Public Garden and the Common, up to Beacon Hill, over to Faneuil Hall and Quincy Market and back through downtown and the theatre district. We did not get as far as the North End, but we could have walked another 15 minutes or taken a cab over. The beauty of Boston is that everything is accessible! Took the T (subway) on the green line to BU and on the red line to Harvard Square. There are PLENTY of great restaurants near the hotel; plenty of shopping; and the DUCK tour is a pleasant 15 minute walk (a must do!) Warning: all the walking you will do will be exhausting in the heat of summer! Go between Sept and May and have a great time!

I have stayed at this property twice, while attending a meeting nearby. The service at this hotel is great; very friendly staff greet you upon arrival, are eager to please, and are quite accommodating throughout your stay. Also, the free breakfast has a great selection, and the manager's reception is a welcome endcap to a busy day.
All said, this hotel is in need of some TLC. The paint was chipping on some of the walls, the carpets look worn, and the elevators were terrifying (one actually broke while we were there). I don't know that this would ever prohibit me from staying here in the future, since it's not terrible, just in need of refreshing, and the service is so good. Also, the rooms are quite large, which is great if you are traveling with anyone.
What does make me less inclined to stay here is that every time I have been there (both times on the weekend), there are children's birthday parties, bachelorette parties, sweet sixteen birthday parties, and children's sporting teams galore staying there as well. This does not translate into a quiet stay, as the rooms all surround the very acoustically lively atrium (parrot included). This does mean that the hotel is very family-friendly, though, and I would imagine it's much quieter during the work week. 
I would recommend this hotel, but make sure it coincides with your needs (quiet sleep versus family time).

title_masked: Just an average place in a great location
text_masked: I stayed here this past week for one night. I felt like the check in process was a little long and the line long. The hotel is older and isn't super fancy. The bedding seemed older on my bed and the texture of the comforter bothered me. The soaps and shampoos were really awesome in the bathroom. The halls and interior seemed a bit dated and beat up. The fitness room was a bit of a joke. I also felt like they need a bellman or at least a sign pointing to parking. I pulled up and had to stop with flashers in a no parking zone to run in and search for someone to ask where to park. That made me anxious. There is a garage next door that they have an agreement with. I also think it would've been nice to be able to grab a bite to eat in a hotel restaurant. Still, the location can't be beat. It's almost next to the Hancock building and just a short walk to the back bay area and Boylston Street.

This is a perfectly fine Omni hotel in a perfectly dull area. But for a quick business trip to North Dallas, I got a good rate ($122) and it was convenient both to where I needed to be and to the airport. You absolutely need a car unless you plan to eat in the hotel. There was no charge for parking. The king sized bed was comfortable, linens fine, room clean, end tables a little worn. I wouldn't go out of my way to stay here, but if I needed to be in this area for no more than a night or two and the rates were good I would book again.

After reading some of the reviews on here, the hotel was much better than I expected. My room was a decent size and clean. The building is old but I did not smell anything funny. The hotel is kept very cold and so I was happy that there was a thermostat in my room. I prefer about 70 degrees. No problems at all with check in or check out. They held my bag the last day and I picked it up 8 hours later before catching my train out of Boston. The location is great if you need to be at Boston University (which I did). It is right on the campus practically and there are restaurants nearby at Kenmore. The T stop is a block away and very quick into downtown Boston--only a few stops. 
I ate breakfast there only a couple of times. It was your typical hotel continental breakfast with coffee, tea, bagels, fruit, yogurt, cereal, juice. They had waffles but I did not eat that. My room was also very quiet. I have no complaints. It is not a luxurious hotel, but if you are there for school, business or perhaps baseball, it's not a bad deal.

My wife and I took a 4 day trip to Chicago and had the good fortune to stay at The Silversmith. We had a king bed room but upon our arrival were upgraded to a suite which gave us a little more room to unpack and get settled in. The hotel itself is right downtown, steps from the "L" and a block from Michigan Ave and Grant park. The location made trips to the Sears Tower (having lived in Chicago a number of years ago I refuse to call it the Willis Tower), Field Museum, Shedd, Art Institute, etc very easy to manage. The one downside was a very small exercise room, but when I come back this will be my first choice to stay.

title_masked: Boutique hotel close to everything downtown
text_masked:
We spent the evening in Denver during the 5280 Restaurant Promotion and would definitely stay at Magnolia Hotel again. The friendly staff began with the Doormen and continued into the Lobby and Front Desk. Check in was a breeze, the room was nicely furnished and clean and Harry's was a fun stop to end the night. 
Unfortunately we were on our way out during their Happy Hour in the Lobby, but there were probably 20-30 people who looked like they were having a good time. 
The Breakfast Buffet had the usual selection of scrambled eggs, sausage, and oatmeal but hit the spot and was included, so how could you go wrong?

My wife and recently stayed at the Omni Hotel. The hotel is located right in the heart of Downtown Charlotte, which we loved. The room was very nice and big. The bed was very comfortable. Also, we found the concierge to be very helpful. There is a Walgreens and several restaurants (including Starbucks) on the plaza level. Overall, we really enjoyed our stay. 
There were only a couple of things that we didn’t like. First, while the room is large, the space is not used well. The bathroom ridiculously small…to the point that was hard to get out of the way of the bathroom door when closing it. The sad thing is that there is unused space that could be used to expand the bathroom. Second, though the room clean, there were certain things (the curtains and the counter) that we could tell hadn’t been cleaned in a while. Despite these two shortcomings, we liked the hotel and would stay there again.

We were with a conference group and they went over and beyond to make sure our stay was OK. For instance, when the hurricane was arriving they shut down the restaurant so employees could go home but they also had pasta delivered to our group (instead of just appetizers) so no one went to bed hungry.They have a nice tavern (Diamond, I think) that we ate at for dinner and breakfast. The crab cakes are a MUST! Loaded with crab and delicious. My husband liked the breakfast buffet. The room had a flat screen TV and a king bed. Carpet a little worn, but all was clean and neat. Would stay here again. You can walk to harbor area which is really pretty.

title_masked: Great hotel to call home for a week
text_masked: We stayed here for almost a week and it was really nice to be in a place that almost felt like home. The beds were comfortable, the evening reception (M-Th) offered a great variety of foods and drinks, the breakfast offering was very complete with a different "main" course offering each morning. This hotel is close to San Diego and the beaches so it is ideal for business or pleasure. The staff was very friendly and anxious to please. All in all a great place to stay in this area.

Location: Unbeatable. Two blocks or less from BART, MUNI, and a cable car line. No dragging suitcases onto a street car.
Service: Speedy check in, very nice staff. As I had a conversation with the front desk clerk, he told me that apparently some travelers are not aware that a hotel (any hotel) will put a temporary authorization on your credit card before the final bill is tallied. This is a common practice of hotels and rental car agencies world wide. Welcome to the 21st century. Enjoy your new BetaMax.
Cleanliness: No grossness to report. Yes, I checked for bedbugs: none.
Room fixtures: Everything in working order: lights, tv, etc.. Shower water became hot quickly, in room climate control was nice. I stayed in February so I cannot confirm whether or not the room had a/c.
Security: Room locks were sturdy and worked well. The elevator requires room key activation and the stairwell is near the front desk with camera coverage.
The View: I had room 429 with an inside view, i.e. a view of the other rooms right across the corridor. Otherwise, this hotel is between tall buildings with no real view to speak of. San Francisco is one stunning scenic view after another, so you will not suffer for lack of scenery. If you insist on a skyline vista out of your window, walk on by.
Breakfast: Nothing remarkable, but nice. Pastries, fruit, juice, coffee, etc. Just enough to get you going and out. Breakfast is on the 5th floor. The ice machine is on the 4th floor. Request a high room.
Size of the room: Yes, the room I had was very small. There was no more than 3 feet of space between the bed and the wall in any direction. I had to store my suitcase in the surprisingly large bathroom. I did not object to this, but I was disappointed to discover no traditional table or desk with a chair in this room. The room was just too small for any more furniture.
Noise levels: With an inside room on the 4th floor, I had absolutely no night club or street noise. The walls were a bit thin, so I could hear my neighbors' activities. If you honeymoon here, you may see an admiring crowd giving you a standing ovation when you exit your room.
Overall recommendation: Absolutely yes. Despite some mild issues mentioned above, this property is a great option for those looking for a home base from which to conquer San Fran but still want a real, grown up hotel.

title_masked: Theatre Weekend at The Muse in NYC
text_masked:
Spent a long Theater Weekend at The Muse Hotel in NYC (7/19-22, 2012). First time at a Klimpton propoerty and was more than impressed. Last trip was at a large 2,000 room property, we didn't enjoy it. The Muse was wonderful from the moment we arrived out front -- the doorman grabed our bags and welcomed us to the Muse with a big smile. In fact the Front Desk was all smiles -- the whole weekend! Lots of how are you's? Can we help with anything? Have some water, or have a glass of wine (hapy hour 5p-6p nightly). Marc Camacho one of the Concierges was a big help in resolving a problem we had (none-hotel related). The room (we upgraded to an Executive Suite was roomy, the AC was chilling, and the water pressure in the shower amazing (ok, so that may only be important to me). Tastefully decorated, having a separate bedrom from the sitting room was a nice plus, and not that much more per night! The location of the hotel is really good for the Theatre District -- two blocks from Times Square (but none of the traffic and noise), and most of the BroadwayTheatres are within a 6 six block radius -- even in the rain, a 10-15 minute walk to most places. We had such a pleasant experience will will definitiely return again and again -- I read other reviews on TA before we booked/travelled, and found most of the good points true, but didn't see the negatives that some wrote (go figure?). Bottom line -- I'll go again! (The fact they support Diversity, are "Green", and appear to be a very P.C. company also made me feel good about my choice!)
If you book there - I can only help that you have as wonderful time at The Muse as we did!

hello to who ever reads this i highly recomend this hotel for you r extended travels the staff is very helpful in many ways its a safe feeling that there is always a member of security there in case anything happens there is always someone to get ahold of on the phone if you have any questions just wanted to say thanks eisenhauer you rock

My husband and I stayed at the Flatiron hotel for two nights last week. We were there to celebrate our anniversary to to catch up with old friends because we moved away from NYC 10 years ago.
Location: Perfect for us. We both used to work in the neighborhood, so we're especially comfortable with the area and it was easy for all our friends to come meet us in the Toshi bar downstairs.
Toshi Lounge: Loved it. Added a good vibe to an area that we remember being really dead at night. My husband couldn't help but notice and mention (repeatedly) what a good looking crowd of women were at the bar on Thursday night. Obviously, if we still lived up there, that would be his new Thursday night hangout. :)
The room we were put in on the 9th floor was a good size, so judging by the other reviews on here, ours may have been bigger. The bathroom was especially spacious, so we must have landed a good room. Husband also liked the TV in the mirror. Typical guy. He likes pretty girls and cool gadgets, go figure. 
The front desk staff could not have been nicer. We mentioned we were there for anniversary when we checked in and they made a big to-do about it. You would have thought it was our honeymoon instead of our 17th year together. Made us feel very welcome.
Overall, the place was clean, comfortable, safe and welcoming with a funky vibe that made me give it the full five stars. Def planning on staying here again next time. Thanks so much!

The most impressive quality of this hotel is its service. The staff are very responsive and very attentive, an added bonus to just a great hotel. The rooms were decorated tastefully and are quiet. The bathrooms were large. And, the place was clean. The roof top pool and jacuzzi were quite enjoyable. My only complaint is that my king size bed was really a queen size as demonstrated by the difference in the headboard and mattress size. I chose not to take a different room. The location of the hotel is also nice. Not too close in the center of everything on the Riverwalk but not too far away either. I will definitely stay here again.

title_masked: the price is high, but it is Beverly Hills babe!
text_masked:
I found this hotel very expensive. However, it was worth the money for the location, treatment and ease of stay.
the check-in staff were very friendly; thanking me for being a priority points member - make sure you join these things; they are free and on my holiday here I got lots of perks. (room upgrades, goodies, preferred parking, reduced resort parking rates etc)
If you stay here, you will be pleased by the in-room coffee (I had spent 3 weeks travelling drinking in-room coffee with 'creamer powder', but this hotel give you proper milk. (well, you know the sort in the mini pots but it is better than powder). 
The bathroom is quite small, but the beds and general luxury around make up for that. 
A really enjoyable stay with on-site parking ($22.00) but you expect that in central LA.
Check this one out if you're happy to spend the extra!

title_masked: Good location for shops and cable cars, but slow breakfast.
text_masked: The hotel is just by Union Square which is the heart of the shopping district and close by the cable car stops so ideal. Service was good and facilities fine. The bedroom was a little dark and the queue of up to 30 minutes for breakfast were the only negatives. We enjoyed our stay. San Francisco is excellent.

title_masked: A Decent Motel in the Castro Area
text_masked:
We stayed here two nights. Off street parking was a major plus, especially after walking down one of the side streets coming back from lunch and seeing a broken car window with the glass still on the ground. I would recommend a second or third story room if you want some security. First floor rooms are literally open to the world. There is only one elevator and no hand carts for luggage were available the night we checked in.
Be prepared as most rooms don't have AC. We had windows open (there is a bar that prevents each window from opening more than 6") and the fan running. Even with the window open, the place was relatively quiet, especially considering that you are right on Market Street. 
Yes, the complex is old, but the location is right. The front desk did claim they were planning to renovate the place this winter. The room was clean and modest, with a flat screen TV, a refrigerator, and a large closet. The bed was acceptable. Public transportation is a short walk away. In a nutshell, it served our purpose.

This hotel has everything!
Location cannot be beaten,friendly staff,gorgeous rooms and views, delicious breakfast and a comfortable lobby.Definitely the best choice for a New York vacation!

This was our third stay at the hotel and we were not disappointed. The quaint boutique hotel continues to delight us and we recommend it highly. 
On this occasion we opted for a junior suite as the standard rooms are fairly small (very well equipped though) and we prefer more space. The cost of the larger room was only marginal. In fact overall the pricing is fabulous. Not only are the room rates very well priced, there are some excellent inclusions including; complimentary continental breakfast (wide range of options), tea and coffee avail all day, daily evening wine and cheese between 5.30-7pm, turndown service with bottled water, cookies in the evenings and a range of other things. Whilst there is no restaurant on site, room service is available based on the menu of Morton's steakhouse next door.
The staff are excellent and offer a very personal yet professional service. Nothing is too much trouble. As always, we were made to feel very welcome.
The location is also a bonus. Located just at Union Square, the hotel is within easy walking distance of the Union Square shopping precinct, restaurants, bars, China Town and the famous cable cars. Areas like Fisherman's Wharf, Golden Gate Park, etc are a short taxi ride away. I'm sure public transport would be easy too. 
A highly recommended hotel for your next visit to San Francisco. We will definitely return!

I love this Hotel! It was tastefully decorated, and unique. The bar serves wonderful drinks too. Every single staff person was extermely friendly. The room and bathroom (with Bliss products-yay!) had all the bells and whistles!

We stayed three nights for a spontaneous weekend trip in NYC.
Even before our stay we got everything organized and prepared very professiobnally by the two concierges Vanessa and Sergio. They managed to letting us have the best nyc trip we could ever have. From theater tickets to reservations in top restaurants to nightclubs, a heli tour and personal advice for the best city sightseeing tours, they have done everything for us. Sergio even managed to arrange an appointment for a luxury appartment inspection - just another example for our superb service experience. 
Our room was small but very cozily equipped. Bathroom appeared very hygienic, bed was very comfortable.
Although we stayed on the 12th floor, we could still hear the cooling system from outside quite loud in our room.
In total, the concierge service made the difference for us which we have never experienced in such an intense way before.
Thank you Vanessa, Thank you Sergio for your great support :-)
We will definitely come back!
Regards
Benni

I have stayd here a couple of times when in town for buisness. good location to Garden, North End restaurants, and T. Rooms are small and furnishings look a little worn but the bathrooms have been updated and are clean. Very personable staff at the front desk.

This is my favorite Seattle hotel! The standard rooms are nice, but their suites are totally worth the price. Yes, the hotel is in an older building but that is absolutely part of the charm. The rooms are well appointed and comfortable. The staff is always friendly and helpful. The bookstore bar makes fanastic hand crafted cocktails.

title_masked: trains at night will wake you
text_masked:
This hotel was unwisely built next to an EXTREMELY LOUD train station and trolley station. The staff provide earplugs, but forget it. 
Yes, the property is clean. But the train...prepare to not sleep when the trains go by, HONKING their horns.
The room was a little small, but clean and nicely decorated, nice marble tops in both rooms and clean bright bathroom. Hotel was nearby everything and easy parking.

After 11hours of flying from england, we just wanted a shower, some food then a comfortable bed! We waited about 25minutes for the free shuttle bus as it was full the first time it came past. Then another 10min wait at reception to check in. Once in our room there was a live bug, about the size of a dime ( or a 5pence coin ). I called house keeping...waited about 30minutes, called again then very quickly a guy came and took the bug away. He asked if wanted to change rooms but we were just so exhausted we said if there were anymore bugs then we would but since there weren't, we stayed put. We woke up to find complimentary vouchers for a continental breakfast due to the whole bug in our room. That was a nice touch I thought.

title_masked: A S0-S0 Time at the Dana
text_masked:
I recently stayed four nights at the Dana for a birding festival in San Diego. The facility is in a series of two- and three-story buildings. I believe that the two-story buildings are the "older" buildings, while the three-story building (which has marvelous views of Mission Bay) is a newer building. I stayed in one of the older buildings.
Good Points:
1. They have a shuttle to/from the airport. The shuttle is $9 pp/each way. When I arrived, I called the hotel and within 10 minutes, the shuttle was there. The shuttle driver, along with all Dana staff, was incredibly friendly and gave me lots of tips on eating, shopping etc. What a great start to my vacation.
2. The room was clean and housekeeping did a great job of keeping it clean.
3. Front desk staff were very friendly.
4. The hotel did a good job of accommodating us birders as they had shuttle buses available at designated times to take us to our meeting facility.
Bad Points
1. The rooms are basically standard-fare motel rooms with a tiny wash stand/vanity outside the shower/toilet area.
2. You could not access the ac/heating unit because the writing desk totally hid it. The first night I slept in a relatively warm room as I did not know where/how to use the heat.
3. I had to call the front desk three times to get someone to show me where the heat was and how to use it. The room did not have a remote that you could use to adjust the heat. Even with that, you had to get down on your hands and knees to see what the temperature setting was. UGH!
4. The fire alarm started beeping and that, too, required three phones calls to fix. (Fortunately, the noise started after I woke up one morning.)
5. I asked the front desk for a "quiet room". The front desk person said she could accommodate me, but me in close proximity to the pool.
While the staff were incredibly friendly, I do not know if I would stay there again if I were to revisit San Diego.

lovely, perfectly located, friendly--what more do you need. Union Station is less than a block away; Starbucks is a block away, and the restaurant here is wonderful if you want an upscale meal. Wine is served at 5 in the lobby--if you are around--but why would you be when every Smithsonian Museum is within walking distance and each one better than the next.

A small city center hotel near to the Empire State Building, half way between downtown and uptown and with the underground station just nearby.
A very good breakfast included in the room price is waiting for you.
..................................................................................................................................................

Clean rooms, but be aware some rooms are extremely noisy overnight. We changed rooms after the first night because of a loud, bus sized airconditioning unit attached to the neighbouring building directly outside our window. Sounded like we were on a plane. It did not stop overnight although we were told it would. The second room was much quieter. Good location.

The Edison Hotel NYC was 1/2 block from Broadway/Time Sqare...between 47th and 46th st...
and 1/2 block from 8th ave. From check in to check out...everything and everybody went perfect.
Price, location, room size, all were great..only one problem only ice machine was on second floor.
we stopped there on way up to our floor...11th...great beds, flat screen tv, old fasioned tub shower but fun and very clean...all hotel employees were extremely helpful...

We stayed here for a week. From the moment we checked in until the moment we checked out the service was impeccable. Every person we interacted with from the front desk staff to the bellhops to the servers in the lounge to housekeeping was fantastic. The turndown service was a great added touch as was the two bottles of water that were provided free. The pool was clean and so refreshing after a long day of sightseeing. Our room was quite small but we weren't in it much anyway so it wasn't a big deal for us. 
The location of this hotel is great. You are literally less than a 10 minute walk (we're slow walkers) from the metro and there are tons of restaurants and cafes in the area. If you're looking for a nice fine dining Italian meal I recommend Posto's. Logan's Tavern is great too. 
I would definitely stay here again and highly recommend it.

title_masked: Above Average in some areas, Average in others
text_masked: The hotel is situated right in the middle of the beatiful botanical garden commons area of the city. It was very centrally located and there was tons to do the area. My review of the hotel is very up and down...Firstly and most importantly, the hotel staff were bar none, incredibly attentive and highly service oriented. They would always stop and ask how your stay was going and if there was anything they could do the make the experience better. That said, I had an "interior view" (which means you face a wall w/ no view) room, which honestly left a little to be desired. It was very large, but you could see from the lousy paint job, the old wall unit and chair, it hadn't been updated in a long time...but strangely enough when I walked in the bathroom, it was done in marble and had very nice finishings. The mattress was comfortable, but really should have been better. The room service was very good, but mini bar was hidden in the same small wall unit stuffed in the smallest hidden refrigerator you've ever seen. The rug was dated, but clean...the desk was small and WIFI not included, but the business center large and accomidating. I could go on, but as you can see from my revew, my stay was a little bit of a mixed bag, a lot of was done right, but there is some tangible downside in staying at an "old hotel". In short, I'm positive about the overall experience, but still felt for the price or overall expectation of a "luxury hotel" that someone would be able to put it all together with an updated large room w/ furniture that actually fit (insted of a wall unit and small TV that looked out of place), a new carpet and some new paint.. A few improvements would go a long way, as everything else was spot on. Maybe that's why the Ritz left and bought a new hotel as it was too expensive to re-do everything, but if someone invested a little more in the suggestions mentioned above, the hotel could be the best in Boston (and still very well might be already, just need to be reaslistic about the place showing it's age).

I drove to the hotel and the DC like most cities has a no left turn policy which was driving my GPS crazy. Parking is $42/day which is a bit pricey and it took about 30 minutes for the valet to retrieve my car. I am always irritated that expensive hotels charge extra for internet which is $14 per day. The TV is hi def which means as a channel surfer it is cramping my style because it takes several seconds for the screen to appear when you flip to another station. I thought my room was too large. You get a good work out walking from the bed to the bathroom. ; ) There also was a kitchen/bar area and they brought me a refrigerator for free which was stocked with bottled water. I think they were left behind by the last hotel guest. Service is really good. The breakfast buffet was a bit lackluster on the ground floor and the continental breakfast was spartan on the executive floor. I would stay here again if someone else was paying the bills.
I did not sleep well here, but I think it was me and not necessarily the room. I did hear from one of my colleagues that you could not close the curtains in the room, but I did not try myself.

I was really impressed with this hotel. It is located in the heart of downtown Philadelphia and numerous attractions are within walking distance or a short ride. I used the train to get to/from the airport, which was a money saving (yet unglamorous) way to travel - the station is just 1 block away.
My room was on the 19th floor and was very quiet. The only thing I heard was an occasional door closing. Bed was comfortable, room was clean, the A/C worked great on a hot. humid week, great TV, internet access, and the shower had plenty of hot water. I just wish there was a fan in the bathroom.
We attended a conference on site and found the wait staff very attentive and helpful. When checking out it was a bit crowded and I notice two more people jumped it to help at the check-in desk. That was a nice show of service.
The lobby is pretty noisy but I didn't spend much time there. Also, the pool is rather small, but it's not the main focus of the hotel. Overall any complaints were minor so I'll rate this hotel as 5 stars.

Conveniently located but that's about it.
Free breakfast was good actually.
Room tiny! I really took my cat and could not swing it!!!
Funny old posters from The Cass Hotel give weekly rates of $10!

title_masked: 3rd Stay Here - RUDE bartender. Nice hotel.
text_masked:
Arrived on a Saturday afternoon. There was a 5-10 min wait to get the car valet parked. Check in line was very long, but the 2 reps behind the desk did a very good job of working through the crowd and kept the long line moving.
Got a room on the 17th floor. Headed to the club level to get a couple soft drinks before the wedding we were going to. The bartender was incredibly rude. This hotel would have received 5 stars had it not been for the rude bartender. He acted as though we were inconveniencing him by ordering a couple soft drinks. I would normally tip the bartender for serving 2 soft drinks, but this guy was too rude. Maybe he had a bad day... but no need to take it out on the hotel guests.
Returned to the hotel late that night and asked for a late check out, which was granted. 
The in room alarm clock went off at 6:45AM. We had not gone to bed until 3am, so this was a very unpleasant surprise.
Clean room. Great location. Comfy bed. Wish the bartender wasn't incredibly rude and the alarm clock didn't go off at 6:45am. Trying not to hold these things against them, I would probably return to the Magnolia.

We visit Seattle a lot, and this was our first time at the MarQueen. We will be back! Love the atmosphere, size of rooms, charm, and location. Parking can be an issue if you don't use the pricey valet service. Continental breakfast was entirely satisfactory, and you cannot beat the proximity to Seattle Center.

We stayed here twice during May at the beginning and end of our holiday. The staff and owners could not have been more helpful and friendly. The rooms were compact but very clean, plenty of parking. Other reviewers commented on the noise but we found it very quiet and it was graduation week on our first stay no problems, we will be returning.

title_masked: Comfortable and with a GREAT gym
text_masked: This is a traditional hotel that has recently been renovated. Since we normally like contemporary hotels, this was different than our normal hotel, but we got a good rate on Priceline. If you like grand old hotels, you'll like this one. The room was had was very comfortable and fine. Location is perfect for centre city right on Walnut and Broad. I guess the best part for me was the gym which was a separate facility connected by a walkway. This was probably the best hotel gym I have ever been to (compares well to the Houstonian, which also has a great gym). If you like to work out, this is the place for you....pool, basketball, squash, boxing, gym, yoga, classes, you name it.

cost effective,convenient ,very friendly staff and polite staff ,clean room ,room service every day
in particular walking distance to Philadelphia Conference Center 24/7 snack bar good

title_masked: Good Location and Near to Union Station
text_masked: Short distance to Union Station, you get a good view of the Capitol Building when you cross the street to go to Union Station look to your right, if you happen to get up early in the morning around 7 AM then you can take a picture when there are not a lot of car, it is different when you take a picture at the Capital building. Hotel was clean, amenities are normal same as other hotels. We ask met one of the house keeping in the hall way and asked for a shower cap, he told me to call house keeping! Lobby is noise with meetings and convention, but don't let this deter you from staying here. The hotel is across from the Art and Soul restaurant, highly recommended to splurge the extra money to try it. NO FREE INTERNET...you would think now a day that it would be included in the room.

The hotel worked great for us as it had 2 bedrooms and two baths, plus living room and small kitchen. We took our grandsons and wanted to share the accomodations, but let them have privacy. It included breakfast, but that was a waste of time. Everything else worked great.

title_masked: Nice location, but very large property
text_masked:
Good choice for seeing historic Boston. Twenty minute walk to Fenway. Lots of restaurants on Boyleston one block away. Attached to a large mall. Beds very comfortable and nice fitness center with lots of cardio, machines, and free weights. 
Reasons it is not rated a five:
Parking. $35 self park or $46 valet. Two tricks. There are about twenty meters two blocks south on Huntington that are $1.25 an hour two hour limit 8 a.m-8 p.m. (street cleaning Thursday 12:01 a.m until 7 a.m.) We parked there Thursday night for $2.50. There is also street parking in the residential neighborhoods but it is residential permit parking only at night. However, the ticket is $40, six dollars less than valet.....
Internet. $12.95 a day. Really! In this day and age. I bring my own mi-fi but be aware, free Internet is only for Gold members and above; silver members pay full freight.
Elevators. Lots of them, but we got the same two every time and they were usually crowded. The higher your floor the more stops you will make.
One last tip. Thornton's for breakfast two blocks south. Good food and one third the price of the hotel.
Cheers.
Marius

My husband and I had a Facebook offer and stayed one night while visiting family in Austin. We thought the property was gorgeous. The hotel is older, but very elegant with a Texas flair. Our room was large (king) and had a great view of the pool and golf course. We arrived early to hang out at the pool. We checked in and since our room was not ready, they gave us guest passes with our room information to use on the property. They called me when our room was ready and had our luggage in our room for us. The pool was nice and clean and there was plenty of shade around the pool with beautiful trees and umbrellas. The food and drink at the pool was kind of expensive. The bed was comfortable, bathrobes provided, too. Our FB offer included 2 buffet breakfasts and the buffet was wonderful. Many choices and great quality. Overall we enjoyed our stay and thought it was a great value with the FB offer. We would definitely stay here again.

I have been in the travel industry for many years. This is the first time I have rated a hotel online. This hotel is luxury,clean,reasonably priced and in the Upper West Side.My family and friends all stayed here in April for spring break. Very safe neighborhood. Subway station and Central Park were a couple of blocks away (this is very close for NY).
We have been to New York many times and always stayed in Time Square. I loved the Upper West side neighborhood so much more.
 Going to Time Square was very easy. 2 blocks to the subway station (5 minute walk)and 2 stops on the red line and you were in Time Square.
The hotel staff could not have been any more pleasant and helpful. We spoke with a couple of other guest's that had been repeat customers for years.And they love staying OTA.
We stayed in the Penthouse Suite and it was amazing, especially the balcony. The chain hotels in Time square charged around the same price for a regular hotel room w/o a balcony.
One of my friends stayed in a standard room, I would not do this.
The only advise I would recommend would be not to stay in a standard room at the OTA hotel. They are very small and cramped.I would upgrade to a Deluxe, Panoramic Deluxe or Suite for a small fee. I had the most expensive room she had the cheapest, I paid less than $100.00 a night difference.
If you don't get a balcony room, they have a nice balcony for the guests on the 14th and 16th floors that have awsome views, and you can take great pictures.
I will 100% stay here again and recommend this hotel to everyone I know.
Thank You,
Lisa M. Lexington, KY

The Westin has their signature heavenly bed. The name speaks the truth. The beds deserve their own review -- 2 thumbs up! 
The other great thing about this particular hotel was the location. It is situated in the heart of Washington DC amid tons of restaurants, bars, and lounges. Plus it is just a few blocks from the metro, which means you have full access to the monuments and historic DC. You can go anywhere of interest in a few steps. 
The hotel was well kept, the staff was nice, and it had all the amenities. I would revisit this property.

We stayed for one night at this hotel in the Hugman Suite. The views from the windows are fantastic --- great for people watching from the comfort of your bed. 
The room was quite spacious with extra high ceilings.
Note that this room can be quite loud from the outside noise of traffic and pedestrians -- did not bother me, but if you are a light sleeper, this may not be the best room for you as it has several windows that might add to the noise. They do have a white noise machine which I used and liked.
Breakfast was put out and had a good selection of fresh fruit, pastries, bagels, bread, cereal. I thought it was a nice touch that they had "to-go" coffee cups and lids next to the coffee should you want to take some coffee with you.
I thought the location of the hotel was great. Walking distance from the Riverwalk - basically steps away from it. Also just around the corner from the Alamo. Many shops nearby too.
The staff was warm and friendly, and check in was in your room which is different, but not bad since the innkeeper will show you were things are in your room.
Just a couple of notes: the lighting in the bathroom/shower area is dim -- would have been great if the lighting was on a dimmer instead. Also, the AC unit located on the wall above the bed was blowing out a small amount of black dust -- not too much but enough that you could notice it on the white bedding. The innkeeper tried to help clean the unit and also offered to move us to a different room -- we decided to just shut off the AC unit and stay in the room as the views were great, plus the AC was not really needed since the weather was cool out. The other thing that would have been great is valet parking. Hotel does not have parking -- had to drop bags off, then move the car to a parking garage --- not bad when I was there but would be pretty inconvienient if it was raining.
Overall, even with those minor items (the parking mostly), this place really is great and I would stay here again when I'm visiting San Antonio.

I stayed here by myself for business and I would certainly stay again. The staff was fantastic, helping with public transportation directions, bags, food, etc. There is a complimentary breakfast every morning which is pretty good and other more expensive hotels I've stayed in while visiting Chicago do not have provide breakfast. The location is great if you would like to shop or visit downtown Chicago. The bed was great, there was a TV and a desk, as well as a large tub and shower in the bathroom. If only I had had time for a bubble bath! 
My only complaint was that the walls are so thin I could hear everything that went on in the hallway! I had neighbors who would wake up early to sightsee and it was hard to get back to sleep. I also had neighbors who woke me up by yelling to each other up and down the hall.

title_masked: Had to work at this hotel-
text_masked:
Everything was an effort I booked through Hotwire and this was the hotel we received - we requested 2 rooms- our party were 3 adults and 2 teenagers. We arrived at 4 pm to find we were assigned 2 rooms with 1 king sized bed each. What?!? Can you believe my husband had to sleep in a bed with his 74 year old father and I (mom) had to sleep with my 6' 2" and my 5'7" daughter in the same bed! Someone call DYFS! The other option that was suggested at check in is that there was one double room available on a different floor OR after the first night we could pay $25 extra for a roll out bed.
The next morning we contacted the Mgr and Kelly who was a gem showed us 2 Queen rooms that we could move to. My husband and his Dad moved but it was too much of an effort to move myself and the kids so we stayed in the king room and my son moved to the couch. Unfortunately it was not the original intent that my husband and I expected to be separated but this was getting exhausting.
Btw the rooms vary greatly - the original 2 kings were hugely different in size which is why the reviews vary. 
Also I read there was a $1.00 add on if you wanted the high carb breakfast buffet- but I was told at check in it was $14.95 - ridiculous since theres a Pinkberry breakfast yogurt shop half a block a way with Greek yogurt fruit and coffee as well as Starbucks
 Okay if you want free Internet it's easy to sign up at the Kimpton rewards program but I didnt receive a notice of a $10 honor bar credit that another reviewer mentioned.
The free wine and appetizers do not compare to the Hilton Homewoods resort - Kimpton is more of a tasting- but true to the other reviews Rick is a great bartender.
I was also surprised that there was no coffee machine in the room- I asked about it after checkin and I was told the theme was serenity and theres a hot water kettle and herbal tea in the room- WELL AT THIS POINT IM NOT SERENE AND GETTING EXTREMELY STRESSED OUT AND I WOULD LIKE A CUP OF COFFEE IN MY ROOM LIKE EVERY OTHER HOTEL IN THE US WITHOUT HAVING TO GO DOWN TO THE LOBBY IN MY PJS AND NO MAKEUP AND HORRIFYING THE REST OF THE GUESTS!
 Very shortly I was sent up a Kuerig machine - whew
I had to ask for towel service for the third person in my room- in all I felt like I had to ask for A LOT. There was not a lot attention to the basics here but a lot of attention to the fluff- and the yoga hype? I guess you can somehow request a DVD but there isn't room in the room to work out. 
Btw - check my other review on trip advisor - this is the first time I ever made a negative review on any site- Maybe it was Hotwire ( won't use them again for a hotel) and Kimpton? IDK -maybe if I had a dog..
Btw - we used on the street parking - paid the meter and maybe we were lucky? No ticket - no 42.00 fee- 3 nights!

title_masked: Awesome place to stay if your going to Fenway
text_masked: We had a great stay. The staff was very accommodating, the restaurants were wonderful. The room very comfortable. Couldn't have asked for anything more,for our first visit to Boston.

The Hyatt is located right next to the Chicago River, so there are lots of great things to see nearby. The room was quite nice and we slept well, and the bathroom was beautiful. The restaurant is only so-so and a bit overpriced. 
I was attending a convention at the hotel, and it was a kind of odd and inconvenient space -- lots of up and down escalators and running from one tower to the other to get to events. However the Hyatt did a great job of managing having thousands of guests running around -- there were staff everywhere, the public bathrooms were cleaned several times a day and never ran out of towels, etc., they managed the guest flow on elevators to keep things running efficiently, and there was tech support quickly available in the larger rooms when help was needed with lighting and equipment. I was very impressed with how well the Hyatt supported the needs of our event, even though the layout was far from ideal.

This hotel was ideally situated with 5th Avenue round the corner, the Empire State Building the road in front, Macy's and Madison Square Garden a few minutes walk away and Times Square about 10 mins walk. Returned last Friday morning after an overnight flight and would definitely return to this hotel. I booked through British Airways and I wasn't given the option of a room upgrade, in saying that the room we had, although small and a little update wouldn't go amiss, was quiet and comfortable. The bed I would have brought back, I thought it was that comfortable. We didn't have a view but it it mean't a good nights sleep that was fine by me. The room had USB sockets as well as regular ones and a decent sized LCD TV. The bathroom supplied, soap, shampoo, shower gel and hair conditioner as well as a hairdryer. The room had a fridge (empty) and a free safe. Breakfast was included which was continental and consisted of various bagels, croissant, danish and bread to toast. Apple or orange juice, tea and coffee, yogurts, butter and spreads as well as bananas, apples, etc. We found this enough but for others they may want to go elsewhere. Tea and coffee is also available 24hr a day free of charge in the breakfast room. There is also a business center on the 1st floor which you can use to check your emails or print out reservation tickets as I did for the 911 memorial - all free of charge! Go up to the penthouse floor and the outside terrace for great views of Empire State Building. Overall I was impressed with the hotel and the staff there.

The Westin Oaks is a recently renovated and highly convenient hotel. It is attached to the Galleria shopping center, which gives you a number of great dining and shopping choices. We stayed at the hotel five nights and found the room, particularly the bathroom, not terribly clean. Moreover, the front desk was not as efficient as one would have hoped. We would stay here again for the convenience, but not for the service.

I stayed at this hotel with my Dad and son as we were attending an Airliners International event at the hotel...
Upon check-in was given an Executive Floor (2705 top floor), the only thing is this: this is the only floor that you have to climb up some steps to get to your room...so if you have a cart with bags be prepared to go up some steps after stepping off the elevaltor...all the other floors you can go straight from the eleveator to your room with no problem...
Room was comfortable and had a great view of the skyline etc...
Restaurant was (Rooks) was busy each morning that we had breakfast, however the omelette person was more then accomodating and friendly each morning...as well as the restaurant staff...
The revolving door in the front entrance was not operating so there were staff opening the door for you when you arrive/departed...
The Pool was very comfortable and the water was very warm and my son really had a good time...the Fitness Center overlooks the pool so it was nice....
The only thing is the hotel is 9 miles from the airport which is not a big deal, however they do have a lot of people that go to/from the airport...
Downtown is a 20 minute drive (comfortable) 
Free Parking is a (+) for self-parking and they do have valet (but is a $9.00 per day) charge..
Would stay here again...

The hotel was clean and comfortable, with a nice convenient and complimentary continental breakfast each morning. The staff was friendly and the location is close enough to the attractions in the area, without have to pay the high price to be right beside them. 
As mentioned in some of the other reviews, the hotel could use a little upgrading as far as making the rooms more modern, but they were comfortable and well maintained, so it did not matter to us. The complimentary wifi was also pretty fast for a hotel, which was wonderful.
The hotel also has a pool and fitness room, but we did not take advantage of these ammenities during our stay. They looked nice though!
I would choose to stay at this hotel again the next time I am in the area.

I attended a four day conference in Chicago that was held at the McCormick Place Convention Center and we stayed in the Hyatt, which is attached to the convention ceter. Of course, this is very convenient. Though, it should be noted, that even the hotel is attached, it was a lengthy walk (all indoors) to get to the Expo Hall where we were displaying. So, bring your walking shoes. I checked in and was given a room on the 4th floor, which unfortunately faced a large (and close) building under construction. I immediately called the front desk to have my room switched, as I wanted to be able to have my shades drawn at some point and would not have been comfortable with contruction workers waving in to say "hello". My room was immediately switched and they sent someone up with new keys for my room on the 5th floor, with a lovely view. In hindsight, I should've asked at check in for a room on a higher floor, with a good view, but my mistake. The room was newer looking, quite clean and very comfortable. The beds and pillows were exceptional. Each of my encounters with the hotel staff were above average in service, I was very pleased with the front desk, concierge, maid service, bar service and coffee counter staff. The hotel is not very close to the downtown area, so I would not plan on exploring the city from here by foot, though we were able to walk to several restaurants found within a mile or so. But, there is always a healthy line of cabs available out front to take you where you'd like to go. Overall, an excellent lodging experience and I will likely return to the Hyatt for my next conference stay in a few months.

title_masked: Don't pay full price for this hotel. Actually, look elsewhere!
text_masked:
Please, do yourself a favor, and stay at another hotel....
 First off, let me say I am so glad that my family did not pay full price for this hotel. On the other hand, maybe the level of service we received was a result of us not paying full price. 
 Our check in went well and we did not have any problems there. Front desk staff was very polite and helpful. However, the trip only continued to go downhill from there. We drove to our room, we were on the first floor room (tucked into the back of the staircase) with no view of anything. *Again, maybe a result of us not paying full price for the room.*
 There was a dead spider stuck to our doorknob, which should have been a dead giveaway right there, but we continued into the room. We decided to "inspect" the room before unloading our luggage. (Good Thing!) I immediately noticed that the flat screen was missing from our room. Where did it go? No idea. Well, the flat screen stand was there, but no flat screen. Instead, in its place, was a cheap standard, fuzzy screened, very old television. I decided that we could live with this because we did get the room for so cheap. But, then when my 2 year old decided it was time to take a nap on her buck-bed (yes, some of the rooms have buck-beds, which are kind of cool) she began to grab at something between the bed and the wall. I immediately checked to see what it was (USED TISSUES) lined the wall. SO GROSS! I grabbed my daughters hand, called the front desk and asked for housekeeping to come a re-clean the room.
 Well, we waited and waited and waited, but no one ever came. Finally, after over an hour, my husband went down to the front desk and he had to ask to switch rooms. Our new room was much nicer, so we thought. After we unloaded all our bags and finally put down our children for nap time, we discovered that the air-conditioner was broken. Seriously?
 My husband and I were so tired we just put on the fan and decided to just try and make the best of it. We left early the next morning and did not return back to the hotel until 3:30 pm. We were sure our room would have been cleaned by then. WRONG! No housekeeping? I decided to change my children and at around 4 pm. there was a knock at the door. Yes, it was housekeeping they wanted to clean our room. This late? Really? My husband asked if she could come back in 15 minutes. We would leave and get some dinner while she cleaned. So, we left and returned around 7 pm. 
 Guess what? NO HOUSEKEEPING AGAIN! Finally my husband called the front desk to find out what the problem was. They apologized for the inconvenience and told us to call them when we were leaving and they would have housekeeping come and clean the room. LEAVE AGAIN??????? I thought we were staying at a hotel, so we could rest and actually stay at the hotel? 
 I would not and do not recommend this hotel for anyone. Unless, you like paying for a hotel that you cannot use or enjoy!!!!!!

title_masked: Good For Some But Not For Us
text_masked:
The hotel is right across from beach which is good. There is no charge for the parking, good. We have stayed at many hotels around the world. In today's hospitality industry it's very competitive. We find it hard to believe no hot water to take a shower(or no pressure) in the morning or others in the hotel are using it up at that time.
All the reviews are spot on which we read before. We really want to point something out. We felt like we were on the runway at SD International airport. The planes use Ocean Beach on approach to land. This starts at 6 a.m. If this is not a concern, then by all means stay here. We will not be back. Not sure what else we can say, maybe the planes change the path they take to land at different times but not while we were there.

This hotel is about 4 miles from SEA and they do have shuttle service every half hour to the hotel. The shuttle leaves a bit to be desired as I was shuttled back and forth on a normal passenger van opposed to a mini-bus, which created issues with the amount of people it carried. Any way, upon arrival to the hotel it appears to not be a newer hotel and when you're inside it is confirmed by the somewhat dreary, or darker appearance. 
Upon check-in the front desk staff was excellent and the process was speedy. In fact, while my room was not ready upon my arrival, they sought me out in the restaurant personally to hand me my key when the room was ready to be occupied. The room itself was a corner suite and I found it to be acceptable but nothing extraordinary and certainly very dark. The TVs were newer flat screens but they did not offer HD service and the cable options were limited.
The room service I ordered was good food, they just didn't get the order right as I received incorrect beverage and condiments. However, in the restaurant itself, all went well and the food was actually surprisingly good.
The staff in the restaurant and bar area, specifically Erika and Susan were excellent. Very friendly, well attentive to the needs of the patrons and were extremely courteous. It actually was refreshing to see them interact with the guests and even laugh with them.
Greg was an excellent bellman who assisted upon arrival and the waiter Gabriel was also superb, relative to his friendliness and overall service.
The stay was ok, but it was made better by the staff. The hotel just seems older and outdated to me but I believe it to be one of the better options if you need to stay near Sea-Tac. My rate was $170 per night and both nights I was there, they were full.
Again, this hotel is made by its staff.

My wife and I stayed at this hotel for 6 nights. It was my 40th birthday and my wife's first time in New York and the USA.
From when we first stepped into the hotel on that Sunday afternoon, we knew we had chosen the right hotel; the doorman was ever so obliging and so was the reception man. Sorry but forgot their names.
Hotel is in a great location and if you want to avoid the hussle and bussle of Times Square, you can turn right when you leave the hotel and slip towards 5th and 6th Avenue if you prefer a quieter walk downtown and around!
The room we had was superb with a cool Bose stereo and even a tv in the bathroom. Lovely use of space and great air-con, which I hear is hard to come by in some hotel reviews we read.
Everything we experienced at the hotel made our stay so very much enjoyable and we will certainly be going back, probably sooner than we think!

title_masked: Luxury next to the fire station
text_masked:
FIrst, let me start by saying I'm not a Hyatt fan, but I've found Park Hyatt's to be a distinct step above in amenities and luxuries over your typical Hyatt hotels. This property did not disappoint. It has a lot going for it. A great location, terrific rooms with luxury baths, impeccable service (by the doormen and front desk), friendly staff, very clean and beautiful furnishings. Even complimentary internet!
I didn't give the hotel 5 stars for a few issues...one that really is just a function of its great location across from Watertower Place. There is a fire station with an ambulance a block away. It must be the busiest station in Chicago because they had a call literally ever 30 to 90 minutes both nights I was there. Although I couldn't hear a sound from any other room, I was woken up continuosly by the sirens wailing by the hotel when I was trying to sleep. Others in the hotel complained of the same problem.
I was at the hotel for a business meeting and we had food catered by the hotel for both breakfast and lunch. It was good, but I wouldn't say it was great, given the price. I would venture out of the hotel for dinner.
My only other issue was poor service in the hotel bar.....which was annoying given there weren't many guests in the lounge. Our server was very nice, just moved the pace of a snail.
Overall, you'll really like it hear provided you're a sound sleeper or there are few fire calls!

I stayed for 6 days for a meeting. I used the concierge service (especially Bette), Aura restaurant (on site), and the gym/spa. Everyone treated me with kindness, and was helpful. I was also very pleased that I did not have to worry about tipping, as I was very busy every day during my stay. The bed and pillows were comfortable and conducive, and I had a lovely, albeit sideways, view of the harbor. The only black spot was a drunken wedding party on Saturday night out in the hall (and these folks weren't the young ones). I waited a bit, and when they didn't stop, I called the front desk. The problem was promptly addressed. Went back to sleep. I mention this, as it seems to me that judging by some older reviews, the hotel management took the complaints to heart, and have apparently remedied the situation. 
The reason why I am not giving 5 stars for sleep quality is the above. Location: easy to the airport, great shuttle to downtown (but doesn't run on weekends), although being close to the water and the airport, was farther from other attractions. It's an older hotel, so the rooms are a little small, although that does not bother me personally--the bathroom was more than large enough, and there was room enough for two nice stuffed chairs near the windows.

My husband and I greatly enjoyed this Hilton. We stayed in a corner junior suite on the Hilton HHonors floor and I would highly recommend this room -- I peaked into the regular rooms when housekeeping was going through and they were very small -- room enough for just the bed. The suite has a seating area with plenty of room, and of course with the corner you get two windows, plus a closet and large bathroom. 
The free Starbucks is a nice perk for Hhonors members -- you get a piece of fruit, pastry and drink. My husband and I are not coffee drinkers, however, and don't like to eat a lot of pastries, so this wasn't terribly useful to us. If you go by 9 am the line isn't too bad.
The pool area was quite nice. I particularly enjoyed the super comfy lounge chairs which are great for hanging out and reading a book and taking a break from reading. All of the staff were very kind and polite, especially housekeeping.
The hotel is near lots of shopping, but it is a trek to get to Fisherman's Wharf area. Cabs add up, for sure, so my husband walked to Fisherman's and back which was about a 5 mile walk, which isn't a huge deal aside from the enormous mountain in the middle of the city -- haha. Bring your walking shoes!!
All in all, this Hilton was great. My biggest tip is to make sure you are a Hilton HHonors member so you can check in at the much shorter line, and get a junior suite.

title_masked: Four Star Spa Hotel Worth a Visit!
text_masked:
I enjoyed a staycation at this beautiful resort. The rooms are gorgeous, the staff is hospitable and accommodating but the daily parking/resort fee stinks! Which is the only reason I'm not giving the resort 5 stars.
If you want to enjoy a beautiful resort near Six Flags and La Cantera, Eilan is worth a visit!

We have been to NYC a number of times but our most recent stay at Blue Moon Hotel has given us a new home away from home. It is a small boutique hotel with character. Located in an old tenement building and converted to a hotel, it is like visiting someone's home. The rooms don't have numbers, rather they have names. We stayed in the Jimmy Durante room. Large by New York standards, we had a large bathroom, sitting area and comfortable bed. Also a fridge was provided. The location is convenient to Katz's deli and Donut Plant on the East side with the subway very close. They serve fresh New York bagels every morning and offer. A glass of wine in the lobby. The decorating is kind of old but the black out curtains won me over, even if the room is orange! There is no doubt we will be staying here again!!

title_masked: Good value and Close to Airport
text_masked: It is a good value and has a gated garage which is nice in the city. They have food/bar on site and it was open until 11:30. The room was clean, but you tell it has been a while since they've been updated.

I recently stayed at the Doubletree for my birthday weekend with some friends who were in from Chicago. We wanted to stay downtown somewhere with easy access to Greektown Casino. We booked last minute and received an amazing rate. 
Upon check-in we were greeted by the friendliest staff. Getting set up with valet parking and our room was a breeze. What was even better was the amazing warm chocolate chip cookies we were given before we were sent up to our room. Can you say delicious? Our room was huge! There were three of us, and with two beds and a pull out couch, it was very nice to each have our own space to sleep. 
The People Mover station was only a block away, so it was easy to hop on and go the few stations to Greektown. You could technically walk there, but we felt safer taking the ride at night. If you don't want to take the People Mover, take their complimentary shuttle. We were on more of a schedule, so we didn't feel like waiting. But we did see the bus with the giant cookie on it cruising around town. 
The following morning, we enjoyed the breakfast buffet. The only hang up was that they were out of eggs. I enjoyed a Belgian waffle, fruit and sausage, so this didn't really bother me at all. There was a really nice selection to choose from, and about 15 minutes into breakfast, the eggs were available again. 
I've stayed at a lot of hotels downtown, and I have to say this place had the best service of all of them! I would definitely stay here again.

title_masked: Great location and service, Small rooms need update
text_masked: The rooms are dated, and need to be updated, the TVs are old, and the rooms are small. The common areas of the hotel are very nice, the service was very good, the location is great for Austin, the only negative would be the small dated room. If they made some upgrades in the rooms, I fell this would be a top notch hotel. I would recommend this hotel and would stay there again, but would like it much more if they did upgrades.

title_masked: Nice Place Friendly Staff Concerned About Plumbing
text_masked:
I recently stayed 3 nights at this hotel and it was a good deal The staff was very friendly and the room was clean. The only thing I can say negative is about the water coming out of the sink an shower.
I turned the hot water on and noticed the water was dirty brown. It never got clear and turned a towel brown. I was a bit concerned and afraid to wash my face and hands.
Overall even with that negative it is close to everything and a good price.

My mother and I checked our bags when we arrived and when we checked out. It is a small hotel, so service is easy and immediate. The four bellmen we dealt with, to check our bags and to retrieve them, were all helpful and gracious. There are just eight rooms on each floor, so all are convenient to the two elevators, but none are next to them. This hotel is half the price of super-stylish hotel just one lot away on the same street. The savings are worth having just plain ordinary furnishings! Our two-queen room was small, but there was enough space to walk between the beds, desk and desk chair, and the fridge/microwave/tv/drawers/wardrobe unit. The beds have comfort-dial mattresses, so we each set the mattress to our desired firmness. (Finding the dial was a bit tricky - under the sheet and behind a cover.) The smooth sheets and fluffy duvet, and two types of pillows, are conducive to comfortable sleeping. The location is near Penn Station, convenient to the street corners where all the intercity buses drop passengers. It is also near the subway. We were going to art exhibits on the East Side, but it was far less expensive and actually more convenient to stay on the West Side and take the subway and 79th Street crosstown bus, and walk short blocks to the galleries and museums, than to walk long blocks from hotels on Lexington, for instance. Being near our bus drop-off point was a major plus. The drug store, Greek diner, and bagel place/deli nearby were handy. The location is in the flower district, so it's kind of interesting to see all the wholesale plants and gardening and decorative supplies in motion and lining the sidewalks. Nice thing - smoking is permitted only on the top floor, so there is no smoke smell in the ventilation system or on any other floors.

The best thing about this hotel is the customer service hands down. Our server name was [NAME], A+++ service and can't say enough good things about him. Outside of that the rooms were average and needs to be updated. The Wifi connection in the guest rooms are poor at best. The lights in the bathroom are dim and the ironing board didn't work. I'm very dissatisfied with my room and if I stay there again it would only be for the great service provided at check in and in the restaurant. Thanks again Gerald!! You're the Best!!

title_masked: Not the nicest Hyatt, but still pretty good
text_masked: I stayed here with my husband last weekend. We stayed in a suite in 2233 which was very nice, though kind of odd as the was no dedicated dresser. We had to put our folded clothes in the media cabinet. The wall behind the bed was either paper thin or the woman staying in that room was the loudest human alive (possibly both are accurate). Upon arrival we requested that a bottle of wine and a fruit & cheese tray be sent to our room. It took almost 50 minutes for these items to arrive. Finally, the couches in the lounge look so inviting- especially the brown ones- until you get close and see all the stains. Yuck. I think it's time to replace those with something newer. Now then, all that being said, the staff was super friendly and helpful. The hotel itself is situated right by the Metra so it's easy to get around. There's also interesting stuff in the nearby neighborhood, so if you've got some time then you should walk out the front of the hotel and head north just to take in some of the neighborhood feel. So, despite all my complaints, I would stay here again.

title_masked: Great boutique hotel west of Times Square
text_masked: Stayed for 2 nights using Choice Privileges points, selected based on high TripAdvisor rating and location. Front desk staff were helpful and pleasant. When I first checked in I was given Room 603, on the back east corner of the building. My AT&T cellphone got no signal in the room, though, and when I reported this and asked to be switched to a higher room or one facing a different direction, was switched to #405, where the AT&T signal worked fine. The supervisor was pleasant enough about my request, though I know it helped to be firm in requesting the switch. The room was adequate sized for Manhattan, with a reasonably-sized bathroom (stand up shower only). Water pressure was good. Bedding was good quality, though mattresses are somewhat soft. More lighting in the room would have been welcome. A Keurig coffee maker in the room was a welcome touch (I brought my favorite K-cups from home). Air conditioning was quiet and efficient; the windows can be opened. A small safe was adequate for a 13” laptop. There was plenty of drawer space. There was little noise. Elevators can be crowded going down in the morning, especially for guests on low floors. I did not eat in the restaurant; there are plenty of nearby options. The lobby was comfortable, albeit small. I did not find the neighborhood problematic, even late at night.

My wife and I stayed in the Beekman in May. We were given a suite, with a kitchenette. We didn't use the kitchenette because there was a continuous stream of ants crawling through it. We mentioned it to the staff on our way out to walk but when we returned the ant parade was continuing. At checkout we re-informed the staff of the ants and they seemed very concerned, but I am doubtful they did anything - they didn't while I was in the room and I have no reason to believe they did after. The rooms were outdated but clean, no bed bugs (I always check very carefully). The mattress was fairly old and uncomfortable, and when someone got up it would pop up and down...I use a c-pap and had to move the night stand to reach the plug - bad idea. The plug had no cover, there was a hole in the wall, and there was years of dirt and grime there. Not pretty. Overall, I would not stay in the hotel again, when there are clean new hotels for the same price to be had. We left and went to a Doubletree for a few bucks less and had a much more comfortable stay.

The Roosevelt is a modernized older hotel with 1940's character. The hotel is ideally located in downtown Seattle about 3 minutes off the I-5 freeway and about the same to get back on. Nice decor, amply sized junior suite, parking available (included in our special rate), and staff exceptionally courteous and I am sure helpful should assistance be requested.

I was very happy with the sonesta hotel, the booking in and front desk staff were lovely. The room is clean and a very good size almost large, the only thing is that the bathroom is extremely small, however we got a deal that was very reasonable so I feel that you really cannot complain. The shampoo etc was really nice. Plus there are four lifts so you don't have to wait too long. Downstairs is a great pub, restaurant very nice with good food at a very reasonable price. Great stay wish we had more time, good location too.

title_masked: Wonderful new hotel in Manhattan's business area
text_masked: The Conrad is a new facility, open only about 5 months ago. For business in the financial section of downtown it is the best location, otherwise one needs to use transportation to get to mid- and uptown. Beautifully situated facing Battery Park City, it is of the highest standard, magnificent architecturally, extremely comfortable, with attention to the most minute details (they even have Nespresso machines in each room). Service is efficient and friendly. The only part that needs improvement is the Business Center: very restricted computers that need to be more accessible and effective. Generally speaking: I think hotels on such a level should offer free internet access everywhere; yes, they might add a bit to the price, but the customer will definitely feel better and be less negative about the stay in general ($15 per 24 hours is upsetting, no matter how much money you have).

We needed somewhere affordable and convenient for 2 nights stopover before our cruise to Alaska and this fitted the bill. The room was clean comfortable and quiet. We were in a room fairly low down, but on the side street so no noise. Free wifi was good and the breakfast was excellent. We did not try the evening food on offer as we preferred to go out, but a lot of people did use the facility. We did not use any public transport (prefer to walk) except on the day we had to get to the port, when a taxi was ordered and took us there in no time. My advice to anyone going to this hotel for the first time is to walk down hill to eat, as uphill there were a few homeless people on the street, which can be a little offputting on your first venture out. Lots of good shopping nearby.

We arrived late and couldn't get room service so it was suggested I buy frozen food from the lobby which I did. At the same time the air-con died and at 11:30 pm I had the air co man in my room pulling the air co apart. I was told quite abruptly that there was no other room they could give me and with no apology or discussion that was the end of the conversation. Air con was eventually fixed and I took out of the microwave a most horrendous soggy pie. When I looked around there was only 2 wooden sticks that I could use to eat it with. No plate, no fork not even a spoon. I drink tea and no electric jug could be found in the hotel so I was told to use the coffee maker. It wasn't working either so a new one arrived. Thank goodness it was new as I can't imagine the taste the tea would have had it had been heated through a coffee filter. The next evening I needed a cork screw and the reception couldn't find one either so I had to take the bottle down to the bar to get it opened.. I have stayed in Hilton Hotels all over the world and couldn't believe the lack of a supplies in the room. However the bed was comfortable, the room clean and I eventually calmed down and enjoyed my stay. But you need to take your own picnic set if you stay.

Stayed here in August 2012. Hotel room was fine but not so in the restaurant. The locale of the rooftop restaurant/pool area provided a lovely view of the Hollywood skyline. My girlfriend and I wanted to take advantage of it to end our evening. I checked earlier in the day to verify that it closed at 11 pm. We arrived there at 10:40 to have a starlit glass of wine. They rudely said we're closing so no glass of wine. I reminded them that closing was 11 pm but they said they were closing anyway. Of course, several other tables were full of patrons. I stepped away for a moment and my girlfriend said they had changed their mind.
