We sat at the bar and I quickly ordered two Petite Syrahs not bothering to look at the wine list because they were clearly not wanting to serve us anyway. The bartender poured what was left of a bottle, saying "We'll thats the last of it." He filled each glass about 2 oz. definitely not a normal amount. He then returned to his closing up duties. Still getting looks like "What are you people still doing here?" we quickly drank the little bit of wine and asked for the bill. It was definitely my error in not reviewing the wine list first, (I did the next day to verify the amount), we were charged $48.00 for those two sips of wine and with quite impolite and unwelcoming behavior part of the price. Apparently, management and/or staff of the Hotel Wilshire don't think they're in the hospitality business or don't really care.

Great location overlooking the ocean. We saw dolphins passing by from our balcony. We have been staying here for the last 4 years, unfortunately others have identified this great place to stay. The prices have increased and availability is getting slightly tougher to obtain rooms based on the popularity. 
Beach front location is good for those wanting to take in all that San diego has to offer.

Grace Mate has an excellent location at 1 minute from Times Square.
Personnel is friendly. The hotel has vibe and a nice internal swimming pool which is very good after long walking touristy hours.
Some external refurbishing prevented from opening the windows and the curtains. The rooms are quite new. We had 3 beds rooms with the extra bed on top of the queen size bed such a canopy, which did not allow to stand up and was a kind of risky for the head when exiting the bathroom at night.
Recommended for couples and families. Within its peers it is premium priced to account for the location.

title_masked: Your best bet on the Upper East Side
text_masked:
Fantastic location, close to the museums and great shopping on Madison Ave.
We encountered only the nicest service, from our telephone reservationist Patricia, to the front desk mgr. Channing. The bellman couldn't have been nicer. They took good care of our car and nothing was too much to ask.
Rooms are lovely, clean and stylish. I love that they offer 24 hour room service.
Bed and pillows SO comfy! Had a great nights sleep and the 77th Street view had minimal noise as opposed to a Madison Ave. room.
The only reason I gave the hotel 4 stars instead of 5, is they had no docking station to charge our phone! Even the gal at the front desk said it was kind of odd in this day. We managed to survive the weekend without a phone, and they were willing to charge it for us at the front desk.
Also we had some miserable stains on the rug in our room, but I guess that's life in a hotel!
We will definitely return to this fine hotel, they couldn't have been nicer. Thank you!

The hotel wasnt bad just nothing special but what the hell is the point of them having their own parking lot if they still charge to use it.We already over payed for a room with only a tiny shower-no tub-and a old cheap bed that was hard as a rock and down like pillows which i absolultly hate due to their lack of support.Room was clean staff ok but PLENTY of room for improvement.

title_masked: Great experience at Four Seasons Hotel Boston
text_masked: I can't say enough about my stay at the Four Seasons Hotel Boston. Customer service on overdrive. I was in town for the Boston Marathon so the location was ideal from the finish line. Beyond that, the personal touch for those doing the marathon were untouchable. Pre-race goody bag filled with appropriate items (energy gel, gatorade, etc...) and perfect bananas in the lobby race morning...meaning perfectly ripe! So Four Seasons to even nail the banana ripeness. The grand finale and the sure bet I will stay there again - the greeting after the finish. The staff clapping, offering up perfectly chilled cotton cloths and a recovery food and drink buffet fit for a queen. Need I say more?

Booked this hotel because it was the venue for a conference I was attending and speaking at. At every turn, we were impressed with this property and its operation. Late check-in, multiple bags brought to room with us by front desk clerk, unloaded and tip refused -- there is a no-tipping policy. We had a corner suite on the waterfront, and only the absence of a separate shower stall gave any downgrade to the room. Staff was attentive. The concierge, Betty Salemme (one of Boston's best), worked magic, made helpful suggestions for dining "with Bostonians", arranged transportation. Great meeting facilities, too. Rooms have free wireless access, and ability to print to a central color printer. A very "with it" place, comfortable and friendly. A redeveloped area, with many amenities.

title_masked: For the room quality we got, we should have just stayed at the Motel 6.
text_masked:
I should have read the reviews for this place before booking it, but I've stayed at a Quality Inn before and they have been decent for the price so was expecting the same standards.
Firstly, we were told the room would have two double beds, they were more like king single beds. Also it was suppose to be a non-smoking room but someone had been smoking in the bathroom previous to our stay. 
The room also had a very unpleasant smell, we had to leave the door open to air the room out. I also used lysol spray and that helped a bit but overnight when we had to close the door, the smell was there again in the morning.
The chairs in the room were stained, the towels that were provided were shabby. Shower head in bathroom had black mould. 
I would not stay here again, I feel for the price we paid $99 plus tax we should have just gone to the motel 6 down the road. At least there you get what you pay for. 
No issues with the staff, just the room.

title_masked: Teeny room, kitschy decor, poor location
text_masked:
We stayed here because priceline had it rated 4 stars and in the Pike Place Market area; both grossly inaccurate! Our room was slightly larger than the full size bed (aka "queen" according to the front desk) and two people could not stand at the bathroom sink at the same time. There was no desk and a bedside table on one side only. Our room was quite warm when we arrived, despite a thermostat setting at 60.5°; we complained and when we returned the room was at 72°F (22°C).
The lower room numbers are quite close to the freight train railway crossing, and a note in the room explains that some guests find this romantic — especially the bells that ring each time the gates go up or down? — while others will want to use the "complimentary earplugs" they provide. I counted at least 4 crossings during our night there, between 11pm and 8am.
They do accommodate pets and were great with our dogs.

We booked 10 rooms for a girls soccer team - 11 year olds! Group total was 42 individuals. Staff was very friendly and accommodating. Breakfast staff was helpful and opened early to accommodate our schedule. Great value for a large group.

Great location in a nice tree lined neighborhood that is great for walking. We loved the simple, understated and sophisticated design of the lobby and the rooms. It felt pretty trendy but not snobby - the front desk people are very nice and not trying too hard (NOT that aloof, your-not-cool-enough-to-stay-here type)- the price is pretty reasonable given the location and you can always find deals. No, there is not coffee in the room but that was a positive for us- the room coffee is always crap and the chintzy plastic machines and set-up just clutter things up, which goes against the simple clean design. Go to the lobby for a great cup of coffee, the morning jaunt will do you good! 
It is a classic old hotel with plenty of charm - sure the elevators are kind of slow during peak traffic, so just chill a little, slow down and enjoy life.
We look forward to a return visit!

Recently stayed two nights at the Hotel Indigo. I'm glad we picked the right spot! The boutique hotel was a perfect "home base" to enjoy a couple of days in the Windy City. The hotel is tucked into a quiet neighborhood - nice to forego the hustle/bustle of the city hotels. There are numerous bars/eateries within a block or two - great location!
The room was refreshingly different (boutique, beach feel). The beds were very comfortable which is a huge plus! The Service Desk was efficient and friendly, especially Tom who went above and beyond to accommodate a last minute request. Great place to stay -

My husband and I stayed for 2 nights, after a Carnival cruise, out of Manhattan Pier.
Check-in was a breeze, though it was a very busy weekend.
All staff we encountered, from bell-boys, desk clerks, concierge desk, housekeepers...were very cordial & professional.
The property is immaculate, especially considering the huge traffic.
The room was spotless : a very spacious suite. There were plenty of towels, a robe, nice bath toiletries, safe, coffe maker, LARGE flat screen TV, and the MOST plush, comfortable bed & bedding, ever, in a hotel stay...including a DUVET, instead of a blanket.
Food & convenience store items on the 8th floor lobby are rather costly...you're better off walking to the very near-by WALGREEN's, to get over the counter-type items, and soft drinks, or yogurt.
The best thing about this property is LOCATION, LOCATION, LOCATION!!!
You're literally on TIMES SQUARE..just step out of the hotel, and you're right smack in the middle of great N.Y. action....plus right in the middle of the theater district. There's even a half-price TIX booth, right in front of the hotel. You also have the play "EVITA" (starring Ricky Martin) right at the hotel's 3rd floor MARQUIS theater. It is also within walking distance of hundreds of eateries, 5th Avenue, Midtown, Empire State bldg; Rockefeller Center, Bryant Park. Also, double-decker tour buses have stops right in front of the hotel.
As for the elevator system.....once you get the "hang of it", it makes a lot of sense...and it expedites the huge elevator traffic.
All in all, we had a GREAT time! I would highly reommend this property!!

Upon booking my room for one night for myself, my wife and my two kids(age 4yrs and 11months) I was told that a room with two double beds would be reserved. When I checked in the guy at the front desk said all they had left was a king bed with a pull out couch. Pull out couch it was not! It was two foam pads that stack on top of each other to make a couch. When they are pulled together, they resemble anything but a bed. Once we got to the room we realized there were no pillows or linens for this make shift bed but we wanted to go to dinner so we decided to wait till we got back to request them from the front desk. When we walked in the lobby(approx 10:00pm) and requested extra linens/pillows, one of the guys at the desk rudely told me it will be at least 30 minutes before they will be brought to our room. Surprisingly only took about 15 minutes before they showed up at the door. The room itself appeared to be fairly clean...however, we allowed my 11 month old to crawl around on the floor while we got ready for bed and within 10 or so minutes, he legs and feet were absolutely filthy like she had been crawling around in the dirt.
Overall, our stay was failry pleasant. We felt that we should have been compensated in some way for not getting the roomn with two beds we needed/requested. But what can you do? Had we known from the begginning that we were getting a king room, we probably would have brought the pack and play for the baby to sleep in.

title_masked: Beautiful Building but beware the ground floor rooms!
text_masked: We spent a long weekend @ The Mansion on Turtle Creek . First, we were assigned a ground floor room---where there was an obvious mold issue (apparently in the air conditioning vent system?). After we complained (and my wife developed a throbbing headache as she is allergic to mold spores), we were given an upper floor room. It was a totally different atmosphere---fabulous accomodations. Staff was marvelous---they certainly went above and beyond expectations to make us comfortable!

Having read the numerous stellar reviews I looked forward to a great 2 day stay at Hotel Commonwealth. We were accompanied by several friends who also had rooms there. My opinion was very mixed and, in conversation, others readily agreed.
The good: 1. Great location, 2. wonderful bed, 3. attentive and well trained reception staff and concierge, 4. good exterior sound insulation for a difficult location (Kenmore Square just outside and loud bars on the ground floor).
The tired: 1. room interiors are plain gloomy, 2. towels may be Frette but they were downright worn, 3. $8.00 for a small bottle of in-room water and $3.50 for a cup of not good coffee downstairs.
The bad: 1. for over $300 a night one would think you'd get a coffee machine in the room, 2. no newspaper?, 3. no hooks in the bathroom, 4. we did not receive fresh shampoo etc... on our 2nd night, 4. dark, dark, very DARK.... the lighting maybe energy efficient but it is dim in there... try shaving or putting on makeup without blood or a pencil in your eye.... and it makes the room unpleasant.
So good points yes but quite disappointed.

I stayed at this hotel because of Expedia's bargain deal (USD54+tax). I did not know which hotel I would stay until the booking became final. Usually, I try to avoid an old, historic hotel like Camino Real. I was not excited about going to the hotel at all. It turned out that the room was surprisingly clean, spacious and modern. The bed was comfy and the internet was free. 
One thing I need to mention is that parking is not free (USD6). 
As long as the price is right, I will definitely stay here again.

I had to log on to the Internet and didn't know the code. Upon dialing Service, Sheila, the hotel Operator, welcomed me by name and gave me the code in proper Military phonetics. She was kind, quick and stayed with me until I got online. 
Rooms are nice, spaceous and comfortable. Hotel is within 0.5 miles of several good sites and restaurants. Try Rittenhaus Square if you're in the area.

staff always going out of their way to help you, which was lovely. they were happy to arrange our tours, give us pointers and advice, and in general be super to us!! 
our room over looked the bay, house keeping came daily and were great- they did a turn down service too.
take advantage of the amazing breakfasts they do!! never seen so much choice! further more, their afternoon cheese and wine was always great too! :)
provided free wifi, bikes, and the hotel car to take you places within a 2 mile radius.
fairmont here puts the other fairmonts in the chain to shame!!

I got this hotel on a same-day Hotwire booking for a great rate; then I read the reviews on TripAdvisor and was concerned I'd made a mistake. Fortunately, that was not the case. My room was delightful, on a top floor, and there was no noise from other rooms, which was my concern after reading the reviews here. It's a big, busy hotel in an expensive city. I expected to pay for parking. I didn't need to pay for internet, used my smart phone instead. We went out for breakfast to The Diner in Adams-Morgan, and could have chosen lots of other places within walking distance as well. My only complaint was that they could have used more registration staff, as the wait to check in and then to solve a very minor issue was longer than I would have liked. But I stayed for two nights at probably less than half what one night at the Four Seasons would have cost, so I could put up with a wait at registration!

title_masked: You actually get what you pay for
text_masked:
This hotel is expensive (well, they all are in NYC in Jun...) but lives up to its expectations. Great location in an area I would not have thought to be ideal, right near the Brooklyn Bridge and South Street Seaport. It has a boutique feel without being (--)-trendy, if you know what I mean. It is a Hyatt and reminds me more of a Kimpton, or a W. The restaurant was good (for brunch), beer garden and farmer's market with outdoor drink bar, and a free espresso bar in the lobby.
This hotel is really getting the coveted fifth star because the of the staff. The elevator at the parking garage across the street (DO NOT park in the Quik Park on Front St, apparently this is a recurring problem) was broken and we were stuck for six hours with a baby under three months old and tons of luggage since they couldn't get the car from the lower level. Michael at the desk arranged a room for us and reinstated my account and gave us a 1400 check out. When 1400 came and went and push the check out even further to help us out. In the end we checked out around 1600 with no extra charges to the bill. It was nice to see someone thinking on their feet and helping someone out of a jam since the hotel had the space to make it happen. Would definitely stay again.
Clean and spacious and good location...would not be my first choice for family traveling but fine for business...needs some upgrades!

.i was in town for a convention for which this was the official hotel. Overall the rooms where cleanly and roomy. The breakfast buffet was excellent and the staff where helpful and friendly. 
Highly recommended

You can't beat it. Right on the corner of 47th and 7th. We chose this hotel because we needed to be at Good Morning America early in the morning and its only 3 blocks away. We came in on the Staten Island Ferry and took the R train right to the front door. Its the 49th street stop but when you get off the train you can go either way, 47th or 49th exit. We checked in at noon on a Sunday. Our room wasn't ready so we just dropped off our luggage. When we came back at 3 we were assigned room 2711 a king suite w a pull out sofa. Perfect for our family and what a great view. The room had a coffee maker, fridge, mini bar, safe. Theres a bar in the lobby and I think a restaurant in the hotel. We weren't in the hotel much but I would highly recommend it and can't wait to go back. Oh yeah, theres a TKTS booth right out the front door!!

I had stayed here serveral years ago and found that the staff was very cold and the atmosphere univiting. I must say that I was very pleasantly surprised when I returned this month. The staff was very friendly and helpful. The elevator system has been replaced with a new logic system assigns you the most efficient elevator for your destination. Room was very nice and comfortable. View was very nice as well. Overall a very good stay.

Booked with Virgin to travel to San Fran for my Husbands trip of a lifetime for a "special" birthday. Although I'm not sure I would bother to pay the extra to travel with Virgin again I would definately stay at the Holiday Inn Fishermans Wharf again. A great clean hotel in a fab location not far from Fishermans wharf and not far from the cable car turnaround.
The breakfast all you could eat buffet was expensive at $21 each but our youngest ate free and the breakfast was super. Everything you could possible want to set you up for the day, oats, fruit, youghurt, bacon, eggs, omlet and best of all freshly made waffles and pancakes - the kids couldnt get enough. The bar service in the evening was a little hit and miss but we only had a nighcap as we were so shattered after sightseeing all day. Each room had two wonderfully comfy beds and was neither too hot nor too cold. It was a little noisy in our room as we overlooked the Canery, but I think San Fran is non stop, anyhow it didnt ruin our stay. The rooms were sparsly furnished but had everyhting we needed. The concierge in the hotel is a great place to get information as were the staff on the front desk, always happy to help.
Great comfy hotel, kids made really welcome and super breakfast to set you up for a days sight seeing!!!

title_masked: desirable location, but my 3rd time wasnt a charm
text_masked:
This was my 3rd visit to the hotel for business. I used priceline to get a great deal most recently. 
Self-parked which left a maze to get back to hotel. Felt I needed to leave some bread crumbs to find my way back!
Used the convenient self-serve kiosk near the check-in counters to check-in and get key. 
Pros: comfortable bed. last trip gave me a great view of the river/wrigley building.
Cons: felt compelled to write a review this time due to my less-than clean room. I found several stray hairs in the bathroom and on bed linens. The toilet, sadly, was not fully cleaned either. 
Overall: prefer to stay somewhere else during next visit.

I've stayed at a number of JW's over the past year on business, and while this is not your typical JW (it really is not a resort), it is class all the way! This high-end hotel is very well taken care of, contemporary and situated in a prime shopping district next to the mall and other boutique stores. There is a whole foods and Starbucks just a couple of blocks away. Club level has beautiful views of the mountains and an excellent breakfast. The chicken noodle soup in the adjoining restaurant was amazing! The hotel is a little pricey, but you get what you pay for!

Room quoted was not what we were given. Full beds, not queen. I also noted a peculiar smell when we went to bed, but, woke up covered in red bumps! We were not informed of any free breakfast until check out!

My husband found this hotel on the internet and after reading the Tripadvisor reviews, we booked our stay for 3 nights in Midtown NYC. The hotel is central and in a calm street. We arrived with a rental car at 8am and we were pleasantly surprised to find a parking right next door to the hotel. 
The person at the reception was very nice and even if we had booked the hotel the night to come, she offered us to go and take the complementary breakfast in the lobby. In the meantime, I asked her to find the address of a pizzeria in Brooklyn and she printed the pizzeria's info and brought it to me.
The room was supposed to be ready at 3pm but as it was ready before, we were able to go to our room at midday. It was a one bedroom suite with 2 Queen beds + 1 sofa bed. Perfect for a family of 4 with 2 children who didn't want to sleep in the same bed!
We were told that there is no view as it is a small hotel (18 floors) but it was a view for us (see photo below)! 
The hotel receives a lot of Spanish speaking hosts and it is nice and cosy family hotel. Each and every of the employees we met during our stay were nice and helpful. A man at the reception even did a magic trick to our son who laughed in delight. Complimentary umbrellas were offered to use when it started to rain which was much appreciated.
We found restaurants all around and the area is nice and relatively calm which was good as we were able to choose different food depending on our mood.
A hotel we will definitely go back to. A very good place to sleep and spend calm and quality time to rest.

Well, I stayed in this hotel for 3 nights. The poor experience starts before I arrive. I sent emails to it and asked if I may order something online and ship to the hotel before I arrive but never got any reply. Okay, that was fine. I checked in and was placed in the 3rd floor. The 4-star hotel had a wacky and poor elevator. The carpet had some bad smell and was very dirty. Well, that was fine as long as you don't sleep on it. How about the dripping faucet? The dim room, the old CRT TV, and the outdated furniture fitted the old style hotel well. However, I cannot even find a coffee maker or kettle! I had lived in a 2-star hotel in down-town Chicago for 50 including BF, and it was even much better than this 4-star one!

title_masked: Fantastic hotel at a great price
text_masked:
I initially disappointed that my customer discounted hotel was unavailable for a week in which I'd be in town. I immediately searched AAA and found this hotel with a few reviews. I then went to another site and found 200 reviews: All glowing! I added a few requests to my reservation and found that the hotel met them all, including a higher floor (I was on the top floor-3rd, on the quiet side of the building, and away from elevators & vending. 
So, I booked the hotel online, received my AAA discount and checked in after work. Boy, was I surprised. Although the hotel receives a 3 diamond from AAA, they should consider adding a half diamond. This place was so immaculate and I've stayed in quite a few upscale resorts, both in and out of the US. I couldn't find a speck of dust anywhere. 
Although the fitness room was the standard size, the equipment was good, the AC very cold, and I was the only one using it before work for one week so I was more than happy. My first night the AC unit kept me up all night because it was somewhat noisy and I'm a light sleeper. I reported this on the way out to work and the Angie asked if I would like the hotel to move me to another room if the AC couldn't be repaired by the time I returned from work. I decided to stay in the room. More about the later. When I returned after work the front desk representative indicated that Hector fixed it. I slept that night and every night like a charm. The hotel responded very quickly and the staff always has a smile and is always very professional.
Breakfast was free and pretty good. Much better than I expected. A wide assortment of hot and cold dishes to choose from was a pleasant surprise.
While looking at their website I also found that free wireless and wired Internet access was available. I was pleasantly surprised. I always carry a LAN cable when I am staying in a hotel. Wired is so much faster but many hotels, even those rated higher than this one, do not offer wired Internet access to it's guests. And certainly not free. I worked from my room using my wired connection and found it to be about the same as my connection at my home.
Overall, this was an exceptional hotel. If I come back on business I will stay at this hotel.

This would be a 5-circle review were it not for some caveats. Let's get to the great, first, though: the renovations are complete and the lobby, bar and roof bar are all killer cool, and the service is top-notch. You'll feel like a celebrity upon check-in. The W seemed to spare no expense. It's impressive.
And then you get to the rooms, and you will see where the expenses were spared. My lungs and heart deflated a bit when I got to the room. It looks cool and is well-designed: comfortable bed, mirrors, cool sofa-thing near the window, flat screen, super modern. The problem is in the perceived cleanliness: the rugs are old and stained, and as all the furniture is white, scuff marks are everywhere. So in theory they could be clean, but the scuffs are still there.
The bathroom looks posh, however, once you take a shower things go downhill fast. You'll see. It's a simple matter of form over function: The shower is long - tub shaped - but is only covered by half a glass partition. There is also a hole in the glass (think of how a breaking-in Bond might cut a hole in a glass window) to reach your arm through to turn the knobs. The problem is that water gets everywhere. And I mean EVERYWHERE, no matter how you aim the shower head. All over the bathroom floor, outside the shower, behind the toilet, and the worst - all over the toilet. It is disgusting. 
This is a fix that the W will be forced to make due to complaints or rust, whichever becomes intolerable first.
For the non-partier type: Saturday night was BUMPING at the roof bar (on floor 3) so it was loud and sleep was difficult even on my floor, 9. I can't say I had a problem with it, because I've been those obnoxious party people before. But there are others who would not enjoy it, so just be sure to ask for a room on the other side of the roof bar. Or quit your whining and go join the party.
One external issue also plagues the hotel, and that is its location. You're smack in between Little Italy and Gaslamp (two restauranty and hang-outy areas), but both require a bit of a walk, and to the Gaslamp you will have to pass through bail bondsmen and a gauntlet of homeless beggars. Taxis are recommended for your jaunts. I walk around a lot of strange places in cities I don't know, and this one in particular felt too unsafe even for me.
Would I stay at the W San Diego again? Well, no, because I like to stay at different hotels when I visit cities. But yes, I would stay there again if I was the type to go to the same place. Because while the rooms are meh, the hotel itself is pretty rad.

We stayed on the executive level in a King room. It was a nice size, with a couch in front of the TV. The bathroom was tiny, and the shower worked well. On the executive level, there was a complimentary "continental" breakfast, which was quite extensive!!, and good. There were hor d'oeurves from about 5pm to 7pm, also quite a nice spread. And there were soft drinks and other snacks available throughout the day. It was well worth the extra $20 or so per night for us! We got a good rate online for this hotel, and I would stay here again.

Fantastic location made for a great Chicago experience. We were there for our anniversary and the Conrad sent up some chocolates and a note which was really unexpected. Loved the pillow options, comfy bed and coffee bar in the morning. Staff were very friendly. Lots of little things added up to a fantastic experience. Well done! Would stay there again!

title_masked: good, but could use some attention to detail
text_masked:
Overall, very good - the room was very clean and reasonably set up, quite comfortable. Construction was handled well, as other reviewers have noted. The staff were friendly and helpful. The breakfast was convenient and the coffee very acceptable. The little convenience-store corner by the front desk was very convenient indeed, particularly as there are not many alternatives nearby. Check in and out went very smoothly.
On the other hand, some attention to a few details would have made a good experience much better. My room had a brand-new shower, but no matter how carefully I closed the door, it leaked. A new door did not seem to be soundproofed, at least on the 1 night that a neighbor was home late from the bars. No staff member ever asked how the room was, nor was there a comment card. They leave a card that says to limit ecological impact, they launder towels on request - to wash, leave on the floor, to keep, hang up. No matter how carefully I hung towels, they were changed.The breakfast was much as you would expect from a business hotel buffet - not bad, not exceptional, but I *detested* eating off plastic plates with plastic utensils. (To give credit where credit is due, they did have ceramic coffee mugs.)
No restaurant, but nearby is the North Market and Knead - both are highly recommended.

The Sorrento served as our Seattle home base for the weekend. We were within walking distance to downtown, given some wonderful restaurant suggestions from the concierge, and enjoyed live music each night in the hotel's lounge. They offer a car service to anywhere within 2 miles of the hotel, so they picked us up from dinner one night too. The beds were comfortable, rooms spacious, and bathrobes soft. 
Can't say enough about how accommodating the staff was, and how personalized our experience was; we were greeted by name when we returned to the hotel throughout the weekend, and it was very welcoming. Also, the lemon drops were a perfect refresher and sweet treat at the reception desk! 
We will definitely return to the Sorrento when we're in Seattle again.

title_masked: The ONLY place I will stay in SD from now on!
text_masked: We traveled from Vegas and got to the hotel around 3:30pm. Upon entering valet we were greeted by 3 employees that asked us if we were checking in. Heading over to the front desk there were a couple people in front of us but they promptly called out another front desk agent to help. We were given room 704 and when we got off the elevator on the 7th floor we couldn't seem to find the room. There happened to be someone from housekeeping on the floor so I asked where the room was. Instead of pointing where the room was the gentleman actually walked us back toward the elevator lobby where the room was located. The room was smaller than we expected but everything was clean and up to date as far as furnishings. The bellman brought up our bags right away (without us calling to ask for them) and he happened to be someone I know from coming in to my work back in Vegas (small world). He left and about 10 minutes later he called the room and said he had a room upgrade for us. We weren't expecting that much to be honest but once we walked in to room 1001 we were blown away! Hard wood floors and a staircase leading downstairs to the living room, kitchenette, formal dining room, and outdoor patio (from what I was told this was 1 of 2 rooms that had an outdoor patio). The view was great as well. It looked towards Petco Park and had a nice view of the Coronado Bridge as well. The upstairs bedroom was huge and has a great bathroom with a larger walk in shower. This was above and beyond anything we expected and greatly appreciated. I've stayed in some great hotel rooms over the years but its really the staff that sets this place apart. The bellman Ryan was very informative and accommodating, Mark from the concierge was kind enough to print out our Padres tickets for us and even offered to have them delivered to our room (I declined since we were walking out that way anyway and I also wanted to tip him). He even highlighted a map, giving us walking directions to the stadium. Room service was faster than I've come to expect and both servers went above and beyond. Eating breakfast on the outdoor patio overlooking downtown San Diego was great. The $35 valet seems expensive since it's free everywhere in Vegas but the price is right on with mostly everything else in San Diego so I can't complain. The only complaint (I'm digging here) is that we always thought the gift shop was closed. On our last day we actually read the sign and it said to let a front desk agent know and they would open it. Our fault for not reading it but one suggestion I would have is to maybe leave the lights on inside. I think people would be more likely to approach the doors if that were the case. Again I am absolutely digging to find one MINOR issue and like I said in my title, this will be the ONLY place I stay in SD going forward.

title_masked: Still Good the Second Time Around
text_masked: I love the comfort inn in Ludlow because of its central location to all the great vegan restaurants. The neighbourhood is very lively even in the wee hours of the morning. Hotel staff was very helpful and friendly and the rooms were tidy. Breakfast has not changed and it is very carb heavy. They should offer a non dairy milk as an alternative. I will come back again.

title_masked: Poor service and poor value for money
text_masked:
I stayed at the Mansfield for 4 days and was really disappointed. We stayed in a double double parlour room (one of the more expensive) and it was pokey and very dark - more importantly it wasn't clean. The bedside table and desk were covered in dust and the counterpanes on the beds were filthy. Twice the sheets on my bed had big rips in them. The room also looked out on to the street and was incredibly noisy.
We really struggled with the internet here when we critically needed to get on so would not recommend for anyone on business. The staff were very little help when we asked for help to get on the internet or to move rooms with one notable exception (F&B manager). Throughout the stay staff would look at you blankly when you asked for help and we needed to follow up two or three times for anything to happen.
There are much better hotels in NY at this price bracket - would not recommend.

title_masked: Nice room, not so nice restaurant
text_masked: The rooms are relatively up-to-date and the cleanliness is above average. The restaurant is sorely lacking - unfortunately. When the restaurant is closed and the service has shifted to the bar things go quickly downhill. The bartenders are overwhelmed with more than four customers and the kitchen consistently delivers the wrong sides. The food is unremarkable at best. If the restaurant issues ever get sorted out the place will be excellent.

I stayed here one night only but i wish i could have stayed more. The room was nice, clean and cool. the staff was very professional and help a lot. Parking was expensive, $25.00 per day, but you cant expect it to be cheaper as it's close to LAX.

Mark at the front desk was excellent attending to our arrival, with an upgrade due to our room not being ready when promised. Our room on the Plaza floor was very small but with a lot of character. Items that need a little attention to repair were not done which somewhat made the difference between old with character and old with needing attention. Our sleep quality was affected by the two full days of constant demolition of a concrete foot bridge just below our 17th floor room. The location to the Inner Harbor is great, and if you like to walk, it is close to Fells Point and Little Italy as well. The parking is a little out of the way but no big deal.

I just completed a week long stay at the Sofitel and my room was first rate -Clean, quite, spacious, excellent desk, comfortable bed, excellent linens, pillows and towels. The entire staff is gracious and competent, Carlos Alcazar, Assistant Food & Beverage manager does as excellent job along with all of the culinary staff and outrageously convenient to the Mall and beautiful on top of the other superlatives.

I stayed here last weekend with a friend and had a nice stay. I read the reviews before I went and therefore requested a room away from the construction site, which was no problem. I didn't hear any noise during my stay but it didn't seem like any work was being done during the 4 days I was there anyway. I had a lovely view of an office building about 20 feet from the window but it was no big deal really. I didn't come to DC to sit in the hotel and stare out the window. The windows opened, which is always nice. Also, there was a fire escape right at the end of the hallway which was convenient because my friend is a smoker. The mini bar was a bonus, not because we bought any of the overpriced snacks but because we had a fridge to put drinks in. The bed was comfy and the sheets were really nice. Everything was very clean. No problems with the internet. Didn't have any problems with the staff, got checked in and out with no problems and they looked after our luggage the day we checked out until we flew home that evening. I booked the room through a special they were having so it was much cheaper than others in the area. It was a bit on the outskirts of the tourist area but still walking distance to everything.

title_masked: Perfect place for easy access to the airport
text_masked: I arrived in Denver a day early for a ski trip. The complimentary shuttle was reliable and the hotel was clean. The room was as good as advertised and the bed was super comfortable. The staff was very accommodating and the woman who checked me in asked my preference about a first floor room or higher. The continental breakfast was decent and the waffle maker was a nice touch. I would definitely stay there again if the opportunity arose.

This hotel is very new and is fabulous as far as room cleanliness, decor, location. It's one block from the subway stop and one subway stop away from Penn Station on the 1 train. The King bed rooms have the best rooms as they are offer a better city view than the double rooms. As written by previous reviewers, make sure you don't get a room on the top floor as the noise from the rooftop bar is ridiculously annoying. Free breakfast (part of package) was nothing to brag about, especially given the price difference from that of a normal-priced room. You'd be better off going out to the streets of NY for something to eat. My biggest gripe with this hotel, having stayed here before and having experienced the same issue, is their need for 'tips' for just about everything. We arrived early and our room wasn't ready. No problem; we left our bag in the luggage room--tip needed. We came back, checked in, and found that our bags had to be 'delivered' to room even though we were standing there and could easily have wheeled them up ourselves--another tip needed. We asked for an extra set of towels to be delivered to room since we didn't get the extra set we had requested, and then left for dinner. No towels upon return. Asked for them again and left to go out for evening. No towels for the second time. Finally figured out that they wouldn't deliver them since there was no one there to give a tip! Ice bucket--tip needed. Bottle opener--tip needed. In conclusion, I would certainly recommend this hotel, but just be aware that you need to have lots of small bills in your pocket for the tipping. It was also disappointing to learn that they have done away with the mini cupcakes upon check-in. This was something that set this hotel apart from others.

I am of the opinion that hotels in Washington state are almost always garbage even when you are staying in ones that are rated 4 stars. This W is one of the oh so very few exceptions with a great location right in the heart of Seattle.

title_masked: If you're not claustrophobic, it's nice
text_masked:
I'm not claustrophobic, but I'm also cost-conscious. It was the best deal for the weekend of the NFL Draft in late April. However, there was literally 18 inches on both sides of the bed, while seated my knees touched the wall opposite the toilet, and the only way to iron was to lay the board out on the bed.
Otherwise, the decor was contemporary, the guests and staff enlightening and international. Though I found it odd that when I asked for the nearst bar, 1) they didn't recommend their own bar, and 2) they didn't recommend the bar next door - Three Monkeys - which was a pretty cool place all its own.

My wife and I just got back from staying one night in DC before meeting up with family outside the city. You expect great service at a hotel like this but yet it's still a surprise when you actually get it. From the minute our cab pulled up someone was there to greet us and immediately take our bags. The woman at the front desk was gracious and quickly got us through the reservation process. Our room was in great shape, my wife loved the shower. As folks have said, location is great. We were able to check out the next day, leave our bags and walk to a ton of your typical tourist sites from Lincoln Memorial to the Capitol (well we walked to Lincoln at least but you probably want to cab from there to the Capitol and only a short cab from there back to hotel). When we got back to the hotel and although we had checked out, service as still great. They had our bags ready to go quickly, radioed to have the valet grab a cab and when I asked the woman at the front desk if I could get one more of those Evian bottles for my wife before leaving she was nice enough to provide gratis without pointing to the closest vending machine. Small things like that can make an impression.

The Hotel Valencia Riverwalk is an older hotel, which makes its outside look interesting. On the inside it is as modern as anyone could wish. Well appointed decor. Nice, helpful staff. Its prices are comparable to other 4-5 star hotels on the Riverwalk. We would stay here again, as well as highly recommend it to anyone staying in downtown San Antonio.

This hotel has a great downtown location, you can walk almost anywhere downtown if you choose. We booked this room thru Priceline 1 day prior to our visit. We self parked in the underground garage for $22, which was the going rate at most area garages. Check in was flawless. The entire hotel was modern and clean. The 4 elevators were fast enough, we never waited more than 1 minute for one to arrive. Our room was clean with a great view of the city. The beds were a bit small, not really suitable for 2 people and the sheets were a little rough for my taste. I never noticed any construction noise, but did see workers in the building. The hotel is connected to the Circle Centre Mall, which was a bonus. There is a Subway, Pizza place and another small resturant in the lobby. I would not recommend the hotel resturant for breakfast as the prices were high, $26 for 1 childs breakfast, coffee and a chorizo burrito.

Superb stay - just 3 blocks from Empire state.
We asked on arrival for a room with a view- the 36th floor gave this- wonderful views over lower Manhattan. Comfy bed with wonderful pillows!, kitchen area to store your wine or beer! Contemporary design- clean and modern.
Friendly staff, good location. Would recommend a stay here and would come back again.

title_masked: Nice Hotel with Hilton quality, will stay again !
text_masked:
I arrived in the "Red Eyes" flight when I visited my son in Providence; I know I won't be able to sleep in the flight, therefore I have requested an early check in when I made my reservation. I received the e-mail right away from the customer services of Double Tree Hotel. When I arrived Boston on 02/11, it's a very cold day, when I arrvived the hotel around 9:00 A.M. the front desk gave me a warm welcome as Hilton Honor member, and the room is ready for me.
The room is spacious, bright and clean, after a hot shower and 2 hours sleep, all my energies back and I am ready to meet my son ! Regardless of the location, a good hotel need to consider the need of their clients, this is much important than anything else.
Will stay in this hotel again !

title_masked: Good location, nicely looking hotel, good bar.
text_masked: Right in the middle of the "European-looking shopping district" (and I thought I flew 12 hours to be in the US?)... It's a cozy environment, the hotel looks nicely, rooms pretty big. Pretty good breakfast, roomservice also OK, food is not unhealthy like in many other places. Bar with balcony/terrace that overlooks the street, nicely done, service varies a bit from day to day. The beds are a bit too high and too soft for my opinion.

This outstanding property is less then 3 years old and fills all my criteria as a business traveler:
(1) Clean, well maintained property - very modern without being uncomfortable. Quiet location an appropiate distance off of 281. Rooms are spacious for work w/ wireless.
(2) Restaurant with solid, quality entrees. Salmon w/ citrus glaze was something I expect from a higher end joint.
(3) Above average fitness center and spa - although no relationship with a local gym for those wanting more. ** Also is close to San Antonio's popular McAllister Park for runner's.
(4) Truly enjoyable staff.
Traveling year round, this is one of my top properties to stay. It's a no-brainer if you are in this area. Enjoy!

title_masked: Exactly what you expect a Hampton Inn to be
text_masked: The title says it all. If you want to stay in this location, and all you need is a clean and comfortable room, and the price is right, this will fill the bill. The included breakfast is also just like every other Hampton that we have ever stayed at--which means "adequate".

title_masked: Avoid at all costs; $45/night to park!
text_masked:
This is a giant, heartless Hyatt with a wonderful location - and nothing much else. I can't imagine a single good reason to pick this place above others in the area. The staff was rude and ineffective. The extra charges - $11 for internet for 24 hours, $45/night for parking, $2.50 for a soda in the machine - are beyond absurd - they're flat out insulting. I just can't think of a single reason to stay here. There's a Hampton Inn not far away, cheaper, newer, and no absurd fees. On the plus side, the location is wonderful, the street is quiet, and the rooms are comfortable enough. 
Hyatt has become the American Airlines of the hotel world - unyielding, unwelcoming and outperformed by cheaper competitors. Avoid.

This hotel is in a fantastic location and extremely good value for money compared to a lot of other hotels in the area. I was a little nervous about what to expect being so cheap but I was very happy with our choice. Room was very clean and comfortable. Highly recommend,

title_masked: Nice enough, but employees are lacking. I expected more for the price.
text_masked:
Had a 1 bedroom suite which was fine. However, maid service was crummy - didn't empty trash or even attempt to pick up coffee area. No creamer for coffee provided, so I had to go downstairs and pay $3.00 for a paper cup. Parking is $40 or $45 per day, can't remember exact amount. 
Most of the employees have difficulty with speaking English.
Beds were comfortable, room was good. Interesting hotel, but I expected more for the price.
Breakfast buffet was $25.00 per person.

I am long overdue in writing this review. I have stayed at this hotel on many occasions while I am in the Boston area. I work in the hotel industry so I know what is to be expected. This hotel does a wonderful job maintaining their property. The staff is always very friendly and accomadating. I would recommend to anyone. Keep up the good work!

I stayed 8 nights. The location is very good, 10 minutes to Central Park and very close to Times Square, which is a place to avoid! The bed was comfortable. The room, while nicely decorated, was small. For a couple it would have been quite cramped. The shower splashed everywhere and towels were quickly soaked. The WiFi was quick, but at $10 a day, or $25 for three days, is too expensive. These days WiFi should be provided free, like toilet paper. Free WiFi would encourage people to choose Ameritania over other hotels.

title_masked: Staff surprisingly service oriented. Hotel a little grim. Blankets a tad tired.
text_masked:
This hotel is not in the city centre and is about a 8$ to 10$ taxi ride from say the water tower. You get what you pay for - not an expensive hotel. The rooms relatively spacious for a city location, are very clean and all of that. The pillows were just fine, but the blankets just don't allow for the most soft nor comfortable experience.
Ask for a room on the 15th floor advertisted as a quiet floor - with a hotel engagement to have 'no children, no leisure groups, no marching bands, and no circus animals'. Nice to see a hotel with a sense of humour these days. The only thing is that they couldn't stop the noise from the traffic hurtling past 15 floors below. Also, I'd advise you to ask for a room that doesn't have a connecting door to the room next door. I had a neighbour who spent a lot of time on the telephone - from 6am - or had the television turned up loudly. 
A special word all the same for the staff who are very helpful, and for the management who must appreciate their teams as they had ordered pizza for all of the staff today. I was there when the trolley load of pizzas was being delivered.

title_masked: Great Time At The Inner Harbor
text_masked: Friendly,helpful and professional people, great location and the best value for you money.

title_masked: Great Place to stay and relax
text_masked:
Loved this hotel, besides the "Grand Slam" type cooked to order breakfast and 2 Hour Manager's reception in the evening, the place is spotless. The front dest staff is on the ball along with the airport shuttle driving who goes out of his/her way to deliver you on time! While its not part my view of hotel, advoid their in house resturant, its overpriced and the food isn't even
fast food quality.

title_masked: Great People, Great Service and Great Time
text_masked: Super service from the valet parking to speedy check in, Great People Great Hotel. We were part of The Mini Takes the States Tour 2012, and were treated like Royalty, with a great corner room on the 16th floor overlooking Downtown Chicago. Thanks Again Don & Shirley Thankful Travelers

We recentley visited Chicago for my sisters birthday and Pricelined this hotel for a reasonable rate. The hotel staff worked with me to have a delivery in the room as a surprise for my sister before arrival as well as surprising us with a complimentary upgrade to a suite with great views. They also called to check to make sure the delivery was made and that we were happy with the room. Those types of details don't go unnoticed!!
The only down falls of the hotel would be the small bathroom, we had three girls and this was not fun :) Cabs aren't as easy to come by at this hotel compared to many of the other CHicago hotels I've stayed at but it was not a big deal. 
Overall, we were quite happy with the customer service!

title_masked: Great stay at a great rate
text_masked: I got a great rate on this hotel and received a nice upgrade when I checked in. The staff was warm and the service was excellent from the front desk to the restaurant. Lots of nice touches, including the charming bell captain who gave us a tour of the room (found a small problem and addressed it). The room was stylish, the bed extremely comfortable. There's not much storage for clothes but it's not a problem. Had 2 great meals in the restaurant. Subway stops are near by, great location. I would stay here again, assuming I can afford it!

The hotel is very nice. It is convinient to downtown Seattle and has really good restaurants close by. There is a QFC grocery store that is just a block away and a seven Eleven that is really close.
The rooms are very spacious i stayed in a regular room it did not have a frdge or a microwave. But if you book a suite than the room is quite a bit bigger and better equipted with appliances..
The breakfast is really good it has all the foods you need for breakfast..
overall really nice place...

From the moment I walked in and was greeted by the front desk (Daniella I think was her name) to my meeting with the sales team (Kathy is terrific) (I am planning a business meeting there), to the bar staff, Valet staff...everyone.....this hotel excels in every area
It is so comfortable, so quiet, and yet still so close to the Riverwalk hot spots.
Some hotels that "try" to give great service it comes off as fake but for the staff of the Contessa it really seems as if they care that you are having an outstanding stay ....
Do yourself a favor and visit this hotel....... I see where it would be perfect for a romantic get away yet functional for a business meeting ...

title_masked: Nice Little Hotel around The Domain
text_masked:
The room was nice and clean. I really liked the updated washroom which were very contemporary. It is walking distance from The Domain and the MoPac highway.
Overall good experience in the short visit to Austin.

title_masked: This is one of the most beat up Marriott's I have ever stayed in.
text_masked:
I am currently suffering here at this property due to a convention I am attending and without paying highway robbery prices to switch hotels (they are all packed) I will have to stay for another 4 nights.
This Marriott looks like something out of the 60's and while centrally located in downtown LA there is not much more I can say about choosing this hotel unless the only other option is the soup kitchen down the street.
Pros: 
Location and very friendly staff. Great attitude and I feel for them working in such a run down hotel. This hotel is going through rennovation and the rooms are in desperate need that is for sure. Maybe check back in a year. Food was decent in the cafe downstairs in the lobby. Flat screens in the rooms. Jr suite good size room with separate living room. The pool area is nice but small. The freeway is behind the pool area and there is some constant noise but that is to be expected.
Cons:
The lobby smells of cheap soap. Not sure what is going on here but it smells like bathroom soap and very strong. The lobby has been refurbished so it looks pretty decent. Free internet which is nice in the lobby. 
Rooms are frankly horrible. looks like some grandmother's self furnished retirement home quarters. Right out of the 60's with green pink carpet and beat up furniture. We are in a Jr Suite which is a good size but the furniture is so uncomfortable that you really do not want to use it for any length of time.
The beds are miserable just miserable and I put that fact down to our room has not been refurbished. (God i hope so because if our room was redone...then yikes) Everytime my spose or I moved while sleeping the mattress moved with us. I felt like I was on a ship which was rocking and rolling all night. The quality of the mattress is one of the worst I have ever experienced. I don't expect much sleep over the next four days. Room is dark and depressing.
The club room is a nice place to work on your computer and the food is decent however they have three flat screens in the room and this morning (Sunday) at 6:45am) all three TV's were blasting away and so loud we chose instead to go downstairs to pay for our breakfast than eat in the cub room. Who is watching sports at 6:45am on a Sunday morning?
I would not recommend staying here until they have finished their remodeling job. If one cannot sleep then the hotel has not real value especially when traveing on business. Too many other good hotels in the same area including the JW Marriott which is very nice.

Ended up here during Pride Weekend with a last minute reservation. The room was clean and not unpleasant. Oddly the bath was nearly larger than the room. The service was not rude or pleasant, just there. Had no trouble but many others were very dissatisfied. If you want to be in the center of the city, the location is wonderful.
nice hotel.... difficult location to find but good value..... difficulties with keys... took three times to get it right....

The room was large and clean. My husband particularly liked the large TV! There are not many eateries near this location but I was pleasantly surprised to hear that they can shuttle you to a nearby restaraunt if you needed to go. Also, we used the shuttle to get to the airport. Just to forewarn, they run every 30 minutes in the morning so plan accordingly (our flight left at 7:30 am) so we had to wake up extra early to ensure we got on the right huttle. They were very nice though so I am sure they would accommodate you if you asked to go inbetween the half hours. Overall a great stay!

I don't usually stay in boutique hotels, but I am so happy that we stayed at the Library Hotel. The location is perfect: 2 blocks from Grand Central, walking distance to Broadway/Times Square, and a longer walk to the Hudson, Lincoln Center and Central Park. The service was AMAZING! Actually the staff was the best that I have ever experienced (and I do alot of traveling). The books all over, the wonderful breakfast and snacks, the cocktail hour-all just wonderful! I wholeheartedly recommend the Library Hotel. We will definitely return.

Long haul from Cuba, wanted a break before heading back to Australia. Free shuttle bus is always just damn nice, late night check-in was a breeze. Courteous and engaging latino at reception, he was responsive to our request for an upgrade. Club Lounge is the only way to go, my mate was captivated by watching the planes take off and landings (no noise). The continental complimentary breakfast was more than adequate (Starbucks coffee), fresh fruit and even boiled eggs. We paid an extra $50. for a 1800 hrs late check out, worth every cent. We were treated to a sort of late afternoon tea in the Club Lounge, stuffed ourselves silly, I'm an expat Yank and forgot how generous Americans can be, you can even buy beer or wine at a very nominal cost during that short period of time. Oh, yeah, the internet was free whilst in the lounge. Downside, the hotel bar was just a bit pricey for our taste, but thats the reason for duty free grog, ice and soft drinks are available on every floor. We will stay again, next year.

This property is 3 blocks from Hollywood Blvd and 4 blocks from Kodak Theatre. I was skeptical of the location having been to Hollywood before but I was pleasantly surprised. They offered valet parking (I think for security reasons) but it was refreshing to have someone handle the car at a Holiday Inn. I've stayed at some of the nicest hotels around the world and while not on that scale, this hotel was very clean, comfortable, roomy and relaxing. The breakfast was filling and included biscuits and gravy. I had my wife and teen/young adult with me and it was wonderful to park the car then walk to the Hollywood strip. You can feel comfortable choosing this location.

title_masked: A big fan of Hotel Palomar
text_masked: I've loved this hotel for a long time. In the middle of everything, yet pin-drop quiet. Small but welcoming lobby, extremely friendly staff, lovely design and spacious, comfortable rooms. I had a luxury king with the jacuzzi tub, which I used every night. Downsides: the restaurant was closed on Sundays so had to find elsewhere to eat, and in-room safe was broken. Fresh and comfortable bedding, good breakfast and love the wine hour. My favorite place to stay in SF.

I stayed 3 nights in the Alexander Inn, and it was a perfect choice. The guys on the desk were very friendly - nothing was too much trouble. The room was spacious, very clean, and the bed comfortable. The decor is very cute - lots of original art work, original tiles and moldings. A reasonable price, free wireless, a good continental breakfast (hard boiled eggs, pastries, juice, coffee, tea, cereal, yoghurt, fresh fruit). Who could ask for anything more?

title_masked: great hotel, location,room and comfy bed
text_masked:
We loved this hotel, great location especially if your awake at 3am with jet lag, pop out and have a coffee in Time Square, watch the world go by.
Rooms were great, we stayed in a renovated queen, beds really comfy, with fresh clean sheets everyday, had everything we needed.
Great location for a great rate.
Would recommend it to any traveller who wants a great hotel at a good rate in New York.

I book the travel arrangements for our employees visiting Boston on business and have been booking them into the Back Bay Hotel for the past 6 months. Unfortunately, due to several complaints regarding the accommodations, I have been requested to find an alternate hotel. The problems cited range from the inability of our employees to access the wireless internet to the extremely loud air-conditioning. Additionally, we request interior rooms above the 3rd floor as a standard request at this hotel, however, upon check in there never seems to be a notation on file and often the rooms requested are unavailable by this time.
Otherwise, the experience has been great from a service perspective. The staff is fantastic and they really do what they can to accommodate requests.

For business I recently stayed for two weeks at the Marriott Residence Inn. I was surprised how much this hotel exceeded the Marriott standards! The Assistant Manager, Bill Green, was helpful, and permitted late checkout with no problem. The desk staff and porters were all friendly, knowlegable of local attractions and restaurants. Housekeeping was prompt and thorough each day. Staff was outstanding all the way around.
Room was large with adequate storage and plenty of hangers in the closet. There is everything in the kitchen area to prepare a meal (using microwave) if you wish. 
The location is better than you expect. A few blocks down to the waterfront, and the National Aquarium. Located a few blocks from major hospitals [be aware of frequent ambulance sirens in the area as a result]
The real gem is the restaurant! The food and sevice far exceed Marriott standards. The diversity and style of items is exceptional! Prices are most reasonable. Service is helpful, quick, and attentive! Make sure you visit at least once even though you'll be enjoying a great breakfast each morning there too!

Stayed here overnight courtesy of the airlines due to a delay. 
PROS: friendly staff; clean rooms; nice furniture; kitchenette; air-conditioned; swimming pool; complimentary appetizers sodas, and beer in the evening; free hot breakfast in the mornings, including waffle maker; free shuttle service to airport; free wi-fi
NEEDS IMPROVEMENT: even though there is a kitchen there is no cookware/silverware; not enough pillows, beds were a bit hard, signs of wear and tear in the rooms, such as walls and moldings along the floor; very strong smell of cleaning supplies
OVERALL: would stay here again.

My Wife, Daughter and I went to San Diego for my little girls 2nd birthday. 
Stayed at the Bay front for 4 days. Wanted to stay downtown and near the water and near the Zoo and SeaWorld. This place is perfect.
Checked in process was quick and easy 
Thanks to Robert front desk (Cleveland. Ohio) 
There was a line but, didn’t wait long at all, Hotel have plenty of staff checking people in. 
(There was a huge conference at the hotel)
Andrew Bell man check us in, did a good job
Concierge, forgot the name but she was from (Sweden) did a great job helping me around town with directions. She picked a great place at Coronado beach to take the little one to ocean. Sweetthing an ice-cream shop in the bay front was awesome and staff was great.
Pool are great, grounds are clean, the breeze coming from the bay felt like heaven.
I didn’t want to leave...

The location of the Kitano could not be better for access all over town. Less than five minute walk to Grand Central. The room was spotless and extremely quiet. The service was outstanding. Didn't have time to try out the food or any extras but it is often hard to find a quiet room in Manhattan and this surpassed expectations.

Our first time to Pacific Beach. The price was perfect for us. We wanted to stay at least 3 nights. our room had a patio set outside our front door and could see the ocean from our room. It was a short walk to the boardwalk of Pacific Beach loaded with rentals, wonderful stores for shopping and many choices for eating. 
The beach was clean with a beautiful pier. 
The parking at our room was free. We had continental breakfast every morning. Laundry room,
ice, swiming pool with a grill and showers to get the sand off from the beach. 
The room was simple but clean, plenty of room. We loved it and the maids and the front desk staff were GREAT. Can't wait for our next trip.

We really enjoyed our stay at the Magnolia in downtown Denver. It's definitely one of the better deals downtown for a boutique hotel in a fantastic location. We actually spent the night there after dinner and a show at the Paramount. Service was great, rooms were impeccable and comfy, and the whole place felt very modern and classy. The only reason it's not a 5 is that I didn't love the shower--not enough heat or pressure for me. Hard to get clean (partly because I'm 5'3" and the shower head is so high by the time it reached me it was more like a sprinkle). I could easily look past this and recommend this place for short or long stays.

The hotel lobby is very nice. AND the location is easy to get around. Morning staff are very friendly Greg and Genevie. But the afternoon shift are not helpful. And the manager is not
around when the staff needs him/her which is not good.The room itself is very comfortable.The decor is very hippy. The price is reasonable. But the parking is too expensive and it will take you
30 minutes to get your car. I would recommend this hotel.

Perfect place. Service was excellent, room perfect for my husband and I. For a romantic getaway, I suggest the deluxe which has a fireplace and big round tub. Great location, few blocks from Times Square and a few block from Central Park. There is a parking garage next door that if you are a guest at Royalton it's $35.

We are regular visitors to NYC and usually stay uptown, however we decided on the new Trump SoHo as it had good reviews, was in a great location and we wanted to stay downtown for a change.
On arrival around 8.00pm we were warmly greeted by the doormen and reception staff, they couldn't have tried to be more helpful with luggage/check-in and assistance. We were offered an upgrade if we wished to pay a reduced rate, but declined as we hadn't seen the room yet that we booked.
Being on the 38th floor the room we booked was not only of good size but had superb views and offered all facilities that you could ask for. Having unpacked we went to the bar and had a light bite, where Rick the barman makes a great cocktail. The food, drink and chat were also very good. On returning to our room we noticed that there was a loud whistling noise coming from the door and when we investigated we realised it was coming from the lift core. The wind was quite strong and we felt being that close, the noise would keep us awake. Also having being placed by the lift core, we could hear other guests quite clearly, so we rang guest services to ask if we could change rooms, which to be honest was the last thing we wanted to do as we had unpacked and were travel weary.
To my surprise we were told it was not possible to be moved, the hotel was full for the next couple of days and they were sorry. I was taken aback at the attitude, having had such a friendly welcome, and knew it to be false, having been offered an upgrade earlier! We went to reception to talk to the duty manager, again the last thing we wanted to do, however resolved this and they moved us to room 3805, a junior suite, which I presume was what they had tried to sell us earlier. It was just a pity that they made the situation awkward. The new room, which was absolutely stunning. The views are just the best, as it’s a corner room, and although we didn't need or really want the extra space, as the bedroom and bathroom are the same as the room we moved from on the same floor, it was extremely comfortable.
The quality of the products, linen etc are first rate, the hotel is cool, very busy and with a great buzz and I would strongly recommend it for location, style, and comfort, together with the pricing. Downsides are that while the finishes are great they have an inherent problem which I believe they will find hard to resolve and that is insulation from internal noise. The walls are thin and we could easily hear conversation/TV from the next door room. The room below us were playing music until the early hours, and whilst it didn’t bother us too much, it does seem to be in inherent problem. Housekeeping was erratic and turndown missed on one occasion, great gym and spa, both which we used. Just one gripe that I repeatedly hate, is when they charge €15.00 a day (or any amount) for internet access in the room, its so cheapens the 5* product offering. Its free in the public areas, so someone not staying and paying room rates gets it for free! If they continue to charge they need to sort out the charging system as if you have more than one device, you have to pay each time you log on. We had to have them remove 6 charges from the bill over our 3 night stay as a result
Overall excellent and will definitely stay again when I return in May. They have a quality GM in Mr [NAME], who has a great pedigree of hotels behind him. Nothing is ever 100%, but this came pretty close and I’m sure with him in charge any small glitches will be sorted, perhaps with exception of noise insulation .
I enjoyed my stay. Rooms are gorgeous, 5 star for 4 star fee. Looking forward to booking again soon for girls nite out. Thanx a million for the great hospitality.
No problems, stay was without any problems I would stay again. Close to Shopping and other places of interest. Close to the main highways . Easy to find.

title_masked: HUGE hotel with tiny rooms. Clean and convenient
text_masked: I chose this hotel because of the location. It is an enormous hotel with a lobby that is always full of people (maybe free wifi?) The rooms are clean and beds comfortable, but the space is really tiny. Overall a good experience, but I wouldn't stay here again as it was not big enough for me and my children. Also - there were 4 of us in the room, but we were only given 3 towels and 1 small shampoo bottle every day. Had to call the maid service to request more every day. Pool is heated and kids enjoyed that.

title_masked: Great Boutique Hotel - BEST NYC HOTEL so far...
text_masked:
We booked 2 Double rooms (for 2 couples) at the beginning of January 2012 for a trip at the end of March - we got a great deal online and then an even better one when we got there. Due to their availbility we were all upgraded to their junior suites and the rooms were amazing and very clean. 
We were greeted by friendly receptionists, who were helpful and attentive to our needs. 
The hotel is in a great location, you have a number of Diners and Japanese restaurants around you and shops about 2 mins walk away. It was also handy to have the subway station just down the road. 
Although they don't have a restaurant so can't serve up breakfast the hotel puts out cakes, fresh fruit and hot drinks for free for all their guests from 7am in the morning.
My husband and I have visited New York 6 times and this is by far the best hotel we've stayed in and will not hesitate to return - The Moderne Hotel will be the first NYC hotel we pay a repeat visit to. 
Thanks again for your hospitality.

My daughter and I spent a wonderful ten days (and nights) at "The Willows".We enjoyed the neat hotel in a very pleasant neighbourhood. As tourists in Chicago we were very glad to be able to reach all sights without any difficulty.The hotel staff was extremely friendly and eager to help. The (complimentary) breakfast was more than sufficient to start a busy day. For lunch and dinner thre were a great variety of restaurants in walking distance. On the whole, "The Willows" has proven to be a lucky choice.

From the pictures I had higher expectations of this hotel, especially being a Wyndham member. Its outdated. It needs some updating, the wallpaper in the bathroom was peeling, the sink was cracked a lot and the faucet was a bit corroded. It was clean. Very small room, there was my husband, myself and two of our kids (ages 5 & 7) and we were cramped. We used one of the side doors to go in and out of since it was closer for us. It really needs replaced, especially the door frame. You could tell it had been broken into and just rigged to fix it. NOT safe if you ask me. Probably wouldn't stay there again.

title_masked: This property has turned it up a notch!
text_masked: I have stayed at this Hampton several times in the last 4 years. This last visit was the best yet. Elle was working the front desk and just terrific. I was tired and ready for a good nights sleep. Her pleasant personality was a nice end to my very long day. The front seems like it has been refreshed. The rooms are very nice. This is a newer Hampton and they deserve praise for keeping the bar raised. The carpet, pictures and accent furniture could be in a much for expensive property. They have installed a lamp behind the TV in the corner. A very nice touch of subtle lighting. I don't really understand why the Hampton has decided in the last couple of months to have yellow sticky notes on the headboard stating the Duvet and sheets are clean for my arrival. I would hope the sheets would be cleaned, and expect it. A sticky doesn't make it so. It makes me wonder "has this been a problem?" It is a company policy apparently to make that statement. Very odd. The room was nice and quiet, cold A/C, and I like the way they present the towels and coffee service in the bathroom. It's a great area with many things to do and places to shop. The ideal spot for a business or pleasure stay in Phoenix.

title_masked: 2012 and Pre-Judging is alive and well...
text_masked:
Stayed @ Crowne Plaza Feb 1st for 1 night..Had connecting flight next morning..I normally stay @ Radisson next door but price @ Crowne Plaza was better and pics on website looked nice.
.From the moment I walked off the airport shuttle upon my arrival 2 Crowne Plaza, I felt like The Brother from Another Planet..The bellmen out front looked at me as if I wasnt supposed to be there..I gathered my 2 bags and walked into the front desk area..As I reached the front desk (which was occupied by 3 female and 1 male employee, they all stared at me like maybe I was lost..(all except the black american employee)..So I walked up to the next available clerk who looked at me with a blank expression and asked, "can I help you?" Now I am a 53 year old black american male wearing a nice buttoned down collard shirt and dockers with a smile on my face...My appearance should'nt have given off any red flags of trouble..So I checked in and while I signed papers an approximately 30 year old white make wearing t-shirt and jeans approached the same lady who was assisting me..She greeted him with a smile while stating ."Welcome to Crowne Plaza sir, how may I help you?"..Wooooooooooooooooooooooooow....So I then go up to my room....
Once inside room I must say I was pleased..Great room..Everything looked fresh, new and up to date..See Pics below..I was very impressed with the room..All tho there appeared to be some construction still going on, it did not affect my stay..I then decided to go back down and attempt to reverse the negative vibrations I was receiving from the 90% Hispanic employees of the hotel, with kindness..
I contacted a doorman (ref computer in lobby that allows airport check in) and a different clerk behind the front desk to use a pencil..After me killing them with kindness there attitudes appeared to relax a bit..Except for a employee wearing a nice suit who didnt say anything but appeared to be watching all the employees and there actions..
I then went into the restaurant and sat at the bar..The bartender Temo (older hispanic male) gave me the same negative reaction as the doormen and desk clerks) As I sat @ the bar he asked if I would be eating there. I stated yes..As I looked @ menu a older white couple sat at the bar and Temo smiled and greeted them with "how may I help you"..Thru out my dinner I too killed Mr [NAME] with kindness and left him a big tip as well..Even tho I had to ask him twice for more water..Ordered the salmon and it was cooked perfect..Great meal..Left bar and went to gift shop...
Met a wonderful Philippino couple who worked in the gift shop..I only purchased bottle water and a news paper but had a 30 minute conversation with this couple..Very nice and pleasant couple..These two are an assist to the hotel..
To sum up this review, I loved my stay at the Crowne Plaza Hotel..The room was great and the food was great..Im aware that there has been a issue/problem between blacks and hispanics in the L.A. area but I did not know that it carried into a 4 star hotel..

Very nice upgrade to a suite paying only more 200 US but when I paid had the nice surprise of being charged 51 US a day of parking, attention that no one inform about that, being an European, in none of our Four Seasons we pay parking!!!!
Very noisy room because of the wind!!! Not informed as well when I did the upgrade!!!
i was arriving from the Ritz Four Seasons in Lisbon where charme and courtesy are in the house!!

Just returned from spending 2 nights at the Henley Park this weekend. Check in was so pleasant and easy - not having to stand in line at a large convention hotel. The hotel is lovely - very European feel. Our room was wonderful, beautiful decor and was the cleanest hotel room I've stayed in for a long time. Even the tile in the bathroom shone. The location is excellent - near the convention center and many cafes and restaurants. It's close the Metro as well. Staff were very helpful and friendly.
