We'll be visitng famly in DC often and will plan to stay at the Henley Park again.

I was pleasantly surprised by the quality of this hotel. Prompt service on check in, lovely lobby, very spacious. We stayed here because of the proximity to the airport, which proved to be a good choice. I was also very happy that the continental breakfast started at 4AM! The food was not great, but at least you got something to get you going (and coffee!). We did not use the shuttle service, so I cannot comment on it. One negative was our room was at the end of the hallway near the elevator, so you could hear the dinging of the bell whenever it stopped at our floor.

We paid $200 a night for the accomodation here at Sheraton about 2 weeks ago and stayed 2 nights. For the price, we got ripped off. The rooms were very tired looking and after watching their in room Sheraton channel about the amount of money spent on upgrading sheratons worldwide, I can tell u now, nothing was spent here. 
The location was good, but I would have liked to be closer to the Westfield mall. The Westin is literally next door to the motel, and of much higher quality, and as we are going back to San Diego in 3 weeks we booked into the Westin and guess what, we got the rooms for $130 each night on Priceline.com. Cheaper and way better than this Sheraton. I must say the staff here were lovely, but another downside is the food in the hotel. It's so expensive and is awful. My dad ordered a sandwich and the bread was still half frozen. I would not recommend staying here.

title_masked: Clean and comfortable, but overpriced for the lack of included amenities
text_masked:
I acknowledge that I used to more affordable hotel prices as I am from the midwest and not used to San Francisco prices. However, my biggest complaint about this hotel was that I paid $160/night (which was a discounted rate) and did not have free internet access or any complimentary breakfast. For me, this was unacceptable because I was traveling for work, and was counting on having access to internet without having to pay $15 per day. They do have a "business center" with a few computers with internet, but you cannot use a flash drive with these computer, so if you need to send an important email with a document attachment, you are pretty much out of luck... unless you want to pay $15.95.
Otherwise, the room was clean but the beds were not that comfortable. The hot water stopped working for several hours one the afternoon (affecting many rooms), but it was resolved. The room was rather noisy because of street noise, and I could hear people talking in the room next to me. The location is great, very close to a BART station, restaurants, shops, and streetcar lines.

We were a little apprehensive after reading some reviews but couldn't agree with some of the bad comments regarding service. The front desk were very good as were the bell hops. Early in the week we had no problems with the elevators but I have to say that closer to the St. Pats weekend, they were slower. We were on the 5th floor so easily walk able. The room we had was large especially for New York. Two double beds in a corner unit. Beds comfortable and clean. They have made some renovations to the room but the bathroom definitely could use some work as the grout in the tub was covering over moldy previous grouting in a roughshod manner. To be honest all the bathrooms probably need upgrading which would cost thousands and put the room cost up accordingly. We were able to overlook this. The noise at night from road works going on at different hours of the night was pretty loud. My daughter wore earplugs and was unaffected. I would wake up but was so exhausted from our days adventures I went right back to sleep again. Based on this experience I would stay here again - probably not for the more affluent traveler but as long as the bed is clean and the daily room service is fine, I'm happy. Our focus was New York and being so close to Grand Central station was a bonus. Everything was walking distance including the better restaurants - you just had to walk a little further.

Hotel is very clean . Room was very clean. And ... location .. location ... location . Many things to do within walking distance. Also the employees could not have been nicer. There really isnt much of a " wow " factor here and the walls are a little thin but all in all ..... a nice place to stay

I have stayed at the Bedford Hotel several times over the past couple of years. I usually come into Grand Central and it is short 2 blocks to the hotel. It is comfortable and reasonable, the staff is always pleasant (we had help with our bags up to the room), and, best of all, perhaps because I am a frequent visitor, I sometimes get upgraded. My last room was very large for the 2 of us-- on the top floor with windows looking out in 3 directions. Rooms and baths are clean. I generally walk at night to nearby restaurants without worry about so-called "unsavory characters" mentioned by one reviewer. All in all, a terrific place to stay.

Just checked-out after a 4day stay - the suite was large and had a pullout bed in the living room and a great Queen sized bed in the separate bedroom. Bathroom was basic but clean and amenities provided - the FULL kitchen, microwave, blender, dishwasher were a bonus - especially if you needed to save money by cooking or making your own breakfasts. The location at the corner of Hyde and North Point is at the crossroads of both the Powell-Hyde cablecare or the MUNI bus which will take you directly downtown. Of course you will spend most of your day exploring Fisherman's Wharf - 2 blocks awayfrom the main strip.
The staff are excellent - helpful and always cheery. Parking is tight if you have a car - small spaces and ther SUVs take up most of the spots. Free WiFi - bonus. Great roof deck to read and have a view.
Highly recommended - only issue : noise from the roads nearby - you can hear the cablecars and buses - so if you are a light sleeper the suites will not do.

This is an awesome hotel. The breakfast is a very excellent size, and the kickback was delicious and filling. The free popcorn and soda was great too. The rooms were also great. The beds were very soft and nice. The pool was disappointing though.

title_masked: Average Comfort Inn - clean and comfy
text_masked: Stayed for 1 night while in NYC to see Oprah. Checked in at 11:30 am as we had arrived early form Boston. Had a room right off the Lobby, which was a little noisy, but not horrible. Probably would ask for a room not in the lobby if I stayed again. The breakfast was free and good with eggs, bacon, toast and bread, waffles, juice, coffee and all the other basics. Not bad for free. Overall the rooms are small, as are most NYC rooms, but efficient with everything you need. They are clean and comfy for a couple nights sleep. Great location, convenient to Times Square and Midtowmn, if that is your thing.

We stayed at the Hotel Monaco on 6/29 for our anniversary. We love the Monaco, the staff is always wonderful. Michael the bell captain took great care of us both at check in and check out. Frances at the front desk is always gracious, we remembered her from a previous stay and she is always helpful and considerate. There are more I could name as well. It's obvious that the management of the Monaco genuinely care about your experience staying there and encourage the staff to go to extra lengths to make your stay enjoyable. And don't forget about the location, it's convenient to everything. We were able to walk to State Street, the Magnificent Mile and the restaurants on Rush Street.

We LOVED this place. We stayed in three hotels during our stay and this one took the prize! Staff = Excellent ; Location = Excellent; Room = Excellent Across from Lincoln Park, walking distance to great cuisine and a great coffee shop on site. View of the Lake, to die for. Walking distance or a short bus ride to Molly's Cupcakes, Sushi Mon and many wonderful places to eat. Neighborhood was nice, we walked every day all around the location and had ZERO complaints on the location. Staff greeted us immediately, very friendly, answered all our questions and helped get us directions when needed. the room was cozy, clean, roomy and had a great view. This place is a gem! Nice lounge area upstairs & exercise room. We will make this our spot when traveling to Chicago.

Wonderful, wonderful staff at the front desk! Rooms were small, but didn't feel cramped for the 2 of us. Fit two big suitcases plus backpacks. Not a lot of storage space, and would have appreciated some hooks on the walls.
Wifi was free, and a really good speed.
Room was made up each day.
Booked right through the Hotel 373 website and got complimentary breakfast at the Oxford Cafe, which is right next door, for each morning. Appreciate that so, so much!!
The cheapest souvenir store we found in Manhattan (and we were in quite a few!!) was two doors down, just on the other side of the Oxford Cafe.

This was my first stay at the Arctic Club Doubletree. I was very happy I chose this hotel. Check in was fast and the staff was very friendly. The hotel's lobby was cozy. My room was very well decorated and very clean. I loved the coffee press in the room with the Starbucks coffee. Nice touch! Breakfast was overpriced and embarrassing for what you received. I would not recoommend eating at the hotel, there are many other options very close to the hotel. The bar in the hotel's lobby was closed on Sunday which is very odd. Parking is overpriced. Valet is always such a pain. You do not have the choice to self park for the hotel's lot. The quest rooms were very nice though, so I would stay here again.

title_masked: Great place to stay esp. when you have a car
text_masked:
I chose this location based on TA reviews and was not disappointed. I agree with the others. The staff is very helpful with local transportation & attractions. It is on the quiet end of Lombard Street. They have free parking but only enough for 1/2 the rooms, so once we had our parking space, we didn't want to move the rental car. We used public transportation to go downtown.
They had tea and cookies available in the afternoon, but free breakfast is pretty limited.
A computer is available if you have to use the internet.
It is an older California motel but clean and well kept.

Pacific Terrace Hotel was such a great experience and the perfect choice for a quick birthday getaway. Right on the boardwalk our room had huge sliding glass doors out to a balcony that was so close to the water that the surf was the first thing I heard every morning. 
The service was absolutely excellent and the employees clearly love their jobs and sincerely want to provide a good experience. They even put bottles of water in our car as we were leaving in case we needed a drink on the way out of town!
The hotel itself is lovely, the room was spacious (third floor suite), everything worked, very nice breakfast buffet option and absolutely the closest to the beach location on Pacific Beach. Everything PB has to offer is literally right outside the door. We will definitely stay here again next time we're in San Diego.

Our daughter is a student at Butler University, and this is our mainstay hotel when visiting. Very conveniently located off I-65 and accessible to the north side of Indianapolis, this hotel never fails us. Typical HGI rooms and amenities, and with an exceptionally friendly and accommodating staff. Ample parking, and a Starbucks just across the road. Didn't enjoy the breakfast offerings at the hotel, however, but there is a full-service restaurant and a bar in the lobby.

title_masked: Excellent hotel, location, and staff! Our new go to hotel in Seattle!
text_masked:
My husband and I stayed at The Paramount Hotel four nights on our honeymoon and we loved every minute of it. This hotel is a great value and better quality than most high end hotel chains! We stayed on the 10th floor and facing the Harbor and Pike's Place Market (fabulous views out each window)! The beds were extremely comfortable and we loved the soaking tub! Our first night at the hotel we were given bottles of Fiji water and Frans salted chocolates (YUM!). These little touches really explain the experience you get at The Paramount. There is nothing better than feeling like you are getting so much for your money!
As far as location, you are close to everything! Including our favorite, Pikes Place Market, and tons of shopping and food! If you are looking at hotels for Downtown Seattle this is a no brainer!!

We reserved a queen bed for one night and were given an upgrade to a king suite, which was a great sized room. There was a nice little lake with ducks right outside the room. The front desk attendants were friendly and there was very little road noise. But the room needs some help!! The door didn't close tightly at the bottom, there was a huge cob web in the corner of the living room part of the suite, the hairdryer didn't work, the curtains are threadbare, carpets had stains and both TV's had horrible reception and few channels. Worst of all when you flushed the toilet, there was such a powerful pressured flush that the water sprayed your legs. Not sanitary! Breakfast was a little sparse. Not bad if you are on a budget and don't mind a room with rough edges, but I won't stay here again.

As we had booked a 'queen bed' room, we were expecting a smallish room. However, we were pleasantly surprised! It was spacious, very clean, fashionable, had an amazingly comfortable bed and in a great location for a sightseeing holiday. The concierge was always very helpful with sightseeing queries and finding out where to go on nights out. 
Definitely recommend it!

My husband and I attended a movie premiere at the Nokia Theater and we stayed at the Westin Bonaventure. This was our first time at this Westin and people told me "you can get a good room or a bad room". The hotel is showing its age; the elevators are on the outside so you can get a view of the city. The room was pretty clean (housekeeping left a few dirty spots on one nightstand); the bathroom was clean however. My husband loved the bed. I thought it was okay. All in all, it was a good stay. The Westin's customer service was excellent. The staff helpful and friendly. We were on the 30th floor and had a great view of the city. The revolving lounge on the 35th floor is very nice. If you have the chance you should check it out.

Beautiful and trendy hotel located in (not (yet) very trendy) Hell's Kitchen on 11th av and 48th between the car dealers, Fedex and Verizon trucks (keep in mind that you have to walk some 15 to 20 minutes (through not very exciting streets) to go to for example Times Square or Central Park).
We were upgraded to a Hudson Suite on the 12th floor. Very nice, large room with floor to ceiling windows all along, sitting area with flatscreen, comfortable bed room with flat screen, lot's of storage facility, wifi throughout the hotel (register for free as an Ink48 member and wifi is for free). Magnificent views over the Hudson river, New Jersey, the Intrepid, the cruise piers, ... However, the airconditioning made really a lot of noise (not possible to put the fan low; we mentioned it, but either it just is like that or they were not able to fix it during our 5 nights' stay). The aluminium frame of the windows is not isolated (making the temperature in the room drop if you put the airco of (which is necessary for us to be able to sleep)). The same flow of cold air can be felt when seated in the bar or restaurant near a window or door. For the light sleepers, be aware that the hotel is exposed to quite some outside noise, but hey afterall it's NYC ... (bring some ear plugs).
The restaurant is really excellent (see our comment on Print restaurant).
The rooftop bar (Press Room) is also very nice. Cosy, loungy atmosphere, great views.
Breakfast is only à la carte, which makes it a bit more expensive than a typical continental all-in breakfast buffet (+/- 35$ per person, compared to a more standard +/- 25$ buffet formula).
The hotel has a daily happy hour in the lobby area with complimentary wine. There is also water available in the lobby all day and complimentary coffee/tea in the morning, which is just an example of the many small things that this nice hotel does to comfort its guests.
The hotel has two bikes available on a first come, first serve basis. We used them for a day to go to The Cloisters (great trip, beautiful destination at the very north end of Manhattan island). A bike is really the best way to discover NYC (provided that it does not rain). If the bikes of the hotel are taken already, there are plenty of places nearby where you can rent one. 
The staff is very friendly and helpful. It is clear that they aim for customer satisfaction.
Overall : the pluses definitely outwheigh the minuses. We will be back !

I spent three nights at this hotel with two girlfriends as a brief getaway. We shared a lovely room with balcony on the 6th floor, the view of the river was wondertful and worth the extra. It had a king bed and easily accomodated a rollaway for our third. The bathroom was well appointed and had a lot of storage including a nice table with shelves in the corner -perfect for three women and all our stuff. We arrived and had lunch at Trio's, the hotel's restaurant, and had such a good experience there that we had a number of our meals at Trio's, including all breakfasts (we had a breakfast credit with our room) and a dinner. The food was excellent (and I am from Boston a nd very spoiled) and the staff were friednly and knowledgeable. The breakfasts were amazing - do not miss the local farmer's breakfast!!! Trio's has a wonderful outdoor area and the landscaping and views of the river are lovely.
 We had late drinks in the lounge two nights, very comfortable and friendly.
BEST OF ALL though was the pool. It is gorgeous, far more that what I expected in a city hotel. It is a non-chlorine "salt water" pool. We spent two entire afternoons there under wonderful big umbreallas. The staff can't do enough for you - they bring around ice water regularly, and little complimentary treats like small cups of frozen grapes or small oreo frappes - yum. There is free sunscreen available if you forgot yours, and a big bin of floaties so you can hang in the pool. It was HOT, so we and quite a few others did plenty of pool hanging. The menu at the pool is just perfect and we lunched there twice. Good mojitoes and spiked Arnold Palmers!
We used a happy hour special at the spa and had massages for $50 off - nice! The personnel were terrific and my Swedish massage was great.
ALL in all, this is a wonderful hotel - right in town but with all the comforts of a resort. We loved it.

OK, I have to admit that one star is probably due to the fact that we were upgraded to a 2 room suite, but I still have (mostly) good things to say about this hotel!
When checking in, I wanted to verify a King bed, and the kind woman who helped us mentioned we'd been upgraded. We sure had! The decent-sized bedroom was attached to a very large room with a dinner table for 6, chairs, a sofa, and a Murphy bed. There was also another closet/dressing area and a second bathroom. The decor I would describe as "1990s Conference Room", but it was the space that thrilled me.
Yes, the hotel is old. That is it's charm as well as it's problem. Walls were thin, but this was only an issue when other patrons felt the need to shout at each other like they were at Fenway when walking past our room at 2 in the morning. That is, if people behaved decently, you wouldn't care much about wall thickness.
The room was very clean, and the bed was quite comfortable, which are ultimately the most important things.
It was Marathon weekend, so the place was ridiculously packed. I was on the 8th floor, and it was impossible to get an elevator, so a very nice staff member brought several of us around to the service elevator so we could get downstairs.
Not at all thrilled to be gouged for wifi, but as they are primarily a business hotel full of people charging their employers for it, I can see why they do it.
Great to have Au Bon Pain, a pub, The Melting Pot (fondue restaurant) and other restaurants right in the hotel. The hotel is also close to Boston Common and the Public Garden, as well as amazing shopping on Newbury street. We crossed the Common to get a beer at Cheers (formerly Bull and Finch) a few times, since the walk was so pleasant (give me a break, I'm a child of the 80s)
To sum up- comfortable bed, friendly staff, clean, great location, thin walls, costly wifi. I would stay again, actually :)

This is a decent hotel, needs a little updating but I stay here pretty often the price is fair, the staff treats you nice. The rooms are fresh & clean most times and I get a good quiet nights rest. This Best Western is convenient to a lot of stores and restaurants. There is Also truck parking for truckers.

If location is what you are looking for then this is the place. We could see LAX from our room. We did an overnight stop when travelling form LA to Chicago, The rooms are quite small and unfortunatley our room had cigarette smell ( smoke free hotel!) The bed is soft and comfortable however the linen had stains on it. It is quite old and could do with a bit of TLC but overall as a stopover hotel this is pretty good. Would stay here again if need be. Also the A/C is quite noisy, you may need ear plugs. Staff are polite.

title_masked: Bad experience made me change my mind about this place
text_masked:
I have been using Staybridge hotels in various cities in the USA and been very impressed with services and suites to the stage that I became Platinum Member.
The last experience in Memphis was the worst! I don't think I will stay there again nor would I recommend this place.
The room smelled with smoking even though we were promised non-smoking room.
The bed linen looked old, my wife brought linen from outside.
On the third day, we were attacked with large cockroaches in the living room. I informed the front desk who verified similar problems, the room was sprayed afterward.
The worst part, on the last two days, the bathroom produced a terrible smell after 10PM, to the point that we had to avoid the bathroom during these hours, the staff could not fix the problem the following day

There is not a nicer hotel or experience than this one. From the moment we drove up to the moment we drove away it was pristine and blew us away. The staff is amazing and the attention to detail is phenomenal. You must have dinner at Addison. This was my husband's 50th birthday and were treated like royalty the entire time. The luxury and appointments of the resort and grounds exceeded our expectations. The food was sublime. We stayed in a suite and I highly recommend it. The spa was the nicest I've ever been in, and we have traveled a great deal. The spa treatments exceeded our expectations as well. 
We truly had a magical weekend. Our trip coordinator after I made reservations helped me make excursion plans and everything went off without a hitch. They truly know what they're doing and are very good at it.

title_masked: Home away from home in DC
text_masked:
Wife and I stay here everytime we're in DC to visit friends and family - at least 3-4 times/year. Staff/concierge are very friendly and helpful. Lobby has coffee in the morning and wine hour in the afternoon. Rooms are good size with nice furnishings and comfortable beds. We liked their pillows so much we bought some from the kimpton website. 
Location is great - Dupont/Adams Morgan/U street/Georgetown all walkable. Have even walked from here to the Mall - about 45 mins. Dupont circle Metro is very close. Plenty of good restaurants & coffeeshops nearby. Parking is a snap, valets are good and fast but pricey (like everywhere else). 
Kimpton's our new "go to" brand when traveling, and this is still the best we've stayed in. Have tried many other hotels in DC, and this is the tops for us.

title_masked: Good Choice for Overnight Airport Stay
text_masked:
Summary:
Rooms relatively updated.
Best rate out of 6 Trip Advisor recommended hotels. Offered distressed passenger rate due to hurricane - very much appreciated.
Bed comfortable (device to adjust bed comfort level did not work in my room)
Hallway carpets need cleaning (smell slightly like a college dorm)
One elevator was not operational
Did not elect to eat from dining room. Appears to only be open in evening.
List of restaurants and map locations available from front desk.
Front desk staff knowledgeable about the area.
Directions to airport pre-typed
Shuttle service appeared to be very accessible and timely although I elected to keep a rental car due to early flight departure at 6 am.
No automatic hot breakfast - not great if traveling with kids or don't have a rental car.
Front desk offered to print boarding pass b/c Business center printer is sporadic. Didn't like having to give her my airline flight passcode to print the boarding pass.
Relatively easy access to airport.
Dislike mirrored elevator - vertigo-like experience!
Couldn't get temperature in room comfortable - too hot or too cold. Somewhat noisy but very functional.

title_masked: Busy HI near I-10. Experience wasnt the greatest.
text_masked: Was passing through El Paso on business and had arranged a night at the HI Sunland off of I-10. It appeared to be an older HI that had been remodeled in recent years to bring it up to today's HI standards. They did a good job with the remodel but the rooms are somewhat smaller than todays new ones. It is right off of the interstate in a very busy section of town and near a huge shopping mall. There was lots of traffic. The rooms are exterior and face the road so there was road noise. The hotel seemed full and there were lots of noisy kids in the pool and running around the corridors. My room was non-smoking but it seemed lots of guests stood on their balconies and smoked which came in through the AC. They did have a nice looking restaurant and bar. The business center was basically in the bar so if you needed that for some business reason you would be in the bar with big TV's blaring. Due to the busy city area I was somewhat leary of leaving anything in my car. There were several safety messages posted around about not leaving valuables around. The whole area had that uncertain feeling. The room had a nice large flat screen TV, a mini fridge and microwave. Some parts of the room were a bit worn. The staff at check-in were very nice and helpful. Overall a typical somewhat older HI. I would likely not stay here again as I would want something in a less busy part of town.

title_masked: Above and Beyond Service at I-10 West Fairfield
text_masked: From the moment I stepped in the hotel I was greeted with a warm smile of Laporche whom was working the desk that morning. She also granted me an early checkout without a hassle. She continued to educate me on all of the anemeties the hotel had to offer. The presence of the hotel was also acceptional. There was no flaws that was seen. My room was cleaned to perfection. Every morning I walked down the smile and salutation from the front desk was awesome. I loved it and cannot wait to come back. Thanks

I have stayed at this hotel over 30 times over the last 5 years and it is very reliable. The rooms are clean, albeit some are very small with very unusual bathroom configurations, but I guess that since I stay at corporate rates, I tend to get the smaller rooms. The hotel floors are gigantic and you can sometimes feel like you walk a mile to get to your room, but it is fairly priced and a minor inconvenience. The rooms are fully-equiped (iron, hair dryer, etc) and I can only remember one time when something didn't work. 
The lobby is to die for and is a glorious place. No matter how many times you stay here, look up at the ceiling and you will be wowed yet once again. The location is great, right in the heart of everything. I recommend this hotel.

The hotel is rated 3.5 stars by Priceline, but its more like a 2.5 star hotel. Very average property with a below average location. The property is located very close to San Pedro's Port's of Call Village, but the surrounding area is sketchy and not very good. I wouldn't feel safe walking the area at night. I went to the Von's market a few blocks from the hotel and there was a security guard stationed at the front door of the grocery store. 
The non-smoking room also smelled like smoke when we arrived. We asked to switch rooms, but the only other rooms were adjacent to the elevator and the manager said those rooms were very noisy. They sent the cleaning staff to the room to spray a deodorizer, but the room still smelled like smoke. 
The positive aspects of the hotel are its proximity to Port's of Call, free self parking, pool, work out facility, and it was clean. However, I will be staying in Long Beach the next time I visit the area - Hilton, Westin, Hyatt, and Radison are much nicer properties and they are also rated 3.5 stars. The area in Long Beach off of Ocean Avenue is much nicer than Seaport Village in Long Beach is so much nicer than Port's of Call Village. Nightlife near the properties I mentioned in long Beach is also much better-There are numerous nice restaurants and clubs for dancing (movie theater, Long Beach ,Aquarium, nice views of the Queen Mary and Long Beach Harbor, great areas to bike or walk along the harbor).
we were pleased to find a pet friendly hotel that was clean and comfortable. Breakfast was great. Will definitely stay there again

We had five nights here (on Marriott points - LOVE the Marriott points!)
Well appointed room - very modern hotel - recently refurbished. The staff were very helpful and great views of Time Square from the R Lounge.
We had breakfast included in the R Lounge which was lovely with a change in the hot offering every day.
Is close to everything and even though it's right in the square, our room (on the 24th floor) was very quiet.
Would recommend.

title_masked: Great service, great location and overall, great hotel
text_masked:
We just finished a lovely four day/three night stay at the Hotel Eventi. In NYC, we've previously stayed at 70 Park Ave and Ink 48. We really liked 70 Park Ave but didn't like the Ink 48. Hotel Eventi was even better then 70 Park Ave.
Both 70 Park Ave and Hotel Eventi had top notch service. And, both are in excellent locations. But, the Eventi's locations was more convenient to my schedule. It's right next to Penn Station and easy access to the subway lines that I was using.
We were in NYC to meet my parents for a Broadway show. My parents usually stay at a Hilton or Marriott, but I convinced them to stay with us at the Eventi. The hotel staff sold my parents on the Kimpton hotels. They were incredibly impressed with the gracious service and they really liked the coffee in the morning and fruit water throughout the day. Unfortunately, with our schedule, we weren't able to go to the wine and cheese gathering in the evenings but they liked the idea.
Both of our rooms faced the Empire State Building. The views from the odd numbered rooms have great views. The beds in the rooms were also very comfortable and I didn't notice any noise from the hallways.
I highly recommend the hotel, especially if you are seeing shows on the west side. It's also easy access to Chinatown on the subway lines.

when we arrived my wife said she was disappointed cause it looked nothing like the picture showed. the rooms were clean but it look like it need some major repairs to the building as well. They were nice. It just wasn't what we thought it would be. We always stay at Super 8 even when we go to the races but this one just wasn't as nice. There wasn't even enough parking spaces. the breakfest was good. This was a surprise trip for me since I'm from Memphis. We will probably stay somewhere else next time

title_masked: Ok for business; not really for vacation
text_masked:
This hotel has had what appears to be a fairly dramatic makeover recently,and it shows inth elobby and rooms alike. that is until you look a little closer. Althought the rooms are comfortable, including the bed, the sliding doors have not been updated. they are circa 197X aluminum framed, and do not make a tight seal, allowing downtown city noise to penetrate. 
The bartender on duty was cheerful, and poured a solid drink, and the front desk staff was very friendly and efficient. Value for money, but please fix the sliding doors!

Excellent position that allows tourists to walk to most attractions, apart from the far south. Mixed feelings about the hotel, was expecting a lot more - but it was adequate for people who are out all day and return late at night. Nice reception, bar and restaurant. Bedrooms slightly disappointing, very clean but rather small. As usual in NY the view from the window is a brickwall overlooking air conditioning units. Bed was not as large as a standard UK double bed. Bathroom very clean but a major update required, hot water very hit and miss, and not thermostatically controlled. Has good air conditioning. Iron already in the room, with coffee making facilities and fridges available on request

title_masked: Nice room, great location, no HDTV
text_masked:
Stayed for a couple of nights this past week after the lobby renovation was complete. Very nice looking lobby with a casual check-in, beautiful fireplaces and sitdown areas. Check-in was efficient, but not very accommodating with regards to asking for a different room view.
Room was very nice and everything appeared brand new as they completely gutted their rooms and updated them with wood floors, nice walk-in shower, and very comfy beds.
Ordered room service and it was fine, nothing outstanding, but came very quickly and the server was very friendly.
Location is excellent- right across Union Square from Macy's and within walking distance to a ton of shops and restaurants.
My main issue was the fact that they've spend millions on renovating their rooms, a big, new lobby and restaurant, nice new tv's, but no HDTV signal in their guestroom!? C'mon, this is 2012- almost every decent hotel has HDTV signals broadcast. Might not be a big issue to some, but I enjoy watching sports and non-HDTV is almost enough to turn me away in the future.

title_masked: In the heart of the City by the Bay.
text_masked: Always feel a little hesitant staying in a huge urban hotel. But San Francisco is no typical city and this Marriott, even though it's huge, offered the services and personal amenities that made our stay comfortable and very personal. The room was in fine shape, had good lighting and spacious. The concierge staff provided great help with all our questions about transportation and sights to visit. Even the work out room and pool were pleasant and well maintained. For a mega hotel in a city, the Marriott was just right.

title_masked: If you like a noisy old style hotel
text_masked: Reception was friendly and cold at the same time. Elevators are slow and small , general apearence of hotel is used old and dirty. I would not advise business trbelers to use this hotel surely not if you want a restfull sleep you might be surprised by the garbage collectors who find it amusing while they are working infrint of hotel to shout and laugh very loud so the entire hotel would wake up. Note garbage collectors are infront of the hotel at 4h30 in the morning.

Excellent Hotel next to Macys and the Empire State Building, great location. You can walk to Times Square in 10 minutes too. Comfortable Beds, OK the rooms are quite small but have everything you need. I would definitely stay again.

We recently returned to the Barclay Intercontinental in NYC and as always Anmara Gayle from Guest Relations greeted us with a smile and presented us with the key to our room. She is very knowledgeable, attentive and has a warm personality. Leslie was also there to greet and welcome us as she always does when we arrive to the hotel. One pleasant surprise was that the old TV in our room had been replaced by a last model big screen HD set. Everyone was great from the porter and bellmen to the ladies from housekeeping that kept our room fresh and clean. We also love their restaurant/bar and they always take good care of us. Fernando was not there this time but Julio was and did an excellent job. This hotel has an excellent location and is close to 5th Avenue and the Theater District. We will continue to stay at the Barclay anytime we return to NYC; everyone there makes us feel at home.

title_masked: Charming boutique hotel in great location
text_masked:
Stayed in a suite with hubby & kids which was roomy. The decor was a mix of hip, contemporary & old world charm. The location was fantastic - within walking distance to Times Square & Rockefeller center. We were surprised at how quiet it was, considering the hotel is bordered by streets. Only downside to the room is no view, probably due to its lack of height. Room service value was ok - have had better at other NYC hotels. 
We had a terrific short getaway in NYC to which the Algonquin definitely contributed!

We have come to expect the best from this Company. This property, falls short in some areas.
The studio suite we stayed in with a queen size bed, was small. The placement of the bed, allowed access from only one side of the bed. If your by yourself, its no problem, but for 2 people, and being senior, one must crawl into bed from the other side. If a late night trip to the bathroom is needed, and not wake the other person, get ready to crawl out the front of the bed. Not a very good setup. The breakfast was ok.....something you would find at a days inn, not up to marriot standards, Only one elevator working the day we were leaving....being on a lower floor, elvator was always full to get to the lobby. Had to walk the stairs. Being handicapped did not help the situation. There is free wifi ok kitchen, and a ipod docking station.,, and the valet parking was great. Parking garage is a bit of challenge if you self park. I wrote management in response to their email on how i enjoyed the stay. They apoligized for the elevator, and said that if I called in advance, they would see if they could find a room with a bed that had access from both sides. Am I missing something ? I have never stayed in a room at these rates that was not big enough to accomodate walking room around the bed. I love the Marriot Brand, but it seems that this property must have belonged to some other company, and Marriot tried to raise it to their standards. I will always try to stay at a Marriot Property, but will start asking more questions by calling direct, rather than booking on line.

My husband and I, along with our 4 adult children, stayed at the Inn the end of August to attend my nephew's wedding in Baltimore. From start to finish, this was the best hotel I have ever stayed in. First, I really loved the green, eco-friendly commitment of the property. This results in a modern look with no rugs which took a minute to get used to, but once you realize how energy efficient the building is, I actually felt proud and excited to be supporting such an endeavor by staying there. If every building could be like this hotel, we'd definitely solve the world's energy crisis! 
 The beds were super comfortable so kudos to whoever picked out the mattresses, pillows, and linens. Made to order breakfasts were terrific. The neighborhood is really fun with lots of great restaurants and sites to see. 
 Apart from all of the above, what makes this hotel so incredible is the people who work there. I have never met a team of people so dedicated to making my stay so enjoyable--Alicia, Stephen, Dimitri, and Ryan are just some of the amazing people I came to know during my stay. Ryan, in particular, wins Hospitality Host of the Year. If that award doesn't exist, it should. A few examples--I needed to get to a store quickly to pick up something for the rehearsal dinner. When I went to the front desk to ask Ryan for directions, he told me that it was too far to walk so he had someone cover for him at the front desk, grabbed the hotel owner's car, and drove me himself. The next day, when a member of the wedding party became ill, Ryan jumped in, and along with Dimitri and Stephen, literally saved the wedding. Without their help, there is absolutely no way we could have gotten this family member to the ceremony. 
 Everything that everyone did for us that weekend is something that I will never, ever forget. Their kindness made an already special weekend even more memorable. If I am ever lucky enough to return to Baltimore, there is no place I will stay other than the Inn at the Black Olive.
Very comfortable and cllean. It was nice to have the refrigerator and microwave in the room. Very quiet at night even being next to PCH.

title_masked: InshAllah - Will never return to this Hotel
text_masked:
Arrived and checked into my room during my 2 day trip to Seattle. Reception dated and property very old. Customer service as expected is poor. I was asked to wait untill 3pm as the room wasnt ready. Rooms VERY basic and amenities below avarage. Restaurant mediocre and breakfast is awful !
Paid USD 200 per night but its definitely not even worth this amount. Its a fit for purpose site especially if one is going to drop to Hotel only to sleep and has to shell out no more than USD 100 -150 a night.

We were welcomed with a glass of fizz and a cheery smile and so continued the high quality service we received at the River Inn. We sipped a glass of champagne overlooking the Mississippi River and dined in the French restaurant, Paulette's. The food was excellent. Breakfasts were delicious and certainly set us all up for the day. The bedrooms were charming, with chocolates and port supplied each evening. I would absolutely recommend this hotel.

Normally this would have been an excellent stay, however, when paying with more than one form of payment, they don't know how to do it. I was charged twice and they refused to credit my card back until they "secured payment" from another person for the room because "the room was occupied". I authorized one amount and signed for it, however, they charged me for someone elses room fee also. Good customer service would be to correct they error on their part and then worry about contacting the correct person. Extremely disappointed... they seem to care more about their money then correcting their mistake. Would not recommend this hotel to anyone traveling in a group that wishes to use more than one form of payment. When they did "secure payment" from the other person in the room, I still had to wait for my money to be returned to me! BAD CUSTOMER SERVICE!!!!

title_masked: Not What It Used To Be
text_masked: I have family in Philly and have been staying at the Sofitel in Philadelphia for at least 9 years. It used to be a great hotel but over the past 2 years it has gone downhill. The bathrooms need to be renovated. The shower in my Junior Suite looked like it hadn't been cleaned in a year. It smelled of mildew and what appeared to be the soap dish was just corroded with scum. Where the shower meets the floor on the outside of the shower was moldy and the floors in general need to be replaced. The wallpaper over the tub was peeling. The sofa in the living room is the same sofa that's been there since I started staying at this hotel in 2003! Sofitel has redone their lobby and bar at least twice since I've staying there probably because they do a lot of business with weddings and the bar. Chez Collette, the hotel restaurant, has been open and closed several times. I've stayed at the Palomar across the street and although the rooms are smaller at least they are updated and appear clean. I love the Sofitel but I probably won't go back unless they give me a deal or renovate the rooms.

title_masked: little hesitant at first - but great property
text_masked: I'm a long time fan of the IC Barclay on the eastside of Park Ave, so when this hotel opened two years ago, I was hesitant to stay there. It's smaller - much smaller, although taller, much taller. But the front desk staff and bellmen were OUTSTANDING. We tried out two rooms for this stay. The first was an executive king and was larger than the corner king we had the second night. I love a wall of windows, but the executive was nicer. There isn't, however, that impressive feel that you're at an intercontinental. It's very Westin-like, which is sad because i can get that next door at the Westin Times Square. The views are outstanding. The details done right. We'll be back because of the location - just far enough from Times Square (it's close, not on Times Square) that it's not noisy, gritty or dirty, yet close enough to hit the theatres - they're right there. There was a wonderful street fair on 8th ave the Sunday we were there. good and bad: Beds are uncomfortable, rain showers, and the internet costly. The concierge helped with theatre tickets, but the bar closed really early.

Chose this hotel because of the central location, and in that respect it didn't disappoint. However, the room was excessively small! We don't usually mind small rooms, but when there is absolutely no storage space for the bags of 2 trans-Atlantic travellers, that I find unacceptable; there was literally no space to store bags without climbing over them. Other than that, cleanliness was good although the decor was showing signs of wear and tear in places. Breakfast was fine and wi-fi excellent. Contrary to other posts, the rooms in this hotel are not bigger than those in Europe; of note, we stayed in another 7 hotels during our road-trip, and every room was at least twice the size, and I'm not exaggerating! In sum, helpful staff, great location, clean but tiny room and a little expensive! Recommend it? Maybe, but travel light!

title_masked: One of the Finest Hotels in Boston....
text_masked: This is a great hotel located in Waterfront Section of Boston (South Boston). As soon as you are greeted by the bellman you know service is a emphasized. Hotel rooms are first class. This section of the city has some great places to eat, including one of the best sports bars Jeremy Remmy’s, Steak Houses, Mexican and two Legal Seafood facilities close by. You have all of the choices you need within walking distance. Great Hotel, Great Value…

title_masked: Terrible value and not worth the stay
text_masked: Was advised by a friend to stay there because of the location and to pay extra for balcony view. What a disappointed and waste of vacation dollars! Business class is supposed to be able to check in early and they claimed there was nothing available when we arrived--yet we stayed for three days and saw no one in the other balcony rooms. They gave us a lower level room and we couldn't see anything and requested a room move to upper balcony room. Still can't see anything sitting in a chair, the balcony views are blocked. One evening we requested a wake-up call to go on a wine tour the next morning--never came & we woke-up an hour late and not able to eat breakfast before our tour. The rooms are small and the hotel needs serious updating. My husband and I travel frequently and went to New York and paid way less for a NICE hotel there. This was the biggest disappointment I have ever had on a hotel. I would not recommend, there is much nicer than this in San Francisco at a better value.

I stayed at the Grand Hyatt San Francisco for one night while traveling on business. The lobby area was going through a renovation during my stay (July 2012). Hotel is perfectly located very near Union Square. Valet parking is very expensive, but this is San Francisco. Staff was quite friendly. Club Lounge on 32nd floor is spacious and has great views. Rooms are recently upadated and very modern. The view from my room was amazing! This hotel is a definite recommendation if within your budget.

title_masked: Great Hotel with an Outstanding Location
text_masked:
Arrived in San Antonio in the middle of my four city Texas trip and this hotel was excellent.
LOCATION
The location of this hotel is right in the middle of downtown San Antonio, which is the perfect spot for the two main attractions of the Alamo and Riverwalk. Drove right up to the front door and had valet take the car. The valet cost $23 per day, but this was not bad for a couple of reasons. First, the hotel is in walking distance of the main attractions so a car is not needed and secondly, the price is comparable to other parking lots in the area for people driving to the attractions, yet not as close as the hotel. Now there are some reviews saying that the Alamo is 3-4 blocks away from the hotel. This may be true in "San Antonio" blocks, but being from NY my definition of the word "blocks" is different. The Alamo is about a 5 minute walk equal to about 1 1/2 NYC blocks. The San Antonio blocks are so short that I anticipated the walk to be much longer. A nice short walk to the historic area.
An entrance to the Riverwalk is about 150 feet away from the hotel. Perfect since you could do what you needed to do at the Riverwalk and be right at your hotel when done. There are a few shops in the area and a 2 minute walk to a nice sports bar where we watched Italy defeat Germany in the Euro Cup. The area of the hotel is very clean and very safe. After drinking at the bars at the Riverwalk until closing time (2am), we decided to take a stroll to see the Alamo at night. Very peaceful as the Alamo is guarded by armed officers 24 hours a day. Just to be in the front of the Alamo in the quiet of night is very special. 
ROOM, PRICE, CLEANLINESS and COMFORT
The price of the room was about $160, but we got the biggest suite they have. The room design was a bit awkward, but I was only sleeping there, not buying the unit. You walk in and there was the bathroom to the immediate left and the kitchen setup to the right. Had a microwave, sink, fridge (all new all stainless steel), but no stove/oven. After passing the kitchen it opened up into a HUGE room. The only problem is the beds are all in the open area. There is no separate sleeping quarters. The open space had a desk, chair and flatscreen TV that the people on the couch could see and then a random piece of wall that had a flat screen for the two beds to see. Everyone was in the same room and when both TV's are on you can hear each others shows. Don't know the purpose since you could see both TV's from one of the beds. 
The couch turned into a bed which was one of the more comfortable pull out beds. The regular queen beds were very comfortable and provided a great sleep. The A/C worked good, but since the beds were all the way over on the far side of the room, it seemed like the coldest area was the kitchen and desk areas because there were not any blowers near the beds. The second you check in, put the A/C on the coldest you can so the room can have the cold air move toward the beds. Remember, the bed area is much warmer than the open area. Don't be fooled. There was a window in the room but our view seemed to be a non usable enclosed hallway. Another design flaw. 
The bathroom was very clean and interesting. There were not bathroom bars of soap (you have to bring it if you want it), but soap dispensers on the wall of the shower. Liquid body soap and shampoo. I actually liked this idea and thought it was pretty cool. Since I was not sure how to work it, I nearly broke one of the things trying to get the soap out. Eventually, my college degree came in handy and I figured out how to use it. I think it is much better using the gel instead of using the same bar of soap that everyone in your suite will roll over their dirty bodies. The rest of the suite was perfectly clean...no issues at all.
BREAKFAST and OTHER AMENITIES
The lobby had some sort of 24 hour soda/juice kinda thing but to be honest I really didn't listen when they were telling me so I am not sure what it was. Since this was the ONLY day on my trip I was able to sleep late, I am unable to tell you about the breakfast which they do have and did sound good from other reviews. The lobby is very open and has computers, couches, bathrooms, front desk, ATM etc. all in one big area. Access to the hotel after a certain hour was by card key only so that is good to keep anyone from coming in off the streets to use the bathroom. 
I would not hesitate to use this hotel again if going back to San Antonio. Easiest location to get around, plenty of action, and plenty of good places to go.

title_masked: Nice but needs to iron out some kinks
text_masked: This hotel is brand new and is very nice and clean. The property itself is great. Clean, good layout, very inviting, etc. I won't go so far as to say that the staff sucked, because they were all nice, but none of them were very good at their jobs. Service at the bar/restaurant was so slow, particuarly for the fact that it wan't very busy. Nobody seemed to know when/if the restaurant would be open. I felt like I wanted to like the place, but it was hard to at times. The pool was closed for maintenance or something, our refrigerator in our room didn't work, etc. I guess I would give the place another shot because it is very new/clean, when the pool opened it was nice, the workout room is nice, the restaurant/bar outside of the service was good, parking was convenient, etc. In sum, a nice hotel that needs to get it's "stuff" together.

Very pleased, we arrived late at night and the reception was great. Very friendly people, even at that time Mat help us to get a city tour for the next day. Good location. We had a studio with a queen bed, clean and comfortable. The continental breakfast was even more than we expected. Thank you Mrs [NAME] (Assistant General Manager), Ian, Mat and the very gentle man we met upon our arrival. Monic B. Canada

The front desk staff was very nice, our room was lovely with views out all sides. We were upgraded to a junior suite, no complaints here :) Only issue was that parking was $47/night, pretty steep. The room had a comfy couch and chairs. My daughter loved the reading lights in the headboard on the bed.

The Four Seasons is all about service. Our recent stay was no exception. The location is perfect and puts you in the middle of things. The Bart station is convenient to the hotel and makes the entire city accessible. The rooms are very comfortable and have all the amenities. I would highly recommend this hotel.

The room was very clean, it had a decent amount of space, and the double beds were very comfortable. The one inconvenience was that the front door and bathroom door were adjacent and therefore made for an awkward exit. After going out in the city, it was the perfect place to crash. It was a great central location and we felt very safe returning at night.

We ended up getting the Palace at a really cheap rate through expedia and were stoked I guess this was due to a refurb happening at the time as the whole courtyard looked like a construction site which was a shame. However this did not impact our stay and we enjoyed our time at the Palace. 
We had a standard room and it was sufficient for us the rooms were clean the staff were also very friendly.
We had a few small problems, we found was that it was a little out of the with regards to the Subway and getting to where we wanted to go. We also found there was a lack of fast food options available and mainly just upscale restaurants in the area so to get a feed we had to plan when we were out & about to grab something before we returned. We were also disappointed that Wi-Fi is not included which we found included at Park Hyatts & Fairmont's across our journey through the US.
I would stay at the Palace again if the price was right but I have stayed in better value properties that include wi-fi & breakfast etc that were just as clean but maybe not as elegant in NYC for a cheaper rate than what is usually available at the Palace.

title_masked: Terrific Hotel in a Terrific Location
text_masked:
If you're looking for a hotel near the convention center, this is a solid choice. It is conveniently located within walking distance from local shops, bars, and restaurants. The pool and other facilities are elegant, the property is extremely clean and well taken care of, and the view from the rooms really adds to the experience. Staff are friendly and extremely helpful. Be sure to take advantage of the knowledgeable concierge staff. The bar is also solid and offers nice appetizers. 
Drawbacks: room service is WAY too expensive compared to hotels in it's class and the quality doesn't live up to the hotel's performance in other areas. I'd advise you to take a short walk to one of the many restaurants nearby. Valet is pricey, and not necessary - there's a parking lot directly across the street.

I stayed here one night on business. I was pleasantly surprised. The hotel appears fairly new. It is located in an undeveloped business park next to a Hilton Garden Inn; there is absolutely nothing within walking distance. The Hilton Garden Inn has a full service restaurant, however.
The staff was friendly and the rooms very modern. I liked the walkin shower with one of the best showerheads I have seen in a long time. The internet is free and is cable. Flat screen TV. Bed was very comfortable with great pillow variation. 
IT is located near the airport and I started to hear planes land about 3 AM. 
Breakfast was just average or below.

Our family stayed 3 nights at the Pearl in New York City in August 2012. The hotel is situated very close to the heart of the city with most venues withing walking distance. The Hotel was very clean and the staff was very attentive and helpful.
We had 2 rooms, one with a terrace. The rooms were very clean and remodelled. We didn't spend a lot of time in the rooms, but the Terrace was quite spacoius and provided a spot to unwind for a bit and enjoy the sounds of New York. The Terrace rooms were only on the 10th floor, so they didn't provide a "birds eye view" of the city. However, it still did provide a confinced view of New York. The rooms were very quiet and you barely heard a sound from the hallways, although there did seem to be a "low hum" in the Terrace room at night from the street .... but nothing that should keep you up at night. 
The room had a nice alcove that had a sink, small fridge and even a microwave. The bathrooms were updated and clean although some what small. 
Although the rooms are somewhat on the higher end of the price range, overall, the Pearl was a very nice hotel to stay at especially if you are a traveller who expects clean, comfortable and updated accomodations.

Satyed here for NYE festivities in DC. The room was bigger and nicer than I was expecting for a standard room. I loved the decor in the room and in the lobby. The location is great - in Chinatown, near Verizon center and great restaurants. Breakfast was included in the price, making it an even better value, but I wasn't up early enough to enjoy it.

My wife and I stayed at the Lenox the week before this year's marathon. We quickly saw Boston transformed in preparation for the big race. The Lenox really is a great hotel in an outstanding location. The Prudential Mall is half a block a way, Atlantic Fish Co is nearly across the road, Copley Square and Newberry Street are one block away and the Copley train station means the rest of Boston is readily accessible. One of the real bonuses of the location was the proximity of Marshall's to the hotel. As keen shoppers we found this store a treasure trove of bargains and will definitely visit the next time we are in Boston. We only discovered it by accident and it should be as famous as New York's Century 21 store. Marshall's is similar but neater, organsied and cheaper.

title_masked: Service was excellent, great location and one of the few hotels that offers free breakfast!
text_masked: We stayed at this hotel for 3 nights for a long weekend getaway in New York. The location of the hotel was great - one minute walk to Times Square. Make sure you book a Deluxe room or above, as we booked a Standard Queen and the room was really small. When we asked the manager if we could change rooms, we got a free upgrade to a Deluxe room which was much more spacious! We were very grateful for this. The service was prompt and the newly renovated hotel is very appealing. One of the few hotels in NYC that offers free continental breakfast with your booking.

We just finished a 3-night stay at the Westin Copley. We were visiting my daughter who attends Boston University. Everything is very close via the subway, or a short walk. 
We had arrived at 4 am due to an airline delay and the only room available at that late hour was a double queen (we had requested a king). The next morning the management had contacted us with apologies and upgraded us for the balance of the stay to a spectacular 1-bedroon suite with a large living area that had two walls of glass windows overlooking the Charles River - the perfect setting for visiting with family members. ( I can tell you that the same thing happened to me at the JW Marriott at LA Live, arriving at 11pm, and despite complaints to management, all I got was a rude, "you can try some other hotel if you like")
In reference to someone's complaint that this property is in need of refurb, it just ain't so. Everything was on the newer side, nothing was worn or broken, and the hotel was extremely clean, inclluding the lobby, elevators, hallways and rooms.
The Westin Copley rates amongst my favorite Starwood properties - and Starwood properties are by far my favorite hotels across the globe.

I don't get to NYC often enough, but the last several times I've stayed at The Benjamin and it's always so easy. The staff bend over backwards to be helpful. The concierge got us tickets for The Book of Mormon ahead of time and although expensive, it was nice to have it taken care of so we didn't need to worry about it during our short hectic visit. The location is wonderful and the neighborhood is good. It feels safe and there are a number of decent restaurants near by if you don't want to go too far. It's about a 20 minute walk to the theater district and various museums and shopping are all within that distance. The subway is also very close.
We arrived late on a Sunday night, so we ordered a fruit bowl for the next morning. One of the nice things about the Donatello is the little kitchenette, so you can have a simple breakfast in your room if you want to. However, the fruit bowl was expensive and not very good. After that, we bought our own fruit (there's a street vendor during the day right across Lexington). They also charge a lot for WiFi access in your room which always annoys me. My friend and her daughter shared the king sized bed and I used the pull out bed in the sitting room which wasn't real comfortable, but I did manage to find a decent spot on it and the special pillows were nice. This hotel is definitely a fair deal for the cost.

title_masked: Recently upgraded to a very nice hotel
text_masked: Stayed here for a business trip after being away from El Paso for 18 months. Since last time, the lobby has been nicely upgraded to a beautiful lounge with several TV's and greatly improved. My room was also remodeled with an HD TV and upgraded bedding and new carpeting. A much nicer hotel now with free airport shuttles on demand and computers in the lobby. Even though I am only Marriott Silver, they gave me free access to the concierge lounge, a perk normally given to Gold and above.

We just returned from a 4 night stay at The Wall Street Inn. The room was nice, clean and comfortable. The bathroom was a bit small and didn't have much room to set things down or get ready. The bed and linens were clean and comfortable. Cleaning was done quickly in the morning as to never disrupt your stay. Breakfast was small but complete w/toast , bagels, pastries and fruit. The breakfast room was small as stated before however there is another dining room right next door that is more than large enough. The hotel is very convenient to everything IE. ferry, subway and sights. The only complaint we had was as noted before the front desk staff (especially at night) is very unwelcoming. I actually heard a guest ask the desk how to get to SOHO and their reply was "I don't know what SOHO is." WOW! Aside from that issue I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone

We were in Washington DC for 8 days and stayed at this hotel. The first day they put us in a room next to an elevator. I went back downstairs and asked for another room. This room was a handicap room and we could not hang our cloths because the closet for three feet high. They finally gave us another room which worked. Four times during the stay we had to go back to the counter because our room key did not work. The elevators are slow and you have to complete with the whole staff to use the elevator. Now the go part, there are dogs everywhere. I like dogs, but who brings their dog on vacation with them? They charge for wi-fi so everyone goes to the lobby for free connection. The furniture in the lobby is something out of a quick buying trip to the salvation army store. The best thing is just stay away from this hotel and use the Hyatt across the street.

title_masked: The Best Hotel we stayed at
text_masked: This is not a hotel, it is a small apartment. Every room is a suite and yes it is worth it. Our last night was blissful thanks to Homewood Suites. It was nice to lay in bed and watch my show while he was able to shut the bedroom door sit on the couch and get caught up on his shows. Yes vacations are meant to be spent together, but after 6 days anybody would need a little me time.
Great staff and very convenient location. The rooms are comforable and clean and the breakfast is quality. Internal courtyard by pool is a great place to relax and enjoy friends and family.

For years the Empire Hotel, across the street from Lincoln Center, was a seedy, rundown venue. In those days, it deserved the comment I once heard from American composer Morton Gould: "I don't mind the cockroaches, I just wish they wouldn't charge you double occupancy for them." But the hotel closed for a few years, was rumored to be converted to condominiums when the real estate bust hit, and it was eventually taken over by the World Hotels chain and completely renovated. It is now clean, elegantly appointed, and continues to benefit from being across the street from Lincoln Center.
Unfortunately, the renovation did not include re-building the rooms. They are tiny, as are the bathrooms - where there is barely enough room to change your mind. The poorly designed shower makes it impossible to test the water temperature before being subjected to it -- unless you are a contortionist. You must stand under it to turn it on. The shower also has only a half-door, so you must get the bathroom floor wet. But, on the positive side, for its small size the bathroom has very good shelf space for your toiletries and medicines.
There is no easy-chair in the room (no space for it) - a bed, desk and desk chair, and a few feet of floor space to navigate your way around. This would be acceptable, perhaps, if the price weren't so high - I paid $399 for a room there recently.
If you're willing to pay the price, and need to be close to Lincoln Center, then it is acceptable. The service is very good, the folks are nice and efficient, and, as I said, it is clean and elegant.

Stayed at this hotel from June 7, 2012 thru June 10, 2012. This is a very nice place with an excellent staff. They really go out of their way to ensure that you feel welcomed and comfortable. I met some really nice people here...just like family. If I am in the Charlotte, NC area again, I will definately stay here again!! I will also recommend this hotel to family and friends.

title_masked: Nice comfortable and friendly place to stay
text_masked:
We came here for two nights prior to the beginning of a Texas Hill Country bike tour, and then returned for one final night following the tour. Location is excellent -- right downtown and adjacent to the bridge where the bats come out at around 7:30 (we didn't see them). Stores and shops were convenient, and we began our walking tour to the state capitol building easily from the hotel -- not a far walk. Pleasant stroll down Congress Avenue. 
We were met at the door by friendly doormen who helped carry our heavy bags (include our bike cases) into the lobby. We were then greeted by the very friendly desk rep who quickly checked us in. Room was very nice and everything was provided that we needed. Clean bathroom, with exterior vanity area from the main bath, extra shower amenities and hair dryer etc. Bed was comfortable too. They have a couple of restaurants, including TGI Fridays and Starbucks, located offside their lobby, and we had their buffet breakfast in the mornings. While our freshly-cooked omelet was excellent, other members of our group said the cook burned theirs the first time and had to redo them. But we were very satisfied, and the options for the breakfast were more than sufficient to get us started on our bike tour. 
All in all a very pleasant stay with exceptionally helpful and friendly concierge and service staff.

title_masked: It was by definition a "boutique hotel"
text_masked: It was by definition a "boutique hotel" so yes it was small, but definitly worked for the 4 nights we (2 people) were there. This hotel was right in the middle of downtown and right around the corner from tons of nightlife (bars, clubs) and great resturants. The nightclub that is attached to the club gets noisy at night, and even the staff says is overpriced.

title_masked: Not a fairy tale - dust and more dust - Asthmatics beware!
text_masked:
Perfect location - but that's it ! It was as if the room had been cleaned once upon a time and then closed up and left for dust to take over. 
The curtain pelmet in both the the living and bedroom area was so dusty if you beat your hands against there was a cloud of dust which when settled you could clearly see your hand print. The cords from which the light fitting hung looked as if it had developed some form of hairy growth. I wrote The word dust on the base of the light fitting and photographed it. along with other evidence throughout the suite. In some instances the dust had turned sticky to the touch.. The overall condition of the suite was dust dust and more dust and as an asthmatic I was not happy!. I had difficulty getting the attention of management, after two calls and then a personal trip to the front desk. Management did not bother to visit our suite to investigate, I can only assume what I was saying they knew to be true, or they were not really interested. They did schedule a" special clean up team" for the following day ...
For a establishment that charges what they do, we were unimpressed, not only by the condition of the room but the lethargic response to our very valid complaint. We wont be back and I suggest anyone who is asthmatic beware!

I won this hotel through a Priceline auction for a very decent price, considering I stayed there on a Saturday night. Though I requested 2 double beds, we were given a room with 1 queen upon arrival. The room was very nicely appointed with a modern feel, although for a higher end hotel, I was expecting more. 
 PROS: 
-Decent location in the downtown area
-Connected to a Whole Foods store for breakfast and snacks
-Free internet usage
-Nicely decorated with decent linens
CONS: 
-Valet parking was about $40 per night, which I thought was high. 
-Shower needed better cleaning, particularly on the grout
-Bed could have been a bit more comfortable
-Showerhead wasn't as powerful as I thought it would be...possibly clogged with mineral deposits?
Was it worth what I paid for it? Yes, probably so. It is in no way comparable to some of the other luxury hotels out there though.

Stayed here last weekend in June, nice rooms, large in size. Gym was good, with lots of cardio machines. The only negative was that there are 3 elevators, but apparently it isn't sufficient enough (seemed like only 1 was working the entire visit). location is in close proximity to Market St and Union Square. Friendly cleaning staff. Overall very good.

When the receptionist heard we had come from NZ and were staying 5 nights she kindly gave us an upgrade which was excellent. It is a lovely old building decorated beautifully. The room had lots of seating and an extremely comfortable bed. A coffee machine with decaf pottles! Walking distance to Magnificent Mile and all the shops. The concierge was very helpful and all the staff were very friendly. The restaurant attached had a modern menu and reasonably priced. I know this sounds trivial but the shower controls were easy to use, some hotel showers are tiresome!

My Partner and i just got back from a weekend in new york in the Helmsley Park Lane Hotel. Our room was very clean and roomy, the decor was a bit dated but still very smart, the bed was especially comfortable and cleaners came everyday. I would recommend that if you go to breakfast you should go before 9am as we had to queue up and wait for a table but the food was very nice. The location was good there was a bus stop right outside aswell which was very handy. We was a bit annoyed that reception tried to charge us for taking some items from the minibar when we didnt have anything but when we confronted them they took it off the bill without any questions. Overall a very nice hotel i was made very comfortable.

Clean, spacious and luxurious television in lounge and bedroom areas. Plenty of storage areas and comfortable beds. Room service was quick. Being in the centre of town the free shuttle runs down 16th avenue to great shopping and restaurants.
The hotel is in a very nice location and we found the staff very helpful and friendly. The rooms are very small but clean and well equipped.

title_masked: Family of four out on the town
text_masked:
We arrived a few hours before check in and Raj was able to have a room readied for us within 30 minutes. He could have made us wait as some hotels would have but he went above and beyond to accommodate us.We found the hotel staff to be very attentive to our needs. The rooms are very clean however a little small. The location is a bit farther from the national mall than i had hoped for. The breakfast is very good with a nice selection. The staff namely, Kimberly (food service), Raj (front desk) and housekeeping crew are extremely helpful and available to you. i would not hesitate to stay here again and definitively recommend this hotel.
one other note: we were supposed to have two tickets to the spy museum included with our stay but never received them. I didn't even think about it until on the plane headed home.

The Hotel employees are very gentle and kind! Thanks to the chambermaid and the attendant called [NAME] who helped us to get back some forgotten items. The whole family liked the Hotel very much, specially the kids!

We stayed for 4 nights in the two bedroom suite and it was good. Clean, quiet,15 minute walk to Times Square, 10 min to Empire State. It's a bit old, the fixtures and furniture are aging but it was good and probably good value for a suite with two bedrooms in Midtown Manhattan.
The doors do self close and although we didn't hear them because the bedrooms are remote from the suite's main door, my guess is that if you're in a single you could be disturbed by the noise.

My wife and I just got back from a 3 night stay at the "W" Westwood and the "W" never disappoints. We were upgraded to a suite and the room was simply amazing! And that was just the beginning... From the Front Desk, Concierge, even the room service staff, they could not have been any more accommodating and helpful. They always went above and beyond to make sure our stay was nothing short of spectacular... Would Highly recommend the W Westwood as "THE PLACE TO STAY"! The location is fantastic if you do not want to be right in the center of the LA Hustling scene, but close to it!!

Much to recommend this hotel - great location, pleasant bar, quiet rooms - but too many problems. 
Bathroom was pretty much open, toilet had a glass door which gave little privacy. No tub and shower had no curtain, so much water ended up outside the shower. The room was small but adequate. Parking very expensive. Took over an hour to get our luggage brought up, and then only after I called. Definitely not a four star hotel.
This hotel is convenient to the airport, Light Rail and most Phoenix tourist spots. The staff was friendly and efficient and the breakfast buffet was above average with wide variety.

title_masked: High price, lots of flash--lacks a lot.
text_masked:
I was surprised at the level of ineptitude exuded by the staff at this location. Sadly, that’s only one of the many problems at this hotel. Check-in was the first stumbling block during our stay.
There were four of us, and we booked one room with two queen beds. Our reservation clearly stated the number of people we had in our party and that we had reserved a room with two queen beds. While the gentleman at the reception desk was very kind, he was not tuned into his job. It seems that he glazed over the details of our reservation.
After getting our keys, we waited at the elevator bays for a good chunk of time for one of the five elevators to make its way to the lobby. Once we boarded the car we stopped on every floor, all the way up to the 24th floor, and that was the case during our entire stay. While it is understood that the hotel employees cannot control elevator traffic, there is definitely a bottleneck in traffic when it comes to using the lifts. If you stay here be prepared to spend 10-15 minutes waiting for, and riding on, the elevators. 
When we finally got to our room, it only had one king bed. There wasn’t a pull out sofa, either. I called down to the folks at the reception desk to advise them of the issue, and the person that I spoke to didn’t understand what the issue was. I explained to her that we had reserved a room with two queen beds, but the room that we were given only had one king bed, and we were four people. The logistics were going to work. She still didn’t understand. After a few times of explaining what the issue was to the woman on the phone, she then asked me, “So…you want another room?” Finally, she got it.
When we made the 10 minute journey back to the lobby, we were told that there were no rooms with two queen beds available. Given that I had reserved and prepaid for a room with two queen beds, I was a little put out by this new information. How is it that a hotel will “book” a room for you, take your money, and then not have the room for you when you arrive? Not a good way to get repeat guests, that’s for sure. 
The hotel’s solution to our issue was to either, go to another hotel, or rent a second room from them at the discounted rate of $399.00 per night. At that point, it was all I could do to keep my cool. After we had already paid over $500.00 for a room with two queen beds, we arrive at the hotel to find not only do we not have the room that we reserved, but now it was going to cost us an additional $400.00+ because of the hotel’s error—how convenient. Considering our prepaid room was non-refundable it was going to cost us just as much to stay at another hotel than it would have been to stay at the Grand Hyatt, so reluctantly, we took the second room.
