It was a rock and a hard place situation, for sure.
After wasting an hour dealing with the room debacle, we were told that the second room would not be ready until 4:00 PM—another strike for the Hyatt. Completely perturbed at the situation, we returned to the room on the 24th floor to freshen up and make the best of the rest of the day.
When we returned to the hotel that evening, it became apparent that this location placed all of its cash into flash and glam and in doing so missed a great deal of the creature comforts that most hotels have. 
First and foremost, we did not have a coffee maker in our room. I have stayed at hotels that were less than $100.00 a night, and there was a coffee maker in the room. 
To add to our experience, the water temperature was not stable. When showering or washing ones hands, the water would fluctuate from cold to near scalding. The bed linens were worn, and the pillows were very small. They were almost akin to European throw pillows. They were not pillows that belonged on a queen or king bed.
Lastly our rooms did not have alarm clocks or radios. Again, someone that should be a given at a hotel like the Hyatt. Everything considered our stay was very underwhelming. While this hotel is conveniently located, there are many other hotels in NYC that have rooms at similar prices, have better amenities and better skilled staff.

title_masked: Mold in bathroom, blood stain on pillow
text_masked: Wow, Hotel Carter was so trashy all we could do was laugh about it. We get in the room, it is TINY. There is a chair in the corner of the room that you have to squeeze between it and the bed to get to the bathroom. No remote for the TV. Mold all over the bathroom wall. We found a blood stain on the pillow case and it had soaked through to the pillow, so who knows what was up with that. It was scary. Oh and when we told them about it they said, "Oh I'm sorry, here is a new fluffy pillow." We stayed for 4 nights, and the cleaning person came in only once during our stay, and the only thing they did was make our bed. We had to go down to the front desk ourselves to get clean towels. There were no wash cloths, just towels. We also had to go down there to get toilet paper. We had to just bag up our trash and set it in the hallway, which seemed to be the popular thing to do because we saw bags of trash outside of other people's rooms too. Also, I have never been to a hotel where they make you pay to hold your bags until your check in time. $2 dollars per bag. I know it isn't too much, but still that is normally something that is complimentary. Also, the window was stuck open and it was like 40 degrees out, but the heater was on full blast so the temperature was comfortable but it was just weird. The curtains were right over these old school looking heaters and it looked like the place could catch on fire at any minute. But it was right by Time Square which was cool. Perfect location, Good old Hotel Carter. It is cheap and trashy, but who goes to NYC to stay in their hotel the whole time....no one. So if you just don't mind a little mold, bloody pillows, and having to go get your own towels and take out your own trash, then Hotel Carter is the place for you!

We stayed at this hotel from 8/2-8/6 for a college showcase soccer tournament . The hotel was located approx. 5-10 minutes from the soccer complex and right off I-70. The hotel staff was one of the finest that i have ever encountered. The most enjoyable group of staff had to be by far the breakfast staff lead by Mama. You were always greeted with a big smile and how are you today !!! If i am ever close to Denver again I would for sure stay at this hotel! EXCELLENT STAFF AND PERSONNEL!!!!! 5 Star all the way!!!!

title_masked: Terrific and large room, fastest room service ever and overall great statt
text_masked: After reading the mixed review of this property, I was a bit uneasy. But after staying - I'm a fan. I was booked into a Deluxe Room in the newer section and the room was quite nice. Very large room with a very large bathroom. While every room details wasn't what I'd consider 5-star, the overall feel, quality and comforts were - and it was an outstanding stay. Perhaps the most amazing part of my stay was room service - it was lightening fast. I've never experienced such speedy and quality room service. Even on a night when they were swamped and I was told 45-minutes, it was less than 30 and most meals were about 15 or 20 minutes max. The public space was nice and the front-desk staff as well as housekeeping were terrific Love the location and having stayed at a lot of San Francisco hotels, I'd happily return to the Westin St. Francis.

My husband and I just returned from our trip to Southern CA and one of our stops was San Diego. The Palomar Hotel was a wonderful choice--the location was perfect for us; it was at the top of the Gaslamp District, which is full of great restaurants and entertainment (also very close to public transportation). The accomodations were top quality with granite countertops, plush bedding, dark wood floors, and stainless steel features. The pool and rooftop bar were very nice and not too crowded. The best part of our stay, though, had to be the service. Johnson and Michael (along with every other staff member we came in contact with) gave us the utmost care and always offered to help with making a dinner reservation or reserving the Hotel shuttle to take us to our destination if it was not walkable. Michael, the Concierge, gave us wonderful advice on what areas of town we should visit and good places to eat. I can't speak highly enough of this hotel--choose Palomar San Diego and you won't regret it!

We travel a lot and it has been a long time since we had this poor accommodations. We usually pick a Comfort Inn or another Choice hotel when we just need an overnight enroute to our destination. Just somewhere to get a nights rest and be on our way again. This one was not clean, had a bad smell, thin walls, dirty chairs, dirty carpet, sink and tub that didn't drain, and wallpaper was peeling. Oh, and the shower handle pulled so hard that I could not get the water turned on. When we arrived my husband found the toilet tank had no water in it, so he took the tank lid off to investigate only to have water spray all over him and the bathroom. There was only one hand towel and we needed that to wipe up the floor. I had to go to the desk to request more towels. I guess I would give them one good thing...our room was on the first floor with parking in front so it was convenient. The breakfast was standard fair, except the decaf coffee was just slightly colored hot water and the eggs and gravy were not out yet when we were there. My recommendation, go down the street to the next Comfort Inn that looked newer.

title_masked: Good Hotel but needs to learn from its Mistakes!!!
text_masked:
We stayed in the Liaison for 3 nights in Nov 2012, having read some of the reviews i can see there are some recurring problems and Management really needs to learn from this!!
The Good
Large comfortable room with 2 very nice queen beds, 
Very clean and well maintained
Public areas very clean and well maintained,
Lift more than adequate.
Nice little shop (not well advertised) which is open late if you have munchies.
Staff very friendly and helpful (apart from 1 doorman see below for details which unfortunately means the service rating was poor)
The bad 
Wireless in this standard of hotel should be free throughout, Charging for it seems like a really daft thing to do as it means the lobby is always crowded with people making it seem very small and disorganised. 
No hotel should produce a check out report at 3.30 am unless the customer is checking out at 3.30 am. They do this for speedy check out however it made check out a lot slower as we had to add extra bits on to it, it also looks on the bill like the amount has been taken already without permission (even though they assured us it hadnt!!! ) i havent checked my credit card bill yet!!!
The ugly
Breakfast included should mean breakfast included. Breakfast included should not mean up to the value of $50.00 per room and oh by the way its between $15 to $20 per person for a decent breakfast so you will have to pay extra if you want both coffee and orange, oh and by the way you have to pay extra for tax. 
DO NOT use the door man to get a taxi for you. We requested a taxi from the door man and even though there were 2 waiting outside he waved them on and waved an old taxi over ( we have since realised this was probably a friend of his). We were only going to union station (5 min walk) but as we had 5 bags we decided the best thing was a taxi. We asked the door man what he thought the cost would be (we have been burnt by not asking before) and he advised not very much at all. When we got to the station the meter stated $5.50 (quite reasonable we thought) however the driver insisted we pay an extra $5.00 as we had 5 bags ($1.00 per bag). We didnt have time to argue as we were late for our train. We asked in the station and were advised that this was not standard policy in DC. We then asked another door man when we were in New York and were told that they had never heard of that policy in any state. As you can imagine this left a very bitter taste our mouth.
I would consider staying in this hotel again as the location was perfect but i would also look at others in this area as it was not perfect by any means.

The rooms in this hotel are very comfortable. Beds are comfy. There is a good size desk and a chaise lounge type chair. The bathroom has a walk in shower. The bathroom floor can be heated which is a nice touch.
The location is excellent. The hotel is a block away from the Dupont Circle metro stop. It's across the street from an independent bookstore, Kramer Books. Lots of restaurants nearby and shopping, too. 
The bar was busy and noisy but no problem with noise on the third floor.

While the Four Seasons was generally a nice property, as to be expected, it lacked any real character and was WELL overpriced for what it offered.
Our initial room wasn't cleaned and so we had to return to the lobby and wait for another. While I'm not usually too picky about this type of thing, we didn't appreciate the condescending attitude of the front desk when we brought up the issue.
When we checked-out, there were several charges added to our bill (movies, I believe) that we hadn't ordered. And because we checked-out in a hurry without reviewing the bill (a mistake on our end), we had no recourse for rectifying the issue. The callousness with which it was handled almost made us feel like this was a common practice.
Overall: if you want a luxury property with luxury service, stay somewhere else.

Just returned from the Sheraton after 10 days in San Diego.
We stayed on the 8th floor of the Bay Tower, the one down the road from the main hotel and I'm glad we did. It was much quieter in terms of a less busy reception and had less aircraft noise from the nearby international airport.
Our room overlooked the bay and Naval Air Station in Coronado. The other side faces the beautiful marina but be aware that you will notice more aircraft noise from the airport on that side.
Having said that, San Diego is a working Naval base and military jets and helicopters often fly over or near the hotel. One morning, we opened the curtains to see an aircraft carrier sailing into port! I found all this fascinating and it didn't bother us - but if you want a totally quiet holiday in terms of aircraft noise, then San Diego probably isn't the place for you.
The hotel bedroom was big compared to UK standards. Lovely bed, nice clean bathroom, minibar and a fridge available on request. The TV channels are fine although you won't receive BBC World News, which isn't a bad thing.
You can eat in the Bay Tower or at the main hotel although for breakfast, there is a superb small cafe next door called [NAME]'s Deli. You can get a great breakfast here for $7, lunch and any snacks up until about 6pm.
Don't be put off about "the walk" to the main hotel. It literally takes 3 minutes along a nice path that lets you look at all the expensive yachts.. 
The Sheraton will pick you up and return you to the airport for free in their regular shuttle and if you want to get into town, you cannot go wrong with the new Big Bay Shuttle that links the hotel with all the attractions on the waterfront.
It runs every 15 minutes and costs only $1 for a whole day! Where in the world could you get a service like that? A one way taxi costs $12 one way so check it out at http://www.portofsandiego.org/community-service/big-bay-shuttle.html
Overall, enjoyed the Sheraton and glad we stayed there having seen the hotels along the waterfront, which don't have quite the same outside environment.

I have been meaning to stay at the Metro for some time having heard some good reviews from others. I finally stayed there for 3 nights and would recommend it as a great choice, and it's a stone's throw from Macy's. The staff were very good, and I was efficiently checked in, and was advised of the facilities available such as a complimentary breakfast, a business centre and free wifi. I had forgotten to print my travel voucher, and they were fine about this, allowing me to check in first and settle in, and then print it out at the business centre. They do control access to this using keys at the front desk. 
I was fortunate enough to get a room upgrade to a Premier room located on a higher floor. The room was decently sized, but as with many New York rooms a bit dark. There are some nice extra touches to the room which made it a great experience, including a large screen flat screen TV, a Keurig Coffee Maker (with some tea cartridges) and a fabulous shower which gives you 3 options to shower (rain shower, standard and hand held). The bathroom has been refurbished to a nice contemporary standard. It provided generously sized toiletries comprising of soap, shampoo, condition and lotion. A shower cap is also provided alongside a hotel style hair dryer unit. On their website they advertise a fridge with a welcome beverage for this room class, but I did not get this, although this might be as it was a room upgrade. The bed was fantastically comfortable. In addition to these facilities, the room also had an iPod dock, laptop friendly safe and iron. The air conditioning was an old style model under the window which did make some noise, but was controlled using an electronic thermostat.
The hotel also offers a complimentary continental breakfast which was very handy. It served tea/coffee, apple and orange juices, bread, bagels, muffins, pastries, yoghurt, cereals and fruit. I would say that the offering was on par with that at the Park South hotel, but not as extensive as the Staybridge Suites which also offered some hot options like oatmeal, waffles and eggs. In addition to the breakfast, it was possible to get complimentary tea and coffee all day. You can also pick up a copy of the New York Times from the front desk. 
I would thoroughly recommend staying here and it now on my "go to" list of New York hotels.

We stayed here using our Marriott points and are so glad we did. The front desk staff was very friendly and helpful. The room was clean, and attractive and best of all the bed was comfortable. 
The location can't be beat, a short walk to the Metro station and Chinatown itself is a fun area to explore. The only thing they are missing is a pool which would be helpful when traveling with kiddos.
The breakfast was what you would expect, and the coffee was good. 
Would definitely stay here again if back in DC. Highly recommend this!

title_masked: If you're going to Universal Studios, this is the hotel!
text_masked:
Easy to get to by car and there is a self parking available, if you don't want to pay for valet parking. 
Very friendly and helpful staff - as expected at Hilton.
The room was outstanding. Clean of course, but it was spacious and we got a great view.
The pool area was nice and good tempered. The Jacuzzi felt great after a hard day at Universal Studios. 
A free shuttle bus takes you to the Universal City area where you find a lot of restaurants and shops. 
As a Hilton Honours member, complimentary continental breakfast is included and you can upgrade to the buffet for a small cost. Free Wifi for one hour is also included if you're a member
(a little bit cheap in my opinion...).
We had the dinner buffet which I would not have undone. Pricey, but you find things you've never tasted before - just make sure to be really hungry when you go there.

I spent one night at the Loews and expected it to be a bland ordinary hotel. From the moment I pulled up in my cab, a very friendly bellhop greeted me and walked me to check in. The design is very nice--modern, colorful, elegant Art Deco. That theme carries through on the carpets and conference rooms. The staff in this hotel is really a step above. They were extremely friendly and energetic. They must hire the best and compensate them well. Every employee I encountered was terrific, including the AV team (Jamal).
My room was large and very clean, with more than enough towels and washcloths for 2. The towels were also spotless white and in excellent condition. There was a shelf in the shower and the blow dryer had three settings. Connecting to the Internet was seamless. I had room service and it was quick and delicious. The design of the room shows real thought into the needs of the traveler. The lunch at my meeting was excellent. 
I travel quite a bit for business and I've stayed in dozens of hotels. Few stand out. This one really does. I would definately come back for business or a weekend get away.

This hotel has been rennovated and upgraded with new room types. Excellent and appreciated results. The kingsize room with increased and improved ammenities was a great value. I try to stay here at least once during trips to San Antonio. Great staff and wounderful beverage bar for wake-up coffee.

We had no issues with the Sofitel. The location cant be beaten. Being a Platnium Aclub member, we were upgraded to a higher floor. No view. Received a welcome drink on our first visit ( we stayed 2 nights then went on a 2 day tour, then checked back in for another 2 nights) but on the second visit, didn't receive one. 
Room was small, but as this is our first visit to the Big Apple, not sure if this is the norm. 
Beds are up to the Sofitel/Pullman standard, very comfy.
Overall a nice place, but not sure if worth the $350 average a night price.
Ken

I just returnd to Ireland after a 5 night stay. My first ever visit to NY and i was delighted with the hotel, Great location, the staff were so friendly and helpful. The room was great i didn't know what to expect and i was really pleased, very clean and comfortable. Thanks to all the staff, Breakfast the bottles of water and the cookies were great also.
Great first visit. I would strongly recommend it.

My favorite "go to" place when staying in downtown San Antonio. I always get a room overlooking the tranquil courtyard. Great food and wonderful bartenders that know how to fix up a drink! easy walk down the steps to the riverwalk, the Majestic Theatre, and fun bars. Highly recommend this hotel. Doesnt look like much from the street...but look out! You'll be pleasantly surprised once checked in!!!

title_masked: First class everything at the New Yorker
text_masked:
Travelling from Australia as a family of four with kids aged 8 & 5. We were originally booked into a midtown apartment but, while in Vancouver and with only 36 hours notice, the apartment suffered a terminal plumbing issue and became unavailable. After three anxious hours late night searching on the 'net we found the New Yorker. Despite calling at 03:00 NY time, the front desk staff booked us straight in, for 14 nights, room with 2 double beds, and even managed to arrange early checkin as we flew overnight via Toronto.
Without exception, the staff were great - curteous, efficient, friendly. The room had a point blank view of Empire State Building. And was everything it should have been (well, maybe the bar fridge should be standard). Bathroom was completely functional though a little cosy on space.
Location, location, location. The hotel is beautiful and one of those fabulous NYC iconic spaces. Deco vintage but refreshed for contemporary needs. Tick Tock Diner was perfect for breakfast and we had a fine dinner at Coopers, the hotel restaurant.
Overall, it was more expensive ($350/night) than we had budgeted for but, for a hotel stay, it was fabulous, fun, and a great introduction to NYC. Highly recommended.
Les, Samantha, Elsa, Joel.

Me and my family stayed in the Crowne Plaza back in October for 5 nights. We found the hotel location perfect for tourist attractions as it was right on Times Square and right beside Broadway! The rooms were clean but were quite small. We paid extra to be on the concierge floor and I would recommend doing this. We had a good view onto some of New York's skyline and had access to breakfast in the lounge with a continental breakfast selection. The wifi in the room was also free but we were disappointed that it didn't work down in the bar.
Overall a great hotel for a short stay trip in the big apple!!

Mandy was very helpful during my relatives stay when they came to Houston. She made sure they found every attraction and restaurant they thought would be of interest to them. They told me she was very knowledgable of what Houston has to offer and her customer service was top notch. I would definitely recommend this hotel & Mandy.

Spend three nights at the Marriott that is connected to the Convention Center in San Jose.
Check-in and check-out was quick and easy. It's your typical Marriott - high-mid-level hotel. There is a Starbucks style shop in the lobby - they aren't Starbucks owned, but do serve Starbucks coffee. You can also get your sundries here. They have a display case for bakery items, but every time I went down in the morning, it was pretty much empty. They said that the deliveries are made at 7am. So if you don't need to be up before then, you'd probably be alright.
There is no free parking at the hotel - there is only paid parking in the convention center lot ($20/night) or valet (unknown cost). The elevators are very frustrating - four of them and you can expect to wait a while for any of them.
The room - decent sized room, but the bed was WAY too soft. Wireless is NOT free (WHY is it that hotels still charge $10-15/night for wireless? It's obnoxious with how much the room already costs). The bathroom is up-to-date, but the shower does not have a lot of water pressure.
If you find yourself with the munchies after 9pm, you're hard pressed to find anything outside of a full-serve restaurant.
San Diego State University is about 4 blocks away and there is a large number of restaurants within walking distance. That being said, if you walk the wrong four blocks, it seems to be sketchy.

The water park is fantastic and both kids loved every minute spent there. The resort itself touted several kids activities that would be held throughout the day poolside. However they actually offered none. They have instead a kids club for a fee. When confronted with the misinformation, no one could answer to it and we got transferred to several different people. They all said so and so could help but there was just no consistency with the information we received.
The rooms are outdated and in southwestern decor but very comfortable, quiet and allowed for the kids to have their own room. The beds were extremely comfortable. Water was very hot and AC was very cold.

title_masked: Well located - the rest is very ordinary
text_masked: The last stop on our pacific highway journey from LA to San Francisco was in the city of the Golden Gate Bridge. We looked forward to Fishermans Wharf and ran the Golden Gate - by the way its a 15KM run from the Wharf and a brilliant one! So all in all a great city and a great stay... if it wer´nt for the Hotel we stayed at. The location is brilliant the rest... not so! The rooms were cold and damp. The beds felt as if plenty of Frisco Fans had already stayed there. The service - unfreindly and very standard operating process orientated! All in all very disappointing and not one of our favorites!

title_masked: This hotel is amazing. To bad I only statyed 1 night
text_masked: Received an upgrade to the presidentail suite. WOW!!!. my room was the same size as my house in san antonio. The Hyatt has always taken good care of me along with the Hilton. This hotel is very innovative, clean and the staff was excellent. It is pretty far away from the airport though. Food at the bar was very good as well. A busniss hotel from the feel of it.. Yes i will return for sure.

We just arrived home from a wonderful "getaway" couple of days (and one great night) in Seattle and wanted to be sure to give big kudos to the Hotel Andra for making our mini-vacation perfect. Our suite was wonderful - comfortable and the staff at the hotel made sure that we had everything we needed close at hand (including a personalized note welcoming us from the manager, a sweet snack, well-stocked bar, luxury robes, big shower, and generous amounts of soap, shampoo and conditioner). The staff (valet, conscierge and front desk) were highly professional as well as personable. We had dinner at a downtown restaurant and a nightcap at Lola (always great). Our bed was just right with the softest sheets (cozy and comforting). I was surprised that a downtown hotel room could be so quiet. We slept well and, in the morning a taxi was waiting to whisk us off to the Gauguin exhibit at the Seattle Art museum - just a couple of minutes away. Didn't get to stay for breakfast at Lola (great reviews) but hope to get back soon. The Hotel Andra makes a single night away from home feel like a real vacation! Thank you!

When I walked into the lobby I was in awe of the lobby. We had to wait about 30min before we could check in. We were there for a soccer tournament and there was also a convention for folks from India or from that culture. Made the place very colorful. The room was clean and had no issues with our room. Breakfast was a plus at this hotel. It was a hot breakfast. Eggs, Bacon, Sausage and Potatoes were served along with fruit and cereals and pastries. I was impressed with the breakfast. The room had a nice flat screen HD tv. Hotel was just off the highway and that made it easy to drive to restaurants and other locations. All of the staff we ran into was very friendly. The only thing I was say it needed was more than 1 washing machine and dryer. Although this is right next to some major corporations and I doubt they was their own clothes. It just so happened other soccer parents were trying to wash uniforms.
It's a no brainer - beautiful views, right on the sand - all amenities available - perfect part of San Diego - just about everything is within 2 miles. Keep thinking back and smiling.

Stayed here for three nights recently. I loved the hotel from the moment I checked in. I had a really nice room with balcony in the Tower section. I was on the 9th floor overlooking the ocean. Beautiful grounds and great staff. I'll definitely stay here again. Location was a bit out of town but it was nice to be beside the beaches and have some space.

title_masked: Good place to sleep, but not to dwell...
text_masked: I picked this location because it was perfectly situated near the best of everything in NYC. I attended a concert @ Carnegie Hall, so all I had to do was literally walk out the hotel and up 1 block. As others have mentioned, it's walking distance to Central Park and nice restaurants. Because of its older decor, and the rooms are small (but decently cleaned and appointed) it might turn off some people. If you're looking to stay longer than 3 days, I'd say spend more money and stay somewhere else. But if it's just for a weekend/couple of nights to see NY, stay here. I found the staff to be helpful and courteous.

I'm a big fan of Hilton hotels for their sleek and updated room decor. This is, in my opinion, a business hotel. The rooms are small and well equipped for the business traveller. Big flat screen TV, nice marble bath, desk with all needed ports and power. 
As mentioned by several reviewers, the hotel directly overlooks (past cranes) Freedom Tower and the 9/11 memorial. I made the mistake of booking a lower floor (15) and I could really hear the drone of machines all night long. By the third night I was too tired to hear it or care! 
When I first stayed here a few years ago there was no coffee in the room which really bugged me so I was happy to seek a nice single/double brewer when I checked in. Nice linens, soft towels and comfy pillows, my favorite.
There is a lot to see within walking distance of this hotel. WTC, Wall Street, Tribecca, Hudson River walk, South Street seaport. And, a great discount department store right next door. The path is across the street and the subway right at the corner. There are a lot of one way streets in this area so it's usually faster to walk and hop on the subway than get a cab. There is a LOT foot traffic here too so wear some durable shoes and merge into the jet stream!

title_masked: Great hotel for San Fran Downtown/Convention Center
text_masked:
I would recommend this hotel for people wanting a central location in downtown SF or someone coming to SF for a convention being held at the Marcone Convention center. Nice lobby and many people to help you make plans around the city at the desk.
Stayed 6 nights in the Marriott Marquis in downtown San Francisco. King bed. Standard sized room. Nice amenities. TV location near the window was an odd location for watching from bed. I had to turn the TV about 45 degrees for a head on view.
This was a great hotel for me because of the central location. It is also 1 block from the Marcone Convention center, which was the reason for my trip to SF. Very easy walk.
Sky bar: Bar on the top floor of the hotel with amazing views of the city. No need to go anywhere else. We had all the people in our group coming to our hotel for the view. Made for a nice short walk home at the end of the night.
Very close to Market street where you can catch all kinds of mass transit including the BART or trolly or surface bus. Very convenient to get anywhere in SF. Just use google map directions and it was very easy. 3 blocks from Union Square, another nice shopping area. 
Hot tub was really big and well maintained; this was used more than a few times on my trip. Also had a lap pool and very good work out facilities.
Nearby shopping included a walgreens for incidentals and foot. The hotel was even nice enough to bring us a minifridge free of charge to keep some bottled water cool for day trips.
Did not use parking so can not comment on this service but valet is available; also self parking available on Mission street some of our friends used and might be cheaper.
CON: Not near the water or the warf; will need to do 20min walk to water (near bay bridge) or taxi/bus/trolly to the fishermans warf. The F trolly will take you right to the warf and picks up on Market street and is very easy to do.

As with the other reviewers, the hotel is "average" but it is clean and in a great location. The location is everything. For sure, you can't beat it. I don't want to gloss over the Hilton service as per usual. It is - but Hilton should be proud. The staff at Fisherman's Wharf are very good. The front desk is well run and very helpful. The hotel room was clean due to the attention the room staff paid to their duties and would like to commend the restaurant staff as they were diligent and helpful. Overall, I would stay at this hotel again if I visited San Francisco. The staff really contributed to our fantastic holiday there. Thanks Bill.

title_masked: excellent location, comfortable, clean and tidy room
text_masked:
The hotel is in an excellent location.
You can easily get to Time Square and to any point in Manhattan.
Subway station two minutes away.
Rooms are very good, comfortable, clean and tidy. Staff very kind, helping each request and question.
Because Sandy storm, we stayed another three nights at the hotel not planned. The staff was very kind and tolerant to all our requests.
Highly recommend hotel. 
I am Sure that we return to this hotel for our next visit to New York.
Great location & a very nice room. Excellent breakfast.

title_masked: The Best Location on the Riverwalk
text_masked: We recently stayed at the Westin Riverwalk for a great weekend getaway with our 2 teen boys and visiting grandparents. After a 5 hour drive from Houston, we pulled into a somewhat underwhelming hotel entrance, but that impression was short-lived once we unloaded our bags and checked in. The hotel staff were very accomodating and managed to give us 2 rooms on the same floor, despite being full. The rooms are nicely appointed, with a large-ish bathroom, modern amenities, and the much-appreciated complimentary bottles of water. Our small balcony overlooked the river as well as the pool. ALthough we had a nice view, the pool was a gathering place for late night partying and kept us up Saturday night. Therefore, I suggest requesting a high floor, close to the elevator (1204 was less noisy). As for the location, as the title of this review suggests, I believe this to be the best location possible. The mornings and evenings sitting out for breakfast or evening drinks was lovely with a cool breeze (we were extremely fortunate with the weather) and minor tourist traffic walking by. On the other hand, you are a comfortable 6-7 minute walk from all of the action. My parents are not the most mobile and struggled a bit with some of the steps when walking from the "loop" of the Walk to the hotel. So if there are moobility issues, you can take the street method, using the elevators or handicap ramps at certain locations. That said, this is not a particularly handicap-friendly place to visit. Two final notes: 1.) The pool is small and gets packed by 2 or 3:00, - and is basically all adults (could be good or not depending on your situation). 2.) Although the setting is great for breakfast, the $16 pp price tag for the buffet is hefty considering there is little to choose from and no made-to-order options such as eggs or pancakes - unless of course you can expense it!

I have owned a timeshare at the Donatello for 20+ years. It is much more like a hotel though than a typical timeshare. I can break the 7-days per year into two 4-day stays, and just pay a
special "friends and family" rate for the extra day. The best part of the hotel is actually the location which is walkable to everwhere and only 3 blocks from Union Square. The rooms are always excellent with daily house keeping. For me, it was worth buying a timeshare on the secondary market if you like San Francisco as a re-occuring destination.

I enjoyed everything. Just wish the water pressure was better in the shower. We had an issue with jumping from upstairs. reported it and it stopped immediately. Everyone was very nice and helpful. Loved the Texas Waffles. I will be returning to this hotel in 2 weeks.

title_masked: Spacious suite but bathroom not up to par, great location
text_masked:
Third stay, wonderful location .This time got room 906, both the bedroom and the living room are nicely sized but the bathroom was not. The toilet is behind the door and placed so you have to sit on it SIDEWAYS which is really not right in a hotel of this caliber. Moreover, there only a shower with a wall mount. You have to move the waste basket around to fit in the bathroom and it does not even fit under the small sink!
Also the maid came and asked me twice before 9am if she could make the room on the first day and another maid came at 10 and 11 on our last day. That is too much, the room should be serviced at OUR convenience. Plus there was a really dirty hand imprint ( five black fingers)on the door from the bedroom to the living room and the shower tiles have some mold.
Our son"s room 1506 was fine.

We arrived after a long drive, and check in was fast and friendly. On request we were granted a very late check out, it let us enjoy the town. The location was excellent, right were we wanted to be, parking handy and at $25 not too bad and the lobby was roomy, with free and fairly fast internet. The room was fine. The elevators were very slow and on the blink, they were being worked on the next morning. The shock came the next morning when first there was no hot water, then no water and then luke warm water, hard to shower. Went to exlore the town, thinking to shower then. When we returned at noon, again no water, we could not even flush the toilet. Front desk was not very helpful, we checked out then to go to our next hotel in Fisher, thinking it will be better there. And it was. Check out again very fast, and very good directions were given to get to Fisher. All in all not the best stay, but after writing to a manager we did get 2000 points for our trouble. That should have been offered on site, without asking for anything.

At first glance and with the review ratings it looked like a decent hotel at a decent price. When I walked into the room it was tiny, then there was a huge stain on the carpet, then the pull down window shade wouldn't stay down (it would only stay down after I piled up the phone books with the bible with the iron placed on the pull down shade), then the pipes in the bathroom made noise constantly even if I wasn't in there with water running, then the shower head would shoot water everywhere, then the the air conditioner (whether it was on or off) every once in a while would sound like a mechanical cat barfing, then to top it off during the middle of the night when i had the air conditioner on it would go from working fine to pumping out HOT air. I should have stayed somewhere else for the price they charged me.

I spent 62 nights in this hotel in 2010, probably 30+ in 2009, and 2011. Everything was always excellent to me. Breakfast buffet, rooms, staff, location, proximilty to great food! It is Houston, so you sometimes hear sirens at night, but that would be anywhere you stay in such a large city.

We stayed at this hotel over St. Patrick's day with our two kids. What a great hotel and a great location. The hotel room (we had a suite) was very spacious and very comfortable for the two of us and our kds. The bathroom was a nice size. The suite was very spacious. Great idea if you are travelling with kids because the bedroom has a door so if you are both watching TV you could both watch comfortably. Everyone that we encountered at this hotel was so nice and welcoming. The workout room was clean and we had no problems getting a machine. The hotel is right across the street from Central Park. Get a Central Park view....it's incredible! You cannot beat the location at this very affordable (by NY Standards) hotel. We will definitely be back!

title_masked: A great hotel in a great part of NYC
text_masked: We checked into a Standard room which was quite small and the AC didn't appear to be working. We notified the front desk and they not only moved us to a Deluxe King room, they also comped our breakfast. The roof top terrace has great views of the city and was nice to start our day eating our breakfast up there. Wonderful service and a good price for a NYC hotel.

title_masked: Wish I could have stayed longer.
text_masked: I was only in town for one night and stayed at the Renaissance hotel. On a busy street so be careful getting out of your car, but at least the valet was on top of it all. The lobby was a bit smaller than I would have expected but it was very bright and ornate, quite beautiful. The staff was very nice and the concierge was very helpful with restaurant recommendations. My room was a bit out of the way of the elevator and a little difficult to find. The hallways are numbered rather awkwardly and had to keep looking at all the doors. I felt like maybe my room was in a different building but eventually found it. My room was a good sized room and felt very spacious. I had two full beds but my coworker had a queen of the same sized room with a seating area. The bed was very comfortable and I just sank into the mattress. There is an actual floorlength, three foot wide mirror in the entryway which would be on any lady's wish list. The bathroom was quite ornate with a nice sized tub, couldn't wait to soak a little. It was close enough to the visitor attractions, but there is not much else in the immediate vicinity. Overall quite a nice stay. I'm sure this is a good price for DC, but I don't like to pay this much on a vacation.

Was moved to this hotel at the last minute... - Wasn't massively impressed when I walked up to it, but the receptionist was great and knowledgeable. The rooms aren't massive, but are very clean, modern and come with free water, snack bar and other unexpected touches. 
The breakfast was pretty awesome, and I'd return for that alone : )

We stayed 4 nights at The Whitehall Hotel. The location was outstanding, one block from The Hancock Building, less than one block from many bus routes, less than one block from The Magnificent Mile! The hotel itself is a little worn, the rooms are small but the staff were very pleasant! Would I stay here again? Yes just for the location alone!

Good location on Louisiana Street, a major road in downtown. Connected to the tunnel system via stairs in the lobby. Yes, valet at $30 is pricey, but in/out privileges. You can park in the Regency deck (not affiliated with the hotel) connected to the hotel via 3rd floor skyway for $15, however with no in/out privileges. Einstein Bagel place in lobby is good choice (and you can charge to your room), still a bit pricey however probably not as much as the affiliated hotel restaurants. Travelling into the tunnels would land you a great many more choices (note Allen Ctr food court), but all are closed at 6am if you want breakfast. 
Rooms are niced sized. They face the large and tall atrium, which makes the sounds from the lobby/restaurants reverberate to the romms, even on the 24th floor. Wireless was very poor, so don't plan on getting work done at this hotel. Wireless and slow drain preclude a 5 rating.

title_masked: Good hotel for family of 5 close to LAX
text_masked:
Couldn't find any hotels around LAX that will take a family of 5. We chose this place because they took 5 of us in one room (with rollaway). 
The hotel is a little older, but, they seem to keep it reasonably clean. 
No lifts to the 2nd level. It was a little inconvenient for the amount of baggage for a family of 5. 
Rooms were fairly noisy with both traffic and aircraft noise -- but, that is to be expected and it becomes a constant background drone so you get used to it. 
Breakfast was great. 
We only stayed here because we only needed one night close to the airport. It is perfect for that. Beds comfortable. 
I probably wouldn't use this as a base for a longer holiday, but , it was perfect for what we needed.

Booked via priceline and didn't know what to expect. However very pleased upon arriving, top notch service, location, and look & feel. Had a great stay and will stay here next time in Fort Worth, others in our group stayed at other hotels in the area, all agree, Renaissance Worthington is the nicest.

I can't imagine why there are such good reviews here. Staff members? Their parents? This hotel has a very good location, but the lobby is as minimal as possible and all the public rooms have a dark, dingy feel. The breakfast was also minimal -- compared to the Hampton Inn, where we also stayed on this trip. 
The hallways are very narrow -- to the point where I was wondering if they're wide enough to satisfy the fire code. We had a suite in the back of the hotel. It was adequate but slightly run down. Dingy again.
We requested a late checkout, just an extra hour. They demanded an extra $15. We said no, thanks. They then offered to store our luggage as if it was a big favor.
Just an all around downer of an experience.

title_masked: A lovely elegant hotel in the heart of a lovely city
text_masked: As was expected, the service provided by the Ritz Carlton hotel employees was courteous and impeccable. We were upgraded to a lovely room with a beautiful view of the lake just beyond. The beds are typically comfortable with lovely, expensive sheets. The amenities in the room and bathroom were adequate and appropriate. The bathrooms however were a bit small. I was surprised to discover that there were no coffee/tea making facilities in the room. In fact most luxury hotels are now wooing the guests with Nespresso makers in the room! The location is fantastic and is walking distance to anywhere and everywhere fun in Chicago. rooms are comfortable with lovely, The spa was elegant and lovely but the pool was disappointingly small. It was confusing however to find out that this hotel is run by Four Seasons while there is another Four Seasons just close by.

4 nights here in late july over the weekend. price point was good in comparison to other hotels in the area. location was wonderful, short walk to times square and easy access to the subway at either grand central or bryant park. room itself was extremely comfortable with excellent amenities both in the room and in the lobby itself. staff were wonderful, welcomed us warmly and were able to assist with wonderful recommendations.

good location, great value for downtown phoenix. The owners are friendly and accomodating. the rooms were very clean and very recently renovated. the beds were very comfortable. Only here for a one night stopover. advertised complimentary transport to hotel. assumed could call the courtesy shuttle from airport hotel directory but they are not listed. called the hotel and they said a 24hr advance booking for courtesy transportation was required so we had to take a cab ($22o/w). however they did accomodate the rtn transportation for the next morning on short notice. would definately stay there again.

I was an in town guest last night, having to stay somewhere for the night while my floors were being done. I was blown away by the great TA reviews and rushed to book my room.
At $321 for a "first class room", I was "ok" but not thrilled. First of all, the kiosk wouldn't allow me to check in. I had to go up to the 4th floor and wait for 30 minutes while they checked to see if my room was ready. After about 20 minutes I went back to the girl and told her that I needed her to personally go see if the room was ready. I found that to be a lack of strong hospitality skills - if the maintenance or housekeeping person isn't answering or getting an answer for your patiently waiting guest, do it yourself. Take charge, make decisions. I was sitting there like an idiot for 30 minutes after telling her that I was exhausted. And this was at 5pm, well after check in time.
Aside from that, the things I didn't like...
- You can't charge your bar or restaurant charges to the room - "we're a separate company" - most hotels have independent vendors that allow you to bill directly to your room. I have NEVER been a hotel bar or restaurant that refused a charge to a room. Figure it out people.
- NO glasses - all plastic cups. I came back with wine (thank god I had the wine store open it). The Yotel bar refused to lend me a glass. I was shocked, especially since I spent $40 at the bar earlier that night. So I went to my room and had to peel the saran wrap off a flimsy plastic cup in the bathroom like I was staying at a Toledo Airport Travelodge or something. So cheap and really angered me, at $321 a night.
- Kleenex is in a cheap little plastic pouch instead of being readily accessible
- Cheap and cheesy "spaceship" furniture - like a massive TV-case with plasticky shelves that will never be stored with books. Either stock the shelves or ditch them for simplicity.
- No room service
- The shower was marketed as a "monsoon shower" - not really - its just a basic shower with a square head.
- The bed is overly firm - no box spring - just a rather thin mattress inside a bed frame
Things I liked: 
- Very clean room
- My first cabin had a cozy couch with a lot of space to sprawl out
- Great bathroom products that I was considering buying
- Amazing pillows that I was considering buying
- The galley on each floor has awesome free Lavazza coffee with takeaway cups
- Free wifi, which was pretty fast
- The happy hour at the bar is good and the menu looked interesting
- Even though I was on the 8th floor, had a nice view
- A little foldable map of NYC, very nice touch
- Bright airy bathroom with a huge window overlooking the city
All in all, I was disappointed more than I was jazzed, especially by the check-in, plastic cups, bed quality, etc. But liked certain elements.
Bottom line, I would probably not bother to stay here again. Tons of choices in NYC and it didn't draw me in.

I usually don't stay at Hiltons - but having come for business, the hotel was already picked out for me, plus I knew that it had a great location (actually, the location was the best thing about the hotel) so I agreed to stay here. The hotel itself (the lobby, appearance) was very nice - the service was wonderful, I asked to be moved twice and they complied (one time because I requested a double bed and was given a single) the other because I wanted a higher floor. So in that sense they were accommodating. But my main complaint was - this was not the cleanliness of a 5-star hotel. First of all, the room had a weird feet smell to it. The bathroom had a sweaty/old water smell to it, even though it was renovated, the cleaning crew did not do a good job - I found hair on the wall and some in the tub, the walls had some stains, wallpaper was peeling, etc. The beds didn't have bed bugs so in that sense I was happy. But there was no working fridge- would have been nice to put my drinks in there especially since it was warm in NYC at that time. Overall was just OK - if the price were $100-150 a night I would not complain. But the rate was $479, and in Europe if you pay that much (in Germany, and the UK) you get a great, clean room for the same price.

Clean, convenient. First time at a Hyatt Place.
Only some minor waiting for reception, not a big deal.
Good breakfast, a little more interesting than most free breakfasts.
Would definitely stay again.

title_masked: Nice beds, rooms are kind of small
text_masked:
The bed was really comfy but the room itself is pretty small. The building itself is pretty. Location is decent but can't really comment since I was there for work and basically had to drive out to the suburbs for the entire day. Close to Short North where we had some good Italian food at Marcella's...i think that's what it's called.
The lady at the front desk was nice but not really answering our questions about where to eat.

I stayed at the hotel over the Easter long weekend.
Pros
Fresh, lovely decor.
Large rooms.
Friendly front-desk staff.
Very convenient to shopping, sightseeing.
LEED-certified - liked the idea of using the room key to turn on the lights, and turn them off when leaving the room.
Cons
Sound transmission between rooms - the child in the next room had frequent melt-downs in the bathroom - several times/evening. He also woke me up at 4am, and 7am with his screaming. Not the way a single person wants to spend a relaxing weekend.
Room location - near the elevators. This was a busy weekend for the hotel, with an anime conference down the street. I could hear conversations at the elevator, through the door.
Some serious structural work needs to be done to control the noise level.
I paid the seniors' discount - I wonder if that's why I got the room close to the elevator.

Hotel is beautiful, located in the river walk. The rooms are spacious and nicely decorated, rooms have a separate are from the rooms that looks like a living room, 2 TV's were in my room. 
 Best hotel I've ever stayed in San Antonio.

We ended up in San Francisco in our return trip from Portland, Oregon, at around 12:30 PM. We had not made any reservations and we passed other properties outside of the city limits. All of a sudden we were super tired and got lost on or around the center of the city. Finally, through the technology of our GPS, we found the Holiday Inn mentioned above.
The room was expensive: $200+ (or perhaps the night clerk saw my tired face and stuck it to me), the parking alone was $45 for the night. It was too late so I bought the room or my traveling companions were going to lynch me for not being better organized.
The room had two queens and a sofa bed. The carpet was very dirty, the beds hard and the pillows very firm. No breakfast, no newspaper the next day, our emergency stay (almost) did not yield any dividend. This city is cold in more ways than one and that night I found out how cold. A person traveling would be better served by locating better properties, that I am sure abound, but staying at this location is very stressful. Advice? Skip it all together!
This city is unforgiving when not properly prepared and everything cost more money than usual. We also went to a new peruvian restaurant at El Embarcadero and that finish us off. 
Less than 12 hours and we had already dished out around $400.
The rooms at this Holiday Inn are somewhat spacious but everything else is unimpressive and expensive, as I mentioned earlier.
Travelers must be warned to look for the best deals before setting foot in this town. The Holiday Inn mentioned is not the best deal by a long shot. Sucks big lemons, if you know what I mean.

The best thing of this hotel is its location. The staff is not very gratefull and sometimes rude. The breakfast is a normal continental breakfast and the breakfast room is veryyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyy tiny for a lot of people.

Staff was very courteous and hotel was only a few doors down from ABC and close to Times Square. Room was small but clean. We had a horrible view since our window was in the inside square but we really didn't stay in the room much. There was a lot of snacks on one of the places you could put your things and we didn't realize it but if you move it around the computer automatically charges your room. Guest services did take off our bill since we didn't eat anything. Would have been nice to have coffee pots in the room since coffee pot in lobby was empty by 8 am. There is a store/deli only 3 doors down that has everything though.
Overall I would stay here again.

I booked a long weekend to tour DC with a visitor from Japan. I chose the River Inn because of its location and price. Having lived in Washington, I knew that the George Washington University region was safe, close to many tourist locations and easily accessible to the metro. What surprised me was how delightful the River Inn was.
We arrived mid morning and encountered a very kind desk clerk who found a room ready for us. I had booked a smallish room for a great price (with breakfast), and was offered a considerable upgrade at a a great deal, so I took it. I was not disappointed. The room was huge and looked as though it had once been a good sized apartment - with a large living room, dining table and well appointed kitchen (no oven, but a good microwave). There was coffee in the bean and a grinder so you can make coffee as you like it in the coffee pot provided. The bath and bedroom with two double beds were modestly sized, but clean and very acceptable. The furniture in the living area was in fine condition, not fancy, but serviceable. 
Our room came with a full American breakfast at the Dish restaurant. Service was very pleasant, and the breakfast was good - more than I could eat. We also stopped at Dish for a glass of wine in the evening, and we found the service pleasant and very friendly. The restaurant filled up a bit early - about 6 PM, which we attributed to locals catching an early dinner before heading to the Kennedy Center for a show a couple of blocks away. 
The River Inn is located adjacent to the GW campus and is only 2 blocks from the Metro station, which provides accessibility to many other locations throughout the city. Georgetown is only 5 blocks away, the Kennedy Center is only two, and the Lincoln Memorial, WWII and Korean Memorial are about 5 blocks in another direction. There is a Trade Joes two blocks away to pick up some groceries and a Whole Foods around the corner to accommodate the grocery gourmet. I would say that this hotel is perfectly located to access traveling necessities and enjoy the sites and entertainment. Importantly it is a safe location - as we were two women walking alone. 
I like to exercise when I travel, so I used the fitness room. It is small but the equipment is clean and in good condition. It is located adjacent to the business center where visitors can print boarding passes. 
All in all, I would say this was very pleasant surprise - an excellent value for the money. I would definitely stay here again.

My wife and I spent a quick weekend at the Mark with another couple. The service is gracious with European touches and the Mark’s rooms were generously sized, especially for NY standards.
Liked: Free wifi (rarity at this price point); location well suited for boutique shopping along Madison Ave; Jean-Georges restaurant was excellent; vibrant bar scene; well done room Crestron room controls; plenty of closet space; most comfortable beds ever!
Anomalies: Extreme room service pricing and delayed well beyond quoted time (as in 20 mins turned into >1 hour; questionable room servicing/cleaning

title_masked: Top of the line in every way
text_masked: I am Platinum SPG member and stayed for one night on business. Had an early flight next morning so thought I would stay near airport. It was only about 10 min drive in the morning to airport. Some good things and some great things about this place. Was upgraded to one bedroom corner suite. WOW, what a nice room. Very clean and very BIG!. The bed was as you would expect from Westin (excellent). Shower had rain head and wall mount. There was also a large free standing tub! TV had large selection of Hidef channels. Internet was fast and free for Platinum members. There was a lounge but selection was so so. You do have to pay to park and there is NO shuttle to airport but still worth the stay. I would say this is one of the nicest non resort rooms I have ever had. The staff were all very friendly. I can not think of anything that could have been better about the room!

Spent 4 nights at this hotel with some friends. Hotel property is clean, close to airport and has all the usual amenities. Parking, breakfast, week day dinner, week day early evening beer / wine, fitness center and WiFi are all free. Room was clean and service was excellent. Lots of walking paths, a Vons and Trader Joe's nearby. Quick drive to expressways and Gaslamp Quarter. Well done, Hilton!

title_masked: Great hotel for the price in NYC
text_masked:
My husband and I really liked this hotel. It's only a few blocks from the metro, the natural history museum and central park. 
We found the decor to be pleasing and the price was incredibly reasonable for the hotel room and amentities offered. The decor is modernish and is as pictured on their website. The king bed was super comfy with a down comforter and feather pillows. There were wood blinds as well as thick curtains that truly block out the light. The bathroom was well appointed and the shower was roomy. 
We booked directly through the hotel's website and got a great deal on a package that included valet parking. They then emailed us a link which allowed us to "share" where we'd be staying for a room upgrade. We did so and submitted the upgrade paperwork when we arrived. They almost told us they couldn't accomodate the upgrade but then the gentlemen checking us in found a deluxe room to put is in on the "quiet" side of the street. I had selected a superior room since the standard (like most hotel rooms in NYC) looked really small. The deluxe room we were upgraded to was quite large, actually, especially by NYC standards. And when the gentlemen said he was putting us on the quiet side of the hotel, he wasn't kidding. When we exited the morning after we checked in, they were doing street construction or some such right across the street and it was very noisy. FYI - There is scaffolding surrounding the hotel at this time which doesn't inprove the exterior facade any and, I am sure, blocks the view for anyone on that side of the hotel but, once gone, this will be a pretty hotel. If this concerns you, check "street view" on Google maps to see if the scaffolding is still there. 
The best part of the hotel are the public lounges (which also serve as smoking areas for any smokers out there who are feeling ostracized these days) on the 14th and 16th floors which have multiple green privacy screens erected and great views of the city. These are great places to go out and relax and have a cocktail and catch the view. 
Lastly, every staff member we encountered was genuinely friendly, including the valets, and our check-out process was incredibly smooth. We would definitely return and recommend this hotel to others.

To begin The Surrey has an excellent location. It's within walking distance to the Metropolitan Mluseum, Guggenheim and other 5th Ave. museums. Around the corner, on Madison Ave. the 3 Guys diner offers a resonable alternative to the upscale Cafe Bouloud located within the hotel. Many other dining choices abound either on Madison Ave. or nearby side streets. If arriving by auto (like I did) check in can be a challenge because town cars often block the hotel's entrance. I was able to pull in at a hydrant accross the street and the doorman provided excellent service by quickly coming over to take charge of my car and bags. My welcome at the check in desk was equally prompt and warm. Our room was large. I especially liked the double sinks in the bathroom. The towels were thick and the hot water endless. I found the shower to be of hurricane force and there was no way to adjust this. All our needs, such as a request for ice, were promptly answered. Likewise when it was time to check out a bellman appeared quickly. Our bill was calculated without error and checkout was easily done. A sore point the the charge for WiFi. In this day and age this is just an outrage. On the other hand we got a freeee NY Times each day. A plus for the room was its two comfy easy chairs. The large work desk with its comfortable easy chair was also a plus. The bed was comfortable too.

My husband & I really enjoy this hotel due to it's location plus it is just lovely! We know that it will be a clean and comfortable stay. Breakfast is always delicious & quite filling. See you again soon!

We hadn't been to SF for a while and decided to splurge since in was our anniversary. The hotel is spectacular! Staff was great, room was pretty much perfect, and with great views of the city. We told the staff at check in of our anniversary and they sent up champagne and strawberries (super nice!) We stayed in the newer tower for a bit more money ($30), but it was definately worth it, as most of the lower floor rooms had only a view of the building next door. Location couldn't have been any better if you want to stay in the city ... no car necessary. My only reason for not giving it an excellent was the price and the crowds. Everything was super expensive including the hotel, restaurants, shopping. We got a CityPass before arriving, to cover transportation and some touristy sites and museums, and it was well worth it, if you're staying for 4 days or more. In doing the research, I found that most all the hotels in the city were comparably priced, so if we go again, the St. Francis would probably be on our list.

title_masked: Great family reunion at extended stay
text_masked:
The staff (Andrea & Joe) were most professional in helping us plan our family reunion. We were given a great conference room to hold our group get together, and the staff was very accommodating. We had over 70 guest and about 25 rooms, the pool area was perfect for our outside activities. We will def be back again. Love the rooms and this location has access to everything within walking distance. (the kids loved the magic mountain).
Thanks so much Andrea, Joe and Tito

title_masked: Dated but comfortable hotel in a great location
text_masked: I choose hotels on a bunch of criteria. Price, location, amenities and wifi. As I travel mainly on business there are things that are important not just the room. This hotel is an older hotel that has very nice and well appointed rooms. It is in a great location with good views from the upper floors. The rooms are large and well appointed but like most American hotels have terrible showers. :). The wifi was good the only issue was noisy neighbors. Sound travels between rooms too well. I may as well have been in the conversation next door. Staff were ok. Not overly helpful but pleasant. The restaurant was an odd mix of revival 70s decor and the hit brekkie was not all that appealing. I'd stay here again it is a great location and a huge pool.

title_masked: Noisey with no help from Security
text_masked: We were there for a three night stay. There were people screaming and yelling throughout our first night. Security was called three times and three times their efforts were geared more to trying to make peace with the party people versus keeping things quiet for all guests, thus no sleep. In other fine places where we have stayed, if the first request for quiet is not honored, a second request results in an escort out by police. And in the AM there was no hot water.

title_masked: Best location and service, terrible street noise. Time for renovation.
text_masked:
Stayed on the 8th floor. Windows are not double glazed and old aluminum work. Street noise especially at night was a real nuisance. 
Bed was also approaching it end of life, sinking in the middle.
Seems it is time for renovation
Other than that, huge room, great service, best location possible
Very nice large room. Beds very comfortable. Everyone friendly and helpful. Room service excellent. Overall experience very good.

Not such a bad place..in fact, a great location and comfortable bed, but I found a pair of men sox just under the bed ...yuk...and the woman at the desk regarding local information was more suited for a prison wing. I was very happy to have my room 'done' every second day as perfectly capable of pulling up a quilt but even though i told them not to bother, it was still done. A big hotel and obviously busy housekeeping staff....its a good thing to lessen their load but when they do clean it, do it thoroughly. Otherwise, go there...it's very okay.

We only had an overnight opportunity to commemorate our 40th w/Easter, Sunday, our anniversary, and our son's 21st birthday Friday, but the quality of our repose was extraordinary. Don't know for sure who upgraded us from a simple waterside room w/full view to the 4th floor suite, but we were totally spoiled w/the accomodations and enjoyed the jacuzzi, the dining room/adjacent sitting room, and the open deck. The seagulls entertained us, catching some left overs in mid-air as they circled overhead. Mount Ranier and the snow-covered Olympics were grand this morning. The various colored lights of the city, especially the commerce area, the docks, were so beautiful last evening. I am totally refreshed with such comfortable sleeping facilities. My husband almost filled his photo card again w/all the photo opts. We had a truly memorable experience!

We travelled to Denver for Thanksgiving and booked a room at the Embassy Suites because we had two adults and two kids and Embassy Suites tend to work well (and I am a Hilton Honors Diamond member). When we checked in we realized how dated the hotel is and it really shows in the common area and the rooms. It was so dated that we moved to the Hilton Garden Inn at the Tech Center on the second day for the remainder of our stay.

My husband and I love this hotel. We celebrated our anniversary and the entire staff took wonderful care of it. We are elite members with Marriott and really appreciate warm service and clean and warm surroundings. We will be back for Thanksgiving

title_masked: Nice hotel - details lacking for a 5 *
text_masked:
We arrived at 4:00 and told room was not ready - didn't get our room until 5:30. No offer of complimentary food or drinks - left to our own devices in the interim - unacceptable for a 5* hotel.
Charges added to our room that we did not incur - cancelled upon request. Told we had to check out after two nights when we had reservation for three nights. Was forced to provide confirmation of reservation.
Room was nice with a great view of L.A. and Hollywood sign. But, floors were wooden and walls were too thin so heard all of the late night stuff.
$350 rental for the cabana for the day is a bit much.
Good location but many details lacking for a supposed 5 * hotel.

I stayed here for a week late in April on Business. I got in late at night and first impression was odd as the industrial design of the place leaves it quite dark. I was a bit upset that my luggage had not arrived and must say the hotel lift up my mood when I got to my room to find a welcome card and a set of cupcakes. Thank you!
Location can't be better as you can walk to the myriad of shops and restaurants in Soho, nearby West Village and Tribeca. Many people here complain about room size, but having just arrived from an European holiday, getting a room with walk in closet and multiple storage in the bathroom was a welcome plus. It also helped that my room faced the side street, which means little noise despite being on the 6th floor. All in all, the room was extremely comfortable, spotless clean and had a decent size bathroom with great amenities.
No doubt this place is hip, full of models and wannabes, but you get out of it what you want. The reception lounge transforms into a bar at night, and the Yard bar gets really packed on sunny days. You choose to join the crowd or go your own way.
Despite the trendy looks, the staff was one of the friendliest and most helpful I ever encountered, on helping me locate the lost luggage, to getting a cab on a rainy Sunday when no driver wanted a ride to La Guardia. I am also greatly thankful to the lady that cleaned my place each morning.
This is my favorite area in NYC and I'd come back here anytime on a heartbeat.

title_masked: Front desk captain Ms [NAME] runs a tight ship and makes dated facilities tolerable.
text_masked: Hotel in obscure location. Low rate but dated facility. WiFi is tenuous at best. Ms [NAME] at front desk is a gem and helps compensate for the many shortcomings of this dingy hotel. Breakfast is great for a 2 star facility. Room key cards need to be rekeyed almost every day as they easily erase when in contact with credit cards, etc. WiFi marginal. Mr [NAME] is a little eccentric but can fix if Ms [NAME] contacts an encourages him. Not a bad value because of Ms [NAME]. Complimentary minifridge and microwave provided. Coin laundry on site.

This Hotel has everything, Location, service, entertainment and comfort. I had a great time here, the rooms did not feel like a hotel room at all, more like a swanky loft apartment. My only con is that room service is a bit expensive.

My husband and I stayed at the Hotel Monaco while visiting friends in Denver. Full disclosure: We stay at Kimpton Hotels a lot in San Francisco and were using Kimpton points for a free stay on this visit to Denver. We had never stayed in the Monaco before. Another hotel might have given us a room no one else wanted, given that we weren't paying for it, but we got a top-floor room with a (limited) mountain view. Everything was about as perfect as it could be: the room was clean; the amenities, generous; the staff, super friendly. As with other Kimpton hotels, there was free coffee in the morning and a free wine happy hour in the afternoon. The coffee could have been stronger; on the other hand, there were delicious snacks with the happy hour. 
As an example of the good service, after checking into the room I called the front desk to ask for a second robe and a second luggage stand. Later, they called back to make sure it had arrived and to see if there was anything else we might want!
Also, the downtown location is great. At 17th and Champa, it's just off the 16th Street mall, and we enjoyed long walks exploring the downtown area.

Nice Hotel great location. However the highlight of my vacation was the service that I received from the concierge Sean Kullavanijaya; I was overwhelmed the personal attention I received. He made himself available 24 hours bases. He cut the learning curve, provided access to all the best events and the best restaurants. I will not return to Washington without first notifying Sean.
the room was clean but a little bit outdated, it looks like 3stars rather than 4stars. customer service was superb though.

I have stayed here a few times and things seem to get better each time! The staff is always the best! Maria does an excellent job with housekeeping-left jewelry by mistake and the hotel called to let me know! The breakfast is always upgrading-changing things out I think from feed back from hotel guests, which is NICE!! There were cranberries, granola- different flavors for your coffee, etc. Not the same "chain" kind of items! Fresh coffee 24/7 and nice tea choices. The patio/pool area and tables are clean. Very nice to sit out and enjoy some sun! Get the rooms with the pool side-especially if you are planning on going out and having pool fun! The Koi/pond is a nice added touch but the cleanliness of the rooms/pool area/lobby is what I look for 1st in a hotel! This is a nice hotel and I will stay there again!

Very nice hotel - the room is very trendy, nice backlighting, very large TV. We stayed Sunday - Tuesday, we parked on the street since we were driving around LA - parking is free on Sunday and at night till 8am the following morning.
The toiletries are very nice - lime scented, so nice we bought some at BLISS store. We used the Acura Limo service - very nice and courteous. The Lobby Bar is a great area - we had a fantastic Jazz Singer on Monday night, the place was packed !!
Drais takes over the hotel pool on Sundays and bouncers are all around the hotel, but they recognised us instantly as guests and there were no problems getting in.
We got the Hotel on Priceline for $100 and we asked and got an upgrade overlooking the inner courtyard with a view of the Capitol Records Building.

title_masked: Grand Hyatt at Grand Central, NYC
text_masked:
We chose the Grand Hyatt at Grand Central for its location. It is pretty much in the middle of Manhattan and handy for Grand Central station - you don't even leave the building. Although it is neat and modern up to and including the lobby, it is showing signs of age inside. Furnishings are rather dark and a bit old-fashioned and the lighting is muted. We asked for a roll-away bed for or seven year old; it was so large that there was barely space left to move about the room. Fortunately this did not bother us too much as we mainly used the room to wash and sleep. Although we were not high up, there was no external noise. Neighbors could be heard rarely. Staff attitude was generally good and occasionally exceptional.
A few things niggled: I was not notified of mail deliveries; I phoned to ask a written message to be delivered to my wife and it did not happen; internet access is around 16USD per day and is not free in the lobby; the room service menu is average (macaroni cheese, that famous comfort food, was not good) and there was a 20 minute queue for breakfast. Reservations were advised for the latter. In that time I bought a good breakfast in Grand Central and brought it back to our room.
Would I go there again? For the location, yes. I can take or leave the rest.

title_masked: Lots of little annoying things make for a bad stay.
text_masked: Cool "looking" hotel room and cool "looking" bathroom. Trendy, urban, contemporary. Thats where the cool ends however. Elevators didnt work right, coffee machine in-room broken and no coffee in morning in lobby either, or any breakfast offering (not even to purchase), low water pressure for shower that is just small and awkward with no door so the floor gets all wet, no pay per view movies on the tv with only basic channels, the remote control would only channel up and not back down so you had to rotate through 24 stations just to get back to the only lousy option you already had and on and on and on with the inconveniences. Too bad, this hotel has a lot of potential but when at every turn there is an annoyance it kind of ruins the place. I would not stay there again. The adjacent Benjamin Steakhouse is absolutely fantastic however and adds as in-room dining to the hotel....that is the only redeeming quality in my opinion.

I stayed her with my mom and daughter and was very pleased! I've stayed in a lot of NYC hotels, and this is a favorite. The location was great for getting around and so easy to get anywhere in NYC with a close subway stop. I liked the size of the hotel- not too big but still bustling with people and energy, and then also quiet at night. 
I'm a stickler for comfortable beds and nice showers- both were great.
I didn't see too many kids there, but they treated mine very well. Definitely an upper east-side experience with a lot of fine dining and older-set crowd. (comparing it to LES and Soho), but a really nice location for enjoying this part of town. I felt like a resident and less like a tourist. Everyday we walked with my 3 year old to Central Park which was so nice to do. They have a great park near the closest entrance, and the zoo is pretty near as well. Seraphinas pizza was also a frequent stop since its kids friendly and popular for all ages- its down the street from the hotel. 
All the staff was pleasant and sweet, always wanting to help. Highly recommend if you aren't looking to be around the bustling streets and trendy areas.

This was a nice property and good value for the money. It was a great jumping off point for Mission Valley and Coronado and San Diego overall. The staff were very pleasant -- front desk and housekeeping. Breakfast was fine -- and the bed was comfortable. I'd stay here again.

This hotel is great, beginning with check in. Staff is very accommodating & strives to make your stay as pleasant as possible. The rooms are spacious & comfortable. Location is perfect for sightseeing & just wandering around the city.

We chose the Crosby Street Hotel as my dog is called [NAME] (but with a z) and I am so glad that we did! When I return to NYC for any future holidays I will be staying here without a doubt.
We paid a little extra and booked a room on the top floor which was worth every penny. Our room deco was stylish and very comfortable with amazing rooftop views. The bed was so big I had to climb into it but was pure luxury. The bathroom had a walk in power shower which was divine.
We ate at the hotel restaurant on the Friday night which was buzzing and had a great atmosphere, pink champagne and the crosby burger was yum! We ordered breakfast in bed on the last day, pancakes with syrup and hash browns were very good.
Being an animal lover the dog theme was great and the deco is very stylish. Hotel is in a great location and the tube is nearby as are the Soho shops.
