Staff were friendly and helpful, concierge did a great job in managing to get us taxis.
The hotel is relaxed and not pretentious, there is no where else in NYC I would rather stay.

We stayed at the night hotel in February for 5 nights , the staff were helpfull and friendly from the minute we walked in. We were given a fantastic room on the 6th floor with plenty of space. No complaints of a small room here unlike some other reviews. It pays to ask in advance as the hotel happily emailed us back confirming our requests, and on arrival a complimentary bottle of champagne was delivered to our room as it was my boyfriends birthday. The rooms were spotless, beds were comfy and the shower was so good we wanted to take it home. 
The hotel is 2doors down from Starbucks, ideal for breakfast or when returning to the hotel with weary feet. You are also steps away from times square and ideally located to explore all that New York can offer. 
Even at checkout staff were still helpfull, airport transfer was arranged for $65 and lap top provided to check online and print boarding passes. No complaints will definitely be returning to New York and will definitely be returning to Night Hotel!!!

Convenient location: very close to National Mall. Specious room. Very clean. Bed is great. Sofabed was as comfortable as our queen size bed. Towels are soft and white. Complimentary coffee (regular and decaf) is in the lobby all day long. Full size refrigerator and kitchenette with all necessary utensils is definitely great bonus. Parking is under the hotel. $35 per night. Complimentary breakfast - variety is outstanding. Friendly staff at reception desk. We would come back.

The staff was friendly and helpful. The grounds were well maintained, beautiful rose garden in bloom. The restaurant and my room were very clean. Miracle of miracles, plenty of outlets to plug my camera, phone, iPad, and laptop in at the same time! On the downside, this hotel, which used to be a Hyatt back in the day, is shabby, and in bad need of a remodel. If you just need a place to recharge your electronics and catch a good nights sleep before heading out on a plane the next day, this is just fine. If you plan to spend any time awake in the room, look for something else.

title_masked: Call Anthony Melchiorri, this is a Hotel Impossible candidate
text_masked:
I found the Sheraton Dallas to be so cheap that I would have been better off staying at a more mid range hotel. They lacked in service, lacked in quality and failed to deliver a good guest experience. Shameful as I now read reviews I see other guests experienced the same problems over and over.
At check-in, I dealt with a front desk agent that seemed overworked and didn't really care to be on duty. The front desk failed to deliver on room location requests, and failed to inform on delivery options for a guest folio or receipt. Apparently you have a choice between emailed folio or delivery to your room. I now wonder if there was a similar choice for newspapers that I was never offered.
Once in my room, I enter to find all the lights off. Guests shouldn't have to fumble for their phones and flashlights simply to turn on a bedroom lamp. The room otherwise was ok. It appeared clean, but was slightly on the small side. There were no offensive odors, but it seemed within fifteen minutes any time I entered the room I began to feel stuffed up and suffered from sneezes. I found it odd the closet lacked a luggage rack, and housekeeping never replaced the laundry bag taken from the closet.
The bathroom was sized appropriately with plenty of space to operate, but seriously lacked towels. I'm all for helping the environment, but leaving a room only stocked with two towels is laughable. They didn't even have a bath mat. Just two bath towels, two hand towels and one wash cloth. I was not pleased. I requested more towels and it took 23 minutes to deliver what would be considered a full towel set. The shower had rust marks on the tub floor and was in need of a full tub replacement. There was a mystery hole in the ceiling above the bathtub.
Bedding wise they offered decent pillows, blankets and sheets, but no fitted mattress cover. So every morning you wake up with a sheet curled under your feet, or feet touching a bare, dirty, disgusting mattress. How can a brand name, so-called full service, hotel not offer a fitted sheet for a mattress? That's something you'd expect from a bad motel.
The Sheraton's hallways and common areas were very dirty during my stay. There were many empty beer bottles just left on the floor in the morning. I came back one night to find a housekeeper's vacuum just laying the floor in the hallway. I think this location needs serious help when it comes to the housekeeping department. Additionally, they need to stop with the cheap green initiatives. It's one thing to save a couple bucks on the lights or skimp on towels, but now they've permanently lost my business because of those aggravations. If I wanted to be green, I'd go camping, I wouldn't stay at a hotel. At a hotel I have a minimum level of expectations that help me with my business travel, this hotel did not meet even minimum requirements.

title_masked: Great to see the old and the new
text_masked: We lived in a Chicago suburb for many years. We went back for a long weekend.... primarily to attend friends daughter's wedding. The out of town wedding guests stayed at the Crowne Plaza-The Metro right near Greek Town so we joined them there. Great amenities at the hotel. We stayed in a king two room suite and it was spacious and comfortable. Good customer service and a great location. We walked or used cabs so no need for a car. The reception was at the Carnivale Restaurant nearby. A funky, fun, colorful place. Walked home safely late at night.

title_masked: Charged for a no show and showed poor customer experience
text_masked:
I recently booked and reserved a recent tripped through this hotel after reading great reviews. I booked in a week in advance in which I received an email saying a confirmation email will be sent shortly through my inbox and not my spam box. After a few days of worrying and nearing the the date I needed a hotel I called the front desk to check if my reservation went through. I gave them my credit card and first and last name. She checked and said I was not in the system or not reserved. I decided to give it time and gave it a few days. I called again a few days later and talked with a different front desk. Again gave them my credit card and name, the person checked again and multiple times. I asked are you sure, she sorry it didn't go through. As it was a days before I needed a hotel, I was forced to book at a later hotel thinking (since I was told) the order never went through.
Surprise surprise three weeks later as I was doing my company card review period it magically popped up with a $320 dollar charge. I guess it went through after all. I called both the reservation department and accountant department to get this resolved, they were far from having an a class customer service. No one answered in their supposed work time where I left voicemails. Finally I was able to talk to one couple days later in which she said sorry you were a no show. I kindly and professionally explain the situation where her own employees told me I was not in the system and I didn't have a room. She explained I should've still came and since I didn't then she'll still charge me the full price for not even coming!!!
I'm with a company and well tell everyone in my company not to use this hotel. Robbed me and I am disputing this charge as I refuse the company to pay for a room I never stayed in. It's as if she gave n excuse for her employees and nickel and dime the customers.

We had a great stay at Hotel 31 on a mid-May trip to NYC. It is conveniently located near the green subway line, a couple of stops from Union Square and Grand Central. The hotel was very clean, we always spotted cleaners at work. The rooms were a little small but comfortable...not nearly as small as I was expecting (pictures of the rooms may be a bit mis-leading. We didn't run into any problems with the shared washrooms, they were never busy.

title_masked: Another fantastic stay at Affinia Dumont
text_masked:
We have stayed at the Affinia Dumont a few times and each time we return, we are met with consistent excellent accommodations and customer service. Many thanks to the front desk staff of Karen and Trang. They really went the extra mile to make our stay outstanding.
The location cannot be beat - you are a few blocks from the subway and within walking distance of the best parts of Manhattan. We walked to Union Square and Gramercy Park and back and forth to Radio City Music Hall and Rockefeller Center.
The rooms are very large, especially by NYC standards, and the kitchen is a wonderful bonus. The decor is very pleasing and kept very well up to date. You cannot beat the value for this NYC gem.
We had a great stay and will certainly be back!

title_masked: Sofitel (DC) continues to deliver quality accommodation in a great location
text_masked: Sofitel is always our hotel of choice when in the nation's capital; we have also stayed at Sofitel in New York, and the quality of both hotels has been consistently good. The DC hotel is at the corner of 15 Street NW and H Street; as such, it is convenient for walking to major landmarks, such as The White House, the Mall, and major museums. This time we had a package which included valet parking and breakfast; for under $300, including all taxes, this seems a good deal for a quality hotel in a capital city. The breakfast choice was extensive and excellently prepared and presented; it was not just a buffet-style breakfast. The room and its king-size bed was spacious and well appointed (see photos). We had a great stay.

First, let me say that I'm a fan of history so I was thrilled to have the chance to stay in a historic hotel, especially one as iconic as the Congress Plaza Hotel. I was still pretty excited when I walked into the lobby and saw all the beautiful mosaics, gilding, and antiques. However, the first indication of what would be a pretty lousy stay was the staff person when I checked in. He was totally "checked out" (pun intended!) and didn't seem to really give off a great customer service vibe. That goes for almost all of the front desk staff I encountered. Most of them seemed to be high school/college age and had terrible phone etiquette and customer service. They really did not match the pseudo-luxury the hotel seems to try to convey. 
More importantly though, my floor smelled like dead fish. It was pretty awful. I have a feeling they knew it smelled weird because they had a window open to air it out. This window was WIDE OPEN with no screen on the eleventh floor. What a lawsuit that could have been!
Also, what year is it? 2003? How is this hotel still charging for internet?
 One nice thing - I had to print a huge document, and the manager let me email it to the front desk and printed it for me for free. That was really kind. They were also nice enough to let you store your luggage for free and have a special room for laptops, but it took a looong time for security to come and open the room so you could get your bag. Glad I didn't need to catch a flight. 
As for the room itself, it was okay. The bathroom was pretty modern, but most of the room was kind of dingy. 
Next time I go to Chicago for business I will definitely stay at a newer hotel. I assumed they had the same sort of amenities that other expensive downtown hotels have, but I was wrong. Maybe that's why it's so hard to find information about their amenities on their website. It is clear that this hotel spends a lot to make sure that the lobbies and public areas look nice and fancy but that they clearly don't put the same effort into maintaining the rooms and making sure their front desk staff does a good job. The security guards were really nice and helpful though. It was mostly the front desk people that had sassy attitudes and acted really unprofessional.
UGH.

First of all, Teddys restaurant is disgusting. The food is horrible, a whole bunch of flys were in the dinning room, service sucked badly but the best thing ws the breakfast. I would never eat at this place for lunch or dinner. The best thing about this hotel were the rooms but there was a cigarette hole in my friends top cover. Stay here for price but nothing else. Front desk staff was nice.

This was our first time to america, and if this had been the only place we were to visit we would not go again.
I had read the reviews before our visit and they were good and bad but we decided to give the hotel the "benifit of doubt" how wrong we were and i so wish i had changed, on arrival staff positivley rude not even welcome to the hotel, the room had not been cleaned properly from previous occupants shower basin full of hair, acute lack of towels.
Someone tried to break into our room whilst we were in there luckily we had the bar across they had got their foot in the gap my husband had to push hard on the door, we told reception again not intrested, no appology and certainly no security walking around. This understanderly (happened within a couple of hours of arrival) made us uneasy for the remainder of our stay, in fact i felt that i couldnt wait to move on.
The room was not cleaned properly throughout our stay and supply of towel hit & miss.
Our last evening we had an early morning flight so had to leave the hotel at 3.30 - 4am to get to Newark we asked for an early call, didnt get it luckily a storm had kept us awake on and off we were checking out my husband asked why we didnt get the call and did he realise that we could miss our flight responce shrug of shoulders, no interest what so ever.
You would have thought that the hotel staff would be at least welcoming on your arrival and security in the hotel high especially in New York but that is certainly not the case
So i have to say it is a great great shame as the hotel is in a good position but management and staff are extremely lacking and would certainly not class this hotel as 4* and this experience has put us off ever going back to New York again which is a great shame that one experience can give such a bad impression on a country

title_masked: Disappointing room in a grand hotel
text_masked:
The Biltmore LA is an older, very historic hotel in downtown Los Angeles. The architecture is beautiful, the public rooms are well maintained to preserve the feel of the original building. The staff are very polished, from Valet to Check-in to restaurant servers. The car valets do an exceptionally good job, as this hotel is very busy, traffic in and out of the hotel is constant. The valet service is a well-oiled machine. The lobby is quite grand, and I suggest you take the time to look up at the ceilings, the crown mouldings, the decor. It's elegant and inviting. 
After such a nice welcome, we were very disappointed in our room assignment. While I appreciate the age of the hotel, and understand that upkeep is herculean, our room was probably the worst hotel room I've ever been in. It was small, dark, cramped, the furnishings somewhat shabby. The plantation shutters were broken. The bathroom was definitely the worst hotel bathroom I've ever been in. With my arms extended, I could touch the two opposing walls simultaneously. The tub was very old and grimy, the toilet very industrial looking, a pedestal sink with very cheap fixtures had a crack in the porcelain. There was one slab of granite, about 3 ft by 6 in that served as the only available shelving. The towels were very well used, and limited in supply.
On a more positive note, the bed was quite comfortable, the duvet was a good weight, the pillows also very comfortable. 
The rooms are noisy; again, it's an old building and you can hear the plumbing activity of your neighbors.
The costs do add up quickly. We had an event rate of $99.00/night, but with taxes, parking fee ($40.00/night!!!), etc, our bill for just one night was $176.00. 
My advice : be very specific about your room assignment. And be prepared for the mounting additional costs.

The Grand Hyatt was recently remodelled and not just the lobby. The rooms, which in my opinion are the most important part were remodled inside and out and are very nice and comfortable. The bathrooms look like something I have only seen in 4 Seasons Hotels and the rooms themselves are very relaxing with warm colors, nice art, 32" flat panel TV's and comfortable beds and furniture. The service, from folks at the counter, to the valet and just staff walking around the hotel were friendly and very helpful. The location is perfect if you just want to park the car and forget about it. Everything is close, Ruth's Chris & Starbucks are right in the hotel and then you have many top restaurants and stores within a few blocks as well as Pike Street Market. If you can get a room for under $225 I would rate it 5 stars

From the window of our suite, we could see the fountain, the cathedral and with a little neck craning, the Barnes, reminders of what an elegant city we were visiting.
That's the best word to describe the Four Seasons--elegant. But the hotel is also understated. It doesn't have the razzle-dazzle of, say, the Ritz-Carlton at L.A. Live. It doesn't need to. It is the right amount of luxury. The only thing that keeps it from being a total five star: The bathroom was dated and didn't have enough counter space.
And, by the way, I want to marry that bed.

We are a family of 3, just spent 1 night at this hotel. It was a last-minute trip, as we had just visited Gettysburg and saw that Baltimore was just an hour away, so we decided to go to the Inner Harbor and the Aquarium since we were so close!
Hotels very close to the Harbor are VERY expensive. This hotel was .38 miles (or something like that) from the harbor and aquarium at less than half of the price other hotels a little closer go for.
Location: 6 blocks down and 2 blocks over and you are at the Harbor. The hotel has no parking but is adjacent to a parking deck. We paid $26 to park over night. The area is not the best, but there were a lot of public safety officers on every block. Still, I don't think I would be too comfortable walking in the dark. Unfortunately, like many urban areas, there are a lot of homeless folks in the area. 
Our room was VERY tiny. I think the bathroom was, possibly, the smallest bathroom I have ever seen! You had to be in the bathroom. negotiate yourself kind of next to/behind the door to close it! The sink was located outside of the bathroom. The room had 2 full size beds (or double, but not queen). Bedding was okay except they use those tiny pillows that are not comfortable. But, full sized pillows for 2 people would not fit on the bed. The room was very small and I would not have wanted to spend more than one night here with the 3 of us in one room. 
Breakfast was typical for a "free" breakfast...egg and sausage, make your own waffles, bread and muffins, cereal/oatmeal packets, coffee, tea, juice. It was as expected.
I would probably stay here again just for the price, but only if it was an overnighter.

The outside of the hotel and the lobby were deceiving because it looks very nice until you get to the room. The room was very dark and small for a king suite. The decor was very old fashioned. However, the room was clean. The front desk, housekeeping, and the rest of the staff was very friendly. They had quite a spread for breakfast! It is in a great location. They only have 1 washer and 1 dryer which made it difficult when you are there for a week with a 7 year old ball team. The 1 dryer didn't work half the time we were there. I went down the street to a laundrymat to wash clothes.

This was our first time staying at a St. Regis hotel and if our stay this time was any indication, we will DEFINITELY be returning. The staff was superior, the hotel is stunning, and the location could not be better. The hotel concierge and doormen are especially responsive to customer needs and from the moment we entered the hotel, everyone demonstrated 5 star customer service. The amenities and cleanliness were features that I found especially appealing. I highly recommend it!

tired older motel at a fair price. toilets, shower/tub need replacing (stained, ugly), good ac.
older tv, good chanel selections.

title_masked: Not a hotel to stay with your family.
text_masked: I booked the hotel online just because it said RAMADA. When i went to the hotel it was a terrible site and it looked like a very old motel. Motel 6 is better than this hotel. I paid the top dollar to stay in a nice hotel but it was a very bad stay. Its not a family place. You don't want to spend time with your family at this place. Moreover this hotel looks like a one night stay hotel for the people coming from Bars and pubs.

The staff was friendly and the service was average. The room was outdated and not exceptionally clean; below average. But the price was decent and it was near the airport. For the 10 hours I was there, it did the job.

I went here for a Conference in February 2012. The rooms were very clean, the staff was very friendly and extremely helpful, and the hotel was very beautiful. I would LOVE to stay here again. It was the best hotel I have ever stayed in!
I have stayed in this hotel before it was a Wyndham. Nice changes to the hotel! I love the location.

Stayed at the Edison Hotel April 15 + 16, 2012, for what was likely my 15th visit to said hotel. I travel to NYC about 3 - 4 times a year. I've stayed at the very expensive hotels and some cheaper, then I discovered the gem of the Edison. Like evrything else - it's all about location, this hotel is literally steps from Times Square. The staff extremely helpful, polite + friendly. Housekeepers give a warm smile and hello daily, the front desk people are more then helpful + professional, right down to the two brothers at the front door who will help you any way they can.
The hotel is quiet, clean and safe, you have to show room key card to access elevators. 
The rooms with 2 queen or 2 doubles are big rooms The rooms with single beds are smaller, and the bathrooms are small - but no one I know goes to NYC to spend time in the toilet. 
This hotel is CLEAN, SAFE + AFFORDABLE, don't be worried about reserving here.

title_masked: Good rooms, Strange/Rude Staff, Copy your Credit Card
text_masked:
I stayed at this property based on last minute availability, price, and location. The property definitely has a motel feel as you drive in and enter the lobby area. I always take price ($140 a night) and star level into consideration when I review hotels (motels in this case). With that being said let’s review the good and the bad. 
The Good: The location was on Sunset Blvd and I found it to be a safe area for walking to restaurants, coffee, gym, and the 24 hour grocery store directly across the street. I was pleasantly surprised on the room itself, yeah it wasn't updated like the Hilton but it wasn't nearly as bad as I was expecting from the tacky neon Saharan Hotel sign on Sunset Blvd. The room put you in the mind of a Motel 6 with old furniture but comfortable. The internet was totally free and worked great on both of my devices during my entire stay. Fridge and microwave in the room.
The Bad: I wasn't impressed with how clean the room was, I kept finding hairballs in my room and that was after housekeeping cleaned it. For the record I am bald and proud! The staff was not very friendly and helpful at all when asking questions. I asked very few questions but I got nasty attitude with the answer every time. They actually make a photo copy of your credit card when you check in. This is obviously a big security risk and when I asked the employee about it he stated "oh we want use it for anything else." That's great that every staff member is so honorable and would never steal the thousands of credit cards numbers the hotel has on file (sarcasm). There is a reason credit card imprints went away and the Saharan needs to step into the secure 21st century. The room entrance and windows surround the pool so the noise levels from the pool to include a man (who I think was a staff member because he was cleaning the pool) playing a wooden flute (see attached picture) were totally annoying at 10:00 in the morning. He was also doing some wierd religous chant that made people come out their rooms and stare. I could also hear kids very early in the morning jumping in and out of the pool. I think there are rooms located on the backside of the hotel so you might want to request a room away from the noisy pool. The television remote only worked for the volume but would not change the station, and all the television channels were fuzzy.

We escaped for the weekend and the Palomar SD was a great place. The hotel decor is awesome and staff wonderful. Kimpton is our first choice in any city and places like the Palomar are why!
The Palomar is located within walking distance to the Gas Lamp Quarter, Seaport Village, Harbor, Little Italy and more.

This is a relatively small hotel in an excellent position - 1 minute walk and you are in Times Square!. It has an excellent bistro type restaurant which is very convenient to take breakfast in. Many bars and restaurants are nearby and If we ever return to New York, we would stay here again.

We had a wonderful stay and the Hotel proximity to the Space Neddle, Art Museum, Pike's Market, Aquarium and fine dinning was all within walking distance.
We had a great lunch at Cafe Presse on Capital Hill and Enjoyied Wine & Dinning at Le Pichet at 1st & Virginia 3 blocks from the hotel.

title_masked: Great Stay!! Great Location!! Great Staff!!
text_masked:
In the service industry, it is the little things that really set places apart. The Catamaran really shines on the little things.
I got a really early start, and went to the Catamaran about 8:30 am or so to check it out and to see what the neighborhood was like. I stopped at the front desk to see when the best time to check in would be. I was only staying one night, so I did not expect them do do very much in the way of accommodating an early check in. Sure enough, they didn't have any rooms ready for me, and the best time to check in on a Saturday is around 4:00pm. I was a bit disappointed to hear this, because I wanted to spend some time on the beach. But then he said that he had a room that was scheduled to be out of circulation for maintenance. What he would do was he would give me a card for that room, I could put my luggage in there, use the key to go in and out of the parking lot, use the key to get to the beach or the pool, and use the room to take a shower in. At 4pm, just see him and he would give me the key for our actual room for the night.
He then gave me some great recommendations for on breakfast and coffee places around the hotel. Just great service. At 4pm, there was an envelope at the front desk with our room keys. 
No muss no fuss! 
The room was clean, and just as we ordered. We were in the 700 block of rooms and found it to be very quiet. We spent a great night.
The beach was a white sand beach that is combed daily. It is free from glass or anything else that might cut your feet. Very close by there is a place that is operated by the hotel to rent, paddle boards, little sail boats, and even jet skis. Complementary beach umbrellas and chairs were right on the beach as well. There weren't very many of these, so you have to get to the beach early to claim them.
The little things matter, and the front desk could have very easily just said, "Come back at 4" and done with me. Instead they went the extra mile to make my stay very enjoyable!

title_masked: This Hilton Hotel could stand some IMPROVEMENTS: Brian are you listening?
text_masked:
I checked into this hotel with an expectation that this would meet Hilton Hotel Standards. It does not. I wonder (and did not ask) if this was a franchise property or Hilton Corporate, not that it excuses my observations. I see the Manager's apology, but as of today, this hotel is no better than the worst reviews. I stay in hotels about 100 or more nights a year, so yes, I know hotels. By the way, I was told he works "normal" business hours: 9-5. Not even banks work those hours any more.
Here are my observations. (Room 813)
1. Arrival went without incident and was efficient. Staff at desk were friendly, but when asked about why they did not honor my HHonors room request they just said that the hotel was "busy."
2. It looked like there was new carpet in my room but the room looked old and tired. See attached picture of the "blond" work desk with missing hardware on the drawer.
3. The bed was clean and comfortable, and this was a saving grace.
4. See the picture of the mold growing on the grout in the shower. There is NO excuse why housekeeping had not reported this and corrected it.
5. The HHonors lounge was a small living room. There were very few tables and this room was obviously dedicated to drinking and TV watching. At breakfast there was almost no place to sit where one could actually eat.
The hotel itself looks dated and could use a bit of refurbishing. I did order room service once and it was good, but pricy for what I got.
I would have to think twice about staying here again. The only reason I would return would be the bed and, oh yes, the nifty way you can control your TV with your iPhone. No need to handle the nasty TV remote.

We stayed four nights in this hotel that is more like a bed&breakfast than a hotel. The breakfast offers a small selection ( not just coffee and rolls). The staff is very friendly and obviously anxious to please us. We chose to not drive in city so we needed information on trolleys, buses,and subways which we were cheerfully given. Most of the guests are friendly and shared advice and opinions about restaurants etc. A real treat for me was to converse with a young woman who is a ballerina with the SF Opera Company next door!

title_masked: I knew the room wasn't going to be spacious, but still.........
text_masked:
This is the smallest hotel I've stayed in all my 42 years. Small as in narrow, with petit furniture more suited to the borrowers than your averaged sized human. We had a double double room for our family of two adults and two children aged 8 and 14. A rollaway bed was definately not an option that could have been considered. I wasn't expecting a room of palatial sizing, after all this is New York and the rates at the HIE are very reasonable. But if you're going to book this place beware that the wardrobe is about 12 inches wide and deep and there are three small drawers. If you decide to unpack there is nowhere to put your suitcases/bags. Its the first time I've ever had to use the top of the wardrobe for storage space! The bathroom is tiny, standing in the middle of the room it was easily possible to touch each wall, and there wasn't enough space for toiletries. The hotel is around 22 stories high with 6 or so rooms to each floor so although a higher room means you don't experience street noise, you won't be far from the lift which ever floor or room you're in. Breakfast is complimentary - bacon, sausage patties, scrambled egg, omlettes, mini bagels and croissants, toast, pancakes, cereals, fruit, juice and coffee but as with everything here the breakfast area is small and cramped and doubes up as the hotel lobby.
Housekeeping start early as do the business guests, so expect noise including the slamming of doors and housekeeping from around 6:30. 
What this place lacks in space it makes up for in location - its perfectly situated between 5th and 6th Avenue with Broadway and Times Square a very short walk away and the Rockerfeller Centre. Grand Central Station and Central Park within easy walking distance as are many subway stations. There are lots of places to eat and shop locally and after all, you don't come to New York to stay in your hotel room.

title_masked: highway noise ruins otherwise good value hotel
text_masked: With a friendly staff, clean, relatively spacious rooms for the price that include a refrigerator, microwave, free internet and extended breakfast hours, it's too bad that noise from the freeway is so loud. I'm a heavy sleeper, so it didn't keep me awake, but it was unpleasant. I wouldn't recommend this to anyone unless freeway noise really doesn't bother you.

Conviently located between the airport and downtown, I was able to get everywhere by public transport. It is located just down the hill from Little Italy which is full of good bars and restaurants.
The room was very clean, plenty of towels, TV had lots of premium channels, the only drawback was a lack of fridge.
I would definatley stay here again and have no problems recommending it.

title_masked: Very, very good. VALET is the only problem: $70 a night...
text_masked:
Everything about this hotel is top notch. Private concierge on the club lounge is amazing. Please ask for Starsky, very good concierge. The location near Union Square, Chinatown and cable car lines is very convenient. Great dinner recommendations from the concierge. Very restful and satisfying stay. 
Prefers to stay at 8th floor

This was My first trip to Chicago, attending a wedding which was held at the JW. We totally enjoyed the accommodations our room was spacious with an extremely comfortable bed. We were provided all the essentials, coffee, iron, hair dryer, complimentary water bottles. The bathroom was beautifully laid out and the tub was a deep soaking tub that easily could accommodate two people. I enjoyed a nice soak, totally relaxing. We had drinks in the lobby bar which was a fun spot with lots of people. Breakfast at the Florentine was over the top delicious! This hotel is in the financial district so it is a little distance from shopping etc. but not so far that you can't walk to the area attractions.

This is my second time staying at this Four Seasons. As one would expect from a 5 star hotel with the Four Seasons name you are treated like gold from the moment you walk in. actually even before you walk in...as I pulled my car up to the front to check in, 4 different people ran over to the car to help us with luggage and check in. The front desk staff couldn't have been nicer or more accommodating to my needs. Many hotels in LA bend over backwards for the celebs staying there and forget about the 'other' guests, but not this hotel. They really managed to treat every single guest perfectly. At one point in my stay a famous movie producer was at reception and I had a question and had to pick something up at the desk. The person excused herself from him and attended to me immediately. Throughout my stay I was addressed by my name and every need I had which was many was attended without hesitation. I highly recommend this hotel over others that I have stayed at in the area.

My sisters came for a visit and we wanted to spend a night downtown. We were worried about the size of the room, because there were four of us. I got the two queen room for four and let me tell you, they couldn't believe how big and beautiful it was. We had a corner room with big windows that overlooked the river is fabulous. Our night pictures from the room are incredable. It is just a short walk to shopping, restaurants and all we wanted to do, plus 24 hour parking and Panera right next door. The beds were the BEST!!! Hard to please four sisters, but they did 100%.

title_masked: A Breath of Fresh and Rejuvenating Air
text_masked:
I have a new favorite hotel in my home city of New York, and it is the Gansevoort in the so-called meatpacking district of New York. The staff could not be nicer and more welcoming. My wife and I live near the big city, but staying at the Gansvoort allows us to have a quick and easy mini vacation, especially with that heated pool on the roof top.
We liked it so much the first time we stayed that we booked it again the following weekend.

We just returned from our trip to NYC. We have stayed in many hotels (including the Waldorf Towers) and my family and I agree The London is the best of all. Best value, large rooms, exceptionally clean and the location cannot be beat. I don't know why some people complained because we have nothing but good things to say about the London. The personnel were friendly, the food was delicious and we even got to see a few celebrities who were staying there!
We were so happy with The London that it has now become our go to hotel in NYC. We will be back!

My mother and 2 young daughters stayed at this hotel recently. It was a great choice. Rooms were nice, not cramped, lobby was cheerful and clean. All of the staff were wonderful, especially Eric who helped me out with a luggage problem. I will stay there next time I go to NY!!

Our 3rd trip to the Harrington, may, 2012, convenient to walk to most major sights, Smithsonians, White House, Ford's Theater, Old Post Office, 1/2 block from Pennsylvania where you can catch a bus to take you to the National Cathedral or in the opposite direction to the Capitol, we ate in both restaurants and found them good, very good for prices and service, 5 old gals stayed in the large room on the 6th floor, 2 doubles, 3 twins, a refrigerator, arm chair, tv, bedside tables with lamps, only one bath, but we are travel veterans who travel together so we worked it out, plenty of clean towels, soap, very quiet considering it had quite a few school groups, they put the school groups on lower floors, if you want a view or luxury this is not your hotel, but if you are looking for a budget hotel with extras especially the location, the Harrington is for you. The beds were very comfortable which is important after a day walking around our Capitol.

Just stayed at this hotel in Dallas. One morning I was ready to leave and I could not get out of my room. My door was locked from the inside and the front desk was not picking up the phone. I thought that something may have happened overnight; if there had been an emergency, I would not have been able to get out of the room. Needless to say, you get what you pay for, although inexpensive, not worth the danger factor.

GREAT warm cookies on check in! Newspaper in the morning.This is an excellent place to stay. Hot breakfast and friendly helpful staff! They even provided a wheel chair for my mother in law who had just had eye surgery.

Nice hotel with very friendly staff and great location. Location was great, right in the center of everything we wanted to visit. The rooms were clean and comfortable. There were long waits for the elevator, but this could have been because all of the rooms were booked in this large hotel. We were not aware that The worlds largest Sci Fi convention that was happening while we were there (which was interesting to say the least) so it was quite busy. All in all it was a great stay and we would stay here again.

We just spent a delightful overnight at Hotel Commonwealth in the Baseball Suite--an upgrade courtesy of Ryan Burns, Front of House Manager. The last time my wife and I stayed at the Commonwealth, the heating system in our room was working overtime and couldn't be fixed. At check-out Ryan offered us an upgrade on our next visit. Well, he was as good as his word--better, in fact. Ryan put us in a Baseball-Themed Suite filled with signed baseballs, old photos, and other memorabilia. Beautiful, even for Yankee Fans!! Hotel Commonwealth runs like a precision watch. No fuss, no bother. Everything in place at the correct time. It's our new home in Boston.

My teenage daughter and I spent a weekend at the hotel and it really was a perfect stay. We obtained an excellent rate by paying in advance, received a large and well-appointed room overlooking Times Square and thoroughly enjoyed our stay. The staff was great and helpful, the room much bigger than I am used to in NYC, and seemed to have been recently renovated. If you want to be in or near Times Square, the location is ideal as it is just north of all the noise but easy walking distance to shows and other sights.

title_masked: Great mid price hotel in the district that has some character
text_masked: Ok look I wont lie. Id rather stay at the Mayflower it's closer in and all round more classy - but you pay a lot of that. The donovan house however is liek a New York hotel in DC. It's great. Got some substance feels European/Asian - great service. I stay here every year. Sometimes light seeps in round the curtains this they should address as I mention it - every year!

the room was at the end of a hallway , so much for a view and the bed felt as though it was broken and kinda sagged to the middle. the room was a jr. suite and for the money it was apporopriate, just needed a new bed ;)

title_masked: DO NOT STAY HERE, It's a SCAM
text_masked: So my family and one of my dad's friend who came out here to visit from Dubai decided to stay here for labor's day weekend. We didn't have much choice on Saturday night since most of the hotels were already booked. Before we booked it we went in for price inquiry for two rooms. The manager was an Indian guy, since we also have an Indian origin, he told us how he's giving us the best price in town and told us the total for two rooms would be $225. we were OK with it even though not satisfied since we didn't have much choice. My uncle introduced himself to the manger and spoke little Arabic and told him he's here for vacation.My uncle decided to pay for the rooms while we decided to settle in. Thirty minutes later once we checked in my uncle came in my room and told me that Manager charged him $500 for two rooms. I was shocked and confused at the same time. Smelled something fishy so I decided to pay the Manager a visit. I asked him about the charge and he said oh I told you guys the price for one room, when in reality "per room" wasn't mentioned anywhere when he told us the price. When I started arguing with him that this isn't right and no one in their right mind would pay $225 for these disgusting rooms, he started threatening me with COPS. I asked him I no longer wish to stay here and would want my full refund, he told me he will only give me 50% back and not a penny more (and this all happened within the first hour once we checked in). He eventually ended up calling the COPS, saying that I am harassing him and threatening to harm which was total bs. I feel like he took advantage of my uncle who he knew was out of States and didn't know much. Stay away from this lodge as much as possible. It's a total rip off. The Cops who showed up believed my story, even though they couldn't do much since it was a civil matter, they suggested that I file my complaint with Better Business Bureau.

title_masked: Perfect spot to enjoy all of Boston
text_masked: Stayed here for New Year's Eve. And even though the hotel was busy with revelers, this never disturbed our stay. I love that the hotel is easy to get to, has great parking, and access to several new hot spots on the waterfront. The room was just perfect - luxurious bed, comfortable furnishings, and just the right touch for bath items.

title_masked: They know how to define Luxury Collection
text_masked:
The San Francisco Palace Hotel was a wonderful retreat on a fun SF weekend. The staff, location and rooms were all perfect with a special nod to the staff. The staff took great care of my wife and I, the other friends we were traveling with and were always pleasant, friendly and helpful in any situation we had (like directions, ideas etc.) They know how to define “Luxury Collection” in every way, shape and form!
All I have to say is that the next time I’m in San Francisco, I will stay at the Palace!!!

Grand old hotel showing a bit of her age but I happen to like that. Quite a bit of history there and with a little imagination you can picture her in her prime. Location is outstanding and the price was great for Chicago standards. Outstanding view from my Lakeview King room. Request a high floor. Some downsides- thin walls so if you're a late sleeper you're in trouble. My room was small but clean and comfortable. There was a strike in progress(never did find out what that was about) so you had to go in the side door to avoid crossing the picket line. This hotel is not for everyone but if you like old hotels with character stay here.

Plz share our experience with other travelers. Recently spent 3 nights at the Crowne Plaza Hotel in Austin Texas and the service was 2nd to none. Roy at concierge gave us an outstanding quick tour of the downtown area. Tim (manager) and Kevin (assistant manager) managed to get us an extra day when occupancy rate was 103%, with 2 major conventions in town, and Auggie in the restaurant made us an incredible breakfast after the breakfast buffet was done for the morning. There was never a problem they couldn't resolve and they loved doing there job. Being in the entertainment/service industry at Universal Studios Orlando, these are the type of employees that make a great vacation, memorable! Wonderful experience, Thank You, Bruce Eakin Orlando

The outdoor pool had leaves floating as well as many on the floor of the pool. The water was murky; no one was using the pool. The sink handle was dirty from the previous guest. There is no free computer in the lobby like many of the Super 8 hotels have. There was a sewer odor in the bathroom. Leaving the bathroom fan on all night did not remove the odor.

I am an SPG Platinum member and just had a great stay at the W Times Square. I had booked 8 rooms for my friends 40th birthday celebration. We had many special requests and the staff (Jenna in particular) made sure everything was perfect. While this is a large property in the middle of Times Square they provide excellent personalized service you would only expect in a smaller boutique property. I have now stayed at just about every Starwood property in NYC and the W Times Square will be my first choice on my future trips to New York.

Although I had asked for a room on the higher floors, the hotel was fully booked so I spent the first night in an extremely noisy room on the 3rd floor. The next day, I moved to a slightly smaller room on the 17th floor, which was much quieter. 
The Paramount Bar is fun but be careful: a 18% tip is automatically added to the bill. I didn't pay attention so I left another 20% tip! When I got my hotel bill at the end of my stay, I noticed the huge tip amount and mentioned it at the front desk. The manager immediately refunded the 20%.

I stayed here for 1 night only during my short trip to NY. The hotel is at a pretty convenient location - 52th street is near everywhere. Room and bed are cozy and comfortable. I order food at 2 in the morning and got it at the front door less than 30 minutes. I took their Limousin service to the airport, it's very convenient and fast at a reasonable price. I would stay at this hotel again should I return to NY for another biz trip.

The hotel just finish renovation. So new carpet, new paint. Antique Bank door and other decoration with ages.The bedding is warm and comfy. The bathroom is giant with rain shower.Hotel restraurant is reasonal priced and provide corn bread with jalapino. Free shuttle bus within downtown. Front desk has many cellpjone charge if you forget yours.
My room has big windows from both side and sardin curtain looks really nice. Only complain is no blackout curtains. 
There is no swimming pool. The gym is in basement with bright red color equipments. But I didn't try.

I read about the over the top service at all Kimberly hotels, and that's what made me decide to stay at Hotel Palomar for a recent girlfriend weekend get away. I was not disappointed, in fact my expectations were overwhelmed! It was clear in every interaction how happy the staff is making your visit exactly what you want it to be. We drove up to a warm, welcoming reception from the bellhop/doorman who helped us unpack the car with much warmth and assistance? Upon check in we were told we missed the wine reception and immediately given vouchers to enjoy a glass from the bar at our convenience, nice start?
The room was a dbl queen room. Nothing special, kind of small, but very! Very clean. We planned on spending time in the room! So I called the front desk to ask if they could bring up a 2nd chair, or move us to a room that had seating for two. This is where things became unbelievable, and our amazing visit began. We were fortunate enough to be speaking with Grant, who without missing a beat said he thought the Presidential Suite extension room would be more to our liking and offered to come up immediately to move us. WOW, what a treat! I don't know which was our greater fortune, moving to the 23rd floor room with breath taking city views and extra space including a lovely chaise, or meeting Grant. Fortunate for us Grant was working all weekend, and from that point on we were in his care. He took the extra effort to ensure every aspect of our stay worked just right for us including making perfect restaurant recommendations and suggesting an ideal venue for live music. But fear not if he's not around, because EVERY other employee we dealt with had a similar approach to ensure we were happy. And it never felt that they were going through the motions, always that they were doing from their heart and really cared. They set the standard of top service in every department - even the housekeeping were incredibly considerate and professional. Having arrived late for coffee and tea in the morning, another person who was clearing the service went out of her way to bring us fresh cups of tea and pastry to us while we lounged at the lobby fireplace. Even the valet went beyond, with a can do attitude and never making us feel put out even when we asked him to look in our car for our misplaced cell phone. 
We visited the Ritz while walking around the city, and the staff also seemed friendly and welcoming, the hotel stunning, but if I returned I would stay nowhere else but Hotel Palomar!

title_masked: Looking for a place to stay in Chicago??....Here it is...
text_masked:
Had the chance to visit Chicago with my exchange student son from Belgium. We stayed here at the Carlton Inn Midway for several reasons: price, cleanliness, location and hospitality.
I made the reservation a few days before the trip, and a day later received an email from the manager (Gary) welcoming me back. He asked how many sons I was bringing this time. I was pleased to think he would remember our last visit, and how he made friends with my kids. Nice to know they take the time to be friendly, and extend a welcome even before we open the door.
Our room was well prepared, clean,and ready for us to call it our home away from home. Located just a few blocks from the Pulaski Orange line to downtown Chicago, the free shuttle was a blessing ride to shelter us from the cold and windy elements. We were even shuttled to a few area restaurants to sample "CHICAGO STYLE PIZZA", and an excellent beef sandwich.
While in Chicago, we visited the Museum of Science and Industry, the Sears (Willis) Tower, and did some shopping on the miracle mile...did not have time to visit Navy Pier or Hard Rock Cafe.
Many excellent restaurants in the area....ask at the front desk on where to experience some excellent Polish cuisine. Don't forget the continental breakfast....and bring your laptop computer as there is a wireless internet connection.
At a cost well below what you would pay for a room closer to downtown, do not hesitate to give this place a try. You won't be sorry.
Mike
P.S. Make sure you say hi to Buddy....

The Homewood Suites was a perfect place for our Seattle experience. The art museum had a Gauguin exhibit that was fabulous and a pleasant walk from Homewood. We also enjoyed a symphony very close to our hotel. The staff was helpful, the breakfast very nice and the room was great. The parking is a little steep but that's life in a big city. A good value.

This hotel was okay I guess.. I was hoping for better though. The location was good, and the staff was nice... They suggested a few restaurants to us and held our bags free of charge after we checked out (before our bus left). But, the rooms are very out-dated. On my first night there, the heater broke and I had to move to a different room. And further more, I didn't have time to move my stuff to a new room at the time (I was getting ready to go somewhere), but they told me that I had to be out of my current room in the next 2 hours. In my next room, the TV made a very loud buzzing sound every time it was turned on. All in all, I was satisfied with my stay there.. but a bit disappointed. It was one of the cheaper hotels I could find, but if I were to return to Chicago I would probably not stay there again.. You could probably find a nicer hotel in that area of town for only a slightly higher price.

title_masked: A good perch for seeing LA
text_masked:
I found agreement with lots of others' comments here:
+Nice location in a swanky neighborhood...It felt very safe
+Free parking (As much as it was necessary to shell out for parking all over L.A., this was much appreciated)
+Friendly, attentive staff
+Small enough property that it does not overwhelm
+Cathedral ceilings gave the room a larger feel; without that it might have felt cramped
+Easy access to Santa Monica which ended up being one of my favorite spots to visit
-Breakfast choices are generally protein and nutrition-lacking (Mostly we ate breakfast out) 
-Easy driving distance to many attractions, but hardly walking distance to anything.
Would I stay there again? Why yes, in a heartbeat.

After the Fairfield Inn and Suites gave away our guaranteed reservation, I was reluctant to try to stay at another Marriott but this one held our guaranteed reservation. The location is right at Times Square and close to many theaters. Streets are very crowded but good for people watching. I liked the new elevators that have you put in your floor number and then indicates which elevator to take. This system prevents everyone crowding around the same elevator and elevators are not crowded. Some of the elevators are glass but only a few of the inside of the hotel. The room I had was on 38th floor and I had a few of the signs in Times Square that were bright and entertaining. There is a concierge floor where you can get free hor d'oeuvres and drinks but alcoholic beverages have a charge-$10.00 for a glass of wine. There is a long window with a view of Times Square. They are also open at breakfast time. The room was very clean and comfortable. It was quiet and there was a blackout curtain so sleep was easy. We didn't get to the revolving restaurant on the top but it would probably be fun. There are a lot of nearby theaters and plenty of restaurants in the area. The subway station is just a couple of blocks away. Taxis are always available. The cost is high but it was very nice.

The room was spacious with a comfortable king-size bed, smelled nice and had all the amenities for travelers that you would expect from a classical American hotel. It even had a microwave oven in addition to a desk, a big round table, chests, ironing board....
I was also impressed by the maids too. They tidied up my room asking for and taking into account my preferences. 
For $58 including tax and WiFi this was an amazing value for Los Angeles. 
The hotel is about half an hour drive to the Westside and less to Downtown LA. Not too bad. 
It has a nice pool, which I did not use.

title_masked: Nice Hotel in a Great location
text_masked: We stayed there one night at the end of July. The room was good size considering the location. Most other similarly priced hotels around there have very tiny rooms. It was clean, comfortable and had good service. We got an email prior to our arrival (perhaps because we are Hilton Honor members) from one of their staff members. So I called that person asking for help on Broadway play tickets and she was extremely helpful in finding the information for us. They also had discounted parking right in the same building. Sometimes we stay in a nearby NJ hotel and come in by bus to see a play. But I would say that if you are driving in just for a night or two and want to enjoy the full New York experience, this is a great place. It was worth the extra money because everything is within walking distance. We were able to get to places and if we needed a little rest in between activities, the hotel is close by.

title_masked: great location , all the rest is just awful.
text_masked:
perfect location you can easily reach times square and the hotel is in centre new york and has a nice view on the empire state depends wich room you got.
the room i got was dirty , very dusty.
the bathroom was dirty, the rooms were small.
th reception staff were rude and unpleasent .
had to wait 25 minutes till elevator arrived at my floor.
and most important no wifi access.

If your looking for a quiet place to get away I would suggest staying here. Clean, friendly
and not to expensive. I enjoy my stays everytime I come. I live in Jacksonville so when I need a quick get away I stay here.

title_masked: Great hotel & free shuttle ride t SeaWorld!
text_masked: We stayed at this hotel in the summer in August. It is a great hotel, with convenient locations all around. Very close to SeaWorld! The staff is very friendly and they go abouve and beyond to make your stay a great one. The best part of this stay is the free shuttle to Seaworld and the driver (can't remember his name) was awesome! He was just so sweet and very patient!! The only downfall was the free breakfast. They ran out of everything very quickly. I'll stay here again for sure!

I have stayed at this hotel when I'm in New York and I love the location. The hotel is right next to Grand Central and you don't even need to walk outside to get there. The rooms have been remodled and look nice and modern. During my stay the hotel was very crowded with teens that were there for some event. I had a concern and the next day Diane W. was kind enough to move me up to the VIP suite and I was given some breakfast coupons. She was very friendly and wanted me to be happy with my stay. The VIP suite is something else. I have never stayed in one like this. I hope her manager will read this because she is the reason I will keep coming back and I will recommend this hotel to my friends. She is what customer service is about.
The only "bad" thing I can say is the TV's need to be upgraded to HD. Overall, great place to stay. There is a nice breakfast place on the corner called [NAME]. Nice breakfast and reasonable prices.

My wife and I stayed at the Langham over this Labor Day weekend to do some sightseeing.
We'd never stayed at a hotel downtown so this was a new experience, but we're glad we chose this hotel. Valet, bell service, and check-in were great - the staff were super friendly and attentive. 
Our room was normal size for an urban center, and very nicely appointed. The TV was modern as was the thermostat. The bed was very comfortable and everything was clean! We really cannot complain about the condition of the room itself or the hallway, etc. 
I had a chance to use the jacuzzi/pool area and that too is very modern, clean, and nice. It was a little strange walking into the spa in order to get to the pool, that's something I wasn't accustomed to, but I guess it keeps the riff raff away!? I will say that the water at the shower *in* the pool area never got hot.
I will say is that the lobby is in the process of being renovated. It's not extremely noticeable, but we did find some exposed sheetrock and such. The elevators are also kind of scary, a little wobbly and old, like 1976 old. We were also turned off with the fact that we needed to pay for WiFi. With what we were paying for the weekend, that seemed a bit 'nickel-and-dimey.'
Other than that everything was else perfect.
I got a drink at the hotel bar, Bond, definitely worth a stop in before you go out for the night. You can't beat the location, you're within walking distance to the Aquarium and all that area has to offer, not to mention the dozens of bars, mostly of Irish persuasion!
Overall I'd say it's worth what we paid and I would certainly return another time.

Hyatt 48 Lex has managed to crack the code in terms of offering an end to end superior New York hotel experience. The concept here is a bit unique - a big brand name but a "boutique" format with just 6-ish rooms per floor with incredibly attentive and friendly staff. Rooms are new and nicely furnished and on the larger size by New York standards. Great TVs, coffee maker, fridge. HIgh speed wireless. Outside noise is minimal (but the higher up you are the better) and interior noise is non-existant. The hotel resaurant (Lexington Brass) is solid. The lounge on the 2nd (3rd?) floor is very nicely done - small but workable fitness room. The lobby is small - very "clean" lines/minimalist decor. Great mid-town location with easy access to Grand Central, shopping on 5th Ave, Roc Center - and if you don't mind a 15 or so min wall Theatre District/Times Square. The most impressive aspect of the hotel however is the staff - personable, friendly, go out of their way to help and make a connection (if you need something just find Carlos - most friendly, competent, helpful guy). Such a far cry from so many hotels (in and outside of NYC) who just run on the script/auto-pilot. And the rest of the team are as on the ball as this exceptional front desk team. Whenever I am in NYC this is my first port of call!

I stayed here while on a business trip for a week in Dallas. The staff are very friendly and very helpful. There is ample free parking right in front of the hotel, and you can either eat in or drive/walk to a couple of nearby places, including the Galleria. The lobby of the hotel is very nice and they even have two swans who inhabit a garden style pond in the center. The happy hour is great! I found it very enjoyable to just grab a glass of wine to take up to my room and unwind, however, there were many guests enjoying the happy hour right at the bar and it seemed an enjoyable and inviting atmosphere. 
I ordered room service a couple of times and delivery occurred in a very reasonable and relatively short amount of time. The food quality was average in taste and presentation (I'd order it again, but wouldn't go out of my way to eat there). I had a couple of different salads and some appetizers. I also had only coffee in the morning, but there was a nice breakfast set up for guests to enjoy. 
The room was clean with the usual amenities. I did not use the pool or fitness center, but did take a look at the pool...it was in a nice room with good atmosphere, but the pool is pretty small (if you're planning to swim for exercise). I did ask at the front desk about running outside and they said it was safe and that I could run in either direction along the street in front of the hotel, but that there were no parks nearby. I did run outside and found the lights take a long time to change and the cars aren't messing around there...they go fast and take no consideration for pedestrians. Regardless, I enjoyed my runs because I could get outside and see the area a little bit. The weather was gorgeous (last week of January-first week of February).

title_masked: Perfect Hotel for a Business Trip.
text_masked: In addition to great service, clean rooms and helpful people behind the desk, the free coffee and wine makes this a perfect place to stay.

I was in Dallas and needed a downtown hotel at the last minute. I called the 800# from my car and inquired about rooms. The young man I talked to sounded a little confused about which hotel I wanted. I told him the Dallas Omni, the new one at the convention center downtown. He found it and said the rate was $99. I was surprised and asked if that was the hotel on Lamar, donwntown at the convention center. He said yes. So I headed downtown to claim my room. 
The hotel driveway was really crowded and kind of chaotic with people directing traffic and confusing traffic barriers. I left my car with the valet ($25) and went to checkin. The nice young lady behind the desk couldn't find my reservation so I showed her the confimation # that had just arrived on my phone. She said that there was a mistake and I was booked at the Omni in Richardson...grrr. I told her that I needed to stay downtown. She said they had rooms for $169. I asked if she could match the 
price I was quoted, she said no and apologized. I was running late for an evening appointment so I took it. 
The lobby is huge and impressive and was full of youngsters attending the weekend volleyball event at the adjacent convention center.
My room was on the 7th floor. When entering the room there is a key port that contols the electricity inside the room( like most other countries) The room was average size and very stylish. It had several modern amenties like a motion sensored footlight that lights the floor for a night time trip to the bathroom, an in-mirror bathroom tv, floor to ceiling windows, a nice desk with two chairs, coffe maker and refrigerator but no mini bar, safe and robes.
The bed was very comfortable and the entire room was cozy and had nice decor and accents. It was also really quiet, even with the young volleyball crowd crawling the halls.
Overall it's a really nice hotel but it's huge and built for conventions. Other than the convention center there is very little around it that is appealing but if you need to be on the southwest side of downtown, at the convention center or Belo this is a much better
choice than the Hyatt.

title_masked: Excellent Service, Excellent Location, Excellent rooms
text_masked: Couldn't have booked a better hotel in downtown Phoenix. The room was massive, the service was 5 star, and the location was steps from most bars and stadiums. As a plus, the rooms are fairly cheap with AAA or other discounts.

What a surprise this was! We are used to staying in Hilton's all over the world but this we rated 'the daddy of them all'! It had everything, old traditional style and quality mixed with updated modern amenities and it was enormous! In fact, when it was originally built in the 1930's it was the largest hotel in the world. After the war, Conrad Hilton bought it for a third of what it cost to build and he performed the most expensive refurb of a hotel in history, a staggering $137,000.000 which I believe still stands today! It has the most fabulous history attached to it with photos of guests who stayed there over the years which include legends like Al Capone and Marilyn Monroe and all the American Presidents that have lived through it's era. 
The quality of the bespoke carpets/drapes/furnishings etc were of the best I have seen anywhere and it is apparent that money was no option when it was put together and because of that it still looks as good today as it did when it was created 50 years ago. It reminded me of our old Savoy Hotel but on a much bigger scale.
I think it has 3000 bedrooms on 24 floors with every floor being served by 14 lifts - truly amazing!
We had a room on the 21st floor overlooking Lake Michigan which is so huge it could have been the ocean. It was our first visit to Chicago and we were very impressed with how clean and safe it was with beautiful manicured lawns and gardens flanking the lake and the citizens were all very happy and proud of their home.
If you are thinking of visiting Chicago, I would recommend a stay here in the Hilton downtown.

title_masked: Shouldn't take 10 minutes to get to a TV Channel
text_masked:
Four Seasons -- was here for a meeting, and got the "cheap conference rate" room ....2nd floor, view of a street and a wall -- noisy and unattractive. Room had a connecting door (another bane of my existence). Only one elevator bank in hotel, and my room was a ridiculously long way from the elevator.
Worst part was the Television menu --- the remote and menu system was so convoluted it took me 10 minutes to find ESPN. The channels were 103.1, 102.2, etc., so you couldn't punch the numbers into the remote, instead had to arrow up and down (SLOWLY). Finally found a paper listing of the channels (no where near the TV or the remote), but it was still a ridiculous set-up.
Mini Bar prices were OBSCENE --- $40 for a half-bottle of wine (that looked like it had been there for years).
Meeting room, catered food in meeting, and the Bar were fine......

title_masked: A Gem in the Birthplace of our Nation
text_masked: The bad news is very short -- the air conditioning is loud but the good news is long. The hotel is a charming boutique-style oasis in the heart of Phillie. With a AAA vacation we had a lovely welcome gift, breakfast, tea-time cookies, & parking included at a reasonable price. The staff are charming, friendly, and provide great recommendations on sightseeing and local restaurants. It is walking distance to Independence Hall, city-wide tour buses, lovely historic neighborhoods, and affordable clubs and restaurants.

Had a nice, although brief, stay at the Bentley a few weekends ago. We had alerted the staff that we would arrive early in the morning after a red-eye from Seattle, and they were able to accommodate our requests for a room on a high floor away from the elevators so that we could sleep while others were checking out. The room was terrific - much larger than others we have had in NYC, with a fantastic view of the Queensboro Bridge. While the location is indeed a bit of a walk from major tourist sites, it was easy to get a cab and only 4 blocks to the nearest subway stop. We opted to find our own breakfast at a diner down the street, as the buffet didn't appear to offer much for $12.

Being in the travel industry, I have experienced it all. Going to Ritz Carlton, you have a certain expectation of things. And this hotel, supersedes all of them.
After a full day of work and then an evening flight, you just want to get to your hotel room. My only problem, after checking in, my girlfriend and I were brought to a gorgeous 1 bedroom suite which stunk of smoke. Unfortunately, I was told that all the suites with balconies are taken by smokers.
After waiting for a quick 10 minutes, a very nice woman came upstairs and moved us to another one bedroom suite. This one was much larger, due to the lack of no balcony. My only wish for the room, windows that open. 
The room was very large and open with a large bathroom and very comfy bed. The room also had a guest closet and guest bathroom. The one drawback for the two closets, only 10 hangars all together. Otherwise, the room amenities were wonderful. The shower was nice and large, wonderful bath, and I LOVED the bed.
I had club access with my room, but never used it. We ate breakfast daily in Fearings, which was perfect.The food was always cooked perfectly, and the one day that I used the buffet, let's just say, I was impressed. We never had dinner at Fearings though. One would think, being a hotel guest you'd be given preference, but that's a big NO. 
The hotel's location was perfect. It was in the nicest part of Dallas, and walking distance to EVERYTHING. But for those times that you don't want to walk, the hotel has a flying spur which took us everywhere within 3 miles of the property. 
The concierges Adon and Robert, were both worthy of being noted. Those two guys went out of their ways to make sure we were happy and treated us not just like hotel guests, but as friends. 
Another thing to be noted, Adon recommended a great shop (within 3 miles and you do need a car) called [NAME]'s western wear. Their prices are cheap, their service is above par, and you're part of the family when you're there.
I must say, I highly recommend this hotel. It's perfect for anyone just visiting the city or coming on business.

This is a nice place to stay in San Diego. It is close to the gaslamp quarter and many other atttractions. The staff are great and the price was good. We upgraded to the rooms with view which was well worth it. The bars downstairs are fantastic places to eat and drink. The rooms are smaller but the beds are huge and comfortable. Some days we noticed that our old towels were not collected but there were new ones replaced.

I stayed at this hotel because it was very close to Gibson Ampitheater. The hotel was very modern and just gorgeous!! I didn't get a chance to check out the bar but it looked very inviting but I just didn't have time. I think they had a good happy hour that I missed unfortunately. The bathroom was fantastic, high class. The bed was beyond fantastic and the most comfortable I have ever been in my entire life. Sooooo comfy.. and the sheets were so nice (I'm very sensitive to all the bleaches that most hotels use)... but it was all good here. I wish I could have stayed in that bed for 24 hours straight but alas I was there to party, had to go. haha. You did have to pay to park which I'm never a fan of when you're a hotel guest, but...whatever...I will DEFINITELY stay there again next time I'm in burbank.

Spent a week here in February. Booked a hostel room as it appeared to be best value for the location. Two blocks to the subway was excellent, and felt like a safe area. 
The hostel itself was interesting, the front area is nice, with hotel vibe but head up the stairs and turns in to a sterile environment. I found the common area a bit small and really loud. It was the only place I could get wifi too. One fridge was available for all guests and the kitchen area was tiny, I wouldn't recommend for the traveller who likes to self cater. I also found it hard to meet new people here, there was a very mixed demographic of guests. Young familys, a group of high school kids, older businessman and standard backpackers. 
Room was pretty standard for a hostel, mine smelt like wet dog however despite seeing cleaners everyday. A two person room travelling solo is quite awkward, especially when you have a male bunker. Maybe it was just my luck, but I would have been a lot more comfortable with a female roommate. A table and chair or some hooks to hang coats on wouldn't be astray here either. 
I was a little concerned with the Warning sign on the front door too- Looked like some type of official notification. Everytime I went to read it, the doorman opened the door so I couldn't however.
Overall, I would be indifferent about staying here again.

title_masked: A Great Escape on Your Way Out of Town.
text_masked:
Whenever my wife and I travel or my wife leaves for business travel we always book our room in this Hilton Hotel. The location is well situated near the airport but not so close that you are distrubed by the nearby air traffic. They have an execellent shuttle service to and from the airport which comes and goes every fifteen minutes. Whenever we check into the hotel we are greeted like old friends and they always give us a few bottles of water, which is great in the desert. The shuttle drivers also provide water to the thirsty travelers which is a nice touch.
The rooms are very nice and spacious and the beds are very comfortable with a nice big screen t.v. if you feel like watching a movie. The bathrooms are nice and big with granite counter tops and marble floors. We usually eat downstairs in the bar because that is convenient but they have a great restaurant with great service.

This is so very well placed to have a quick weekend in NYC. It sits on a side street right off of time square. Rates are always good for NYC and you can get to anywhere in NYC easily from here.
The hotel is clean and modern and very secure. Lovectayingbherevwhen we visit.

Like many others have stated this Hotel is greatly located,as its away from the heavy traffic and 
its not far from the metro subway.(about two blocks)
We stayed at this location last week saturday 3/31/2012-thursday 4/5/2012.
The place was clean but some things need to be improved. The tv remote would not control the volumn on the tv I had to take is down to the mgr desk they gave me another and asked me to put the batteries from the remote we had into the other one they gave me,problem solved.The tv was little 19 inch and not many channels to choose from.
 We discovered that the door handle comes off the outside of the room door we solved this problem by simple sliding the handle back on the door we chose not to say anything about the door handle as it seemed the mgr would not care anyways.
 The internet was TERRIBLE, we could not watch movies on line or neither could we chat with friends on line.(tried to upload photos which was almost impossible.
 We had lots of hot water for the shower at nights but morning hot water showers was impossible. I talked with the man at the front desk about the hot water, his solution was they could move us to another room(dont the same hot water heater supply all the rooms)LOL!
 The restaraunt on the property had a good breakfeast, expensive but good.(we ate breakfeast there only one time)
 The cleaning staff are very polite,thorough and helpful,they will do any thing to make sure your room meets your expectations as far as cleanliness goes.
 There is an awesome fish,fruit/vegetable market within a short walk they also have there fresh cooked seafood(we ordered food from there three times). The sunsets over the river channel out back of the hotel and is a great view.
 We found that we could buy a unlimited metro subway ticket for $9.00 a day,and we could take the metro to union station and eat there cheaper than anywhere else.
 If asked if we would stay at the channel inn again.Yes if its price and location we are looking for we would.

Stayed at Parc 55 on a recent visit to SF. Hotel was in a great location. Steps to BART, dining and shopping. Room was very clean and all the staff were very friendly. Located close to edge of Tenderloin, just know where you're going and pay attention. Would definitely stay again and the added bonus of SFO/BART station convenience make it hard to beat!

Having to park a car, we found this to be a good option for us. We paid $10 more for a "room with a view" -- and that is totally worth it! The view is beautiful -- we even slept with the curtains open. Since we were on the 22nd floor, the street noise was hardly noticeable. 
You could tell the hotel spent money renovating the bathrooms -- it was clean and chic. The room looked quite ordinary though. We were disappointed that there wasn't a mini-fridge, which is very helpful when traveling with small children.
Walking to Michigan Ave takes about 30 minutes, so the cab ride is worth it and not expensive -- about $8 or less.
It was interesting that the service elevator from the below-ground parking is not easily seen from the lot. I'm not even sure I know it's there, but there's quite a number of stairs to climb with suitcases -- we saw other families in the same situation as we were packing up our car.
Another odd thing about this hotel is that there are always dirty glasses/plates in the hallway. When we entered our room, it almost looked like the guests before us were still in the room; to the immediate left of our door was a pizza box and trash, along with dirty glasses/ plates. There were also other dirty glasses/plates by other doors. After settling in our room, we headed out -- while the glasses and plates were picked up, the trash was still there --- very odd. When we returned to our room and even when we checked out, there were ALWAYS dirty glasses and plates in the hallway, some of them were the exact ones we saw previously too.
