Overall, you're not sleeping in the hallway, and the room should suit just fine!

title_masked: Dumpster pick-up at 7 AM on Sunday morning! Seriously?
text_masked:
This is a decent hotel in a great location, but there are some major problems. First, who schedules the dumpster/compactor to be picked-up at 7 AM on Sunday morning? It woke up the entire block. Unfortunately, our entire floor had been awakened at 6:30 AM by Sheraton security looking to reunite Mr [NAME] with his lost wife. I've got one word for you fools: discretion. Look it up! And while your at it, wise up. 
The room would have been ok if the deadbolt actually locked, the night stand drawer actually opened and the shower actually drained, but hey...if they don't give a crap about waking you at 6:30 AM on a Sunday morning.....why would they worry about the comfort and safety of their rooms? Don't pay full price to stay here. Use Priceline and you can book a night for a hundred bucks. You'll need to save every penny because parking will set you back $51.30 a night. On the plus side, the staff is very friendly and they will let you check in early if they have rooms available. Don't be shy about asking.

This is the second time this year that I was able to stay downtown for business at the Omni. This is my first choice for several reasons. The first is that it’s only about a mile from my office so I can walk back and forth quite easily. The location is also great for restaurants and shopping since it’s right on Michigan Ave. 
The service here is top notch. I am a select guest (free to sign up) so I can check in online and pick up my room key when I arrive without having to wait in line to register. I also get free beverage service in the morning and free internet access in my room. This last trip I had a wonderful room on the 7th floor right above the gym balcony. It was a corner room facing both Huron and Rush, and at the end of the hall so it was quiet for the most part. There is some noise from ambulances, but that was not very often and I didn’t have trouble sleeping through the night even though I am a very light sleeper. This is a city after all and for staying on the 7th floor, the hotel was very quiet as quiet as my previous stay on the 16th floor. 
Here are some other great benefits of the hotel:
-Very nice modern gym facility with cardio (TVs built in, headphones provided) and weights, towels and wet wipes for cleaning the equipment after use. I work out at every hotel I stay at so excellent fitness centers are a big plus for me.
-Online room service orders with prompt delivery. I ordered breakfast the first morning and it was delivered right on time using the online service. The second night I ordered dinner using the online service again for an 8pm delivery due to a late meeting. When that meeting ended early, I called down to see if I could move my order up and got it just 10 minutes later. The In-Room Dining Manager that night went out of her way to ensure that I got the right tea flavor that I specified, accommodated my change in delivery time and promptly sent up a staff member to remove my tray as soon as I was done. Her friendly demeanor and attention to detail set the Omni miles above other hotels that I have stayed at. I wish I had gotten her name so I could personally thank her yet again for her exceptional service.
-Top-notch transportation team. On the first day of my trip, it was quite cold so instead of walking I asked the doorman to catch a cab. Instead of hailing a cab, he offered me complimentary car service to my office location which was a nice surprise and very welcomed. 
-Finally the Front Desk Manager called me the night before my departure to make sure I had transportation to the airport and that everything I needed was taken care of. That’s an extra personal touch that you really don’t get at the big chain hotels (unless you are top tier) and makes me feel like I am a special customer who is treated very well every time I stay. 
If you are looking for a great hotel in Chicago where you will be treated like a guest who matters and stay in a well appointed, quiet suite, this is the place for you.

title_masked: So glad I picked this hotel
text_masked:
We are a couple who stayed here for 5 nights in February. Yes ok you are not in 'the centre' of things but a very cheap and quick subway ride takes you to the hustle and bustle easily. I enjoyed coming back to the Hotel to enjoy a walk along the Hudson and drink in the relative calm after a day sightseeing.
We had a lovely room on Club level with Statue view. Well worth the extra cost . Bed the most comfortable I have ever slept in. Luxurious fittings , large bathroom. Room very quiet and equipped with black out curtains (I dont normally sleep well in hotels but had no problem here ).
Staff without exception were pleasant, friendly and accomodating, especially all the staff who worked the Club lounge. All in all one of the nicest hotels we have stayed in .
The checkin gentleman was very helpful and courteous. The breakfast was a full one and not just the normal pastry, etc.

New York hotel rooms are usually cramped, but not here. The two room suite had room enough to entertain fellow guests. The staff in the lobby was helpful. I wish their internet wasn't $13.00 a day, given the price of the room. The hotel is very near the 6 and the E subway lines and very convenient for Rockefeller Center, Museum of Modern Art, and the 5th Avenue shopping area.

title_masked: A really great place to stay!!
text_masked:
We stayed here in the end of June and it was perfect situated close to Time Square.
The beds were great, slept so good...The staff was really helpful and did there absolute best to help us out with every thing we asked for.

Recently, six friends and I visited Hollywood and stayed at the HIE because of the location and other reviews we read on Tripadvisor. This is my first time actually writing a review and I felt obligated to do so, specifically, because of Bailey and Omar who helped us immensely. We had more people joining then we had planned and they made adjustments quickly with a smile on their face. They also filled us in on activities and restaurants to visit close by. Great staff, nice rooms, wouldn't hesitate to stay there again!

This has to have been one of the largest hotels I have ever stayed in, and it didn't make a good impression.
On the plus side, it does have a central location, and our room was clean.
However little things started to irritate: no complimentary water, no free wifi ($13 for 24 hours!!!), rip off prices in the gift shop), the corridors smelled musty, no fridge or mini bar, no gym. Also we were woken by the people in the next room at 3am, though luckily they weren't noisy for long.
The hotel staff were reasonable in their quality of service.
The other hotel we had used in Boston a few nights before was much more pleasant, and if I returned to Boston, I wouldn't be heading back to the Boston Park Plaza Hotel.

title_masked: Safe, modern, & get your money's worth.
text_masked:
I flew in from Houston to spend some time with some friends for ACL weekend, we wanted a place away from the noise & found Hyatt Place Arboretum to be situated in a very nice area. Walking into the lobby there is no confusion where to go, the desk is immediately within view and the front desk staff are prompt with their welcome greetings. Check-in was speedy and we felt very welcomed. Lobby decor was modern and warm with plenty of seating area. There is also a 'bar' to the left as well as a cafe. I wasn't pleased with the mix of my drink, but I wasn't expecting much being that I saw my friends drink made from a pre-made mix (she was pleased with the taste). Despite, the customer service more than made up for the drinks ordered & the price wasn't ridiculous either. The lobby & it's restrooms were very clean, well kept, and nicely decorated.
I stayed on the fifth floor & had the double bed room. Room is huge!!! You definitely get more than what you paid and everything was in great condition. I'm big on cleanliness & I definitely felt comfortable. The colors are all warm & inviting and as pictured on the professional photos. There's a living room area, 2 person dining area, something like a butler area with a fridge, small pantry, coffee maker & its complimentary items, as well as a big mirror above it, and there
is also a wireless phone by a desk area complete with a comfortable rolling computer chair. Entering the bedroom area there is a little divider and a huge flat screen that comes equip with allowing you to plug in whatever devices you have to go through using the tv, a vanity area with so much counter space, a huge mirror, and another head to floor mirror as the closet door with a good amount of space for your luggage & belongings. I always read about water pressure & this hotel's own was strong. Not much of a view outside but you are on a quiet side of town.
First night here, I took a taxi ride downtown to 6th street, it's about a 15-20 min ride and fares ran from 25-30 each one way trip. There are restaurants located within walking distance from the hotel. Hotel staff was once again extremely accommodating and attentive with checking up on us with the arrival of our taxi when we were waiting roughly ten minutes & had also made the initiative to call the company again to order another to get us to our destination. 
I stayed here from Friday till Sunday and the impression I got from this hotel was that they all acted as a team. No matter the job position they held, each one was ready and willing to accommodate you with a smile and friendly exchange of words. From the front desk to house cleaning, whatever it is that you need met with your stay, all you have to do is call front desk and they are so quick to fix or fulfill that request. The team running the place is doing a great job and I just feel they are living up to the brand name & what true customer service is about. Lovely stay, will be back with every Austin trip!

I was prepared to come here and write a very bad review but the staff at this hotel fixed what could have been a horrible experience. First I'll say I was in DC for a concert at a local venue. This hotel was perfectly located for an easy commute to the Venue (Club Love - about 2 blocks away). This hotel is not in the most glamorous areas of DC but it's a short drive away from most of the "must see" DC attractions. Everyone who attuned the event must have chosen this hotel because it was at full capacity. Check in was speedy and the front desk staff very friendly. The hotel lobby is very neat and welcoming. The room was decorated with modern finishes and very clean. I was actually surprised by that. 
Now the bad - Parking was $15. The hotel was at full capacity so there was a shortage of towels and washcloths. I called down to the front desk at least 4 times to request more and they never came. I finally got tired of waiting and went down to the front desk where the staff honestly informed me that they were out of them. A little strange but OK. This problem carried over to the following morning... requested towels/cloths again and learned that the laundry was being done and there was about a 45 minute wait for fresh towels. We also woke up to find that there was absolutely no hot water. This problem lasted all morning through late afternoon. The staff offered a late checkout while they waited for a repair man to fix the problem & had no ETA for resolution. At 1pm there was still no hot water so my guests and I just said enough and decided to head home. At check out I received the final bill & the Front Desk Manager had credited the entire stay. That was great customer service. I didn't complain or request it at all. I had given them the benefit of the doubt since the hotel was so busy .. I just kind of went with the flow and to have a two night stay credited without asking showed great service. (Being an Elite Member probably helped a bit). 
Long story short - Great hotel, nice and clean rooms, free breakfast, short drive to DC attractions, close to 2 popular DC night clubs, no great restaurants nearby (only a 24 hour Checkers, Taco Bell, KFC, McD & Wendy's), no great shopping, small pool and hot tub, very friendly staff & great stay for the price. I felt safe & I would definitely stay again.

I think it is too expensive for so little rooms, dirty moquette in the bedrooms, dirty sofa in the hall...
It was impossible to open our luggages because there was no much more space for us to stay even standing...
The bathroom was clean but very very small..
The air conditioner was very noisy...
The elevator very slow...
The goods things are that it was very close to the principal New York's attractions so you can walk to time square , the fifth avenue rockfeller centre ecc...
I have been in the same chain of hotels, Confort inn, in Charleston and I payed 1/3 and it was fantastic....

title_masked: Thanksgiving visit with family in Austin
text_masked: Convenient, only 8 minutes from my son's place near downtown. Easy access and reasonably secure parking. Standard but new and nice rooms. Comfortable beds. Some airplane noise (expected). Great, quick, and easy breakfast. Managers make us feel welcomed and offer a military discount which is always appreciated.

Made our reservations through the zoo website and got a great deal. The beds and pillows were very comfortable. It was nice to have free parking. Last year we stayed at a hotel on the north side of hotel, paid for parking in a cramped lot. Rooms are clean and without any odors. The rooms are on the small side. We had two double beds and there wasn't a lot of extra room to walk around. Our family had rooms 363 and 349 and did not have any complains. The air conditioner/heater was new and quieter than most motels. The bathroom fan was also very quiet. Lights in the room were also bright, something we appreciate when we are reading. We chose not to eat at the restaurant attached to the hotel, it seemed over-priced, especially for breakfast.

title_masked: Club Quarters World Trade Center Is In The Center Of It All
text_masked:
We stayed two nights in this hotel, our last day was one day prior to the arrival of Hurricane Sandy. This hotel is hard to find for cab drivers. If you ask to go there they know the general area but with all the construction going on around Ground Zero and all the streets either shut off or under consruction it was like an obstacle course. Once at the hotel the desk clerks ordered us a car (limousine/Escalade/etc.) everytime we needed to go Uptown. That was for a flat rate of $30.00 plus tip. This was excellent service and the drivers were great.
 The desk clerks were very helpful, courteous and friendly. They went the extra mile to make sure we had an enjoyable stay. Since our flight didn't leave until 5:00 p.m. they stored our luggage for us on checking out and brought it out to us when leaving. We didn't have to lift a finger.
 The rooms are small. For one person in New York on business or alone to tour, the rooms would be fine but for two people we were tripping over each other and our suitcases all the time. The hotel is three years old so the rooms (as was the whole hotel) were clean and well maintained. They have a wonderful little lobby equipped with a fireplace, televisions, comfortable chairs and a free coffee and snack service.The bed was a double bed, comfortable but not exceptional. Windows are floor to ceiling so if you're queasy with heights that may be a problem.
 The hotel has a few features that we enjoyed. Fresh distilled water dispensers and bottles are available on each floor free of charge for the patrons. Public washrooms are on the second floor for your use after checking out as long as your key still works in the elevator. The most awesome feature of this hotel is their rooftop (20th floor) dining room and terrace overlooking the 9/11 Memorial. We enjoyed dinner in their restaurant one night and the food was excellent, the service was terrific! We also had breakfast in the dining room the morning we left and it was a buffet style breakfast. Awesome selection, very good food, hot and tasty. I discovered the Sunset Terrace on the opposite side of the hotel roof from the dining room, complete with comfortable wicker chairs and open to the sky and view of the city. It was a great place for pictures and just to work on your laptop with the hotel's free wi-fi.
 This hotel, like many hotels in New York is not cheap but it was cheaper than the ones in Midtown and Uptown so that's one reason for our choice. The other reason was its close proximity to the 9/11 Memorial which we visited on our last day. There are some great little restaurants around the hotel for an evening snack or a dinner meal. Pizza seems to be the order of the day in a lot of them and if you walk and explore the area you will find a restaurant that you prefer; guaranteed. If it's your first visit to New York, this may not be the hotel for you since it is far from Time Square, the Theatre District, Central Park, Rockefeller Center and the Empire State Building. This hotel is for those who have a knowledge of the city and can use the subways and buses without difficulty or those who have business in the Financial District.
 I would definitely stay here again. In October the weather was beautiful for touring and walking without the humidity of the summer. Be prepared to see large groups of NYPD on the corners and streets all around the hotel and the 9/11 area. It was a little disconcerting at first with the impression that something was going on but on asking an officer we found out that the police are out in full force like that everyday. We enjoyed New York and would recommend this hotel to singles, business people and to couples who plan to not spend a lot of time in their rooms.

The management called us liars. We complained that we did not receive any keeping housekeeping service. The manager told us we left the do not disturb tag out. We never hung that tag, even when we were there sleeping. The manager said the housekeeper knocked on the door the second day and we refused service. No one ever knocked on the door and in fact we were out of the room all day. The manager then went to the room and acknowledged we did no receive service. It was a room with 2 queens and we were only sleeping in one, so she said "well, you have another bed". Unacceptable. I will never stay in a Super 8 anywhere. To be honest I only stayed there because I wanted to be downtown, and short of paying $500 a night, it was the only thing available. I didn't expect much but i did expect basic housekeeping. And oh by the way the breakfast is pitiful. We went out out breakfast.

For our first trip to Chicago my friends selected the The Talbott. We loved, loved, loved this hotel. Small and warm and just a stone's throw from all the action. The rooms are beautifully decorated and immaculately maintained. The staff is OUTSTANDING, knowledgeable and friendly. We got very good advice and help from the wonderful Concierge staff. Had wonderful breakfasts al fresco and great cocktails in the bar.
 When I return to Chicago (and I cannot wait) I will be back at The Talbott.

The staff at this hotel could not have been more pleasant and helpful, from the front desk who found a room for us at 8am so we could check into the hotel, to the doorman who provided a complimentary ride into town (and insisted we call for a return journey) and to the train station the following day. Most good hotels have similar amenities and the rooms provide much the same facilities. But ultimately its the service that leaves the lasting impression and this hotel's staff certainly did that! The room was comfortable and spotlessly clean. Overall, excellent value. The only drawback to staying at this hotel was its location which is about 15 mins drive to the centre of the city.

title_masked: Great Hotel to celebrate 20th wedding anniversary
text_masked: This hotel takes you back in time. I must admit that when my husband first told me that this is where we were celebrating our 20th wedding anniversary I was thinking "Oh, I wonder what kind of hotel this is." Well, was I pleasantly surprised. First of all, this hotel is a beautiful old historic building which I consider a hidden gem in midtown. The location could not be better. Quiet at night after a busy day in the city but so easy to walk to the hustle and bustle of midtown. Everyone we encountered at this hotel was beyond pleasant. We had a beautiful suite overlooking 6th Avenue. What an incredible view. For NY standards this room (we had the Warwick Suite) was very generous in size. The room was spacious, and the living room was a wonderful size. We could sit and relax in a nice couch. Bathroom was small but very modern. The heating system I felt was not working well. We had to open up a window because it got very warm in the room but otherwise, it was great. We had champagne delivered to the room and we had personalized champagne flutes that we brought along with us. The following morning housekeeping took away our personalized glasses and left the regular flutes that they had brought up. I called immediately and within 20 minutes they brought back the flutes. Service was phenomenal! The restaurant was great for breakfast. They have a very nice selection. We went to the bar after dinner for an after dinner drink....which was pleasant enough. All in all, I would recommend this hotel and would return. Oh and I forgot the BED was SO COMFORTABLE as were all the pillows. Thank you to the Warwick staff for making our 20th anniversary a celebration to remember!

Comfy, clean rooms. Tasty food. Friendly staff. My only gripe was the fact that the A/C operates via a motion detector. If it does not sense movement (like when you're asleep), the A/C turns off and won't click back on automatically until it hits 75. Insane. I had to get up every other hour to get the dang thing to click back on. The person who decided to install these motion sensors should be shot.

From the outside of the building I wasn't expecting much but the lobby is quite nice and appeared to have been recently remodeled. Room was on the small side but very bright, clean and also appeared to have been recently updated. The location is nice for walking around downtown and transit was right outside the hotel. Very reasonably priced.

title_masked: I Would Definitely Return to This SF Hotel
text_masked:
I stayed at the Chancellor Hotel in SF from December 31st - January 3rd. There were 2 adults in our party and we booked a room with 2 twin beds. We absolutely loved this hotel.
Our stay @ the Chancellor came at the tail end of a nearly 10 day trip to the Bay Area so we were looking for clean yet comfortable accommodations. We were very happy that we chose to stay @ the Chancellor.
First off, the location cannot be beat. If you are a tourist looking for a good home base in city from which to start your exploration and site seeing, this is a wonderful spot. The hotel is centrally located to NUMEROUS modes of public transit - i.e. the Powell-Mason cable car line stops in front of the hotel, it's about a 5 minute walk to the Powell Street BART station (goes directly to SFO which is approximately 40 minutes away), the Market and 5th area is a cluster for many buses and street cars, etc. It's so easy to get around from here. And please do not think that it'll be noisy in your hotel room given that you're so close to all the action. Our room overlooked the front of the hotel -Powell Street - and I was amazed at how well our window blocked out the sounds of the people, of the cable cars, etc. I was so impressed with the sound proofing of the window. SIDEBAR: A helpful note to 1st time travelers to SF: the city has an impressive web of mass transit. However, unlike NYC where all the city buses are all with the MTA, SF has multiple transit agencies that oversee its public transportation and they don't necessarily cross honor each other's tickets. So the best route is to purchase a Clipper card from a Walgreens or similar retailer as that is card is rechargeable and accepted by all the transit agencies (BART, MUNI, etc.). It is also worth noting that steps away from the hotel is a Walgreens pharmacy and 7-11 (which surprisingly sold deliciously fresh glazed donuts - so good that they rival NYC's beloved Krispy Kreme). There's tons of other shopping near the hotel - Macy's, Sack's Ross, etc.
Second, the staff was very pleasant and helpful. They were always friendly and willing to answer all our questions.
Third, the Chancellor has the wonderful feel of a boutique hotel without the designer price tag. I myself am not a big fan of the gigantic convention center-esque hotel experience. The Chancellor feels so intimate. The hotel was originally opened in 1914 and the decor is reflective of that era. So though the lobby may not be flanked with flat screen TVs and sleek modern furniture, the property appears to be well maintained. My friend and I did quite a bit of research before booking here and found that the prices of the Chancellor were some of the most affordable in the area. Having now stayed at the hotel, we know that we didn't sacrifice any quality for the price.
Fourth, the hotel is clean with comfortable amenities. I do want to caution folks that in a dense city like SF or New York, your typical hotel room will tend to run pretty small. The size of our room at the Chancellor was modest, but we never felt like we were on top of each other. It was definitely a plus that our room came with a walk in closet. The bathroom had a glorious classic bathtub that's perfect for soaking. The room came with free WiFi internet as well. There were also wonderful little perks like free coffee and tea and cookies in the lobby throughout the day.
If we had to, one SMALL issue we did have was with how the elevators (of which there are 2) were rather slow at times. And even this was not a big issue at all.
All in, we loved our time in San Francisco and loved our time at the Chancellor hotel. We would definitely return to the Chancellor and would not have any qualms in recommending this place to friends.

We spent one night here, two adults and our 4 year old son, and really enjoyed the hotel. Perfect location, next door to the wonderful Sears restaurant, cable cars outside the door, Union Square and all the shopping at Market street very close by. The room was very clean and had everything we needed. We also had a nice view of Union Square. 
Staff was very helpful and we really can't complain about anything. 
What impressed me the most was the e-mail communication I had with Voula Theodoropoulos before our arrival - she helped me book with a special Facebook discount and also helped me when I needed to change our reservation. No matter when I e-mailed I always had a response within a few minutes.
The hotel was easy to find; reception was quick and pleasant. Room was spacious and comfortable. A good value for the price.

I stayed at the Stanford in September 2012. The location is excellent, a short walk to subway, Empire State Building and Times Square. The staff are fantastic, very friendly and helpful. The rooms are small, but that's to be expected in New York. Housekeeping are excellent, the room was always spotless. Great wine bar on the first floor, definitely make a stop there for happy hour. We stayed on the 10th floor and out our window we could see the Empire State- magical! The breakfast is very basic, coffee/tea/juice with one choice of fruit and bagels. It's enough to get you started, there are plently of other restaurants around if you dont want to eat it. Highly recommend this hotel.
This is a super small hotel. Perfect for a relaxing visit to New York. Great room, location and friendly atmosphere. We're sure to stay again.

I stayed in the Double Tree for Elvis Week. The staff are so friendly and helpful. The rooms are comfortable and clean. TJI Fridays is great for food, breakfast and evening meals are great. Looking forward to staying there again. Very central location.

I had a handicapped accessible room that was poorly designed. 
2 out of 5 days the maids didn't remember to make up my room.
The carpet was not clean. There was debris that looked like mouse turds next to the wall. I requested the house man to vacuum this up, which he did.
The maids did not leave enough clean hand towels each day to replace the dirty ones.

The hotel is conveniently located on the magnificant mile.and the doormen Willie and Stan are very friendly and helpful in giving you directions to all the various sites in Chicago.I live part -time in Chicago, next door to the hotel,and the front desk manager ,Simon has been very gracious in getting very favorable rates and upgrades when my family comes to town.If I were a tourist I would always stay at the Intercontinental Chicago.

title_masked: Nice Property, Staff Friendly, But Incompetent
text_masked: Stayed here for 2 nights while moving my son into UT. Paid $95 on Priceline. The staff was friendly and professional, the property is nice, the location is OK. Three things made me give it a lower rating - one, I needed to make a conference call in the early AM, and didn't want to do it in my room. Tried to dial an 800 number using the phone in the business center - didn't work. Called the front desk, they said the "phone bank" should work - hurried over there, but all the phones had been removed (the front desk didn't get the memo, I guess). Two, I asked for a 3:30 wakeup and 4:00 taxi to make my early flight out. They got confused and missed the 3:30 wakeup call - luckily I just woke up on my own about 5 minutes to 4 and went down to check out. The 3rd thing is they tried to put internet charges (which should be waived for members of Omni's loyalty program) on the bill - I had to remind them to waive those. Big issues? No, but don't have to deal with this stuff at the Hilton...

We stayed here two nights and couldn't fault anything at all. The other nice touch was the very friendly staff throughout the hotel, even offering an umbrella because the doorman said it would rain later and offering water when they knew we had a long drive to go. All small touches but they make a big difference. and lovely views, too!

We loved the location of this hotel in the center of everything in Chicago. The room was on the small side but very comfortable and pleasant. Our view of the Chicago River was spectacular. I would definitely stay there again.

title_masked: A cavernous Hilton with some history
text_masked:
First the history - It was at the lower south entrance to this hotel that John Hinckley shot Ronald Reagan. For some reason, it's not the most prominent thing in this hotel's advertising plan....
The rooms are Hilton standard, which means adequate for the business traveler though not plush. Hilton's standards are fairly high, and just about any Hilton I'd rank would get at least a Very Good rating (though I've made exceptions), and this is in that category.
But if you're not here for one of the vast number of conferences this hotel hosts, then there are probably better choices. It's not really near the main tourist action in this town (though if you learn how to use the Metro, and you should in this city, getting around is fairly easy; this hotel is a few blocks uphill from the Dupont Circle Metro). The place is big, awkwardly so in my opinion, and it's hard to navigate if you are a business traveler trying to find the room in which your meeting is being held. It's also not particularly quiet, though I've never had too much trouble sleeping here in a number of visits.
In short, it has the quality you'd expect of a Hilton, but is really nothing special. You won't at all mind staying there, but the visit may not be memorable.

title_masked: Perfectly acceptable little hotel if the price is right.
text_masked:
First off, my husband and I don't usually worry about the star rating when booking hotels - so I'm not really sure what to expect with 4* booking, We base our bookings and expectations off of reviews. What we were expecting was a clean and larger-than-average New York room with comfortable beds. That's exactly what we got. The location was quite convenient - 3 blocks from Grand Central for the subway, but also within walking distance to Times Square and Rockafeller Center areas. We took the Subway almost everywhere and found the location made it easy to get around this way.
We got to the hotel at 7am. They were able to start the check-in process for us and store our luggage. We returned at about 1:30 figuring that our room would be ready. However, it was not ready and we had to wait until 3:00pm - which is check-in time. After reading many reviews about free room upgrades, we were kind of hoping for one, but it turns out we didn't need it. The superior king room we booked was plenty large enough for our needs! We had a not-so-great view of the building next door, although if you looked out the side a bit you could see a lovely-looking courtyard. As we were mainly in our room when we were sleeping, and thus had the blinds closed most of the time we were there, this didn't bother us. The lady who checked us in stated that "the view isn't the greatest, but for five nights, I figured a quiet room was more important" - they were doing construction on the streets out front, and since out room was in the back, we didn't hear any of it in our 11th floor room.
The room itself was pretty much as advertised. Everything was clean, and nothing appeared overly "worn" or "run down" as I had read in some reviews. Our huge king bed with feather pillows was very comfortable. There was a bench at the foot of the bed that fit our 2 large suitcases so that they didn't have to be on the floor, in the way. The closet was a good sized, with a chest of drawers inside. There was a counter with mirror in an alcove that housed the closet and minibar fridge. There was a little seating area with a table and two chairs.
On the surface, the bathroom looked great. It was quite clean and had an ample supply of fresh towels. There is no counter, just a pedastal sink, but there is a ledge above the toilet that can be used to place toothbrushes, make up, etc. The shower head had adequate, perhaps not great, pressure. There were a couple little blemishes we noticed after a bit of time, but, again, nothing that overly interfered with our enjoyment of our stay. There was a hole (literally) in the ceiling of the bathroom where the sprinkler was. I'm talking a hole cut out of the drywall - unfinished. Part of the faucet control lever was loose and unattached to the rest of the fixture. The bathtub did not have the best drainage - there was a bit of water pooled by the end of an average-length shower.
Service at the hotel was fine. Front-desk staff was pleasant enough. There was almost always at least one person at the door to greet us and open the door. Baggage storage was fast and easy - the one time there was a bit of a wait, they offered to have someone deliver it up to our room. The front desk let us borrow a pair of scissors. The one thing that appeared to be missing from the room was a book that described the hotel services, etc - so we were a little bit clueless about the services the hotel offered. I had to call to find out if there was a place to print from a computer and was informed that there was a business center on the 2nd floor. I didn't end up needing it, so I can't comment on the center itself. We were wondering about vending machines and ice machines - we never did find out about those (it was never important enough for us to ask). As we were leaving I noticed some people getting ice from the conceirge desk, so perhaps there were no ice machines? As for vending machines, there is a convenience store across the road and two drug stores down the down the street, so they weren't needed anyway.
Wifi was free and seemed to work well on our laptop. The TV had a decent variety of channels. The air conditioner worked well and kept the room plenty cool. I heard a man in the elevator complain that the air conditioner was loud and he couldn't sleep with it on, but we didn't find it overly loud or disruptive - possibly because we have window air conditioners at home.
There is a restaurant attached to the hotel but we didn't try it. There was also a bar on the other side of the lobby. It was a bit louder in the lobby if we returned later in the evening, but all the commotion seemed to be happening on the other side of a ceiling-to-floor curtain.
As I said, we don't usually bother with the star-rating of a hotel, but if I were to guess, I'd probably say this was more of a 3-3.5-star than a 4 star-based on accomodations and services. That said, for the $145/night we paid (via a Quikbook Secret Sale), we weren't expecting the Plaza. If you're looking for a clean, comfortable place to stay in a good location, I'd definitely recommend looking into St. Giles - The Court. If you're looking for a luxary hotel with tons of services, perhaps look elsewhere.

title_masked: "Constant use had not worn ragged the fabric of the Algonquin."
text_masked:
To borrow a phrase from Dorothy Parker...
I was fortunate to spend three nights at the Algonquin earlier this month with my college roommate whom I haven't seen in five years. Our room was small -- as they usually are in vintage hotels. The bed (we could only get a queen with my Marriott points) was incredibly comfortable, the shower, hot and powerful. SCORE.
I found the front desk staff amenable and helpful except for Matilda, who was catty and aloof. (For those of you unaware of the Algonquin's history, Matilda, is the resident feline.)
While the cocktail lounge was a throwback to the New Yorker-Roundtable era, the food in the dining room was rather disappointing. I found the prix fixe menu wanting, the dishes oversalted and the desserts unremarkable. Service, however, was gracious.
And you cannot beat the location of the hotel. The 42nd Street/Broadway subway stop is close, there's a Duane Reade drug store for emergency toothpaste runs and Time Square is at your disposable. I will gladly return to this hotel for my next stay in the Big Apple!
The f but they usually are at older hotels.

title_masked: BEST & most accommodating hotel in New York!
text_masked: This hotel is just the right amount of modern and comfort. Located in Tribeca, walking distane to SoHo and other boroughs. The staff at the Smyth are what make the hotel what it is, from the maids to the front desk everyone has a smile on their faces and they are there to make your stay as smooth as possible. I was in town for a conference and they even held my items for me, I had them shipped from CA. Nothing was lost or damaged. The concierge helped me with whatever I needed whenever I needed it, I honestly felt like a rock star at Smyth Tribeca. I'll be staying here every time I come back to New York. I highly recommend staying here!

This Crowne Plaza is not up to the usual CP standards. Dated decor and furniture in the rooms, and not the type of Crowne Plaza I'm used to. 
Pro's - Parking is reasonable with the self-park and it is connected via an under-road tunnel. 
Cons - Old Decor. Too far to be considered part of the core "Riverwalk" attraction area. It is about a mile from the busy restaraunts and while this could be a plus with a quiet environment, the hotel was noisy the weekend we stayed there.
The biggest problem on this saturday was about half the children in Mexico City were staying here for a soccer tournament. They had little supervision and were running the elevators to every floor and setting off fire alarms all evening on Saturday.
I SHOULD HAVE PAID MORE ATTENTION TO THE NEGATIVE REVIEWS.

title_masked: Nice Resort in a Good Location
text_masked:
We chose this resort due to many of the ratings on Trip Advisor as well as the price. The campus is very well maintained and right on the bay in a great location. There were pleanty of restaurants and places to go within walking distance (in the Mission Beach/Pacific Beach area). 
The room was pretty nice. The beds were comfortable. The bathrooms were clean. They have a window facing the exterior hallway instead of a fan, so you're stuck having to open it after you use it unless you want passers-by to check out your business. It's not brand new by any stretch, but did not have a musty smell like I have encountered elsewhere.
We only used the restaurant for coffee and dessert, so beyond that I cannot speak. We did not use the spa, though there is a charge to use the spa pool and facilities.
Regarding service, when we arrived, we were told that our reservations were not for the dates which we had booked through Travelocity. The person at the counter was quick to point out that it is not ususally their fault, but was going to check anyhow. While I was on the phone with Travelocity, she found out that the snafu was in fact their fault, and we were given our keys. We booked a king room, but were given two doubles. The room we received was on the "back 40" - basically we had to walk around the outside of the resort to get into our room, and go back around to get to the beachfront. They charge $13/day for parking, which seems a little steep considering they only charge $10/day for non-guests. 
All in all, it wasn't a terrible place. Like I said, it is a great location. Our activies ended up being downtown, and we probably should have looked at staying there instead. However, we would have missed the quiet atmosphere of Pacific Beach.

I chose Donatello to be near to my conference location at the Hilton- I prefer to be away from the conference hotel. Donatello is 2 blocks away and also just 1 block from Union Square. We had a spacious suite with in-room microwave, fridge and tea/coffee making. I liked the top floor club lounge which has tea and coffee all day and a gym and sauna. Peter the concierge is a great source of local knowledge- such as directing us to a viewing point for July 4 fireworks on Russian Hill rather than over-crowded Fisherman's Wharf. Downsides were outside noise despite being put on 8th floor- window glazing isn't great- and those Hotel Frank demonstrators are still protesting loudly in early hours. Also I failed to get an internet connection. But overall we enjoyed our stay at Donatello and would consider returning.

My wife and I stayed at the Lombardy Hotel over the October 6-8, 2012 weekend. It's great place: very reasonable price, perfect location (between 2 metro stops), and a great sleep quality bed. Our room was very comfortable and clean. LCD tv and free internet. The hotel is a couple of blocks away from 2 CVS stores, Starbucks and several restaurants. About a 20-min drive from Reagan National by cab or about 35-min by metro/walk.
Two negatives: 1) low and/or inconsistent water pressure (we stayed on the 10th floor); and 2) mediocre restaurant. 
Otherwise, I highly recommend Hotel Lombardy for any visitor to Washington DC.

I am a travel agent and have stayed in many of the world's finest hotels and it is not easy to strike up the enthusiasm I have for the JW Marriott San Antonio Hill Country. The property is immaculate in every category. My bathroom appeared as if it were brand new as well as the rest of the room. What is truly outstanding is the service and it was across the board. I lost my IPhone and was totally stressed out about it. I contacted the operator and spoke with an Agent named [NAME]. She totally felt my pain and immediately begin to get me calmed down by telling me she was going to waive the fees for long distance calls so that I could alert my family and important business contacts of losing the phone. The next morning was a hand written note under my door expressing her empathy with my situation and confirming the waiver of telephone fees. I was here for a conference and the theme was to be extraordinary and that applies to Asia. I would also like to recognize Cruz in banquet services who was our server at a number of events. He always recognized me and would inquire if I needed anything. One morning I was physically ill and Chris Q a waiter in the 18 Oaks Club Restaurant was so pleasant and kind I walked out of there feeling so much better. The food is absolutely delightful especially in light of this being a convention hotel. This property is perfect for large meetings and families. You should rent a car because there are no stores or restaurants within walking distance. I incurred a $43.00 taxi fare trying to get to a pharmacy. The ones closest to the hotel will cost about $15.00 round trip. Neither of those stores had what I needed or were not open so I had to go further away. The shops inside the Marriott are very expensive but well stocked. It is also about 30 minutes from the Riverwalk if there is no traffic.

title_masked: Nice Hotel in Really Nice Location
text_masked:
i can't say that i ever stayed at a Sheraton before so i was quite surprise when i first walked in. High Ceiling, very open, bright, and classy. 
Your Typical customer service at the counter. Smiles and hellos and asking to make sure you had everything you needed. I was quite surprise they were so accommodating to switch my room from a 1 King to a Double without a fuss. I'm sure that's not always easy especially if they are completely booked, but it was a nice touch they did so quite easily under normal circumstances.
things i liked were:
-the typical customer service you would expect. Pleasantries such as employee's smiling faces and saying Hello, and front desk clerks asking questions to make sure your needs have been met. 
-the cleanliness of our room (see pic i took) and of the bathroom. i read another review here where a patron complained of a great deal of mold. not so in my case. but i would imagine it can be expected somewhere in an older hotel like this with many, many rooms. Don't know the exact count for this hotel. 
-i appreciated the complimentary water each day, the Starbucks coffee for your coffee maker, and the extra pillows. 
-The towels were ample and plush.
-I totally appreciated the location of the hotel to Downtown. this is the type of place where you can be close to the action without being IN the action. literally 5-6 minutes from the Epicenter of downtown. 
Some concerns:
-they charge a fee to use the internet in your room. that sucks. look, i do understand hotels are getting strained with the high usage of internet in their hotels thus the amount of cost that may be incurred because of the high demand. My two cents is that i do understand whey some hotels charge however, it would have been nice if there was a least one place in the hotel where you could go and use WiFi for free; like at the restaurant or at the pool. 
-they use real feather pillows. i just don't care for feather pillows as they are never fluffy enough for me. again, this is just a concern to me because I'm sure there are many of you who are perfectly fine and appreciate feather pillows. 
-we really couldn't get a handle on how the thermostat in our room worked. there was no heat and cold selections. more of a select the temp you want and either the heat kicked in or the a/c. a little unusual, but we managed to keep the room comfortable. 
All in all, a good stay and a fair price. 
i would definitely stay again.

title_masked: Some real pluses but negatives too.
text_masked: This Fairfield Inn on west 37th proved to have a wonderful desk person in Daniel who greeted us and made us feel very welcomed. Both elevators worked well with our recent visit and our room was very quiet despite the construction next door. Breakfast was included in the price and ample with fresh fruit, yogurt, breakfast sandwiches, bagels, hard-boiled eggs, waffles, cereal, juice and more that I can't recall. However, the room was very small for two people with barely enough room to walk around the foot of the bed. The bathroom was very small with minimal room for toiletries, although the shower pressure was strong with plenty of hot water. The king-sized bed was comfortable and flatscreen TV terrific. The lobby is tiny with a couple of outside tables, but not an area conductive to relaxing. Only wired computer access in the rooms although it is free. Location is several blocks from Times Square, but walkable, especially to Herald Square and a metro station to get around the city.

This was a beautiful hotel and the amenities are wonderful. I liked that I was able to keep my dog in the room. It was because of my dog that I found a piece of stale pizza in my couch which led me to question the cleanliness of the rest of the room. Also, the cleaning staff I assume was short handed because my room was not cleaned in the in between day until 5 pm. I did not like having to pay a non refundable fee to have my dog for a dog competition that was going on in the hotel. She is cleaner than most people. I would have liked to have seen the room be inspected and that to be returned upon leaving. Otherwise everyone was very friendly and the hotel was a neat layout.

When we arrive at the front of the Hotel, we were slightly confused. Where is the doorman or bellmen to assist with guest checking in? ..then we noticed to the left of the building was a single automobile entry way indicating to pull in for Hyatt parking. The guest reception is on the side of building rather than main front entrance. The Lobby itself was small in comparison to other Hyatt Hotels, behind the 6 feet wide reception counter were two ladies, very friendly and professional. We were staying only one night and was informed we could upgrade to a patio room for additional charge....so we took to room upgrade.
It is a spacious room had features to accomodate the disabled but it had a set of stairs that leads up to outdoor patio? Oh yes..the patio we paid as an upgrade. The patio had a rattan sofa, no smoking allow, no view at all, totally enclosed by walls and frosted glass BUT the people walking down the stair case from the upper floors has full view of our patio. Bad choice of upgrade.
The two double beds were comfortable but the housekeeping was poor. The shiny surface of the headboards were filthy, the two armchairs in the room were a bit dingy, there was a spot of dried pink foam left on the bath counter. Oh..and the bathtub curtains were NOT waterproof even with the lining secured inside tub, each time one of us took a shower water dripped heavy outside onto the floor.
This hotel has the "older" feel and both of my teenage kids felt a bit spooked by it. In my opinion, the Hyatt at Bellevue needs an update (was later told by check-out staff the update is in progress although I didn't see evidence in either hallways or lobby). I gave this hotel 3 stars because the reception staff and the bellmen were very professional, also they were kind enough to reverse the patio upgrade charge due to displeasure. 
Overall, the pros were spacious room, great location and the availability of self parking. We paid over $300 (including taxes and parking) for a single night stay without the upgrade fee. Due to the older style of this hotel and the lack of value, we will not be revisiting this Hyatt.

This hotel was only 3 blocks from Times Square and 3 blocks from Rockefeller Center. What a great place for convenience with a nightly price much lower than bigger names. Rooms were large for NYC with a flat screen, nice bath, and desk. Breakfast was continental, but it was fabulous. You can definitely get a great start for your day. The subway was just around the corner, which will take you to JFK. We left a cell phone in our room the day of departure and when we called about it, the phone was already at the front desk waiting for us. What a great staff! I just can't say enough about this hotel. You won't be sorry!

I was staying for a conference in Chicago and chose the Intercontinental for its famous swimming pool (I love swimming and most hotels pass oversized tubs as pools...), I was not expecting much more, given many negative reviews on trip-advisor. I arrived to discover the pool was closed for renovations, expecting a bad stay and it was all uphill from there. 
The staff were excellent throughout my whole stay, friendly, efficient and knowledgable. Everyone at check-in, the concierge, waiters at breakfast and even house-cleaning staff, were pleasant and helpful. 
I was given a lovely room on the 33rd floor in the historic tower. The historic tower has all the impressive beauty of old-world grandeur, but the space is up-kept and renovated with all modern comforts. I got a spacious and comfortable room. Well furnished, for both taste and comfort. The bed and all the extra pillows gave me a comfortable, dreamy sleep. One of the better hotel beds I have had in a while. The bathroom was huge, and the walk in shower was a real treat. I had a very comfortable work area with large desk and good office chair, I did not feel cramped. The room was kept very clean, house-keeping was excellent. The room exceeded my expectations and sleep quality in the bed was first rate. 
The buffet breakfast at the Continental was better than I expected and very high quality. A very large and varied selection of high quality breakfast foods. 3 days in a row and I had completely different breakfast items, enjoying each breakfast. It was one of the more generous breakfast buffets I have experiences in a while. Also, the ENO wine bar, while expensive, is great fun. 
Internet was very fast, the fastest rates I have had in a hotel for a while. I could download huge data files and even stream movies without a glitch. There was one time I had a bit of internet problems and they connected me with a very courteous technical support that immediately fixed it. 
The gym/spa itself is not much to write home about, fancy looking, the machines are a bit cramped and crowded, the main event in the pool which was closed. But, they did offer complimentary use of the Baily's fitness center next door which was good. Also, I arrived before check-in on the first day and they let me use the spa to shower and change from my flight before the conference. More than I have been offered by many other hotels.
Location was great, walking distance to great sights, so even while attending a conference I could do some sight seeing right around the corner for an hour here and there. 
All in all, it was a great stay that exceeded expectations.

From the minute I arrived -- "form of payment & photo ID!" -- I've been treated rudely at this hotel. Multiple calls to the manager on uty have yeilded ... No response. Le Meridien has always been the benchmark of hospitality for me. After my experience with this property, I calledmt travel agent & said "Never, ever again."

Clean and bright with beautiful views of the marina. Right next to the airport so it's very convenient if you have early/late flights. The staff was very friendly and there's a shuttle that will take you to the airport that runs every 15 minutes! 
I stayed in the Bay Tower property which is a little off from the main property but I did not mind at all. The main property is bigger, more standard of a Sheraton with a bar and Starbucks but the Bay Tower is only a 5 minute walk away. 
We loved it and will definitely stay there again if we travel back to San Diego!

Stay 4 nights in in January after attending a NYE wedding.
Beautiful hotel, and friendly staff. Room was upgraded, so we got a beautiful Suite and Balcony. Staff we helpful but not overpowering.
Had a bit of a nightmare at check-out as card had been charge more that quoted when book, which put me over credit limit. liuckily the transaction went through and I was able to have the error amended with Credit Card company.
Worth double checking final price at check-in.
Overall great experience and luxurious stay.

title_masked: Great Experience for a Week! Great Value!
text_masked: We had to move our son to college so we needed a place to stay that wasn't too far from Downtown Denver, but not too expensive. This Quality Inn really was great. The area is a little industrial but for Denver, it is pretty quick on and off the freeway. The rooms are clean and comfortable and the hot breakfast buffet is great! We realized I had booked a King with 2 adults, but when we got their I figured that our son would need to stay with us at least 2 nights before staying in his Campus apartment. They quickly changed us to a room with 2 Queens, did not charge us any extra and never asked when he would come or go. Also, they had a refrigerator and microwave brought up to our room upon request...in 15 min from when we asked. The staff was very welcoming and helpful. There is a shuttle too and from the airport, there is free parking and although it is old, it is a fine place to stay. You do have noise from the freeway, but we don't mind it, it is "white noise" us!

My husband and I Love to stay at this small friendly hotel in soho. The location is perfect for walking, great restaurants and so convenient to the subway for getting to midtown. The hotel staff is extremely friendly and accommodating. They seem to know all their guests and call you by name! The rooms are immaculate...but small. Shower has a great shower head with great pressure and the bathroom is a decent size. The only reason I gave 4 stars VS 5 is because of the room size....but when in NYC you should not be spending time in your room! So much to see and do!

The hotel is very conviniently located within walking distance o many business and entertainment districts. The staff consistently makes an effort to make you feel at home and cared for. Free non alcoholic drinks and snacks at your fridge give it a nice local touch, can't complain about the free wine hour at the hotel lobby. Food and drink options are great, the tapas bar in the basement is a must. I have stayed three times during the last 2 years and can tell they are really growing up to the Andaz expectation.

The Omni on the Riverwalk is great, the view is awesome and the hotel staff are all friendly and very inviting. Overall the room was great, modern furniture, and very clean. However you will have to park across the street to avoid the $32.00 overnight Valet Parking Fee. The building has a historical design.
This was a great hotel in a great location! We walked from the White House to the Capital and everywhere in bewteen. Staff was great and the rooms large and clean!

In town for business, and this is really a good location. The room I'm in is a queen room, and although expensive by any other city standard, the room is lovely. I've stayed at multiple places in NYC, and the room is about the same size as other hotels. The hotel layout is quaint, with lots of older millwork and central staircases. No view to speak of, but that is not an issue for me. I found the duvet cover to be kind of stained on the outside, pulled it down and found stains on bottom side as well. Staff replaced within 15 minutes. Relatively quiet, and front guest service people are friendly.

Once again the Warwick Hotel exceeded out expectations. From the time of arrival, each staff member, from desk, to door, to housekeeping, to restaurant offered a smile and cheerful assistance. Accomodations are excellent, but the service "sells" us every time.

title_masked: Needs a renovation and a better kitchen...
text_masked:
I recently stayed here for 2 nights to attend a conference. Following is the summary of my experience:
Pros: comfortable beds, reasonably sized rooms, flat screen TV, friendly & helpful staff.
Cons: outdated bathroom, street noise despite being on the 16th floor, internet problems (no VPN). Also, we stayed in for dinner on the first night and regret that now. I don't easily complain about food but price/quality this was not up-to-par. Bartender was very friendly and accommodating however (credit where it belongs!)
So, overall, this was a very average experience for me and I will most likely not return here next time I'm in downtown LA.

A seventy two hour business trip. Hotel was excellent and the staff accommodated every request perfectly. The hotel is perfectly situated in the heart of Chicago. Hotel restaurant was OK but not brilliant. Overall the hotel is not cute boutique glamour ---- but is supremely functional and easy.

title_masked: Not really a hotel, more like a scam
text_masked:
My god what a dump !! This is the second worst hotel I have been in in my 25 years traveling. It's dirty, scuffed, worn and is a trap for out of town tourists. I had my new secretary book me into the dump. Got a first floor room that was like attempting to sleep on a loading dock, the bed was lumpy and hard. This was a $350+ room !! There was a grimy air conditioner that at least gave a "white noise" to block out the doors slamming, conversations in the lobby, sirens, people yelling on the street. This hotel isn't good enough for streetwalkers.
Who are these people staying there again and again!??! Have they never stayed in a decent 4 star hotel? Or perhaps they are super cheap and happy to save money despite the miserable conditions. Women, if your husband or boyfriend book this hotel for your trip to NY he is either a moron or doesn't love you.

We stayed here because it was close to our daughter at GW. They upgraded our room to a suite which was great, 2 rooms etc... The hotel is an older building which has nice character but does not feel old- meaning it is clean, fresh and nicely detailed with updated furnishings. Towels and bedding are really nice. The staff is super friendly and we loved the breakfast at the cafe. This is the best hotel close to the Foggy Bottom that we have stayed at. We will be back.

My husband and I have actually stayed at this property twice. It is definitely on the nicer side for a Hampton Inn. The lobby is very clean and classy, the rooms are spacious enough and clean, and they offer in-and-out overnight valet parking for $23 a day, which isn't bad. Service is very friendly and fast. We requested extra pillows our first night and they were brought to us immediately. They offer free internet in-room and free breakfast (not just muffins and bagels - there are eggs and other hot foods along with a Belgian waffle station in addition to the usual hotel breakfast foods). There is also a crepe restaurant attached to the lobby, which I thought was better for dessert crepes than savory crepes. The best part is the location, however. It is around the corner from the convention center and walking distance from shopping on 2nd street, bars on 6th street, and the river. Literally a 2-minute drive to the restaurants and shops on South Congress. If you are looking for an ideally located, clean hotel that offers extremely reasonable rates, I recommend this Hampton Inn.

Stayed two nights (Sat/Sun) given a newly refurbished room on the 19th floor. Very clean, quiet and comfortable. Love the little garden oasis on-site, but having a full Starbucks at the property, are you freakin' kidding me! Next time I'm asking for a room in the Starbucks.
Front desk staff was very helpful and professional, big shout-out to Jorge; he took good care of this HH Gold member. Found me new digs for LA area stays....bye-bye Hilton Warner Center.

I booked a room at The Mansfield for a long weekend in Feb 2012 and was glad I did. There is no shortage of hotels in the area but The Mansfield was great value for money. The location is unbelievably awesome...turn right out of the hotel and walk for 30 seconds and you'll be on the famous 5th Avenue...home of all the great shops and lets face it, people heading to NYC for a long weekend are probably there for the shopping and the sights. From 5th Avenue, you can hit the Rockefeller Center and do the Top of the Rock tour, walk down to the Empire State Building or go for a walk around Central Park. Turn left out of the hotel and walk for 5 mins and you're on Times Square...and I mean right on Times Square...right in the middle...fantastic during the day and even better at night when it's lit up.
The room I was given was on the 4th floor facing out the front and onto W44 Street...I wasn't expecting a view because the city is all highrise so bear that in mind, but there was nothing wrong with my view. The room comes with a mini bar (price list is in the room) flatscreen TV, comfortable double bed and a nice bathroom with plenty of towels. Maid service was offered everyday and the staff are fantastic throughout. The hotel has a reading room with free tea and coffee and the wi-fi signal is all over the building and is fast enough for any use. You can come and go as and when you please and staff are always on hand to assist.
I would highly recommend The Mansfield hotel to anyone visiting the city on New York.

When I booked this trip for my 14-year-old daughter and myself, I looked into competitively priced hotels. When I saw that the Waldorf Astoria was consistent with and even better than moderately-priced hotels, I didn't hesitate in booking it -- I wanted to brag that I stayed at The Waldorf! We were not disappointed -- upon check-in (we were a little early), they didn't have any of the queen bed rooms we we reserved, so they upgraded us to a king. My husband and I stayed in NY when we were younger and on a more limited budget and had a room we couldn't both walk in at the same time -- this room was fabulous -- the bathroom excellent. We didn't splurge on any of the restaurants on site -- they looked very fancy for a teenager and I, but the location was very close to everything we wanted to see: Rockefeller Center was a short walk, not to mention great shopping, Times Square, etc. Very pleased with our stay and the staff was excellent!

We traveled to NYC on the spur of the moment. Although we've never stayed at this property we like the area. Michelle, the front desk person, was very professional. She greeted us, told us about the property, helped us extend our stay another day, and treated our children with lots of care and thought. 
Another front desk person clearly did not have the same training but Michelle was there to pick up the slack! Dear owner of this property- give her a raise!
Other than staff performance, the location was perfect (3 blocks from the Canal street subway stop), a few blocks from high-end boutique shopping, and convenient on street parking on the weekend. The water pressure was great, bed was comfy, and the free breakfast in the morning was good. A great stay! We'll be returning to NYC in a few months so we know where we're staying.

title_masked: Great stay @ Red Roof Inn in Phoenix
text_masked: The Stay we had at the Red roof Inn in Phoenix was great, When to Phoenix to see the Rams play the Cardinals, The evening attend at the Red Roof Inn, was Amanda, She helped us in every way possible, From printing out directions to the movie threater, to a nice place to eat, and sunrise donuts...and much more!!!

title_masked: Location good, but as for the hotel itself: there is room for improvement
text_masked: I stayed at this hotel for 7 nights. The location of the Whitcomb is good, because you can get everywhere really easily. I walked or took tram F or bus 71 (both stop just outside the hotel). Also easy to reach from the airport by BART. You go up the escalator at Civic Center station and the hotel is just in front of you. The room was a good size and it was quiet. I was on the fifth floor. The bed was good, the pillows were terrible, so I slept on a towel which I had folded. The room was cold! So the duvet was not warm enough at night. As I had a double bed to myself, I was able to fold the duvet to make it extra warm. The information in the room says you can control the temperature in the room. Maybe they mean you can choose between cold and colder.......You really need to put on a sweater when you're in the room. I had breakfast in the restaurant (I believe it was called [NAME]) twice; it was good! The people at he concierge desk were great! Especially Vicky was really lovely and helpful! Olga at check in/check out was a little snooty. For the rest, I think use of the Internet should be free. It is in most hotels where I have stayed! This hotel charges 5 dollars for 20 minutes, 10 dollars for an hour; ridiculous! And, yes, many many homeless people in the area. One of them wanted to talk and got a little angry and aggressive (started to shout) when I didn't want to and just walked on. Some of them come up to you to ask for money, but on the whole they don't bother you. There is some police presence, but not a lot.

I started out on the wrong foot with this hotel as there was an issue with my booking. Maryann White the general manager, went the extra mile to accommodate us.
I don't like to give out 5 star ratings and I would rate this 4.5 if I could. I decided to give this hotel 5 stars as the staff really put it over the top. I know that I taken care of in part because of the issue I had early on, but all of the staff I encountered were extremely friendly and they treated all of their guests' well.
This a large older hotel and it shows it's age in places, so if you're looking for new and pristine I suggest you look elsewhere. I found that this hotel really excelled at accommodating my 2 year old twins. The hotel's best feature is it's outdoor pool... it's a great environment for families and groups of adults. The gym is also top notch, and not just a dumbbell and treadmill so many hotels call a gym.
I thought the location of this hotel was fine, and I think many of negative comments are from people not used to urban areas. This is NOT an Inner Harbor hotel, the Inner Harbor is about a 10-15 minute walk. Camden Yards is about a 5 minute walk. I suggest for a good meal/bar scene very nearby you check out Maisy's.
This hotel has room for improvement, but hosted a wide range of people well this weekend. I was apprehensive after reading some of the negative reviews here, but my family truly enjoyed our stay.

This is the second time my husband and I stayed at this La Quinta. The first time was a wonderful stay. No complaints. This time, however was not as enjoyable. I read about the roaches and did not notice any on the first night we stayed here. On the morning of our check out of our two night stay, my husband noticed a small brown roach crawling on the wall and went behind the picture frame. I was glad to be leaving because I don't think I could have stayed another night knowing there were roaches in the room. Other problems, when we arrived we were given keys to a room that had not been cleaned yet by housekeeping. We were immediately offered another room which had been cleaned. It appears that others have written about roaches and yet the hotel management does not take care of the issue. I guess they are not concerned since they are not the ones staying in the rooms. We will not return to this La Quinta. Too bad because we really enjoyed our stay for the most part, but cannot bare the thought of returning due to the unsanitary condition of the hotel.

title_masked: I was wrong. Please forgive me.
text_masked:
At best, I’m neutral about Hampton Inn hotels. They are usually ok in small towns, but I’ve been burned by Hampton’s in larger cities. I’ve passed by this hotel dozens of times during my trips to NYC and just assumed the worst. 
My sister and I stayed here for one night using her points. She had to convince me to try it because she knows how I feel about value priced hotels in large cities. This Hampton Inn has changed my perception. This hotel is great. It’s close to being (bleeping) awesome. 
The rooms are standard size Hampton rooms. The hotel didn’t downsize the rooms just because it was based in NYC. The hotel is clean and well kept. The free breakfast and the other Hampton amenities were available. Plus, the hotel has a few extra perks that aren’t normally found at Hampton Inn hotels including a concierge, doorman, security and welcome desk. The location on 8th Avenue is convenient for Times Square and other NYC attractions.
To all of the Hampton Inns that I’ve snubbed in the past, please accept my apologies. I was wrong. You’ve won me over.

The lobby is always noisy with music and lots of goings-on, adjoining the lounge and pub as it does. Each room has a guitar (which was not only in good condition but in tune!), and the decor is rock/pop themed - e.g. etched into the marble stairs as you walk up from the basement toilets to the lobby lounge is "Everything is going to be alright". The groundfloor coffeeshop serves up some of the best coffee in NY. Overall, this hotel keeps putting a smile on your lips...

title_masked: Great place to stay in Seattle
text_masked:
First I have to give a big hand to the staff we dealt with at Best Western. My initial contact was with Marsha (Marcia?) sorry unsure of spelling. She helped us with initial reservations and setting up car service from the airport to the hotel to the pier and back to the airport. She was very pleasant and easy to deal with. She was very helpful with suggestions and cost saving information. When we called to confirm prior to our trip we spoke with Justin, he was unable to confirm our car service and did not have all of our info. He said he would call us back. He called [NAME] at home and they were able to figure out the details. He did call us back and had the correct info and gave us a break on the transfer to the ship because of the confusion. When we checked in, Elisabeth was at the desk. We were a little early due to our flight schedule. She took our bags for us and secured them in the office and made a great recommendation for lunch, when we came back our room was ready. Great job to all of the staff at this location! 
The hotel is in a great location for walking to the Space Needle were you can easily catch the monorail to get downtown and to pike's place, etc.... The rooms are nice. The AC is a little noisy, but not too bad. The beds are comfortable. Everything is clean and neat. The breakfast was really good and had a nice variety. Overall a good hotal at a decent price in a good location. Would definitely recommend

We stayed at the Crowne Plaza LAX before taking off on an international flight the next morning. First off, they offer great military rates. We were pleasantly surprised by newly renovated rooms and very comfortable beds. The airport noise was next to nothing, and we had a decent view of the LA area. The hotel restaurant felt like something out of the 70's, but the service and food were good.
I would stay here again.

This Marriott is in a great location for federal workers traveling to GSA or ATF's central offices. It's an easy metro ride from DCA and just one stop past Union Station. There are some places to eat within walking distance, but many more just a redline metro trip west to Gallery Place. Overall the hotel is new and clean. The staff is friendly and helpful. Other than free internet, there really isn't much offered to Elite Marriott members, e.g. no free drinks, breakfast, etc.

We stayed in a two bed suite that was perfect for our girls week-end out. It had a sofa, two chairs and a coffee table in the living room. There was a deskspace area and a kitchen area with a sink, microwave, small refrigerator, and a coffee maker. It was great having two bathrooms so everyone could get ready. The beds were so soft and comfortable and the air-conditioning kept it cool at night. The rooms were large and clean. The front desk people were friendly and fast. Breakfast was the usual offerings.
One elevator was not working, but we never had to wait long for the other one to arrive. But it wasn't working when we stayed here in November either. This is a great place to stay for a week-end. It was next to the interstate, but we did not hear the traffic.

We had 2 rooms and spent a couple of days in Memphis seeing the sights. The first room smelled like smoke, so we changed rooms with no problem. The desk staff was helpful checking in and out. The hotel is about 12 miles from downtown and 19 miles from Graceland. It was easy to get to the interstate. Plenty of places to eat nearby. The bad stuff, no refer or microwave in my room. There was also no clock or hair dryer. The bath tub didn't drain very well and you stood in ankle deep water. It is an alright place for the money and also a good location to use as a home base.

title_masked: Short break in the Big Apple!
text_masked:
I was staying in this hotel for work and then stayed on for three more nights. It's a chain hotel and the reception is fairly nondescript. The main positive is location. One block from Times Square (you can hear the hustle from the 22nd flr, but it's not too bad), close to the theatres, a short walk from Hell's Kitchen and the restaurants, and the subway is under the building so travelling around is easy if you don't fancy walking.
The bar is nice and the service good, but why put it on the 2nd floor! Stick it on the 42nd and you'd not spend the evening looking at the fashing lights on 8th St.
Room is a good size for NYC although for the rates you're paying, you would hope it would be better than average!

We have stayed here twice - once at Christmastime and once around July 4th. We love the location - near Times Square but away from all the hubub. The staff has always been wonderful, the rooms clean, the breakfast in the a.m. ample and fresh. The rooms are actually a good size for NYC - I visited a friend in a neighboring hotel and you could not move in her room with the bed - but here no problems at all.

Seldom do I take the time to write reviews but would feel remised if I didn't take a moment to mention what a remarkable time my family and I had this past weekend at the Sheraton Hotel and Towers. The General Manager went so above and beyond the call of duty by making my family feel so important and welcome that I'm not sure words would accurately describe how well it went.
There is no doubt in mind that whenever my family and I stay in Chicago, it will be with Mr [NAME] and his staff at the Sheraton Hotel and Towers.
Thanks again for making our weekend SO special. The memories will last forever.

I've stayed at many hotels while in San Francisco and decided to give the Parc 55 a try after a friends recommendation... and I'm glad I did! The location was central, check-in was quick and friendly, and I actually found my room quite quiet, being so close to Market and Powell Streets! The property and room was extremely clean, and I was fortunate to be in corner room which has a spacious bathroom. I will definitely consider the Parc 55 on my next visit to San Francisco.
Kelly

Nice business hotel very convenient to Century City, excellent alternative to nearby Hyatt. 
Rooms are modern and clean, bathrooms excellent. Some rooms have windows that did not open, so if this is important you may want to make a specific request.
Public areas were inviting and newly redone. Resaurant nicer than most, with very cute individually controlled TV's at some booths. No pool, but nice hot-tub on deck.

Our room was on the 16th floor with great three sided views of downtown San Francisco, very pretty. There was a sun room to sit in with floor to ceiling windows to enjoy the view. The whole experience was a nice treat !

I love having tea at the Four Seasons. The food & service are excellent. The Swan room is so cozy and the view of the fountain is awesome. For any occassionor just to treat yourself, this is a special treat.
