Stayed here once because I had an interview in Austin. I loved this hotel it was affordable especially compared to the other hotels. The interior and exterior of this hotel was perfect. My room was very clean and the beds were comfortable. I used their Shuttle Bus service to go to and from the airport it was great. Their breakfast was great too. I'll always stay here from now on when I have to go to Austin.

We stayed at this hotel the last week of October and first week of November 2012 for the Sweet Adelines Convention. The hotel was clean and very modern. The rooms were spacious and I loved that all the rooms looked down into the atrium. The all-you-can-eat breakfast was spectacular! Tommy made the best omelet I've ever tasted. He even came to watch the contest! The staff was incredibly friendly - especially the valets. We used Abdul to pick us up and drop us off at the airport. He was very knowledgeable, polite, timely and friendly! The happy hours were a wonderful treat - even though they ran out of red wine :) Our room faced 16th Avenue and it was quite noisy....good thing I brought ear plugs. I would HIGHLY recommend this hotel to everyone!!

title_masked: NIce but expected more from a luxury property
text_masked: For 10 years we have stayed downtown the Fri. and Sat. after Thanksgiving. We like trying new hotels so this was our first experience with this property in Chicago. We were really looking forward to our stay since this hotel just made Conde Nast Best in the World 2012 list coming in at number 9 in the midwest. Well it was nice but, top 9 in the midwest? I dont know what critera they used but I did not think it lived up to the rating. The hotel definitely caters to a foreign guest. The lobby was nice but unlike most of the other Chicago hotels sported no holiday decorations. Couches were of a chaise style making sitting awkward at best. We received a corner room. It was much smaller than I expected. The bed was very comfortable and the linen was of very good quality - however there was no top sheet. The room had a Bose radio. The closet was lit and had a safe, padded hangers and robes. We set the thermostat at 65 degrees and the room never cooled to that temp. When the fan ran it had an annoying whistle hum. The window did not open. The view was non descriptive. The tv was placed on the desk in front of the mirror cutting the limited work space in half. It should be hung on the wall in my opinion. The bathroom was large with a huge walk in shower. There was a window in the bathroom which was nice. There was a thermostat in the bathroom but that did not cool down to 65 either. Our kids were in a room with double beds. Their room seemed even smaller than ours and had a tight desk arrangement and no easy chair. We had to call housekeeping twice for extra towels. The first time we called no one ever came. Also called for a top sheet which was needed because the room was so warm - and having to wait 30 minutes for that when you want to go to bed was annoying. I have no complaints with this hotel but was expecting something a bit more exciting. As far as location - if you are doing Michigan Ave it is great. Over the years we have come to enjoy a RIver North Hotel location more because of the proximity to State Street, Michigan Ave and River North restaurants and bars. For me it would come down to the price. At over $300 a night I don't think it is a value. However if you snag it on Hotwire or LMT ($150) it was worth it.

I stayed here for a work thing. My room was HUGE it had two double beds, a table and two chairs, a desk and chair with a network point, a TV bigger than the one I have at home, huge chest of drawers, balcony, mini bar with loads of drinks and snacks, two wardrobes and iron and ironing board and an amazing bathroom....... huge two person bath, walk in large shower, hair dryer, premium toiletires, more fluffy towels than you will ever need in a life time, robes, slippers.... need I go on?
Everynight there was a turn down service who brought chocolates and ice and in the morning the local paper was hanging on your door.
I had room service one night and was really impressed. I had the Cesar Salad (starter size) and it was huge, when it came there was water, more ice, full set of conidments, silverware etc. And it was super fast service 
The public areas were all lovely and really well maintained.
We had a conference room at the far end of the Business Centre which is a huge facility. they have numerous conference and meeting rooms. 
Our conference was well served with great lunches and snacks. 
There is a internet room you can use that has a printer and, randomly, a cash machine. 
We had dinner in the Gallery restaurant once night and the food was excellent, though the service was a little slow, I think that had more to do with our party's faffing about than the staff themselves.
Overall I was really impressed and would not hesitate to recommend this hotel.

title_masked: Poor service, small rooms, no hot water
text_masked:
Chose to stay at the liaison based on the reviews. It was the most unpleasant stay of our 5 week US trip. Arrived in Washington by train and walked to the hotel, in this process I fell over due to the uneven paths near the hotel (ot hotels fault). When we got to the hotel with a bleeding hand and knee, the hotel staffed advised there were no rooms clean and we would have to wait ( this was well after the 3pm checkin time). After waiting half an hour in pain and still bleeding we asked if a room was ready and they said one had just been finished. Still no help offered with our bags or any information given about hotel.
Room was very small with no space for bags. There was no hot water each morning, so it was cold showers for us, not good in cold weather with children.
We went and asked directions to the pharmacy to get bandages for hand and knee and still no offer of assistance from the staff.
We did not eat at the hotel as when we went to the restaurant the staff were rude and said you can only get room service as they were full ( plenty of spare tables both at this time and when we came back from another restaurant).
The hotel charged me for the accommodation even though it was prepaid with a voucher. They corrected the charge on check out but the refund took over 5 days to be back on my credit card.
Avoid this place there is better accommodation in Washingon DC.

Loved this hotel, rooms were great, very clean. Nice comfortable bed, big rooms fully equipped kitchen. Concierge were lovely even at 1 am in the morning when I was doing my washing and kept hassling them for change. I had no problem with train noise however our room didn't back onto the train tracks. Would definitely stay there again especially if I bought my children back to San Diego. Not far from little Italy where the food is Devine.

Hotel 140 was one of the most most pleasurable hotels that I've stayed at in Boston. For the price, you can't beat the pleasant and accomodating staff or the location to all of Boston's finest restaurants and acitvities. I would highly recommend trying Hotel 140, and you will likely never go anywhere else.

title_masked: Can't beat location and price with kids
text_masked: 5 blocks from the natural history museum and central park, one block from Grom gelato enough said! Two kids on solo vacation with Mom. Construction didn't bother us because we were gone from 9-5 and then again in the evening each day.

We had a weekend stay at this hotel (2 nights) for a short holiday.
The Residence Inn and Courtyard are next to each other (same entrance, same parking, same breakfast). We chose this because we were 3 people (wife and a friend) and needed to use the sofa bed.
The stay: The stay was comfortable. The rooms and not as large as typical Residence Inns but that's very common in any downtown. Everything looked renovated. We were away from the noise (6th street),s o the sleep was great too. The shower, amenities were pretty standard. The breakfast was probably the best part. Complimentary, continental, plus biscuits and gravy which is my favorite. The internet was slow at best but did the job. The sofa bed was comfortable too according to the friend. No complaints whatsoever here.
Note: Self-parking here is $21/day, valet is $27/day.
The location: In short, PERFECT!! We chose this hotel looking at a map and it worked out great. Walking to one side was 6ht street, so convenient! On the other side, half a mile away was the bridge where the bats come out in the night and also a place where we could rent canoes. The drive to UT is so close, plus we did not feel far when we went to Barton Springs.
When in Austin, in addition to the common attractions, do check out the Austin Steam Train Hill country tour and take your swimwear to the Barton Springs Pool.
b.

Conveniently connected to the prudential tower. If you are taking the train in from the airport. get off at the Prudential stop on the green line and you go right into the mall. Short walk to the sheraton. The hotel was packed when we visited, though we still managed a upgrade to the starwood preferred floors. The room though had a small closet for hanging your coats and clothing. Mattress was slightly worn, needs to change soon. Bottled water complimentary 2 per day. A continental breakfast was offered, fresh fruit, yogurt, pastry, cereals and beverages. Pretty much the same spread everyday. Computers (2) were available to use in the lounge and at the lobby but for some reason they were very slow in loading the pages. Took the taxi back to the airport, was about 30 dollars.It was a good stay here at the Sheraton Boston. Will visit again,

title_masked: our recent stay at the palomar hotel, philadelphia
text_masked:
We are a couple of tourists from Turin, Italy, and have just returned from a trip to the States spending in our last stay at the middle of September a couple of nights at the Palomar Hotel of Philadelphia which left us greatly disappointed.
The building in itself lacks of charm with a cold, falsely stylish lobby where, as well advertised, every day it is possible to taste a glass of wine free from 5 to 6 pm with no side dishes, not even a slice of ham, but popcorn.
This, I am afraid, is nevertheless the only frill of this hotel where breakfast, not included in the room price, is served at the first floor in an unpleasant environment : we tried it the first day and consisted in few and cold pastries and little more.
Rooms are large but another time with no charm.
With the exception of the central position and the friendliness of the staff I find it hard to find anything positive about this hotel, maybe more apt for job meetings (hoping people are eligible for price reductions) than for tourists: in this last case the price requested is grossly overcharged.
Overall we left with a very poor impression and would not recommend it to anyone.

After weeks of searching for the perfect area,hotel,activity to do for a weekend, away from all the grind. Malibu would have been nice and remote, SaMo is great but very busy and too city-like, Manhattan Beach is great but a bit out of touch and old. All in all, we settled on Venice Beach and the Hotel Erwin for the perfect location.
Of course booking is the first part of a process, the next is waiting for the date to come around. Once it did, it was as if the weather cleared up the day we arrived just for us.. With two days of 75 degree weather, and sunshine our major activities were as such: Surfing & Paddleboard lessons (Awesome), Bicycle rentals to cruise miles along the beach (Must-Do), and the rooftop lounge for Sunset.
Now, Venice isn't for everyone but the Hotel Erwin makes a decent attempt with the friendly and responsive staff. I would come here or recommend the Hotel Erwin to any of my family or friends, and really enjoyed the time away with my girlfriend for a weekend.

We throughly enjoyed our stay at Doubletree Guest Suites Times Square. First of all, we could not have picked a better location! It's smack in Times Sq. To the left of the front door of the hotel is the entrance to the train station. Most of the main Broadway shows are a hop,skip and a jump. Rockefeller Center is a few blocks a way, a little further is Central Park, the list goes on. Staff at the hotel were wonderful in helping us with directions. We bought our hop on and hop off pass at the hotel. We went with the red bus. We NEVER had any problems catching the bus. It's a busy city and there were plenty of buses . Back to hotel. It was very comfortable! Someone had previously posted that the suites are 200sq.ft divided into two rooms. I don't know where this person stayed but it wasn't at this hotel. Each room was 200-300 sq ft. Living room had couch,chair,table ,flat screen tv. wet bar,frig ,microwave. There is also a seperate snack refrig. that you can pay for (too expensive). Room had king size bed ( very comfortable-slept well),flat screen Tv.We ate at Roxys (expensive but very good),Johns Pizza (excellant), Ellens Stardust diner (where wait staff sing and dance -FUN). Heard an excellant three piece blues band at BB King's, saw David Letterman,World Trade Center Memorial, walked around Central Park. So much to do and not enough time, we are going back and staying at Doubletree again.

After a 12 hour day from Nashville, my wife and I were looking for a problem free hotel. We thought we'd give the Knights Inn chain another try (after a previous horror story). I walked into the lobby and was greeted by a friendly couple. They made our check in and stay very agreeable. The room was spacious and welcoming. Very positive experience.

Just returned from a 3 day weekend in NYC. By pure chance, we stayed at the Hilton Times Square...and what a nice hotel. The room was spacious and comfortable, the location is superb (just a block from the Port Authority) and convenient to theatres, public transportation and good restaurants. The staff is accomodating. The Sky Bar and restaurant is good for drinking and people watching (good breakfast buffet, too). The only drawback was no food service after the theatre...but there are plenty of late night places closeby.

Stayed here on a work/play trip in mid november and I was pretty happy with it. First off, for people expecting an opulent looking luxury hotel, this isn't one of those. This is old hollywood vintage/modern, charming hotel with a bit of history to its property. I actually prefer this type of hotels with a boutique feel than cookie cutter "luxury" so this worked perfectly for me. 
The rooms are ample sized, with the bathroom being a tad tight but nothing too crippling. I was situation in room 101- probably the best/worse room due to easy access to the pool and the bar but also annoying and noisy due to drunk people making noise at night. 
The location of the hotel is excellent, if you are a tourist, I don't see how it can get any better. You've got all your hollywood sights plus some good shopping within 2-5 minute walking distance. The hotel food is also great (I ate at 25 degrees a few times and it was all yummy). The staff are great, I was with a friend who is a regular at the hotel and everyone knew him by his name and were very accommodating- a sense of community and relationship with its clients. The only bad I can report is that the concierge was no where to be seen when I needed some help- I called and called and called and even visited the desk to no avail. Also the WIFI is not free and is $15-21 dollars- a little high if you ask me. For a hotel of this repuation and price point, I expect wifi for guests (or at least for frequent guests) to be complimentary. But then again, it's forgiven because they have the best, most charming pool in LA. The pool is always heated and so warm so make sure you take advantage of it!

title_masked: Most Centrally Located, Best Value Hotel in NYC with Super Staff
text_masked:
The hotel is smoothly run with friendly, helpful staff. Front desk staff were working so hard to make check-in as quick as possible for everyone, considering so many people were checking out when we arrived. This is a popular hotel so book early as service and amenities are so much better than expected of a Hampton. This was the BEST Hampton we've ever stayed at. All of the Day front desk staff were wonderful. But there was one b-class evening front desk gal who seemed lazy, only interested in herself, and not in helping hotel guests at all. 
Our room was on a higher floor looking out to the street, the Empire State Bldg, and Macy's (it is worth the extra $ to face the street as you really feel like you're in NYC) and even with construction on the street(they were just working on a small section and are likely done by now), with the double-paned windows closed, you barely hear anything. The room, while not large, was spacious enough for NYC. It was renovated recently so the bedding was very new. The comforter was not lumpy like other Hamptons. The bathroom was very clean with a great shower. There were not many rooms to each floor so housekeeping was not noisy like we've experienced at other hotels where they yell across the floor while cleaning. 
Considering this hotel was only $5 more dollars than the stingy old Courtyard Tremont in Boston(which did NOT provide breakfast) and included breakfast for up to 4 people as well as complimentary bottled water at the front desk if you ask, this hotel is the best bargain in NYC. The breakfast has a vast selection of food. The most choices of any Hampton I've been to across the country. And quite a few healthy options too. The breakfast room is modern, very clean, airy thanks to a covered "alfresco" section. But get down there early as it will fill up even on a weekday unless you don't mind waiting your turn to get items, and sharing tables with other parties. 
For first time visitors, there are 2-3 subways stations within 5 minutes walk of the hotel. The Empire State Building, Penn Station are just a block away. Times Square is an easy 5-7 minute walk (it's safe to walk to at night, filled with tourists, and it's pretty all lit up) as are theaters. Grand Central and the Library is also an easy 10 minutes walk. If you are active you can walk to Central Park, and museums but you'll probably want to take the subway/bus back. To take the bus, you have to have exact change if you don't have a metro card(which we didn't yet due to jetlag), and the drivers are not nice about it at all - they were the only rude people we encountered this time. 
This is the PERFECT hotel to stay at if you're going for the Macy's Thanksgiving parade or New Year's Eve since you won't have to walk far at all in the cold.

title_masked: South of Market but convenient to Moscone Center
text_masked: This hotel served as the "overflow" hotel for the 2012 ASCO GU meeting, which itself was held at the nearby Marriott Marquis. I am delighted that I was referred to this porperty. The rooms are spacious, the breakfast is excellent and the fitness facility is well equipped. The location just next to the Moscone Convention Center is ideal for the conference traveler

Pros: Great location, quiet rooms available in the heart of the city... spacious spa rooms. The staff is very kind and friendly, late checkout was allowed, dupont circle near by, restaurants are close by. I loved the tubs...large enough for 2, and they provide bath salts. Well done!
Cons: could use a couch vs. the 2 small chairs they offer. The lobby could be bigger... they offer wine service during the evening, but there is literally almost nowhere to sit. 
I'd return for meeting but it's not quiet luxurious enough or expansive to feel like you're truly getting away for a weekend. Great for a business trip or for travelers out of town.

A group of 4 couples stayed at La Canterra the weekend of Sept. 28 - 30. My husband & I have stayed there several times, but not in recent years. The stay was as enjoyable as it had been in the past. We had a deluxe king room with step-out balcony overlooking the courtyard. Very nicely decorated room in creams, whites & browns. The bed was very comfortable and there was a nice vanity area outside the bathroom. The bathroom has double sinks and a large tub/shower with a rainhead showerhead. Internet is included in the resort fee of $24/day and was easy to get on. All the staff were very friendly and courteous.
Late September is a great time to go for a couples vacation because there are fewer children. That's one of the reasons we stopped going to large resorts - to many children running around and that's one of the things we're trying to get away from. This weekend was especially quiet. The pool areas were well kept and very quiet. The views from the Adult pool is spectular.
The ladies all had a massage at the Castle Rock Spa. It was wonderful and I highly recommend the skilled hands of Stephanie. We all stopped afterwards and enjoyed more quiet time in the Tranquility Room. Very soothing. The changing room has a dry sauna that we also enjoyed.
One night the group enjoyed late nite drinks at Steinheimers. Great bar, plenty of room and we loved the blue lights on the trees outside the bar.
A very nice stay.

title_masked: Another Trip to Quarter Horse Congress
text_masked:
We came back to our favorite hotel for a weekend at quarter horse congress at the ohio state fairgrounds.
I have reviewed this hotel before and have been quite happy here. This is an older residence type hotel made up of several buildings each containing about 8 suites. The Desk Clerks have always been local people with English as a first language. Always very pleasant.
We made our reservations early and arrived late. They have two basic types of rooms. the lower suite room that is more like a regular hotel and the upper level suites that are a bit more expensive but have a private bedroom with its own bathroom and a loft room with its own bathroom. There is a nice little kitchen area with dishes and a fridge, stove sink etc. All set for an extended stay if need be.
What I believe they do is sell out the rooms as people come. I had reserved the smaller room this time because we were traveling a lot this year and trying to save money. We arrived late, almost midnight and were surprised with an upgrade to the executive suite or whatever they call it. That was like a $40 a night upgrade. I think they were able to sell our lower cost room and just put us (a twice a year customer) into the better room.
This was like the fourth different suite we have been in at this hotel. Remember that it is old and there are some things that are just worn. For example the sink in our bathroom was just slow draining. There was a patch on the bathroom floor. But the room was fairly clean and didn't appear to have bugs. I've read other reviews on here and I think many people confuse the worn out rooms with dirty rooms. This place is clean folks, just well worn out. (saving you $$$)
I've stayed in rooms that cost nearly $300 a night and all we got was a very clean bed, bathroom and lcd tv to watch. This place gave my daughter privacy and her own tv, I had a TV in the living room (crt screen but okay). a coffee table for my feet and a full sized sofa.
My wife got the whole bedroom to herself until I finished watching TV and came to bed.
Upon arrival we were told that on the weekends, room service is by request only. I immediately asked for it (During Congress - October - they need to make it regular on weekends). We came back to the hotel and there had been no service. I called the desk and they brought extra towels for us and apologized for the inconvenience.
I took pictures but they are on my iphone and I just don't want to go get the cord for it.
There is a breakfast in a nice dining room in the morning. We ate well with fruit, eggs, sausage, waffles, sausage gravy and biscuits, juice, milk, coffee, yogurt, muffins, bagels etc etc. They even have replaced the table. There was a nice lady keeping everything stocked up. I think her name was [NAME] (just kidding family Guy fans).
Again, overall the place was not super nice but considering the best rooms are only about $130 a night and you get plenty of privacy and breakfast in the morning it is a great value. I'd also stay here if I planned to spend a lot of time in the room.
If you want a newer hotel people have told us to go to the Polaris Parkway. However the rooms are more expensive, smaller, and a couple miles away (but my have jacuzzis if you are lookin for that)
While it is not all perfumed and new smelling, there are not turn-down services or free newspapers this is probably our familys favorite hotel at a value price!

Would not stay anywhere else in the area. Clean rooms, friendly,outstanding staff (even if I left somethings behind) they arranged for me to get it returned to me. Will be staying here again in the future. Weekly rates also allow a great stay at a reduce price in the middle of the city

i don't know what's the deal with the front desk attendant ( not sure what his name is but it's the elder guy he talks with an accent ) . but for some reason he is very rude. ok he called my room saying people keep calling my room back to back, so i replied i didn't receive any calls. then he replied tell people to stop calling you we are busy here , and when i tried to respond he kept talking well actually fussing at me as though i was his child then hung up the phone..he was very very very rude and this wasn't his first time speaking to me in this manner. he was unprofessional. and by the way how can i tell someone not to call if i don't know if their calling

We were in N.Y. in May 2012. We chose this hotel because of the proximity to Time Square. Desk staff were very courteous and very helpful. We chose a larger room which was very clean and very comfortable and we had free WiFi. A basic breakfast was included in the downstairs bar area.
We would certainly recommend this hotel to everybody.

Front desk was exceptional in arranging a change request after arrival.
Property and room was very clean and trendy, as is my experience with the W hotels.

This is my second time back for business. I love the way the staff treats me a family. They are accomodating and friendly. Jacob, the conceige, sends me to all the best farm to table resturants and they have been fantastic. The hotel is half a block away from the center of Time Square, yet the hotel is quiet and restful. They have a wonderful rooftop bar which has a great comfortable intimate feel. I've had a large room and a smaller room here. I am very happy with this gem!

A great room for $87 a night! We had an early flight and wanted to be close to the airport, so I booked this room for some place to flop for a night. This was NO FLOP HOUSE. The room was huge, king bed, great pillows, not only a flat screen TV but it was actually HDTV! The bathroom showed some age but everything worked fine. The shampoo smelled so good I took it!
If I had to find a fault it would have to be the curtains. There were shears with a heavy curtain but they didn't close. So my wife was afraid of someone watching us from another hotel quite a ways away...

A small super efficiently run hotel. Friendly staff. Immaculate rooms with wonderfully comfortable beds. Large modern bathroom with oversized walk-in shower. Lovely restaurant with reasonably priced delicious breakfasts. 
We had no complaints and highly recommend this hotel.

Great location just a few blocks east of all the restaurants and stores on M street in Georgetown and just a few blocks west of DuPont Circle. And just a five minute walk to the Foggy Bottom Metro station. 
Room was clean and very quiet - thick walls and windows. Nothing really special about the room, but it was what I expected. Comfy heavenly beds. Nice flat screen TV. Your basic chair and desk. Bathroom clean though a bit spartan. No tub. 
A bit dissapointed the pool was not open, but it was mid April, notwithstanding the 90 weather in DC while we were there.
Check in and doormen were efficient. The pitcher of lemon water in the lobby was a nice touch.
Did not eat in the hotel or drink in the bar, as most of the time we were out sightseeing.
I give it average because it was what I expected from a Westin - nothing more, nothing less..
But again, great location.

Got four rooms with a group for a weekend. Matt Whormes and the staff at the CQ Boston showed us exceptional service: helping us correct our rooms from one bed to two, getting extra blankets, helping us store our luggage after checkout. Somehow, that guy was everywhere in the hotel!

The hotel is beautifull. The area also beautifull & we felt safe. Very close to eatery's, things to do, and Airport. 
I said nothing about service because I was only there to sleep for 2 nights and the most contact I had was that my 2nd key card never worked, even after having it made 3 times. I got tired of going down and back up, so we made do with one card. 
I do not know why nor did I ask the reason we had a handicapped room. It was very uncomfortable. No room for my mother & self to put our toiletries in bathroom. I decided to open ironing board in bathroom to use as a table. 
The pillows were bumpy. The room was the smallest we have ever stayed in & very uncomfortable, we are accustomed to more room, we usually stay at Holiday Inn Express at most of our stays any place we go. This is the first time we stay at a Baymont Inn & Suites. The room we had was more suited for one king or queen bed only, not for 2 beds. I know the cookies do not need to be offered and it's a nicety on your part, Holiday Inn usually has them also, but yours were not very tasty, I suggest a change in brand. Breakfast was good the day I could have it, the next day we had to be on our way by 3:30 AM, I asked if there was anything I could get at that time a yogurt, juice, anything & was told no. I know breakfast is not till 5, but 2 yogurts will not break the bank. But rules are rules.....
We did not make use of Services so I have no rating for them, we traveled instead. You need to add N/A (not applicable) in your survey.
I would recommend your hotel as long as it's one person staying in the room. I do not know how your other rooms are, guess I should have requested a change of room but we arrived tired and we just wanted to sleep. So I can not say if it would have a difference.

I redeemed a free night that I had earned through Marriott Rewards at this hotel, so keep in mind that I didn't pay a dime to stay here.
I was very pleased with the room. It did feel slightly dated, but it was large, clean, and comfortable. The person working the front desk was extremely friendly, as I would expect for a Marriott. The free breakfast was fantastic! Couldn't have been happier there.
I have always enjoyed staying at various Marriott brand hotels, and this hotel was no exception.

This is a cracker of a hotel. We stayed 2 nights. The front desk staff are friendly, warm, welcoming and really know their city. There is a brilliant supermarket right next door with a great wine selection and good service. This lovely old Hotel is in a good location and the rooms are of a generous size. Breakfast is really good with plenty of good coffee as well. Has good internet access and a lovely lounging area. This hotel really knows how to cater for travellers and tourists alike. A nice atmosphere and we really enjoyed our stay.

We have stayed here many times as we embarked on a driving tour or cruise from Boston. We have been struck by the helpful, upbeat attitude of the staff. The shuttle drivers were there to help, and always had a smile. Ditto for checkin desk, maids, and the waiters on the restaurant. I needed several items from the gift shop and they too scurried out and helped me locate exactly what I wanted. Yes, it is a bit pricy but the beds are comfortable, it is quiet, the breakfasts in restaurant were hot and tasty and the positive attitude of the "team" cannot be overemphasized. It makes a difference in the attitudes of the guests when they feel valued. Keep it up

During a recent trip to San Fran we stayed for two nights at the W. 
1. Ambiance - this hotel and most W properties exude this impossibly hip vibe. Beautiful people, club music, funky furnishings. It doesn't negatively impact your experience but it doesn't make you want to buy a black turtleneck either.
2. Staff - Awesome. Nice efficient. Helpful. TV in room not working? One call to front desk results in pleasant service guy at my door within 10 minutes who fixes problem. Ahhh...
3. Location - great location for exploring the city. Very central. No need for car.
4. Room - clean, small but efficiently designed. Am I the only person who hates the clock with the IPod docking station that WON'T CHARGE AN IPHONE? I suspect not. Let's do away with them and just dangle charging cords. Toiletries keep getting smaller and there was enough shampoo to wash 1/3 of your scalp but these are minor complaints. Room was comfortable and quiet.
5. Other- the Acura MDX drop off service is the best. Sign up at the desk adjacent to the front desk and you'll get a free ride where ever you want to go. Only, unfortunately, they won't pick you up so plan ahead.

I recently stayed at this hotel with family. We were in town for a funeral. This is a very large hotel that has an Omaha Steaks restaurant located on the first floor. You can do in-room dining or dine in the restaurant. The rooms are spacious, if you're lucky enough to not get a corner room where the living room is significantly smaller. I was moved to a corner room the second day because our bathroom wasn't functioning properly. The staff was very helpful and professional about the situation. This hotel has the best hot breakfast hands down. So many options and the sitting area was very relaxing. I will definitely stay here again if when visiting family in Charlotte.

We recently stayed at this hotel for one hight, prior to an Alaskan cruise. There was an error (by CelebrityCruises) in notifying the hotel of our paid reservation. The front desk was great inhandling the situation- immediately found us a room, upgraded to a corner King room, called us back when allwas straightened out, an an apology from the hotel. Yes, Chris was especially good at his job at the front desk (as a previous reviewer noted). He was not the concierge but he said he wears a lot of different hats and would help us anyway he could. He found us a great seafood restaurant around the corner called [NAME] and we received an appetizer upon handing the waitress a card from Chris. 
The King room was plenty nice enough and the view was urban, but nice. Very quiet room and the place was really clean and luxurious. 
The cafe on the first floor was hip and busy the next morning, but I managed to get them to fresh-squeeze some orange juice for us "to go" (not on the menu).

In Phoenix for business, I stayed at Springhill Suites which was very close to the baseball stadium (Chase Field) as well as the shops downtown. The hotel was clean and the staff very friendly. One night an alarm was sounding for quite some time in the wee hours of the morning. Guess they took care of it as it went off, but no good sleep that night! Other than that, I liked the refridgerator and microwave in the room. And the complimentary shuttle will pick you up and drop you off at the airport.

title_masked: Great location, convenient shuttle.. but could be cleaner!
text_masked: Stayed at this hotel closer to airport since had a early morning flight next morning. very near to airport and have convenient shuttle, but the room and property could have been little cleaner than what it was.

What a great hotel staff and service were brilliant and made the stay here first class.
will stay here again when on business.

title_masked: Really old, but really sweet hotel Old-fashioned, not for corporate types, that is for sure!
text_masked:
This is a cheap hotel that has kept its charm. I must immediately warn, though, that this is not a hotel for people who want a top shelf boutique hotel. Although clean, and relatively well maintained, it is very old fashioned, and looks aged. However. It looks like a real old-west hotel, and the rooms were gigantic for a surprisingly low price. In addition, the staff are both gruff and at the same time helpful. I was going out to get a quick bite, and they directed me to the far better of the two quick-eats places (I know because I specifically checked later by tasting at both:).
If you want a cheap hotel in the middle of everything, or at least no more than 5-6 blocks from everything, well, this is it, look no farther. The breakfast, though, well, you should just skip it and go to a diner nearby!

Stayed at this hotel during a business trip. As a LaQuinta Gold level rewards club member I frequent this chain. Once again I was not disappointed. Neal, the front desk manager was courteous and handled my registration smoothly and quickly. He was very quick to ask if I needed any assistance with anything and when I asked to be upgraded he did so to a great King room with a HUGE plasma screen TV. THe room itself was clean and the bed was super. I commented on the bed and Neal said all the mattresses in the hotel had been replaced about 4 weeks ago. THe room also had a refrigerator and microwave and both were spotless.
I would definitely stay here again.

The hotel's location is excellent: very close to a lot of restaurants in the back bay area, a walking distance to the bay promenade, shops, down town, close to metro. The staff is friendly. The things that I did not like: very small room, if you open a window there is constant background noise either from construction or the highway and you need to sleep with air conditioning on although it is not too warm outside.The room has no wadrobe, frige or a coffee maker. You can store something in a frige in the lobby and there is a coffee machine downstairs.The bathroom is very small.

title_masked: Cool with breathtaking view of city
text_masked: Very cool boutique hotel in Hell's Kitchen. It is not the greatest location but a room on the higher floors have spectacular views of the city skyline...which is definitely worth a few extra blocks of walking. Young eager helpful staff. The roof top bar, unfortunately had a private party and was closed the night that we were there. The premium rooms have large bathroom with soaking tub and shower, I will be back.

title_masked: Great Stay -- just hope they don't charge me for two rooms
text_masked: This hotel is ideally located; close to everything. It's a little rundown, but if you don't plan to stay in the room much, it's a great hotel. The beds were fantastic. The bathrooms were clean; water pressure amazing; view of 7th Ave. amazing. My only complaint is when I checked in they did not show our reservation made through Book.It.com (even though I had called two days prior to request early check-in; seemed to find my reservation then -- or did they?). Thankfully I had my Book.It.com confirmation with me so I gave it to the manager and she said she would look into why my reservation wasn't showing up in their system, and stated it was probably because they had a new reservation system. They stated they were unable to offer early check-in and advised me to check back @ 1:00. When I came back @ 1:00 they stated they still did not have rooms available for early check-in, but this time they had 2 rooms reserved under my name; I told them I had only paid for one room through Book.It.com, at which point they said they would cancel one room. I stated I was concerned I could get charged for two rooms and to PLEASE make sure to cancel one room, at which point she said she had. She also said to come back @ 3:00; that no rooms would be available until normal check-in time; came back @ 3:00 only to find they STILL had two rooms reserved under my name; again I asked to please cancel one room. At the end of our stay I asked what was needed to check out; they said the room was already paid with no incidentals, so all I needed to do was to leave my keys in the room -- BUT I forgot to ask if they still had me down for two rooms -- just hope they don't charge me for two rooms !!!

Great location - in walking distance of the Metro, Little Italy, East Village - very basic amenities.
You may need to ask for extra towels, or toilet roll- Happy with Clean beds. Bathroom could be updated - as with the carpeting throughout the property. Located on Forsyth Street opposite open community space/park. Nice change from being boxed in.

title_masked: Great Place to Stay in San Francisco
text_masked: We stayed in a one bedroom suite here over the Fourth of July weekend. We actually took advantage of a special rate they were running that included the parking fee ($50/day). This was an excellent opportunity to save some money and stay at a beautiful hotel in a convienient location. The service was excellent and the hotel has wonderful amenities. I stayed here several years ago and the property has not changed in quality. It is close enough to use public transportation and there are excellent restaurants near by.

This hotel is trying very hard to be trendy. The rooms are tiny. I've stayed in many hotels through Manhattan, and this is by far the smallest room I've been in. The room seemed very clean, but there was urine down the front of the toilet in the bathroom. The towels and sheets and toiletries are all premium. There was a jug of flavored water in the lobby by the elevators, that was a nice touch. The workers were all friendly and helpful, though the management let me down (story below). Everything from the mini-bar to the food and drinks were incredibly overpriced (even considering the area).
I really was hoping to love this place, especially considering the location and amenities. However, I had a pretty poor experience that I had detailed below.
My boyfriend and I went away for a weekend anniversary celebration. We arrived Friday and when we woke up Saturday, our A/C unit had leaked all over the carpeted floor of our small room. I informed the front desk of this and they sent someone up to replace the unit. Four hours after this, I returned and the floor was still soaking and the AC would not blow out air. I called the front desk and they sent someone up to replace the breaker on the AC but sent no one for the floor. The man working on our breaker told us he would request someone to come clean the floor. We left the room with the AC working. When we came back to the room four hours after this, the floor was still wet but considerably less so. The AC was not working again. The front desk told us that because we were checking out the next day we would have to stay in the room, but that someone would fix the AC for us while we were out (this is at 11 PM). I stressed the importance of the AC working overnight, as the room was significantly warmer than the common areas. I was given a few free drink tickets and free breakfast tickets. When I returned to the hotel around 3AM, the AC was still not working. I went down to the front desk to speak to a manager who was very polite, but informed me that we would not be able to switch rooms and someone would fix our AC for us right then. He also invited us to a complimentary breakfast and an extended check-out time, which was nice considering it took almost an extra hour to settle this issue and have maintenance swap out the AC units. I asked for a fan to be sent to the room in case the AC went out again overnight, we never received it but luckily the AC worked fine. The manager also mentioned comping us for the bill, but the next morning he wasn't working and when I contacted corporate they just sent me some points to their rewards program (not enough to redeem for anything).

We have stayed in NYC many times (at The Plaza, Pierre and Peninsula hotels) and this is the first time we were made to feel like very special guests. We decided to try a smaller, boutique hotel this time and were not disappointed - great room, great location and wonderful hotel staff who welcomed us by name each time we returned to the hotel. It was our anniversay and my husband wanted to order roses for the room. He had a small problem faxing the requested details. When the staff were notified of the problem they quickly made the necessary fix and then gave us a room upgrade to compensate. Upon checkout, we weren't charged for the roses either - truly beyond our expectations. The hotel room ammenities were on a par with the "big name" hotels around the corner, but at a much more reasonable rate. When you consider the inclusion of the continental breakfast and other extras it is a great deal. Our junior suite was very spacious, however the bathroom was small in comparison and it had very little shelf space for our toilettries. The bathroom lighting was romantic, but not great for applying makeup. The only thing we can complain about is the "industrial strength" toilet paper, it could use an upgrade.

I cannot say enough good things about The Belvedere. The service at the front desk was top notch, Ilianna was the best and was very accommodating when I asked for a room on a higher floor with a view. The beautifully decorated Executive King room I was given on the 15th floor had a nice view with windows that open. The room was spacious and everything was brand new (not refurbished) as they recently remodeled. The room was incredibly clean and quiet, even though it was directly across from the elevators. I never once heard any noise from the hallway as the actual bedroom is set down a long hallway away from the door. I did hear a little noise from the room next to mine, but that was only because the people in there were shouting. Luckily, it only lasted a few minutes, otherwise it was quiet. The bed was a little soft for my liking but provided a good night’s rest. The room was equipped with a little kitchenette/bar area with coffee maker (including coffee, cups, sweetners, etc.), sink, microwave, and fridge. Very nice, well lit closet with plenty of storage space, a safe large enough for a laptop, iron, and ironing board. There was a working desk with a great chair and lighting, wired and wireless internet, good sized LCD television, a small table with 2 chairs, and another larger chair on the other side of the room. The bathroom was small but one of the cleanest I’ve seen at a hotel, and the water pressure and temperature were perfect. The hotel does not offer in-house room service, however, they have partnered with a few restaurants in the area that will deliver right to your room door for a very small fee (under $3). Patzeria is one of them and the food was very good and pretty cheap. There is also a great market around the corner, The Food Emporium, where you can pick up just about anything you need. I absolutely have to have cream in my morning coffee, so I picked up a small carton for the fridge along with some fruit and yogurt for breakfast. They have lots of prepared foods and baked goods as well, if you’re not looking to order from delivery menus. I have read several reviews here where people have complained about slow elevator service, so I was pleasantly surprised to find that the elevators were anything but slow, tiny and oddly shaped, but not slow. Perhaps they have serviced the elevators since those reviews were written, but I never waited more than a minute for an elevator...and I was in and out of the hotel many times during my stay. I would absolutely stay here again!

First of all, the property is absolutely fantastic. The hotel sits over the Marina, is right near the airport, and is convenient to La Jolla, the bay, and Coronado. The lobby is impressive and the fitness center is great. You can walk to the waterfront in 3 min, and the bar in the hotel is great. The rooms are good, not great, and it is an older Sheraton which has been rebadged. But, you dont lack for anything in the rooms and the balconies looking over the marina are a nice touch. San Diego is a fantastic city and is so underrated as a travel destination.
Thus said, the service was extremely dissapointing. The front desk help did not speak great English. The "green" program they shove off on you is an excuse to not clean the rooms, etc. and not pay the staff to be there - otherwise they wouldnt hand out towels by the boatloads in the gym and heat the pool year round (much worse for the environment than cleaning the rooms!). We finally asked the front desk to have our room cleaned and.....nothing for 2 days. 4 days total. Not acceptable at all. We also made dinner reservations through the front desk and......that's right, the reservations were not made. It was almost a disaster for some clients we hosted.
I would still stay here again but it is definitely not for the service, that will disappoint anyone who thinks paying 279 a night for a hotel will get them good service. This property still has a lot to learn about being a luxury hotel.

title_masked: Well situated and good value for money
text_masked:
Stayed for two nights on a business trip in June 2012.
Location was good (last two trips to SF have stayed at the W, not quite as good a location but more expensive although rooms are good, with nice touches) so was well situated for shopping, the cable car, most things on the door step.
I had a superior double which was a good sized room, simply furnished but clean, if beginning to look a little tired round the edges, large comfortable bed. Staff are very polite and helpful.
Like most Morgan's hotels add-ons are quite expensive, internet, room service breakfast, bar drinks. But being so well situated there are lots of other options just outside the front door.
Wish tripadvisor had a "good" setting, as better than average but not quite sure if its v good.

I enjoyed my stay at the Paramount Hotel. Staff was friendly. The location is close to a couple of the big downtown shopping centers. I didn't go to the Paramount theatre but it is only a block away. The room was decent sized and comfortable. There aren't a whole lot of channels on the tv but they do have HBO and movie rental selections. My room had a small refrigerator in it. I would definitely stay here again.

My husband and I chose this hotel mainly because of its location. It is of a 5-minute walking distance to the Santa Fe Depot which is great. You can simply walk from this hotel to places including the Seaport Village, Gaslamp Quarters, etc. The hotel design is very classic (quite old-fashioned though). The hotel room is big, comfortable and quiet. We did not have problem sleeping at night. We were quite disappointed that this hotel only offered paid wifi access while the Starbucks at the nearby trolley station offers it free.
This hotel will give you a $5 beverage/food coupon each day you decline housekeeping. An excellent green idea.

I was not aware that this hotel was right in the middle of everything. It sits right on the Riverwalk, Is across the street from the mall. (Yippee!!) and is a very short walk to the Alamo. The mall has an IMAX theater (if you prefer to catch a movie while in town). Every Riverwalk restaurant is in walking distance.
Once valet parked my car, I never retrieved it until I checked out. The hotel lounge, Bar Rojo, is a perfect place for a Happy Hour drink or a nighcap. They have fresh, made to order Sushi as well. 
The restaurant Achiote River Cafe has EXCELLENT food. Definitely worth trying. I recommend the Miso Salmon. I also reco'mmend dining there (along the Riverwalk banks) at night after the sun sets. It's beautiful. 
This is the newest hotel in San Antonio and it shows. I would not hesitate to stay at this hotel again.
Really nice hotel. Lassandra makes a great omelet in the morning and the staff are very friendly. Very nice experience all the way around.

We are Indy residents and have stayed on several occasions at the Canterbury when events take us downtown for an overnight and have recieve good or better service each time.
Greetings from the Valet and front desk are excellent everytime.
We love that this hotel has kept its old world charm and makes me think I am in Europe for just a while when I am there.
Unfortunately its proximity to Lucus Field reminds me I am still in the midwest when I see the dress of some of its patrons!
Our recent stay found us arriving late to the hotel and requiring a quick turnaround time to gets our things upstairs, clothing changed for a black-tie affair at a nearby hotel and a cab flagged to get to the event on time.
Brandon the valet checked our car in, delivered our luggage personally to our room, saw that we had fresh ice and said he would have a cab ready for us at the time we designated so we could get to our affair.
He was there the folllowing morning when we left to go home with the same smile and attention to detail. He should be moved to a managing position soon as he is deserving!
The same cannot be said about the Restaurant however. We loved this place some years back but the attention to fine dining has been lost here I am afraid.
We were only having breakfast this time and the only two persons in the restaurant at an early hour. The TV in the bar was heard in the dining area, not a local game mind you but something just noisey. Coffee was barely warm when served, grapefruit juice tasted like a kids drink and not fresh squeezed, ordered a Belguin Waffle and syrup had to be requested to go with it. I asked that it be hot and it arrived out of the bottle and not warm.
Service was generally just slow and unsatifactory. The last time there we had the same bad service for the dinner meal. We have decided that the restaurant will not be a destination in our future visits which is unfortunate since it is so charming and convenient however we will still keep coming back to the hotel as long as it doesn't follow the same course.

I stayed in this hotel on July 28,2012 before going on my cruise and wish I could have stayed longer. It was clean,the staff welcomed you with a smile and a bottle of water for each person. There was lemonade also at the front desk that was very good. The room was clean,it had a refrigerator in the room , the beds were very comfortable I wish I could have stayed longer. I am planning on going to New York City and this will be the place I will stay , it is reasonable walking distance to good eateries and good shopping especially the famous Macys' department store.

I came to Philadelphia to visit my daughter who is a college student at Swarthmore and brought my teenage son so we could explore Philadelphia. I decided to stay in the Old City and selected the Omni based on other travelers' reviews - mainly for location and moderate price. Great selection - the hotel itself is terrific, the staff is super helpful and friendly, and the location is perfect. Obviously it's in the heart of the historic area, but it is also very easy to walk to almost everywhere in the main part of the city. Over the course of two days, we explored from Penn's Landing all the way over to the Art Museum, center city, China Town, the Italian Market, Society Hill, and many other destinations in addition to the historic sites - all on foot. 
The Omni was top rate and everything about our experience was great. The rooms are plush and has all the qualities you would expect in a high-end hotel. Getting in and out of the city from here is actually pretty easy too. Parking was pricey at $37/night for valet parking, but it was no hassle and probably worth the premium given that parking is hard to come by in the central part of the hotel. Overall a great hotel and I would definitely stay here again.

Since I was last at the Royalton, the look of the hotel changed in a great way. My room was perfect, with a fireplace, and round soaking tub, very conducive to a romantic weekend getaway. However, I was alone this trip and felt very comfortable at the hotel for my 3 night stay. The bed had to be one of the, if not the, most comfortable beds I've ever slept in. When I needed an amenity, it was brought up to the room pronto. Drinks in the Lobby near the fireplace were right in every way. The Front Desk staff was quite helpful when I needed info. An added bonus is the location. As I made my way to meet a friend, my trek became even better when I noticed Magnolia Bakery only 5 short blocks from The Royalton. I had to indulge in some of the famous cupcakes which possessed the fluffiest icing I've ever tasted. The Royalton's location is so convenient to all, near enough to Midtown or Central Park, whatever your destination. Also, 2 minutes from shopping on Fifth Avenue. Have to say, didn't eat at the hotel as I was with my friend most of the time near her place so didn't have a chance to indulge but I'm sure the food is up to par with the other Morgan Hotels. Would definitely stay here again with my husband so he can enjoy as much as I did. Very accommodating staff.

title_masked: One of the best Marriott properties!
text_masked: Phenomenal views, outstanding customer service, perfectly located. What more can I say? It was a sheer delight to stay here. I absolutely recommend it. One tiny criticism: lack of seating in main lobby. Would be nice when you're waiting for someone. Otherwise, absolutely NO complaints here!

title_masked: Very nice hotel and a great location
text_masked: I was happy with my stay here. The rooms were small, but very clean and comfortable. The staff was friendly and accommodating. The location is fantastic and less than a block from the subway. I have to agree the breakfast wasn't very good but that is my only complaint.

My husband and I like space so we opted for 2 adjoining kings that share a bathroom. The bathroom was rather small but it served its purpose. We were on the 2nd floor *(a little noisy at times) for two nights beginning July 3 -- the hotel is centrally located near major shopping venues and the staff was very pleasant and helpful. Complimentary wine was served each afternoon and coffee was available in the lobby each morning.

Wow! You can stay 1 block from a Metro stop, inside DC (not 20 miles out), in a very nice, clean hotel, with a very helpful staff, and including a FREE breakfast for UNDER $200 (that includes the stay and the parking fee .. and it was WELL under $200) ?!?!?! Yes, the breakfast might be a little "cramped" -- but they really do have quite a bit of seating - as much as possible for a hotel in a downtown location can ... I've seen MUCH smaller in large cities. And the choices were just as good if not better than a lot of other free hotel breakfast. (they even had chopped walnuts for your oatmeal -- most hotels won't do that due to price of walnuts!) Get there early -- the area seemed more packed after 9am -- we got down there at 8am and it was fine ... just plan your morning!! Yes, there is a parking fee -- but there is one EVERYWHERE in DC. The area is in China town -- some people have an issue with that, but being that we have family members that are from China we LOVE going to China town anytime we can in a large city, so we were happy to be so close. Had lunch there. I didn't see anything crazy going on the night we were there. And we came home late due to the Nationals game and concert after. There were a lot of young people hanging and walking around. The hotel is nicely decorated, fast elevator, helpful staff, and seemed very very clean to me! We only heard a couple people in the hall way for about 5 minutes after we went to bed. We even had the areas Church outside our window that had bells that went off every hour---and barely noticed the bells. GREAT hotel -can't wait to go back!!

title_masked: Nice Choice If Visiting Occidental College
text_masked: I stayed at the Rose Bowl Motel in Eagle Rock while my son was visiting Occidental College. It is a cute little place, neat as a pin, harkening back to the days of motor inns. It isn't exactly modern, but the bathroom shower was recently tiled. The 1 queen room was small, the bed was ok, but could use a few more pillows, but it was quiet at night. I don't think I have stayed in a cleaner motel; pride of ownership really shows. The family who owns this motel was constantly cleaning, sweeping, and gardening during my stay. They still use old-fashioned keys. Very limited breakfast, but there are so many great choices in Eagle Rock that I didn't use it. If you prefer cookie cutter chain motels, this may not be to your liking, but if you like to stay in places with a little more personality while supporting the small business owner, then give Rose Bowl Motel a try. I would definitely make this my motel of choice if my son decides to attend Occidental. I really liked Eagle Rock, also.

We spent two nights in this wonderful hotel which is loaded with charm and character and is in a great location. We were upgraded to a lovely room with a seperate sitting area; they even provided a complimentary bottle of champagne for my wife's birthday. The staff couldn't have been more helpful in recommending restaurants, attractions and transport advice. Ann on reception is an absolute gem. The manager was also charming, and hosted free drinks and nibbles every evening which is a great opportunity to chat with other guests and exchange ideas. We would definitely stay here again and recommend it to anyone looking for a boutique hotel.

We needed a place to stay when traveling to San Jose for a concert at the HP pavillion. The location was a quick 5-10 minute drive from the downtown area.. The hotel was very clean, the price was reasonable for the area. The breakfast was decent, the front desk staff went out of their way to be helpful. No charge for parking. The only complaint I have would be the squeaky ceiling that impacted our sleep everytime our upstairs neighbor moved. We would stay here again (but ask for the top floor)!

title_masked: Lovely hotel at a GREAT location
text_masked:
I have stayed a couple of times in this hotel in the past 2 years and it never disappoints. The hotel feels new, fresh and very well maintained. I really like the beautiful spacious lobby that is very welcoming and cheerful.
The room is nicely decorated and spacious. The guest service laundry facility (on seventh floor) is awesome and very useful as the hotel laundry service in general is very expensive.
And, of course, you can't beat this hotel's location! It is very near (one block) from union square and thus is also close to the bart/muni station and many shops/restaurants. At the same time, it still has the necessary distance from the union square as to not make it too overwhelming (as comparison, there are some hotels right across the union square that woud always have crowded walking-by people in the hotel's front pavement)
Can't recommend it more!

Lovely clean rooms. Good size beds. Lovely complimentary toiletries. Excellent location for main tourist attractions like The White house, Capitol Building,etc. Don't confuse this with another Renaissance property located not so far away and from the outside did not look half as nice.

I stayed at this Homewood Suites on City Avenue. The rooms are clean and the staf is very friendly. The General Manager was extremely helpful. parking was $5/night or free if you could find a space on the street. Breakfast was good and I was there for one evening dinner which was good. The beds were very comfortabel. I will stay here again on my next trip to the area.

The hotel itself is very beautiful...and the rooms are ok, but average compared to other hotels that are less expensive. King size bed is comfortable. We have. View of 6th Street which was awesome, but the group we were with were on the other side of the hotel which had the view oh I-35 and convention center. So if you are looking for a view, then I would definitely ask for a room facing 6th St. The staff is very pleasant and helpful. The only big complaint is that if you don't have the Hilton HHonors or AT&T then they charge you $13.00 a day for internet in your room. However, they have free Internet in the lobby. But, who wants to drag your laptop down there? On the rewards card you have to earn your points to a silver or bronze level before you can earn free Internet. This is done by staying in their hotels.

Stayed at the Allegro on a recent business trip. The staff was for the most part extremely helpful and pleasant. Nice afternoon happy hour. Room service was good. Maid service was good.
Room itself is quite small and starting to show wear. Biggest complaint - the pillows. Very big, stiff foam. Others in the group complained of neck aches from the pillows. Crazy how such a little thing can affect your sleep.
Overall fine stay. Convienient location. Good staff.

We only had one night in LA so wanted to be downtown to be close to the train station. Loved the hotel, the rooms are spacious and comfortable, very modern esp. the shower which is quite visible from the room ;).Rooftop bar is nice for evening cocktails. Restaurant is only average so skip. Lobby area is funky, take some time to explore it!

title_masked: Off the Avenue, Fifth Avenue, that is...
text_masked:
The Manhattan real estate from 5th Avenue to 6th on 44th Street is a favorite stretch of mine, fine hotels, shops and eateries and many of the structures on the street are designated landmarks (The New York Yacht Club, for one). I have stayed in most of the hotels on Forty Fourth and was always intrigued by The Mansfield Apartments, a lovely building on the south side of the street, ticked it off my list, just last week.
Spent two nights in this unusual property and enjoyed my stay. I understand there are a number of jail cell sized rooms in the hotel but I had a sizable room that had character and windows you could open ( a rarity). Comfortable bed, small but more then adequate bathroom. I was in the back part of the hotel so noise was not an issue. 
There is a stylish bar adjacent to the lobby and across from it, a study with couches and chairs and a cappuccino machine at the ready. 
As for the Property Vibe;The Mansfield doesn't feel like a hotel and that can appeal to many who are tired of characterless lobbies and rooms that could only be in a hotel. 
Happy with my Mansfield experience and location,location,Location.

title_masked: The best hotel in San Francisco
text_masked: I have been looking for a hotel in San Francisco and finally found the perfect place. Comfortable and intimate, the Hotel Drisco fits all my needs. The staff is very genuine in their warmth and hospitality. The decor is luxury without being pretentious, while the complimentary breakfast is a feast not to be missed. Set in a quiet residential neighborhood, it is easy to get around town and near the steps at the Presidio, perfect for walking or running.

Love this hotel! travelling with my two young girls, Mum, step dad and 17 year old brother so had two suites, just down the hall from each other, rooms good size, chose hotel due to fantastic location on times square and the fact that my little brother had a bit of privacy from the parents! (sofa bed not the most comfy but more than suitable for mini-break) were due to stay for four nights but due to the unfortunate visit from hurricane sandy, our holiday was extended by 1 week! the staff were fantastic through this time, kept us posted with regards to housekeeping staff shortages and restaurant food availability, one hadn't seen his family in over 2 nights! and yet served us with a smile on his face, Another wore his Cowboy hat and sheriff badge with pride over the Halloween weekend! welcome cookies were delicious! stayed on the 15th floor hotel, really reccomend this hotel! we're still here!

When I checked into the Sheraton it didn't help that I had to wait 20 minutes. I was asked at check in if I would be a "green" patron. I asked what that meant and it was that housekeeping would not change out my towels and that they would leave me a voucher for the restaurant / bar for $5. I stayed 4 nights and what it meant was that housekeeping didn't come at all to empty the trash or make the bed. Also, these $5 vouchers could not be combines to go towards an overall meal, making you either use them for drinks at the bar. On top of that I was slapped with a $22 / night charge for self parking (most likely because of the marina). Outside of these comments, the hotel was nice and clean and the service was okay. If you don't have a car, it's a reasonable place to stay, otherwise, I'd suggest that you find another hotel in the San Diego area.

My friend and I went to Philly for a girls weekend recently. We had a great experience at the Sheraton Philadelphia Downtown Hotel. One of the best parts of our stay was Mary Mastrobuoni, the Concierge. Every question and need of ours was taken care of by Mary. She really seemed to want us to enjoy our time in Philly, and made great spa, restaurant, and historic site recommendations. Thanks for a great weekend!

This hotel is fantastic really good location, I expected it to be not so good for the reviews written but I only take them with a pinch of salt!
I have to say the hotel is expensive for food and drink but I thought all of new york was for food.
The rooms are really nice I found them compact but neat and tidy and the beds were sooooo comfy!! The bathrooms are really nice too.
The service at the hotel was good I couldn't really fault anything.
The location is perfect try the irish bar 2 streets behind for food and drink it is lush! Soho is amazing for shopping so get yourself there for the bargains. Times square is a couple of blocks up from the hotel, it really is a good location.
I'd also reccomend the helicopter ride over newyork AMAZING.

I am an event coordinator for a conference company that organizes over 70 events a year so if I pay a venue a compliment that means they were really really good. This is the first time ever I have decided to actually write a trip advisor review. THAT is how amazing I think this hotel is. The staff bends over backwards to make sure you are not only extremely comfortable and accommodated but they also manage to make you feel like family. They remember your name, what you like to eat and other extremely minor details that any regular place would instantly forget. This kind of hands on attendtion thoughout the entire hotel is what you would expect from a much more expensive venue. Five star hotels. I was just at The Fasano in beautiful Brazil and the feeling was similar there but I was paying over a thousand dollars a night. Darn right you better know my name (haha) anyway, my point is this hotel is a great value. You'll receive 5star treatment and pay very reasonable prices.
I love the Houston Marriott by the Galleria (West Loop). The name is long but totally worth learning.
:)

title_masked: Good hotel for the right price
text_masked:
I stayed here with my partnet for 2 nights in March. We paid ~$160/night which was a relatively good deal considering the price of other hotels in the area. 
The room was clean and very well presented but was a little cramp for two adults. The AC worked but we never used it because it roared everytime we tried to turn it on. Our room faced Thomas Circle which gave us a brilliant view but also A LOT, and i mean A LOT of traffic noise. We were woken up at 6-7am each morning from the relentless honking from (disgruntled?) DC drivers.
The location is ok and is about a 10 minute leisurely walk to the subway station. There are good but pricey restaurants well within walking distance of the hotel. 
Good hotel at the right price.

I was only at the hotel for two nights, but I could not ask for anything better. I went down with three friends for a football game and we decided to stay at the Marriott because that was where Big Blue Travel used, and I can see why now. It was within walking distance to the football stadium. The staff was very friendly and helpful and the city was very enjoyable. I would definitely stay there again, and would consider staying at other Marriott Hotels due to my great experience!

The Baltimore Marriott Waterfront is a prime location on the Baltimore Waterfront. The hotel has beautiful rooms, facilities, and views. This hotel is nestled on the waterfront in downtown. The hotel is also in walking distance from some of Baltimore's most famous attractions. The Waterfront is great for friends, family, solo-travlers, business people, and pretty much anyone wanting the harbor experience!

i just returned from two nights at the Edison and I was very disappointed by my room there. The beds were hard and the pillows were lumpy...the linens were old and worn. The bathroom had a distinct odor of mildew and the towels were skimpy. The furniture in the room was also quite worn and there were too few outlets for charging electronics. For the price, it was just a terrible room. The only positives are the location (if you like the hustle and bustle of Times Square) and the coffee shop next door. Never again!

I am a repeat customer here, I stay here to go to shows at the Majestic. My last stay the restuarant and bar wait staff was completely inadequate during my entire stay. Don't know if there was a temporary scheduling problem or what. There was not an issue with the facilities being too full, I would say the restuarant and bar were operating at below 20%, but still could not get service.

The hotel is conveniently set in the heart of Midtown at Lex in between 47th and 48th. Great location and excellent people to greet you. It's nice to have free wifi too for a change. The bed was extremely comfortable, and the rooms are among the largest I have ever stayed in New York, where I can fit most hotel rooms in my bedroom closet. But, and this is a big but for me, I thought the rooms were filthy. I can live with the stray hair on the floor, but hair was gunked on the underside of the conditioner bottle. I threw it away. The glass shelves in the bathroom were so dusty that I wiped them off myself, essentially sacrificing my wash cloth for the day. In the corner between the bath tub and toilet, soot seemed to be fermenting. It was just flat gross. But, the thing that irritated me the most was the waste baskets still had Kleenexes in them when I first checked in, and the cleaning lady never emptied them during my four day stay. I suppose I could have asked for a better clean up, but I'm in town for work, not for managing the cleaning crew. This is truly a fine building with wonderful art inside. It would easily be a 4 star, maybe even a 5 star, in my opinion if it were just cleaner.

title_masked: Great location, wonderful view, full service
text_masked:
Stayed here for a week while attending a convention. The location is excellent as it's only a short 5 minute walk to the convention center. It's right on the bay front so I walked each day to and from the center along the bay. 
My room was on the 20th floor overlooking the courtyard. The hotel itself consists of two towers and although I was facing the opposite tower, it is quite a distance away so that I had a great view of the bay. The room itself was standard with no special touches but the bed and pillows were very comfortable. And like all hotels now it had a large flat screen TV which I don't believe I even turned on. The wireless Internet had very poor performance. The wired connection was much faster. There was a mini fridge which I stocked with beer. There was a coffee maker which I used for hot water as I like those individual servings of coffee you can buy at Starbucks. And I bought a small bottle of milk and kept it in the mini fridge. 
The lobby of the hotel is very grand with high ceiling and large murals to give it an old world stye. I ate at Redfield's sports bar one evening while watching the game and the beer was cold and the chicken in my caesar salad was tender and juicy. Believe it or not I never did make it up to the roof-top lounge. I didn't even know there was one there. I'm sort of disappointed I didn't check it out! 
The outdoor pool is large and there are lots of lounge chairs. It was cool when I visited so I used the two hot-tubs. The water wasn't too warm in the tubs and as you sat in them you really didn't have a view of anything. I suppose it would be romantic if my wife was with me but being solo it was a rather dull atmosphere. And as the pool area is actually not on the ground floor of the building, there isn't any grass or trees so it was rather stark. I was at the Mariott next door and their pool area was rather tropical with palm trees and water-falls. 
I made it to the gym a couple of times and although the weight equipment is well worn it has enough to get a decent workout in. And there are ample treadmills all lined up along the windows so you get a good view for your cardio workout.
The hotel is in a great location on the bay and close to downtown and the convention center. Right outside the door is the touristy but nicely landscaped Seaport Village shopping area. Petco Park is about a fifteen minute walk and only about five minutes to the base of the Gaslamp District. And there is a mall - Horton Plaza - just up 1st Street which I did some shopping and actually ate at the food court twice for lunch. At the Seaport Village I had a beer and slice of pizza with a great view of the bay. And I bought some souvenir t-shirts for my kids at a sports shop. I also walked over to the USS Midway and spent 4 hours touring the ship.
It was a business trip so fortunately it was paid for. Otherwise I found the rate rather expensive. I suppose the convention I was attending had filled up most of the hotels as this was one of only two hotels that had availability when I booked. I was trying to get into the Hotel Solamar as I really like the Kimpton boutique hotels but it was obviously booked.

Just a two night stay,but treated like a regular. From the phone to the desk they make you feel welcome. Breakfast buffet was very good and wait staff friendly and stop to chat with you...your OJ glass is never empty. The only exception was waiting for the Etrusan restaurant to open, I should have listened to a staffer leaving...hinted I should try elsewhere. When the Etrusan did open the waiters were indifferent at best. Told them we theater tics and ordered the pre-theater menu,but needed to be out by 6:30. Dinner got mixed reviews (desert was very good)...but at check time, the waiter add ten dollars for two coffees...I told him it was included. He loudly declared it wasn't, so I had to escort him to the window at the door displaying the menu. He said well they must have changed it. Through out the dinner the staff mainly talked to each other! Did not get into the taxi until 6:50...for a 7pm curtain! Another good point about this hotel, besides location, is the doorman can get you a taxi when none are to be found!

There is a bit of construction in the lobby area but the rooms were very clean and modernized. The service was great. The room service breakfast was very good. And the central location of the hotel was wonderful. Very nice views and a very good restaurant on the 37th floor. The restaurant will be replaced by a banquet room. So sad to see the restaurant on the top floor go because we saw a beautiful sunset from our dinner table. All in all, a great stay.

Loved this hotel for it's proximity to Penn Station. We flew into Newark, and the train from that airport goes to Penn Station, so it was a short walk to the hotel (no need for a taxi or subway ride).
