The room was nice and quiet for NYC and the bathroom was quite nice. (14th flr). We had a package that included wifi, b'fast and late check out. We had to remind the front desk of all the add ons as the wifi code and b'fast coupons were not offered until we mentioned the package. As well, we had to remind them about the late check out - and the keys stop working at noon or so, so when we came back the last time to check out at 2pm, we had to go back down stairs and get our key swiped before it would work. I wish they had mentioned that when I confirmed the late check out that morning. It would have saved an extra elevator ride and a bit of stress. B'fast was nothing special at all so we only used the coupons once - there is a Brooklyn Bagel Co. a few blocks away, (really good bagels) so that was a great local option. I would stay again due to the location, and comfort of the rooms.

Stayed at this hotel as part of US tour Oct 9th-11th. Very disappointing, small room overlooking backyard, bathroom cramped with only sliding door and no ventilation. Plumbing suspect.Staff not particularly accomodating. Compared very poorly with other hotels used in Falmouth and North Conway.

A truly amazing Central New York Hotel! We stayed here earlier this year for our first holiday to New york! Staff were fantastic, hotel well maintained and extremely clean. We had a double room on a high floor, very quiet throughout the day and during the evenings. Cannot fault the hotel in the slightest. Attention to detail second to none, fruit bowl for your room as a welcome from the hotel, small touch but a very premium and upmarket approach to customer service

title_masked: Not my favorite place to stay, in fact I wouldn't go back
text_masked: Our friends talked us into staying at Intercontinental. The room was average for an upper end hotel, and was not very clean. The pool was closed for repair, and the check in staff was less than helpful when we tried to change rooms. The room was very noisy with what seemed like some kind of plumbing issue? The bed linen felt very low quality and the bathroom sink area was not in great shape - some of the finished areas were pealing! Not what I would expect of a 3 star hotel let alone a 4 or 4.5 hotel. Go to the Marriot across the street, same great location and a much better hotel.

Pleasant experience from the time I checked in until check out. I stayed 2 nights and was there for business. It was during fashion week, so the hotel was full ( I only know this because some of my colleagues were trying unsuccessfully to stay there). It did not feel like there were a lot of people staying there so it is very quiet. The location is great, near the subway and getting cabs were no problem either.
I actually had a suite (I guess they upgraded me) and it was very roomy. Maybe all of the room are suites. Needless to say, I was not expecting a large room in a New York “boutique” hotel so I was pleasantly surprised. The bed was comfortable the staff very pleasant and the bathrooms clean, well appointed and roomy. They also offer complimentary breakfast and free WiFi.

When planning our family weekend trip to DC, we booked a room at the St. Gregory. At check-in, the manager was very accommodating and gave us a room upgrade as I follow the hotel on Facebook and Twitter. We enjoyed our large room with kitchenette facing the courtyard. The room was clean, the bathroom was large, and the decor lovely. The location in downtown DC is safe and within walking distance of Dupont Circle and Farragut North subway stops. We ate breakfast in the lovely hotel restaurant on the day we checked out and had a wonderful full breakfast, good value for the price and great food. The only drawback to the room was the lack of a flat-screen TV, but since we were out and about most of our stay, it wasn't a big deal. Overall, a good choice!

From the moment of arrival until collapsing in the heavenly bed, the experience was exceptional. The bellmen, especially Erwing and Amadou, were wonderfully friendly and helpful, the front desk courteous, helpful and welcoming, room service perfect and housekeeping immaculate. We've come to expect such from Westin and, again, we were not disappointed!

title_masked: Best in Boston (Most of the time)
text_masked:
I love this hotel.
Made sure to stay at the Copley Square during a recent business trip, even though my colleagues had made bookings at the Sheraton, Hilton, or Westin around the corner. Over the course of a week I stopped by all three, and never regret my choice. The Copley Square is the most charming, elegant, friendly, and comfortable stay in Back Bay and perhaps all of Boston. My seventh floor room was quiet and spacious with a fantastic view. Free wifi and bottled water made me feel well taken care of.
All that said, the Copley is in the middle of MAJOR renovations. Every morning at seven thirty workers would start banging away just outside my window. Luckily I was up (and wanted to be up!) or I would have been hugely annoyed. I fault the Copley not making this abundantly clear during booking, and worse, not acknowledging the inconvenience during my stay with anything but an apology. Surely a drink coupon or bottle of wine would have shown more care?
So, do stay at the Copley -- just be wary!

The hotel was a very good value for a weekend where most hotels added a premium for the Formula 1 weekend. However, when I when to pull the comforter to go to sleep, the bed sheet was stained with blood. Not faded and washed stains, but what seemed like unwashed blood stains. Needless to say, not an acceptable bed on which to sleep. So, good value in $$ for the weekend, but at the cost of a low level of cleanliness.

title_masked: A good hotel and great location
text_masked: I stayed here for four days on business. The location is great and surrounded by shops and restaurants of all kinds within a few seconds walk. The front of house is very nicely designed and the first floor bar area is relaxing and great place to have a drink. The rooms are nice but a touch smaller than I expected and are quite conventional in design. The reception and concierge service were both top notch and were helpful, friendly and efficient. The only meals I had in the hotel were breakfast via room service. The food was excellent and delivered quickly but quite pricey. Overall I had a very good experience and I would certainly stay here again.

Our Stay at this hotel, Thurs to tues. May 31st to Tues. June 05. Thanks to all our stay was great. Many.many thanks for the upgrade. I always want to aquire my points. The check in was fast, friendly. At first, it was 2 people staying in a double room, I call the hotel a few days earlier to say a total of 4 people(my husband, myself,2 teenagers) were coming, thanks to the hotel the check in was great we were booked in a room w/ 2 queen beds. Housekeeping was great,no problem was communication always gave us what was needed. room service room quick, fast, great food. ( but costly). This Starwood Hotel calls your room for wake-up call even for more than one morning (yes, I have had a hotel not call my room for wake-up). The Rest. in the Hotel was great. Staff was so friendly, food was sooooo good. I loved the Subway was just outside the door, this was great when we would come back late at night. 
Security, I loved the security at this hotel. 1st. each entrance I had to show my room key to "get pass the ropes and walk to the elevator". If each person is going to a different floor,then u must use your room key for each floor. I liked those "checkpoints". My teenagers were able explore the hotel on their own. Yes, this hotel is not for little kids, but we knew this before I booked. The activity in the night club yes, u could hear it (I was on the 7th floor) but it was not all that bad.. My guess is the lower floor your room is, the noice level is greater. Our room on the 7th floor was quiet.We came back in to the hotel at different times of the day/night. We did not see any questionable people or actions.hint, hint. All of the people could not have been nicer from Guys at the front door,front desk, housekeeping, rest. etc. Having the Taxi always waiting outside 24/7 was great. they were some little things, but overall our stay was great. oh, the floor matts nice touch, they changed w/ the time of the day.

Travel to DC can be extraordinarily expensive...or if Congress is out of session...a surprising value. This stay the town was full and the room was $400/night, the Hyatt on Capitol Hill was full, The George and the Hay Adams were full and The Willard was over $600/night. I got in very late, the bellman was quick and check-in was flawless...as I registered I was called by name, got a smile and a nice room on the concierge floor.
My room was clean, nicely appointed and everything worked. The bathroom had plenty of light, linens and shelf space. There was zero noise in the hall for my two-night stay. The bed was terrific and the only hiccup I experienced was the room service breakfast I ordered for delivery between 7:30 and 8 am came at 7:59 am. Barely on the mark, but the waiter said they had been swamped...to the hotel's credit it was hot and as ordered.
I had none of the negative experiences related in other reviews, but when one travels to a high volume, convention-type hotel, missteps are inevitable, especially when it is at capacity. I typically stay at one the hotels named above for their proximity to whatever the week's activity dictates. I found this Hyatt to more than acceptable and have no qualms about returning. They met my expectations with professional and friendly service.

We are two couples travelling together and we stayed at this hotel for one night. The location is fantastic right near Times Square. The decor is modern and best of all the rooms are spacious. We had stayed in a hotel almost opposite this hotel where the rooms were tiny and worn and the Muse was actually cheaper and much much nicer! I would recommend booking this hotel online and checking the website carefully for specials as the room rates can vary. Breakfast is not included which would have been nice but you can buy it close by at a reasonably price.

Stayed in the historic building facing onto Geary st. While it was a bit noisy it didn't disturb us.
The rooms had been renovated to a very good standard however the structure itself (hallways needed a makeover, floor was a little uneven, no soundproofing) was showing definite aging. We had no problems with cellphone coverage, maybe other reviewers were in the other building. But has to be given full marks for location, so handy to transport, shopping malls, food outlets, information centre.

I work out of New York twice a year and i typically choose either Hilton along Ave of the Americas or The Jewel as my office is around the Rockefeller Plaza area. I always hate the big crowd and the impersonal service at the Hilton. Jewel works for awhile but overtime they have jacked up room rates so much that the price is no longer justifiable for the quality of the hotel.
This is my first stay at Omni and what I like about Omni are as follow: a) location; b) quiet lobby as well as in the room (I have requested for a room at the back); c) loyalty program which starts on day 1; d) good lighting in the room (as well as bathroom). The hotel does not provide free drinking water (like Jewel) but there are free apples in the lobby. While staffs at front desk/concierge are not exactly very friendly, they are not sullen either, unlike those at the Hilton. Room service is above average by New York standard; I requested for a coffer maker and one was delivered to my room. I stayed for 7 days at Omni and will definitely consider using this hotel for future trips to New York.

Our room and bathroom were very clean. The neighbourhood was calm and the room was very silent, and we were never disturbed during the nights. The location of the hotel is perfect, close to the Central Park, offering plenty of opportunities to walk and run in the park. We were also very pleased with that the price was so moderate.

Just stayed this past weekend, for our annual girl's getaway. We have stayed at the Sofitel for many years, but decided to switch it up this year....partially due to the fact that the Sofitel was not offering a very good rate. We were all very happy with the Palomar. Wonderful staff in all aspects of the hotel. The 5:00-6:00pm complimentary Happy Hour made for a fun and festive kickoff to the evening. We had a standard dbl queen room. It was just fine...not huge though. This was expected at a boutique hotel. I prefer my bed a bit softer, but didn't have an issue sleeping. The hotel was hip and stylish with a very cozy and inviting lobby area. Fantastic location for everything that we do...dining, shopping, bar-hopping. We would stay here again.

I stayed here for a conference nearby in midtown Manhattan. I arrived pretty early and was unsure if a room would be ready. But, after a warm greeting by the front desk staff (who recognized my Marriott Gold elite status), I was upgraded to a corner suite on a high floor (20s). 
The room was very nice--no doubt big by New York standards. Though the sofa seemed a bit dated, the flat panel TV had plenty of channels and the bed was comfortable. The view was breathtaking! One big downside was the HVAC system. It tended to cycle on and off frequently (which quickly became annoying).
I ate two breakfasts there. The restaurant staff was very pleasant. The buffet offerings seemed above average for a Courtyard.
I found the hotel to be very clean and quiet. The location cannot be beat. The subway is just steps away from the front door!

Not far from downtown Charlotte sits this estate which is surrounded by gardens. We stayed in the carriage house. The King bed was comfortable in the Magnolia Room and the bathroom spacious. The breakfast was ample and the dining room ambience old timey elegant. My only concern was that I could not locate the thermostat in the room. Yet, the temp was okay. I just like to know where the thermostat is in case I want to adjust it.

title_masked: The Post hotel is not a good place to rest your head.
text_masked:
This hotel may have asbestos in the rooms and hallways. The owner/manager has "painted" over instead of removing the asbestos.
The elevator may or may not work.

A beautiful cool hideaway in a baking 105 degree Dallas! The room was clean, nice and cool, well presented with a very confoartable bed!! Loved having a fridge and microwave in the room and the coffe shop opposite the car park was very handy! The staff were lovely and helpful, I'd come back here in a flash!

title_masked: Good hotel for the price and location
text_masked: We stayed a couple of nights and were impressed with the emphasis on comfort and staff attention. Food selections are good, and the hotel itself is in the center of things downtown within easy walking distance to the stadium. The rooms are getting a little worn looking and the towels were paper thin, but the bed was comfortable. They make an effort to keep the noise volume in the hallways down through guest reminders - not that some people were thoughtless anyway! We would stay there again when we need to be in downtown Phoenix.

I recently stayed at the Ramada-Dallas Love Field and I really enjoyed my stay there. I felt welcome when I walked through the door and the rooms were very comfortable and clean. The people at the front desk were kind, friendly, and professional. The restaurant in the hotel was clean and had good food. I will definetly be staying there again. 
Thanks

I stayed there the past week. It is on the far end of the riverwalk and close to restaurants, bars,shops and the Alamo. Other plusses include clean room,plenty of towels, friendly cleaning and maintenance staff and extremely helpful porter(he helped us get to all the best restaurants and shopping). Negatives are unfriendly front desk, unavailability of refridgerators, worn decor(ceiling was peeling in four places in our room),and absolutely horrible food in the restaurant.

Staff was the greatest and very helpful in every respect. The rooms were large and very clean. Those complaining of cab fair could have taken the free van service to downtown which is just a short walk. Those complaining here are either spoiled and/or just wanting to complain.

We have stayed at this Marriott several times. The location is excellent. The service is good. The rooms have been redone and look good but can be small which typifies a big city. Great shopping nearby and great access to all elements of Boston. They do charge for roll away beds which I feel is unnecessary. A view of the Charles River is lovely. Valet parking is well coordinated and efficient but pricey.

Our group of 3 couples spent 3 nights here recently and loved that we could walk to so many places. Room was clean, comfortable with view of river. Bath was a little small but we managed fine.The staff was very friendly, helpful and accommodating; that is always a pleasure. The free breakfast was nice with a lot from which to choose (the bacon was inedible though.) I would definitely recommend staying here, especially if you want to experience the city by walking to restaurants, Beale St., etc. We enjoyed our experience here.

title_masked: Thank you for a great experience
text_masked:
I was booking this hotel over the phone asking for a lot of information about places I could visit, restaurants I could go to and such. Christine at front desk was extremely patient and friendly with me and gave me all the information and suggested some places I could visit while in San Diego. 
The room was nice and clean and I do love the kitchen in the room.
Will definitely come back.
Just wanted to say Thank you to Christine and all the personnel (sorry I forgot names) I have met in there.
I will definitely stay in your hotel again and will suggest it to friends and family.

As a platinum member, we have come to expect a very high level of service which this hotel did not deliver. We requested an early check-in, which is normally anywhere from 12-2pm. Not only did we not get that request met, we had to wait for our room until after 5 pm, due to another platinum guest in the room requesting a late check out (which is suppose to be based on availability). Gave us full brkft, which was mediocre at best, super expensive for a Westin and included an automatic 18% tip in the bill (we were 4). I definitely would not recommend this Westin. Recommended restaurants by concierge were not expensive and not worth it.

title_masked: You can't find better for the price
text_masked: For NYC it doesn't get any better than this for the price. Prime location, well appointed rooms, fastest check in/out ever. Hallways a bit loud though. Breakfast bar was good. Overall: Happy people, modern concept, great stay! We'll be back

title_masked: Nice Room - Valets Ego Bigger than Hotel - Check In Delays
text_masked:
I had stayed at this property at least 5 times since 2006. I recall it being listed as a 3.5 star a few years back and now suddenly it is listed as a 4-star. I think [TEL] is more realistic for the property. I see no evidence of improvement that would warrant an increase in the rating.
We were given a handicap accessibility room although not handicapped. The room was fine, carpet cleans, and bed comfortable. For the pricepoint, the room was perfectly acceptable.
A few areas where the property falls short relate to staff training and attitude. You will find dramatic differences between West Hollywood or Beverly Hills property staff and the LAX Hilton staff; expressed primarily in a latent dispect for the customer base which bleeds through artificial smiles and QC/CS expressions.
Some points to note:
1. The prominent security relate both to the geography and the customer base serviced and you will find similar security in nearby food establishments.
2. The check-in queues were SUBSTANTIAL and there are no automated check-in alternatives at the property and thus you should prepare youreself to stand for some times amidst the noisy crowd from the most recent tour group laying over.
3. The valet process is irritating. They have an automatic ticket reader for retrieval and are quick to direct the customer to try to use the machine vs. helping the customer to do so. My guests from the film industry were shocked by the attitude of the valets and remarked aloud "this would never happen in Beverly Hills". Once again, HILTON and CUSTOMER should be advised that they EXIST and TRAVEL for the EXCLUSIVE financial benefit of the Valets who are not in a subserviant facilitating role; but rather a leadership role and you the customer should benefit from their learned discourse and warm glow of their presence and genuflect in their presence.
4. The parking validation. You have a few drinks. The bartenders have their contention with the wait staff over transfers trying to defend their tips. You give them 20% to your room and this not being cash-- you get an angry look. They then run-off with your bill with no invoice. The valet tells you that you need a validation. So you go back to the bar. Your bartender is not there. You have no ticket. No one knows who you were though there for 2 hours just minutes prior. You ask another staffer who shrugs his shoulders. You ask another bartender too busy to help; afterall your tips have already been given. You spot your old bartender; but he's too busy also. It seems a 15 dollar or 20% tip is just not sufficient for any basic form of Customer Service. Once again; the SILLY CUSTOMER forgets to genuflect while in the presence of the staff. 
Make sure you do the room check-out -- because the check-out queues can be quite lengthy as well-- and you wouldn't want to miss your flight on account of it. Also call the valet for your vehicle at least 30 minutes ahead as well just in case of that queue. 
And always remember...... you are ONLY the customer.....

Eh, hard to put my finger on it, but this hotel is just OK. What I liked: good location, clean room, comfy beds, decent toiletries. AND, Nickie the concierge was WONDERFUL. Not so much: housekeeping was very spotty: turndown skipped one night, and they never seemed to grasp there were 3 staying in our rooms so we never seemed to have enough towels, coffee mugs etc. We did call for things a couple times and they were prompt and friendly on arrival.My big complaint: we had a bottle of nice wine we couldn't get open with the horrid wine corkscrew they provided. The bartender would not open it for us -- OK, so that's a law. But he also wouldn't let us borrow his wine key for even a moment. REALLY? Side note -- they place we bought the wine from (recommended by Nickie) Bacco, was incredible. Great wine and cheese and takeaways. All in all, for what we paid, it was a decent stay but I am not inspired to go back. Just eh.

I would have given a higher rating had it not been for the noisy AC in my room. The beds are perfect with individual firmness controls on each side. The complementary business office was very handy since this was a business trip and I needed to print some documents. The restaurant food is decent, but there is a myriad of good restaurants within a six block walk, so I would recommend heading to 16th Street and check for your favorite cuisine. You will find it there.

Though a convention driven hotel, the location, service and comfort is what you can expect here. Friendly staff help make your stay more comfortable. There are several restaurants and at least one bar and a Peet's Coffee and Tea, a local company which makes great coffee, located at this hotel. I only tried Katie Mullen's which was predictably a "bar" type food. Fitness center, which is always what I am interested in is excellent with plenty modern equipment not crowded and has a nice view of the street. Bath room is small but functions well with a working drain. Hotel layout is confusing as part of the hotel is actually located at the other side of the street. If you are in Denver for business and want to get a little taste for this city, this is a very acceptable place. But I am sure there are more unique, boutique like hotels that may be more attractive.

title_masked: Hotel is great - until there is a problem
text_masked:
I believe that any hotel can train their staff to say 'please and thank you' and 'enjoy your stay', but how they deal with unexpected situations is the real measure of good service.
My husband, two young children and I stayed at this hotel Mar. 25 -27th. Check in was smooth. Because I was hoping for a quiet room, they happily switched us to a corner room furthest from the elevator. So far so good, right? 
What a mistake that turned out to be.
The room itself was standard hotel fare. A little dated but tidy, and quiet, just like I requested. On our last night, my husband was sitting by the window when 5 year old daughter ran over to give him a good night kiss. That's when we heard a loud thud. It turned out the corner of the bed frame stuck out by an inch and a half and she had sliced her shin open about three inches. Not having any bandages large enough to cover her wound, my husband ran down to the front desk to request help. He returned right away empty-handed. The hotel informed him they don't have a first aid kit available. (Seriously? There is no expectation that some one, might at some time get hurt in a place that sees hundreds of people?) Anyway, they said were going to send security up to assist us. So we waited. And waited. Meanwhile my daughter was screaming in pain. While we were kept waiting I noticed how deeply she was cut and we decided to take her to the hospital.
On the way down we stopped off at the front desk to show them how seriously she was injured. All three desk staff stood like deer in the headlights. No help there. We left in our own car and drove to Harbourview Medical. I have to say, the hospital was amazing. Seeing my daughter so upset, they saw to us right away. Fortunately the doctors decided to glue the wound together instead of giving her stitches and distressing her more.
The next day was check out and we once again brought to the hotel's attention the protruding bedframe that caused our daughter's injury. Their response? 'Oh, you should have told us sooner!' This, as they handed us a bill for our overnight parking. By then we really weren't expecting anything more from them.
Good thing we took pictures of everything because I'm very disappointed in the lack of empathy from this hotel. Needless to say we won't stay here again. And my daughter has a nifty souvenir of her stay in the form of an inch long keloid scar.
If you're planning a stay here, just hope nothing out of the ordinary happens to you, because if it does, you can be sure you will get no assistance and no sympathy from this hotel.

We stayed here for about a week in April as it was convenient to visiting our family. The service was great; the manager went out of their way to help us out. The rooms were clean and roomy. The only problem was oversized pillows, but they are planning to replace them soon. They are close to a grocery store and several restaurants. The free breakfast is fine, better than many other places. This was the best deal for hotels near the airport and a real nice place to stay.

The suite was so spacious. Especially the bathroom with the deep jacuzzi. Everything was beautiful and VERY CLEAN. Very helpful staff. There was actually a vegan option on the restaurant menu! The tofu+quinoa scramble wrap with fruit was really quite good. I wish the Kimpton restaurants would add more vegan items to their menus. Especially the late night room service. I love staying at Kimpton hotels, because they allow my three big dogs at no extra cost and with nothing but acceptance. At this particular hotel, you have to walk your dog a couple of blocks for the nearest place for them to do their business. Not bad though. I really appreciated the dog information packet I received when I checked in. It let me know about other places to take the dogs. Cornelius was especially helpful with me and my dogs when I was checking in and out. Thank you Cornelius! I hope to stay at Baltimore Monaco again.

I only stayed for one night to attend a show at Madison Square Garden. The location was what drew me to the hotel and the fact the rooms had been renovated recently. What I wasn't expecting upon arrival was to be told they had overbooked the hotel for the weekend and our room had been upgraded to a suite. I was shocked to say the least. 
When we were given our room, it was clean, smelled wonderful, had a full kitchen and quiet. I was surprised to find that I could sleep. I'm usually not one who does well sleeping in hotels but at Affinia, I had no problem.
The staff was wonderful and went above and beyond the call of duty. The Front desk staff in particular was a joy to interact with, always friendly and always helpful. There is no problem too big that they weren't willing to help tackle and solve. 
I've stayed at many hotels and this was by far the best experience I've ever had. If you are going to stay in a hotel in NYC, there is no better place than the Affinia Manhattan. It may be a little pricey for some people but it is well worth the money.

Booked 2 rooms through Easytobook,and fortunately called in route to hotel.Only one room was booked for me on a sold out Easter weekend.Strongly recommend calling the hotel immediately after online confirmation,as it did not transfer well to the hotel.I booked 2 rooms for 5,and they registered 1 room for 1.A crafty Millenium register named [NAME] saved our trip by finding another room for us...all of their employees worked hard for good service.

title_masked: Great Location but that's pretty much it.
text_masked:
We booked this hotel for my birthday weekend because the photos from their website made the rooms look cozy and very modern. The room that we were given looked very lacking of furniture and decor (like they did the bare minimal job or it was still being furnished). 
On the plus side: the room was very clean and spacious since our room seemed to consist of two rooms 
1) sitting room (lacking in any real furniture, it had one lounge and a desk)
2) the bedroom (full size bed and tv). 
Needless to say the layout was very strange! Our bathroom was very tiny and the shower water pressure was lacking and there wasn't a real bathroom door... they put in one of those bi-fold closet doors instead. 
Yeah, I don't have many good things to say about this boutique hotel. Both my boyfriend and I were pretty much underwhelmed considering we made a decision to pay more for this hotel thinking it would be a nice unique experience. Instead it felt very much like we were staying in a poorly furnished guest room.

Super friendly and helpful front desk -especially the manager who was really clued up on good restaurants .
There were problems with WiFi access in our room but they did all they could do sort it out and offered compensation for the inconvenience. 
The hotel is in a great location for shops, sights, restaurants etc

I had a great stay again thanks Kirsten!!! Kirsten you are great !! Thanks for ordering the flowers for my wife she loved them... thanks for being so kind and real, thats makes a big difference when someone stays away from home.. I will be back once again... All your staff is great but you just standout!!!

This is a two-tower, massive convention hotel, and it serves its purpose very well. The staff and rooms are up to the (high) Marriott standard.
There's a very nice, large outdoor pool area for families and vacationers (and perhaps a few conventioneers) to enjoy, and the fitness center is large enough and well enough equipped to handle convention level crowds.
There's a Starbucks in the lobby, and there's a great lounge space nearby. The lounge space was always being used by people doing e-mail/surfing the internet, but it never seemed too crowded. 
There are many fine GasLamp District restaurants within walking distance. 
The San Diego Convention Center sits between this hotel and the Hilton. I had some meetings in the Hilton, and came away feeling that the Marriott was better outfitted for convention business. The upside to the Hilton was a large amount of ballroom space in addition to what is available in the convention center. But the Marriott had the feel of a much better hotel.

title_masked: Starting to show wear - lives mostly on convention
text_masked:
This is on the Riverwalk - if it is your first time in San Antonio and on the Riverwalk, you will likely be thrilled - and be happy with the Westin. But if it is not your first visit, there are much better properties there. The Mokessa, the Hyatt, and the Drury are far better properties.
To begin, the curbside is a mess - the bellmen do not do a very good job of managing the checkin and checkout traffic. They are likely the worst I have seen in this city. The check in process is fair but not that friendly. (Please keep in mind as you read this review, know that I have hosted 7 meetings at this hotel over the past 8 years. It has clearly gone downhill.)
The rooms are starting to show wear and tear. Even though the week I was there with two meeting groups and they were doing touch-up painting, other areas show wear.
The restaurant and bar on the Riverwalk has horrific and slow service. It is interesting to note that on two consecutive nights two different hostesses did not really care if we were seated or not.
Housekeeping is fair. The amenities have gone downhill - again, it seems clear to me that the hotel is living off its convention and meeting business.
Meeting services were below average; service slow; caddy tables not bussed frequently enough; lunches very mediocre.
While it has been a good deal in the past, I think it is worth trying new hotels.
Once again, if this is your first trip to San Antonio and the Riverwalk, you will not have a basis for comparison. The Westin has become like the Marriott Riverwalk - full of itself, busy enough to turn a good profit and maintain a high occupancy, and yet quite mediocre and three star at best.

I was at the Dallas Westin Galleria on May 4, 5 and 6, 2012 for a conference. I had a room with a king sized bed which was very comfortable. I love the window seat. It is great for sitting and reading or just gazing out the very large window. The "heavenly" shower is very nice and is a nice sized shower (no bathtub). The "heavenly" shower consists of two shower heads that you can choose to use only one or both. I highly recommend using both! The towels are oversized and nice and there is a robe in the closet to use. About the only downside to this hotel is that they charge you for the internet in your room ($9.99 per day). However, you can go to the lobby for free WiFi but they do not make this public knowledge. Overall, this hotel is a very nice property. Oh and I forgot to tell you that it is attached to the Galleria Mall - not need to even walk outside - which is a wonderful mall. Upon arrival to the Westin, you will be pleasantly greeted with the signature scent of the Westin - the white tea scent - it is awesome. This is the 4th year that I have come to the Westin for my conference and enjoy this hotel.

title_masked: Great room and great location if you need to be downtown
text_masked:
I was here for 4 days for business. Did not use the conference facility but it looked really nice. Fantastic Fed Ex business center. Expensive but you can make copies and fax anything. You can rent a computer but it was 40cents a min. This to me seem really expensive but if you don’t carry a laptop I guess you would pay it if you needed to use a computer. There is a place downstairs by the front desk to print boarding passes for free. 
I had two meal at the restaurants but the food was ok. There is a place called [NAME] that is only about a city block. Easy walk down the sidewalk next to the water. It had a pretty wide selection of food. I really enjoyed the food from the Mexican restaurant. Huge portions and the price was great! The food was really good. 
The only reason I did not give this hotel a 5 is because the pool was a bit dirty for me. It was not just dirt but it had paper and other item floating in the pool. The bottom needed a good cleaning. The hot tub was not super hot but comfortable and it needed a good cleaning also. The only other reason is no refrigerator or microwave.
The rooms were good size with a great view if you ask for a river view. I had two queen beds in my room and the bed was really comfortable. Housekeepers did a great job with my room. The curtain the bathroom was dirty when I arrived in the room but it was changed as soon as I mentioned anything. Great pillows but they are feather so if you are allergic you will need to ask for foam. The other positive being female the toilet paper was actual decent for a change. 
Great room, great view, great staff cannot ask for much more. Had a wonderful stay and will return.

Just returned from a night's stay at Distrikt. It is my second time there and it would be difficult to find a better place for the price in NYC. Rooms are attractive and comfortable. Staff are friendly and very helpful. Booked the hotel and had theater tickets to celebrate my husband's birhtday. The staff went out of their way for him and even treated us to a complimentary dessert. Located right near Times Square theaters, shopping and restaurants are in walking distance of the hotel. Will definatelay be staying at Distrikt again

title_masked: Great vintage hotel with modern touches
text_masked: Stayed here for a week in late May. Really liked the room. Warm and cozy. Decorated in a craftsman style. Dark wood and earth toned paint. Large bathroom with a great shower. The in-room coffee press was a nice touch if you don't want to leave your room early in the morning. Very quiet part of the hotel. Slept great and loved the light the room got during the day. Seems like it would be a great hotel for business or a couples trip. Not sure its set up as a place for families. Not a lot to do for them. The value for the rate we paid was average. Living in a big city, +$200 rooms are the norm. Location was a little on the south side of town right near Pioneer Square. Loved that you could take the train from the airport and exit 50 feet from the front door.

Great rate great location. Free suite upgrade . Wonderful breakfast as usual.
Only negative (but a big one) was the group of neighbors who started partying at midnight and it didn't stop until 330AM. Too bad since the hotel was pretty empty.
But it was overall a very positive stay. I love tis place!

This is my first review for tripadvisor, but I felt compelled to write since we had such a great experience staying at this hotel the first weekend in April. Besides being at a great location, the hotel has wonderful amenities: two pools (one for families and one for adults only), a fantastic gym, and tennis/basketball courts, all of which we enjoyed using. We stayed at the Seaport Tower after reading the reviews that the rooms in the other tower were not that great (Seaport is newer). And we actually really liked our room. I know other reviewers have complained of thin walls. And yes, at one point during our stay, late at night, we did get a bump on the wall from our next door neighbor signaling us to be quiet. With four people in the room talking pretty loudly and the TV on, I’m sure we were being too loud so we lowered the volume and didn't get any more complaints after that. As for us, we didn't hear any noises from our neighbors. 
But I think what really sets this hotel apart is their customer service and their helpful staff. From the moment we walked in their beautiful lobby (which does look majestic as others have noted), we received great service. The gentleman who checked us in immediately accommodated my request to be put in the Seaport Tower and not only that, he upgraded us to a premier room with a beautiful view of the harbor. So considering I had booked the room at Priceline at half their listed rate, that was pretty cool! We definitely did not get inferior service because we had paid less for the room. 
So perhaps the experience was sweeter for my husband and me because it was very economical, but my teenage sons also loved the hotel so much that they asked if we could stay at Manchester Grand Hyatt whenever we go back to San Diego. And the answer is a definite Yes!

title_masked: Walk to the ballpark.....enjoy the room service
text_masked: As downtown hotels go, the Sheraton is a winner. Located about 0.4 miles north of Chase Field and American Airlines Arena, the hotel is easily within walking distance. The area is well lighted and very safe, devoid of undesirables, and a definite first choice for overnight stays for those two venues in particular. The Club Level is a great choice; in fact, I was upgraded to a Sr. Suite based on my SPG level. Great room, very comfortable bed, large shower and tub (separate), a second guest bathroom, and two TVs with ample sitting areas, and a 4-place table. Room service was partiularly notable. Great sandwiches, soups, and organic salmon (whatever that is). Servers are very courteous and promptly deliver the meals. Downstairs on the lobby level is an open bar, gift shop and business center. A very good fitness room with cardio workout equipment is also available 24 hours. Definitely a place to stay.

The staff couldn't do enough, including giving us rides to local attractions. The only downside is the restaurants all require going outside to go inside. That matters in Seattle's pouring rain, but the lobby staff seem to have large numbers of umbrellas to share.

title_masked: Must stay if you want to be close to all of the action!
text_masked:
Stayed here for one night. Parking was on the block of the hotel and offers a discount to anyone staying at the hotel, $30 for cars and $37 SUV's and trucks- what a steal! Minutes away from Times Square, MSG, Empire State Building, and 5th ave. Starbucks is a block away for you coffee lovers! 
Rooms were clean and roomy with modern decor. Big bathroom, flat screen tv and comfy beds. It can be a tad noisy, but I've never stayed at a hotel in NYC where that didn't occur and it's usually during daytime hours.

title_masked: Very good for price, great location
text_masked: I read many of the one-star reviews and was wary about my stay at Congress Plaza, but I was pleasantly surprised. Yes, it's an old building. Yes, it could use some updating. Yes, there were picketers at times (though they simply went about their business of picketing). However, my room was very clean (much cleaner than some places I've stayed in Chicago for twice the cost) and the bed was quite comfortable. I enjoyed being in an historical building that hadn't been gutted and whitewashed to fit some generic standard. If you want a sparkly hotel with rooms that seem as though you are the first ever to stay in them, this isn't the place for you. If you like a bit of character, then I recommend it. I wish I had ponied up for a room with a view, because it looked like those would be lovely. The location is perfect and easy to get to by L train blue line from the airport. My only real complaint was that all of the reports of no truly hot water were confirmed when I took a shower. The hotel does need to update its plumbing system.

My husband and I could not find a room in Austin during a special event weekend, obviously, but luckily we found the last room available at this Hotel! It was great, got checked in, slept comfortably for the night, and then left the entire next day. The best thing about the Hotel, is that everything is so close, restaurants, shops, downtown!! We heard the area was a bit sketchy, but we were totally fine with leaving our few pieces of luggage and important items in the room. Anyway, great hotel for the price!

title_masked: Luxury without leaving a hole in your wallet
text_masked: I have stayed many times at most of the 5 stars in Philadephia when traveling alone however on this visit I had others with me who needed rooms so i gave the Sofitel a try and came away duly impressed. Its my new desitnation in philadelphia! The rooms were spacious, clean, tasefully decorated and the bath and accesorires were first rate. The price of my suite was half of what i usally pay and i liked it better! It even had a Bose Wave unit in the room versus the "if your lucky" - Bose iphone alarm clock)

Just stayed one night but it was great. 1/2 hour or less walk to famous restaurants and sites. Magnificent mile, Hancock tower, Portillo's (Chicago dogs and Italian Beef), Gino's (deep dish pizza with a corn meal crust), Garrett Popcorn (one of Oprah's favorite things, the chicago mix is to die for) North Bridge Shops, etc. Can catch the Chicago Trolley & Double Decker Co. tours within walking distance. $40 cab ride to O'Hare.
Service was superb, you really felt taken care of (thanks Bianca!), the breakfast was decent for continental (make your own waffles). Very nice clean room, comfortable, great cable, lots of channels, not just 10 or 12. Room itself was quiet, no street or neighbor noise, however the a/c is a bit loud. That forces you to raise the tv volume, but it works great (kept me and my soda cool). Definitely would stay again. Used my points for the stay.

My family and i enjoyed our stay. The room was cleaned daily. We are a family of five so the room would get messy pretty fast. The housekeeping did a wonderful job cleaning our room. I really like that there is a nearby location to catch the trolley. The front desk employees were very helpful! The only complaint I have is BREAKFAST but what can I expect for free breakfast. We only had breakfast in the hotel once. We decided to eat elsewhere every day after that.

The staff was extremely friendly and helpful. Location was great with the wharf, tours and restaurants within walking distance. The rooms were very clean and spacious. The atmosphere at the wine tasting each night was warm and friendly and open to all guests. Overall we had a very enjoyable stay in a great area.

title_masked: October prices are amazing for wwhat you get.
text_masked:
It was a great hotel... a paradise in Mission Bay I was told from BlueVan Shuttle driver.
Service was excellent, the room was awesome. Good TV, good internet connection, so quiet, good contrast leisure vs. conference. It is nice to walk by exotic birds, duck, lake and palm tree's on your way from the room to the conference venue.
The conference venue has an excellent catering and magnificient view from mission bay beach.
I loved it! Stood there for one week. The lobby is a nice place to stay if you have a late-evening flight... no need to waste up time in the airport.

Great location, great value; efficient, friendly, professional staff. Clean, quiet, and safe.
Parking is a big plus.

title_masked: Super hotel in a super location!!
text_masked: Located right on the cable car line, this hotel is just steps from great shopping on Powell street and in Union Square. Rooms are nicely updated.. and while the bathrooms may be a bit on the small side, the great showers make up for it. The staff is also SUPER friendly and helpful. If you need help finding anything, be sure to ask for Perri!

I stayed here one night on a business trip. It's convenient to the airport. The room was clean. Check-in was easy. One downside was the lack of heat. I turned on the heat and cold air blew out of the vents. It never warmed up. Also, since I'm a Hilton Honors member they gave me two free bottles of water at check in. I put them into the refrigerator in the room but they never got cold. Also, the desk is too far away from the closest electrical outlet to plug in a computer. The bed wasn't very confortable. It was a bit mushy,
Finally, breatfast was just so-so.

My wife and I booked this property for our yearly sojourn to Toy Fair-perfect location, walking distance down 36th. Area prices had increased, told due to improved economy, so we shopped around. Our "nameless" not-as-nice hotel where we were regulars didn't compare! Checked rates, read reviews, took the jump. Nice landing here!! Warm cookies, walking distance to our usual eateries, clean, friendly. We were on 12th floor, typical small queen bed room, large bathroom(so nice!!). Workout room looked decent, restaurant/bar on 1st floor. Only negatives were size(small) and number(2) of elevators for a building this size, which housekeeping shares, and error in final room billing(overcharged room rate). Thankfully I had booked direct, so no issue straightening it out. Just pay attention. Also had problem finding my Hilton Honors member # in their system. No biggie. So, if you're headed for anything near Convention Center/Times Square/Midtown, this is a winner. We must have had a more recently renovated room-no issues like other posters. Perfect mid-level hotel.

title_masked: Great value for money and a VERY nice airport hotel - rather like a resort near the airport
text_masked: We stayed here for one night on the day we arrived into Phoenix in January 2012. We booked our room using Priority Club points. We booked a king-size suite and requested a crib for our 15 month old son. After a very long flight it was really nice to be picked up by the kind shuttle bus driver & taken the hotel. Probably one of the friendliest people we'd ever encountered, he helped us bring our bags in (with our long flight/jet lag & late hour it was definitely appreciated!). We checked into our room & requested some milk for our son - there in a flash. We also inquired if the restaurant was serving food & indeed it was :) We went to our room to put our son to bed and the crib (requested in our booking) wasn't in our room, but we called reception & it was brought really quickly by the very kind maintenance crew man. He even brought us extra sheets because he very honestly said, 'I wasn't sure what you needed.' We got ourselves situated - our room was great as we were able to put our son to sleep in the bedroom (in his crib) & shut the door, then sit out in the sitting room/lounge area. My husband went to get food from the restaurant for our dinner as it was about 9:30 PM now. He got us a salad and one of the yummiest Turkey Focaccia sandwiches we'd ever had!!! So, if you are at the hotel, I'd recommend that sandwich for sure. The salad was so-so, edible, but nothing to get excited about, but the sandwich, wow! Then, we retired for the evening. Had a great sleep & woke up in the AM, then walked up the road a bit to have breakfast at an IHOP (International House of Pancakes). A nice stroll up there & back, then we left the hotel to head back to the airport to pick up our rental car for our stay. The staff at the hotel, Zachary in particular, were really helpful and nice in letting us check out a bit late as our son was napping. We would happily stay there again if needing an airport hotel in Phoenix. Also, (although we didn't take advantage of it as we were off to visit with family after our first night there) I would expect it's a very convenient spot to explore downtown Phoenix.

title_masked: Really expected a lot better room
text_masked:
I did a Priceline and wound up with this hotel. I read some reviews before I arrived, and while they were all over the board, I was very wary of what I would find. 
My room was VERY dated. Not what I would expect for a 2.5 star hotel. Check in was pleasant, and I was told to park between the two hotels and use the side entrance to the hotel. Parking was well lit, and I am glad as this is not the best area in town. Road construction in front of the hotel was a real challenge, but all construction is and cannot be the hotel's fault.
My room was hot. The a/c had not been turned on. It must be a central a/c unit as all I had was a very worn control. It has cooled slightly in the past 3 hours, but no where near as fast so I could have a comfortable rest. 
I held my breath when I flushed the toilet as it was very anemic. The shower handle leaked water. Watching TV has been a real challenge. You would expect a better picture with no snow and roll from a flat screen TV bolted to the dresser. Some channels are better than others, but not by much.
No fridge, no microwave. Shows how dated this hotel is as in most hotel's that is a standard in the room. Dark colors, poor lights, and carpet that would have felt at home 20 years ago.
One thing I will say, the room was clean. No complaints in that department.
The towel looked so inviting, until I used it. The chemicals in it were too much, and now I feel that burn when I went to bed. 
I will skip the Priceline thing next time, as their standards are not up to mine, and will pay a few bucks more for a better room.

While the Manhattan at Times Square is somewhat mis-named (it's on 7th ave at 51st St), the hotel has a great location, responsive staff, quiet room, comfy beds with nice linens, and very fast elevators. Nightly cost via Priceline made our Memorial Day weekend a real bargain but I would stay at the Manhattan again even at a higher price.

title_masked: Why stay anywhere else for overnight?
text_masked:
Out the front doors of international terminal, turn right and walk about 5minutes and you are there! No need to wait for shuttle. As long as its not raing or real cold you are better off walking. You have to pass the smoking section but maybe that will work for some.
Service was good, room was okay. We open drapes just to look out at a roof with air conditioner but for one night that was not an issue.beds very clean and "Radisson" comfy. We didnot eat breakfast there as leaving early ...and again walked to airport. We have always overnight on our Alaska Air run to Mexico for the winter. This is our favorite hotel in Seattle.

Its a good location and customer service superb. I agree with a previous reviewer about the lack of a mirror in the room (only one in bathroom and on bathroom door) but its not a show stopper.
Rooms are roomy and have character. I don't know if some people are giving reviews on the Dupont Circle l page by mistake for another Renaissance location.The rooms are spacious.
We stayed during memorial day weekend, so quite a diverse crowd was there (never felt unsafe) just very interesting people, lol.
Overall, Love this hotel, would stay here again, everyone is trying to make sure your stay is comfortable and safe.
Also nearby to Walgreens, and CVS as well as restaurants for every palette everywhere, you don't need to go more than 5 blocks to find what you will need.

I have stayed at many Starwood properties including the St. Regis brand and this property was the best. What stands out the most - is the service of the concierage and the warm welcome from all the employees. We also were at the property over the NATO Summit weekend and we still managed to have a great time!

I came here for a business trip & stayed here with low expectations. I was greatly surprised though. The hotel staff was very friendly. I arrived at 2 am & had to be at a meeting downtown 5 hours early. The staff was kind enough to give me a wake-up call.
Breakfast was small, but better than most Americas Best with Waffles, pastries, fruits & juice. They gave me an extended checkout.
Wi-Fi worked good. Rooms are large. Flat screen TV. Ended up staying an extra night. Great motel for people on a budget. In a good safe area too. Has an indoor pool which I didnt use.

title_masked: Bring Vodka, clean sheets and towels!
text_masked: The hotel is connected to Cheetah's Gentleman Club. As we walked up the stairs at the main entrance, we noticed the following: 1. An "OUT OF ORDER" ramp for the disabled, 2. A large congregation in front of the 2 elevators, and 3. A strong nauseating odor of cleaning supplies. A lady from behind a counter with slots and lockers close to the main entrance yelled "May I help you?". The check-in was at 2pm into Room 938. I must say that I am an avid traveler and have been to many continents and this was the very first hotel that has EVER charged me $2 per luggage to store a backpack and for simply 2 hours. The bellman complained that there was too much luggage to handle. We returned at 2pm to get our keys for Room 938. The wait for the elevators was about 10mins. We opened the doors to Room 938 and there was no maid service since last checkout? The front desk representative quickly said I gave you Room 939 (while I was still holding the yellow sheet with Room 938 clearly written on it). To our dismay, it was far from acceptable. The room had a broken desk (with no handles on the drawers), the sheets were dirty and quite thin, the comforter had stains of bodily fluids, the nightstand was also broken, the telephone seems to be disconnected from the wall and the small TV had 14 channels. I cannot even describe as to how filthy the carpets were and the bathroom walls looked as if it had not been cleaned in more than a decade with mold and mildew everywhere. There is no hairdryer or ironing amenities. The 3 towels were small, stained and torn. The only way that we were able to sleep in that room was after we finished a bottle of vodka, went our for beers and came back intoxicated. After numerous bug bites, we checked out before the actual check-out time. Please pay the extra 40-70$ and stay elsewhere. Don't ruin your vacation over this mess!!
I always enjoy myself staying there. Many sweet small things accumulates and make a big difference. The staff are firendly and remember my preferences as a regular customer, well abort of.

It was a bit strange to stay here during storm Sandy. The hotel was very busy and the lobby was overflowing with people looking for a warm place to stay for a few hours and to charge their phones etc and to use the wireless. The staff seemed tired and overworked but they did their best to deliver the service. So the circumstances were not ideal but I had a nice stay anyway. The hotel is in a good location. The room is spacy. The bed very comfortable. The view from the high floor incredible. I thought it was a good price for what you get. 
I also tried the spa. I think for the money you pay you are better off somewhere else. The spa is nothing special and the massage was fine but a bit businesslike; in and out not very personal. 
What I liked is that I asked for a water boiler so I could make tea in the morning and they also delivered a small fridge to the room!

Loved celebrating with dear friends in this wonderful hotel dead center of this city . Kelly( front desk) heard it was a 60th and sent a chilled bottle of wine up to our room after we came back from shopping OVER the top !!! Service the BEST!!!
Right around the corner to Newbery Street and the Bell Santa Spa (voted best in Boston)

Another Sheraton Airport hotel disappointment. I have stayed twice across the road at ALOFT, which got dirtier with each stay so decided to try here at Four Points. First, there is no wireless in the rooms. The only wireless access is in the lobby, but there is no workplace or business center in the lobby. I was working in the open restaurant/bar area and although it was not full, was asked to leave. When I asked where I should go to work I was told to go next door to the Sheraton Suites. 
Although they have upgraded the rooms cosmetically and it looks clean, it's not. My sink drain is slow, the toilet runs, the grout and tile is dirty and stained, as are the wood floors in the entrance. You cannot open the closet door without hitting the door closer on the entrance door. 
I can't wait to check out tomorrow.

title_masked: A little gem in the flower wholesale area
text_masked: I stayed at the Hotel Indigo for a business trip I took to New York City in preparation for the launch of a NYC area CIYO (Coming Into Your Own) women's leadership program that will take place in October 2012. I was in NYC for 4 nights and have nothing but good things to say about the Hotel Indigo. Front desk staff was friendly and efficient. The rooftop bar has a beautiful view of the city and is small enough to feel like a special 'find'. The location in Chelsea is perfect for visiting galleries. And the rooms are modern and quiet if you select a higher floor (I was on the 5th).

Client's office is in walking distance of this hotel. Good value, great breakfast, and nice manager's reception. Only negative is that the bathroom of my "non-smoking" room reeked of a previous heavy smoker. Would stay again.

My very first time to New York. Arrived to New York on Jan 1st so you can imagine how crowded New York was. The hotel was really well located to help you get anywhere in town but the photos on Booking have nothing to do with the reality especially the ones of the lobby - although the people at the Information Dest were honestly pretty helpful. The room was spacious but due to the hotel's location you could hear every single fire-brigade vehicle since the station is just next to the hotel as well as all the taxis in front of Madisson Sq. Garden. The bathroom was really small. The worst thing is that even though I stayed at the hotel for almost 7 days I doubt the staff changed the bed sits more than twice!!!

title_masked: Another fantastic stay at the SLS
text_masked: Once again had a wonderful time at my favorite hotel. Front desk team with Lisa and Raahi could not have made me feel more welcome back and the concierge team always amazes. Casey got me fantastic reservations at INK for a friend's 50th and Fredo took care of everything else. The entire team is so warm and so obliging and always professional. Small touches like Nerieida on the phone make such a difference being away from home. Thank you too to Crystal who takes advance care of my room needs and the bellstaff. Had great experience too at Ciel, with its fantastic manager Amanda and new premier hair team. WOW! I can't say enough about the hotel with its whimsy, style, delicious food, and superb staff. Go, go, go....as soon as you can. And then, like me, come back again and again. Amy

We wanted this to be a high-engery, wonderful, "last fling before the ring" weekend and knew that the best place to make that happen would be the Hotel ZaZa. What we did not know is that we would receive such excellent service and special treatment from everyone at the ZaZa. From the Valet parking to the ZaSpa.... the upscale rooms through the restaurant and the very unique DragonFly bar... the ZaZa was the perfect spot to make our vision become a reality. You could tell that the entire staff knew we were coming and treated us in that manner. Thank you so much for your attention to all the details that made our experience unforgetable.

AMAZING!!! I love everything that has been done to the hotel :) We stayed Thursday- Sunday during the week of NIOSA, the staff was great!!! We had room service during lunch time one day and it was delicous ... As my three year old daughter would say it was too yummy for my tummy :) I can't wait to stay again !!!

We had a perfect stay at 6 Columbus in August. My sister and I shared a deluxe double room. The room was not huge, but we had enough space. It was clean and the beds were very comfortable. The location is perfect - subway across the street, bus nearby, Central Park across the street, food shopping steps away. The hotel staff is amazing - everyone is so friendly and helpful. This hotel is highly recommended. We will be back soon!

We stayed at the Skyview Plaza this past weekend. Upon checkin, we had to wait 10 minutes to be waited on. Once we got to our room, we found that the bathroom was covered in roaches and their was a hole in the ceiling. We called down to the desk and the person that had checked us in stated he was going to send someone up to check out the problem. No one ever came. It was disgusting and we will never stay there again.

The hotel has a great location but beware the constant up charges- we were told free wifi but it turns out only in the lobby - if you want it in your room its $14 a day- they charge $36 per day in parking- $10 per day to use the gym. When we booked with priceline we were told this was included-Also wether or not you out going long distance sall is answered ,once you dial it they charge you $11.20 per call, which no one at check in informed us of this. 
 the beds were very comfortable but our room, though renoveated had mold in the caulk and the pipe was expose on the shower head- we were missing the coffee maker,robes, and duevet covers- when we called for them the were brought to us - but ther was lipstick on the cup that came with the coffee maker and holes in the robes. We also booked a king size bed and we given 2 doubles because we were told the hotel was sold out and they would make sure to have the king for us the next night, that didn't happen either. 
the staff was friendly and helped us learn how to get around the area and the location was great. We paid $85 a night on priceline but add the $36 parking and no promised amenities. I wouldn't pay a dime more than this and this hotel appears to book for $197 a night everywhere else which is a rip off in my opinion. Not sure I would stay there again.

Nice hotel, but a few flaws considering the rates. At check-in (1 PM), the room wasn't ready: had to wait till 3,30 PM to get inside my corner one bedroom suite on the 26th floor. Which was very large by NYC standards and well appointed, with an extremely comfortable lounge. The Italian restaurant could be better. Wifi in the room was offered free of charge. Nice neighborhood, a few block from West Broadway and Soho. Good overall, but keep in mind the prices.

title_masked: The Pod Hotel - tiny but does the trick
text_masked: My daughter and I stayed at the Pod Hotel in New York last weekend. We had a bunk bed room with a shared bath. The room was even smaller than I expected but we pretty much knew what we were getting into so no complaints there. There was only one chair so one of us had to sit on the bed if we were both sitting down. The room was very clean and we never had any hold up on getting into one of the shared bathrooms. there is a monitor in your room telling you which of the four bathrooms someone was in. They were never full. Two of them were right across from our room. The staff was very friendly and helpful. There is a beautiful waterfall/garden oasis across the street where we had lunch one day and that was really nice. The hotel is a few blocks from the 6 and the E subway lines so that was also convenient. Even though we have decided we wouldn't stay there again we would recommend it to anyone on a budget who has a sense of adventure!

title_masked: Price & Location is Right, But Details Lacking
text_masked: Loved the location and price was good for area but the guest room stocking closet was always empty and wash clothes and regular coffee was almost always asked for as we either didn't get them or shorted. Staff needs to know just a little bit more of what restaurants around just then the attached Elephant & Castle. Very spartan, no bathtub, but bed was comfortable.

Stayed one Saturday night w/2 children in tow (ages 9+13) and it was great. Upgraded us
to a slightly bigger room upon checking in. 2 queen beds w/view of Bay Bridge and Ferry Building.
Comfortable bedding, great bathroom w/Fresh toiletry products, clean/contemporary decor. Quiet night's sleep. Had the valet take the car to lessen the hassle - $48 for overnight and could use the car in that time period as much as we needed. Great breakfast at restaurant in the hotel in the morning. All in all - great stay. Love proximity to Ferry Building across the way for easy lunch/dinner and view of bridge/water was nice.

Very nice staff, extremely clean hotel and I actually slept better than at home!! 
Brittany was working the night shift and was so extremely helpful and professional.
The breakfast buffet was a value. We were there for a pom competition and the teams didn't seem to get on the staff's nerves at all. (i'm sure they did, but the staff was so professional they didn't show it!! )

This is quite a large hotel across a couple of different wings, so some rooms may be much better than others. My room (which I picked up on a last mintue style site) may have been one of the older rooms as it was in need of a refurb and update. The room was large enough, although the decor wasnt overly fresh and the bathroom was a bit old school. 
Certain areas around the hotel could also do with a refresh. I'm sure their newer rooms are quite well done however, just make sure you get a new one. 
The location is good, just a few minutes walk will have you to several restaurants, found a litte vietnamese place just up the road on a little laneway - brilliant food - and you can walk to Fishermans Wharf but might take about 45 minutes to an hour.

Stayed overnight on way to cruise. Hotel is within walking distance of Port, if you are in walking condition. Otherwise taxii is good price. Not far from Link service from Airport. Seattle is a good city for walking, many sights can be walked to from this hotel. Hotel is not in center of town, but is safe otherwise. We are seniors. Hotel is clean, neat, friendly and knowledgeable staff. Very helpful. Breakfast is included with stay. Choices are quick and easy. Nothing fancy but great for quick start. Coffee all day!!!! Would recommend and would stay again if in the area.

title_masked: Dirty and in need of refurbishments
text_masked:
Although the location was good, and the hotel is across the street from a marina and an awesome seafood place called [NAME] Seafood, overall we did not have a very pleasant experience. The hotel is clearly very old and in need of refurbishments. The front desk staff was very nice and accommodating at check in, but the experience was all downhill from there. My friend accidentally booked us in a smoking room, which was not at all the fault of the hotel, but upon arriving at the room we discovered cigarette burns on the comforter and the carpet. Since I don't usually stay in smoking rooms I don't know if this is typical, but it certainly put me off. The bathroom fan made a weird screeching noise while operating, and while I was taking a shower the lights and fan randomly went off for 5-10 seconds... not safe and pretty sketchy. 
We were also awoken at about 7:30 the first morning of our stay by what sounded like hammering and construction; we later found out that they were renovating the bar underneath our room. Maybe 7:30am is not the best time for a hotel to be doing construction near guest rooms? We headed down to the continental breakfast, which was actually pretty good and had a wide variety, but there was not enough seating in the breakfast room so we ended up eating on couches in the lobby.
The first night of our stay we found a water bottle cap left by previous guests that Housekeeping did not remove, and the second day we returned to the room to find a large bottle of cleaning chemicals left in our bathroom. The last morning of our stay while packing, we discovered a small cockroach by the bed.
Overall, the hotel was old and dirty and I would definitely not choose to stay there again. There has to be better options for the money.

title_masked: Best value in the Gaslamp District
text_masked:
When you first look at the Ramada Historic St. James Hotel in the Gaslamp District, you may think, "Yeesh". But this hotel has almost everything you need for a business trip, or a weekend of partying in the Gaslamp. It is in the heart of the Gaslamp, but I have never been kept up by the noise of the street. Great value, amazing service, and perfect location. Add in a free airport shuttle and free wi-fi, and I can't see spending double the price to stay a couple blocks away. Also, be sure to go up to the roof-top deck. A gorgeous view of downtown makes for a great place to have a few drinks and relax!
A couple of important things to know/note: The rooms are small, but I have never spent less time in a room then when in SD. The beds are comfy and everything works. To say their elevators are "old school" is an understatement - the nearly 100 year old elevators still run at the same speed. You have to open the door and pull back the gate to get in. IMHO, it only adds to the charm of this hotel, but just don't be surprised. 
Only thing to look out for - As I said, there is some noise and clammor that goes on if you are close to the eleveators. If you are in for business or are not "night owls", make sure you request to be away from the lifts.

Excellent hospitality...great comfort! we were in this hotel for 2 nights and all our meals we had at the cafeteria at the hotel. Neat and clean cafe....quality of food was superb. Staff is very cooperative and the overall experience was fabulous. Highly recommend.

We've stayed at the Carlyle several times for overnight DC visits. The location is in a great neighborhood within walking distance to Dupont Circle and the Metro. It's a perfect homebase for my family as we explore the Mall, museums, and sports & music events. The spacious suite is roomy enough for an energetic 10 year old boy and the kitchenette is handy for preparing snacks and breakfast. The room was very clean and the staff is friendly and helpful. And the bed is a Tempurpedic--LOVE! I can't recommend it enough.

My husband attended a conference held at this hotel so I tagged along. Our room was on the 12th floor with a very nice view of the sunrise each morning. We had a reservation for a king bed suite with a seperate living area and kitchenette but on arrival were told that our room had been given away. We ended up with a king bed with a hide-a-bed couch. Smaller than expected but o.k. Had latte's at the little coffee shop every morning. Sweet little lady working there was very friendly and helpful. The gentleman at the concierge desk was very helpful with directions and information on the downtown area. There are two pools, one indoor one out. We used the indoor pool and hot tub since we had rainy cool weather. Plenty of clean towels available at the pool. This hotel is about 10 miles from the downtown area were most of the tourist attractions are. With a GPS I was able to navigate around town fairly well. This hotel was nice and I would probably stay here again for business. If your going to San Antonio to see tourist attractions I would suggest staying downtown.

The location is wonderful, the olives bar a lovely spot, the service and attention was flawless. The service is friendly, housekeeping quick to bring extra towels, soaps and robe, and checkout instant. The bathroom was a little old and could have been cleaner. In a hotel of this location, I am sure they have had so many people through it needs extra scrubs.

title_masked: Reasonable size rooms for New York
text_masked:
We stayed in Four Points for 4 nights, we arrived very early on Monday morning but they were able to put us in a room straight away. We were put on the 25th floor and our room over looked the port authority car park, so it wasn't a great view but it was high enough we could see New Jersey and parts of time square.
I had done a bit of research on the hotel and knew it was next tot he parole office so I was a bit unsure what to expect from the area, but it was fine. I felt safe coming to and from the hotel any time of day or night. It's a great location for times square which has shops open till midnight and Broadway and comedy clubs are within walking distance from the hotel.
The room was a reasonable size, we have 2 large suitcases so were a bit tight for space once we had spread everything out but we could still get around okay in the room. The bed was large and comfortable with good pillows. The air con was old and very noisy when it was running, so we tended to leave it on high power during the day while we were out and about and just had the fan on at night and it worked well. We were given 2 bottles of water every day and the room had free wifi that worked at a good speed, good enough to skype without the connection stalling or buffering.
The staff were friendly, we booked broadway tickets through our concierge and he got us tickets for the show we wanted on the night we wanted and was upfront about the price which let us make a quick decision. We took advantage of happy hour in the hotel bar which was fine, the barman was able to recommend beers to my husband.

The hotel is in the Uptown area of Houston, near great restaurants and shopping. My husband and I were in town for a family event and the relatives stayed at the hotel. I have to say the hotel is tucked away and Neverlost had a bit of a problem getting us to the hotel entrance. This was somewhat aggravating. However, at check-in I was offered a complimentary glass of Champagne, which put a big smile on my face. Every time I was in the lobby area during the weekend, a staff member was there to ask if there was anything I needed. The staff was very attentive. Our room had nice neutral decor and a very comfortable bed. The robes were a nice touch. The bath did not have any type of grab bar and the floorcof the tub was a bit slippery. Water pressure in the shower was great; water pressure in sink, not so much. Plenty of counter space in the bathroom and nice lighting. Phone in bathroom is always a nice feature. Bath towels were better than average and long like a bath sheet. Every time we left the hotel there were at least 2 or 3 people outside to get you in your car and help you at the door when you returned. Only ate at the hotel Sunday morning for a family brunch. Food was excellent. We would not hesitate to stay here again if we wanted to be in the Uptown area.
This hotel made me feel like I fell back into the 60's. It is a good location that has an outdoor pool. Parking was grossly overpriced at $45.

title_masked: A good, budget hotel with pros and cons.
text_masked:
Firstly, bare in mind that the Grand Union Hotel is a BUDGET hotel, do not expect anything more than this. But! Although the hotel inexpensive, it is very good for the price you will pay. My fiancee and I booked the hotel through mybooking.com as we were happy with the price and the reviews that we read. 
Pros: 
- Location is fantastic, very close to Empire State Building, Flatiron district, Times Square, Macys and Grand Central. All within walking distance. 
- Near by Subways. 
- Good Deli's 
- Good house service (very polite maid) 
- Very clean
- Comfortable bed
- Big HD tv with cable (good for keeping up with the weather on NY1)
- Secure (swipe cards for stairwells) and luggage holding room is free.
- Little fridge that worked well
- Hair dryer
- Iron and ironing board
Cons:
- Air con is LOUD at times. 
- Some rooms have no views whatsoever 
- Thin walls
- Reception staff are not approachable 
- Shower temp tended to fluctuate 
**Note** There is a fixed rate fee for taxi's taking tourists from JFK to Manhattan. The fee is $50 (includes toll) - The hotel booked a 'taxi' for our return to JFK which turned out to be a private car which turned up half an hour early. We were also charged $68 in stead of $50. We were not warned by the reception staff. We had no change as we expected a taxi where you can swipe a credit, debit or travel card. This resulted in a stressful dash to find an ATM that would accept one of our cards whilst rushing to get to our flight.
