Overall, a good, clean hotel that is affordable and in a great location. The double room was spacious and comfortable. My partner and I both agree we would stay there again.

I visited Washington and stayed her for 2 nights. It was very convenient. I was able to walk to most of the local sites, it was not too far at all. The accommodations were good, not fabulous. It was a bit noisy in the morning,but overall no complaints. The food served for breakfast was tasty but quite expensive. The staff was pleasant and were very professional. I would stay again but eat elsewhere more affordable.

title_masked: Good location and price. Fair sized rooms.
text_masked: Have stayed in other "boutique" hotels in same area (Bush & Powell) and Orchard Hotel best so far. Rooms larger and modern good size bathroom in standard king bed room. Easy access to Powell cable car, short walk down Bush to Grant (entrance to China Town). Yes Bush and Powell is about 3 blocks from Union Square and a couple of moderately steep hills, but this is San Francisco! Friendly staff and clean throughout.

This hotel has everything you could possibly want when in D.C. for business or pleasure. Has parking available, attached to a great restaurant, and you are in the heart of D.C. close to DuPont Circle and within walking distance to many companies and businesses. Also very solid security (key card needed for elevator) and the staff were very accommodating. My only issue was the various construction happening outside my window early in the morning which woke me up, but then again this is D.C. so there is construction happening somewhere at sometime always. All in all a great stay and I will probably return again if I need to be in that location in D.C.
Nice and clean Hyatt Place with a very friendly staff. Good location to the freeway although it can get a bit noisy if you have a room on that side.

title_masked: Place could use a remodel, but the best service I may ever have had at a hotel.
text_masked: The location is good. While it was a long walk, we walked to Balboa Park from the hotel. The city tram was three blocks away and there were restaurants and shops near by. The best thing about this hotel was the staff. They were awesome! Incredibly sweet and helpful. The one woman, in particular, when we checked in was unbelievable in her service and she even called to see if we liked the room and when we saw her in the lobby as we were leaving she asked if there was anything else we needed. She supplied us maps and gave reallu good ideas about what to do with the time we had and how to ge there. The hotel itself was a bit worn, but clean. The breakfast buffet was packed, but they did a good job of keeping it filled, even though there were not enough tables for everyone (and there was a lot of tables). We paid $80 and for that price and the service this place gets an excellent by me.

The stay started well with Gerald providing the services of a 5 star hotel. The room did have an odour yet was pleasant and suitable for the stay. I have nary a complaint especially because of the excellent location in Baltimore.

I stayed at this hotel on a business trip this past week. The location is excellent, right next to the 16th street mall (a 20 block pedestrian mall with lots of shops, restaurants and bars within easy distance of the hotel). The front desk staff were friendly and efficient, and moved me to a room with a better view without my asking (and the room did turn out to have a nice view of the downtown area).
The guest room areas of the hotel need some work. The floors in the Plaza building are arranged in a square, with only one elevator bank per floor. My room was on the opposite side of the square, down two and a half very long, narrow, dimly lit hallways. It was a hike, especially when you’re lugging a laptop and a rollerboard. The carpeting both in the hallways and in the room looked worn and dated. The tub in my room had quite a bit of rust around the drain. And the walls are thin enough that my neighbor’s alarm woke me up…at 5 o’clock in the morning. 
The public areas of the hotel are in better condition, and I liked the option to decline housekeeping services in exchange for a $5 food voucher or 500 Starwood points for each night that you decline the service. Note that does mean that they won’t replenish the coffee packets in your room, so plan ahead when deciding how many days to decline!
Overall, it’s worth staying here for the location, as long as you don’t expect much from your room.

title_masked: One Stop From Union Station, - but "Where am I?"
text_masked: My wife and I stayed here for 2 nights, 8/12/12 - 8/14/12. We arrived via Amtrak from NYC and walked from Union Station, which took us about 30 minutes. We would stay here again, but would take the Metro the 1 stop as we did when we left. The hotel staff is very pleasant, and hospitable. We arrived at around noon was allowed to check-in immediately, which was nice. The room was very clean, no bathtub or microwave, but we didn't care. There was a view of nothing to write home about. The air-conditioning worked fine. There is complimentary coffee on the 2nd floor in the morning. The indoor pool is rather small, 3 feet deep, but again it was ok since we had it to ourselves when we used it. It was a great value as far as price is concerned. My sister works for Marriott and we got a discounted rate, but if I had paid $99 a night I wouldn't complain. The Metro is conveniently located on the corner and there are several fast food choices across the street, or within a block. There's really nothing around there though. All in all, a nice average Marriott hotel worthy of a return stay.

very clean and stylish rooms. free wifi and free coffee/tea/muffins in the morning. pc at lobby is also available for free. perfect location at times square, market, subway and bus station in the near. friendly hotel stuff and service.

I agree with the reviewers who talk about the hotel being right in the middle of everything. If you don't want to walk, one of the many mass transit or tour bus options are available close by. The rooms and bathrooms are comfortably sized for an urban hotel. The bathroom products are one of the few I have taken with me from a hotel chain. Also, the staff is extremely helpful - holding doors and elevators for me when my hands were full of coffee. (Their titles - intuition specialists - are a bit pretentious.) I did think the room amenities were slim - namely no refrigerator. I have no problem with no snacks or minibar in the room, but the prices to have them delivered were ridiculous. The food in the hotel was good enough - try one of the many other options in the area instead. The water delivered to the room, printed sheet of tips from the staff, and managers wine reception are all nice touches.
I had this for two nights on the front end of a business trip. I wish I had been there the whole trip.

As a fellow hotel general manager, I have very high expectations of great service, and this place delivered perfectly. Everyone we encountered was super friendly, and any request was met with an immediate and perfect response.
We stayed there twice, once when they didn't know who I was, and the second time when they did, and both stays were perfect. The breakfast that comes with the room was excellent, and the salsa is the BEST!! We also really liked the bacon, and the fact that the fruit was served nice and cold was a bonus.
The only thing we think should be improved is the water pressure in the shower, which was on the weak side. The decor is a bit dated, but who cares! It is clean, comfortable, and a good value. 
You will not be sorry if you chose this as a place to stay. We highly recommend it.

We stayed in this hotel while visiting friends over in Ponte Vedra. We chose it because we know the continental breakfasts at Country Inn & Suites are great. We were definitely not disappointed. Very good choices and lots of variety. Scrambled eggs, seasoned potatoes, bacon, oatmeal, cereal, toast, etc. Very friendly and helpful staff in the breakfast room. Go early as it fills up fast and only has about 8-10 tables. Breakfast is from 7-10:30 which is nicer than some that end at 9.
Hotel was immaculate inside and out, very pretty and nicely furnished. We stayed in the rooms that have the king bed in one room with a door and then a couch and chair in the front area that folds out into a bed. Perfect for us since we had one of our children's friends with us. It gave us adults some privacy while changing and sleeping.
Pool is posted that it is only open until 6 but if you ask at the front desk they can keep it open longer for you with no problem. Front desk even let my daughter use their inner tube which was very nice. Pool is not huge but is a nice relief to the heat and is located on the east side of the hotel so it is shaded in the late afternoon.
Staff was great and very accommodating when we needed extra towels, shampoo and conditioner.
Room was clean, neat and had everything we needed. 
Pillows were awful though :( Not sure why but it seems all the Country Inns we have stayed at have the same pillows? Bring your own though, seriously, or you may not sleep well. I am not that picky but these made my head feel like a bowling ball when I laid down. My head sunk all the way to the bottom. Fortunately my husband had brought his from home so I was able to sleep.
Otherwise, I would recommend this to anyone. Plenty of places to eat and shop around it as well as easy on/off of main interstate which made it fast to get to our friends' house.
Jordan was awesome! As was Shaughnessy (I think that was her name?). Shaughnessy was the desk clerk when we checked in and was fabulous. She did tell us all about the Carlton Club and was able to sign us up (it's free) so we could gain points from that stay. I appreciate that since I did not know about it at the hotel we stayed at the previous night. She gave us the option of a 2nd or 3rd floor room and we took the 2nd floor. Heard a little noise from room above (toilets) but otherwise it was quiet.
Jordan was the evening desk manager and was absolutely fabulous at accommodating our extra towel and amenities needs. Very nice and happy to help in any way he could.
We would definitely stay here again when we come back down this way.

The location is fantastic, but above that, the staff at the hotel is extremely warm and friendly. Rooms are big compared to other rooms in NYC. We stayed on the 21st floor and had the most amazing view of Times Square. Again, I can't say enough about it! Clean fabulous rooms with amazing views and a fantastic staff!

The location is great. That is the only good feature here. We thought that this would be a modern boutique hotel. Older building that has been redone on the quick and cheap. Nothing particularly nice about this hotel. The pictures make it seem more modern than it actually is. Mattress was terrible. Woke every morning with pain. Will not stay here again.

Great location for The Alamo and the Riverwalk - and saves you a bundle!!! Clean, nice rooms with full frig, stove, sink and microwave! Wonderful bathroom. Staff is polite and helpful. Variety in hot breakfast a plus.

This Hilton has a very good central location. You can reach by foot the main points of interest of Boston.
For the rest, nothing particular to declare. The Hilton quality : professional staff, functional great rooms (one bedroom suite), ... Of course, no breakfast included. For free internet, you need to go in the lobby (it’s better than nothing). 
In few words : quite good value for money, no surprise.
Breakfast tip : at 0,6 mile, the North Street Grill (229 North Street).

We paid 140 dollars to stay right midtown Manhattan right off 5th Ave and it was one of the nicest hotels I had ever visited. Super clean, super comfortable, staff was super nice and the breakfast was super delicious with a wide variety of choices! Walking distance to EVERYTHING! WOW! Wish I could have stayed longer. This was one of the best deals EVER!!!!!

title_masked: Great hotel in a fantastic location
text_masked:
My husband and I stayed for three nights at the Doubletree Mag Mile in May, 2012. We were very pleased with this hotel. We arrived at 11am and were given access to a room immediately. We stayed on the ninth floor in a room with king bed. The room was a good size and we overlooked the pool area (although the pool was not yet open). We did not hear any street noise at all. The room was clean and the bed was very comfortable. A convenient store is two minutes away from the hotel for bottled water, snacks, beer and wine. 
The location of this hotel is fantastic. 10 minute walk to Navy Pier, five minute walk to the shops on Mag Mile and one evening we walked home from dinner in the financial district (about 30 minutes). We took a cab only once to a restaurant which was too far to walk to (Girl & The Goat which I would HIGHLY recommend - but be sure to make a reservation well in advance), otherwise we walked everywhere.
The conceirge at the hotel was incredibly helpful and the front desk staff were also very pleasant. My only issue with this hotel is that WiFi is not availalbe free of charge in the rooms. It is, however, available in the lobby at no charge. Having said that, the lobby was always quite busy with people sitting around using their laptops, etc.
We enjoyed the Art Institute, Millenium Park, and the architectural boat tour was well worth the money. Chicago is one of my favourite, if not my favourite, cities in the US. There is so much to do and see and luckily for us is a very short flight from Toronto. We went to the House of Blues one evening (our original plan was to go to Kingston Mines in Lincoln Park but we felt like walking instead of taking a cab), so it was great to hear some live Blues.
If you are not from the US and are shopping at Macy's be sure to ask about the visitors card which entitles you to 10% off your purchase on the spot. 
I am looking foward to a return visit to Chicago and I would definitely stay at this hotel again.

title_masked: Great for going to Camden Yards
text_masked: We stayed here the weekend of August 24-26 when we came down for an Orioles game. The location is perfect. We stayed on the 20th floor and could see right into the park. Hotel is also walking distance to the Inner Harbor and M&T Bank Stadium. Concierge level was worth the extra cost for us, free breakfast and snacks kept the expenses down. Parking is on-site, but a little expensive. Didn't need the car as everything is walking distance. My only complaint was the pillows were too wimpy.

title_masked: Great location, but needs some maintenance
text_masked:
My family and I recently stayed at the Residence Inn Charlotte SouthPark for three nights. The hotel is off of a main street, so noise was never an issue. There were plenty of shops and restaurants near the hotel. Also, the hotel was about a 15 minute ride to Uptown Charlotte.
The layout of the room was fine; however there were several maintenance items that needed to be addressed (i.e. running toilet, sitting chair with numerous pin holes in the top, kitchen cabinet doors that would not close, and paint touch ups). The staff was friendly and the breakfast was great. 
Overall, we enjoyed our stay in the area. Hopes that the hotel addresses the maintenance items to be in line with the area of town it is in.

We stayed at this hotel prior to leaving on an Alaskan cruise. The reason I chose this hotel was because they allowed me to leave my auto while we were cruising. My complaints include; a bed that is so high my wife had trouble getting on and a chair that was so low I had trouble getting up. The bathroom was super small and had a tub that was so high that both my wife and I could not get in to take a shower.The shelf had no room to put our toiletries on so we had to leave them in a bag and use them from the bag. And when you shut the bathroom door and sat on the commode their is a full length mirror facing you. I did not like looking at myself while I use the commode.Their was not any listing for the tv channels and I couldn't find anyone that had one. The breakfast is $$$$ and the food did not justify the high prices. The front desk people were super nice My cost for 2 nights at this hotel was $429.16 Definitely not worth this price.

Having to be in Charlotte for my sister's surgery, I choose the Morehead for both its convenient location to the Medical Center and its intimate atmosphere for the week Philomena and Darrin could not have made my trip more pleasant. Each evening when I came back from the hospital they accommodated me in every way possible and comforted me with words of encouragement. I loved the rooms, and the breakfasts fortified me for long days at the hospital. I would highly recommend a stay at the Morehead Inn, nice facility and great people.

Enjoyed a great trip to NYC with two friends. The Warwick is an older hotel but is clean, spacious with great beds. Very quiet too.
For transportation, the NY water taxi is a great way to get out to Statue. If you take the hop on and hop off buses, you go out on Staten Island ferry and lineups can be very long. 
If you're going to Empire State bdlg, go first thing in the morning bc lineups are unbelievably long as the day goes on. Also, the 9/11 Museum isn't technically open until next month but can t see that it will be bc it appears behind schedule. You go to Memorial Museum (still in an adjacent building) and with the $15 entry you get a free pas to the Reflecti Pools which have a timed entry. Again, lineups can be long, but they generally move pretty fast. 
Hop on, hop off buses great.value for $. With freestyle you get 3day ride pass plus 3 attractions or food opportunities. We used them all and they really work slick. 
One feels very safe in Manhattan. Personally I like staying downtown manhattan. Some people say you should stay in Queens or Brooklyn and take subway or Amtrak over. I would never do that bc I'd prefer to spend the extra $ to be right near Broadway. Shows are great.

The Madison is an elegantly appointed and conveniently located boutique hotel gem in the heart of DC. Although I originally had reservations for one night, my sister and I wound up staying there for two nights thanks to an unexpected downpour during our double decker bus tour. Although we'd checked out earlier in the day, the front desk staff were understanding and quickly booked us back into our original room at a great rate. 
The accommodations exceeded my expectations, the staff were gracious and efficient, and the rooms decorated with an eclectic elegance. Also, it was a short and pleasant walk from the Farragut North metro station, if you are so inclined. On my next weekend foray into DC, I will definitely plan to stay here again.

title_masked: Perfect hotel for a short city break - fantastic location
text_masked:
Myself and my friend stayed here for 5 nights in feb/march for a short trip to NYC. We booked a standard room with bed and breakfast. The accommodation was a great price and for a little bit extra we could add breakfast!
The hotel is in a great location - you come out of the doors and turn right to Central Park and left to Times Square! And the subway is literally outside.
The rooms are small (when you sit on the toilet, your knees almost touch the sink), but when you are busy sightseeing all day, all you need is a shower and a bed! The hotel is quite dated with old fashioned decor, but very clean and comfortable.
Breakfast is served in the small cafe attached to the hotel and consists of either a tower of pancakes with syrup and sauces or fried eggs, bacon and re-fried potatoes and veg (bubble and squak) with toast. This comes with an orange juice and tea or coffee. If you are a resident in the hotel they give you a ticket to take into the cafe for a free breakfast, and they turn you around quickly because you wont be spending any money! But they are very polite nonetheless!
The staff were all very helpful and polite and I cant fault the hotel. For what we paid, I was really pleased, it was very good value. I would definitely recommend this hotel for anyone visiting New York for a short trip and would go back again.

Hotel is very clean and staff friendly. Location near time square is great, just a short walk. Only downfall is that it is across from the bus station and near the parole office. There were some people lingering on the street and some sleeping at times, but we never had any issues. Overall it was a positive experience. I would recommend that if you come back late at night, take a cab that will drop you off right in front of the hotel.

title_masked: Clean, Friendly, great location for getting around on transit
text_masked: Stayed here three nights last week with my teenage son. Very clean. Desk staff friendly and helpful. We purchased the three day Muni passes for $21 apiece and were able to catch buses right outside the hotel, and cable cars and trolley cars a few blocks away. It was very convenient location for getting to all the downtown sites, Alcatraz cruise departure pier, Haight Ashbury, and fisherman's wharf. Chinatown and Union Square both walkable from hotel. Complimentary continental breakfast of pastries and fruit included. Requested a quiet room on a high floor as I am a light sleeper. We were on 7th floor, and even so, the evening street noise bothered me. So bring along some earplus. I would recommend to others and definitely stay here again myself.

I have no idea what hotel these people have stayed in although I am quite certain it was NOT this hotel. I have never complained about a hotel although I thought this was a visit to complain about, and for others to know about. When I walked into the hotel it wreaked of carpet fresh. The room had hair on the table and in the refrigerator, as well as food and grime. I cleaned the room from top to bottom, replaced my beddings, sprayed with RidX and still ended up with a rash all over my body, including my hair, and bites all over my arms (from what I could only assume were bed bugs). I requested that my room not be cleaned by the staff, for my first hotel stay EVER! I consider myself a down to earth person and definitely not judgmental for the most part, although this experience has made me realize that I do not ever wish to stay in a hotel that is not of a name that I am familiar with and try to stick with the norm

Pacific Shores Inn is located in the heart of Pacific Beach. Just a 1 minute walk and you are on the sands of the Pacific. 
The hotel has clean rooms and Jim is a great manager. He is willing to help with everything from extra towels to getting cabs if you plan to leave the area. 
The great thing about the location is you can walk to eat / drink or just soak up the sites.
Downtown and Sea World are just minutes away by cab it you want to travel outside the area.
I have stayed many times and this is my place of choice when in San Diego.
Highly recommend this place and will be returning soon.
Thanks to Jim S. 
GB Salt Lake City Utah

After much research we picked this hotel based on Trip Advisor reviews and we were very happy with our selection. The room was large, clean and quiet (I had called ahead and requested a room away from the nightclub noise). We found the staff went way beyond the expected to help us and the location was perfect.
The kitchenette was great for breakfast - we requested a toaster - and there were several reasonable restaurants near by.
A couple notes:
- car rental pickup on O'Farrell is two blocks away;
- Lefty O'Tools is a great sports bar and is 1.5 blocks away;
- you can easily walk to Chinatown/NorthBeach or look into the Bus #35.
- we continued our vacation by renting a car and driving to Monterey along Highway #1. VERY easy from this hotel. One right turn, straight drive to the ocean, and turn left on Hwy#1. Beautiful drive and well worth it. Don't let anyone convince you to take the freeway to Santa Cruz - you will miss it all.

My wife and I went to NYC for her 30th. She's been before and it was my first time. Staff was efficient and accomodating. Facility was clean. Room was clean. View was nice. Water pressure was great (random but important). Bar staff was friendly (for the quick drink we had). Elevators were pretty cool. System was very efficient. Decor was great, especially since my wife is a huge Judy Garland fan.

We stayed 6 nights at the Manhattan Bridge Comfort Inn. The hotel was in a convenient location close to several subways and in Lower East Side. We had a duplex room and were lucky enough to get the corner room so we had views of Manhattan Bridge, Downtown and Lower East Side. The rooms were clean, well equipped and comfortable. The upstairs part of the room was useful to store our suitcases and clothes, otherwise the room would've been a bit cramped. The breakfast buffet was excellent and set us up for the day.
After our stay here we took a coach trip to Niagara Falls which we found out stopped about 2 doors down from the hotel!
Only downside was the wireless didn't work too well on our laptop so we had to use the internet cable. The problem was that the cable provided was very short so you had to use the laptop on the floor when using the internet. I would recommend bringing an extension cable.

title_masked: Good hotel in a convenient location
text_masked: Stayed at this hotel for 1 night in early March. I selected the hotel primarily because it is conveniently located to MSG and Penn Station. The front desk staff was very friendly and accommodating. We really appreciated that they were willing to store our luggage for us both in the morning before we checked in and for a few hours after we checked out the next day. The rooms were clean and in good condition with modern decor. I didn't notice much noise from the street (room was on 11th floor), hallway or adjoining rooms, which was nice. There was a large variety of food options offered at the free breakfast and, even though we went down for breakfast after 9:30am, there was still plenty of food available. My only complaint is that the pillows were not very comfortable. Overall, a really good hotel and I will definitely considering staying here in the future.

We first arrived for a one night stay turned out bad! Our first room was on the 4th floor and the elavator was broke..Then moved to another room where the air conditionor was removed and a window unit was installed...then we went to use the tv and the remote was broke inop..at this point we shut the lights off and went to sleep.
The front desk staff seemed that it was just a job ,they took care of what we needed but felt like we were intruding on their time..
The internet seemed ok and the rooms are tiny,but if it's a one night stay it's very expensive for one night.good luck I myself did not read the reviews on this property and should have ...beware

Room was pretty nice, bed was nice and clean, washroom was big and clean again. Shower was huge. Big TV, lots of space. Right beside the bay w a path to walk along and take in the scenery. Pool was nice also. Deep but not too huge. hot tub was decent.
Overall it was a very good for the price. It was by no means a 5 star place but you should expect that based on the price.
I wouldn't stay there again personally but it was a cool getaway to shelter island and good for the low cost on last minute deal!

The Harborside Inn is a boutique hotel 1 block away from the Rose Kennedy Greenway and ferries to the islands of Boston harbor. The hotel is small & the lobby is undergoing renovation. coffee and computers with printer in the lobby, this is a visitor friendly place. Staff was helpful. the room is compact, with an exposed brick wall and new-appearing contemporary furnishings. Bed was comfortable & the room was very quiet. Bathroom is pretty with a good size shower and gray tile on floor. The only shortcomings are limited space around the sink and no magnifying shave/makeup mirror.

title_masked: Midtown Manhattan - Mid Comfort - Mid Satisfaction
text_masked:
We booked this hotel as we had an additional night to spend in NY on our way back to Europe. The check in clerk was friendly and efficient
The overall deco is a bit bleak and dark
The Pod room we were allocated was very small and dingy
The bathroom was clean and ok stocked
The price we paid was ca. £170 for one night incl. tax
Location is good within easy reach to the Metro Station and Columbus Circle

title_masked: Best stay in a long time.
text_masked: I travel a lot for business and I have had my share of bad experiences. I usually find myself going to my meeting and coming back to the hotel room to sleep without using any of amenities. However this time upon check in I heard the front desk talking to other guests about what the hotel has to offer. Front desk was nice enough to give me a breif history of the hotel and told me I should really go take a look at the hotel. I was so suprised how big and clean the rooms were. After getting settled in I decided to take a tour around the hotel and I was really fasinated with the history and detail in this hotel. I had no trouble getting internet access and this is a huge plus when I work from my laptop. Hopefully I get sent back to San Diego soon..

I did get a good deal for a hotel a stones throw from Lincoln Center and Daniel Boulud's culinary corner, but I would not give it the same rating as say the Essex House.
If you like animal prints and loud techno music, if you are impressed by dark lighting and heavy handed decorating, this is your place. Smoke and mirrors was my takeaway.
The front desk does not seem to know how to accommodate travelers the way any other 4 star hotel does effortlessly. When we returned for a third try to get into our room at 3pm, we had to wait in a long line for half an hour. By the time we got to the counter the bigger better rooms with a real view were gone.
Imagine a queen size bed with a one foot clearance on three sides - that was our room. Imagine sitting sideways on the toilet so your knees don't hit the opposite wall - that was our bathroom. Imagine looking out your window into the window of another room just a few feet away - that was our view. Not luxurious or sophisticated as they advertise, not even charming or cozy. Just really really tiny.
We got a call in the middle of the night from housekeeping - 2AM or so - because they wanted to deliver ice and we didn't answer the door. What? Still wondering what that was about. At about 4AM, the party of what sounded like a dozen loud young hipsters arrived across the hall with doors slamming and shouting for the next 45 minutes. I wonder if Megan ever found her phone.
On the other hand, the location was ideal and the bed was comfortable.

We were very happy to get a really, really good rate in a location like that.
Checked in well past midnight.
When getting ready for going to sleep, we found a dirty sock on the carpet (hardly noticeable because of it being black and the carpet very dark) and then a pair of male underpants in the bathroom. On the towel rack, underneath a fresh towel...
As it was in the middle of the night by then we didn't bother calling anyone. When we wanted to go to bed though, one of the beds didn't have a duvet. So I called reception and told them about the underwear as well as the missing duvet.
The underwear didn't get much of a comment, but he did get housekeeping to come re the duvet. They turned up quickly, but with a duvet for a double instead of a single bed and one that looked like it had seen better days and was very heavy. 
We asked the guy to go and strip a bed in an other room which he refused to do. So we asked for a woolen blankets which he went to fetch, huffing and puffing though.
No mention of the underwear.
In the morning I went down to the lobby and spoke to a member of staff who was very apologetic and organised free breakfast for us.
So overall, if you can get a good rate, go for it, the location is prime. Would probably stay again if I got a good enough deal.

The "Hip" Belmont is no San Jose (in Austin TX). It was totally overrated and over -hyped! The deluxe (rooms ) are really (motel) small with tiny bathrooms and window air conditioners which were attached to wire extentions in the Bathroom ( is that a code violation??/). The water in the taps was SCALDING !!! ( Which we were informed was due to the copper water pipes. Admittedly it was over 105% in Dallas on August 35rg 2012 but come on how does that account for the smug establishment to brush aside the complaint with a lame excuse of it being a hot day?
What are they charging high rates for and why the qualify to be on the Tablet Hotels list is a mystery. The upside? The much advertised views of downtown Dallas. I give them that. Not staying there again . Oh yes and the neighbourhood is seedy to say the least.

title_masked: Lovely Hotel for a Fraction of the Price
text_masked: My boyfriend and I stayed at this hotel that is very convenient to Union Station and the Capitol. The price was very low (under $100 per night) so we were kind of afraid of what we were going to get, but we had a huge room that overlooked the glass mezzanine. There was a 40" flat screen tv, two arm chairs, and a foot stool. It was a pleasant and welcome surprise.

I traveled alone to LA and had booked this hotel. After reading some of the reviews I got really scared. But the room was very clean and the staff really nice!!
I was on the 9th floor.
It's a great location and good price.
There are 2 metro stations really close and also a lot of bar and restaurants.

After I checked into the hotel, I took the elevator to the 25th floor. When I got off the elevator I found a naked man on top of a screaming woman. I got the man off of the woman. I then found myself standing between a crying woman and a naked man. After a few moments she headed for the stairs. I told the man to get in his room, but he had no key. I called security and they came and took him to his room. I was later told by security that the man taken a prostitute to his room and she had taken his money ($150). He chased her into the hallway and tackled her. This is not what I expected at the InterContinental Hotel. When I complained about what I observed and had to do I was told, "Welcome to the hotel business." Since I was a paying guest, I thought this was an inappropriate response. 
I travel on business frequently and won't be returning.

Our room was clean & comfortable (AC was perfect). The bed was FANTASTIC (so soft & comfy)! The only issue we had with the hotel stay was the renovation that was taking place in the room above us at 8am. We heard a clang, clang, clang that made us worry someone was beating on a wall for help. The hotel staff was very nice & most helpful when we asked for ideas for things to do in the area. The front lobby was nice & the internet access was good.

We took the train into Chicago to enjoy a weekend of sightseeing, shopping and family time. We booked a room with 2 queen beds at the Hotel 71. Our 11th floor room overlooked the river and also had incredible views of the Magnificent Mile. We arrived early and the staff was more than willing to see if they could check us in early, which they were able to do. The room was spacious and included a large bath with 2 separate sinks and an adjacent room with large bathtub, walkin shower and stool. The bedroom was spacious with the two beds, desk and chair/couch sitting area. It was a short walk to the Metra station as well as to several shops and dining establishments. We would look no further than the Hotel 71 for our next Chicago run.

title_masked: First time visitor who WILL come back again and again!
text_masked: Having never been to this hotel I didn't know what to expect. There wasn't a king size bed available for my wife and I but the room was awesome and the view was even better! The two full size beds were very satisfactory. The staff were helpful, professional, courteous and on top of their game from check-in to check-out. The area around the hotel was clean and pleasant to be around. The restaurant was one of the best I have been in in any of the hotels I have been in throughout my life. The buffet style breakfast was THEE BEST I have ever had and the food selection was unbelievable. I recommend this hotel for any professional stay, recreation stay or if you are just looking for somewhere to go to get away for a enjoyable weekend.
Very helpful hotel staff and very nice stay. I really appreciated the staff being so accommodating about my Living Social Coupon.

I stayed at the Westin Times Square while on a week vacation in NYC in August 2012. My experience and recommendation can be described by the below:
Location
The hotel is definitely at one of the best locations you can stay at in NYC. Located in the heart of midtown it is exactly at times square with all major attractions and entertainment facilities located in a radius of 2 to 3 blocks: 5th avenue for example is only 3 blocks away while avenue of the Americas is 2 blocks down. 
As soon as you step out of the main entrance, you are on 8th avenue, 43rd street just seconds away form a variety of restaurants and bistros from all around the world. (Shake Shack is just in front....just cross the road).
Furthermore, the hotel is at really close distance from all artistic attractions of Broadway. the Minksof theater where Lion King is playing is just two blocks ahead and all other theaters at a walking distance. The Intrepid museum is on 12th avenue accessible on foot or 5 minutes by cab including the NYC traffic.
The hotel really has one of the best locations to be in while "touristing" in NYC.
Hotel and rooms
The building is really nice both on the outside and on the inside. Main entrance on 8th avenue is lavish and holds the security and baggage claim desks. A large escalator takes you all the way up to a grand front desk and concierge services as well as a really cozy and elegant seating area. The experience starts really well at the hotel the minute you step inside the lobby.
The hotel also has another entrance from 42nd street which is equally nice.
Rooms are quite large and very well decorated. I was in a two double bed that was very spacious and really comfortable. It was on the 24th floor boasting a great view on the Hudson river and the surrounding area. The bathroom is neatly decorated and equipped with all services you would expect.
The only drawback is that on some floors the halls are a little complex and intertwine with one another. Halls are all greyish so some light or colors might make things look way better. But it is not a note that will push you away from the hotel, it is just a small note I picked up while there.
Service
Service at the Westin can't be described by nothing other than just perfect. You are greeted with a beautiful smile that makes you feel welcome every single step of the way. I would like to extend the best compliments to "Sarah" at front desk who was just wonderful in making the check in process one of a kind knowing that my room was not available at time of check in. She was really great in the way she reassured me and greeted me at the premises. I truly recommend that you ask for her if you check in at the Westin.
As for room service and house keeping, they are also very nice. I have been provided with all my requests and more by really great personnel who never refrained from being there whenever they were needed.
Security and bell boys are extremely helpful, they were great in helping me with directions and booking of cars and taxis. 
Service at the Westin is one of the best I have ever experienced in a high end hotel 
Prices
Well to be honest it is not a cheap hotel. I ended up paying USD 370 a night and that was a discounted rate. But I think it is a perfectly explained price for such a hotel, location and time of the year (high season). It is really worth every penny.
I strongly recommend the Westin times Square for your next stay in NYC.

We enjoyed our stay at this hotel. The lobby was finally finished on Saturday 14th April. We had a refurbished room which was nicely decorated with a bit of colour. The hotel had free internet. Although there was three of us, the complimentary breakfast was only for two. A bit odd. 
Our maid "Amy" was particularly welcoming and left a lovely note when after we had left a tip.
Fishermans Wharf and Pier 39 were only minutes away as was the "F" route street car.

The decor of the room was nice and contemporary. But if you look close the room was not cleaned very well. The A/C control looked like there were boogers or something stuck on it. The door jams of the bathroom door and room door has finger prints/marks. Light switches also were gross and had build up of dirt and grime over the years. The blow dryer also had gross markings all over it. I felt very dirty staying here but I had no choice and was very glad it was only for one night. I was in room 701. 
If management is reading this review, please retrain your cleaners. Or at least inspect their work.

My sister and I stayed at the Homewood Suites last week while visiting Chicago. The hotel is clean, the complimentary breakfasts and weeknight dinners and other amenitites are very nice, but I have to say the staff at this hotel is the friendliest and most accomodating of any staff I've encountered at a hotel, especially Noah, who we encountered upon entering the hotel our first day in the city. Doors were held open for us each time we entered and excited the hotel, we were asked how our days were upon entering the hotel in the late afternoon (and I felt the question was genuine) and the dining staff were always very pleasant and re-stocked food right away and cleared dishes from our table very efficiently. One staff member even offered to bring us additional beverages so that we would not have to leave our table, when this clearly was not his job. Kudos to this hotel for hiring and maintaining such wonderful staff members!! They made our stay so welcoming, and I've already recommended it to family members and friends who plan to travel to Chicago in the near future.

title_masked: Don't be fooled by the pictures
text_masked: I booked this on Priceline and thought I was getting a great deal on a cute hotel....when we arrive after a full day at Seaword we find out that we have to pay $22 to valet park or find street parking, really at 9:30 pm on a Saturday. We booked a room for 2 adults and a child, when we get to our room we have one queen bed for all three of us, we were forced to sleep crammed in one bed. This place reminds of a refurbished motel, that was badly done. So small even my 8 year old asked us why the room was soo small. We way over paid.

I chose this hotel based on other Trip Advisor reviews - and its proximity to my neice's home in Ballard. I was very pleasantly surprised. The hotel seems to have been refurbished very recently - or is extremely well maintained. I got a generous two-room suite at a highway motel price. Extremely comfortable. Excellent service. And there IS free parking - but the garage is small. Best to get parked before evening. I have already recommended this place to others.

title_masked: Less than great location but nice hotel!
text_masked:
We really didn't like the location, but it turned out okay as their shuttle bus was convenient and quick. 
The staff was excellent, and the adjoining restaurant--Jimmy's on broadway--was great. 
We were pleased with our room and with the parking. The parking levels were brightly lit and secure.
Nice hotel great service. The bed was comfortable and staff was very friendly. I will return! This Hotel is also very clean.

I don't usually leave reviews but recently left my first negative review on a hotel. I decided I should start leaving reviews for the excellent stays too. This hotel is definitely one of them. It is located out by the Denver Airport - not much around except other hotels - sort of a bunch of hotels in the middle of nowhere. The suites are very nice. There is a stove, microwave, fridge (full size) and dishwasher, as well as two tvs - one in the bedroom and one in the living area. The staff was very friendly. Someone else commented on the lack of a store. There is a Ruby Tuesdays within walking distance, as well as an Italian restaurant. Also, if you have a car, about 3 miles down, there is a large grocery store with about everything you could need. We were very impressed when even the cleaning staff stopped and welcomed us. It seems as though the employees enjoy working at the hotel and pass that positive feeling to the guests. The hotel is very clean, quiet, and well maintained. This hotel provided an excellent stay. No complaints at all. We would definitely recommend it. Thank you!

Did an overnight in Downtown Boston. This location was ideal, for walking to all our destinations. Parking a bit steep @ 40Buks, but that is big city parking for you. Room was very clean, hot Chocolate Chip Cookies on arrival. Subway/Orange Line right across the street. Price was very reasonable compared to other hotels in the area. Chinatown, Theater district all in the area within blocks.

title_masked: A nice experience at the W Chicago - City Center
text_masked: While in Chicago for a wedding recently, we had the chance to stay at the W Chicago - City Center. Overall the experience was very positive. The hotel has a distinct decor and flavor that is very different from some of the other traditional high-end hotels I have stayed at recently. The lobby had a upbeat and artistic design that was reflected by the rooms at the W. Our rooms was well appointed with unique decor and lighting. I am not sure what the exact title for the room was, but it was a standard double room with two full size beds. Plenty of room in this room with space to move about. Beds were very comfortable, although I can never figure out why hotels insist on putting full size beds in a room when they could certainly have queen size beds in the room -- other than an attempt to make more money. Aside from that minor issue, the rooms were clean and an excellent place to stay in downtown Chicago. The location is very close to the Willis Tower (can't we just call it the Sears Tower to avoid my aged confusion, please), State Street, Michigan Ave. and the Chicago train stations. Area around the hotel seemed to be very safe during the daytime and it is well served by cabs and other public transportation. Parking was a bit expensive...but I guess this is downtown Chicago, so one should expect that type of extra fee. Would definitely consider staying here again in the future.

Not only was the overall value the best in the city, the Paramount hotel saved me and my friends from hurricane Sandy! I would like to mention two front desk employees in particular that were absolutely fantastic, Crystal and Kathy. Amidst the chaos due to the severe conditions of the storm, they both remained extremely courteous and composed. The cleaning staff was also very friendly and accommodating especially considering that the hotel was at capacity.
I highly recommend a stay at the Paramount!

Walking distance to eateries. Nice clean room with Aveda products. We had the jacuzzi room. Parking is pricey but there is parking nearby if you will be staying for a few days. Staff was friendly. Pet friendly!

Cool and sleek. We even had a boy band staying at the hotel and endured the screaming preteen girls outside. Hotel did a nice job controlling the crowd and remembered that we were actual guests at the hotel. Upgraded to suite so had plenty of room. Bathroom was oddly tiny for such a large room with zero counter space. Great neighborhood. Valet parking is 35 a day but they were very good. You don't go to LA expecting a bargain trip.

title_masked: Big hotel, but never felt overwhelmed
text_masked:
The Manchester Grand is one of those hotels that attendees to conventions in San Diego often find themselves. It was a nice hotel, with clean rooms that are even a bit stylish, good beds, well-functioning internet service and a convenient location.
The hotel is made of two large towers, and however I did not feel overwhelmed by the hotel. It has a majestic lobby, and the rooms and hallways, while not as gorgeously appointed are nevertheless pleasing. I did not have an opportunity to use the pool, but it looked fantastic.
My one complaint would be the rather limited selection of restaurants within the hotel, although immediately outside toward the water are several other restaurants.
Overall- a very nice hotel, and I would not mind returning in the future.

One of the best all around lodging experiences I have ever had. We stayed here for five nights and we could easily have stayed a month. The Steinhart balances apartment-style living with hotel convenience at a very affordable rate. Our suite of rooms at the back of this venerable building on the 4th floor was quiet, stylish, and spotlessly clean. We had four large rooms, including full kitchen, dining room, living room and bath. This all for about $200. per night. Although the hotel does not have a cafe, room service or other conventional amenities, the immediate neighborhood offers these services in abundance. Turn right and there's a well stocked market; turn left and find Cup a Joe, a wonderful urban coffee shop/cafe. The location boasts easy access to tourist enclaves like Union Square and authentic residential settings like Pacific Heights, or you can trek through the panhandlers of the Tenderloin to SOMA. Rent a car around the corner at Hertz for $40.00 per day, all in. 
The kitchen had everything we needed although we mercifully ate most meals out. Wireless was free and though the two large flat screens are not high def, they have tons of offerings. The wire cage elevator is fun and there are two set of stairs that anchor the wide, pleasant central hallway.
Maid service is once a week, but the suite was well stocked and we'd rather have the privacy.

title_masked: Staff goes out of their way to help you
text_masked: I was one of the last guests to arrive and they didn't have any more room in the valet parking - there was an event going on at the hotel. I was a little concerned about parking in an overnight parking and walking back alone. One of the desk clerks offered to drive with me to the lot and walk back with me. Then another employee overheard our conversation and offered to park my car on the street in front of the hotel because he knew that one of the guests at the event would be leaving after the event and that spot for parking would be available.

title_masked: Better than expected for a "freeway" hotel...
text_masked:
When our sponsor told us they had booked a Marriott out on the east side of Indy for our conference I was not overly excited. I've spent some time in Indy and have come to feel downtown is the place to be. But, I have to say I was pleasantly surprised.
This hotel was renovated about three years ago and now features two different sleeping room areas as well as a conference center. In addition it has a wonderful, huge outdoor patio area. We were there in March but caught the warm spell and the patio made for a nice place to sit at the end of the day.
Sleeping rooms were what you would expect these days - good beds, good bathrooms, flat screen TVs. Thanks to the upgrades places like Hampton Inn and Holiday Inn Express did a few years ago the "big boys" have been forced to follow suit. 
The fitness room is adequate but I'd suggest your iPod and a head set. They have three or four TVs around the room and when I was in there folks were watching different channels and it was confusing. There are some weight machines, enough to get an OK workout in.
The real highlight for us was the restaurant. At first glance, you might be tempted to just have a drink at the long bar and go somewhere else for dinner. That would be a mistake. The restaurant/bar is a big open area that's a part of the lobby, which a huge, cool fireplace blocking it from the front door. We were going to have a drink, then go somewhere else but decided it was late and we were tired so decided to eat at the hotel, not expecting much.
Wrong. I got a 500-calorie dish on the wait staff's recommendation. Normally I'd be highly suspect of a 500-calorie entree. But, in this case it was excellent. It was a pasta-based dish with veggies, chicken chunks and a low cal sauce and It was good enough I'd order it again. One of our folks got a filet mignon he said was "awesome." In fact, the next night we went to the fabled St. Elmo's Steakhouse downtown and when we were leaving he said "I think my steak at the Marriott was just as good."
I'd also give this place solid marks for staff. Everyone one we dealt with was attentive and we appreciated the service we got from the folks involved in the meeting room setup. 
Be advised this hotel is a hike from the airport so you will need a cab or rent car. I'd suggest a rent car if you are going to be there more than one night and want to sample other restaurants or clubs in Indy. It's only about a 10-12 minute drive to downtown, depending on traffic.

This is such a pretty hotel. The lobby area is gorgeous. The service is very friendly and helpful. The location is terrific-right on the Riverwalk. I enjoyed having breakfast outside looking at the activity on the River. My room was very comfortable and spacious.
One issue-make sure you do not have a room facing the street/parking lot-it is extremely noisy. Request a room facing the river.

For a recent business trip to NY, one of my colleagues recommended this hotel as he always stays here. The location is great if you are a tourist, and happily was within a short walk of the client I was visiting. Having checked in during the evening and out again at 7:30am, I can't really comment on the facilities. However, there was no room service menu in my room, no hotel facilities directory and no breakfast card. This would have annoyed me if I had been staying longer.
The room was quite small, but the bathroom was well appointed and the shower was great. I'd stay here again on business, but wouldn't take my husband as he likes to have a bath as well as a shower.

title_masked: Stay at this hotel but skip breakfast
text_masked:
You can't really fault the rooms at Chambers - spacious for NY standards, amazing showers, comfortable beds, quiet rooms, great minibar etc. The entrance hall is very chic and you are welcomed with a fireplace and a free drink. Staff were all charming and eager to help. I had forgotten half of my wash kit but they had everything that I needed for me in my room within 5 minutes of calling housekeeping.
I didn't really rate the breakfast at all (I went once and then went out the other days.) Breakfast is served in the actual bar, so you're surrounded by alcohol. There are only a few tables so you most people have to sit up at the bar. There aren't any freshly squeezed juices (which you'd expect in a 5 star hotel) and limited healthy options. All in all breakfast felt a bit amateur.

I have stayed at the Hampton Inn and Suites Shady Grove twice now while in Memphis on business. The service is Outstanding!! This second time around I was placed into one of the "model rooms" which happened to be the Hampton by Hilton room; what a treat!

Stayed here two nights and had no problems. Good location in a safe area and close to the airport. Resturants were close by. Mamagement was very nice. I stayat sleep inns al the time and this was a little better than the average Sleep Inn.

Stayed at this Marriott the night before we flew out for vacation. Very convenient to Midway airport. The hotel was nice and the staff was very helpful. This hotel is grouped with several others that seem to share a shuttle to Midway, but other than that cluster of hotels, the area around Midway is really nothing to write home about. Great place to stay if need something close to Midway Airport.

title_masked: An exciting affordable hotel in the heart of Manhattan
text_masked:
I was in need to check into a hotel after an unfortunate planned accommodation had to change... I booked the hotel at 12:00 noon and got there an hour later.
WOW what a hotel, I kept checking again and again that the price is really 270$ for two nights. and it really was. Very affordable compared to other hotels I have been seeing while trying to search for one.
At 15:00 my room was ready. The room is VERY small but I am used to European hotels. it is beautifully designed, the shower is transparent to the bed area, but could be hidden if it bothers anyone.
Walls are a little thin and i could hear a lot of the noise my neighbours were doing. but not a big deal, I have no problem to sleep in little noise.
A glass of Chardonnay at the bar downstairs was unreasonably pricey- 16$!!!
Aside from that - service was at a very high level. Definitely going to try and find a cheap deal like that again.

title_masked: Great views of Central Park and located close to all Midtown things
text_masked:
A half block from the subway, two blocks from Central park, 5 short blocks from Times Square.....I cant think of a better location to get to do all the things we have learned to love about New York
The Hotel being an SPG lodging means a lot for us as I just used points to upgrade to a wonderful view of Central Park. The people inside make the stay enjoyable and the Burger Joint gives a person hunger pains the minute we walked in for check in
We will stay here again soon

title_masked: If you want something cheap and out dated this is your place
text_masked: The place is in a time warp from the 80's. It is a funky place but it works if you are going to the Fillmore to see a show and do not want to deal with a cab after the show this is one of the places to look at. Our room was clean but it definitely showed signs of wear and tear. Nest time I think I will pay $30 more and stay downtown and get a place with breakfast.

We stayed in this hotel 3 weeks ago and I have to say the staff are the worst I ever encountered. Am i asking too much for a thank you, how are you ? etc? Every staff memeber we met bar one was rude and in no way friendly. 
The bar menu for what you get is over priced and the quality of the food is not great. We eat there once and decided not to again..
Yes the hotel is located in a very good location but after that there isnt really any positives. it seems the motto is try to get as much money from the guest as possible while showing them as little respect as possible! Overall we spent 3 days there and I must say it was a major disappointment. If you are going for a romantic break then avoid this hotel !!

My wife and I got married on Marriage Island right outside of Hotel Contessa on the Riverwalk and booked a room for that night. We were just looking for a place to stay but quickly found out it would be much more than expected. The wedding was one night after the lighting of the river (a very busy time.) Even considering that the service was amazing, the room was clean, and everyone was very friendly. We were so impressed, Hotel Contessa has become the hotel we choose for any future stays on the Riverwalk!

I debated whether to give this hotel 1 or 2 stars. I decided 1 because it was such a horrible experience all together. The hotel itself was decent, looked promising from entry. Service was good. Then it all fell apart upon entering our room. Room was clean, but the weirdest setup. First, our view was on top of the roof (2nd floor) of the air units. Wonderful. Second, the tv. Why in the world did they put it on the side of the bed. Impossible to watch comfortably. Didn't make any sense either because the bed would have been fine on the wall facing the tv. Room was small, but not too bad. Just the use of the space was silly. Bathroom was small. Then the most important part, the bed. It did not seem to be a king size bed, felt smaller. They had some kind of cheap mattress pad under the sheets that did not even cover the whole bed, and everytime my husband or i moved, it woke the other up the bed was so thin and horrible. Neither one of us slept all night. Also, for allergy sufferers, my throat swelled up immediately upon entry and is just now returning to normal. This is by far the worst experience i have ever had in a hotel room. My first stay at a Marriott will be my last one.

We only stayed one night but it was a very pleasant experience. The staff was outstanding. Enjoyed the roof-top pool and hot tub. The rooms were spacious and very clean. Will certainly look into staying here again on my next trip to LA.

We live in Los Angeles and wanted to celebrate a very special occassion last Saturday night away from home. We are so grateful to have taken the chance at this hotel that is in our own back yard! I spoke with Chelsea when making the reservation about the specialness of our stary and she went above and beyond for us. The stay was memorable in so many ways but Chelsea's efforts brought it to another level. The hotel is modern yet sexy. I was so pleasantly surprised. We will continue to send our family and friends to Custom and we will definitely come back and celebrate other 'special' anniversaries here. Thank you Chelsea!

title_masked: Put a stay in "The Rock Star Suite" on your bucket list!
text_masked: It was amazing! We had an intimate celebration with friends in this suite, as well as spending the night. It's the ultimate. From the skyline view from the balcony to the mind blowing decor - don't miss this one when over the top entertaining demanded in your planning. The staff is always ready and available for your requests.

title_masked: perfect stay in an excellent city
text_masked: very stylish hotel * perfect location * friendly staff * free lavazza-coffee and w-lan * big tv-screen with a lot of chanels * bed with interessing features * party if you want to...

Service is outstanding from when you first hit the property. The rooms were very comfortable. The furnishings were modern but still managed to keep the room light, thanks to the huge picture windows. The restaurants were excellent. The staff handling the conference services were great. 
One tip, if you plan to order food to your room, don't bother with the in room menus. They will deliver anything from the main hotel restaurant.

Although some of the Ritz Carlton properties in large cities can be disappointing, the Boston Ritz experience was outstanding. Great service, great restaurant, beautiful room. Add an exceptional location, and you will certainly enjoy your stay. Not cheap---but worth it.
It was a good experience stayed 1 night. Suites work wll for us. Just iwsh we had 2 bathrooms - would have been easier with the grandchilfren. Breafast was great!

Boutique Downtown Hotel with charming Lobby. I stayed at this hotel for 2 nights. Located with blocks from 16th street mall and tons of restaurants. Pet Friendly. Great Staff. 
Wonderful Panzano Restaurant (Yumm) Must visit.. Price is right.. Loved it.. 
And the Spa was awesome 
The evening reception with 5 minute back massage was perfecto

Needed a room quick as the flights were overbooked and we were unable to get home. Called the hotel from the airport 'Hot Line" in the baggage area, and within 15 minutes the shuttle driver Cheree (sp) was there with a smile and the friendliest demeanor I've ever had the pleasure of meeting. She told us the best place to eat for and even mentioned that she would be happy to shuttle us there and back to the hotel, which she did with even more smiles. The front desk clerk was also just as nice and made us feel better about having to spend an additional night in JAX. The room was clean, the bed was soft and although we were out early the next morning, I'd come back to this hotel in a minute. What a fantastic duo they have taking care of their customers!

Stayed here as part of a multi centre holiday .Had a room with 2 double beds overlooking the courtyard. It was very quiet, very clean and with all the amenities you could wish for . It wasn't a big room but perfectly fine for 2 ladies with lots of bits and bobs ! Very tasteful furnishings and the mirrored wall behind the beds gave it a spacious feel . All the staff we encountered were very friendly and very helpful . We were given vouchers for complimentary continental breakfast in the adjoining restaurant every day which was a nice surprise . The location is perfect - two blocks away from Fishermans walk - we actually walked everywhere , to Chinatown , Union Square , Lombard Street , Alcatraz Pier , Coit tower , Ghiraldelli Square ,ideal for tourists like us . We only managed to attend the complimentary wine reception once , but it was very lively and sociable ( and the staff were very generous with the wine ! ) Once we'd checked out it was just a very short walk to pick up our Hertz hire car for our onward journey .All in all we were very pleased with the Tuscan Inn .

We stayed several nights and experienced perfect service. The bed/pillows led to a wonderful sleep. We were on a high floor and experienced no street noise. We ordered breakfast several mornings, which arrived quickly and was delicious. The hotel is centrally located and was close to the convention center, and we left without any complaints.
Our one negative had to do with bookings.com, which didn't allow us to cancel, well in advance, one night's stay, which we had to pay for. We were told that we could cancel only the whole reservation, and since the hotel was full, we wouldn't be able to re-book. However, the hotel allowed our son to use the room that morning after his arrival in D.C. on the red-eye. We will definitely stay there again but will book the reservation elsewhere.

Stayed at the JW Marriott Chicago for business. Beautiful lobby, very expansive. Rooms were nice and spacious, but the view was other rooms on the property ('inside view'). Had breakfast at the Florentine, which was decent, but priced like any other hotel restaurant. Valet parking was expensive ($55/day). Meeting rooms/facilities were decent.
Very friendly staff, especially the breakfast ladies. Good location if you want the bustle of the Times square Area.

Attending conference with colleagues here and many said they wish they could stay indefinitely. The day before my checkout at near 5 pm I received a call from the Asst Manager. She asked me to give her a time that I was going to vacate the room. I told her early tomorrow. She told me I needed to move now. Clearly there was a mix up. They were of no help getting another room. I found this most unusual for this quality hotel. I honestly don't know whose fault it was but I've rarely stayed in a hotel where the manager was so unhelpful. I found a hotel nearby with help of colleagues. The cab ride was $15 plus they charged me half a day for leaving late.
Great balconies over the water. Active bar. Great rooms and robes. The manager appeared to be an attractive young woman in her 20s who was pleasant but remarkably unhelpful.
Very comfy bed and a nice continetal breakfast. Clean rooms but no refridg. or microwave. Also no place to hang clothes. Fine for a short stay only. Overall not bad.

title_masked: Wonderful hotel in a great location!
text_masked: This was our first trip to NYC and so glad we stayed at the Flatiron! The Toshi Corner Suites are so roomy and bathrooms are great. The hotel staff was so helpful, especially Steven and Alex. Steven suggested a great steakhouse for my daughter's 18th birthday dinner(Steak Frites) & helped us order tickets for 9/11 memorial. Great midtown location! Can't wait to visit NYC again and stay at the Flatiron. I have already recommended this hotel to friends who will traveling to NYC this summer.

title_masked: It Doesn't Get Better Than This.
text_masked:
First class property with a location to match the quality of its rooms, atmosphere and food. Very clean, very classy, elegant hotel almost on the top of Nob Hill at the intersection of two cable car lines (Powell and California). The rooms aren't big, but they are well appointed with a work area (including a safe in the middle drawer - Thank You!), easy chair, table, chest of drawers (with an honor bar no less) and a bed table. King size bed with clean linens with a sufficient number of decorative and useful pillows. (I hate hotels that give me 7/8 pillows that, when taken off the bed, take up a third of the room.) Bathroom was clean with a pocket door separating the bath/toilet and the sink closet area. The closet was an open area in the bathroom, which I prefer, but may be difficult for those that feel they need to hide stuff. Bar was great with excellent food and a great wine list. The Happy Hour wine was a Malbec, in California no less. Club level was very good,but on this visit, breakfast was a bit crowded.
All in all, this was probably the best hotel i stayed in all year.

It was my first time in San Diego, and I liked it immediately. Nice little city, friendly folks. La Jolla is not far from the downtown area, and was a really nice (if a little posh) beach community. The Hyatt itself is not near the beach, but it's within a short drive away. The view of the ocean from La Jolla Village was breathtaking. 
The hotel was nice, if somewhat dark and nondescript. The room had a very comfortable bed, one of the best beds I've ever slept on. The sheets were super soft and cool, and the pillows were just right: not too soft, not too hard. I was surprised that there was no fridge in the room, though. When I'm on a business trips, I like to stock up a little milk and some fruits, so a fridge would have been nice.
The only problem was with the bill. There were some items that were wrongly added, and it took a few calls to get it rectified.
All, in all, one of the better business hotels I've stayed at.

I shared a bunk bed room with my daughter for 3 nights and was quite impressed. The room was a bit like being on a cruise ship but when I'm in NYC I don't spend any time in my room other than to sleep, shower and change clothes. Our room had a sink and each bed had it's own tv. There were several bathrooms to use, and we felt like we were the only ones using the one across the hall from our room. The shower was marble, large and extremely clean. There was an option to turn on shower heads that hit you at mid body in addition to, or instead of, the overhead shower. I loved this because I don't wash my hair every time I shower. The location was perfect - 2 short blocks to subway. The lobby has a place to purchase very reasonably priced snacks, wine, etc and you don't feel like you are at a bargain hotel. They have a helpful concierge to take care of your questions and it is clean, clean, clean with comfortable beds. We paid $310 for 3 nights. You can't beat that.

arrived 11/24, checked out 11/25. dirty room, musty smelly room. air or heat was noisy. live insects on the bathroom floor. dirty floor under bathroom sink. requested a 5:10 am wake up call when we checked in on novenber 24th, luckily we got up early enough to make our flight, did not get a wake up call. this is another fine example of a overrated hotel in the priceline system.
dont waste your money.

We stayed here for a week in June 2011, and since that was a great experience, we just stayed for another week in April 2012. We were not disappointed! The hotel staff really cares about your needs - just let them know! We were given a great room upgrade by Toral, and she had to work really hard to "make it work" - but she did it all the same! THANK YOU, TORAL!! There is a microwave, a fairly large mini-frideg, and an in-room safe! I do agree with some of the other reviewers who wrote that some of the furniture needs an upgrade - it does, but that is happening floor by floor, and should be completed soon. But the beds - very importantly - are the same wonderful beds for which the Hampton Inns across the nation are famous. Maria and her friendly staff make sure you are well fed at breakfast. THANK YOU, MARIA! Jeffrey, at the reception desk, helps make sure you have a smile whenever you walk by. On to the great location - right across the street from a bus stop and two blocks away from a Metro station. If you will order a "Smart Card" from the D.C. website, you can load the card with however much money you think you will need (we ordered two $30 cards) which will take care of all your transportation needs - it can be used on the Circulator (costs just $1.00 a ride - even all the way to Georgetown), the busses, and the Metro. SO EASY! We rode the "yellow line" Metro in from the airport and saved BIG BUCKS on a taxi. I was a bit skitterish about riding the metro in with suitcases, but it was easy, fast and I felt safe the entire time. We took the "green" Circulator route to the Woodland Park Zoo. That was easy, and only cost $2.00 roundtrip! We also took the "red" Circulator to Georgetown for a fun day of shopping and eating! We had a great meal at Old Glory Barbecue in Georgetown. We rode the yellow line Metro to Alexandria. Great shopping and dining there as well! If you use your Smart Card and fearlessly use the public transportation available in D.C. and the surrounding areas, you can see soooo much in a city WORTH exploring - and do it all knowing you will come "home" to the Hampton and be treated like family. They'll even have free warm cookies and lemonade for you to start your evening off right!! You'll be happy you booked your D.C. vacation here!! We'll be back!

Cannot complain at the price offered through Travel Zoo. We arrived to discover an enormous generator running full throttle outside. Unfortunately the hotel had received a power cut a few days prior which had yet to be fixed. Our room was on the top floor above the generator, so not much sleep for us, after walking all over Boston that day. An older hotel with charm and friendly staff, and an overpowering smell of cleaning fragrance in the entry foyer. Our bed was very firm to sleep on along with the pillows. No give or take there. We overslept, so ate breakfast around the corner at Dunkin' Donuts.

Great first impression, which lasted throughout our three-night stay. We arrived at the hotel early in the morning from the airport and weren't expecting to check in. We were just asking at the front desk if we could store our luggage. However, we were told that a room was available and that we were welcome to check in early. Thank you!
The hotel is very large and kind of cold in a sci fi/"city of the future" way (with its glass elevators and tremendous abstract sculpture in the lobby), but the staff was amazingly warm-hearted and helpful, starting with the woman at the front desk. I'd like to compliment the concierge, too, who gave us clear, patient, and excellent advice on how to get around on public transportation. 
The room was basic but extremely quiet. I usually don't sleep well in hotels, but the bed was very comfortable. The showerhead was so strong and soothing that I could have stayed in there all day, but that's not way I came to San Francisco. I wanted to get out and experience the city! 
The waterfront location was excellent for doing just that. We walked along the Embacadero every evening, walked to Chinatown and Little Italy. We hopped on the BART right outside the front door to ride straight to the Oakland Coliseum for a baseball game. We caught the #5 bus about a half-block from the hotel and rode straight to Golden Gate Park and the fabulous science museum.
At $160+/night (my wife was here for a convention and got the convention rate), the room wasn't cheap, but this is San Francisco. Go ahead and splurge on the buffet breakfast in the lobby ($25) if you want, but the Ferry Building Marketplace is right across the street on the waterfront with plenty of cheaper options. And what better way to start your day than to bring your coffee out the back door of the Marketplace and enjoy it with beautiful views of the bay and Bay Bridge.
Overall we had a great time at this hotel and highly recommend it.
my room did have any towels or soap or plug in for lap top they did not bring my towels I had to dress and go get them.

title_masked: Great Hotel and a Great Team of Employees
text_masked: The Hotel Four Points By Sheraton located at the Philadelphia Airport was a refuge for me following Huricane Sandy. All of the Front Desk Staff was very caring and very friendly. The Room was first rate with a comfortable bed very well suited for a Business Traveler. The Hotel Team performed more like a Resort Staff rather than a Hotel Airport Staff. They seemed to go out of their way to insure my stay was first rate. I would like to point out Annette and Fran who daily asked how I was doing and how I was getting along after the Hurricane. The hotel is of course very close to the Philadelphia Airport with Free Shuttle Service for Pick Up and Drop Off to the Airport Departures. Since my Car was a victim of Hurricane Sandy I relied Heavily on the public transportation. The Philadelphia Septa Train at the Airport is very convenient and can has drop offs to Philadelpha 30th Street Station and from there I could take another Train or Bus to almost Anywhere in the City.

title_masked: Just OK - NOTHING to do in Groveport
text_masked: Honestly, this hotel has it's ups & downs. Perks: friendly/caring staff, ice machines on every floor, and a plentiful, hot breakfast, good sized parking lot. Negatives: There is NOTHING in this town to do or see. (you will feel trapped). There is a Subway, gas station, dental office and a Giant Eagle. That's it. We road around for 35 minutes and came back. We spoke to another family w/ the same problem. There's no shopping, no restaurants, no movie theatre, no mall, nothing! Lots of boarded up buildings. I am stressing the LACK of anything close. Only one pizza shop delivers and it's thru the roof - $49.95 for two small pizzas, a 2-liter, and a garden salad. Other negatives: Small pool that never has any pool towels, dirt in the corners of the room, VERY hot hallways, scratchy towels, no exhaust fans, and our a/c barely pumped, heavy room door I could barely open. There was also a domestic violence situation going on at the hotel and cops were called. And in your room, you can hear everything going on in the parking lot. There was an uneasiness about the neighborhood. Soooo, like I said, 3 stars for this place.

We arrived late afternoon after a pleasant Amtrak journey from NYC. Was received at the front by a very helpfull young man. Was installed in our nice room in minutes.
Bernadette told us how to get to Connecticut ave. A short (10 min) walk through a very nice and quiet neigborhood. We found a nice restaurant "Bistrot du Coin" recommended by a native.
We departed the hotel at 5 am so we had a meal in our room the night before and hid the sack, after taxi was arranged by Bernadette. Sight seeing in Washington was easy by Metro within easy walking distance.
Jørli & Lars
Fur
Denmark.

This was my first time at this hotel. I had heard great things about the hotel so thought i would try it. To get directly to the problem, the noise level in the rooms is terrible. I was given a room on the 25th floor just below the roof top nightclub. I discovered after midnight that the noise from the music reaches the room. When i called the front desk i was told that there was a private party and they would continue to play music until 2:00 a.m. !
