Beside the music from the roof top club, the room doors and walls between rooms are very thin, so every time someone slammed their door, my whole room vibrated. 
I must say the style of the room is very nice. Shower and bathroom we well designed. And overall the room was clean. I would have enjoyed the room more if i had slept. 
I was also very disappointed with the attitude of the front desk when i called in the middle of the night. His attitude was, sorry we are having a private party so live with the noise. He never offered for me to change rooms. 
I do not recommend this hotel. Even if you have a room on a lower floor, the noise level is very high.

After much travel, we arrived at The Madison. The attention we received was phenomenol. The attention to detail wonderful. On our return, after having been there previously, we were treated extremely well. The location is great. Close to car rental and "The Center" of things.

title_masked: Great place to stay with a young family.
text_masked: I stayed at the Grand Hyatt Washington from 2/23/12 - 2/26/12. I must say this hotel was great. My wife and I have an 8 year old daughter and a 3 year old daughter. This was our first trip to DC as a family. I was the only one who had been prior and that was 22 years ago. Needless to say I was little worried about the big city and certainly didn't want to stay in some sketchy section . We felt very comfortable walking outside the hotel and along our way to the monuments. We also used the Metro extensively as we zipped around the city, very convenient to be directly under the hotel! I pre-purchased the breakfast buffet and we thought the food was fantastic and worth the cost as there didnt appear to be many options right outside the property for breakfast. I will certainly stay here again. Gorgeous lobby, clean rooms! We had a Atrium view on the 7th floor and did not notice any loud echo noices (as others have described). My girls loved looking out the huge windows and see the vast open space of the Atrium. I did the Self Park option and three days worth of parking cost me a total of $96. There is quite a difference when it comes to weekday and weekend guests. Business suits everywhere during the weekdays and families in blue jeans were everywhere on the weekend. Very happy with the Grand Hyatt !

title_masked: Cleanliness is a bit of an issue
text_masked:
Stayed here a couple weeks back on a business trip. Was nervous because of the negative reviews on this site, but had to stay here due to location to the client I was visiting. This hotel seemed average to me in most categories. At over $150+tax per night midweek, I expected "higher-end average" at this location, which is a 20 minute drive from the downtown area. 
First thing I noticed in the room was the "dirt" in the bathtub. Not sure what it was, but it had collected near the drain of the shower. It was disgusting and I immediately regretted staying here. I turned the shower on and let it was the dirt away. The bathroom itself is on the small side and not very comfortable for toilet use.
Thankfully that was the only issue I found. The bed was fine. Not great, but not bad either. I got a good night's sleep. The room size was fine for just me on this business trip and the desk was sufficient for the laptop work I needed to do. All standard really for a "business" stay. Self-parking lot was a half-block away. I didn't eat at the restaurant and didn't have time for the pool.
I want to also note that the ladies at the front desk were really polite and friendly at check-in and again when I checked out the next day. I didn't have any special requests but I give them marks for being friendly. Some places are polite without being friendly. I like the extra touch.
Clean up the rooms a bit. Lower the price per night by about 30% and this becomes a 3 star property and a decent value for the money.

I stayed at the Courtyard on Valentines Day with my girlfriend to watch the Red Wings win their 21st consecutive home victory. The location was convenient. Although we were given tokens for the People Mover which runs through the building, we were walking distance from The Cobo Centre and Joe Louis Arena. (I live outside Toronto but I'd rather drive 4 hours to support the Wings than the undeserving Leafs.)
On arrival, the valet staff, and front desk were polite and helpful. (Indeed everyone who we encountered who worked at the hotel was friendly and professional). The hotel must have had recent renovations; the carpet was new, tasteful decor, comfortable bed. 
We walked through the gym on the 8th floor and it was large and well equipped. 
I wouldn't hesitate to return to this hotel.

We stayed here for the evening to celebrate my sister's Bachelorette. Upon arriving at the hotel on Saturday Sept 29th about 5pm, it was pouring down rain. There were probably 20+ cars waiting to valet park when I pulled into line. I was very impressed, as I maybe only waited about 5-10 minutes max. The valets worked quickly and diligently to get cars valeted and into the garage and get us out of the rain. They also helped us immediately catch a cab to our destination. Upon checkout, by the time I walked out of the hotel doors, up came my car. Talk about service. They definitely do their jobs well. Check in and Check out was a breeze and Kevin at the front desk was personable and friendly. We booked through priceline and they had us in a king room, he moved us to a double room no problem. The room we stayed in was very comfortable and clean, and even overlooking the city surprisingly quiet. The renovations that have been made on the hotel so far are very nice. Price was great too and very competitive with hotels in the area. I just wish I had more time to explore the hotel while I was there. We ordered in room breakfast and it was fantastic. If I am ever looking to stay near downtown again, I will definitely consider the Hyatt Regency Dallas.

I travel to New York a few times per year. We usually stay at The Alex on Lexington, but this time there was no space there so we decided to try something new. In my opinion the boutique hotels are pretty hot places, just because the vibe is different from that of the typical Times Square Hotels. The Marcel is a very chic hotel located in a very hip part of town (SOHO). There is a subway about 5 minutes away, and since it is located in the 20's, you are close to soho shopping as well as Macy's and Midtown.
The staff was helpful, however it seemed there was a problem with the people before me. To all fellow travellers, if you are emitting negative energy, do not expect people to try their best when it comes to helping you. Remember that saying, "You catch more bees wit honey than you do with vinegar". 
Anyway, we had a great stay. The only negative comment that I have to say (really it isn't that negative) is that the rooms are very small. This is actually normal for New York. Living space in general is smaller, but this room was very small. We did however have the opportunity to upgrade to a bigger room, but since we really only spend the time unconscious at our hotel, we figured we'd have drinks with the money we saved.
Young couple, girls weekend, mother daughter trip, this boutique hotel is a great find!
OH! and the rooftop terrace is a unique photo op!!!

I stay at this property regularly and like it very much. However, for the third time in two years I have been charged the wrong amount on a reservation. When contacting the hotel and Starwood they see the mistake, but getting my $600 overcharge credited back to my card has been an unacceptable experience. I hope the hotel reads this review!

My partner and I stayed at this hotel for 3 nights and we would definitely stay again. It is in a perfect position right near fisherman's wharf. We were lucky enough to stay in room 300 which has a direct view to alcatraz. The rooms were clean and very large they can get quite noisy due to the trams but its fisherman's wharf theres trams everywhere. The kitchen is very handy with a grocery store within walking distance. Bathrooms and complimentary toiletries were great and house keeping did a great job. 
Front desk staff are amazingly friendly and would do anything to help you. Carparking was about $20 per night. I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone wanting to be in a great spot in San Fransico!!

I've had the opportunity to visit the Grand Del Mar each August for the last three years as part of a small conference that includes serious half day meetings and fun interactive afternoon events. Every year that I return, the hotel gets better. The customer service is unequaled. One morning I needed copies of an outline I had prepared for a presentation. I went to the concierge to ask where I could find the business center. Instead, the concierge volunteered to print out my documents on the spot. She did so quickly, with a smile, and free of charge. One more example, upon checking out of the hotel early one morning, the person at the check out desk encouraged me to review my bill. I noticed that there was a charge for one of the hotel restaurants on my bill and I had not visited it during my stay. I mentioned the $60 charge and without hesitation the check out assistant waived the charge. No "I will need to speak with a manager" or even a follow up question or two. It was prompt and decisive. Impressive. 
Similarly the help by the valets and attendants at the golf course were stellar. When I noticed that my golf bag did not include my wedge (grandchild strikes again), the attendant went and got me a brand new quality wedge at no charge. Speaking of the golf course, it is one of the best that I have played. It's fair and fascinating, with each hole offering a unique challenge. Greens are fast, the conditions are outstanding, and the caddies are energetic and knowledgeable. It's pricey, but worth the experience. 
Lastly, I have to add that the hotel itself is gorgeous. The grounds are immaculate. Forget the fussy comments elsewhere, this is a first class hotel with great, plush rooms, expansive bathrooms, very comfortable king beds, and nice furniture. The common areas are attractive, nicely decorated, and rarely too crowded. Next year, despite the business meetings, I'll want to ensure that my wife joins me. This is too nice a place to experience alone.

Our Family stayed for 4 nights and loved it. We felt very comfortable in our suite. The Staff and Manager were very accomodating and helpful to make it possible for us to stay another night. Thank you Jessie, Megan and Della! The hotel is beautiful and the amenities were extrememly upscale. We will stay here again! The beds were so comfortable we did not want to get out of them! We felt we were centrally located for all we had set out to do. We went to Sea World, Six Flags, and were a couple of blocks from The River Walk and Alamo. (Highly recommend driving to the River Walk area.) We even squeezed in a day at the beach in Corpus Christi at Port Aransas. We love San Antonio!

title_masked: Not as great as these reviews say
text_masked:
First off the staff were great, and couldnt be faulted.
View of a concrete wall and alleyway was disapointing from 3rd floor room. Australian travellers beware of location, not as close to union square as you may think. Wouldnt dare leave the hotel after dark...
On first arrival, we instantly had a bad feeling. We had to drive through the so called tenderloin to get to the hotel. This neighbourhood is very rough. The best part of the hotel is the lobby Then it goes down from there. Although the hotel is very clean, the bathrooms and room in general are small and outdated. We had a dividing door to the next room therefore could hear kid screaming and smell cigarette smoke coming under the door. 
The toilet you have to sit on an angle because of its close proximity to the wall. The shower floods everytime you have a shower being a bath/shower and we found the bath only drained when it wanted too...
We felt very unsafe staying here for 4 nights i would reccomend to stay near pier39/ the wharf. The serrano can only work with what its got being an older building ( and the neighbourhood its in ). Updating rooms is a must. 
The connecting resturant was great. sitting at the window in the resturant will give you a good idea at what your in for on the outside. You get hit up for money and smokes when exiting most buildings and c stores by bums and crackheads.
For the money your paying for staying here, there are many better options around san francisco.

My wife and I spent a weekend at Admiral Fell Inn in Baltimore on April 6-8, 2012, it was our first time there and I would like to say, we would definitely return in the future. We received a very warm welcomed, the environment was very charming and customer service was the best, overall. However, we would like to extend our utmost gratitude to Mr [NAME], he was extremely courteous, pleasant and helpful, he took time to help us with our every interest; dining recommendation, car service, etc. I work in a Financial and Sales environment and I think he is a great asset to the Admiral Fell Inn Hotel. I would recommend the Admiral Fell Inn Hotel to others because of the outstanding service we received from Mr [NAME].

I have stayed at Embassy Suites in different locations and have had no issues. This location in Downtown San Diego was extremely disappointing. The furnishings, first of all, are outdated and the carpets need a good shampooing. For the rate you pay here, you would think they would have updated furnishings. But I can live with that. The service, on the other hand, was unacceptable. First, no remote control for the TV in the room. We have to call down to get it - they take FOREVER. We ask them also "Could you bring up a wine opener" They inform us they are out of wine openers and we have to take our wine all the way down to the bar and ask them to open it. Really? You couldn't come up and open it for us since you are out of the courtesy wine openers? We get dressed, trek down to the bar... they say they don't open wine bottles for the hotel customers -- they are a separate entity. OK... now what? The next day, housekeeping does not clean our rooms. We arrived back to the hotel about 8pm. There are dirty dishes FROM BREAKFAST in the hallways along with dirty towels. They have been sitting there all day, no one has cleaned the halls or our room. (See attached pictures). I go down to complain to the manager. He makes excuses and recites them as if it's common to get complaints. Finally, he says "What do you want me to do?" I have never stayed in a hotel where the manager made so many excuses and didn't jump to make a bad situation better. Clearly the service in the hotel is a reflection of their management. They ended up crediting me one night (still waiting for it, but they said they would give credit) but I will never stay at this hotel again. Even the hot tub was out of commission for part of our stay.
On a plus side, the complimentary breakfast was cooked to order and good. The lines were long but at least this hotel offers this service and the free drinks in the afternoon to offset their otherwise shoddy service.

I spent one night here in March. The rooms seemed like they could use sprucing up - not typical to other HGI's I stayed at. The room price was in line with other rates in the city that I looked at. I was not able to adjust my bed whatsoever so it was a rather uncomfortable nights sleep.
I had dinner upstairs at the 10th floor restaurant which was average. I just had a turkey burger with sweet potatoe fries. Service was good.
I needed a cab to take me to the 30th St. Train station the next morning but none were to be found. I had to wait while the bellman tracked one down. 
Front lobby staff was very pleasant and did help ship a package via FedEx for me.

Great hotel on the edge of the theater district. The rooms are small but stylish and clean. There's no restaurant on site but there's a coffee shop right around the corner for breakfast. There are many nice bars and restaurants to choose from just a short walk away. Boston Common and the Freedom Trail are with walking distance also. I would definitely stay here again.

The room was pleasant and quiet, the bed extremely comfortable. However, my accolades are for the staff. We were there due to a death in the family. The staff could not have been more accomodating and courteous. The front desk personnel were, to a person, the most polite of any we have ever encountered in any hotel, including 5 star properties! A particular mention to Margo, who, understanding our situation, went out of her way to insure we were not inconvenienced. We would stay there again in a heart beat. In the comments below, when I say room service, I mean the staff who cleaned the room and and gave a little bit extra. The restaurant was a breakfast only affair, so no harsh criticism is intended.

title_masked: Great choice, I would recommend staying here
text_masked: We stayed at the hotel for 2 days while attending the volleyball tournament at the Convention Center. Check in and out were so easy, and fast. The valet process was very smooth and the wait for the car was almost none. The rooms were clean and comfortable. The bar/ lounge area was nice and the staff even let us use a microwave so the kids could have popcorn. A couple of things that would have made it better, the pool was so tiny, it was clean and nice but really tiny. The elevators were very slow, there were alot of people around so I am assuming that was the reason, but be prepared to wait.

We stayed at Radisson Seattle for our family trip to Seattle. The hotel is easy walking distance from the airport, in fact its kind of down hill. Exit the baggage area to the outside and walk to your right. Pass the bus stops and head downhill toward the traffic light. The hotel is at the light. 
Check in was a breeze and being from an Eastern time zone we appreciated being on the top floor. The room was spacious and the beds are comfortable. Some have said the furniture is a bit dated. It was great. We loved having all the space on the desk and the drawer unit. 
The shower head was very neat, it felt good on the back of my tired neck. And it was so refreshing to have ice water with oranges in the lobby.
This hotel was a very short walk to the light rail station. Exit the hotel and head to your right on the sidewalk. We also walked left to Dave's Dinner which was very good and Denny's which was not so good. 
The hotel pool and exercise areas were always neat and clean. It was refreshing to swim before going to bed. A great wind down for our daughter. If we are ever fortunate enough to visit Seattle again we will be back at the Radisson!

Just returned from a 3 night stay at Staybridge Suite. It was my girlfriend's first visit to NYC, but was my third. We were both thoroughly impressed by everything to do with hotel.
Great location, no issues with Parole office or bus station (even at night.) Felt safe walking past at all times.
Perfect for walking to Times Square, Empire State Building, Macy's etc. Ideal location if you have got bus from Newark to Port Authority, it's across the street. Subway two minutes walk. 
Room was great size by NYC standards. Huge bed, nice bathroom. Nice touch with the kitchenette, with large fridge freezer, hob, microwave, dishwasher etc. 
We were on 20th floor & had no complaints over the waiting time of the lifts. 
All staff polite & friendly. 
We enjoyed our stay so much I proposed to my girlfriend, who is now my Fiancée. 
My Parents are having a 3 night stay in New York at the end of October & on our recommendation have just booked a stay at the Staybridge Suites Times Square.

Average hotel rooms but very clean and good service. It is a walking distance to everything in downtown Seattle and the Monorail to the Space Needle is across the street which costs 2.25 for a one way trip and a 90 second ride. Several malls and flagship Nordstrom store a block away.
I noticed long lineups in the morning at the front desk so I would suggest booking out the night before or get up early. 
With a family, we got a City Pass which let us see most of the Seattle attractions at 50 percent off

We stayed 4 nights in a junior suite. The hotel is very well located to explore Boston. The staff were all very nice and helpful. Our room was spacious and comfortable but the bathroom was very small and pokey, we are not big people and very found it very small. It was disproportionate compared to the size of the junior suite. We had to pay for the wifi connection and were disappointed with it, it was very unstable and kept dropping which I would not expect with a paid connection. It was very frustrating. Having said all that if we were in Boston again we would stay at this hotel again.

My boyfriend and I stayed here for three weeks in early September when we moved to Seattle. This was a great affordable option for a long term stay. The hotel is modern, the rooms are nice, it's super clean, beds are comfortable and overall it's generally quiet, except for the noisy family that stayed across from us for a couple of days. But mgmt. actually spoke to them after we called the front desk. The staff was really friendly and helpful as I was always asking them to help me print copies of my resumes, which they did for free and housekeeping worked around our schedule since we had our cat with us and wanted to be sure we around when they came. The kitchen was a huge plus, though it is a little sparse on the cookware, but the Kmart next door had everything we needed. The location is great, it's not scenic but it is convenient. The bus ride to downtown Seattle was really easy. My mom is staying here when she comes for the holidays.

We were supposed to stay at the Best Western next door. For some reason there was a mixup on our room. So at 2:30am we were stranded without a place to stay. The Staybridge Suites got us a great room and we were checked in quickly. 
Breakfast was great. Lobby was clean & smelled good. We were really impressed with our stay.

Very nice hotel in downtown Houston in a convenient location besides the Convention Center - Restaurants were top shelf with fair prices - The guest rooms were very nice with one of the best mattresses I have ever had at a Hilton property. All in all very nice Hilton property.

Stayed at this Drury Inn & Suite for one day during my trip. 
The hotel is excellent, especially at this rate. It is a little far from the airport, at Pinnacle Peak, but location is not bad, close to highway and surprisingly quiet at night. Building is very new, room is spacy and clean. Big LCD TV and free wireless internet, and the internet speed is the best among the chain hotels I've ever stayed. 
Staffs are very nice. When we arrived at dinner time the front desk lady was helping at the dining area. A kind note was left at the front desk, and the lady showed up in half minute when we tried to find her. Free snacks and drinks during dinner time, and good breakfast too. 
This is not a luxery resort but at a rate of $80 this is the best.

I stayed at the Westin for a sales meeting. With a tight schedule between conference calls and meetings I grabbed lunch and breakfast at the restraurant. The staff was very attentive, informative and accommodating.

title_masked: Disappointing service from front desk, A/C not working properly.
text_masked:
For a moderately priced hotel, I expected better. When I asked the front desk to extend the stay, they told me to go online and reserve. I had to leave the front desk and go get my computer, then go back to the front desk and present my online information. She should have offered to look online for me if that's what was required, but she didn't.
The AC in the room the first night didn't work at all, it was oppressively hot... so much so, that it was hard to sleep.
And there was an unannounced $50 additional charge added to my credit card that was NOT on my receipt online and was NOT on my bill that they slid under my door. It only appeared on my credit card statement. When I called about it, I was told that was "standard procedure" and would be reversed. I have to wonder if it would have been if I hadn't called, since there was no indication on either of the bills I received.
If you stay here, watch your bill and make sure you ask to see the room first if you are concerned about the view. Our room overlooked the lower roof and parking lot. :( And ask at the front desk how to get online, since there's no information on this in the room and a username and password IS required, even if you sign up as "just a guest" to bypass that.
On a good note, housekeeping did a great job.

Love "On the Ave" Hotel because it's clean, friendly, centrally located and has the best beds in the city! Whenever I go to New York, I stay here and know I'll be warmly welcomed and feel like I'm in my own home. I highly recommend checking out this extraordinary hotel!

title_masked: Great service, early check-in when needed, and wonderful location
text_masked:
My daughter and I went to New York for a short vacation. Since I had some business to do in midtown Manhattan, I searched all the hotels close by and Best Western President Hotel popped into my eyes due to the location in Time Square.
Before the trip I went to tripadvisor and read some negative reviews and made me very anxious, However the reality is totally out of my expectation. We arrived early Sunday morning, got early check-in around noon, and even got upgraded! The room is clean and servicable, the restaurant Saigon48 we tried has homey noodle soup.
Only the water temperature in the washroom and the room temperature need to be more stable and not so hot.
I'll definitely recommend stay there. 
Love the location in the center of Time Square, Broadway, Rochfeller center and St. Patrick Cathedral closeby plus many good bagel restaurants and Roxy bakery with walking distance...
,

We had great service from the staff. We found the lobby staff friendly and knowledgeable about the history of the hotel. Our room was a bit on the small side, but we loved the 2 bathrooms. Service at Kitty O'Shea's and the restaurant were great, the conceirge booked us into some great restaurants in the area for suppers. 
My only bug a bear was the cost of internet service AND the fact that there is not wireless in the conference rooms. It is a rare presenter nowadays that doesn't need internet for their presentation. There needs to be wireless throughout the hotel AND it needs to be a more reasonable fee charge - regardless of the "support" for internet provided it is simply FAR too expensive.

This place is similar to my other favorite, the HIlton Garden Inn 2 blocks south. The only difference is 1) No fridges or microwaves in rooms (a negative) and 2) They serve free hot breakfast (a PLUS). At HGI you don't get breakfast unless you're a top-level Hilton Honors client. So if you're a breakfast person stay here; if you need a fridge/microwave stay at the HGI. They're both good. This place was also very friendly.
There's a 24-hour Duane & Reade nearby, a 24-hour deli, a Food Emporium 1 block South, and of course restaurants all around. Great location for Broadway shows also.
A card said the duvet was replaced for each guest and it looked clean so that's great, many places never replace it for many months.
No room service or swimming pool.
HIGH RECOMMENDATION.

This is a very large business style hotel in central Boston. It is all you would expect from a Marriott and the staff are very well trained and helpful. If you have limited time in the city it is a great base to start exploring this interesting city. The bar is ok...Champions, nothing exceptional but in house if the weather is bad. The hotel is connected to a mall nearby complete with a good food court and a 24 hour supermarket is opposite the hotel if you arrive at a late hour. The" Duck Tour "buses also go from opposite the hotel. If you want to walk to Boston Common and on to Quincy Market these are all withing easy reach and will take around 30 minutes to reach from the hotel. All in all a great hotel and location.

Leon and Linwood at the Front Desk where very nice and pleasant young men made sure I had a pleasant stay the whole week of my stay. The breakfast was ok However Holiday Inn Express should have another type of breakfast meat for those who do not eat pork . The shuttle bus driver was a sweetheart ( Mr [NAME] ) . The Hotel was clean the rooms where nice . I will definitely recommend family and friends to stay at the Holiday Inn Express Baltimore Stadiums.

title_masked: I cannot believe the good ratings!!
text_masked:
Here is a list: One reading light for a king-sized bed?
Air Conditioner roars when cooling; no way to keep fan constant
Tub stopper does not work, and you cannot direct water to faucet; only the shower works...but it works well...but what if you want to take a bath?
Lavatory does not drain
Room is old, dark, not enough lighting.
If you are sitting at the working desk, you freeze since the A/C blows directly on you.
OK, so I am picky, but the big sign says $59.99 per night. I am paying $80. When I asked about the difference, I was told that there were only a limited number of $59.99 rooms, and they were all gone. I asked if there really ever were any $59.99 rooms, I was told there were, but they were all gone...The sign still said $59.99 rooms at 6:30 PM...false advertising? 
Oh, yeah: The bed was comfortable, and the towels were really nice! And they have the Golf Channel. 
But then, to top it all off, there were a bunch of what appeared to be gang-bangers hanging around the entrance when we returned from dinner. Comforting...
I am a big Choice Hotels fan, but this is not one of their best...I hope someone from Choice sees this and either fixes this hotel or pulls their franchise..

title_masked: a little expensive for what you get
text_masked: nice staff- they were willing to chage our room to one with a view of the water- made the stay nicer- this hotel has 2 seperate buildings- so make for a busy breakfast area in the morning- could use a little more room for this-as the lines are crowded to get your food and not enough places to sit- good thing the weather was nice- as many sat outside to eat

We stayed here for 4 nights and had an amazing time!! The hotel was clean, friendly and in an excellent location with Fisherman's Wharf and Pier 39 being within easy walking distance. Plenty of places to eat too! Did find San Fransisco more expensive than the other places we visitied in the states (LA and Vegas) but definately our favourite! As previously noted TAKE A HOODY AND A JACKET!!!!! It really is cold some mornings but also be aware that the wind burns just as much as the sun!!!! We were all very red!! Parking here was extremely expensive but if you booked your holiday through Virgin you did get it half price which for us was a huge 80 dollars difference!! Would recommend Alcatraz as an excellent trip and also the hop on - hop off bus trips, Powell and Hyde cable car trip was fun - a 9 mile an hour roller coaster!!

title_masked: Best hotel experience in a long time. Meeting group had an over the top dinner with reception there first night.
text_masked:
Everything from room to meals to cleanliness to service was tops!
Wish I had known about lobby coffee earlier, but selection of newspapers was superb and made up for my ignorance!
Lobster was served to large meeting group, and was hot and cooked to perfection. Breakfast selections were fine, and special requests (like plain yogurt) was delivered immediately.

My wife and I just arrived home from vacation in New York from October 1st-8th. We found that with this being our first trip to the city it was difficult to choose from the multitude of accomodation options available. We couldn't be more thankful for having chosen the Cassa. The location is ideal within only a short walk of Time Square and only steps from access to the Subway. I am an avid runner and was easily able to take the subway to Central Park for daily jogs. Our room (King Bed) was of good size and very clean/modern. The building is in very good condition overall and elevators are fast/efficient. The staff is the real treasure of the hotel. Front desk personel was continually helpful in providing direction and advice in terms of enjoying the city in addition to continually offering assistance with any accomodation questions/thoughts we might wish to discuss. Really, we didn't have any questions as the hotel was exceptional. Will definitely recommend the hotel to others and will quite possibly return.

Iv'e stayed at this property many times and have always loved the location and service but our most recent experience was the epitomy of Great Customer relations. We had a mishap that was completely our fault in which we feared for the safety of our children. All of the staff and managers at Courtyard dropped everything and made our childrens safety the most important issue in the world. It was handled with both class and professionalism. I would never stay elsewhere while in Denver. I cant express enough gratitude to all involved.
Special thanks to the Night Security Man, Maintenance Man, Daniel at the Front Desk and Erica the General Manager. Your kindness, concern and dedication make this location superior.
Many Thanks

My husband and I went to Seattle for an anniversary long-weekend. I chose this hotel because I had airmiles gift cards for Best Western to use and the hotel was close to the Amtrak train station (less than $5 taxi fare). 
It turned out to be a perfect choice. We were welcomed with a celebratory bottle of "champagne" for our anniversary, and two bottles of water and cookies after having signed up for Best Western Rewards. I asked for a quiet room and we were given a king sized room that overlooked the inside roof. No view, but very quiet and a lovely spacious room and nice bathroom. The bathtub was a small square with a bit of a seat in it. Good for showering (with the waterpik shower head), but not for taking a bath. The Neutrogena bath products were very nice (and they even had make up remover cloths).
Nice large flat screen tv, but we felt the bed was a little bit firmer than we would have liked (and my husband prefers firm beds). After the first night we asked if they had thinner pillows and were given new pillows and had a better sleep. But, oddly, housekeeping replaced them with the thicker puffy ones the third night and by the time we realised it was too late to call front desk (we were already in pajamas and sleepy and ready for bed). So the only downside was we didn't sleep very well for a couple of nights.
Complementary breakfast was lovely in a separate room with tables covered with tablecloths. Lots of good, individually boxed Kellog cereals, fresh fruit, yogurt, bagels, cream cheese, bread to make toast, and delicious make-your-own waffles (complete with strawberries and whipped cream!). The only downer was the doughy egg, cheese and bacon pockets.
The location is fantastic. Walking distance to several key sightseeing spots, lots of restaurants and pubs, and there is free transit within the downtown area. 
The front desk staff are really friendly and very helpful. We would not hesistate to stay here again!

I actually LIVE in San Diego, have my entire life, but this was my first time at the Catamaran. My niece was married at the Mission Bay Yacht Club so we decided to make a weekend out of it at the Catamaran. It's such a great location and so much to do, I wished we could have stayed a couple more days! My husband and I rented Segways, OMG they were a blast, I want to do it again. And we also rented a Hobie Cat, so much fun. Best weekend I've had in a long time! Thank you Catamaran! We won't forget our weekend there :-).

My husband and I stayed at the Trump Soho back in February 2012 with our 1 year old son and had some problems with our room and how the situation was handled by the hotel staff. I was later contacted by the hotel manager to discuss the issues and invited back to give the hotel another chance.
This past weekend we were finally able to take advantage of the invitation and spent the weekend at the Trump Soho, again with our child (now 19 months). To say the hotel redeemed itself in our eyes would be an understatement. From the moment we checked in to the moment we departed, the staff was amazing and the hotel was pristine. This is perhaps one of the most kid friendly hotels I've ever stayed at, complete with a full sized crib, bath accessories and toys and anything else you might need for the little one. The pool deck was absolutely gorgeous and again the staff treated us with the utmost respect and consideration. My son had an amazing time playing in the pool and neither the staff nor any of the other guests seemed to be annoyed by his laughing and screeching.
I would highly recommend this hotel to business and personal travelers alike -- especially if you have children!
Thank you Trump Soho for making our family weekend so much fun!!!

title_masked: Good value compared to other places
text_masked: Stayed here 2 nights last weekend and it was well worth making reservations ahead of time. I made mine 1 1/2 months ago and people were walking in off the street asking for availability. Of course there wasn't any availability. It is 5 blocks from where the wharf starts and it is closest to the Giradelli square side of the wharf. The hotel room was small but clean (had a queen size on the 9th floor). No problems with noise or bugs or anything. The employees were very courteous and helpful. There is off street parking ($26 per night) available and recommended. There just isn't any other place to park. There is an underground garage that is VERY tight manuevering, so I recommend the secondary upstairs lot that is outside but still secure. My wife and I were there for our 15th anniversary, and it was very enjoyable and relaxing. There is a large restaurant area with lots of seating for their complimentary continental breakfast. They had a pretty good selection to choose from. I don't particularly want to pay $400 per night, so this will be the place for me again.

title_masked: Our stay in Seattle at the Georgetown Inn
text_masked: When we checked in we were greeted by a young man named [NAME]. He was so pleasant & most helpful. Our room was as what we saw on the website, very clean, & we never had any complaints except the heater never shut off. The continental breakfast was good, fresh fruit every morning.

My husband and I were staying in Jacksonville only one night and booked this hotel. What a great decision on our part !! This hotel was crouded that night, but we did not hear a single sound the whole time, sleeping was great, and we had a great stay here !! The rooms were clean, the bathrooms were spotless, and the HOT breakfast the next morning was great !!

title_masked: Classic hotel in a great location
text_masked: Just a couple of blocks from the Blue Line (to O'Hare) and the Red Line is right outside - they even include the directions on the website. Super convenient downtown location in a fairly recently restored classic building. Gorgeous lobby and ballroom. The Executive Floor Lounge is a little odd because it's not in a room, but in the elevator lobby on the executive floor. I prefer this property over the Chicago Hilton.

best place to stay in when in washington. when i saw it from outside i thot i have made a mistake but i was wrong. the exterior may be deceiving. The reception is small nothing fancy but the people are really great. the room was fantastic. i was upgraded to a balcony room without me asking for it. the room looks better than in the pictures. Aaron is the guy to meet.he was so helpfull. keep up the good work buddy. nice place dunno abt the food dint get a chance to eat anything but the restaurant was always full.

A great choice - apparently public areas have been remodeled and the rooms will follow suit soon ... even so we were very happy with our [upgraded] room. This was a short visit; service was excellent as always.

title_masked: Great value for those on a budget
text_masked: The staff were very helpful & friendly. the room was a twin bedded on e. Very clean, clean bedlinen..basic but clean!! only problem was somebody having an argument at 2am in morning.....otherwise o.k. Bathroom was 2 doors down and spotless!! Only stayed one night but was v. good value.

My sons took me to the Miramar Air Show on Saturday October 13. My two oldest grandsons got to go with us (the whole reason it was so great). They are almost 2 and almost 7 years old. We stayed at the Marriott Residence Inn Scripps Poway. The suite was perfect for us all. The young one slept great just around the bedroom wall from us. We loved the kitchenette, the breakfast, the pool and spa, and the restaurants right next door to the hotel. The beds were wonderful, the bathroom seemed all brand new, and everything worked perfect. Internet, Flat panel TV (two sets).

This was my fourth stay at the Fairmont. Service is very friendly, the rooms are comfortable, spacious and quiet, bed is very comfortable, and the restaurant is excellent. The fitness center is a full blown health club with a wide array of equipment, many exercise spaces, dry and wet sauna, pool, and jacuzzi. Join the President's Club online (at no charge) and the fitness center and internet are free. The hotel is conveniently located to several nearby great running courses (fifteen minute run along the Potomac to the Lincoln Memorial), an easy walk into Georgetown or up to Dupont Circle, and a quick Metro ride to the National Mall. I have never been disappointed by this hotel; I'm pretty picky and I would rate the Fairmont a five-star property. I paid in advance and got a great rate directly with the hotel.

Very accomodating to get extra shuttles for party members' safe travel to and from wedding and reception. Good food and service. They even got a new American flag after the grandfather of the bride made a suggestion!

title_masked: close to airport but not worth it
text_masked:
I chose this hotel because we needed something close to the airport and the pictures looked great, not my best decision.
The pictures do not look like the rooms provided, the windows were filthy the shower bath had the linoleum half missing from the bottom of the bath so there was no way i was getting in it and it looked dirty.
The service was also poor.
We waited at the shuttle pick up spot for 45 mins and the hotel driver drove past us TWICE even tho we were waving and pointing and jumping up and down- just rude.
After walking to the hotel we were greeted at reception with a friendly "Welcome Mr and Mrs [NAME] name, your room is ready for your and it has 2 single beds " I laughed because it was so dumb and from seeing the look on my fast she replied with "How about a king bed?" considering that is what I requested in the first place it seemed the appropriate response.
The concierge staff were rude and completely unhelpful when we asked for directions and were more interested in talking to their friends and looking at their mobiles and I would never ever stay here again even if you paid me too.

We stayed at the Washington Plaza for 3 nights in September. We found the rooms very clean and comfortable and slept very well here. It is well located and maybe a 20min walk or so to the Washington Mall. We also walked to Georgetown which didn't take that long, perhaps 30-40mins. Only slightly disappointing thing was that the pool was closed (it closes after Labor Day). Given that it was still warm in the city in late September it would have been nice to have a swim after a day out walking in the sun! We didn't eat at the hotel but found a number of places to eat nearby. We had breakfast at the Corner Bakery on 14th st which we liked. We really enjoyed Washington DC and would recommend this hotel.

and exceptionally nice and helpful staff, they are great here. very simple and all the perks of a travelers chain hotel in ny, such as free breakfast and the best thing an actual coffee maker in the room!!! you never see that anymore and besides the great location that is why i choose this hotel for coming in for work, i don't have to leave the hotel or call room service when i first wake up. just a great and affordable place to stay. make sure you join choice privileged's and you get a free late cheek out too!

the hotel in more like a motel and very basic the elevator does not work the reception was very drap, rooms are big and clean but are very dated (it did say in the holiday book ) hotel has inspired rooms to reflect the stages in Elvis life thats why we book this hotel , inspired i do not think they have two photo of elvis in the rooms so you could of been anywhere , breafast you eat with plastic knive and fork and take away plate and cup that sum it all up ....so the only thing this hotel offer you that its very close to his home and Elvis home was amazing and we loved it

I didn't have an idea of how the hotel was going to, but when I arrived it surprised me how good it was for its price.
The room had all that was needed: sink, table. closet. refrigerator and tv.
Then, my other big question were the bathrooms: EXCELLENT! There were some with just a toilet and a sink, and other with a shower too. They were looked very nice, considering the price, and clean! 
The location was great too. Maybe it's not the most beautiful neighborhood in the city, but it;s very close to powell st, market st, chinatown, and other places you might wanna visit. And there are many bus lines you can take nearby.
I wouldn't doubt of going back to this hotel in my next visit to San Francisco.

A great place to stay for business or pleasure. Stayed with family. A " flat hotel " as known in Europe. Friendly staff, valet parking ( perhaps pricey at $ 25 ). Breakfast bar, which forces us to get off bed as it closes at 09.00 am.

This W Hotel is funky like most of the W Hotels. It is full of energy. Great breakfasts in Trace Restaurant. The room was comfortable (you know the beds and pillows at a W Hotel are always very comfortable). Great location...across the street from convention center where I had a conference.

We stayed at this hotel during the July 4th weekend and we very pleased. The rate was just below $125/night which was quite good. The chain hotel was very well decorated, great DC location and very well organized. Would stay there again for that same rate but normally I think it is quite a bit more.

The Tremont is about a 6 block walk from the Inner Harbor. It is located near many places to eat. We stayed here because we needed access to John's Hopkins hospital and this hotel is located about 5 min drive from the hospital. The hotel has a very reliable shuttle service that we used at no charge. When we called for pick up we never waited a long time. The employees at this hotel were very friendly and super helpful. The driver, front desk clerk, wait staff. The room was a clean tastefully decorated mini suite that included a microwave, fridge and sink. There was a coffee maker with some coffee packets and also a couple free bottles of water. There was a couch that faced a flat screen TV. The bed was very comfortable and had a nice comforter on it and a selection of pillows to use. There were some ornamental pillows as well. The bathroom was set back behind two doors. The first door was to a dressing area with a mirror and closet and room safe. The other door was the door to the bathroom. The bathroom was a nice size but not what I'd consider large. It had a hair dryer and some complementary toiletries. My only complaint was that the shower did not have any grab bar. None. Well, unless you count the soap dish. So be very careful getting in and out of the shower as it is very easy to slip. We had dinner at the restaurant Tugs, which is located on the 2nd floor. They have a bar and table service. The food was very good for hotel fair. They have fish, burgers, crab cakes, salads and soups. There is also a deli in the lobby area that has drinks and prepared foods. Hotel has free wifi. There is valet parking and self parking. Valet was very efficient and the employees also very nice people. Baltimore also has a bus called the "Charm City Circulator" that is a free bus to different parts of the city including Inner Harbor. There is a green line, orange line and I think purple. We were able to take this bus from John's Hopkins down to Inner Harbor area and back very easily. We would stay at the Tremont again if we are ever in the area. Didn't use the fitness area so I can't comment on that.

My son graduated from boot camp in Lackland, Tx, in July, 2012. My family and I traveled from Pennsylvania to be with him for a 5 day vacation. When we arrived, we were told we had rooms on the riverwalk, which we did, but the location was awful. It was at one of the ends of the riverwalk, where trash piles up on the water, and the view was not desireable.
The rooms were dirty, and the balcony must never have been swept, or cleaned...trash, and cigarette butts, and stained cement from spills, etc. The lobby was very pretty, and very deceiving to the rest of the hotel. They need some serious updates, since its supposed to be an attraction on the riverwalk!

I was traveling the East Coast for a week, with stops in NYC, Boston and DC. I stayed at 4+ star hotels in each city and Hotel Commonwealth was the best. Each employee I interacted with was very kind and accommodating. I stayed in a junior suite and the separate living/work room is very spacious and welcoming. The suite was immaculate and I actually wished I was staying longer to enjoy the room.
The location is also central, with lots of shopping and restaurants within walking distance.

Booked Zaza while in town for a wedding. We have a king balcony w/ beautiful, upgraded linens and a very good bed. Even the pillows are good! The furnishings are unique, nice quality--the bathroom is spacious for this smaller king room, the shower is wonderful. Very classy. The staff are smiling, friendly and helpful.
This is a great hotel to book if you want to be near Rice, the Medical Ctr, Museums and parks. Good downtown vibe.

The hotel is staffed with exceptionally friendly people - every person I encountered from the front desk to the hallways went out of their way to smile and greet me. The room is typical of a boutique hotel - a little on the smaller side (although not really that small for San Francisco) and well-appointed. 
The location is not great. It's certainly safe but it's a little walk to Market Street either via the not-great area or via the super tourist area. 
Check in and out were extremely quick and efficient.

Recently I travelled to NYC for a business meeting. I booked the Gansevoort Park Avenue hotel on the basis of convenient location close to my meeting spot. I was not disappointed!
The hotel is located on Park Avenue South and within walking distance to many of the tourist spots, i.e.: Times Square, Broadway Theaters, Empire State Building, Madison Avenue and 5th Avenue Shopping, etc… It is far enough away from Times Square to feel insulated from the hustle and bustle but within easy reach of everything in Manhattan.
My wife and son flew in from Atlanta to join me after my meeting as they had never travelled to NYC before. We stayed at the Gansevoort Park Avenue before and during the Labor Day weekend (stayed for five nights). No question – the hotel is definitely a smaller, almost boutique in size hotel with very interesting decorations. The hotel is located closer to many residential buildings so it seemed to be much more quite than many of the NYC hotels I’ve stayed in before. 
Our check in was quick and very efficient and we received a very warm welcome by the staff. Our room was more than acceptable and the extremely large bathroom was great touch. My wife and I were impressed by their linens and towels more than in any other hotel we’ve ever stayed. The room size was average along with average bed size, but it was very comfortable and we all slept well! The small refrigerator in our room was a welcome addition and stocked as well as many of the Trump hotels in which I’ve stayed. The pricing at the mini bar left a little to be desired, however this is NYC – what can you expect? Also, the rooftop pool and bar area are fantastic – but too much of a party atmosphere for families with younger children.
Within one block of the hotel I counted several large chain type eating establishments – McDonalds, Starbucks and California Pizza Kitchen to name a few. In addition, there were several up-scale Italian Sidewalk restaurants and Steak Houses all within a block. One great welcome addition was the pharmacy across the street that was well stocked with all the staple snack and grocery items we could want (including stuff for my teenage son).
Comparing the prices of other NYC hotels to what I paid per night for the Gansevoort - I do not think it can be beat. All in all, the hotel is great for leisure travel but I do not think I could recommend it for business use as the meeting rooms were chopped up and the elevators were somewhat small and slow when the business travelers were in the hotel.
Needed to check in early and have a room conducive to working. Duke came through and made it a great stay. Definitely recommend this hotel.

How awesome was it to come from Kentucky and be greeted by the nices Coloradians!!! This hotel was soooooo clean. They gave us top floor with Mountain Views. It was sooooo super quiet. The food in the restaurant was so good. The breakfast? Best Buffet with omelet station EVER. I am sooo happy we started our week long trip off by staying here. I will definately go back when I come back to visit. Everyone was so nice!!!! Did I mention Clean rooms? CLEAN!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Our theatre company holds auditions in NYC frequently, so we've stayed at many hotels there over the past 20 years. This one was heads and shoulders above any other hotel we've stayed at!! The staff was SO friendly, the rooms were well-appointed and clean (although small but, then again, what reasonably priced hotel in NYC doesn't have small rooms?), parking was conveniently located directly across the street, they accommodated every request (from early check-in, to storing bags 5 hours past their normal cut-off period - in fact, when I offered the hotel staff person a small tip for the luggage accommodation, she politely refused and asked me to just write a positive review of the hotel!), and price could not be beat. The only minor negative comment is that the fan for the room heater went on and off frequently throughout the night - finally just turned it off. We've already recommended the hotel to others and will most definitely stay again!

title_masked: Now I know what tips for getting a good room means...
text_masked: This hotel is actually an excellent place. The staff is friendly, efficient, the room's really clean and comfortable and the breakfast is great. When we checked in a group was eating dinner in the breakfast area - they had brought in pizzas. The desk clerk told me they would be there until around 8 pm - and that was no problem as we were headed out to dinner ourselves. When we returned the pizzas were gone but the guitar came out and some of them were singing for a bit. You could hear that in our room, too, but even that didn't bother me as they were gone by 10. The buzzing noise I began hearing at 6 am was a bit disturbing. I thought it was someone's alarm, but it went off so frequently and I knew there were not that many rooms near us. Upon finally getting out and going to breakfast I realized what it was - the waffle machine! Checkout was super efficient and the place truly is great - just don't take a room behind the breakfast area if you want to sleep past 6.

I was very satisfied with this hotel - it's location and proximity to everything in Downtown Chicago was just superb. 
The room was exceptionally clean and fresh. Every nook was cleaned and wiped down as I would expect from any hotel at this price range.
Housekeeping services were first rate.
The bathroom was gigantic (I do believe we had a wheelchair accessible room) - I did find the "open shower/no door" a little strange - but grew to like it over the 4 nights I stayed there.
Customer Service...a different story...I found 1 particular agent EXTREMELY RUDE and condescending. When I initially booked the room a week prior - I was told that the parking package I selected included valet parking and she was adding complimentary internet access. Upon receipt of my email confirmation of the reservation - I noticed that both Valet Parking and Internet access were noted as "add-ons" - I quickly called back - where she assured it was listed in the system. Unfortunately I took her word for this and didn't demand written confirmation so upon my arrival - I was notified that my package only included "self-parking" and internet is "never complimentary"
I gave up on the parking situation as the agent downstairs was completely unwilling to look into my concerns. As for the internet - I was referred to SHIRLEY (operations manager I believe?) who basically said "if you can't remember who you spoke to - we cant do anything about it now..." - I suggested she look into my initial booking and I'm sure she could at that point tell who was taking reservations in house that evening - she refused. As for the internet - she said "since you need and it seems to be a big deal to you - i'll do it for 50% off" - at this point I was tired of arguing to just accepted her terms...
Other than the one rude and condescending agent and Shirley - I have no other complaints and would definitely return - but on my next booking will be taking down names, times of conversations and demanding written confirmation of terms if they differ from the standard email...

title_masked: Decent for so close to Times Square
text_masked:
We had a junior suite which was a queen or king, with a fold-out couch. Bathroom was hugh. Bubbler bath (but bubbler didn't work) and a separate shower. We had to clal twice to have a refrigerator brought to the room. We also had to call to have the room safe opened. But other than that ,we had no problems with the service. The elevators (2) are small but again, not a big problem. 
The one complaint we had was not something the hotel could do anything about. We were on the side of the hotel next to a fire station. So we got to hear the siren each time they left the station. 
Overall we were happy with the hotel and very very happy with the proximity to Times Square, theaters, restaurants, etc.

I stayed here in early October for a few nights and really had a great stay. The staff were very friendly upon arrival and quickly got me checked in and to my room. The property is in fantastic condition. I was most shocked by the size of the rooms. The room, including the bathroom, were huge! the room was so clean and in such great condition that it felt brand new. I also appreciated the quality of the beds and linens. I really slept well while I was there. 
I had a breakfast and lunch at the hotel restaurants and also had room service one night. All the meals were good with above average service. It was also nice to have a Starbucks in the lobby for that early morning jolt. 
There is a nice selection of equipment in the fitness center, but the cardio equipment was always very popular in the mornings! Go really early or plan on a later morning workout if you want to do some cardio. 
I'd highly recommend this as a place to stay!

The room was more than I expected. Only one thing. Get some garbage disposal cleaners and use one after each guest leaves. It makes the room stink for a while. The disposal cleaners will take care of this small problem. The breakfast was great hot and fresh no powder eggs they were real !!!

We are having a great time in Chicago, so this is not just a review written by some disgruntled traveler. This is an honest assessment of this crappy, substandard hotel that we were unfortunate enough to have booked. Here is what we got:
First, in order to get a $40 per night discount on the room, we had to pay up front on the phone... two days and nights, unrefundable. Okay, so we did: $103 a night as opposed to $143. So the room was paid for and he HAD to stay there.
Finding the hotel was VERY difficult, even with a GPS. We had to use the GPS and call the front desk.... "we think we're in the area, but we're underground in what looks like a boiler room." "Yes, that's the parking area. Park and take the elevator up...." So we parked in this dingey, damp, VERY DANGEROUS looking underground roadway, and scurried to find an elevator to take us up before we were mugged, robbed, raped, and plundered.
So we get to the lobby... and keep in mind, we are, two casual acquaintances....and we had ordered a room with 2 double beds. NOPE! Although we paid in advance for our two double beds, the hotel had none. Instead, we HAD to take one king sized bed and a roll-away. We argued, begged, pleaded, etc. But there was nothing we could do. We paid in advance, so there was no refund...... and now we HAD to take the single bed and the roll-away. There was no alternative and the hotel guests made it VERY clear, almost to the point of anger.
The room had a dismal view of a parking lot. No mini fridge (you can get one, but it's $30 bucks more). The shower head WAS GREAT! The only thing that was good about this hotel. The WIFI costs $19. It is not free!
AND.... have you ever heard of a "continental breakfast" that costs $19 a person? Yep! No free breakfast here. 
This is really a crappy place! As I said, we are having a great time in Chicago. But this hotel is clearly a low low low point of our trip. This is a city filled with hotels. If you want to stay somewhere nice and accommodating......who won't pull a bait-and-switch, lock you in and give you something else, give you a room with a poor fiew, charge you for a fridge, wi fi, and breakfast, and give you poor service on top of it all, then YOU DO NOT WANT TO STAY AT THIS HOTEL!!!!!!!!!!!!

title_masked: Well located to explore SF from
text_masked:
I was in San Francisco to celebrate my birthday, and was happy to get an excellent rate at The Serrano. The hotel itself was a great place to stay as it was well situated for exploring San Francisco, and had many, many easily accessible transit routes. I was able to take BART in from the airport, and able to take transit to go to the Japanese Tea Garden, Fisherman's Wharf, Pier 33 (for an Alcatraz tour), and transit to and from restaurants at night. The Serrano is within easy walking distance to Union Square, and all the shopping and dining that area has to offer. A quick trip down Taylor (be warned, it doesn't take a long walk to get into the heart of the Tenderloin) took us to our favourite brunch place, Dotties on several mornings. 
All of the staff was friendly and helpful, however I'd like to mention that the concierge named [NAME] was amazing. When asked for walking instructions to the shops on Union Street (not Union Square), he suggested a great route along Polk where we were able to avoid marching up and down hills, and able to stop into a number of great shops along the way. When we complimented him on the excellent route the next morning, he told us it was his wife's favourite wandering route as well. 
Our room was lovely, and had a great number of electrical outlets. This might seem a strange thing to mention, but as someone who travels with an iphone, ipad, chargable camera batteries, and an ereader - it's amazing how many times I'm at a hotel with no where to charge my electronics without unplugging lamps, tv's or mini fridges! Way to go Serrano! :) The Serrano also placed me on a higher floor - which was much appreciated. A lovely view from the 16th floor. 
This is my 3rd stay at a Kimpton property, the other two were Ink48 in NYC and the Argonaut, also in SF. Of the 3 Kimptons I've stayed at, I'd rate this hotel as my second favourite after ink48. ink48 edges out the Serrano as the staff at ink48 went out of their way to provide me with a fantastic experience for my birthday last year (complimentary sparkling wine and pastries sent to my room, many suggestions of places to go celebrate, front desk recognizing me each time I came past, etc.); it was also my birthday when I stayed at the Serrano, and no special fuss was made for me. I guess this is the difference between a New York hotel, and one just about anywhere else in the world! :)
That being said, this certainly is a place I'd stay again the next time I head to San Francisco! The Argonaut is also fantastic, but as it's right on the Wharf, it is a little more difficult to manage as a base to explore the city.

We stayed here for a convention at the conference center (literally a stones throw across the train tracks). Overall had a good time although had some complications during the booking process as originally assured (twice) that we could have a rollaway bed in our room however right before arriving told this would not be possible. We were offered another room but this was a king rather then two beds so again not better for our party of three. We were however refunded promptly for the price difference and the staff tried their best. We loved the room - had a good view over petco park. The corridors are dark and a little confusing for some reason. The security in the hotel appears good (since at the w/e there appeared to be a big regular kind of pool party resulting in some 'worse-for-wear' scantility clad people riding the elevators...
Would definately stay here again when back in San Diego, for business or pleasure.

title_masked: Best Service I've Ever Had in NYC
text_masked: I stayed in the Sanctuary Hotel for three night for business. The staff were the most helpful and accommodating I have ever experienced in NYC. The concierge Brandon was a highlight. He went the extra length to help my colleague and I get tickets to a show and all his restaurant recommendations were exactly what we were looking for. The hotel itself was good as well. The room was clean and well laid out for an efficient use of space. The rooftop bar was beautiful and a hopping even on a Tuesday night. Also, you can't beat the location. Right off Times Square, but you would never know since the street is relatively quiet. I'll definitely be going back next time I'm in town...

I have stayed at this Hampton Inn four different times and continue to be more pleased each time. While everyone is welcome at this location, they cater especially to those going to the Mayo Clinic.
The rooms are clean and well appointed. We had a microwave and mini-fridge and were therefore able to save money during my visits to the Clinic. The television is a 32" flat screen with an excellent selection of programming.
They provide a substantial breakfast each morning - everything from yogurt, fruit, and coffee to steamers with eggs, sausage, and my personal favorite - scrambled eggs on half a bagel! It you have to fast before going to the Clinic, they have meals to take with you so that you have something to eat once you are able. Along with the fabulous breakfast, they also serve fresh baked cookies at 5PM! Yum! There is also a pantry in case you get a case of the hungries during the night.
As for the staff, they couldn't be friendlier or more accomodating. Checkin and out is quick. If you need something they will find it for you. Another outstanding service they provide is a shuttle back and forth to the Clinic! You let them know ahead of time what time you need to leave (on the half-hour) and they are ready. When your day is done at the Clinic just call the hotel and they will send the shuttle to pick you up. It certainly saves time, cost of valet parking, and provides the peace of mind of knowing that all you have to concern yourself with is what you will be doing at the clinic. If you plan your return right, the cookies will be fresh out of the oven upon your return!

We stayed here last week for two nights on the way home to Northern Ireland. This hotel was central to everything, in a lovely area of Boston, some other areas that we walked through I personally did not feel safe! We are a family of four (2adults & 2 children) and the room we were given was quite large, the bathroom was beautiful, heated towel rail, bath and shower and toiletries - nice smell for a change! Everything was really clean and it was a lovely touch to have turn down service at night. The mini fridge in the room was really handy, as was the coffee machine!!! All of the staff were very friendly and helpful, especially girl on reception. Only thing I would ask most hotels including this one to consider, is providing two king size beds when there are four people in a room, two doubles are not big enough especially when your children are tall!! I would have no hesitation to recommend this hotel and would stay here again.

After having this hotel booked through a conference organizers, we arrive to Boston only to know that we had a loss in the family. The hotel management immediately allows us to cancel the rest of our booked stay at no cost. We spent a night in the Back Bay. 
A spotless room with a fantastic, contemporary bathroom and very comfy bed. The view was to the other hotel's building, but they say that you cannot have everything, right?

Just had a wonderful stay at the NY Palace. Perfect location, excellent service, large and well appointed suite (junior/executive suite) with a gorgeous view of St. Patrick's Cathedral. If you go, be sure to stay in the Towers. It is well worth it, and the private lounge for Towers guests is so convenient for grabbing a quick breakfast or for meeting up for cocktails and snacks in the late afternoon and/or before dinner. 
If you can afford it, by all means splurge on a suite in the Towers. The Junior Suite is very nice and spacious. We started in a 1-Bedroom Corner Suite, which is HUGE, but unless you are planning to cook meals in the kitchen and entertain in the dining room it's wasted space. Furthermore, the hotel will not guarantee a cathedral view in the 1-Bedroom Corner Suite. They will only guarantee a cathedral view in a Junior Suite. Whatever room you book, be sure to request a cathedral view (facing the WEST side); otherwise. you might end up with a view of the inside of a boring office building!

I've no idea how this hotel has been rated so. I've also stayed here many times over the past few years, on business, purely on the basis of its location. The hotel is in an area that's predominantly offices and unfortunately as there's no other hotels close to Greenway Plaza, it holds the monopoly and thus, has no competition. 
This may explain the lack of investment? 
Yes, the bar area has had a refit and the CRT screens have finally been replaced from the bedrooms. But overall the hotel would be best suited to a museum dedicated to the early non-cool 80's retro. Simply awful! The rooms are large but the bathrooms are small and it's impossible to sleep with the aged and very noisy air conditioning switched on. There's no in-room minibars, little to no sound proofing nor simple things like soft close doors. The latter would prevent the constant noise of other guests allowing their room doors to bang close! The room service menu is very limited and i'd avoid the main restaurant for similar reasons. The gym is small and they've now closed the changing rooms and with it the sauna. The pool is fine but the landscaping, concrete. 
My colleagues and I have all decided that in future we'll be staying elsewhere. In pursuit of a restful and pleasant stay, an additional $10-20 a day on cab fares is a small price.

title_masked: pool rocks with super friendly staff
text_masked:
The new Qantas flights direct to Dallas from Sydney are a refreshing way to visit the US. The Omni is a great hotel for your stop over. It is new , with a fresh design and vibe. Located close to Dealy plaza for all JFK fans it is walking distance to the old part of town. 
The best part about the Omni is its terrific rooftop pool and bar. With soaring temperatures it is definitely the place to relax and take in spectacular city views. The bar staff are fantastic and really work hard to create a friendly , party atmosphere. Just as quick with clever wisecracks as they are with helpful insights on what to see and do in Dallas . I know the hotel reads these so make sure you look after cameron , Garry and Heath they are doing a great job for you up there
The Owners Box sports bar ialso has a great atmosphere with plenty of sports on show and possibly the worlds largest indoor screen.

title_masked: Good hotel in an excellent location
text_masked: The Westin on Market Street is very well located within walking distance of Union Square, and near 2 BART stops. Moreover the hop-on, hop-off tourist bus has a stop in front of the hotel. Spacious and clean rooms, and an excellent breakfast buffet. Adequate fitness room (but a bit small at peak hours). Professional and friendly staff. Good concierge service.

I stayed at the Seattle Sheraton recently while attending a conference. Having stayed there previously, I was looking forward to the experience. The hotel has a fantastic location in the middle of downtown Seattle, but the service quality left much to be desired. The check-in staff members were not the most helpful (bordering on the rude at times) and the reception phone wait was typically 1-3 minutes. I am a member of the Starwood club but that did not seem to make much of a difference in the allocation of the room or any other privileges. This Sheraton is not a patch on the Sheraton hotels in most parts of Asia!
Disappointed!

title_masked: Noisy place, unhelpful staff... it could have been great.
text_masked:
As many review mention, it is a family place.
So if you are not fond of kids running, screaming, etc... chose another place.
We asked for a top floor, and were told there was no availability (we checked in at 4pm...).
3 nights out of 4, we had to bear the noise of whoever running, jumping, in the room above us.
Called the front desk who casually replied they would look into it. Nothing happened.
And they boast a "guaranteed satisfaction" offer that was never presented to me.
If it had, I would have complained that for USD 175++, we could have received better treatment.
Location is perfect.
Staff is hardly polite and certainly no helpful.
Maybe because we are not Americans, so for them, a one-time guest not worth much.

title_masked: Great Value, excellant room layout for families.
text_masked: I agree with the reviewers who said the neighborhood isn't the best. However the hotel is in excellant condition and the staff was great. The breakfast was mediocre, but if you looked there was oatmeal, fruit, yogurt and hard boiled eggs. The room configuration was the best I've seen for a small room with 2 beds. The bathroom/shower was separate from the sink/sink bar and it was all hidden behind the wall with the beds. Ideal when some are still sleeping. Free parking in downtown Seattle is also a plus.

I was looking for a hotel for a weekend getaway with my fiance for our anniversary. Our intent was to do a lot of sightseeing and use the room as simply a place to crash. However, we wanted something nice enough that was clean and comfortable, with some nicer amenities. In NYC this can be hard to find for a reasonable rate. This hotel was everything we wanted. The staff was so nice, which is rare for NYC. Each floor has a bottled water station, where you can use provided empty water bottles to make your own to-go, or to have in your room. The bed was comfortable, and the hotel was quiet. The furnishings in the room were nice and modern. Everything was clean, too. The room was small, yes. But that is NYC, and who cares- when you arent there to be in the room anyhow? We got the smallest room they offer and it was just fine. The bathroom is small, but they made use of the space very well with shelving fixtures that allowed room for you to lay out all your things. 
One a separate note- they have been accommodating me very well with a problem I am having after my stay. Left a valuable piece of jewelry in the room unfortunately. The housekeeping manager is being very helpful in the investigation, and personally says she tore the whole vacuum bag apart to search for my missing item. I am upset b/c the piece is sentimental to me, but at least I am not being disregarded since I have already came and left the hotel. 
This hotel is exceptional for the price and is in a GREAT location, close to everything.

If you're looking for a reasonably priced hotel in Union Square and do not care about appearance or quality, this is the place. The building is very old, as are the windows which makes for very noisy nights. The bathrooms are very tiny with the sink in the room versus inside of the bathroom. This can, however, be a benefit if you're traveling with multiple people. We received no washcloths and the towels are dingy. The elevator is creaky and often takes several minutes to get where you're going. 
This hotel is great if you plan on spending very little time in the hotel, but don't expect any extra amenities, like shampoo, conditioner, coffee maker, etc.

We stayed here on a quick trip to Austin. Perfect location for what we were there for. Nice rooms, comfortable beds. The staff was extremely friendly. The manager's social that evening and breakfast the next morning hit the right spot. Will definitely stay here again when we are in the area.

How could we have missed this jewel of a place to stay in Seattle? In the past we have stayed in the downtown Seattle area, dodging the traffic, paying for tight parking; but Lake Union's Silver Cloud was tucked away close to downtown with FREE, secured parking and gorgeous views. We all loved the FANTASTIC work-out equipment and great morning breakfast! Room was comfortable and well-decorated. We definitely will stay here again on the next trip to Seattle!

title_masked: Great place for conference be careful of rooms
text_masked:
Attwnded a week long conference. Great facilities for meetings. Grounds are beautiful.
All hotel personnel are friendly,efficient, kind and helpful.
Room are another story.
Checked in 1hour early and told our room wouldn't be ready for 2hours.
Went back after the 2hours. Strangely enough, no one around and not busy.
Booked a king. Shown to a 2bed room that smelled very funky. Not a chair in the room . Just 2 beds and 2 benches and an armoire. It was in the royal palm tower.
Called down and asked for a king. This room was awful. The terrace and chairs overlooked a brick wall, the seats of the chairs were sprung so we had to put a pillow on them to sit without falling through. The bedspread was dirty and no blanket. The room overlooked the back of the conv center. We heard the garbage trucks and the hum of the refrigerated semis all night. We decided to check out at a $50 per day fine and at least have a decent place to stay. Remember we had to wait 2hours to get this room....The mgr at the desk was very kind and found us a beautiful room in the same bldg on the fist floor with a little patio. There was no comparison. My question is, why would they ever put someone in those rooms. The hotel was not full and we were paying $150 per night.
