Check in swift and smooth - room (14th floor) was a little dated but had a comfortable bed and hot working shower. Bathroom was VERY hot which in turn led to bedroom being too hot and we could not get the AC to work which was the only negative point. Used Edison Café for breakfast of which there was a wide choice and reasonably priced. 24hr Deli next door if you get peckish during the night. Did not have a lot of dealing with Reception staff except when we had to access our Safety Deposit box. Location was excellent but Times Square can be very expensive - all in all a pleasant stay and would recommend this hotel

Bayside Bungalow was great, nice and comfortable, wonderful view of Mission Bay
Close to Old Town San Diego
Walking distance to Sea World
Lots of activities
Nice Pools
A Bit Pricey
Guests were nice
Thanksgiving Weekend

My husband and I were part of a large wedding party staying at this property. 
Location: right off I-17. IHOP in walking distance. Restaurants and a huge Wal-Mart a mile away. Loved Mellow Mushroom for grinders, pizzas, pitas...
Check-in: easy.
Rooms: modern, nice furniture, large TV, wireless service. Only 60 rooms have a small fridge, so if you need one, ask for it in advance.
Workout room: small. 2 treadmills, 2 ellipticals and free weights
Pool: shared with neighboring hotel. Whirlpool. Chaise lounges have cushions (they need to be replaced), however, pool towels are accessible at the pool gate and will cover the cushions. If bringing beer, I would recommend cans and not glass. The front desk asked if the beer in my hand (glass) was from the pool...of course I said No. :) Smaller basketball court~basketball available at front desk.
Bar: Opens at 5pm. No food available.
Breakfast: not complimentary. Nice service though here! Buffet includes, eggs, bacon, oatmeal with fresh berries, waffle station, bagels, juices. 
Again, the customer service from every staff member was wonderful! Thank you, Grace, for all your efforts in finding out how much it would cost to clean my dress. The front desk called me to let me know the price FIRST and to see if I still wanted to have the dress pressed via their laundry service. So thoughtful to check with me first! And the front desk staff was always smiling!

I'm conflicted when it comes to my review for Distrikt Hotel. Part of me says this hotel was perfectly fine, clean, friendly staff. But the other part of me says the rooms were small, it's across from Port Authority and every 24hr Adult DVD store.
Hell's Kitchen has it's pluses, good spots to eat and not far from any of the Metro lines but I find for close to the same amount of money (which is expensive no matter where you stay) staying on the other side of 7th ave or on the Avenue of Americas side, let's say for example 44th and 5th is a nicer side with good hotels near Times Square.
When it comes to Distrikt Hotel overall I have nothing but good things to say. The staff was very friendly and helpful if I had any questions. Free coffee in the morning and tea in the afternoon. Checking in and out was smooth. Rooms are clean. One really nice feature that you won't find at too many other hotels is that they offer free 24hr use of brand new iMac computers in the lobby (big props for that). However as I mentioned before that the rooms are small including the bar on the ground floor. 
So I remain conflicted. Would I recommend Distrikt Hotel? Absolutely. It's an option while in Manhattan but I would explore my options next time on finding a hotel on the other end of Times Square as well.

I agree with what many of the other reviewers wrote. The beds were OK and the room size was adequate (though barely).Very good location (walkable to the theatre district, Penn Station, Empire State Building), but otherwise far from comfortable. Reception staff were neither friendly nor helpful. Room air conditioning was old, and the reception area, elevators, and corridors had no A/C, which was awful in the summer. Our bathroom sink was blocked. The breakfast area was very small and basic, which meant often having to wait for a free table in the morning. The breakfast itself was simple, but adequate. Ice machines, located only on some of the floors, were broken during most of the duration of my stay (5 days) despite reporting it to the reception. The T. V. channel guide in the room was completely wrong. Very long waits for the elevators and often when they finally arrived, they were too full to enter. I frequently walked up and down the four flights of stairs (whew!) The cleaners' cart was parked in the hall just outside our room from afternoon to morning. There were free phone calls allowed to anywhere in the U.S. Also there was a small room in the basement with 3 computers and a printer that guests could use free of charge, and there was also a fitness center downstairs which would be a nice bonus if I had had time to use it.
My mother and I paid around $200 per night for this 2-bed room, so it was no bargain. I wrote to the manager and did receive an apology from him, with an offer to give an upgrade or a discount during our next visit, but I would not stay at this place again.

title_masked: Many good points and a not so good. Overall not a bad experience.
text_masked:
Our family stayed at this motel at the first of July 2012.
My first impression was terrible, the place doesn't look like much from the road and it is only feet from I5 ! When we first arrived and went to our room the airconditioner was on the fritz but the management was able to quickly resolve the problem, the AC unit couldn't be fixed so they moved us to another room, no problems.
The amenities turned out to be quite nice, hot tub and pool were nice, and breakfast was just good, plenty to go around. The other nice touch was the small convienience store in the lobby, this turned out to be just the place to get our late night ice cream fix !
This place seems a bit out of the way at first but we quickly learned that old town San Diego ( we had never heard of it before our trip ) was within easy walking distance and a lot of fun, Mission Beach and Belmont Park were a short drive ( just past Sea World ), and the drive to the zoo took us about ten minutes.
I would definately reccomend this motel for a fun family stay.

My husband and I stayed at the Shoreham for a long weekend in January and found it to be a very pleasant experience. We arrived earlier than anticipated and we were able to check into our room early. The staff was unobtrusive yet accommodating -- we were offered a glass of champagne or bottle of water upon checking in and whenever we had any questions, they were more than helpful. We had a king room that included a massage chair and although the room was small - it was just what we needed in the city. The room itself was very clean and had a modern, minimalist feel. The hotel is just a few blocks away from Times Square, Rockefeller Center and the MOMA. I would definitely stay in this hotel again.

The Congress Plaza was originally an annex to the Columbia Exposition of 1893. The lobby is magnificent. Since the 19th century, we have had microfridges and microwaves, but not in the Congress. One would have liked bright lighting in rooms and corridors, nice views from the windows, and quiet air conditioning, all absent. From our room, we saw the fire escapes.
On the plus side, there are excellent breakfasts and, on site, the very good Rafael restaurant. For its location, the Congress’s $220, inclusive of tax, for a triple is quite nice. It fronts on Michigan Avenue and is steps away from Buckingham Fountain and State Street.
If you need central location for a moderate price, you might overlook the drawbacks. If price is no object, consider the nearby Hilton, for example.

I had a fantastic experience at the Andaz Wall Street. As a Diamond, I have high expectations of Hyatt properties, and my experience has exceeded my expectations across visits. 
From the friendly greeting in the lobby from the staff member who remembered me, to a special upgrade in recognition of my birthday, to friendly and attentive staff at the Wall & Water restaurant (who also remembered me), I have had an excellent experience.
The rooms themselves are big and modern (I had an incredible suite on the most recent stay, but have also had very nice "standard" rooms), and the location is good downtown. The concept is also great (e.g., free minibar) -- and they had a helpful running map for my 7-mile run along the East River.
One nit: the complementary Diamond breakfast ($50 credit) needs to be taken in the restaurant, and cannot be applied to room service (unlike the Andaz 5th Avenue, for example). 
I am very much looking forward to my next stay.

We stayed at the Wyndham for 3 nights in October. The hotel is very old-world and cozy. There were several minor concerns with the room and they were dealt with extremely quickly to our satisfaction. The Peabody Conservatory of Music and the Walters art museum were quite close, as were some good restaurants, including George's in the hotel

This is a wonderfull hotel and a relief from all the straight concrete hotels you can find anywhere else. History can be found in any corner of the hotel and the ducks are the real star guests, an attraction on itselfs with star arrogance of the duck themselves.
Rooms are a bit dated in terms of size (especially bathroom) but comfortable. Lobby is splendid although a bit dark as everywhere in the hotel.
Definitely worthwile a detour to stay here.

Had the one bedroom apartment, the separate living area works really well if your other half is to bed early. The kitchen is great for having your own breakfast, you would be hard pressed to cook a proper meal given the limited cooking utensils. Having said that Fairway across the road have some fabulous fresh pre packaged meals that you can microwave. The liquor store close by has an amazing selection of wines, plus lots of cold ones if you are in a hurry. The air con is noisy, we just simply switched it off which may not be an option in summer/winter. The lifts are slow at busy periods, some times I just walked the 11 floors (to keep fit!). The laundry on level 7 is an absolute winner if you are travelling on, as we were. If you are going to Newark airport, ask the concierge to book you the shuttle bus, it's far cheaper than the metered taxi. Great location, just a bit more upmarket feel about it, compared to downtown.
Only gripe was booked months prior, and asked to be as high as possible, but ended up on level 11.

I wrote this great long review in all capital letters and then it was rejected because I used capital letters -- I use them because I am a terrible typist and have arthritis. So I am not typing all of that again -- yell at Trip Advisor. So to be blunt the place is great for the single traveler a step or two above hostel, and three steps below the Four Seasons. I don't have the energy to type the rest.

My husband and I spent 2 nights November 18/19th in a superior queen.Why is everyone so surprised at the small rooms? Doesn't anyone "google" before they go? We went expecting small but I asked for a corner unit and they obliged us - 2 windows makes a difference. If you are getting a Priceline DEAL: (as we say in kindergarten) "you get what you get and you don't get upset" The breakfast coffee was $4.00 but it was delicious and served in a large cup.Wonderful ambiance in the library with the fireplace and New York Times - I loved it! So glad this wasn't another cookie-cutter hotel, we were well received at reception, and at baggage storage.The design elements of the room were very well done and, if you need drawers and extra hanging space for 2 - 3 days, you've packed way too much. Plasma T.V. was a real treat.
Rented bikes just east of hotel and did Central Park Loop 6.4 miles in 1 hour - I'm 65 and I was wearing a skirt. What a joy it was! We will most definitely return.

We booked the Omni through Hotwire and got a good deal for a Saturday night stay. The location is fabulous- between 5th and 4th close to shopping and strolling The Avenue. The staff was excellent and very solicitious. Our room was elegant, clean, a calm decor with lovely marble bathroom (only problem was the tub stopper was faulty) The bathrobes are super soft and luxurious. We were surprised not to have a free paper delivered at the door in the morning. We didn't eat there. It was a super deal. We'd do it again!

I could just copy the comment of drwn, two posts down! 
We also got a deal on Priceline which was about 75$. And that's a fair price for this hotel which isn't that bad as some reviewers stated. On the other hand if i would have payed over 100$, i would have expected more for my money.
It's a little older, but it's clean, has a friendly staff and free coffee in the lobby, which we drank at their courtyard-gazebo in the morning.
We thought for the money we payed, it was ok, and since we were visiting Easton Center, the location was ok aswell.

My partner and I had a very comfortable and easy stay (4 nights) here and highly recommend it to the cost-conscious traveler. Super clean, well run, good service, and the bathrooms down the hall were no problem at all: no waiting ever, clean and modern. The room itself was bare bones (no closet, no sink counter, no microwave) but the bed was comfortable and they provided lots of pillows when we asked for them.

I have just arrived back from the US i went to stay in Seattle first then down to San Fran for 7 days i arrived in this hole and booked into another hotel, it smelt the bed linen was dirty and no room at all, the web site does not show the true Hotel Fusion, i have no idea where those rooms are because the people we spoke with all said that there rooms were small, i stayed across the road at the Parc 55 at a massive cost but onto the travel agent .......great location but that is it

If you are looking to explore all that DC has to offer you can't get a better location than L'enfant. That being said I was disappointed in the lack of modernization of the rooms.Somethings cannot be addressed without extensive renovations however there are things that can be done to make it appear "fresh". The chrome was worn off of the bathroom faucet and the floor tile was out dated and the grout was dirty. The grout around the sink was peeling. The shower preasure was very weak and I use low pressure heads in my home. The toilet had to be flushed twice just to get the paper to go down. For $300.00 a night I would expect there to be more than just the local stations available on TV for free. It looked like to was hooked up to an antennae (fuzzy). And $10.00 a day for wifi come on! Don't get me started about the plastic cups in the rooms. Even the Ramada gives you real glass. This may sound picky but if a hotel wants a 4 star rating it should prvide 4 star amenities. We booked 3 rooms 2 months in advance and they couldn't even provide a king or queen in any of them.

title_masked: Great location for Inner Harbor visit
text_masked:
Completed our second stay at this Homewood; we're Hilton HHonors members and this is a particularly unique Homewood, sharing the building with the Hilton Garden Inn. Super location at the east end of Inner Harbor, next to Little Italy. Everything harbor-related is walkable, including Orioles Park. (We were on a Red Sox Road Trip.)
Panoramic view suites are amazingly large - apartment sized large. We had one last year; this time we opted for a standard 1BR suite and were fortunate to get 1153, at the end of the hall. This suite has a "corner" feel like the panoramic suites, with I think an even better view (partial water view from the bedroom and living room.) The woodwork was a little worn - could use new varnish - but kitchen counters and breakfast bar looked relatively new. The suite was immaculately clean and the linens were in good shape. Good HDTVs, comfy sofa and chair, big windows to enjoy the harbor and city views. Fluffiest, softest towels of any Hilton property we've used before. Soft but comfortable mattress, and about 10 pillows (why can't you get standard poly fill pillows at Hiltons? They're always those goofy down or fake down squishy types. Hate 'em. Minor quibble.)
Right now the breakfast lounge is out of service for renovations (on our last stay it was closed due to water damage - maybe we're bad luck.) This currently works in guests' favor, as breakfast for both Homewood and Hilton Garden Inn are being served in the HGI's restaurant area. The cooked-to-order eggs, waffles, pancakes etc. that HGI guests pay for were complimentary for Homewood guests due to the change (the standard Homewood buffet should be back in their own lounge by mid-June.) Breakfast choices were of a little better quality than in other Homewoods, except for the coffee which was just as awful as always. (Don't panic. There's a Starbucks steps away from the lobby.) The staff was extremely friendly, as always. We didn't use the "light supper" of pasta, salad, beer/wine and soft drinks - went to the ball game instead. That's served Monday-Thursday and the menu is posted on each suite's fridge.
This time we skipped the $22 self- and $34-valet parking and used the open air lot a block away, on the corner of Eastern and President (heading towards the hotel on President, turn Left on Eastern and immediately left into the lot.) We paid $24 total for Sunday 4PM through Tuesday 9AM. The lot is monitored but not manned 24/7 - there's an honor box for when nobody's there, with posted rates. Remove all valuables from the car, as you should anywhere.
The hotel has an agreement with the Maryland Athletic Club rather than its own pool/exercise room. I used the club for cardio equipment and my husband used the lap pool. The club is open early AM (5:30 I think during the week) and the staff was very welcoming and friendly. Hotel guests enter the club from the 2nd floor (the HGI side,) check in at the desk and can use any of the equipment as well as attending classes, space permitting. They ask you to not use the members' locker rooms, and let members fill the classes first, but otherwise it's full access. Loads of new equipment in excellent condition. Although the pools are specifically for laps or pool aerobics, families can (and did) use them, but logistically it's a little odd - club towels can't be removed, and it's a long walk. A more family-friendly feature is the Harbor East movie complex on the other side of the health club, with digital screens and discount matinees. And there's a Haagen Daz on the other side of theater. Ice cream and a movie, with a white chocolate latte after? Now that's a great hotel location!
This continues to be one of our favorite Homewood properties, for location and staff friendliness. Considering it's a major city location, you get a lot for your money. Highly recommend this hotel for anyone looking for a suite-style property in downtown/Inner Harbor area.

Pleasant and helpful staff, clean and spacious rooms, incredible location. Deco style lobby, property is not luxurious but very functional. Safe and quiet street. We stay a week at a time and are repeat guests - pretty sure there is not a better price-weighted value in Hollywood or Los Angeles.

title_masked: Great Hotel in the Heart of San Antonio
text_masked: This property is a cut above the rest. From the time you enter the valet area to when you end your stay you are surrounded with professionalism and warmness. The workout facility has a great view of the pool and has a good amount of equiptment. Although it was raining both times I stayed, the pool looked inviting. I loved the live harpist during the "Happy Hour" time during the week. This is one of my favorite places to stay on the Riverwalk!

title_masked: Great stay in King Spa Room
text_masked:
This was a wonderful hotel. I stayed at the Palomar for 2 nights for a mini staycation. I booked a King Spa room, getting a discounted rate because of my Kimpton InTouch membership. Just prior to my stay, Ashley from the Palomar emailed me to ask if I had any special requests and if it was a special occasion. I informed her that I was celebrating my birthday, and also asked for a DVD player and early check-in. I was actually unable to check in much earlier, but only because the staff was trying very hard to get me a specific room and it wasn't ready when I got there. After I told them that I would take any room, as I had to be somewhere shortly, they quickly scrambled and checked me in to a different room. The DVD player was installed and the maintenance man helpfully explained how to run the machine. They also sent up a bottle of champagne for my birthday, which was a lovely touch.
The room was very spacious. I gathered with four friends in the room before going out for dinner and there was plenty of space in the sitting area. Wonderfully comfortable bed, and the room was very quiet, too (a must for me). There were lots of kids and dogs in the hotel, and there is a lot of traffic outside, but I wasn't bothered by any of it (fyi, I was on the 10th floor, so this may have helped with the noise of the traffic). Also, I LOVED the blackout curtains - made it easier to sleep in in the morning. The deep soaking tub was awesome. The room also had a large, separate shower.
The wine hour is very nice; I believe this is done at all of the Kimpton hotels. The workout room was very clean and well-equiped. There is also an indoor pool, but I didn't have time to try it out.
The staff was very helpful. Housekeeping was unobtrusive and thorough. I mentioned to Ashley that I was thinking of trying Yolk for brunch; she told me to tell them that I was staying at the Palomar because the hotel had preferred seating there - totally worked, we didn't have to wait at all to be seated. I read other reviews about the front desk area being chaotic, but I checked out on a Monday and did not have any problems. 
I really liked the location of the hotel, too - close enough to lots of shopping (another must for me) but without being right in the middle of crazy Michigan Ave. Also, there are lots of dining and bar options nearby.
Side note on parking: I didn't park at the hotel, but used SpotHero.com to reserve a spot at the garage kitty-corner from the hotel. I bought 48 hours of parking for less than the cost of one day at the hotel (It was my first time using this service so I wasn't sure what to expect, but everything went smoothly). 
My only teeny tiny quibble during the entire weekend was with the TV remote - it had no numbers and I could only scroll through the channels in one direction. But you're not supposed to waste your vacation watching TV, so it wasn't a big deal.
I've also stayed at the Palomar in DC (which is what prompted me to check out this hotel) and had a great experience there, too. I've become a big fan of the Kimpton hotels. Hoping to check in to another one for my next birthday, whether it's in Chicago or elsewhere!

title_masked: Great hotel close to sights in Baltimore.
text_masked: My husband and I were visiting Baltimore and had a hard time finding the hotel and the staff at the front desk was very pleasant in getting us there. We were also given maps to get to other locations when we checked in. We also request a refrigerator if staying more than a weekend and this was the first time it was actually in the room on arrival instead of having to wait as we've done in other hotels. It was very clean as was the rest of the room too. As another reviewer said the only complaint is the lack of space to put your things in the bathroom. In other Hampton Inns there's usually shelves under the sink but this one didn't have them. Otherwise the breakfast was great; the staff always greeted us and the hotel looked very clean and bright everywhere Also it was Memorial Day weekend and the pool was open outside and the whole pool area was very clean. We also liked the location as it's close for sightseeing in Baltimore which we did that weekend. Overall we were pleased and would stay at this hotel again.

We stayed at the Hampton Inn DT location for my husband's brother's wedding. The hotel is within walking distance to the Lady Bird Trail and good restaurants ( Max's Wine Dive is across the street, the Whole Foods flagship is about a 15 minute walk away!).
Breakfast is pretty good (watch out for the business suit vultures at 7am) and they have a veranda on the same floor so you can have your breakfast outside. The construction next door served as a welcome distraction during breakfast so our very vocal one year old did not disturb anyone as we ate on the veranda.
We were on the 7th floor and it was perfectly quiet. I found the rooms to be clean and the staff very courteous. The hotel has an actual crib and not a pack and play for those parties needing a crib.
ABOUT PARKING: Seriously people, a 24 hour garage is literally right across the street for $11/day. It may not be come and go parking, but it's cheap and you can walk everywhere you need to go. Also meters are all over the street by the hotel. Why people pay the $23/day fee is beyond me.

This is our favorite place to stay when we come to Chicago. Its close to Midway airport, if you want to go into the city you can get the shuttle to take you to the airport and then take the orange line into the city. 
Rooms are very spacious, comfortable and very clean. Also, very quiet since its right by the airport. 
The staff is always friendly and helpful.
The hotel is connected to the TGI Fridays, just a simple walk through the lobby and you are in the restaurant. 
I highly recommend this hotel.

Location can't be beat-just cross a quiet back street and you're at the hollywood and highland ctr. Ctr has numerous shops and great eateries (starbucks as well) After walking through the Ctr you are on Hollywood Blvd. Manns Theater is also attached to Ctr, Walk of Fame also.
The hotel itself is a little dated as far as decor goes, however, the rooms are very clean. Actually they are more like suites than rooms, with full kitchens-micro, fridge, stove. Our room had a living area with sofa bed, kitchen/dining area, bathroom, and separate bedroom. Bedroom and living room each had tv. A/C was fine. Pool was clean. Breakfast was nothing fancy, but adequate-cereal, fruit bagels, juice coffee, yogurt, etc.. Staff was friendly and helpful.
Also impressive was security-need key to enter front door and secure underground FREE parking.

I had read a lot of bad reviews on this hotel and was not looking fowdard to staying ,got a surprise nice hotel ,mostly nice staff ,nice room ,very clean, ,wifi free in public arera s .No tea and coffee makers in room very dissapointed .when portor put away your bag on check out from just outside left luggage door he had his hand out for a tip and when you went back to collect you ware also expted to let a tip .Great that the hotel is so near to every thing

The Wharf Inn has free parking for guests, compared to hotels in the fisherman's Wharf area charging $30 to $50 per day. The rates are reasonable but the sound proofing from the street is non-existing. I was told I had a partial view of Fisherman's Wharf, and a partial view of downtown San Francisco. The first view was the upper part aof a stored crane, the other the top of the trans america spire. My 100% view was of a hot spuds across the street border by a 24 hour 7-11. The street people evidentally start looking for coffee around 4 am, and the 7-11 is most accomidating. A few screaming matches, followed by threates, but no blows were landed. Could use some sound proofing on the balconey door.
nice situated. Very good rooms. Free Internet. Close to Brodway and to many intersting places . The service is nice and the reception clerk is very polite and ccooprative

Stayed here as it is on my favorite shopping street in Los Angeles. For me, fabulous location.
Website promises a European boutique experience. I understand the hotel has been gradually upgrading itself. There are definitely some things that still need work, but bottom line I'd probably stay again.
First, the staff was fantastic. I had several phone calls before asking for advice renting a car in the are - they were very patient and helpful. Once at the hotel every person I dealt with at the front desk and valet desk was excellent. They clearly try and that is greatly appreciated and noted.
The first impression is not great - when you get off the elevator, the corridor is somewhat dark and institutional looking. A spiff up would help greatly. The door key mechanism is old-style, reinforcing the impression that you are in a place that needs an update.
Our room was pretty good size and comfortable. It appeared to me like there were some recent updates (the bathroom looked really nice) with some legacy items left (the light switches throughout the room looked like something from the 70s). Comfortable bathrobes and nice soaps/shampoos etc.
Bed was decently comfortable and while the pillows were far too firm, housekeeping brought up much better (softer) pillows in a matter of minutes. Nice small couch and plenty of shelf and closet space. Good coffeemaker. Our room (#205) had a small balcony right over West 3rd Street - great for people watching (and they can't see you!). There is a bit of street noise (didn't bother me at all), so light sleepers might prefer a room on the Orlando Street side. 
Wi-fi in the room was frustratingly weak/spotty - we were here for the weekend so it wasn't too much of an issue but I'd be annoyed if I was trying to get some serious work done.
On the 2nd floor, the hallway area near the elevator several times picked up the food odors from the restaurant. I wouldn't want to be staying in the few rooms right near the elevator. The smell did not make it through the fire doors and we didn't notice it in our room.
The fitness center is small (three piece of equipment) but they are brand new, with great TVs to boot. Room looked like it had recently been recarpeted. Very nice, though if there were a lot of people using the gym you'd be out of luck (I was the only one in there the two times I used it so this may not be an issue).
Overall the hotel worked for us and my impressions got better as time went on.

We have just returned from new york and stayed in the Affinia for a week 12th jan to 19th jan 2012 this was our second time staying at the hotel and the staff and hotel are amazing, nothing was to much trouble for any of them, my daughter celebrated her 21st birthday whilst we were there and her boyfriend proposed to her :), the time and effort the hotel staff put into making there room special for them is beyond words, rose petals and champagne and chocolate layed out beautifully in there room was a lovely suprise, we enjoyed a lovely meal in the nile restaurant aswell, we will be staying here again, thanks agian to all the staff x

title_masked: Great Location, Good Staff, Nice but Dated Rooms
text_masked:
Had a wonderful stay in Washington DC from July 27th to July 29th. The Hotel Lombardy is good hotel that sees itself upgraded to a VERY good hotel because its location is simply amazing. The Hotel is within walking distance of the White House, Treasury Building, and Eisenhower Executive Building. It is also within walking distances of tons of restaurants including Founding Farmers, The Bottom Line, Cafe Asia, Bertucci's, Friday's, ConE Island, The Prime Rib, etc. (there are tons of restaurants). The National Mall is a bit of a longer walk, but we did it on 95 degree days and got there with no problem. In the spring or fall it would be more than walkable. If you do not want to walk all the way to the mall or other attractions the hotel is within walking range of 3 different metro lines. 
As far as our actually stay at the hotel we arrived from Amtrak at Union station around 12:00 (check-in is at 3:00 PM) and were promptly upgraded from a Executive Parkview Room to a suite in room 803. The suite was a very nice upgrade and provided an extremely large amount of room with a living room overlooking Pennsylvania Avenue. The room and bathroom were very clean and we had no issues in that regard. As far as street noise, I did not really hear anything particularly noticeable (I am from NYC though). We did hear some sirens but I wouldn't expect to not hear them. The floor boards from the room above us did seem to creak a little, but again nothing that I think I would have even notice had I not read it on reviews here before our stay.
The bed was extremely comfortable. However, many, including my co-traveler would probably find the pillows too thick. 
Throughout our stay the staff was attentive to our needs and happy to answer questions about DC attractions and amenities within the hotel. All appeared to be happy to be at work and that was much appreciated. 
Now for some negatives. The bathroom in this suite was EXTREMELY small. I would say that the door to open the bathroom had less then 2 inches of clearance from the toilet bowl. The shower was equally as small and was mad worse by the fact that the water pressure was extremely low.
The television's were nice but did not feature the typical hotel features (movies on-demand, viewing of your bill/checkout, etc.) 
The suite lacked a "hotel" feel because of the furniture selections. It feels very much like an apartment, which many will like. I appreciated this and do not really see it as a negative but I am partial to a slightly more hotel feel. 
Unfortunately, we did not receive turndown service or complimentary waters the second night of our stay. We also had an issue with the wake up call and did not receive a wake up call for the second night. 
Overall, I would not hesitate to stay at the Hotel Lombardy again especially at the excellent rate that we received ($111 per night). If such a discount was not available I would probably shop around again but would definitely consider the Hotel Lombardy.

I am in New York for work multiple times a year and love when I am able to stay in this place. Most hotel rooms in the city are quite small - not Trump SoHo. The rooms are fabulous and big. The bathroom is also quite spacious. The staff is extremely helpful and will do anything to make your stay better. The neighborhood is also great with a lot to do within walking distance. Everything about this place is 5 star.

Thank you to all at the Embassy Suites for making our stay in Washington DC memorable. In spite of a late night arrival we were greeted with enthusiasm and care. The location is perfect for hearty walks to downtown, the national mall, and Georgetown (Clyde's is just a short walk away) and we can't say enough about the benefits of the manager's reception and full breakfast. After a long day of trekking through DC we always looked forward to relaxing at the Embassy Suites.

We spent 2 nights (Friday and Saturday) there and had a room overlooking the parking lot below. The parking lot that charges $22 per night... I don't know why people say it includes breakfast. It doesn't and we booked straight through the hotel. Not any fancy online sights. The room is tiny, the bathroom even smaller. The towels had blood stains on them. They knew we were a family and only put 3 towels in the bathroom and one of each soap. You could hear the trains nearby. San Diego is such a beautiful place. Spend your money elsewhere.

title_masked: Bad service, good price, no parking
text_masked: Breakfast was cool, all the rooms smelled like water got on the carpet and soaked it. Pool was in a corner and had a camera pointed right on it, which felt weird if the front desk was watching my girlfriend in a bikini... but I think the worst part of my stay is when the front desk called me an HOUR before checkout to REMIND me that checkout is at 11am. What a jerk. Hotel rate was great for a walk-in on a Saturday though. I was just offended as hell when I had to jump out of the shower to answer the phone after the 90th ring for the front desk guy to tell me to leave when I KNOW when checkout is. Oh yeah and the bed was broken. And theres only about 10 parking spots for all of the rooms, on a first come first served basis so don't plan on going anywhere.

I recently stayed with my fiance at the Holiday Inn Express. We loved the location, the staff was incredibly kind and the free breakfast was a plus. The rooms are teeny tiny, but perfect for people who don't plan on staying in the hotel for a long period of time. I think the prices should be lower per night, but I guess you are paying for location, not the actual quality of the room.

There are some hotels that are just too hip for their own good. Dream is elegant and modern, but not too over the top hipster. It's not cheap, but it is lush and comfortable. The whole place has a feeling of decadent romance due to the materials used...fabrics, wood, steel. All very well executed.

rooms clean, modern and the bathroom was wonderful. the toiletries included things like fingernail files (good ones.) when I asked the concierge where I might buy contact solution, he pulled some out of the closet behind the front desk. 
room service was fast and the food was great. the 'light' menu is amazingly flavorful and filling with calories listed on the menu.
my friend was asked to wait 15 min bec. his room wasn't ready. they upgraded him to a suite as an apology.

I have stayed at this hotel in the past and vowed that I never would again. it was getting very run down. But the location is excellent! So when I saw that they had undergone a major renovation, I decided to give it another try. I have to say my room was renovated and much nicer than the last time I stayed. However the bathroom was somewhat dirty and didn't look like the cleaning crew had done a very thorough job. 
To me the worst part of this hotel was the concierge service. The lady was not very nice and definitely not very helpful. I found that to be very disappointing since when I am in NYC, I usually rely on the concierge to guide me. I do like the fact that this hotel has a doorman and he always helps you get a cab. Overall the only reason I can see to stay at this hotel is because of the location. The rooms are typical NYC, very small! And very sparse!!

Stayed here with family of five for four nights in August. Requested high floor as research seemed to indicate this would be good choice to avoid street noise. Room was quiet. Only drawback of high floor was somewhat slower elevator service at peak times, but no big deal. Had a room with pull out sofa and separate living area made feel somewhat roomy despite five of us. Location is great. Close to many attractions and also easy walk to Clark/Lake or Grand on Red Line for CTA. I parked car out at Cumberland after unloading and saved over $100 for overall parking bill. Slight hassle but paid for a dinner for my crew so worth it! Breakfast spread was excellent and re-stocked often. Got crowded but to be expected at peak time. All of staff were very friendly and we had no issues at all for length of our stay. If we come back to visit Chicago, would definitely stay here again!

title_masked: Very Convenient for San Diego Marathon
text_masked:
I stayed at the Hampton Inn last weekend for the SD marathon and I wanted to provide some feedback. Having the shuttle to and from the race was great! I did not have to rent a car and it was just one less thing to worry about on race day. The special breakfast on Sunday was also very nice, again - one less thing to worry about as eating before the race is very important. I appreciate being given a 1:30pm check out so that I could quickly shower after the 1pm shuttle brought me back to the hotel. That is very key for me - I was traveling later in the day Sunday and being able to shower as soon as I can after the race is very important to me. It was nice not to have to travel still sweaty and gross from the race.
One suggestion for improvement would be to also offer a shuttle to/from the expo on Saturday. The walk to Old Town and the trolley was not all that far, but the day before a marathon, I try to walk as little as possible.

title_masked: The Best Hotel - El Mejor de NYC!
text_masked:
I stayed here with family and we loved it so much! Everything is so nice and bright and clean. Everyone is so friendly and nice, they give you anything you want here! We ask for a higher room and Simone gave it to my family no questions! She is so nice and funny, she really treats you as if you were a star, my mother adored her most. At night, we always talk to Noe and he will spend time with you to make sure everything is okay, he made maps for us through the computer, he teach me how to call home to Ecuador and he is so cool to talk to!
We had no complaints! Both my brother and mother loved it, and we think its really cool how so many people there speak everyone's language. Our room always clean, at this hotel, they will really spoil you. We not wanted to leave, but we will be returning for sure!

Extremely clean, friendly staff, large rooms, lots of restaurants outside the door, beautiful pool area, centrally located....would definitely stay here again! My only complaint is that parking is pricey.

title_masked: Great option if going to Arlington attractions
text_masked: Booked hotel based on great price and proximity to Arlington. I had tickets to attend a Rangers game 7/23 and was not thrilled with the hotels available in Arlington. I always check the reviews that others post on trip advisor, and the rooms available in Arlington seemed too expensive based on the reviews. I also had no desire to be in a hotel near Six Flags that would have lots of kids running over my head at night. This Holiday Inn is great! All staff very professional and accommodating. Common areas clean and well decorated. Prior to arrival, I had requested a room on the top floor away from the elevator and that was what I got. Room was large, modern fixtures, comfortable bed and furniture, very large walk-in shower. Room also had a microwave and small fridge, which was totally unexpected. The only problems I had were housekeeping issues. I had asked for extra pillows, but due to late check in, only the hotel driver could get them for me and when delivered, they had no pillowcases. On our 2nd day, housekeeping did not touch our room, so no clean towels and no pillowcases. The hotel manager said he would credit my priority club account 500 extra points for this inconvenience but it was not done. If you are a priority club member, you do get a voucher for a free sundry and a free drink at the bar. Overall, a great hotel for the money.

Me and my friend stayed at this hotel last week, we were looking for a room with 2 beds, which was more difficult to find than we had anticipated. Compared to similar hotels at the time it was also reasonable priced.
The rooms are the standard new york size, but clean and big shower. The location was perfect for us because we could walk nearly everywhere and in the evenings was easy to get taxis to go to restaurants. 
There is a Whole Foods opposite and Penn station is only a 5 min walk away. 
The staff were always helful and friendly.
The only very small problem is that somejtimes you have to wait a while for the lift.
At the right price will definitely consider staying here again.

I'm reading these reviews, and I'm wondering if these people are corporate travelers (who actually know what to expect), or occasional travelers who have no idea what to expect when traveling. I was here for a conference across the street at a 4 star hotel ($129.rack rate with $22. daily internet fee and $22. daily garage fee). This 4 star had no fridge and no microwave. For all of the people who are commenting on the free, let me repeat, FREE continental breakfast there are several restaurants in the area. For $50./night, be glad they're giving you the free coffee in the lobby (once again, the 4 star doesn't). I found the continental breakfast to be absolutely fine. There were cereals, breakfast beverages, fruit, pastries, and a hot item daily (usually scrambled eggs). There was also an attendant who would make a "made to order" omlette for $1.99. $1.99, REALLY? You couldn't buy the items and make it yourself for that. Now....on to the room. When we arrived, we were expecting marginal service due to these reviews. There was a very pleasant young lady who checked us in and there were no issues. She did have us sign a damage waiver. It is not uncommon to be charged for things you steal or damage and I admire them for clearing this up in advance. EVERY hotel is going to charge your credit card at check-in for incidentals and other fees, (once again, the occasional traveler doesn't know this). Once we got into the room, we were impressed. The room was clean, had a new flat panel TV just recently installed, the down comforter was nice, the desk, nightstand and entertainment center were actually wood (not pressboard junk). The desk had top facing outlets for internet (wifi was free). I checked out the bathroom to make sure the tub was ok after seeing these reviews. The tub was spotless and was actually the heavier porcelain and NOT the cheap hotel junk that eventually cracks & grows mildew. The towels were spotless, and the ceramic floors were spotless. I never once felt "unsafe" as they have onsite security. The people at the desk, as well as the people in the restaurant in the morning were helpful and very courteous. If you are looking for a good, clean room at a WONDERFUL price, this is it. I plan to attend the same conference next year and I will absolutely come back. For anyone who doesn't understand that free means "FREE", there are many restaurants in the area. The hotel doesn't HAVE to offer anything in the morning. I think it's a nice touch. They're trying to do a little extra for their guests and I see that it's causing them more problems than if they didn't offer anything at all. People who don't travel have unrealistic expectations for both hotels AND airlines. These will be the same people fussing about lines at the airport and having to suffer a bag of "peanuts" after the airline itinerary stated they would get an in cabin "snack". 
An absolutely wonderful stay!

Stayed at the Setai for one week . Booked a Capella King Room and got upgraded to the Capella king with view of Empire State Bld. Wether you had the view or not would not bother me but do ask for a high floor, you will still hear some noise from the street but it's that buzzy sort of NY noise that you learn to appreciate after a while.this Hotel is absolutely First Class in every way. The rooms are Huge by New York standards and the modern decor is very classy. Beds are ultra comfortable, the women will love the massive wardrobe and bathroom and everything you can ask for is in the room, nespresso coffee machine , fridge full of complimentary sodas , water etc... After walking the streets of New York all day it is an absolute delight to come back to this fantastic room. Being a relatively new hotel every conceivable thing is new and works . Internet is free and fast. The gym is well appointed , plenty of brand new equipment, free water and fruit.we did not dine in the hotel there are just too many other great places to eat in New York. We did have room service one evening and it was absolutely delicious. What really makes this hotel is the staff. They are genuine, friendly , courteous and treat everyone with a warm smile. From the doorman to the front desk to concierge, the cleaning staff, the charming man who fills your fridge up every day. I could not say how pleasant they all are . The management of this hotel are doing a wonderful job and everyone should be congratulated . In nNew York you get what you pay for so don't be put off by having to pay $700-$850 a night for these types of rooms , they are worth every cent.thankyou Setai , we will definitely be staying here again when we come to New York.

The rooms are spacious, the kitchen suites are lovely. Great for a family stay. Pool area is lovely, breakfast included is acceptable. Great location for being steps away from Italian area of San Diego, great restaurants! Only downside is the noisy train going behind the hotel!!!
great location, huge rooms, happening bar in the lobby - the gym is ok not amazing but for a work trip was fantastic

Renovations were going on when I was there. This diminished the quality of the stay, but hopefully things will be better soon. However, the rooms were well-kept and service was mostly good. No real flaws or problems here. I got charged for something I didn't use but they politely changed this when I lodged a complaint. Just get the building done!
You can walk to most of the historical locations from here. Whole Foods is also close by. Go there for dinner if you want an interesting but unpretentious dining experience.

I was at Washington Plaza for 1 night only. The experience was good in general. The bed was comfortable, the room clean and there is complementary wifi. The room I got was a bit noisy due to the DC traffic and also some weird loud noise every time the heater came on. I'll blame that on the room itself and since I didn't ask for another room, I won't hold it against the hotel.
The location is pretty good, Thomas Circle is very lively and there are a number of restaurants in walking distance.
I pretty much got what I paid for, a nice room, with a nice bed for me to spend a night in. No complains here. The staff was very polite and pleasant as well.
hotel was clean, staff was considerate, maybe an earlier check-in would be nice. room was small but clean, and quiet for sleeping...thanks GEM

title_masked: Simply top drawer, had a memorable stay
text_masked:
First, the Diamond check in (Mary) was exceptional. Spent so much time with me, I almost felt guilty :)
It was the first hotel I can recall that actually had a Diamond desk check in. Plenty of help and service for a Hilton property in the USA. Honestly, I felt like I was back in Japan. It was an added plus that they upgraded me to the 41st floor (out of 42 floors) while using an Expedia reservation. That doesn't happen very often. Hotel was exceptional, definitely one to remember. The only downside was the valet parking was something like $50 per night...expensive for sure, but I had to wait over 30 minutes for my car, and I called in advance. Very inadequate valet parking. Hotel was great though, and again, thanks to Mary!

Stayed at this hotel for 3 nights and let me say....valet parking was great; NO PARKING, and having them to park cars in the back with no security,....makes u worry. Checking in Customer Service made it seem like the most pleasant place on earth...but when it came to getting instructions and tourist information, it sucked! Elevators....SLOW, walking up and down the stairs to get to floors was probably the easiest but not when having to carry a 8 month old in a carseat. Cleanliness hmmm let me seeeee.....rooms are looking great but what sucked was having early construction and remodeling in the same hall when u are sleeping was the worst part ever!!! WE WERE NOT AWARE OF THAT, until we got to the fifth floor where our room was at. ROOMS= NO A/C OR HEATER UNIT WORKED SO THEY HAD TO TAKE US A FAN, AND windows were hard to open but we got them to open. Kitchenware let me say the one thing that was working was microwave (thank goodness, or else how would i warm up my babys water for her bottles), and let me say the refrigerator and coffeemaker. One remote to the whole suite. And once accomdated in room they manage to say they are missing a dresser in room, so they take it in. Hmmm makes u wonder their rooms are NOT READY. WIFI DID NOT WORK Cleanliness was great until we had to let valet make the front desk aware that we needed cleaning services in our room while we were out. In at the Roof top for continental breakfast was great. Views from the top were amazing. Overall this was a good stay at "Inn at the Park", but they deffinately need to work on some stuff before someone checks in and making them aware of whats going on =REMODELING, DUST, NOISY, CAUTION!. PRICING WAS GREAT OF COURSE ON PRICEWIRE (:
RATING THIS HOTEL A 3 1/2

We chose this property for the location which is between two T stops. Couldn't be more convenient! It is also within walking distance of most tourist attractions. We booked 11 months in advance so we got a fantastic price for our room during one of the busiest (and most expensive) times of the year. The room size was adequate, especially since we didn't spend much time there. We were on the 8th floor and it was very quiet, even over the weekend. Loved the coffee/hot chocolate, newspapers and computers in the Club Room. We took advantage of the bottled water which was a nice amenity. Overall we would stay here again!

Although the staff was friendly and helpful, the rooms were old and needed an update. Our family stayed for two nights at the Brookshire Suites. We had trouble checking into our room and then when we did get a room, it was not the best; very dusty cold-air return, stained carpeting, and grimy coffee table. The ceiling developed a leak in the Cloud Room during a rainstorm on the first morning and the lobby smelled musty. It seems like the building is having overall problems. Disappointing...

title_masked: Rooms & location were great, other details need work
text_masked: The room was very nice & spacious, but quite noisy if you're at the back of the hotel where there are some popular late night spots hopping on weekends. There are elevator problems - only two elevators on each side meant long lines & lots of stair walking. Management sent an email after the fact stating elevators were malfunctioning that week, but staff had told us they were always like that during the day. Hotel was clearly understaffed over Easter weekend (stayed Thursday thru Wednesday). Two women at the front desk seemed to do everything at the hotel - operator, front desk check-in, concierge, etc. so lines were always long. I will say those women were always incredibly friendly, calming & helpful. There are no ice machines - you have to go down to the front desk area to get bags of ice - not an easy task when you have to wait in line for elevator use. Sink had no water pressure - staff said it was intentional to save water. The location is prime & the neighborhood safe. I might give it one more try if I find a really good rate.

Chose the Coast Gateway for a day layover in Seattle on my way to Costa Rica. The room was a bit small, but sufficient for just myself. May be a little cramped for a couple. The room had a large window, a comfortable bed and was very clean. The hotel is extremely close to the airport (5min shuttle ride), so it is extremely convenient for layovers. The wifi access is great and the desk in the room was perfect for me to buckle down and get some work done. The restaurant next to hotel has decent food and is open late. So far this is my favorite hotel to stay at when traveling through Seattle on my way to other destinations. Definitely recommended.

my name is [NAME] and is stayed at the embassy suites in indianapolis north for a week while i was in town on business. Now, with my job and the irregular hours that i work, sleep is very precious. I had one day off and was up early in the morning which is really rare for me with the hours i work and decided to try their complimentary breakfast. I gotta say... this breakfast was absolutely amazing. i travel alot and stay at a lot of hotels and have tried a lot of food from these respective hotels and i must say that what makes this breakfast unique and better than the rest is the cook there, Lassandra. Not only is she very courteous, but cooks pretty much anything you ask her for and when i tasted her ham and cheese omelette... it was like an explosion of taste in my mouth! Not only does the embassy suites here have excellent room service, beautiful and comfortable suites/rooms, an amazing spa, bar/restaurant, fitness room, all of it was excellent, but the free breakfast with Lassandra as the cook beats any of the MANY hotels i have been to with all the traveling i do on business. California, New York, none of them compare to this awesome breakfast! If it were up to me, Lassandra would be the highest paid employee at this hotel! You'd better watch out embassy suites, i may lure her to cook breakfast at my office!

title_masked: There should be more hotels like this!
text_masked: We stayed here for 2 nights and wished that we would have stayed longer. After long days of touring around, it was really nice to come back to a hotel that felt this comfortable. Considering its an old hotel, its very clean, well kept, the included breakfast buffet is excellent and the location is in a safe and beautiful area. The lobby had an area where coffee/tea and water were always available, a nice touch we used both nights. The parking was free which was much better than the $48 per night we paid at another hotel a few nights later, but it does come with a bit of car juggling, if you plan on parking it for the day. The parking signs say 3 hour parking from 8:00 am to 6:00 pm, so you can park from 3:00 pm to 11:00 am the next day and the hotel will make sure to move your car during the times you could get a parking ticket, a really nice service. This hotel has a GREAT staff, you won't be disappointed

Incredible location as others have mentioned. Staff very responsive, refrig delivered along with extra pillows immediately. The bed was exceptionally comfortable. We had access to the 14th floor lounge and although small it was well stocked. The lounge offered complimentary drinks our first night there. The food offerings changed each night and the offerings were plentiful. Examples of food in the lounge were Oriechetti pasta with basil cream sauce, crab cakes, spinach salad with vinegrette, cheese, cracker assortment and fruit. Cocktails , wine and beer available to purchase. The rooms were smaller then other Marriotts of this caliber.
Liquor available next to the hotel. Valet Parking at $40 pèr night seemed excessive,with no good other options available. A car is not needed here since the metro is very close? Don't miss the food trucks on 12th Street between G and H at lunch.

Fantastic location and overall nice hotel.
Some staff rude but I've been told that's just the way New Yorkers are.
 Norma's food was amazing and the Burger Joint was spectacular....best burger ive ever had!

I was amazed at how wonderful this hotel is. The rooms are large and furnished to an exceptional standard (including a great bed and pillows). The grounds are beautiful and green. The staff are warm and welcoming. Our family (including a teenager who has high standards!) was thrilled that we booked this place when we stopped over in Seattle. And this place is easy to get to from the airport. A wonderful experience overall,

This review has been hard to write. First the location on Nob Hill may have been prestigeous in history, but today it is out of the way for those wanting the true walk about San Francisco experience. The trolleys do have a stop behind the hotel and down the hill which allows for a great ride, but you still must wait in long lines to get on. Forget about the Top of the Mark being something other than a wonderful view. The once famous hot spot is now just the basic hotel restaurant. You know the one they have to have to earn a certain star. Think running children and cheap placemats. A diner with a view. The hotel rooms were nice and I would give them an above average for decor and comfort. We had a lovely front facing bay view. However do not expect any internet! Remember we are in the heartland of the U.S. computer industry. For some reason this property was left in the 19...(when did we not have internet)! The hotel entrance was a traffic disaster with cars almost to the front door, juggling valets, bellhops, conventioneers and tourists. The lobby was tiny and as there was a convention in full swing in this relatively small hotel the convention overflowed into the lobby so there was no other guest seating, or corner to hide. The desk staff had attitudes and were most unhelpful and surely. When I asked for a manager an arrogant desk clerk claimed the title and was no help. I travel a lot so I demanded to see the true full manager of the hotel. I am a paying Intercontinental Loyalty member so I made a few calls and wham, the "Twist". An incredible, helpful, friendly capable manager! She came to our room to listen to our complaints and then acknowledged our concerns, apologized for the true and lousy internet (complete new system on the board for Jamuary, 2013), the lack of any gracious dining, rude desk help etc... She knew our complaints were not frivolous and made arrangements for a car and driver to take us to the sister Intercontinental in the Financial district which has quality internet and a gourmet restaurant, full facilities and a pool. This was a true Intercontinental. I realize all chain hotels and locations are different, however at the level of the chain there should be some consistant standards, and the Mark Hopkins has been left to live off of its history and former glory.. Intercontinental I hope you give your dedicated manager something concrete to work with and allow investment in this historic property.

From the friendly greeting, this hotel was very comfortable, spotlessly clean. All staff were very obliging. tv didn't work for two days! still not sorted when we left. we would've liked it to keep up with news. very good location right opposite madison square garden, 5 mins from maceys, 10 mins from empire state building and times square. no tea bags in room!!! only coffee making facilities. penn station right opposite. we were very comfortable and location was great

title_masked: Great location, knowledgable staff, reasonable rates.
text_masked: Room was very clean and stocked well with the usual items like soap, coffee, and towels. The only room available was a smoking room but it didnt have the odor of a smoking room. Staff was very knwledgable and helpful.

title_masked: DO NOT STAY HERE! BED BUGS!
text_masked:
I found this hotel listed on The Bed Bug Registry the day before we were to check-in. I didn't want to book at another hotel and have to pay more, so I made sure to look at the bed as soon as I got in. They have these covers on the mattresses so I couldn't really look directly at it, but anyway I didn't see any. No bites during the night. However I saw one crawling on our pillow while getting ready the next morning. We presented it to the front desk and they offered to switch rooms but we were checking out that day. I doubt it would have mattered cause this place is obviously infested. My husband found one crawling on his neck on our drive home.
I would've given this place a good review otherwise, but it's not worth staying. I have a friend that had bed bugs follow her to three different homes after bringing them home from Europe and she still has them even after getting a professional exterminator. I'm terrified that I might bring them into the house even though we were careful to wash everything. For all I know I could end up bringing them in from my car.
Ugh, I wish I would've just stayed somewhere else. If we do get infested it would not be worth the one night.

The hotel itself was nice. Located near nice landmarks, and some nice restaurants, it was fairly convenient. The rooms were HUGE which gave the hotel a homey, non traditional feel that was comforting. The staff was so kind and friendly.
I stayed there the wrong weekend though.
The ILMUNC model UN conference was the same weekend I stayed, and it was a mess. The elevators, at certain times, would take anywhere from fifteen to thirty minutes only to be packed into a tiny elevator with fifteen snooty teenagers making jokes. The noise level was INSANE. I heard screaming, singing, and laughing until two or three in the morning, and smelled some nasty things coming from the teen rooms.
The breakfast was delicious, yet so crowded with so many high schoolers. I heard that one group of high schoolers threw a water bottle off the balcony onto someone's car; sounds dangerous to give high schoolers balconies. There were usually some groups of teens barreling up the staircases at all hours of the day. I heard there was an apple fight, with the teens throwing apples at one another in the lobby, and some practical joke with a giant stuffed horse showing up in random places. I'll never understand teens.
Overall, I would go back. It was a great hotel, I only wish the hotel would give sufficient warning to those who are staying during a large high school conference. I have the humor to overlook these small inconveniences, but some people may not.

The rooms were nice, the views even better. We had a room that had a view of the marina and the San Diego bay cityline. The nighttime view of the city lights was great. 
Rooms were well appointed, comfortable bed, clean updated room and bathrooms, even have Peter Thomas Roth bath amenities (as a woman, I appreciated this very much! ^_^) It was a short trip to get downtown, SD Zoo and Seaworld and not too bad to Coronado as well, where we had dinner plans one evening. There is also a hotel restaurant for convenience. Across the hotel is a walking path by the water which was also nice. The area has restaurants and bars within walking distance and is also by the airport (which is good for plane watching or aviation photography -my fiance enjoyed it)
Overall it was a great place to stay. Nice, clean convenient and parking was not far nor crowded and it was fairly cheaper than downtown hotel parking. I would give it 5 stars except the room we had was a bit small. King bed and furniture with one large suitcase had us walking over our stuff to get to the bathroom. But traveling as a couple, I wasn't bothered much by it.

We booked 4 nighs at this hotel thru Hotwire for my sister's first time visit to Big Apple and she had a blast. It is not a five star hotel but it is nice enough for your short trip in NYC especially with a nice manager like Lidia Garibaldo. She had made the trip worthwhile with an upgrade room to accomodate my sister and her dad to make her trip so wonderful. 
Thank you Lidia and we will be back.

We went to New York on the 5th November and we were worried things wouldn't be the same since hurricane Sandy but New York did not disappoint at all.The Lucerne hotel was just perfect!Its in a perfect location just a stone throw away from Central Park and is situated in a friendly neighbourhood were there are lots of bars,shops and places to eat.We were often still out late on and never felt uneasy at all.The hotel was lovely and clean and the room was a nice size for a family of 4,beds were lovely and comfortable.We just can't wait to go back.Everything was perfect!!!!

title_masked: Great location and value for two room suite, but not a luxury property
text_masked: We visited over Spring Break with our two teenagers. Chose this property because of the two-room configuration. The wet bar in the living area is a plus as it provides an extra sink and vanity for getting ready in the mornings. Had an actual mini fridge as well as a mini-bar ($) with snacks, drinks, etc. That is important to us for leftovers, water bottles, etc. Also a microwave. Hotel provided a rollaway bed and the sofa sleeper was high quality, so both teens slept well. Bedding was nice and comfortable. The only negative was the lobby - dark and small, with only a small bar off to the side ($4.50 for a club soda and no conversation from the bartender - look out!). Great service from the front desk staff (Cowboy with the badge and hat was very animated and friendly), but the concierge was cold and unhelpful (very unusual for this area). Very nice and helpful bell staff. If you travel as a family and enjoy a little "separation" from the kids, this is one of the only properties offering the two room suites. Would stay there again at the right price. Booked an air/hotel package through Expedia - no problems. Walked to Wicked on Broadway, as well as Rockefeller Center, St. Patrick's Day parade, etc. The pizza place on the opposite corner is awesome and one of the best values we found in the city - they have pastas, salads, veggies, and even breakfast.

You are not going to get much better in terms of space and cost. True, you are at the bottom of Manhattan Island, but transport is so easy and at such competitive pricing, the cost difference is worth the extra $20 in subway fare and the few minutes in travel time. Breakfasts are great, staff are friendly and very helpful. I don't intend to go back to NYC for a while but if I were, I would stay at the Mulberry again. Canal street is not a pleasant experience; fish market and astonishingly congested.
If you are looking for a great place to eat, cross over to Brooklyn and check out Diner, 85 Broadway; http://dinernyc.com/.

I was there for a three-day conference. The location is obviously fantastic right next to the National Wall, White House, etc. The hotel is standard 4-star. You pay a premium for an excellent location and decent accommodations (with smallish bathrooms). Service was friendly.
For a US hotel, the fitness center was pretty good size with plenty of machines in working order. The pool is medium sized--maybe 15 yards long.
Don't be dismayed at the very high prices for booze in the hotel bars and room service. There is an excellent liquor store right outside the hotel. And a CVS around the corner to if you don't want to pay WAY too much for munchies in the hotel store. 
WIFI worked well in my room though it wasn't free.
Positive Surprises. Cool elevator system where you type in your floor destination before you get into the elevator and your told which elevator to get into. Apples and fruit provided in fitness center and pool were fresh and good.

title_masked: Superb hotel, again shy of 5 stars
text_masked:
I have to admit, this is my hotel of choice for NYC as it's just so close to everything. The staff are all extremly nice (well, not all but most) too which is a suprise for NY too! 
I have to admit, we did have a few issues about our stay, and ofcourse, i was not pleased about them but was more than happy with the responce from George Drepaul. I do think the housekeeping staff need to be a little more attentive though, as our sheets were not changed in ages. Do keep an eye on this. Also, our bathtub had hair in it, so we had to clean this ourself. 
As a General Manager myself, i personally found this to be extremly unacceptable but after talking with front desk, it was solved with no issues, but i do not know if this was a usual responce or because they knew i was a GM but I am happy enough. 
The doormen too, quite often, would be talking on their personal cell phones, or talking to a pretty girl (not opening the door or flagging a cab), and ignoring their dutys. Not a huge issue but as their job is to open the door, failure to do this, is not good and shows bad on the hotel as these people are seen first.
And the bellboys who take your luggage to store, I think sometimes they need to learn manors too. On departure, they offer to take your bags and store them for you, and while its nice to give a tip, if the smallest note you have is a 20, you can't very well ask for change, so we decided to tip on the way out. The bellboy did not seem to like this and muttered under his breath and seemed to be moody like a child. Again, while a small thing, not what I expect from staff. 
To summerise
Bellboys need manors
Doormen need to do their job properly 
Housekeeping staff need to be more attentive and change bedding frequently instead of leaving it for a week+
Despite the negitives, the fact this hotel has amazing front desk staff, superb management (most noteably George Drepaul and Joseph Rauer), i think it's these people, who make this hotel, exactly what it is. 
Will I be returning again next year? If the price is right, without a doubt.

Contemporary. Sleek. Modern. Tech Savvy. What am I describing? No, not a new smartphone or tablet. Not a new luxury car or pc either. These are the adjectives I use when describing The Hotel Wilshire.
The Hotel Wilshire was not at all what I expected – but in a good way. Upon arrival the narrow valet with entrance similar to a New York parking garage, I must say was daunting, but once inside the NY vibe disappeared. A modern, glass, crisp interior awaited. I may not be the typical traveler, then again, maybe I am as I travel with two mobile phones, a tablet, and at least two laptops (among other things); and the ability to use my devices as if I’m at home is usually not a luxury. However, I was wrong this time and The Hotel Wilshire delivered in spades meeting my demand. I’m not sure what inspired such tech savvy, but wall a mounted dock for HDMI, VGA, S-Video, RGB, IPOD / IPHONE / IPad, LAN, USB, and audio? Mitsubishi climate controls, LED lighting, Wi-Fi that wasn’t anemic, and more. I had to ask myself: “Where am I?” Is this a sort of Shangri La?
In addition to the technical “everything” I just mentioned, the room is styled oh so well. I am a high rise dweller that enjoys modern decor with a hint of minimalism – I couldn’t have picked a better place. One will note ample closet space and a sexy chaise with hidden storage below. Quite possibly the softest bed and pillows in my last six months of travel, crisp and clean lighting, and a bath with utterly sleek surfaces. I also note the intense cleanliness of the room, not a spot on the shower glass – noticeable. The interior design is perfect for one week, one month, or whatever your stay. Mind you: I’m not even discussing the great rooftop pool in this review!
If you are looking for something traditional with dark woods, and earthy furnishings this may not be the place for you. If you are looking for a modern room with technical flair, I recommend you visit this weekend. A new addition to my “Best List”, The Hotel Wilshire is all Aces in my book!

We returned from SF yesterday and spent three nights at Intercontinental. Nce hotel. Great amenities. The beds, a different story. Terribly uncomfortable. We had our first good night's sleep after we left and stayed at a Marriot Residence Inn (not in SF). We were shocked at how uncomfortable the beds and pillows were. Not expected in such an expensive hotel.

title_masked: Nice stay for a meeting and with my family
text_masked:
We stayed for two nights at the Hyatt Capitol in August 2012. We had room 443 which overlooks the pool (and a half completed garage), and was very clean and bright. The room has two double beds which wer very comfortable and the room was spacious enough for four, two kids two adults. There isn't a refrigerator in the room, which would have been nice.
We had the breakfast buffet and everyone was thrilled. My kids actually ate! The food in the buffet Was on the healthy side of a breakfast buffet with lots of fresh fruit, whole wheat pancakes, omelet station etc. and the coffee was terrific. 
The Capitol was right down the street, we did the tour which was fun. There is a fair amount of food nearby, but there are a lot of homeless around, which was disconcerting when two individuals decided to have a screaming match on the sidewalk less than a block away From the entrance. 
The pool is small but not too busy. There was a sauna in the locker room, a weight room, free weights, and machines, bikes and treadmills. There always seemed to be one machines.

I recently went to NYC with family for a weekend. From the minute we walked in, we were greeted with a friendly welcome. The location was perfect, the staff were excellent, the rooms were very nice, but small. The front desk personel were very helpful and personable. The breakfast room is a bit small for everyone tofit in when the hotel has many guests. They called a car service for us upon checkout. Great overall experience!

title_masked: Great location - good choice for business or pleasure
text_masked:
The location and service are good and walking distance from all the usual places you'd want to visit. The hotel is always busy and packed and there is a good, lively atmosphere in the lobby. The bars were always busy too with quick table service and a great choice of cocktails. These were pricey but that's what you'd expect in a NY hotel. 
The room was large and the bathroom a bit on the small side. The minbar is locked and you have to request key at reception. There is no wifi in the room which would have been ideal. 
The toilet was blocked onthe 1st night and they came and looked at it very quickly. Same thing happened the 2nd night so I was moved to another room and they did not charge me for the 1st night which was very generous of them. The staff are friendly and helpful but you can sometimes wait a long time on reception as they queues are sometimes long. Overall I think the place is good value for money and I'd stay there again.

Just back from our honeymoon at the bryant park hotel and thought i would write my first review to let everyone know that if your going to new york then make this hotel your choice to stay in. We arrived about an hour early for check in and our room wasn't ready, not a problem, we got upgraded to a bigger room that was ready(great start i thought), we put our cases in our room,freshened up and went out to explore the big apple. Times square, 5th avenue all within 10 minutes walking distance,(kept getting better and better!), we went back to our room to find a bottle off champagne,balloons and a congratulations card from the hotel(brilliant we thought!). The hotel itself is amazing, but what makes this such a great place to stay in is the staff, everyone off them helped make our honeymoon amazing. Thank you to all the staff at the bryant park hotel, we will be returning.:)

In seeking a hotel to fit my budget, I chose the La Quinta based on previous reviews as well as its location in downtown Seattle. I just returned home in mid-March from a three-night stay at this hotel, and would like to confirm the praises from previous reviewers.
Everyone at the front desk was professional and helpful; you can tell they have a great team attitude, towards both the guests as well as one another. The staff is youthful and enthusiastic and you just feel good from the moment you walk in. 
I reserved a room with a king bed, microwave and refrigerator. I asked for a quiet room with a view and was delighted to be on the top floor with a great view of downtown Seattle. My room was spotless. The décor was comfortable, the room was spacious and the bathroom was recently remodeled, with nice tile and fixtures throughout. Towels are fluffy, linens are plush, and windows had blackout drapes plus nice sheers layered over them. It was a plus to have the refrigerator and microwave, because Whole Foods is just around the corner and I made a couple of grocery runs for late evening and early morning snacks. 
It appears the entire hotel is being upgraded, including the lobby, which they are in the process of remodeling and should be completed soon. This did not interfere with my comings and goings. In addition, if needed, there is a computer with a printer in the lobby to print your flight reservation or check emails.
The location was perfect. I like to walk, and I was able to walk to the Space Needle, all throughout downtown and Pike Place Market several times during my stay.
