If you don’t care to walk, you can catch the bus routes, which are very close to the hotel; just ask the staff where you would like to go.
 My compliments to all the staff at this location; they go above and beyond for you. You won’t find a better hotel for the location, price, cleanliness, comfort and friendly staff.

We stayed at the Blakely Hotel New York for 5 nights. This was a birthday trip with my partner. The Hotel is ideally situated on 55th Street between 6th and 7th Avenue. Times Square and Central Park are within walking distance and the subway and hop on hop off buses are right nearby too. We stayed on the 13th floor facing the rear of the hotel, you can hear the traffic but it didn't affect our sleep. The room had a mini bar and tea/coffee making facilities, also a microwave. The room was very clean and we also had maid service everyday. The only criticism I would have is that there wasn't enough wardrobe space, only one small area for hanging! Plenty of drawer space and also a free safe, ironing board, iron and hairdryer supplied. The reception staff were very friendly and helpful and recommended a fabulous restaurant which we went to during our stay. The breakfast was continental but limited choice. Overall I would definitely recommend this hotel for a city break in New York.

I stayed at this property for 3 nights in April 2012 for a convention. I loved the close proximity to The Prudential Center Complex (right across the street where the Hynes Convention Center is located), Fenway Park, and the Charles River, which are in short walking distance.
The property itself seems to be well maintained and the staff was friendly and helpful when I asked for directions or information about landmarks and destinations in the area. 
The room I had was spacious and with a large flat screen TV. I was also on the 24th floor which afforded a great view of the city. The beds were comfy and I had no problems with the initial cleanliness of the room or how it was maintained. 
There were some noise issues that were bothersome, the toilet flushing was extremely loud and I could hear toilets flushing in the rooms surrounding mine. There also wasn't great insulation from hallway noise. Additionally the air conditioning unit was frighteningly loud. The unit turned on almost explosively and I was startled and jumped every time it cycled on. These annoyances were very disruptive when I was trying to go to sleep.
The things I hated about staying here was the parking rate (an exorbitant $41 per night) and the internet policy (in room internet $14.95 PER DEVICE). If you must charge for in room internet, why charge the fee per device? The charge should be per room regardless as to the number of devices you use while in your room. Hilton, that's just greedy!

The service is excellent with no attitude. The beds are so comfy and the rooms are comfortably sized with adequate dressing and make up space. Ir is. Pleasure and a privilege to stay here. The staff make every effort to assure your satisfaction.

title_masked: My new go-to hotel in New York
text_masked:
This is a great hotel -- new, modern, beautiful rooms. I was a little hesitant about the location since this was a leisure stay, but I decided to give it a try and I'm glad I did. The main reason we stayed there was because it's one of the rare properties in NYC that allows large dogs. We were traveling with our 70-lb dog and most hotels in NYC have a max of 25 lbs. Conrad allows up to 75 lbs and doesn't charge an extra fee. Kudos to Conrad -- you'd never know our dog was there and he certainly leaves less evidence than most children! And as a bonus, their policy got me to try their hotel and we've now become big fans and will return even when we don't have our dog with us. I travel to NYC about 5-10 times a year on business, and will try to stay at the Conrad from now on.
The surrounding area of Battery Park City is great -- you have the whole west side Henry Hudson park, lots of green parks, playgrounds, waterfront restaurants... really nice.
We got upgraded to a corner suite through the e-standby upgrade program, for $70/night, and it was well worth it. Our suite was HUGE and beautiful. It was larger than most one-bedroom apartments I've seen in NYC.
You can't go wrong with this hotel, I highly recommend it.

title_masked: It is a nice category 4 marriott hotel
text_masked: Considering it is an airport hotel, it is nice and comfortable. We used our marriott certificate stay there. It is worth it. It is near the airport and shuttle is convienent. And we also get upgrade to a junior suite. Next time I need to stay in LAX, I will definitely choose this hotel.

This is an old hotel showing its age. However, you can't beat the location, value, cleanliness, friendliness and excellent service. This is known as our third home; we visit our UCLA student frequently: just ask the welcoming committee Leo (aka Leon), Scott, or Lupe at reservation and front desk. (Ask Lupe for a beach front room, a standing joke)
There is a spacious visiting area, communal kitchen, free coffee/tea, and free WiFi. Basic room, no TV...so it's quiet. Lots of international visitors, we feel at home. At $69 a night, you can't find anything for that at Westwood.

I stayed here for 3 nights at the end of May 2012 and loved it. The staff was attentive and so very helpful. They provided excellent advice on how best to travel in Baltimore to the Inner Harbor, the Charm Circulator (which charges nothing!) and takes you to where you need to be. The hotel was clean and a wonderful experience. I had to modify my plans and book two additional night before my scheduled arrival and they took care of it within minutes. I found Tavon, the front desk clerk to be a joy. He had a great attitude...said he looks at the people who stay here as important visitors, not just strangers. Housekeeping staff was excellent...very friendly and so eager to help. Valet parking was a dream...helped with my luggage and made the check in so very easy. Hilton Hotels has a winner...a hotel to be proud of.

Our first stay at Hotel Commonwealth left something to be desired. I wrote an email to the manager explaining, and we were invited back for a second night. They went above and beyond to make sure that we had a fantastic night for my birthday. Our room was absolutely gorgeous, the jacuzzi tub was lovely, marble everywhere. Loved the separate shower...the bathroom was literally the size of an apartment I once had. The beds are so comfortable, love the pillows, the sheets, the bathrobes and the slippers. They came in while we were out to eat and neatened the room, turned down the bed, left chocolates on the pillow. It's the little things like that that make a hotel stay special. 
The staff, especially the front of the house manager Jeff, were extremely attentive and friendly. Everything we requested, from a fridge to an extended checkout, was given to us quickly, efficiently and with kindness and warmth.
 We have tried both adjoining restaurants, loved them both. Island creek has a great ambiance, Eastern Standards' brunch is very very good.
We truly enjoyed our stay. We will absoutely be back and we recommend this hotel for any kind of stay, business or pleasure.

Had a wonderful time! Family of 4 with a 9 and 11 year old had a blast. The nightly DJ / Dance party around the pool from 6 to 7:30 was great fun and provided lots of laughs. Followed by a kids movie around the pool was brilliant. The pool service and food / beverage set up was perfect. Food was good with lots of variety. Spent a couple nites at their competitors resort and this stacked up way better for our family. Very impressed in all aspects. 
Only downfall was the water park was so full we had to sit in the grass. Apparently they are open to public which did make for crowded seating conditions. I feel that every hotel guest should be able to have a seat to sit in!!!!! The park was large enough that the lines were not long, the pool was not over crowded. The lazy river did get congested but was still very relaxing.
There are lifeguards which makes for some relaxation for parents.
The water was heated and comfortable.
The rooms were perfect with a bedroom to close the kids off. Small refridgerator but no microwave............... darn it!

I stayed here recently on business using my Starwood Preferred Guest points.
I travel a lot for business and usually alternate between Westin, Sheraton and Marriott hotels. I've never stayed at a W hotel before, so I thought I'd give it a try. The W Times Square looked swank, contemporary and very appealing for a young professional.
Unfortunately, it was a disappointing experience. Notwithstanding, its location is incredible and within a 15-minute walk of most major attractions in Manhattan.
When I checked in, I asked for a single bed. I was told none were available, but was promised an "upgraded double with a nice view." This was hardly the case. My room was literally right across from the elevator and my view was of what was basically an alley. I called down and said this was unacceptable and was moved to a new room, but the only thing that was different was a slightly better view.
Both rooms were very contemporary. While it was stylish, it was a little too basic and frankly came across a little cheap, in my opinion. It reminded me a lot of the brute minimalist Aloft brand of hotels.
The internet was fast, but expensive. The rooms could have been kept up better, especially in the bathroom. One day my room wasn't done by housekeeping though they strangely replaced the water in the room. The housekeeping cart and trash cart sat outside my room for two consecutive days. I also had regular problems with my key, which made going down to the front desk to get a replacement quite annoying.
At night, the hotel does have a strong vibe with lots of late 20-somethings and early 30-somethings in the bar, drinking and socializing with live music. The Blue Fin restaurant downstairs at street level has amazing food and reasonable prices, especially by New York standards.
All in all, this is, in my mind, an overrated hotel with a great location but poor service. I would rather stay at a Marriott, if I had to do it over again.

Being a Starwood Employee myself, I knew to have high expectations for this property. I was treated like Royalty (despite having gotten a great rate). Everything was pristine and the beds very comfortable. Two showerheads!! I was astounded with all aspects of this place, especially the people working there....

This little gem is hidden in the Houston Downtown area. When we first arrived the valet guys rushed to the car and opened the hotel doors. The hotel is really dimly lit but very trendy, same goes for the hotel room. The check-in was not so pleasant and I was forced to withdraw money from the onsite ATM(for damage deposit) because they wouldn't accept my Visa card. The hotel and hallways were very quiet and overall had a great experience. 
Pro: Modern, sexy, well priced, free shuttles downtown, 
Cons: Homeless alley around the corner, check-in, no ice machines.

We chose this venue because it is right on the waterfront, right behind the North End and small enough to feel like a home away from home and big enough to accommodate our wedding of 130 ppl. This venue is unique and very classy without being overstated or too fancy. Our contact was Ashley Lamy, who was incredible. She walked us through the whole process and made us feel that we didn't need to worry about anything--and we didn't. She tried to accommodate all of our requests and even threw in some extra perks which were a great surprise. On the day of the event, everything we asked about was there and the event was flawless. We had our ceremony and cocktail reception outside with part of the reception in the Maritime museum onsite. We then moved inside for dinner. We had a buffet and the food was so good. Everyone commented on the food and how friendly the staff was. People were really impressed at the high level of service. Everyone has been telling us that this was one of the best weddings that they have ever been to and a lot of that credit goes to Ashley, the chef, the service staff, the A/V department and the bartenders (who everyone knew by name). Thank you, thank you for making this event so easy, memorable and fun!

My family just returned from a great stay. Everything was exceptional. We arrived late and tired, and asked the receptionist for a dinner recommendation. She recommended the hotel restaurant, and though skeptical, we were too tired to venture out. It was outstanding! The hotel is surprisingly quiet, clean, comfortable, and friendly. The rooms are fairly large for Manhatten, the beds are great, and the bathrooms have new, high end fixtures, including Toto toilets, which I've never seen in a hotel. Close to Times Square, Grand Central, Starbucks, and a sweet grocery store with a nice variety of prepared food.

title_masked: overpriced and in need of a serious face lift
text_masked: I have stayed at this hotel 3 times in the past 2 months and each stay was worse than the previous. On the last stay the knobs were both broken on the filthy air conditioner so it could not be adjusted, there was trash under the bed and the shower curtain was covered in black mildew stains.

title_masked: Another Fantastic Stay at the Back Bay Hilton
text_masked:
I was a frequent visitor of the Hilton Back Bay when I traveled to Boston for work frequently several years ago. Recently I had an opportunity to return to Boston and stay at a long time favorite hotel in Boston for three nights with my wife.
Once again the stay was fantastic. The thing that always sets an hotel apart for me is the staff, at the end of the day lots of hotels in Boston are similar to the Hilton, but the staff takes very good care of you here. One example was when I was returning to the hotel at night and because of a party there were no parking spots. The doorman talked to the manager and found us a spot in the "permit" parking area, going out of their way to assist us.
The rooms have been recently renovated and were very nice. They were a good size, very comfortable bed, sofa, desk area and HDTV. I liked the updates to the room with the exception that they have bolted the balcony doors closed so you can't go out anymore. One thing I do like about the rooms however is you can open the window for fresh air which is rare downtown and something I always appreciate.
The hotel is a perfect size, not monolithic and crowded like some of the surrounding hotels so you never feel crowded. They have a great workout area and indoor pool and a starbucks in the lobby. The location of the hotel is perfect for getting around, just across from the Pru Center.
Always look forward to returning to this long time favorite.

title_masked: A nice hotel with great staff but very small and loud room
text_masked: This hotel is chick with a lot of history. The lobby is unique and decorated with beautiful old New York charm, its no wonder that it was the favorite of so many writers. The staff are friendly and helpful. My only complaint is with the size of the rooms, the rooms are incredibly small. The bath rooms are much nicer since the renovation but still very very small. I like the new improved work out facility, but it can use newer equipment. Apart from the room size this is a very good hotel

Our first visit into the city of New York and have to say that staying here at this brilliant hotel made our vislt to this fabulous city all the more enjoyable. Quiet street in the best of locations. ALL the staff we met were superb, very polite and could not have been more helpful. Free internet 24 hrs a day, complimentary coffee and tea in the lounge area, free use of the gym and great complimentary hot breakfast, lots of seating outside on the patio area. We stayed here for 4 nights and could not have been more happy with our choice of hotel. Within walking distance of all the major attractions close to Macy's, Madisson Square Garden, Empire State building, (view from our bedroom window), Chrysler Building. Grand Central station, Times Square, and both the underground and Penn Station. Loads of places to eat nearby. We walked from the hotel to Central Park and to the other end of the island to the 9/11 memorial and Staten Island Ferry.
Twin and double rooms avaialble all with en suites which have baths and showers and complimentary toiletries available should you forget something, wi-fi in all rooms good quality beds and tv's.
We caught the airtrain from JFK airport to Jamaica, last stop on the airtrain at the airport and then the Long Island Rail Road train from Jamaica Hub to Penn Station about a 1/2 hr ride. Penn station is located 2 blocks from the hotel on 31st . So easy to access and very easy ride directly from the airport to the centre of the city. Cost $5 for the airtrain ticket, payable as you enter or exit the airtrain at Jamaica, and $6 for the LIRR train ride. We caught the underground from Penn Station on the E line back to Jamaica - Sutphin Boulevard $2.25 then airtrain $5 back to the airport, would recommend the LIRR train which was much quicker due to the stops on the subway, felt safe but was crowed on the underground. 
Thanks to all at the hotel for making our stay so pleasant cannot recommend highly enough, we loved our stay in NYC.

I stayed here during a convention, for four nights. Pluses: breakfast better than expected (oatmeal, hard boiled eggs); complimentary wi-fi; pleasant staff; convenience to conference center (easy walk, via covered walkways); across from museums and park; very quiet, the only noise I heard was if someone was in the hallway.
Cons: no full length mirror in room (c'mon, there were several walls / doors where a mirror could be added); no convenient hook for towel next to shower (partition between commode and shower would be a perfect spot); no trays in breakfast area; styrofoam/plastice dining utensils in breakfast area. No refrigerator in room.
Not sure: my room had a view of....the air handler for the JW next door. However, the low hum from the air handler was kinda like "white noise", and I slept very well. I had no issues with the pillows. 
For the price paid, this was average value.

This hotel was fabulous! If I could afford it, I'd stay here all the time. The room was very comfortable and we managed a partial water view. The bed was great, the bathroom huge and the in-room coffee was actually good. The evening turn down service was a nice treat. 
What I was surprised by was how much I liked staying so close to the North End. It's not super close to the T, but there is lots to see and do in the area and it's a great place to come home to. We were lucky and were able to attend the Fisherman's Feast in the North End while we were there. It was perfect!

title_masked: Best I've had in the City
text_masked:
Universally, an exceptional staff. Friendly and helpful from the get-go through check-out. When arriving, my room was not ready but they were quick to accept my bag for later return. But as soon as I let my bag go, I realized I needed something from it for my first meeting and requested it back. Usually, this is a great time to get a little NYC attitude but no, he was helpful and understanding then, having mentioned a meeting, asked if I need a cab or directions. I didn't but I very much appreciate being attentive to potential needs. Later, check in was friendly and efficient, breakfast was good again with helpful staff and on checkout I was intercepted to see if I need a cab. I did, and he fought the NYC traffic to flag down one. Simply excellent. I will return when business takes me to this part of the City. 
Rooms are silly-small, but that is NYC for you. HVAC units were noisier than I would like but it did keep the room comfortable.

title_masked: Wouldn't Dream of Staying anywhere else in NYC
text_masked: The James Hotel was such a wonderful find. The rooms are modern and give more of an apartment feel than hotel room. We had amazing views and a large window line. I can't say enough about the service at the James. Everyone I came across was so friendly and helpful. You were greeted EVERYTIME you come and go. The staff is so accomodating and you can tell they love what they do. The manager, Mark was very gracious and kind. When I arrived there had been a problem with my room, but they already had it resolved before I arrived and took great care of me throughout my stay. The girls at the front desk (Amy and Jessica) were delightful and fun. I really wish I could remember everyone's names, because each and every staff member deserves to be recognized for their wonderful service. The hotel is close to so many wondeful retail stores, restaurants and bars, as well as one stop on the Subway from the Downtown scene. There's a roof top pool and bar offering a relaxing yet hip environment with amazing views. Don't miss out on this gem of a hotel.

This hotel has a convinient parking garage, spaceful and clean rooms but somewhat old furnitures and a bit worn out. Friendly and very helpful staff. The breakfast was good. Location.. Well convinient due to nearby sights.. But a poor area in our eyes (?) Make sure to eat at the sights - no restaurants/diners close by the hotel as far as we could figure out. Laundry close by which was convinient. Subway next door. We stayed only two nights due to road trip in California.

title_masked: Was hestitant based on reviews, but it wasn't bad
text_masked: My family and I recently stayed at this property for 3 nights in a 2 bedroom suite. It was very nice to have the extra space, and 2nd bathroom. Kitchen and living area were nice. Property itself was average, nothing "Beverly Hills" about it. Only one elevator at this property. I was glad to have requested a low floor so we could use the stairs. This hotel does offer a free shuttle within a 3 mile radius. This was very nice to use as cab rates are extremely high. However the shuttle stops at 6:30pm which is early. We didn't take advantage of the daily breakfast, but rather ate across the street at Factor's Famous Deli. The food was good and reasonably priced. Most of the hotel staff were friendly with the exception of one nighttime front desk clerk. He had an attitude and was full of sarcasim. Not what I expect out of people employed to assist other people. We did have an issue our second night with drunk, noisy neighbors. I had to call the front desk twice. Not sure if anything was done about their noise, or if I just finally fell back asleep. I was awakened around 1am with screaming, and what sounded like breaking furniture. I was not happy about that! Hotel is within walking distance of restaurants in Beverly Hills, i.e CPK and Cheesecake Factory. Several local eateries too that looked really nice. Overall, I found it to be a good property.

We stayed at the Omni during the ACL festival. The hotel was nice but the best part of the stay was the great staff. They all went out of their way to make you feel important and were always asking how they can help. Room was okay, nothing over the top. I would stay there again if need arises.

title_masked: Good price, near airport. Showing age.
text_masked:
My stay on Sat, April 28, 2011 was a last minute reservation due to a need for an extra night in San Diego, the extreme rate at the Marriott ($325 for an avg room) and a very early a.m. flight necessitating being at the airport at 5am. I found the Sheraton online via Orbitz with same day availability under $200/ni. 
Pros: The room was good size. The price was good in comparison to other options. The check-in was easy, fast and they had a room ready at upon early arrival at noon. There were a couple of decent onsite choices for meals (affordable). They have an onsite spa/fitness center - so I could squeeze in a no-frills massage. 
Cons: The room was musty smelling and showed plenty of signs of wear and tear. The 'view' was of the parking lot and on the 5th floor it was too easy to hear traffic noise, people talking, etc. The Sheraton wanted to charge a daily rate for internet access (when will SPG group get with the program?? Priority - aka Intercontinentals and Holiday Inns - offer free wi-fi to guests. Great for biz travelers). 
Another pro: while it is 'across the street' from the airport - it's still a bit of a hike wheeling luggage. The Sheraton provides shuttle service every 15 mins - even at 5 am. Very convenient for that.
Good, solid property if you aren't looking for anything too fancy and don't mind a little bit of noise.

title_masked: Great hotel near stadium and tailgates
text_masked: This year marked our team's entrance into the Big 12. We had no idea what to expect when we booked our trip to Austin. We tried to locate a hotel in walking distance of the hotel and close to tailgates since we wanted to experience the game in every way. We flew into San Antonio, because it was cheaper, and drove to Austin meandering our way through Texas Hill Country. Check-in was organized and easy and we were given the hotel's famous hot outta the oven chocolate chip cookies. The hotel also appeared to be pet friendly which would have been nice if we were local and brought our dogs. The room was spacious with a very nice separate kitchen, which was perfecting for preparing bottles and food for our 12 month old. The bathroom was very nice and the view overlooked the Texas state Capitol. We hung out our WVU banner over the open balcony too and the hotel didn't mind! Across the street is the world famous Texas Chili Parlor, made famous in song and by movie. Great frito pies and beer for all. Avoid the Mad Dog Margaritas though-- they carry a punch. Great hotel, terrific fans, and we're definitely coming back next time. Go Mountaineers and thanks to our new Texas friends too.

title_masked: My friends were so jealous that I was staying here!
text_masked: Was in Chicago for a conference and my colleagues were all staying at various hotels. Mine was hands-down the best. Great staff, big room which was clean, stylish. Wonderful amenities that my friends at other hotels had to pay extra for. It really was wonderful. The only negative would be how close it was to Nordstrom (negative for my wallet that is!).

We stayed in a premier queen room in the 10th floor for one week. In fact, we were upgraded by the hotel.
Spacious room for a Manhattan hotel. Very comfortable, very clean and very quiet. The lighting was conveniently installed. There was a coffee-maker (used capsules were replaced every day), a flat-screen TV (we did not use it), mini refrigerator and ironing equipment. The walk-in closet could store two large luggages and the safe was large enough to store a notebook, a large camera and other smaller stuff. The bathroom was well-thought and comfortable: rain, hand and fixed shower heads, magnifying make-up mirror, very powerful hair dryer.
There were two small issues which are not a big deal compared with our general satisfaction. Whenever we left the AC working in the late afternoon, the room smelled like garlic sauteed in oil. Probably a leek from the restaurant's ventilation. For me it was no problem but my husband was uncomfortable so we kept AC off in the afternoon. Second, there was a problem with internet connection for a couple of days but we were not left without connection. I only had to call the service provider to let them define each of our devices manually to the network. Not a convenient way but we had our internet and such problems may occur once in a while. Anyway it was completely solved within 2 days and the wi-fi connection was very good in general.
The breakfast room was nice and comfortable. It was more like a living room that made us feel at home. Donuts, pastry, fresh fruit, yoghurt, cereals, jams, butter and cream cheese. Coffee and tea is served whole day. The roof terrace is wonderful even in January while it is snowing. I assume it is much better in warmer times. Just do not forget to take your drink upstairs with you.
The location is most convenient. Especially if you like to walk. The subway station is just on the corner 1 minute walking distance. Penn station, path station, macy's all are within 5-8 minutes walking distance.
I do not think I will look for another hotel in Manhattan as long as they have room.

title_masked: Always and excellent stay in NYC...
text_masked: Stayed here for 3 night over President's weekend. I have stayed at this property many times over the last few years and always enjoy it! While this hotel is right in the heart of all the action in Times Square and is always jumping with activity...once you get into your room - all of the chaos disappears! Newly renovated, quiet rooms offer a very relaxing night's sleep. Great view of Times Square...worth the few extra dollars. My room included the free breakfast buffet in the newly renovated restaurant - Corners. What a great improvement!! The buffet line was always so crowded in the old restaurant...not anymore! Great choices on the buffet...well worth the money. If you are looking for a great place to stay, right in the heart of NYC...this is it! Close to the Subway, Broadway, Rockefeller Center and 5th Avenue...just great!!

title_masked: Heart of the Theater District Gem
text_masked:
I recently stayed at the Hotel Allegro for a one night business trip. The hotel is conveniently located in the Loop, an easy walk from several "El" stations. I was greeted promptly at check-in by a very friendly front desk clerk who was able to put me in a room even though it was only noon. When I expressed concern about noise from the "El," which runs next to part of the building, she assured me that noise was not a problem, but that she would put me in a room away from the tracks. 
The room itself was on the small side, as others have indicated, and the bathroom was great for one person, but might be a problem for two. That said, the room was immaculately clean and had everything you come to expect from a Kimpton: an interestingly stocked mini-bar, the animal print bathrobe, and strong WiFi. My only complaint about the room is that the king bed was a bit saggy on one side. Since I was traveling alone, this wasn't a problem, I just slept in the middle of the bed!
Overall, I would not hesitate to stay at the Allegro again on a future trip to Chicago.

I recently met up with 2 friends for a weekend in Chicago. In order to save money on the hotel we stayed near O'hare. The shuttle bus was fine and we had very little wait at O'hare. Once we got to the hotel it was conveniently located off the blue line (about a 5 min walk). It took about an hour to get downtown but we only did it once in the morning and once at night. We weren't planning to go back and forth to the hotel so it wasn't a problem. 
We selected a suite so we could have more space. My friends shared the bedroom which had two small beds and I took the sofabed. It was pretty dirty and uncomfortable. When we opened the sofabed it was full of food and stains and didn't have any sheets. I called the desk and requested sheets which took a while to arrive and then we had to make the bed ourselves. It was extremely uncomfortable and once it was unfolded no one could walk by it. This would have been great for two people but not so good for 3 unless two can share a small bed.

title_masked: Would have loved to have stayed longer!
text_masked: My friend and I stayed at the Magnolia for just one night. After working all day and then travelling we were greeted by the very friendly reception staff. The availabilty of milk and cookies hit the spot. The room was clean and the bed was comfy. We checked out the next morning but not before we hit up the very genourous breakfast that is included in the room rate. The spread was plentiful and allowed us to fuel up for the full day of sightseeing we had ahead. Also, the hotel is located just a short walk to the 6th Floor Museum and other sites!

Stayed at the Carlyle recently for 3 nights on business because my regular NYC options were fully booked. There are aspects of this hotel that I love-- location, art deco design (particularly in the lobby), Bemmelman's bar, excellent service.
That said, what I do not love is that the hotel-- and in particularly the rooms, hallways and elevators-- feel old, tired and threadbear.
There have been some efforts made by laying new carpet in the rooms, updated beds and bed linens and a few other touches, but the overall feel is tired. The bathrooms are very old. They used top of the line materials when they were build, but after decades of use they look worn and outdated. Same goes for the old, rickety herringbone wood floor. Most of the furniture in the rooms looks cheap and very outdated (as opposed to fine quality, and antique).
The Carlyle is pricey. There is a cost for all this history and prized location. But, as its long-time customer base ages, serious changes (upgrades) will need to be made if it's going to retain its position at the top of the market.

Stopped here on business during the week after a delayed flight from NYC and was grateful that the hotel was so close. Service was great at check in - very fast and they offered bottled water while waiting, a nice touch. The room and linens were fairly standard for a hilton - crisp white sheets, lots of tv channels, mini bar, iron, hairdryer, etc. The bathroom was a bit dated though with towels that were ok but not as plush as what I have gotten at other hiltons.

title_masked: Nice hotel very centrally located in Baltimore
text_masked: This is a very nice, recently remodeled hotel centrally located in downtown Baltimore. The adjacent parking is very secure and the staff is over the top friendly and helpful. They went out of their way to insure we knew all of the attractions in the area and made us feel like family at the thursday evening complimentary cocktail party. This was another Choice Hotel that met all of our expectations and presented us exceptional value for our travel dollar. Be sure to talk with Lou to find all the out of the way insider things to do and see.

At first glance, The Valencia Hotel had to win me over. It had the kind of dark-wood interior that I associate with private clubs where men sit around and smoke cigars. However, the hotel won me over pretty quickly.
The good:
- The rooms are quiet and well-appointed. There is the large-screen TV with a good range of TV channels, including a program guide. I even found an ambient content channel that provided soothing company while I got ready in the mornings.
- The rooms have the quietest air conditioning I've ever experienced (and I've experienced a lot). It's whisper quiet.
- The beds are very comfy, and the pillows are heavenly. (Though the last day they must have flipped the mattress because it suddenly became so tall, I couldn't climb onto it!)
- FREE IN-ROOM WIFI. There's actually a cabled connection, as well, in case the wifi isn't strong enough. This made my stay infinitely more pleasant, as I ended up using it a fair bit at night.
- Lovely breakfast. It is included in the price, and has a good balance of protein and carbs. Each day, the recipes varied so I didn't get bored with eggs. And they had a great variety of tea - I have a fondness for genmaiche tea, and they had a good-quality variety.
- Free self-parking. This was a little tricky as the parking lot around the corner always seems to be full. Every night but one, I found a spot, though. The night I couldn't find a spot, I handed over the keys to the valet, who whisked the car away to be parked.
- The views. From rooftop bar to lovely courtyard, it's a sight for sore eyes.
- Lots of shopping. It's on one of those rows of high-end shops with chi-chi everything. It's not my thing, but the other two people I travelled with seemed to enjoy the selections.
The not-so-good:
- The rooms are filled with mood lighting (the older you get, the more light you need to see properly) so if you're there on business and need to work, you really do need to position yourself under one of the lights.
- The chair to sit on while working is uncomfortable. It is woven something-or-other, and meant for very tall people. To keep my legs from going numb, I had to pile on some pillows and turn the trash bin on its side as a kind of footstool.
Overall, this is a luxury hotel and I wouldn't hesitate to recommend it to anyone.

For the price of these rooms, you would think that the hotel would not charge you for parking AT ALL! Plenty of parking space next to the hotel, $11 per night is rediculous; especially of outdoor parking.
The hotel is nicley laid out and the atrium is beautiful. Get a room that overlooks the outside rather than the atrium if you like to see sky. The pool is beautiful and has music playing on good quality speakers. On a beautiful day, one could just sit out by the pool and relax. The stone work around the pool is perfect. At night when the air is crisp and cool it would be nice to have a fire place by the pool as well but they dont and the lighting is poor.
The rooms are very nice and clean. The bathrooms are very clean. You could sleep on the floor if you wanted to. The curtains, bed spreads, desks, etc.. are all very well done. The beds we had were two double beds in each room and they were not very good. They bounced alot and didn't offer support for the back. Perhaps this was just in these rooms or the double beds in general. One would wonder what the king or queen beds would feel like.
The suite doors that shut between the two rooms are not very thick and one can see the light of the other room through the cracks. The couple next to my room got up at 6AM and I could hear their conversation and radio. But the radio was up loud.
The wireless signal in the rooms is very poor however each room comes with an ethernet cable. My son's room had an issue with the ethernet connection though. We thought it was the cord and they brought up a new cord. It wasn't with the cord so we called the 877 number that is printed on the card next to the cable and they figured out the problem over the phone and fixed the issue by having another signal "pinged" to the room.
The hotel is only 7 miles from the center of Austin and there are two ways to get to the University from here. You can take 71 West to I35 but you are going to hit the I35 traffic. Or you can take 183 South to MLK and take MLK to downtown; this is the perfered route and it takes you right to the stadium and campus. The hotel is not that far away.
The hotel has many great and spacious meeting rooms. We walked through many of them and they are big and nicley laid out.
Would probably stay here again, but probably won't due to the parking fee. Many of other nice 3 to 4 star hotels closer to campus that do not charge for parking.

It is what it is, and it will be what it is: a hotel with everything a traveler on a budget needs: a clean room, a wonderful staff, an a decent breakfast. I spent from Sunday, August 19 afternoon of last week until Wednesday, August 22, afternoon of the same week with them. I was on a "mini-vacation" and my first visit to NYC. The staff was so friendly and efficient...even though I got a bit lost from Penn Station to the hotel...(that's not THEIR fault I'd never been to NYC!)...I also work in a much larger hotel, 405 rooms of full service in a smaller city, and after perspective of MY guests complaining about "small rooms"..I'd ask them if they'd ever been to NY? In the end, I had a WONDERFUL time in this hotel. Thanks to those that helped me have the vacation of a lifetime! OH: did I forget to say the room was very clean, I was very comfortable and felt safer in NYC than I do in my own hometown? I appreciated the hospitality and NY hospitality may even rival our own here in Savannah!

We had a really nice stay at the Ramada. We've stayed at a number of hotels/motels in the Columbus area, and this Ramada is the nicest of all of them for the best value. The biggest perk is the friendly, accommodating staff. I love the continental breakfast. The rooms are pretty nice, too (mattresses are a bit hard for my liking, though). This time, we had a water spot on the ceiling, but all else is really clean and tidy.

title_masked: Not the place to stay . . . even for one night!
text_masked: We moved to Colorado, and rather than rent a place while looking to buy a home, we decided to stay at the "Best" Inn & Suites on Quebec St. in Denver. What DID sell us was we had pets that were allowed to stay here. However, from there, it goes downhill. In a one-month period (Feb 2012), they shut the entire building's water off 3 weekends in a row . . . . for hours at a time. Then mid-week we come from work to our room only to have the water shut off AGAIN . . . for hours!! (Constantly told they were working on the "boilers".) The washing machines are often broke. They only "clean" the long-term rooms on Wednesdays, and if you have pets and are not here, you're out of luck for "maid service." You have to go get your own linens, make your own bed, clean your own bathroom and borrow their sh***y vacuum that leaves the carpet gross. The walls are sticky with stains, the blankets have holes and their WiFi is poor. This building is very old and the fact that they don't even have shut-off valves on the water to shut off only certain areas at a time, is an indication of how out of code the building is. We ONLY stayed because we weren't sure when our house was going to close, and not knowing the area, we didn't know if we'd end up some place worse. At this point . . . I highly doubt it. I wouldn't recommend this place to anyone except the homeless and they should stay for free!

Stayed here recently for a conference near Times Square. Loved this location. Walked here from Penn Station, to the conference in Times Square, and to the West Village for dinner. Very convenient. The hotel itself was very nice. The room and bathroom were a decent size for NYC. The bed was comfortable and the room very clean. I had some trouble getting the thermostat to work properly, but otherwise a problem free stay. A good choice for a stay in NYC.

Hotel thinks that because of its location, it does not need to provide a comfortable enviroment. (location is good for downtown mainly) We stayed in a Jr. Suite which had ample room, but very uncomfortable furniture. In an attempt to update the hotel to "modern," they have furnished the rooms with the most inappropriate chairs and couch. The bed was of the poorest quality. Even with the requested foam mattress, it was impossible to sleep on. I may as well have slept on the floor. The room service is very slow. I was put on hold for 12 minutes while trying to order food. Not once but twice. I could have run across the street and got food quicker.
The street noise is VERY LOUD, and in the city, it usually lasts all night long. Hense the
ear plugs that are provided in each room. The rooms are clean. The food in the resturant is good. The apps in the bar are terrible. Room service food, which you can get it. is also
good. Parking is $50.00 a night and valet only. Which, in the city is "the usual". There are too many hotels to choose from in this area. Because of the room quality and odd layout of the hotel, we probably will not be staying here again. Bart and bus service is closely available. Which if you have no car, is a big plus.

Genuine welcome, excellent Gatti's pizza delivery recommendation, near a local #350 bus stop, free shuttle between airport and hotel, big well-placed TV on wall, big full breakfasts. A great Microtel - not your usual Mictrotel.

While staying in LA over the weekend between business trips, I was looking for a hotel that was close to Hollywood but far enough away that I was going to be able to catch up on some much needed rest time! This was the perfect fit. 
First, don't let the outside scare you away. It looks like an old dorm building (and probably was at one point considering its proximity to UCLA) and even a Starwood veteran like me wondered how they could possibly have made up for it inside. But they did - the lobby is open and modern, the rooms are retro but cozy and our rooms had wall to wall windows that we could open and look right out on the campus. There are also some fun little quirks in the hotel like video picture frames in the elevators. 
Second, the hotel has good social space without being the socialite gathering place. There is a fantastic pool area and nearby bar, but it gets crowded on weekends so make sure to stake out your place early if you plan on getting that prime seat. The hotel bar was nice, but never very full...it could be because we weren't staying out past 11pm, but never saw more than a handful of people in there.
Third, the service is outstanding. When a front desk agent overheard me saying how much I wanted to go to the spa, she gave me two 20% off coupons. When we were charged for a bottle of wine the people before us had opened, the front desk removed the charge, no questions asked. All of the staff were friendly and knowledgeable throughout our stay.
The only big drawback we found was that you do have to valet unless you can find a spot on the street in the nearby neighborhoods. This is fairly standard for a W, however. 
Bottom line, this hotel comes with the W standards but with a toned down nightlife - perfect for us.

We stayed in Philadelphia for my Brothers graduation in the Month of May 2012. For the 1st two days we stayed in Residence Inn Marriott and the next two days we stayed here. This Hotel by Hilton is at a beautiful location and the suites were large enough for 4 people. We had our room at the 14th Floor, and the view from above was absolutely awesome. The whole square lit up at the night and the view from above is beautiful. The staff seemed a bit arrogant initially, but later on it was ok, may be bad day sort of things.

Stayed here 9/13/12 and 9/14/12. Very nice location and beautiful lobby/restaurant area. The staff was great. The rooftop bar was an amazing way to take in the city. The only downside for the hotel was the rooms (happens to be a very important part of a hotel stay). Our room was very small - even for NYC. The other major drawback to the rooms was very slow draining in the shower and sink. By the end of the shower, the water was up past my ankles...

Service was great, very helpful but you need to be aware if you get a front room facing the road, that there is no sound proofing and there are only blinds in the windows - which let in a fair amount of light. 
In addition, on one particular night a fellow guest in the room next door decided to hold a impromptu party at 3am. The noise was so loud, we thought it was coming from outside. After we realised it was coming from the room next door, the hotel security acted very quickly in evicting the guest and his friends - but after travelling for 12 hours this was not something we appreciated.
The restaurant was great, friendly quick service, and good food. Our 2 year old was appreciative of the complimentary crayons/colouring book.
The rooms were clean and spacious. Hotel is in a good location for shopping and visiting local attractions.

title_masked: Lovely facility. Lovely rooms. Wish the TV reception was better. That's the only complaint.
text_masked:
Perfect room, perfect bed. Wish the night stand radio accept iPads. These days, it's only iPods or iPhones.
Delighted to have ice in my room. I wish they'd find a way to let me know they do it. I was surprised to pick up the ice bucket to travel to the ice machine only to learn the bucket was full.
Stunning! Food is out of this world! The service is stellar...I love all the high end amenties that this hotel has to offer. I will be back again!

Stayed 3 nights at the end of May 2012. Due to several arrivals at the same time, we ended up taking our luggage in ourselves. Other than this, our stay was perfect (minus the illness). We were surprised with a room upgrade to a suite on the 8th floor. The suite was towards the rear of the hotel so it was quiet. There was plenty of space for the 2 of us with a separate living area with sofa, another TV & desk. There was a soaking tub & separate shower. The bedroom was large with a king bed that was very comfy. The robes were comfy as well.
Our package included breakfast in-room or in the restaurant. My wife, of course, opted for breakfast in bed. The room service was prompt, hot & delicious. We arrived on Memorial Day and the restaurant was closed for the evening. There were so many restaurants to try in the Dupont Circle area that we never made it to the hotel restaurant otherwise.
The staff in the Palomar were all great. Whether it was opening the door, the evening wine tasting, housekeeping or the front desk, everyone was friendly & helpful. My wife became ill late at night and needed medical attention. The help was prompt, efficient & understanding. We couldn't have asked for more. Thank you!
Will definitely return to the Palomar when in DC.

If you want a comfortable, clean room with all the amenities in midtown manhattan, this is the hotel for you. small and tucked away right around the corner from Macy's it is so convenient to the shopping areas, eateries, and transportation. The staff is wonderful and accomodating and friendly and courteous. They helped accomodate me when I had to unexpectedly stay an extra nite and was able to stay in the same room, much to my relief, even though they were booked up!

My husband and I spent Columbus Day week-end in NYC. It was the first trip for us. This week-end was a gift from our children and our youngest son arranged the accommodations. He could not have chosen a better hotel. Our stay at the Hilton Times Square was fantastic. We had a corner room with views of the Empire State Building and the Statue of Liberty and 8th and W. 42nd. The room was huge, clean, and comfortable ( although we spent most of the week- end out and about in the City). Although this hotel is right in Times Square, it was quiet and the energy and noise from the city could not be heard in our room. Our flight arrived well before check-in and we were able to check our luggage early. Our return flight home was after check-out time and we checked the luggage again. Sure beat dragging around NY with us. Everyone at the hotel was more than helpful. As newbies to the subway system, Long was very helpful to us on Saturday and Sunday helping us with the correct subway and transfers. On Monday, our final day, Chad inquired on our stay, the sights we had seen, and asked how our trip and stay had been. Irene, at concierge, helped us with return subway and air train directions back to JFK. I would recommend the Hilton Times Square. It is convenient to the subway, the heart of NY, the staff is friendly and very helpful. The rooms are big, comfortable, and clean.

The hotel had a perfect location for our short visit in Chicago. We got a great price for a beautiful hotel. Our high tech room was very comfortable, quiet, great shower and nice balcony. The staff are attentive and friendly. I enjoyed the company of my friends at the contemporay bar/lounge, the pool and hot tub. Overall, had a good experience.

The hotel has an unusual entrance (escalators) but the lobby is very nice. It ressembles a hunting lodge and clearly is a bar scene for locals. We booked a Deluxe Queen room for 3 nights but when we said that we were intending to have our simple civil wedding at the hotel, the Guest Experience Manager ("GEM") immediately upgraded us to their suite (their best room) at no extra charge. We decided to hold the ceremony in their Penthouse Suite with private terrace. The Suite was extremely expensive for all but the very rich (>$4000/night) but we were able to hire it for an hour for $500. The GEM covered the floor with rose petals and candles and made it look great.
The other thing that I definitely want to mention was the outstanding service and care provided by the various concierges. They recommended and booked at great restaurants and made sure that the next concierge on duty knew everything that had been spoken between us. They arranged ground transportation and called me on my cell phone multiple times to ensure that everything was right.
One negative point which I see others have noted too is that while the A/C is very effective, it makes all manners of clanking sounds.
In summary, I would say that the rooms are pricey and too small for what you get (unless you get a free upgarde). Location is great, but what really gets the 5 Star treatment is the service by the GEMs and Concierges.

title_masked: nice property and that's about it...
text_masked: First, we stayed on points, and this was a good value for the amount of points required. Our room was large and clean and new. Now for the bad: the staff was impersonal--my husband checked us in, and as our family walked in, no one at the desk acknowledged us (the desk and lobby were empty). The kids wanted to swim in the indoor pool, and it was trashed--dirty towels everywhere, trash left out and no clean towels. When we asked at the desk for pool towels, she replied "there are some in there". We told her there were not, and she insisted on coming to look for herself then stormed off to bring more. While in the pool area, she did not clean up a thing. There is no breakfast offered, so we headed up to the local HEB grocery every morning. On our last night, there was a auto break-in on a car parked right in front of the hotel. Definitely will not be back.

As always this hotel was superb, has clean spacious rooms, good value for the money, but the return pick up could be better, they are a little slow and directions were unclear on where to go exactly...

The Rooms are small , but nicely furnished.
My son loved the internet which cost around $12 a day, but he could download lots of stuff, that he could not download in other hotels that charge almost the same, but put a limit on the
band-width.
Like others we were hoping to get Two beds since we are Mother and son, but ended up in one bed which was big enough for both, no big deal.
Did not eat there, so could not rate the food. The area is full of resturants, so we ate at diffrent places daily.
Nearby work was being done at night, the managment offered ear plugs and an apology letter, our room was on the other alley side , so we felt only a little of the noise, and managed to sleep.

I've loved this hotel for years, staying there many times in it's previous incarnation as the Rihga Royal. The all-suite layout boasts a promiscuous use of space by NYC hotel standards. The recent renovations provided the polish and sophistication befitting a top notch luxury hotel. Combine that with world class dining, perfect location and efficient courteous service and you have one of the best choices in the highly competitive NYC luxury hotel market. 
Only one issue marred my otherwise flawless stay. When I arrived, I was taking my rollerbag out of the taxi. The doorman attempted to take it from me. I said, "No worries - I've got it." He insisted, wrestling the bag out of my hands and then rolling the 30 pound bag to the check in desk less than 20 feet away. While the agent at the desk was welcoming me and asking for my credit card and ID, he stood there staring at me. Eventually, I realized that he had no intention of leaving without a tip. Nor did he intend to help me with the baggage to the room. 20 feet of unwanted assistance, and then he demands a tip?! While tipping has historically been customary with NYC bellman, it is a rarity elsewhere on the planet. But even if you allow that tips are traditional, this sort of aggressive behavior verges on a scam and is unworthy of an otherwise lovely hotel.

Very friendly, great service, centrally located to great shopping .take the "L" train to get there and back to airport was easy because the kind staff helped us. The city is clean, beautiful and Chicago people are so very friendly.

I'm not usually one to leave bad reviews but there was just too many little things that bothered me about the hotel. It is now apparently the Chatsworth Hotel but I had originally booked it as a Radisson. For a moment, we thought were were in the wrong place since the sign out front had changed but nothing else.
We needed a place close to some family, which is why we chose this hotel. The distance from where we needed to be was good but that seemed to be the only thing. When we walked through the hotel to the 3rd floor, we could definitely see that the hotel was in desperate need of some maintenance. The rugs were worn, there were questionable stains in the hallways, the sleep number bed remote wasn't working, etc. The hotel said they had room service but there was no menu in the room, nor was there any information in a book as most hotel rooms provide.
There was pounding throughout the night, almost as if people were running up and down the halls or even up and down the walls themselves. We had to call down for extra sheets for the sofa bed, which was fine and they opened up the sofa bed for me. The set-up of the room wasn't that great as the sofa bed was directly in front of the air conditioning unit which made for me being freezing and my sister not getting enough air. I also have bad allergies to dust mites and kept coughing and sneezing the entire time I was in the room. The moment I stepped out, I was fine, which made me wonder how clean the place really was.
I had booked the hotel for my sister and myself over the phone and asked for all price quotes and charges that were part of the bill so I could make a decision about this hotel and another nearby. I was given the quote of $81 a night with AAA for the weekend plus hotel tax. Okay, that's normal. Imagine my surprise when my credit card was charged $150 more than what my final bill was as I was checking out of the hotel. When I called, I was told that the hotel charged $50/night for incidentals and that it was on the website. Yes, but I didn't book through the website. He said I was GIVEN a form that outlined this when I called. I was passed along a sheet of paper that had my dates of check-in and check-out, and requested my sister's information (as she would be holding the 2nd key), the make of our rental car, and the license plate number.
The man on the phone was not helpful and told me that so long as the room was in the same condition as it was before we arrived, the money would be returned in "maybe 3-4 days, maybe longer."
While the hotel was near where we needed to be, I would have much preferred to stay at a hotel slightly farther away for a cleaner space, a room with the desired information, and better service. While Jose was helpful the one night, it seemed no one else cared whether or not the guests were comfortable or were given basic information.

very nice desk staff at arrival and check in very easy,room and bathroom very good.hotel is a older 1 but i thought it was just fine.hotel is about 2 blocks from the mag mile,so there is heaps of shops close by and more places to eat than u can poke a stick at.recommmend chilles around the corner.breakfast was good with a egg choice thru to grits,potatoes and meats and ceral,youghurt and pancakes.
had a good 2 night stay and would stay again.

title_masked: Great Value Hotel With Good Location
text_masked:
We recently stayed at the Rodeway Inn PCH on a west coast road trip and it was definitely worth the money we paid to stay there. While it isn't right in Los Angeles, it is close enough to so many major highways that you can really get anywhere in the metropolitan area quickly enough (assuming you're not needing to travel during rush hour). We were able to travel to Malibu, downtown LA, and Hollywood from here without any real traffic delays, which we did not expect going in. 
As far as the room itself, it was basically what you expect from a Rodeway. This certainly isn't a five-star resort, but the rooms were very clean and mostly quiet. The bed was very comfortable and that is much appreciated given the low quality beds at many similarly priced hotels. Overall, this hotel was definitely worth the money and it was a great spot for us leaving for our next destination in San Diego. The owner was very nice and accommodating as well, which added to the positive experience.

We were travelling through San Francisco and stayed at the Galleria Park for 2 nights. The hotel's location in the city centre, less than 5 mins walk from the Chinatown gate, is great. It is easily accessible from the BART station as well, also less than 5 mins walk. We had a rental car but did not park at the hotel - they charged $38 per day for their valet service, but there was a carpark about 50 yards up the road which offered overnight parking for $15.
The hotel itself was simple. The interior decor was alright, nothing special. The building is not new, and as such the rooms were not either. The bed was comfortable and the bathroom amenities as you would expect. Everything was good, just nothing special.
The website makes the hotel look very modern and swish. It doesn't quite match this in real life.
If location is your main requirement, we would recommend this hotel.

title_masked: Good hotel, but service is average and too expensive
text_masked: We stayed at this hotel for an entire week, the rooms are clean and the location is fine. We arrived from Europe after a long flight at 1.30 pm. We got our rooms at 4pm and we had to call the front desk at least 6 times in order to find out if the rooms were ready. One of us got a room so we could wait there - but definitely this is not what you expect. Rooms were made always in the afternoon, excluding on the day of departure - on that day the cleaning lady showed up at 8am!!

I got an OK deal on Priceline for the Wardman Park for three nights (Fri-Sat-Sun) at the end of June. When I checked in the desk clerk assigned me to the oldest part of the hotel ("the Wardman Tower") which was built in 1928. I was actually happy about this, because the rest of this sprawling convention complex dates from the late '70s and lacks character and charm. 
The historic wing where I stayed was a bit threadbare and would benefit from a sensitive renovation, but was nonetheless tidy and has retained some of its old-school grandeur. Perhaps because I was traveling solo, I was assigned one of the smaller rooms (#3343) with just one bed that seemed to be a bit smaller than a queen but larger than a double. Definitely NOT a king, which might be a problem for a couple staying in this room. 
The room was traditional in appearance but clean and comfortable and seemed to have been refurbished in the not-too-distant past. The air conditioning kept it nice and cool during a record-breaking heat wave. The cold air blew directly onto the bed, but I improvised a solution by tucking a FedEx envelope into the grate to serve as a diffuser. The spotless wall-to-wall carpet rolled up and down a bit in spots, prompting me to wonder about the condition of the flooring beneath it. 
The bathroom was unusually long and narrow with a nice old sink with chrome legs. All very clean and the pink wallpaper appeared to be rather new.The bathroom actually had a window, but I don't know if it was still operable. (The big window in the bedroom was a replacement window that looked old-fashioned but could not be opened.) No tub in the bathroom just a generic square plastic shower stall. The water pressure was excellent but, as others have noted, the shower head was so low that I had to duck my head beneath it to wash my hair.
No minibar in the room. It would have been nice to have a refrigerator, but I wasn't in the room enough to really need one. The selection of TV channels was rather limited, I'm guessing that management hopes you'll splurge on pay-per-view. WiFi was $13/day for basic and $17/day for better speed. I went for the upgrade and had no trouble streaming content on my laptop. The hotel has two underground garages that offer self-parking for $32/day - there isn't really any other option, because on-street parking in the surrounding residential area is a total crapshoot.
The modern areas of the hotel are so rambling and featureless that it's easy to get lost. But every cloud has a silver lining: I did some excellent air-conditioned hiking without stepping out into Washington's summer heat and humidity. Still, for future visits to NW DC, I would look into staying at the adjacent Omni Shoreham Hotel, which is more attractive and inviting.

We stayed two nights in this extremely clean motel that is only a slow ten minute stroll to the Ripley's Believe It or Not Museum, Kodak Theatre , Madame Tussauds' Wax Museum and more. The staff is very pleasant and helpful, and for the price it can't be beat.

My wife and I stayed here last weekend while my son and his wife had their reception at the Green Room at the War Memorial in SF. What a gem. We were treated with great courtesy and we loved the room. I wish we had time to stay longer. 
The hotel is perfectly positioned in Civic Center where we needed to be. We actually fell out the back door of the reception to land a few hundred feet from out hotel. 
The staff was great, hospitable, and the accommodations perfect. Our room was really nice. It was a great way to finish off our son getting married. 
The other big item was the value this hotel offers. It is generally very expensive in SF during the summer months for tourists. We live only 30 miles away. So this is another reason for the recommendation. 
This would be a good spot for tourists too, as it is centrally located to other points in SF. It is close to shopping and Union Square is a short cab ride away. So is the Wharf and North Beach are a short ride away too. Other forms of public transportation are close too. 
I will definitely stay here again. It will probably be my first choice as a matter of fact. 
It is a boutique hotel with great service, charm, and hospitality. Go for it. 
Bill M.

title_masked: Great renovations at the Arizona Biltmore
text_masked: Just returned from my annual visit to the Arizona Biltmore (annual conference for work). The first night I was in a room in the main building which was quite large and beautiful but the echoes from outside made it nearly unbearable to sleep before midnight or after 4 am when they were moving furniture around outside. So they moved me to the Ocatilla Wing. Great renovations to those rooms. The bathrooms in particular were very nice. The greatest improvement at the hotel was the wifi available in the rooms! It is always a beautiful place to stay with a great gym and spa. Just avoid getting a room on the 4th floor of the main building if you can.

My wife and I stayed for one night prior to attending the Strictly Sail Show at Navy Pier. We found
the hotel via the Strictly Sail web site, which had an arrangement with the Sheraton Towers hotel. We upgraded to a 'Deluxe' room, which overlooked the Chicago River facing west. The Club Room was very nice, with a nice selection of snacks in the evening. The staff both in the Club Room and hotel was very polite and friendly.

Close to DIA. Clean rooms, nice hotel staff, good buffet. The rooms were very clean as was the whole hotel. Within walking distance to restrauants. Hotel shuttle very dependable. Cant beat the price for what you get

Stayed here while attending a conference (in east harlem). Hotel is centrally located a few blocks from grand central (subway ride to conference was about 10 minutes) and easy walking distance to many various tourist attractions, museums, restaurants, ect. Room was very clean but did have a funky oder (like wet carpet) . The size of the room (queen) was comfortable for one person, (two would be quite cozy) and surprisingly quiet.Staff are very friendly,helpful and informative. Rooftop bar has a nice view and was a relaxing haven during a warm sunny autumn day. Downstairs bar had just opened up on the day I had left, but there are numerous neighborhood bars in close walking distance. With it's super convenient location and reasonably priced rooms this hotel is definitely a gem!

This weekend, I stayed at the InterContinental because I was a contestant in the Miss [NAME] pageant, and that was the hotel where the pageant was taking place. However, when we first got there, the line was a mile long, which at first I assumed was just a bunch of other pageant contestants and their families. Later, I found out that the majority of those families were going to talk to the front desk because they had complaints. Later, I found that you could take your pick: Only 3 of 6 elevators worked, making going up and down from the rooms to the lobby and ballroom take approximately 10 minutes just to get down there, they charged for Wi-Fi (THE HOLIDAY INN HAS IT FREE!), they charged for parking (THE HOLIDAY INN ALSOOOO HAS IT FREE), they had no refrigerators in the room, and they screwed up our reservations, so my mom and I ended up staying in a king bed instead of two double beds, the way they said they would arrange it. There was also no breakfast available, although my mom and I discovered a room for breakfast, supposedly if you have a special card on the 15th floor. I'm not sure, but I think that they didn't tell any of the people with National American Miss that there was a breakfast room if you had a card, just so they wouldn't mob the place upstairs. I can't really say that's fair... Because if we're going to be paying $110 dollars per night PLUS a ridiculous amount of tax, I expect good service. That's why I was not impressed really whatsoever with the InterContinental. The one good thing going for them was that the rooms and bathrooms were very pretty and clean. I feel like if we had just stayed at the Mariott across the street or the Holiday Inn down the block that I would have been able to get to the Pageant activities quicker (seeing as the elevators moved like 1 foot every minute...). Unfortunately, I would not recommend the InterContinental to a friend. But if you plan on staying there, you can decide if you like it for yourself!

title_masked: Great location, great staff, great hotel.
text_masked:
We stayed here after reading all the favourable reviews and we weren’t disappointed. We had a room on the 10th floor at the front and, whilst you could hear traffic, it was never loud enough to keep you awake. Mind you, we crammed so much in that staying awake wasn’t an option anyway – New York is such a great place to visit.
The hotel staff were excellent – always friendly and helpful – and the breakfasts were very good. The afternoon tea and coffee (wine as well during the week) were excellent too – it’s great to come in after a day’s walking around and sight-seeing and have a cake or biscuit with a nice cup of coffee or some wine with cheese and biscuits. The free wireless is a bonus too – I had to keep up with a few work emails whilst there and it was great to not have to think about the costs etc.
We went to the Waldorf Astoria whilst we were traipsing around and whilst it is grand and very opulent it’s also a bit of a rip off in the bar and they certainly don’t give you much for free. The Elysee by contrast is more humble but just felt really comfortable and homely. Our room was a King Deluxe I think and had a massive bed and lots of space. The bed was really comfortable and the sheets were nice and soft. There’s the odd review around talking about bed bugs – I think these are from 4 or 5 years ago so they may have been true but there was nothing of the sort whilst we were there. The whole place is very clean and well looked after.
It was my 50th birthday – the reason for the trip – and the hotel gave us a nice bottle of wine and some chocolates. It was a really nice gesture.
We’d go back in an instant if we ever go back to New York – and we probably will!

This was our second visit from when we spent our honeymoon on last year and had such a great time that we decided to go back. From the moment my wife and I arrived at the hotel, Phil greeted my wife and I with the most prestige greeting you could give someone arriving at your establishment. The bellman expedited our luggage to our room and the check in was a breeze. The room was immaculate and a breathtaking suite. They even had an edible white chocolate card with strawberries acknowledging us on our special day. All throughout the weekend we were treated like royalty. Thumbs up twice...this is our favorite place to go!

A welcome retreat in NYC. Away from the midtown crowds, and close to the Met, Frick, Whitney, Central Park and the general luxury of the Upper East Side. Overall, a nice boutique (Relais) hotel with all the charm, attentive service, and comforts that one should expect. Clean and hip decor-- part Art Deco, part modern 50's, artistic and chic. No stressed out business types that I could see Spacious rooms, view of Madison Ave passing beneath us, marbled bathroom, great shower. Missed the coffee in the lobby somehow, but decent breakfast place around the corner, and missing shampoo, but we survived. In sum, in from CT for the evening and will definitely do it again.

My best friend and I stayed at the W City Center for a girls weekend get away. The location was fabulous! Within walking distance from the train station as well as some of the best shopping in the US. Our favorite part of our weekend trip was complimentary tickets to Kristin Chenoweth at the Cadillac Palace - (thanks to the Concierge Eden - she is the best!!). We also used the complimentary Acura car service twice. Rian and Hillary in the bar were great, as well as Christiana in the resturant. My only complaint was our room was very small and had writing on the wall. I called ahead to see if we could have 2 double beds - when we booked online we were not given the option to choose this - I was told we would have to wait to see. When we arrived we asked again and were told we would have to pay a significant upcharge for this. The individual checking us in stated this was due to us booking online where we "must have received a significant savings" - I thought this comment was very unprofessional. If it were not for these two small complaints I would have given the W City Center an Excellent versus a Very Good rating.

title_masked: Above and beyond. Great rooms and service.
text_masked: Just stayed one night for business and found a good rate online and decided to book Hotel 1000. The new construction (2006) was attractive and its downtown location near meetings and shopping. Upon check-in the staff was great, offered us a complimentary drink and upgraded our room. Rooms are spacious (saw two) and contemporary in style (more Four Seasons than Ritz). Complimentary newspaper, coffee and donuts in the morning were a great surprise along with free wifi. As we left, we could not be happier with our stay at Hotel 1000 and found two new water bottles in the cup holders from the valet. Many hotels aspire to exceed expectations but Hotel 1000 deliver with professional and friendly service. I highly recommend this hotel.

We (my wife and younger adult son) stayed here for two weeks in May. Suite was clean and spacious; kitchen facilities very good. Bed was uncomfortable though as one rolled in towards the center over time! Room service was erratic at times; often we had to call down for towels, etc for the third person; then, we would get double allotments. Location was definitely convenient to the museums, to the subway/train station, to the historic sites, etc. A new visitor's center is just a couple of blocks away in a beautiful pocket park where one can have coffee and plot out the day. Always felt safe in this vicinity whether day or evening.

title_masked: Great Hotel, Wonderful Staff, Great Price!
text_masked: Title of my review says it all. I would have loved to stay more nights, but it was already booked solid. There is a reason it is booked solid, and it is because it offers everything a traveler wants and needs: location, price, service, space, comfort, and amenities.

I'm honestly pretty shocked at the few bad reviews I have seen for this hotel. My family I had two rooms here for 3 nights and we enjoyed our time!
The rooms and lobby were so unique and it was enough room for us. We had 3 adults and 2 kids and opted to have two rooms, so perhaps this was why. The front desk associates were gracious enough to have our rooms next door to one another.
I loved the fact that the toilet and tub were in two seperate rooms with sliding doors. This way, if I was in the tub for a bath, my son or nephew could still use the toilet without disturbing me or me having to hear their bodily functions. Ha! 
The extra sitting area was appreciated as was the mini fridge and microwave. We were able to store Capri Suns for late night thirst attacks and use the microwave to heat up leftovers from dinners out. 
There are SEVERAL restaurants very close to the hotel and Walmart is literally right next door if the small "store" the hotel has in the lobby isn't enough for you.
The workers were all very friendly and the only minus is the small pool. It is indoors (which is a good thing to me) but it was small. It was good enough for us, though. There were multiple outside smoking areas for smokers complete with nice seating. The free breakfast was good enough for us and included an egg dish, a meat and the usual offerings of cereals, various breads, yogurts, milks and juices.
Should we visit San Antonio again to visit SeaWorld (which it was only minutes away from), we will certainly come back to SpringHill Suites Lackland/SeaWorld. The price was a great deal, we felt, for everything we received.

The Swissotel is connected to the building that houses our Chicago office, so it's very convenient for me. The rooms are stylish and clean, and I had a nice view of the lake, river, and Navy Pier. I would stay again.

We stayed at this hotel for 3 nights while in LA.
We found the downtown location very convenient, once we rented a car, and it was easy to drive to wherever we wanted.
Check in was relatively easy, and the rooms were nice and well appointed.
The bed is heaven. This is the second Westin we stay at, and we find their beds always comfortable, with very nice linen and pillows.
The bathroom is a bit small, but on the other hand, the shower is great.
We stayed at a high floor and had nice views of the city from our window, which was great.
The hotel lobby is gourgeous, and the panoramic lift was such a nice touch.
The only cons we have about this hotel are:
1) Cost of parking - found it extremely expensive. OK, I know we're in LA, but c'mon.... 
2) No self park - nothing against vallets, but we find self-parking super easy and convenient ( =no waiting in line for your car)
3) No wi-fi in the room (only in the lobby). I still don't get why hotels offer free wi-fi as a complimentary service... Nowadays, free wi-fi should be a must, and nothing to distinguish one hotel from the other. Everybody is wired, so why charge for you to have internet in your room?
4) Room service: we ordered some soups for our first day at the hotel, once we arrived in a holiday, with very options to eat nearby (this must be another con about staying downtown). The soups were tasteless, and considering the amount we paid we should've gotten something much better.. Also, be prepared to stay at least 30 min over the phone in order to place your order. Room service is definetely a NO at this hotel.
