Considering the price we paid for the room, and the opportunity to stay at such an iconic hotel, we would come back, but would certainly try to find another option for parking.

title_masked: Don't be fool by 5 Million Renovation ads.
text_masked:
Great Location very convenience to subway with attractive big lobby didnt made up for such a small room, black mold between bath room tile and $39 self parking for the 4 stars price. 
Boston is beautiful out door flea market is a short subway ride where you could shop and have a 'BEST' New England clam chowder served in the round bread in the food court.. delicious better than an exclaimed Legal Sea Food. such a beautiful City. nw

You're probably here for the location, which is the top selling feature of this hotel.
THE hotel in the heart of Times Square. Really, right outside, TKTS booth steps and the area where everyone congregates to hang out and take photos. You're across the street from The Lion King, and eventually Evita will be downstairs, and Ghost the Musical will also be across the street. You can't get any more central than this.
The room was fine. I did not ask for a TS view, so looked more into the office building across the street.
The elevator system is probably the most entertaining thing (kids will likely love to play here). At the large bank of elevators (in a semi-circle), you enter your floor number, and it tells you which letter elevator to go to. This computer elevator traffic control is handy for such a big hotel. Also, the elevators are see-through, so you can watch the outside floors pass by quickly. Probably not great for those with fear of heights or vertigo, but entertaining and kind of a rush.
For me, however, I think this is probably too big a hotel. It felt more like an office building than hotel. You enter from TS and need to take the elevator to the 8th floor for the Lobby. I prefer either more of a boutique hotel, or one with a real lobby as you walk in from the street. But perhaps a minor thing.

We had a room facing the Empire State Building. Even if the room was very confortable, we spend half of the night enjoying the view :o) how could we sleep when we had such a fabulous view on New York !
Great costumer service at the reception with a very special "thank you" to Luidin for his help !
Everything was nice but breakfast is quit poor and could really be better.....also the service was there not very friendly.....

title_masked: Great experience for what it promised
text_masked:
My team and I booked several rooms here for a business event, and I got the king suite. It was the perfect size for a small meeting, and one thing I love about Courtyards is they get business. They know you have stuff to plug in, so there were several outlets for all our laptops and phones. Only beef is the staff told us the landline in that room had a speakerphone, and it didn't. 
I think someone else commented on this, but while the room was great, the design was ridiculous as there's a door in between BR and LR that is always in your way, and always swinging open. It should ideally open into the LR to be out of way, as you're continually going by this corner to the bathroom and into the BR/LR. 
Love the open lobby with plenty of seating for gatherings and places to charge your laptops. 
Decent fitness center, and I loved how it had windows that overlooked the pool. I can't stand gyms that have no windows. Only complaint is that the A/C wasn't quite working well in the gym.
Downstairs breakfast is handy to have in the a.m., and there's free coffee at the bar if you ask for it. 
Staff was always cheerful and happy to help. One of the cleaning staff wasn't too bright though, as I asked her in the downstairs hallway if there was free coffee in the lobby. After a pause, she said, "well, no. but if you ask for the complimentary coffee... that's free." Ohhhhh boy. Perhaps a bit of training needed there. But at least everyone was pleasant!

should have known better than to stay here.NOTHING is free.no free internet even though i have a hilton honors card.parking is $25 a day and i had to park six levels below the hotel.To top it off,housekeeping did not bother to clean the room one morning.This is a hotel strictly for businessmen with an expense account.

Had not stayed in Soho area before so wanted a change of scene. Took ages to decide on The James and was looking for somewher that offered a bit of personality as well as good location and high quality rooms. Overall The james ticked these boxes. Rooms were well furnished and my deluxe king was adequate for one and probably squeezy for two if you have lots of luggage. Beds sensational bathroom shower good. I had paid for deluxe because it offered higher floor ( with views) but on checkin was given a lower floor with no view and quite dark. Request to move was unable to be met that night but was moved next day. 
Hotel has small guest area in foyer that offers basic tea/ coffee and pastry in morning. Staff were pleasant and answered requests promptly but they werent looking to offer assistance. Some were not as knowledgeable as they should be when informing visitors of attravtions, sights to see. 
Used the free area car service once and this was great service. Rick the driver was really helpful. However dont rely on this being available as they werent able to offer if on two other requests.
Doorman Christopher set the tone for really impressive welcome but sadly some of his colleagues were less than pleasant and quite off hand. 
Cant comment on restaurant but couple of room service meals were ok however menu could do with few more light and healthy options. One visit to the rooftop bar was enough. It was crowded with younger set, and not comfortable for a solo traveller. 
Location is noisy, busy and a real eclectic mix of high end shops mixed in with low end cheap and cheerful. It is interesting but a bit gritty. Transport options make getting around pretty easy. 
Generally a pleasant stay but really need to take more care with the small details ( carpet in hallway needed a good vaccuum and vaccum cleaner was left in hallway two days running) if really want to justify the prices charged.

I was in Indianapolis with my son who was bowling at the Youth Nationals. We spent 5 days at the Hyatt Place and then moved to Carmel for the following 5 days of the tournament. This hotel is absolutely beautiful, very clean in all areas, the beds are really comfortable. The staff was great at all times. We saw a patrol car one evening and asked if there had been a problem, he said no, the hotel has them circle through a few times a night just to keep an eye on things, that was nice to know. Rooms are large with a nice sitting area. The only glitch we saw in the layout of the room was the vanity goes right up to the closet and blocks one side completely making it hard to utilize the entire closet. Breakfast is fine, all the basics and always clean. They leave the breakfast area open all the time which made it really convenient to bring restaurant meals back to the hotel and grab real plates and silverware to bring to the room. No microwave in the room, but the breakfast one is available all the time. Easy location right off the highway with minimum highway noise. We requested a room on the back side of the hotel and our stay was very quiet. This was our third trip to Indy, I would stay here again in a heartbeat!

This motor inn is walking distance to Fisherman's Wharf, trolley rides, shops, stops for sightseeing buses and much else that San Francisco has to offer. A garage allowed us to park our rental car there the last night. We walked to Denny's for breakfast, but there were many other upscale places available. The room was quiet and clean and had a good view of San Fran. Felt very safe there.

I stayed here in May and had a fantasic time at the Tuscan Inn. Great hotel, lovely staff and the location is really good for both the wharf and north beach. Felt more like a 4 star than a 3 star, with good sized rooms and comfortable beds. I Highley recomend it.

We travel a lot as a family and I travel a lot for business and the customer service at this resort property was some of the best we've ever encountered. The staff was outgoing, friendly, courteous, professional and unbelievably helpful during our stay. From the front desk, to housekeeping, to the pool staff, not only was everyone helpful but every single person wore a smile. It truly was refreshing.
The grounds were gorgeous. Picture perfect from every view. The waterfalls actually extend from the top of the mountain down into the pools area. 
The pools were fantastic. There are two main pools in the Falls Village and then smaller family and adult pools scattered throughout the resort. The Falls Village rivals those pools in Disney and Vegas in my opinion. The food available at the pool was good too. Everything was fresh, not packaged. The portions were big and delicious. Example of options and prices:
Basket of Fries: $5
2 Churros: $3
Big Pretzel: $3
Big plate of veggies, pita and hummus: $10
Chicken Wrap w fries: $10
Quesadilla: $10
Etc
Drinks range from $6 for 20oz cup of domestic beer, to $10 for typical fun pool beverages like Blue Hurricanes, etc.
We got a Cabana for $54 per day (we were mid-week) and it came with Wifi, fridge, TV, loungers, table, waters, newspaper and probably the best Cabana person ever, Veronica. Thanks again for putting up with us!
The rooms are as advertised; clean, modern and spacious. The standard two-room suites (one bed, one family) made staying with the family a lot easier. Our room was in the main lobby building so parking and getting around was a snap. Balcony was a plus too.
We dined at Different Point of View as well as Point in Tyme. Those reviews are up separately.
We took advantage of the hiking trails as well. There is an under ground tunnel that takes you to a State Nature preserve that had some easy and challenging hikes. We saw some wildlife like jack-rabbits, lizards and road runners.
Overall, this was an excellent choice. Having stayed at AIs in the Caribbean, this property truly had a "resort" feel to it. I would recommend it to anyone.

title_masked: Great hotel, great staff, great location - definitely recommend
text_masked:
My fiance and I were visiting New York for a week and after researching a number of hotels on Trip Advisor decided to stay at the Warwick - we had a great time and really enjoyed staying at this hotel so would definitely recommend.
Location:
Location is key when youre a tourist in New York and this hotel is in a really great spot - smack bang in the middle between 5th Ave, T. Sq, Broadway and Central Park. The Warwick is within easy walking distance of the main tourist attractions as well as being close to the subway for quick access to the rest of the city. 
Hotel Staff:
From check in to check out the hotel staff were always friendly and happy to help with anything we needed. My fiance and I often enjoy exploring local food stops and the concierge were great at recommending restaurants that were slightly less touristy.
Hotel Rooms:
We stayed in a delux room on the 15th floor - some reviews have mentioned that the rooms are run down but ours was classically decorated and quite lovely. I have a feeling that some may have been refurbished while others havent.
I had also read in previous reviews that corner rooms looking out on to the Americas had a great view and initially we requested one of these. Unfortunately the bathroom was tiny (literally thought it was a small closet before we opened the door) so we decided to sacrifice the scene for space and take a different room. 
I would probably recommend asking for a quiet room at the back of the hotel because there is currently construction work going on at MOMA across the street. On the final 2 nights of our stay we were kept awake until after 1am with garbage trucks collecting the days rubble so we eventually asked to be moved. The staff were very understanding and quick to help us shift.
Tips:
Try to expolre Soho, Greenwich and little Italy for food and drinks - sometimes its nice to get out of the tourist traps in T. Square.
There is no free Wifi in the hotel other than the business centre which allows you 15mins before charging begins (this was fine for us since we were on holiday and only needed to use the net for printing out boarding passes etc)

I spent one night at The Independent Hotel in early Oct. in a king deluxe for single use, and I loved it! The room was very well-appointed with comfortable furniture; rich décor; and a spacious bathroom that had a shower with a wonderful double-shower head, lots of hot water, and great water pressure. The breakfast was there when I had requested it, with all the items I selected; the options include a very reasonable (but understandably not unlimited, array of normal breakfast options) - one could choose to have one each of a fruit (apple or orange), juice (orange or cranberry), cereal/grain (as I recall, oatmeal, a cereal, granola bar, or croissant), and yogurt (1 of 2 or 3 different flavors). It was nice to be able to make coffee in my room whenever I wanted. 
The hotel is also very well-located, close to various bus and subway stops and within what I considered an easy walking distance of Rittenhouse Square and City Hall.
The Independent is not a full-service hotel. If that's what you are seeking, you might be disappointed. I was not looking for that, and was very well satisfied.
I look forward to my next stay at The Independent Hotel!

title_masked: BED BUG CITY BUT COOL LOUNGE AND ROOMS AND BATHROOMS
text_masked:
Both the hotel and the lounge are WAY cool. Burtonesque decor in the lounge, good music and a live crowd. Here is my issue: BED BUGS. I had my bed bug cherry popped at this hotel. 
And ya, i live in Toronto, but in this city it's not nearly as large a problem, and in the building I live for example, we have NEVER had them. The reason I bring this up: the hotel manager emailed me and told me that Toronto has a problem too and i could have brought them from here. 
So...all you club and lounge seekers. Imagine a person staying there like me, unknowingly carrying salt grain size eggs from my room to the cool couches in the lounges..and you pick some up to infect your bug-free building. NOT a good thing to wake up to; and you WILL lose sleep. All I know is, after losing my cherry...hotel stays and travel generally speaking will never be the same.
Ignorance is bliss...sigh.
Kevin
PS the Jane hotel offered no compensation for my troubles and scars. PLus i was so paranoid I had my place sprayed when i got home.

We arrived at 3am and check in was really quick. 
We initially had a non-renovated room as all the renovated rooms were not available at checkin, but we were able to change to a renovated room on request on the second day. The non-renovated room was pretty good anyway, and I actually liked the wallpaper decorations better in the older rooms (the designs in the old rooms are homely vs modern in the renovated rooms). The bathrooms in the renovated rooms were better (better water pressure and newer).
I could hear drilling and hammering above me during the day as currently the top levels are being renovated so if you are going to be in the room during the day it is better to request for a room on a lower level.
The service was really good. The location was also pretty good. It is close to Chinatown. We were in Washington DC on a holiday and walked to most places, and took the metro to Capitol Hill. 
The only minor issue was that when we requested a spoon from the kitchen we had to pay 3.50.
Taxi cost from DCA was 16 in the middle of the night. Taxi to Dulles was 74 in the afternoon.
Free wifi is available in the lobby but if you want to try your luck in the room you should go for a room on the lower level. I could not use my laptop in the lobby as I did not see any powerpoints.
There is a Starbucks in the lobby but it seemed to close in the mid/late afternoon.

Great hotel within walking distance to many downtown restaurants. The views from the lounge area look down on all three branches of the Chicago river. At night the lights are magical. A quick walk througn Chicago's famous Merchandise Mart connects you to the "L" trains to all of downtown. Rooms are very comfortable with a very helpful Concierge to make your downtown stay memorable!

Large hotel complex - almost campus style - across the street from SeaTac airport. Front desk staff was exceptional, friendly and smiling when you checked in.....Had dinner at the hotel and Halibut was outstanding....Beer was expensive, 10 bucks for a large. Bed was comfortable and room was large on the HHonors floor. Excellent place to stay for an early flight our of SeaTac airport. Took 30 mins from leaving hotel, returning rental car, going thru security and walking to my gate - not bad for a 0600 flight.
Long ways from downtown Seattle so if your touring, then you may want to pick somewhere closer....strictly and airport hotel.

Stayed this summer for 4 nights at the James Chicago. Great hotel if you prefer a modern clean aesthetic and something different than your normal luxury chain hotel. I booked a suite which was beautiful. It even came with a screening area (projector television) and king sized couch...lounger so the room literally had two king size bed areas in it!!! I had a friend stay over for one night and he had his own king sized bed in the screening/projector area. Very organic decor with filtered water in glass bottles. The staff was extremely courteous and friendly...concierges were wonderful....great with local recommendations and very helpful with navigating the area. Bathroom amenities were great. Turn down service was also present, and housekeepers always left a treat at night on the bed. Beds super comfortable....stark white bed linens (I guess this has become the standard of 5 star luxury). Very comfy bathrobes. Would stay here again!
Only downsides:
I found the air conditioning unit to be quite noisy....which was at times bothersome. The only major problem I had with the place is that the projector never worked in my room in the movie screening area. Even after calling daily. There was no communication on whether it was fixed or not. And this happened daily. I let it go the first night....but was starting to get irritated. It still never worked, and they offered to transfer me into a different room the last night...but by then...to pack and repack for one night i thought was silly. They did offer me a free breakfast in the morning....which was fine....but I DO think they should have adjusted my room rate...since that projector never worked, so it was . Otherwise the hotel was great!!!

title_masked: Great location, good for conferences, average room
text_masked:
I booked this hotel as the conference I was attending took place here. The location of the hotel is great; walking distance to many of the city's attractions, including the Navy Pier, so a good base to explore the city from. My room had a great view over the Chicago River which was lovely.
I was greeted warmly upon arrival, but check-in was impersonal, mind you the hotel has 1200+ rooms. The room I stayed in (regular) was ok in size for a downtown city hotel and clean, but the decor was dated . The bathroom was small, dated and amenities were scarce. My room was a little noisy, I could often hear people in the corridors and adjacent rooms. 
The bed is great and with the blackout curtains I had some good nights sleep.
The gym is open 24 hours, is complimentary for guests and opens with your room card. I recommend going for a run outside instead though as you are at the waterfront in just a few minutes and it's a great way to see the city. The views from the gym are nice and they had some bikes on the terrace too. Equipment worked well, a little dated though.
WIFI is available in the rooms, but you have to sign up for a 24 hour package which is just under USD$14. 
They have a cafe below the lobby (The Link) which is great for breakfast, they serve Starbucks Coffee and pastries, yoghurt, sandwiches, bagels, etc.

This Hotel was great. The location was nice. Its alittle more separated from the husstle but still pretty lively. Subway stations were right outside so getting to Times Sq, Broadway ect. was super easy. Rooms were nice, very inviting staff & they even held our bags & set up a cab to meet us for the airport ride after we checked out.

We have stayed here twice now in the Lux King Suite and have loved it. The separate living area is great for putting the little one to sleep then enjoying time with the hubby in the other room. There is only one room with a bathtub and we managed to get it the second time around. Not necessary but makes it easier to bathe the little one. The bed is super comfortable, the windows open for fresh air and when closed keep out about 95% of the street noise. We haven't had any issue with noise and I'm an extremely light sleeper. The room is always cleaned well and in the lux suites you receive evening turn down which is nice to come home to after dinner. The location is superb for getting to pike place market and eating at some great restaurants, most of which are owned and created by the famed Tom Douglas. We never rent a car(take the light rail from the airport- its super cheap and takes about 35 min- its the last stop and just a few blocks from the hotel) so it's great that everything is close to walk too. Even Whole Foods is just a 5 minute walk away. I love eating at Serious Pie, Dhalia Bakery for a breakfast sandwich, Top Pot Donuts, Lola(downstairs) and Whole Foods. Check them all out while staying here. The only con I can say is the front desk staff could be a little more warm and welcoming. And the check in is a little inefficient. But nothing that would steer me away from staying here. This is the only hotel I've ever stayed in twice because it's that convenient and nice.

title_masked: Close to everything in downtown Indy
text_masked:
Stayed here for a conference that was held in the Convention Center. Very short walk to the convention center and lots of restaurants nearby! There's also a mall across the street that is connected to the convention center and other hotels by sky bridges, which is very convenient if it's cold or rainy. 
The breakfast in the morning was great and the woman helping with it was so friendly and helpful, going out of her way to help people and make sure everyone had what they needed. The desk staff was very friendly as well- they offered suggestions for places to eat, and lent me a marker and some tape when I needed to mail a package. 
Rooms were standard Hampton Inn- beds, as always, were comfortable, and shower had good water pressure. The housekeeping staff did a great job, since the room was spotless every day.
If I'm ever back in Indy, I will be staying here again!

title_masked: Quirky, great art on in reception, friendly welcome.
text_masked: Great desk clerk; she was helpful, real and funny. Realised we were in a rush and sorted out travel directions to our comedy show. Room was large and well stocked but we spent very little time inside. Would have liked to stay longer. Downside was our room (John Garfield) was a bit too orange but bed was super comfy. Old pipes meant shower was noisy but we came away feeling we'd had a good 24hrs in NYC. Most definitely helped by our last minute choice of a cool, but service driven hotel. Recommend it.

So as a family we decided to rent a suite for our family for a 4 year olds birthday. The room was very big and accomadating if not old. It looked as if the whole hotel was run down. It is is need of a serious update. I have stayed at numerous hotels in lots of different cities and this was by far one of the saddest I had seen. It was very dirty. It needs a good scrub down. There was no fan in the bathroom and mold in the shower. Luckily the family lives in the area so we didnt have to use it. The dryer in the room for bathing suits was very handy. The waterpark itself was alright. There was lots of things for the kids to do. As an adult I was pretty bored.Their snack bar (if you could call it that) had horrible food that was microwaved. I would def not stay here again. Though the kids had fun. I was grossed out most of the time.

I booked this hotel because (a) I love Kimpton Hotels, (b) it was within walking distance to my destination while in DC (here on business) and (c) the price was not stratospheric (which DC hotels can tend to be). I was very pleased with the hotel - clean and spacious room (as an InTouch member, I received my one category upgrade from the basic level), cooler than cool "pod" shower, great CO Bigelow amenities, comfortable bed, good temperature control, yummy restaurant and rockin' bar. My only complaints, and they are really pretty minor, are these - I did hear street noise from time to time, and pretty lame water pressure in the rain shower. I've stayed in a lot of five-star properties, and I would be more than happy to stay here again. Thanks for another great stay, Kimpton!

It exceeds the type of service one expects of a Luxury Hotel. IThe staff makse you comfortable even before you walk through the front door the rest is close to prefection. I have stated a Four Season properties across the country and Houston Fourseasons is at the top of my list.

title_masked: Good location, not the best Radisson
text_masked: I stayed in this hotel from friday-sunday. I have stayed in a lot of Radisson Hotels, and this was certainly not the best one, but it was clean and in a good location with subways close by, and in new york, everything is really in walking distance! There was free Wi-fi in the lobby which also was a plus, compared to other hotels trying to charge 14 dollars a day even though you can walk over to your closest starbucks or Mcdonalds and get it for free!

have just returned from the most amazing trip to NYC - the location couldn't be better. A stones throw from the historic area and good bars/restaurants around South Street, a great place for a jog along the river early morning. Subway stations to head uptown are one block away, the hustle and bustle of the Financial District is on your doorstep and the fantastic shopping around Soho is well within walking distance. The staff really go out of their way to be courteous and helpful and treat guests with a warm respect. I would recommend this hotel to anyone. With regard to the construction going on around the World Trade Centre, it is fantastic to witness the regeneration of this area first hand - and you can't make an omelette without cracking eggs. It changes daily and it's really interesting to witness the development. It's New York - no one said it was quiet!

I stay in this hotel with my wife for one week. The rooms are spacious, luxury decorated with all the benefits of modern hotel. The location is great for visitors of the University of Philadelphia and the restaurant serves very good food for reasonable prices.

My Husband and I recently booked part of our anniversary trip to the west coast at this hotel. It was a wonderful experience. The hotel staff was friendly and helpful at every turn. From the front desk, waitstaff, concierge and bellmen they all went out of their way to make sure our "20" Anniversary was extra special. I just Loved visiting this area and this hotel is so "spot on". 
My only regret was that the fabulous "Parmesan Grits" we found at breakfast Monday Morning where not repeated later in the week.
I hope the Giants make it to the world series, if so , I'm thinking my Baseball lov'n, hubby will want a return trip this fall.
We visited the week of February 26th

title_masked: Microtel Inn University Place, Charlotte NC
text_masked: Have stayed in hotel on and off for 12 years. Have found it to be more than adequate for my needs. This is not a luxury hotel, but a clean place that has a courteous staff. Will stay there again on my next trip to Charlotte.

Perfect location to everywhere! Room was small but clean and quaint as we were issued a corner room (standard king size) on the 9th floor. The bathroom was huge! Noise was not a factor. A few complaints - channel selections totally limited; remote control didn't work (they did bring up another one). I needed to heat up a Thanksgiving plate that I had brought for my boyfriend since he'd missed Thanksgiving dinner the previous day and I was told that I would have to pay $50 for them to bring a microwave up for me to use to heat that one plate. I was both frustrated and dissapointed that they were not able to provide such a simple service to their clients. Also, throughout my two-night stay, not one housekeeper had bothered to pick up a half-eaten plate with food that was placed for pick-up right outside the adjacent room's door. Overall, a good (not great) stay.

I've stayed here a number of times during Anime Expo and other various events and I just can't find anything wrong with it (other than the $40/night valet parking fees - are ya kidding me)? Service has been impeccable each visit, the rooms are cleans and very comfortable and the while place just screams class and elegance. It's not the best JW I've seen, but it definitely ranks up there.
I will definitely return every year for as long as Anime Expo and the Rock n Roll Los Angeles 1/2 marathon remains.

Room was very clean. It had an adjoining smaller sitting room with a couch. Bed was very large and comfortable. Conveniently located close to good restaurants and harbor activities.
Only bad experience was street noise and airplanes taking off from San Diego Airport. If you are a light sleeper, bring earplugs or noise canceling earphones. Front desk staff very helpful and friendly.
This is a good hotel if you are in need of clean cheaper accommodations while in San Diego. Good value for the price.

I believe this is a totally renovated and built on to hotel versus a new hotel. The rooms are spacious and beautifully decorated and the cleanest of any hotel I have been in. All of the staff is expectionally helpful. The hotel was almost completely booked with two wedding groups, one of which the wedding was at the hotel. We checked in as the wedding was starting but were greeted professionally and attentively despite the many wedding guests coming in to the spacious lobby for the wedding. There is a very large comfortably outdoor lounging area with a builtin fireplace overlooking the beautiful brand new pool.
Opportunities for improvement: we were disappointed that the biastro closed at 10 on sunday morning espeically since there are no restaurants within walking distance.

This hotel located on M street is terrible safe your money and go to westin located in george town.When we checked in room was not ready and they offered us upgrad we had to wait 2 hours,and when we get there tv did not work ,ac was broken,bed sheets was dirty,toilet mirror dusted.Poor management .

I think your stay is going to depend on your mindset going into this. If you go into this thinking you are going to stay at an upscale, romantic hotel you are going to be dissappointed. If you go into this thinking you are going to stay in a great priced, awesomely located, older motel you should be fine.
 Like the other reviewers have written, this is a quirky/retro motel in the middle of everything S. Congree street has to offer. We stayed in room 126, one of the smaller rooms with a full size bed. Did not sleep well, the bed was a little uncomfortable for me. The bathroom is small but has the basics. The toilet was uncommonly loud. As a woman, I had a hard time with the vanity-mirror-blow dryer situation but eh...my hair was dry in the end.
 Talk about awesome location though! Everything is in walking distance. Need your iced latte fix? Right on the corner. Ice cream craving for the smoothest ice cream imaginable? Across the street. Best pizza in the world? couple of blocks. Cool shopping? Live music? Interesting food from food trucks with interesting names? You get the point.
 Would I stay here again? Yes. I would try to get one of the bigger rooms if possible, but if I got this room again it would not be a deal breaker.

'Victorian' influenced hotel, has a very 'homey' vibe to it.
Very spacious and inviting.
Quite 'old school' but has everything you need.
Loved the afternoon biscuits and sherry.
Great breakfast every morning!
It is a good 20 minute walk into the heart of union square..
#TIP##### Take the town car instead of a taxi tot he airport, costs $50, smae amount (or less) than a taxi, and is a lot more comfortable! Set amount so the taxi drivers cant rip you off...

title_masked: great for a one night stay
text_masked: my sister booked a suite at the gansevoort for my bachelorette party this past saturday. we had a great time staying at this hotel mainly because of the location and because of the rooftop! it is on the high end of my price range so i would never be able to stay more than a night but that said i didn't see much of a wow factor for such a "high end" hotel. we called room service at some point to bring up extra glasses and they charged us....why??? it's not like it costs them any money...they didn't go out to buy the glasses. that was ridiculous. other than that, if you are looking for a fun, great neighborhood to stay in i would highly recommend

Hotel Commonwealth is top shelf in every aspect--service, value, location, cleanliness. The staff are personable and helpful. We have stayed in all levels of rooms and each one is spacious, comfortable, spotless. If you have a car, the staff are very accommodating in retrieving your car throughout the day as you come and go. A car is really not needed as there is a T stop on the same block. Located perfectly for Boston University - virtually on the campus. Eastern Standard restaurant (attached to the hotel) has become our favorite spot for drinks, appetizers and dinner.

title_masked: Nice hotel, still a few issues
text_masked:
I stayed for a week in this hotel and I only had a few issues. the hotel is located in a bit of a "ghetto" area, a lot of hobos and drug addicts walking about at night in the parking lot. But the hotel is pretty nice. A loud train goes right past the hotel and is very loud, also when the AC kicks on it is VERY loud, it actually made me jump out of my sleep. my shower was clearly unwashed as someones bar of soap covered with hair was still in it and hair was on the shower walls. other than that the room was pretty clean and the bed was very comfortable. nothing was broken in the room and the tv/internet worked well. The tv has limited channels but im not a big tv person so this wasn't an issue. The hotel breakfast was VERY expensive, i initially thought it was free, then saw it advertised on their site as $4.95 then i was charged $9 every morning for it and it is even more if you take it to your room. I went nearly broke just eating breakfast. The food is decent, but the staff is all Hispanic and clearly do not know English well. there were large language barriers going on. Luckily the hotel is very close to stapleton and a large shopping/restaurant area that they have free shuttles to. The hotel was not too far from downtown denver, about 10 minutes, less for uptown. Also was a short drive to Cherry Creek. 
Overall this hotel was nice and not as expensive as other area hotels. i slept well most of the time and was close to food/shopping/entertainment. The check in staff was friendly and check in/check out was speedy, (they also told me they were lenient on late checkouts). I would probably recommend this hotel to other travelers.

Great price, Great room, Great experince. Was in town for one night on business and stayed in a private bath room. The room was clean, comfortable, and perfect for my quick turn around trip. My dinner meeting was with in walking distance and it was a great way to enjoy the sites and sounds of the city. I would stay again.

The hotel is located a short walk from Union Square and not far from cable/train links on Powell Street. There are lots of car rental places nearby too which was handy as we needed a car to drive to Yosemite Park.
The room was clean if slightly old fashioned and the staff were very friendly and helpful.
The hotel has free WiFi.
There is a great cafe directly next door serving really good breakfasts and the free WiFi from the hotel reaches here.
Avoid Ellis St to the south of the hotel as there are a lot of tramps hanging around here but everything North of this is fine.

I just returned from a large conference that was held in the downtown area. The Marriott was the designated conference hotel. Our room was very nice and spacious. The hotel staff were extraordinarily helpful and nice. The biggest issue was under-staffing. There were not enough people to help in the restaurant, bar or even at the front desk. As noted by someone else recently, our room was not serviced until late and one day it was not serviced at all. That said I think the staff were working really hard. There were just too many people and not enough help. This is something that the management needs to fix. They certainly knew that the conference was scheduled and I don't know why they didn't gear up for it with some extra help.
But Memphis is a fabulous city for a convention! I would recommend it to anyone.

This is a small to medium sized hotel and seems to be quite new. It’s an easy 2-block walk to the subway, 3 blocks to Macy’s, and Koreatown and the Empire State Building are around the corner. In fact, we stayed in 1201 and had a view of the ESB from our room. There are plenty of good restaurants and bars in the area.
The room was spotless and the bed was comfortable. The water pressure in the shower was tremendous and invigorating.
The staff were quite friendly and helpful. I can’t say anything bad about this hotel at all. Tremendous value and great experience.

I spent this past weekend in Boston, having been there before. This was a great hotel in a perfect location. Boston is a walking city and you are adjacent to the North End and the Waterfront. About 2 or 3 blocks from Faneuil Hall and the Quincy Market, great dining. Hotel staff was extremely accomodating. Rooms were modern and well kept. Lobby was very nice with lots of nooks and crannies. Would stay again.

We checked in Friday afternoon and were immediately and nicely given a top floor room when I asked, even though the desk clerk had already made the keys for a lower floor room. The 2 queen bed suite was huge, even with the sofa bed out. The room was extremely clean and hotel was very quiet. (Our room faced the back parking lot toward the Alamo.) Great location...very close to the Alamo and a short distance to the Riverwalk. The breakfast was amazing. Huge variety of food... sausage, eggs, bacon, fruit, pastries and "make your own" waffles. The staff was very friendly and made the stay even nicer.

This was such a great experience...great location...great staff! Stayed on the top floor...40th floor...view of the Empire State building right out our window! It was better than expected...would highly recommend!

We loved the contemporary beautiful Hotel. The rooms were very spacious with floor to ceiling windows for a gorgeous view of the city. The staff everywhere we went in the hotel were outstanding! It was close enough to walk to many places and right next to the cable cars, which we used often.

title_masked: Property is average but the staff and location make up the difference.
text_masked: This is our 2nd or 3rd year to stay at this property during the Mid-South Gin show. I knew exactly what to expect from the room (average at best) but the staff and location are wonderful. Right across the street from the Peabody and only a short walk from the convention hall and Beale Street, this is one of the best locations for the money. The staff is top notch!! Elisa at the front desk is so friendly and willing to help in any way! Will probably book again for next year!

My husband and I stayed at the Marriott Union Square for a long weekend.
The location was perfect! One block from Union Square, three blocks from a Bart Station and close to lots of restaurants and shopping.
The rooms were clean; but small. Ladies, if you're planning a girl's trip, there are a couple of things you should know. First, The bathroom mirror is the only well lit mirror. There are only 2 plugs. There is another mirror in the main room; but the overhead lighting is not ideal for makeup application. Again, the room was small; so one large bag each is perfect. I'm making a special note of this because I travel often with my girlfriends and I kept thinking we'd be fighting for space if we stayed here. It was perfect for the hubby and I though.

This hotel lived up to the good reviews. It was super easy to arrive at when we entered at the Lincoln tunnel. The front desk was very friendly. Our room was very clean, and also large for NYC standards. Location is convenient to sights. My only negatives are that we personally did not find the beds to be to comfortable. Slept on worse, but have slept on alot better. Also, be prepared to wait at the elevators.

I visited the Courtyard LAX for business this week and had a very positive experience. The hotel is literally right next to LAX, which is convenient for travel into and out of the airport, but it is also relatively central to other LA locations. During my trip, I was in South LA, West LA, Santa Monica, Pasadena, Downtown, and North LA, and I was able to get from the hotel to each location in an hour or less, even with LA traffic. 
The room itself was very nice: a standard spacious and clean Courtyard room. The hotel was very convenient for business travel, with a business center, free, fast wifi, etc. Parking is valet and costs $20/night; I have to admit that it was very convenient to hand off the car in front of the hotel after a long day of driving! 
While the hotel itself was excellent, the aspect that made it special and would lead to my returning on future trips was the staff. Whenever I returned to the hotel, there were kind, welcoming, and helpful. The valet staff always asked when I'd be needing the car and had it close and ready when I came to pick it up; I never waited more than five minutes. The front desk staff was very helpful, sorting out a small billing issue with ease. I want to mention Toyia in particular, as she went above and beyond to make my stay comfortable. She was always ready with a welcome and a smile whenever I returned to the hotel and provided assistance with everything from wake-up calls to local transportation and attractions. In short, the staff made this already positive stay even better, and I would recommend this hotel as a result. I'll certainly be returning the next time I'm in the area!

title_masked: Nice extra touches at this hotel
text_masked: Room was clean and large. Staff was very nice. Loved the free happy hour and milk and cookies in the evenings. Gym was very nice. Only negatives were that the bed comfort was average and the colors were a very drab gray. Otherwise, we had a nice visit.

title_masked: Recently renovated rooms, but not all.
text_masked: Got a high floor room due to PRC Plat. Rooms are newly renovated, but very basic. Other colleagues go lower floor rooms and are old and tired. Checked in twice in the period of 2 weeks. First front desk staff do not recognize me as Plat member. Second did and offer a bottle of water and cookie. Breakfast was good.

title_masked: Excellent stay in the City of Brotherly Love
text_masked: We loved our stay at Sofitel Philadelphia. We upgraded to a Junior Suite, and couldn't have been happier with the accommodations. The front desk staff were very helpful and cordial upon our arrival allowing us to check in several hours before the standard check-in time. Our room was beautiful. Very comfortable bed, large, wonderfully fitted bathroom and a nice separate lounge area. We used the package offered on the hotel website that included parking and breakfast. The breakfast buffet at Chez Collete, the hotel restaurant, was exceptional. We enjoyed our stay very much, and would definitely stay here again!

title_masked: Good Smaller Convention Hotel in the heart of Ausin
text_masked: Check in was smooth. Room was fine with two queen sized bed. Good decor and over-all clean. However, I made the mistake of walking around barefoot in the room for a few minutes and got sticky something all over the bottom of my feet (went against my own rule of always wearing socks in hotels rooms). Well, white socks that I wore a few other times over the few days I was there turned black in no time. This seems to happen to me and my family at quite a few Hiltons (not good). Room service was good. Food, drinks, and everything were great at this location. UPS store within the Hilton had great service (although there were very high handling charges for packages that I had shipped in). Convention room and services were great (even the internet)....oh, but that reminds me of the $13.95 per day charge for internet in the hotel room. I won't pay that I enjoy free internet at the lesser Hilton brand hotels (Hampton Inn and Hilton Garden Inn). I just bring an internet card with me. Over-all great stay.

Nice staff, conveniently located and everything walking distance. 
Rooms are clean and "tipical size" for NY

title_masked: Good location at a good price for San Antonio
text_masked: This was a good choice for us while in San Antonio for a visit. The place was being renovated while we were there, but the management did a wonderful job accommodating all the customers. Breakfast is served each day and we found the room clean and comfortable and the staff very helpful. We were very close to all the attractions and the places we were visiting with easy access to all the highways. Best part - no charge for parking and close to the Market Square area.

This place was the worst. Hair all over the bathroom, mold on the walls, rugs were dirty, curtains falling off the walls, stains all over the bedstread. As soon as we walked in the room we call management for them to see these disgusting rooms. They sent up a newly hired 17 year old male staff with keys to different rooms. One floor up and they were slightly better. The staff are rude and not helpful. We travel to NYC once a month and have stayed in several different hotels this was the worst place I have ever stayed and the price unacceptable. We paid over $250 for three rooms each and our stay was wasn't worth $25. Do Not stay here.

Checking in took a long time, kid were getting antsy waiting even though we made our reservations ahead of time online. There was construction going on around the hotel and it made getting in and out a little inconvenient but it wasn't too bad. Parking on the main level was a mess, we opted to park in the parking garage underneath which was much better. Once we got to our room we were extremely surprised to see how small the room was. Barely enough room for the two beds, no room for our kids to really move around. Pillows were really small but got the job done I suppose. Walls were a little thin. Bathroom was pretty decent, great water pressure and kept temperature. The breakfast wasn't too bad but they ran out of food often and it took a while to refill. I stood in line waiting for a refill for the waffle mix and after over 5 minutes I just gave up and settled on my toast and eggs. Plenty of extra seating in a room around the corner from the breakfast area. The man in charge was very friendly and helpful. 
Always walking around asking if everyone was doing ok or if they needed anything. We chose this hotel for 2 reasons. Walking distance to main attractions and the indoor pool. Was seriously disappointed in the pool. It was such a small space and hardly any seating. My husband took our boys down once in the 3 nights we were there and it was very crowded. They had fun so that's really all that matters, but I wasn't able to sit and watch because people were using all the chairs to drape their towels and personal belongings on. Even if I had been able to sit and watch I most likely would have gotten soaked since a splash from any side of the pool soaked all sides. On our next trip to Seattle we will most likely try to get something better for our money. It was mainly just a place for us to sleep but it was not worth the money spent.
club level ritz carlton, is an excellent choice for a special occasion, very comfortable beds and good size room.

Everyone who works at this hotel is very friendly and makes sure that they get you what you need. From the waiter in the restaurant, the cleaning staff and front office, EVERYONE I encountered was very friendly. The rooms are clean and modern, and the beds are very comfortable.
Location was good, the farmer's market just one block over on Sat mornings was awesome! About a 10 minute walk down to the water. 
Courtesy shuttle was clean, just remember to call them when you land, because it takes them about 15 minutes to get a shuttle over to the pick up area.
I was a little bummed that after a fire alarm was pulled at 12:30am and we were evacuated and stood around for an hour in the middle of the night that they didn't offer us free breakfast or anything - especially because of the confusing instructions the guests were given while the alarms were going off.

I had written a somewhat negative review of the hotel about a year ago and was invited to return this year. I would now like to say that the staff was very nice, as the last time I was there, the hotel much quieter, the bed excellent and I had a very good albeit short stay. I would recommend this hotel for couples of people on business downtown Manhattan.

We stayed for 3 nights in the South Tower (tower3) on the 14th floor so had a skyline view of the city. The room was extremely clean, modern and the bed was very comfortable. The maids came in everyday and did an excellent job. Checking in and out was very easy and straightforward with polite and helpful staff especially Caterina. We used the pool which was good but a little small for the size of the hotel. Seaport village is in easy walking distance and that is worth a look. The hotel also offers a free shuttle bus to and from the Zoo which we took advantage of. We spent 2 nights having a few drinks in the Elephant & Castle pub which we enjoyed as the bar staff were very attentative and friendly. Also was pleasantly surprised that the drinks prices were not expensive. We also ate a late breakfast in the Hazelwood Deli which is located in the front of our tower and does 10% discount if you are a guest of the HI.
Would definitely stay here again!

title_masked: Wow.. impressive all the way around.
text_masked:
Booked a King 1BR suite for a one night's stay. Room was huge! Almost like a small efficiency apartment with huge kitchen, living room, separate bedroom and big bathroom with large walk-in shower..
Clean and very modern with furnishings.. 
Will stay here again soon.
Very good hotel,huge rooms, we really enjoyed our stay We've never stayed at such a friendly place!

title_masked: Great Experience at the Sheraton City Center
text_masked: We were at the Sheraton Baltimore City Center for an event, and the service was off the charts. The convention management by Brett Caplan and Terry Forbes was the best I've every had. I can not say enough about one houseman, Donte Langley, he helped us with EVERYTHING, from lunches and drinks to loading and unloading deliveries! Gert Garrett, Chu Blische, Michelle Bell, Karl Taylor, Gary Young, Sonya Norman, Shannon Butler, Karon James, Calvin Wilson, Darrell Coates in banquets, hooked us up! Ms [NAME], Ms [NAME], Ms [NAME] in the kitchen and Chef Warren kept us full of delicious food! This is a group of people who are really good at what they do and who really enjoy doing it and it SHOWS! Highly, Highly reccomended if you want a great experience!

Everything everyone has said positive about this hotel is true. I would definitely stay here again. This was the same price as a junk hotel all the way in Jersey that our friends stayed in thinking they were saving money. So glad we went with this hotel instead!

They have done a lot of work and replaced a lot of old equipment. So much better and nicer than it was. They still have work to do, but it is so nice to see that the owners are investing money into this property. Much cleaner.

title_masked: Excellent big room and great location.
text_masked:
Stayed there for 3 night while on a conference trip. 
Room is clean big and with a separate living room and microwave and coffee machine! We can always make our coffee to kick start our everyday. The microwave is a great help for us to warm up food that we took out. Chills and lots of eateries were just opposite the hotel! 
Excellent location with the famous city hall just at the doorstep. Macy was just round the corner for shopping. Subway station just 5-10 min walk which has the direct train down to the airport.
Highly recommended for business traveller, family. Great value hotel for the price paid.

Stayed here while on a business trip in April 2012. Great location for all the historical sites. Great restaurants nearby including the old City Tavern. Best pork chop ever! Short walk to the very ecclectic South Street. Lots of shops and neighborhood pubs. Would recommmend this location for eitehr leisure or business travel.

title_masked: My new favorite place to stay in NYC!
text_masked: The staff at the Beekman, from concierge, front desk staff, restaurant staff and anyone else that we encountered, were outstanding!! All friendly, more than willing to help and truly felt like a 5 star service type of establishment. Our room was on the 13th floor and had a pretty good view of the upper east side, the queensboro bridge and the east river. The bathroom was newly remodeled and had a modern feel. The room itself was huge for a NYC hotel room, with a separate office, bedroom and bathroom. The location was great, so many great attractions nearby requiring a short walk. Awesome room, great views and phenomenal staff! My new favorite place to stay in NYC from now on!

title_masked: Excellent Customer Service and prime location
text_masked:
We had great customer service plus we were able to enjoy our last day in SFO. As advertised, this hotel doesn't charge for extras such as wireless, tea, concierge service. I think this is a great business model which takes customer experience seriously.
I would highly recommend Club Quarters for an enjoyable city stay.

Our choice was based on anothe good hint from Tripadvisor. The hotel is in a quiet area, although somewhat distant from the center, but well located for those who do not mind walking. There are some convenience stores and a CVS nearby, to supply the fridge and make a good breakfast or lunch in the large kitchen. The overall space in the room is large but the kitchen equipment is simple and some items require maintenance, but for a stay of a few days the cost / benefit ratio is favorable.

We stay in San Diego frequently & had yet to stay at this property. Loved the location as I used to jog on the bay often when living in SD. Having a patio straight out to the bay was beautiful & lovely with the oversized chaise lounges. My only couple complaints were the size of the room was mediocre & very dark. However the bathroom was quite large & parking was easy & accessible.

We reserved 2 rooms. We requested the top floor with both of our rooms close- The front desk at check in around 7-8pm was GREAT!!! He went WAYYYY out of his way to make sure our rooms were great. One of the rooms had an odor, and he immediately switched our room and upgraded it a bit. The hallway had a bit of an odor. The hotel is super close- within walking distance to a strip of restaraunts. We ate at Gloria's which was really good. The rooms were clean. The breakfast was perfect. Service was amazing. The pool was clean and warm because it is "heated". I loved our mini vacay here! WE WILL BE BACK. This hotel is also super close to the Fort Worth Zoo, which we visited the following day. :o)

title_masked: Nice new rooms, Very helpfull staff!
text_masked: First I want to say that I would have given a 5 out of 5 but the area of the hotel was questionable, too many homeless for my tast, but they did not cause any problems and the staff made sure that we were not bothered and made me and my family feel secure. The room's were very nice as many of the other reveiws stated, I was told they had been recently remodeled. My family stayed in a room with two beds and we were provided a extra small bed we requested on arrival at a very small cost. The bathroom had a granit counter top and the bathroom and shower had very nice tile in it, the beds were comfortable as well. The staff was very helpfull with any questions, I have to point out one staff member in particular because I told him I would when he asked me nicely to please leave a reveiw for the hotel about he new rooms. His name is curtis or curt. Very nice man and he never once said no I can't or I will try, he just did what I asked, and beleive me I had many requests. But the whole staff in general was very helfull as well. They were able to give directions in the Hollywood and Los Angeles area which they seemed to know very well. they do have a resturant and bar on site but have very limited hours on the weekend which was dissapointing but there are many other places for food in the area. I will recomend this hotel to friends coming to the Hollywood and Los Angeles area, and if I come back to Hollywood or Los Angeles I will stay again.

Wow! What a place. I'm a Platinum Premier Member, (which means I stay at a lot of Marriott's..)
By far, this Hotel definitely ranks in my top 3. The building, the food/drink, and last but not least the staff. Funny, I see in prior post talk about Henry; they're right he is awesome! From the moment you pull up to the front door until you leave, he's there to help, treats you like your old friends. This guy needs to be schooling all other Concierges around the country on behalf of Marriott. It's not just Henry at this campus, all of the staff does a GREAT job of making you feel at home. This Hotel is definitely the place in Indy to stay.
Chris H.

title_masked: Very nice people and great location
text_masked: Hotel is in a great location, right next to grand central station. The staff was very friendly and accommidating. The beds are a little small, but we had never been to NY City before so maybe all hotel rooms are like that. The restaurant was good, we ate breakfast there every morning. There was a small problem with an article of clothing that had been stuffed down in a couch that my daughter found by accident, but the manager came up to the room to discard the item and made it right with us. All in all we had a great stay there and would rec commend the hotel to anyone.

title_masked: The only place to stay in Downtown LA
text_masked:
This is the second time we've stayed here - love being Downtown and away from the madness of West Hollywood/Beverly Hills.
Foyer is dark and private, check-in process is smooth, rooms are huge and have everything you need.
Rooftop bar is iconic and absolutely worth spending some time up there.
Complimentary wifi is great and I wish all hotels would jump on board with this. Plenty of options to eat nearby, although you can't really do LA properly without a car...
Given the extremely reasonable rack rate for the rooms; we wouldn't stay anywhere else.

A colleague and I spent four nights here while in town on business. The property is adjacent to the airport and on the border between a light industrial zone and a office/hotel/retail area. There is a light rail station in front of the hotel which attracts passengers who sleep under the trees on the hotel grounds. Despite this, the place seems secure.
The rooms and public areas are comfortable, although a little dated. The breakfast buffet is well stocked and the food good.
There were three issues which would cause me to look for alternative hotels when I return to Phoenix:
1) The free in-house internet service was virtually inaccessible. Both my colleague and I were successful in logging on in only about 10% of tries. Even then, the connection would drop out. The front desk clerk said she did not know how address this problem and did not offer to find out.
2) My room had the loudest air conditioner I have ever encountered in a hotel. It ran almost constantly in an attempt to deal with the 100 degree-plus outdoor temperature.
3) As with many hotels its age, the rooms are short on electrical receptacles. There was only one outlet at the desk and I had to move the bed to find an outlet to plug in my CPAP machine.
There a several other hotels in the immediate area that I would try on my next visit.

My husband and I stayed at this hotel for a weekend getaway and to try the Tempur-pedic bed. The hotel is lovely....clean and friendly, helpful front desk personnel. However, about 20 minutes after we got in our room, my husband went out to get water. I was in the bathroom and heard the door open. I called out my husband's name, but heard as woman's voice, in very broken English, say something about checking the room. The next morning I overheard another guest complaining to the front desk about a member of the housekeeping staff using her key without knocking and walked right into their room! Also, when our towels were not replenished for the 2nd night, I called the front desk to get towels to freshen up before dinner. Two hours later, and after 2 more requests, we finally got towels. On the positive side, the hotel had a very nice hot breakfast (not free but very reasonably priced) and we had a nice dinner at Twist, the restaurant there. The view from our room was lovely. We could see the capitol and Washington monument. Stunning at night! There was also free parking in the hotel garage which saved us about $80 for 2 nights. I would recommend this hotel, but be sure to keep the deadbolt on in your room.

This hotel is a ten minute walk to the national mall. It also sits on top of a metro hub and has an elevator from lobby to subway. This proves to be extremely convenient for sightseeing. My 10yr old daughter and I came to DC for four days. We felt safe at hotel and on subway. The hotel is lovely and the staff are so friendly and helpful. I almost cancelled my reservation after reading the negative reviews about how "run down" the hotel is. I am so glad I kept my reservation. Don't listen to those other reviewers. The wallpaper is old fashioned but everything is clean and well cared. Our room had a balcony that overlooked the river. The staff is as professional as any hotel I have visited. I would definitely stay here again when in DC.

As a surprise for my girlfriend's birthday, I booked a room here for the St.Patrick's Day weekend. I had researched the hotel and location a little prior to doing so, and everything turned out just as I wanted. Some of the highlights:
* The Spa within the hotel. My gf loved her spa session. Had we not had dinner plans, I think she would have stayed at the spa! After your massage session, you can go to a relaxation room, or the sauna. Extra perks! 
* My gf's favorite restaurant is the Wildfire. While I initially thought we would have to take a cab, turns out it was within walking distance. And there are several other great restaurants within walking distance.
* Vertigo Sky Lounge. In case she decided to have a few extra drinks, all we had to do was take an elevator down to our room. The Lounge was great also. You can go outside, and if it got a litte cold, they had robes to wear so you could be warm, yet still enjoy the outside on the 26th (I think) floor! 
All in all, we had a great experience. We were on the 23rd floor, at the corner, yet we not disturbed by any noise from the Lounge. I would definitely recommend this hotel.

We were very happy with our stay at Embassy Suites in DC. The suite was spacious, well equipped and suited our 6-person family perfectly, at an affordable price. the lobby was lovely, with waterfalls, streams and fish. The kids are given fish food to feed the fish in the mornings.
The hotel was a 25 minute walk from the white house, which is really great.
My only complaint, is that the free wifi was restricted to a tiny corner of the lobby, and not available to all rooms -- this was a nuisance and very disappointing. Most hotels are providing free wifi to guests nowadays!
All in all, I great hotel for family vacations.

I wanted to take my girlfriend to a great place, this had it all, location, facility, an amazing staff, lots of plusses, including a stunning rooftop bar and exclusive access to one of the coolest clubs purely based on being a guest. It is 2 blocks from a very lively 5th street, and offers the best of SD at your doorstep. I will return again!

Upper East side location is great - quiet but close to everything. 
We found the service to be outstanding, including room service. 
Rooms are bland but comfortable and a very good size for NYC.
The wireless in rooms and the internet fees in the business centre are too high but wireless in the lobby is free.
The power breakfast began at Loews and continues to this day...we found the service and food very good, albeit expensive. 
Hotel is very efficiently run - get a good deal and you will not be dissapointed.
Hotel is close to metro stops, dry cleaners, laundry (off Lexington), top restaurants, conveneience stores, shopping and central park........
Far away from all Memphis attractions. Poor service. Ok rooms. Good price.

I stayed at the Driskill in the early 80's for months and it was a great old classic hotel. Both Austin and the Driskill have come a long way. 
I stayed there this week for the first time back to Austin since then and the Driskill has gone from the great to spectacular with its 1850's elegance brought back in both architecture and atmosphere. The place was buzzing with music and activity in its great bars and restaurant and the live entertainment ranged from a country music singer in the bar to a string quartet doing new age in the lobby. 
This is the place to stay in Austin.

We stayed at The Westin, San Diego and were pleasantly pleased. The location was excellent, about 3 blocks from the Gaslight Quarters where there are hundreds of restaurants and shopping to choose from. The young lady at the front desk, Jackie Burkett was exceptional. We wanted a high floor so that we could get a good view of the bay and Jackie was accommodating to say the least. She asked us our reason for visiting and we told her we were celebrating an important anniversary. The room was lovely, very clean with the most comfortable mattress and bedding. We had an LCD 32" inch tv in the room. The bathroom was a bit small but the double headed shower head made up for that. Every day near the elevator there was a basket of green apples. The elevators were awesome, with the glass all around and being on the outside of the building when you were going up you could see everything on the Bay, especially nice at night. When we arrived we left our suitcases in the room and went out to scout the area. When we came back there was a beautiful strawberry plater, gift and card to congratulate us on our special anniversary. So thoughtful and unexpected. I would not suggest using the self parking for $24.00 but instead use the Valet for $32.00. Everytime you go in and out of the parking they charge you by 15 min increments, so if you plan to go in and out often better to just go with the valet parking. I asked for an Irish coffee at the hotel bar late in the evening and they didn't have coffee, but went over to the restaurant and got me coffee and made me my drink. Went over and above. The hotel restaurant is a bit pricey but with all the restaurants in close proximity that is not even an issue.
I would definitely recommend this hotel.

great hotel with really lovely staff from housekeeping, maintenance through to front of house staff. The room was large and the breakfast was plentiful everyday - it's also lovely to be welcomed everytime you walk through reception. I loved that the tea and coffee was available in the foyer as it was great to collect one as you arrived in

Stayed for 2 nights while on business.
Room is an OK size, bathroom OK and had good service at the front desk. Bed was comfortable and it was clean.
10 mins walk to the sea front and 10 minutes walk to the downtown area the other way.
All in all, nothing to complain about but at the same time, I'd not demand to stay there next time I was in San Diego.

This hotel offers a great location for Baltimore visitor/tourists. The Inner Harbor is directly across the street. The Aquarium, Childrens Discovery Center, and Convention Center are within a block or two. I would suggest requesting a room above the 6th or 7th floor to avoid noise from the bar/restaurant in the lobby. The outdoor pool is very nice and the fitness center is one of the best I have seen in a hotel.

Boston is a very special city to my husband and I, so it was important to me that we find the perfect place to celebrate our 6th anniversary. XV Beacon was it. They accommodated an early check-in. The room was beautifully appointed, albeit a little small by American standards. But that's what you get for booking the most basic room category in a city centre. It was absolute perfection, and very romantic with surround sound and an electric fireplace that we enjoyed very much despite the hot summer weather. I also liked the intimacy of 7 rooms per floor. Staff was very nice. 
The only less-than-positive comment I have is for the restaurant, Moo. We went there for breakfast one morning and while I can appreciate that they have a set breakfast menu, I was disappointed by the response when my husband asked for a burger instead (it is a steakhouse after all...) It was a little after 10, and we were told they don't serve lunch until 11 or 11:30. The irony is that Moo handles all of the room service, where a burger WAS on the menu. So if we went back to our room and asked for a burger, that would've been feasible but at the restaurant itself it was not. Only after we flagged that did the waiter come back and tell us that it was okay but that the chef may not make the fries that comes with it at this hour. As it turns out, we did get the fries and the burger was absolutely delicious. The fries were addicting. Something to note: at breakfast they tack on an automatic 20% gratuity. 
I'd stay at this hotel again in a heartbeat. Just book it!

Overall great value. Areas for improvement---
1) Bar way too expensive, no wonder there was no one there most of the time. Try giving free drink vouchers at check in, and lower prices to those of the area. 
2) Rooms dated, CRT TV's? Quaint.
3) Got rude treatment over phone when enquiring about an item left in the room after check out. Was told too busy to talk, send me an email. Was corrected when another lady came on line and helped find the item.

title_masked: Quoting Ferris Bueller "If you have the means, I highly recommend picking one up"
text_masked: Oh what a night. Spent my 40th birthday downtown and stayed the night at the Waldorf. Hands down best urban hotel experience. Fantastic service from check-in all the way to check-out. Received complimentary upgrade to a Waldorf Suite with luxurious amenities including a gas fireplace, deep soaking tub, and Gi-Normous shower. Wonderful linens and bedding made for peaceful slumber after a late night out on the town. Room was opulent, cozy, and comfortable. Complimentary hotel car service to our dinner location - driver wouldn't accept a tip. Neither would the bellman who helped us with our bags. Breakfast in the restaurant was delicious - and great service. Easy to understand why this hotel is tops in Chicago.

I stay there for almost one week, every floor provides the coffee machine, but my floor that one was faulty, and over a week nobody fix it..., room won't provide any amenties, only 2 bottles of soap, no shampoo, provided. The breakfast provide the muffin, and it's fine. My hushand called to hotel and try to connect to my room, he rang for 4 times, but still nobody answer the general line. This is a hotel if you stay only one or two nights, not for business trip which they can provide the services what you need.

title_masked: Review of Recent Stay During Convention
text_masked: I loved my recent stay at Hotel Icon in Houston from November 1st through the 4th, 2012. Erica at the front desk was absolutely fantastic at making my trip go smoothly. She made all of the inconveniences of travel go away and had a very pleasant personality that was constantly focused on taking care of all of the hotel's guests. I was with a very large group and she was helpful to everyone in my group, as well as everyone else i saw her interact with while staying at the hotel. The bartender in the lobby bar was also fantastic and took care of a lot of people (and the associated chaos) easily. Overall, everyone I interacted with gave fantastic customer service and made staying at the Hotel Icon an enjoyable experience. I have stayed there before prior to Marriott buying it and was pleasantly surprised to see the same level of customer care demonstrated under the Marriott ownership.

We stayed at the Crowne from the 14th to 18th September. From the outside the building looks dated but after our easy and quick check in we were shown to our suite and found it to be quuite nice. The room had been updated but after our cramped stay in Vegas I loved the fact we had 2 seperate rooms. The bed was huge and comfortable and trhe kids found it easy to sleep on theirs.
 We ate at the hotel 1 night and the meal was OK. There is a RALPHS supermarket within easy walking distance and we grabbed a couple of meals from there.
 The staff were nice enough to give us a late check out which we really appreciated but there was one incident with the baggage that annoyed me. When we arrived the bell man helped us with our luggage which we had a fare bit of and I tipped him accordingly but when it arrived at our room there was a different bell men who was also looking for a tip. Not really the hotels fault but pretty sneaky on the bell mans behalf

This is my hotel of choice when going to Red Sox games. It is an easy, comfortable, secure walk to Fenway. (apx 1 mile). Theres lots of stores/restaurants etc allong the way which makes the walk easier. The parking fee ($18) is waived if you have game tickets which is a great option. They have a concierge in the lobby who is always available for any questions on the city. They also sell some of the tour passes there which is convenient. Rooms are larger than regular double rooms which adds to the comfort of the stay. Located about 4 minute walk from Prudential Centre which gives you easy acces to subway/shops and the Cheescake Factory.
Breakfast at Thornton's is an excellent choice, but Thornton's is very busy!

Located within walking distance of Union Square and the Civic Centre, the Hotel Carlton offers excellent value and a very welcoming atmosphere. The reception staff were very friendly, the lobby a comfortable place to hang out with daily "happy hour" complimentary wine from [TEL]pm. 
The rooms are very comfortable (we had a King Sized bed) and provide adequate space. 
Not too many negatives to comment on - the complimentary wifi was inconsistent and the elevators a bit slow, but otherwise I'd highly recommend staying here. The general location is a bit on the "gritty" side, but gives a perspective of the real San Francisco.
The patrons were of all ages and nationalities.

We stayed at the Hotel Solamar while attending a wedding in San Diego. All of the employees went out of their way to be friendly and accomodating. The management of this hotel really cares about creating a very welcoming atmosphere. Our room on the ninth floor was quiet, clean, and comfortable, and we had a view of the Petco baseball park. The location of the hotel is excellent. The gaslamp district is within a short walk, and features many excellent restaurants and bars. Valet parking is expensive, but the attendants did a great job parking and retrieving our car. We would definitely stay at this hotel on future visits to San Diego.

We booked this hotel through Expedia.ca as part of a fly/stay package. Never having stayed in NYC before, I really had no expectations. I had read that the hotel was older and maybe needed a face lift. That's maybe true, but the rooms were clean, the beds comfortable and as I always travel with earplugs, I wasn't bothered by traffic noise or other guests. True, the room wasn't overly large, but I'm not in NYC to spend time in my room! The hotel is definitely within walking distance of some great sightseeing spots (Times Square, 5th Avenue, Central Park and Grand Central were all an easy walk, even for my 76 year old mother-in-law). And it was a pleasant surprise to wake up Sunday morning and find Lexington Avenue closed to traffic in front of the hotel for a vendor's market that stretched for blocks. I'd give a special shout out to Craig, the concierge, who was able to obtain fantastic tickets for us to see Zarkana at Radio City Music Hall (I would have gone 10 more times!) and to Jimmy the doorman for recommending a wonderful pizza restaurant within walking distance of the hotel which didn't break the budget! It might not be the biggest, brightest, newest hotel in NYC, but I enjoyed my stay and would definitely stay there again.

title_masked: great deal, if you don't mind cozy
text_masked:
My boyfriend and I stayed here because it was one of the cheaper hotels downtown, I was impressed. The rooms are very small and the bathrooms smaller, I think my knees touched the bathtub from the toilet. The size didn't get to me though because everything was immaculately clean and high quality. The king sized bed was actually two twin beds pushed together, but comfortable. Tan and navy hues and high quality fabrics make you feel like you're staying at some fancy country club. They charge $40 for a late check out though, so prepare to be up by noon.
My favorite part of the hotel is the living room style lobby. Plush velvet couches surround a TV, fireplace, and computers. With free coffee and tea all day, it's a great place to cozy up and people watch. You feel like you're in your friends living room, not a hotel lobby.

From the moment we checked in, the disappointment began. We were met with a snooty representative who, among other things, informed us that it would cost us an additional $45 per day to park our car. Whenever we wanted to take our car out, we'd have to wait to get it stamped at the valet, whose stamp was only good for 15 minutes! Most of the desk staff we encountered were dry and unfriendly.
The room, although clean and roomy had some interesting features. First, if you want to turn on the light to the toilet area in the room, the light over the sink, which is exposed to the room comes on and there's no way to turn it off, meaning that if someone gets up to go to the bathroom at night, everyone wakes up! Right outside our window, very early in the morning, and very noisily, they emptied the dumpsters. Every. Morning.
