The bright spots? There were a few. The concierge was very helpful securing us tickets to Alcatraz when it was otherwise sold out. The location was great, just a short walk to the Wharf, but there are lots of other places to stay nearby. 
I like to give credit where credit is due and have written very positive reviews about other places that we've stayed, but honestly, find another place to stay.

There are good hotels, there are nice hotels , there are average hotels and there are classy hotels. The thing that separates them are the attention that is paid to the details. The Hotel Sorella just has that ambiance of class. From the time you enter the main entrance which is a wood staircase to the time you check in, to the time you walk down the hallway, to the time you go to your room, the atmosphere is one of class. There is so much detail in the decor. It really is a beautiful hotel. The check in was quick but the the receptionist was very friendly and helpful as she explained the amenities. We had a corner room which had a great view of the courtyard, swimming pool, and a lot more of the City Centre. The room was very big with a king size bed, a 42" TV, a couch, a lounge chair, a round table and 4 chairs. The bathroom had a walk in shower and top of the line hair care items. Again, the room and bathroom had so many fine details that just separates it from the normal hotel. The hotel also has an outstanding restaurant, Bistro Alex . The food and attention from the wait staff was above and beyond. There is a club/bar known as the Mona Lisa which along with everything else in the hotel just exudes class. A continental breakfast was served in the morning starting at 6:30 which was unusual for a Sunday morning. It consisted of a variety of fruits, dry cereals, pastries, and breakfast drinks including made to order specialty coffees. You had the option of eating in a very open lounge area or outside on the balcony.
The area around the hotel is known as the City Centre with multiple places to eat from fast food type places to really nice restaurants. There are places to shop, a movie theater, and a family friendly commons area where live music was being played and kids were playing on a turfed area as people sat around the perimeter and ate, drank or just watched.
There are nice hotels, good hotels and then there is the Hotel Sorella--a classy hotel.

If you like not sleeping, noise all night long and a parking garage that is nighmare stay at this Hampton Inn. We had a room next to the train track and heard the the train noise starting before sunup. The mandatory ear plugs they give you are litlle help. We were lucky to be out that evening until mid-night but still heard trains at 1, 2, 3 AM. Also, the parking structure is very small and many people had parked in the on and off ramps making it impossible to turn around. We got lucky and found the last space otherwise who know where we would have parked.
My advise spend a few dollars more and get a better place.
had no hot water in room for entire stay of three nights.no continental breakfast.would not stay here again!

This was just a quick, overnight stay in Charlotte but I am more than satisfied with the accommodations! From check-in to check-out, I have only one complaint, the shuttle not running on Saturdays. Although this was a bit disappointing, the front desk happily gave me the number and approximate cost of a reputable taxi service since I did not want to drive to my destination. I actually had a few other questions as I have never stayed in this area of Charlotte and each time the staff were polite, friendly, and patient to answer me. Check-in was timely and efficient even amid the number of people coming in for a conference being held at the hotel. Additionally, I was pleased with the rooms. I suggest trying to get on one of the executive levels. These rooms provide water bottles upon arrival and breakfast in the morning at the Lakefront Restaurant. I highly recommend this Hilton and will definitely being staying there on my next trip to Charlotte!

We have stayed at Phoenix Park many times over the years and each time we enjoy it more. The staff is always smiling and willing to help in any way. We were on the Penthouse floor in 909 and it was lovely. Order breakfast in our room and enjoyed a hot breakfast at our large dining room table with a pleasant view. Yes, breakfast came to our room on time and stayed hot through our meal. Eggs were done perfectly as asked. Bed was king size and extremely comfortable with feather pillows as we requested. AC was good and maintained temperature through the night. It was a scorching day around 99 degrees. 
There is construction going on at the building next door but we did not hear anything from it. Check out was at one so there was plenty of time to enjoy the morning, go to our meeting as still have time to check out without being rushed. If you like small initmate hotels this is the place for you!

Baymont was just great. Cloe to DIA,and great service shuttle. Rooms were just great.
Breakfast items were pretty good.

We were there for four days at a conference.From check-in to check-out staff could not have been more accomadating. Rooms were ready upon arrival with a gorgeuos view of the arizona desert and the mountains surrounding Phoenix. The pool area was super with a lazy river for relaxing. Plenty of chairs and excellent poolside service. The outdoor seating areas are numerous with many spots availabe for conversation and reading.Great music played in the evening in the lobby area. Food and beverages were reasonably priced and the hotel offers a shuttle service to the local mall area which had many small restaurants and shops. I would definetly recommend this for families and conferences.Food was excellent.

I just came back from my 2 night stay there and I have to say....I so wanted to give this a 5, but one main point prevents it....location. The hotel is very nice and the staff was great. The indoor pool and gym were very nice and clean. The outdoor patio was great to sit and watch the game while the wife smoked....Very comfortable seats and was always being checked by staff for cleanliness. The breakfast in the AM was great. It was not very crowded when we were there, but there are lots of seats there, so seating should never be a problem.....My only issue was the location. It's not the best location in Philly and get's a little nervous at night as it's not very busy. Other than that, I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone and would be happy to answer any questions about my experience there.

My fiance and I came to Charlotte to have a nice little get away from home. We stayed for one night and it was fantastic! We came in at 9 in the morning we did not think we would be able to check in but we thought why not lets give it a shot. We were surprised we were able to check in early! The front desk was very friendly and helpful. When we got to our room we loved it! The decor of the room was just so nice and the bed was so comfortable and nice we slept through the night really well and we didnt want to come home! The bar in the lobby was really neat and when we had breakfast it was really good. We would like to come back in the future and stay longer next time! :)

Booked the penthouse suite with a balcony three months in advance. Received a call two days prior to arrival to say they were overbooked and that I would have to take a non-balcony room. The gentlemen who called was pleasant and said he would comp us a couple of movies and some other crap. No big deal, just can't see how you can overbook a hotel room that I paid for in advance with no option for cancelation. We show up and the room was as originally booked, not sure what happened, no one said a word. This room which cost me $750 for two nights was far from impressive, badly needs a remodel job. The master closet door was falling off the track, the safe was locked, the master bedroom TV volume would work intermittently and the master toilet wouldn't flush........nice. The balcony door lock was broken so they had a bar to pry against the frame to secure it. A nice amenity of the penthouse is the skylights but in this case they were filthy with an added makeshift, water stained, Plexiglas panel over the bottom of it. This room had a kitchenette with a dining table, the table had huge bubbles in it from water damage. Some light bulbs were out and the ones that worked were so dim from dirt it was hard to see. Another amenity of this penthouse suite is the balcony, or so we thought. Directly below is the Weber Grill restaurant so we were bathed in grilling smoke while on the balcony, how romantic. The room seemed dirty, old and musty, won't be back. Great location downtown but not even close to the Conrad across the street which we stayed at earlier this year.

title_masked: You will never be dissapointed.......best location, service and ambiance.
text_masked: best location, best service. had my kids come up and brought some friends, went to Gibsons and shopped at Bloomingdales all within steps.............went to the pool at night, (you have to see it!) cookies and milk for the kids in the room! what a view from all rooms!

We chose this hotel to stay in during parents weekend at George Washington University. It was only a few minutes walk to the campus, and we were also just a short walk into Georgetown. Although the hotel does have parking for about $35 per night, we were able to find a spot BOTH nights on the street nearby. The hotel is very pretty, clean and is located near all the other finer hotels on every corner. The front desk and concierge service were very good. We did have a problem in our room with the air conditioner. The first night we did not use it but the second night it was so loud, it kept waking us up. I did let the front desk know but they did not offer us any compensation. We did call up for a cot as my kids dont like to share a double bed and the cot came almost immediately. The bathroom was very spacious with a private toilet area so more than one person could use it at a time. We did not eat in the hotel at all so I can not comment on that. Over all it was a nice stay. We got an excellent rate per night booking it many months in advance directly with the hotel so it was refundable if needed. I would defintiely come back to this location again.

The typical great DoubleTree hotel. We didn't visit any of the amenities as the trolly stop is right across the street and allows guests to get all around San Diego. This hotel was cheaper than others in the prime districts in San Diego but due to the trolly stop we were able to go anywhere we wanted and save some money.

This hotel is located right on the Riverwalk so it's right across from the Convention Center and a short walking distance to all the downtown locations. The room is spacious and the staff is pleasant and always smiling. The pool is nice with half indoor and half outdoor. The health center is 24hrs so it's convinient. I do agree that this hotel needs a makeover as it really is showing its age. With other hotels nearby, Hyatt and Hilton, it would be smart for Marriott to spend some money to renovate. If that happens, I'd definitely give it a five start rating!

title_masked: Good value for central San Francisco
text_masked: We stayed here for two nights, room 224. Room was clean and reasonably spacious with a fridge/microwave/coffee maker and comfortable beds. Front desk was very helpful and friendly. Breakfast was sparse, but at least free if you're on a budget - we used it to supplement the box of cereal we bought. Castle Inn was pretty easy to find and seemed to be in a good area - free parking another bonus. Thankfully the hotel had an elevator so we didn't have to drag our bags up to the 2nd floor (rooms have outside entrances). We didn't really try to walk anywhere from the hotel, so I can't say if it was conveniently located to things like the cable car etc. Our only complaint was the internet was terrible here, was really patchy and barely worked. We told the front desk but nothing really happened to fix it - being that other reviewers have commented on this, it was a little disappointing that this was still an issue. Other than some very rude guests calling loudly to each other back and forth outside at 2am (don't know why management didn't hear them?!) which due to the shape of the hotel facing the wall seemed to echo, we had a good stay and I would stay there again.

Specifically because of the difference in remodeled verses older rooms, I would give this hotel a 3 1/2 rating. I stayed at the Drake October, 2011 and again October, 2012. And it is truly a lovely hotel. If you have one of the updated rooms on a higher floor then the location and price for the rooms are more in line with one might expect. And last year we had a lovely room, on a higher floor and it just felt more high end. This year, we were on the first floor and the room was an awkward layout and it didn't feel at all like the quality we had the year before. Both times I traveled with my husband over the Chicago marathon week end. I mention this because the hotel was busy, it has a convenient downtown location and people love to go there based on historic reviews. Every knows the Drake. However, I think they need to have completely different prices for their rooms that are not yet remodeled. We paid over $380 each night for our average room. For that amount, I want to stay in a much better room. 
I hope this review is helpful to you, hit the helpful vote if you liked it. Have a great time in this wonderful city!
Stayed one night. Very clean room, modern amenities. Very attentive staff. Will definitely return.

title_masked: Checked In 7/2 and Stuck Here Until 7/9
text_masked:
I find it amazing that so many hotel chains treat customers, yes customers who are buying their services, who shop around for the best price with such poor service and disregard. Such customers, like myself, receive the "shadow class" service. This is our third stay at this hotel over the past few years and while on trips where we booked directly with them all of our "select guest" preferences were honored, on the other two trips where we found a better price somewhere else, we were stuck with rooms that had someone paid the full price for, would have complained. 
When will the hotel industry learn that they hurt their own business with these practices? We will never stay here again and never recommend this hotel to anyone that we care for. How much money does it cost the hotel to provide an extra pillow? How about a corner room when the hotel is clearly not booked? Provide an extra roll of toilet paper when they only provided a partial roll? Provide adequately working air conditioning? We've set the thermostat to under 70 and it still can't catch up and cool off and it is day 2! Provide a full size room as this one is clearly not the square footage of the rooms that we had in the past?
Very disappointing as we thought that the Omni would stand out from the crowd of hotels that are out there just to make a buck.

title_masked: Great hotel right near the action of Times Square
text_masked: We recently stayed at the Fairfield Inn Times Square and were very pleased. The staff was friendly and pleasant. The lobby and room were immaculate. Decent size for family of four. Could not hear any outside nose. Street was relatively clean and definately safe. Breakfast was good. I agree with other reviewers that bacon would be a nice change. Sausage was gray and unappetizing. Breakfast staff very friendly as well. Will definately stay there again in future!

The Kimpton Hotel was the wedding home-base for our family, and we cannot say enough good things about the property and it's excellent staff. Everyone from Darryl and Daisey at the front desk, to Chris at the restaurant, and the hotel assistant general manager took great care of us and made sure that all our needs were met. We took advantage of the rooftop pool and enjoyed the great views. The lobby happy hour was a very pleasant treat, it gave an opportunity for everyone to catch up on the daily activities and make plans for the evening. Thank you Donovan House and Kimpton Hotels for another job well done.

This was my second stay at this location. I was there for a conference, at a negotiated rate, but do was only able to get the conference rate for one night of a two night stay. This mixed up their reservation system and I had to re-check in the next day. Even then my bill was still incorrect requiring another trip to and long wait in the temporary lobby. The lobby is under construction, and the temporary lobby is tucked into a corner. Signage is poor and there is lot's of confusion as multiple folks navigate the narrow corridor looking for different services. The staff, when you could find someone, was friendly enough. They seemed very poorly trained, however, and usually unable to accommodate requests. There was hardly ever a doorman, concierge or bell clerk around. 
The rooms are nice, although starting to look somewhat worn. I had a later check out, and when I returned to the room, the maid had already cleaned the room for the next guests.
The location is okay, but just far enough off of Michigan that it's 10 minute walk to get anywhere. Given all this I'd likely stay somewhere else next time. For the cost I definitely did not feel I was in a 4 star hotel.

title_masked: Great location, staff and room for budget price.
text_masked:
We stayed at the hotel over Labour Day weekend. I was with my 74 year old mother and 15 year old niece. John checked us in and out. He was calm, efficient and very helpful. We were upgraded from a dorm room with shared bathroom to a king-sized room with a pullout and its own bathroom. The bedding, towels and bathroom were clean. The location was fantastic - close enough to walk up to Times Square, the theatre and down into meat district. Our room was big, but typically The only negative was our room faced 8th Avenue, which is a main street. We found it very noisy with only 1 or 2 hours in the wee hours where traffic (people and cars) died down. The air conditioner helped drown it out as did exhaustion from a day of walking. 
When looking for a hotel you need to know what you're looking for and understand that space is at a premium. For example, if you have lots of heavy bags, then you need to consider that there are no lifts. We wanted a no frills hostel/hotel that was clean,safe and close to the heart of the city at a budget price. The Chelsea Star met all our needs. We'd stay there again.

We have stayed here twice for extended periods and have enjoyed our stays. Staff is very friendly and the rooms were completed updated last summer. Pool is heated and breakfast and evening snacks have been great! Love the burger and hotdog night! Your pets are allowed as well.

I was @ the Hilton,new york.av. of Americas..for the New years,,its a average four stars cause you can tell is aging,,but very clean and organized..I was lucky got a room in the 39 floor (executive) and the view was great. The best Thing about this Hotel is Location and as they say in real estate: Location, location, you can walk to a ton of attractions and that saves you alot time and money! cause cabs in traffic suck your wallet off. The best way to know the NYC.. by subway or metro whatever you whant called it, its old and dirty, but takes you fast and cheap from A to B.

title_masked: The Baldwin is a great value choice!
text_masked: Four star rating for value, location, cleanliness and staff. This is definitely not a posh property, but is a great choice for the budget traveler. The bed was very comfortable and everything was clean - maid service did a great job, including cleverly shaped towels on the bed in animal forms. The hotel is less than a block from the Chinatown entrance gate on Grant St., and an easy couple of blocks walk to Union Square.

We stayed for 3 nights this past weekend; we were supposed to stay 4 nights however with all of the weather issues in the East we left a day early.
This is the perfect hotel to relax and rest...pure serenity. Like others have pointed out it is not a "hustle bustle" hotel and that I truly love! You have all of the amenities of a large hotel with a boutique feel. The room was perfect from the design to the amenities, very smart layout with plenty of space and a lovely fireplace. I actually loved the quiet lobby; I cannot stand waiting in long lines of noisy travelers so the quaintness was welcomed. The staff is very attentive and thoughtful; even though they are a tip less hotel the service is still wonderful. We had packages delivered to the hotel and champagne sent up every night without a flaw in the service. The bar in the restaurant is great for a drink and some charcuterie and the other cozy bar opens around 4 pm. The location is great for all of the high end shopping and a short brisk walk to the lake. We will stay again!!! It is expensive but that is understood if you know the hotel brands/industry so if you are on a budget you may want to stay at a Hilton or Marriott.

hotel was clean, staff were very helpful and friendly
rooms were adequate, bathroom very small and could do with some TLC
Breakfast and bar prices were fairly good
Not a great view from our room and poor lifts always stopping and alarm going off

This is a typical Marriott product with a great location in LA. Breakfast in LA Market was mediocre and somewhat expensive for what you received. The noise level when concerts are happening is the greatest drawback of this property - I was on a high floor and I could hear the music until 11 p.m., which is not good when it's a weeknight and you just want to sleep early. The front desk clerk I spoke to upon checkout expressed regret that I didn't call her and get the free earplugs. ;-)

Well, no bad words about this property.
I have reserved my stay 2 months before my staying period thru a 3rd part website and when I arrived my reservation was immediately found and within minutes I had my room keys in hands.
The room is large, clean, well serviced (coffee machine, tea, frigobar, iron and board, great wardrobe, hair dryer, hot water in the tap) fully carpeted (except the bathroom), cable tv, cabled internet (free for low speed usage, but I didn´t find it slow at all), air conditioning, soundproof windows and daily maid service impeccable.
I didn´t have meals there but there´s is a resturant and a bar but I didn´t try or saw the prices.
Anyway, there´s a 7-Eleven store in the same building by the street and the New York Ave metro station is wall to wall the hotel.
The neighborhood is quite empty on the weekends once this a commercial area but not so bad. Is a fact that sometimes I saw some weird faces walking around at night.
If you have free time, the Union Station is a 20 mins walking down but it´s hard the way back due the distance and straight up the avenue.
Also, I didn´t realize till my 2nd day there that the building in front of it is the ATF Builiding. I don´t know if there´s public access once I didn´t ask.
I had contact only with front desk staff and security officers and both my check-in and check-out were very fast and efficient and everybody were polite and friendly.
Just a note: the street level door isn´t the front desk, it´s a security pre-check that if it´s closed or empty you can open using your room key or use the intercomm to contact the front desk in the 2nd floor. 
No complains, no worries, I liked and easily could go back.

title_masked: Very average, but good location & value for NYC
text_masked: Best thing about this hotel is the location. You are yards away from the subway station entrance and only 10 minutes to Time Square. The staff was friendly and room was clean. This is a room you would pay $50 a night for at a turnpike exit. Neighborhood was very nice. Definetely felt safe here. Biggest complaint was that the windows were covered only with cheap plastic blinds so even in the middle of the night the street lights made it seem like daytime and there was no barrier to the street noise. The TV was an old big box that only got 10 channels. Old time elevators, but good old building with good noise barrier to other rooms. Our room was right behind the elevator and we didn't hear a thing (except everything going on outside). There is a cafe right across the street with adequate food at all times. Central Park was a 15 minute walk. It would have been nice to be a little closer to the action, but for the price this was a good NYC option.

This is a conveniently-located hotel - as noted by others, you don't even have to go outside to catch the Metro. The lobby is very attractive, and the staff are quite friendly. There's a Starbucks in the lobby, along with Zephyr, which is a nice place to grab a quick breakfast or lunch. The rooms were very comfortable. I was in a room right across the street from the construction site, but wasn't bothered by the noise. I would stay here again for business travel.

title_masked: Inn at the Park San Diego
text_masked: We enjoyed our stay at Inn at the Park. The location was great. We had a rental car, but fount the Tram, which stopped 2 (short) blocks away, was better they dealing with the car. The tram took us to all the museums in Balboa Park. We used the Tram several times during the trip. The staff at the hotel were wonderful and the resturant in the lower level was very good and convient. The continental breakfast always had frest fruit, yogurt, cottage cheese and the regular things. The hotel is old (1926), and is being renovated. It was very reasonable,but that might change. The only down side was the bed. It was very hard. I hope they get new ones as I would definitely return. I loved San Diego, La Jolla, The Midway, Balboa Park and the Zoo. Could have stayed more that a week.

I just spent 11 nights at the Distrikt Hotel, and left most impressed, and wanting to go back!
I was fortunate to have an amazing view room, which was great to sit and look out on when in the room. 
The room was clean, and the cleaning staff really were amazing and friendly. It was very clean.
By NYC standards the room was a good size, I had 2 suitcases, and found they were not in my way at all. You also have a chest of drawers, and a good size wardrobe to use if you want.
On arrival, they delivered me with a dozen cans of coke (Cherry, and Diet) and a note from a friend. It turns out the hotel arranged it all at their cost for my friend, an amazing gesture. Thank you Distrikt, that really floored me, especially since I was worried at my friend spending money she does not have!
The service staff were wonderful at helping with luggage, and shopping, and general chit chat. I am pretty shy, but people were always chatty and friendly in the lifts, both staff and other guests alike.
I also spent 1.5hrs sitting in reception one afternoon while waiting for a friend to pick me up, and observed the customer service at many levels. Exceptional, they even went so far as to help one guest fix a watch they had bought, at the hotels expense. That is service I have never seen in any other hotel. I felt comfortable just sitting there quietly.
Most days, you were greeted as you passed through reception by the staff, and told to have a great day/night, or asked how your day was. This created a true feeling of family. I am mostly a guest who comes and goes without words as that is what I am used too in hotels, but i did appreciate it, and it made me feel important to the hotel.
The tea and coffee at reception, and the computers for people to use were popular and wonderful. The free internet is a great bonus.
The hotel is in close proximity to the subway, Times Square, Broadway, and off Broadway shows or for the shopper, Herald Square. I was a female alone, and I never felt unsafe walking down the street the hotel was on, there were always lots of people around.
I have definitely found a new favourite NYC hotel, thank you for a wonderful stay. Please keep up the great service, and prices, as I want to be able to stay here again and again when I visit my favourite city outside of New Zealand!

In Dallas last week for business. Hotel is a 25 minute drive from DFW. Hilton Anatole is a large elegant property. Rooms are spacious, quiet decorated with a modern tasteful Asian influence. Has several restaurants, stores and a business center. Offers array of services, a quality relaxing hotel.

I had a wonderful experience at thr W New York! We went to New York to See the Rockettes and do some shopping. Our show started before Check in. The W allowed us to leave our luggage and offered to call us when our room was ready. The gentleman that check our luggage was not only very friendly and professional but he was very attrative. All of their employess in the lobby during our brief stay were quite handsome. I enjoyed that! I got a call from the W before the show was over letting us know that our room was readyand that we could check in early. Upon arrival we found out that they had also upgraded our room, which was great because the room was on the smaller side but I expect that in NYC. The beds were amazing! Super comfortable and cozy. The street noise was a bit annoying but once again it's New York. The hotel is in a great location. We walked to Radio City Music hall, Madame Tussauds wax Museum and Times Square. We got a great deal on the price and it included 2 free drinks as well. We had a great time and will definitely be staying there again.

My husband and I travel alot, we have to say this is one of the best hotels we ever stayed at. The hospitality of the staff is excellent. Raymond, the desk clerk is a great asset to the hotel staff. Also, they have a free shuttle for the guest to use. The driver Roland goes above and beyond to get you to your location and back. There is also a free continental breakfast included in your stay. Also, the guest rooms are beautifully decorated. We definetly recommend this hotel.

Positive - 
Hotel's location is blocks to Broadway, Rockefeller Center, Central Park, and two major subway north-south hubs. You can get downtown from this hotel in about 20 minutes on the E line, for example. 
Bedding was very comfortable. 
Average- Areas of Improvement:
Room condition, carpet, and furnishings are okay. The bathroom had issues with low water pressure for a 5th floor room, drainage issues with the bathtub and some smells. Toilet did not flushing properly about half the time. One had to flush a couple of times. When this was reported, we never received a response. 
Check-in. Not exactly fast but we held to the 3pm check in time. That was understandable, however, on checkout day, housekeeping let themselves in at 8am! (with an I'm sorry). I told them we were checking out at 10:30am but they came back 4 additional times before 10am. I don't blame the housekeeping team, clearly they are doing this at the direction of housekeeping management. It was slightly annoying to be held to the 3pm check-in but then to get the feeling they wanted us out of there well prior to a 12 noon checkout time. 
They dollar you to death at this hotel. There was no free wi-fi. To store bags when checking out, it was $3.50 per bag, and then you had to tip because there is no guarantee those fees are being distributed to staff. Food prices, especially room service were outrageous. It would have to be a blizzard or monsoon for me to order up food at those prices. ($22 for grilled cheese and fries? LOL) 
Public restroom. Since our room was not ready, I used the public restroom near the marketplace restaurant. It was filthy. Urine water all over the floor from where a urinal overflowed. I went to the front desk (waited in line again!) to report the conditions in a polite manner and received a shrug and an "okay" for my trouble. It is a warning sign when a hotel is indifferent to these kinds of issues.

I booked this room 2 nights for my Honeymoon. Room was very small no drawers to put clothes in very very small but comfy bed..Asked for a fridge to but a few items in and was told just take out what was in the bar and leave it out. People pay alot of money for that stuff do they know its cold the warm the cold again...No special anything from this hotel for our wedding. Ordered room service got a call back No Bacon and the same thing the next day. How do you run out of bacon? Staff was amazing and very friendly was not impressed about hotel. Verigo bar open at 5pm and we went up around 10 and nobody to take our drink order. Balcony so small. Upgrade to a bigger room. Best was staff, towels in bathroom and great bed. Very loud in hall doors slamming.

title_masked: Very Good, But Need Some Improvements!
text_masked:
The Hotel is Very Good, but need to take some care with some Issues. 
For example, I Wanted to use the pool, which opens at 9AM, It was 9:15 and nothing, I had to go to the front desk to ask to open the pool. 
The rooms are clean, but not as cleaner as their "Brother" hotel, the Hampton Inn, I've stayied in Hampton inn in Saint Louis and notice a big difference
The Rooms are clean and big, but a little old, they should refurbish the rooms
The staff was helpful when necessary, but not proactive.
It's a Good Hotel, Grade 7 from 10 for me, but need some improvements to reach the 10.

title_masked: Very good place. The receptionist Laura is very helpfully and friendly
text_masked:
The price is good for the location and the accommodation level. Laura one of the receptionist is very helpfully and give friendly support, all time.
Les recomendamos mucho el lugar estan en pleno centro y pueden caminar al Gas lamp y otros lugares de interes.
I recomend this place.
Andrés

My family and I stayed at the Sky View Plaza hotel on June 13th 2012, when we got there the room was disgusting, the lock didn’t work, the sheets were stained, the phone nor tv didn’t work, there were holes in the wall and ceiling, we didn’t want to complain because it was one night and we didn’t want to be “those people.” We got back from vacation and the driver picked us up almost killing us, speeding, texting and driving, slamming on his breaks, as well as talking on his phone. We got back to the hotel and our tire was slit in their parking lot. I was fed up and went in to talk to a manager, no one was there. I tried calling as well as emailing the next day to talk to the manager. After a week he finally decided to answer my call and told me it was too late to refund my money. Well if he didn’t ignore me for a week it wouldn’t have been too late. The workers there are unprofessional, and I do not advise anyone to stay there.

title_masked: Good deal in a good location
text_masked:
We were looking for a reasonably priced hotel while my husband was spending time at the Javits Convention Center on business. This hotel fit the bill in terms of location and price. The room was clean and comfortable and the service was excellent. This part of Broadway may seem a little seedier but it's quieter and top hotels have moved in across the street. I recommend the Oyster Bar across the street (part of the Ace Hotel - I think).
So the lobby is tight, the breakfast is so-so and as is the room decor, but it's affordable and easy walking distance to Macy's!

We stayed at Towneplace while in town for a reunion and found the room in excellent condition and very clean.The staff were friendly and accommodating and we were very happy with the place in every regard.

title_masked: Fabulous staff- smiled all the way through Hurricane Sandy.
text_masked:
I went with 5 friends for one of our special birthdays, cakes and card greeted us in both rooms as they were not sure which one that she would be staying in.
Great small central hotel, staff are very helpful and despite having to stay 24/7 during Hurricane Sandy they kept smiling.They were so helpful when we had to stay an extra 2 nights due to cancelled flights.
We went because of good tripadvisor reviews and were not disappointed and I would definately go back there.Breakfasts were reasonable and great, due to other reviews we tried an number of breakfast options before using the hotel but wished that we had used the hotel more often as some of the others were not as good.

One of the cool things about this old hotel is that it has Westin refinement but also a "real worldness" almost "grittiness" about it.
This is a historical place where a lot of very cool things have happened. 
This place has the most unique lobby space of any hotel I have ever patronized. It is part mall... part flea market.. part cafe... part boutique... part bar..it is just a blast is what it is. All under an old darkwood mahogany feel. 
Perfect Check In. 
The hotel... even though the most recent room remodel is wearing off... it is still sharp. The concierge, and bag service are impeccable.

title_masked: Caveat Emptor...Don't always believe the "glowing" reviews
text_masked:
I was compelled to write this review, not only because this is THE worst RRI I have ever stayed at, but because of all the glowing reviews about this place. I am sorry, but these glowing reviews can't possibly be real. I am writing this review on 2/17/12 while sitting in room 307.
This RRI is VERY old and rundown. The popcorn ceiling says it all. The carpet is stained throughout the place and the rooms smell of mold and dampness (I changed rooms since the first room, #115, smelled musty and damp). Lucky me, #307 was no better.
I am a RediCard member and stay at RRI's whenever I can (see my previous review(s) about other RRI's) and I am just amazed at the reviews here. Someone should look into this. If I was RRI, I would come by and take a look for myself. I know I wouldn't want my name on a place like this.
The young man at the counter was friendly and helpful and the lobby looked and smelled good, but the rest of the place, well, Caveat Emptor!

We recently stayed for 4 nights. We arrived two hours before check in-the clerk was very courteous-he even let us park there and recommended things to do until check in (and how to use the bus line if necessary)! The room was spacious, clean and quiet. We were given a room in the back without asking. The location is excellent- there are are so many boutiques and restaurants in the area around the hotel. IHOP 2 blocks away for breakfast -or several local coffee houses. Painless check in process, short and I was guided to my room.
Close to shopping and great restaurants, it took me 2 min to walk to Bloomingdales, and about 5 min to walk to a great bar.

Updated room amenities
Great value!!

My husband and I stayed here for a long weekend in April. The staff at this hotel are all extremely friendly and eager to help. But the best part of the hotel is the room. I spend 150+ nights/year in hotel rooms and this one was by far my favorite. Great hotel, very nice attentions from the front desk, very fancy and big, you can stay up till late and walk in the area because it is in front of times square and near everything. The elevators are so fast!!! woowww! you can be go to floor 38 in like 10 seconds. A great place to stay in nyc.

We stayed at this hotel over spring break on our way to Steamboat Springs. The hotel is very nice with a centrally located indoor pool and hot tub next to the refreshment area of hotel. title_masked: Best & Most Stress-Free Hotel in Houston
text_masked: I always stay at this hotel if possible when I visit Houston. The colors, food, staff, and rooms make it well worth it!

The Palmer House Hilton
This hotel is the nicest Hilton we've stayed at. The lobby and various ballrooms and function rooms are as storied as they are classically elegant. (We read a book on the history of this historic hotel—in its third incarnation).
Our 18th room floor, facing north, wasn't particularly spacious, but it was very nicely appointed, with marble and granite bathroom fixtures, thick crown molding, sold wood doors with wide wood trim and solid brass door knobs. 
As Hilton Honors members, we had access to the Executive Lounge on the 23rd floor, where we had an excellent complimentary continental breakfast and hors d'oeuvres in the evening that could pass for dinner if need be. We also had complimentary access to the pool and fitness area. The pool is quite small, not large enough to exercise in, but the fitness room was well appointed with free weights and machines. 
Our only complaints about this hotel are the elevators—you can wait quite a while for one—and the location, which seems to be panhandler central. You are in a business district rather than an entertainment district, so plan accordingly in the evening. 
Otherwise, the hotel is centrally located on Wabash within the Loop, a block in from Michigan Ave., Millennium Park, the Art Institute, etc. The Red line subway is right outside the hotel on the State Street side, and the El is right out front on Wabash. 
There's not much to eat in the immediate vicinity in the evening, except for the Beef and Brandy near the State Street entrance, which is quite good, and Miller's Tavern near the Wabash entrance, which is serviceable for late night eating (in fact, it's the only choice outside of the hotel). 
For food inside the hotel, you will pay the Hilton premium. The drinks and food items are small, expensive, and tasty, but the setting quite elegant. Potter's Lounge is small, dark, loud, and mostly young. 
We would definitely stay here again but plan our dinners better.

My mom and I came to DC for vacation in mid-July and spent 6 nights at the Washington Plaza. We couldn't stop talking about how glad we were that we chose this hotel. Some of the highlights included:
1. Best pool in DC: This large outdoor pool has a a deep-end (8 ft) and an outer ledge that allows you to take in the sun while relaxing in a few inches of water. The loungers surrounding the pool were comfortable (big pillows included!) and there were always plenty of them to go around (which I thought was fantastic, considering that the pool was quite busy due to the high temperatures). There were also plenty of sun umbrellas, tables and clean towels. One of the best parts of the pool area was the service! James and Tracy were two of the very friendly servers we encountered and they took great care of us the entire time. They kept us in cool drinks and made sure we were aware of the $6 bar menu (from 4pm-7pm) which included tasty items like quesadillas and flat breads.
2. Great room with balcony: We were pleasantly surprised to find a large, covered balcony (complete with table and chairs) when we first checked in to our room. Not all rooms have balconies, but we assume that they gave us this room because we booked early and were staying longer than average, but I'm guessing this could be requested. The hotel is still undergoing a few final touches on their recent renovations (bath tub/showers need to be updated, but were very clean), but overall it looked great. The beds were very comfortable and our bathroom had double sinks.
3. Professional, friendly staff: Never once did we walk through the lobby without being greeted by someone at the front desk or in the valet area. We had great room service (in room dining and housekeeping) and as mentioned earlier, the pool side service was perfect.
4. Perfect location: Very central, close to everything. There was a 24-hour CVS (drug store) and a Starbucks right across the street. We took taxis to most of the major tourist areas (national mall, Georgetown, water front) and never had to pay more than $10.
Things they could work on? I really have no complaints but I guess I would recommenced that they stock their rooms with proper coffee cream (as opposed to those powdered substitutes), although they never had a problem bringing it to me free of charge when I called room service.
Wonderful experience! If I am ever in DC again I wouldn't consider staying anywhere else.

My daughter aged 15 and I stayed in this hotel for a week which included five nights during and after Hurricane Sandy. The holiday was her 16th birthday present and I was hoping from the reviews that it would be a great hotel and the rooms would be as nice as they sounded as we would probably end up spending some time relaxing in our room at night after lots of sightseeing and shopping!
 The hotel is in a really nice location, mostly very helpful staff particularly reception and the room cleaning staff. We had a king size room with kitchenette which should have been great.
However, what really let the hotel down was the response to the loss of power after the hurricane. Despite days of warnings on the news to stock up on batteries etc, when the hotel lost power, the only thing the staff had to offer was a glow stick per room. Ours didn't work. There were some nightlights on offer later but these lit up a small part of the room and lasted about 6 hours so it still meant creeping around in the dark. When I asked if more lights were available, I was asked to hide the nightlight in my pocket as they had run out of even those.
Some guests went out and bought their own extension leads so they could use the sockets in the corridor but the hotel management didn't seem to consider buying any. 
I expected the hotel to reduce the price to compensate for the lost facilities but when I checked out and asked what reduction would be made on the bill, I was told they would check with management and the feedback was:
'you're lucky, other hotels have had to shut and guests have had to move'
'you're already on a reduced price' - not sure what this meant as had booked direct with the hotel??!
I was really surprised that the management considered this a reasonable and fair response to the lack of services - I will not be staying there again.

title_masked: Becoming a fan of the Holiday Inn...
text_masked:
I travel a lot for work and personal reasons, and tend to stay in more expensive hotels, but the Holiday Inn has shown me a lot over the different cities I've stay in it. The customer service really seems to always be friendly, and for the value they always tend to be well worth it. Whenever booking a holiday inn, if you are not already, become a priority club member! You get a few perks thrown at you for just being a member, and it's free. They upgraded me to an executive suite for free. 
The downtown hotel is in a great location! It's a few blocks away from the mall and all the Smithsonian museums. Best part is that it's a few steps from L'Enfant Plaza metro station. This is important because DC has a good subway, but it's not big and doesn't have stops in a lot of key areas, so the fact you're close to one is great. L'Enfant is a main "hub" for the DC subway, and you can connect to different lines from the stop. 
Back to the hotel - it's in a great location and it's a nice holiday inn. There is a bar/grill downstairs. WIFI is free. Our room came with a refrigerator/microwave so that's good for people staying for awhile and visiting the town. There is a CVS pharmacy next door which you can buy snacks, water bottles, etc (not very common for this tourist area).
To the negatives, as others mentioned, definitely needs to be upgraded as far as furniture, etc. The Air conditioning in our room was SO loud! You could barely hear the TV. Also, our room windows were by a railroad track and trains run in the early morning hours. I was woken up a few times in the morning. If you are looking for the nightlife of DC, you won't find much at all in the area of the hotel. It is where the museums are; but as mentioned, jump on the subway or catch a cab. Everything is not too far so fares won't be too high.
There are only a couple downers in an otherwise good hotel in a great location. I would recommend it; we live in the suburbs of DC and just spent the weekend downtown but can tell it would be a good choice for visiting tourists.

Great place to spend a few days in DC. Located several blocks from two Metro stations (Foggy Bottom at GWU and Dupont Circle), the Washington Marriott is only several blocks from the shops in Georgetown, a 20 minute walk to the Capitol Mall (Lincoln Memorial side) and lots of restaurants in the Dupont Circle area (10 minute walk). Not that you need to stray far from the hotel to get great food (the late night bacon cheeseburger is the best) and well poured drinks (Sam the bartender took VERY good care of us and remembered me & the family from a visit a year ago), and a very good breakfast & brunch (Anthony and the rest of the restaurant staff are excellent!!). Check-in was quick and the rooms was very clean; and housekeeping stayed right on top of it. Free internet in the lobby which has three TVs (two in the bar and one in the lounge area). Food is served in the restaurant or in the lounge and the service is excellent! I have considered staying in other hotels closer to the Mall, but the staff at this Marriott make it worth it. I almost cringe to write this...if more people find out about this place the price will go up. We won't stay anywhere else when we visit DC and we come here several times a year.

When we arrived, they did not have our reservations fully put together. Six of our group members had to sit in the lobby for 1.5 hours while the indifferent/lazy front-desk workers meandered about. At one point during breakfast, which was free (the only redeeming value of the hotel), the attendants left the front desk for more than 20 minutes while a line accumulated and the phones rang nonstop. The wifi was terrible, albeit free. The keys to our doors did not work for more than 24 hours at a time; not surprisingly, when you went to the front desk to ask for new keys the attendants were incredibly rude. At checkout, the front desk atttempted to call our room, however, the room's phone had not worked since we arrived, so we were unable to answer. Accordingly, the front desk sent an exceedingly rude representative to our room to inform us that our checkout time was approaching and that the time at which we desired to leave was "irrelevant." I would recommend staying as far from this hotel as is humanly possible. It represents Jacksonville, FL really poorly as the other people we have encountered have been very gracious hosts. Stay away from this hotel and, especially, its front desk.

title_masked: great deal in a great location!
text_masked: Charming old-style decor, fairly quiet for right in the middle of San Francisco, great location to walking to shops and restaurants, much cheaper than all of the surrounding nice hotels. I was here for a conference with a friend and my partner came in for the weekend, so it was great for both business and pleasure. I had a room with 2 beds for when my friend was here and asked if they could change me to a queen room for when my partner came in and they were very gracious about it.

My wife and I get up to San Francisco a few times a year for some R&R. Generally we are Four Seasons junkies and stay there or the Grand Hyatt, but this time we got a deal at the Ritz and decided to stay there for four nights. We knew that the experience would be different - we expected that the Ritz would be more old world charm and elegant compared to the trendy modern style of the Four Seasons.
First I do want to acknowledge some good aspects of the Ritz: the hotel was spotless and in perfect condition. No chipped tiles, missing grout, dinged floorboards that you see at even some other five star hotels. The hostess/waitresses at The Lounge and the bar at Parallel 37 on Friday and Saturday nights were fantastic - perfect discrete yet attentive service. Every concierge that we talked to during our stay was knowledgeable and helpful. The car valets were very professional and helpful.
But we had some issues. First off, the service in the restaurant side of Parallel 37 (their main restaurant) was very spotty. Some, like Reinaldo, were perfect. Others not so much. In fact at one breakfast we finally gave up after waiting 10 minutes for the bill and simply got up and left. Really! I can't remember the last time I've done that at even a Burger King, let alone a Ritz. The restaurant itself, as well as The Lounge, is a bit of a conundrum. The hotel is old world style, yet the restaurant and lounge have been renovated to a modern style - coincidentally very similar to what I'd expect in a Four Seasons with the sleek lines and chillaxing music. Somehow it just didn't fit. One minute you're in an ornate marble lobby, the next you're surrounded by sleek wood and metal. Huh?
Another issue was with housekeeping. We tried and tried, but somehow our schedule must have perfectly conflicted with room cleaning and the evening turn down. Even though each day we were out of the room from 8-10 and 11-4, then 6-8pm. Finally we called and asked for at least a special turn down so we'd have some clean towels. At other five star hotels they uncannily know when you're gone - presumably some spies in the lobby or something - and the room mysteriously gets cleaned each day regardless of schedule.
The hotel itself is at the top of a steep hill. Only a couple blocks from the Union Square shopping area, but those two blocks are MUCH more difficult than the two blocks from the Four Seasons to the same Union Square, let alone the Grand Hyatt right off the square. One odd thing, that perhaps just brings out the hotel snob in me, is that at no time was there a doorman to open the doors for us. Of course we can do that ourselves, but I guess I've come to expect it.
The rooms are nice - perhaps a bit small but that's ok. No separate shower, which I like. The courtyard view rooms are very quiet - almost too quiet! Some noise in the hallways in the mornings, but nothing significant.
Don't get me wrong - it's a very very nice hotel. Just not what I expected from a Ritz, with the level of perfectly attentive yet discrete service I've come to expect at any and every Four Seasons. Which is where we'll stay, again, next time.

Very good with a combination of a great hotel, great room, and service. I stayed at this hotel one night after a nearby conference. I'm diamond elite and I was upgraded to a large 2 room suite - I believe a Jr. Suite. I also had access to the Exec Lounge for afternoon appetizers and breakfast. Typical offerings there. Free wifi (for elites) with a good strong signal, too. What I was most impressed with was the "space" for an older hotel. Service was outstanding, everyone was friendly. We stayed 2 nights in the La cascada and 2 nights at the Riverside and enjoyed both. We were surprised when we read some the the negative reviews especially after we stayed at the Riverside. It is a Historic building and very charming in its features. Very enjoyable. My wife and I wirh 2 of our grand children had a 1 bedroom on the 3rd floor overlooking the Riverwalk. Our son, his wife and 2 other children had a 1 bedroom on the 7th floor---their oustide view was not as nice. However, we worked it out. We had not planed to spend a lot of time our rooms so they were very adiquate and unique. The whole experience was a little different than at any other resort we have stayed in and that helped make the experience even better. The only problem we encountered was the noise in the streets at night. When I asked one of the staff. I was told that due to the nature of the Riverwalk area the city does most of their work at night and very early morning---Garbage collection, street sweeping and deliveries. So if you are a light sleeper you might want to be prepared. Only 2 of the 8 of us were aware of the noise. Great time and a great experience. We would do it again without any question.

title_masked: Never Again Will I Stay Here - Horrible Hyatt
text_masked:
I should have learned my lesson. Every year in March I attend a meeting held here. I usually stay around the corner at the Fairmont or just up the street at the Swiss Hotel. For some reason this year I forgot how horrible this Hyatt is. Here is a summary:
1. Failure to honor a reservation. Even though a special room was requested at time of reservation and even though i called the afternoon I was to arrive to verify that special room request, when I arrived at 6:30 pm, the room was not available. "There is nothing we can do, we are full."
2. When I arrived in the room (6th floor West Tower) the room reeked of cigarette smoke -- really?? Yes, really, even in 2012. And those f you who have had this know that nothing can be done. I did call -- I told my story and then was sent to a second person to tell the entire story a second time -- the first offer was, "we will have housekeeping come and spray." Of course those of us who travel frequently know this will not work. Then "if you can leave the room for a couple of hours, we can put a machine in there." Leave the room? Not possible then - certainly the next day. "Well, we could buy you dinner and then you could return to the room. Again, I had work to do, not time to sit alone for two hours in a restaurant waiting for the room to be de-odorized. And of course, they were full. NOTHING could be done.
3. Room service -- the first night -- to begin with, I was on hold for 15 minutes -- at 9 pm and then I ordered tomato soup, a reuben with fruit as the side choice and a glass of chianti. Ten minutes later i was called and told they did not serve the tomato soup any more and it should not have been on the menu. I was offered tortilla soup. Five minutes later called to be told they were out of tortilla soup (it was St Patrick's Day and they offered me Irish stew) - I chose the chicken soup. And yes, there was one more call. 15 minutes later I was called and told that I had an old menu and that they did not serve the chianti by the glass any more. Well, that was quite an experience.
4. Bell service - simply put, when they have a large convention, do not expect any bell service unless you are willing to wait 30-40 minutes for it. Enough said.
I could go further but this is already too long. I stayed at the Fairmont for the rest of my stay. Thank goodness.
And later in the week I get to go to Dallas where there is a great Hyatt. never again for this one.

The St. Gregory is in a convenient location, just a few blocks from the Dupont Circle Metro station. I stayed there for three nights on business, and the rate my group had was just $140 per night, which is very inexpensive for NW DC. The room was large, consisting of a small living room, good sized bathroom, and bedroom. The decor in my room hadn't been updated in 15 or more years. The bathroom had 90s-style teal wallpaper, and a strip of those big dressing room-style lights. Everything was functional. My primary complaint was that the air conditioning unit was similar to those at a cheap motel along the Interstate. Each time the air conditioning came on, it did so with a loud bang and it was noisy enough to wake me up a few times during the night. I expect better from a hotel that describes itself as luxury.
Our business group had dinner one evening in the hotel restaurant, and the food was surprisingly fresh and good.
Overall, the St. Gregory is fine, but could stand to upgrade the rooms, particularly the HVAC units.

title_masked: Hospitable and efficient for such a large hotel.
text_masked: Our family stayed here for 5 nights Aug 10 through and were visiting for a family wedding. Our room was in the convention tower wing and was HUGE….2 queen beds with a separate sitting area and high ceilings. It was extremely quiet, and unlike some of the other comments posted, we had absolutely outstanding service from the moment we pulled up outside, from the moment we left. Housekeeping liked to service rooms by 10am, though came back after noon when we were still around. We did not use the valet parking for $45 per night, and instead found $17 per night parking 2 blocks away……staff actually helped us unload our car, stash the luggage and then advised us where to go for alternate parking!! Only real negative was lack of internet, except in the lobby, which is actually the ATT wireless service from the starbucks in the lobby area….it's sort of crazy that wireless is not available for free these days. We did not dine at the hotel (except for the wedding reception….which I would rate 4/5) but used the starbucks a lot, and right under the 'bridge' beside reading market, there was a diner that served decent eggs at a reasonable cost. The lobby area gets a bit 'dodgy' at night (some bizarre-looking people around)…………but there is a lot of security around, especially around the tower area where we we staying. Pool was great and staffed from 8am-11pm, and every day we used the pool or gym, staff were diligently cleaning. All in all, we had a very pleasant stay and truly found the staff to be utterly accommodating and hospitable. The Italian restaurant across the street on the corner was surprisingly decent and very reasonably priced!!! Great kids meals and huge portions, so we would share an appetizer and have starter-sized salads with meat / fish for our main course.

I recently went to San Diego where I was once a resident of 12 years to visit my 4 children and as usual I chose the Loma Lodge. The staff was friendly and professional, the breakfast bar was a great way to start the day and meet other travelers and when I had problems with my visa card the staff went out of their way to accomodate and help me. I plan on coming back in July to enjoy their beautiful pool!
Really clean, the location is perfect, the atmosphere is nice & original, really closed to restaurants & shops in a safe district, perfect deal!

Our stay at this hotel was awesome. We stayed for four nights. The staff was very friendly and helpful. We took advantage of the shuttle bus to sea world. Drops you off at the sea world entrance. The cost of the shuttle bus is only a one time fee of ten dollars. You can use it everyday of your stay. If you decide to drive yourself you will pay 15.00 to park at seaworld. The front desk and the drivers were very knowledgable and informative about area attractions. the place was very clean. Beds very comfortable. The pillows were so comfortable that I purchased some when we checked out. We came here after spending three nights at schiliterbahn. Microtel was 156.00 cheaper a night. Again extremly nice hotel would highly recommend this hotel.

There are other Marriotts in the same neighborhood that are better for the same price range.
Nothing was wrong with the hotel, just the little things seemed off. The king room was small. The elevators were very very very slow (and there are two "towers" so if traveling with family or friends you may need two rides to get to another couple's room). If you prefer stairs, sorry, one of the tower's stairs are emergency exit only...
The service was fine, but we were there for a wedding and the bar closed before 1 am. The valet was also a bit tricky. Your only parking option is valet, and the price was comparable to what you would pay anywhere downtown (except that $3 lot on Caroline). However, the driveway for the valet was tiny and crowded and the valet was painfully slow at times (we were in and out a lot due to the wedding and waited 20+ minutes on more than one occasion). Lastly, the rainfall shower head did not have water pressure sufficient for the rinsing of soap.
Also, and it seemed to be just our room, so it may not be indicative of the hotel as a whole, but the room smelled very musty.
Again, not terrible, the hotel was clean and the service was fine. Did I feel like I was on vacation or living in luxury...no. Was it usable...yes. Would I stay there again...probably not with all of the other options nearby.

Got a room on July 4th via priceline...we were upgraded to a junior suite since no double bed rooms were available. Staff was very accomadating and pleasant. Gabriel was very helpful with directions for a walk to the esplanade to watch the fireworks. The room overlooked fanuiel hall and was very clean and spacious. Enjoyed our stay....

I stayed here recently and was impressed by the lobby/common areas. Very modern. The room was your typical Hilton room with a comfy bed and modern bathroom, nice amenities, etc. The only two things I would point out are 1-the bathroom ceiling needs to be wiped down. When it gets damp from showering there are spots, hair, etc. 2-the housekeeping staff needs to take an attachment and vacuum the edges of the floor by the bed. You could see they stopped where the vacuum hit the ridge on the bed and there is still about three inches left--you can see the dust, etc. These are minor details but important. The breakfast was standard--I thought they'd have more pastries, etc but they didn't. I would stay here again. All in all it's a decent Hilton property. The ppl were are super nice!!

We live in the Washington area, but stayed at the Palomar one night after the Derecho of 2012 left us without power. We chose the hotel based on its location in Dupont circle for easy access to restaurants, shopping and parking. The lobby was very crowded with other storm refuges (many with dogs, which are welcome here), and pretty chaotic and noisy, but if the front desk staff were harried or over worked, they did not show it at all.
Our room (7th floor overlooking P street) was spacious and well appointed. The Aveda bath products and quirky animal print bathrobes are a nice touch. There was little or no noise from the street, but we could hear everything that went on in the hallway (including shrieking teenagers at 1 am... Given the unusual circumstance of the storm and power outages, I can't say if this is a common problem or not.)
The pool is a nice size with comfortable surrounds (it even has outdoor canopy beds, making one feel like one is an extra on an HGTV set.) The lobby bar "Urbana" is well stocked and comfortable. We were glad to have the chance to vacation in our hometown at the Palomar, and would recommend it for business or leisure.

Thank you Windham for the back-ache and foot injury due to a bathroom sink that was extremely low, a very saggy uncomfortable bed, and a tub wall that was incredibly high, but that was actually a good thing to help hold in the water from the tub that didn't drain. The shower curtain was dirty, and by the way, what decent hotel these days doesn't have a curved shower rod? The closet door didn't close, and the room smelled of BO. The hallway was dark and a little scary. Thank you but I'll gladly pay $50 more to stay at Hilton, Hyatt or Marriott in the future. Wyndham never ever again!

This gorgeous hotel is an absolute gem - staffed by great guys who made me feel like I was a VIP guest. The location is perfect - just metres from a subway station and so close to all that this end of town has to offer. The room was large with a great bathroom and whisper quiet which I didn't think was possible in NYC and together with a comfy bed I slept very well! Breakfast is delicious and healthy too with lots of fresh fruit - such a treat. All the guys are very helpful, and nothing is too much trouble as they take a genuine interest in helping you find the attractions that suit. This hotel is fantastic value and well worth every cent - I have already recommended to friends who are traveling later this year. Thanks again for everything - it was a perfect start to my NYC trip.

title_masked: Unbeatable location directly across from Central Park South
text_masked: This hotel is exceptionally well located, right across the street from the south end of Central Park. Although this Grand Dame is showing some wear and tear, our room was comfortable, clean and provided everything we required for our week long stay. All amenities are close at hand including a subway stop steps from the front door. Hotel staff were friendly, efficient and accommodating.

I got a room at this hotel to get some sleep after a night out on the town. A little hard to do when the heater kicks on, and rattles so loudly I had to get up to adjust the fan cover with my fist. This occurred a number of times throughout the night. I woke up feeling like the walking dead! I bullet to the head would've been welcoming at the point. It makes me wonder if they don't take care of this kind of stuff, what other corners are they cutting?

Stay at the Loews in Hollywood OCT 6 to the 8th After coming of a cruise, The location is perfect right in the heart of Hollywood great for restaurants and shopping.The service we recieved was excellent any thing you asked for was no problem from where to go or if you needed any thing. The rooms are very clean and large with very clean bathrooms.The Hotel is getting a face lift as this was originally the rennassance The hotel restaurant was good but a little pricey.Lots of choices in the area try Mels Diner for lunch or breakfast good food and not to bad for price The pool was a pleasant surprise as it was heated great for swimming when the weather gets a little cooler.When booking get a room on a higher level with view of the Hollywood sign .Only snag to our stay was the four oclock check in, we arrived at 10: 00 and had to wait to 3:00 for our room.If I Stay in Hollywood again I would defiantly stay at the Loews Hollywood

I recently stayed at the Intercontinental Barclay for a business trip. I was only in town for a short time, but this hotel was excellent. The room was comfortable, the bathroom was a bit tiny, but nothing horrible. The location made it simple to get around the city. The reception desk was pleasant and able to answer all my questions about where to go.
I would definitely stay at this location the next time I am in NYC

We stayed at this great hotel over St. Patricks Day weekend and was thoroughly impressed with what it had to offer. The location is prime as it is within steps to Times Square and is very accessible to other areas of the city, easy to get a cab outside. The room itself made me feel at home and was one of the cleanest I have ever stayed in, especially in NYC. The king size bed made it difficult to get up and go in the morning, very comfortable! There's a single serve Keurig machine in each room with a few flavors to choose from. The bathroom was gorgeous and offers a large shower enclosed with glass. 
Before our stay we were notified by the manager, Colin, that we might hear a lot of noise as there is a bar directly below the room we booked. Being St. Patrick's Day we figured it would be an issue but we barely even heard any noise. It wasn't an issue at all but appreciate management notifying us beforehand and giving us another option if we decided it was too loud. We're not sensitive to noise, so people who are might think of booking a room on higher floors just in case. 
Overall, the great stay contributed to a wonderful weekend in NYC and will recommend to other friends staying in NYC in the future!

Stayed at this hotel for a week long training program. This hotel is a must stay. Very quiet street and very knowledgeable staff. Hotel is on very quiet end of town across from water garden. Bath robes were a $85 "c'mon Man" moment for me. Otherwise this place is great!!!

title_masked: Kitchen in room if you want to cook
text_masked: Selected for the location, this is a basic place to stay with a kitchen if you want to cook. The bed was comfy and they had good pillows. They have a small breakfast room with a selection of danish & breads, cereal, yogurt, boiled eggs, & fruit. It was helpful to have my coffee travel mug for the coffee in the lobby in thermal carafe's whenever you want it. There is a Starbucks Coffee drive thru and two other hotels nearby. The location is about a half mile to the freeway.

I was in town for meetings for two days and when I took a look at Trip Advisor, I saw that the Palomar was rated the number 1 hotel in Philly. I decided to give it a try and am very glad that I did. It was right in the neighborhood of the meeting venues, so I could easily walk to all of my meetings.
Almost all of the staff that I interacted went out of their way to be friendly and helpful, the room was bright and well laid out, with lots of extra nice touches - like their fun, animal print robes. The bed was very comfortable, and after my last few trips where half of the bed was sagging, this was incredibly welcome!
The Palomar is a green hotel and they actually seem to mean what they say. At this hotel they actually honor the "linens hanging on the towel bar will not be exchanged" policy that many hotels say they have adopted, but the housekeeping staff routinely ignores. The shower was still very good, even though it featured a low-flow fixture.
All in all, it was an exceptional hotel for the price and I would definitely stay there again the next time I had to go to Philly.

No surprise at all. Marriott standards are fully respected.
Very attentive staff and suites at the corner are spacious for a reasonable price.
This hotel remains among my favorites in Charlotte.

We stayed at the Marriott on a trip to Houston for which we did not expect to have a car. We ended up having one and it can be a little tricky to find if you do not just take Monroe to the freeway and head south. They were friendly and helpful. The Internet was free in spite of receiving notice upon sign in that there would be a charge. You should probably check as we were told it was a promotion. It is fairly standard Marriott and the beds were comfortable. On the eighth floor we had no trouble with freeway noise.

My husband and I stayed here on our way back home to Texas from Aspen. For some reason that night was $250 and up at the hotels we normally think of but we got a great rate at the Grand Hyatt. The staff are great from the second you pull up. The location is super close to everything at 16 street. The restaurants/bars were also great and there is a Starbucks connected to the hotel. We had appetizers at the hotel restaurant and they were very good. The only negative was that you do hear some city noise (sirens) but no big deal. We would def return.

We arrived via the Amtrak and walked to the hotel. We were early for check in and our suite was not available. The front desk staff offered to check our luggage, gave us a key to the pool, and made suggestions of places to grab a quick meal. We have been to other hotels and arrived before our room was ready and the staff never even offered to let us leave our luggage. I was super impressed they offered---we did not have to ask. Our room included complimentry valet parking, but since we arrived via train we did not need the parking. The staff offered us drinks at the bar or market instead. Loved that they replaced the parking with something else! During our stay the front desk was able to answer all our questions.
The location of the hotel is great. We were within walking distance of everything we wanted to do. I felt like we were right in the center of it all. If you needed a taxi there were always a few parked by the hotel. When we return to Fort Worth we will stay here again.

title_masked: If the price is right, stay.
text_masked:
I recently stayed here for one night for a wedding just north of Charlotte. Since I needed two rooms, I looked at the Starpicks website and decided to give this property a try.
The hotel is located right next to a light rail stop, which is a plus if you are looking for a hotel outside of Uptown to save money. It is easy to stop off the main road, however it's parking area is tucked away. My female travel companion was nervous walking upon our late night return, and it didn't settle her that there was a police vehicle out front around 1am. Not to speculate this hotel has problems, this could be what the Charlotte police does as courtesy for businesses in the area. The hotel could benefit from me exterior lighting, especially if you have to park behind the hotel and walk to the front / side building entrance.
We enjoyed talking with Alex and Jeff at the front desk, they were entertaining and made us feel welcome from the start. The lobby area felt very small to me, both in overall size and height in the ceiling. I guess this feeling comes from comparing other Four Point previous stays and overall Starwood hotels, but didn't care too much for it.
Our rooms were 505 and 506. Her TV in her room worked fine, mine every channel was blurry or static. Maybe I did not work the control panel properly, but even with the air on (or so I thought I had it set), the air would go on and off throughout the night. This resulted in me waking up multiple times to either throw the blankets off of me when the air was off or reaching for them when the air was on. Good blankets that obviously trap heat well if you sleep cold, not so much if you sleep hot. The room itself was alright, not much too it and not to aesthetically pleasing as compared to other Four Points. The bathroom was too small in my opinion, but the water in the shower was hot so that is a plus.
I don't mean to say this is a bad hotel, however there is nothing here that really hooked me to change from my usual Hyatt Place stays when I need one room in Charlotte. If you are passing through Charlotte and need a comfortable one night stay, I would say look here especially if you are a SPG member. Get the stay and a few points, and continue on with your travels.

title_masked: Excellent Service in a Beautiful setting
text_masked:
My husband and I spent 3 nights at The Jefferson over thanksgiving and were really impressed with this lovely small hotel.
The location is perfect, easy walking distance to everything (monuments, great restos, fab gym) and super close to the metro. 
Rooms are very nice, ours had a nice view of 16th street and was very well laid out with a great bed and small details like individual reading lights that i do expect in a hotel of this price but often are overlooked. The bathrooms (at least ours!) was truly incredible, double sinks, big rain shower and a huge tub. 
We also both got massages at the spa- my masseuse Darlene was hands down the best massage i have ever had. She really listened to what i wanted. I felt like a new person- highly recommend booking a massage with her. My husband loved his masseuse also, but i dont remember his therapists name.
Drinks and dining was excellent, we had a few lazy room service days and were always very impressed with the quality of the food, especially the freshness of the salads (i am vegan so super picky!) 
Finally, what really makes this hotel special is THE STAFF, every single person that works at this hotel delivers attentive, genuine, friendly service that is a breath of fresh air. From the Doormen with their efficient and attentive service, to Lyn the Concierge who was so helpful and made excellent recommendations to In Room Dining Staff to Housekeeping to the Front Desk, literally every member of staff left us feeling so well taken care of. 
This will be our hotel of choice for any future DC visits, highly recommend it!

title_masked: typical Homewood Suites - nice and comfy, but don't expect luxurious
text_masked:
My family and I spent Thanksgiving weekend at this hotel, and the stay was quite pleasant. It was very convenient to our extended family gatherings up in Lewis Center, and as two of us had tickets to attend the Ohio State-Michigan football game (GO BUCKEYES!), we were thrilled to find COTA shuttle bus service, within walking distance of the hotel, to and from Ohio Stadium. The housekeeping staff seems to be a little "skimpy" with replacement towels, and we had to remind them three times, over a four day stay, that there were four people in our party, not three.
