However, extra towels and toiletries were cheerfully and expeditiously brought up to our room.
The lobby and breakfast room are located in the "lodge" (main building), which necessitates a short outside walk from the guest rooms. Parking spaces were at a premium until Sunday night, when the post-game crowd thinned out considerably.
The staff is friendly and helpful, and the breakfast was tasty and well-stocked. As we were not there during the workweek, there was no evening Manager's Reception with dinner.
The hotel is in the Crosswoods section of Worthington, with several other hotels, restaurants and mostly empty office complexes (it was a holiday weekend, after all). The roads can be somewhat confusing in this immediate area, and there seemed to be many unfamiliar and inattentive motorists driving around.
The king suite is nice and roomy, but our two "big" sons found the shared sleeper couch to be a bit cramped. We had requested a rollaway bed, but the hotel does not offer them, due to fire department restrictions. We were made aware of this unavailability in advance of our stay, so it was not a surprise to us, and we appreciated the advance notice.
Overall, we had a nice stay at this property, and paid a very fair room rate.

Had a two-night stay here for an airport meeting. The sponsoring company got me a special corporate rate; I saw on the Hilton website the available general rates were quite high. As a Hilton Diamond I was placed on the 10th "Preferred" floor. A moderately sized room, nothing special, but absolutely quiet and nice blackout curtains. Nice view of the runway. No Executive Lounge.
The "extras" here are pricey, probably not surprising as this is the only hotel at O'Hare. Mini-bar candy bars at 4-5 bucks, Minibar and downstairs bar drinks 12-20 bucks, and so on. On the other hand, my $20 double Manhattan was quite well made. The "Gaslight Club" and restaurant are quite quirky, dark and evoking a Playboy Club feeling, definitely Chicago-ish for me. The buffet breakfast ($23) had decent standard choices and good fast service, though it's a long way from options at European or Asian Hiltons (I miss the smoked salmon).
The location is awesome, right in the middle of the airport, a 3-minute stroll to Terminal 3, for example. For gambling addicts like me, a $12 cab ride or (if you lose) a $3 El ride can get you to the Rivers Casino in nearby Rosemont, where there are also many restaurants.
On a business account, no question this place is worth it. There's no better place for an ORD overnight layover, as well. I were spending my own money I'd make sure I have a manageable rate and watch the prices carefully before eating/drinking at the property.

title_masked: 5 star hotel and 3 star price! Great value and service!
text_masked:
My girlfriend and I stayed at the Pan Pacific for one night after our Alaskan cruise. After having a not-so-good stay on the night before our cruise at the Best Western Airport Executel, we were extremely pleased once we got to the Pan Pacific. Upon arrival, we were greeted at the door and then received outstanding service at the front desk when we checked-in. The staff was eager to help, provide recommendations, and offer any assistance. They really made us feel like they were happy to have us stay there. They even upgraded us to a King room with a view of the Space Needle for no extra charge. Great start.
When we arrived at our room, we were floored by how clean, modern, and stunning it was. The bathroom was amazing with granite countertops, a garden tub, and a really nice tile shower. I also really liked that the bathroom had a little opening which could be closed or left open. It gave the room much more openness and a more modern feel. 
The room also had all the amenities (hair dryer, robes, iron, coffee machine, etc.) as well as a lot of modern upgrades like ethernet connections, flat screen TV, and ergonomic desk chair. The bed was very comfortable and the sheets were amazingly soft. The bath towels were also quality. Also, instead of a loud, nasty ice machine, each floor had it's own ice buckets with individually wrapped ice bags. Great idea. No complaints at all about the room.
The location of the Pan Pacific is arguably not downtown. You will probably need to take a cab if you want to get to Pike Place Market or the piers. You could walk but I'd say it would take around 20-30 minutes (about 1.5-2 miles). The Space Needle and Seattle City Center is very close however and only a 10-15 minute walk. For us, not being down by the piers or market wasn't a big deal and not an issue. There was still plenty to do around the hotel and within walking distance.
It was also very convenient to be located on one of the nicest Whole Foods I've ever seen. After spending a week on a cruise eating cruise food, it was nice to have access to real food. Plus this Whole Foods had a Noodle Soup bar. it was so nice that my GF and I had dinner and brunch there the next day. Whole Foods FTW!!!!!
Overall, we were extremely satisfied with Pan Pacific and would/will recommend it to friends and family. For the money, it was the nicest hotel I've ever stayed at. My only regret is that we couldn't stay longer.
The only suggestion I would make is to have the free courtesy car run a bit more frequently on weekends. I think it only ran for a couple hours (10am-12pm) on Sunday morning.

I have stayed at the Raffaello many times, and it was always one of my favorites. My recent stay was a let down. The place is understaffed. It can take a long time to get the front desk to answer. Little touches that made it a great place to stay are now gone. A good example:they no longer provide bathrobes. My sister's room had a very old 'hasn't been remodeled in 30 years' feel. My guess is that the upper floors (where I've stayed in the past) were redone, and they ran out of money before they could redo everything. The staff is very nice and the location is great, but the place has lost its sheen.

I have just returned from a week long stay at the hotel. I was there on business so I was concerned over reports that the WIFI was poor. I called the hotel before I left home and they assured me they had just completed a full replacement of the service with a new provider costing them around $65k.
I have to say that any problems they had before are definately fixed. I was able to get full service in the room or the bar or anywhere else in the hotel and it was fast and stable. I even picked up the network from the 31st floor of the John Hancock tower down the road (although I couldnt connect from there). The food in the hotel is excellent. The main restaurant was always almost empty yet the food and service was as good as in any of the high end restaurants. The waiter in the main restaurant was probably one of the best I have ever come across. They had a special when I was there of oven baked sirloin steak which was to die for. The room was large and had two beds. I really liked the in room fridge which was always stocked with bottled water. The shower was also excellent. Easy to operate and had a constant temperature. One nice feature was that the shower curtain was on a rail which curved out away from the line of the bath. This gave you a lot more room in the shower. Another nice feature was that the bathroom had a gente light on a motion sensor that came on at night when you went in there. There were also robes in the room and the closet was big with plenty of hangers. There was a decent iron and board. So often the irons in hotel rooms are cheap and light. The only thing I found to be a bit flaky was the morning room service. I ordered room service every day for breakfast. On 6 of the 7 mornings I ordered eggs benedict at around 6.30am. On two occaisions I could not get an answer from room service at all. Also, on two occaisions the breakfast arrived with no tomatoes. One morning the hot water for the tea was far from hot. Having said all of that the breakfast when done well was fantatstic. When done badly it was still very good. I would have no hesitation on staying here again.

Wow! What a stay! My husband and I stayed here to be able to celebrate my birthday in town without driving. It was a few blocks further from the market area that I wanted, but well worth the extra steps. EVERYONE at 1000 was awesome, from valet to concierge to front desk where we had a glass of bubbles at check-in. They knew it was my birthday and the valet even brought me a red rose :)
The room was gorgeous and comfy. Like everyone else, we loved the bathtub (it's perfect for 2) and I could have stayed in it all night just drinking champagne and listening to the Mood channel.
I look forward for another reason to spend a special night at the Hotel.
Thank you!!!

Just returned from another stay at the Edison Hotel the location can not be beat
 the lobby is spacious and comfortable glad to see the rum room has reopened
 we had two rooms on the 10th floor one renovated one not 
 the newly renovated room was modern and well decorated
 the older room was worn and tired looking but very clean kudos to the housekeeping
 staff (don't recall the housekeepers name i believe she is russian and serviced rm.1042
 dec.8th-dec. 12 thanks)

Excellent location for visiting Gracelands which was our main tour for the day. Staff were friendly and efficient and check in was smooth. Our room was no 111 which was a ground floor room next to the stairwell, there was a bit off noise with people coming and going but nothing to major.
The room itself was basic but comfortable, we found the bed comfortable and not to hard like some previous reviews stated, I think it comes down to preferance.
The bathroom towels were very thin and we had no toilet tissue, a quick visit to reception and it was sorted.
We went to breakfast at around 8.30am and a bit disappointed with the choice, there was bread, cereal, bananas and a waffle maker, there were no muffins etc left, the juice was very watered down though the coffee was fine, the lady on duty seemed very efficient.
We were able to leave our car in the carpark after we checked out whilst we visited Gracelands which was very kind and it saved us the 10 dollars car park fee, being Scottish that is always a bonus!
All said, this hotel is a must for Elvis fans and we would recommend it for this reason alone, the reason I have gave it an average rating is based on the other hotels we have stayed at whilst touring the deep south.

What a great place! My BFF and I stayed for 3 days and 2 nights (will stay longer next time!). The all inclusive package is the way to go as it includes 3 meals and snacks, you just pay for alcohol. I loved the "no tipping" aspect as it was included in our all inclusive package and don't worry, you're not treated by the staff as "I don't have to be pleasant because their not tipping me anyway" attitude. Everyone treats you as a valued guest and are very personable and accommodating. Activities were fun and broadened my outlook (meditation, aqua yoga, bull riding (for the abs!). Definitely sign up for the Watsu massage - unique experience and very relaxing! The infinity pool is georgeous.I'm glad to see a guy review Travassa, because most of the couples I observed looked like the girl was having a great time and the guy looked like he would rather be doing anything other than lounging at Travassa. I would love to keep this place a secret, but its too good to keep it to myself!
The location at 48th and Lexington can't be beat and is convenient to the theater, museums and Grand Central. The bed was comfortable and the room was quite spacious, especially by NYC standards.

title_masked: Acceptable but dreary hotel in great location
text_masked: We stayed here for four nights recently. The pros are that the location is fantastic, right in the heart of Boston near tons of restaurants and public transportation with the Colonnade two blocks up with a discount for their fabulous food, the customer service is really strong, the shuttle is less than a taxi, and it's cheaper than any other area hotel. However, the cons are that it still cost us about $185 a night for what would normally be considered motel-quality. This hotel had so much potential with a bit of renovation that it was depressing to see how poorly appointed, dimly lit, and how few amenities it had. Our door actually hit the light when you opened it. It did have a coffee maker, daily housekeeping, a pizza vending machine in the hall, and an extremely comfortable bed. Our room had a view of an alleyway and was very dark. It was a little grimy feeling, with old paint and a weird room layout. The hallways are mismarked and labyrinthine, but I thought this was funny more than anything. Also, the elevators are ancient, tiny, and there's just nothing to do in this hotel. It's more like a $60-$80 motel you stay while on a road trip. Would I stay there again? Yes, because there's nothing else in area at this price and it wasn't a "bad" hotel per se. It just wasn't a place you would go to stay in the hotel itself other than to sleep. If anyone ever decided to put some money into this place and renovate it, I can easily see it turning into a real beauty.

We arrived early in the day and the The Pearl allowed us to check in which was great to get to our room and freshen up for the rest of the day. The front desk was efficient and professional but not as freindly as I would like. It is great that they have lemon water in the lobby and snacks which was nice as I was traveling with a young teenager and they are always hungry. I thought the breakfast area was great and had a good assortment of food and beverages and of course The New York Times and there was no probelm getting a table and it was a holiday weekend in October. The location of our room did not have a good view of anything except for another building but it was very quiet which was great not to hear all the street noise. The location had easy access to many places (Times Square a ten minute walk at most) and public transportation and anything you might have needed was just a couple of blocks away. We saw Wicked and it was less than a five minutes walk to get there from the Hotel.. Although the room was a little expensive for the size of the room it was money well spent for the quiet. I would not want to be in the middle of Times Square with all the noise and craziness going on all night. The Pearl was very clean and the beds very comfortable. I would stay there again in a hearbeat.

I am a HHonors Diamond memeber and stay at Hilton propeties exlusively for business and pleasure. I am currently staying at this hotel, which in of itself is not bad. The bed was nice and the bathroom was clean (my biggest concerns); however, my check-in experience was unacceptable for any guest and espically for diamond level guest. The guy working the counter was not friendly, was not professional, did not offer a room upgrade as a diamond guest(which was fine, since the hotel looked full). He told me I would have drinks and snacks in my room, but they were not there. I called the front desk to ask and he simply just said I could come down and get it if I wanted drinks. This made me mad, as I had just gotton up to my room and had been working and travelling all day. It is hard to get to Diamond level status and I feel you should be made to feel like a special guest when staying, and that did not happen. If you are looking for a decent hotel in a more central location, not a bad choice, just do not expect quality customer serivce, because you will be disappointed.

Good central location. Easy to find and only 3 blocks walk from the nearby barts station (direct line from the airport 35 min transfer $8 ppn). Huge room. Very quiet. Street views might be noisy. Car park on site. Round thd corn er from hertz. Try loris diner for breakfast 2 options close by. The daily grill (on site) serves great food and has a busy bar.

title_masked: Stay at the Mansion and feel like royalty!
text_masked: We live 40 miles outside of downtown Dallas and have attended parties and gone to dinner at the Mansion over the past 30 years. We have always enjoyed it and its' service. This weekend, my husband surprised me for our 45th wedding anniversary and we spent the night, had dinner and brunch. The staff was wonderful and made us feel like old friends. Our dinner, served in the library was fantastic and our brunch the following morning was delicious. The room was spotless and so comfortable; I really didn't want to leave.

We stayed at the Astor for 6 nights at the beginning of April 2012. We expected the rooms to be small since it is New York so that wasn't a problem. We got room 207, a room facing the park which sounded great. However, the windows were filthy and one of them had toilet paper dangling from it. This was never addressed during our stay. Facing the park you must also beware that you directly above the subway track which adds to the noise that you get from the street. The room was clean but the towels had small rips in them, the bathroom ceiling had water stains and the pipes were leaking water into our bathroom from the room above! All that said, this is one of the cheapest deals if you want to stay in Manhattan, around 900 for six nights.

title_masked: no real complaints but no wow factor
text_masked: Most of the basics are there, comfortable bed/bedding, good plumbing, acceptable service attitude, and rooms that have aged relatively well. The confirmed Gold Passport Diamond upgrade landed us a Park Executive Suite or at least that was what the front desk agent called it. The 1-BR suite was spacious and contained 1.5 baths, a long sofa, and a square living room table in lieu of a more traditional work desk (no work surface in the bedroom). We took advantage of the loaner bicycles at the concierge. For the cost conscious, the valet parking is $48 per night. Perhaps a way to describe the property location would be ‘near the center of everything, but close to nothing’, except for the independent cinemas on the back side of the hotel, but not a big deal if you are planning to drive everywhere as we were. While I would rate this property ahead of The Williard, in comparison to Park Hyatts in Asia, this location falls way short.

We stayed at the Embassy the night before our trip to Aruba. The cost of parking our car for the 10 days of our trip and the one night stay cost about $50 more than parking at Logan's long term parking and this was soooo worth it. The room was nice and the shuttle to the airport was so convenient. We did have a hard time contacting the hotel upon our arrival back to Logan, the phone just rang off the hook. After about 15 minutes of continuously trying, finally someone answered and took our car ticket number. The bus came about 10 minutes after so a good 25 minute wait but when we got to the Embassy our car was parked out front, just had to load luggage and we were on our way! Nice and relaxing way to start and end our trip. No hassles or worries about getting to airport on time or parking in the economy lot.
We ate at a great restaurant called the ECCO just a couple of blocks down from the Embassy, it is on the top of the list that the concierge gives you and it was fabulous. The bartender was fun, the manager was very accommodating and the food and drinks were excellent. Beautifully decorated and a nice terrace for outdoor dining too. They have off street parking which is great for Boston. We walked from hotel about 4 minutes. There is a pizza place everyone raves about across the street, we took one to go really good, both places are owned by the same people.

We recently stayed with our 2 young children and were pleasantly surprised. This hotel is perfect for a family. There is a Harris Teeter on the corner and a CVS across the street. We saved money using the grocery and the comfort of knowing the CVS was there if we needed it. The front desk staff was exceptional. Whitney checked us in early with a great smile and we got a late check out. They are conveniently located to a red line Metro stop. The first night was noisy but our kids were exhausted and slept threw it. We called the front desk and they stopped it immediately. I felt like we could have been moved the next day if that room hadn't checked out. Our kids loved the indoor pool. Our room was very clean and the beds were comfortable. Free wi-fi was an extra bonus. We will definitely be staying here again!

title_masked: There`s a reason its so cheap
text_masked: Stayed here for one night on the 16/04/12.Had to ask to move room twice,first room smoke alarm would not stop beeping,second toilet was leaking all over the floor.Plugs are hanging out the walls with wires showing,hotel is dirty and old.Cheap for new york city (£70 per night) but i would recomend staying somewhere else if you can afford it.Only good point it is in a great location (Times Square).

title_masked: Whoa.... how do you review this Inn?
text_masked:
After a business trip in the valley I wanted to stay downtown for my last night before flying back. I booked on the basis of the reviews and the photos. I would not have stayed here had I just pulled up without a booking, my wife (who wasn't with me), would have said, let's just go somewhere else. You might get the feeling it's not the most appealing place seen from the road, and you'd be right.
But I did stay so let's look for the positives. It is in a good location, lots of restaurants in the vicinity, along with strip joints and topless dives, and it's cheap, $150. Parking is a very good positive. Chinatown looks to be fun.
The rooms are very old, and whilst it maybe clean, you wouldn't want to walk on the carpets with bare feet. Some of the reviews are very positive, so I guess it's just a matter of taste and budget, personally I'd have preferred to spend another $100 and go somewhere nicer.
And yes the people on the front desk were very pleasant

Presidio Travelodge in San Francisco, was a very pleasant surprise, This hotel was clean, comfortable, recently renovated and better than any travelodge I ever stayed, it was a great price for San Francisco, anything less you wouldn't want to stay. Now part of the Wyndham Group, I believe it's helped a little with this hotel. The manger, Bruce was very helpful and accommodating. He and Nikki took very good care of us and our other party who stayed 3 of the 4 nights in a second room. The 1st rm ( 2 QB ) was nice, comfortable beds but w/small bathroom. It was up stairs, and I needed a 1st floor, I'm Handicap ( walk w/cain ) and no lift. He moved us to the 1st floor to a small 1 kg bd, the bathroom even smaller, its a room not used normally but he had no vacancy on the 1st floor. Also it had free open parking, ( only 1 handicap space ). the continental breakfast was very simple, assortment of muffins. cereal, oatmeal, of course coffee, tea, juice and milk. It's location is fantastic right at the Presidio's Lombard gate, a lot to see in the Presidio, including the bridge, easy drive to gold gate park and most everything else you want to see and do. All-n-all I'd like it and will stay again next time we are in San Francisco. It's the staff that has me coming back.

If you want a cool, modern and high-energy hotel near PHL, this is a good choice. I stayed at this hotel for a night on a Thursday. The lobby bar was jamming with music and guests partying when I checked in at 10 pm. Check-in was fast and easy. I like their modern room design - simple and smart. My room was clean and well-kept.
Hotel offers complimentary airport shuttle service every 20 mins. Their shuttle buses do fill up as they pick up guests from 4 Points & Sheraton too. Fortunately, Aloft is their 1st pickup stop.
Hotel also offers complimentary WiFi (good connection), but not breakfast. However, they have a snack store in the lobby with some healthy food choices.
I would consider staying at this hotel again for the fun and energy. But I would not choose this hotel when I am travelling with family (kids). It feels like a 'club' hotel, and partying guests are LOUD. During my stay, the hotel lobby and courtyard was filled with loud chatty guests. At 5am, I could hear a guest shouting in the hallway giving breakfast orders to his spouse. The hotel bed was comfortable, but I didn't sleep well because of the noisy guests.
It could be a good hotel choice if you are in the partying mood!

title_masked: Had to stay that little room!
text_masked:
When I was planning our NYC trip I expected that the hotel rooms would be an American size as they were extremely expensive! However, when we saw the room with two double beds as were 3 adults and a baby, we couldn't set up the cot bed and also luggages were on the way to the toilet! Also we requested mini fridge for the baby food, so there were not any space in the room. We couldn't find any available rooms for that weekend in the city so had to stay there.
When we stayed there in June 2012, rooms and breakfast area were clean. Breakfast was not very good but at least it was free! Staff were quite talkative and friendly. Easy to walk everywhere. Liked the street as there were flowers every day!

Arrived early on Thursday 6/7/12 for a mother/daughter get-a-way 3 night stay. Flew in early & called ahead on way from airport to see if we could get early check-in as it was 11:30am. Melissa confirmed on the phone our room would be ready as well as the arrangements for an ajoining room for our family a few nights later. All was as promised upon arrival & check-in was friendly and a breeze. We were in our room in minutes. Melissa at the front desk was wonderful, friendly & helpful. 
The room was immaculate! The beds were wonderful and the bathroom spotless. (I have to say I was hesitant and at last minute looking into more upscale hotels (Ritz, Fairmont, JW Marriot) but b/c we got a great rate and this was a great spot to catch the trolley to Chinatown, Union Square and walk to North Beach, Ghiradelli Sqare, The Marina, Fisherman's Wharf, Pier 39, & a Starbucks, this location can't be beat! The comfy room, cleanliness, quietness and service surpassed all my expectations.
We had an interior room and it was very quiet. (Being a hotel there will be noise from guests walking down the hall at night or you can hear the shower from another room, but hey, you're not at home & overall throughout the night, it was very quiet.)
The Concierge was awesome too with helpful suggestions and directions. Another great surprise was the concerige recommendation to go to "Royal Thai Massge" just steps out main door to the left. Would have passed this thinking it was a little corner sketchy spa place, but found out it is Zagat rated & has received Best of San Francisco for neighborhood spa. After a long day of walking, go for foot reflexology or massage. You won't be dissapointed. They are so accomodating and stayed open late one night just for me.
We requested a late check out as we were flying out late in the evening and the manager was so accomodating too. I would absoluely return again to this Marriot. They are doing W.I.T.! Their Motto: What It Takes!

title_masked: lovely staff, but a few hicups!
text_masked: Our first stop in the US. The staff were lovely we did have trouble with our room key 2 nights in a row, on the last night our door had to be 'jimmied opened' which took close to an hour in total for maintenance etc. We had to ask for an upgrade for the inconvience, which they told us wasn't available and got moved to a 'crap' room with no view, we complained and got moved but only after we asked. Staff were lovely the whole time - I was frustrated and it was clear but they were still gracious. Breakfast nothing to rave about just average. We did feel that the hotel wasn't close to shops to stroll around after day out. Good to visit parks or do tours and come back for a rest.

I was lucky to get a room at the back so it was very quiet. Room was fine, king bed, very confortable, lots of comfy pillows. There was a nice big TV, microwave, refirgerator, coffee maker which is always nice for a 2 week stay. The noise from the planes was not so bad since the flight patterns changed constantly - they did not keep me awake. Breakfast was nothing special but the lady who ran the breakfast area (Marilyn) definitely took care of the customers - she is the type of person every hotel needs to be successful. The barkeeper Mike was awesome and very efficient, he made the best Bloody Mary's from scratch and always had a pleasant word for every customer. The hotel runs a free shuttle service to and from the airport as well as to stores within a few mile radius. The drivers were great and took us to Walmart, Ross, North Star Mall, The Quarry Market etc.- this service in itself is a great reason to stay here. Sure some parts of the hotel are faded but overall I thought it was perfectly adequate.

This is a good hotel if you're looking for quick access to the airport or passing through Indianapolis on I-70. The staff upon check in were friendly, efficient, and helpful. The lobby has been re-done in new Courtyard modern style. It is a nice place for a snack and drink. Computer kiosks and free wireless are welcomed. The rooms are adequate, nothing special but good if you're just looking for a night's sleep. The pool and hot tub are also pretty standard for a Courtyard (have I seen it in Denver or maybe Rochester); they were appreciated after a long day. 
You could do worse.

I was in Seattle recently for an opera. Based on a previous trip I knew there was a Hampton Inn nearby. YES!!! On north 5th St., just north of Mercer, is a Hampton Inn. Price is right and breakfast is included. It was convenient and comfortable. I may well go back (for more operas, of course) and plan to stay there again.
My ONLY comment is that the bathroom was meant for a giant--sink too high for me as was the hook on the back of the bathroom door. (NOT a complaint, as I dealt with it.)

title_masked: The hotel was clean, staff extemely pleasant and our room was spacious!!!
text_masked: We had a wonderful time, the hotel was fantastic!!

Besides the fact that the street to get to this hotel is a steep hill (as they all seem to be in San Francisco), The Orchard Hotel is in a great location. 
I arrived early and my room was ready so I was able to check in early. That was a great start to this trip. (I stayed for 5 days end of Aug - to Labour Day.)
My room was large and the bed was SO COMFORTABLE. 
The hotel was in a great location. 
-3 blocks away from Union Square which is a main shopping area 
-5 blocks away from BART (the subway system)
-1 block away from a Walgreen's
-right on 2 of the 3 cable car lines which both get to Fisherman's Wharf
-2 blocks away from China Town 
-1 block away from a bus stop of the 2 buses (#30 and #41) which sort of take you across the city pretty much
-5 blocks away from Market Street on which the F-line train runs which takes you either to Fisherman's Wharf or to Castro
David, one of the concierges at the hotel, is awesome. He was incredibly helpful in organising the daytrips I was interested in (Half Muir Woods/Half Wine Country, as well as a trip to Winchester House in San Jose) and answered all of my questions. He also asked how they went upon my return to the hotel. I liked the fact that he made the effort to follow-up about my excursions. As a guest, it was a nice personal touch. 
I quite enjoyed my stay here and would recommend it to others.
(Also, I feel like by the end of my 5 day stay, that hill to the hotel didn't seem as difficult to climb. Either that, or I just got used to constantly going up hills all over the city, what's one more? Besides, it was great to have such a comfy bed.)

I stayed at the Catamaran in mid-June for a conference that was held onsite. The staff were very helpful and friendly. My room (in the high-rise section) was right outside the elevator but I was pleasantly surprised that noise was not a problem. It was clean, spacious, and very comfortable - and it even had an attached kitchen that I didn't use but would have been nice had my family been with me. We were fortunate to get to have all of our lunches outside and an evening meal/party - no bugs, great atmosphere, food was still wonderful (even though served outside) as were accommodations - and they pulled it off without any problems. Had an evening cruise on their boat - what a beautiful boat - highly recommend it if you can. Our conference used 6 of their rooms on the second floor, and the 'lobby' area around the rooms - all worked great. The tech equipment worked well too, and they had staff right there making adjustments as/when needed. But the best part for me was the location - being right on Mission Bay, and only 2 blocks from the ocean - it was so wonderful! Sitting out in the chairs on the beach was relaxing, taking a bike ride around the bay was interesting and fun - great way to see more of the area, very good restaurants within 1-3 blocks of the hotel. Didn't use the spa, the on-site restaurant, or the fitness facilities. I hope to go back and play some beach volleyball, rent some of their watersport equipment, and just relax more on both the Mission Bay beach and the ocean beach. Finally, I did read the brief history of the resort on their website, and was glad I did - I make a point to look for items they mentioned, and they really give the place the look and feel of a tropical resort.
Fabulous hotel. Great free breakfast. Very helpful and pleasant staff.

title_masked: Great Location and Great for Kids
text_masked:
We don't usually stay in boutique hotels but this looked like the best option with my husband's miles. We were very pleasantly surprised with the Hotel Monaco. It was recently renovated so everything looked clean and new. Nice colorful but tasteful decor. Hotel was less than 10 minute walk to Pike Place, great shopping and the new Great Wheel. Easy walk with stroller if you take 4th all the way to Pike. Neighborhood was busy but not crowded and felt safe even at night.
Kids LOVED the hotel. You may need to ask but they will give a goldfish for your room, a goody bag, a free toy from the treasure chest and if you fill out the "scavenger hunt" in the goody bag they'll bring warm cookies and milk to your room. Unfortunately my kids only like chocolate chip and they brought oatmeal raisin and pb cookies. Very nice touch though and my husband and I enjoyed them. Free Starbucks coffee and tea in the morning, lemonade in the afternoon and 5:00 wine. They ran out of coffee and lemonade one day but you can probably ask them to refill it.
We had some problems with our air conditioning but it was fixed quickly and they compensated by giving us free movies AND free parking! At $39/nt that more than made up for the inconvenience. (Call valet before you head down and they'll have your car waiting for you.) Our room wasn't cleaned when we returned at 3 p.m. but they quickly took care of that. No microwaves for heating milk but they let you use the one in the Porter's room. Pillows are super hard but you can ask for feather ones.
Overall we enjoyed our stay at the Hotel Monaco and will definitely consider staying there again on our next trip.

title_masked: Convenient, Friendly Staff, Overall Great Experience
text_masked: Stayed at the Amalfi for business. Staff was extremely friendly and having free breakfast on site was convenient since I was running around for business meetings everywhere. Room was very nice, big, clean and with all the amenities expected by any other big star hotel. Overall, a very good experience. I will definitely consider re-booking there.

I thought hard before writting this review, but at the end the result was the same: this hotel is not worth its price, or even a portion of it.
The lobby and other public areas are very nice. It is a historical building and those areas are well kept. But after you make it past them, it's a nightmare.
The hallways look like something out of the movie The Shining. There is duck tape holding down the carpet - and I checked with other guests in other floors, this is true on every floor.
It is very dirty. You see cobwebs in window sills and pieces of paper and trash on the floor.
The rooms are small and ill-equipped for the price charged. Two of the lamps in the room didn't work, and calls for repair went unaswered.
The air conditioning was very loud, clicking on and off all the time, making it hard to sleep.
This might be a minor thing, but for the price (over $225), I expected to have a sleep timer function in the TV.
The bathroom is very small and the bathtub had chunks of ... paint? porcelain? pealing off.
Tub was stained (dirty?) and there was mildew in many places. Closet doors didn't close properly and the carpet, again, very old, torn and dirty.
I had dinner here once and the food was mediocre at best. Breakfast was acceptable but very pricey.
Save yourself a bad stay and select another hotel. The Hilton and Westin are both within walking distance. Just come and see the lobby, if you want to.
This is our 2nd stay and this place is awesome. The indoor pool, Jacuzzi and weight are the best. The location is within walking distance to the Gas Light District.

title_masked: Operates leaf-blowers beneath guest room windows at 6:23 AM
text_masked: I was awoken at 6:23 AM by the shrill sounds of a leaf blower being operated to clean the outside of the front entrance to this property. Called front desk to get them to stop it. Cerk did not know what a leaf blower was (!) but understood after a couple of tries ("loud landscaping equipment," "power equipment"). I was phoned back shortly with an apology and informed that the cleaning "soon" would be finished, but that the hotel was "required" to operate this equipment at this this very early hour of the morning. Huh? Usually there are noise ordinances about such operations, but I've never heard of a hotel actually allowing landscaping equipment to be in use before dawn. Other than this major thing (which gives the property an overall "poor" rating since it prevents sleep), this is a perfectly fine sort of "city edition" Courtyard. The staff are pleasant, the place is clean. But this is a Marriott, so shouldn't we take this for granted?

Stayed here on a Hotwire reservation, so the price was fine. Easy to find, smooth check-in. I knew there would be parking charge, but it just seems odd for a 2 1/2 star hotel to charge for parking. Room looked nice enough, had a large flat-screen tv, coffee maker and refrigerator. Odd empty spot in one corner of the room, looked like there should have been a recliner or something there. Wifi 
Place was swarmed with families, lots of inattentive parents and screeching, over-tired children. Breakfast room was a nightmare, hot and noisy, so I ate quickly and headed back to my room for a bit of quiet before checking out. The hotel even tells you in a laminated sheet to expect a wait for tables if you arrive in last hour of breakfast, so should tell you something!
Probably wouldn't stay here again unless the price was really, really good.

After staying at Homewood suites for 4 days - I would never stay any place else. The suites are clean, comfortable. Kitchen has all you need. Bedding comfy. The breakfast and dinner in evening included in price! Connie in dining room is very helpful as well as the weekend staff. Great location, walking to all parks and museums.

The Kimpton Hotel Palomar provided my wife, chocolate Labrador and me an extraordinary port in the storm during the recent Hurricane Sandy event and aftermath. The hotel itself, including the room, restaurant-bar, common areas, were top shelf, but perhaps the most distinguishing component of the Palomar value proposition stemmed from the entire supporting staff. From the time you are greeted and assisted at the front door, to the time you check out, it speaks to all that can be outstanding from a customer-company experience that genuinely places a premium on customer service. From the bell stand, to the concierge and front desk, to the housekeepers and all service personnel, you get a non-scripted, authentic "we're glad you are here and we value you as our customer" sentiment from people who are proud to be delivering a first-cabin product. Thus, if you ever need a personal "port in the storm", a terrific business venue or simply want to kick back and enjoy the many wonders of Philadelphia, the Hotel Palomar should be an integral part of your plan.
Kevin & Linda

We were very impressed with the reception and service we experienced when we arrived on Aug. 3rd, after a long day of travel and without our baggage which US Air had lost. - The reception staff ( especially Nick) were very accomodating with all of the toiletries we needed, free drinks and a lot of help in shopping for needed items and finally receiving our bags. - Everyone in the hotel and Rest. seemed to go out of their way to make our visit to Phila. a good one. The Bell staff was especially good also.

title_masked: Fantasic location and hotel was great!
text_masked: Stayed here for 4 nights in the month of april and the stay was good. Rooms were actually bigger than what we expected, and very adequate. Shower was big, nice designer toiletries and free internet was a huge plus. Location of the hotel is superb really, just next to Houston Street station on train 1 line. We were in room 303 and were facing the main road. It is noisy, though it didnt bother us and we slept through it. For those light sleepers, pls avoid rooms ending with 05,04 and 03 as all of them faces the main road. If you do get those rooms that ends with the above mentioned numbers, i would suggest going for higher floors, namely 7 and above. The gym was good, equipment was brand new, towels and water were provided though it was a tad too cold in there! In addition, the hotel was just on the outskirts of soho, and its great to just walk around. 20 mins from little italy, 5 mins from soho literally and nice food all around! We paid USD $230 for it and it was well worth it, knowing that its in NYC. Would definitely stay here again for sure!

title_masked: Wait until the renovations are complete before booking
text_masked: I have stayed at this Embassy Suites hotel a number of times for work. Usually the hotel is fine. This week, it was very poor. The room smelled very bad, like stale cigarette smoke. I wonder whether the hotel being shut down for 3 months had something to do with it (i.e. perhaps the rooms were not climate controlled the entire time.) I'm still coughing. (The smells likely exacerbated my asthma.) The atrium area was not air conditioned and it was pushing 100 outside, negating the managers reception. Even if it had been air conditioned, the loud noises would have caused our group to go elsewhere. Also, the hotel allowed very loud construction to occur until 9PM. Really? Not relaxing, not good, not looking forward to returning.

Great bed, nice room. No wake up call as promised, billed for Valet parking when a friend dropped me off at hotel. Then my credit card was charged for the entire room when it was a direct bill to Harris County Metro Transit Authority. Tried for seven days to correct problem without proper action or a call from this establishment. They are collectively incompetent on Customer Service. I strongly suggest you select another hotel when in downtown Houston.

title_masked: In and around the Chancellor Hotel
text_masked:
Great location for easy walking to everything. Easy to jump on a cable car. Short walk to the Muni. Plenty of eating and drinking spots within walking distance. Very central. My first visit to San Fran and had a ball. Grab a nice breakfast at the hotels restaurant before heading out.
My room was smallish but comfortable and clean with a nice view over Union Sq.
If coming in by air, catch a city shuttle. $17 and will take you to most city hotels. Much cheaper than a cab and you get a bit of a look at the area on the way. Will drop you right outside the hotels too. May take a bit longer to get into city on the shuttle, but you get to see a lot on the way, in and around the city.

My family of 4 stayed here less than 2 weeks ago for 3 nights and can't fault the place, the staff at the front desk are so genuinely helpful. I have stayed at my share of so called 5 star hotels that could learn from this place. The included breakfast is a bonus for families and the walk is less that 5 minutes to the "Hollywood Walk of Fame".

title_masked: Wish we could have stayed longer
text_masked: My husband and I stayed for one night when we attended a wedding at the Franklin Institute(a very pleasant walk through the park away). The room was very comfortable, had a great view. The service was excellent: they let us check in early so we could get to the scheduled wedding photos on time, and they mailed my husband's shoes to us which we had forgotten in the room.

title_masked: Great location, and so the price
text_masked:
The hotel is located very much in the down town and offers easy access to public transportation.
The room rates are exorbitant and on top of that Breakfast & internet are not included. Try to take a room above 10-12 floors and facing the city side.
You can access the bus & tram service from just outside the hotel. 
Note: Visit to NASA on your own by using public transport would cost you only 2$ each way. There is a bus directly to the Johnson space center & return from outside the hotel (Milan & Dallas cross bus stand).
The hotel tourist bus will cost you 69 $ including 20 $ of entry fee !!!!!!!
Room size was good.

I was here attending a post grad course, and the course was being held at the hotel, so it made sense to stay here.
Reception/check in was easy enough, and i was offered an upgrade due to having AMEX card, the room looked like any other tbh, not sure what the basic room would have been - I have come to believe that often the 'upgrades' aren't, they are simply the same room they were going to give you but an attempt to make you feel better.
Sleep was good, shower was adequate - TV channels were odd, I was desperate to watch some sport - but, considering this is a business hotel, most of the channels were old films, which you had to pay for, or lots and lots of adult channels ....
Internet, was expensive, and somehow, even though i had paid for the weekend, it blocked out as soon as i entered the conference rooms, we could purchase conference wifi, but this was $$$$ - so everyone was popping their ipad/iphones/blackberries just outside the door during breaks to catch up their emails etc - daft really tbh.

The front desk staff was wonderful, very friendly and helpful! I would come again! I did think it was a bit pricy however I understand its Chicago! I did notice the elevator was a bit sketchy and might think twice about using it again!

aloft is ultra contemporary - very IKEA. Welcomed with smiles and welcomes. I got a great rate for one night as we were in town to visit the NASCAR Hall of Fame in conjunction with the Coca Cola 600. Everyone was accomodating, pleasant and knowlegeable. There are so many choices for food in the EpiCentre complex. Room was fine, Chelsea filled our request for higher floor. Our room (1426) overlooked Whiskey River, Dale Jrs. bar-no food. aloft does not have much choice for food, but lots of choices just out of elevator. We got a parking deal of $10 but had to leave by 10 AM. Try Whiskey River to drink, may or may not get waited on, Blackfinn, excellent fare. Will review Hall of Fame, Whiskey River, and Blackfinn under their titles. Barkeep is also sweet and personable. Knows alot about the area, which is rare sometimes.

This was my second stay and it was, as before,perfect. Everything in the hotel is designed to make it an exceptionally lovely and relaxed stay. It was greatly appreciated. I'd say also that given the level of service, amenities and the beauty of the place (not to mention that tastefully--in all senses--curated snack basket in the room), it is one of the very best values in New York city. (I've paid almost as much for a far less outstanding stay.) A very special hotel with exceptionally warm and efficient staff. Thank you.

I've stayed many places in San Francisco and this has to be my favorite. My wife was attending a meeting and I joined her for the weekend. We couldn't have been happier. The service was outstanding. The rooms are old fashioned with the tall ceilings, but very comfortable. Sunday brunch is amazing so treat yourself and you won't be disappointed. The price o0f the rooms compare favorably to Marriott and Hyatt, but with an independent classy style. Walking, MUNI or BART convenient.

I didn't expect much.. so it was great to check into a convenient, tidy, clean hotel with nice staff and great service. Loved the room. It was quiet and reasonably priced. I'll stay there again next time I'm in NYC!

My wife and I were celebrating our anniversary with a trip to Chicago this past Sunday-Tuesday. You just knew from the second you walked into the hotel that this wasn't your standard hotel. Everything from the warm greeting from the valet attendants on the street, to the smiling and attentive guest attendants (more importantly the line of guests checking out were all smiling!), and amazing interior, our stay was handled with the greatest display of professionalism and customer service we have ever experienced! We arrived early Sunday morning and Glenn checked our bags (check-in is 3pm). He was amazing! (My wife said she wanted to put him in her pocket!) Since it was our anniversary, he offered to upgrade us to an available lake view room overlooking Lincoln Park Zoo for just $10 extra a night (usually $40) and we bit. After running about the city that morning/afternoon, we returned after 3pm to check-in. Our room was located on the 11th floor between 2 elevators and the ice machine. Needless to say, we weren’t initially feeling it. However, it never was an issue during our stay (note: we passed out during our stay vs. fell asleep, so your experience may vary!). Views overlooking the lake were great and room (queen bed) is adequate for 2. About 10-15 minutes after arriving to our room, we were greeted with a bottle of Chardonnay on the house with a personally hand-written card from Glenn. Seriously, who does that anymore? Unbelievable! From this point forward, if we got a little attitude or insincerity, we could probably live with it (sad, expectations of customer service have sunken that low, isn’t it?), but we never did. From the food/beverage manager who most likely took a risk in letting us up to the J. Parker rooftop bar/restaurant 10 minutes prior to opening (ok, it was so early they were holding a staff meeting and a landscaper was removing dead leaves from pots). This was a perfect opportunity for the hostess or servers to give a dirty or unwelcoming glare from afar, but it never happened. In fact, we were welcome openly by both the hostess and front-of-house manager that let us in to the rooftop area and said they would be with us
shortly to take our drink order, and they were. Exceptionally world-class hotel with a friendly, competent, and willing staff that clearly exceeds expectations! One of the first 
things they teach you in customer service/sales, etc., is to smile, because it’s difficult to 
fake a smile, but most importantly the smile is contagious and it is passed right on to the guests! Thanks guys/gals for a great stay, we will be back!

We booked this on line and it was a very nice hotel to stay at. Friendly at check in. The rooms were nice and clean. The breakfast was nice also and area was clean. It was close to good resturants. It was also close to the stadium and race track.

The Omni is a standard mildly upscale hotel, nothing special. The beds and pillows are fine, the rooms clean and conservative, and the staff nice is nice, albeit mildly inept. 
Here's what soured me on the place: The wifi in my room was spotty so I had to move to a less desirable location. Apparently routers are only on every other floor - they may want to correct this, it's pretty easy to do. The business center charges $28/hr for computer use (?!), an obscene fee I've never experienced at any hotel I've stayed at, usually it's free. The last straw was when they wanted to charge me $175 for accepting pre-paid packages I had shipped to the hotel. All they did was store them in a closet for a day. I refused to pay and they relented.
There's lots of choices in downtown Indianapolis and you'd be wise to stay somewhere else. I cannot recommend this place --although clean and comfortable it left too many bad tastes in my mouth.

When you book on line,you really don't know what you are getting. I'm always a little worry till I get there.I was in for a shock! What a room. One of the best room we have every stay at. Great people, great services. Everything GREAT.

title_masked: A beautiful, safe and worthy gem in the heart of NYC!
text_masked:
We arrived at the Stay for the last part of our honeymoon. After four full days in Cancun we were looking forward to city life. 
We tried real hard to get a very central hotel which looked clean, decent and did not cost a fortune. And hard it was to find. But I must say we did manage to find a real gem. The Stay is just off Times Square, literally, have a look at the photos from our window. I cannot complain in any way re location or price. It was excellent value for money. 
We had read loads of reviews from many hotels, many complaining how expensive most of them were (oh yes) and how dirty they could be. Also, many commented on the size of the rooms. 
I suspect we got a bit of a larger room than normal (maybe cause we were on honeymoon), so I can’t really comment. I am happy and relieved though that we could feel like our room at the Stay was our ‘home’ in NYC. To me, that means clean and safe, and it was. You are in the heart of the city, yet you can get a very decent night’s sleep. 
Also some reviewers had commented on the elevators and how slow they were. Let’s just say they are not the fastest elevators in the world, but to me those are very tiny, negligible details. 
Just consider where you are, your location, the price you’re paying, the cleanliness of the place and how stylish this boutique hotel is. And just forget all about the elevators and wait for them!
We did not have breakfast included, but had breakfast once at the hotel and was delicious. Plenty of choices for breakfast lunch and dinner around the hotel though.

This hotel is in a great location within walking distance to a lot of sights (and shopping.!). Stayed on the 15th floor in an executive king room which had plenty of room for 2 people and a nice view of the Empire State building. Some reviews stated there was no dresser for clothes but we had a large dresser and good size closet. Free breakfast and internet with Starbucks coffee available 24 hours a day. The rooms were really clean and the staff friendly.

title_masked: Great location, nice staff, but small rooms
text_masked:
You simply can't be more central to Times Square, but this is reflected in the cost. I paid $399 and $ 349 for a Tuesday/Weds night. The hotel is quite comtemporary and clean, but the room I stayed in was tiny - barely any room either side of the standard double bed and a closet so small that I struggled to hang my clothes. The air conditioning is also quite loud.
Internet access was $ 13.95 for one day and the registration page says that this is for each device. On the second night I got complimentary internet access. The staff are friendly and customer centric. Nerma at the front desk looked after me and offered a complementary cocktail after my long flight. Decent hotel and superb location, but a bit on the expensive side given the size of the rooms.

title_masked: great location. the suites are inexpensive for families
text_masked: my niece and her husband and two kids and i rented a suite. huge with great views. least expensive in downtown chicago. the staff was friendly. the hotel was within walking distance to a lot of attractions and very convenient to bus stops. the lounge offered very reasonable happy hour prices. only negative was that the only breakfast choice was the buffet for 21 dollars.

I stayed here with my wife and two young children (4 years old) for four nights in August. This is the second time we have stayed here and we will definitely be back. 
Great location near Pike Place Market and within easy walking distance of downtown attractions. Great service and kid-friendly. One major plus is that you can get a whole bag of kids' laundry done for 10 bucks! Spent lots of time at the pool and my only criticism is that it can be hard to find a chair when it is busy in the afternoon. Room was spacious and comfortable with an excellent view of the harbour.
Seattle is a great destination for families in the summer as there are a myriad of things to do. We look forward to returning.

Traveling for business, I didn't have a choice in the hotel I stayed at; however, this hotel was wonderful. The facility was very well maintained, and the workout room, though small, was also very nice. The outdoor patio/balcony off of the pool area was huge and provided a great view of the city. My room was right next to the elevator, so despite the noise, the size of the room and view from the room was worth it. The hotel is within walking distance of many cute and quaint outdoor dining restaurants, and parking structore next to hotel is convenient and relatively inexpensive ($10-$15 a night). Of course, you also can't beat the freshly baked cookies at check-in!

Everyone that worked at the hotel provided excellent service. Anail , who worked at the complimentary breakfast, was incredibly friendly and helpful. The location in the Gas Lamp section was very convenient to everything!

title_masked: Best bed ever but beware credit card withdrawl
text_masked: We booked direct with the Hotel for a four night stay. If you allow them to advertise on your Facebook, you receive a free upgrade. As we rarely use Facebook this was not a problem and we enjoyed a lovely studio apartment, for about A$225 per night. The Hotel is very well located for enjoying all the sights of Chicago. Just off Michigan Ave just north of the River. The Hotel is well appointed, pleasant helpful staff. The studio room was spacious, small lounge area, very nice large bathroom and bar area. Room was pleasantly quiet, it was at the end of the corridor. The large king size bed was one of the most comfortable I have slept on. Only problem was that on checking my internet banking after arrival note a debit of US$400 had been made to my credit card account, no entry as to who had made it. As I feared fraud, I rang my Bank in Australia and was advised it was The James. On checking at the desk it was confirmed they deduct US$100 per day from the card you used to make the booking. Only problem no one told us, also it was a card I had put into credit if I needed to make a cash withdrawal. Now I had US$400 less. So beware. Otherwise recommended.

The Four Seasons is very conveniently located near the business and entertainment districts. Yet it is quietly nestled on the bank of Lady Bird Lake. Our room was nicely appointed and comfortable and well maintained by housekeeping during our stay. The fresh fruit and juice that
was available to guests in the lobby was a nice touch, as was the quality coffee and tea selections. I particularly enjoyed the quiet and shady sitting areas on the grounds. Perfect for morning coffee and the paper, or an evening cocktail. Would like to return in the future.

Loved this hotel. Very good location in Union Square. Amazing front desk staff. Tip: if you have a car, it takes a long time for them to bring it around. Plan on calilng down for it 30 minutes or more in adfvance. Resident Pug Max adds to the amblience. Rooms are smaller but nice. Not luxury by an means but a decent hotel.

title_masked: Decent hotel- with some big flaws
text_masked:
This was a decent hotel, but for the amount of money we spent, I expected it to be much nicer. I'll detail the pros and cons of the hotel.
Pros:
1. The location is amazing! It's literally steps away from Chinatown and a 5-10 minute walk to Union Square. If you like to walk, Fisherman's Wharf is about 25-30 minutes away. During our entire stay in San Francisco, we walked everywhere and found this to be an excellent location.
2. Most of the staff is super friendly. They were always welcoming, chatting with us and smiling. They also made some good recommendations on restaurants and things to see in the area.
3. The room was much nicer than I expected. After reading the reviews on Tripadvisor, I was apprehensive that the room would be the size of a shoebox! It wasn't. The bed was SO comfortable and the couch was a nice touch. The bathroom was also a decent size. 
4. The hotel is so quiet! This is the main reason I picked this hotel, as I am a very light sleeper. I was happy to discover that it IS actually very quiet, and I slept so well during our 5 night stay!
5. I LOVE the eco-friendly theme. The recycling box in the room is wonderful- I wish all hotels did that! 
The cons:
1. For the expensive price, I expect a bit more regarding the amenities. For example, there was no microwave in the room. There is a mini-fridge but it's filled with the mini bar items. Also breakfast is not included in the nightly rate. For over $300 a night (with the valet parking) I expect at least a small, basic breakfast.
2. The room was mostly clean (no bed bugs or anything like that) but there were 2 things that grossed me out. When we arrived, I pulled down the comforter on the bed and there was a long black hair in the bed (we both have light brown hair). Gross! Even more disgusting was when I pulled the plush robe out of the closet only to discover dried blood stains on the front of the robe! Needless to say I did not wear the robe for the rest of our stay...I didn't bother to bring up this issue because the housekeeping staff, although very friendly, do not speak any English.
3. I know that you probably won't be spending a lot of time in the room, but for the price of the hotel I expect the TV and Internet to be better. The Wi-fi signal was so weak the majority of the time I could not even connect to the internet from our room. The TV is an ancient model with terrible picture quality and they only offer 20 channels! If motels for $50 a night can offer HBO, why can't the Orchard Garden for $300 a night?
4. The staff, while extremely friendly, was unable to help me with one major inquiry. I called the front desk for assistance in booking the Hornblower Brunch Cruise and the girl at the front desk didn't know what the Hornblower Cruise was! Her lack of knowledge caused us to almost miss the only cruise during our whole trip that we could take. Another issue is that they don't offer any tourist brochures on San Francisco. Also, during check-out, the lady at the front desk asked me how our stay was and I said "it was okay, with a few major flaws". She said, "Oh". She gave me the impression that she really didn't care how our stay was. 
5. On top of the astronomical price for the hotel room and the valet parking, the staff "forgot" to tell us during check-in that on top of the $40/day for the valet parking that there is another $6/day in taxes added on to that figure! How nice. 
All in all, this hotel served its purpose of being a decent home base while in San Francisco. But next time I'm in San Francisco, I think I would want to spend a bit more money and stay in a nicer hotel.

title_masked: Worst hotel experience in the world and reception staff is a bxxxh
text_masked:
when I was trying to ask the receptionist questions, she stopped me several times and there was even no eye contact or any explanations when she did that. 
when I just wanted to double check with her which of my credit card would be charged for second night (I booked two rooms for two nights for me and my business friends, and I used two credit cards to pay), she stopped me again and spoke to me rudely, so I couldn’t put up with her, then I requested to speak to her supervisor or any other staff. What happened next is she yelled at me saying, “I am not going to deal with you”, and then she slapped the keyboard, turned back and walked in the room behind her. 
I even wrote an email to the hotel's customer service staff afterwards. 
There is NO APOLOGY, NO EXPLANATION, NO FOLLOW-UP whatsoever, and it looks like there is nothing to the W hotel.
IF YOU WANT TO GET HUMILIATED IN PUBLIC, PLEASE COME TO STAY AT THIS W HOTEL!!!!!!! 
More info about this hotel: no coffee or any complimentary drink/snack provided, and its rooms are very small, maybe even smaller than master suite bathroom in your house. There is no view at all: my room was at 12 floor and only 4-5 feet away from a office building (I could see clearly people doing in that building, and vice versus). The lobby is crowded and loud.

I stayed at this hotel for the Democratic National Convention. I was working at the convention and my employer booked several rooms at this hotel.
I arrived at CLT on a Friday afternoon and called the hotel upon arrival. The hotel shuttle arrived at the airport within 15 minutes. I was checked in quickly and efficiently. I didn't have a car, but there is a convenience store next door so I walked over there to get some snacks and beverages to last during my stay. I ordered takeout for dinner on the first night and the delivery person was able to come straight to my room.
The hotel breakfast was decent with a good variety of food. The dining area was large and had a good atmosphere.
The rooms themselves were nice in that they felt like a little apartment. The kiing sized bed was super comfortable. It was nice to have a separate living room with a second TV and a DVD player. The desk in the bedroom didn't have enough accessible power outlets, so I set my laptop up on the kitchen island / desk. The kitchen appliances were a little outdated, but honestly it wasn't a big deal as all I needed was a fridge to keep things cold and a microwave to heat things up. I didn't use the dishwasher. I liked having real dishes and silverware.
The one downfall of the hotel was the hotel gym. Upon entering the gym it was hot and muggy. I looked around for the climate control, and realized there was a hole in the wall where the AC unit once was. You could see through to the outside world, so whatever temperature it was outside was what it was in the gym. Now, it was early September in Charlotte so it was pretty hot. I just pretended I was running outside on the few days I did use the gym since it was so hot.
The hotel offered free shuttle rides to the closest Lynx station. I took advantage of this one day. The ride to the Lynx station was about 5 minutes and then it was just another 10 minutes on the train to reach Uptown Charlotte. I called the hotel when I was on my way back and they sent a shuttle driver to pick me up from the Lynx station.
I will probably not have a reason to book a hotel in Charlotte in the future since my in-laws live there and I have a free place to stay, but I would recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a nice place to stay near the airport. There isn't a whole lot of excitement on this side of the city, so the location is the only caveat of the place.

title_masked: Great place to stay in a beautiful city
text_masked: This is what a business hotel in a big city should be. Modern attractive decor, clean comfortable rooms and gorgeous city and harbor views. You can't beat the location, right on the harbor promenade and across the street from Gaslamp Quarter.Breakfast is good, but the hotel gets a lot of business traffic being located right next to San Diego Convention Center, so you may have to wait to be seated between 8-9 a.m.

title_masked: My review of extended stay north park
text_masked: I really like it here it is the best I have been, nice people to accommodations I need. Its very clean quiet and the management is superb. I want to say the best person I like here is Michelle she does an excellent job with customer service she goes out her way and I thank you sooo much.
Excelente experience, everyone very nice, very good location

This was definitely one of the more interesting hotels I've stayed at for business. Four towers with different colour names go to different "wings" of the hotel. 
First the lobby - very big and basically goes around in a large circle which made it a little challenging to meet with business associates but I managed. Plenty of seating which was good. 
Room - It was fine, clean, bed was comfortable however the room itself was quite small which doesn't tend to bother me except that there was a door to an adjoining room hence it felt a little intimate being able to hear someone russling about on the other side. I was however annoyed about the card swipe into the room (which is amusing seeing someone else comment on this.) After checking in, I had to return to the reception as my cards didn't work to get into the room and to get them re-magnetized..... lo and behold, they still didn't work when I returned and after trying them again and again, finally managed to get the door open. Every time I returned I would have to swipe 15-20 times to get the card to register (and I stay at hotels regularly hence am not unfamiliar with how these work!) They need to look at fixing this as it's frustrating.
One very positive note, after finally going to get some dinner at around 9pm I decided to eat in the lobby bar and had an amazing prawn fajita....great value too.
I liked the fact that it was real close where I was going to be in church and the room was HUGE I loved my stay I wish it would of been longer

Having wanted to catch a play in Central Park, I stayed one night at the hotel and am glad they granted me an early check-in at 11. Room is comfortable and shampoo,conditioner and soap are provided. American Museum of Natural History is directly opposite the hotel, and Shake Shack is just 5 minutes walk away. However, wifi is not complimentary and as other travellers have noted, service staff are not impolite but rather curt.

I would like to take a moment to recognize the outstanding service of Lassandra. She was our "breakfast chef" for the three days we stayed at the Embassy Suites earlier this month (March 5 - 7). Lassandra was extremely pleasant and very helpful each day. She made an awesome omelet and always served it with a smile. We will be returning for business several more times throughout the year and I will be looking forward to Lassandra's service each and every time.
Regards,
Carlene Harper
B Braun Medical

title_masked: Determined to get it only 95% right
text_masked:
I just returned from a five night stay at the Double Tree. Overall the stay was ok, the room was nice, the bed very comfortable, all as to be expected from a Double Tree property. The location of the hotel was convenient for my purposes, very close to the client I was working with, and my reason for being in San Diego.
I also would like to point-out that the room service was good. The food arrived very promptly and was tasty (I had room service four out of my five nights).
The reason I am giving this property only an average rating is for a couple of little annoyance that could have easily been avoided, but added pressure to my very crazy/busy week:
1. The check-in process was not up to par. The front desk personnel was efficiently checking me into my room (Sounds great - right?), totally ignoring to elaborate on any of the circumstances of my booking. I had requested some upgrades via the Internet. Additionally, the room I booked used a company rate that included parking and the Internet. I had to prompt the employee to look up what upgrades I received as well as what was included in my room rate. Prompting the front desk to to take these things into consideration should not be my responsibility. What really bothered me was the uber efficient air the employee had, as if I should not have to ask. On top of it, the answers I got from the employee were not correct. Which I only found out, after I reviewed my reservation, once in my room, and had to call down to the front desk to get further clarification.
2. The next morning, while drying my hair, the hair dyer stopped working (probably because it was so clogged with dust and dirt in the back that the airflow was restriced and led to overheating the hair dryer). No problem - I called the front desk and requested another hair dryer, which arrived promptly (Great!). Only for me to discover that the new hair dryer was in no better shape that the first hair dryer. At the end of the day, I tried one more time to get my hands on a decent hair dryer, by taking the hair dryer to the front desk, explaining my issue and asking for another one. The front desk called housekeeping for a replacement, and asked me to return to my room, taking the hair dryer with me, since they would not know what to do with it, and to wait for the replacement, which would be dropped off at my room. Guess what, the this hairdryer was just as old and clogged up. The maid did not understand what I was asking her, and in the end I gave up and used tape and q-tips to try to unclog the hairdryer as much as I could on my own.
3. Day 1: Already being late from the hair dyer incident, I was rushing to get a quick breakfast on the executive floor (which was an upgrade I paid for), only to discover that my room key was not programmed to let me take the elevator up to the 11th floor! I had to go down to the reception, ask them to change the coding on my room key so I could have breakfast.
4. Along with the crappy hair dryer goes the really bad/old ironing board and iron in the room. I only tried to iron one piece of clothing. It;s almost as if the hotel renovated and tried to save money on the appliances.
5. Just as a final good bye gift from the reception, the morning of the departure, I received only page two of my final invoice under my door - I wonder what happened to page one? Once again I had to stop by the reception.....
Next time I have to stay at this property, I will need to recalibrate my expectations. But now I know what things to look out for. I understand that this is not the Ritz, but neither is this property a low end hotel, not for close to $200 per night. Also, I travel for work close to 30 weeks per year, and it has been quite a while since I was frustrated enough to write a hotel review.

Stayed at the Courtyard by Marriott for 3 nights. We paid for the the package with breakfast at the hotel. Had upgraded to a water view, third floor, Sunrise was lovely every morning. It overlooked the pool, but at this time of year it was never too loud. Staff was very nice. Waitress at breakfast also was very friendly. We had the buffet each morning, fresh fruit, omelets, salmon. Lots of trendy new restaurants opening in LIberty Station, we ate out every evening. Location was central to every place we went, Balboa Park, Old Town San Diego, La Jolla Cove. As others stated, walls were a little thin, but nothing we couldn't manage. Fairly new hotel so everything was shiny and new. Coffee in the lobby and flavored waters all day was a nice plus too. We'll stay there again.

I think it is hard to overestimate how much an enthusiastic, cheerful greeting can brighten your day and affect your perception of a hotel, maybe even of a city in general. So kudos to the Palomar staff. Every staff person we encountered went out of their way to be pleasant and welcoming to us. The personable attitude even made up for a mattress that could be more comfortable, a very small bathroom and some quirky details like lack of coffee in the room and a too-short hair dryer cord. We try to stay in a different hotel every time we visit DC (which is often since we live fairly close). The Palomar is our favorite so far.

My wife and I loved everything about this hotel and our junior suite. A clean, safe beauty with the perfect San Francisco location. Fantastic staff. Comfortable beds, quiet and a spacious, well-lit bathroom. A small and wonderful place to stay. I didn't want to leave and I can't wait to go back.

Way over the top trendy from the blue lights in the elevator to the lounge/house music in the lobby to the ikea-esque furniture in the rooms. Not the cleanest place (the room smelled a little musty and the carpets could use a cleaning). But the location was convenient for visiting the MOMA and we did have a nice, open view from our window (even if they did sell condoms in our hotel room and all the hotel staff looked as though they could have doubled as bouncers/coat check girls at a nightclub). If you want a young, sexy, flashy place to blow your money like a rock-star, this could work for you. Kudos to how quiet our room was, how comfy the bed was, and how helpful the staff were.

The rooms are nice for the price you pay, never go with family because there is no security, people walking the halls that have nothing to do with the hotel.
The manager is very arrogant and very bad service

title_masked: Wasn't that crazy about the neighborhood, but it was okay
text_masked:
We stayed here for one night since we were flying out of SD Int'l Airport at 6:30 AM. The fact that it seemed to be convenient to a bunch of stuff down in this area of town might be of importance to you, it wasn't to us. Lots of stuff in walking distance, though - right, like anybody walks in SoCal.
Thought it was pretty wack that they had signs up all over the place crowing about the fact that they change the bed linens for EVERY GUEST! Really? Has it gotten commonplace that ALL hotels don't do that? Pretty creepy if you ask me.
This place was a pretty good place to stay, only had one gripe - if you need an airport shuttle, make sure their schedule is going to work for you. As close as they are to the airport, having one ride per hour may be convenient for them, but if you have a 6:30 AM flight, it gives you a choice of going at 4:30 AM or 5:30 AM. Cool, just what I wanted, get to sit at the airport that extra half hour at 5 AM.
The room was good, pretty large and adequately equipped. Really liked the hot Otis Spunkmeyer cookies at the front desk, mmmmm. The neighborhood looked a little dicey, but on the other hand, if you're wanting to spend some quality time at the "World Famous Body Shop" (stripclub), it's real convenient for that. Just saying...

We stayed at the hotel couple days ago and my wife's rings (wedding ring and engagement ring) disappeared from our room. It either happened when we were out of the room, but most likely she forgot them in the room when we checked out. We returned to the hotel couple hours later but they said that housekeeper hasn't seen anything. Moreover, the front desk said "we are sorry" without any attempt to show that they care, like if it was pants that we forgot and not expensive jewelry. They haven't bothered to tell to the manager and call to security personnel. Only three days later they checked the log for the door to see who else could enter the room when we were out. We reported to the police but no hope left to recover the rings that have so high sentimental value to us.
A minor remark, the room we stayed in has a door to another room, and it is extremely noisy when the adjacent room is occupied. If you have to stay in this hotel, don't take kids with you.
