I recently had my wedding at this location. This hotel is perfect! I wanted a wedding on the water but didn't want to break the bank. Ashley was the coordinator and she was outstanding! She helped us every step of the way! If anyone is looking into a Boston Wedding, I HIGHLY recommend the Renaissance Boston Waterfront Hotel.
This hotel is near the underground station, you can take the underground direct from O'Hare airport to the shopping centre, and take one minute to this hotel

title_masked: Great for tourism and nice design
text_masked:
I mostly stay around Union Square but this time I wanted to try the more touristy area with the family. We stayed in a double Queen on the first floor. Service was very good from valet parking (expensive!) to baggage handling. Nice design for a Sheration, very close to everything but not noisy at all. You have plenty of places nearby ranging from great restaurants (Gary D.) to a Trader´s Joe! 
Rooms are not very big but standard for inner city location. Try Hollywood café for breakfast. 
If you find a good rate it is a good place to stay.

I stayed the Doubletree for one night. I must stay that I have stayed in fancier, more expensive places, but the Doubletree staff outshined most of them. I found the staff genuinely friendly and helpful. The temperature in Phoenix was over a 100 when I arrived and so I turned the a/c up. After a couple of hours, the temperature did not change. I called the desk and they immediately sent Miguel from the Maintenance Dept. to check the a/c in the room. He was very professional and helpful. After trying to fix the a/c, he called the desk and had my room changed. He assisted me in moving all my belongings and then brought me a courtesy bag from the Hotel filled with snacks. 
My room was comfortable and clean and would certainly stay there again when I'm in the area.

title_masked: Lovely stay at the Hampton Inn
text_masked:
Make sure you request a room at the front as they are lighter unless you are on a very high floor as the higher rooms at the back have a view of Midtown, the first room we were given was at the back and there were several faults, one of which was quite major but read on. I complained and we were moved straight away . The staff were very friendly and efficient,breakfast has excellent choices and fresh fruit salad not tinned as we seem to get in Britain. The 24 hour tea,coffee and juice was very welcome especially as we often brought take aways back and ate in the dinning area or roof terrace. Fresh cookies in the afternoon pleased my husband and free wifi my teenage son. 
On first impression area seems a little run down but explore it has loads to offer. Very close to subway and a lovely walk along the river to downtown. All in all I would stay there again. I found the previous review about directions helpful but taxi driver took no notice as they do not want to get stuck in the Holland Tunnel traffic queue which is constantly outside hotel. Beds were also very comfortable and the bedding was changed once during the week we stayed.

I have stayed at the Villa Florence on several occasions. The hotel staff is always very accommodating and helpful. We've been lucky on several occasions to be able to check-in early and have our room for the entire day. The hotel is located half-a-block off the bustling Union Square. The rooms are typcial SF - small with a lot packed into the space. Free wireless internet is available in the room - bonus! We recently stayed in a Jr. Suite and it was roomy! The sitting area with couch and chairs made it comfortable to relax in the room without having to sit on the bed. Be prepared for traffice and blocks of people if you are bring a car into the city. The parking rate is outrageous - this past weekend it was $45 for a night! I know that in a big city that space is at a premium, but that seems outright ridiculous. Aside from the parking rate, the staff is helpful in matching room rates found on websites such as expedia.

title_masked: Great budget hotel in a great location
text_masked: Reading the more critical reviews, I wonder if they were expecting the Ritz Carlton at Motel 6 prices. Ultimately, you get what you pay for but I feel this was a great deal for a stay in an otherwise very expensive city. I stayed in a queen studio with a sink and shared bathroom. The rooms are smaller but clean and the beds are very comfortable. The queen studio would be perfect for a couple spending most site seeing out of the hotel and not looking to stay in the whole day. There is a convenient sink in the room and the shared bathrooms were always very clean and tidy. I paid about $100/night which I felt was a great deal for this city. The location was excellent, located close to Moscone Center, Union Square and great shopping districts. Always felt safe in the area. There are always cabs waiting for fares across the street at the Marriott and a parking garage for the hotel so local transportation and parking are convenient. The staff was nice and friendly. Unless you are a 4 star hotel snob willing to put up the money, I think this is an excellent choice on a budget in an otherwise expensive city.

I recently stayed here on a business trip and was pleased with the hotel. This is a great place if you are looking for somewhere close to Union Square with plenty of shopping and restaurants just steps from the front door. The room was quite nice, with recently updated, modern, and stylish decor. The food at the restaurant was also surprisingly good -- much better than I tend to expect at chain hotels. And the view of the Bay from the restaurant/bar area is absolutely stunning (worth a look even if you don't stay for food/drinks). The concierge was very helpful in arranging taxis and airport shuttles, and the front desk staff were courteous. My only complaint at this hotel would be the lack of free wireless internet.

We booked this hotel for a one night stay. Our flight arrived into CLT after midnight and we need a place to sleep for the night. It was a very pleasant stay. We arrived late and were accommodated immediately so there was no wasted time checking in. Our room was very spacious and very clean. There was a comfortable king size bed and a pull out couch. Plus a huge flat screen TV in the room. The free breakfast the next morning was wonderful. This isn't your typical hockey puck biscuits, canned fruit and frozen pancakes. This was a real breakfast. There was so much to choose from! It was all tasty, fresh and delicious. Great coffee too! The staff was friendly as well. Overall a great stay and priced well too.

title_masked: Probably the nicest hotel I've stayed in!
text_masked:
I just love this place - so I am rating it again since my last visit. This trip, I was upgraded to an Executive Luxury Suite - and I must say..WOW! The room was beautiful, very large, and extremely comfortable! The bathroom was very impressive - a huge oval tub you could almost swim laps in, and a separate shower you could have a party in!
Staff at the hotel is awesome, and although it's a brand new property - they kept alot of the charm of the old building. You will not go wrong here for business!!

'Whatever Whenever' Service is brilliant.... it is actually whatever you want whenever you want it!
Lovely hotel, very clean, very friendly staff.
Couldn't have asked for anything more.
Location is perfect and the pool is beautiful.
No complaints.

title_masked: Went for work, will be back for fun
text_masked:
I recently stayed at this resort for a conference. The views are breathtaking and I really enjoyed the layout of the resort. Bring your walking shoes if you do not have a car. The gym is nice, but pass it up and take a hike around the resort trail. Even just around the buildings will get your heart rate up with the hills. 
A Different Pointe of View and Point in Tyme were both excellent in my opinion. The view from A Different Point of View is what will bring me back. I cacn't wait to come back on vacation to play some golf and enjoy this resort again.

My husband stays here often when in NYC for business & it is his favorite NYC hotel so I wanted to check it out. The regular rooms are huge by NYC standards and included a really nice sitting area with both a couch and a desk area. The bathrooms are great - lovely and bright with a fabulous shower (although I did miss having a bath...). We had breakfast twice in the restaurant "maze" and it was really good quality even if it was a little on the expensive side. I also ate dinner at Maze with my oldest daughter and we both loved the tasting menu. Even though I changed the reservation from the fancier Gordon Ramsey as our train was delayed and we arrived feeling a little frazzled, the host could not have been nicer seating us graciously and even sending over a glass of champagne for me and a ginger beer for my daughter. This is now my new hotel of choice in NYC!!!! Swanky, gorgeous with great rooms and a cool bar, my 3 kids gave it the thumbs up too...

title_masked: Island life without leaving the mainland
text_masked: I never get to leave the states; so loved being transported far away in just a short drive to Paradise Point in Mission Bay. Upon driving up, you are greeted by friendly people you would like to meet everyday; not just another establishment with trained uniforms and protocols. Many friendly ducks and other animal greeters are equally happy to see you. The greenery, landscaping, and waterways about the complex are amazingly beautiful, as well as all the paths in and about the resort. There's no need to hurry for anything and you won't mind if you get lost on the way to your bungalow. Some may intrepret the era as a blast from the past, but all of the buildings are modernized and certainly well maintained. My visit was a business function in which all of the facilities and support services were well catered. If I'm ever in San Diego and looking for carefree, no hussle and bussle relaxation, I will definitely consider spending my time off at this unique treasure of an island.

location is terrific--if you like to eat or want to catch a ballgame or wish to explore the seafront and maritime lore. Beds are comfortable, the place is clean and, for my money, gives good value. Also a pretty good restaurant, especially for breakfast, right next door and at any time you please. Don't look here for luxury, though. I don't much mind that the building is old and quaint (which I sort of like) and needs a refurb. Plus window ACs which some don't care for. I gave it a four because a. 3 and 1/2 isn't an option, b. I don't spend much time in the hotel anyway when I visit somewhere as vibrant as San Diego and, 3, once again, because the staff is GREAT and will go out of their way to help you any way(s) they can.

I stayed at the Atheneum one night and found the level of amenities superb. The price was very reasonable and I felt like I was staying in a Marriott for a Courtyard price. I would stay there again without hesitation!

Stayed her over the Easter weekend and loved it. The location is just right and close to a couple of my favorite restaurants like Goode Company BBQ/Seafood/Tex Mex and Lupe Tortilla. Right off, Anne Marie was a breath of fresh air with an easy smile and efficient check in. The Concierge, Mandy was there to answer any questions. So many little touches make this a stand out hotel. It’s located right on I-59 and were facing the highway but the room was very quiet and had the best blackout curtains I’ve seen. And lastly, the breakfast buffet was outstanding with fruit, assorted breads and pastries and a full omelet station. Overall, an outstanding stay. We’ll be back.

stayed there for 3 nights on a business trip to Houston. There is another Marriott property nearby so I had a little confusion as I was travelling on a taxi from IAH. Rooms are nice and clean with good temp control. wifi was stable. All my requested extra things for my room was ready at my check-in. Also they agreed for a 2hr late check-out on the first day. There is a market place nearby with many restaurants and bar. One thing I must mention the hotel staff were very friendly and helpful. I am definitely going to come back to the same place during my next stay in Houston.

title_masked: Perfect Location, Great Staff, Good Room, Right Price
text_masked:
My wife and I stayed at the hotel for most of Thanksgiving Week 2012. The location is perfect for walking all over mid-Manhattan. The staff treated us very well from phone calls before our visit from Atlanta to the moment we departed. Cynthia and Elizabeth took care of us by phone, David beautifully checked us in, and when the room was cold the first night, and the TV remote needed a battery, David corrected the problems. Ellen was the star of the show for us from the desk staff. Unasked, she gave us 2 complimentary breakfasts in the City House dining room for our inconvenience with the temperature and the remote. Nice touch. We met the delightful Winson B. there, our server, who made dining a fun experience. Fine job, staff!
The room was pleasant, the sheets and bedding very clean and comfortable, and the price for a Manhattan hotel was right. Central Park two blocks north, and Times Square 10 minutes south. 
The hotel is an older building, and there was some stale smell in our hallway. Perhaps some new carpet would do the job.I hope some of the current renovation takes care of this problem, just as former renovation provided the very nice workout room. The lamps in the room needed some dusting. Other than those things it was a very good stay.

title_masked: Crowne Plaza LAX - A great place to stay
text_masked:
Upon arrival at the hotel the front desk staff- Imelda was really most helpful in upgrading my room for an extra day due to my late departure long haul flight the next day at no extra cost. This enabled me to tour around LA for the day , return, show, refresh before a 15 hour flight home. This made all the difference to the end of a 6 week trip to north America.
The room was clean, quiet, and very comfortable. 
Breakfast was great in the restaurant.
Free wireless internet was provided from the room until departure

title_masked: I suppose trendy isnt really my thing
text_masked:
Staff was helpful. Walkable to Seattle landmarks.
Lobby is small. Larger area is part of the bar (which feels weird to stand in if you are not going to the bar).
No wi-fi which is just ridiculous and no where to really hang out and check emails downstairs (unless you are in Trace which requires being dressed up).
Hallways are super dark and trendy (which was kind of depressing). Rooms and amenities in the room were good. Thermometer had a mind of its own and didn't react to you changing the temperature. Room service was crazy expensive (which is expected I guess). Hotel binder still had the number for the Seattle SuperSonics which were moved to OKC 4 years ago...

We stayed at the Topaz Hotel in Washington DC from Wednesday, August 15th to Monday, August 20th. Never have we been treated with as much courtesy, and cheerfulness. The people at the front desk were exceptional. They were very attentive yet unobtrusive – a fine balance that they performed naturally and artfully. When the front door magically opened to our comings and goings and we were personally greeted each morning and evening, we truly felt like welcomed guests. They were sincerely interested in our experience. When we asked for directions, we later found a print of a Google map slipped under our door. The service during morning coffee and hospitality hour could not have been better. Again, polite and attentive, but not obsequious. And the location and room were perfect. The lighting was in all the right places and the alcove was ideal for morning coffee and reading. The entire experience made it feel like home away from home. Having visited some 40 states and over 20 countries, we consider ourselves seasoned travelers. Never though, have we had a hotel stay as satisfying as this one.

Stayed here 5 nights from 1/21-1/26 2011. This is a great location, very close to lots of restaurants and shopping. Hotel is nice but nothing very special. Rooms were small, perhaps this is the norm for downtown properties. Food and service were good but again nothing special. If you have to stay downtown this is a nice option. Bar area is nice but got crowded quickly. 6 nice TV screens made game watching easy and fun here.

Stayed for a Monday night and chose this for its proximity to a business meeting. Had a room on the 8th floor - which was comfortable enough although slightly cramped. Good lighting by writing table, armchair and in bed. Bathroom basic but clean - not the kind of tub which tempts you to soak. Staff we met in lobby, reception and the Grill were all efficient and friendly. Even though the location is on the edge of Downtown DC it's close enough to an excellent choice of restaurants, a bit of a walk to shopping and a pleasant walk to the Mall. Valet parking in garage adjoining was easy and cost $38 plus tax a day.

Every staff was happy and helpful. Cally gave me directions to a great sunset viewing beach park with a playground for our 6yo - Del Mar city beach/Powerhouse Park. When I realized we would miss evening social, I asked if it would be possible for them to box it some of it up and put in our fridge - no problem. Nice coming "home" to some already cooked food while I began the cooking process.
Room clean and stocked. Pull out sofa comfy and room for our son, who never complained about noises anywhere and the bed - however he passed out in 5 minutes after a day at Legoland! Do note that when the sofabed is out, it takes up the entire living room and blocks the desk.
Hubby used the gas grill next to the pool next to our room for cook our steaks. Good breakfast. Be on your toes ready to pounce when a new batch of food comes out...blinked and waffles were gone. Like the communal table in the center of the room. We enjoyed conversing with other guests.

title_masked: Great location, property a bit outdated
text_masked:
Had a 2 night stay in September. The location of this hotel is ideal, if you are staying downtown. In the retail core, near Nordstrom, H&M, Washington Athletic Club. Easily walkable to Pike Place Market. 
Inside is generally unremarkable. There is nothing wrong with it, but you wouldn't confuse it with a luxury hotel. It is a large hotel and was very full when I was there. The rooms and bathrooms are outdated, but pretty on par with other hotels in this price range. 
Someone near me was shouting in the middle of the night, and it was very loud. Showerhead leaked continuously throughout the stay, but it was a slow leak.
As a Starwood platinum, I had access to the lounge. The lounge was nice and had great views. In the evening a nice cheese and appetizer selection was available. 
If you are not spending much time in the hotel, this property will do.

This was my first time in Chicago and I must say I will be going back. Upon arriving at this hotel I was greeted with a smile & professionalism. The rooms were clean and spacious. The bed was was super comfy and the linen was white. If I did not have to go anywhere I would still be in that bed. The hotel amenities were excellent. The manager Janita was very helpful and professional. If you are looking for a wonderful and pleasant experience you should stay here.

This was not my first stay at a W Hotel - check my previous reviews. If you like the format, you will take comfort in the consistency of the brand and service. For me, it just seems to be more about style, rather than substance.
The bar looked stylish, and was certainly well-attended. Staff were well presented, and friendly. BUt the front desk person seemed to lack local knowledge - couldn't give me correct directions for my desired destination. Ended up walking for over 90 minutes, when she said it would take no more than 20.
The room was of average size; bed was comfortable. As usual, paid wifi @ 14.95 per 24 hours.
Bathroom amenities are good quality - take some home with you!
When receiving your room allocation, remember to stay away from the lifts. The music just pumps out of the lift during the evening hours - might disturb your sleep.
Great gym, with wide variety of equipment, and some room to move.
The hotel is located in Boston's theatre and entertainment district. Great for late nights, and stumbling back to your hotel room. Not so good for harbour views, or shopping. Stay near the Prudential Centre for the best shopping at your doorstep.
What else can I say? If you were to appraise the hotel on a checklist; all the boxes would be ticked. This was a comfortable hotel for my business trip of three nights. HOwever, for reasons I'm just not sure of, if I were to return to Boston with my family, I would stay elsewhere.

Just arrived home from a vacation in New York and an 8-night stay at wonderful Chambers Hotel. We are a family with three children, age 9, 7 and 2,5 years old who stayed in a Studio King room which was absolutely lovely, with a fantastic bathtub and shower. All the staff were amazing, friendly and extremely helpful, cleaning great, and during the storm Sandy we all gathered in the mezzanine level and the hotel treated the guests with complimentary wine/cheese/popcorn, a very thoughtful gesture. Absolutely recommend the hotel, stunning decor, excellent location close to Central Park and shopping, will definitely return, already longing for it!

I have to give a rating for this to register, So 5/5 for the location
 This is GENUINELY what happened to us... We arrived on the 6th Sept and was given a room on the 10th Floor, the room we where given was the smallest room we have ever stayed in, there wasn't any room to store any of my wife's dresses and the wardrobe was only big enough to hang about 8 "T" shirts, we asked to be moved, we were moved to the 15th floor when i entered the room there was a man laid on the bed, luckily he had the safety catch on. we got moved AGAIN(3 Rooms in 15 mins) the final room was on the 8th floor (the noise of traffic and roadworks in the area was non stop 24 hours a day (no soundproofing).
 We where going out so i had a shave and the sink wouldn't drain and the tap kept on dripping, we reported it and asked them if they would be good enough to have it sorted by the time we got back,which they ALMOST did. Tap was still dripping. anyway we got back at 12.45am, we flushed the toilet and it kept on flushing, i reported it after 15 mins still flushing, the front desk said sorry sir can we send an engineer up immediately ? i said yes if he comes now, 30 mins later he arrived, didn't totally fix it because the same thing happened the next day. at !.45am , the engineer decides to try and tell me what had happened and how the piping system worked. i told him politely to go because we where shattered.
 This particular room was supposed to be one of the bigger rooms in this hotel. the bath had enamel chipped off the surface bottom shower curtain was falling apart.
On leaving the Hotel at check-out we was asked "did you enjoy your stay" we said we loved NYC but the hotel was abysmal, when asked what the problem was i told the lady at the desk everything and she just smiled and said oh dear.....And the final insult when we vacated our room we asked if we could leave our luggage whilst we went for something to eat before our flight and was told to take our luggage to the second floor which we did we had two cases and a very small back pack and was charged 8 dollars could not believe it have never been charged for leaving luggage for one hour in any hotel we have ever stayed in. if you want a fantastic location their are plenty of other hotels, we will never stay at the paramount again and would not recommend it to anyone. Also don't forget to take a torch , you will need it to find your way around the corridors. Shop about you will find a lot better hotel out there, it maybe better to pay a little more and find a hotel that will make your holiday not ruin it. BUT i would like to end on a positive note in defence of the Paramount, This hotel is ideal if you only want to stay for Part of the night AND you don't have a change of clothes
 YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

The New York Marriott Marquis is THE place to stay in Times Square. Yes, it's quite pricey in every sense of the word, but hey, it's Times Square! It's one of those indulgences that's worth every cent.
With commanding views of the excitement of Times Square, it's something that you will remember the rest of your life. The location puts you right in the midst of all the flashing neon and hustle-bustle. It's also conveniently located next door to the Minskoff Theater (currently showing The Lion King). Three blocks away and just a couple minutes walk is the 42nd Street Port Authority terminal to catch the subway. Across the street are the studios of "Good Morning America", so you can walk out the front door of the hotel and be on TV!
The hotel has EVERYTHING that you need: restaurants, shops, souvenirs, bakery, snacks, concierge, tickets, fitness center, computers in the business center, and much more.
The rooms are large, luxurious and extremely comfortable. The staff is extremely friendly, polite and accommodating. Check in time is 3 p.m., my early flight into JFK placed me in the hotel at 10 a.m. and they still let me check in to my room! I was able to secure my belongings, freshen up and head out to explore the sights with no problem. Now that's service!
Again, if you're pondering whether to stay here or not because of the price, take the plunge, splurge and treat yourself to the New York Marriott Marquis ... it'll be the best investment and experience you've ever made!

For those of you who know Japan, you know that building materials are not designed with soundproofing in mind. The Japanese, especially those who live in the big cities, try to be respectful and relatively quiet. This is a hotel built with that in mind.
I don't think the walls are actually paper-thin as they felt solid, but you can hear everything in the next room. From the bathroom, you can hear everything going on in a neighboring bathroom. There were times when I opened my eyes, startled, because I could swear someone else was standing behind me. There wasn't. It was just an ordinary conversation from one of the surrounding rooms. People weren't being inconsiderate. It was just that this hotel is so poorly constructed that whatever passes for walls here seems to amplify sound rather than deaden it.
When I asked the woman at the front desk if there was a room with soundproofing, she complained about overly-sensitive people. Maybe I am when it comes to sound, but I don't want to hear my neighbor using the toilet. I don't want to hear every single word of a conversation in a nearby room. They know this hotel was poorly built, and it's a good value if you're used to hearing your neighbors.
Hotel Kabuki is in San Francisco's small Japantown, which is a nest of restaurants (many quite good) and shops with goods (some manufactured in the area, but many in Japan) you can't find elsewhere. It isn't that convenient to other parts of San Francisco, but public transportation is reasonable. You can self-park in the Japantown lot, which goes under the hotel, but be careful of the hourly rates in the middle of the day. The hotel quotes only the daily rate of $22.

I recently stayed at this hotel back in January. Supposedly the hotel is under renovation. I stayed in a room that wasn't renovated, was quite dated in fact. The smell in the room was musty, the gym was ancient. Overall the hotel does not deserve at 4 star rating. The location, however is excellent. I stay in New York every 2 weeks at 4 star hotels and I can tell you that this one does not compare favorably.

title_masked: Nice hotel, just expect a 7am wake up
text_masked: Nice hotel, friendly staff (even if they will be waking you up the next morning at 7am with loud hailers and cow bells!), great rooms, great location. Hopefully the dispute will sort itself out but if you are not an early riser then I would avoid this one and any hotel in close proximity without really good double glazing to block out the noise that lasts about an hour, there are easily at least 2 hotels that must suffer as well.

Great hotel centrally placed in Midtown. Clean and good rooms. We stayed here for several nights with family and friends. The hotel is value for money. The rooms are pleasent and good. Extremely many airlines have their employees staying at the hotel. Close to Empire state, Penn station and Macy's. Also close to Times Square and close enough to central park. We stau+yed at the hotel during the hy\urricane Sandy and the presidential election. Memorable days and an exiting vacation in New York City. The marathon - however - was cancelled.

title_masked: GREAT STAFF!!! FRIENDLY AND HELPFULL... AND THE FREE SHUTTLE SERVICE IS AWESOME!! THEY TAKE YOU AND PICK YOU UP FREE!
text_masked: .very good staff and friendly.. free shutle service for some near places from hotel.

We have just returned from our visit and I truely can't say enough good about this hotel and especially the managment there. 
We got a really great rate so we booked there and shortly after our booking I got an e-mail from the hotel offering to help us plan our stay there with all kind of suggestions. I replied to the e-mail asking for information about some discount we were looking for and received apersonal message back and asking if there was anything else I needed.
We had to arrive very late but that was not a problem at all. 
Our rooms were always very clean. The shuttle service was a very nice bonus. We were having a wonderful time there when I got an emergency message that I needed to come home at once. It was around six or so in the evening and the manager was very understanding and gave us half off of our rooms 
We would definately stay at this hotel again and highly reccomend it.

As a woman traveling alone, arriving well past midnight, and without a reservation, I was pleasantly surprised to come across the Dolphin Motel. The staff was warm and welcoming, even in the middle of the night. Close to the airport and centrally located, the property is well maintained and rooms are very clean. This is definitely a no-frills motel with rooms on the smaller side, but adequate for the price. They offer free high-speed internet access and provide coffee, muffins, fruit, etc. each morning. I highly recommend this property for those looking for a good value.

I stayed at the La Quinta inn for 2 nights. The hotel is very close to the airport. You could walk to the airport. Approximetly a 10 minute walk. 15 minutes to the train , airport to downtown.
Get the unlimited day pass ticket. It's not a big price difference in price and you can ride as much as you want for the day. A few restuarants near the property. Good places to eat. As for the hotel. Like I said close to the airport. Staff was nice. Breakfast was ok . Usual breads, waffles, oatmeal and juice. As for the rooms Let me say it was ok. From a scale 1 to 10 I give it a 6.7. When I walked into the room I looked at the bed and there was a huge stain on the pillow. I had housekeeping change it . The A/C was a bit noisey at night,but I do have to say the beds were comforable. I did sleep decent. As for the bathroom nothing great ,just average. Good cable,and internet was downstair adjacent to the checkin desk with a printer. That was useful because we checked-in for our flight and had our tickets in hand. For $65 per night to me it was ok . Nothing great,but price was right. If I came back to Seattle agian if I had to stay here I would ,but if there was another place with a better deal comparible to the location (like the hampton inn, or raddison). I would stay there instead, if the price was right.

I stayed at Homewood Suites Phoenix Airport South for one night in July 2012. The hotel is easy to find, just off I-10.
I checked in on a quiet Saturday afternoon. The check-in was quick but quite unenthusiastic -- even for commonly unenthusiastic Finnish standards. The hotel is still pretty new, and everything seems to be in good shape.
My room was standard Homewood fare, spacious and nice. Everything was clean and in good shape.
Except for the guest laundry I did not use any of the hotel facilities, so no comments about them.

title_masked: For overnight near the airport, an OK place
text_masked: I was one of many travelers staying overnight to be near LAX for an early morning flight. I chose this hotel because it was close to the airport, within walking distance of the rental car return, and had a 24-hour airport shuttle. The good points are (a) the price was reasonable compared to the other hotel chain properties nearby; (b) the staff was pleasant and welcoming, (c) the rooms are adequate and comfortable with free wifi, and (d) the hotel is one of a half dozen that sponsor a single shuttle that runs every 15 minutes or so and on which this was the last stop before the airport. The hotel restaurant did not look particularly inviting, so I had a light meal in the bar, Brewster's. This bar boasts 100 or so beers, and has a good selection of wines by the glass. It is easy to fall into informal conversation with other travelers and that was fun, so I talked to couples from Dallas and London, England, respectively. All in all, I would stay here again on an overnight visit. For longer stays, definitely not -- Marina del Rey and Santa Monica beckon one down to the water.

We booked this hotel through Priceline and got a great rate. We were told about the $32/day parking rate when we called to request a specific type of room. For some reason we were not charged for the parking when we checked out which was a great surprise. The hotel is right off the I5 on Mission Bay, and is literally 5 minutes from Sea World. There is a free shuttle to Sea World that the hotel offers and we took advantage of it to save on the $17 parking fee at Sea World. The room was a nice size and included a fridge and a large flat screen tv, however the tv signal is still not High Def. The room was clean and the beds were comfortable. The pool area is great, and the pool is heated. The only complaint I have is there was no wifi in the room, there was an Ethernet cable for internet but it was useless with an ipad. There is free wifi in the lobby, pool and conference area and the connection speed was good. The staffs were friendly and accommodating. I would recommend this hotel for families looking to be near Sea World.

Just returned from a trip to the big apple and truly enjoyed our stay at the Barclay. We were in a king-bed junior suite which was large by NY standards. The room was very clean and well-maintained. Our only complaint was the attitude of one of the men working the concierge desk. He did not want to help us and instead of offering to make reservations for us, told us how to do it. The others were very helpful. All in all a great stay and we highly recommend this hotel.

The motel is located on a freeway frontage road, and a bit trickly to get to. Our GPS could not find it, nor did it tell us which exit to take. When you venture out, you are always looping around the freeway and there is a lot of traffic, even on weeknds. The rooms were generally clean, although I did find dust behind the nightstand and gooey spilled soda on the nightstand. There are not enough outlets so I had to plug and unplug items in order to plug in my laptop. The wi-fi was horrible. When it worked it was fine, but it often did not work at all. Our TV barely worked. Some channels were perfect and other had so much fuzziness in the picture that they were not watchable. The people above us were literally running back and forth in their room for over an hour. I called the front desk to complain. The noise stopped, but only briefly. The free continental breakfast is average. There's a Wal-Mart nearby. The motel is in an area of chain restaurants galore, but most are not within walking distance. But for the money, it's really not all that bad. It was half of the price of similar motels that I had just stayed at in Austin.

title_masked: last night of a business travel
text_masked: Quite easy to reach by car from the motorways of the area, parking service for some dollars. The building seems new, absolutely comfortable and warmful look. Located near to pedestrian walks, 15 minutes walking to Beale Street. We went there with no reservation, but fortunately no problem. Clean rooms and very fine new furniture, the bathroom as well. Not exactly the cheapest, but absolutely in line with the overall quality services. All people has been gentle.

My friends and I met in Chicago for a weekend away and stayed at the Intercontinental. I'm so glad my friend found this place. The location cannot be beat! Right on the magnificent mile and we could walk just about everywhere (including the Sears tower). The rooms were a bit on the small side (why would you spend much time in your room in such an awesome city), but very nice and clean. The concierge was AMAZING and so helpful with restaurant recommendations and sightseeing options. I will definitely stay here again on my next trip to Chicago!

Californians are unique and wonderful people who live in a world full of beauty and great weather. Explore it. You won't be disappointed.
Next time, I will bring the woman of my dreams, and it will be perfect. I was there for a 
conference, but my California friends were wonderful. I'll be back.

title_masked: Great Motel No Matter What Your Reason for visiting San Francisco.
text_masked: We stay at this motel anytime we come to SF if is available. Our trips to SF the last few years have been because my husband is going to the UCSF cancer hospital on Diversidero. We originally chose it for location. We come back because of the service. These trips can be stressful & we want them to be as enjoyable as possible. We love SF & want to keep that feeling about SF. We are always treated well by the staff. We have stayed as little as one night & 3 times for a week, so we have met most of the staff - they are great people. We will keep our fingers crossed that they have a vacancy each of our coming visits to SF.

I stayed here off and on for several weeks while a loved one recovered in an area hospital. The staff was friendly and gracious. The room was large with a refrigerator and microwave. The bed was so comfortable it was hard to get up. The unique decor of the room made my stay very pleasant. I felt warm and cozy, not cramped. The guest laundry made my life easier during my long stay. The machines were kept in good working condition, and the area was kept clean and tidy. Free breakfast every day! I'm not talking a bagel or doughnut, there was bacon, sausage, eggs, waffles, biscuits and gravy, etc.., it was wonderful.

We stayed 4 nights in room 503. We had a queen bed, loveseat sleeper sofa, a desk area (no chair). We felt the room was very comfortable for the two of us, had our teenage son on a couple of nights and then that felt a little cramped. Truth is, we don't spend a lot of time in the room, so not a huge impact. Our room was more the mid-size type (not the smallest or largest.......just like Goldilocks!). There is no door man, no pool, no workout facility. There are 2 computers and a printer for guest use.
Breakfast was simple: coffee, orange juice, donuts, bagels, fresh fruit, and instant oatmeal.
We did not have a car and used mass transit. It was a surprisingly easy ride on the T from Logan airport. We arrived late into the city and the cab line was so long we figured we would use the train as the wait time seemed to be longer than the train ride. Easy! We arrived at the hotel in about 25 minutes (Copley Station).
The location of the hotel is really great. I had friends recommend the hotel but when I read reviews of the small rooms, I didn't want to even try staying here. The price made it seem like a "too good to be true" type thing. I tried making a reservation at other hotels and the $4-500 rates were painful! I figured I would give this a try and am glad I did.
The bar area was lively hosting a birthday party one night. Personable bartenders with great recommendations for area restaurants, etc. The front desk staff always friendly and helpful. 
My only negative is that we had noisy neighbors and the room and hall noises could be intrusive. For example, I could hear the rumble of the vacuum cleaner in the room above. On a positive note, no street noise--but we didn't have a view of it either. Our room was right across from the elevator.
I would stay again, book earlier, and explore options. At the time we booked, not many available.

From the moment my son and I arrived at the Back Bay Hilton, we were treated like family. The staff could not have been more helpful. They were constantly giving us upgrades, asking about our stay, and making our visit to Boston more enjoyable. It was a perfect location for our Berklee College of Music visit. I will always stay here when visiting my son at Berklee. (just a note: it is less expensive to book and pay online upfront, rather than using the Berklee code for a discount)

after reading the reveiws on here i was wary of what i might find ect. but i was pleasently surprised.
the hotel was clean, loved the location as it was near little italy and the famous "katz deli" (where harry met sally" the most fantastic food i have ever eaten and the subway was pretty much opposite. the staff were lovely. bit of 70's decor but was absolutly fine. people are far to picky for a budget hotel, will be coming back xx

We loved his hotel the room was very nicely decorated and the bed was very comfy, the views to the ocean were great and the night view of the city was amazing. The employees were very friendly and willing to help you. I truly look forward to our next visit. This is the only hotel I would consider staying at in San Diego.

hotel clean and relatively easy to get to; right off I-17N @Thunderbird Rd; friendly welcome, comfortable snacks
Free am buffet
Cons: not enough table space to eat breakfast; breakfast too many carbs
would likely stay here again

We recently spent 4 nights at this hotel. It's incredibly well located, the staff couldn't be nicer and more helpful and we were upgraded to a wonderful room. 
Unfortunately, the air conditioning in our room was not working properly - it was quite warm. Not bad enough to move to another room which the hotel offered, but definitely not comfortable. Each day we asked them to fix it and they said they would. We went three days like this and finally, on Day 3 it was fixed. If it could be fixed on Day 3, it could have been fixed on Day 1.
Also, we stayed at this hotel specifically so my wife could swim. They have a modest sized pool that met her needs. Unfortunately it closed of maintenance half way through our stay. So, just unfortunate timing for us.
On the other hand, the staff was incredibly helpful when I discovered I had left one of our suitcases on the baggage carousel at LGA, in making restaurant reservations at some of the top restaurants in the city, directions, etc.
While we chalked this up to back luck, the bottom line is that we will stay elsewhere next trip.

The Palomar consistently exceeds all of my expectations and their attention to detail continues to surprise me on each visit. The staff is attentive and the level of service is commendable. The week of my stay they contacted me to see if there was anything that they could do to assist me with my trip. Their timing was perfect and the Palomar was able to make dinner reservations for me prior to my arrival. This saved me time and left a favorable impression on me. The King Spa suite is worth the extra expense. I appreciate how quiet the rooms are when compared to other hotels in the area. The roof top terrace is a find! Sable restaurant has a great atmosphere and the fresh sorbets are worth the visit. The server recommended the apricot and mint combinations, and I can not stop thinking about it! I also recommend stopping by the wine tasting that they offer. It is a great way to start out the evening. The elevators can get crowded during peak times so allow a few extra minutes. I will be staying there again at the end of June and will post an update. I highly recommend the Palomar!

My husband and I stayed at The Buckminister for three nights earlier this month. While not in the immediate downtown area, the location is great for Fenway, and very close to the T, which will get you anywhere in the city quickly and easily.
We were upgraded to a king suite after having reserved a queen room. This was a nice plus, which was appreciated. Having stayed in the suite, we realized that a regular room was probably rather small.
The bed was comfy, the pillows were not ( no down or feather pillows available). Breakfast was continental, and nothing to write home about.
The Buckminster, however, is a good value in a city of very pricey accommodations. If you stay there, try UNO right next door for great pizza or just a drink and friendly helpful service.

Flew in to NYC from Friday until Sunday, Club Quarters was easily accessible by the M train from NYC Penn Station - subway right around the corner. VERY central area - beautiful spot in Rockefeller Center, Magnolia Bakery, Saks 5th Avenue, TD Bank, pharmacy/grocery. 
The hotel attendants were efficient, friendly and the process of checking in and out was quick, and while check out is at 12 p.m., you are allowed to store your baggage and collect it later in the day. 
Clean, smaller rooms but perfect for couples or traveling yourself. Was VERY pleased to see an iron + ironing board. 
Would highly recommend and stay again - who stays in the hotel room while they're visiting NYC anyway?

My husband, 9 year old child and I went to Phoenix for Spring Training and stayed at the Hilton. What a great family hotel! Our suite was on the 4th floor with our balcony over looking one of the pools. The suite was very nice...wish it had a small microwave, but it did have a refrigerator which came in handy. They also charged for internet in the room..which I think should be included. The entire staff was very nice. The first morning I asked house keeping for extra cream and sugar for coffee, and everyday after that they put a few extra in our room without having to ask. The RIVER RANCH is awesome! The waterpark complex is very nice! My son just loved it...so did we. The lazy river was great. We ate at several of their restaurants....really liked the Hole In The Wall. We will for sure stay here again next year! I can't say enough about the place! I am a flight attendant for a major airline and have traveled many places. GREAT family resort!!!

I love this hotel and this location. Great friendly staff... in a perfect location. EVEN though a fire interrupted our stay. The whole weekend was perfect. We used the location for biking, walking and enjoyed the people we met along the way.
 I plan on going back as soon as possible!

title_masked: great for a simple, reliable stay in New York
text_masked:
I stayed at Hotel Indigo, Chelsea for 2 nights (Feb. 6-8) 
It was a business trip. In a nutshell: it is an excellent hotel. 
I always wanted to try it out but the price was not right; finally I got an incredible deal for it on Priceline. I really like this area (we call it Chelsea hotel row, between 24th and 29th st) - it is quieter and to my taste, nicer than any other hotel areas in the city – and everything is nearby.
The hotel is well furnished, with good bathroom supplies. Free New York Times and USA today. The rooms are clean, everything was spotless. As a former New Yorker I thought the rooms were of a decent size – so was surprised to read the comments about small size rooms. People should understand that many new hotels (incl. those between 24th and 29th) were built on the place of old buildings, meaning they could go as high as designed but not wider. But for those who can compare - It definitely at least twice bigger than the basic room in Paramount or Hudson ( which are small, even by New York standard)
Really like the fact that they provided cork-screw ( it’s my pet-peeve in all the other hotels where you cannot find it). 
Couple negative comments: as in all Chelsea hotels, the elevator is really small – so in a rush hour, you might end up waiting for a longer time ( but it is not as bad as in nearby Holiday Inn, where we ended up walking up and down 12th floor basically every time we had to use the elevator)
The ice machine is in the basement, by the workout room – so if you are on the upper floor, you have to use the elevator (see my previous comment).
And my final negative comment has nothing to do with the services – there are (or, at least were) 2 dead palm trees at the entrance to the hotel. Ugly dead, fitting for a compost pile - not for an entrance to a hotel. The person who takes care of the plants should know that it is go below freezing in NYC and the palm trees do not tolerate freezing temperatures. But what makes it so weird is the fact that the hotel is in the flower district – right across from it they sell healthy palm trees (and more). 
But again, it has nothing to do with the services inside the hotel. 
My advice won’t be about the hotel - it is about the dining options in the area. Don’t get upset by a poor choice right by the hotel. If you walk just couple blocks east there will be a lot of great places (Eataly one of them). Another thing that we love doing when we stay in Chelsea area – go to Whole Foods on 24th & 7th and get some oysters - they shuck them for free; and their salad bar is always a great place to go when you want something good but have no time for a proper dinner.

I often stay here while traveling on business. Its always quiet, the staff is friendly and the building sits off to itself, so there is no foot traffic to speak of in the parking lot except for guests. My room is clean, and the A\C is kicking. The breakfast here is top notch, hot and plentiful.

Thanks to all the staff for our last stay.Too many people to mention for all of the fun we had.But thank you Romeo for my b_Day Present,And always thanks to Yolanda,Jeff and Sherman,The ODonnells will be back their soon..

We stopped in San Antonio on our cross country move to Houston. We had been staying in Drury Inns all along the way (combine the dogs-stay-free policy with the free breakfast and cocktail hour, we never really thought about staying anywhere else!). All Drury Inns have a very upscale feel to them, but the Drury Plaza has a really great vibe to it from the moment you walk into the lobby. The location is perfect, as the River Walk is right outside the hotel doors. And the views from the rooftop pool are absolutely amazing. But those are all just added extras to outstanding customer service you will get at this hotel. My husband put it perfectly when he said, "they make you feel like you are someone important." Every one you come in contact with is eager to help make your stay more enjoyable. The entire staff is personable, helpful, and committed to going above and beyond. From now on, any time we travel, we will be looking to stay at a Drury Inn.

I will say first that due to mixed reviews, we chose the Cova as they listed airport transportation #1 on their amenities list. NOT!! They do offer shuttles to several locations but not the airport. Since we booked thru Hotels.com, I contacted them and they gave us a credit for $60 to cover the shuttle cost. You can book Super Shuttle for $30 for 2. When we arrived, the staff was extremely friendly and helpful. The room is clean, quiet and the rooftop deck has expansive views and is quite lovely. We did venture out in the afternoon and must agree this area is a little dicey ---motel 6 has people hanging around out front on chairs, etc. We were never harrassed, etc. Got a sidewalk referral for a Thai restaurant which turned out to be very good - Osha Thai at Leavenworth & Geary - a short walk from the hotel. At night I think any large city has opportunities for disaster. Also, we thought the complimentary breakfast was very good, cereal, waffles, fresh fruit, cheese, cold cuts, oatmeal, juices, boiled eggs, etc.

Really enjoyed my stay with the Omni for 3 nights. This is one of the kids friendly Hotel. The handed over wonderful gifts to my son.
Will surely come back ...Great location ,excellent service and the bed was excellent too..Felt nice to rest after a ,long exhaustive day in NCY

This hotel was more reasonable than many in New York while still being clean, even a bit funky. The crowd at the hotel was both younger and a bit international, and the overall feel of the hotel was a bit upscale hostel. The rooms, as the name suggests, compact. We had a full, if tiny, bathroom in the room, but some rooms have the WC down the hall. If sharing the room, make sure you're there with a friend or a loved one, as the space is small. Indeed, the clouded glass doors can either cover the bathroom or help shield the glass in front of the shower, but not both. We were also a bit disappointed that the front desk seemed to dismiss our mentioning of leaking AC unit.

title_masked: QUITE NICE STAY AND CONVIENIENT FOR CRUISE DEPARTURE - GREAT FOLLOW UP CUSTOMER SERVICE
text_masked:
We had two nights at the Fairmont prior to departing on a cruise to Alaska Late Jun.
The Hotel is conveniently located in the centre of the city and only 10 mins walk from the Celebrity cruise terminal (5 min taxi).
The Hotel foyer is delightful with magnificent fresh flower displays, sitting area and Grand Piano - which was lovely to hear in the evening whilst having a post dinner coffee. We stayed in Washington DC for 5 nights and overall the standard of the rooms and beds were very good. Breakfast was well catered for and the quality was very good,but do not have an evening in the restaurant as after coming down to go out one night it was torrential rain and we had been out sightseeing all day we were convinced by the restaurant manager to dine at the hotel. $80 dollars later for 2 starters and one main we left within 30 minutes as the waitress was so over powering and the food was so awful! We did complain but to no avail!
As long as you never eat in the restaurant the hotel is clean, efficient and fantastically placed for all the sights in Washington DC.

The Omni is a nice property near the riverwalk in Jacksonville. It is very comfortable and the decor is lovely. It is quite pricey and not a good value. Breakfast was $17 in the hotel restaurant. Really! This is Jacksonville, Fl, not New York. I won't be doing this again.

Doubletree's slogan is "Where the little things mean everything." While their intent is surely to imply that their attention to detail offers a superior hotel experience, it should be noted that the converse is also true. When little things are overlooked over and over again, it adds up to a pretty annoying stay. 
Start with arrival: 4 women on a trip carry a lot of luggage. We pulled up to the front so that we could unload our bags prior to parking the car. My friend went inside and took the elevator up to the lobby to request a bellhop. The person behind the desk pointed to a luggage cart and said "You can use this." 
So, after tipping my friend $10 for loading the bags, we went to park the car. The facade of the hotel is on S. Front Street in Columbus. That is where you enter. On the same block, just down the street, is a parking garage, which one would assume is where guests at the Doubletree would park. Being the only parking garage anywhere near the hotel, we parked. When we entered the elevator and saw no indication of buttons leading to a hotel lobby, we figured out we were at the wrong place. We headed down to street level and walked up the block to the hotel entrance. Doubletree's defense, the parking garage had no signage indicating that it was Doubletree parking. In our defense, it had no signage indicating that it wasn't. We later find out the the ACTUAL Doubletree parking is in fact around the corner from the entrance, not just down the street from the entrance. Here is where a sign at the main entrance stating "DOUBLETREE PARKING AROUND THE CORNER" would have been most helpful. 
Upon check in we neither asked for, nor received the signature chocolate chip cookie that Doubletree hangs its hat on. Our room was a decent suite, with the bedding being the most stand-out feature of the room. The outlets were poorly accessible, with an outlet in the lamp base nearly shorting out my phone. There were ample towels and the room appeared clean, if not a bit dated. 
The next morning we pulled out of the (wrong) parking garage and were asked for our parking voucher from the hotel. What parking voucher? Exactly. I imagine our chocolate chip cookies were somewhere wrapped in the parking voucher. We paid the full price and decided to deal with the parking issue upon our return, as we had an appointment to get to. 
Upon return to the hotel, we went to the front desk to rectify the parking snafu. The woman explained that we should have asked for the voucher when we checked in. We explained that they should have presented the voucher to us (along with the cookies) when we checked in. Sensing a stalemate, the clerk waived the parking fee for the prior night and presented us with the necessary parking vouchers for the following day. 
But what about the cookies? As we wrapped up the parking predicament, a cookie sounded like a delicious idea. Lamenting diplomatically that we had "missed out" on the cookies the night before, would the clerk mind providing some now. Oh if only she could. We're out of cookies, she said with a shrug. See, here is where a little thing like "...but I'll be sure to send some up to your room as soon as we get more!" would mean everything. No. We're out of cookies. When we expressed disbelief that a hotel chain that features said cookie prominently on it's literature, in its ads, and on its website would be unable to provide the lure, the clerk shrugged again and said "People kill for those cookies." I'm not sure if that was meant to be an explanation as to why there were no cookies, or a hint as to how we could procure some for ourselves. At any rate, no cookie. 
The next morning at checkout, the lobby was a buzz of hysteria. Apparently, there had been a rash of break-ins in the (right) Doubletree parking lot. Windshields smashed, property stolen, glass everywhere. The clerk (same one from the previous night, clearly on a 48 hour shift) seemed dejected, but not defeated. She remained calm, cool, and polite, even as we four parking perpetrators approached her station to check out. Her only concern was whether we too had been broken into. We hadn't. She heaved a sigh of relief, checked us out, and handed over 4 chocolate chip cookies. Still warm.

Great location on Michigan Avenue, close to everything downtown Chicago. The concierge guys are very helpful - great suggestions for food and activity and how to get around.
You can walk to the Bears game and in the other direction to the Magnificent Mile. In addition the El Station is nearby. Will be going back again very soon.

I have been at this Hotel in the past and never had any bad experiences with the Hotel or with the Room. 
My niece and I were there for a Bridal shower in March. The room was okay. Inside room. Shower handle was broken, we were missing the toilet paper holder, but they did bring that up. The Front Desk Hotel Clerk -Ellen- was exceptional. She is an assett to this Hotel. It was a pleasure having her as a person to speak too.
Kathy

We have just returned home today from a 3 night 4 day trip to New York and must say The Crowne Plaza Manhatten ticked all of the boxes. We travelled as a family of 4 and had a lovely
room on 31st floor. We stayed in room 3105 and had a view of Times Square. The room was beautiful with two good size double beds that were the most comfortable we have ever had in a hotel. The bathroom was also immaculate which is a must for me.
The position of the Crowne Plaza is perfect as its right in the middle of all the action in TimesSquare. Ever single one of the staff are very helpful and professional. We loved Andaz San Diego! The Interior design details throughout the property are so unique and lovely. Our personal assistants, especially Tom, were courteous and helpful. Our room was perfect, we enjoyed the complimentary snacks and beverages and enjoyed the signature cocktails in the lounge. The Ivy nightclub was not open as we stayed on a Tuesday night so the hotel was very quiet. The rooftop deck was beautiful and we had the entire space to ourselves late at night. Andaz was the perfect hotel to enjoy our big night out without kids! Adult date night success!

Expectations were too high to deliver. The grand entrance and lobby were spectacular; old world charm with a warm and inviting character- such a shame this didn't carry through to the rooms. Our room was musty and quite small, nearly no room between the two queen beds and the wall paper needed serious restoration or replacement. We did request extra conditioner - delivered promptly, free of charge and wrapped in a cute little posy. At the bar we females sat, drank and promptly left after my mother-in-law received inappropriate advances from a resident and staff.

title_masked: Pursuit of Happyness in the Tenderloin?
text_masked:
Okay I've stayed in SF numerous times, so when I was looking for a deal, the Cova was the winner.and it was no suprise for me about the neighborhood. The Cova site listed the hotel $18 more than Bookit.com, when I asked if they would match the price, they did. Here's what's good for this sometime budget traveller: 1) Room rate and room decor, 2) valet parking $25-cheap by SF stds, 3) Breakfast included-adequate if really going on the cheap-I opted out but it does have nice city views on the 8th floor. There is a large outdoor space there as well with tables that you later go up and relax or picnic up there.
Here's a couple things I didn't care for: 1)Needed earplugs as my room was right over where the cars are dropped off for valet parking and the people arriving late at night could easily be heard in the hallway. 2)Wanted to rent in room movies and when I didn't see it on the menu, I asked 2 of the hotel staff it they were available and they were unable to answer whether the hotel had it-apparently no.
This is the Tenderloin and what does that mean to people who aren't familiar with SF? It means this is the area where homeless, drug addicts and the disinfranchise inhabit. Glide Memorial Church is several blocks down the street with their overnight shelter and soup kitchen where the aforementioned people line up. For a visual, view Will Smith's "Pursuit of Happyness" based a true story of a man who was homeless for a year. Mixed in with this population are people with families who you see shopping, out with their children, living life in the Tenderloin.
I didn't stay out late but had no problems. I was asked several times for money but had no problems when I declined. (I have had far more rude responses around Union Square from the pan handlers there than the people asking for money on my sojourn thru the streets of the Tenderloin.)
For those who love Asian food, turn left as you leave the hotel and go down 1 block to "Little Sagion" on Larkin St. Numerous restaurants for the budget conscience. Lee's Sandwiches make delicious Vietnamese sandwiches and other deli items that can be eaten there or be taken out for picnics elsewhere e.g. the Cova Rooftop! The Asian Art Museum is also on Larkin St. There is a movie theater at Larkin and Polk St. Didn't see Starbucks close but lotsa different coffee shops up on Polk St
Here's the bottom line, lots of inexpensive restaurants of different ethnicity in the area. 
SF has many homeless who seem to congregate in this area, but did not threaten this traveler. I do agee with a prior review that recommends going down Geary St and turning on Hyde St to access hotel instead of travelling down Ellis St.or O'farrell St. Also, I have done quite a bit of walking and dress down so I don't look touristy and helps with not being asked for money..
If you are a first time visitor to SF, I would not reccomend this hotel due to the neighborhood ,not necessarily because of safety issues, but because I think especially for a first time visit,it is more fun staying closer to the action of Union Square, Chinatown, Cable Cars etc. 
If you are a repeat visitor and get a deal, it might be interesting to experience a different part of the city. When I first started coming to SF, I stayed in the Wharf area or Union Sqaure, but is has been fun to explore other areas of the city that aren't so touristy.

My husband and I spent three nights at the Omni to celebrate our 25th anniversary. We splurged on a suite on the 17th floor; it was very spacious, and so nice to have a separate bedroom and "living" room. The room was spotlessly clean and all the appointments were "just so": plush, over-sized towels; soft sheets; lots of pillows; etc. 
The service there is impeccable: from the friendly doormen to the solicitous & knowledgeable front desk folks to the housekeeping staff, everyone was nice and bent over backwards to make our stay enjoyable and stress-free. The hair dryer in our bathroom didn't work; we called downstairs & they brought us a new one within 10 minutes. At checkout, we mentioned we were catching the train home, and they offered us a complimentary copy of the Sunday New York Times. 
The only thing I didn't like was that our room was dark. Up on the 17th floor, the windows are small, set with deep sills, & high up on the wall. As an architectural element, it looks cool. But as a lighting element, it's not that great. You could also hear a lot of street noise in the middle of the night, even way up there. I couldn't help wondering if the windows weren't single-paned, as it surprised me that the construction noise from next door was so audible. Ear plugs helped.
But we didn't spend that much time in the room, as the whole city was awaiting us downstairs. We splurged on dinner at La Folie -- oh, my God, what an experience! -- and spent the rest of the weekend walking all over. We used to live in SF but had never "vacationed" there. It was such a thrill, and staying at the Omni such a good decision.

title_masked: Good location; was not treated like a Platinum member
text_masked: I guess I'm used to being treated well at Holiday Inn sites when I check in because I'm a platinum member. Though this is not like any other HI I've been to where the staff is always great, the staff at the front desk here was not very nice when I checked in. They were not great when we had breakfast the next day either. All that being said, this is a terrific location that is really within a mile and a half of whatever you need. I ran along the water and it was beautiful. The work our room is better than most. The amenities at this location are more overpriced than other locations so be sure to not forget anything (the deoderant I bought was the worst in overcharging). Bare minimum in amenties in the rooms so don't forget your conditioner or mouthwash. Also, there is no safe so don't bring those valuables.

Stayed in this hotel for 3 nights in May, on arrival we were upgraded, room was great clean, modern, spacious for NYC and even had a little kitchen. Location of the hotel is perfect if you are getting the train for newark airport, penn station is straight over the road, lots of places are within walking distance, though lovely and quiet in the hotel, couldnt hear any noise in the room and comfy beds, great sleep!

I thoroughly enjoyed my stay at the Liberty in Boston. Very friendly and helpful staff. Loved the glass of champagne they poured for me at check-in. The room was super comfortable and quiet. Bathroom was large and luxurious. Public spaces were great. Friendly bartender. Incredible views of Boston and Cambridge. I love the location, but I am familiar with Boston. I can see how out-of-towners might be confused with the driving in this part of town. Just park once. The location is so convenient that you can reach everything on foot or on the subway. Suggestion - I skipped the $42 valet parking, and parked on my own at the Mass General garage a few steps away, which was very reasonably priced. I will definitely go back to the Liberty.

It has only been a week since our trip to San Diego over the Thanksgiving holiday and a promise I made myself was to be sure to do a review on Trip Advisor. I am not often that ambitious about doing so but this is a hotel worth trying if you are heading to San Diego. The setting is gorgeous along the San Diego Bay - upgrade to a higher floor and ask to be on the Bayfront. Our view was stunning as we overlooked the Bay, the bridge to Coronado, and the Embarcadero. The hotel staff was absolutely incredible. Who expects that your wait servers would be as sweet and caring as Carmelita who served us in the Vela restaurant twice. Such a wonderful, kind lady who actually took time to make us feel at home. Our bell men and concierge services were equally impressive - always taking time to reach out, assure we had directions, assistance and a few laughs, too. Whoever is managing this hotel has found the right formula... kudos to them for making sure that you have outgoing, friendly employees. Even the FedX shipping clerk was kind and helpful. The hotel food at Vela was delicious... specialty pastries, wonderful breakfast buffet with an omelette chef who cares about his customers and was also engaging and a great chef. We enjoyed sitting outside by the firepit area which is an added bonus on cool evenings when you just want to prolong the wonderful San Diego weather (70 degrees). I can't say enough about this hotel and would recommend it in a heart beat. Go there, walk up to Seaport Village, eat at the wonderful restaurants, tour the USS Midway, take advantage of a Segway tour (we did and that was terrific as well -Another Side of San Diego, go to the Safari Park, La Jolla - especially the hiking at Torrey Pines State Reserve, visit the Zoo, take a harbor cruise) - it will be the best vacation ever.

title_masked: A Beautiful and Unique Baltimore Hotel!
text_masked: I can't say enough about our stay at the Hotel Monaco in Baltimore. Housed in the beautiful B&O Railroad headquarters building, the incredible architecture alone makes staying here worthwhile. Add to that a well appointed, clean, spacious room with high ceilings, a marble bathroom, and truly comfortable bed. The staff here are very accommodating and eager to please without being overbearing. Breakfast at the restaurant was excellent, a nice atmosphere with good food and service. The hotel is within walking distance to the Inner Harbor and Camden Yards. We will most definitely return to the Hotel Monaco!

Location is great - especially if you want to take the family to Navy Pier (or the beach in summer). Rooms are typical 'W'. The opening between the bathroom and sleeping area is a combo of 'chic' and slightly odd. Views are great. Parking is expensive, but it is Chicago. Pool is great. Has a deep end and was warm - even in February. Kids voted it their favorite hotel pool in Chicago (and we've done almost all of them). All around great hotel. The difference maker here is the staff. Everyone that I have dealt with in my multiple stays has been friendly and helpful. I would put the staff close to the Ritz or Peninsula, but the W is a fraction of the cost. If there were a measure for "service/dollar", this hotel would be tops in Chicago. I don't know how others reviewers could have had issue with the staff - I think it's more an indication of them, not the hotel.

title_masked: Very snazzy place that isn't too expensive.
text_masked:
Rooms were very big and modern. Lobby and lounge were so much fun and very well decorated. Very close to food, bars and short cab rides anywhere in the city. Very cool place to stay.
I met Young Jeezy in the lobby of this hotel. :)

title_masked: Very Dated and could use renovation
text_masked:
I stayed at this property for an entire week for a convention. When I checked in, I asked for a room NOT on the west side of the building and a king bed (which is what I reserved). When I got to my room in the FURTHEST tower on the very back of the property, my room was full on afternoon sun, two queen beds and with a view of an open trash area and the parking garage. 
The room was very dated, but it was clean. I will give them that. The carpets had been recently cleaned and during my stay they vacuumed every day. Housekeeping did a nice job. 
The property is very spaced out as it is a resort type, but truthfully just needs to be updated. The grounds themselves were decent, but if I stayed again for this convention, I would definitely not stay in one of the towers.

title_masked: Great location, Free Wine Reception, Great staff
text_masked:
Great hotel. I have stayed here several times this past year. My room accomodations have included the King Deluxe, Double Double Deluxe and the King Premier room. (The King Premier room is larger and my favorite to date...but it does cost more.) Allegro has 2 onsite restaurants/bars, 312 and Encore. Both are nice but I prefer 312 which has a more refined atmosphere where Encore has a nightclub vibe.
Pros: Great downtown location. Free wine reception in the lobby from 5-6. Staff is super. Great hotel for business travel. 
Cons: Rooms are on the small side (although not a huge con because who hangs out in their rooms when there are so many cool things to see and do in Chicago?!), small bathrooms, the walls are thin so you can sometimes hear guests and the TV from adjoining room (I downloaded a free "white noise" app on my iphone which helps with this issue.) No pool.
Tip: Be sure to join the (free) Kimpton InTouch Guest Loyalty program which allows you to have free internet service at the Allegro and other Kimpton hotels.

I have stayed at this hotel numerous times and nothing changes, it is first class top to bottom. Great location for the George R Brown convention center with a skywalk joining the properties, perfect during bad weather. Good restaurants, service, everything is new and up to date. Not sure I can find any negative information to share with you, just enjoy.

title_masked: Feel like a true New Yorker and stay at the Nolitan
text_masked: If you've ever dreamt about living in downtown NYC but missed out on that life experience for one reason or another (like me), this is your chance to do so without breaking too much of your budget. The Nolitan is one of those contemporary, luxurious, yet uber-low-key boutique hotels that you really don't want the whole world to know about. From its location to its service to its well-appointed rooms, everything is perfect. We were lucky to have one of the upper-floor rooms with a balcony, plus a beautiful view of the Empire State building and Williamsburg Bridge. Head to the rooftop with your complimentary breakfast or glass of wine and soak in the NYC skyline. Unlike some of the hotels nearby, there really is no "scene" here, which was really great for us. Our vacation just ended but we already miss our stay at the Nolitan...see you next time!

I am a Diamond Member of Hilton Hotels and consider myself to be a real admirer. But unfortunately this is very definitely not one of the best. When we were there in late May/early June, not only was it completely full but there were two very large conferences taking place. Sadly I have to say it was mayhem. There were long queues stretching down the corridor for the EXECUTIVE LOUNGE (unbelievable). We were given tickets for a take-away Starbucks deal or for the very simple continental breakfast in the buffet. We opted to wait in the 20-minute queue for the Ex.Lounge because the breakfast there was marginally better than the Market Restaurant but it was still the absolute minimum with no alternatives to hard-boiled eggs, cereals, doughy buns and toast. There were queues for the coffee machines, especially long on Saturday morning when one of them broke down and wasn't fixed until the next day. Only soft drinks were offered, otherwise it was a pay bar. The barman didn't hesitate to show his displeasure at people who only wanted Cokes. Out of three lifts serving our floor, only one was ever working so more long queues, although there was a notice saying you could travel by service lift but that never seemed to be available either. Leaving the hotel with luggage was a nightmare. The only way to get into the lift was to take one going up and then travel down again, stopping at every single floor as dozens of frustrated guests realised that yet again there wouldn't be enough room for them to get in. Whilst we were there there was an electrical shutdown for three hours and a water shutdown for three hours - in an hotel of this standing? Extraordinary. The room was dated and looked in need of redecoration. Once again, fine for a cheapo on Times Square but we're talking about Hilton's New York flagship. The hotel's infrastructure and personnel numbers couldn't cope with this number of people and the cost-cutting in the restaurants was shameful.

Hi, Spent 7 night at this hotel and only have good things to say about it. It is very well located, lots of really good restaurants within walking distane, good shopping nearby as well. The room was clean and although a little on the small side was very comfortable. Staff were very helpful as well.

title_masked: Love Elvis,,, you'll love this hotel
text_masked:
I agree with others who say it is a little tired but I wouldn't have stayed anywhere else. I loved the Elvis music, TV and concert footage being streamed around the hotel and missed it when I left. We were picked up from the airport and had a very friendly and polite drivere who had an Elvis CD playing - the shuttle bus is regular and a fair price. I wasn't keen on the 'breakfast biscuits and sausage gravy' but the rest of the breakfast was more than adequate.
I enjoyed every minute and would quite happily go back again but I think a bit of a spruce up of the decor and soft furnishings wouldn't go amiss.

title_masked: A little pricey but a great location and nice hotel
text_masked:
A contemporary and fairly small hotel on a very pleasant street, this seems to have been recently refurbished and certainly scores top marks for location. There are plenty of restaurants near by, although many are of a similar level, and quite a few Italian. Choice is perhaps a little limited if you want something more casual, or just a drink.
Reception staff were all helpful and friendly. Breakfast staff were a little less on the ball, with some really not with it at all. Note also that a 18% service charge for your "free" breakfast will appear on your bill. OK, so it's not a massive amount, but it's not free is it?
On the downside, our room was allegedly a queen, but if this was the case I'd hate to have seen a standard. It was also a little noisy from the street outside with just single glazing. Although it's not a main road, it's still busy enough and by the time the street cleaner has woken you up at 02:00, the recycling guys at 03:00 and the rubbish collectors at 04:00 you start to get a bit fed up.
