There were no tea/coffee facilities in the room, or a safe although there was free wi-fi as well as a PC you could use in the guest's lounge. The lounge was right outside our room so I was concerned about potential noise from that, but in the event I didn't see anyone using it.
Prices also seemed a little steep, although I dare say that's par for the course in these parts.

We stayed at the Hard Rock while attending a wedding in the city and had a pretty good experience. We used the valet service to take care of our car, and while pricey, it did allow for in and out service which was important to us. We were checked in quickly and headed to our room. To be honest, I was a little disappointed in the room. After seeing room pictures online, this room was much smaller and the room's window opened onto an inner courtyard that hosted all the HVAC heating/cooling equipment, so the blinds stayed shut. As some others have commented, the rooms are not brightly lit.
The bathroom was very nice and the complimentary soaps, shampoos, etc were good. We also used the hotel restaurant for breakfast and enjoyed the meal.

I stayed her for 6 days for work during a very busy and stressful time and being at the hotel made everything so much more pleasant and bearable. When I travel for work again or even for pleasure (if it is not too expensive) I will definitely try to stay here again. Lots of attention to detail and very on it staff. Feeling of living in luxury without any pretentiousness.

My wife and I stayed at the Courtyard by Marriott in the Capital Hill/Navy Yard location on Sep 22-25. We were there to see a Brewers/Nationals game as well as use our location as a base to see some of DC's monuments (ML King, FDR & Jefferson) and a few Civil War battlefields. Their staff is extremely courteous and helpful with getting settled, & getting around the area-especially if you are inclined to walk. The hotel has been there 7 yrs but is sparkling & very well maintained. Parking within the building. This is an area with lots of new apt/condo construction and only a few blocks from National's Park for baseball fans. Plenty of great restaurants within a short walk on 8th St such as Belga Cafe & Senarts.
The hotel at times square is clean and i would recommend it to people who wants a good hotel very very near to times square. It has free wifi, pc with printer and free coffee / tea / chocolate :-)

title_masked: Close to Riverwalk, but thats all on the "plus" site
text_masked:
Booked this hotel over booking.com where it had quite a good rating and was sold for a apparently reasonable price. Not sure where the good ratings come from.
Neighborhood, noisy and a bit frightening at night. Lots of traffic only a few feet away from my window. People in front of room making noise till 2 am and from 6 am.
Room, dirty carpet, spots everywhere (bed, seat, wall, floor, furniture). Small, dark unfriendly. TV not working properly, door not closing properly. Dirty bathroom. 
Breakfast, sweet and really low end. Greasy room. Served till 9 am only on a Sunday!
Reception, got the impression that guest are disturbing the staff.
Pool, next (a few feet) to parked cars and a garbage area.
Overall no value for 80 bucks in comparison to other hotels in TX.

Exquisite Hotel in the heart of New York City! The staff was fantastic and everything was wonderful from the moment we walked in to the moment we had to check out. First Class service, hospitalable, and absolutely the best! Breakfast was awesome, the ladies that worked each morning served us with a smile and were so kind. They did everything to make sure that we were comfortable and when we came in from the city, it was so nice to come up and have a plate of cheese and crackers, a cold glass of water and a nice place to sit and relax. The other hotel guests were all very friendly as well. When we come back to NY City, we are definitely staying at the Casa Blanca and will refer friends there for sure! Thank you to the staff for an incredible stay and we thank you so much for a making our trip a memorable one! The quality that you have is above the rest for sure! "Hats Off to You" for incredible service, great location, and the best staff ever!

title_masked: I just dont understand how or why!!!!
text_masked:
I was shopping for a hotel and decided to bid on priceline to get a great hotel at a really good deal. Little did I know, that I would end up with Crowne Plaza a 3.5 star hotel. I think 3.5 stars, that cant be too bad, WRONG ANSWER!
First when we arrive, we find out that there is an 15-18 charge for parking. They were going to charge $18 for valet parking that was less than 10 feet away or charge $15 to park your own car and walk the 10 feet to the building per day. Next, trying to get in and out of the parking area was a major issue because the machine fail to work. When you buzz the office for assistance, no one responded. I then had to back-up and return to the main doors and request someone to assist me getting in and departing out. 
The hotel halls had this bad odor as if it had rained, it was a mildew smell that was extremely alarming and I wondered was it safe. Once I arrived to my room, the scent disappeared, but the fact of having to walk through that scent was horrific each time I entered and departed the room. I was in a double room, on full size beds. To add comfort to the beds, the hotel added a pillow-like padding to the bed. Unfortunately, this tool failed to assist in the comfort of the bed. I have slept on some bad mattresses, but this by far was the worst mattress that I have ever slept on. I woke up in unbelievable pain the two nights I stayed at this hotel. 
The breakfast was over-priced in which the buffet was $9 for a coffee, muffin, and some other small items. It was nothing as I originally expected it to be, definitely not worth $9. 
Each day the housekeeping staff came around 8 or 9. I ask that they come back because I wasn't dressed, but they never came back. When I ask for more towels at the front desk, they always requested my name and room number as if I was trying to take the towels and they had to document that they gave them to me. Takeout trash, room service, and other trash was always sitting outside someone's door and sometimes it carried over to the next morning. Which is really horrible to walk by this trash each time you enter and depart your room. 
I have stayed at about 15 hotels this year for business and pleasure and this by far has been the worst experience. I don't understand how or why, because this place has the potential to be a very good location, but the services and the quality were just unacceptable. I will never stay at this hotel again and I encourage you to do the same.

Not only was location walking distance from all the sites the staff at this hotel goes way out of their way to help!!!
Special thanks to Garrett at the front desk for his insite on back routes to LAX for early flight or we would all have missed departure time!!
Thanks Buddy!!!!

This was a great hotel to relax and kickback in after sitting through meetings all day. It is a good location if you want to go out and have dinner; or you could stay in and eat at the Lockwood and have a drink in the beautiful lobby. I was lucky to be upgraded to a King Suite. My colleague was not so lucky, and was in the "Double Double" room and it was VERY tiny. The hotel was full the first two days we stayed so she was unable to move, but the staff was able to move her to a more comfortable room for our last 3 nights there. The staff was very helpful and the concierge service was excellent.

Great location right across from the Chelsea Market. The rooms are small but its nicely arranged. The bathroom was surprisingly large. The decor was classy and modern along with the rest of the hotel. The club inside PHD has an amazing view of the whole city and its atmosphere is perfect. Not too crazy, but just lively enough. The staff inside is great as well. I used their gym a few times and it was nice and clean. They had free weights, benches, and cables as well as the typical cardio machines. Very, very nice hotel!

title_masked: Historic hotel, very convenient to Dupont Circle
text_masked: Room was large and well appointed, separate seating area. Bathroom was small but it is an historic hotel so that's to be expected. We walked everywhere we wanted to go from this room. Air conditioning was heavenly on a hot August weekend and it was central so it didn't cycle on and off like in some hotels with individual systems. Would definitely stay there again....close to Phillips gallery and Kramer Books and the Metro!

This was a last minute booking that turned out perfect for our family of four. We got into Chicago a little later than planned but were so surprised at this hotel, it's staff, it's cleanliness and it's amenities. We missed the free cocktail hour but by simply stating this fact the front desk took it on themselves to offer free wines coupons for the bar. The 17th floor patio had nice background music to enjoy our free wine while the kids swam indoors right next door. Late night milk and warm chocolate chip cookies were ordered from room service and free continental breakfast which we brought up to the rooftop patio. Overall we were very well taken care of in an excellent location. BONUS: They allow dogs. We will take advantage of this on our next trip.
Sorry below. I did not use the spa and clicked inadvertently.

We arrived after a long day on motorcycles. We were grubby, hot and ready to be done for the day. The staff helped situate the bikes on the courtyard area between the hotels and assured us they would be well watched. There were a number of other motorcycles already parked in the same area and it was very secure. We were given a room with a balcony and walk-in shower - it was spacious and very comfortable. Everything was very clean, well decorated and inviting. After enjoying the sights and tastes of Memphis we stopped back at the hotel bar and bought a bottle of wine to bring back to the room. Enjoyed the wine on the balcony while watching the trolly cars and horse carriages go by. Highly recommend this hotel!

A very well maintained and friendly hotel. The room was large, the bathroom small, but not a problem. My room had a sitting area, large screen TV, coffee maker and robe and slippers. The bed was comfortable, the room quiet at night - altogether it was a great stay. The location is perfect for shopping, walking to the SAM and the market. Buses are free in a downtown area. I also had a restaurant voucher for IL Fornaio (in Pacific Place Mall, across the street) and had a lovely lunch there. I would return to both the hotel and this restaurant

I recently stayed two nights at this hotel with my husband and daughter and loved it! The staff was very friendly and our room was extremely clean! Would definitly stay here again if in the area. Thanks again.

title_masked: Nice hotel with unbeatable location, parking costs only drawback
text_masked: Stayed at the Philadelphia Downtown Courtyard for 2 nights recently for a friend's wedding. The location is amazing, right across from City Hall in the middle of Philly's City Center area. There are a number of bars, restaurants and attractions to walk to, including the Reading Terminal Market, an excellent indoor marketplace that is literally steps from the hotel. Rittenhouse Square and other nice areas are just a 15 min walk or short ($7) cab ride away. The hotel itself was very comfortable, beds were good and the rooms were adequately sized. Hotel staff were friendly and accomodating, and rooms were equipped with mini fridges. There is a bar/restaurant on site that is huge and very comfortable as well. There is also a pool and fitness center, the pool was small and is only 3 feet deep but at least they have one I guess. The only real downside in my opinion is parking, which costs $31 for self-park or $38 for valet. However, there was a hidden $7 "valet tax" on top of that bringing the cost of valet parking to $45 a night. I understand there isn't alot of parking in this area but that is kind of an insane amount to pay per night for parking in my opinion. However, besides that I had an excellent stay and would probably return. Definitely recommended.

We enjoyed our stay at the Crowne Plaza Dallas Market Center. We were there before it changed its brand to the Wyndham. The room was very spacious, and we liked that the bathroom was attached to the bedroom rather than the living area. Our son, age 3, slept on the sofa bed and wasn't disturbed by our using the bathroom after he went to bed. The room was quiet and clean. There were two things I didn't like. There is no free breakfast, not even for kids. Second, the Internet was very poor in the bedroom part of the suite. My iPad didn't even pick it up in that part of the room. My phone did, but it was horribly slow no matter what part of the room you were in. We were on the 5th floor, I recall. The pool was fun for our son. He liked the indoor/outdoor aspect of it. The pool was cool despite the fact that it was July and very hot outside. The In-N-Out Burger in the parking lot is very convenient! Also this hotel was easy to find and was also a very easy drive to the Dallas Galleria. We got it through Hotwire and were not disappointed, the main annoyance being the Internet.

I travel about seven months out of the year for work, and try to stay at Kimptons as often as possible. They are always pleasant, and are like a little vacation while you work. 
I used my Kimpton InTouch reward stays to book my recent night at the Eventi. I checked in at the peak of hotel traffic (4pm) but was still quickly and kindly attended to. I was reminded to attend the wine hour (as if I could forget!) up on the second floor which was serving red and white wine, sangria, and had a lovely selection of cheese and fruit. The second floor outdoor seating is beautiful, though many of the seats are reserved for the restaurant so get there early if you want to sit outside. The olympics are currently being broadcasted in the park to the side of the hotel so it was the best way to keep up with the events and medal counts if you are an Olympic fanatic which, guilty as charged, I am.
My room was beautiful (the King Deluxe Suite on a mid level floor); a three room hotel with a giant California King bed room, living room, and bathroom with walk in shower and soaking tub. The room was well kept and the design is simple and relaxing yet young and trendy (think Design Within Reach meets CB2). The bed is simply heavenly. Its large, the mattress is firm, but topped with a down mattress topper and tucked engulfed in a large down comforter. I practically had to be dragged out of my room!
As it was my first stay as a Kimpton InTouch Inner Circle member, I returned from the wine hour to find a lovely, perfectly timed, and delicious gift with a personalized card!
I also had an opportunity to eat at the restaurant, which I suppose I should review separately, but if you are debating eating there--go for it. My tuna nicoise salad and side of Macaroni and cheese was outstanding!
While the area is not the prettiest in Manhattan, the location is great if you are looking for access to amazing shopping and some of the best Korean food in the city. Close to Penn Station and within walking distance to the Chelsea galleries its a great location especially if you are going to be meeting up with people in various parts of the city. Its still a very busy area, but you don't have to deal with the crowds, noise, and expense of staying near Times Square.
I had an amazing stay with the Eventi, and hope to be back soon. This was the last Kimpton property in New York that I had not yet stayed at and has set a high bar as one of the nicest, yet affordable hotels in the U.S.

title_masked: Needed to stay close to airport due to a cancelled flight...
text_masked:
We choose very last minute to stay at the Courtyard Marriott mainly due to the location because of our cancelled flight. 
We found the shuttle to be quick and convenient and easy to located. The rooms were clean and up to date. The staff was helpful. The location is isolate so the food choices within walking distance were not convenient however they did offer to shuttle us downtown. We ate in the diner located in the lobby. Nothing fancy but convenient. 
I would stay again if I was back in the area.

My husband and I stayed for one night at this hotel in June 2012.
We originally booked this hotel when it was a Marriott using points. When they switched to Loews we were told that our reservation would still be honored with the points, which was good to hear. 
Upon arriving we had the choice of valet or self park at the public (mall parking) ramp attached to the hotel. We self parked for something like $9 per day, but no in and out privileges. We did go in an out and just handed over another $9, but it was still cheaper than the valet service.
The check in line was a few people deep when we arrived around noon and it was about 10 minutes from when we arrived at the hotel to when we actually checked in and our room was available right away.
Our hotel room was on the club level with a nice view of downtown LA and the Hollywood sign. The room was of average size as was the bathroom. The only downside was the bathroom where there were no towel racks and only one sink.
We also had club access from our prior status and reservation with Marriott. The club was on the small side, but rarely did we ever see anyone else in it. We were disappointed with the tiny/mini water bottles they had in the club rather than the normal sized ones. Breakfast in the lounge was ok, but nothing amazing. It was what we would expect from a club lounge breakfast. 
This hotel is attached to the Loews (Kodak) theater and shopping mall. After a short walk through the mall, you’ll on the Hollywood strip with thousands of tourists and easy access to any Starline tours you might have booked. Overall, this hotel has the best location for easy Hollywood sightseeing.

This is a new (only a year old) hotel, so the facilities are very modern. Upon check-in, the coffee table in our suite had a disgusting spill that had hardened...obviously had been there a while and never cleaned? We reported it to the front desk, and the response was, "we'll make sure you are not held responsible." I told them my concern was having it cleaned, not whether I was going to be held responsible (!), as it was gross! They did send someone to clean it while we were out. The bedside table was also dirty, but I wiped it down, myself. 
Breakfast on the weekends is from 7 to 10. We got down there around 9:45, and there was no coffee left (none!), and it didn't appear they were planning to make more. As in other reviews here, the breakfast left much to be desired in both offering and in quality. We were on our way out that morning, so I don't know if the coffee was replenished or not. 
As some have mentioned here, parking is sparse, especially late at night. The location was okay...there were not any local types of decent restaurants nearby that we could find (a new Bob Evans we "recommended," by the staff, and was right next door, but that wasn't what we were looking for in our visit). 
As some have mentioned here, the walls allow you to hear everything from outside in the hall and from adjacent rooms.
Anyway, for the prices charged for a two double-bed suite ($190 and $160 per night!--not during football season or school year), we were pretty disappointed, overall; also, for this to be a Marriott hotel and very new, it just didn't meet our expectations for cleanliness and service.

Overall I found this hotel extremely great value, comfortable and great location. The bedroom was comfortable, clean and warm and the bathroom was clean. 
There is still renovations going on in the hotel and the noise of them working away woke us up a couple of times too early in the morning. 
The one thing that really put me off was a particular staff member on the day we checked out. She was unbelievable obnoxious and rude. I had a problem with paying with my debit card and although perhaps I should have checked whether they accepted it before we checked out I had thought that there wouldn't be an issue. I thought americans prided themselves in good customer service but I was incredibly let down by her attitude with me over the fact that they couldn't accept my card. She repeated several times in a rude loud voice " We don't accept that card". Then told me that I would have to get money out down the street and again kept repeating the same thing. She made me so angry I told her "ok ok" and walked away from the desk, she then turned around to my friend and said "you know if she doesn't come back we will be charging to your credit card" in a rude manner. She was bang out of order and she would not have not been to able to authorise that. She ruined my morning with her attitute. I of course I am an honest person and had she been nicer to me I would have apologised profusely for the inconvience. There was also a queue of people behind us which would have heard her talking to me in that manner.

This hotel may be a little hard to find, but it is a top recommendation for staying in Philadelphia. It is small and very quiet, but the service is good and friendly, and the rooms are sensational. It also offers a normal breakfast cafe in the basement. The location is ok, the street being much more like an alleyway, and is surrounded by much taller buildings, but is a block away from Rittenhouse Square.

Great location, 2 blocks from Union station. Concierge was excellent.
Very odd hotel. Strange uber stong perfume smell in the lobby, it made us dread entering as it made us somewhat nauseous. Fortunately, the smell was only in the lobby and not the room. Music in the lobby and elevators could be described as 'european disco". Again, odd.
The rooms were incredibly small, I had to walk across the bed to not step in my husbands suitcase. Super small bathroom. However, everything was very clean and new, which was a plus. Overpriced for the room size.
It seems like the ultra modern decor is fighting to fit in the elegant old beautiful and classic marble floors and surroundings.

Booked online direct with the hotel - the process very smooth and efficient.
The main selling point of the hotel - LOCATION!!! Everything is on your doorstop - the tram, restaurants (highly recommend Lori's diner at the inter-section on the left as you leave the hotel for breakfasts) and shops (Macy's, Saks, etc).
The open-top bus tours stop less than a 100m walk from the hotel, so convenient for sightseeing too.
The rooms were adequate - small and quite old, but in working order and comfortable enough for a city hotel. We were on the 9th floor and were not disturbed by street noise at all.
The hotel tour desk is helpful, as were reception. The complimentary cookies, apples and tea / coffee / water were a nice touch.
Would recommend to travellers after a secure & comfortable city hotel with an EXCELLENT location, without the glitzy price-tag.

The bed was very comfortable, with good linens and pillows. The building is old, however, so street noise is fairly audible. We brought out own sound machine for white noise, which I'd recommend. The breakfast at XIX was great...if you are very lucky, you'll get either Danielle or Catalina as your server, both of whom could not be more attentive or helpful. The breakfast buffet was $20.00, but included fresh berries, smoked salmon, assorted cheeses, lots of high quality fresh baked goodies, along with typical hot breakfast items. The location of the Bellevue is ideal...close to everything. We'll go back.

title_masked: We loved this stay with our 4 and 6 year old!
text_masked: We traveled to Denver from Estes Park, CO to spend two nights for spring break and enjoy Denver. We chose the Hotel Monaco and are so glad we did. From the moment we pulled up we were so welcomed with our 4 and 6 year old, the valet was so friendly, the front desk accommodating, and the room perfect! They brought the goldfish as promised and the kids were thrilled! It is in perfect walking distance to great restaurants, the Pepsi Center for a Nuggets game, and a very close drive to the Zoo, the Aquarium and the Museum of Nature and Science. We will stay here again!

We checked into the hotel and requested a king bed and were immediately given attitude and denied our request. We walked into the room we were given and it was tiny, dark and dingy. The bathroom is so small that we had to walk into it sideways. We do not recommend staying here...especially for the rate. You are paying for location and there are many other hotels in the same location with better rooms and facilities worthy of your business. Save you money and sanity and skip this rotten joint.

We had paid in advance for a double queen room. I purposely did this because although there were only two of us, the single queen room pictured on the lodge's website appeared to be small. Upon arrival, we were placed in a single queen room. It was what I'd seen on the website. It felt like a dorm room. (This would probably be okay for someone traveling alone.) I called the front desk, and was told they'd call me back. Thirty minutes later, someone came to the door with the pass cards for our new room. This lodge was so highly rated, that we did not expect to be waiting in limbo for 30 minutes. When we get to our room, we like to unwind and unpack some things. He said they were busy. Later in the evening, the common area in our building ran out of ice. My husband called the front desk and was told that the restaurant was responsible for providing the ice. Really? After some conversing, the desk offered to take some ice to our room. Again, I just expected better treatment for the rates we were charged, and all the good write-ups. The complementary breakfast was good. We did not receive a statement under our door - for checkout. I called the desk, and was told that we had no additional charges. She instructed me to leave the keys in the room, which we did. By doing this, we were locked out of the middle building, which we needed to access to pass thru in order to reach the lobby. Instead, we had to go down some stairs to the restaurant, and walk through the area in which housekkeping was mopping the floor. We then took another elevator to the lobby to catch the shuttle. Upon check-in, we had reserved two seats on the 9AM shuttle to the airport. It was clearly before 9, and the shuttle had already left, without us. The desk called and got the driver to return for us.
great location, large room, clean, friendly helpful staff. a stones throw from epmire state building .

Due to a missed connection, my husband and I were forced to book in to this hotel at 1.30am. On that basis alone I am thankful but unfortunately any gratitude ends there. The hotel STANK of what I can only describe as a dirty smell masked by cheap air conditioner. The carpets on the hallway were disgusting and badly stained. The room also had a really strange smell. The bedding was clean but even after a shower I felt dirty as nothing in the place seemed properly clean - we were both really anxious to get out of there the next morning and wanted to avail of the free shuttle. We wanted one for 10am and were advised there would be none until 12pm with a palpable disinterest from all the staff we dealt with. While I'm grateful that they accomodated us when we were stuck, it was worth $24 rather than the $94 - I'd avoid going here again at all costs.

title_masked: Budget accomodation - ok for a couple of nights
text_masked: budget accommodation but good for a couple of nights. Room was a bit noisy (at Lombard street). Breakfast was very basic, just boiled eggs and beverages (hot and cold), have not seen muffins which we thought were offered as well.

As two closely related families travelling together in the US we had booked two rooms at the Salisbury, but on arrival Reception upgraded us to a two-bedroom, two-bathroom 17th floor suite if we wanted to stay together. The suite was lovely, with a little dining area and a spacious living room in addition to two large bedrooms. Everything very clean and well appointed.
Our relatives took advantage of the hotel breakfast each day at an additional $9 per person, but we did not after the first day as, although the breakfast and the dining room were quite OK, my wife and I are not fans of American-style breakfasts and made our own arrangements through the excellent delis close by.
Staff were so helpful throughout our three-day stay and arranged a very impressive limousine to take us out to JFK on departure at a very reasonable price.
The hotel is ideally located and not expensive by Manhattan standards. A 10 minutes walk to 5th Avenue and Central Park and about 20 minutes walk to Times Square.
Thank you, all staff at the Salisbury Hotel for making our stay in New York such a comfortable and convenient one.

title_masked: Inn at the Park (San Diego) - a 1920's jewel gets a sparkling polish!
text_masked:
This gorgeous old roaring-20's hotel is getting a make-over and it's going to restore the gem to her original luster, with refinements! The Inn is right beside Balboa Park in the middle of Hillcrest, which is an ideal location for visiting all of the Balboa Park attractions. The property has a roof-top terrace with 360 degree panoramic view of the city; the rooms are very large, with high vaulted ceilings and apartment-style layouts, with kitchens, living rooms, etc.
The lobby and restaurants are all top-notch (albeit a little dated, until renovations are complete). The entire property is undergoing a remodeling, having recently been acquired by Shell Properties. Shell is investing in upgrades that will restore and enhance the property. The new suites are stunning. We are delighted that Shell has acquired this property and are pleased that Shell is retaining the character and charm that this property has sustained, but is giving her a new look that reflects the property's origination, with modern enhancement.
We arrived, pleasantly surprised by the elegant quality-service of the staff, to enjoy the Friday evening happy hour on the rooftop, which was like stepping back in time to the gay roaring 20's. It was fun to see the twinkling lights of the city among the locals who were enjoying generous libations served by vivacious bartenders.
We dined in style at the restaurant that not only presents a well-rounded continental menu, but also offers entertainment each night by local musicians. The singer we heard was superb - singing jazz and playing piano. He took us back-in-time to the Sinatra era with songs like, "Come Fly With Me," and everyone in the bar joined in singing, making it a a rousing dinner experience. We dined on crisp calamari, a very generous plate with honey-mustard and the traditional marinara sauce; slow-cooked ribs with vegetables and mashed potatoes; and a French-dip roast beef sandwich. We complimented our dinner with tasty cocktails - like a pear mojito with muddled mint and fresh pear.
We will come back to this property again and again. It takes you back to the happy, heady days of the 1920's with a fresh 21st century perspective.

We had a horrible experience at another hotel in DC and Holiday Inn Capital was great. The people were friendly and helpful. The rooms were very accommodating and comfortable and the restauarants were great. We will ceraintly stay there again and recommend to friends!

I stayed for several nights through a major national meeting which was at McCormick Place. 
The location on the Magnificent Mile, the suites and the buffet breakfast, which caters for different national food preferences, were great. 
If there is a downside to the hotel, its the logistics of getting in and out.
The hotel has a relatively small street frontage and the entrance is a little clumsy with people milling around inside and outside the door. There is limited space for taxis act at the front. The lobby itself has a coffee place that sells sandwiches and drinks to go and some seating. 
The in/out issues were evident when on the first morning, I needed to get to McCormick Place early. Allowing an hour, I rounded the corner to the conference bus in front of the Westin, to find the queue extending well up Michigan. I returned to the Hotel and asked for a taxi - they have a lot of trouble getting taxis to come in busy times. I eventually got picked up by someone in taxi headed to McCormick. 
Message: if you need a taxi - reserve one ahead.

Booked a Family Staycation for the weekend and the Avenue Apartment we were in was really fantastic. Beautiful view, beautiful decor, great ameneties, and more space than I could have imagined. Perfect for kids - the in unit washer dryer was fantastic, I was able to do all our laundry before we left. Loved being able to use the house car and the complimentary drinks. And not being charged for wireless like you are at so many other luxury hotels is just a very sensible perk. A lot is made by the hotel (on the website) over the Pretasi linens but I didn't find them to be all that special. There was nothing wrong with them, just not great. The giant fluffy towels, however, were very nice. My husband said the mattress hurt his back. I didn't find it that bad, but I've definitely stayed in chain hotels that seem to have the comfy bed thing figured out nicely. Turn down service was great.

We were told the room was going 199$ than when we checked in we were told it was 229. When we finally got to our room, we got a text message from our bank saying we were overdrawn. We found out that without telling us the hotel charged 319. They never mentioned they charge 20% just in case we get room service. we were not planning on room service. They charged us 90$ more than they said they were going too. 90$ more than my husband signed to pay. I do not understand how they could charge and not tell us the actual amount. It ended up making it so we could not go to the Willis Tower because the money was being held. Very disappointed. Also, the lady checking us out forgot to ask us for the room keys. we didn't realize so we had to walk all the back to the hotel since we could not afford a cab. Location was great. The room didn't even have a fridge. The vending machines were right outside our room so we got woken up a few times by other hotel visitors during the night. For the price, I think it was an awful experience.

title_masked: An Ideal San Diego Getaway Destination
text_masked:
We live in San Diego and the kids, all 4, had their own getaways one certain weekend. This never happens! My husband and I were looking for a getaway that we could get to easily on a Friday afternoon in the crazy commute that wouldn't take an eternity. I'd never been to the RBI and the website looked inviting. I phoned and got a fabulous spa package. 
The property was sold out when we arrived Friday and we were put in the Fountain Building on the 3rd floor above the A/C unit. During the day its fine when you close your door but at night you hear the roar of the fan circulating. This was over our A/C unit in the room which itself was very loud. It did stop working our Saturday night stay. Thankfully we were on the 3rd floor and able to sleep with our screen door open. And thankfully our bed was remarkably comfortable.
The spa is lovely and I was given a wonderful massage by Sherry. The ladies working in the spa were gracious and welcoming. The steam/ jacuzzi area need a bit more care. There were washcloths to wipe your face, in a bowl, but with no ice. All the trash cans were overflowing. 
The spa pool was remarkably relaxing. There too the bar ladies were kind and expedient. 
I have to say overall the service at this property, from Paul in reservations, to Paul and Camille in the restaurant, really everywhere you went, the employees there seem to enjoy their work.
While the property itself needs renovating, the grounds and employees make it a welcoming getaway for anyone who just needs a break.

title_masked: Great family hotel with a touch of elegance!
text_masked:
Stayed at the Palomar April 9-11 with the family (kids 12 & 14). The hotel was very attentive to your request and just plain friendly! Pool on the 17th floor was great, too bad it was too cold to sit outside and enjoy the scenery. Have to tell you the Happy Hour each night was a pleasant surprise and the manager on duty was great to talk to and very friendly. The rooms were very nice and modern. Kids really like them. The location of the hotel can't be better, close to Michigan Avenue which besides shopping also gives you close access to just about every bus line you would want to get to things like Shedds Acquarium, the Museum of Science and Industry and other like places. 
The restaurant onsite was a great appetizer place before we went out for the night, kid friendly and the food was very good. I would recommend this hotel for anyone who wants a fair value, great service, friendly staff and close proximity to just about everything! Try the Weber Grill Restaurant right across the street, it was very good!

title_masked: First time visitor to this hotel - won't be my last! Excellent hotel!
text_masked: Travelled to downtown Seattle on business and I'm glad we picked the Renaissance. Although my room faced the freeway, it was surprisingly quiet. The bed and pillows were comfortable and I slept like a baby. My co-worker and I had supper in the lounge one evening and we thoroughly enjoyed it. Our breakfasts were served promptly and the servers were all friendly. Although the hotel was extremely busy, none of the staff were too busy to smile and go out of their way to offer us assistance. Anytime I have business in downtown Seattle, the Renaissance will be my first choice.

I've stayed at the Lucerne many times in my travels to NYC. It is situated in a fantastic UWS location with easy access to the Subway system (one block W or two blocks E). There a literally dozens of quality restaurants in this thriving area and it is one block away from the NYC landmark Zabars. The rooms are large by NY standards and a very well appointed, especially if you opt for the more deluxe categories. It was very hot the last time we were in NY and the a/c in the Lucerne may be some of the best I've ever experienced in the city! The staff could not be more pleasant, and if you stay for more than an day or two, will know your name and recognize you instantly. While the Lucerne isn't 'fancy' by any means, we try to stay there when we can. The Waldorf may have more 'prestige', but I'll pick the Lucerne any day over the Waldorf. If you want to blend in and feel like you live in NY, there is no better spot to do it - this isn't a highly touristy area. If you watch carefully, the hotel runs specials on a regular basis, making it even more affordable at certain times. Enjoy!

I only spent 7 hours here, but it was well maintained, very comfortable beds and convenient to the interstate. Since I arrived very late, it was nice that they had all my paperwork sitting out and I got my keys in just a couple of minutes. It doesn't have a free breakfast, but the restaurant was good and fast.

We stayed here for 2 nights. Fantastic for visiting Universal Studios as the hotel offers a free shuttle service to and from there. A couple of minutes from the highway, 15 minutes from the Hollywood sign and 20 minutes from Hollywood boulevard. The room was clean, the bed was comfortable and the receptionists were really helpful, printing off our boarding passes for us. I would stay here again.

My wife and I went up on July 5th and Stayed two nights. We drove up from Portland and parked the car (10 bucks a day) and walked everywhere. About 1/4 mile to the Space Needle and monorail, which took us within a few blocks of Pikes Market. Service was great and it was very quiet, right up until about 1:00 am when the people upstairs came home and started slamming stuff around. My bad for not caling security. I told the Manager upon checkout and he was very responsive, adding bonus points to our rewards program. Breakfast was great and rest of the staff very friendly. Even used the workout room. All this was topped off by doing the King Tut VIP package. The package is only for one night and we added an extra night. Great time. Do yourself a favor if you get the Tut Package and buy the audio tour. It enhances the whole experience and it's even narrated by Harrison Ford.

This place is so good at courting their guests. They think of so many great details that make this place feel homey and comfortable. Unlike most stuffy hotels where the air is stale and the rooms smell/feel strange, The James does all the right things to make you fall hard. 
They leave cookies on your bed, water by your bedside, and a comfortable robe in time of need. The bathroom products are divine, the hallways smell great and you can even open your window for some fresh air. 
The lobby is super cozy and they have hot chocolate around the clock when it's cold outside, fresh juice in the summer. They have a great gym with fully functioning machines and TVs. Also, the prices are generally affordable if you book far enough in advance. 
If they keep this up, I could certainly develop a lifelong relationship with The James.

Dream Downtown was a fantastic hotel, the room was large and very modern styling, the views from level 9 where breathtaking, we even watched the 4th July fireworks from the comfort of our bed. The location was great, as close to restaurants, shops and the river. There is a 24hr gym within the hotel and the customer service provided by the staff at Dream was fantastic. 
If you love to party or if you are in New York to relax and enjoy the beauty, Dream Downtown is perfect. Each day we took to the streets to walk and see all there was to offer in NYC and in the evening we enjoyed the hotel and the many restaurants in the surrounding districts.

Front desk was very helpful and easy to work with when I had to switch rooms because the tv did not work in the first room.
This was my second stay and both were very pleasant.
Good location and comfortable rooms. Very clean.
Lots of eating/shopping choices in that area.

Amazingly great location! Located around so many good restaurants, bars and minutes away from shopping :) unless we had to go to Pier 39/Fisherman's Wharf we took transportation other than that we walked. From the hotel a lot is in walking distance
The rooms are very spacious! We had a king bed, with a table and chair and also a couch in our room with plenty of room to walk around. The restroom is big and so is the closet. We loved our room. 
Over all great experience in San Francisco with our room, plenty of stuff to do and see.

title_masked: You get what you pay for
text_masked:
I booked via Hotwire and was quite concerned after reading all the negative feedback on Tripadvisor. Sadly, I found out a lot of it is correct.
The good: The service. The staff was friendly, helpful and welcoming. It was freezing in our room, but we immediately got offered a space heater and some extra blankets. We changed rooms as the first one was really small and we wanted separate beds. First room was horrible. Second room was spacious with two double beds.
The bad: The first room we had was small and cramped, not very well cleaned and was right next to the staircase, so it was extremely noisy when drunk people were coming home from a festive night out. The cleaning was...well...you could tell the cleaning staff did a (very) quick job, we found leftovers from other people in both rooms (hairpins, hair on the floor in the bathroom and even one in the bed, ew) There's only wi-fi in the "lounge" and it's pretty slow, we went to the Starbucks next door and used the wi-fi there.
The ugly: The carpet. 
To sum up: the hotel is not great. The beds aren't comfy and the hotel is kept in dark colours (red and blue) maybe to cover up the fact that the hotel is a bit run down and old. However, it was a cheap deal via hotwire and the hotel is located fairly well seeing as it's close to the subway (Line 1, right outside your front door). The area is nice, with a lot of good restaurants esp. the Hungarian Pastry Shop on 1030 Amsterdam Avenue is worth a visit.
Would I return? No.

The Andez 5th Avenue is a perfect hotel. The staff is efficient and welcoming. The location which seems a bit too downtown from 59th street is actually NOT as it is an easy bus, cab or stroll to that area, and to such sites as MOMA; The 57th Street galleries and stores, Lincoln Center and Rockefeller center. The big plus is the easy access to the theatre district and to both Byrant Park and Madison Square Park and Grand Centeral. This Hotel exceeds Hyatt expectations and it is a refuge where one really could enjoy NYC from one's room. The cusine is good, the views embrace the Manhatten skyline, the rooms speak of a fresh and exciting environment. and the staff truely knows NYC and is always ready to assist and recommend. A guest at Andez can become a NYC insider with their help and find quality experiences and unique adventures. The immediate access to the architecture and exhibitions of the public library is unbeatable. Stay at Andez 5th Avenue and this will become your home and office away from home. E. Cameron; Community Arts International.

A decent room. The lounge attached to the Ramada had a cover charge. We may have used it if the front door to the Ramada wasn't locked, so we would have had to walk all the way around the block, at night in downtown LA. So we didn't visit the nightspot. This was dissappointing because we were trying to escape our room, where the heater didn't work. The fan did, and it blew the cold air really well. So we stayed in windy 65 degree room. This may have been nice in the summer, but not on a rainy December day. The front desk was less than helpful. I didn't use the pool or room service, so I can't review them. I did try to use the hotel WiFi, which was free, but unusably slow. I used my iPhones hot spot instead.

The room was decent. But you have to pay $10/night for parking! Also, internet is not free and it doesn't offer continental breakfast...
For the price you're paying, this hotel is not worth it at all. You're better off staying at one of the hotels closer to downtown.

title_masked: A great NYC alternative close to Times Square and Central Park
text_masked: I was pleasantly surprised by Le Parker Meridian in many ways. Great location, well designed and appointed rooms, excellent staff-no disappointments. I strive to find great fitness centers, and this one is very well done. They have a diverse array of fitness classes including yoga, spinning, and cross training which was a pleasant surprise. Highly recommended for those wishing to stay in shape while in NYC for business or pleasure.

I've being staying at multiple Marriott properties during last few years. I would say probably over 20 full service Marriott hotels in last two years(not counting Residence Inns and Courtyards ;) . Eventually, most Marriotts have similar rooms setup, bedding, toiletries etc.
What make this Houston West Loop property different - is folks working there. 
So here is a summary:
1. Location: very well positioned on San Felipe @ 610 where you gain access to all uptown business building practically effortless. If the noise from I-610 is a concern for you ask to get a room on an upper floor of the south-west side of the hotel - this should make it really quite.
2. Rooms: nothing exceptional. Marriott standard equipment and bedding. Nice and clean though.
3. Fitness, sauna, pool - nice set of equipment, always clean and well maintained. Bunch of folks staying there work out.
4. Reception: guys working on reception are awesome. They met you as you came to their wedding party ;) IF you have any requests - turn them in - most likely you'll get what you asked for (unless it is kind of insane request)
5. Lounge: nice and quite; menu is pretty good; Amber - the lady who supports the lounge at evening hours is amazing.
6. Management: these guys work to provide you with the really pleasant stay. If you would stay for a longer period - you would mention customer appreciation receptions on Tuesdays and other small but very nice things to make you feel at home.

title_masked: Do not stay here. You will regret it.
text_masked:
Booked this through Priceline, but even with the discount, the room rate will still too much. This isn't a motor hotel - it's a crap motel:
Toilet was running, had to adjust tank kit.
Floor and wall lamps don't work
Freezer doesn't freeze
TV remote volume button doesn't work.
TV picture is fuzzy
Sofa upholstery torn/dirty
Furniture dirty
Only 1/4 roll of toilet paper provided.
Sheets/ towels do not feel fresh; pils on sheets.
Mold in shower.
Noisy.
Room smells like cigarettes.
Very narrow parking spaces.

Stayed twice in this hotel in the past week. The Courtyard at Logan is and old Ramada that I stayed in almost 25 years ago but they have done an excellent job in refurbishing it. Rooms have been upgraded and are spacious, there is free Internet and the shuttle to the airport runs every 15 minutes round the clock and will even pick you up if you return a rental car the night before departure. The breakfast, while there is a charge is plentiful. Because of Boston's compact size, you can do business in the city and come back to the Courtyard for a relaxing evening. If you are on vacation, it is a good jumping off point to other destinations as well.

I stayed here for four nights with a incredible deal from booking.com. The location was great. You could walk or catch a bus, trolley or river taxi to any major attraction. Get an outside room as the interior rooms are noisy due to the lobby noise. I switched rooms ten minutes after checking into my interior room. My exterior room was too bright at night due to a street lamp right outside my window. However, I made it work. Curtains or shades would work better than the shutters. Breakfast was nothing special, so skip it at least once and take the river taxi to the Institute for Culinary Arts Cafe at the Pearl complex for breakfast. I had wonderful French toast with rum raisin sauce and coconut cream and one of the best hot chocolates ever. Prices are very reasonable. Don't forget to pick up a bakery treat for later. I had the XS cake and it was chocolate heaven.

This hotel looked nice, was clean, had a friendly staff, and was in a great location. Located next in Times Square and near the Theater District. You can walk everywhere you want to go. Hotel rooms are a little narrow but it was enough room for us. I recommend this hotel!
Great hotel. Very good service. Large rooms. Excellent Amenities. Great location.

title_masked: a Great Waldorf and Cole Porter's piano.
text_masked:
Great location in Midtown.
The Hotel was everything what we expected, Hotel lounge was even more than expectation, what a feeling entertained with live music played with Cole Porter’s piano, extra vibes for Pianist and us, with same time fantastic cocktails.
We stayed at seven nights and legendary service as well as the staff were all very lovely, the queue at reception to check in and out were very quick. Concierges gave us good tips for very best and different jazz clubs, etc. 
The room was comfortable and spacious enough for us, the bed were comfortable too with very best pillows, the wardrobe has room for luggage and the bathroom was lovely, powerful shower and plenty of room, in the mornings was newspaper at our door. The air conditioning was adjustable.
We stayed in the Hotel in July, the front of the hotel was undergoing renovations, so we used mostly the Lexington entrance which was also closer to several subway lines.
Value for money, we would definitely recommend this hotel for couples

This hotel is built into the old train station. Our three day stay for Moto GP was a good experience. Very large lobby with multiple sitting areas made for a very open atmosphere. Our room was bottom floor which opened to the large atrium area so no outside windows for us, which I didn't care for but no big deal. Bathroom needed some attention, loose tiles due to water damage & sink is on the outside of the bath / toilet area. The huge steel riveted girders incorporated into the hotel structure were impressive. Indoor pool was ok nothing outstanding. Staff were all pleasant especially the parking valets. Would stay there again, a little pricey, but your right in downtown Indy so to be expected. One thing not in the brochure is that the elevated trains still come by on the outside rear area of the building so several times, 2 or 3 times a night you can really hear them.Maybe not so much in other parts of the hotel but very audible from our room.

title_masked: Refined Elegance and a hotel that sweats the small stuff
text_masked:
After a massive tour of SF, Santa Cruz, LA and then San Diego, the highlight of the trip was the oasis called [NAME] Del Mar. 
San Diego is a great spot, and coming to a hotel that understands its location, surroundings and most importantly guests personas makes the premier hotel in the North SD area. Tucked away in Carmel Valley, this gem on the side of the hill, surrounded by an amazing golf course is like an onion you peel away and find better and better layers as you dive deeper. 
Location is one of the best in SD. Not too far for exploring and close to Torrey Pines and the best beaches in SD. Also you miss a lot of the "merge" of the 805 and 5 traffic.
Hospitality is top notch. Service is super-friendly, not pretentious and everyone from the front desk to housekeeping was ultra friendly. I give this place the US - Uber-Service award. Smiles everywhere, and great attitudes.
Amenities are outstanding. from the mango lemonade and cookies at reception to the chocolate covered Oreos at night by your bed. Rose pedals, complementary bottled water in your room and so much more. They really don't miss anything here and it seems so natural. One of the best beds I have slept in and the only thing I would suggest is that they upgrade the flat panel signal to HD.
Food in the downstairs restaurant was excellent for breakfast and the complementary coffee in the little and yet very well stocked cafe area was a welcomed treat at 6:30a when reading the paper overlooking the adult pool. Yes there are many pools and activities, like a great spa, gym etc.
Lastly I will say that I had the pleasure of staying here once before when Vh1 Divas was held in San Diego. This hotel gets even better with age, and it was GREAT for Divas!

My wife and I were very satisfied with every aspect of our stay. The staff was very helpful and everything was exactly as it should be in a hotel. We especially enjoyed the breakfast buffet. Will definitely plan to stay again sometime.

title_masked: Great hotel, but check prices before you book
text_masked:
The hotel is located in hill country, which isn't real close to shopping or places to eat. 
BEAUTIFUL resort and my room was awesome. Very clean, great view of the golf course, and maid service was exceptional. Great work desk as well. Room was laid out well, bathroom well stocked, and everything worked.
I did not play golf, but did eat on site for breakfast and dinner. Again, check prices. 
Largest complaint - room price, and I got charged for room WIFI. For what I paid - throw in WIFI.
Very comfortable bed and stay overall. Reserved a taxi for a 4:00AM departure, and they took care of everything. Great service check in, out, and concierge.

title_masked: Rude valet guy ruined nice service of hotel
text_masked:
The hotel was overall alright. It is a 100 year old building but nicely kept. It is located in the heart of downtown SF but the windows are not double pane so it is kind of noisy. When I checked-in in the middle of the night, Jesse was very helpful and friendly. 
I had a good impression of the hotel until I checked out and I had to get my car from the Stockton/Sutter garage to pick up my luggage (Sept 25th, 2012 at 10:35am). As I walked out of the lobby to get my car, my partner already told the valet guy that I would be back to pick him up along with the luggage (just a few bags) in 10 mins. 
When I pulled in front of the hotel (white zone) and stepped out of my car, I instantly told the valet guy that I was there for only 60 seconds to pick up my luggage. Obviously he got a problem with that (may be he wasn't getting a tip?) and start questioning me why I parked there (hello??). I explained to him for the second time he just kept harassing me and wouldn't shut up. 
I just go ahead and walked into the lobby and picked up my bags and walked right out. He kept harassing me EVEN I got my bags and start loading my bags into the car and told me I was over reacting (again, hello??) and he was just trying to help. I told him that he could use a smile instead of being rude about it (he still would not shut up at this point and kept at it). My partner was very surprise that a valet guy could be so rude and told me that I should speak with manager. I just called and spoke to a supervisor and she was very apologetic about this incident and told me she would relate the message to the management. Would I stay there again? probably not.... It is amazing that how one rude guy could do to ruin a nice experience and the reputation of a nice hotel.

This small Inn is near the Getty Center and within walking distance of Brentwood's restaurant area. The former motel has been skillfully renovated under the direction of a Brazilian architect whose sense of color and proportions converted otherwise small spaces into a very pleasant accommodations. The little breakfast terrace, near the reception, is beautiful. Management was most helpful in providing us directions, and in booking dinner and Getty Villa reservations .

I stayed here for three nights on a recent trip to SF and was pleasantly surprised. The hotel is located right next to the cable car and is within walking distance to Union Square. Upon arrival, I was notified that I'd been upgraded from a deluxe king to a king suite! I stayed in room 701, which was right next to the elevator. I could hear the elevator, but it wasn't disruptive and didn't prevent me from sleeping. The room was very clean and had a large bathroom with a separate tub & shower, a living room, separate bedroom with a sitting area and a king bed. I could hear the street noise, but living in downtown Miami, it didn't bother me. I'm only mentioning it in case you're not a sound sleeper. The carpet should probably be replaced, but other than that the rooms are well maintained. The staff was very friendly. They arranged to have a car pick me up for my trip to the airport and when I explained that my plane was delayed, they took care of calling the driver to change my pick-up time. If I was staying in the downtown area again, I'd definitely stay here.

Stayed here for one night. Nothing really remarkable about the stay which is a good thing. Just a nice, clean hotel very close to the airport. Didn't use airport shuttle, so can't comment on efficiency.
Pros:
 - Quiet Rooms
 - Clean and modern, looks like it was recently built
Cons:
 - Beds slightly uncomfortable
 - NOTHING around the hotel - need a car or cab to get to anything

Stayed at the Palomar for the Notre Dame/Miami game 10/4-10/7. It was also the weekend for the Chicago Marathon, which passed in front of the hotel. That in itself speaks to the location of this great property. Large room was upscale with every amenity, including jacuzzi. Especially liked the lobby lounge; very comfortable and terrific coffee. Front desk staff was consistently helpful and I liked the fact they were dressed to the nines. Very professional image. I've stayed at other nice facilities downtown but none compare to the Palomar. I'll be back...

My daughter and I traveled to NYC to celebrate my 50th birthday and was thrilled at our choice of lodging. Great location--close to Times Square and within walking distance of Central Park. Bryant Park was just down a block from the hotel--what a great place to sit and people watch! The room was very comfortable and clean--loved having the fridge and microwave. We could reheat leftovers easily and keep drinks in the room--a nice money saver!! Another money saver--the buffet breakfast they served in the morning--good food and a good selection. The staff was friendly and helpful. No doubt this will be out hotel of choice when visiting NYC in the future.

This is a very sleek, modern hotel. Kimpton generally has quality properties, this is definitely in that mold. Good location in an area of town with many restaurants and night spots. Close to Michigan for shopping. Overall a great stay.

Stayed here for 2 nights a few weeks ago. The previous time that we visited NYC, we stayed at the Westin (just down the street), but unfortunately the Westin was quite disappointing; the rooms at the Westin seemed run down and poorly maintained. So this time we decided to try the Intercontinental Times Square and it did not disappoint! It was absolutely amazing!! This hotel is brand new and clean, and the rooms are beautiful! Also, the bed in the hotel room was the most comfortable bed I've ever slept in! (I missed the bed at this hotel once I got back home!!!) The hotel is centrally located in Manhattan and the staff were friendly and helpful; both at the front desk and when trying to get a cab out front. The only downside to this hotel; for such a nice, new Manhattan hotel, I was unimpressed by the lobby; it seemed small, yet sparse and cold. Also, it would have been nice to have a bit of security at the entrance to the hotel (the hotel entrance goes directly into the lobby). Overall, the hotel was amazing and we had a great stay here! We will definitely stay here again in the near future!!

title_masked: Great location for my business in Financial District
text_masked:
I had never stayed at this hotel before, but I was quite pleased with the location and the service. Check-in was a breeze. The room was nice and well appointed. The bed was comfortable. The TV was updated and the channel selection was good. The desk was laid out OK for working; however there were only 2 electrical outlets on the desk itself. 
Coffee is in the lobby in the morning, which was a little inconvenient when you just want a cup to start the day. 
The hotel is connected via walkways to The Embarcadero Center, so you have access to restaurants, movie theater, and services. (If you need a dentist, there seem to be dozens of them in this place).
Peets Coffee and Starbucks are around the corner.

Staying at the L'Enfant Plaza Hotel was the icing on the cake for our trip to D.C. Snow/ice storm while we were there and chose to use cabs but great location, lovely stay, comfortable beds, good food. Combined with Travel Zoo this was a deal and a half.

The rooms at the Waldorf are definitely showing their age.... It is down right dingy..... the finishings are old, fixtures in bathroom are rusted, cracked, stained, half patched..... the carpet is dingy.... pretty much a disaster..... Further, the bathroom was not cleaned properly as I found hairs all over that were not mine... YUCK, YUCK, YUCK!!!! The rooms are in definite need of an upgrade...... Wish they would make the same investment on the rooms that they made on the lobby and hallway areas.... Very disappointing for the amount they charge per night..... Also, the room service lady taking orders was a little rude... she needs to get an attitude check if she is going to be dealing with guests. I will not choose this hotel again until they make some upgrades. My money is better spend somewhere else.

title_masked: Great location, but noisy and very basic
text_masked:
First of all the positives, the hotel is situated in a great spot, about 15-20 minutes walk to Fishermans Wharf, and right next to Chinatown and Little Italy. Mostly everything was within walking distance.
The room was clean and there was free parking included which is a big bonus, however this was a very expensive hotel with next to no facilities.We paid 698 dollars for 3 nights stay at the end of September! Which was more than we were quoted at the beginning. There was no air conditioning, it was EXTREMELY noisy, there was no fridge (which we could have done with) or microwave, the T.V. was not up to much, although to be fair we were not there to watch T.V., the wi-fi was not very good and it is close to the local fire station so there are sirens going very often including half the night and the walls are thin, so you can hear other guests including when their showers were turned on as well as all the street noise.
It is very basic, and scruffy, although clean inside the room.
The maid leaves a couple of danish pastries and there is a coffee maker in the bathroom with coffee, whitener, and sugar but that's it. We travelled for two weeks up the Californian coast from L.A. to San Francisco and this was the most expensive and least value for money place we had stayed including Hollywood, Long Beach, Santa Barbara and many more.
Even with the location and parking we would not stay there again.

I have stayed at Pacific Shores Inn 4 times in the last year and would not hesitate to recommend it to everyone. The location is close enough to walk to all lots of shops and restaurants but far enough for a quiet and peaceful stay and of course the beach is only steps away. Staff is super friendly and helpful. Rooms are large, clean and nicely decorated. The only thing I would have loved having is a hot tub by the pool!

We spent 5 nights in this hotel, rooms we clean and comfortable. The location was perfect for getting to downtown, the zoo, shopping and restaurants. We took a few excursions north of San Diego and getting there was breeze due to this location. Paying $16 a night to park was the only downside but the room rate was so reasonable it was still an affordable stay.

Pros...
+ Good location. Walking distance to shopping areas, e.g. Macy's, although subway stations are a good few blocks away. 
+ Good rooms. Good size rooms, considering it's located in midtown Manhattan. Comfortable beds. The entire hotel looks fresh - I believe that the hotel is quite new. 
+ Helpful frontdesk staff. Check-in was a breeze. The friendly staff also gave us good directions & suggestions. 
+ Reasonably priced. 
Cons...
- Lifts brokedown. No repair timeframe and/or apology were extended. We had to walk down 16 storeys as we couldn't wait any longer. My 73-year-old dad was with me. Luckily no cardiac arrest - otherwise, I would have to evoke my "never been done on a live-specimen" CPR skills. But what's a family vacation without some drama, right?? 
Overall, a good stay. I would recommend this hotel to my family & friends. 
P.S.: I'm an airline pilot who has stayed in hundreds of 3-5 star hotels.

We recently stayed at the Westin Galleria with our two teenagers and had a great time. I was a little concerned that the staff would be stuffy but we found them to all be extremely kind! The convenience to the Galleria made for a great time for us to shop, have dinner and enjoy the pool. The room was spacious and very clean. I would higly recommend this hotel!

Perfect location! On the fourth of July after the firework show the bellboy offered bottled water or juice for us ( we where all thirsty) he took us to our room bottled juices and water and did not accept a tip, we where impressed. It was late and he was soooooooo nice! Absolutely coming back to this Marriott

This is a wonderful hotel in a great location. Union station and the metro are a short walk away, and the Capitol is right around the corner. Room was clean and well-appointed and the staff were more than friendly. The rooftop pool was a great place to cool off during the hot summer days I was there. Highly recommend to families and business travelers. Available WIRED internet in addition to wireless was a nice feature (fast).

This was our first trip to New York as we were celebrating our 15th Wedding Anniversary! 
The first thing you notice when you walk in the hotel is the amazing scent in the lobby...it smelled so good!! 
Check in was wonderful and we were given a complimentary upgrade to a Sky View Room on the 29th floor for being Platinum Priority Club Members. 
Within 20 minutes of settling into our room, there was a knock at our door with a delivery of a complimentary bottle of champagne, chocolate covered strawberries, and 4 delicious plums in celebration of our Wedding Anniversary!! Our trip was off to an amazing start!!
The hotel is conveniently located in the Theatre District (44th Street & 8th Ave.) One block from Times Square and close to 9th Avenue where you can find a variety of amazing restaurants. If you are planning on seeing Phamtom of the Opera (like we did) The Majestic Theatre is just a 5 minute walk...so convenient!! If you like Jazz...Birdland Jazz Club is right across the street from the hotel. The subway is also conveniently located right next to the Hotel.
The bedroom is a nice size..not the biggest I've stayed in, but it was cozy with an amazing view!! The room had a King bed which was very comfortable and the pillows were also very comfy...every night we would lay down and sink into the pillow....Awww.....Heaven!! There was also a desk with a computer, which we found very useful for checking in for our return flight home. The bathroom was very nice and had a great rainfall shower. Every night there was turn down service as well as a complimentary chocolate left on the night table. The room was very clean and very modern...loved it!
We used the concierge service and Adrian was very helpful!! Actually, all the staff members were very friendly and always said "hello" to us everytime we walked into the hotel.
The hotel's restaurant "Ca Va" was great! A bit pricey for breakfast but the food was delicious!! In the evening we would have a drink in the lounge which was fantastic!! The decor was beautiful and very modern and we loved the Chill Music they played throughout the evening as well as throughout the entire hotel during the day. 
We absolutely loved this hotel and always felt very welcomed. I highly recommend this hotel if you are staying in New York....I know we will definitely be back!

My mother and I stayed here this past weekend to attend the North Wood Women's (?) Club dinner event. We mainly went to hear comedian Jeanne Robertson. As soon as you pull up to the hotel a valet comes up to your window and greets you and asks for your name. He brings a cart and puts your luggage on it (while you just stand there and watch) and takes you to the front desk. At the front desk I asked for a complimentary gold fish, that is advertised on the website (you can get one if you were unable to bring your pets with you since it is a pet friendly hotel.) They were out of gold fish at the moment, but Gavin said he would see what he could do. The bail boy will not only take you (he's pushing the luggage cart) up to your room he will unload the luggage cart and set the items neatly on the bed. In the closet you will find comfy animal print robes. We had two beds and one robe so I called the front desk and they said we should have had two and they would send one up. Not even five minutes later there was a knock at the door. We opened to a guy holding a black and white zebra print robe AND a vase with a gold fish. The room was pretty and clean but we didn't see where the full price tag came into play (we got a discount on the room due to attending the event.) There isn't a gift shop or vending machine anywhere but there are (pricey) snacks in the mini bar. The bathroom has a sliding door which is very odd as it doesn't feel as private as the bathroom should feel. There was a rattling noise throughout the night, but we never did pinpoint if it was coming from the vents or not. Even though we were on the sixth floor we could hear traffic as if we were on the first. We enjoyed a massage at the Exhale Spa (which is located to the right of the hotel) which was lovely. I had a hair and make up appointment at the Pompeo Salon (which is to the left of the hotel.) The Pompeo Salon was very up scale, it even had a bar while you were waiting. The lady who did my hair was nice (not to mention gorgeous) and so was her assistant (he started on my curls and then she appeared at the end to finish the style) but I wasnt impressed with my overall experience there as far as my hair goes. The only product she put in my hair was hair spray so my curls fell out and were flat and crunchy before the end of the night. The lady who did my make up did an excellent job. She was very down to earth and would talk to you. I dont think the hair stylist said more than 10 words to me the 30 minutes I was there. After the event we wanted to get something to eat but didn't want to fight the Dallas traffic so we asked Gavin, at the front desk, how we call a taxi, he offered to do it and then said if we wanted to stay in he had a couple of menus from restaurants who deliver until 3am (it was 1:30am). We stayed in and ordered spaghetti from Zini Italian and it got there at 2am. (Oh! They dont accept cash passed midnight!) The spaghetti was so spicy we only had a couple of bites and threw it away. The Zini bread is really good though. Overall it was a fun and exciting experience (we not only got to meet Jeanne Robertson we also got to hang out with her in the Palomar restaurant) but nothing real breathtaking.

There were four of us staying here for 5 nights from the 8th of October 2012. The hotel is still undergoing renovations but our room was newly renovated on the 14th floor. The room was clean, modern and quiet. It was small but apparently most hotel rooms in New York are small. We knew this before we booked and knew it wouldn't be a concern as we didn't plan to spend any time in the room other than to shower and sleep. The location is fantastic and close to theaters, restaurants and shops. This hotel was perfect for us as we didn't want to spend a fortune on a hotel room just for sleeping in. There was one day we didn't have hot water due to the renovations and the only fault in the room was the air conditioner which stopped working after the first couple of days. We called the problem through twice but it was never fixed. We didn't worry as the weather was cool and we just opened the window slightly.

title_masked: Facilities nice, reservation management needs improvement
text_masked:
I am a Kimpton fan, and found this hotel, overall, in keeping with the brand's image and execution. However, they mucked up my reservation pretty good, caused significant inconvenience, and then mucked up their apology. Net, a lot of muck ups.
I extended my reservation by one day, the reservations agent assured me that this would be included in my original reservation, no need to change rooms or check out and re-check in. When I checked in, they had the right dates, everything seemed fine. I returned to my room to get materials for a meeting and found I was locked out (because they did NOT extend the reservation as promised and as indicated when I checked in). The ensuing chaos resulted in my being hugely late for a meeting. They attempted to compensate by giving me extra coupons to use with the minibar, but then wouldn't honor them (you can only use 1 per stay!). When I brought this up to the front desk staff, they said there was nothing they could do. 
Really disappointing. Not sure I'll stay at this Kimpton again.

We stayed 3 nights at the Embassy and were well impressed with the setup of the hotel. From the first experience at reception the service was very good to the room which was well equipped and very clean. The beds were very comfy and the pull out bed was more than adequate for the children. The all inclusive breakfast was extensive and just about anything you could wish for was on offer. It really set us up for the day and we hardly needed to have a lunch! 
The overall location was good ie fairly quiet (apart from the kids on the lower levels who were obviously enjoying themselves) and was only 10 mins from the airport and 15 mins into Beale Street for the bars and clubs

clean, close to all downtown restaurants, easy walk (10 mins) to convention centre.
The hotel is small but makes you feel special. Many personal touches ie, turn down service, hotel car service etc.
The rooms were nice and dark for sleeping. Ask for the larger suite rooms.
The pool is small but unique as it has a glass wall that you can swim up to and look down at the city street. Excellent pool side food. Burgers are huge and you can share....tasty too!

title_masked: Old School Charm; New School Feel
text_masked: This is a new and clean facility and everything is state of the art. From the keys to the carpets, to the LCD screens. The Lobby is not in the ground floor. It is very conveniently located for people visiting Penn's Ivy League Campus and close to most of the on campus shopping, dining and entertainment. They have nice Penn inspired details, photos and decor yet it is not as kitschy as the Inn at Penn which is "too Penn". Breakfast is good but not excellent. In our case the scrambled eggs were baked and dry. The make it yourself waffles were good. Believe it or not, its valet parking is competitive with the nearby University facility. The hotel is clustered around renovated townhomes and apartments suited for off campus housing of students. It has a swimming pool and great internet connection. The staff is quite accommodating. When we arrived they did not have the room we requested and gave us one that was not made up. They apologized and took care of us by giving us a better room. That was nice. The beds were the most comfortable I have slept in for quite a while.

We have stayed here many times as carefree singles, a married coupe on a business trip and most recently as new parents with 4 month old in tow. This place never disappoints and we never get a bill that makes us feel guilty. With a sexy bar, easy wifi and attentive staff amd killer comfy beds we always enjoy our stay. Even with a four month old in tow we didn't feel skid dish or out of place. They have a wonderfully diverse clientele that always makes the bar a great people watching pew. It's our home in new York.

We pedaled up to the DoubleTree in the pouring rain after an all-day mud-filled bike ride. We were tired, filthy, and soaked, and there was no way we could (or wanted to) make it to our planned destination, a campground 10 miles up the coast. I walked into reception, my muddy shoes leaving a trail behind me across the highly polished lobby floors. The staff quickly found a room for us, offered to store our bikes in a back office, and even took us around back to fill buckets of steaming hot water and help us wash the dripping mud off of our bikes. This location offers a shuttle service anywhere within six miles, so they drove us out to dinner, waiting while we picked up our food and drove us back again. The hotel itself is spotless, new, and comfortable. I highly recommend.

Alan was very thoughtful and kind during my stay on Radisson Lexington Hotel.
The hotel is cheap and well located.

I stayed here for three nights while in the process of moving out of my house and out of state. The room was quiet, comfortable and clean, and it included a mini-fridge and a small microwave.
