Pets are welcome, which is great because I was moving with three cats in tow. When I travel with pets I often stay at La Quintas, and I've stayed at some which were really not so nice. This one, however, I have no complaints about.

title_masked: Would've been "alright", check out made it "forget it".
text_masked:
Booked well ahead, and requested a room away from the highway, but were assigned on the highway side anyway. Alright, no big deal - yes, you can hear it, but after a few days travelling it wasn't a huge deal... light sleepers, however, should insist on being on the opposite side as the noise is certainly there.
The room was furnished decently and clean, exactly as one would expect but nothing exceptional. A bit dark in the furnishings, but cozy nonetheless. No love lost on the sliding washroom door - no lock and a little gap would be uncomfortable for many no doubt, even we found it a little off-putting (and we're not the shy type). Though the purpose is obviously to cut down on the intrusion of a swing door into the space, the execution left something to be desired. We weren't offered a selection of beds either, and were given a room with two twin beds. For a couple, it made for an uncomfortably cramped night, not to mention the obviously older spring mattresses had lost some resilience over the years - sitting on the edge landed me promptly on the floor at one point as the mattress edge crumpled away beneath me. Good for a laugh, if nothing else, but not the high standard that it seems the property is going for.
Staff were great from check in to room service, always helpful, polite and courteous. Some exception was taken to the valet/bellman whom seemed to disappear each time we started to approach, but could be chalked up to poor timing. The spoiler for the whole stay, however, was on check out. We intended to check our baggage and grab lunch at Pike Market (the hill is very steep - consider heading down 6th to Pike for an easier trek), and checked out at the desk well before noon when no one else was around. As we checked out, the desk agent, Sarah, was efficient if curt in processing us, however she did answer the phone in the middle of our interaction without so much as an "excuse me" and generally appeared disinterested or unhappy. We felt as though we'd interrupted her and were rather unwelcome. Chalking it up to maybe a slight misstep or peculiar moment, we were disappointed when we arrived back to collect our bags and encountered much the same attitude. Nearly no eye contact, barely 3 words spoken, and a very disinterested feeling. Felt like a burden to get our bags - half expected a sigh about the request, honestly. Not sure if this particular agent was having an off day or just a foul person, but certainly didn't leave us wanting to hurry back.
Bottom Line: Even booking well ahead and getting a better than average price, the stay wasn't worth it. The lack-luster experience and obvious non-attention to details like the twin beds and ignoring the "not highway side" request was topped with the single least interested desk agent we've ever encountered. Dressing up a 2 star experience in 5 star prices and attitude doesn't cut it. Our next trip to Seattle we'll be staying elsewhere.

title_masked: decent accommodation if you're paying under $200 per night.
text_masked: Room was alright and breakfast leaves nothing to be desired. Location is relatively good, far enough from Tenderloin area to seem safe. However, too many other choices around San Francisco to settle Found it over-rated. Should be just average..

title_masked: Great location, clean, spacious rooms, on a hill though!
text_masked:
Great hotel, parking is about $60, but secure and they are quick to get your car for you. Very friendly check in staff, gave us a great room on the corner of the bulding (bigger than the other rooms) Our room was a twin, 2 huge doubles, very comfy, mattress toppers, best nights sleep ive had in a while! Bathroom clean with a nice little walk in waldrobe and dressing area. Internet was $15 for 24 hours, however because we are Marriott timeshare holders the concierge waived this for us (always worth asking). 
Situated in the beautiful Nob Hill area, 5 minute walk (steep hill!) or tram ride down to Union Square and Macy's. Great Irish pub on O'Farrell down the road (great beers, lively atmosphere, have the wings!).
Overall a fantastic property, beautiful building, great staff, perfect location. Worth staying on this side of town rather than Fisherman's Wharf which is a bit grotty.

The title pretty much sums up the stay. Mold throughout the bathroom, dirty floors which I wouldn't recommend walking barefoot on, and cramped quarters. Fantastic ambiance with beer bottles being thrown against the walls in the alley below as well as people yelling and fighting all night NOT!. I have stayed at MANY Seattle hotels, this one should definitely be included on the "Worst of Seattle" list. EXTREMELY over-rated and over-priced, NEVER again.

Was at this hotel with my friend and we truly enjoyed our stay. The pool area is very nice, clean and great towels, plenty of sun beds. The rooms were spacious, clean and with great ammeninites. It is also the perfect location. I would definitely stay there again.

This hotel is in a great location. Super clean. Trendy. In the middle of everything. Its the perfect place for business people, or people who want to party and crash downtown. I can't think of as many cons as pros, but it just wasn't my style. My room was paid by a third party, but I don't think I would have enjoyed it near as much If I had paid $200 bucks for it. There wasn't enough signage. Very hard to find. I'm not used to paying $20 a day to park. I know this sounds negative, but I realize that this hotel is perfect for the people it caters to.(young, party people, business people who need to be downtown.)

Then on top of that the next day the other guy that was in the room was allowed back into the hotel after being released from jail. Cops came back out again as he fled from paying his cab far. I told my husband it was time to get our children and belongings and get the hell out of there.

We went to Boston for a 1 night get-away and Hotel 140 was perfect. Location was convenien (right off 90), public parking was right next door and we walked to the T, dinner, and the theatre. The staff was kind and thorough. Although a little on the warm side with the air on (we tend to like it cooler than others though) the room was just right. Simple, clean, with the appropriate amenities for a nice stay. Highly recommended for last-minute, affordable nights out!

We got this deal on priceline, which was a little bit disappointing. The location was ok, near the Japan town. The furniture is classic but old. The room is too small, and there is no customer service. Parking was expensive.

Our daughter was attending orientation at DePaul University and we were looking for a hotel relatively close to the school, and not wanting to spend a fortune. I happened onto Hotel Indigo during my internet search, the reviews were very favorable, and the price was right. We really enjoyed our three-night stay at Hotel Indigo. We were on the 10th floor, and in a corner room, with two queen beds. It wasn't the smallest hotel room I've ever had, but definitely couldn't be called large. However, the beds were quite comfortable, we enjoyed the little sitting area, and it was fun to be in a hotel that actually had some color. 
This hotel is in a mostly residential neighborhood, but is in a really great location. We had reservations to see a show at Second City, on Wells Street, and were about a 15 minute walk from there. If you are looking for lots of nice little cafes and such, Wells Street is an excellent place to go. It is also an easy walk to the north end of Michigan Avenue, near Watertower Place, and the Hancock Building, though you can also take the El. The Clark/Division El stop on the Red Line is about a block and a half from the Hotel Indigo.
The employees at Hotel Indigo were all friendly and helpful. The room was very comfortable and clean. We will definitely be staying here again on trips to Chicago to visit our daughter.

Clean but dark rooms...price is alot much than it worths...furniture is getting old...location is good..car rentals are close..central park is close..fitness center is small but ok...i was hoping better because it is a butique newyork city hotel with a very high price level..but hardly satisfied...

Excellent stay with very attentive staff. Would be happy to recommend this hotel and would return if in Chicago again. Front desk staff exceptional and extremely friendly. Very helpful with regards to directions and general questions regarding Chicago

We stayed at Distrikt from 17Sept for 8 nights. Check in and check out was quick & easy. Staff were always smiling and super helpful with directions, reservations, and restaurant recommendations. The room itself was lovely - clean and modern. Nice touches with brownies on arrival and weather card, news paper iced tea at reception, in room coffee machine and chocolates daily. Great view from the 28th floor. Easy walk to subway, times square and thearters.
The bistro serves inexpensive meals (we loved the breakfasts) and the staff in the bistro are great too!(Miguel).
The only smal negative is that there isn't a usable inroom fridge, but that would in no way stop me from staying at the distrikt next visit, in fact, I wouldn't stay anywhere else.

title_masked: Great staff, great accommodations, and location to subway was nice too.
text_masked: Everyone from the girls who checked us in & gave us YUMMY cookies to a young man on night shift who I think did something w/laundry maybe his name was [NAME]? The guys who kept our suitcases safe & the bartenders were extremely accommodating as well. All the services where fantastic. We weren't sure if we should have stayed uptown by time square or not, but We liked the quaintness of the area and easy access to subway. There were enough bars & restaurant in the gerneral area & neon wasn't keeping us up. We would FOR SURE stay again. Sorry for not having all the names of staff, but anyone we came in contact w/ @ hotel was great- keep it up!

...however $29 for valet-only parking is utterly ridiculous. Also, management needs to be able to plan/think ahead for large groups and the inevitable breakfast line barrage. One morning the line was out the dining room and nearly down the stairs to the lobby. A separate ready to eat hot/cold buffet line could have been put up in an adjacent room. Good beer on tap and adequate snacks during managers reception were a plus as were the work out room and spa tub.

title_masked: They take good care of you here!
text_masked: I was just at the Sheraton for two weeks for work purposes. The staff was wonderful about making me comfortable and seeing to my needs for quiet and rest when done with my day. I really appreciated that they had a cut off time for pool parties. Not to rain on anyone's parade, but some of us have to work on weekdays, so the good news is that pool parties cut off around 10 pm, a reasonable time for anyone needing to wake up early, as many of us did. Special thanks to Dee Carson and Lonnie at the Sheraton Cimarron Restaurant. Dee keeps the coffee coming and always has a warm smile for everyone. Lonnie is great at making delicious omlettes or eggs any way you like 'em! Thanks for helping us get off to a great start ladies, we really appreciated it!

We stayed here for a night while visiting Austin. The room, which had 2 queen beds and a separate small living area with a desk, another tv, and a mini fridge, was perfect for our family of 4. Smooth check in and check out. Great service and beautiful, inviting lobby area. The location of this hotel is ideal if you want something in North Austin.

My husband and I live in NYC, and we went on a "staycation" and celebrated our one-year anniversary at Ink48. I did a lot of research to find a hotel that would meet our high expectations for our celebration. Ink48 gave us the experience we were hoping for. We had a beautiful, large room with an amazing view. The rooftop bar was beautiful, as was the lobby, and I loved the complimentary coffee in the morning! We did not eat at the restaurant at Ink48 so I can't comment, but the rooftop bar had a good crowd when we got back from dinner and it seemed like a hot spot in the city. Jeffrey sent wine and chocolates to our room to celebrate, which we loved. Everything was so clean and it felt very peaceful, which is harder to achieve in a bustling place like NYC. This hotel is a little bit off the beaten path of stores and restaurants that fill up other streets. We liked that, and preferred to get away from the large crowds as we walked back to the hotel. My only suggestion would be if you want to be in the center of the hustle and bustle of Times Square and the city, then this is probably not the best option. If you don't mind walking over an avenue or two to get there, and appreciate feeling some peace and quiet in the place you relax and sleep, then you will love it here.

We spent a week with the kids in NYC, The location was a good choice. The kid’s room could sleep 4. They have a deal for $200 per room plus tax and it is worth no more.
The rooms are clean and comfortable and if you are lucky to get a high floor with a park view or if you can afford the extra charge, don’t miss it. The rooms definitely need renovation. The location is best for Central Park and Fifth Avenue. The service is good and the staff was very friendly.
Would be nice to have a coffee machine in the room. Don’t waste money on the hotel breakfast. There is a Sarabeth’s next door, or if you can walk 2 blocks, don’t miss having breakfast at Le Pain Quotidien on 58th and 7th.

DC was at full capacity on my recent visit and the only room I could get at a hotel near my meeting was a "Club" level room at the Renaissance. Expensive, but I had to pay the price for convenience. As has been mentioned, this is a busy convention hotel with a well designed lobby with nice bars and creative nooks and crannies for conversation. The lobby seems to serve as a "home base" for lots of non guests having little one on one meetings, which I am fine with for this type of business hotel. Food and service was as expected. The only strange thing seemed to be that my "Club" level room was a very standard twin room on a very standard floor. My key did give me access the "Club" (nice little appetizer buffet, honor bar) but it was on a mezzanine off the lobby and not near my room which I thought was unusual and inconvenient. Other than that, a fine business hotel.

We checked into our room around 4pm only to find that our room had not been cleaned at all. Instead of putting us in another room they made us wait in the hall for 30 minutes while they cleaned. The walls were filthy and the comforter was torn. The window screen was secured in place with paper towels. We paid $15 for pay per view on an old 90's television which was static the whole time.

This is a great choice in a hotel! The staff was very friendly, and prompt when needed! Being in downtown Dallas, the valet parking was a plus. My room was on the fifth floor, which was a little noisey at night, because of the outside noises. The next night when friends arrived, we stayed in a room on the 23rd floor. This was much better, being higher up the noises weren't a problem! The hotel was conviently located near resturants and bars in walking distance. Will definitely be back!

Just come back from my annual shopping trip to New York, stayed at th eAffinia Shelburne. Always looked after at this hotel. Asked for a quiet room before we went, and got just that on arrival. Nothing was too much trouble for them. Rooms are big and well furnished and the staff great. I am a massive fan of New York and seem to find something different to rave about every year. Places I would recommend, The View at The Marriott Marquis in Times Square. This revolving bar and restaurant on the top floor of the hotel, views are incredible, go at sunset for the best experience. Never eaten there but the cocktails are lovely. My other new find which I loved was a restaurant called [NAME], a mecca to all food italian, 5 italian eateries under one roof plus a huge Italian deli all in one building. This place is in the Flatiron district, really relaxed and it was buzzing. Food great and the cheapest and nicest glass of wine $7.00 that i have ever drunk in New York.

Though it doesn't look too good from the street, this hotel is a little gem! The room we were in was spacious with a magnificent view of Alkatraz. We could walk to Pier 39 in minutes and the wonderful trams were minutes walk away. The staff were extremely helpful - the best we had in New York, San Francisco and Las Vegas, nothing was too much trouble.
As a tourist you need breakfast to set you up for the day, and in America that is all you need for about 8 hours! We had breakfast in the I Hop next door - which was a fairly typical diner, mountains of food at reasonable prices. Closes at 10pm.
The hotel does not have a bar or restaurant, which means that you have to make the effort to go out to eat, but you can order in and sit around the fire pit with a bottle of wine - splendid if you have had a long day out and really 'can't be bothered' to make the effort. Wish I had spent more time in this wonderful city

title_masked: Cheap, Central, WIFI not that great
text_masked:
This long-stayed hotel is probably the best value you get if you stay at the galleria area and it is member of the Holiday-Inn club.
Staff is great, very helpful. A 24h store with an honorary system is available to you (no beer though)
The WiFi is just horrible - you have to login each and every time you unlock your phone and it is just too slow - just use your 3g.
Great deal if you're on a budget - almost 50% off the main hotels around this area.

We paid $189 base rate for a queen room. We chose this place because we wanted a place close to Pike's Market but didn't want to pay the high prices. The Mediterranean Inn charged $189 base price in July 2012. We took it. 
We had to walk 30 minutes to Pike's Market (which was fine with us...got to view the area while walking). It is downhill going to Pike's Market, but UPHILL getting back to the hotel. Take the buses for $2.50.
The room was nice....NO ac, but it was cool enough that we didn't need it. They do have ceiling fans and an oscillating fan when asked. The room was very clean (which is the most important thing) but the mattress was average. Everything was clean, clean, clean....that's what we care about, right? 
There is a Safeway grocery across the street which was very convenient. We had breakfast at the Mecca Cafe about 1/2 block down...AWESOME! Very good, casual, eclectic, reasonably priced.
Don't neglect the great roof-top view at the Mediterranean Inn. You can see the harbor on one side and the city on the other. Many guests take a glass of wine or other beverage to enjoy the view.
The employees are very friendly and accommodating. 
Starbucks is attached...SURPRISE

We were in town for the Quilt Show and this was a perfect location. The staff were extremely helpful, even for infomation about the area, not just the hotel. Great job Shelby, Mag, Nicole and Pedro (the bartender). It was convenient to eat at the hotel restuarant and the food was excellent in taste and value.
Great to have the coffee and snacks in the lobby and good access to internet. We will definitely stay there again if we come to another Quilt show

We just returned from staying at this particular location. We have stayed at many other locations of Homewood Suites and they have been good experiences. The bedroom had a strrange smell as well as the hallway and the bathroom. The bathroom smelled of old urine. The beds were not too comfortable but when you laid in them you could smell an old musty animal smell like it was in the mattress and the pillows. 
The lady named [NAME] in the kitchen was late at getting the food out for the breakfast and was very sharp and rude to us. 
I did also notice a cockroach near the main floor bathroom. The staff was notified and sprayed the room. 
I would not recommend this location until measures are taken to clean it up!

The hotel is exactly as pictured on the webpage- nice size room, small fridge, sink, microwave (no utensils or cookware provided though). It was clean, and included breakfast was good with both hot and cold items. Staff friendly and small issues were taken care of very rapidly. 
The hotel is very convenient to light rail which as a solo traveling female was fine in the morning. However, returning around 8:30 pm, I did have a rather uncomfortable moment where a group of young men yelled some questionable things at me after passing me on the sidewalk as I walked from the stop to the hotel. I didn't feel in acute danger, but the situation was stressful enough I would hesitate to make that trek by myself after dark again. Unlike many others in the neighborhood, the doors to the rooms are in the interior, which helps with security.

title_masked: Poor management leads to a poor hotel
text_masked:
Before i write this review folks, please review my other reviews to see that I have been nothing but positive up to this point. Also please go back through the reviews of this particular hotel to see that many of these issues that I am about to bring to your attention have been brought up numerous times before in past reviews and you will notice that the management of this hotel always responds to cover their hineys by saying "we are unaware of this" or "sorry we are working on it" or " We apologize but we will look into this" but they never seem to do anything about it.
Also folks, if you are looking for a location near sea world, there is a hyatt hill country right next door to this hilton that has wonderful reviews and we wish we would of stayed there instead.
We went to san antonio for the weekend. There was four of us. Myself and my wife and my two very young children. We picked this hotel because of the location and the price. For us it was about $150 a night. When we first arrived in the hotel, we were told that the hotel was booked solid and we could not take advantage of our suite upgrade. When we went to our room, we noticed it was very warm in there, but it was very late and we were tired from driving 5 hours. We brought to the front desks attention that it was hot in our room but was told that there were no other rooms available. We were tired and wanted sleep.
We had two queen beds. Each adult slept with one child. Before we went to bed we decided to shower. We noticed that there were only 3 bath towels, no wash, no hand and there were 4 of us in the room (this was written about in previous reviews and they still have not fixed this issue). So i of course had to go on a towel run at 11 o'clock at night. The room was warm but we made it through the night.
The next day we left and went to sea world. We had a blast. We made it back to our room about 8 pm and once again noticed the room as hot and you guessed it, only 3 towels for 4 guests. I went to get more towels and told the management to come check our AC. The guy that came to check our air said our air was blowing at 77, there was ice on the line (which in my book means a blown compressor) and that we should move to another room. But of course once again there were no other rooms available so we had a choice. We could stay in our hot room, or pack up and move to another room with one queen bed and 2 of us would have to sleep in a roll away. As we were checking into our new smaller room (just as hot) we were approached by two other people on our floor that had broken air conditioners too. One of them was having a wall unit put in, and the other was going to check out and go somewhere else.
We were told by the management that we would have both nights taken care of and we would not have to pay for our stay given all the issues we had. When we checked out of the hotel, only one night was removed and i was told to call and discuss the other night with the service manager of the hotel. After numerous messages to them with no return calls, i called hilton directly- they contacted the manager and he said he was not going to cover our stay and didnt care what circumstances we had. I will not stay at this property and probably not another hilton property again for a long time until they get their act together. I work in the travel industry and i book hotels and airfare for people with medical conditions and to think that one of my customers may of been stuck in this hotel scares the daylights out of me.
I would strongly suggest staying elsewhere. Lets see the manager write one of his "i was unaware" follow ups to this review.
A couple positive notes - it was close to sea world, and the kids pool was great. BUYER BEWARE!

Stayed here on a business trip and I am so glad I did. This hotel seems to operate very smoothly. Front desk staff was helpful, and offered excellent dinner suggestions. I stayed on the 6th floor and the view of the city was actually quite nice. The bed was very comfortable and clean.
However, the real treat is the Press Lounge. The view and the atmosphere are nothing short of awesome.
I highly recommend this hotel.

It was not our first stay there but it was the first one since the rooms were refurbished. The hotel did a pretty good job but it seems there is less space in the room now (we had a 2-double-bed one)... The bathroom appeared to be definitely too small and not convenient. Moreover, there is still no breakfast commodities within the hotel.
Ok, these are not big issues but quite a pity regarding the price per night (more than $300 + taxes!) and amenities offered by other hotel brands for equivalent (or even lower) fees...
The good thing : the hotel is quiet (we had a room on the swimming pool) and well-located for sure (even though I think Fisherman's Wharf is not the nicest neighborhood to stay in San Francisco : this is a highly touristic spot!).

We stayed at Le Parker for two full weeks and didn't have the slightest complaint. We were located on the 29th floor (no park view) and we didn't have any issues with either outside noise or room temperature (it is true that it takes some time for the air conditioning to really kick in). 
Room was spacious and actually visually better than how it seamed from the pictures. Cleaning was amazing. Very efficient and discreet, we were never bothered, not even once in 14 days! 
Location is amazing, just look at the map and you will easily understand that. TV sets are old but I know that they currently replace them. WiFi is not free (only at the lobby and the bar) but that's the case in every NYC hotel that I checked with (I really don't get why this happens, free wifi is a plus for someone to choose a hotel nowadays)
Last but not least, sleep quality was very high, bed and pillows were perfect!

within walking distance of central park,times square,grand central and the empire state building..rooms large enough to sleep and watch TV but that's about it.
fridge provided and ironing board but no iron.
no tea and coffee facility's in room.
safe would not lock so I had to get security to re set it.
the air con when you put it on sounded like it was going to take off with a large grinding noise and would not give any hot air out so I reported this to the reception who said they would get an engineer to look at it whilst we were out,if the did then the certainly didn't fix it.
when we checked in the gentlemen on reception said welcome this is you room and go to the lift your on the 22ND floor and that was about it.he may of said a few more words than what I have typed but this is how it felt.yet when we were going a couple booking in got the guided tour of new york ,broad way eating places and anything else the would of needed to know.but what a contrast in there meet and greet to ours.
watch out for the lift its not the fastest in the world,there is 3 but when ones broke you need to expect a wait.
as you walk into reception there is a lovely bar area but is not in use as well as the dining area.considering its advertised outside as an international lounge and restaurant its a large disappointment.
out and about is as easy as walking around at home and the underground is cheap and easy to use.dont bother with the yellow cabs they ar a waste of money ane time.evan to and from the airport we used the http://www.supershuttle.com its half the cost and very reliable.
the stay in new york was great and you can do just about anything at any time of the day or night.
the down side is the NYPD - not helpful at all and dont seem to smile.street sellers constantly in your face on every corner and the shops hit you with the tax after you see what you have decided to buy what you want

title_masked: Excellent location, room amenties and staff!
text_masked: Location can't be beat -- an easy walk to Times Square, and even easier walk to the diverse restaurants of Hell's Kitchen. The room was very quiet, the bed was heavenly, the kitchen was a huge plus, and the staff was very accommodating -- welcoming us with bottled water and snacks, allowing us a 2 p.m. checkout the day we left, and holding our luggage til we left for the airport. We'll be back!

This was the worst hotel I have EVER stayed in.!The lobby was gloomy and the staff not welcoming. Our room was dark and dingy with old, ugly window treatments and an in-the-window loud air conditioner. The bathroom floor was sticky UGH! There was no light over the ridiculously low mirror over the sink and no place to put your toiletries. There was some kind of tape over the wiring by the mirror (probably for the missing light), I had to stoop down to look into the mirror. I actually had to bring a chair into the room so that I could sit and dry my hair. There also was no cover over the toilet seat. When they made the bed, they just threw the pillows haphazardly toward the headboard. Hotel is nothing like the website portrayed it to be. I couldn't wait to leave and won't ever be back.

Stayed at the Doubletree this past weekend after arriving on the Amtrak from Minnesota. The location is fantastic and the staff was very professional. Kenneth and John at the Concierge desk were always on task answering any questions we had about restaurants, shopping and other attractions. They always took their time with us and gave us great information. The front desk staff was very courteous and provided the kids with hot, fresh cookies whenever asked, which was a lot! Rooms were very clean and comfortable. The gentleman handling the luggage and storing it for us on Sunday morning was very professional and was working very hard for his pay. Kudos to him as well. We would definitely stay here on future trips.

I recently traveled to Chicago for business and stayed at the Sheraton Chicago. If you are up for experiencing the amenities of this beautiful city and staying in an "over the top" hotel, this is the place for you. 
This hotel is strategically located within walking distance of one of Chicago's best shopping experiences: the Miracle Mile, and is just blocks away from Navy Pier. Taking in these must-see experiences in downtown Chicago will be convenient and enjoyable while staying at this beautiful hotel.
The view of Chicago's skyscrapers at night from my room was absolutely breathtaking. This, in addition to a beautiful decor, cleanliness and "over the top" service, makes this hotel my #1 choice when visiting this city. This hotel is an expert is sleeping comfort. You will sleep in comfort as never experienced before with this hotel's signature mattress and bedding series.
Parking is convenient and safe with the Sheraton's valet or self-parking options, with elevator service directly to the hotel lobby.
All of these services made my experience the best that Chicago has to offer with my stay at the Sheraton Chicago.

I moved here from the noisy Sir Francis Drake hotel for my last 2 nights in San Fran. This property was farther from Union Square so wasn't so loud. I also didn't have a corner room. That helped. Being sleep deprived from being on the 6th floor at the SFD, I requested a high floor at the Parc and ended up on the 23rd. The BIG disappointment about this property is the lack of sauna. The information provided said that there was one on property. But when I wen't to sit and sweat, is was no where to be found. After calling the front desk from the house phone in the fitness center, they informed me that it had been removed when the fitness center was expended. Bummer. Instead, I went back to my room and opened my book. Aside from that, the room offered a nice view of the city, plenty of lounging furniture and space, a great bed, perfect climate control, and hot water that is one degree from steam...watch it! I would stay here again. Especially because I enjoyed a wonderful night (2) of uninterrupted sleep!!

Usually I do not write hotel reviews, but I believe that Four Seasons Boston deserves an excellet review. Four Seasons exceeded my expectations in every single detail especially when it comes to baby care. The staff starting from the bell boy to the receptionist were extremely friendly, They greeted my 19month baby with a collection of toys and made him choose what he liked.
The location is perfect, its right infront of the Boston Park and a minute away from newbury street. I really enjoyed my stay in Four Seasons, and would definitely stay in it again if I visit Boston in the future.

We stayed at this hotel for a week in November. It's in a great location, really close to Bowery and Grand Street subway stations between China Town and Little Italy. We got the airtrain from JFK airport then the subway to Bowery station then walked a few blocks to the hotel. The journey took around 1hr 30 mins but it wasn't too bad. 
We had a Queen Room on the 8th floor and it was adequate for our needs. You can hear slight noise from outside traffic but its to be expected in a large city. After a day or two you get used to it. Noise also travels along the corridor outside and you can hear people coming and going. 
Breakfast in the morning was great and there was loads of choice. Bread, pastries, muffins, various types of eggs, sausages, yoghurts and fruit, juices and tea and coffee etc. Breakfast was served from 7am - 10am every day. We made the mistake of going around 9am on our second day and pretty much everything had gone. When I asked if I could have a yoghurt or a banana I was told they had all gone because of the sheer number of people and there was no more. So we tended to go earlier around 8am and had no problems.
Staff were helpful proving information about the local area and maps etc. You can store your luggage at the hotel on checkout for 5 dollars as well.
On the website it say there's a gym. Its on the 10th floor and consists of 2 pieces of gym equipment! You literally step out of the lift into the gym! As we did plenty of walking on holiday I didn't need to use it. Can't imagine it gets too busy though if you did want to use it.
Will definately stay here again when I visit New York. It is only a few stops away from Times Square and Central Park on the subway. It was clean, tidy and everything we wanted.

This hotel was very nice and right in the middle of all the fun. It's only about a mile to the Navy Pier, beach, shopping, and restaurants. The room as well as the hotel was very nice and clean. The staff was very helpful and pleasant. My only complaint is there was no microwave in the room. As nice as this hotel was you would think they would have offered a mini refrigerator and/or hotel. Even though there was no microwave the in house restaurant was nice enough to warm my food for me. I will definitely stay at this hotel again and will highly recommend this property. I will say too that it is about a 20 min cab ride to the ORD airport (est.$40).

title_masked: Modern use of Old World Charm
text_masked:
Great great hotel. wonderful wood panelling and decor. Great charm and ambience.
Wonderful restaurant setting. I would not suggest the buffet breakfast as this was limited when compared with other international hotels around the world. Order off the menu. The rooms great and comfortable even though on the smallish size. Very convenient location close to Quincy Market and Boston Common. Would definitely recommend as a super place to stay in Boston. So much history at and around the hotel.

My wife and I travel to indy at least once a year to go to a colts game. We have been staying at this same motel for 4 years now and find it to be very clean and comfortable on each of our visits. rooms are spacious and comfortable. Breakfast is good and they have a nice selection of food items. easy access off of route 65 south. A short distance to lucas oil stadium so motel is convient when I am in town. the staff is friendly and eager to be of any help that you might need. Very well lit parking lot with plenty of parking. We always have a nice stay at this motel

I stayed with my 2 young children, and the room as clean, spacious enough, and the location was fantastic - a few feet from the beach AND a great playground! There are plenty of shops and restaurants within walking distance. Staff was helpful, though since it is the beach there is a laid-back vibe. Nice views from rooftop bar. We booked a suite so we would have a kitchenette plus a little more room for the kids, which was great.

title_masked: One of the nicest Days Inn's
text_masked: Traveled down with my brother and a couple fo friends to CBus for the OSU Spring Game and booked at this hotel. Normally, I overlook Days Inn Motels because I find that most of them are disgusting. However, since my brother booked this hotel without my knowledge, I decided that since it was only for one night I would grin and bear it. Needless to say, I found that this is not your typical disgusting Days Inn. The hotel was very clean as were the rooms. The grounds were tidy and it really looks like the owners take pride in this hotel. The staff was excellent and we had no problems. The price was right and the next time I spend the night in Columbus, I will definitely book here. There are also many restaurants within walking distance from this hotel.

Such a fun place to stay if you want to feel the full glam of LA. Great customer service and great on-site partying! We ended up extending our stay an extra night because we were enjoying ourselves. Great design and rooms look fabulous.

my wife and I stayed two nights this past weekend. The hotel is beautiful, the staff is beautiful - and so nice - no attitude, just glad we were there. Location is close to everything you could want, right across from Chelsea We were on the 11th floor and the room was great but a little close to the club. When we asked if we could change rooms the concierge Carly Skinner was so helpful and moved us down a couple of floors and upgraded our room without our asking. Our bags were moved and the entire experience was painless. I would higly recommend the Dream and plan to stay there in the future.

title_masked: Holiday Inn San Antonio North Hill
text_masked: Spent a week in San Antonio for the 2012 GSA Tradeshow & Expo. First time in San Antonio. Great time of year to come. Summers get pretty hotttt! I'm a regular Holiday Inn customer and was very happy with the staff and services. Definitely a solid 3 star hotel with a 5 star in services. Manager Shawn Kenworthy does an excellent job as General Manager. Being so far away from my home in New York, Shawn and his staff really went out of their way to make us feel at home. I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone traveling to the San Antonio area. Staff recommended Smoky Mo's for Barbeque and it was excellent and the prices were very reasonable. Only 5 minutes from the hotel too. Thank you Holiday Inn! r/ CJ Byers- President- Pleasant Valley Energy, LLC [--]

Yes, I will agree with some others that have left not so good reviews about the area. If you have never been exposed to a "rough neighborhood" than you may be a bit uneasy. But then again the DC area is heavily populated and there are quite a few rundown neighborhoods. But I'm not going to knock the hotel because of it. In fact, this was one of our best hotel stays ever. The hotel staff were all friendly and accommodating to our needs. They were helpful in directing us to area tourist attractions. Everyone we encountered made us feel welcome! As far as the rooms go, the beds and pillows were comfortable; the room was clean and fresh smelling; and the bathroom is big. The fitness room came in handy and had all the necessary essentials. The pool was a little small but we didn't get to use it much anyway. The breakfast is well stocked and there was a staff person in the room every morning to help guests if need be. If you don't mind the 8-10 mile CRAZY (30-40 minutes during rush hours on weekdays) drive to downtown DC I highly recommend this hotel.

title_masked: Great Place with Super Friendly Staff.
text_masked: It's a Great place with super friendly staff. The thing I liked most is that the staff would not only ask you how is your stay in the hotel but hows your stay in San Francisco. They would recommend places for you to go as well. Front desk was always there with a smile on to help you anytime.

title_masked: One of the several hotels we stayed in LA
text_masked:
Our experience at the Courtyard was pleasant and we liked the outdoor area near the gym very much. The ffeling is very relaxing and nice to sit out side for a drink in the evening.
We have called the day before to request for early check-in and were given a room when we arrived at about 12 noon. The room is spacious, although not the biggest that we have stayed in LA during this trip. Overall the standard is good.
The only drawback is the size of the Queen bed. It is definitely smaller than a normal Queen size (compared to the other hotels and also Courtyard at SLO). It was rather tight for my son (12 years old)and I to sleep comfortably.

The staff is wonderful and the hotel is ideally situated for a large conference. I stayed in the old tower and my only complaint would be the pedastal sink in the bathroom which makes it very difficult to place make up and toiletries. Asked the concierge for a few restaurant recommendations and was not dissappointed by any of them.

A basic hotel but great value in Hollywood. Situated Close to Walk of Fame, approx 5 -10 minute walk. Nice reception area. Room was basic, a little dated and dark, bathroom clean and tidy, bed comfy, fridge, safe, wi fi,air con, and a complimentary breakfast was provided in the morning. It was basic but considering the price you paid for this wee place compared to anything else in Hollywood it wasn't bad. Hotel had a swimming pool which didnt look the cleanest while we were there. Staff were happy to store our luggage for us for the day before checkin and seemed pleasant enough. If you are in the Hollywood area to sightsee I would recommend a one or two night stay. We were not prepared to pay the high prices in Hollywood knowing we would hardly be in our room so this was adequate for our one night stay.

This is our second time staying here. You wouldn't even know it was located in the building. You take an elevator up to the hotel. The rooms are very comfortable with the usual Four Seasons flair. It's the service that makes the difference. They are there to help you with whatever you need! The food although on the pricey side is excellent!

We stayed here for two days (8/10/12-8/12/12) to start off the first part of our vacation. What a fantastic hotel! I never once spoke to anyone who was anything less than stellar in their customer service. Everyone (including the guests) were so friendly! The rooms were beautiful, very clean, and had a balcony. It was a short, 20 minute drive to Universal Studios and Hollywood. Hotel was near restaurants, shopping, and banks. Also, the hotel was in a very safe neighborhood. 
Yes, the Internet is not free and neither is the parking. However, the parking garage was very convenient and connected to the hotel.
The ONLY complaint I had was the beds were double beds and not queens. However, that was stated in the description, and I am not faulting the hotel.
I would stay here again in a heartbeat!

title_masked: Average - expensive - other choices steps away
text_masked: Stayed here as the client booked the room. The room was large and functional but it was the noisiest hotel room in NYC I have stayed in ... I stay in NYC about 30 days per year and I had to use my ear plugs to block out the street noise. It seemed very expensive in a cheep way -- meaning the nice mini bottle of water next to the bed was $7. I am not shy about prices but its been a while since the bottle NEXT to my bed had a price tag on it. Room service was excellent - my special order was done perfectly and delivered on time. There are only two elevators and about 25+ floors - the trip down in the morning frequently took over 5 minutes waiting for an elevator with space.

We had a beautiful room with a balcony and great views, and noted that the lobby has been modernized from what we saw on the web site before the trip( it now shows the hotel as it is). Service was excellent, room and beds very comfortable. Internet was fast, but went out once. A very courteous man soon came to have a look and fix it. We liked Greek town but did have some long waits for the #20 bus. The stop is very convenient, though - just across the street.

title_masked: Perfect location, not recommended for a long stay
text_masked:
I have reserved a standard room (queen bed) via Expedia, finding the weekly rate quite competitive vis-a-vis hotels located in the same area (10036) like Sofitel or Hilton. The room located on the 21st floor turned out to be pretty small: the queen bed was actually a mini-queen and the closet was really tiny, difficult to manage two medium size suitcases around. The bathroom was nice and clean (great shower) and surprisingly large considering the room.
I was offered an upgrade to the deluxe queen room, king bed (located on the same floor) for a daily $105 (+taxes) rate and decided to accept as my wife and I were to stay for a full week. The new room was definitely more ample although the king bed was actually more like a (real) standard queen. The bathroom was exactly the same size as in the standard room and the closet was (again) super-tiny size, definitely not indicated for stays longer than 1 or 2 nights. Each and every room sports the same closets (super-tiny) size, they told me. The first 10 digital channels of the LCD TV were not working and I was told that in certain rooms they were out of order (offered another room change I said no, thank you!). Other than that the hotel was clean and confortable, very silent at night.

One of the things that we appreciate when we are in holidays in a different country is to be in a place where all the people that we meet there, make feel you like home. That’s why we always look for a place to stay where we could be confortable. 
The first week in August we were lucky because we could enjoy a very good days in New York. 
For us, it was our 5th visit to New York but it was our first experience in Bentley Hotel and it was one of the best places that we have stayed ever. 
At Bentley Hotel, we had a pleasant stay, feeling like home. It is a very good hotel, very confortable and fully equiped. But its strong point is the people who work there.
We want especially be grateful to Robert who was very kind. He always was asking us if we need something, he gave us a lot of information about the city and he made us our stage very confortable and familiar.
We also want to appreciate the work of the manager. He made sure that we had everything and that we could enjoy our best visit to NY. And he achieved that!.
Thank you all for make our stage in NY as the best holidays that we could enjoy.

The location was great. There were a lot of nice restaurants and shopping in the area.
The hotel room was nice and breakfast was good. Staff was nice but not overly friendly.

Tabard Inn is a landmark, and it is fun walking through the labyrinth of halls with old and dusty furniture. The restaurant is very popular and usually booked for dinner and brunch. The lunch of pumpkin soup and beet salad was well done. We stayed in Room 54 which is large with a seating area in the front of the building. The bathroom was fun, but needed better lighting. The bed was comfortable enough with nice bedding. The building is quaintly creaky and voices carried through the walls. Breakfast that came with the room was pretty good. The lounge is very nice with a real fireplace, but not enough lighting for reading. Some of the staff were not service oriented and minimally friendly. Street parking is pretty much unavailable, unless you are very lucky. Valet parking is an extra $25/night. A clearer fire escape plan would be appreciated since the building is very old. It is feeling a little tired, so the Tabard Inn could use a good cleaning, better lighting, and a bit of updating...all of which would contribute to its charming ambiance, because it is a cool and fun place in the heart of DC.

My review would be 5 stars, but I only stayed overnight and did not get a chance to check out all the amenitites. The service level was wonderful from every staff person I spoke with. The room was clean, lovely and quiet. The room was also quite large by Midtown standards. Three adults mangaged very nicely. As for the location you are one block from The Port Authority. Three blocks from TKTS and avery possible theater is in 10 minutes walking distance, even in snow conditions. If you want to be in the center of the action, don't hesitat to book at this wonderful hotel.

title_masked: 5 Stars - we would definitely stay here again
text_masked: Great service, nice room, wonderful experience. We typically stay down town but all hotels were booked. They took us last minute and rolled out the red carpet for us. They will now be our first choice next tme we go to Austin.

title_masked: Quiet, unique rooms and great service
text_masked: Stayed at the Monaco in early June. The rooms are not the standard generic hotel fare. They are interestingly decorated and fun to stay in. My room was very quiet and the wifi signal was good. This was my first time at a Kimpton hotel and now I am hooked! Will definitely return.

First, I have to start by saying that we love Omni. We have stayed many times in the past at the other Austin location (Southpark) and love it every time. We had a free night from all the stays we have done in the past and decided to try out Omni Austin downtown location. We had a great time and wished we could have stayed longer. The receptionist was very friendly and got us all checked in immediately. When we went up to our room, we were pleasantly surprised to have been upgraded to a suite (this has never happened to us before so we were loving it). It was my husband's birthday and they had put out two cupcakes and two chocolate covered strawberries with a birthday card. Again, what a great surprise. The room was lovely and very spacious. The parking was convenient and we were able to walk to 6th street without a problem. And, remember to sign up for their select guest loyalty program. They will bring you a free breakfast drink to your room in the morning. You will also get free internet. And, your stays will add up so you can get free nights, late check out, etc. We will definately be staying here again when we are back in Austin. Austin is a great town with so much to see and do. I highly recommend this hotel and this city.

We were really pleased with this hotel, mainly due to its ideal location and helpful reception staff. Our room was spacious, although I'd have liked it a little further away from the main road as I'm a light sleeper. What interesting and attractive shops there are in the locality! Also, there's no shortage of restaurants, while the one first left outside is ideal, and excellent value, for breakfast. The reception staff helped us find buses when we needed them, ordered taxis on time for the airport, and even enabled us to confirm our flights for us. It was just a 2-night visit, but if we ever went again we'd choose this hotel for its top value for money and convenience. Thank you!

title_masked: Not an airport hotel but a good choice for the area
text_masked:
From this hotel it is about a $10.00 cab ride to center of Boston.
You can take a subway into town and there is a hotel bus to pick you up or leave you off at airport or subway station. BUT IT WILL NOT GO TO TRAIN STATION JUST ABOUT 1/2 mile away. sad to say. 
It is a standard three star but has some welcome features. Very good beds, clean sheets and room, good breakfast with alt. outside seating, business corner, free parking and helpful desk. 
Bathroom very small, but there are two chairs and microwave plus fridge in room and that is welcome. Shopping center behind hotel. Rooms very quiet. 
Not particularly fancy but a good hotel if you are looking for accomodating features and not a lot of splash. I found the front desk cooperative and friendly. if you don't want to eat out, there is a choice of takeout places who deliver at very reasonable prices.

The best thing about this hotel is the staff, both of whom I met were very nice. Now, on to the serious problems.
Cleanliness: the hallway outside my door was not vacuumed for the 4 days I stayed at the hotel. I know because there was trash of varying sizes -- from very small (pieces of paper and lint) to much larger (several entire tissues wadded up and containing God-knows-what) -- strewn across the hall. Additionally, the trash can outside the elevator on my floor was filled to overflowing and never once emptied during my 4-day stay. Inside the room, a long, dark hair was found within the bed sheets (clearly not mine, as I am bald); and more hair was found inside the tub. The elevator had a relatively large puddle of red soda-like liquid that stayed there as long as I was a guest. 
State of repair: in a word, the hotel's physical shape is deplorable. To properly close, the door to my room had to be either pushed from the outside to close or pulled from the inside. In either case, the deadbolt did not work as it did not align with the latchplate on the door jamb: that's a bit unnerving. Over the threshold leading into the bathroom there is a thin metal plate that, when stepped on, caused a loud pop. The bathroom door had some kind of trim work running down the length of both sides of the door; however, this trim was curling up at the bottom on both sides. The decorative caps that cover the bolts holding the grip bars in the bathtub would not stay in place and instead continually slid down to the bottom. The trash cans in the breakfast area, which had foot pedals that ostensibly opened the lid, did not work, thus requiring the user to bend down and manually lift the trash lid. The glass front door of the hotel never closes entirely, staying about 8" open instead. 
In general: a friend of mine who was staying in another room on a different floor checked out a day early because he saw "a critter" scurry across his floor. 
It takes quite a bit to skeeve me out, but the Best Western Envy managed to do it. The name of the hotel makes me question what anone would envy about someone staying there. The price was reasonable, but certainly not worth the sacrifice of quality and cleanliness.

title_masked: Great Location, Size Makes it a bit Impersonal
text_masked:
In August I spent two nights at the Sheraton Seattle and considered it a solid option in downtown Seattle. Positives: Great location, quiet rooms, nice amenities. Negatives: Huge size means long lines at the concierge desk, reception, and other facilities.
The hotel is conveniently located on the corner of 6th Avenue and Pike Street, in a bustling commercial district. It’s two blocks from the Westlake station, which is the terminus of the light rail system that links the city and the SeaTac Airport. The Westlake station is around the corner from the Seattle Monorail station, so you can easily get to the Seattle Center. The walk from the station to the hotel may be a bit challenging with large luggage, but it’s manageable. The area around the hotel is filled with shopping (Niketown, Nordstrom, Gap), and restaurants. The Pike Place Market is six blocks away.
The hotel was hosting a big conference that week, so it was sold out. The large number of guests meant lines for everything. The free Internet computers in the lobby were always mobbed. It was frustrating to try to speak to the concierge around dinnertime, as well. The line at the reception desk snaked halfway across the lobby. I’m a Starwood Gold Member, so I proceeded to the Gold/Platinum line to check in, since it was significantly shorter. The clerk rather curtly aksed me if I really was a Gold Member. The hotel has two towers and I stayed in the one along 6th Avenue. From my room I could see parts of the Seattle Center, but not the Space Needle itself (not high enough). If I craned my neck, I could catch a glimpse of Puget Sound. The hotel had all of the standard amenities, including a coffeemaker, flat screen TV and a room safe. I was pleasantly surprised that the hotel was quiet on the guest floors, even with a full house. On the second day of my stay I saw a huge family check in to the room next to mine. I didn’t hear them at all.

Loved this hotel. The rooms were huge and the beds were more comfortable then my bed at home! There was no tub but a big shower with a rain showerhead. The staff was very friendly and helped me to find Old Town. Located conveniently to many sites in Phoenix. The breakfast was great in the morning. Different choices every day, and all very good. The pool was nice but a little cold.

We just recently stayed in the New Yorker Hotel over Thanksgiving Holiday 2012. We had a wonderful time, the room was very clean, no problems with anything. I have been a flight attendant for 20 years traveling all over the world, so I know my hotels. The staff was very polite and accommodating. I would recommend this hotel for another trip, we will definitely will be back. It is very close to the Empire State Building (short walk), Macy's Department Store, Hearld Square also short walk. Madison Square Garden right on the corner. So much to see and do, Broadway Plays and Time Square not far. We walked to everything and it was very safe.

Excellent location on Michigan Av. The room was clean, had a very comfortable bed and was quiet and all of those are important. However, compared to similiar priced hotels, the room was dull and lacked some small luxuries. I also found the restaurant slightly expensive for what was served.

We stayed six nights in a classic suite. The room was large enough, clean and quiet. The hotel has good location, nice architecture and design. The main lobby is stylish.
The staff are very friendly and polite. Breakfast, 24 h free coffee with bakery and fruit, and wine+cheese are a bonus.
We are happy we chose Giraffe and would love to return. Without any doubt we can recommend this hotel.
New York is a great city and staying in Giraffe makes the visit even better.

This hotel is sketchy and dirty to the max! The first room we stayed in had what appeared to be dried blood on BOTH COMFORTERS. The desk kindly moved us next door, where it was just as bad, if not worse. The bathroom door would not lock or close, the bathtub was rusty, the ice tub had the words "extra keys" written on the side, and the room overall was shabby. Worst of all, there were BUGS CRAWLING out of the nightstand all night. GROSS. People were also running and screaming down the hall all night long, and the elevator was covered in scratch graffiti. I would NEVER EVER EVER stay here again.

We picked this hotel because of its proximity to DuPont Circle for a two night stay. Despite its name it is a few blocks away but the neighbourhood is lovely. The staff are very professional and helpful. Our room was spacious and quiet. The hotel seemed much more personal thn it's size would suggest.

We enjoyed spending two nights at the Hotel Solamar over Labor Day weekend. The hotel was extremely busy, but the service was still excellent. I've stayed at this hotel before and this visit was just as great as the last. 
The hotel is very clean. Housekeeping did a great job. All employees were polite and friendly. We stayed in a king spa room. The bathroom was beautiful. The huge jacuzzi tub was amazing - especially after a 15+ mile bike ride on Coronado Island. 
The Solamar's location cannot be beat. It's right in the heart of the Gaslamp district. There are many shops and restaurants a short block away on 5th Ave. Jsix Restaurant and Lounge (at the pool) were also great options. We ordered room service for dinner one night. Robin took our order and brough it up to our room in record time. He is a hard worker! The food was fresh and delicious - would definitely do it again. 
There were a lot of dogs staying in the hotel over the weekend. We did not hear any barking/yapping like a previous reviewer did and we were on a pet-friendly floor. It really depends on how courteous the guest(s) is. We did hear a bit of music across the street from our room at Stingaree at night. The noise was not loud enough to bother us though. We were so tired from such amazing, fun-filled days. We will be back! Thanks, Hotel Solamar!

We travelled to SF from Ireland as part of our honeymoon and we absolutely loved Hotel Vitale. The staff were amazing and very welcoming, especially Brandon at front desk (who arranged for a bottle of Prosecco to be brought to our room) and John in Americano. The location is excellent as well and we found it very easy to get around SF with the cable car just outside the hotel. We had a superior waterview room which was excellent with great views of the Bay Bridge. It was great to use the Spa in the hotel and I would thoroughly recommend. We will definitley be back in SF and we will definitely stay at Vitale again!

Located only a few blocks away from busy Financial District and Ground Zero, this cosy but modern hotel was a nice discovery. I stayed for four nights in a queen room on the third floor facing busy Church Street, but not experiencing any noise at all. The bed was comfy, the room average sized and the bathroom with the walking-in shower was flawless. The room was also equipped with a modern flat screen TV, radio with iPod docking station, hair drier, toiletries, bathrobe. Plus complimentary access to a fitness center nearby is provided and included in the rate. 
Breakfast was not included in the room rate although complimentary cookies, freshly baked every day, were in the lobby for all guests as well as orange-flavored water. 
The staff proved to be very friendly and efficient. I am sure I'll stay at Duane hotel again on my next visit to NYC. 
This hotel has it all: great location ( also easy to reach by subway), clean rooms, modern amenities, friendly and helpful staff, great value for money. 
Highly recommended

It was my boyfriends birthday and about 20 of us were going to the Padres game and heading to Gaslamp after, so I decided to stay at the Hard Rock because I felt it was appropriate since we were there to party. We arrived at 4:30 (later than we expected), so we were in a rush to check-in, drop our stuff off and head to meet everyone at the Padres game. When we get to the hotel it seemed like the hotel would be awesome because we were greeted by super friendly valet staff. Our bags were picked up for us and when I was ready to check-in, I was told the room was not ready. The advertised time for check in is 4:00pm and it is about 4:35pm, so I keep my patience and was told it should be very soon that they are just finishing up. While we're waiting in the lobby, we figured we can't waste anymore time waiting on them we were about to head out to the game at 5:00pm. However, as I was about to leave I received the call that the room was ready. We decided to go ahead and get settled as quickly as possible so we wouldn't have to do it when we get back. I finally got to check in at 5:00pm (an hour later than the advertised time) and gave my ticket to the concierge person to get our bags up and she said they'll be there right away. However, I wait 15 minutes and they're still not there. I call the concierge and am told that "they should be on their way." At this point I am losing my patience because my plans are thrown off because of the hotel. I called back 10 minutes later and tell him that I NEED my bags because we have to get to the game that started at 5:35pm. They still did not come and after another ten minutes I called back and was told the same thing. Finally, I went downstairs to make sure that they were not sitting in their holding area. Basically, my plans were thrown off an hour because of the hotel and this should have not have been the case. Half an hour was wasted because the room was not ready until 5 and another half an hour was wasted because our bags did not get there until 5:30 and the game started at 5:35; in addition, we had a lot of people waiting on us. For spending $300 a night this is not what I had expected nor wish to have experienced especially on someone's birthday. I could have stayed at a motel for this kind of service. Also, the bell boys were rude. When we initially decided to just leave to the game without checking in, we had to grab stuff from our bags and one of them had to supervise us. He had an annoyed face and was not friendly at all (I'm sure because we were delaying him from getting his tips from other people), but that would not be happening if our room were ready as advertised.

This was my first visit to Los Angeles, but unfortunately it was only a short day and a half stay. So, it was important to me to stay at a hotel that was centralized to the places and things I wanted to see. The location of this hotel delivered on that and so much more. 
HOTEL/ROOM: Overall, the hotel was very well maintained. From the hotel room, to the hallways, down to the lobby, everything was very clean and well taken cared of. The hotel staff was exceptional! Very friendly staff whom would always engage you in conversation about your day and offer up suggestions of places to see or eat that you may like. There is a small pool on the 4th floor, a tiny gym with cardio equipment, and free breakfast in the morning. Breakfast consisted of bread, eggs, biscuits, a pancake machine, variety of cereal, sausage, milk, juice, etc. As in most major cities, there is a cost for parking, which at this hotel is valet. Wifi is free! The room was fairly spacious. Flat screen TV, desk, & refrigerator. 
LOCATION: For me, this hotel was in a great spot because of the things I wanted to see. It was within walking distance, about 3 long blocks from the Hollywood Walk of Fame, Kodak Theater, Grauman's Chinese Theatre, & an outdoor shopping complex filled with restaurants. The Hollywood Bowl is 4 blocks away and you're about 15-20 minutes (traffic permitting of course) from Dodger Stadium, Warner Bros Studio, Universal, the Hollywood Sign, The Grove, Beverly Hills, Paramount Studios, Sunset Blvd., Staples Center, & the Nokia Theater.
OVERALL: I would certainly recommend this hotel and stay here again in the future. Unfortunately, it's a bit pricey for my wallet, so if I were going to stay in LA for a week or longer, I would certainly look into not be so centralized in order to save some money on the room. However, don't count this place out. Check the rates and go for it if it's within your budget.

This hotel was an unexpected gem. I travel to NYC frequently and have had the opportunity to sample a variety of hotels ranging from small boutique hotels to well known corporate chains. This by far exceeded them all in hospitality and service. Everyone was exceptionally helpful and eager to assist. The breakfast including made to order cappucinos was a great way to start the day and wine and cheese by the fire the perfect way to end the (work) day. The room was spacious, clean, and comfortable. The bathroom was well stocked with great bath products and spa robes. I particularly appreciated the special requests option prior to checking in. I had asked for down pillows and a lighted mirror and everything was waiting for me. What really seemed above and beyond was the staff's concern for a sick colleague staying at the hotel for 3 days. Tea, ginger ale, and toast were graciously offered along with frequent inquiries about how he was feeling. Thank you staff of Casablanca! The hotel is a convenient location to 5th ave, Museums, Theatre, Times Square and subway station.

Not a bad hotel. We were only there for 2 days but it was nice and central.
Right opposite Grant Park which was lovely and within walking distance of Lake Michigan marina, the Aquarium and Museum.They have a brasserie attached to it so somewhere to eat and the Yolk restaurant is just up the road.

title_masked: Great location do not expect a great service or room
text_masked:
We were a party of 20 people and had some issues to book for such a big group. We decided to book directly at the hotel web however, there is no option to book a group at once, you have to do it room by room and there is no discount for groups. The check in process was tedious and slow despite they had all details we had already entered through their web. They got confused with the names. We were charged a Group Tax of $7.20 per room however we were never treated as group, in fact, we were accommodated in different floors with no connecting rooms. As family members, we would have liked to be on the same floor. Check in staff was very impolite to us. 
Renovated rooms but size is small, cannot even open the suitcase and wardrobe is small, however everything, room and bathroom are clean. 
Heating is contradictory (too hot in corridors, extremely cold in rooms if you use air conditioning. Insufficient plugs (3 plugs, one broken) in the room and no adaptor, considering that most of the guests are European (mainly Spaniards) it would be nice to provide these in the room. Escalator and lift to reception was broken upon our arrival. The lift was not working one night due to renovation and had to use the stairs. Staff provided us with bottles of water to compensate. 
The hotel is fine but has no extra facilities/services that make it special. The value we got is fine but not outstanding. The best thing of this hotel is location despite it is noisy (do not come to this hotel if you need a quiet place to sleep), despite the building is under renovation and has a scaffold around it. We were not impressed by the friendliness. It is a fine hotel but do not expect great service.

title_masked: My Dad and I had a great time here!!!
text_masked:
My Dad thought it would be fun to have a boys only weekend. 
At first I thought it was going to be pretty boring with no video games or tv and some weird awkward camping trip where I would have to learn to be a man.
It was actually pretty cool and he suggested I let other people know how much fun a 15 year old and his Dad can have.
We went to Galveston for a day and had some fun but the really fun part of the weekend was when we stayed at this Crowne Plaza. We went swimming in their pool. Then ate a huge plate of ribs and got to lounge in the room, watch tv, even ordered a movie on pay per view. 
Definitely a cool hotel.

The hotel room was great - spacious with everything you need, while a little dated and stale in the air, I'm not really picky and it's perfect because you're not exactly shacking up in your room all day if you're visiting Philly. Great views, great location. The lobby was a disaster. It smelled like vomit when we checked in and it someone kept sprinkling that deodorizing powder on the carpets throughout our stay. They were also undergoing renovations, which was annoying but definitely necessary. It didn't ruin my trip because I'm a realistic traveler and the price, location and room fit my needs. Hopefully the renovations will have been completed and the lobby will have received a much-needed face lift before my next trip!

We stayed here on August 19 and 20, 2012. This was our second time here and it has been great both times. Our rooms were real nice and the staff is very pleasant and accommodating. We asked about taking a cab to Cellular Field and they recommended taking the train instead because it would be much more reasonable. We ended up doing that and it saved us about 70 dollars! By chance the next day we met the owner in the lobby and she spent time talking to us and we shared stories about prior travels. The breakfast is really good. You have to try the waffles. We brought our bicycles and they never acted like they were put out when we asked them to retrieve them for us. This is a very good place. We will be back! William R.

title_masked: The standard all other hotels should live up to.
text_masked:
This is the best Embassy Suites and one of the best hotels I have ever stayed in. This is my second stay, a few years apart. My first stay was a few months after it opened. I wondered if time would have changed the hotel or service at all. Nope. The hotel has gotten even better. The hotel itself is beautiful head to toe. The design elements are so pleasing. This trip I brought my mother and my sister with them and they couldn't go 15 minutes without commenting on the wall paper, the lobby chairs, the windows... something. The rooms are typical Embassy Suite size with lots of room to move. The rooms here are particularly functional, in my opinion due to the well designed living room. My guests were floored that the manager's reception is free and that the high quality, hot breakfast is free as well. The service was TOP NOTCH. From the valet, to the front desk, just five stars, really. If there was one thing I had to say for the ES Denver to work on is the valet parking fees. $30 a night is really steep. 
If you need a downtown Denver hotel, don't look any farther. You just can't go wrong with this one. Right next to the convention center, mountain views available. So close to 16th street, everything is right where you need it.

stayed for 3 nights to see san fran, great position 1 block from zoo tram $2.00 to town easy to use , free parking , ok rooms , basic breakfast , but best part is the great manager , really helpful , great guide nothing to much trouble . 
All hotels in city a little pricey but if you want a good basic room with freee parking, easy trasport and a caring staff choice this days inn 
Diner two doors down good food and staff

I deceided to pamper myself and use up some (alot) of points to stay at this beautiful resort on mission bay. 50000 points is alot of points to cough up, but T.C. at the front desk upgraded me to aa awesome suite facing the bay with private porch and my own firepi t(thanks again TC!). I got a bunch of coupons for free and discounted stuff (free slider with craft beer!) and breakfest coupons as well. As a jogger or a walker, there is a great path all around mission bay.
2 negatives-parking is very high over $30.00 and the gym for a "resort" is cramped and inadequate
But I love to come here and decompress

I was traveling by train so it was nice that the hotel was so convenient to the train station. The hotel has an attractive lobby with an adjacent restaurant. The room was clean and comfortable, and the staff at the desk was pleasant and helpful. The hotel is not close to the Magnificent Mile, which was disappointing, but the desk clerk was able to recommend some nice restaurants within walking distance. I was only there one night and overall it was a nice stay.

I stayed at the Ballantyne for 3 nights last week. I went alone to give myself a relaxing getaway at the spa. Every single person I came in contact with during my stay were so friendly and professional, If I asked a question, someone took me over and showed me what I needed. The room was so beautiful and spacious. Loved having the view of the golf course. I would most definitely return in the future. Class and elegance combined with a warm, friendly and professional staff. What more can you ask for!!!

title_masked: Great Location and facility, service not so much
text_masked:
On booking we thought the young ladies seemed quite helpful. But on viewing the website they did not advise us of all of their special deals and discounts. On asking about taxes (as we are not local or national) they said they had no idea which was clearly incorrect as on receiving our bill at the end (by the same young ladies) all of the taxes were specified and identified - and they must do this all day every day.
The location is awesome - quiet but really close to the city - and not on the flight path - and the military flights nearby do stop about [TEL]pm.
The decor is older - but adequate and very tasteful - as is the general motel decor. Great bonus of a fully cooked breakfast included in the beautiful dining room with great harbour views. though not if you're paying $120 per night though.
The walls are thin so if you have neighbours there are no secrets - and no sleep if they are noisy - especially on weekends. Gymnasium is great with some free classes.
But the service is poor - the staff in the dining room are well past it don't seem to be happy nor enjoying what they do and are almost outright rude.
We were out for the whole day and came back and our room wasn't serviced. We called the front desk. 1/2 an hour later a guy ( we later found out was maintenance/grounds/security combined) appeared with a couple of towels and glasses. Way less than half the towels etc they normally get. There was no apology, offer of doing the room, discount or anything. In fact the guy refused to take away the old towels, glasses or rubbish - as if it was beneath him.
So overall, awesome location, good facility, but poor customer service.
.

The employees are always friendly and helpful at this hotel. Hotel is always very clean. Lois Evans is an expectional employee always courteous and very helpful with my needs as I often have to stay there at the last mintue.

We arrived and were not impressed with this Kimpton, as we have loved other Kimpton hotels in LA and Denver. The lobby was small and looked outdated. The hallway leading to our room, and the room itself smelled muggy and like a smoker had stayed there previously. The staff was nice and valet was helpful - but it's definitely overpriced for what you get. Would not stay here again.

I just spent two nights at the Sheraton Downtown and came away unimpressed. The location is great, the staff reasonably friendly, the price not bad ($179 a night) but that's about it. My room on the 10th floor was old and needed renovation. The plug sockets in the walls were loose, so every time you unplugged an iron or phone you felt the socket might come away in your hand. The air conditioning system was noisy and oddly designed -- when I turned it off there was more noise than when it was on. The bottom sheets were six inches too short so my feet (I am 6 feet 2-1/2) began getting caught by the end of the bed.
What really bugged me was the staff's total indifference to the chaos around them.
