My stay coincided with a student music festival and there were teenagers wandering around the corridors pretty much 24 hours a day. A colleague had to call the front desk at 2 am to complain about people playing the ukulele loudly on his floor. I mentioned this to the check out staff and they said "Sorry about that" but didn't seem too bothered. I won't be back.

As a single traveller I value customer service. The staff were very helpful and the hotel is very central to public transport. I walked along the beautiful heritage Commonwealth Avenue and enjoyed the architecture and beautiful trees and gardens.

title_masked: Good Property and One of the Better CQs
text_masked: I stayed here for one night in early May to visit the DC office of my organization. First, the location is fantastic. It is right next to the Farragut West Metro stop. This makes it simple to take the Metro from the airport without having to transfer lines via the blue line. As with all Club Quarters check in and check out is quick via their kiosks. I had a room on the 6th floor. The room was clean and good sized. It also had a microwave - although I didn't use it. The bathroom was small but adequate. The room had free Wi-Fi and a good sized desk area. I've stayed in most of the Club Quarters in NYC and this one was by far the best I have stayed in. It is not super glamorous, but it does the trick.

This Motel 6 is bad on so many levels. Usually Motel 6's are cheap and still nice places to stay; I have used them in quite a few states in US by now. I booked this Motel 6 in Houston for 12 days, and had already decided to move to another motel the next day. The first impression, as many other reviews have written here, is that the motel is increadibly noisy, being near a large highway. When checkin in, the clerk told me the internet was down and the pool was under reparation... Then going up to 3rd floor, I noticed the walls in the corridors looked like the walls of an underground bunker, not of a hotel! Then the room: Well, the room was probably the only positive thing. It was clean and large, although the floor didn't have carpet but solid "laminate" type covering, which is strange for a hotel, but OK. The bathroom was quite new and very clean. During the night, I could hear the neighbors speaking on the phone (I think); the walls do not seem to be that thick. During all the evening, there were two police in front of the building talking to a non-police person for hours. I have no idea what they were doing, but have police for hours in front of your hotel is never a good sign. One other good point though: The staff was friendly, and totally understood when I cancelled the rest of my stay. I know moved to the 'La Quinta Inns & Suites'. I'm writing this review from the 'La Quinta' hotel room, which b.t.w. has free (and working) wifi, and already I'm so happy to be here now! That being said, I still think most Motel 6's are OK, just not the 'Houston Reliant Park' one.

title_masked: Nice clean hotel close to the airport
text_masked: We chose this hotel because we liked Staybridge when we stayed there in Miami. For only 140 bucks you get a one bedroom suite with a fully equipped kitchen. Breakfast was pretty standard - the stuff you usually get in two-three star hotels such as BEst Western, Baymont, Comfort Suites, etc.

I really was surprised by the clean and modern, but comfortable!, decor at the Doubletree. My room was on the top floor and had an unusual shape that gave it character. The bed was very comfortable and was very quiet even though I was relatively close to the elevators. My only complaint was that the toilet was positioned that I kept hitting my knees on the door. Otherwise a great stay with very nice staff. Don't pass up the warm cookie at check in!

title_masked: Low maintenance people will be happy
text_masked:
We just returned from a 4 nite stay at The Milford Plaza hotel. Overall it was really a decent little hotel if you want bare bones amenities. I didn't even realize they had an exercise room - not that we had a moment to spare for that anyway. If you travel in a group, be forewarned to utilize the bellman both arriving and departing. They tout "because of the Union" they have to charge you per bag - regardless if they assist you or not. Little did we know until check out and of course handled our own bags both ways. Oh well - live and learn.
The lobby construction - big changes going on. Willl eventually be nice. Very rude cleaning staff that made me feel terrible about having to use the facilities on the lobby level because our room wasn't ready yet. I clearly distrurbed her. Then we sat in the bar area while waiting for the rest of our group to meet us and another cleaning staff employee was aggrevated because we, along with several other hotel guests, were sitting in the bar area (not another inch of space left in the lobby to even stand). He wanted to clean it, actually pulled a chair away and removed it from the table when 1 person stood up to go chat elsewhere. After standing there pouting for 20 minutes, he finally took his angry face and stomped away. Luckily, No other negative encountes the rest of the trip. Jennifer at the front desk was very friendly.
The rooms, yes were small but we assumed this going in. Our room was very clean - only missed face cloths one evening. We were so exhausted at the end of each day that we were just happy to shower and hit the bed. 
The hotel offers no amenties to speak of - no free internet, no coffee, no nothing. Again, we knew it going in and still survived. No issues with the elevators. 
The bathtub floor surface was quite slippery. Happy to have survived it without incident.
Left a voice mail for the concierge - never heard back from them. No special kudos there.
Location was awesome to theater district, Time Square, Restaurant Row....we walked and used the subway everywhere. Would I stay there again? Yes - I think I probably would. We were satisifed with our accomodations. It was just a place to shower and sleep - no extras to make us do more there anyway.

title_masked: Review of Four Seasons Hotel Chicago
text_masked: Stayed here during a conference. Got upgraded to a two room suite on the 42nd floor with excellent views of Chicago and the lake. Service was very good. Hotel is an older property and definitely very expensive. I ordered a room service (one pizza and a soft drink) and the charge was almost $40.00 Restaurant was ok, strange lay out and too dark. Location of the hotel was good, very close to Michigan Avenue. In summary I can recommend this hotel for the great service provided by its staff, however, next time I will stay at either the Park Hyatt or at the Peninsula. May be then I will have a better comparison.

The JW San Francisco is located just near the Massoni Center which was great for me while there at a conference. I've stayed at the hotel several times and am never disappointed. Beds are great, rooms over $550 per night...pretty expensive.

Very nice staff, quick to respond to my needs. My room had a toilet that did not flush after 2 uses, and a hair dryer that was faulty. Both times I called down to the desk and within 5 minutes we had someone up to repair successfully our issues.

Pros: Convenient location if you need downtown or Market St location, 2 blocks from BART station, efficient front desk, clean room and comfortable bed.
Cons: Noisy neighborhood noise will filter into your room, ear plugs provided if that tell you anything, Street noise audible even on the 24th floor, nighttime cleaning activity, numerous panhandlers on the street outside, Expensively priced mediocre breakfast buffet,

title_masked: Marriott East Side. Great location, friendly staff, nice rooms.
text_masked:
Just back from the USA where my wife and I stayed in New York for nine days broken up by side trips to various location. Each stay was three days and at a different hotel each time. The last was at the Hilton Time Square, which was horrible. Like staying at Grand Central Station. The second was the Millenium Time Square. Which was quite expensive, but lacked everything you should get in a high end hotel. The first, which spoilt us for the rest, was the Marriott East Side. This is by far one of the best hotels in New York. A fantastic location, being an easy walk to all mid-town attractions. The staff were very friendly and extremely helpful, and the rooms are as good as you get in a hotel these days. Clean and comfortable.
I would highly recommend the Marriott East Side, and if I ever return to NY, that's where Ill be staying.

Everyone at this hotel was a wonderful host when my choir stayed there Thanksgiving week. Such a busy time, and yet I never felt rushed or mistreated. The rooms are lovely...spacious for New York...clean and very comfortable. Our room was right by the elevator, yet we never were bothered by noise. The location is terrific. It was an excellent spot for the Macy's parade. We ordered room service one afternoon and the food was delicious. We did get a good group rate as we were there with a large group. My husband and I travel to New York often and definitely plan to stay here again!

My husband and I stayed at the Hotel Monaco last night. We had a party at the Hopkins House which is located close by. We were upgraded to a Delux King room. There is an "Alice in Wonderland" theme in this hotel and our experience was truly fantastic. We paid one dollar more than our rate and got two free cocktails at the Red Lantern pub whic is in the hotel. The bed was sooooo comfy. His and her robes and slippers were a nice touch as was the

I just completed a two night stay at this hotel. In town to meet with a client at the nearby Warner Center Towers, I chose to stay at the Hilton because I am a Diamond member and as such have a few extra perks and benefits that I wouldn't get at another hotel. Overall, my stay was very pleasant. The entire staff is friendly and helpful. As a Diamond my preference is set for a king bed and upon check in the gentleman informed me that he didn't have any king beds available but could upgrade me to a junior suite. I agreed that was fine and didn't think much of it. Later I realized that he must have been talking about there not being any king beds available on the executive floor which is where I was expecting to be placed. As it turns out, I was placed on the 5th floor (this hotel has 15 floors) which is not one of the executive floors. Not a huge deal, the room was spacious but I think I would have preferred a room on one of the executive floors with upgraded amenities. I will definitely be back and will know to ask for next time. Overall the room was nice. It was plenty spacious but there were a few things that could be improved. The heating/cooling system in the room is really loud. I didn't need to use it much since the temperature was consistently comfortable but I imagine that in the summer this might be a bit of an issue, especially when trying to sleep. Another issue is with the hot water in the morning. My first day the water temperature was lukewarm at best. I prefer a hot shower in the morning to help wake me up and I assume because everyone else in the hotel was taking a shower at the same time the water barely made it to tolerable. I imagine this is because it is an older hotel. Additionally the water stream from the shower head is very narrow which makes it even more difficult to enjoy the shower when the water is barely warm. The second day was a bit better but I think this is because I got a later start to my day and not as many people were showering at the same time. The hairdryer in the room is a small travel sized one with no nozzle for air control. That was a huge disappointment and inconvenience that I hope/assume is remedied by having a room on one the executive floors. The wi-fi was reliable and strong and as a Diamond member it was free which was a great bonus. 
The hotel shuttle is very convenient. As long as you are within three miles they will take you where you need to go. This morning I asked to stop by the Starbucks first and he was more than happy to do it. 
There are plenty of dining choices nearby. The Cheesecake Factory is right next door which is very convenient. A few blocks down is an El Torito and on the other side is a BJ's Pizza. As a Diamond I had access to the Concierge Lounge on the 14th floor. As "club" lounges go, this one was nothing to write home about. Breakfast was Continental style and the espresso machine wasn't working on the second day. It was free so my expectations were low anyway but I have had better club lounge experiences at Starwood and Intercontinental. 
Overall, I had a pleasant stay. I will definitely be back and now know for next time to ask for an upgrade to an Executive floor room regardless of available bed size.

I have stayed at this JW Marriott twice, for a total of 4 nights. My experience has been pretty consistent.
I like hotels in historic and older settings and this is a recently renovated structure, which is a plus. The lobby is large and opulent. The rooms, too, were well-appointed and had a "luxury feel", including LCD tv's, wide molding, granite countertops etc. The sheets on the bed were of a high thread count and very soft. The staff was friendly and attentive.
So why not excellent? Well, a couple of things. First, although I paid close to $300 a night after some sort of preferred rate, I still had to pay $15 for wi-fi. Really? I'd pick an internet connection over a TV or many other things in the hotel. It sure as heck doesn't cost them anything close to $15 for a night. If you are a Marriott platinum or some other high level "elite", the internet doesn't cost extra, but I travel all over and, frankly, while it is generally very good, Marriott isn't always the best alternative so I don't have the high elite levels needed for "free" internet access. 
Second, I thought the prices in the restaurant and the lobby were rather high. The prices for wine by the glass were more than I would pay for an entire bottle at home. They are certainly entitled to a fair profit, and I support their right to one, but $18 a glass for wine that would cost $12 a bottle retail is going a bit too far. Having said that, I had a chocolate martini at lounge bar, an occasional indulgence for me, that was very good (it was $18.50 with tax and tip).
In short, they have a beautiful and thoughtfully restored building and an excellent and responsive staff. I was annoyed, however, by the nickel and dime-ing on things like excess charges for internet access and beverages in the lobby. If you are already Marriott elite of a sufficient level, the internet won't be a problem, but you would likely be staying here anyway. If not, however, I would look at the entire package to determine whether the hotel is worth it. I'd leave it up to you.

Nice boutique hotel in a great location. The bar, lounge is awesome with great service. It is a dark place and the rooms don't have good lighting - which is ok with me. The only negative I have is that I upgraded to a business package deal to get 1) an upgrade to the room 2) passes to Equinox gym 3) free breakfast and 4) free wi fi for a higher price. I didn't really care about the wi fi and am not a breakfast person but I was excited to try the Equinox nearby and get a room upgrade. The person at the front desk didn't even know I had upgrade to this particular package..... I had to tell her and then when she looked at the computer she seemed to know. She promptly gave me my passes to Equinox and my breakfast vouchers. 
Unfortunately there was no room upgrade. I specifically asked her what time I could use the breakfast vouchers and she said 8-12, When I went down at 11:15 day 2 they said the voucher was only good until 11a. Oops. They were nice enough to rebound and make accomodations for her misinformation and I got a nice breakfast.
The Bose system also did not work in the room and i had no music to listen to. When I called to ask if I was doing something wrong to engage it, I was told "i'll call you back" and got no call back.
Overall the room was ok for NYC and the location was good and the gym was sufficient. I would say the the bar/restaurant staff make this place one to go back to.

1 - I arrive at the hotel - The super rude staff asks for 300$ security deposit - Never mentioned to me while I was booking the hotel.
2 - The receptionist rudely suggest me to leave the hotel if I really want that money.
3 - The rooms are contemporary! In a bad way. The bathrooms are from the 1950s and are unclean. 
I request you - Please DON'T try the hotel!

MileNorth is located literally half a block from the Magnificent Mile, not from the Water Tower and the John Hancock Tower. The location is unbelievable. We took the L-Train in from the airport on the blue line and then transfered to the red line at Jackson station. The fare one way is only $2.25. From airport to hotel takes about one hour and easy to do. The hotel staff at arrival were friendly, courteous, and helpful. The rooms are reasonably spacious and have a modern feel.
The biggest surprise was the hotel restaurant. The food was incredible!!!! There was a nice variety from yellow tail tuna tacos to pasta to out of this world deserts. Everything was gourmet, cutting edge, and deliciously adventurous. It was like have 5 star meals at 3 star prices. I have stayed at dozens of hotels around the world and usually skip the hotel restaurants for good ones, but MileNorth restaurant and bar on the 29th floor are hidden gems in Chicago.
When we go back to Chicago next year, we will be staying here.

title_masked: Part of Starwood Group, Great Location, Room costs+taxes r High.

I go here off and on and absolutely love the location. It's close to Columbus Circle and Central Park and minutes away from Fifth Avenue. When I think of traveling to NYC I immediately think
Of staying here. They often have Flash sales or promotions for the $250 to $299 range, however

Will pay or have disposable income( which I don't)then who can really afford that? The last time I stayed there was last spring for a few nites, I was awoken very early in the morning with sounds

I must stay the staff is very friendly , and beds are very comfortable and location great,but unless you get good value then look elsewhere, there are plenty of hotels in New York City,
Ly

I have not been here for 2 years, and I was looking forward to going back because of the great bar and restaurant on site. I was surprised at how updated the rooms had become since I was last there. Completely remodeled, and the decor was gorgeous....wish I was there for more than 1 night to enjoy!

After reading some of the reviews I wasn't sure I had picked the right hotel but our room was clean and spacious. Wifi worked great except for the period when it was knocked out by the storm. Staff was friendly and helpful, and breakfast was as advertised - a continental breakfast and the hotel is easy to find

Nice motel, clean, rooms are warm and smell good. Bathrooms clean. Has free wifi! Parking is $18/night, but this is good considering most of the other motels and hotels charge $25. Great blackout drapes, quiet neighborhood. Restaurant is a little pricey, but nice. Restaurant only open at odd times but there is a McDonald's on the next block. This place is almost next to the Space Needle! 
I like this place, handy and inviting with terrific front desk staff.

title_masked: Great Stay At The Handlery Hotel San Diego
text_masked: Friendly staff as always!:) Great location; convenient everywhere; food was affordable; clean room. I would stay here again.

My recent trip to Seattle was made even more amazing by my choice of hotel!! The service at the Renaissance Hotel was beyond outstanding...when we checked in, the front desk suggested that we use the concierge if we needed any suggestions for places to go and places to eat. We took his advice and met the concierge, John-Paul, who absolutely made the rest of the trip. He was extremely knowledgeable, polite, and passionate about the city of Seattle...he referred us to a restaurant that served the best steak that I've ever had!! We also met the bellman, Seth, who was also extremely helpful, positive, and remembered us after only having met us once! His recommendations for Pike Place Market made for the perfect day. When we left our room one morning, even the maid greeted us warmly and with a huge smile! I've never experienced service like I received at the Seattle Renaissance Hotel! 
The rooms were spotless and the only thing I could even complain about would be the wall-unit AC that made the room inconsistently warm/cold...the workout facility was clean (very small, considering the number of people in there), but a little warm for a run!
I will DEFINITELY return to this hotel upon my next visit to Seattle!

title_masked: Great hotel for the business or leisure trip
text_masked:
The location was great. Just a block up from Market Street and the Mall Line, which will zip you anywhere downtown. The check-in staff was courteous and prompt. Even though I booked on Hotwire, they honored my Platinum elite status and I received complimentary internet and an upgrade to a mountain view room. The room service cheeseburger was decent, albeit overpriced. On a $13.00 meal, an automatic gratuity of $5.73 was added to the bill.(Shows as “Service Charge” and “Delivery Charge”) Not a big deal since I was on an expense account, but a little pricey for a late night snack.
The bathroom was good and they have great beds and ample pillows. The TV is a little small, but it was workable.
Overall, a very pleasant stay.

I had a disheartening check-in experience as an Omni Black Select Guest member the weekend of May 4-6. I was attending a wedding in Houston and flying out to Orlando on business after. 
In addition, the air conditioning unit in our room was not working the first night. After calling downstairs around midnight, a maintenance technician came up to check the system and told us that the water pump had been turned off. Who turns off a water pump when the room is used regularly? 
After calling downstairs the next morning, we were told that the air conditioning unit throughout the hotel had recently been upgraded. The front desk manager was very nice and upgraded us to the Presidential Suite bedroom. Again the air conditioning worked poorly and we noted that the entire hotel - lobby, hallways - was extremely warm. 
I was sweaty the entire lenght of my stay on the property and opted for checking out early to seek refuge at a restaurant until my flight later that early evening. The air conditiong in my vehicle was preferred to the air conditioning on the property and even a maid made a comment as we were leaving our room and I was fanning myself about how hot the building was. 
Overall - the stay was frustrating and disappointing.

I've stayed in this hotel a couple different times and I'm always surprised how poor it is given the Hilton brand. The lobby area is nice but very cramped. The rest of the hotel is in very poor condition. Carpet looks like it was installed in the 1980's. The rooms wer also very disappointing. The doors to the hallway are very poorly built with large gaps near the floor that allow you to hear practically everything that goes on outside your room throughout the night. My room was connected to two other rooms and the insulation between the two was terrible. I could hear one individual snoring so loudly it sounded as if he was in my room. The food was terrible. I ate one evening at the Boardwalk and should have taken a hint when only two other guests were dining there. While the airport is very conveniently located for flights into Houston Hobby, there isn't much available on that side of Houston so you end up driving for even a decent meal. Overall, very unimpressed and unless I'm required to go for business, I will never stay at this hotel.

title_masked: Home Away From Home in NYC!
text_masked:
I cannot say enough about this property from the staff as soon as you walk in the door at check-in and the bell desk to the quality and cleanliness of the rooms. I could sit here and talk about all the wonderful amenities, but just know they are all great! The concierges are top notch and know all the best spots. Showers, Beds, Rooms, Elevators, all top notch ( I say elevators because of past frustration with elevators at the nearby Marriott Marquis ). Always willing to accommodate and help. As a Marriott Gold Member, I received free continental-ish breakfast (did have eggs and sausage as well) on weekdays. The restaurant in the lobby is a little pricey, but most people just eat out in the city.
#1 Property in NYC!!!

I stepped into Hotel Chandler on the morning after Sandy. Previous day was a nightmare having no power and water in Roger Williams hotel just across the street. I had a room in that hotel, a tiny one at that while comparing to what I saw in Chandler. I went into Chandler to wake my colleague from whom I had to collect a key for our office which was just a block away. Walter was the man in the reception and from then onwards everything was smooth for me. He followed rules but at the same time helped me to get to my colleague. I got a room then and there and stayed for the next three nights until the end of the week so that I could manage our disaster recovery operations from the city. I found everything nice with this hotel and wondered why I did not go for it in the first place. I recommend this hotel very much.

The location is fantastic if you want to be in the thick of it all. Rooms are OK, clean & neat but the cleaning staff are unfriendly & complain. Our rooms were missed twice & when asked to come back they asked what we wanted done - well cleaned obviously. They then complained about the mess in the room, which was unmade beds, overflowing bins, towels in bath??? Went for a wonder wee hours & security was hot on our tail, friendly facade but not wanting us wondering around -threatened to call security???? Bell staff so helpful & friendly. Wouldn't stay there again.

We stayed one night - Friday night. For the price we were very pleased. Totally impressed with the beauty of the Mayflower's lobby. We loved the chandeliers and the beautiful Christmas decorations. Desk service was great, and we were offered a complimentary glass of champagne or water before going to our room. We were a little disappointed we did not have a view of the street (faced the inner court) but perhaps it's just as well - would hate to hear street noise. The room was small, but we did not need lots of room since there were only the two of us. Carpet was dated, but we loved the marble floors in the bathroom! There was quite a roomy shower also - although the water pressure was less than even the cheapest motel! King size bed was roomy, but not the most comfortable we've slept on. BIG tip - bring your own pillow! These pillows (at least in our room) were horribly hard! Due to the pillows, we had a terrible night's sleep. Our room (9th floor) was very quiet, though...we never heard a noise from above, below, or next to us. We were going to try the breakfast buffet, but at $25 per person, we passed, and ventured to a cafe not far from the hotel. I would have given the Mayflower an "excellent" if they had better pillows!

I just returned from a business trip to NYC. I stayed at this Fairfield Inn & Suites and was pleasantly surprised! The hotel was in a great location - close to the Empire State Building and Penn Station, the red line subway was a block away, and like most of NYC, I had a Starbuck's and many good eating establishments within a 5-10 minute walk from the hotel. The hotel and my room were both clean and neat and the staff were extrememly friendly and helpful. The front desk staff assisted me with a city map and subway directions. My room was on the 15th floor with a great city view, WiFi, and with no loud city noise. My room was a little on the smaller side, but much better than most that I've experienced while staying in NYC. I would return to this hotel the next time I'm in the city.

Nice hotel with the typical Hilton quality in terms of the property and staff. Not much else to say about this hotel, everything about it was good and I'll stay here again. The hotel is easy to get too and there's lots of shopping and restaurants nearby.

We had a terrible time getting the door open to the room. Went back to front desk They said the locks were old had to be pushed very hard to get into the room. It still took 2-3 tries each time to get in, and I actually hurt my hand doing it. But the room was comfortable. However it did not meet up to the normal standards we see in LaQuinta. The next morning we went to breakfast, and is was so bad, we ended up at MC Donald's.

Right by Rockefeller Center, within walking distance to many of the NY sights, the Palace is our only place to stay. The service is excellent, the rooms are clean and comfortable and the amenities the Tower offers are very enjoyable. $$$$

My wife, 10-year-old daughter, and I had a great experience staying in a suite at the Hotel Erwin. The room was great, service was excellent all-around, with special kudos to front desk person Miguel, who went out of his way to to assist us with traveling advise, recommendations, etc.
The outside of the hotel was unimpressive as major renovations were being made to the exterior and it was covered with scaffolding, but the suite was delightful. You're one block from the beach.
If you're looking for pure relaxation and beautiful surroundings, this is probably not where you want to stay. You're in the heart of the very lively Venice Beach neighborhood which is very active and a little scruffy, but the hotel itself was delightful. If you want to stay in Venice, this is a great place to be.

Our stay in Loews Regency was only for a couple of nights on our way to 
Anaheim and then onto Panama Canal cruise. The reservation had been made through Disney Vacation Club as part of their Concierge collection, using our vacation points. Check in was quick, as was delivery of the luggage to our room. We knew we wouldn't be in the hotel very much due to our hectic plans, only a place to lay our heads overnight. The room was large and clean, bathroom small. Adequate for our purpose, but had we wanted to spend more time in the room we felt it was under par, especially as we knew it would have cost at the time $500 per night, we would have been disappointed. The bottom of the bathroom door quite poxy and furnishings could do with an update, which we appreciate is going to happen in the refurbishment. No tea and coffee facilities in room. Better use of space near the window. Minibar had inadequate glasses. We did have breakfast downstairs which was enjoyable and cost us approx $88 dollars for eggs benedict and coffee including our gratuity.

The greatest virtue of this hotel is its position. It is in Midtown near the Lincoln centre and theatre district. Columbus circle subway only 3 minutes walk away and you can get most places easily from here. Rooms are tiny for the price though thoroughly livable and with everything one needs...I had to move rooms as the street-side was very noisy - the courtyard side of the hotel was better...airconditioning was noisy but effective...wifi included which is great...price is a lot for anywhere else in the world but probably fair for new york...concierge helpful and I liked modern lobby...breakfast is over-priced so better to eat at one of numerous new york cafes around...

The big rooms are quiet even with its proximity to the airport. Our parking was free. Nice breakfast buffet. All lunch and dinner meals are in the pub/grill so you cannot avoid TV screens. Rather than a reservation desk, there are several small "stations" around which are a little confusing.

I stayed at the Red Roof Jacksonville Southpoint recently on a drive to Florida. The location is great, as you are right off Butler Blvd and close to restaurants, highways, and not too far from the beach. It is a great location for a long drive.
I have stayed at this location a few times. Check in was fast and efficient. I used a red roof points certificate, so my room was free (the regular charge for this time of year was around $90 - $100). 
The room was decent, but as soon as the door opened, it was very musty smelling. Fortunately, the window opens a little, which helped to air out the room.
The room itself looked clean, and we had a superior king with refrigerator and microwave. The bed was comfortable and the bed linens looked clean. I would like to see them move away from those old comforters (which had several cigarette burn holes) to duvets though.
The bathroom was clean as well.
The grounds are fine, and the hotel was crowded for a one night stay. There is no breakfast, only some coffees in the morning. Wi-fi was strong throughout.
Overall, this is a budget hotel that is probably not worth the $90/night, but is great otherwise. I have stayed before, but would like to see them renovate like many other Red Roofs to modernize.

title_masked: Drury Plaza Hotel Riverwalk is the BEST!!
text_masked: The service and hospitality of the staff was wonderful. This is absolutely the place to stay if you are looking for was a wonderful stay in San Antonio. This Hotel is defiantly a tourist attraction, the food was fabulous, and the Kick Back was unbelievable. I must say, the breakfast had a lot of choices. Our room was VERY clean and comfortable. Overall, this was a great place to stay in and we will be back again. Planning my next stay!

title_masked: Amazing hotel - very clean, super friendly and helpful staff!
text_masked: The staff were so helpful, no request was too large or small. The beds were very comfortable, the room was bright and clean, the bathroom was spacious and lovely. It was great to have full kitchen facilities - even a dishwasher! We enjoyed the hot breakfast every day. We would stay again in a heart-beat, and have recommended it to several friends. We liked being able to walk to the theatres and shopping areas. The Staybridge is a veritable GEM in Times Square!

We booked 3 nights at this hotel because of its location..It is walking distance from the Alamo, Riverwalk and Entertainment. The Rooms were clean and quite spacious, loved that we had a microwave and mini fridge, it came so in handy with all of our leftovers. Lobby and Breakfast area was nicely decorated and clean. The laundry room should have at least another washer and dryer, I believe one of each is too little. $21 a night for Valet is a little too much. The breakfast is okay, but for the price "free" you shouldn't complain. Overall we loved the Hotel..We can definitely stay here again when we return to San Antonio.

My husband and I enjoyed a getaway weekend to the Adolphus. The hotel is absolutely gorgeous, the rooms are beautifully furnished, and it really is a magical place. The old world elegance is breathtaking compared to other modern looking hotels. We stayed in a very large junior suite.

Checked in evening before Alaska cruise, dog tired after 4 day train trip.
Front desk people were fantastic- couldn't be any nicer or speedy in getting us to our room.
Great suite with a marvelous view from balcony. King bed was very comfortable.
Very nice kitchen with coffee maker.
An extremely generous breakfast, really above and beyond. With fresh blueberries on the serving line, I was in heaven - love those blueberries.
Great overall experience - would absolutely stay again!!!!!!!!!!!

Repeat stay because of past good experiences and proximity to family, but one major additional factor was the made-to-order omelettes available at the breakfast included with the room cost, all cooked by one truly excellent, extremely friendly chef. Go early to beat the long line, but it's definitely worth it. Gets your day off to a good start. The room was fine, even though showing a little wear (particularly the somewhat tired matress). Definitely would stay here again.

My mother and I stayed here for a girls weekend when she was visiting me in the city :-) Needless to say we had an absolutly amazing time! It began a check in where the level of service was far superior to many hotels where Ive stayed (and I travel heavily) and the staff is so dedicated to making sure each individual guest is having a great time. This attention to detail coupled with the sexy chicness of the hotel over all make it a homerun in my book!
P.S. The view from the top floor and the goosedown bedding is to die for :-)
P.S.S. There housekeeping staff is totally on top of it!!!

Arrived a few days before Hurricane Sandy.Nice clean rooms.Was moved to a higher floor upon request.had a nearby parking for my car which was good for NYC.Was tough during Hurricane Sandy;limited menu,no room service etc but we were notified ahead of time and was kept updated.Felt bad the cable was down so TV channels were limited and the bar does not offer mocktails.

We were in San Francisco for a trade show at the Moscone Center. This property is located within a short walking distance from the Center. Great value, clean rooms and friendly service. Breakfasts were the only meals we had at the hotel. It was a buffet and fine. The bar was always well subscribed. We visited it once and there was available seating. A fridge would have been useful. I had to sleep in the middle of the bed as both sides had indentations.

title_masked: 2nd Time...and still love it for park and fly!
text_masked: We've stayed here twice before leaving out of philly airport....and we've been glad we did both times. It's a really cool hotel and the shuttle service is good! It costs more than parking alone, but not that much more in my opinion. I'd do it again!

title_masked: Granted a 2pm late checkout but incessant vigorous knocks from housekeeping at 12:30pm!
text_masked: Overall fair stay but I was really upset when hearing incessant and vigorous knocks on the door from the housekeeping while I was taking a shower in bathroom at 12:30 pm on my checkout day. This was despite the fact that I had been granted a 2 pm late checkout. If you have permitted your guest to check out late, leave the guest alone until the late checkout time!

Like most 'boutique' hotels, the service is poor. The staff are always amateurs who would prefer to be doing another job - and all far 'too cool for school'. This place still thinks that it's the real deal. It isn't. Not only that, but is needs a makeover as a matter or urgency. Everything about it is tired. They should invest in double glazing because it has to be one of the noisiest hotels in NYC. By the way, it is unacceptable to have to wait 25 minutes to check-in.

There was nothing to complain about at this hotel, which was unknown to me until it was recommended by my travel agents, Trailfinders. Its location in Chicago was perfect. The room was very good though a separate shower, away fom the bath, would have been even more pleasing, The service was excellent, particularly the room service. The concierge and bell boys were friendly and most obliging. It is a business man's hotel. I wouldn't recommend it for a romantic stay but it fulfills all the needs of travellers on business, or for folk like us, tourists in Chicago..

We enjoyed staying in this hotel. The room was very spacious, It's an older hotel. The elevator was small and very slow. Not scary, but it was SLOW to wait for the elevator. I would say that was the only downside and it wasn't a big deal as we were on the 4th floor, so if we got tired of waiting, we could take the stairs without a problem. The staff was very friendly. The pool area was great and provided towels. There is a poolside bar, which was very convenient. I would definitely stay here again. The kids loved it. We loved it. The hotel is located near Rock Creek Park and the National Zoo. It was a great place to stay and a good value.

You can't go wrong with the location, literally right in Times Square. They have valet parking, so all you need to do is drive up and they'll take care of your car (not cheap, but pretty convenient) Once you learn how to use the elevators (you punch in your floor on the keypad and it tells you which elevator to go to), getting around in the hotel is a breeze. The service was fantastic from the front desk to housekeeping to the restaurant. I only gave it 4 stars because I felt that some areas could stand with a good scrubbing - the hotel is very busy and I'm sure it's hard to keep up with keeping the glass elevators in pristine condition.
We were in NYC for college tours of Columbia and NYU - great location for using the subway.
Taxi tip - there is a taxi stand right outside the main entrance on the ground floor - be aware that taxis will not take more than 4 people, even the mini vans. We had to use two cabs for all our trips.

title_masked: Nice hotel, not a great location
text_masked: The hotel and staff were nice, but the location was not in the best area. My room was nice, very spacious, but my colleague said his room was very noisy as he was on the freeway side. The staff was nice I just wish there was more in the area.

Went travelling in America for a few weeks and so glad I found this little gem! Very clean rooms, well kept hotel and extremely fried sly staff not to mention excellent location. With lots of great restaurants and bars all close by such as Hard Rock Cafe, Rainforrest cafe and traditional pubs. Other features of the hotel include roof top indoor pool and balcony giving decent view of the city, especially at night and only a two minute walk away from the metro system. When I return to Chicago will definitely return to this hotel.

title_masked: Quality Hotel in a Great Location
text_masked: This is an older hotel with very nice rooms. It appears that they have been recently updated. Staff were extremely welcoming. Parking was very convenient to room location. Pool area was nice with an outdoor fireplace. We didn't eat in the hotel but there was a restaurant that appeared to be nice. Stay at this hotel for proximity to great vacation hotspots without the huge pricetag.

The room needs an update and smelled very stale. I wore my socks so I didn't have to walk on the carpet. TV reception and # of stations was poor. Felt like a "flop house". Staff very professional and efficient.

A very good revamp of the hotel, very clean and modern, a great place to eat and a very good chef, only one complaint the noise from the traffic if your room is on the front apart from that it is a good location, 5 mins from the main attractions, two massive beds in our room, television, free wi-fi, hair dryer , iron and ironing board, coffee maker, shower and bath, fridge, microwave, staff are brill and very friendly, all in all a good place to stay and relax and visit sights, almost forgot air con is very good as well.
hostess looked a little tired and smiled with difficulty but this hotel is nice, quiet and very will located between Time Square / 5th av and Central Park/Macy's

My husband and I went to NYC for a show and to see some sights. Location was great. The hotel staff were excellent. The room was ready on time and the staff were able to help me figure out exactly what we wanted to do. We only came with a few ideas of what we wanted to do and an open mind. We managed to catch a show with all the major shows within walking distance. The subway was close when you wanted to get out of Times square. The breakfast was great. There were always drinks and treats available whenever you came back to the hotel.

This was my first visit to LA and I was delighted with the location of this hotel. We were within a short walk of the main sites on Hollywood Boulevard and we used the nearby metro station to visit other attractions including universal studios. This is a great hotel to stay in if you're not planning on renting a car because of its central Hollywood location. We were in LA for 5 days and walked to all the local sites and used public transport to get around with very little difficulty.
The free hotel breakfast was good and there was a choice of juices, tea, coffee, bagels, pastries, cereal, fruit, etc. The vending machines in the hotel were very reasonably priced and had a good range of drinks and snacks. There are a few places to eat nearby, including the ihop across the road, the In n Out burger next door and a 24 hour Subway a short walk away.
The room itself was excellent value. It was clean and comfortable and the free wifi was useful but a little inconsistent. Our room faced into the pool area so this was a little noisy sometimes during the day. Overall however we were delighted with this hotel and I would definitely recommend it to others.

A bit tired and worn but the staff were warm and friendly. The room was large, comfortable and well equipped with a decent bathroom. The hotel is in a charming, relatively quiet area within easy reach of the metro system. We felt there was a lack of places to eat close to the hotel. If you enjoy walking, it was well placed for sightseeing. Just across from the metro station is possibly the best food market/deli we have ever visited, selling a vast array of groceries, wines/beers and take away foods to meet all tastes, so the lack of an oven was never a problem. If you want to be in the middle of the action you may prefer Georgetown but if you want a quieter location at a very reasonable price then this represents good value.

I will be honest, I only ended up staying at this hotel because I did Priceline's "Name Your Own Price". The thing I hated most is that the parking is valet only, plus a $22 parking fee per day. I'm not the type of person who likes to deal with valets, so this feature made me pretty uncomfortable. And I figure if I'm already paying to park, why am I tipping someone else to do it too? 
The road this hotel is on, is not the greatest. It's pretty easy to miss your turn to get to the hotel because there is only one way in. It looks pretty on the outside, but when you walk in the inside to get to your room, it's pretty dirty and less appealing. The annoying thing is that the place where the valets park your car is right underneath you, so every time they lock a car and it honks, you can hear it inside your room. 
The room was pretty unremarkable. It wasn't dirty or anything. There was a mini fridge, which we liked, but it didn't keep anything cold. Their elevators are extremely slow, and I disliked that there wasn't a pool or at least a jacuzzi. 
So all in all, this hotel isn't completely awful, but it's not breathtaking either.

Really good experience. The hotel was able to upgrade my room from one king to two double beds at check in. We then had a wonderful time in Chicago with suggestions from the W staff. Great ambiance and service.

This was our first time staying at the ChelseaSavoy Hotel. I took a group of 9 ladies to NYC for a shopping, sight seeing long weekend. The hotel was fantastic, clean, quite and all around perfect for us. The people at the front desk were attentive and nice. The breakfast was small but so very good. The coffee was excellent. They serve donuts, bagels and other pastry. They are not the fanciest place to stay, but I will sure stay again.

My wife and I stayed there for the first time looking for value and location. Boston hotel prices are ridiculous but we got a good price calling the hotel. The room was small but nice and clean. Location was excellent with a short walk to the North End. Staff was very friendly and willing to help. Happy hour was also nice before we went out with the wine tastings. We will be back.

we recently made a trip to Austin to meet up with friends & stayed here. The front staff & the manager were quite rude & unaccomodating. I wish they understood the meaning of the business they are in "HOSPITALITY"!!! Anyways, I would not stay here ever again & would not recommend to any one else either.

We stayed here for 6 days and found this boutique hotel to be a great respite from the hot chaos of Manhattan in the summer. We have stayed in a few neighborhoods & found this to be our favorite - it isn't in a particularly touristy area yet is close to Central Park, and 10 minutes to the heart of the city. It felt a bit like staying at a friend's flat.
The room was fairly large by NYC standards, and ours had a good view up & down Broadway. The window air conditioner worked well though was kind of loud. The room was simply appointed and the beds and linen were of high quality. The bar fridge in the room was nice to have, esp. given the nearby market on Broadway. Everything is close, with a subway station 2 short blocks away at 79th. The staff are quick to help and despite the lobby reno in progress the place is very clean. We would definitely come back.

I stayed at this hotel with my 7 year old Golden retriever. The hotel itself is nice with good decor. We had a great deal from booking.com
After we checked out they charged a whopping $250 saying that there was urine on the floor. 
I know for a fact that there was no urine, but the part of the floor was wet where left my dog's water bowl. My dog has never peed inside since he was a puppy and I have taken him to many pet friendly hotels before.
So those of you thinking about taking your pet, be aware!!!
They act like they are pet friendly, but they are not!!! They will just charge you after you leave.

title_masked: Great location for the dogs with the park. Even got the RV into the free parking...and out!
text_masked: Very friendly staff and a perfect place to take the dogs for their walks. Staff was super friendly. The noise level of other guests was way too loud for the majority of the night and made it very hard to get any sleep for both us and our two dogs. Perhaps it was because we were under the stairwell and on the 1st level for the dogs. We needed the king size bed, but it made the clearance between the foot and the dresser/fridge/tv very narrow and hard to navigate when the bed covers were turned down.

title_masked: Excellent Hotel and Service in Great Downtown Location
text_masked: Fairmont's usually provide exceptional properties and service, and this one is no exception. A very nice property, beautiful lobby, and good size and well-appointed rooms. Plenty of staff to take care of your needs and make you feel at home.

Hotel was clean, neat, quiet, and still reasonable rates. The people who greet you were
very polite. The housekeepers were very attentive and pleasant. I will continue to stay 
there when I go down to visit my daughter in San Diego. Thank you again Yvonne

My fiancee and I stayed for 4 nights during the US Open week in August. The Hotel was very nice and the room was lovely and spacious with a nice big bathroom. The Hotel was ideally located for us to get into town close to Grand Central and only 15min walk to Times Square. Had a really tasty meal at Rare Grill Restaurant which is on the bottom floor of the hotel. Also super bagel place called [NAME] and Scottys Diner were both regular stops for breakfast. Overall couldnt fault the Hotel the staff were friendly and we thoroughly enjoyed our stay at the Affinia Shelburne.

What can I say, everything was perfect: Location, Guest Relations, Room, Noise Level, Restaurant for breakfast, everything. I was contacted a couple days before check-in by Joanna Butcher in Guest Experiences. I told her about how I wanted a room on a high floor (as I had read previous reviews about being able to hear the subway from lower floors), and she made sure I had a room on the top (15th) floor. She also made sure that all my other preferences were honored (King Bed, feather pillows, and complimentary breakfast at the restaurant under my Gold HHonors status). We were even able to check-in with no problems at 10:30 a.m. (well before check-in time) as I let her know we would be arriving to the city early. Joanna even surprised us on Saturday with a bag of goodies for our Gold member amenities, complete with a nice note from the Hotel manager and herself. We really felt important and like we had individual service catered to our needs, although I know we were just two out of hundreds of guests that weekend. As we made our way around the city throughout the weekend, we realized more and more about how perfect the location was. We were in walking distance to Times Square, Rockefeller Center, Radio City Music Hall, Central Park, FAO Schwartz, Broadway, etc. And there was a subway literally a block away for when we travelled to lower manhattan to see the 9/11 Memorial, NYSE, Washington Square Park, etc. The restaurant was also wonderful and convenient. Anything you would ever want for breakfast, quick service, and it was free to us as Gold members! So we could roll out of bed, grab a wonderful breakfast to give us energy, and then get out and about! Our stay, again, was perfection. Thank you so much to Joanna and the rest of the Hilton Garden Inn Times Square staff. We will be staying here when visiting Manhattan again.

title_masked: WOW - W Hollyood matures with age !!!
text_masked:
I have stayed at the W Hollywood on a yearly basis for business since its opening, and it is like a fine red that is maturing with age, the first experience was a new hotel with hip young team members with a very much "whatever !!!" attitude, plenty of talk and not much action. My most recent one night stay was nothing short of amazing, great service from the bellboys, reception and room service, a group of employees who really show pride in their job and enjoy making their guests part of the W Hollywood experience. 
For people wanting to be part of what Hollywood is, lively, vibrant and fun this hotel is perfect, well located on Hollywood Boulevard with just a short walk to most attractions. I will be back, thanks for a great stay.

We stay at the Gergetown Suites located in 30th. I dont have any complain with this hotel, everything was perfect, location (close to the main street M in georgetown) (if you want to go to the monument and museum, close to the hotel is a bus stop that take you everywhere), services, cleaning, decoration, the room was huge, well equipped. This hotel include the breakfast that for my family was great, included: cereal, bread, pastry, juices, coffee, fruits, eggs and sandwiches. I have a great time with my family.

It took me a while to decide on a hotel in San Francisco but I finally decided on the Clift and it was a great decision.
The location is great - very close to Union Square, Westfield Shopping Centre, Cable cars, Chinatown, sightseeing buses and shops and restaurants. I had read some reviews which mentioned it was in the Tenderloin and not in a great area so was a bit worried about that. But I though the area was fine and always felt safe there
The room was a decent size and the bed was so comfy. The bathroom was a bit on the small side but did me fine.
The staff I encountered were all very friendly. 
The breakfast was expensive so I didn't eat in the hotel - there are loads of places nearby to eat anyway.
Wifi isn't free but there is a Starbucks across the road from the hotel. 
The only thing to note is that the hotel puts a hold of $150 a night on your credit card for incidentals. I was staying for six nights but they only put a hold for 3 nights on mine.

Return from Panama too late for connecting flight so I stayed here with check in @ 2AM! While the LAX airport is lousy in every way (one hour taxi from touchdown, 20 minute bus ride to gate, one hour wait for US Immigration/Customs) this hotel met all needs for quick check-in, clean and quiet room, prompt and courteous airport shuttle, and surprising full breakfast with real eggs! While I hope not to use LAX again for flying, if need be, this place is just fine!

This is the 2nd time I've stayed here, and I love that it is central for all the tourist stuff you want to do. 
it has a lovely restaurant attached to it and a cool bar, so should you wish, you could also hang out here on an evening. Rooms are large, modern, quiet and very clean.
We normally skip the breakfast at the hotel and go to the Europe Cafe on the corner, which is great value and great choice.
The 5pm "free" drinks is a great idea, and they charge out the Brooklyn beer abou $7-8, so if you can have 3 at 5pm, its great!! 
I would definately book here if I was going to do touristy stuff in NYC.

This is a 2 star hotel in a great location. If you want to pay two or three times the price you can find a much nicer place. However if you just want to stay in a clean room with slightly noisy air conditioning, in a safe location close to Fishermans Wharf at a cheap price then this is the place.

We recently stayed at the Four Seasons in Boston. It was a phenomenal experience. The hotel, staff, and location are unparalelled. The staff's wholehearted attention to any and all of our needs was truly appreciated and most enjoyable. The highlight was "Sundaes on Saturday" , an array of ice cream, toppings and desserts that would put a smile on anyone. I am looking forward you our next visit!

I stayed at the Hotel Pierre for a week end in June. We were upgraded and occupied a small suite (3908) with fantastic views on Upper East and Central Park. Service and food (croissants and OJ are perfect) was stellar. It was the best experience I had in NY.The best thing is that you do not feel yourself in a hotel but in your own small penthouse.

This was our first trip to NYC. We decided we had to stay right in Times Square: in the heart of things. There were 3 of us and we were able to book a room with 2 queen size beds and 1 pull out bed. Amazing location! Great room! We could walk everywhere and we did! Even to the Empire State building. We were able to get the hop on/hop off buses right outside our door. Tons of theatre. Activities all night long in the Square. It was the perfect hotel for us.

title_masked: Wonderful stay in San Francisco with kids
text_masked: We just finished up a tour of California with a stay at the Omni in San Francisco. I chose it because of the wonderful reviews regarding service and it was absolutely true. Our kids 11 and 9 were not too thrilled to be checking in as there was no pool. By the end of our 2 night stay it was their favorite hotel. Upon checki in they received a back pack filled with goodies. At night the chocolate chip cookies were a huge hit. The staff was wonderful to them. As to the adults the Omni is a wonderful classic hotel. Rooms were very comfortable and clean. Valet parking was easy. We actually lucked out and their was a promotional rate for the valet for the two nights so even affordable. The concierge gave us a wonderful suggestion for dinner very close to the hotel after a long day of sight seeing. I would definately stay again. My only negative is that because it was right in the middle of the financial district it was pretty quiet around the hotel at night. However that did work for to our advantage as when returned from dinner we easily hopped on the cable car in the front of the hotel. Because it was slow they let us ride up and down California and we only had to pay once. The kids loved this and actually rang the bell the whole time.

This is a wonderfully appointed and staffed hotel. The rooms are small but very well organized so they don't feel cramped at all. The bed is motorized and converts to a sofa or a lounge. They have a free comtinental breakfast with a wondeful assortment of muffins. The WiFi is free as well. It is located in walking distance to Times Square and the Theatre district. Be sure to check out the robot that will store your bags if you arrive early of want to do more exploring after you check out.

Really nice staff, clean, and great location. Right in the middle of it all- can walk or catch a subway to most anywhere in NYC here. Typical New York hotel, rooms are not real large but they are comfortable and clean. Recommend this property without reservation

Considering That my son and I were at The Aloft between 28th October and 1st November during Sandy, I must say we had a great time there. All the staff were extremely helpful. They have a great bar with a pool table adjacent to it. We spent a lot of time there. The only hiccup during the trip was a breakdown of the net between 31st October and 1st November.

title_masked: Cozy Stay in the Heart of Chi-Town
text_masked:
Having traveled a lot for work lately, I was delighted to learn I'd been booked at the Monaco for my most recent trip. The location was selected by our meeting organizer, but I'd had the Monaco on my "to-stay" list for several years (I visit Chicago almost every spring). It's location off of Wacker is ideal - close to everything one could want in the city, and proximate to all of the mass transit options as well. 
Monaco is discreet from the street - located in an former hat factory, you might never know of the jewel that lies inside. I arrived at almost 11:00 p.m. and was warmly greeted by both the doorman and the person who checked me in. There was one small glitch in finding my Kimpton rewards number (you're a member, right? More on that soon...) but once that was located, I was delighted with my "raid the mini-bar" coupon and free wi-fi. My room was on the 7th floor in a quite little alcove, removed from the noise of the elevators.
Inside, my King room had everything I needed at my fingertips that night. Lamps with plugs in the base made it easy for me to recharge my various electronics, and a dock for my iPhone meant I could recharge it while listening to my own music and setting my own alarm. The bathroom doesn't have many places to set toiletries (my toothbrush kept falling into the sink and the hairdryer fell off the edge twice as I got ready for bed) but I have the same problem in my own home. :) The bed was scrumptious: huge, piled with white fluffy pillows and a billowy white down-alternative comforter. I did not have any sort of view (unless you count the side of a building as "view") but that also meant I didn't have any noise from the street or trains. I collapsed into sleep. 
In the morning, I had *almost* everything I needed, except coffee. This is my second stay at an upper-end hotel that didn't include in-room coffee. I have read on other reviews that one can request an in-room coffee maker...I guess I wish that this was made clearer either at check-in or on the website when making a reservation (or even a sign somewhere in the room?). It seems like the more one pays for a hotel room these days, the less amenities (coffee, free wi-fi, bottled water, etc.) one can expect. A shame. That said, once I got up, got dressed, combed my hair, put on my glasses, and treked to the lobby for coffee, it was tasty. My shower was good and hot, and had ample pressure, and there were plenty of white fluffy towels to bundle into after. The minty Aveda shampoo helped me wake up nicely.
That evening, my colleagues and I enjoyed the complimentary wine reception, which also included a delicious watermelon and basil sangria. The bartender came and made a delicious cocktail with apple brandy, bitters, and grenadine that sang with flavors (and I enjoyed watching her work - she makes it look easy!). We went to dinner at nearby Catch 35 (recommended!) and I was happy to come back to my cool, cozy room at the end of a long workday.
On my last morning, I ordered room service that arrived exactly on time and piping hot. There was plenty of food and all of the condiments I needed; it was a great way to start the day (plus, coffee! In a ceramic mug instead of a paper cup! Lovely.). Checkout was seamless and I was off to my next adventure. 
If you're not a Kimpton rewards member and travel at all, you should consider signing up. It's free, and the complimentary wi-fi alone is worth the couple of seconds it takes to sign up online. I enjoyed raiding the mini-bar (the $10 coupon got me some snack-size Snickers and cheese crackers for the train ride home) and am happy that my points are starting to accumulate for a free stay at a Kimpton property in the future. I would definitely use them to come back to the Monaco in Chicago! Thanks to all of the staff who made my stay so pleasant.

Small hotel but central in SoHo area and good value for money. The room was clean, bathroom small, the beds were really nice and soft. Unfortunately we experienced bad service from the front desk staff as we had ordered two suites with balcony and view facing Empire State Building. As they had a double booking it was understandable that they couldn´t give us the rooms we had ordered. However we would have expected a more service minded attitude when we asked for a compensation for giving us smaller room that we had paid for. We needed to spend time both when we checked in for having a reduced price AND when we checked out because they had not kept their promises regarding the compensation we agreed upon. As a customer this felt really bad, and they were not fulfilling the service level that hotels in the Hilton group promise. Too bad because this was an opportunity for the hotel to give great customer experience in a situation were the customer had a negative first impression.

There’s more to a hotel than its brand name and group association. Crowne Plaza Time Square offers the basic amenities known for its name – clean and comfortable room, comfortable bed, clean bathroom, space to work and/or relax.
What distinguishes one hotel from another is its staff. The Crowne Plaza - Times Square Manhattan has a staff that rivals many associate facilities and competitors alike. Now for the important stuffy why we post and read reviews:
Cons: Night light courtesy of a nearby bank building – but, this is Times Square NY – where everything is lit up. Lack of a refrigerator was a minor inconvenience, but after all I was not in the room all that many hours. Shower head that did not fit the hanger – would have liked to take a shower where I was not against the wall. Ironically - not a great location to find a taxi from the street -- use the hotel's greeters for the best response and service.
Pros: Location, Location, Location. Ideal to walk to the office in some of the midtown sites. View was wonderful – even with night light. You are in the middle of Times Square - comfortable walking distance for many of the Broadway plays, television studios. For the most part, the local food establishments were on the healthy side – only two fast food restaurants. Bed comfortable, lounge chair comfortable to work, nap, watch TV. Pull out work desk was an added plus. Close to the subway system.

title_masked: Ok to stay here for a night or two.
text_masked: Got a decent Hotwire rate to stay here for one night in order to avoid traffic to lax for the next morning's departure. We had requested two beds, but they sent us to a single bedded room. The front desk then sent us to a properly equipped room but was a smoking room. The third time was a charm and they finally got it right. The guy said they wouldn't move us again given that they were "sold out". It wasn't very crowded and there were an awful lot of empty parking spaces for the place to be sold out. I just think Hotwire guests are not treated well. Have heard that as a generality before and this placed lived up to that! I guess I would stay here again if I had to. Very small outdoor pool that my kids enjoyed for about an hour while I laid on a lounger watching the planes on final approach every 2-3 minutes. This is a decent hotel close to the airport.

This is a pretty hotel and the staff is attentive. What the rooms don't have in size is made up for by proximity to downtown and campus. The standard double rooms are normal size, but the bath area is smaller than average. The bathroom door is this weird sliding door that doesn't lock. This wasn't great with children in the room! We stayed here when dropping my daughter off for ABT.

i stayed at this hotel for 1 week and it was great and the location was outstanding. it was next to the river walk and resturants. the service from the hotel cannot justify my enjoyment staying there.

This is a beautiful historic hotel in Nob Hill, San Francisco. We had a great time in San Francisco, and the location of the hotel certainly helped. One thing to be wary of is that the hotel is located at top (right at the very top) of a very steep hill. I knew before booking the hotel that it was located on a steep hill, but I didnt realise it was this steep! But, not to worry, the hotels are located right next to the cable car lines, and you can easily take the cable car up the hill. The cable car is certainly not the fast mode of transport, but it is good fun, and definitely worth a try when visiting San Francisco. The hotel is located a short walk from Union Square (yes.. walk down to Union Square, but i suggest taking the cable car or taxi to get back to the hotel from Union Square unless you want a good workout!)

This is my second stay here, and it's been refurbished since my first stay. Now, there's the in vogue dark fake mahogany wood look. Small bathrooms. The dining area has some nice comfortable seats and benches, and the breakfast seems improved. Service is good and the staff friendly. Reasonably clean. There's a Bone Daddy's across the parking lot. All in all, it's just fine.

Service was extremely friendly, often not the case in an LA hipster hangout. Extremely comfortable bed. Nice toiletries. Lovely rooftop bar, with choice of übercool hipster side or the quaint Biergarten that served German beer & food. I chose the latter, & as a German cuisine aficionado, thought it was very good! Oh, and a great gym to work it off. Only downside was that the blinds let in too much light for perfect sleeping.

I was in New York on business for one night and wanted a hotel in the theatre district. I normally stay at another hotel, but it was full for the night I needed and so decided on the Paramount based on the recent reviews. I was given a room described as a superior queen size bedroom (a true contradiction in terms as the size must of been for the queen of the ants it was so small) and charged a discounted rate (!?!) of $350.00 (including taxes) which in my mind was one third more than the value of the room at any given time. Even though I was on a high floor, I was kept awake most of the night by the street noise because of the very poor sound insulation from the window in the room. I find little to recommend this hotel and can only assume it appeals to the most naive of tourists who like it because of it's very central location and who would assume that they are getting a great deal for their expenditures. I for one, shall not be recommending it to anyone.
Hotel is very convenient- just around corner from L'Enfant Plaza Metro station, walking distance to Mall and all the sights. Quiet area with limited restaurants.

title_masked: Value for money & excellent customer service
text_masked: My partner & I arrived late evening on 1 May, 2012 and were greeted warmly by the front desk. Although the hotel only offers buffet breakfast; there is a tea/coffee making facility near reception which is a whole lot easier to make before you retire to your room. There is coffee/tea making facilities in the room as well but we never used it! The hotel is conveniently located near restaurants, 24 hour CVS (supermarket/alcohol/pharmacy), walking distance to Macy's, subway & other NY attractions. A 2-minute walk along 6th Avenue will bring you to a $1.00 per slice pizza parlour if you want something cheap & tasty late at night. The complimentary buffet breakfast is superb; offering continental & hot food and for the person on the run; a pre-packed breakfast which you can pick up at reception! Yes - the hotel is basic but cleanliness, superior customer service and value packed offerings, it would be difficult to stay anywhere else. In fact this hotel set the bar for all the other hotels that we stayed at on our tour of the East Coast and far outclassed the competition. It does not matter what time of the day/night you enter or leave the premises, all the staff at the desk would acknowledge us with a hello, have a great evening or just a smile! It's also great that WIFI is free in your room; but you can also use a computer at no charge in the reception area. I am currently writing this review on our 2nd visit to this hotel and nothing has changed. Would I ever stay here again? Absolutely!

We stayed here for 4 nights in November. Yes the decor is slightly dated but who goes to New York to sit in their hotel room?! If you just want somewhere clean and spacious to sleep then this is ideal. The room was the biggest we had seen whilst searching for hotels in the city. The bed was huge, the room had plenty of space for getting ready amongst our shopping! The bathroom was clean, shower was powerful and there was plenty of hot water. We had a kitchenette area but we had no need to use this. The staff are all very friendly and helpful if you have questions. We were able to slightly extend out checkout time at no extra cost and then our bags were safely stored until our taxi collected us. It is about a 5 minute walk from Grand Central Station which is ideal if you need to travel downtown. We had a road facing room on the fifth floor but we didn't have any problems with noise. I noticed other reviews of people commenting on the fact there was only 2 lifts. We didn't find this was an issue at all. Overall, a great hotel which just added to our amazing New York experience.

title_masked: Exactly what budget travelers look for!
text_masked: Taking my husband and 2 kids to 6 CA amusement parks/zoo in a week (!!) definitely needed some creative financing, and the Dolphin Motel's cost and amenities were worth more than every penny. Loved the Yoplait yogurt, not usually offered in other "continental breakfast" advertisements. The room & bathroom was small, all reviews I read about how CLEAN the place is absolutely true. Though you have to ask for a hair dryer, the staff is very friendly and even offer their picks on where to visit. And, they provide a laptop upon request, so I didn't have to lug mine all around CA, and wifi signal strength was awesome. It was too cold to use the pool, but it looked inviting. What else can you ask for?

perfect location, minute away from Washington Avenue, where you find anything you need from food to clothes. we had spectacular view from the window. breakfast had a lot to offer, our kids loved it, the coffee was delicious, really great. the only problem we seemed to have was bathroom not cleaned properly as we found quite a lot of hair on the shower curtain and even though we reported it straight away only the next day after approaching a member of housekeeping dept. on the corridor the bathroom was cleaned. there is a great pizza place right next to the hotel if you want to eat there, where apparently some celebrities hang out.

title_masked: Nothing "PLUS" about this hotel but the location
text_masked: We were checked in by a man named [NAME]. Not the most pleasant individual. Mentioned it was our anniversary... not a word back from him. Just given our room keys and pointed towards the elevators. Room was ok, small, as most NYC hotel room are. It was clean, the bed, while not the best, was comfortable enough. Lots of street noise, even up on the tenth floor, which didn't bother us but if you need quiet to sleep, don't expect it here. Best thing about the hotel is the location, which is fantastic and obviously what you are paying over $300/night for. Decorating theme is a bit bizarre for my taste but my husband liked the light up bust of George Washington that was in our room. Just an "ok" experience overall.

First arrived after a long flight and we were very tired so they upgraded to a high room so no traffic noise. Also whilst waiting for the room we had a drink FOC. The staff really looked after us very polite and pleasant. The staff could not have done anything else they really made us stay welcome for a weeks stay. It was both business and a break with my boyfriend. The rooms very spaceous and also have a small desk for laptop and work space. The beds are very comfy and clean. The Kitchenette is great also with a coffee maker and replensihed every morning. Definitely recommend this hotel the location is great to get around everywhere in NYC. You can walk or taxi. To end the holiday the hotel can take you to the airport in their limo just a little bit more expensive than a taxi but it's a nice end to your holiday. Hope you enjoy NYC love it and will definitely go back..

title_masked: Overpriced, Clean, & Good Service, but not worth it
text_masked:
I hadn't been in San Fran in years and wasn't familiar with Union Square. This place is in the heart of it. I would compare it to staying in Times Square in NYC. The area has all the big chain stores that every major city has and it's crowded. If you're not American, this may be nice. If you are, you may want to see what unique things San Fran has to offer, not the same old stuff most cities have (Macy's, H&M, Uniqlo, etc).
The room was very small and we barely had a view (it must have been a room off to the side). Complimentary water, apples, cookies, teas, coffees in the lobby are a nice touch. The room was clean, but the photos online made it look a bit more "boutique-y" than it actually is. 
I prefer the character, bars, and shops near Valencia and the Mission and would stay closer to there (or anywhere else) next time. I feel like you can definitely do better for a location with more character which is less expensive.

title_masked: Excellent hotel in a great location!
text_masked: My husband and I stayed at this cute deco hotel that is nestled in a great location. It is located within walking distance to Chinatown, the mall and even Little Italy which is a good walk but not too bad. The staff was incredible helpful and very nice. The concierge provided us with excellent help in choosing activities and informed us of the BEST tour company! The front desk employees were extremely helpful as well and were able to assist us with late check out which we were very grateful for with our time awkward flight delay. The room was VERY nice and clean. A desk for you to work on, nice TV and the beds were extremely comfortable. You can't beat the location, you can walk right out of the door and catch a cable car! I recommend this hotel and if I go back to SF I will only stay at this hotel!

our 12x12 "room" had dingy walls, mold on the shower curtain, broken ac/heat, peeling paint from the ceiling, old worn out bed that was quite uncomfortable. and it was dirty. by far, the worst hotel room ive ever rented. also, the electrical outlets were in hazardous condition. we had a nice view of a brick wall through our dirty window. also, had a problem with the tv controls. and something broke on the sink during our last day there. but other than that, it was great

Centrally situated with great access uptown and downtown, the Waldorf remains a favourite with awesome beauty. Good service and willing staff all fits in with the legend. Best rates available online on the hotel website about 3 weeks before arrival.

title_masked: Great make-over of an old hotel
text_masked: We just stayed at the Public in Chicago. It was formerly the Ambassador East and they made the Public into a modern, clean hotel. Love the neighborhood and ease of walking. The lobby and restaurant seems hip and trendy.
