We stayed in a suite on the 27th floor. Our adult daughters had a fold out bed in the lounge room which wasn't overly comfortable but our bed in a separate bedroom was lovely. Our room had a kitchen with a microwave which was very handy. The hotel is having some renovations in the foyer. The position is very handy, especially if you plan on using the subway right across the road. I was very surprised that the police sirens could be plainly heard even on the 27th floor. It took us a few nights to get used to them and sleep through the night.

I was at The Blackwell for OSU Orientation in June. This is my 2nd visit to The Blackwell, a year apart and I am happy to say that it was a great visit, as it was last year. This visit, my daughter and I used the complimentary Airport Service and it was on time and great not to have any worries. Upon arrival at the hotel, our room was not quite ready, so they held our luggage while we found our way through campus. The front desk gave us a great map and upon return we were able to go straight up to our room. 
Breakfast buffet was included both days which for us being small eaters, was perfect. The food was fine, but if we wanted fresh made to order food, we would have ordered off the menu and payed ourselves, not a big deal. I loved the paper in the mornings and the coffee in the room was great as well.
This is the best hotel to stay in, plus it is really part of the campus. I think it is run by OSU Business School and run very well. All employees are happy, polite and knowledgable especially because I was very unfamiliar with the campus to start with.
There are plenty of walkable restaurants, but the front desk will call a cab for you if needed. Also, there is a complimentary Business Center on the Mezzanine Level where I was able to print out our boarding passes.
We will be frequent visitors here!

I spent one night at the Intercontinental, which was good enough for a business stay. This is a very large convention hotel and when I checked in the huge lobby was packed with people and very noisy. My room wasn't ready at 2:50pm, so I explored the neighborhood, which is not interesting, for about 30 minutes. 
When I first checked in I could hear the guests in the room next to me and some traffic noise, but it was quiet in the evening when I went to sleep. The A/C was loud so I turned it off. The bed was very comfortable and the shower was pretty poor.
The view was not interesting - I'd asked for a harbor view not expecting to get one because I booked last minute. So, when I was told at check-in that I had a view, I was pleased - until I saw the view - which was of the other tower and if I stood at the window (which had a desk in front of it) and looked at the correct angle, I could see the view. 
The spa is average and I could have done without the sales pitch from the massage therapist for a product he was clearly trying to sell. The breakfast is overpriced and average. The hotel is only 15" from the airport, which is nice.

This hotel has a great location, especially for the price. I've never been to San Francisco before, but we easily took the BART from the airport and walked to this hotel from the Powell station. We were on the 8th floor facing the street and it was a little loud late at night. But, we were so exhausted by the day activities, that the street noise didn't bother us much. If your looking for a great location, and can't spend $250-$300 night, this hotel is a great option.

We went to Houston with a group of 100 people. The rooms were fantastic. The staff informative. Terrance! Terrance was full of information and recommendations that truely think he made our trip. The rooms are comfortable, spacious and clean. Love the Starbucks coffee in the room, that was a special treat! Location couldn't be better! Great shopping, great city. I will say this, we went to the Houston game as a Raven fan and note to anyone who is traveling for this reason. Now, I know we got our butts handed to us, but it wasnt necessary for the fans to throw plastic bottles and throw beer on us. Bad enough we lost. I will not go to a game in Houston again.

What really made this hotel stand out was the superior service from the moment we stepped out of the cab. The porters immediately grabbed our luggage from the trunk and whisked it onto a cart where it was delivered to our room. The checkin was quick and effortless, our request for a room with two double beds was immediately accommodated, and we were provided with a list of area restaurants within walking distance as well as coupons for the restaurant we chose. The entire staff was polite, friendly and helpful. The room was quiet and comfortable. The free breakfast was convenient and tasty, although quite crowded on Saturday and Sunday mornings. The location is right in the middle of many downtown Chicago attractions. The only minor distraction was noise from the neighboring room which we could clearly hear from the living room area. The bedroom however was quiet and there was absolutely no street noise during the night. I would highly recommend this hotel for value, cleanliness, comfort and an overall pleasant experience in downtown Chicago.
OK. The staff was very friendly and the hotel has some character. But the rooms are too pricey for their quality.

stayed here for 4 nights for a business trip. Facilities were clean and modern. Staff was pleasant. Ate at the bar, restaurants, and room service with no complaints. Gym was clean and well equipped. My only complaint would be location. It seemed hard to get around if you were a tourist there to site see.

We travelled over over from England and had booked the Palomar for 10 nights in September. After a long haul journey we were very warmly welcomed,frustratingly can't remember the two gents names who checked us in but they were both great and really friendly offering help and assistance with the local area and attractions etc.
We were lucky enough to receive a complimentary upgrade to one of the apartments/suites - We were impressed. Smart, modern and spacious rooms with some decent views over the city. Two bathrooms, one with dual showers etc. If I'm splitting hairs the only draw back to the room was being situated over the generators so we couldn't really benefit from the two balconies the room had on offer due to the noise ( as a note the noise was not audible from inside the room). Overall a very homely feel, and the bed very soft - struggled to get out of it everyday it was that comfy! 
Housekeeping did a fantastic job every day without fail, in addition maintenance were prompt, polite and professonal when we had a small issue with the dial of our shower -fixed straight away.
Pool area lovely, it is small so would have the potential to get crowded during peak season but this is a city centre hotel so it depends on what your expectations are. We were there to see the city and not to sit by the pool so this aspect wasn't high on our agenda of hotel 'must haves'.
Just regarding previous comments around the amount of homeless outside the hotel, please don't let this put you off, there are not sat on the doorstep of the hotel at all and as with any city they can be found anywhere. The location of the hotel was great, right at the top of the Gaslamp so close enough to everything and quiet too so you get the best of both worlds. 
We had a great time and loved the hotel and have no hesitation in recommending the hotel as a definite 'go to' place if in the area. Stylish, friendly, professional and smart - well done Palomar!

Stayed 1 night prior to an early flight. I stay at many Hyatt Place Hotels and this was pretty standard for the brand. Comfortable, spacious room. Very friendly staff, got a great dinner recommendation, and enjoyed a few adult beverages after dinner at their bar. Reserved a cab to airport because we were nervous about getting their on time with the shuttle, however shuttle appeared to be running on the half hour just as promised.

We hadn't stayed at the St. Francis Hotel for over 25 years and we didn't even realize there is a new high rise attached behind the original structure on Union Square. In fact, there's no obvious connection between the new and the original if you enter on the Powell St. side and use the lobby area and other amenities. We stayed in a modest twelfth floor room facing away from the street with only a view of the rooms opposite. We had reserved a month ago and everything was in order when we arrived. The desk staff was polite and helpful. There was the usual larger than seemed necessary group of bellmen waiting to help but they weren't aggressive and didn't seem to mind that we carried our own luggage, which isn't much any more since the airlines have turned luggage into a profit center. The room was clean and appointed about like every other room in well-kept older city hotels that we stay in. It had a snack rack and a mini-bar with a sign that told us that items removed are billed within ten seconds. I'm not certain how that happens but we made sure to not remove the $6.00 mini-bag of Cheetos and we didn't even risk opening the door of the bar fridge. The window had a shade screen and a drop down drape. The shade screen does not obscure your activities, or at least it didn't screen the folks across the way, so we didn't do anything we wouldn't do in public and we lowered the drape in the evening and while sleeping. The bathroom had minimal counter space and a small medicine chest without a door. It had a good mirror and a great two-headed shower with a notice that said they hope we wouldn't use it. Something about conserving water and being green, I think was the reason, but I used it anyway and enjoyed every minute of it. In room wi-fi costs $14.95 per 24 hours or somewhat cheaper if you sign up for a larger block of time. (I learned the next day from a guy in the lobby that free wi-fi is available in the lobby at "westin lobby." His laptop had picked it up when he turned it on.) The TV worked fine, closet space is modest, the in-room desk is adequate. When we asked, we were furnished without charge, a fridge and a microwave. Parking is expensive in the hotel garage but there are at least three parking garages within a block and a half and we had found a Groupon for three days parking for $60.00 with unlimited ins and outs at the California 
Garage at O'Farrell and Taylor, about a block and a half away. That wouldn't cover one day at the hotel. I asked at the desk about public transportation to AT&T Park and was given incorrect directions about where to get on the muni bus. If you're going to a Giants game, walk down Powell to the end, turn right and go down the steps, or use the escalator, and take the Inbound N train to the Park. It isn't obvious where each train stops so ask someone where the Inbound N train stops or walk along the walkway until you see the sign. It takes fifteen or twenty minutes and you get off right across the street from the left field side. Return is just as simple. Seventy-five cents for seniors and I think, $2.00 for regular people. If you stay for more than one night at the hotel, you are offered a $5.00 credit for use at Hotel shops if you decline maid service. One credit each day, except the checkout day, of course. The elevators work quickly and well. They have a small fitness center and a usable Business Center. We dined at Bourbon Steak, the Michael Mina restaurant that's in the St. Francis. The meals for our group were all enjoyed, the wait staff is excellent, there is an extensive wine list but a short beer list, and don't forget to fill your wallet before you go. All in all, the St. Francis is okay. There are about 60, yes 60, hotels in that immediate area of San Francisco. If only for their greed about the wi-fi we will probably not go back for another 25 years.

Wonderful little Artsy hotel on the quiet part of the Riverwalk. A little walk from the tourist noise and bussel but a nice leisurely stroll in an uncrowded and beautiful part of the Riverwalk. Great staff and management. Very helpful. Ask for a riverview room with a Balcony on the third floor. Patio below has been noisey but not for long. It's different but great. Great bar and casual breakfast area. Nice pool, too. Parking is expensive and across the street but it's ok on this end of St Mary's Street. Enjoy!

This hotel is just what you pay for....cheap, but ok for one night of a quick stay - $75.00. HOWEVER, I was shocked when I learned on check-in that there is a $15/night parking fee, for an unsecured, open parking area on street level - not even a fence to secure the cars parked there. Thankfully, I had a rental car and nothing happened. It was incredibly unacceptable that there would even be a fee. it would have been better to list the room rate $15 higher with free parking, than to put a value on this "ammenity." This is probably way too much to say about it, but it's the principle of it.

My room was immaculate-the only thing I wish it had was a fridge!!! Other than that, from the beautiful reclaimed wood hardwood floors to the lush king size bed to the large flat screen with premium channels, it was wonderful!!!

title_masked: Friendly, helpful and safe place to stay
text_masked: My daughter and I stood at the Dolphin Motel from July 8 thru the 16th. Everyone at the Dolphin was super friendly and helpful if you needed anything- directions, advice were to shop or eat, maps, etc. and they kept an eye on everyone who came and went, so that we felt very safe there (video cameras around the property as well). The rooms are clean (painted white) and the linens (most important to me) were exceptionally clean and in great condition. The mattress was comfortable and we both had no trouble falling asleep. They try to keep the outside noises down for sleeping from 10pm to 9am, as the sounds can travel into the rooms. We checked in late at night and the TV wasnt working (no biggie for us as we went to sleep) and they had a new one in the room the next morning. Continental breakfast of coffee, juice, yogurt, bananas and muffins was a great start for the morning. Would definitely recommend and stay again.

We stayed at the Omni Shoreham this past weekend, and thought it was a great deal. The location is great, even if it is necessary to ride the Metro to the Capital area. The Metro station is only a block away, and there are many good restaurants within a block or two of the hotel. It is an easy walk to Dupont Circle, Adams Morgan and Cleveland Park, and there are more great places to eat, drink and shop in those areas. Our room was large and very comfortable, and the employees were friendly and helpful.

The hotel was pretty fab; I had my two teen sons with me and perhaps this is a better place for swanky couples and singles who can live it up at the free champagne hour every evening. The metro is quite a walk in this heat wave, but the DC Circulator bus stop was very close. I was thankful for the cold water in the lobby, but felt strange about getting a cup of tea or coffee...no one had explained the breakfast going-ons and there wasn't anything about it in the room. The staff were extremely busy multitasking and I felt like I couldn't ask them mundane questions like about breakfast or how to open the mini-fridge (it was locked). Many of the guests were so demanding of the desk staff, I wanted to tell the guests "shame on you" for their rudeness and foul mouths. Like most businesses, I guess they can't afford to have enough staff and keep costs low. 
For the room, it was clean, deliciously cold (in this heat wave!) and comfortable. Even though we heard our neighbors while walking in the hall listening to music, our room was pretty soundproof. All-in-all a good room in an expensive city.

Very nice hotel. CLEAN and the staff was ever so helpful. The breakfast was incredible and they even had Espresso coffee drinks and Soy milk. The rooms are spacious and quiet. The beds are comfy and towels soft.

title_masked: Andaz Fifth Avenue-a five star way of delivering service, service, service
text_masked: I have visited NYC on many occasions but never have I enjoyed every aspect of a hotel as much as this wonderful boutique and novel way of caring for guests. My first experience was speaking to the Director of Rooms Connie Wang. She was so excited about the hotel and the accomodations and after answering my questions about the room types her excitement made me even more excited about my visit. On the day of arrival, I was surprised and impressed to receive an email allowing me to check in by computer so that I would have very little to do when arriving at the hotel. I have never experienced this before but it was so considerate of the hotel to make arrival easy after arduous travel. On arrival, I was greeted by at least three caring, wonderful individuals who made me immediately feel right at home. What I found unique was the hotel offers free wine to guests in the bar beginning at 6pm and all non-alcoholic beverages and snacks in the minibar are free. I can honestly say that I have never been given these amenities as a guest in the finest of five star properties I the US or abroad. What is also unique is that there is a seamless caring for guests by the lobby staff and they are referred to as "hosts". The hosts do whatever little is necessary to check in, they gave us a hotel tour, took us to our room, acted as doormen at times and also as concierges. This works incredibly in that rather than division of labor where staff did not get to know me or my likes, our host Dana Steer amazingly checked us in, advised us as a concierge on dining experiences, greeted us at the door and took care of any of our hotel needs. He made our visit truly special! The rooms are a true"wow". The other couple with us had a deluxe room and me and my wife had a splash suite. Both rooms were spacious, modern with comfortable bedding, wonderful linens and big elbow bathroom amenities. The TVs were flat screen and there were wonderful lounging sofas in the room. The bathrooms were state of the art with wonderful shower heads. The hotel has an amazing restaurant that we experienced breakfast in. The concept is farm to table and the ingredients are fresh and dishes innovative. I experienced the Dutch pancakes and my wife had lox that was supplied by Russ and Daughters which is well known for their wonderful fish products. I cannot wait to visit this hotel again. The combination of innovative service, wonderful caring staff and a beautiful facility makes it a New York City must. My hat goes off to Hyatt for creating Andaz. It is the truly humane and caring hotel to visit!!!

title_masked: Standard rooms are very small, but great amenities and location
text_masked:
I stayed here as an alternative to a $250/night conference hotel, and I feel that I got my money's worth. I booked on Hotwire and the room was only $60/night. The location of the hotel is easily walkable to the Gonzales Conference Center, as well as the Riverwalk and pretty much any other tourist location you can think of, including the Alamo. 
The property is beautiful, the lobby grand, and the fitness center very up to date and hardly utilized. The pool is small but useable.
The room I was given (631) was quiet, but had a view of the rooms of the hotel in another wing. I thought it was cloudy every morning until I went outside, and I realized that the other tower was blocking the sunshine. The room had a nice queen sized, high up bed that was very comfortable. However, I would estimate that the entire room was about 15' x 15' -- very European. The TV was dated, the bathroom was tiny (imagine sitting on a toilet and having your elbows touching the wall and the shower curtain). However, I wasn't in the room much due to the conference, and for one person it was more than adequate.
I am pleased with the price I paid and the experience that I had at this hotel. I would definitely stay here again if I could get another deal through Hotwire.

The Hyatt Regency is classy enough in any city, but in Austin you have the added thrill of it being right next to the Congress Street Bridge--home to the largest bat colony in America. At dusk, thousands of bats emerge from the bridge struts and fly out over the river. Quite a site!
The hotel boasts the most comfortable hotel bed I've slept in this year. Plus their bar is awesome, they have sushi chefs just off the lobby who, if you challenge them to be creative, will prepare some of the yummiest sushi rolls around, and live music too. 
And did I mention they're in walking distance of the infamous Sixth Street and famous Threadgills? Well they are. Plus I could see the Aussie's outdoor volleyball courts from my window.

Great disappointment with the hotel airport shuttle! I arrived at the airport and found out that the courtesy phone call booth does not include Hawthorn Suites. The hotel required you to call them upon arriving (they do not allow you to book in advance via email whatsoever which I emailed them 2 weeks before my arrival and received a reply that I must call them personally) in order for them to pick you up from the airport unlike Hampton Inn. I was waiting at the hotel shuttle area and I saw Hampton Inn van came 3 times to pick up their guests. I almost wanted to forgo my hotel reservation and board the Hampton Inn's van. Waiting in the cold. So when I called them on my cellphone, guessed what 'engaged tone' (umpteen times). Finally, I took a cab them which cost me US$33. When I feedback to the front desk, he didn't even try to explain and just smile at me. It seemed that he didn't care. Sad.
The reason I booked this hotel was because of the airport shuttle. Cost-saving I thought. Who knows I paid more! I will not stay there again for sure!

I was initially atracted by the Jefferson's membership in Relais & Chateaux and I was delighted to see that it lives up to that standard. This was my second stay at the Jefferson on business, and I have already booked my next stay. Great features abound, including a well-appointed library accessible to only overnight hotel guests. Very classy..

title_masked: Hip Hotel in the heart of it all
text_masked: very modern hotel with an asian feel that is close to everything. I would stay there again.

We were in Boston for a wedding and chose the Hyatt. The employees were very accomodating, friendly and generally made us feel welcomed. We had room service twice which was very nice and the food well prepared. Loved the location as it was easy to walk around and to Fanueil Hall, the harbor, etc. Beds were so comfortable that we didn't want to get up!

Had to stay here overnight waiting for a connecting flight. Traveling with our dog, and they accepted pets. Was expecting something minimal, and just enough to get through the night. Turned out to be clean, friendly staff, and overall good experience.

title_masked: Everything was fine, just bring your own towels!
text_masked: Stayed here four nights and just could not make housekeeping understand the need for towels and washcloths. Each morning I piled the used towels on the floor, as requested by the note in the room. Two of the four days we stayed here the towels were removed from the room and not replenished. I could see it happening once, but twice was ridiculous! Everything else was fine: great front desk, great concierge, very clean, morning coffee and newspaper in the lobby. Happy hour wasn't too, but the cocktails were a little weak and full of fruit instead of liquid. I would stay here again probably.

title_masked: Does Crown Plaza Really Know My Love Language?
text_masked: First, things first, when I'm in Austin there is a specific hotel I stay at every time. I DON'T LIKE CHANGE!! I want my cookie every time I go, and a 2nd floor view. So, I was already skeptical when I was told I would be at the Crown Plaza, because it was not what was normal for me. I walked in, and the hotel was very beautiful, ok check, what's next. I walk up to the counter and Kevin greets me. "Good evening Mrs [NAME], thank you for choosing the Crown Plaza, here is your complimentary drink ticket to the lounge, and would you like a cookie?" Whaaattt, was Kevin a psychic?? How in the world did he know my love language was getting Gifts! How did he know I was upset about not getting a cookie at check in? Was it the pearls that adorned my neck that gave him the clue I was high maintenance!! Was Kevin my soul-mate, how did he know!!!!!! Check-in was smooth, friendly and fast, how did he know I'm impatient! I went to my room and it was very nice, clean, and very upscale. To my surprise more gifts in the bathroom wrapped nicely in a towel on the counter!! (Oh, Kevin, you shouldn't have!!) Ok, check, so far so good. After taking in how well put together and nicely decorated my room was I went to the lounge. It was great, the service, the food, everything was great. I have already booked my stay next week, here at the Crown Plaza, why wait!! As it turns out, Kevin treats all of their guest this way, It's the Crown Plaza's way of doing business, and it doesn't hurt to be a Rewards member either. I know I will get a good nights sleep tonight my bedding is so comfortable and soft!, and as I anticipate this good nights sleep and telling Kevin tomorrow about my good nights rest and sweet dreams, I have a strange feeling he already knows!!

We stayed at this property for the first time prior to a cruise on the QM2. As frequent travelers to New York, we had overlooked this hotel. What a find! It will now be our New York hotel. Location is great for theater going. It is far enough away from Times Square to be out of the tourist bustle, yet convenient to all. Upper floor rooms have great views. Ours on the 31st floor even had a small view of times square, but with an open city view. The room decor/design was sophisticated and great style. We particularly liked the bathroom with indigo glass tile shower. The credenza that ran the complete length of the room was very functional as well as stylish. Beds were phenomenal. Linens soft and cushy. Service was stellar. We had married in New York and comp bottle of champagne and strawberries were sent up, along with a nice message. We ate at Todd English in the lobby with friends and the food was amazing. Once again, great food styling and delicious. Creative selections. They offered a three course meal at lunch for 30.00 that was a great buy for food of this quality.
This hotel scored a perfect 100 points with us. As seasoned travelers, this is rare. Congrats to the staff and others making this a great place to stay.

We started staying here while my son was looking at colleges. We have since stayed four different times over the past year. 3 visits I would rate 5 stars and the last would be a 4 only because of the noise next door. The hotel itself is extremely clean and the service could beat any top hotel in the city. The building is old and so the soundproofing between rooms is not that great. One nice feature though is the hotel management clearly state quiet hours and have no problem taking care of complaints if they arrise.
Luckily, even though our neighbors were a bit noisy on the last trip, they were not late night people nor were they extreme early risers. They also had a full room of 4 adults and were with a group of people who were staying just below them - so lots of coming and going. Which is fine - they are on vacation after all..
I would suggest requesting a room on the south side of building (closest to USC campus) as there are apartments on the west and north sides - and I did hear someone complaining about noise from the apartment on the north side which the hotel can't do anything about. Many USC students rent these apartments so Thurs - Sat nights can have more noise.
But for the price and proximity to USC especially - you can't beat Vagabond USC. Free parking and pool!

title_masked: Excellent Location, Nice rooms - good value for the money
text_masked: Stayed for one night. Rooms are carefully planned to maximize space and efficiency, all the way to the USB sockets in the walls to charge your phone/isomething. Friendly staff and small but meaningful perks (complementary Wi-FI, worksatation and printer to print your boarding pass) made it a very pleasant experience. Highly recommended.

title_masked: Great Value, good service, but have realistic expectations!
text_masked:
I came here for Thanksgiving weekend and booked months ahead and got an amazing deal of $75 usd a night! not only that, but the very nice front desk gentleman honored my request of a room looking toward the street. We are heavy sleepers, so noise did not bother us, in fact, I like to listen to the world go bye! 
The building is old, but clean, and our room was extremely clean! so important, as I was going with my 12 yr old son. 
Wifi worked good, close to chinatown, which my son loved loved loved! and a few blocks from the Bart station, Union Sq, etc... 
With all that said... you have to know that if you book this hotel, you are OK with a budget room... this is one of the most recomended hotels for budget travellers... if you are used to the Westin... no mater what they do, you'll be dissapointed. 
All the staff was great, always with a smile, and ready to help us!

Hotel is withing walking distance to harbor, stadiums, etc. Valet parked the car and didn't use it for 3 days! Room was clean - rm 1013 - a bit on the small size, bathroom very small - but nonetheless clean. I read some reviews the area is "BAD", please keep in mind this is a large city - as with all large cities - there are good areas and better areas and just some areas you don't walk through at night. I was with my 24 yr old son and we walked everywhere, both day and night. Price was wonderful as I grabbed through hotwire - paid what you would pay for Red Roof or hotel in that category. Bellman, front desk, lounge all helpful and never made you wait. Yes, the hallways and rooms could use some updating - not terrible but a bit dated. I also read check in at 4:00 and they wouldn't budge, we checked in a little earlier with no problem and our checkout was noon, which was a pleasure! Bed was comfy, down pillows, comforter and down blanket.

Staff were fantastic from start to finish. Room was small (typical NYC) but very well designed and laid out that we never felt crammed. Beautiful bath, very comfortable bed and sound-proof windows (helps with crazy cabbie honking going on 24/7). great mood lighting options in the room (huge benefit to boutique hotels). Rooftop access at Jimmy was great - fantastic views of the whole city surrounded by cool decor/people/drinks.
no breakfast - which is fine with us as we like to eat out - why else go to NYC? They do offer some fresh baked goods and coffee in the lobby - which was a beautiful area to hang out.
Artwork throuhout the hotel was also a nice feature to appreciate.
Great place... excellent staff... great location and good value (for a boutique hotel). Would definately stay again if i stay in SOHO.

title_masked: Great location and clean bed sheets !
text_masked: I enjoyed our stay, the rooms big, we were in 6 th floor, newly renovated, the beds are clean, nedsheets smell good, no bugs , roaches or anything !! I would definitely stay again at this hotel

One night stay, to be able to visit Graceland and move on to the next adventure. Hotel is clean, beds are real comfy, and continental breakfast was good. Typical Days Inn. Staff was friendly and helpful while checking in. Just a NOTE... Graceland is in the middle of a not so nice part of town, which threw me off a bit.

If you are looking for a clean hotel in a descent location and NOTHING more then this is your hotel. I never usually complain or give bad revews but this hotel is NOT what they advertise. Our trip started by being told our room had been cancelled because we didn't show up one day early? Oops... I think someone screwed up! They then proceeded to tell us we wouldn't be able to have the room we booked with 2 queen beds but would have to have one with 2 fulls (for the same price LOL). After holding firm and having to waite a few hours we were finally given the room we paid for. Upon entering the room which was very clean but very old we noticed our beds were so bad you could see how sunken they were in the middle before you even layed in them (and this was not because they were pillow top mattresses because they weren't). On top of it, all night we had to listen to the comotion and sirens from the gentleman club accross the street along with the rattling of our in-room air unit. So needless to say if you are looking for a good nights sleep DON'T stay at the Sixth Avenue Inn!!!

I just wanted to say that Norma Perez is a great housekeeper--very nice. My family comes to this hotel a lot and always has a good time. It's affordable for the area--close to everything in the Hollywood area.

title_masked: A lovely weekend at Park Hyatt
text_masked:
We stayed last weekend for two nights for my daughters graduation. Our favorite in DC have always been both DC Ritz Carlton Hotels. We decided to try Park Hyatt this time. My overall impression is very positive. I must mention few irksome points first. We arrived at hotel around 11 AM. Only one check in area was open and we were number three in line. Soon a young man arrived to check us in but no hello or any greeting or even eye contact. No one offered us help to bring our luggage nor directed us to where the elevator was. This was a disappointing experience after being spoiled by Ritz Carlton welcome.
Room was spacious and no complaints here except the bathroom seat in our suite's second bathroom was broken. 
Highlight of the stay was restaurant. We had dinner and lunch. Both were fantastic. 
I am sorry for not giving 5 stars, I wish our check in was smooth.

Loved this place.....the convenience, the rooms, the breakfast, the ambiance, the artwork and most of all, a wonderful, friendly staff. Got this room at a wonderful price through 'priceline' just a few days before we left. It was a steal. Loved walking to '16th Street Mall' and 'LoDo'. Could have wondered the whole place for hours just looking out the large lobby windows into downtown Denver and checking out the great artwork throughout the hotel. Not a large, but a very sufficient breakfast spread. Breakfast staff were very prompt and very friendly in making sure our plates were cleared and we had everything we needed at breakfast. Front desk staff were friendly and courteous as well. Rooms were spacious, clean and modern. Loved staying here.

title_masked: Fab hotel let down by the unwelcoming/unhelpful staff.
text_masked:
Fab hotel. Located in excellent position. 
Rooms of very high standard. Comfortable and well equiped, including free WIFI, i pod docking station and a coffee maker with lovely complimentary coffee. Very modern bathroom with lovely large shower. 
Wonderful amenities located on the 3rd floor, large outdoor and indoor pools, hot tubs and running track. 
However this is all a little spolit by the unfriendly and unwelcoming staff, offering little or no information on the hotel. 
At one point the fire doors on the third floor were all locked. 
Another time we found the main hotel door blocked off. No signage on how you leave the hotel or assitance was forecoming. 
For two days we had to put up with someone doing maintenace around the outdoor pool area, with a machine making a noise I could only compare with a pneumatic drill. 
The outside bar area was closed for two days as the sidewalk was being dug up.
The swimming pool towels is the hotels best kept secret . 
Staff need a lot of customer care training. It is my thoughts that they do not care about the individual guess and prefer to concentrate on large parties and groups. 
Would I use the hotel again? Doubtful.

title_masked: The opposite of a NYC view
text_masked:
At check-in time I was told that even thought I'm a Platinum Starwood member, I would be much happier in a king room with a park view on the 31st floor, than a junior suite on a lower-level. Not so. Starting at 6:45am, there was incessant banging and clanking -- so loud, that even my Bose noise canceling headset failed. So loud, that I needed to take a work call on the toilet with the door closed. 
At 7:00 I opened the blinds to find 15 hard hat wearing construction workers staring into my room. On the 31st floor! Oh, and the park is completely blocked by the new structure. See accompanying pictures.
There's no way I'll stay at the Le Meridien again -- far too many excellent hotels in NYC to bother.

title_masked: Good Nite Inn is not just good...they are excellent!!!
text_masked: we enjoyed our stay in good nite inn...room is clean...bed is comfortable...facilities is great...their rate is so affordable...just less than 20 minutes drive to Universal Studio...Mc Donald and Dennys is just 5 minutes walk...

The hotel and room were excellent, but breakfast at $18.95 is overpriced.
As a Priority Club member, I received a coupon from them for a drink in the bar or a Starbucks. That was a very nice perk.
My one huge complaint was that their one and only kiosk for printing boarding passes had a note hanging on it stating "out of toner" when I checked in at 3:00 pm. The note was still there at 7:00 am when I was leaving. A Big problem for an airport hotel!!! The employees behind the desk were very kind about it, but I left without a boarding pass. They couldn't have went shopping to buy some toner????

I stayed at The Jane for 10 days. For the price you pay in NYC, it was actually pretty good. Rooms are clean, always tidy at the end of the day, clean toilets and always available for use. The service was very good, friendly staff (including a Portuguese-speaking) and available. The room is small but ideal for 1 or 2 people, should go more than that, better to book the captain's cabin. As I was on the 5th floor, I was not bothered by noise or nennhum insect. At check out there UJM problem in recovery, but that was promptly resolved by the responsible person at the reception. Almost every day there some kind of exclusive party, but the noise does not reach the fifth floor, so ask for an upper chamber and the window does not stay on the road side, you are not a beautiful view of the river, but as probably the room is only for sleeping, there will be missed. The hotel is very close to some subway stations and is in a bohemian, but peaceful, with several people walking down the street with their dogs at night. The Jane would be back in no problem.

My husband and I choose this hotel because of the location and it looked like a nice hotel. When we first pulled up to the hotel there was no one in the front of the building to valet our car. So my husband has to leave the car and find someone. When he went inside there was a African American lady that barley wanted to assist us. When i came into the hotel the same lady that gave my husband a problem did seem like she wanted to help us. She hurried me for my information she she could keep talking to her friend. When we got to the room we unpacked and started unpacking to get ready for our night. There was a ipod docking system in the room but did not work. When we realize this we called the front desk and asked if someone could give us a new one or just look at ours because we might not have been doing it right. The lady advised us that someone will be up shortly to help. We continue to get ready and noticed that no one had come up so on our way out I went back up to the front desk and asked about the docking system again and she apologized and said it would be fixed by the time we returned. We returned to our room 2hr later to find that the docking system was not working still and we did not have any extra towels that we asked for when we first came to the hotel. I went back down stairs and talked to the same lady and she advised me that she will have someone to get on it right then. At that time I asked her about the pool area and asked if everything was working because my husband and I wanted to enjoy the pool and hot tube and wanted to know if we needed to bring towels from our room and she advised us that there were plenty of towels in the area . When we got down to the pool area we see that there are no towels so when we finished with the pool area(the hot tube was not working at the time) we had to walk from the area to the elevator to the 5th floor soak and wet!!! When we got back to the area we still found that the docking system was not working. My husband and I were celebrating our 1yr anniversary and our entire stay was ruined. We were trying to decide if we wanted to stay here or the Aloft next time we will not be staying here.

title_masked: Nice building and staff, poor location
text_masked: Nice room, comfortable bed, decent breakfast with waffles and selection of cold foods. Had pool and hot tub. Nice helpful staff. Bad location facing the freeway - only the rooms in back were quiet enough for good sleep. Odd location for a Marriott - had to enter across large abandoned parking lot, lousy first impression.

I honestly can't say enough good things about this facilty or its staff. From the moment I set foot into this beautifully rennovated historical mansion, I was greeted by friendly and knowledgeable staff members with warm smiles. The check-in process was quick and I was given the best possible room they had without asking! Clearly, these folks know a thing or two about customer service.
The event I had held at one of their charming lounges was a HUGE success! Again, the staff went out of their way to assure that I had access to the lounge to prepare, help with arranging furniture, catering, bar service, and anything else my friends and I needed before, during and after the event. My guests had a fantastic time and were so impressed with the venue, that they are considering having their own events there too. Needless to say, I HIGHLY recommend and encourage future events there! 
The following day, several of us enjoyed the champagne buffet brunch at their dining facility and it was AMAZING! The variety and quality of food was top notch! And once again, I couldn't have asked for better service. Our server never let my mimosa glass go empty and was more than happy to get items not on the menu for us or even stop to take a dozen photos for us! And of course, always with a smile. :)
So, whether you live locally and want to have a luxurious "staycation" or you're visiting from afar and want to get a taste of the sweet life of the Bay Area... you are in for a treat at the Dolce Hayes Mansion!!!

The rooms were gross!!!! It was over priced and there was no pool. One room they tried to put us up in had mold under the sink (my mother is allergic) and another room smelled like dog pee...finally they put us up in a room where the carpet had just been replaced. But if we had any other option we would not have stayed there at all!!!! So glad to be out of there and would never go back or recommend it to anyone!!!!

title_masked: Excellent service in exciting new Boston Location
text_masked:
We spent two nights at the Westin Boston Waterfront Hotel from 11/16 - 18. The hotel is quite large and is connected to the new convention center. Although the hotel is a good 12-minute walk from the South Station T station, it is a pleasant walk over the canals along Summer Street. There is a bus extension that takes you closer to the hotel if you prefer not to walk as far.
The lobby was very hectic with business travelers and guests taking advantage of the free lobby WiFi. The check-in area was pleasant with non-standard free-floating check-in stations. It felt more personable and welcoming. We were happy to receive a room on the 15th floor facing east to the Harbor. The room was new with standard Westin furnishings, wonderful large bed, large desk and work space, decent clean bathroom with nice amenities and the famous Westin dual massage shower heads.
Although the room was otherwise very quiet, we unfortunately had an adjoining room where there were two small children. The doors between adjoining rooms allow a lot of noise to travel between rooms and we were awoken early the next morning by the cries and screams of the children. A phone call to the service express line immediately remedies the problem as we were given the option to move to a new room across the hall that did not have a door between rooms. To top it off, this room faced northwest, above the convention center and had a spectacular view of the entire Boston skyline. We heard no noise during the rest our stay.
Every service call was answered within minutes, if not on the first ring. The promptness of service was as good as I have found anywhere in the world. Although the area is a bit far from downtown, it is in a newly gentrified section of Boston that is full of exciting residential conversions, eating options, and museums including the Institute of Contemporary Art. Don't miss the Flour bakery for a great lunch or delicious sweets.

title_masked: Nice place. Less attitude would be nice.
text_masked: Was pleasantly surprised with the updated rooms and specifically the cleanliness. The only issue, which I have seen echoed by other reviewers, is the unpleasant attitude/unfavorable treatment by check-in regarding priceline bookings. Not a great start when you feel as though you're being treated less favorably because you booked on priceline, and first impressions are important. Management should keep in mind that many people would not even have found their way to the Renaissance without priceline, and if treated well on a first stay, most will generally be back. Nonetheless, will likely return and would still recommend this hotel to others.

checked in last weekend ...nice location, room and bed were great. Air conditioning was impossible to control ... either froze or burned up all night...Bathroom tad bit small. Love Paulette's...disappointed that roof top bar closes at 9 on Friday night and they (all the bars and restaurants had never heard of St. Germain ??)
Breakfast included but only in restaurant ...champagne at check was quite in nice, and port at turn down...but Lindt truffles for $270 a night in Memphis ?
Loved the 24 access to the well equipped and spacious gym ...
friendly service.

Stayed here for business. Positives: staff is friendly/helpful. Conference food was very good (much better than typical hotel events). Place is clean and generally well kept. I heard (but didn't see it myself) that the gym was fantastic. For an event, the conference/ball rooms are very nice.
On the negative side: this is a very average hotel catering to a business customer. It's currently going through renovations (June 2012), so that has an impact on "ambiance." 
The location is so-so: good if you are doing business downtown. But after dark the area (downtown crossing and china town) can be a little sketchy. It is convenient to public transportation.

title_masked: Excellent stay and hospitality from the staffs
text_masked: We had arrived early from a morning flight at 8 .30 am .. We were given early check in (at no extra cost) with a complimentary breakfast for both days where as we were stayed for a night. The room was spacious , comfortable,breakfast was good.. Overall a wonderful experience.as dogs are allowed .. So anybody sacred of them then please be careful.

title_masked: Great location! Great staff! Great room!
text_masked:
I stayed her for 4 nights (March 7th-10th, 2012) and after reading some of these reviews, I was a little worried. But rest assured, I had a great experience here. Yes, the rooms are small, but I wasn't holding any banquets or concerts in it, so that was okay. The bed was comfortable and the decor was great. All I was doing in them was sleeping in this room, so I didn't need the Taj Mahal space for that. 
The only slight problem was that the windows are too thin. I can hear the street noise. But after I fell asleep, it didn't keep me up. The staff was very helpful, asking if I needed anything, trying to hail a cab as I left every time. The location is close to everything. Central Park, Rockefeller Center & Times Square. The subway line is right down the street. Very convenient. 
On my last day, I had the hotel hold my bags for me because my flight wasn't until the evening, and it took them no time to retrieve it when I returned to pick it up. Make sure you take care of the staff! 
I would definitely stay here again.

The hotel is located on Hollywood blvd, and that's it's best asset. The history of the hotel is all it can live on, the rooms are dated and the carpets in all areas are disgusting.Most areas are dark and only one lift was working,and that seemed to be struggling with the demand. The hotel looks great from the outside,worth a visit for the history, but would not want to stay again. On a positive note, the bell men and receptionists were very good and helpful and the staff in general are good, and the hotel is on the walk of fame and 2 mins from Chinese and Kodak theatre.

We stayed for three nights (3-6 July) in 2 bedroom suite which was perfect for our family of four. Hotel was clean, staff very kind and give as all information we needed.
Since it was the July 4 hotel was very busy but it didn't bother us at all.
The night after fireworks when we returned to the hotel everybody got a bottle of water (for free) what was very nice since the night was very hot. That means the hotel cares about their guests.
We made reservation through the hotel and we got complimentary Wi-fi in our room what was very convenient.
I would recommend this hotel for family trip and we would stay again if we go to Washington DC.

Absolutely superb from the moment we walked in the door. We made a quick trip to NYC for our anniversary to see a Broadway show, and chose this hotel for multiple reasons - a recommendation from a friend, the location, and the outstanding deal (40K HHonors points).
We drove in - there is a valet parking garage right next door that is $30 per 24hrs ($45 without hotel validation). It's run separately from the hotel, so the desk won't call your car down for you, so upon our departure there was a slight wait.
I'd put a note on the reservation that this was our anniversary, and we were just overwhelmed by how the hotel staff responded. We were greeted by a doorman as soon as we walked in, and the front desk clerk was extremely friendly, efficient and helpful, wishing us a happy anniversary and making sure we didn't need any extra assistance. A HHonors associate welcomed us again as we walked to the elevator, and a bellman offered help with luggage. The hotel upgraded our room to a corner room on the 14th floor, and when we arrived in the room, we found a gift bag with a card, two champagne flutes, and a bottle of champagne! Now remember, we hadn't paid anything for this room except Hhonors points and parking.
The room itself was nice and on the large side for NYC. Not brand-spanking-new, but perfectly clean and in great shape. The bathroom was spotless. The view out the large windows was typical for the area - we could see a glimpse of the Hudson, but mostly the city. Street noise was apparent but not loud. Lower floors might be louder, but they may have more soundproofing down there as well. It's part of the city.
The previous month, our friends had asked the concierge for a recommendation for an Italian restaurant for a romantic pre-show dinner. That recommendation - La Masseria - was a knockout. It's right around the corner on 48th, and is some of the best authentic Italian we've had outside of Italy (their wine list is equally superb). From the hotel or the restaurant, the Broadway theaters are a 5 minute walk, so 6pm reservations worked great - we left just in time to walk up to will call as the doors opened at 7:30. No waiting in line for the box office, and we were given our tickets and shuttled inside within 30 seconds of walking up to the Majestic!
After the show, we walked Times Square for a while before returning to the hotel. Again, we were greeted cheerfully, and this time, a doorman was stationed at the elevators to check room keys for some level of security.
Our late checkout request (1pm) was granted without difficulty the next morning, allowing us a stroll through the streets (after picking up our complimentary Starbucks coffee in the lobby) to find a bagel maker and do some window shopping before heading out of the city. The housekeeping staff was very pleasant and each one we passed greeted us. Checkout was painless - our bill for $0 was slipped under the door early in the morning, so I called the desk, dropped our keys in the slot on the way out, and walked to the garage. Several staff members greeted us on our way out and asked us to return.
To top it off, the "Customer Experience" manager contacted us a few days later to make sure everything was OK with our stay. We'll definitely be back!
I can't rate the fitness center - we normally use them but this was a quick trip - or the restaurant, as we obviously ate elsewhere. If I was to change anything in the hotel, it would be to work out coordination between the desk and the parking garage, but that really wasn't a big deal at all.
This is my first review on tripadvisor - the over-the-top hospitality and courtesy we experienced drove me to join and comment.
Maybe Make your stalls a Little BIGGER and LIMIT your cars. MAYBE Get or BUY a lot next to the HOTEL and make it for bigger cars that dont fit in the stalls... OUR rental got side swiped!!!

Recently stayed at the Lakefront for a work trip and if you want to be in the middle of it all, this is the place for you. Never had time for the breakfast but it looked and smelled very good, definitely better than the continental you get in most places. I didn't care for the sky lobby, made getting out and about a little inconvenient. The pool area was quite shabby and sparse and the bathroom in my room could have done with a fan and more than one washcloth a day. Front desk service was neither good nor bad, basically unmemorable. Signage wasn't great, if there were soda or ice machines anywhere in the hotel I never found them. All in all an average stay at a hotel chain that was better than average in days past.

This boutique Hotel is modern, but not luxurious. It is pet friendly, the rooms are spacious, the bathroom is nice, and the staff is very friendly. The location is great, near Union Station (where you can rent a car, there is a Hertz in the second floor of the mall inside) and near the Capitol. Every single attraction is in a walking distance from the hotel. There is also a bunch of restaurants nearby. I would definitely return and recommend to everybody.

title_masked: Great Location in The Heart of San Francisco!
text_masked: Recently stayed here with friends,great location right beside union square.Very nice hotel to stay,we had street view which was a little noisy as every night there was a man singing and playing drums on the street but however we got used to him not the hotel's problem. staff were very helpful and friendly in particular Manny at reception and the conceirge.Will stay here again

title_masked: Sitting in my hotel room wishing I could watch a movie.
text_masked:
So I had been in a convention all day and after dinner put on my pjs and was looking forward to relaxing in front of an On Demand movie. Just found out that they have no on demand, not even an HBO channel. What a bummer.
It's been a while since I have stayed in a business-type hotel without any entertainment options in the rooms. Especially on the 12th VIP floor. So I guess I have time to write this review. Everything else was fine. Very pleasant staff, nice room and great location. 
Just don't look forward to a movie.

title_masked: Beautiful Hotel, but Rm. 2315 needs updating
text_masked:
We stayed the nights of 12-7-12 and 12-8-12. We originally reserved a $200 room on the 13th floor of the newer tower but, it wasn't ready when we arrived at 3pm check-in time. they graciously bumped us up to a $400 suite in the older 5-floor section of the hotel. Beautiful, Japanese-themed suite but, our Rm. 2315 is getting a tad long in the tooth and is missing some basic amenities like a dresser, microwave and refrigerator. 
(Hints: Elevate the mattress off the floor on a waterbed frame that doubles as a dresser. Place microwave and refrig on empty shelf in cavernous closet.)
Here's a list of the worn items that need fixing or replacing, and simple cleaning that's needed:
Both the shower/tub room and toilet room exhaust fans do not function.
Shower room wood door is not cedar and is peeling and mildew stained.
All bedroom seating pillows are worn/torn/stained.
Inadequate closet space to hang clothes.
The sink faucet spigot is very loose on countertop and sink pop-up does not function.
Room divider panels have multiple panes that are buckled and/or stained.
Closet sliding doors slide very hard in tracks (lube with wax, like a candle).
Toilet room wallpaper mildew stained and wrinkled.
Dead bugs in all ceiling lights.
Bedroom ceiling light chipped/broken.
Shower room towel bar very loose on wall.
Mildew in shower room wall tile grout.
Had guest services immediately change the original bedspread/quilt since it was dirty/stained.
We really liked the Hotel and our room though. Visually, the interiors and grounds are beautiful and personnel friendly and helpful. We'd stay again but, would never pay $400 a night for a suite.

The Eastgate Tower Hotel is located in Murray Hill, Midtown East in New York, a great location just out of the hubub of the day to day New York traffic. We discovered Eastgate as we searched in conjunction with our travel agent for reasonably priced hotel/apartment style accomodation for a two week stay in New York. 
What a great venue for an extended stay and while the presentation is a little dated, this is made up for by the competence, flexibilityand helpfulness of the staff. They were outstanding and while we perhaps should not individualise I do need to thank Donna, Yan, Alex, Ashraf Negesti and the housekeeping staff for their assistance. 
Our apartment was spacious and well appointed with plenty of storage. If we return the New York for a holiday our first accomodation enquiry will be to the Eastgate. 
 Maree and Shane McMahon

My wife and I stayed at the Days Inn on Hotel Circle in San Diego Oct 22 thru Oct 25 for our Anniversary.
The Hotel as more than expected as it was well within our Budget and sooo convientent located.15 jminutes to the SD Zoo, Balboa Park and Downtown San Diego plus more.The Staff were all very courteous and helpful. The rooms were very clean. Nice pool and hot tub.
Would definetly stay there again and recommend it to friends. Coffee make in room with Great coffee and a kitchenette. Homer S. Agoura,CA.

title_masked: Even better than the first time
text_masked: This was our second stay here and it was even more unforgettable. We had a massive suite this time round with great view of manhatten and chryslyer building. I proposed to my girlfriend on the Saturday evening at the Empire State Building and I arranged for some roses and champagne to be in the room for when we got back and the concierge was extremely helpful with this. We got to experience the fantastic brunch at peacock alley-highly recommended!!

A friend reccomended this hotel. It is in a really central location, close to transit and steps to Times Square. We stayed for 4 nights. The first 2 were in a room facing the street. It was unexpectedly noisey due to construction at night. The manager was great and changed our room and reduced our rate for the stay to compensate. I wouldn't hesitate to reccomend this hotel!

title_masked: Another Amazing Stay at the Dallas Ritz
text_masked:
I just returned from another incredible stay at the Dallas Ritz. I went to Dallas help my daughter move to a new apt for college next year. During the move I made several unusual requests to the hotel for help finding things for the apartment. My requests were far outside the realm of what they normally encounter from their typical guest. Now add on to that, that it was Memorial Day when the requests were made. Nonetheless, the ladies and gentlemen jumped into action and found everything I needed to make the move successful and smooth.
Every day when I returned the valet and doormen asked how things were going and were genuine and engaging. My car was always up promptly and my bags arrived promptly to my room on arrival and they were picked up for departure within 5 minutes of my call to the bell stand.
My room was a Club Room and I prefer Club because I travel alone most of the time and like the ability to get breakfast and snacks without going down to the restaurant. The Club staff are so kind and helpful and always greet you with a smile and ask what they can do for you and promptly get you what you need. The food in Club is superb and if you are vegetarian, they have something for you as well. The selection of wine is very nice and its nice to know it is there for you after a long day. 
The spa is fantastic and if you have time you must get a pedicure from Bryant and a massage from Leslie. Bryant will make you wish you could have a pedicure every day just to get his foot and leg massage. I promise you that it will be a pedicure like no other you have had. Leslie is an excellent masseuse and I always request her if possible. The spa Concierge, Tanya, is so sweet and makes sure that you want for nothing as you get ready for your services.
Fearings, the five star restaurant in the lobby, is beyond outstanding! And to the review that said that it is monotonous dining because you have only one restaurant to dine in; let me say that I personally could eat at Fearings for a week and not have the same thing twice and I would be in heaven!! The food is flawless, the wine list and Sommelier are outstanding, and the staff is engaging and impeccably trained. The desserts alone will make you want to come back for a second or third meal. The banana pudding with beignets is not to be missed! As for dinner if you like meat try the Buffalo Tenderloin, if you like seafood, try the Salmon or Halibut! And a hint to the same person that said that in room dining was not flawless....you can get Fearings menu in the room! And trust me, it's flawless!
The workout facility is very large and has every machine you could possibly want. It is never crowded and the yoga room looks out onto the pool. Very nice!
The location is outstanding with great shopping nearby and plenty of other restaurants within a block or two. The trolley runs right outside the hotel so if you want to go more than a few blocks and don't want to walk, you can just step outside and jump on for a fun alternative!
I have never stayed in a hotel that gives such attention to detail and to the whims of each individual guest. I'm sold on the Ritz Dallas and it will be my "go to" hotel in Dallas! Hats off to the Managers of the hotel because in my opinion, you run a five star establishment. Definitely my favorite Ritz!

My wife and I spent the weekend at the Millenium Hilton. Its a great location. Easy access to the subway (especially since it rained heavily one day). We had a great view of the WTC Memorial. We were worried about the construction noise, but we didn't hear it at all. The beds are really comfortable as well.

title_masked: Second time around - a bit of a letdown
text_masked: My daughter and I were in town for an event at UNF. We stayed at this same hotel last year - the "newness" has definitely worn off. The proximity to UNF and nearby shopping and restaurants is a definite plus. We were traveling from I-95 north - easy to find - don't use the directions on the hotel's website. As soon as we checked in, i notice the stains and dirt on the desk chair - it sort of colored my impression of the room's cleanliness. I booked our room through the hotel website getting the "prepaid standard room" rate which was pretty good. Although you do not get to choose the room (king v. two double beds), you can make a preference. Based upon what the front desk told me, it is unlikely you will get anything other than a king. I was told the hotel charges more for rooms with two double beds, and based upon demand/availability, why would the hotel place you in a more expensive room?

The Club Quarters in Boston was just what we needed from a hotel in Boston. The location is excellent, as you can walk to all of the sites. It is also very close to the T station. The room was very clean and the staff helpful and pleasant. We really loved the refillable water bottles in the hallway. We would fill up before a long day of walking and take them with us, then replace when we got back. The price was excellent when we compared to other hotels in the district. Over all, perfect location for a few days in the wonderful city of Boston.

The hotel is older and in need of upgrades. Wallpaper peeling and carpets worn. The gym had a good variety of equipment. I tried the recumbent bike, which did not work, but used the exercise bike which was noisy and not smooth. The universal gym and sauna were fine. The lobby was beautiful. The room was small, but clean. I did like the king bed with the Select Comfort mattress. The hotel is in a less desirable area, but an easy walk to the Inner Harbor. We walked back at 7PM and I was not concerned about safety. The staff was very friendly and helpful. We felt welcomed from the beginning and this was the highlight of the hotel. They offer some nice deals, which balance the drawbacks.

I stayed here for two nights in early April and forgot to write a review. My experience started out a little rough but ended well. My first Queen room was down a small cramped hallway off of a larger hallway with workers painting there. It was difficult getting to my room with my luggage because of the guys and all their equipment and they'd just painted the door to my room. Once I got inside the room I was disappointed with how small the room/bathroom was so I picked up the phone, explained the situation, and was told I could switch rooms. 
My second Queen room was much nicer - bigger room and a bigger bathroom. The bathroom even had a small window which was a bonus. The bed was comfortable and I slept well. I love the Molton Brown toiletries. The room was in good shape and clean, but not pristine condition which makes sense because I think the hotel's last renovation was 2008. Overall, I was happy.
This is a large hotel with a grand lobby in a good location in the city. Prices are decent and I would stay here again. If service and amenities are a priority for you there are better places to stay, though. This hotel has recently become part of the Marriott family so I don't know what that means for the future.

I stayed only one night over there because I was afraid about the shared restroom..I can tell shame on me cause cause I didn't stay all the nights. It was great, very clean, excelent location ( close to lots of bars and night life), close to subways, very friendly crew.. A+++ hotel for the price we pay. Recomend to anyone!

title_masked: Nice place, welcoming staff, close to National Mall.
text_masked: Our family of 4 (2 adults, 7-year old girl, 3-year old boy) stayed here for a quick get away during the April school break. The hotel staff was wonderful. So welcoming, thoughtful, and kind. When we arrived, the doorman gave our son some crayons and coloring sheets. Front desk staff, valets, and waiters were also great! The hotel was located pretty close to most attractions. We walked to the Air & Space Museum, Natural History Museum, White House, Washington Monument, and Lincoln Memorial. On an average round-trip outing we would walk approximately 5 miles. The room was clean. The room, like others in the city, was fairly small for a family of 4. The beds were not the most comfortable, and the shower needed some repair work (aesthetically). As we arrived to our room, we noticed that the hotel staff was doing some painting in nearby rooms, so this may be on their agenda :-) We would consider staying here again if we visit the D.C area again (and we do plan to do so!).

title_masked: close to sea-tac, good shuttle service and breakfast
text_masked: My wife and I drove down from Vancouver and stayed one night here to fly to Kona from Seattle. We were happy with everything. Front desk staff was friendly and efficient. Our room was clean and quiet, and we had a nice sleep. Wi-fi in the room was really fast. Breakfast was not fancy, but still good and it was included in your room. The parking lot has decent number of spots. It was pretty full but there were still a few available spots. The lot looks safe. We parked our car there for 10 days and it was all good when we returned. Its location is very close the to airport, about 5 mins drive. Shuttle service was excellent, polite driver, on-time. We only waited for about 10 mins at the airport and the shuttle showed up. If you want to do sea-tac sleep and fly, I highly recommend best western airport executel.

I stayed for three nights while attending a conference in San Francisco. I think this hotel is a great example of a classic historic hotel. I found all staff to be incredibly friendly and welcoming. I used valet parking and my car was always delivered quickly. The breakfast in the Garden Court was amazing. The food was excellent and the ambiance took me back to a much grander time. My room was an adequate size. The high ceilings contributed to a feeling of spaciousness. The bathroom was very well appointed with a marble vanity and small shelf. I did not feel a lack of room. My only complaint is that the shower curtin rod was not one of the newer curved ones that keep the shower curtain away from your body. The amenities were quite nice and plenty of towels were left daily for me. The bed was very comfortable and the linens were exquisite. In all, it was a very nice stay and I would definitely come back with my wife for a romantic weekend. The hotel is located very close to Union Square shopping and the Convention Center.

My fiance and I recently took a trip to Indiana and this hotel was AMAZING!!! The service was top notch, the room was very comfortable, the pool area was nice, and the connection to the mall was an unexpected bonus. Also, I work in public safety and the bellhop that took us to our room (Phillip Sterling) pointed out the emergency exits and the fire evacuation materials. I was in awe. I have traveled extensively-both domestically and internationally-and this has NEVER happened. I was impressed to see that the hotel staff valued my safety as much as I did. Wonderful experience overall. Can't wait to go back!

I parked in front of the hotel and I noticed that they had valet parking, which price was quite steep. The valet parking was almost 20 dollar more expensive than all the other places that I had used before but I decided to use it anyway as I just wanted to get in and relax. The price was 47 dollar a night, so you can say that it was paid.
I was quite surprised when I saw the hotel from the outside as the hotel looked really huge and it not something that I had expected. The valet guys were all over me when I arrived at the hotel and I took out my stuff and gave them the car keys and went to the reception inside.
The lounge area in front of the reception was quite full of people but it was also quite small compared to the huge hotel. The reception was two small desks with a girl sitting behind in an office chair. My receptionist found my booking quite fast and I was given a room on second floor, which I was okay with. 
My room was quite nice and I especially liked my bed. It was large and pretty high, which is a fact that I like because beds in European hotels are usually quite low. The room was really bright and the Wi-Fi worked quite well. The bathroom was nice and I liked my room a lot.

I recently stayed at Marriott's gem in our nation's capital. I was very impressed with the hotel. The elevator was unique in that there were no buttons inside of the elevator cars. After you selected the floor you desired outside of the elevator cars, the unit displayed the car you needed to get into to get to your floor. The executive lounge for Gold and Platnium Marriott Reward members was rather elegant. The heavy munchies were more than enough to eat to fill me up after a day of work. Then before the lounge closed the dessert service was rather nice also. Breakfast in the lounge featured real eggs and tasty sausage. I highly recommend this hotel. It has become my destination of choice when I am in DC for business.

Stayed for three nights during end of June at the Dallas Sheraton. The hotel is really huge, always full of business and convention activity. Definitively not a relaxing environment. We are assigned a room in the North Tower, which I understand is the older one of three (North, South and Central), but were assured the rooms were refurbished very recently. You could tell from the worn out carpets and outdated decor that the North Tower has had its better days. The rooms were refurbished as advertised, but you could still tell the age of the building from the small details that always show up. Our room was very quiet, on the 9th floor, with a view of the pool area and other adjacent buildings. No problem with hot water in the shower, or with the room temperature control. The bed was comfortable and my wife and I were able to have three very good nights of sleep. We did not use any of the hotel's restaurants, or had the need for any assistance from hotel staff. We did use the Sheraton Link facilities. This is a great idea from Sheraton, and it is one of the reasons I prefer Sheraton when travelling. Sans free wireless (or wired) internet in the room, the Link is the next best thing. We are able to surf the web, check emails, etc from the Link every day. There was a wait during busy hours, but we were late night users so no problem with crowds for us. 
The main complaint about the hotel is the parking facility. They do charge $24 for self service parking per day, and the walk from the parking garage to the hotel lobby is loooong. Plan on dropping off bags and people who don't want to take on the long haul, at the lobby and then find a place to park. The walk is confusing and you can easily get lost amid the conference rooms and ballrooms if you don't pay attention to the signage. The front desk told me that I could charge the parking fee to the room, but the payment turnstile at the exit would not accept the room key to do so. I tried both exits with the same result. Fortunately there was no other car in line behind ours trying to get out, but we tried and tried to run the room key with no success. We finally surrendered and paid using a credit card each time we exited. On a Saturday night, when returning to the hotel after dinner there were a couple of large events, one a wedding, and we entered the parking garage as usual. We checked every level of the structure and there was not a single parking space available. We went back down and looked around for assistance, with none to be found. An "unofficial parking attendant" (he did not have a Sheraton badge) approached us and kindly gave us directions to another lot. For this we had to get out of the parking garage, drive a couple of blocks around the hotel and enter a different parkign garage. This other garage also was almost full but luckily we found a spot. It turns out that Sheraton does not have a "guests only" area in the parking garage. I believe Sheraton should arrange to have parking spaces available for their guests always, and have non-registered guests park elsewhere. 
The hotel has easy access from major highways, mainly US75 which was our preferred route. There is next to nothing open during the evenings close to the hotel, so plan your evenings elsewhere. Checkout was fast and trouble free. Overall, a good alternative when travelling to the DFW area.

My mother, sister and I recently stayed here while visiting my son. The rooms were spacious, clean, and reasonably quiet. The housekeeping staff did a great job right down to the towel art. Breakfast was good with plenty of choices and there were enough tables. Check-in and Check-out were easy and getting to the hotel was convenient. We would certainly stay here again.

I can only compare my stay so far at the Ivy Boutique Hotel to that a few weeks ago at the Fairmont Hamilton Princess (Gold Room) in Bermuda—historically renowned for its outstanding hospitality. If the Ivy continues with its formula for excellence, it will surely establish itself as one of the top choices for hospitality in Chicago. When I checked in, I was informed by the front desk attendant that I had been upgraded to a king suite. When I walked through the room, my son and I pulled out our cameras. My son called his girl friend and exclaimed, "This place is crazy!" I took pictures of the entire suite to show off to my wife when I get back to Bermuda—the room is magnificent, with original art on the wall, a television in every room (3), including one that is a part of the bathroom mirror. The bathtub is huge—I could actually stretch out the legs of my 6’1” frame. The king bed is wonderful. I slept like a baby using all four of their wonderful pillows. The only thing that I found as a drawback is that the closet is small. Perhaps that stands out because I just left a king suite in Silver Spring, MD that had a walk-in closet. But other than that this place is over the top. The service has been solid. Room service was quick. The food in the restaurant was great. I actually ackniwledge several hotel personnel by first name. I am definitely going to have to bring my wife to the Ivy on our next trip together to Chicago.

Whilst the Hotel was adequate for our needs it's location on the outskirts of Tenderlion leaves a lot to be desired. The area contains many homeless and beggars who became a nusiance whilst not threaten. Our overall opinion of San Francisco was one of disapointment being expensive for drinks and food and the locals not the most friendly of people compared to the Southern States.

Just returned from a fabulous trip to new york as a family of 5. We were upgraded to the 2 bedroom suite which was more spacious than we could have ever dreamed of!! The 2 bathrooms and the amount of space made our stay very comfortable. Having a fridge and coffee machine meant we could have breakfast in the room before going out for the day. we didn't consider the option of the hotel breakfast as at 9dollars each for a cold buffet breakfast we felt this was too expensive for a family.The rooms were very clean and serviced with fresh towels daily, however they were very warm indeed. We would definately recommend this hotel to any one visiting as the location is perfect- 5 mins to central park and 10 to times square. Would love to visit new york again

Great Location!!! Elevators need to be brought into the 21st century. USC WiFi is Awesome. Rooms need to be Remodeled. Rooms are low end quality, Mold around showers, Ripped Chairs, Noisy outdated A/C unit. Clogged shower drain. Vending and ice machine didnt work. Room Service Breakfast is average. McKay's and Rosso Pizza are good.

title_masked: Modern sometimes at the cost of functionality
text_masked:
