Wrapped up a weekend in NY, we stayed at the Yotel. The presentation and interior designs are pretty impressive. Its a pretty new property so the rooms felt new and clean. We stayed in a Queen two bunk room. The layout was comfortable and the view was impressive.
My annoyances with the room were mostly cosmetic but worth mentioning.
curtain controls are kind of hidden and not really obvious. 
The shower was large but there is no real division between the shower and bathroom floor so water gets out on the floor eventually. I always am annoyed with hotels that use this type of shower design, Its such a nuissance. Like even a small lip or drain along the edge would be great. Nothing is more annoying than going into the bathroom with socks and stepping on a puddle. Same sort of deal for the sink. Its a flat box basin, takes awhile for the water to find itself down the drain. Its mostly due to the design of the sink really. I'm sure the drain is just fine. 
I didnt like not having body lotion within the toiletries, there's two types of soaps to choose from but not one body lotion? Seems strange.
Also the bathroom doesnt lock. Not sure if that's just particular for this room but it would probably be an issue if i was bunking with a coworker or something. 
The highlights are, easy checking-in, you dont have to stand in line or deal with anyone, you just punch up your reservation on the self service kiosk and youre done, im a big fan of self check-in at airports so I love hotels that let you do that to check-in also, the rooftop area bar is great, the drinks are pretty good, pricey. But the view is fantastic, you get a feel for being in the big city.
I'd probably stay again if there was a good deal.

Hey, darned good room, great staff, good service, helpful advice, and diet dr. pepper in the little mini store. How cool is that? My associate had a great morning and evening run through the National Mall because it is so close. Near the Spy Museum and the Ford's Theater. Lots of foodie places nearby.
My only objection to the entire experience was the driver they got me for the trip to the airport. He should never be used again. That guy texted and drove the whole way. He smelled bad. When I chastised him for for risking my life by doing the whole trip on the phone via calls, email, and texting, he blew a gasket...and he gave himself an automatic gratuity. It went from 69 to 89 bucks. I don't know if there is a kick back to the staff who calls this guy or what, but he is really not a good choice and it reflects badly on the hotel who called him on their cell phones to get him.

The Econo Lodge in Memphis TN. on American way/ Lamar, is very Comfortable& Friendly, You will get your monies worth! Room 120 is a Massive King Suite, With Pillow Top Mattresses, And a huge whirlpool Bath. If your in search of nice Spacious suite that fits your budget....Let this be your Choice!

I travel to Houston often, and always stay at the Sheraton Brookhollow. The rooms are great, but the customer service is outstanding. Jose and Jennifer are the hosts in the 9th floor club lounge, and they do a wonderful job in making your stay an enjoyable one. Pepe and Arthur serve up food and drinks in the Tuxedo bar, and Dee serves a great meal in the Cimmaron restaurant. Amanda and Meredith are great at making sure everything works out great for the guests. I can't give a stronger recommendation.
David B.

Easy access to Cherry Creek and clean rooms make this a great choice. 20 minutes to DIA.
The breakfast buffet is better than most hotels in this class, with fruit, pastry, warm items, etc.
Despite the location on a busy road, I heard no noise from the street.
Big pool area which is enclosed.
Friendly and helpful staff.
I left my computer charger in the room, and the manager arranged for its return right away.

This Hilton property is fantastic, coming from Canada as we did through tunnel, you cannot miss the hotel.
From the Valet parking attendants who work very hard, to the front desk, dining and room service people you can tell CUSTOMER SERVICE is most important.
Hotel is clean, very centrally located, safe and feels like home. I would stay again and would highly reccomend. Special thanks to Quinton at check in who gave us a pleasant welcome and a speedy check in.
We will be back. 100%. There are other great hotels in Detroit, but this property should not be overlooked. Thanks again to all staff.

Love this hotel, stayed many times,
The hotel staff are wonderful, and thats what it takes to make a great hotel
It's close to time square and subway is near by.
I can never find anything wrong with the hotel.
Enjoy your stay.

title_masked: Can't beat it for an overnight stay
text_masked:
My wife and I stayed here to be close to the airport for a next-day departure. 
The proximity of the hotel to I-10 and the Phoenix Airport car rental facility was most helpful. The friendly and courteous desk attendant provided us with printed directions to the nearest gas station (so we could fill the tank before returning our rental), as well as the route to the rental facility, which was actually at the very next exit off I-10 to the west.
The whole facility was clean and inviting. No evidence of wear and tear anywhere.
The standard king bed room was spacious enough, equipped with refrigerator and microwave, and very clean and attractive. We had no problem sleeping -- the firmness of the mattress was just right. I did get annoyed a bit by some constant noise from the refrigerator (during regular operation, not just the cooling cycle) but that kind of thing is easily remedied (so long as one does not need to keep anything cool) by pulling the plug on it. Another option is to run the room fan constantly.
For those who don't need a fancy meal, there is a Waffle House just a couple hundred feet away. And, of course, the Hot Start breakfast buffet in the hotel lobby, with a wide variety of offerings. We found scrambled eggs, biscuits and gravy, Cinnamon Rolls, and cereal, among other choices. 
This HIE ranks right near the top of Holiday Inn Express properties at which we have stayed over the years, and there have been a few -- I am a Priority Club member and tend to look first for this chain when seeking lodging.

We were looking forward to staying here but were severely dissapointed with the whole visit. The main entrance looks lovely until you get into your room. We had a family room with a 'supposed king sized bed' and queen sized. I think their must have been an inch of a difference in size, their was no tea/coffee making facilities, the bath had horrible stain marks, the room was old and very outdated and it wasn't as though it was cheap! The only thing good about this hotel is it's location as the staff are so rude. They won't answer you but just point where things are. You even have to pay for leaving your luggage if you are there early. AVOID if you can!

My husband and children were looking for a room to stay while we visited six flags fiesta Texas and since he stays at holiday inn for business we thought we'd give them a shot. First off they offer NO continental breakfast at the very least. Come on how hard is coffee juice and doughnuts? Instead you are offered a 10% discount to their onsite restaurant. Secondly we were given the option of a late checkout and we took it only to find the wifi no longer worked the second day without an additional password that we had to call down for. Lastly, the room was stuffy! We lowered the ac to 69 degrees in an effort to cool the room and it struggled all night. Save your money and head on down a bit further for a better hotel!

Stayed 2 weeks ago and had terrible experiences with many different interactions with various staff. Management is disinterested in resolution or interacting with guests. This used to be a well run property, but current team leads by example of mediocrity. So many quality hotels for the price in San Francisco. No reason to pay for terrible service.

The Westin Galleria Dallas lived up to the reputation of the Westin Hotels. The room was large (2 double beds) with plenty of room to move around, and the bathroom was large as well. Next time I need to stay in Dallas, The Westin will be first on my list to check for a reservation. Being next to the Galleria Mall was a plus--plenty of dining available as well as some of the best shopping--large department stores as well as small boutiques.

I spent six night here and had a wonderful time. The staffs are willing to help. Rooms are clean and lots of restaurants around if you don't want to eat in the hotel. You can go anywhere from here. 10 minutes drive to the airport. Holiday inn shuttle available. It was a business trip but Holiday inn made it more more fun than I expected.

I stayed at this hotel for 3 nights. The hotel was very clean. I thought the room was going to be a little bigger then it was but it was nice. The hotel staff was GREAT, every staff member that I ran into they greeted me even down to the cleaning ladies as I was waiting for the elevator down I had on my Ravens Jersey and the cleaning lady talked to me about football and how nice the staduim was! That was going above and beyound in my book. I also have to speak about Kyle Yount (Guest Services), I have never been in Baltimore and did not know where anything was, Kyle got out a map everytime we left to go somewhere and showed us how to get there. He was so nice. He gave my boyfriend Take out menus the one night we wanted to order! He was so nice greeted us by name everytime we walked in and out! He made my experience much better being that I was from out of town!!!!

title_masked: Good, clean hotel + convenience to airport
text_masked: What you would expect from a Springhill Suites. As a gold member I was upgraded to a king suite. The only difference I believe is a king bed vs a queen. The rooms seem clean. A couple of spots on the light switches which always makes me cringe. The rooms have iHome clock radios where you can charge your iPhone. Mini-fridge and microwave in each room. Nice living room area. TV is on the small side, but sufficient (and is a flat screen). Bathroom vanity is awesome. Not all that big, but dual level which has sufficient space for all of your items. It is better than a dual sink vanity !! The insulation / doors seem to be thin. I could hear normal conversations from the room across the hall as I was entering my room. There is airport shuttle service on demand. It is very close to the airport. Less than a 5 minute drive. Very friendly staff from front desk to shuttle driver. I would definitely stay again if I have the need to stay near the airport. My only suggestion is a little more detail to housekeeping.

title_masked: If it is location you want, this is the palce
text_masked:
Location, location, location. This hotel is near most everything that we visited during this trip to San Francisco. I found most of the staff to be nice and caring, found the room to be a bit small but clean, and enjoyed the bar on the main floor. 
I was on the 9th floor, looking North, and must admit that the view of the roof line was not the greatest. There was a lot of trash on the roof below my room that never got cleaned up, and I think the roof belonged to the Marriott. Also the sound of the A/C units below was a bit loud. I would ask for a higher floor if the view is important to you.
Parking was $55.86 a day, but then, you are in San Francisco.
I had the pleasure of meeting one of the Assistant Managers (Aby) who I told about some of the issues that I felt were not up to the Marriott standard. She seemed to care about my concerns, and guaranteed that she would look into what I had told her about. I felt better after talking to her, and will probably return to this location when I am back in the area.

The Hotel was very clean and well kept. The room was great. The staff was very helpfull with all the questions we had! My husband and I were treated like family. We loved the breakfast the following morning , it was great

Hotel Casablanca is top to stay if you are looking for a hide away in the middle of all the vibrant action in New York. The staff is most friendly and helpful, breakfast tastes really good and the happy hours in Rick's Café are a real treat after an exploration in New York. 
We stayed in a standard room which is small but with a spacious bathroom. Rooms are clean but a bit 'dark'. The beds are small both in width as in length.
The ambiance is relaxed and you can reload your batteries here before jumping into the streetlife again. Big thank you again to the staff !

title_masked: Quiet hotel in the heart of Times Squre
text_masked:
Pros: VERY QUIET, kids had their own space, very good food for a hotel, super convenient to everything Times Square/Broadway has to offer, fast elevators, great staff
Cons: Only complaint is with housekeeping. Found long black hairs in the drawers, on the bed and in the bathroom. Gross.
Overall: Will definitely go back if we need to be in the heart of Times Square
We had a great time in Denver ... New Years Eve was a treat and the staff was exceptional. They are all very guest focused and the fellas behind the omlete station were gettin' it done!!!

This was my first time staying at The Surrey and it was lovely. The room was comfortable, the staff friendly and attentive and the Cafe Boulud delicious. Unfortunately the roof top bar was closed for the season but the bar off the lobby was pleasant. We will be back!

I'll start with a positive. The valet parking staff were very nice, helpful and knowledgable about the city. I felt my car was safe in their hands and they didn't miss a beat in opening a door or with luggage. 
There was one guest ahead of me at check-in. It was later (about 10pm), but it took quite a while to get through the process. Maybe there was a problem with the one person ahead of us. There were two people at check-in, however. Once we finally got to the room, it was average, but nothing great. I've been to other "W" hotels, so I was expecting something a little different, I suppose. The hotel didn't feel very clean, either. I requested a blanket for the 12 year old and it never came, so he couldn't go to sleep for a while. I had to request it again and it finally arrived, but it took two calls and a lot of time. We went to the pool and there is a DJ just next to it with an open wall to the pool area. The pool is outside, which I thought was nice. But on a lower floor. And when people started coming in for the DJ, it was a little strange. Also, we found cigarettes in the pool. It was just not taken care of and I've never before been to a hotel with cigarettes in the pool. Nasty. Check-out was pretty non-eventful, but overall the visit wasn't worth it. We should have gone to a different hotel. I usually don't have the 12 year-old with me, but this hotel wasn't appropriate for a kid or adults who prefer a nice, clean place with a pool. The W sent their own survey and after I had gotten it back to them, they apologized and credited my "starwood" account 2,000 points. This didn't make me feel better. It seemed like a very minor fix.

title_masked: Nice property, but time for an upgrade
text_masked: Stayed here twice in three months while visiting family, for a total of six nights. It's clean and quiet,but the rooms need an updating in the worst way. It's a very busy property for families and business people. Good value, nice sized rooms, but old furniture can't be masked behind quality bedding and towels. Nice shower, though. Rooms tend to have that antiseptic smell, which while good to see they are clean, tends to permeate the air. Good fitness area, and of course the manager's evening cocktail hour and breakfast buffet make this an outstanding value. Staff is there to please.

We stayed for 1 night and really liked the hotel. You step right in off a busy 6th Ave into a very nice lobby that relaxes you immediately. The check in was very quick. We thought the rooms very a little small but very modern and relaxing. This is a great place to stay for a night out in the city. There's a good restaurant connected to the hotel that serves many different types of food and you can sit in a movie theater style set up and watch a huge screen TV (I'm not sure if it was owned by the hotel or not, but was a nice experience).

It's always a gamble when you're trying to pick a nice place to stay online. I spent many hours checking numerous hotel websites, reading untold numbers of user reviews before I finally chose the Seton Hotel. We had our fingers crossed as we entered the lobby hoping I'd had made a good choice. I have to say, we hit the jackpot. The staff could not have been more friendly and helpful. We had arrived in New York early, but they we able to get us into our room right away. A gem on the fifth floor. Beautifully decorated, clean and inviting. We could not have been happier. The location is great for getting around. Grand Central is a few minutes walk from the hotel, and it's easy to get a cab on Lexington a half a block from the door. My wife and I have agreed, that on all future trips to New York, we'll be staying at the Seton.

title_masked: Very pleasant vacation experience! Will definitely return!
text_masked:
My husband and I stayed at the Loews September 23-27 before heading elsewhere in Colorado to visit friends. The staff was very friendly and helpful, and we took full advantage of their free shuttle service. The 'shuttle' is just a large SUV, so during peak times (dinner, sporting events), you may need to wait (it's first come, first served). We waited a little to get to Mile High Stadium, but it was worth it rather than paying a lot of money for a cab.
We also had a rental car, and parking is also FREE - something even just outside of a large city is often hard to come by (we are from the NYC metro area, so we're used to paying for just about everything). 
The cost of Wi-Fi in the room wasn't a huge sticking point as we were able to use 3G service on our phones to access the internet, but if you're paying $10 per day, but not paying for parking or transport if you're using the shuttle, it evens itself out. While the hotel is close to Cherry Creek, it's about 5 miles from downtown so a cab will cost you, but again - take advantage of the shuttle! And if you are as lucky as we are to snag a great AAA rate, the daily cost for a quality hotel can't be beat.
Our room was very large, clean, incredibly comfy bed, and the in-room Keurig coffee pot was great. My only issue was the location of the safe - on top of the shelf in the closet. I'm short, so had I been there alone, it would have taken some maneuvering to get things in and out of it.
The restaurant, while outdated in its decor, was great for lunch on the day we arrived. The food was tasty and the service was friendly.
We were VERY pleased with our visit, and the Loews will definitely be our go-to hotel next time we're in Denver.

Great hotel for the price. Rooms were small but clean and adequate. Nice, quiet residential neighborhood but still within blocks of restaurants and Central Park. Staff was friendly and helpful. Would stay there again.

The hotel met all my expectations. The room was large, modern, comfortable and clean. The Internet connection ($9.95) was OK. The king size bed was very comforatble. Nice amenities. The staff very friendly. 
10 minutes away there is a shopping mall with many restaurants (P.F Chang's, cheescake factory, Smith & Wollensky etc..) I was very tired so I ate at the hotel's restaurant; Surprisingly, the NY steak was very good. 
If you rent a car and plan to return it at the airport, there is a gas station nearby. The airport is 5 minutes away. 
I would definitely come back.

title_masked: Way Better Than Other Reviews Led Me to Believe
text_masked: I got these rooms for an unbelievable price through Priceline so I was willing to deal with something less than perfect. Many reviews led me to believe that the place was filthy and full of grumpy, inefficient employees. We had a lovely visit there. The rooms were clean and the staff went out of their way to be helpful. Starbucks coffee is available from the in-house coffee shop. It does have a fitness center that could benefit from some attention--but it did have bottled water and towels and restrooms.

title_masked: Nice place to hang out for a day or two
text_masked: We attended a four day convention here. The hotel is nice, tucked away but close to the SeaTac airport. 24 hour shuttles and a cookie at check-in makes it even better. The rooms are large enough to accommodate any size luggage. The dresser ample and there is a good size closet. We had the two queen bed option which the balcony overlooked the parking lot (not exciting). The beds were comfy. Flat panel television with a varied array of channels. The hot tub and pool area were nice although we felt it was too cold outside to partake a number of the other attendees made use of it. We had a later flight on our final day here and had to check out way before. The hotel was graciously accommodating holding our luggage while we traveled to downtown Seattle for a day trip. The in-house restaurants were a tad bit pricey which had us off property for the majority of our meals. Luckily there are a number of restaurants close by although we had to ferret these out on our own.All in all with just one hiccup (maid forgot to clean our room the first day) this is a yes kind of place. Preferentially we would stay somewhere downtown but for this particular trip it was perfect.

The Warwick Hotel NYC is spectacular! My husband and I have stayed there for many years!
The location is ideal for business and pleasure. A beautiful, historic hotel that has been well maintained. The staff makes booking and staying a pleasure - from the moment you arrive
you definately feel welcome! The bar and restaurant make eating and relaxing so pleasant -
we especially enjoy the view from Randolph's! The perfect place to host an event also! We have had many meetings and receptions and have always been pleased. If ever asked where to stay in New York, I have only one reply - The Warwick Hotel!

My husband and I stayed at the Westin Austin at the Domain for a weekend to decompress. From start to finish, our stay was fantastic. The entire staff was very welcoming and helpful. The hotel itself is beautiful, modern and very clean. We took advantage of the pool which was very quiet that weekend and the fitness room. Also enjoyed a late dinner at the Urban Lounge. The food was cooked to order and quite delicious. Our room was very nice and well appointed. The shower was very clean which is something I always look for in my stays. The location is perfect. We enjoyed the leisurely walks to the mall across the street. The nearby shopping is fantastic. I am a fan of the Westin hotels and definitely look forward to staying there again..

We had the pleasure of staying one night at this Outstanding Resort.
We could NOT believe all the attention to detail and luxurious ammenities we found. We "oohed" and "aaahed" at each little nuance. 
The decor was like steping back in time; a time of grand elegence of a bygone era!!! It would extermely difficult to find another gem like this to stay at. Everything, everywhere was beyond par excellance!
We said it was almost like being on a cruise ship...with much more space to move around.
Our one regret is not having more time to stay and enjoy the place longer.

I have always wanted to stay in a nice hotel where they treated everyone like royalty. This hotel did just that at a reasonable price. The service was amazing. Room Service was awesome and the free breakfast and milk and cookies at bed time was great. It was within walking distance of many restaurants and Minute Maid Park. The large soaking tub in the room was the perfect way to whind down from the day. The view from the roof top pool was spectacular. I would totally stay here again and again. And i would recommend it to anyone staying in Houston for anything.

My stay at Aloft was very nice, the staff were very accomodating and the rooms were cozy. I almost felt a little pampered. The lobby area is amped up with brights colors and music and built to let in alot of natural light. The rooms have a nice walk-in shower, 42" tv and FREE wireless internet. The only thing was the room air conditioning blows onto the thermastat, causing it to kick off while the other side of the room is warmer, but that is only an inconvienence if you like it really cold. I would remmend anyone to stay here, but it would probably be more appealing to business and younger travelers.

title_masked: Clean Enough; Stay Here For Location & The Burger Bar
text_masked: For midtown hotels, Le Parker Meridien satisfies my usual requirements when traveling for business. I'm not crazy about the gym that you have to pay to use, BUT Central Park is close enough and jogging early in the morning in the park is 'ze best way to start a tiger lady's day. I also like being near Columbus Circle. Yeah, the restaurants are tasty (but pricey) BUT Whole Foods is the best way to end a day... salad bar, yo. This is a wonder to behold in and of itself. Not to mention the J Crew and Sephora for last minute clothing and beauty needs. The hotel is clean, the staff VERY friendly, the Starbucks across the street is among some of the slower services I've seen (go two blocks south or east and you'll find faster ones), but the Burger Bar is the late night, I'm-so-hungry place to grab a tasty meal.. only to run off the calories in the morning! The bar at the hotel is very lovely.. a great meeting place for a cocktail with a client. Oh, the keys are ridiculously large and you have to check it at the front desk if you want to run hands free. It's weird. But its orange so its kind of cool, I guess.

I'm not usually one to complain, however our stay at the Herbert Hotel in San Francisco went from bad to worse... Upon arrival we were checked in and given keys someone else's room... Simple mistake, however slightly alarming... The room was small, but not a major issue as we weren't planning on really spending much time there. Once settled went downstairs to be greeted by a different receptionist and asked if we could be given a second set of keys. No checking of identification just, "what room number are you in?" and just handed them over...once again level of security was alarming. 
We arranged for shared bathroom, however a little surprised that there was only 1 shower and 1 toilet shared across a whole floor (the shower smelt as if someone had been using it as a toilet)... not ideal...
We were hit with the fire alarms going off, not once, but twice throughout the evening which was extremely frustrating (both occasions advised that it was a false alarm). Wifi Access only available on the 2nd floor (which was not worth using as it was constantly glitching) however there was a cable in the room to plug in (which didn't work). 
Room was stuffy uncomfortable at night and the beds rather uncomfortable. The only real benefit was the great location. After the 2nd night we moved to a hostel around the corner for half the price and much better atmosphere. Wouldn't stay there again.

title_masked: Beautiful Rooms, beware of the top floor
text_masked:
We stayed at The Empire Hotel for one night during our honeymoon in April.
To our delight we were upgraded to a Suite in the top floor that was simply stunning, with two bathrooms, walk in wardrobe and a huge living room. We could not believe our luck. And the views on to Lincoln Centre were just the icing on the cake.
Oh, but the drawback: it was right underneath the hotel bar/club and the music did not stop banging until 3 o'clock in the morning, making it impossible for us to get any sleep (we had to get up a 4 to catch a plane). We asked for earplugs but these only blocked some of the noise.
Staff were helpful and brought us the earplugs quickly and free of charge. 
I would recommend this hotel but only if you're young and want a dance club in your room or if you can sleep in the lower floors.

title_masked: Noisy, some problems, but - good location and price
text_masked:
I stayed at this location with my husband and toddler this past week. To get to the nitty gritty (!): 
Negatives: we were given key cards that didn't work so we had to go back to the counter and get new ones (this happened two or three times during our one week stay here!), on the air conditioner unit we found someone's toe-nail clippings (yuck), and the floor felt like it wasn't vacuumed (my feet got dirty from walking barefooted). Also, this hotel was really noisy and I didn't sleep well because of it. Several nights we'd wake up during the night to people making noise in the hallway. In the mornings, house-keeping would start knocking on doors and in a loud voice announce "HOUSEKEEPING!" (I honestly thought at first it was someone pulling a prank on someone, but we checked and it was the actual housekeeping staff doing this) - what's worse is that this would be heard at 7am!! Much too early in my opinion. Finally, we had a city-view room and because the hotel is so close to the highway we heard a lot of traffic noise.
Positives: room has free WIFI, mini-fridge, microwave and a safe. Hotel has pool on-site which is a must in that heat! (It was 104 F when we visited!) It's nice they offer free breakfast, although it consists only of bagels, muffins, and apples, and several times when we went downstairs (around 9am) the breakfast food was already gone. The location is within walking distance to the Alamo and downtown Riverwalk which is great. Parking fee here is less than hotels in the area, which is another benefit.

This is a second review following another stay at the Hilton. I don't often re-review, but I felt like my last visit was substantially more impressive than the previous one. My room was spacious enough and very clean. I found the staff to be very courteous and helpful. The internet worked admirably. Maybe as much as anything, I used the hotel to its strengths.... I came into the airport late, stayed the night, and left the next day out of O'Hare. It was quite convenient and made for a painless 24-hour trip into Chicago.

After a slow check-in the staff were very friendly and always eager to help. The restaurant staff were fantastic - we showed up 30 minutes before opening but they allowed us in and immediately served us! The food was great and moderately priced. Bathrooms in the rooms could use some updating, but overall rooms were comfortable. The two shuttle drivers, Walter and Charles, were so friendly and went out of their way to make sure we got to where we needed to be on time. Special thanks to Walter - you went above and beyond - You Rock!

title_masked: A hotel with a heart in the heart of the city
text_masked: It's located at the corner of Union Square, the cable cars run up and down Powell Street passing its fron door, there is a stop just outside. The reception staff were all most helpful, good fun and yet very efficient. they seemed to be in no hurry and yet there was no delay in processing our bookings/requests. They took the trouble to tell us waht was available...internet, teas/coffee/cookies 24 hours etc. The room was perfect and looked out on the cablecar route. The room had a safe....a great facility and it was free (unlike many European sun destinations). The hotel is within walking distance of great shopping centres (Macy's of course, but Ross is worth a look...very good value and Urban for great shop design). There are art galleries and museums and urban parks nearby. At weekends there is a great art exhibition in the square (they can sell but can't take money in the square...you must walk with the artist a few paces away...a weird law!). A trumpeter played marvellous jazz in the early evening and there are buskers aplenty. The drummers using everything but drums are wonderfu. Two streets down on O'Farrell street Johnny Foley's pub is well worth a visit. the service is first class, the food is wonderful and best value in toen, bands play at weekends but the real gem is the duelling piano bar dwon stairs . we were mesmerised by the two pianists we heard and you can put bread in the jar if you want a request played...you can also dance...we did..couldn't resist!. It was like returning home each night as we went back to the Chancellor. Well done all! Oh Friday lunch at $5! AMazing value.

title_masked: Nice place, but the pool makes it.
text_masked: A well located, nice, clean hotel. The decor is sharp. The thing that makes this a perfect place to stay in DC is the pool. It is a great get-away from the city and is very well maintained. There are plenty of chaises to relax on and there is a friendly service staff to bring you a cocktail or lunch by the pool. The only complaint is a minor one - the water doesn't flow so well from the shower and even though we brought it to the hotel's attention, there probably isn't much they could do about it. We had a blast at the Washington Plaza and would totally go back.

title_masked: Cleanest Inn you could hope for!
text_masked:
This was our first trip to this area and we consider ourselves fortunate to have stayed at this lovely Inn. It was a real treat to enter the building and not smell tobacco or "piped in room fresheners" or oil plug-ins which some Inns have started to use.
It is a very attractive building both inside and outside. There is a lovely garden area in the front. To the side of the lobby is an area where they provide a delightful self-help breakfast consisting of juices, coffee, tea, cereals, waffle-making, hard cooked eggs (a nice touch), pastries, etc.
The rooms (my brother and his wife had a suite) while we had two double beds. Both rooms were ultra clean and had a small refrigerator, microwave, coffee and tea set-ups. The shower/toilet room had a wonderful shower head with various settings. Off the entrance hall to the room was a large mirrored countertop with sink, hair dryer and a very generous assortment of supplies of shampoos, conditioners, body lotions, shower caps, etc.
We always appreciate a window that can be opened and this hotel had such windows which we did not need to use. Some hotel rooms could use windows to air them but there was no "typical hotel/motel stale odor" masked with sprays...the room was clean smelling without trying to use "chemicals" because it was clean.
We were in contact with several front desk employees during our two day stay and all were extremely friendly and helpful.
The price was a special two-night offer and was very attractive. Loved the fact that there are all kinds of stores nearby and fast food restaurants, pizza, etc. We did not look for any full service restaurants because we were there for a wedding but feel sure there are many in the area.
There are amenities which we did not use such as exercise equipment, pool but others might like those.
You will not go wrong in selecting this Inn.

I've stayed in a few Embassy Suites across the country and I would say that this one is right on par with the others and with what you would expect from a family-friendly hotel. The staff was excellent and super friendly (special shout out to Dwayne, the bellman, who spoke to us every single time we passed him). We stayed July 4 - 7 and there was some sort of Irish Dance competition going on. We spent a lot of time on Thursday and Friday waiting for elevators that weren't full by the time they reached us on the 12th floor. Our room was average and clean, but the pillows completely suck and gave me the worst neck ache. We went for the manager's reception the first night and after waiting 20 minutes in line for a drink...decided it wasn't worth it and hit up Dominick's across the street so we could just make our own cocktails in the room. Overall, this is an average hotel with friendly staff and a great location, but prepare to wait for elevators, drinks and breakfast during busier time periods.

I had been staying at Kierland for the past few years and can't believe I overlooked this gem. Last year I was invited to spend 2 days here with family & friends on our way to Sedona. This time I sneaked off on my own for some well-deserved R&R and chose the JWM as my travel destination! From the moment I arrived, I felt relaxed, welcomed and appreciated as a guest. The grounds are breathtaking with manicured landscaping, desert botanical gardens, and miles of walking paths. The abundant wildlife iincludes hummingbirds, jack rabbits, hawks, owls and bats! There's an active pool scene ideal for families and a serene spa pool perfect for discerning adults. The pools, by the way, are sparkling clean, crystal-clear.
But even more important are the high levels of customer service demonstrated by the staff. I have never been surrounded by so many dedicated employees who clearly love what they do -- making their guests happy. To those who cared for me last Memorial Day Weekend (especially Sandra and LeFayne at the Blue Sage Restaurant) -- thank you again and see you soon!

I have stayed at the Hotel Sax a few times and each time I have gotten a great rate on a good room. The beds are comfortable, the sheets are nice, and the room is clean and comfortable. The staff is pleasant and accommodating. The room service was prompt and the breakfast was average. Free coffee in the lobby in the morning was nice. In the shower they offer shower gel, shampoo and conditioner in large shared pump bottles, this I was not crazy about and I have not seen it in another hotel. All in all I would say if you can get it for a good price, this is a nice hotel, it looks just like the pictures, the decor is interesting and there is basically nothing wrong with it.

We just returned from our trip to Chicago visiting our son. He had recently moved to Lincoln Park and we wanted a hotel close to his new apartment. We normally stay on the Magnificant Mile in a chain hotel. Before I booked our room at The Willow, I read the reviews and was impressed with the comments. I completely agree, the entire staff was so friendly and helpful, especially Ricky and Adriain! The Willow is a quaint, clean, neighborhood hotel and I would recommend it to anyone who is looking to save a little money, and be in the heart of shopping and restaruants. It may not be fancy like some of the other chain hotels, but the staff and the accommodations are worth it!
Lisa Z.

title_masked: Nice enough in the cetre of Philadelphia
text_masked: The hotel's central location made it extremely convenient for exploring central Philadelphia. The room was nice enough, however I felt the bathroom could've been in a bit of a better state overall. Would recommend for a short stay.

I have stayed in other hotels in San Francisco but this was by far the most luxurious, however this comes at a cost, although this time the business was paying which made it more acceptable!
The hotel is literally situated at the top of the main part of the bay area. Some of the rooms have stunning views over the city especially higher up, but of course these tend to be more expensive. The hotel is well positioned for all the major sites and the transport network; the famous cable-car stops right outside the door.
The rooms are well apportioned and the daily service was excellent. 
As is the trend nowadays almost everything additional came with a charge, and as one would expect with the surroundings at a premium; Breakfast = $30, 3 drinks at the bar =$30, WIfi = $17/day etc. My advice is within a 15 minute radius of the hotel you can be sitting in one of hundreds of bars, cafes, restaurants etc all serving great food and drinks at a cheaper rate with guaranteed free WiFI access.
In summary if you can afford it, or someone else is paying, then this is a great hotel, if you are stopping on a tighter budget and/or the hotel is just a place to rest your head while visiting this great city then you are probably best being somewhere else.

Just one night so could manage. But a great price! Halls are dark and weird. Rooms are a shoe box for real. Bathrooms are okay, new. BUT things are not clean! Just vacuum and dust. Housekeeping needs to step it up. Yes, some floors are rehabbing but our whole floor was due. Clean up well, and will put up with small rooms. TV nice but only on HD channels? No coffee in room....no place to put...All things could be better...

I just had a wonderful (far too brief) stay at this property last weekend. I used the Hotel Tonight app to book my room, which saved me about $150 off the list price of the room, which still did not make it cheap. But what a worthy splurge! My last-minute reservation hadn't reached the front desk by the time I physically arrived at the hotel, and three apologetic staffers worked in concert to address the situation. Given that I was definitely there on the cheap (compared to the other guests), it was nice to *not* feel like a second class citizen. In fact, this was the place where the minute they learned your name, you were addressed by it the remainder of your time there.
The public spaces are largely done in black white and gray, often with similar toned patterns and textures. The effect is classically elegant, with a slightly modern, very sophisticated look. This decor is carried through to my room. 
Room 809 was a grand deluxe salon, with an open northern view showing the backs of the Fifth Ave buildings, the down on the roofs and facades of the adjacent townhouses and over to the Carlyle Hotel Tower. Nice as the view was, the room was so well designed and appointed, you didn't immediately want to look outside. Everything was top of the line, luxurious and well thought out. You did not want for any creature comfort or amenity. Fabulous bed and bedding. Multiple chairs for reading. A marble wet bar. A work desk. All in one open room. The marble bathroom with inlaid mosaic tiling and glass shower (no tub, for those who are curious) was an extra delight. The rain forest shower head almost had too much pressure for me. When have you ever heard that in a hotel review? Turn down at night included dim lights, music, bottled water, slippers and an individually-wrapped sweet. How chic!
The location puts you in the heart of museums, galleries, restaurants and very close to both Central Park and the 77th st stop of the 6 train. Perhaps not the best for those looking for immediate Times Sq./Rockefeller Center type tourist activities, but I don't think that's the demographic for this property.
All in all, major thumbs up. Well worth it.

Stayed here due to UTEP football game/Minerpalooza pep rally for two nights. We live near El Paso and staying here is more convenient than driving and finding game parking. Only about a 15 minute walk to the stadium. My family has stayed here in the past and we have always enjoyed our visits. I reserved way back in February knowing the place usually sells out and my rate was only $89.00.
The lobby was a hub of activity for the football game vs. Oklahoma that weekend. This is literally the closest hotel to UTEP...right next to the student union parking lot. We like the lobby...hotel restaurant/bar is right next to the check in desk. We have had meals here in the past and have enjoyed nice lunches during the week.. The hotel has a nice little breakfast buffet which is very good compared to other hotel continental breakfasts. You pay for this one ($11.95), but it includes so much (standard fare: eggs, bacon, sausage, pancakes, waffles, etc.), but they will also make to order eggs and omelettes. Additionally you can order from a menu. Good service.
This hotel is very close to a large bar/restaurant area of El Paso...everything from fast food to higher end restaurants are within walking distance. Starbucks, Whataburger, Taco Bell, and McDonalds are about five minutes away as well as the campus Jamba Juice and other campus food venues.
The check in was easy and no problem. We had an upper level room. Rooms are nicely decorated with a large flat screen TV, microwave, and fridge included. Toilet/bath area are both separated from sleepign area. Air conditioning worked great, especially on a hot weekend it was appreciated. Room was clean overall and very quiet.
The pool/hot tub is standard but out ot towners must be careful b/c El Paso is at altitude and the sun cooks you faster here, as I'm sure some OK fans found out who stayed at the pool all day.
The only wear I could see was in the hallways...carpets are showing a little age. The hallways are really wide.

title_masked: Good value in sold out NYC
text_masked: I stayed one night here during the past week for work. All of the city seemed like it was sold out and the hotel rooms that were available were astronomical in price -- except for Hotel Mela. I was a little nervous because it was more reasonably priced than the other rooms I was seeing as available but I wasn't let down. Upon arriving in the hotel you enter a small but clean lobby. I arrived before check-in time and my bags were held until later that night. Check-in process when I returned was very efficient and my bag was promptly delivered to my room. My room was small but very, very clean and quiet. The bathroom was small with a shower stall but bright and well-designed with nice toiletries. The room had free WiFi, a desk and a flat-screen TV. I also had both dinner and breakfast in the hotel's restaurant (Saju Bistro) and both meals were very good and very reasonably priced for a hotel restaurant. Lastly, the entire hotel is smoke-free which is a huge plus for me. I will most certainly stay here again on my travels to NYC and will recommend it to others.

The hotel was beautiful, the staff was amazingly nice and to top it all off, They had Cookies! 
Honestly one of the best stay's I've ever had at a hotel ever. I would recommend them for anyone looking for great customer service with their stay. 
They hosted our convention with professionalism and a knack for being able to provide anything we needed. I can't say enough about the staff. Curteous, friendly and just fun to be around. 
I can't wait for next year to go back. 
Nashan

title_masked: Bigger rooms for just a little more
text_masked:
Nice to have all the comforts of home if you plan extended stays anywhere try the Homewood Suites by Hilton brand. (Don't forget to use your hilton honors points!) 
 I just stayed one night for business mtg. But this would be great for family vacations as it has 2 rooms (kitchen, table,chairs,microwave,fridge,sofa,lounge chair, TV other room has bed,computer table,chair, TV,clothes closet,bathroom sink separate from bathroom.
 It was all clean except for the computer chair that needed stains removed or reupholstered, it was bad enough that I laid a towel over it to sit on while using the computer, I left a note about it also.
Good hot breakfast, sausage, eggs, juice, coffee, etc.
Nearby restaurant/bar (try Redneck Heaven not for kids, with kids try Texas Roadhouse next door)

title_masked: Great if no group events are planned.
text_masked: The rooms are very well kept and clean. Staff is good. We had our school reunion this past weekend. The buffet service for dinner was very unorganized and so unprofessional. The food display was also very amateur. Everyone was bumping into each other...total chaos. The pricey breakfast buffet was good but again lacked organization. We did have issues with the bills...one had a gratuity charge of $28 but the bill was only $16 :/.

title_masked: The Algonquin - What's New & What's Changed? Plenty!
text_masked:
My prior review of the Algonquin was just before renovations, and this June 1, 2012 stay was during the first week of the Algonquin's re-opening. I'll discuss what's new at the hotel and the improvements and other hints along the way.
The hotel has transformed it's appearance to bright and colorful Marriott decor that works well with the Algonquin's historic charm and old oak panelled walls. The changes are especially apparent on each guest floor with updated amenities including L'Occitane lemon verbena bath products, flat screen televisions, new bedding & mattresses and large scale historic photographic lit-panels above the beds. The business and fitness centers has also transformed into workable spaces that are comfortably functional for your routines of work & play.
The lobby remains the best in New York with its rich oak, style and grace. The cocktails in both the lobby and newly expended Blue Bar are high but one sip in this setting and you won't mind.
Dining at the Alginquin is no ordinary hotel restaurant, meals are sumptuous and service is impeccable. I recommend the Roundtable Restaurant for breakfast and dinner. If you - like I - would like to sit at the roundtable, make reservations in advance. Note that faous table has shrunk in sized over the years from 12 to 10 and now seats 8. Save room and plan to share the oversized desserts with loved ones. Marriott Elites will also appreciate the new concierge lounge, but it came at the expense of the Oak Room which helped launch the careers of many musicians.
A few final notes, if you must drive into NYC, parking here is just $35 across the street with hotel validation - a steal for Midtown. The Algonquin is extremely child-friendly especially for well-mannered children. They will appreciate Matilda, the feline in residence and the enthusiastic staff throughout the hotel property. The hotel staff's enthusiasm is contagious.
If you can get a room here at the new Algonquin, book it and enjoy the historical first-class Algonquin.

If you are traveling for business or pleasure and want to make an incredible impression with your travel partner or business associates I highly recommend room 1513 in the Affinia Shelburne...
When I opened the door to my room, I was in awe... My room was an incredible one bedroom suite with a full living room, full dinning room (for six or 8), a wet bar/mini-kitchen, and balcony with the space for at least 15 people with views of the Empire State Building and the city at large...
Above my room was a hot little roof top bar/lounge, called [NAME], which was accessible via the stairs, so there was no need to wait for the elevator. (This is an important detail since Rare View is a bit of a hot spot when the weather is cooperating.)
I met some friends at Rare View and loved the drink menu, the service and the spectacular view... Plus the convenience of having my suite located directly beneath me made me feel like a bit of a VIP.
If you need to entertain for business or pleasure I cannot think of a better more understated hotel suite to do it in. The hotel and my room seem like they were completely renovated and everything was clean and well maintained. The bed was really comfortable and the amount of space I had at my disposal was quite shocking... I don't even think I went into my living room...
When, and if, I move back to New York City I hope I can find a place this nice... The staff was incredibly warm and welcoming and I even found a complementary bottle of Napa Valley Cabernet waiting for me in my room when I checked in. 
This was my first experience with the Affinia brand and they have set the bar extremely high.
My only regret... My stay was only one night...

We spent a few days here in October and judging by the amount of flight crews staying there it was quite a popular hotel. The rooms were clean and the staff were helpful, even though it's a bit out of town we used the shuttles to get to the metro which was very handy. Would happily stay again.

title_masked: Great Room, Quiet, and close to everything in Downtown Austin
text_masked:
I was in town for a business meeting and only stayed one night. I had booked the reservation that the Marriott Courtyard, which is in the same building as the Residence Inn. For whatever reason, I was given a larger room in the Residence Inn.
The room (403) was a large "L" shaped room with a full kitchen (range, microwave, large refrigerator, dishwasher) a table for meals as well as a large work desk with free internet, There was a full size sofa and a king sized bed. 
The hotel is across the street from the convention center. The room included a free full breakfast buffet in the hotel restaurant (Champions Sports Bar). 
For those interested in the local music and night life, you are just two blocks from 6th Street, the live music capital of Texas.
I highly recommend this hotel.

Have stayed there quite a few times in the last couple of years.
The place need modernising throughout.
The rooms still have old tube TV's!
The bar & restaurant are both old & uncomfortable.
Very noisy at night due to the railroad, which although some distance away, the train horns carry on all night!

We stayed here this last weekend ( and have stay here a few times before ) and as always the staff .... very friendly and helpful. The rooms are nice and very clean. Also its very close to the freeway , which helps. Will continue to stay here when we are in the area

You couldn't sleep closer to Obama unless you were a guest in the Lincoln Bedroom - amazing location adjacent to the White House and near all of downtown DC. Very stylish hotel with accomodating staff. 
Rooms are dark, which is part of the style, but a bit annoying. Plenty of amenities in room. This is not a hotel for sleeping - doors slam, people party, ice machines used constantly, many rooms so close to elevator that you can hear it boinging all night. I had earplugs in and still was woken up several times a night for all nights I stayed.
Food was delicious, and rooftop bar is a must for an early (4-5 pm) drink - gets chaotic in the evening.
Have to scale the "velvet rope" to get to your room weekend nights.
Everything is astronomically expensive.

The hotel is very nice. The rooms were recently updated. The only comment I have is I hate when a hotel renovates their rooms but doesn't redo the bathroom floor or the shower, just seems like such a waste. Location was awesome, right in the middle of the action and steps away from the outdoor mall. We had breakfast at Sam's #3, best breakfast I've had in my life you have to order the green chili! Go on a weekday, not the weekend or you'll end up waiting for at least an hour. Second best breakfast I ever had was right next door at Le Grande Bistro and Oyster bar on 1th and Curtis. Had great burgers at Earl's on 16th street and the atmosphere was very nice too. I would definately stay here again.
I had a great stay at the Hawthorne in San Antonio. I would recommend the same to anyone. Would definately stay again next trip.

Just returned from a 4 night stay at the Millenium Hilton (July 11-15). We booked through hotwire and got an excellent deal. Our room was very clean and the beds (2 doubles) were really comfortable! The room was very quiet at night and we rarely heard any noise in the hallway. The location was so convenient because there were many subways close. We could get anywhere by subway conveniently and cabs were readily available in case we wanted to get somewhere in a hurry. 
My only criticism is that the cost of internet is very high (15$ per day, per device). The fact that you have to pay per device is ridiculous in my opinion but maybe it's the standard in NYC.
We really enjoyed our stay and would definitely return.

They sure spent a LOT of money on the renovations! Everything inside the hotel is completely brand new! We stayed at the Latham this past weekend and were totally blown away by the complete make-over of the building itself and the service. Everyone we interacted with was so genuinely polite and eager to exceed expectations. The best part about the "New Latham" was the crazy luxurious Audi A8 that dropped us off and picked us up from the Art Museum. The best part about the car?? It's available to all guests!
We will definitely be staying here again. The service and the new rooms were incredible!!

We stayed at the Helmsley Park Lane recently for a getaway weekend just before Valentine's Day. Excellent location directly across from the park, easy walking distance to Times Square, MoMa, the Natural History Museum, and very close to the subway. We got hit up by the pedicab and hansom cab drivers every time we walked out the door, but they were easy to say 'no thank you' to. We booked a Junior Suite and when we checked in, found we had been upgraded to an Executive Suite on the 43rd floor. We had a view of the city, the park, and could see the river - in addition, we had 2 full bathrooms and more room than I've ever had in a NYC hotel. The room (really, rooms - 2 adjoining, 4310 & 4311) was gorgeous but now I'm spoiled. :) We walked everywhere, from Times Square down to the Penn Station area and back. Our room came with the buffet breakfast, and it was very nice to do room service. They bring a very nice table to your room and set everything up. Hotel breakfast is expensive if you don't have a package, but there's a little place around the corner on 6th (Angela's Rock & Roll Deli) that has a no-frills $6 breakfast and a few tables to sit down at if you just want something quick & inexpensive. 
Bed was very comfortable, and the showers were great - lots of hot water and good water pressure. This is definitely a hotel we will come back to.

I must admit up front that I was totally surprised to stay at one of the highest rated TripAdvisor hotels in DC and have such a horrible experience. If you have stayed at other 4.5 star TripAdvisor hotels, you will surely be disappointed in this one. If not for having mice in our room(s), I would still have only rated this hotel 2 bubbles. 
There are 4 main reasons why you should not book this hotel:
 1) Live mice in the rooms
 2) Street noise (the rooms on the outside of the hotel)
 3) Way overpriced for what you get
 4) Staff is average and not what you expect at this price
I try to be fair in my reviews and give the good and bad points equal time. However I need to make an exception and focus first on one of the worst things about this hotel -- they have a BAD problem with mice. I would like to spare you the pain of discovering this for yourself and advise you to book elsewhere. 
MOUSE PROBLEMS
Upon check-in late on a Sunday evening, we were informed that we had been upgraded to a Robert Mills Suite on the second floor. This sounded nice, except that the second floor is actually at the same level as the street. So when we walked into the room, there were street lights at eye level and lots of street noise as well. The room looked somewhat nice, although it was clearly tired from lots of use. 
Our biggest problem started as we began to make up the sofabed for our kids to sleep in. I always check under the sheets in hotels for signs of bedbugs, and this looked OK. Unfortunately there was mice feces under the sheets and on the bed. See my attached photo as evidence. 
We had to split up our family of 4 into 2 separate rooms on floor 1 (which is the basement) to sleep that night. No signs of mice that I could see in those rooms at that point. Although I did not know where to look at that time. 
We were given a different Robert Mills suite at the other end of the building for the next night. On the third night I awoke to the sound of a high pitched squeak. It was dark and I did not want to wake my wife, although it sounded like it was coming from the walls. In the morning while the family was in the bathroom getting ready, I found the source of the noise (my kids were asking about it as they packed up and I had to lie to them and say it was a bird in the walls). 
Behind the TV console was placed a rodent glue trap. You can guess what was inside of it and making noise. I took some photos of the trap and attached to the review so you can see where to look behind the cabinet. You can even see the back part of the mouse sticking out from the trap. 
We packed up immediately and went down the street to the W Hotel and finished our vacation there. The front desk apologized over and over of course, and they were very generous to zero out our bill. They even picked up the tab for our final 2 nights at a hotel down the street. They tried to make it right, but the damage was done at that point. 
We had problems with mice in 2 different rooms on 2 different sides of the building. There was a glue trap in the room. Need I say more to prove that there is a bad mouse problem at this hotel? Don't take your family here, please. 
STREET NOISE
If you happen to get a room on the outside of the hotel, you will hear a lot of street noise all night long. There is nothing the hotel can really do about that, but please be aware that this is something you might have to deal with. It is not faint, it is loud and it goes all night. 
WAY OVERPRICED
The hotel has great marketing and sells itself as a "boutique" hotel. This is just a way to make you think that paying a lot of money is worth it. It is not in this case. The rooms are undersized, the beds are not that great, and the decor is worn and tired. The bathrooms in our suite however were nicely done and clean. 
The only thing worth paying for is the location. I found the location in Penn Quarter to be great. It was walking distance to everything, there was a great restaurant selection everywhere, and there was never a moment I felt unsafe walking around with out kids at night. 
STAFF
I found the front desk staff to be under-trained and very mechanical. At this price level, I expected to be welcomed and taken care of by a more professional staff. Don't get me wrong, it wasn't bad service. It was perfectly acceptable for a Hampton Inn, but it was not at the level of what you would expect at a highly priced hotel. 
FINAL NOTES
The front desk will say that they did not know about the traps which may be true, but between the cleaning crew and the extermination company someone had to know and someone had to approve this. Hotel staff and management definitely know that there is a mouse problem. 
If a hotel has a mouse problem that is so out of control it requires traps in the room, then there should not be people in that room or in that hotel until the problem has been resolved. If you decide to stay here, the first thing to do is look behind the TV console and check for a glue trap at least. I suspect they will have removed them after our stay and after this review gets posted. I beg you not to stay at this hotel until their mouse problem is resolved. There is no way this hotel should be in the top 15 DC hotels even without a mouse problem.

title_masked: I would return to the Silversmith
text_masked:
We stayed at the Silversmith for 2 nights on our way across the USA by train. We were able to walk from Union Station and it was perfect for what we wanted. I would recommend it for people who want to be reasonably central and close to the El. The hotel is also an easy walk to sights on the lake-front.
Millers Pub is just down the street and is great for dinner. Also another pub with food (I've forgotten its name) further down the street.

title_masked: Campus location but no food or bar
text_masked: There is a nice cold breakfast but that is all the food here. Bring your own teabags because there are only flavored teas at breakfast. You are not near any restaurants although Westwood restaurants will deliver to the hotel. One vending machine has cookies & chips. The soda machine was broken. The free campus shuttle stops here but does not run on weekends. The beds are comfortable and the decorations were nice.

title_masked: Nice but lacking in customer service.
text_masked: The rooms are very nice in this motel, however the shuttle service takes way too long. I called several times for a pickup and they didn't even answer the phone. Also, the refrigerator in my room froze everything I had in it. The controls were on the back and it was a built in unit so I had to call maintenance. They sent someone up to turn it down, but they did not offer to replace all of the items that froze. I was out the money for a six pack of pop plus various other items I had in the refrigerator. I would think twice about staying in this motel again.

title_masked: Really accommodating Staff; typical excellent Marriott
text_masked:
This Marriott had the expected great customer service from check-in, through your stay, to check-out. Rooms were clean, comfortable and quiet. Fluffy towels, soft pillows, quality beds and bedding, all as we have come to expect from Marriott. 
Bar on second floor was nice. Loved the Starbucks in the lobby. This hotel is directly across Fannin Street from the entrance to Methodist Hospital and is convenient for that whole medical and academic area.

title_masked: Not rushing back, would stay in same area though.
text_masked: Poor front desk staff, clean rooms great location for our needs. Jr suite poor air circulation making bedroom hot and front room cold. Door didn't work well to enter room requiring two hands and foot to open. No window coverings on door divider making entire room dark when kids went down. Reason for getting upgraded room was to allow adults space while kids slept. Didn't work out well. This is our second time here and not as good as the first. Think we will try someone else next time.

Good location. Convenient to freeways and Universal City Walk and Universal Studios. There is a free tram to the above locations that is supposed to run every 10-15 minutes but is solely based on the driver schedule for breaks and meals so you may wait up to 45 minutes like we did. The hotel staff is not upfront about possible delays. They state that they don't control the transportation so they are not responsible for the timing-very poor attitude.

The description on the website did not match what we found upon arrival. The door to the lobby was dirty on both sides...mind you, not just a little dirty, but filthy. The lobby smelled of urine and the hallway to our room smelled bad and when we got to our non-smoking room, it reeked of smoke especially the bathroom. The bathroom floor and the furniture in the room was very sticky. We reserved the room at the Park & Stay Rate so we could leave our car parked there as we traveled to see our son graduate basic training. We were asked to fill out a paper saying what flight, airline and time of arrival to the Charlotte Airport so we could be picked up. We arrived early andI called the hotel to inform them. The lady at the front desk said the van was on it way. He did not arrive for almost an hour. It took us 10 minutes to get to the airport when we left the hotel. We were waiting outside all that time. All in all I would not stay there again.

I stayed at the Pearl for 3 nights and had an excellent stay. I was by myself but for some reason was upgraded to a room with 2 double beds. It was a spacious room with a large bathroom. There was no tub but that's normal in New York and the shower was roomy. The room was clean and in good shape. It was also quiet.
Staff was very friendly and I was happy to share the chocolate dipped strawberries my wife had sent for Valentine's Day. The included breakfast was not overwhelming but was completely fine and satisfying.
The gym is quite small. It's very clean and in good order and bright. But there's not any room to lie on the floor or stretch. The equipment was all in good shape.
The location is great. It's close to Times Square if you like that sort of thing but not too close to it if you don't.
The free wi-fi was a huge plus.
I would definitely stay here again.

title_masked: Great Hotel...Very Busy with the combination of Weddings, Corporate, and Local Spa Members
text_masked: Nice hotel, Pricey, Great Food, Room service was a issue late nite. We needed to eat and ordered, the food did not come for 2 hrs. Front desk had no problem removing the charge from my bill.A great perk is if you need to travel within 12 miles of the hotel, the complimentary shuttle will be there .

This hotel will not be for everyone. If you are looking for a hotel in downtown Dallas, or one in a nice neighborhood with walking paths and scenic views, or a newer facility with nice pools and amenities - don't stay here. 
On the other hand, if you are attending events in the Market Center area (and don't want to pay the price of a room at the swanky Hilton Anatole), or looking for a good hotel rate near downtown, or looking mostly for a quiet room and friendly service, this Doubletree will fit the bill. Yes, it's an older property but they've updated the common areas since my last visit a few years ago. The breakfast room was attractive and comfortable and the food was surprisingly good with cook to order meals plus a plentiful buffet area. My hotel room and bathroom were on the smaller side but adequate and, importantly, the king bed was very comfortable (a key feature of Doubletrees and much more important to me than a chocolate chip cookie).
On my first night at the hotel (of a 2 night stay) the power went out at 9 pm. Turned out that it was a black out covering half of the Market Center area that lasted a couple of hours. A bit frustrating but not the hotel's fault. All in all, would I stay here again? Sure. Not a destination hotel, but a good choice when the room rate is attractive.

I have been staying at the Staybridge Suites over the years on business trips. The rooms are quite large, with a couch and full-size refrigerator and full-size microwave as well. Staff is always friendly, they have a nice spread for breakfast as well as complimentary social snacks four nights a week. Great place to stay!

We were notified by the personnel that the phone in our room was not working. The person notified by the desk clerk showed up in about fifteen minutes to let us see the room to decide if we wanted to stay even without the phone. It was a large room with a comfortable bed. BUT once our luggage was in and we were settling down we noticed that there was an iron but no ironing board, the toilet paper roll was quite small and there was no extra roll, there was a coffeemaker and no cups or coffee, no lotion. The TV worked fine but there was no listing of stations.

This embassy suites is newer and super nice- but has no Columbus flavor- it could be sitting in any town. If you are visiting the area for site seeing and want to get a feel for the area, do not stay here. There are plenty of good choices in way more interesting spots. However, for the night before the airport, or a place to sleep- really great, very comfortable beds. The hotel does not allow any outside food to be eaten anywhere in there lobby or pool, makes it hard when you have a large group. Our group of 5 families had to cram into one room after we ordered pizza and they would not allow us to have it in the lobby. We will not choose this one again for our base for Columbus crew games- Again, if this does not concern you it is nice and the people were pleasant, plan on long lines for free happy hour.

This hotel is in a great location, about a 5 block walk to Times Square. I was upgraded to a corner room on the 26th floor. The room was huge but the was one problem the bathroom was so small you really only had room for 1.5 people. The toilet was very close to the shower door, so you had to turn sideways to let a person get in and out of the shower. The closet was huge, had radio with ipod connection, 32" flat screen tv, mood lighting and actual windows that opened. I paid about $300/night which is pretty good for a downtown hotel but still a little pricey for this hotel. I would stay here again if I got a better rate. I am a Hyatt Passport Platinum member and this hotel is pretty average to some of the Grand & Park Hyatts I have stayed at around the world.

Although I was here for a conference, every time I walked by the lobby windows overlooking the pool area I felt like I was on vacation instead. The rooms were nicely appointed, recently decorated. Clean, good lighting. Complimentary wi-fi in the lobby. Balcony with a magnificent view of the harbor; many rooms face the water. Husband enjoyed good food at the pool area while I worked. Dinner at the restaurant/bar was also good. Parking was accessible, if not inexpensive. Friendly and helpful staff. Colleagues used the on-site business center and found personnel to be helpful and efficient. Excellent location, close to restaurants and entertainment. Our room had two balconies and we kept the patio doors open, and the nearby trolley was a bit noisy during the night. Nevertheless, the location and view were wonderful and would definitely recommend this hotel.

title_masked: Fantastic Service by Hilton Palacio Del Rio Employee Esmeralda
text_masked:
Last week I had the pleasure of staying at the Hilton Palacio Del Rio. I was very pleased with the accommodations and the services provided by all of the employees. Upon returning home I discovered that set of car keys were missing. After searching everywhere I recalled that I left them with the valet attendant. I immediately called and the hotel and was connected to Esmeralda in Loss Prevention. After relating my story to her she agreed to call me back. Within minutes Esmeralda called me back and asked me for a detailed description of the items on my key ring. After providing her with the correct information she agreed to send the keys back to me free of charge. Esmeralda acted in a very professional manner and caused me to feel confident that the matter would be handled properly. Esmeralda is definitely an asset to Hilton company and should be commended for the way she performs her duties and interacts with the public. 
Michael Martin
Louisiana
We had a great stay at the St. Anthony. It is truly a historic hotel with some updates. We were lucky to have a large room. I understand from some others that their quarters were very small.

This place does not honor 'late arrival reservation'! I arrived late in Charlotte with a reservation from my corporate travel agency Carlson Travel. Upon arrival at 1:30 AM, the front desk tells me that they have completely sold out, and they don't have a room for me. All they can do is to get me a room at the Drury Inn a mile away. They called a cab that is supposed to get me over there. But after 30 minutes of waiting (apparently Charlotte doesn't have enough taxi cabs operating this time of the night, or morning), I asked the clerk to call Drury Inn, which she did. She found out that the Drury Inn does not have any room available either.
I won't bore you with anymore of my terrible experience. I just cannot believe that Marriott, being a well known hospitality company, can hang a customer out to dry like that. And in the middle of the night! What would you do if you were me?

I have wanted to stay at this hotel for a long time. When I saw the great deals in January, I could not pass it up. I have stayed in a lot of NY hotels and the service here is outstanding. I think that I was greated by 6 different people before I ever reached the front desk. The lobby area is quite grand and beautiful. The rooms were much more bland than I had imagined. I have stayed at much cheaper hotels that have much better rooms (ie The W). Despite having old and dated rooms, the beds were quite comfortable. I had a good nights rest, no issues with noise. There is a nice lobby bar as well as another attached on the east side of the building (Bull and Bear I think). My husband and I enjoyed 5 cocktails and our bill was more than $100. Steep even for NYC. All in all, would I stay here again? No. But I did check a box off of my Bucket List - so it was worth it in that regard.

Beautiful hotel in central area. but thats only one of two positive things I can say about the hotel. Once we checked in, we were suprised by the reception that there will not be functioning bathrooms in the WHOLE hotel till 4:30am due to "unforseen circumstences". they offered us bottles of water, which didn't make sense since water makes you want to go to the bathroom, which you can't flush. So that 4:30am in actuallity turned out to be 6am. Next night, as we walk into the hotel before taking an elevator to the room, we decided to jokingly check with the front desk about water. To our surprise, that joke turned out to be true as we were told 4:30am once again. so when we decided to use the same bathroom in the basement, we were greeted there by the staff saying BATHROOMS ARE CLOSED AND SOME FLOATING WASTE IN EVERY SINGLE STALL. And on top of our outrage, the same front desk person, either in attempt an appeasing us or adding insult to injury, offered more bottled water. the only way he was spared is that the security/police officer opened staff restroom to us. apperently they had working toilets. NO ONE THROUGHOUT THE WHOLE STAY OFFERED TO COMP US IN ANY WAY. Next move is to call the credit card. Given the fact it was 2 nights, not one, it leads me to believe that this was a preamptive repair, which wasn't related to us when booking the hotel on their own website. As for the only other positive aspect of the hotel, was the daytime front desk young lady from Ohio, who was uber polite and helpful when she was helping us store things in the hotel safe room.

Great location near airport, and fantastic shuttle to take you around Manhatten Beach whilst you wait for your place. Concierge were quite helpful. Nice hotel with nice pool area. 
Only disappointment with this hotel was I left an item behind in the room, and despite 2 phone calls to Lost and Found, and 2 follow up emails (the email listed on the website doesnt seem to work) no one has bothered to reply and let me know anything about the missing item, even though the staff member took my details each time. 
Disappointing way to end a nice holiday.

We recently stayed for the first time at the Hotel Sofitel in Beverly Hills for 26 nights due to my surgery at Cedars-Sinai Hospital, which is nearby. I have read a lot of the reviews here and wanted to share our thoughts on Sofitel from January & February, 2012. First, the hotel is also a first, as in first class and we were very satisfied with the two rooms that we were in. Clean, comfortable, very quite and nice. We stayed on the 7th floor and then moved to a handicap room on the 4th. The complete staff from the valet, doorman, bellman, front desk, restaurant, security, etc can only be described as the very best that we have had the pleasure to experience in many hotel stays from Paris to West Virginia's Greenbriar. We ate many meals in the hotel and they have excellent values be it at breakfast or at dinner. They also have a free coffee bar that is opened very early in the morning, which was very helpful, due to our being from the east coast.This was our first stay at the Sofitel and we choose it solely based on being the closest hotel to the hospital, so to have such great experience was such an added plus and I hope that this recent review helps you in choosing the Sofitel for your next visit to Beverly Hills and an added plus, is a great shopping mall directly across the street.

I’ve been a meeting planner for about 15 years now. I’ve worked on the hotel side of the business and the corporate side, Hotel Commonwealth truly is a fabulous property. The service was fanatics they helped with all of my special guests needs. The food is amazing, best pastry chef. My guests had an amazing experience from check in to the moment they drove away. Can’t wait to return.

This hotel is absolutely disgusting!
I had read reviews on trip advisor beforehand so kind of knew what to expect but I genuinely didn’t think that it would be that bad!
