We stepped out of the lift on the second floor and couldn’t believe the corridors walking up to the room! They were actually creepy! Really dark corridors with doors on the rooms that were nearly a hundred years old! 
We walked in our room with disbelieve, we didn’t even put our bags down just walked round the room in utter shock. Cobwebs on the ceiling, paint peeling off the walls, stains on the carpet, an old heater in the corner that sounded like a bus when you turned it on! And you needed it on because the draft that was coming through the window was freezing! It actually moved the curtains! 
Our room was on the second floor, I specifically asked for a floor higher up as I had read reviews previously about the lack of sleep people had on lower level floors, I went straight back down to reception where she informed me we couldn't be moved higher for a room with a view, when I explained that was not the case she just dismissed us and said that she didn't have anything and to try again in a few more hours. 
We lasted one night at The Hotel Pennsylvania, after a sleepless cold night’s sleep (I was piling my coats on top of my covers in the end to keep warm) we decided to phone the tour operator and upgrade to The New Yorker, we had to put a few hundred pound to the upgrade but it was well worth while, we couldn’t get out of The Hotel Pennsylvania fast enough!!! 
Seriously people learn from my mistake! It is as bad as people say!

title_masked: Not 4 stars.. Not even close.. c'mon man!
text_masked:
Well... at least the weather was perfect. This is a super trendy, different color lights in the elevator, $15 for a glass of wine type joint. The nightlife is bumping. This hotel is not suited for families or kids. If you are sub-30, good looking (or 45+ & balding with $$$) you are in the right spot. Valet parking $50 a night. Walk up the street and self park for $25 (2 blocks). Beware of the countless pan handlers at every corner (shaking the cup), Manhattan style.
First room was on the 4th floor.. looked over onto the roof of the graffiti riddled building. Sounds of a loudspeaker blaring through the window.. what the HELL is that noise?? Oh yes, its the hotel down the street whose employees have been protesting outside for over a year. My God. They don't mention that stuff when you book the room.. And don't give me that "we are in the city" stuff either.. cmon man, I live in L.A. ! Went down, complained, was moved to the 14th floor. 
Nicer room - nicer view.. same noise. Thankfully, the protesting subsided after waking me up at 7:24 am on Saturday morning. Later that morning.. I kept hearing this noise that felt like rattling pipes.. took me a while to figure it out, then realized that our room just happened to back to the service elevator.. thanks G !!! It just keeps getting better. Can't remember if we were room 1432 or 1433.. its the one that backs to the service elevator, doesn't get any better!!
Last thing - bathroom marble type tile was clearly molded... Just gross. What am I going to do, yell at the cleaning lady who doesn't speak English? I can be a jerk - but, I won't cross THAT line. As with most crappy hotels, its a management issue (or lack there of). 
At this point, my wife is in tears.. kids are pissed because there is no pool - my bad, honestly, I didn't check.. the last time I stayed in a hotel without a pool just happened to be the Travelodge on Lombard street back in 1995, so I couldn't imagine there are still hotels without pools (hostel?).. Upon checking out, we complain and get the extra $25 a day for a rollaway bed charge reversed. What a load of crap. NEVER AGAIN.

Been to this hotel three times now. First time it was purchased by me to spend two nights for my wife's birthday. We had a number of service problems (cheesecake instead of birthday cake, broken shower head that took hours to fix, dripping water outside room in hallway, missing spa appointments - despite a copy of a confirmation) etc. They comp'd us a night after this experience. We decided to stay two, and pay for another one. This time I got a suite so we upgraded and they charged us the difference between the suite and regular room - which I thought was okay, but kind of weak. The suites are expensive. On this trip, similar problems. Coffee maker shot water out and stained shirt, terrible service in the restaurant, took well over an hour to get our car on departure, and again, they messed up the spa appointments. The kicker was that I didn't have a copy of the letter they gave me to comp the night. They insisted I bring it or mail it for some reason. They charged my credit card until I sent them the actual hard copy of the letter. Now that is client intimate service - insert look of disgust here. After complaining to the manager. They comp'd me another night. I am giving it away to a friend. I have also heard similar stories like mine from many people. The roms are nice because the hotel is new. The service stinks.

title_masked: Okay place. Overcharging on internet access.
text_masked: Comfortable and reasonably priced. Well located for restaurants, Metro. A little short staffed--usually had to wait in line to ask anything at the front desk. Watch out if you have multiple wi-fi devices--$12/day EACH.

Although it was hard finding the entrance into the valet check in area because of all the one-way streets, once you got there, the service was great. A little surprised, though, to find out parking is $60/night! The pre-paid stay was only $139/night and the room and the view was an excellent value! The view from the lounge at the top was so awesome, I had to take pics and text to my friends. The internet connection left a lot to be desired, though, and I couldn't do much business at all. The IT dept. conveniently disconnected me when I called to see what was up. Other than that, it was a great experience.

Location, Location, Location. You may not have a river view but you could not be in a better location for exploring Michigan Avenue, enjoying a night out at good restaurants and finding wonderful jazz bands to listen too. Our bedroom was on the 21st floor and did not face Michigan avenue. As a result, the room was exceptionally quiet. The restaurant in the hotel is FABULOUS & definitely worth eating at. The concierge was incredibly helpful and went out of his way to assist us. All in all, a very good stay!

title_masked: I highly suggest the Georgetown Inn
text_masked:
I had some friends and family in from out of town for a Seahawks game recently and I couldn't find a decent place to stay for the life of me until I happened upon the Georgetown Inn. Everything else was either booked up, a complete dump, or along the lines of hotel 1000, the W etc (really expensive)
This place was clean, the prices are great, the people go out of their way to accomidate you, it's close enough to down town, and the rooms are really comfortable. If you are looking for something reasonably priced and you should absolutely check these guys out.

Paradise Point is always my "go-to" when visiting SD. I have stayed here a number of times and am never disappointed. Great location and easy on/off freeways, beautiful grounds, lovely beach, extremely attentive and friendly staff. Dining: I've eaten at the Barefoot Bar & Grill on previous visits and was not that wow-ed so I haven't been back to eat - only for drinks, and I would absolutely recommend it for that (outdoor patio on the water? Hell yeah!). This visit we ate breakfast at Baleen and it was delicious and service was great. Oh, and thank God for adults-only pools :)

The hotel is clean and very decent, but in a less than ideal location. It is a high rise in central Columbus, but still somehow isolated from the city. It is surrounded by a huge parking lot which makes the hotel very unappealing. On top of this, guests are charged a fee to park their car. There are no shops, restaurants, coffee, restaurants, etc. in near proxomity to the hotel. So I felt very "stuck" in the hotel.
The staff was nice and the room was OK. There is a small pool and work out area.

title_masked: Clean, neat, comfortable, except for the ongoing renovation!
text_masked: We stayed at this hotel in NYC the last week of March 2012. The room was small but very comfortable. It had everything we needed and made very good use of the space. The room was clean and very cozy, smelled great and had excellent temperature control. The staff was nice and very helpful. The free wi-fi was spotty. It worked well at times and not at others. The noise level on the street at night was loud. Garbage trucks seemed to be loading garbage all night long. I am not a light sleeper and still was annoyed by it. But the main problem the week we were there was the renovation going on. Every day it was something new. The first day there was tiling being done in the lobby and one of the elevators was unusable because of this. There were long lines all day to use the one elevator left. Every morning the breakfast area was crowded with tables all jammed together because of the reconstruction being done in that area. It was extremely uncomfortable sitting on top of people and squeezing to get through tables and chairs smashed together. The rest of our stay there we just got our breakfast and took it up to our room which is not the way we would have liked to eat. There was always a yellow taped off area somewhere on the first floor and dust flying. The front desk moved from day to day and the workout room was not available the week we were there. Had I known about the construction I may have thought twice about staying there. The only additional item I was dissatisfied with was the security level. Our friends who stayed in the Hilton Garden Inn next door needed their room key to enter the elevator, a nice bit of safety that I would have appreciated at the Hampton. That all being said, we were still pleased with the room and because of the cleanliness of the room I would consider staying there again. BUT I would call first to see if I was in store for any surprises.

This is a large convention hotel located adjacent to a downtown shopping mall, the River Walk, and just a few blocks from the Alamo. This is a large tower on the edge of downtown (in the direction of the Tower of the Americas) and my room had a beautiful view of the city. The room was large with the furnishings and amenities fairly typical of nicer Marriotts. The hotel is sort of on the edge of the tourist district so you will need to walk a few blocks to be in the middle of the restaurant/entertainment district, but it's a fairly short walk. The walk may seem longer in the summer, though, so being able to duck directly into the mall for restaurants such as Mortons and Fogo de Chao is a real plus.

title_masked: 4.5 Stars - lovely room, friendly staff, premium rooms are huge
text_masked:
We stayed 3 nights in a premium room recently. 
Location/Noise
The location met our needs - the ACE trains are on the same block as the hotel and it is a very easy walk to Penn Station (even with 2 kids and luggage). The amtrak tracks are on the close (8th Ave) side of Penn Station helping keep the walk down. I was a little worried about the police station next door for noise purposes. However, even though we were on a low floor (2) and overlooked 35th just at the police station I didn't find it loud at all. Sirens were very rare and didn't wake me up. (I am a moderate sleeper). We couldn't hear people in other rooms, either and I am pretty sure the hotel was quite full. I am not entirely sure what others experienced to complain about noise. For being in the heart of the city I thought the noise was quite low.
Staff
Check-in and all my dealings with staff from housekeeping, to front desk were professional and friendly. We didn't not use the concierge, so cannot comment on that. 
Room
I never thought I would say this in NYC, but the room might have had more space than was necessary! The "living room" felt a bit spartan and bare with a lot of empty floor space. We normally stay at Marriott Residence Inn’s standard 1 bedrooms. This Tryp room was bigger than any of those I have been in. Plus this one had 2 bathrooms as well. It was actually bigger than the website's picture implied. 
I do wish the room had a microwave and toaster to go with the mini-fridge in the bar area. This would be have been really nice traveling with kids. 
Overall 
Everything I encountered on property was clean, new and functioning.
The only reason I withhold 5 stars is the room just didn't have the fully polished decorating that I would expect from a 5 star hotel. Also, it had a bar area with sink and fridge but no other “kitchen” things. I do understand it was not advertised as a kitchen, but the overall feel felt like it was missing something. And the added functionality for guests vs. price seems like something they should consider. 
I would definitely recommend it and certainly would stay here again.

title_masked: Good airport hotel with a few notes
text_masked:
I have been here a few times before. This time, hotwire assigned me and my family to this place. Probably at the low end of typical Westin hotels: I should not complain since I payed only $120 per night, although this is a big increase from last year when I payed $80 for a room at Hilton which is across the street with a similar quality.
I had no trouble with the stay. My kids loved the little swimming pool and the jacuzzi. Free wi-fi was available at the lobby.
Some complaints were 
- when we requested little items missing in the room such as plastic bag for ice and additional hygienic items, they did not eventually get them to us. 
- Although weak, we could smell urine through A/C. Long time ago, when I visited this property, I had a big trouble with this smell.
- Touching anything in the fridge seems to turn on a bill. 
- Parking may be expensive, but we did not have a car.

title_masked: Don't stay here. There are many better other choices
text_masked:
On the positive side, this hotel is in a nice location near Union Square. 
But, location alone doesn't cut it. The hotel rooms are out of date. My room very noisy. To their credit, they moved me to another room which was somewhat quieter but it wasn't clean. There are many other hotels in the area that are much nicer - including other Kimptons.

The location of the hotel was excellent for me just 2 blocks from central park from one side and 4 blocks away from the other side to the alive Times Square and further 4 blocks to Macys and the heart of the shopping center. Also it is very near to Broadway theaters. And not too fare from Javits convention centre. The room size is also good in comparison to New York City hotels. The check-in check-out was very easy and all other staffs were helpful. Buffet breakfast was very good but $40 per person. 
What I did not like was that the hotel rooms and floors hallways needs big renovations, in my room the carpet was stained and looks old, and the bath room needs to be renovated. Also there is no coffee/tea making facilities and the room fridge was out of order and was sealed! The air-condition was barely good, so I think it will a problem during the hot summer months. One last thing I have booked theater tickets from the tickets disk at the hotel and I discovered that other hotels sold the same ticket for $20 less. And my recommendation is to book the tickets your self from the theater if you have enough time especially that I noticed that the theaters are not very large and you can choose a good seat for much less money if you directly book from the Theater

title_masked: Luxurious stay in the heart of D.C.
text_masked: What a wonderful hotel to stay in while visiting Washington DC. Located in the heart of things, just a five minute walk to the Smithsonian Castle or the Jefferson Memorial and just off of I-395. There is a parking garage and plenty of taxis to speed to around town, or the Metro is a short walk away. You will be hard pressed to find anything lacking at this hotel. Friendly, knowledgeable staff are always at hand, ready to serve you. The food was excellent and the lounge is quite relaxing. The Jazz Trio on Friday night was very enjoyable. The rooms are quiet and well appointed--ours was quite large with a whirlpool tub & a large walk-in shower (with real water pressure), lots of marble too. I never had to wait for an elevator, they are always at the ready. The only drawback to staying here is that your wallet will be a bit lighter upon leaving, but then again, you are in the lap of luxury in the heart of DC.

title_masked: First timer in NYC - couldn't have picked a better place to be!
text_masked: I stayed at the GEM Hotel, Soho back in February this year. Spending almost three weeks in NYC, I was overwhelmed with where to stay and which wouldn't cost me the earth. Given I was flying solo for the first few days, I wanted to be somewhere centrally located - and after doing some digging around on the internet, I stumbled across this little gem. The staff were so welcoming and friendly. My room was clean as a whistle, warm and cozy. The bathroom was spacious and the shower had excellent pressure and hot water! Yes, hotel rooms are tiny in NYC, but what do you expect, it would be a real shame if you were going to the big apple to hang out in your hotel room. Anyway, having only booked in for 4 nights, I knew I wasn't going to get much better, so I extended my stay at the GEM for our entire trip. The location is brilliant! Right out front is a subway station, wholefoods across the road, east village on one side, soho to the other, little italy around the corner, I just couldn't have been happier. All in all our stay was fantastic. I strongly recommend staying here. Thanks to the team at GEM soho, we will certainly be back soon!

I actually have no real complaints about this hotel. Everything from start to finish was pretty good. Check-in was easy, the room was nice and clean, the staff was friendly, the facilities were perfect for the convention we were attending. Probably my only criticism would be the breakfast buffet could've been better, not that it was bad, but it could've been a little better. Overall this hotel needs a little updating, but it's a nice place to stay and very affordable. I would recommend this hotel.

My family and I stayed here during March 2012. The hotel was very nice and clean, however, the beds were very uncomfortable. There is nothing to do in the area. Not the best of neighborhoods and the shopping mall next door....... 70% of the stores are closed and the restaurants leave a lot to be desired.

I have returned to this hotel a couple of different times since staying here in March 2012. I have always stayed in the deluxe king whirlpool suite, which I enjoyed. I value an empty refrigerator that I can put my food and drink. I also liked that there was a microwave oven in the room, a coffee maker in the bathroom, a warm and relaxing whirlpool bath. The next day I had slept in past the usual housekeeping time and did not leave the room until maybe 2:30 pm, and housekeeping still cleaned the room, unlike some other hotels, if you sleep in, you miss housekeeping. I can only assume that they keep track and check the rooms again later in the afternoon indication of the high level of cleanliness of the hotel. Wi-Fi and Plug-In in the room, but since I did not have a computer I used their business center computer for internet access to get the directions to the places I wanted to go in Austin. The breakfast had some choices including biscuits and gravy, sausage and biscuit, waffles, fruit, cereal, yogurt, coffee, juices etc. This location on Highway 71 has good access to Downtown Austin by car.

I had poor service from the time I checked in. Front desk staff were confusing about parking. Internet service was slow and they were rude when I complained. At 10 p.m. they sent a lady to check in my room by mistake! She kept trying to get in so I answered the door and she showed me the card where they had given her my room number. My room was never cleaned. They told me I had to request it. I understand that some places don't change the linens out unless you request it but they didn't even come in my room to empty trash or anything. If it is there policy that you request to have your room cleaned they should tell you at check-in. I will never stay at this hotel again.

I stayed for 2 nights in one of the tiny rooms with a shared bath down the hall. My impression... I was pleasantly surprised. The room was very small but I was just there to sleep at night as I had meeting all day. If you were here on a family trip definitely splurge for a bigger room but it was perfect for one traveler.
The bed was really comfy, the furnishings were new and modern and most importantly the shared bath and shower were very clean. I'd stay here again for sure. The location wasn't my favorite part of town, but it is right in the middle of a lot of action if that's where you want to be.

title_masked: Great View, Great Bed, Otherwise just average
text_masked:
My husband surprised me with a weekend away in Chicago. He had picked the Sheraton for its views of the river and lake and also great location. We were impressed with the short walk to many destinations (Navy Pier, Michigan/Columbus Ave to catch public transport, Millenium Park, etc). We were given a free room upgrade for signing up for their rewards membership (free program) and were given a corner room on the 23rd floor that had views of the lake and river. It was lovely to watch the different boats come in and out of the harbor area. The room had also been recently rennovated. The bed and linens made for a wonderful night sleep. 
Other than the items stated above, the hotel was just average, and I feel now way overpriced compared to other hotels. The rooms are quite noisy as we heard every flush and turn off/on of the sink and shower of our neighbor. As we walked down the hallway we could clearly make out everyone's conversations which made us a little uncomfortable. With a hotel with this caliber and price I would think wireless internet should be included- not a $13 fee per day! I was put off by the motion sensor mini bar and could have pictured quite the bill if my children had been in the room with such easy access! The bathroom was just ok. I would search around the blocks for more affordable and better quality food. 
All in all we had a good experience, just didn't live up to its price tag.

I have stayed in a lot of Hilton Hotels, this one is no better than a Motel 6 and 4 times the price! The ONLY it has going for it is location if you want to be near fishermans wharf. It has no view and nothing at all special. Breakfast area is TINY. They book tons of "Bus Tours" and there is not enough room for all those people at one time. Forget about service and expense. Good thing we had a voucher because NO WAY we were paying 41 bucks for what they had. Hilton should be embarrassed that this Hotel is their property. The Best Western around the corner has more amenities . DO NOT GO HERE. If you book a bus tour here, just know we heard the Driver and tour guide plotting to rip you off...cutting corners for every minute you get to spend off the bus, its all about saving them time and wasting your money.

Stayed at this location mainly because everything else was too expensive in Downtown LA. 6/28 - 7/2 The room was clean, some of the furniture was a little worn. The microwave looked like it had been damaged, because it had a big burn in the top, but it did work. The fridge worked but was noisy. There was no ironing board, so you had to figure out how to iron on the bed. I did have a balcony with patio furniture and a view of the "Hollywood" sign. There was a decent breakfast each morning (cereal, fruit, muffins, danish, toast, juice, coffee, bacon & eggs). The area wasn't the best but it did have a couple of restaurants and was on public transportation. The manager always spoke, but when we were having problems connecting to the Internet, he was rude. The staff was nice.

Small things are important.....Kuerig coffee and tea, water, cupcakes, nice folks.
A great value for this part of the city.

title_masked: Horrible experience at a terrible hotel
text_masked:
This place is terrible, and is poorly managed. They have a bad relationship with their "free breakfast" partner cafe on site, a historical restaurant called [NAME]Par's. Here's what went wrong during our stay with 2 kids and a small dog. I have a one word recommendation for anyone traveling with a family: DON'T. For others interested in a casual hotel stay and plan to spend most of the time outside, the hotel is in a central location with lots of amenities and attractions nearby. But the neighborhood is dumpy, at best. 
1. Upon arrival, I was given 2 breakfast vouchers. I reminded them we're a family of FOUR, and they knew that, because I'd booked a kids' suite. They tried to charge me $7/each kid's voucher. When I complained, a kind lady stepped in and ordered the clerk to give them to me anyway. Also, I was promised bunk beds for the kids, but got a pull-out style bed instead. Not a big deal, as my kids are old enough to manage a pull-out bed themselves. I just don't like the switch-and-bait attitude.
2. A security guard got into an argument with a man that was supposedly smoking pot outside our building, bldg A. He got onto a walkie-talkie and complained to someone about him, probably the police. This was when I was walking right by with my kids. I didn't feel safe there after that. 
3. There were TOO FEW garbage cans around the complex. The one behind bldg. A, that faces the Vons, was ALWAYS full and overflowing. The grass strip there was full of dog poop. There were no dog poop bags available, even though the hotel allows dogs. 
4. DuPar's is clearly not happy with the voucher arrangement with Wyndhams. The free breakfast is very restricted, and they allow NO substitutions (unless you make friends with the staff at DuPar's first). They tried to nickle-and-dime us for every little thing we ordered "off the menu", like pancakes. Even when our kids weren't hungry and are small eaters and didn't want to order the free breakfast, which is too much food for them, and when we had free vouchers. 
4.5: The GOOD thing about the breakfast arrangement is that you can get it anytime, so long as the place is open: 6am to 10pm or so.
5. I asked for a wine bottle opener at the front desk. They couldn't find one and asked me to ask at DuPar's. They refused to open it, saying they'd "already given a bottle opener to the Wyndham front desk"! I couldn't believe I was dealing with adults at this point. I had to purchase a wine opener from the gift shop that night. 
6. DuPar's refused to give us coffee "to go", even though I had vouchers. 
7. Tiny parking spots. We had a Honda Pilot and it was a struggle.
8. Internet access was free, easy and worked fine. 
9. Air conditioning worked, but it was very loud.
10. My kids said the pool was cold, even though it is supposed to be outdoor/heated. Granted, we were there when it was always overcast and foggy. 
I will NEVER stay with Wyndham again. It is clearly a very badly managed hotel company.

This hotel is my new 1st choice in downtown Denver. Previously, I've stayed at The Oxford, Hotel Teatro, and the Monaco, which are all very chic and comfortable but don't deliver the same value when traveling with family. At the Embassy, the beds were comfortable, the rooms spacious and super clean, the pool opened early and closed late, and the breakfast was hearty (and included in the cost of the room). The staff was friendly and helpful, too. 
My only complaint is they charge for wi-fi unless you have a lot of Hilton Honor points, but that seems to be the standard m.o. for most high-end hotels these days.

title_masked: Someone tried to break into my room at night! General Manager could careless!
text_masked:
During my stay someone was trying to come into my room at night. This happened several times and I thought it was my imagination at first but the last night I was there I tucked a towel under the door and the towel was a clean perfect sweep that the door had been opened. Also, the deadbolt would be unlocked and the door latch would be buckled instead of flat against the door. I know I checked the deadbolt and door latch twice that night and each time they were both tampered with which is why I used the towel as my guide. I reported it to security as soon as I discovered it early that morning. They said they would file a report and get it to the General Manager (Sheri) and she would contact me. By 9am I called and spoke with Carolyn (employee) who told me that the GM wouldn’t be in until later because of an incident the night before concerning an employee that they let go. His shift was from 3pm-11pm during the schedule I was having trouble and right after speaking with Carolyn I started received inappropriate texts on my cell phone from a number I didn’t recognize then a man called shortly after from the same number. I asked who he was but he didn’t answer that question and continued with lewd comments instead. I brought all of this to the GM’s attention. Carolyn sent me to a police station of some officers that make frequent stops by the hotel however when I arrived I was told the hotel area was out of their jurisdiction I asked to speak to the officers that frequent the hotel and they were there but it wasn’t in their jurisdiction so they could not help me file a report. They instead instructed me to go back to the hotel and call 911 who have after 2 hrs had not dispatched an officer. By this time it was much later in the afternoon I asked the GM if she had reviewed the surveillance tapes and she said that she looked at some of them but that she would literally have to sit and watch 24 hours of frame by frame in an area where it is really hot and she just didn’t have time for that. She also said she would check the key entries on my door but didn’t do that either. She did however bring the night security man in that I had reported the problem to earlier that morning and he told my colleague there was nothing on the surveillance tapes after I had just been told they were not reviewed. I tried for 3 days to get the police to meet me at the location but they were too busy to come. I know now I should have called 911 immediately when I discovered it however I was on my way to work scared to death and wasn’t thinking clearly. I feel like I was sent on a goose chase by the hotel. I also asked why the employee was fired the night before but was given several conflicting stories I was also give 3 different area codes for the former employee and of course none of them matched the one that contacted me. Basically I changed to another hotel and the Holiday INN Expressed denied everything. My room was not broken into during the day and everything was always in its place the break in’s didn’t occur until I was getting ready for bed so the break-in wasn’t for money or anything like that it was purely for other reasons for which I hate to even imagine. This person has my information and yes I’m truly frightened by what happened and whether if I will be safe from this person in the future. They were up to know good bottom line. Not once did I ever receive a phone call from the GM as promised that morning nor did she show any concern for my safety she totally disregarded the whole incident. 
The GM has an incredible morning staff cleaning crew in all that goes out of their way to make everyone feel at home it’s a shame that the GM didn’t treat her guests the same way.

We were pleased with our 8 days stay at the Bryant Park Hotel.
The hotel room was very clean and confortable even for the desk work.
I really liked the simplicity of room decoration and extra large bathroom.
We`ll definitely come back this hotel again.

title_masked: It's A Big City Downtown Hotel
text_masked: And if that is what you want (as we did) then this is the place in Chicago. We stayed for 7 days on vacation touring all over the city. The location of the hotel made everything easy to get to either by walking or public transit. The riverboat tours are just out the main entrance and down one block. Navy Pier, MiracleMile shops, Art Institute, all easily walkable to. We had booked a deluxe king room and the hotel upgraded us to junior suite for an extra $11 per night (a good deal). We had the "awaken package" which included buffet breakfast for 2 in their atrium restaurant which was excellent. One of the best omelette stations I've experienced in a big hotel like this. Unlike other reviewers, we found all the staff we encountered to be very friendly and courteous. And the only elevator issue we had was on one day when it seemed everyone wanted to checkout between 10 & 11 am and the elevators were loaded up with luggage and people waiting at almost every floor (we were on # 23). We also pick-uped a rental car from Hertz right in the hotel. That was very convenient.

title_masked: Very nice property in a great location
text_masked: This property is in a great location near Grand Central Station. The rooms are pretty big for NYC with a "hip" flair to them. The bed was very comfortable and the room was clean. In a tribute to it's former life as "The Chemists' Club", the drinking glasses in the bathroom are beakers. Very nice and helpful front desk staff. I would definitely recommend staying here, and would do so again myself.

This is a very clean HGI located a few minutes drive from Ohio State. The rooms are clean, the beds comfortable, and the breakfast very good in the morning. We also found our welcome at 9:00PM on a Friday night to be very friendly, efficient, and genuine. We've stayed here before, and won't hesitate to stay here again on a future Columbus visit.

The hotel is easy to get to and it is new. The rooms were nice and comfortable. parking available at no charge and breakfast was good as well. The gym is amazing with all new machines. The front desk was nice and very accommodating. very helpful with directions etc.

title_masked: The Best Stay: For a NYer Returning Home
text_masked:
On a quick trip to NY to celebrate my birthday and return to where I was born, I stayed at the Kimpton this past January. They were uber professional, sleek, beautiful and ultra modern. And uptown feel without the snooty persona. 
I highly recommend the Kimpton. As a New Yorker and someone familiar with the city this was the perfect location, perfectly midtown a small walk to the museums uptown or the a beautiful walk to village and downtown. 
For someone unfamiliar with NYC this may seem a little bit of a walk. But my experience, the hotel room, the above par professionals, the design and guest--made me a Kimpton believer and joined the loyalty program.

We stayed at this hotel for 3 nights the weekend of the Chicago Marathon. I was lucky enough to call and switch to this hotel the Friday before we left after seeing a rate online that was better than the hotel we already had reservations at. We got a great rate on one night and could use Marriott points for the other 2 nights. For a special event weekend it was a great deal! 
We stayed in a king studio with our 12 year old daughter. The room had a full kitchen which was great for leftovers and for preparing our usual pre-long run breakfast. The free breakfast offered was very good. The staff was wonderful and the selection was plentiful. My only slight complaint was lack of storage for clothes. There wasn't really a dresser per say, just a couple drawers under the TV and then the closet. With all of our running clothes and regular stuff and it got a little cramped but we managed.
As far as location, it was fabulous! Walking to the start of the marathon was a great warm up and it was in close proximity to lots of our favorite restaurants and shopping. We would definitely stay here again.

Standard hotel rooms for the LAX area. The room and was clean - Thanks for the coffee and the Valet parking all was good. You are a few minutes from LAX and all the shuttle buses for car rentals. I didn't use the pool or any amenities. The staff was very helpful.

title_masked: Excellent stay at Manhattan, nearby Times Square
text_masked:
We had an excellent stay at Manhattan very close to Times Square. Based on earlier experience we expected rather small room but we were positively surprised about the room size and extra comfort and e.g. selection options for the bed.
We also got excellent service by the staff of the hotel and got even phone call from the guest manager to check whether there is anything else the hotel could help us with. 
This hotel definitely gives you value for your money.

title_masked: I always return to the Michelangelo!
text_masked:
Every time I go to NYC, I explore all the other options: with memberships in "The Leaders Club", among others, I always start with their properties in Manhattan, and every time I come back to the Michelangelo. Why? Because none of those hotels (and all the other 5-star ones you are currently considering!) comes close to the quality-price ratio that the Michelangelo offers. The price of rooms at the Michelangelo (and the perks that come with it if you are a member of "I Prefer" - highly recommended) compared to all others clinches the deal every time. The rooms are generally very large, spacious and elegantly furnished. In many stays at this hotel over the years, I have never had a disappointing room; every one has been over-size, tastefully decorated, with separate dressing/make-up area, large closet, and comfortable bathroom with separate soaking tub. However, there are MANY different room configurations, and some of them do NOT have windows facing outside. In fact, on my most recent trip, I was given an upgrade to a suite, which had windows in both the living room and the bedroom, (on opposite walls) all of which looked out onto an airshaft, with absolutely no outside view. And my cell phone didn't work in that particular room, although texting did, so people just called me on the hotel phone if they didn't want to text. But the lack of view didn't bother me, (even though in some circumstances this would have felt totally claustrophobic) because it guaranteed me the quietest, best night's sleep I've had in a long time! Knowing how noisy NYC hotel rooms can be, I was grateful to trade views for space and quiet, for less than $300 a night. But if views are important to you, make your preferences known, and your room can be right on top of 7th avenue; with the double glazed windows it is still a relatively restful night's sleep, although you'll still hear sirens and horns honking. 
Another nice touch is the basic continental breakfast that comes with the room, although it is over at 9:30, a bit early IMO. There is a selection of nice pastries - good mini croissants and other European style pastries - but the room is down in the basement and is horrible! They have got to do something about this room! Everything about the hotel is so elegant, and then you get off the elevator and walk into this breakfast room and you feel like you've just time-traveled back to a 1960's era Sheraton or worse! In fact, it is so awful that I couldn't bear to remain there for even 2 minutes, so I just brought my breakfast tea and goodies back up to the room and ate there, a perfect solution! The lobby has an actual restaurant, in a lovely setting, with the standard full breakfast fare (for standard high hotel prices), but I didn't eat here. The hotel also often gives you a coupon for a free glass of wine or other perk in the lobby bar.
I generally don't avail myself of services in hotels, so I can't comment on whether the Michelangelo is competitive with the Ritz, for example, in this category. But turndown is excellent, and involves a full cleaning and towel exchange. Check in seems fairly efficient, and I have always been given a room for early check-in IF one is available. If not, they'll store your luggage for you in their locked storage room at the front door. I agree with others that tea or coffee making ability in the room would be nice, especially since most other hotels in this category (and lower!) do and in fact these days are actually providing nice Keurig or Nespresso machines. 
A small detail seldom commented on is elevator wait-time: what I love about this hotel is that there are enough elevators and I have NEVER had to wait more than a few seconds for one, something you can't take for granted in hotels! I hate it when you have to wait 5 minutes for an elevator, common in larger hotels, and even 5-star ones.
I highly recommend the Michelangelo, and don't see how anyone could be disappointed here, especially considering the savings it represents over other 5-star hotels.

title_masked: Needs Alot More Work to "Wow" your customers!
text_masked: Great location. But there isn't much they can do about the paper thin walls. If listening to your next door neighbor's sexual escapades sounds fun then go for it! When we complained they tried to move us to move us to a downgraded room!!! Be very suspicious when you see and smell them using a Rug Doctor shampooer for their daily cleaning in the hallways! They're trying to cover up the smells! Continental breakfast? If Square pre-made (or fabricated in this case) eggs are something you go for then this is the place! Do not eat the crullers!-unless you like the tast of stale grease! When the maid cleaned, she left the cleaning bottle in the room. Maybe that was her calling card cause she sure as hell did not vacuum!! I complained but by then the jig was up. They seem to think that they can gloss over things-make them look pretty on the outside and we'll be fooled. But dude!-we're the ones staying there. It's kinda hard to work around that!

We stayed here for two nights, three days. The hotel was beautiful and the front desk staff was very friendly. We paid a little extra to be on the Executive Floor. Beds were very comfortable and the bathroom was large. The best part was the trolley stop right out front of the hotel. We went back and forth on the trolley the whole time we were there. Cost is $1.00 exact change each way, you can get an all day pass for $3.00 in the hotel gift shop. I only gave it 4 stars because the appetizers and breakfast in the Executive Lounge was just average.

We stayed on a weekend (Friday and Saturday). As others have commented, the rooms were somewhat dated but clean. We got a good rate, so it was okay. Location was excellent for visiting the West End and it's attractions. 
Complimentary breakfast was good with lots of choices. 
One major issue was the rooftop concert at a local club on Saturday night. Not the hotel's fault, but it was sure hard to sleep. 
I might stay here again if we were visiting Dallas, but I also would shop for a good rate elsewhere.

title_masked: In the heart of everything New York
text_masked:
Hotel is located in Times Square and very convenient to theaters and subways. The area immediately outside the hotel is extremely congested but if you want to be in the middle of everything, this is the best location in Manhattan. The hotel entrance is dark, marked only with a "W" and is very unimpressive and you could mistake it for a service entrance. The outside flooring is in need of repair. Silly directional signs are in keeping with other W Hotels (the fitness center is labeled "sweat" - the lobby is "the living room," - the telephone information button is "anything anytime" etc.) As with other W Hotels, lighting is dim and with a predominance of black and gray colors throughout, it is often a challenge finding your way around. The elevators are dimly lit so it is difficult finding the elevator buttons and inserting your access card. The room lighting is also very inadequate and it was necessary to move a floor lamp next to the bed for reading. The bathroom was bright and functional with a glass enclosed shower with a "rainhead" showerhead.
Front desk and other staff were polite and professional. The cocktail lounge was attractive and a comfortable setting for a pre-theater cocktail

I stayed here for a week with my husband and baby while attending a training. This is very much a conference hotel, meaning that the lobby is pretty, the rooms are average, and you pay for every little thing. Notably, refrigerators and microwaves are not included! You can have one brought to your room, but you have to pay for it (although really $25 for the week wasn't bad). 
One touch I was not expecting was that they provided baby shampoo, soap, powder, and even a little rubber ducky along with the crib (which was provided at no extra cost). I received a standard wooden crib at first, but called to have it changed to a pack and play, which was clean and in excellent condition. Also the staff were the friendliest I have ever dealt with in a large chain hotel. 
My room (the 10th floor) was due for some updating (bathroom caulking was breaking up, closet door didn't roll on the track, etc.), but the view of the bridge was very nice. My husband enjoyed the sauna and hot tub. The conference facilities were the usual. The part that I could not tolerate was the absolutely vile water. I know there isn't much the hotel can do about the municipal water, but perhaps they could at least filter the water they serve during meetings? It was undrinkable. I ended up with a headache some days because I could not stomach the water or the $4 for Aquafina.

Homewood Suites on Market Street was perfect for my bachelorette party. Unlike other hotels in the area, they have a very large room that we booked (1-king, 2-queens, 2-bathrooms, 1-fold out couch). There was still plenty of space on the floor for an air up mattress if we needed one. The room was reasonably priced for the size. Beautiful views of the riverwalk from the 9th floor. However, the hotel boasts a rooftop pool, which is tiny and was full of children he two times that we went up there. The views from the roof were awesome, but I noticed many people showing up to the roof in their swim suites, and turing back around and leaving because the pool was so packed. Also, the valet parking is kinda high pricing for one night and SLOW. After checking out, my sister and I had to wait over an hour for them to bring us our car. Definately call ahead, before you head down to the lobby. The elevator was really slow, but really busy

Had a great time at the Eddison - very friendly and helpful staff - the Diner is just brilliant - the Hotel is realistically priced bearing in mind its location. The decor and rooms are full of character!!! If we visit NYC again we will stay again provided the price is right.

title_masked: Always a sound place to stay
text_masked:
One night at the Hilton and first time in The Big Apple so we were apprehensive as to 'quality' and 'safety'.
No worries - Hilton certainly meets these criteria. It is a bit tired but rooms were good, had good views and were clean. Lovely bed linen also. Ameneties were a little basic and we had to search for glassware to have a champagen drink on last night.
Would recommend location wise too. Easy for 5th Avenue shopping and good Resturants in the area.
Staff were very helpful too.

We stayed at the Alex for four nights over our 5th wedding anniversary. The hotel is a short walk from grand central station, we took the shuttle bus from the airport and then just walked the two blocks to the hotel. 
We had a great hotel room up on the 8th floor. New York really is the city that never sleeps so it is quite noisy and we were facing the road but I think it's part of the experience of new York city! We had a really nice room, very spacious particularly for new York, very modern and nicely decorated. Great bathroom with nice toiletries, even a tv in the bathroom! Soo American! 
We had breakfast at Pershing square every morning at grand central and just walked around or hopped on the subway. The hotel is in a great location and you can walk to most places, we went to Bloomingdales and central park then whenever we went downtown to canal st and south street seaport we hopped on the subway at grand central. Very easy to get around and the hotel was a nice place to come back to after a packed day of sightseeing. Reception were really friendly, we managed to arrange a late check out for our last day which was great for us. I'd definitely recommend the hotel for couples!

I needed an inexpensive place to stay in the city within walking distance to North Station and the general downtown area. Went to see the Celts play and had my seafood fill at a few places in downtown/faneuil hall area. This place was perfect for me. It was clean and quiet and the room was well apportioned for being such a small room. I would stay here again definitely. People who worked here were very nice as well.

title_masked: The Palomar service and accommodations at its finest.
text_masked:
Large room, king size bed, flat screen tv, wireless Internet everywhere (free if you join Kimpton membership also free). We were there for 4 nights, with our cat, no pet fee, 2nd floor room with pool view and a well equipped gym. We were offered a room on a higher floor but went for convenience instead. Very quiet, also only one floor up from the lobby, so that early morning coffee was only seconds away.
Located on P street near DuPont Circle which has a great selection of restaurants etc. Every 
Evening upon return we were greeted with a welcome back and if we needed anything. 
All newspapers including New York Times were available at no charge.
Would definitely stay there again.
Richard L.

Embassy suites was a wonderful stay. We are a family of five and the room was large enough for us all and the staff was very friendly and helpful. it was also nice to have a buffet breakfast every morning and a nice reception in the evening after a day of sightseeing. we would definitely make this our choice whenever we come to washington DC. Way to go Embassy Suites!!!!!!!
 P.S. Thanks Delithia
The Johnsons, New Castle Del
At first the guy tried putting me in a standard room when I had a free upgrade. I brought this to his attention, and then we got the superior room, which I and my bf enjoyed.

We stayed here for 5 days while we kicked around San Diego..the room was average but clean, the beds comfy, and the staff was always friendly and willing to bring extra pool towels and things we needed to our room. The pool and hot tub are nice and all areas of the motel were clean. Parking spots are narrow, but we were able to find a spot every night. The best thing about it is it's close to everything, great location! Be sure to read the spiral- bound brochure, it has all the info you need.

I stayed in room 1040 for three nights beginning 4/30/12. Arriving at 3:30 PM I found my room clean with no sign of bedbugs. The check-in process only took about 20 minutes in spite of the fact that the clerk kept wandering off to chat with a co-worker. The dark brown carpet was a little worn and the bedspread was possibly the ugliest one I have ever seen. Other than the outdated decor, I have no complaints. I found the room adequate for my needs as I was only there a few hours during the morning and night.

My company booked me and several other colleagues a budgetary one-week stay at the Carlton Inn Midway during the IMTS 2012 event. Although located in a not-so-nice neighborhood, the property is only a 30-minute shuttle drive from the McCormick Place and walking distance from the Pulaski Orange Line station. My room was a bit dated, but otherwise clean. However, the strongest point was the service. From the courtesy and efficiency of the front desk attendants to the friendliness of the shuttle drivers and the excellent customer service after the stay (I had forgotten an item in the room after checkout and the owner had the obligingness to Fedex it to me at his own charge), the staff went above and beyond my expectations. Definitely recommend it for business trips!

title_masked: Traveling for business: Westin covered all the bases
text_masked: I recently traveled to Houston for a meeting at the hotel. The food was good and the service was generally good, but slightly indifferent at times (the only reason I didn't give it the top rating). The large room (this is Texas after all!) didn't feel cramped at all. In addition it was very clean and orderly with an I-pod radio you rarely see in business hotels. The robe in the closet was a bonus for relaxing after a long day of meetings. I really can't complain about anything other than my wife lamenting that she wasn't there to enjoy the comfortable bed that the Westin is well known for. If you have time, there is a large mall across the street with a sky bridge connecting to the hotel. Last note: If you are taking a cab from the airport, bring lots of cash; it was over $80 with tip.

title_masked: Nice hotel, but pack ear plugs...paper thin walls
text_masked:
I was in Chicago for a business trip and stayed at this property for the first time. The front desk staff was very helpful and kind. Despite this hotel being quite expansive and under renovation, it was easy to navigate as there were numerous signs.
I have only one complaint. The walls in this hotel are extremely thin. I was able to hear a lengthy phone conversation / argument from my "neighbor". I was able to clearly hear the conversation for 2+ hours ending after 11pm. Then the guy next door decided to reengage in his phone argument at 6am the following morning.
When I checked out I told the lady at the front desk about what happened, and got a very canned "oh, I'm sorry". 
While other parts of the property were very nice and the location was convenient, I value my sleep too much to stay here again.

Just got back from a four night stay here. Great position, lovely spacious room, nice and quiet. Staff on reception were excellent. Like previous comments I would only add that there is nowhere to sit and wait. We ended up choosing to go ahead with our journey to the airport and sit there for an hour more! It would be great to have tea/coffee making facilities in the room. Thought 32$ for two cups of tea in the morning (room service) was a little steep. The cocktail bar was a little disappointing. Staff, with the exception of a female member, were sullen and disinterested and the place looks tired. A visit to the restroom clearly indicated it hadn't been serviced, overflowing bin and no toilet paper and that was early evening!! Fortunately they have more than one. Overall the experience was good, I would stay there again the rooms are delightful, loved the decor and double shower. Bed so comfy thinking I need to change mine at home. We will be back.

It looks an hour was 20 minutes to checking in after long driving. on the reservation including complementary parking, but after I come back from dinner the staff wanted to park on the street. Bathroom fan noise is so loud from the next level.

Never stayed at this Sofitel, but have stayed at the one in NYC and in LA. The lobby is beautiful and has an art deco feel. The room is comfortable, and the bathroom is amazing, as all Sofitels are. The tub is great and the shower is separate. Two robes, slippers, 2 free water bottles and L' Occitane amenities are a nice touch. I was surprised that there wasn't a spa in the hotel because the one in LA is to die for, but they had massage therapists that they could call for you to do an in-room massage. I opted for that, but it was a little clunky to have the massage table set up in my room because it barely fit. Overall, I would stay again if given the chance!

The hotel was OK - we had a small room but the beds and pillows were fantatics (memory foam). The hotel is right next to Empire State buiding and 10 min walk from Time Square. 
I recommand this hotel for the confort and location.

In our second trip to NYC in 3 months there was not another choice but Park 79! The location is excellent. After a day of the city the upper west side has many spots for a nice laid back alternative. The staff had been nothing but professional no matter what time of day/evening.

My friend Priya and I came from New Zealand to stay in LA with some friends. We hired a van to get around, but Super 8 was a convenient area. The staff were very helpful and nice. The rooms were tidy and clean. In a way, Pri and I already miss Super 8! It's next to Dodger's stadium, and not too far from the Hollywood sights. We'll be staying there again next time we visit!

title_masked: Service was fantastic in a great hotel
text_masked: The entire service in this hotel was FIRST class - including front of house staff, conceriege, bell staff, valet, and restaurant and bar staff - nothing was ever a problem for anybody and all were friendly and helpful. The grounds are beautiful considering you are in downtown LA - several fountains, green spaces and other relaxing places to sit and enjoy - very spacious and quiet. Rooms, although basic and very standard hotel type, are nicely appointed and clean. Very handy to underground and bus services.

We stayed at the Essex House off of central park and it was wonderful- The location was fabulous, the food was delicious, and the rooms were very clean, roomy, and family- friendly. The room cost us 590$ a night, (we stayed 2 nights 3 days) and wasn;t as lavish as the lobby prompts you to believe, but it was still worth the price- we had a spacious double queen room with an office area and entry way. I's describe it as the nicest room you could possibly get at a Hilton- only with a killer location & service.
I really have no complaints, although that 590$ was JUST worth it, it isnt a great deal. I havent seen Suites or lower-quality rooms at the Essex, but our stay was wonderful.

I stayed two nights in the King bed room. The hotel environment was very nice, the room nicely decoratored and very clean. The price was right too. The hotel security features very good. The down side was the neighborhood. Next door there is a Burger King with an alley beside it and I was not happy to see large rats dancing around in the alley coming in at night. I did not feel safe walking in the neighborhood after dusk. A bus stop is in front of the hotel and many people are kind of hanging around talking loud. It's also very deserted, most of the businesses that are still in business were closed around 6 PM on a Friday night. I am a New Yorker who lives in the Bronx, so I'm not easily frightened. I drove into town and had to park in a lot that's 3 blocks away, carrying my luggage three blocks before I checked in, there's no space for car pull up where you can bring in your luggage. Saturday morning the elevator didn't work so I had to bring down my things down the stairs. It's a good thing I am able. Saturday night when I came in the Hotel desk clerk didn't have the keys for the towel closet, therefore I couldn't get extra towels for a late night shower.

First the location is great, Subways close by, Many places to eat, Both High end & Low end.
As others have said the Bedding is 1st rate, But not the bed, It is a platform bed no box spring
not enough comfort for me.
The staff was fine, And yes the lounge area did seem like a club, I got the feeling I wasn't a member.
Bathroom very clean well layed out, A//C great, Windows the open what a treat.
Cost a little high.....Welcome to the big city!
P.S. Bathrooms have rain showers ,No hand helded showers. Hard not to wash your hair

If you can get it on priceline etc then your probably getting an ok deal. I paid "full price" and I've stayed at better places for less money. You also get charged $15 a day to park your car in a dark cramped parking garage. it's about a 8-10 block walk to Pikes Market and close to monorail and space needle--walking distance. Area was decently safe-no problems. They are updating the outside so you have to dodge workers, equipment etc. no pool very small gym area.

title_masked: Excellent value, very clean and well-maintained
text_masked:
My fiance and I decided to take a little getaway weekend after a hectic workweek and some personal family problems surfaced. We went on priceline.com and got an incredible deal on a room at the Doubletree in Del Mar.
The property is gorgeous, with palm trees, a large pool, jacuzzi, wading pool for the kiddies, shuffleboard court, different levels outdoors... what more can I say? We've both stayed at lots of nice hotels on business and for leisure travel, and this ranks up with the best of them.
The room was very clean, we loved the comfortable down pillows and super comfy bed, and there was a flat screen tv and large, clean and modern bathroom with thick luxurious towels and good water pressure.
The staff was friendly without being phony, we got our delicious Doubletree cookies at check-in, everything was great. No complaints about anything.
Since we rely a lot on people's reviews to decide which hotel to stay at or where we want to eat when we're in unfamiliar places, we discussed what we might say if we were to write a review of the hotel. We both said that it far exceeded our expectations, and anything negative we might want to write would be just because we were looking for something to nitpick about. We thought that the music as we exited the elevator on the 4th floor was a little loud, but the rooms are literally so soundproof that it wouldn't affect anyone except for the second or two it took to pass through the little waiting area in front of the elevators. Also, at around 4:00 am on Sunday morning, we were awoken by a shrill, totally annoying alarm-like sound... at first we thought someone had set the alarm clock by the bed for 4:00 am as a joke, and as I fumbled around trying to get it to shut off, my fiance realized it was the fire alarm! Not the smoke detector, the actual fire alarm!! We grabbed our cellphones and valuables and rushed downstairs with the rest of the guests, where we stood outside waiting for the fire department to do an investigation. Turns out there was no fire, and no one knew how the alarm got set off, but we felt there should have been a little more explanation about what was going on. The guy at the front desk working graveshift was completely unprepared for dealing with the situation, and we were basically left on our own till the Fire Dept. told us we could go up to our rooms about an hour and a half later. Not the greatest way to spend the early hours of the morning of our check-out, but because everything else about the hotel was so perfect, we didn't blame them for something out of their control.
When we go back to San Diego (we're from the Santa Barbara area), we will not stay anywhere else but this hotel. It really is that nice.

title_masked: Great hotel in a perfect location!
text_masked:
I can't praise the Grand Hyatt highly enough! We stayed there for three nights as part of a trip to New York for my partners birthday. I've been to New York three times before, but this was their first trip, so a hotel that is central to all the main tourist must-sees was important. The location couldn't have been better; 5 mins from 5th Avenue, 5 mins from Times Square and central for walks north to Central Park and south to Greenwich Village, Ground Zero and the Statue of Liberty.
The welcome on reception was very warm and helpful, and on finding out it was my partners birthday, the lady offered to send something up to the room complimentary. This turned out to be champagne and chocolate strawberries which was a nice touch. The room was spacious and clean, excellent selection of channels on the TV (not that you should have time to watch them - there is too much to see and do!!!), and a great view down onto the street.
The hotel has a couple of good shops, and easy access to the mini arcade of shops at Grand Central Station.
We didn't eat in the restaurant (why would you eat at the hotel in New York), but the bar was good and not too overpriced.
As other reviewers have said the only downsides are the lack of tea/coffee facilities in the room and that you have to pay for the wifi... this is the 21st century, surely that should be free by now.
But really can't fault the hotel at all, and would definitely look at staying here again in the future.

We spent 4 nights at this hotel during the International Quilt Festival. It is very well located, with a pleasant walk to the Convention Centre & other downtown sights (we found this area of downtown Houston safe to walk around day & night) . The staff were very friendly and tried hard, but it would be even better if the front desk staff were more informed about local things (food store, liquor store, transit). The breakfast & room were great. The adjacent (joined) Courtyard Inn has a bistro that sells light meals and drinks, plus the hotel is between Starbucks and McDonalds (but be warned that everything in the downtown closes by 6pm each day). Four blocks towards the Convention Centre is the Phoenician Market, a fabulous speciality food store that has a casual restaurant and also sells wine and a few blocks to the west is a conventional supermarket (Walgreens or Randalls). We did encounter one problem - due to the festival, we had booked the room 5 months prior using the CAA (Cdn Auto Assoc) discount available on the Marriott website. Upon arrival we were told that the hotel did not recognize CAA and that we would be subject to the regular walk-in rate, which was more than double our confirmed reservation rate. We pulled up the Marriott website which clearly shows that CAA is treated in the same manner as AAA and luckily had a hard copy of our reservation. After half an hour of on/off closed door discussions between the front desk staff and our insistence on being treated fairly, we were finally granted the confirmed rate and allowed to check in . Sadly this marred our impression of the hotel and made for a very stressful start to our trip.

title_masked: Great Price, Great Staff & Great Midtown Location
text_masked:
We stayed at Hotel 373 for 2 nights (Fri-Sun) in February 2012. The location was perfect for us as we were attending the Coffee & Tea Festival just one block away. The rooms were comfortable but small (but hey, we didn't come to NYC to stay in our hotel room!). In our room, there was a small dresser and a desk/chair, but no closet (there was a recessed space to hang coats and other items). We stayed on the 2nd floor, which still has some car traffic noise, but it wasn't too bad that we couldn't sleep. The real asset of this place (besides the excellent location--just 5-10 minutes from the subway and less than that to lots of great shopping) is the welcoming and friendly staff. They really are terrific! Note: The lobby is a little hard to miss if you're not looking--it sits right next to Starbucks and kinda looks like it is a part of Starbucks at first glance.
Pros: Wonderful staff, excellent & convenient location, very clean bathroom & room, Starbucks downstairs, flat screen tv with digital cable (so many channels!), desk work space in room is nice, great price for midtown
Cons: Very little closet space, Window box A/C and heating unit (noisier than central air), 2nd floor room has a fair amount of traffic noise
Overall: I would definitely stay at this hotel again! The staff seemed to genuinely want to help us with whatever we needed....and the location really was perfect. :)

If your business or pleasure takes you to LA, this is a terrific hotel to use as a home base. It's located across from the Beverly Center and is close to lots of great shopping and restaurants. This was our 4th stay here and we have always been able to get a terrific room and a good price. This trip, we were upgraded to a suite (Prestige Suite) for free and were once again treated really well. the hotel's facilities (spa, fitness center, restaurant/bar) are good and everything is done first class here.

We originally expected to spend a week in this hotel. However due to hurricane Sandy we are still here. I must say that the staff and management have been great, in both helping us and extending our stay. The hotel is well placed for exploring NY and just round the corner from the MTA. This at the moment is closed due to flooding. Would recommend this to anyone and will definitely come back ourselves.

We stayed here for 4 days at the end of March. Everything was excellent. The hotel is lovely, the grounds immaculate, and service is outstanding as well. The room itself was very nice and the bed was so comfortable, which is one of the most important things to us. We had great night's sleep. I got a massage at the spa, and it was fantastic-one of the best that I've had. They were very accommodating in booking the appointment with short notice. I enjoyed the whirlpool and sauna while in the spa as well. The outdoor pools were great, and kept quite clean. We liked walking on the grounds, and the location is convenient to so many things. I look forward to returning here again next year.

title_masked: Exquisite, in a class of its own...
text_masked:
Truly exceptional experience! Hotel facilities and amenities, and room furnishings are outstanding, staff knowledgeable, helpful, most elegant in manner... All-around a most wonderful experience!!!
As a long-time world traveler, the Chicago Park Hyatt is a gem - I will not stay anywhere else when in Chicago, anymore... My girlfriend was equally impressed!!!

My wife and I had a good stay at the Hyatt Fisherman's Wharf. The late night front desk guy, William, was beyond earger to help and super friendly. For our departure, he booked a town car to take us to the airport which was $5 less than what a cab would have been-- and much classier. 
The room was very clean and comfortable. There was a fridge in the room for your use. No minibar. My only complaint is that the room was very dark. Even with all of the lights on, it still felt like the room was dark. I find this to be common in hotels these days, but this seemed to be darker than normal. 
Otherwise, the room was great and well situated for a touristy weekend in San Fran. I would definately recommend!

Stayed for 2 nights at the Omni for a conference in June and loved it. Staff was helpful and courteous, room was spacious and very clean. Beautiful decor and the pool and surrounding grounds were lovely. Only complaint was that we had to walk across the street each day to get a cup of coffee in the morning. No coffee in our room and a long line each morning at the small coffee shop in the lobby. Nearly $5 for a small cup of plain black coffee seemed excessive and it was faster to walk across the street than it was to wait in line.

To give you a sense of how bad this hotel is, this is my first hotel review after years and years of traveling for pleasure and business. If you're looking for a clean, comfortable hotel room in downtown SF, keep looking.
I had an early business meeting in SF. I was flying in the night before and immediately after the meeting, flying to LA, so I wanted an inexpensive hotel in downtown SF for one night. I found the Crescent and after reading reviews on Trip Advisor, I was cautiously optimistic.
I arrived from NYC very tired. The Crescent is two blocks from Union Square, but the block is a little creepy. Entering the hotel, I was happy with my choice. The lobby is clean and sleek. All would be good.
I checked in. There was only one person at the front desk so I needed to wait a bit. The lady was friendly but had a very difficult time understanding English. Perhaps it was my thick New York accent, but she only got about half of what I said.
Took the elevator up to room 401. What a dump! Holy cow! And it smelled *so* bad. Maybe from the cleaning products. I'm not sure. I am not at all sensitive to smells, but this was horrible. Perhaps this explained the Dyson air cleaner in the room?
The room overlooked the street and a parking garage. Noise was pretty bad. The room was in a desperate need of a paint job and overall dingy. The heat was lacking and the room was freezing. 
I went to hang up my suit for my meeting in the morning, but alas, there was no closet. Instead, I had a coat rack in the room. I couldn't believe it, so I took a picture, which I've attached.
I went to set the alarm for my meeting, but there was no alarm. There was no clock at all and no radio in the room.
I went to clean my glasses, but there was no tissue in the room. There is, however, a 24-hour Walgreens within 2 blocks of the hotel, so for a whopping $1.59, I purchased a box of tissues. 
Is this how the Crescent keeps their costs down - no heat, no tissues, no radio, no alarm clock? 
In the morning, I went for a run. The woman that checked me in gave me a map, but just to be certain, I asked the gentleman at he front desk about the route she recommended. Glad I did. He gave me a better route that was great. Glad I asked. The guy seemed good, so I asked if he could hold my key while I ran, which he did.
Came back from my run and again there was only one person at the front desk so I needed to wait 10 minutes to get my key. Very frustrating.
Went back to my room to take a shower, No bath towels - just cheap, small towels that had been washed a few too many times. The towels were shredded. I should have brought my own towel.
Had some time to kill so I ate a little bit at the continental breakfast. It was 'ok', at best.
Finally checked out and asked for a bill. I was told I couldn't get an itemized bill because I booked through Hotel.com. (I actually booked through Expedia.com, but that's irrelevant.) I never stayed at a hotel that couldn't give me a receipt at check-out.
I know I went in to great detail. I just wanted to show that there was a problem at every turn at the Crescent. The only positive is its great location to Union Square, but I would have preferred to walk a few extra blocks to get a clean room with a clock radio, no smell and towels that weren't shredded.
If you're looking for a hotel room in downtown SF, keep looking.

We have a group of five people stay for 3 nights. Some of them are first time to this country. It was definetely highlight of our trip in the US. Super nice service, fast reaction, convenient location, great price. This hotel is very well managed.

We just returned from a weekend at The Madison, and could not have been happier with our choice. Within walking distance to the White House, the National Mall, DuPont Circle, and many other historic sites, this elegantly restored hotel evokes all the grandeur that is truly Washington DC. The service is attentive, the hotel is immaculately clean and quiet, and the restaurants are hip and trendy yet in the most classic way. Every dish at The Federalist was prepared and presented perfectly, and our delicious breakfast at Post Script wrapped up a truly enjoyable stay. We will be back!

title_masked: Great hotel. Beds need some help
text_masked: Stayed at the Topaz the last night of our vacation. Great location, on a quiet side street, close to DuPont Circle and Embassy Row. Front desk staff were welcoming and Helpful. Building is older, but the facility has been renovated. Room is a very nice size. Decor is modern (what you would expect from a boutique hotel) although they cut some corners on the renovations: i.e. painted rather than replaced door jams and base boards. But that really is a inor detail. My primary complaint was the bed. The box spring was obviously old and worn. The wood frame made a sound like two cats fighting every time I turned over. Made for a long night with less than a restful sleep. Perhaps this was only a problem in our room however it was disappointing and not what I would expect. Otherwise this is a charming boutique hotel in a great neighborhood.

title_masked: Nice hotel, very small rooms & beds
text_masked:
The hotel is modern & clean. The downside is that the rooms are quite small & the rooms with queen size beds have smaller than normal queens. The queen beds are closer to a full size, so if you are tall get a king bed room. 
Good value for sure, but not good for more than a night or so given the tiny room size!

The staff was very friendly as we checked in at this beautiful hotel. The rooms were very nice and we enjoyed our stay. It is only one street from the 16th St Mall area and we had a wonderful time exploring. There are excellent restaurants and cafes, along with lots of shopping. We would stay here again.

We came to El Paso to visit our son who is stationed at Ft. Bliss. From the time of check in to check out our experience was awesome. Front desk staff was very helpful in guiding us in the right direction to the military post as well as local shopping and dining. Our room was clean and comfortable. We were able to enjoy some adult beverages at the lobby bar in the evening with live entertainment. All the staff were exceptional, especially the front desk. I would highly reccomend this hotel. We look forward to our next visit.

Back to Chicago for a weekend of fun. Highlight of trip was the amazing accommodations at the Swissotel. Altho the new, ornate lobby was not open at the time of our visit on March 30, the hotel did a great job taking care of their guests via the multiple check-in "stations".
Another aspect of the appreciation I have for the staff was the fact that we had a terrific deal through a popular discounter. Sometimes the demeanor of staff seems slightly different when a "half-off" deal is presented. 
However, every hotel staff person did extend their most professional courtesies to us, from check-in to the amazing breakfast buffet. We arrived at the restaurant on the "late side" the next morning. The waiter assured us that they would be happy to create anything from the menu for us- not just from what was still available from the buffet tables. We appreciated that kind of service. Penthouse level pool and spa were also stunning. 
Fantastic view of Navy Pier from our room ( especially at night) and the accessibility of location made it easy to walk back from the Pier and Parks.
Loved the down mattress-topper on bed, and the decor, especially notable- the shower. 
Holding luggage after check-out is always a plus as well. 
I have recommended the Swissotel to everyone since we came back! 
I

My partner and I stayed here for four nights over Labor Day weekend - what a treat! From the moment we arrived until we left, we were greated by our names, always being asked how things were going - in short - attentive Hyatt staff - without being over the top and invasive.
The rooms are small - typical NYC - but very well designed. As a Hyatt Diamond member we were upgraded to a small suite which gave us ample room to spread out. Love the Andaz policy of free snacks in the room, the Nespresso machine made us feel at home and the wine happy hour in the lobby is a great way to ease into an evening in New York! The breakfast menu rocked - and the Hyatt Diamond level free breakfast credit covered two extremely filling and tasty breakfasts each morning. The location is great for shopping, theatre and exploring New York.
The downside - having to leave! Already planning our next escape to New York!

This was our first trip to New York (and indeed to the States) so we had trusted the rating that Trip advisor gave the Casablanca Hotel. We were not disappointed. This hotel truly lives up to its reputation for service and quality and also has the great advantage of being right in the very heart of the city.
