Yes, the rooms are small and our two girls had to share a double bed but space is a premium in most city hotels and the rooms were very comfortable. Lovely bathroom, lots of nice toiletries, iron and ironing board but the real benefits were the complimentary, delicious breakfasts, and the wine and cheese in the evenings. And to give one example of service: we bought some posters at the art museum which turned out bigger than we thought. So we bought a tube and planned to send them by post. The post office was closed by then and it was our last day but no problem for the hotel staff. Without us asking they offered to post it for us without any service charge the next day - and here it is waiting for us when we got home to the UK. We will be back!

Great location, great view (ask for a corner room) and great staff. We were able to check in early and very helpful with everything. It is a little outdated but well worth the $ we paid and the location is just priceless.

title_masked: Extremely well situated and nice hotel
text_masked:
We stayed there early September 2012. The DuPont Circle hotel is very well situated on the lively and pleasant circle, surrounded by restaurants and shops, and on the red subway line.
The overall appearance of both the common parts and of the rooms is very good and modern. The rooms are nice, but a little smallish.
The staff is very professional and helpful. The restaurant and terrace offers food of good quality. Only the extremely noisy bar us to be avoided.
To be recommended if available at the right price. We paid an average of 210$ plus tax per night excluding breakfast which is a bit high but the pleasant location makes it worth.

Excellent place to stay. Very pleasent staff always ready to assit. Great resturant and food. Room was comfortable and very spacious. Located next to a nice small park. Walkng distance to nice shopping areas like Walnut street and resturants.

title_masked: Very nice hotel - Hyatt quality and service, but mediocre restaurant
text_masked: This is a very nice hotel - exactly what you would expect from a Hyatt - quality rooms, furnishings, bed, bedding, desk, lighting, TV, bathroom, towels, amenities, etc. Everything was clean and in excellent condition. My room was directly across from a fire station, however it was surprisingly quiet - I could barely hear anything (so nothing to worry about with this!) The shower was extra nice, however there was no tub (if anyone cares). They had nice personal touches, such as personalized wake up calls, rather than a recording. The hotel is a convenient 10 minute walk to Union station. There are very few restaurants within a 5 minute walk of the hotel and the hotel's restaurant is mediocre. The food was generally unhealthy with much more fat (cream, butter, oils, etc) than necessary. Other than the average restaurant and lack of many nearby restaurants, this was a perfect hotel.

I’ve never been more anxious to check out of a hotel in my life. The thick plexiglass that separates you from the front desk clerk should be an indication of the type of lodging this hotel represents. The “office” is located in the basement that also serves as the breakfast room, housekeeping and laundry room. There is no breakfast. Just coffee, warm orange juice and Nature Valley granola bars. The rooms are large with a kitchen but no utensils, dishes or pots and pans. You wouldn’t want to cook or eat anything in these kitchens anyway. Rather than ramble on with a long winded review I’ll sum it up with a few choice words. Filthy and unsafe. Do yourself a favor and stay elsewhere.

My wife and I stayed at the Burnsley All Suite Hotel on 5/24/12. We stayed in room 1201 which was clean and had up to date furnishings. We booked our room through Hotels.com for ~$120 USD. At that rate we would definitely stay at the Burnsely Hotel again. 
Additional benefits include free covered parking and free shuttle service to within ~3 miles of the hotel. We took advantage of both benefits.

title_masked: Pretty good for an airport hotel
text_masked:
This hotel is one of the better airport hotels I have stayed at. The rooms were clean and the staff was friendly. Bright lights in the parking lot were much appreciated as a theft deterrent. The hotel feels very safe. Nice size room with a good variety of cable TV channels. There is a Jack in the Box restaurant that is right next to the hotel if you need a quick meal or a snack.
The one thing you need to know....you will have airport noise. No fault of the hotel. Just being this close to the airport, sometimes you feel like you can reach out the window and shake hands with the pilot. I did notice that the jet noise was less frequent after about 10:00 pm. 
If you are looking for a convenient hotel that is very close to IAH, this is the hotel for you. I had an early morning flight and was at the rental car return within five minutes. There are also plenty of gas stations on JFK BLVD to replenish the fuel. 
This in fact is one of the best airport hotels I have stayed at in quite some time! Good work Hampton Inn at IAH!!!

The hotel is clean, good breakfast, Nice people. The location is the best. Around the corner of macys and empirie state building. The rooms ar ok, bathroom a little old and the bad thing is you cant open de window of some rooms. Frist we had to stay on the 3rd floor, bljak so depressing. Room 1007 was good, it was a smoking floor but you cant smell it. It was clean and ok. And the window coyld be opende from the bathroom.

The hotel is well located. I took a bus from NYC to Boston and got to South Station. 5 minutes walk from there. 
Front door man was very welcoming and friendly as the people at the front desk.
My room was on a high floor (forgot which one) so I had a nice open view. The room looked like the other Hyatt's, it was clean, well proportioned and quiet. 
You have free wi-fi for a limited period, which is better than other hotels that would charge you for that.
If you don't have a map and are trying to find the hotel, don't ask for the street name, ask for the Hyatt. It will be easier for people to direct you there.
I did not request it but I saw there was a hotel person at the lobby/bar who was advising other guests on where to go and what to visit while in Boston. He sounded really nice and helpful and prepare them a whole plan for their one day visit. I thought that was nice, he took the time to seat with them and do it.
I would stay here again.

We stayed two nights in Feb at this hotel and I must say when I booked and then looked up the comments I was a little hesitant, there seemed a lot of negative comments. However, please disregard most of those, We found this hotel clean, comfy, the staff going over the top to help us with finding places to eat, help us out in any way possible. The "free" breakfast is very good and lots of varieties. Not sure how any one can complain about that. 
If you do not have your laptop with you they have computers ready for you to use, no cost either.
 We will certainly be back and have no hesitations to recommend this hotel to any one who is interested, disregard the complainers , no doubt not much will please them on any given day.

title_masked: Looked nice but the wrong crowd for a family place
text_masked:
Nicely redone and clean hotel but that is the extent of the positive comments 
Young family for an early flight Sunday morning and found out the quiet time started at midnight. Rowdy drunk 20-30 year old crowd having a good time but at others expense, not a good idea for an airpot hotel .
Had a large room at the back of the hotel ground floor by the main a/c unit and could not sleep all night as I could hear it start up through the single pane windows about every 20 minutes
Seemed like there was a gang element at the hotel (ie clean shaven , muscle bound tatoo'd young men driving tinted out sports car in and out of the hotel all night) Police showed up at about midnight on force to deal with some problem.

title_masked: Very Good Motel, Location Not So Much
text_masked: Very friendly staff and spacious rooms. We got a non-smoking room and it didn't smell, the heat worked fine. Breakfast was adequate, overall great for the price I paid. Only drawback is it's a 10-15 minute ride to any downtown locations like Beale St. or Graceland. The area the motel is in is also kind of seedy, but felt safe however.

title_masked: Excellent hotel for infants and small kids
text_masked: Great hotel for people traveling with infants or small kids. I stayed here for a week for work, with my baby in tow, and it had all the amenities I needed: the junior suite with a full kitchen (full-sized fridge with freezer was indispensable for keeping milk frozen) and separate sitting area; a travel crib; on-site coin-operated laundry; spacious lobby with lots of sitting areas (great for meetings); and reasonably priced restaurant and bar with awesome happy hour specials. The staff was super nice and helpful too. The location can't be beat - close to DuPont Circle and lots of restaurants and drug stores. Highly recommended.

We visited Austin for a Wedding. We became Omni "Select Guests" members beforehand to reap the benefits. It's worth it. Internet, pre-check in and all the extras are worth this free membership. 
PARKING-- This is my biggest gripe. We tried to avoid the $18 a day on site charge by parking across the street for about $10 per day. We did this and went over time accidentally and they immediately towed our rental away from the public parking. Not Omni's fault just warning you to be careful. Obviously I parked in the Omni parking the next few days and even with the parking stub, it was saying I owed $24. I didn't have time to argue it and left the premises. This is the last thing you want to spend your money on. One reason I didn't give it 5 trip advisor stars.
CHECK IN/OUT-- Easy as stated due to the select guest privileges. No surprise charges and low maintenance.
ROOMS-- High end fixtures and bedding. It was quiet and the AC was impressively cool. Pretty stocked bar and all sorts of amenities. My quip is that we received two double beds instead of queens or a single king. Perhaps it was due to the wedding party getting a discounted group rate. Not sure but wasn't thrilled. After the first night, the wife and I split off into separate just to avoid the elbows.
POOL--On the smaller side but it does allow for impressive views and the bar is an added feature. Hot tub was out of order which was a disappointment.
RESTAURANT-- We only ate breakfast here once. The food was good, a bit pricey but within reason. The service was slow and inexperienced. We sat there unacknowledged and without drinks for far too long and it wasn't busy at all.
GYM-- Well put together with plenty of options.
BAR-- This is a pretty nice set up. Lots of TVs to appease if you want to catch a game and gets a pretty good atmosphere after dark.
STAFF-- Everyone was very cordial and helpful at all times. The wedding group had a few get togethers in the lobby area and they were quite helpful with providing plates and pretty much whatever we needed.
CLEANLINESS-- It's well taken care of and should be for the normal prices charged. The general decor up to date and warm.
SURROUNDING AREA-- There's not much immediately surrounding the place but just a few short blocks away gives you a really great bar/restaurant/shop scene. A few blocks in another direction and it starts to get a little seedy so know where you are going.
OVERALL-- A nice place to stay but I certainly got more of the business feel than I did a family or romantic feel. I would recommend it though.

Reviews of this property were consistently outstanding; so much so that I was prepared to be a bit disappointed. Well based on our recent stay, I can't say enough good things about this hotel and especially the staff. They were consistently friendly and went out of their way to provide the services we needed. From check-in to breakfast to help with transportation, they were exceptional. The room was as promised - very clean, contemporary, and serviced properly everyday. The breakfast was well prepared, PC service on the mark, and the elevators worked flawlessly. But the most surprising was the help we received when leaving NY. I asked the doorman to get us a taxi to go to the airport. I had already priced car service and because it was mid morning decided it would be less expensive to take a taxi. Well the hotel has an arrangement with a car service and after a brief discussion with an amazingly upbeat and courteous doorman, we took the car service offered (two cars waiting). When we arrived at the airport the driver advised us that Delta now flew from serveral terminals and waited while I checked. We were at the wrong termianl for our flight so he took us to the correct one before leaving. Although the hotel was conveniently located and the rooms better than average, the staff made a good trip to NYC truly great.

Normally stay at the Doubletree, but they were booked. We like the Park and Fly packages. Holiday Inn offered one, so we thought we'd try it. There was a conference going on and I think the staff was distracted. Checking in I was told only double beds were available. This was not acceptable since I had booked my king room 2 months in advance. Desk clerk checked with manager and my request was honored. 
A/C in room only worked in the daytime hours. I had to keep getting up during the night and crank it up to get it to come on.
Bed was comfortable and room was clean. 
Restaurant was good. Service at the bar was OK.
Upon returning from our trip when I called the hotel for a shuttle I was told it was not available and to take a cab. They did reimburse me for the cab fare.
I think more attention to customer service is needed at this establishment. We will probably not return.

title_masked: Rooms Nice, Staff Not So Much
text_masked:
I wanted to have a nice short getaway for my fiance's birthday. After the booking I called to ask if they did anything as far as being able to put a small cake or cupcake in the room for a fee. The lady said "you would have had to call days in advance for that". No problem, I did book the hotel at the last minute. I also asked if there was anything they could add to our room to give it an extra "happy birthday touch". She said I would have to contact concierge for that. She transferred me to concierge and no one answered, so I left a message for them. Over an hour later no one had called back. I called again and asked if the concierge department was open. She said yes, and that someone would call me back shortly. It is a week later today, and I never received a call back from concierge. Oh well. The lady at the front desk at check in was very short, and seemed like she was in robot mode. Lack of personality and customer service. Every time I had to encounter someone at the front desk they were rude, or just short of being rude. 
The room was nice, however housekeeping forgot to empty the trash so someone's leftover food was in our trash when we got there. It made me nervous as to what else the maid may have missed with cleaning. The bathrooms were great. They were actually clean. The bathroom made you feel like you had your own mini spa in your room. The room was nice and spacious, but there was a small film of dust over everything. You could tell the room probably had not been occupied in a while as their Detroit magazines were still dated for the winter/spring season. 
There is a nice selection of restaurants. 
Later on we noticed a cupcake stand in the hotel. Would have been nice if the lady I originally asked about the cake would have just told me they had a cupcake stand there. It was all good though. The lady working the cupcake stand was very nice. Probably one of the only encounters of good customer service we had there. 
Overall we were not impressed with our stay here. The hotel is on the pricier end so you expect good service. Good customer service is very important to us and it is serious lacking in this place. I unfortunately would not stay again.

Very disappointing. Yes, the location is good, and the bed is comfy, but they are the only good things to say.
The room was tiny and badly laid out. You are virtually on the bed when opening the door. There was a tiny window, maybe a foot wide, and with a desk/dresser under it so it couldn't easily be reached to open the blind. Limited storage space, the closet fitted a winter coat and not a lot else. Tiny amount of drawer space, and bedside table on only one side of the bed. Bathroom was a good size, but again nowhere to put anything as the counter space around the sink was tiny. The bath was supposed to be whirlpool - that didn't work. There was a mirror on the inside of the closet, but no power outlet or good lighting near it, so had to use the bathroom for make up application etc, so scheduling bathroom use between us was a chore. AC was very noisy and disrupted sleep. Two rooms on the floor were being used for an event, and one night there seemed to be a party going on, which kept me awake. Advertised complimentary mineral water never materialised and there were no robes, both of which, per the website, are in all rooms.Only one water glass and one flannel for two people. TV reception very poor, with many channels unwatchable.
Lobby areas are tired, and lots of the seats are stained. Elevators were used for laundry trolleys and maintenance, and were tiny, and every day, maintenance people were on the floor, which had only 6 rooms, so to me, that wasn't a good sign. There was a doorman who generally watched people come and go, and when i had my hands full did not open the door. 
i didn't care for the gym equipment. Nowhere to pt a book or ipod.
Generally not a good experience and I wouldn't recommend it.

title_masked: Great stay and an excellent value.
text_masked: You could not find a better value any where near the airport. The front desk was very friendly and helpful and we loved the cookies that they put out in the afternoon. The room was clean and the bed was very comfortable. The shuttle to the airport was on time and the driver was fun to talk to. The one thing I would have liked was to have the business center not in the main lobby where everyone could see what you were checking on while you were on the computer, but that would not stop me from staying there again.

An excellent boutique hotel on lower east side for creative minds and food lovers. Check out the Marque Creative's branding and Grzywinski+Pons's interior design in the hotel. Lombardi's coal oven pizza is just 5 mins away; also Cafe el Portal's Mexican grilled corn with mayo, cheese and chili is the best thing in NYC; and don't forget to take a 15 mins walk to Katz's Deli for it's Jewish corned beef sandwich. Thank you so much to the hotel and Phoenix the man for the complimentary bottle of red and card for our wedding anniversary. Sweet!

I have been 5 nights in the Hotel because a business trip to LA. The hotel atmosphere is nice, the staff really very nice and supporting in all our requests and needs. 
The pool is great (there is always a party!) and fitness club is acceptable.
It is a little bit decadent and rooms should be upgraded... a little bit mainly because the moquette... that is really old. 
By the way, rooms are standard but clean and nothing is missing.
The restaurant (The Public) is good. Breakfast at 25° is also ok.
Located one block off Michigan Ave. and by many great restaurants. Free WiFi, large room with contemporary decor, microwave/mini-fridge and friendly staff. Will stay here again.

If you are attending a conference ,the location of either of the Marriott hotels is very convenient. The two are right next to one another- in fact you walk through the other Marriott to get to the Convention Center.The rooms are nice but not luxurious but with a convenient mall right next door, the locations is nice.

I stayed here for two nights and found it great! Outside it looked just OK but once inside its very plush! The breakfast was lovely, the rooms clean and very comfortable. There was a pool too which looked nice!
The location is fantastic! Its a 5 minute walk to the metro, which is one stop from Universal studios. There are lots of restaurants nearby, and it is very close to hollywood boulevard. I would stay here again and would recommend it to anyone!
Great hotel! Nice location! Unfortunately the breakfast was not edible.

title_masked: Not bad, not great, but cheap
text_masked: Stayed here on arrival in Chicago. The place is a little out of town but probably one of the cheapest places you will find. It was decent enough for the money as long as you don't expect luxury, the bed was comfy enough, the bathroom was passable. The electrics were a little bit ropey but I guess they call that 'character'... all in all, if you need a bed for the night on a budget it does a job!

title_masked: Great place to stay in Seattle
text_masked: We very much enjoyed our three nights at the Paramount. The lobby has warm character, the staff is helpful and courteous, the room and bathroom were clean and spacious. The location is great, within walking distance of Pike Place Market, the monorail, many shopping opportunities and bus lines. I would recommend this hotel to anyone.

We had a large group and with the exception of a few reservation mix ups and an a/c malfunction, we had a great time. The breakfast was good the rooms were clean. Although the pool was small, it was large enough to relax and it was clean.

title_masked: The Warwick is a lovely place to stay in Denver.
text_masked:
I have stayed at the Warwick on a couple of occasions, and have found it to be a lovely place to stay when in Denver. It is a relatively small, quiet downtown hotel, with a good restaurant and bar, and the service is exquisite.
I would not hesitate to recommend it anyone looking for an upscale, comfortable and affordable hotel for the business traveller.

title_masked: Service and style always in fashion at The Brown Palace
text_masked: Having been delighted with a family-reunion stay at this classic hotel in 2010, I decided to revisit for a business trip last month. I'm happy to report that the hotel did not disappoint. Superior, friendly and accommodating customer service are a hallmark of this hotel. There is something genuine about this property: staff who make guests feel welcome; rooms that are clean and well preserved but full of character and an atrium lobby that is as awe inspiring as it is inviting. The hotel is conveniently located downtown, and offers quick and close access to the free trolley transport. Adjoining pub also a find. One of this hotel's best features, though, has to be its affordability. For what might be spent at a tolerable chain property, you can be treated like royalty here, and be surrounded by authentic charm.

My wife and I stayed at the Hotel in June for 4 nights. We had not much experience with the Sleep Inn chain - but what a surprise. The walk down to the Inner Harbor is very short. The room was modern, beautiful and extremely clean. Beds are comfortable The shower was amazing. The staff was exceptionel and everybody we encountered was courteous and helpful. The manager to the cleaning lady everybody is fully committed and motivated.
It is not fair to point out someone but the shining star is Lou from the breakfast service. We never experienced a performance like this.
We will definetely be staying again next year. Cheers

title_masked: Great Place to stay in San Antonio!
text_masked: I stayed 3 nights here for business in San Antonio. Great proximity to the riverwalk and downtown locations. Large, clean rooms with ample sun coming in large windows. The front desk staff, restaurant, and everyone else were very friendly. I would definitely recommend to anyone visiting San Antonio!

title_masked: Not a bad place to spend the weekend on business travel
text_masked:
I really like a lot about this hotel. There are some cons too which I'll discuss below.
I'm in a King Deluxe at the end of the 9th floor, far from the elevator and high up. There are only 10 floors. The decor of the lobby, rooms and hallways are very nice and fancy modern with conservative gray and expresso color themes. I'm here for the weekend because I am taking all day classes on Saturday and Sunday about a mile away.
On my first night I came from Judiciary Square metro. I came down at about 11:00 PM at night. It was a very sketchy walk for a young lady. I wouldn't recommend doing that at night. The hotel isn't in a gorgeous area but you do see the Capital when you're outside. The roads are less traveled. Check-in took a few minutes. I took my card and went to my room. The door wouldn't open. I called the front desk. The front desk lady came up in about 5 minutes with two new key cards. She couldn't get it to open. She had me sit in the waiting area. In about 10 minutes a man came up with a electronic device. He managed to get the keys working but to open the door you had to slam it. This ended up being the theme of my stay. I requested two special pillows from the pillow menu which took about 30 minutes for housekeeping to bring up. I went to bed soon after and slept well for the little sleep I got.
I sleep soundly and my wakeup call was timely. My breakfast was delivered promptly and tasted fine. The in-room dining is expensive, but that's to be expected. 
Coming back from class today I opened my door by slamming my shoulder into it. Not the most appealing way to open a door. I could tell the maids cleaned because the room was put back together prim and proper. The rooms are very spacey, clean and modern... from the bed to the desk to the bathroom. 
I used the recreation center which is a small gym. There are towels on the equipment and TVs attached to some of the aerobic equipment. There are a few weight machines but the total area is probably about 250 sq. ft. There were three other people in there and I could smell someone's odor so it's not super ventilated and heats up easily. An attendant came up while I was there so it probably gets cleaned frequently.
Afterwards I went back to my room to clean off and do work. The shower is nice and heats up quickly. You're even provided with a nice robe. The shampoo/condition/bath gel are in big bottles. The lotion is in a small bottle above the toilet. The bathroom isn't that big but it's fine for what it's needed for.
I ordered in-room dining service which is pretty good and quickly delivered. The attendant was friendly and nice. The food quality is about 3.5 stars. 
I've been working in here the remainder of the evening. At about 10:00 PM I heard a lot of door slamming, constantly. I thought someone was having issues because it was very annoying. I looked outside and saw a maid cart. I heard the sounds for a half hour more then called the front desk. They said it isn't the maid. I said the maid cart is there. He said the maid wouldn't slam doors now. I said the maid is the only one out there. He argued with me more and I gave up and hung up. I wasn't lying about the maid. Not exactly top notch treatment. This being said the room is usually quiet where I am once the maid issue is resolved. The doors in this hotel are very heavy and do make noise in general.
Some of the front desk staff are definitely nicer than others. The guest services Tamara was great. The man from last nice was not so great.
For checkout the invoice didn't reflect a dining credit I was told about and even confirmed last night with the man who said I'm a liar. I called guest services. After being put on hold for 5 minutes I was hung up on. I called back. A new lady spoke with me. She told me I have the credit but only a manager can push it through so that's why it wasn't on my invoice. I told her about the man from guest services last night and she told me to make it up to me, she'd clear my balance for dining. I asked for a new receipt and one was sent up in five minutes.
Overall there are some hiccups with this place, but it is a comfortable stay with fashionable decor. I'd consider coming back again but might try another option based on the hiccups. I was here from a deal website; not sure I'd drop full price for this type of adventure.

LOved this hotel. Great lobby area. The staff were very helpful. Great comfy beds and stylish rooms. The bathrooms were also very nice. It was an excellent location. Coffee/ tea in room or lobby would be nice.

Spacious accommodation and very helpful staff. Microwave and fridge meant we could almost self cater. Breakfast in the hotel - nice but expensive, worth the money if you're prepared to eat a lot! However there is a supermarket about 5 mins walk away open 24/7.
Hotel a little way out of Boston and not near a metro station, however shuttle bus service from hotel is reliable but doesn't run late into the evening. Taxi from hotel to downtown Boston about $12.
Hotel rooms clean and spacious with good, albeit rather noisy.

title_masked: You get what you pay for
text_masked:
I was in town for only one night to watch Atlanta destroy the Phillies and booked last minute. I wanted a hotel with an outdoor pool. On SPG's website, Sheraton Suites is listed as having an outdoor pool when in reality the outdoor pool is across the parking lot at the Four Points. Sheraton Suites, Four Points and Aloft are all in the same parking lot and seem to have reciprocity between them. If I had known this, I would've booked the Aloft because it's newer and maybe a touch a nicer. The printer at the Sheraton Suites was down and so the front desk advised me to print my tickets for the game at the Aloft. The Aloft attendant was very polite and accomodating...as if they're used to guests going between all three properties. 
I think the only upgraded option for this hotel is one presidential suite. It was occupied during my stay. All of the rooms are suites. My room had a couch and tv in the living room, bathroom in the middle and a king sized bed and tv beyond that. Nothing super special. The room was very clean. 
I didn't pay a lot for the room...$80 or $90. It was only a 10 minute drive to the sports stadiums/arena area. Definitely an option for airport customers or people on a budget.

Spent 2 nights here in this fabulous olde worlde charming B&B, the rooms were fabulous and very comfortable and breakfast was very civilised, not the usual American food, so something usual and good too! lovely muffins!

Have stayed here several times when we come to Denver. Good location, nice people, some good weekend rates. 
Hotel has reasonable sized outdoor pool. 
Parking can be expensive but on the last weekend we stayed here it was free in a garage only 2 blocks away. 
Close to 16th St. and LoDo.
Restaurant has a good breakfast buffet.

My family and I stay at the Affinia Gardens every time we travel to New York with our children. There is not a better deal to be had for a suite that sleeps 6! Request a room on the back side of the hotel for the most quiet experience. It faces a pocket park and is lovely and almost silent. A rarity in New York! Bathrooms are small but clean, with good water pressure and nice towels. The beds are really comfortable and you can request special pillows for extra luxury. The welcome has always been incredibly warm, from the desk attendants to the doormen (especially the doormen!). We love the tea in the lobby, and the location, while a bit out of the way, is convenient to the subway and has many good restaurants within easy walking distance.

title_masked: A Wonderful Place, but a little noisy at night
text_masked:
I'll start off by saying I've stayed here many times before and love this great old historic hotel, the place where they had the very first Academy Awards ceremonies. It has a lot of romantic atmosphere, and the service is top notch and first rate. Everyone seems to care that you're having a great time. When I fell on the street the desk clerks were all very worried about me and ran around finding me bandages and things. They even had a guy who was all ready to sew me up, although my injuries were more of the scrape variety. The concierge, who had the same last name as John Philip Sousa, was extremely helpful and arranged transport to the airport and things in a very friendly way. 
I enjoyed the restaurant as well, and had a very nice tasty meal. The highlight of the meal was the freshly baked Parker House rolls, which you should not miss if you eat here. It has a very elegant ambience which makes you believe you're back in the heyday of old Hollywood.
Now for a few caveats. First of all, my suite, although elegant and roomy, was decorated in very dark colors, and didn't have a lot of light. Even finding where the light switches were located was a challenge. Mostly, especially at night, you felt a certain gloomy atmosphere because even the lights that were there were pretty small and didn't shed much light. Well, I suppose that's all right, because the place IS supposed to be haunted. There seemed to be a lot of noise around the pool, because of some kind of "teen event" which means constant screaming, usually until the wee hours. Luckily I had my earplugs. At least they didn't have anything happening one of the nights I was there. 
Other than that, though, the place is fabulous. The bathrooms are very elegant and the mini-bar is well stocked, although I had a hard time finding a glass and water to drink. The bed was roomy and comfortable and except as noted above it was a fine place to stay.
I also had a very nice spa massage, and it was very relaxing after a long day of trudging around Hollywood. All in all I'd definitely recommend this place as being well-located (just across the street from the famous Chinese theater), elegant and roomy.

We were lucky enough to get this room at a great discount. Unlike other reviews I felt our room was spacious enough and was very clean. I am not one to sleep on a firm bed so that was a little uncomfortable but thats the chance you take when away from home.The staff was wonderful and we really enjoyed ourselves.

The rate includes wi-fi, excellent continental breakfast, wine-and-cheese in early evening (both in the 2d floor lounge). Room was comfortable and fair-sized by NY standards. Good bed, linens, towels. But, what makes it stand out is the staff. The front desk, lounge staff, bellmen, could not have been more pleasant and helpful. To top it off, we wanted to take buses to MoMa then back to Penn Stn., which takes $9 in quarters for tourists. To my amazement, the desk had rolls of quarters to sell to guests. Nice work, Casablanca.

title_masked: OK - but only for a transit stay
text_masked: This hotel is located close to LAX and there's a hotel shuttle bus to take you from and to the airport. The hallway that our room was situated looked a little bit rundown so we were a bit apprehensive when we opened the door to our room. It was OK though and there was a coffee machine with Starbucks coffee, which cheered me up (there's also a Starbucks in the lobby area). The room was clean and the beds were fine, but the bathroom looked horrible - like something you would find at a cheap motel. It was, though, perfectly clean. To sum up then, if you just need one night of accommodation near the airport before moving on, it's OK.

title_masked: Happiness at the Chancellor hotel union square
text_masked: Fabulous!!!!!!!!!! Stayed many times, wont stay any where else!!!!

When staying in a city hotel, the most important thing for us by far is noise. This place is very quiet. It is new and apparently well-constructed; we heard no noise from our neighbors or the hallway. We were on a high floor, and there isn't much traffic in the neighborhood, so we had zero outside noise. The room was very well-appointed, if a little small, and the bed was very comfortable. Rooms on the north side have a partially blocked view of the city and harbor. I think internet was included, but we didn't use it. Parking was $34 per day and conveniently located directly under the hotel. You can do valet or self-park. Staff were very helpful and competent. We didn't try the hotel restaurants. Rates are significantly below those for hotels of similar quality in the city center.
The neighborhood is a formerly industrial waterfront being converted to tourist and business uses. Most of the buildings, including convention centers, are new. There are enough restaurants in the area; most are a little touristy but good. The hotel is not in the center of the city action, but it's a short cab ride from the city center. It was perfect for us: quiet but convenient to the city center. For you tourists, the various bus tour lines have stops nearby. I don't know about the subway. Convenient to the airport.

The staff was very attentive. The rooms was large, well-appointed and clean. Turn down service was available and the room was "straightened up". The hotel is well located. The food is excellent and room service was very prompt.

Hotel Andra is our go-to hotel in Seattle (we are so over the W). Beautiful, warm, modern hotel - large enough to provide great amenities but small enough to attend to details. We book the Lux Suite - a nicely sized corner room with separate bedroom. Be advised that the French doors to bedroom are louvered, not solid, so privacy is not quite complete. We recently traveled with our 12 year old daughter - requested a pull-out sofa in suite (daughter reported it was "super comfy"). Located right in the heart of "Tom Douglas world" - Lola is the hotel nosh spot with Palace Kitchen and Dahlia Lounge within a block (make your reservations a few days in advance!). One of our favorite French bistros, Le Pichet, is 3 blocks away, as is great shopping. Only drawback is due to the original 1920s layout: very small bathrooms (but clean, well designed and cool). Didn't find this to be a problem. Very friendly, helpful staff thoughout. Highly recommended.

Spent a night on a business trip at this sprawling hotel near the SJ airport. The rooms and furniture are older, although the desk chair seemed fairly new. The furniture is wood and the "extra" chair was just a basic dining room-style chair that probably once served as the desk chair. The TV was an older version - that kind that we used to think of as large - and tucked up in a corner near the ceiling. It was clean and the bed was comfortable. Nothing fancy but for the $99 group rate it wasn't bad. Two things to consider: 1. It's not well insulated for sound. Conversations in the hallway were crystal clear, and I could hear the person in the room above me every time he or she walked across the room, flushed the toilet, etc. 2. It is spread out over a large area so there's a lot of walking from lobby to room.

Great Location with a very, very outstanding Staff, especially Rosie in the Diamond 14th floor lounge. Other than not having a pool to hangout during my down time, I would definitely come back and recommend

The hotel is located in an excellent location - it was right in Union Square, located next to a BART terminal for transportation to and from the SF airport. I would definitely recommend getting a MUNI pass - my husband and I were in SF for 5 days and this pass gives you unlimited access to the cable cars, buses and street cars for a total of 7 days - it's $27/person - no need to rent a car. We used the pass for transportation to Candlestick Park (take the 79x bus), Fisherman's Warf, Haight/Ashbury district, etc. As far as the Herbert Hotel goes - it was very basic. We stayed in room 602, and there was a bed, bathroom, one chair and a wardrobe (no dresser/drawers). The maid service made the bed daily and left new towels (2) - that was it. The bathroom was not cleaned, nor were the sheets changed during our stay. There was a drink vending machine on the second floor, but no ice machine. There was a coffee maker in the room, but we had to request actual coffee/cups. The bed was comfortable, which was all that really mattered to us, since we were only in the hotel to sleep. Overall, I'd say the Herbert definitely served the purpose for the money that we paid. We had a great time - the 49ers tied the Rams, but at least we didn't lose :) I would stay here again as long as I could get the same cheap rate.
Great location Gracious and helpful staff Lovely amenities We'll be back!

I stayed here Sunday night, May 27, 2012. It's a nice place, very clean and new, modern style. The staff was friendly, the room was large and nicely decorated. The beds were unusually small. Also the tub was tiny, like a typical motel tub, even though the bathroom was huge, but it wasn't a problem. Oddly enough, our room had a microwave, but no mini fridge, which I was counting on. The only thing I really didn't like about the place was that the parking lot was a pay lot, which the public could use and cost $18 for a 24 hour pass at the front desk. I've just always hated getting ripped off on parking when I'm a guest. It's not like you're staying in a cramped downtown hotel, built before cars were invented. This place is right by the huge galleria, where everything was designed to accommodate the car culture we live in. I think you should get a parking space with a hotel room, but that's only my opinion. Anyway, I'd stay there again, it's a good location with easy freeway access, so I can recommend it to you.

At first I was very impress because of the price and the parking included. And close to Time Square, visiting with my mom. Got there, they are telling me I have free Internet in the room, Awesome. Get in the room, one bed...I reserved 4months in advance and ask for a two bed room and didn’t get it and now there are no more rooms left. The mattress was I think as old as the building, very uncomfortable so were the pillows. I had a room with the elevator right on side...could sleep because all we heard was that. Very noise, you could hear in the room aside. I stayed 4 days; I had to come back downstairs to have my room cards reactive three times! No hot water in the afternoon. And the best for the last, they misplace my car key! Brand new car and they lost my car keys..... The employee put them under another room that didn’t have car keys. I had to go myself look for my keys in the security office. I read the previous comments about the rat trap under the bed and I’m glad I didn’t check under the bed. I wouldn’t recommend this hotel to anyone. Even if I had a free night I wouldn’t go, just to give an idea how unpleasant my stay was.

title_masked: Perfect for Universal Studio and Great buffet
text_masked:
After NYC, this hotel provides a relaxed and resort style feelings. Within 5 - 10 mins walking distance to Universal Studio. There are also free pick ups from the theme park from the hotel.
Walk 15 mins downhill and you will get to a subway that takes you to Hollywood Boulevard :-).
The only problem being walking uphill to the hotel on your way back. It was a steep hill :-),... We found a way of overcoming this - there is a trolley bus that takes you up the hill to Universal studio and from there it is a easy walk to the hotel.
Best thing - the fabulous seafood buffet - on one should miss. I have never felf more satiated bboth in quality and quantity,,, Great service and everyone stops by to ask about your holiday...

title_masked: There are better values close to the airport
text_masked:
We chose this place because of its proximity to LAX and the reasonable price. It is actually the farthest away among several hotels along the airport strip and , at $135 nght, there are better values. Nothing terribly wrong with the place: reception was friendly and quick, our room was reasonably sized, with a comfortable bed, a 37" flat screen TV and a view of an oddly open area out the back. The TV had been added recently and the nice artwork was placed awkwardly on the wall just beside the TV, where it must have been before the large TV was added. They had not correctly charged me for the CAA rate and it took some time to sort this little detail out (saving me all of $10).
The Radisson, which is the closest to the airport (they all are on the airport flight path, so will have the same landing noises) is about the same price.
Nice feature is that there is a trolley that serves all these airports and runs to Manhattan Beach and a couple of shopping locations at a cost of $5 each. Manhattan Beach is definitely worth a visit.

title_masked: Beautiful hotel, great location, personable staff!
text_masked:
This hotel is in a great downtown Denver location. We were able to easily walk to our restaurant reservations in Larimer Square. The bellmen are super friendly and helpful. In fact, the staff everywhere was professional and accomodating. The parking is expensive at $20/night, but it's on par with other hotels in the downtown area.
The room was beautiful and had a great view of the Rocky Mountains. It was a nice touch for a downtown hotel to have windows that opened as well. The bed was plush and comfortable. I did take a bath in the oversized tub. Very enjoyable, though my suggestion would be to have bath salts in the room. 
This was the first time I had brought my dog to the property and I was amazed with the pet-friendly accomodations. They had bottled water and treats awaiting my pup and they offered complimentary dog walking throughout the day. Such a nice touch. 
The only thing I felt was a bit tacky was the housekeeping crew using the same elevators as the guests. Since the building seems like historic renovation, I imagine they didn't account for that in the planning. 
I would definitely recommend this hotel to couples or business travelers.

I stayed here for the first time the Fri and Sat before Sandy arrived. The location is perfect for shopping in midtown Manhattan, located between 5th and 6th Avenues, it's also only a short stroll from Times Square and the Theatre District.
While not cheap; I don't believe the term exists in Manhattan; it had everything required. My double room was an adequate size, bed was comfy and shower was good, only gripe was there was no shower gel only bars of soap. I was also surprised that on the 12th floor I could open up my window fully, a word of warning for anyone travelling with children.
Free WiFi and free bottled water was very welcome, as was being able to borrow an international charger. Printing off boarding passes is made very simple with a dedicated PC in the members lounge.
I only took breakfast in the hotel on the second day, continental breakfast was reasonable value at $11 and the dining room is very pleasant with crisp white linen and silverware, a nice break from coffee on the move!
I didn't spend much time in the hotel and unfortunately did not have time to use the leisure facilities but I would stay again based on this experience.

We were in NY for a city break and wanted to be in midst of all the Times Square action. This hotel proved to be the perfect choice in terms of location. Few blocks from Times Sqaure and Broadway, it gave me ample opportunity to walk back and forth. It is located very close to Hearald Sqaure and Macy, adding to its location advantage. The room size for downtown Manhattan was impressive. We asked to be on higher floor and were pleased with the large pane window opening right out to the magnificient Empire State Building. 
The staff was pleasing and i'd like to mention the good level of cleanliness. Overall a great experience to be breathing Manhattan spirit!

title_masked: Cool but compact room, great service
text_masked:
Stayed in a corner, cityview room, which is a little larger than most rooms and has a great freestanding bath (which is nice and deep, and open to the room) and a great view of mid-town and the ESB.
The design of the room is great with an industrial-mid century feel, but despite being a larger room it still felt a little tight and awkward in parts, and the unusually high amount of scrapes and patch-up paint on some corners (for such a new hotel) made me think others found it a little awkward to get their bags in and out too. No big deal, just a shame in such a nice-looking space it wasn't thought out a little more by the architects. Also, there's only one small space for one bag in the closet, so extra luggage ends up on the floor (maybe add a bag-stand, management?). Maybe the standard size rooms make better use of their limited space? I'm just not sure of the value of paying extra for the corner room if you're after more space.
The staff were lovely and gave exactly the service you want when you stay in a small boutique hotel. They remember your name, they always have a smile on their faces, they give you umbrellas when it rains, they get you take out from local restaurants and deliver it to your room! The best service I've had in a NYC hotel, with absolutely no hint of pretentiousness.
The restaurant was closed while I stayed, so a simple breakfast was provided. A nice touch, though it was very basic and felt like it was temporary and kind of thrown together. Still, nice to be able to grab something before heading out for the day.
Two other small things, the AC was REALLY loud and right above the bed, and made it hard to get to sleep the first few nights. The traffic here can be a bit loud, so I preferred AC over traffic, but not ideal. And they seemed to have way less cable TV channels than most hotels, which seems a bit cheap. Weird.
Location is great, moments to great restaurants like La Esquina, Bathazar, and all Nolita and SoHo has to offer. Overall, I would stay again, I think I just expected a touch more on some of the details due to it's excellent ranking.

We came to the Homewood suites for a whirlwind weekend wedding and were delighted by the hotel and the service we received. The rooms were beautiful, clean and well equipped, AND they had fully stocked kitchens which was awesome. The even better part was the complimentary cocktail hour with Chef Matt, and complimentary dinner and breakfast provided by the hotel. Overall it was a wonderful stay for a reasonable price. STAY HERE! You will not be disappointed!

I was very surprised at how clean and new the bathrooms were...all upgraded with ganite very nice. Rooms were clean and well kept, and nice to have a fridge and microwave. I stayed at a couple of others on PCH in the same are, and believe me you will want to stay at Rodeway Inn, as the others were much older dirty and not clean......Worth the money here for sure.

Nice hotel with good service. Great location for JHU, a little remove from the downtown waterfront and sports parks. Have stay here twice when travleing to the Baltimore. Prices are typical for a larger city, high.

A group of family and friends stayed at this hotel for a wedding, and it couldn't have been a better choice in spite of the fact we hardly stayed in the room for very long. We were greeted with a goody bag from the soon-to-be married couple, and the staff made sure we made it to our rooms okay later on. We saw the housekeepers a few times, and they were especially pleasant and friendly.
The decor of the room was perfect. It looked and smelled nice no matter when we entered. Everything was spotless. Really, I don't think the bedroom could have been any better than it was. The location was also perfect. It was in a quiet area, but it was close enough to the action for all of us to take care of wedding preparations and shopping.
The only downside to this hotel would be the breakfast "bar". It was pretty overpriced for the amount of food served. It really wasn't anything spectacular, but we wouldn't have even touched the "bar" had we not had to be on the road early in the morning to make it home before it got too late.
Besides that small detail, our stay was perfect. We'd love to come back for a less busy weekend.

The hotel was in the perfect location for the attractions we planned to see. The room was clean and neat,The staff was very polite and was very helpful with any questions we had with directions.
A.D.

title_masked: Huge rooms, full kitchens, very clean, highly recommend!
text_masked:
Had to book a hotel on the Upper East Side of Manhattan due to a surgery at Memorial Sloan Kettering. This suite hotel was one on a list recommended by the hospital and they offer a special rate for patients. It was an easy 10 min walk to the hospital. Check in was super easy, the valet met us at the curb and grabbed our luggage for us. The front desk personnel were very efficient and gave us a street map of the city. We had a one bedroom suite that was truly huge. It had a full kitchen with a four burner stove, dishwasher and a small but full size refrigerator/freezer. There was a very large desk and chair, a vanity with ottoman, a small sofa and an easy chair. There is a digital safe in the closet. The bathroom is small but newish, all white, great tub/shower combination. The only oddity is when they redid the bathrooms, apparently the toilets were too big so they had to notch out the door so it didn't hit the toilet. Very unusual to see a hotel do something like that. The bedroom was also very big, 2 queen beds, plenty of room, built in shelving for storage. There are thermostats in both the bedroom and living room with the conditioning units in front of the window. They are apparently motion activated because even though we tried to keep the rooms cool, they always seemed warm when we returned. However they cooled down quickly and caused no inconvenience to us. Affinia also offers a small tea bar in the business center area of the lobby. They offered a small selection of organic and herbal teas. There is no restaurant but they do offer room service, which is currently delivery from one of three local restaurants, Jackson Hole (burgers and such), a diner and a Chinese restaurant. However most places in the area offer delivery, so I wouldn't hesitate to seek out food on my own. Be aware there is an early checkout fee, which might be standard for Manhattan.
Overall, this was a great hotel, very convenient within walking distance of either MSK or NY Presbyterian Hospital and I would recommend it to anyone considering a stay in this area.

Great location, close to times square but just far enough to not be busy right outside. Odd lobby system, you walk into an empty area and then must take an elevator 20 floors up to main lobby. Great room.

The first room we were given had no working heat;we were told the weather was going to warm through the weekend...we were cold! That room looked as if it had water damage...peeling paint on ceiling. The room we moved to had its own heater but we could hear everything that happened in the rooms/hallways around us. I also suspected some mold (I'm allergic and had breathing difficulties but can't say for sure it was the room). The internet connection was hit or miss....the restaurant was decent and the staff helpful, the shuttle to downtown a plus but I doubt we would stay here again!

For a last minute booked hotel, it was exactly what we needed.
The bedroom was a little small, and so was the bed, but everything was very clean. The view was really nice. The bathroom and the linenswere very clean.
Location was also good beacause you are really close from the metro !

This hotel is located on the riverfront and if you are fortunate enough to have a room which faces the river, you will be very pleased with the view!! 
The rooms are very spacious and their beds are so comfortable!! The front desk staff are very accommodating and friendly. 
Relax in the lobby area with a good book or stroll along the riverfront walk!! Enjoy your stay at the Hyatt!!

Hacienda Hotel was a very nice Spanish style hotel, very nicely decorated and layed out. The location was great for walking around Old Town. The only negative I found was the rooms were not sounds proofed enough. I heard conversations from the adjacent rooms.

At this hotel for Conference. Desk staff were friendly and efficient. Room, as always at Marriott were clean and well appointed. Your expectations are high at Marriott, and this one does not let you down. Banquet food was a little disappointing.

title_masked: Great location, accommodating service, good breakfast
text_masked: We were able to check in early during our one-night stay, which was just great. Comfy bed, room was equipped with dishes, silverware, and nice little kitchenette. Clean, quiet, slept well. The breakfast had several yummy options, hot and cold. We really appreciated being able to also have a late check out. A very relaxing and pleasant stay.

I definitely will return to this hotel. The staff was very friendly and the location was perfect. The hotel was nice, clean and the room was spacious. We never ate at the restaurants connected to the hotel but had cocktails in one each night. The staff in that restaurant was also very nice and pleasant. Really enjoyed our stay.

Ever wondered what the difference in Springhill Suites and TownPlace Suites is? Well I always wondered but never inquired. On 07-1-12 after my son's track meet I stopped by and decided to ask what the difference was. The difference is TownPlace Suites has a full kitchen with full-size appliances, and outdoor pool and Springhill doesn't have a kitchen and have a indoor pool and whirlpool. Last week I wrote a review raving over how I enjoyed Springhill but after staying at TownPlace, TownPlace is my choice of lodging. My family and I enjoyed a 2 bedroom suite with full-size appliances. The windows actually open. I was WOW'd!!! The manager gave me a rate of only $89.00. Yes, only $89.00 for a 2 bedroom suite. Every thing you need is available within arms reached. The manager was very courteous and very helpful. I need a super late check out and I was granted what I needed. The management is very caring. The location is awesome, .09 miles to Harris Teeter, less than 10 mins to UNC Charlotte, restaurants within 3 mins. My only complaint is the frying pan was missing out of the unit so it took us a little longer to cook breakfast but again the manager was happy to allow us to stay in the unit until we were completely ready. I highly recommend this hotel for lodging and I will not only be back to this location when I am in the area but this will be my choice when traveling other places.

I booked a suite at the Adolphus Hotel in Dallas for my wife's 50th birthday. She is a tea enthusiust so I also had a supprise High Tea set up for her wiith her mother and sisters to attend. Everything was perfect. She said it was the finest Tea she had been to. Detail and service was fantastic. The room was far beyond expectations. Service was incredable but not over bearing.

title_masked: Comfortable. VERY clean. Would stay again, with a few tips.
text_masked: Subway at the end of the street, safe in room, umbrella, coffee maker, good AC, higher-end decor, restaurant adjacent, friendly and helpful staff, CLEAN, lots of towels, will hold luggage after check-out, comfortable-sized double double room. 2 beds, larger nightstand, phone, alarm/radio, desk, office chair, bureau, wall-mounted TV. Average per night was $260 (taxes and all) for 4 and we weren't offered any upgrades. Did get a 15% off coupon for breakfast in the restaurant, but, didn't want to waste time sitting for that, so, we didn't use it. Stayed on top floor, but, had hallway/stair door noise. Room door almost seems open when you approach it, so, make sure to pull it shut, so it locks. For some reason, kept getting 3 washcloths for a room booked for 4 and didn't get any more when I asked at the desk, though they said they'd send them up. Got a few more the one day I left a note for housekeeping, then, back to 3, though I tipped every day. No continental breakfast, or, coffee in the lobby, even. Try THE AMSTERDAM GOURMET on the corner across the street--just the thing. Wish they would have promoted that so I would have known earlier in my trip. No mirror near a plug outside the bath, so, getting ready, or even into the bath, is more time consuming than necessary. Blackout curtains were short. Had to go outside in the rain to access the restaurant, though the door through the hotel was open earlier (when there was no rain). Clean is my number one priority and it was spotless and the location couldn't be more convenient. Any minor inconveniences noted were just thoroughness on my part.

From the moment we checked in to the moment we left we couldn't fault this hotel.
Ideal location, just off Times Sq, reception welcoming, staff polite and courteous throughout. The room was fab for a family of four with 2 x Queen size beds, and all the usual mod cons. Standards of cleanliness were excellent, towels and bed sheets changed daily. Continental breakfast on the 2nd floor each morning from 7am until 10pm was a treat, and set us all up for the day ahead. A good range of bagels, pastries, cereals, juices, fruit and hot coffee and tea made it all the more good value for money. Daily wine tasting, and complimentary crisps were a bonus.
Given the location I would have expected a little noise, but there was known whatsoever and it was a real pleasure to stay, and one hotel I would definatley recommend. If in New York again I will certainly be seeking out this hotel gain.

This is a much more grown up mainstream take on boutique than W. Room is stylish, airy and modern without being pretentious, and a comfortable bed and pillows. None of the tacky nightclub feel of the W or Bryant Park common areas, or the smugness of 60 Thomson or the Bowery. The front desk and host managed to be hip without saying Whatever, Whenever, What is your Wish, and use ipad to point me the right direction for a barber when I arrived on Sunday.
There was reference to a 'welcome drink' on the scrolling ad that was on when I entered the room, but it didn't happen during my check-in. No matter, there is what they call "pantry" in the lobby, "serving drinks and snacks". That's overselling it a bit. It's a guy with a Gaggia, some tiny muffins, and the usual US take on fruit (polished apples and oranges and far too large and shiny to eat).
Soft drinks from the minibar at no extra charge is mature, but on the three days I was there the only sugar free beverage was water. No tea or coffee in the room, so I did visit Gaggia man downstairs more than I thought I would.
Room service is not extortionate, but there are plenty of better options with a minute or two walk.
Design improvements would include a decent shaving mirror, some accessible power sockets near the desk, a bath, and it would have been nice not to have to have to call the host for late laundry return, a button sewing kit and and ironing board.
However, when the tone of a place is right, these niggles matter less. This is much more BA/Lufthansa business class then Virgin Upper Class. I prefer sober, professional, and this hit the target most of the time

My stay at Embassy Suites was absolutely exceptional. I was treated with the upmost generosity and customer service by all the staff. The young lady at the front desk was gracious enough to allow me to use the Business Center upon my arrival [before check in time] and then assisted me with directions later in day. The hotel was superbly clean and quiet. The manager's reception [Happy Hour FREE drinks for 2 hours with snack bar] was phenomenal and not something many if any of the hotels I've ever stayed at offers. And the COMPLIMENTARY HOT breakfast [you name it they had it] was the topping on the cake.

This hotel provided an very updated, clean, quiet room. The staff was great. We felt safe and the location was very convienient to downtown and the Stockyards. I would highly recommend it. The price was great and we got way may then we expected.

title_masked: Inexpensive hotel in a Good location
text_masked: Stayed at this hotel for 2 nights with 2 other girlfriends. Hotel is a bit old, but price is decent considering its location. Room is clean and beds are comfy. Centrally located and easy walking distance.

I would like to thank Deanna at the frontdesk for her excellent assistance on all needed requirements. Correct restaurants reservations. Also to commend the nice supervisor and manager of the Tremont Hotel, Chicago, IL. Congrats to you all!
Mario Geller, MD

This is my first trip to San Francisco and I received a very warm welcome from Mr [NAME] G and Mr [NAME] P at COVA. They were really humble & sweet and checked us in as quick as possible !! Excellent room, very clean, quick check in and the staff was very cooperative and helpful. They guided us to the best tours available around !! We had options to stay at Marriott & Hilton at discounted prices but we chose COVA and that was the right one !!

My wife and had stayed here over Labor Day weekend and it was our first time to San Fran. At first my wife would had preferred a hotel at a more touristy spot like Fishermen's Wharf or Union Square but at the end she appreciated the location of this hotel because it was so centrally located to all the touristy spots around the city. The buses and cable car were so close to the hotel. Plus there was typically a longer line to get into the cable cars and buses at the other hotels in the more popular spots than at this location. If we went back we probably wouldn't stay here again mainly because we saw so many other hotels we would like to try. Not because of the service, I felt the service was good and the rooms were OK, you do hear noise from the streets as mentioned in previous postings which I guess can be an issue if you have problems sleeping with any noise in general but we don't. So for me this is an average (3 out 5) hotel at best at a very descent location.

title_masked: The bad review are correct in most respects - please read.
text_masked:
I stayed for 10 nights - it was prepaid so the front desk will not refund.
Property stolen from room - on the only day in 10 that a maid came to change the sheets - I mean the rooms are never serviced, how bad is that! You have to get towels and soap from reception.
The lifts break down often.
While the location is great - spare a little more $$ and get something else close by - I would have doen this if I had not pre paid - you have been warned!! I suspect the so called good reviews on here about the Carter are dummy reviews by the hotel, it really is that bad.

This hotel has a good location, a few block walk to the Riverwalk. Although it's next to the freeway and near a train station, it was very quiet. The room was very clean and staff was very courteous. Breakfast was good. The only thing they could improve was the room was very dark. It would be nicer if they could get some more light in the room, but it's a great value compared to many of the other hotels in the area. Also, very convenient parking and nice lobby. Room was also very large with an extra seating area.

title_masked: I Will Not Stay Here Again
text_masked:
I gave The Curtis 3 stars because the front desk, valet, and management staff have been so friendly and accommodating. However, I had suspicions about its cleanliness when at check-in, I viewed the smudged elevator walls and carpet that had clearly not been vacuumed recently. I would not let my bare feet touch the floors in my room because it just didn't seem very clean. My suspicions were confirmed when I returned to my room after a conference and found that the beds had been made but my trash had not been emptied, my nightstand still had two glasses and melted ice in the bucket from the night before, the lid was next to the t.v. where I had left it, and the dresser that held the t.v. was dusty. 
I am an admitted hotel snob, and I only ended up here because I tried to save my company some money by using Hotwire. Still I was prepared to give The Curtis a great review based on the attentive service. I'm sorry, but no level of attentiveness makes an unclean room ok. I should add that a spot in the shower which I saw at check-in and believed to be a permanent mark was no longer there after cleaning. I can't begin to express how disturbing that is. I will never stay here again and I am strongly questioning whether I will ever use Hotwire again.

This was a nice place to stay while in town for a conference. The hotel staff were friendly, helpful and knowledgeable. The hotel is very modern and well furnished. The bed was comfortable and everything in the room functional and pleasing to the eye.
The location is convenient with a lot of restaurants nearby as well as a grocery store and drug stores. If you're using public transportation, it is right next to the San Diego Trolley and numerous bus lines.
The pool and poolside bar are pretty cool, and the lounge on the ground floor was a nice place to read and have a drink during happy hour. They have complimentary coffee (both hot and iced!) in the morning and I think there was a free wine reception although I never partook.

The Days Inn reservation center made our reservation at the wrong location from where we specifically asked for. When we checked into our room at the wrong location, the toilet plugged up on the first time used. Staff said they would bring us the plunger to unclog the toilet instead of doing it themselves!! There were two TV remotes in the room, very confusing to use and they didn't work hardly at all. One had to press until their finger hurt to get the channel or volume changed.

On a planned one night stay we chose this hotel based on location and price. We named our price and it was accepted. Check in was quick. We stayed in room 2502 which had one queen size bed and one window looking out to Times Square and a window wall looking out on 45th Street. The room was very clean but is much in need of a rehab. With the exception of the television the furnishings of the room were dated. The vent in the bathroom was rusted, The room did have a coffee maker with both regular & decaf coffee and an assortment of teas. The ice bucket and extra toilet paper was in the closet. There was a hairdryer on the bathroom sink. We stay in NYC about five or six times a year and this was one of the larger rooms we have stayed in. Unless you were right by the door, the room was very quiet.

title_masked: It's practically perfect in every way.
text_masked:
Had a great stay and appreciated the managers accomodating our request or a high floor!
Walking disance to the village and all the cool restaurants,brownstone buildings and shops.
You will not regret staying at this Courtyard,rest assured.

title_masked: Very nice, great views, but dont stay unless you are there for convention center
text_masked: We had a 4 day seminar here. Thehotel has an awesome view, request a high floor. We were on the 30th with a perfect view of lake michigan, navy pier, etc. The room are very spacious. They probably need a little touch up, they are a little dated. Yet, it was clean. The bed was a little uncomfortable, just a sheet and very htin blanket on bed. No comfy comforter or any other nice sheets. This hotel is 3 miles, 25 minutes chicago time away from all the things to do, so i would stay at a hotel closer in to town, if you dont have business here.

title_masked: Charming boutique hotel in really convenient spot
text_masked: The Chatwal is a gorgeous hotel. The rooms were fabulous - we had a suite and a room for our grown up family - but the most important difference is the staff. They were friendly and polite and nothing was too much trouble. The technology in the room was fun although the high tech toilet was a bit scary! It's just off Times square and we found that very convenient.

Just got back from a weekend trip to the city with my mom. We stayed two nights at the Hotel Palomar and we will def. stay again. 
The location is fantastic. Close enough to Union Square, but far enough outside the hustle and bustle. the lobby is small, but it is San Francisco after all.
The staff is by far some of the best hotel staff I have encountered. They were friendly, and on the ball. It was my birthday weekend, so what did they do? Sent up a bottle of wine and cupcakes! Seriously...What hotel does that? Everyone at Hotel Palomar was awesome!
The room was good. Comfortable and clean. Nothing to fancy, but we weren't spending a lot of time in the room. 
AM Coffee and Hot Chocolate was great. Would suggest coffee be a little stronger.

We pre registered because we arrived in Chicago before our check in time. The lady at the front desk told us to go ahead and enjoy the free breakfast! The made to order omlettes were fantastic, and the selection was phenomenal. The lobby was gorgeous! I loved the fountains and foliage. There were plenty of elevators for the large crowd of stylists there for America's Beauty Show. Our room was spacious and clean, and I can't imagine having a bad view! All staff were extremely polite and welcoming. If I come back to Chicago, I will definitely consider coming back here!

Just stayed here for 4 nights; had room 301. Service was good: fresh towels every day, bed made up. WiFi worked for me in the 3rd floor, even though they admit it might not reach higher than the 2nd. No problems even with larger photo uploads.There is an alternative lounge/room for Internet too. Cell reception is non-existent though!
The fridge in the room is nice, but I only used it as a table. A table and a chair would have been more useful actually. Walls and doors are really thin. You can hear people walk and talk when passing by like they are inside the room. Luckily other guests were pretty civilized. Water pressure and temperature is excellent, but the shower has only a fixed head, I don't like that. There is a TV in the room, but unfortunately mounted left and pretty high up from the be, so the viewing angle is close to unusable.
The location is really good imho. Grocery, Radio Shack, a pub around the corner and subway a few blocks away; so is Central Park. The M60 bus to LGA is also very close if you need that.

title_masked: Nice boutique hotel but you will pay for it
text_masked:
Nice relatively centrally located hotel.
Excellent attentive staff that accommodated early checkin.
Comfortable spacious rooms. The room rate was market but extras were very very high priced including breakfast, parking and internet. Health club was good but not excellent
Excellent choice based on service, location and room but do not be fooled by the base room price. This is and expensive property.

1.Rooms were just marginal for the price we paid. There were marks on the walls and doors. It was just sort of clean.
2.The furnishings looked like bad imitations of something more elegant. It is like the hotel tried to make it look good for with less expensive items. 
3. At one point there was a man lying in the street while one man held him down and another was trying to steal his shoes as we and others walked by. There drunks all over the place.
4. Outside my son's window in the afternoon a man was sitting on a box going to the bathroom.
5. We felt very unsafe, so much so we spent more money we had not planned on to rent a taxi to take us back and forth to the ball game, because we didn't want to walk down the streets after dark. 
6.Not a good place to take kids to because of the surrounding element.
7.After the game we went downstairs to the bar to get a drink and there was a homeless woman sitting in the lobby trying to sleep on one of the seats.
8.It was definitely the worst place I have ever stayed in.
9. Poor service at the bar, but it was not the bar tender's fault. She was the only one on duty trying to serve drinks and keep the tables cleared. She made a great drink, but I felt sorry for her trying to keep up with the amount of people in there and trying to bus tables. Even so, she was very personable.

title_masked: Pretty on the outside, great location BUT...
text_masked: They certainly spent money in making the interior look great. There are nice views of Camden Park. But, hotel staff is not helpful, sometimes rude and the rooms are not in their best shape. I will not go back, for sure!

My family spent the night in Chicago during spring break. The staff was great to us and our kids. They had a goodie bag for the kids when we arrived with a scavenger hunt that they loved. The indoor pool and sundeck on the 17th floor provided great views and fun. We enjoyed our stay and all the amenities.

This hotel is located right in the center of historic Philadelphia. The room was large and quiet. It was fun to walk from the hotel to Rittenhouse Square. If you have not been to Philadelphia in awhile, the downtown area is much more energetic. The breakfast in the adjoining restaurant was good and convenient.

Stayed at the Raddison by the bay in San Fran the first week of Oct/2012. Average stay is 350/day.The room we had did not have a fridge, which was a dissapointment,the washroom was clean and modern.. They offer a continental breakfast daily but it is extra. The best thing about the hotel is that it is close to most of the must see things, oh i almost forgot,parking at the hotel is 42 dollars a day ouch. MFK

title_masked: Very disappointed, room request not honoured and hotel was tired
text_masked:
The hotel is in a great location and was easy to get around and the anytime anywhere concierge service was handy during our stay. I regret to say that I doubt I'll be staying in a W again, especially given I'm a consultant who spends lots of time in hotels and am a Starwood Hotels fan. I paid my own money for two rooms to stay in a W on this special occasion in NYC; it definitely wasn't worth it.
I booked in October/early November for a trip in late January 2012. I was staying for two special occasions, my 30th birthday and my mother's 60th birthday. I requested 2 king size bedrooms on the same floor. Here are some observations and reflections from our stay (Jan 25 - Jan 31 2012):
1. When we arrived they tried to put us in a double rooms with no compensation
2. Made no reference to my request for two rooms on the same floor - when i brought it up they said a large party decided to extend last minute and couldn't honour it, they told me to try the following day, when i went back the following day they said not to bother as there was construction and we'd be bothered by the noise. Again no apologies that they couldn't do anything to help us
3. Two friends sent cards to the hotel with our names and the dates of our stays on them scheduled to arrive for the start of the stay, we were not advised of any cards or mail arriving at the hotel for our attention. Given two friends sent cards, I believe the hotel let us down, rather than the US Postal Service but obviously impossible to know for sure
4. The room keys were deactivated every time you put them in the lift to access the room floors. We had to keep one for the lift and the other for the room which meant we each needed to carry around 2 keys! We had to have our room keys reset several times, I mentioned something to the hotel; they sent someone up to reset our room lock, but this was to no avail. They did remove some charges from our room which was nice and appreciated. 
5. On checkout on Jan 31st the woman serving us was unpleasant, inaccurate and rude when we enquired if our credit card had been charged for the additional items on the rooms. Not the service I expect from a W hotel. 
6. The overall standard of the hotel rooms has declined, the bathroom was looking tired with brown mould in the shower.
