There was a champagne cork on the floor in the room when we arrived indicating the level of cleaning could use improvement, and our rooms were inconstantly refreshed with toiletries and bathrobes during our stay. 
7. I wrote a feedback note at the hotel when we left, no one has contacted me regarding my stay. Such a simple thing to do!

The internet wouldn't work, called front desk for wash cloths the night before and received them the next morning. No showers before bed that night. The riverwalk view is part of the river that is not walked or lit up with Christmas lights. Could see the lights in the distance. Paid alot of money for the view and didn't get it. Very over rated :(

title_masked: Very good facility for business meetings
text_masked:
I stayed here for a couple of days on business and our meetings were on-site. The staff was experienced, friendly and attentive, and everything went smoothly. The food was good, although nothing unusual. The hotel room was quiet and the bed was fine. Location is central and convenient. In other words, it is a very good facility for business meetings.
The major drawback is that although everything was clean, the facility looks tired and needs a face lift. The obviously low wattage lights in the hotel room reinforces that impression. If I were planning a trip to Chicago on personal time, I would look at other options.

We had a wonderful stay!! Beautiful redone rooms and the best service ever!!!! I would stay there again for sure. If traveling in the area you will not be unhappy with this hotel!!!! Alson besure to sign up for the Choice promotions. We stayed enough times on our trip to qualify for free rooms!!

It was late when we arrived at the hotel. The rate was great which should of tipped us off to the place but we are so tired we didn't pay attention. The staff was very nice but once in our room it smelled like stale cigarette smoke and there were ashes on he night stand in a 'no smoking' room. We aired it out a bit and went to sleep. Next morning we got a different room which was ok, After taking a shower I reached for a towel and looked at it before drying off and noticed a spot of blood on it but it certainly wasn't mine, We went to the office and said we were checking out. I gave him the towel and he apologized and said he would speak to housekeeping. He only gave me back the money for our second night stay instead of total bill. The only reason I didn't give it a 'terrible' rating is because the desk clerk did try to help us with another room.

We stayed here for one night to visit a family member at John Hopkins. Although the hotel was clean and in close proximity to the ball field, I would not choose this hotel again. I tried to get some
sleep after a long drive only to be awakened by rude patrons from 11:30 until about 4:00am yelling and laughing in the hallways. It appeared that this hotel was used for something other than sleeping. 
The so called valet was parking our car in the small paved area in front of the hotel or on the 
busy street next to 2 bars. I really did not need this extra worry about my car getting damaged.
I would recommend staying in the Harbor East area at the Hilton Garden Inn or the Homewood Suites. Harbor East offered many more nice options for dining and shopping. There is a Whole Foods store right around the corner and many nice shops to browse in.

Our family of five stayed here at the last minute the night before we had to fly out. It is an old hotel and the rooms show it. We stayed in the Bayview Suite which was like a small apartment. Plenty of room for five. There was a little noise from people partying on the roof but it quieted down early. We didn't really notice any street noise. The view from the rooftop deck is great. The valet was very friendly and helpful. The hotel is walking distance to everything downtown but the area was pretty sketchy after dark, especially with kids. Overall, the price was good, location was good and I'd stay there again.

Second visit. This time a room at the front where we could see and hear the cable cars if the window was open. Practically instant hot water and great pressure in the shower, perhaps because it was the 6th floor. Great location and easy for public transport with cable cars passing the door, buses and trolleybuses only a street away and the Muni (metro), street cars and Bart about a 10 minute walk. Parking seems expensive anywhere in the centre of the city. Didn't try the restaurant for lunch as we were away till the evening, but a good variety of bars, diners and restaurants nearby.

Stayed for eight nights. Cannot understand some guests said did not feel welcome.
Every member of staff was frendly in all parts of the hotel. Noisy yes being downtown but perfect location.Clean Rooms.
Will stay here again.

Stayed here one night after missing a flight. The location is great, a 15 minute cab ride from O'hare and next to a metro stop on the blue line. The room was clean and great. The room service was great as well.
It was my first stay in Chicago, but it seems like a great value to be in a great hotel for flying in/out of O'hare and to be a decent metro ride to downtown. I would consider staying here again.

Comfortable, modern, sleek, hip, good location, great for our girls weekend (young 50ish girls). Wonderful bed, nice bathroom, floor to ceiling windows. Only thing that they might address is better lighting in the rooms. Highly recommended.

I stay in hotels all over the USA and I have to say that even the more pricey locations don't provide service any more accommodating than Crossland/Fossil Creek.Clean rooms,friendly staff,convenient location,what more do you want? Simply put it's the best value in the DFW area.

The Adolphus is a special hotel. It has Old World charm, the warmest, friendliest staff and is fabulously located. If you want to feel special without paying an arm and a leg, we strongly recommend this hotel.

title_masked: Exceptional Service from Start to Finish
text_masked:
A couple days prior to my stay I received a phone call from someone on the hotel's staff confirming my reservation and asking if there was anything that they could do to make our stay more enjoyable. In my many years of traveling I have never had that happen.
This attention to detail continued throughout our stay; the hotel personnel were always friendly, knowledgeable, and courteous. 
The room was not only a good size, but it was also spotless. Another bonus were the comfortable beds. Add to this an exceptional location (in a safe neighborhood within walking distance to shops, decent restaurants, even delis, museums, and the theater district) as well as a very good continental breakfast in their library and you have a very special place.... the Hotel Elysee. 
I stay in NYC about six or more times a year and think this hotel is the best of the many places I have tried. 
It was raining our last day there and the desk staff graciously lent both my sister and me umbrellas. As I said, "Exceptional from start to finish."

Was here for a business trip for 3 nights and all 3 nights the internet connectivity was really bad.. and i could see people sitting in the lobby using the net since it didnt work in their room.
Coffee machines were usually dry or didn't have milk :(
If you just want a place to stay overnight its an "OK" place!

title_masked: Stay like a King, pay like a commoner!
text_masked:
We have stayed several times at the Century City Intercontinental, most recently at the end of October 2012 for our son's wedding which was held at the property. I can comfortably say that from the perspective of an overnight guest to that of a major event customer this place delivers, and then some.
We've been upgraded to a better suite nearly every time we have stayed here. By the end of the wedding weekend most of the staff knew most of my family. If that sounds trite, imagine how helpful it is when you are searching for someone and a bellman asks, "looking for your wife, she's right outside."
We love the lobby bar at this hotel. Unlike many of the hotels we have visited in LA this one has a hopping bar scene all evening and into the night (or maybe that was just US!) and the lobby gets lived in by the guests. There are also great outdoor seating areas that get used by the guests. This gives the place a very warm, lived in feeling. No one wants to be the only one sitting in the lobby of a hotel and that rarely seemed to be the case here.
In many hotels I have visited the bell staff seems to be dedicated to carrying your bags in and out. At the IC they are more like roving concierges. It was unusual to move through the hotel without seeing one of their helpful bellmen in the halls or the elevators. They were omnipresent and omniscient. Truthfully, we never spoke to the concierge once, as the bell staff handled everything we needed instantly.
The views from the various rooms we have had have been great. East facing rooms get a nice view of the city and the mountains plus the Hollywood sign. West facing rooms get stellar sunsets over the Pacific, on clear days. Price? It's not cheap but it's a lot cheaper that many other fine LA hotels and the service here beats everyplace else we have stayed in town. Give them a try.

This hotel is fine, but I don't really understand the rave reviews from other reviewers. My room on the 9th floor had a door that opened onto a shared narrow balcony/terrace, but it faced the Four Seasons hotel so no real view. The room is very small, and the ceiling is very high - which is sort of awkward. The bathroom is nice, but it's too dark (hard to shave) and the sink didn't drain for 10 minutes. Service seemed sort of perfunctory to me. No sense of luxury or welcome ar far as I could see. Also the bed was short and my feet hung over it, and I'm only 6' 1". 
I stayed 5 nights, and I would not stay here again. I don't really see what was so great. A big chain would have been just as good. Maybe it's just me, since others seems to love the Teatro.

title_masked: Club Like Atmosphere and Service....Top Marks!
text_masked: The Chatwal is an oasis of luxury just off of Times Square. The property is beautiful and opulent, yet not gaudy or ostentatious. It is clean and stylish. The staff were beyond attentive and super responsive to every need. Long story short-- this propery and is staff are world class.

title_masked: All you could want in a Hotel in NYC
text_masked: Had a 5 night break at The Stay Hotel. This hotel is literally 50 yards from Times Square. Clean and comfortable, really comfy beds. Towels and beds changed daily. Staff are most helpful, would definitely stay here again, no compalints at all. Don't waste money on bigger and more expensive hotels, everything you want is at this fabulous hotel.

I am staying at Suburban Extended Stay Hotel Charlotte longer that I expected to be. I arrived at 3:00 am and was greeted by a security guard. The manager promptly came down and checked me in. I have received the best service from the staff and feel completely safe staying here. I don’t understand the other reviews because I have received the best service - or I wouldn't still be here - 11 months later.

title_masked: Enjoyable stay at the Admiral Fell Inn
text_masked: My wife and I really enjoyed our stay at the Admiral Fell Inn. We actually live in Baltimore and decided to hire a babysitter and take a night off. The Admiral Fell Inn's experience package, which included a bottle of wine and gift certificate to a local restaurant, was perfect for us. The hotel is extremely nice and clean and the room was far bigger than expected. In addition, there are so many things to do and see around Fells Point and the immediate area that it's impossible to get bored.

This has been one of our most amazing trips and experiences ever. The Wheeler mansion is divine. The attention to detail in the hotel is beautiful. The outdoor garden area is lovely to relax and take in the atmosphere. The host was most welcoming and helpful during our stay, to recommend events or places to see, it really felt like a personalised service and experience. We decided to extend our stay and our room was made available at a fantastic rate. I will recommend this hotel to friends and family it’s truly an experience that Nat and I will remember for ever.
Keep up the good work kind regards
Nik&Nat from
Australia

My wife and I had the pleasure of staying at this great hotel during our holiday travel. Our stay was amazing thanks to their wonderful staff who are very attentive and courteous. We had the pleasure of meeting Nicole and Sophie in Taipan who were very helpful, Anna in reservations, Eugene and Alex. Alex made our stay wonderful and comfortable and was very helpful with everything we needed not forgetting Lynn. Our room was comfortable with a lovely view of the Jefferson Memorial. We loved our daily walk to the farmers market. The spa was wonderful. We are conversant with Hilton hotels and Four Seasons in London and we had thought no hotel could top The Four Seasons but we were proven wrong. We look forward to our stay at Mandarin Oriental, London in November. 
Dr. & Mrs [NAME].

title_masked: In the heart of the city!
text_masked: This property is close to everything Chicago has to offer! Walk across the street in front of the hotel and you are at the Chicago River with a fabulous view. Walk across the street in the back of the hotel and you are at the Chicago Theater and multiple subway stops. The beginning of the "pedway" starts just to the side of the hotel on State Street. The pedway is a serious of underground walkways with shops and restaurants and they even have guided tours.

Great location, clean hotel, helpful staff. The rooms a little outdated but nothing horrible.
Free WiFi if you a member of the travel program. However, if you do not use your device for a few hours, you would have to reconnect again.
I would definitely stay there again

Other reviews mentioned that rooms are small and outdated; I agree with them, but as far as service, location and convenience, hard to beat! Took transit at front door to get to many sites , museums, walked to Chicago architecture boat tour, shopping galore! New funky looking lobby area.

we stayed one night in Seattle most recently at the Exec Hotel Pacific. Its located right on 4th and Spring St. Right in the heart of tons of great restaurants and not far from Pike Place Market and waterfront area.
the staff were extrememly friendly. Altho our room was a bit on the small side (one queen bed) it was clean and well worth the $119 that we paid for it upfront online. I'd recommend this hotel to others. You cannot beat the deal to be right downtown for this price!
 best of all little did we know the Seafair parade was happening right outside the hotel on 4th. What a fun weekend.

title_masked: Hawthorn Suites at Universal City Texas
text_masked: We enjoyed our stay at this facility. The room could have been a little cleaner and the bathroom needed some repair. The breakfast was great! The new televisions were nice as well. The mattress was a little too firm for us. All in all we will stay here again.

title_masked: Perfect for pre or post SeaTac Flight
text_masked: We (family of 4) had a king suite for one night before flight, and it was exactly what we needed. Even though we had a room facing the airport we didn't find the noise overbearing (blended with the air con "white noise") and the "sleep number" king bed (you can adjust your side's firmness) was very comfortable. However, the sofa bed wasn't great even for sofa beds, but they tried to make it more comfortable by putting a quilt on top of the springy mattress, which was fine for my kids who shared it (size was double). Front desk and housekeeping staff were awesome (the sofa bed wasn't made when we got there but the lady was there within 5 mins of my call to make it). My daughter accidentally left her Nintendo DS with all her games behind and they kept it in housekeeping until we went back to claim it upon our return to SeaTac a week after. We didn't park our car there while we're away but could have (we had discounted rates at Wally Park) for $10 a day, still very reasonable for its proximity to the airport. We'd stay there again next time we need to fly out of SeaTac.

I was in San Fran for a few days on a work trip and we were staying at Le Meridien. I had never stayed at one of their hotels and was pleasantly surprised. The staff was extremely friendly and my room (which was upgraded to a suite) had a king sized bed, an office and sitting room, and a nice big bathroom. 
Most importantly, it was in a great spot to be able to get around the city. It's in the financial district and was a $5 cab ride from the Moscone convention center for those in on business. If you're there for pleasure, walk two blocks and you'll run into the ferry building (a must see) or go a little further down and hit the fisherman's wharf area. 
A cool hotel in a great spot!

This is a small friendly boutique hotel. The rooms are very large for San Francisco and very well maintained. You are within walking distance to Union Square and a large number of stores, restaurants and wine bars plus ready access to the buses, cable car and street cars. Overall, it is a perfect location. Breakfast is included and changes each day. The quality is quite high considering it is included in the price. Overall, the hotel is great value. We will definitely return.

I finally had a chance to come visit LA after years away and was eager to try out the Angeleno per the suggestions of several of my friends. And boy, they did not disappoint! In addition to a lavish, beautifully kept property, the hotel also boasts a helpful, attentive staff and attention to detail. In particular the young man that works behind the front desk, Chris W, was incredibly helpful in getting me all settled in and made sure I had a stellar experience throughout my stay. I will be back!

title_masked: Great service and a nice room!
text_masked: I am not one who often remembers to post reviews. But I will say that I really enjoyed my stay at this Wyndham. I had read some bad reviews and was a little worried but did not need to be. The service of the hotel staff was great! I especially appreciated the Concierge David! The room was bigger and nicer than I expected. And it was great to have a separate room as we brought our baby and she could sleep without being disturbed! The location was perfect for the River Walk! The only negatives were that finding the front entrance was not the easiest, and that I did not expect to pay for parking. But overall it was great!

Omg I will never let me repeat NEVER stay in this hotel again. In all of my 56 years I have never encountered such a rude bunch of uncaring, unconcerned people. I stayed in hotel 9-21-12 thru 9-24-12 upon checkout we paid cash I discovered that $400.00 was placed on hold on my credit card for the two rooms. On 10-12-12 I called hotel and first spoke to a Julius who then transferred me to the General Manager who's name I did'nt get but both she and the clerk were extremely rude. I explained to the manager that CitiCard said that she would need to call them to let them know that the card had not been charged she refused saying she was not financial institution and that they would have to take hold off I again called the card company on three different occassions as well as hotel and they kept saying that the hotel needed to call them. After the third attempt of trying to get this resolved with the manager I just gave up. Hopefully after 30 days these charges will drop off my card. But the staff made me feel like I was bothering them like I was getting on their nerves but they don't have to worry because I will never come back there or recommend this place to anyone. I'm sure if the situation was reversed they would not want to be treated the way I was.

Great hotel, we have stayed in 2 other Manhatten hotels and was expecting another small pokey room, we certainly did not get that.
Brilliant large spacious room with 2 of the most comfortable beds have slept in in a hotel. well furnished and finished, good shower and bathroom with full range of the usual toiletries.
The lighting switches take a lil bit of getting used to and the air con was a bit noisy at times but this was not a problem as the weather was cool enough not to need to be used.
Although its listed as 54th st and Broadway and this may seem a walk downtown to Times Square this made for a lot less stress and hassle as could bypass the nightmare and maze that can be Times Square / 42nd St Station, we used 50th St which took us downtown to where we needed
Will definetly stay here again and would recommened to anyone wanting a central Manhatten Hotel without the crowds of Times Square

title_masked: Great stay for business or play!
text_masked: I took a chance and reserved a room through Priceline.com and this was the winner! It's great, nice clean room with kitchen (which I did not use) and the service was excellent, staff always had a smile on their face and greeted you whenever they passed. Good easy location to take in the sights in town or for visiting GWU. I would stay here again happily!

The hotel was beautiful. But first, I've gotta keep it real. They advertise a movie at the pool every night from May-Sept, but there was no movie during my mid-week stay. They did have a live band on Wednesday night. When I asked, they said a movie would be shown on Friday. Also, they advertise a free shuttle to local attractions. This they provided, but only with limited times for return. For example, Sea World closes at 10pm, but the last shuttle back to the hotel was at 5pm. So a cab was necessary for the ride home, which cost around $20. Thirdly, the walls between rooms are NOT SOUND-PROOF. Believe it or not, the guy in the room next to ours kept me up half the night because he was COUGHING! It was like he was in the room with us. He turned his tv on at 6am and woke us up again. All that being said, the one incredible bonus to this hotel is the staff. They were outstanding!! AManda at the main desk was so patient and kind, Jeff and Rich, the shuttle drivers - they went out of their way to make our stay a pleasure. They gave us tips on where to eat, the best sites to see, etc. Courteous, helpful, and altogether fun - these people proved that no matter what the conditions of a hotel, it's the people that make all the difference.

title_masked: Great view on empire state bldg
text_masked: Great location at a few minutes walk from empire state bldg and times square. Highest floors front rooms have spectacular view on empire state building. Beware of noise from works in adjacent mariott hotel. Ask for a room far from the works. Roof top bar is great. My room at the left corner was a bit small. Staff is extremely helpful and friendly. Pancakes at breakfast deserve to be tried. Wifi is complimentary. Good hotel overall.

title_masked: Lots of Pluses and some Minuses
text_masked:
While I believe this hotel is vey good, the layout here is not typical of a full service hotel, meaning access to the fitness centre or pizza restaurant is not through the hotel, and requires you to cross the parking out front. The Seastar restaurant operates a small lounge in the hotel and there is a tiny passageway enroute to the bathroom to get into the restaurant, however main entrance is also outside the hotel. Both restaurants appear to operate as separate businesses on the property. Some good points about the hotel:
-good deals can be had if you search around, that include free valet parking
-free wifi, newspapers and large room safe
-good sized rooms with comfy beds
-3 block access to the I5 making access to SEATAC easy
-Whole Foods on the block is great to have for sure and has a restaurant inside (and mini places to eat as well)
-one of the better ranked seafood places (Seastar) in Seattle is next to hotel, and a pizza place that is really good (and cheap) is 2 doors down
-front desk and valet staff are great as others have mentioned
Downsides are:
-location is on the edge of downtown, not very walkable for elderly or folks with children or frankly at night, we walked without issue, but if shopping you may need to take a taxi back
-the hotel does not have large public spaces you might find at other 4-5 star properties, and has a small area of the lobby as the only seating area
-the fitness centre is across the retail parking area and up an elevator or flight of stairs, not convenient at all (we watched people in towels dodging vehicles to get access), we used it and while equipment was great, location was a nuisance 
-for some strange reason the rooms do not have tea or decaf coffee in the rooms, but pods for caffeinated coffee only
-wifi works in the lobby best but was spotty on the 6th floor where we were, so we lost connections often
-mini-bar prices are astronomical (thankfully Whole Foods is open until 10 pm everyday)
-electrical plus somewhat inconvenient in terms of placement (behind the desk) for computer use etc., you may wish to bring an extension cord with several outlets to connect multiple devices
-we stayed in 2 rooms for 3 nights and sheets not changed, only towels (no signs to advise they would not be changed or request a change etc.)

My first time in a W hotel and very enjoyable. Great location and very cool lobby and bar area. Sevice was excellent both at reception and at the concierge desk, TK organised the full gambit of activities from boat ride to bliss spa experience and transport between the 2 hotels. Friendly staff made a stay on my own far from lonely. Only downside was I had half of an interconnecting room and quite noisy through adjoining door

Took the "T" Blue & Green lines from the airport for $2. Drops you next to the door to the hotel. Walked to Fenway Park in 5 minutes. Also walked to the Yawkey "T" Commuter Rail station for my Amtrak connection without problem. The hotel is nice but way over priced. I've stayed @ Disneyland for less in the Summer. The girl @ the lobby counter was nice but too chatty. Elevators are great for security but a hassle. Ice machine didn't work. Eastern Standard Kitchen is noisey & doesn't allow you to put the meal charge on your room bill.

title_masked: Great location, great service, great experience
text_masked:
Stayed at this location for Mother's Day week-end. What a great location! Just steps away from the beach, great pool area and lots of amenities. Only downside was the price at the restaurant. $21 for a simple breakfast, no wonder the Starbucks was so busy. The hotel offered a $5 rebate if you went "green" and didn't have your room cleaned daily...great idea!
Mark (front desk) was very personable and knowledgable. Only thing that was a problemwas the parking. I have disabled plates and unless we wanted to valet at $30 a day, we would have to self park ($22 per day) and walk a long distance to the hotel. Except for the parking - All in all a super place to stay.

title_masked: Two-inch roach in bathroom; I'm not going back
text_masked: Have stayed at this hotel many times over the years. Unfortunately, finding a two-inch size mega- roach in my bathtub was too much of a shock for me to ever consider this hotel again. I mean, I've seen a few roaches scurry around over the years, but I have never seen anything this size. I've stayed in hotels all over the world, but I've never seen a giant roach like this before in a hotel. I tried to give some feedback to the hotel about this, but they don't seem interested. I mean, what can you say? What could cause a giant roach like that to develop? I can only think that there's a major cleanliness problem. Too bad, beautiful lobby and wonderful location.

title_masked: No qualms recommending the hotel! Spacious and comfortable.
text_masked:
Three older women on a girls trip to the Big Apple, stayed 4 nights. Older property but large and immaculately clean rooms, housekeeping is to be commended. Two beds in a large bedroom and a comfortable (at least, she didn't complain about it!) sofabed in the living room. Nice, functional kitchen. Location was within easy walking distance of Grand Central Terminal, the Chrysler Building, and New York Public Library. Little store around the corner for quick deli and snacks open in the evening and a bigger grocery store in the opposite direction. 
I would stay there again and hope to do so soon
.
Excellent bagel spot, Vic's Bagels a couple blocks away. GLUTEN FREE bagels, btw. Toasted everything bagel with cream cheese and cilantro w/onion. I was in heaven.
For gluten-free dinner option try Nizza's up in the theater district. Beautiful fettucini, foccacia and socca for those of us who are wheat-free. Lovely sauces for the pastas and the desserts were great, too.

My husband & I stayed here for 2 nights. We chose the Ramada because of the very reasonable price over other Boston hotels. The hotel is a little ways out of the main part of the city but with the courtesy shuttle to the JFK/UMass train stop it made everything very convenient & easy to get to. The hotel layout is a little confusing with all the additions and extra doorways & hallways. Our room was clean, a good size and we were pleasantly surprised to find that we had a fridge & microwave in our room. The only problem with our room was the noisy heat/ac unit but we were so tired after our long days in the city that it didn't bother us too much. The breakfast that was included with our stay was very good (eggs, waffles, cereals, fruit, yoghurt, muffins). All of the staff at the front desk were very friendly and helpful, as were the shuttle drivers.We would definitely stay here again when visiting Boston just for all the little extras that were included. (Shuttle, breakfast, free parking, free wifi in our room)

title_masked: TOO NOISE - HOUSEKEEPING DO NOT LET REST
text_masked:
Further I was in a renovated room, they have left space between the door and the wall, so anyone can see the light from the corridor, and hear anything happen on it. 
Housekeeping start knocking the door for cleaning since 8:00 am, further I have the sign of privacy.
Concierge do not help you at all, unless you gave them a tip. When I asked if they could help me to move to the Waldorf Astoria (I was changing the hotel), in next block, the answer was, I do it if you pay me USD10. 
I know they are investing a lot in renovate the hotel, maybe the may invest in training their people in client service....

We spent a long weekend here and were happy with the hotel. The rooms were clean and spacious. The hotel was usually quiet, though Saturday night, it got a little noisy (thumping bass). The staff was friendly. The bus stop was close and we had no problems accessing public transportation from the hotel. I loved the large soaker tub, but I wish the shower had more water pressure. As another reviewer noted, it would be nice if they had thicker bath towels. The housekeeping seemed a little odd -- at one point, they took two of our used towels but didn't replaced them. At another point, they loudly cleaned every room around ours, but never cleaned our room. But, all in all, we were happy with the hotel and would definitely stay there again.

I stayed here on a business trip for 4 days mid September 12. The staff were great providing the usual good service you can expect in the USA . The hotel lacks reception space though and somewhere to sit and meet people. The only real options are the lobby (crowded and noisy ) or the bar and restaurant . Piped music here and hard floors make talking difficult . 
The suite I was in had plenty of all the right things but if you are a Brit and need your tea bring your own travel kettle. The room only has a coffee maker. 
One big disappointment in the suite was the poor tv facilities and lack of films. I appreciate you can use your pc/iPad but sometimes it's nice to view on a larger screen especially at the end of a busy working day. 
Last point as the hotel is next to the express way there is traffic noise despite double glazing and being 16 floors up

title_masked: Beautiful Boutique Hotel in an Amazing location!
text_masked: We booked this hotel as part II of our honeymoon trip (part I was Napa!). The location couldn't have been better! Right by the trolley cars (useful to hop on/off when needing to get to the station for the Bart or Muni and just fun in general!). Near all the best shopping, food, and attractions. Super safe area (walked around at all hours of the night). The hotel itself was beautifully decorated/hand painted... really romantic! For those who are light sleepers or get annoyed with "guest noise", this is not the spot for you (it's an older building, so the walls are thinner than what most are used to with chain hotels!). Hot breakfast every morning was wonderful. We were slightly miffed at the note that was left at the coffee/tea nook about how the tea cups cannot be taken to private guest rooms and that a tip should be left (for self serve coffee and tea), but we figured that was a customs gap. Overall, we enjoyed our stay and hope to be back in a few years!

Recently stayed 3 nights at the Conrad while on a family hoilday from New Zealand. Great location, top class service and superbly appointented room. Very friendly and helpful staff. Would definitely stay there again.

Me and three friends had dinner at the Canterbury during Super Bowl week here in Indianapolis. A lovely hotel with a homey atmosphere. The food was very good and the service was excellent. A great place to relax and enjoy a meal with friends. Jack

This Marriott is in a beautiful building and is perfectly situated for exploring all of walkable Seattle. You can fuel up at the Seattle's Best directly across the street before walking just 10-15 minutes to the shopping area or Pike Place Market. Most notable: immaculate rooms, wonderful friendly & helpful staff, good security, and for the purpose of my trip, a 7 minute walk or so to the Amtrak station. Would definitely stay here again.

Visited the Adolphus many times over the years and twice so far in 2012; have always experienced a pleasant and most desireable stay. Beginning with pulling in and being greeted by the nice gentleman captain who seems to be on perpetual duty, registration, guest services, and the other hotel staff have always been courtious and pleasant. Also the reservation people, the restaurant staff, and certainly housekeeping, who enhances the establishment with services I've come to know and love. And not to forget the Adolphus itself,,,,,, just something about the building and all its grandeur that makes me feel a part of her history when I am in her beautiful and majestic setting.

title_masked: High-end Holiday Inn with GREAT Midtown NYC Location
text_masked:
My husband and I just spent Labor Day Weekend 2012 in NYC and our last two days, one night were at this beautiful Holiday Inn Hotel on 31st Street in Midtown. LOVED IT! For whatever reason, the map feature on my iPhone had trouble locating it using the address I typed in from their website, but it was, nonetheless, it was super easy to find on 31st Street between 5th and 6th Avenue (closer to the end near 5th Avenue). You can't miss it!
Here are some of the many reasons you will love staying here:
- Super comfy bed with firm and soft pillow selections and a very nice comforter (not too heavy, not too light-- just right!). And clean, clean, CLEAN!!!!!
- FANTASTIC bathroom! Our room (#1404) had a nice size walk-in shower with fantastic water pressure, plenty of hot water (so much so that I had to dial it back from my usual high-hot-water setting), a really modern and large sink and lovely tile work that made it feel so modern and classy. Oh, and the hairdryer was SUPER high-power. It was a bit on the noisy side but it dried my long hair faster than any hotel hairdryer ever has before - WOW! 
- Plug outlets on the base of the table lamps made me a very happy traveler because it made it really easy to find a convenient place to plug in my iPad and recharge our iPhones. I love it when hotels have lamps like this or other easy-to-access plug outlets-- it is so important! 
- Very soundproof walls. I didn't hear a peep from the bustling streets below or from next-door neighbors-- not even when their high-powered hairdryers were on! LOL! 
- Great black-out shades for a good night's rest!
- Free wi-fi, free luggage room (since we had to check-in early and check-out late), but no free breakfast. That is okay though because Cafe R has breakfast just down the street and Dunkin Donuts is just steps from the hotel -- in fact it is right cross the street on the corner of 31st and 5th. 
-- Nice and quiet!
Location, location, location!
-- Forgot something? This hotel has a Jack's 99Cent Store just a few steps down the block that has EVERYTHING you could need (snacks, sunscreen, sunglasses, etc.) and all for less than $1.
-- The hotel is conveniently located near two important metro stops-- 1) Penn Station (which is a left out of the front door, then head toward 7th Avenue and walk up to 33rd to 34th street, or 2) take a right out of the front door door and then a left on 5th avenue for just one or two blocks and you will see the subway station in the lovely little park area. Both are SUPER convenient locations to trains that get you everywhere quickly!
-- Cafe R is just around the corner and delivers. It has a huge menu selection of everything you can imagine and it will deliver to your hotel! Just be sure to call directly-- it is a lot cheaper than ordering online. We had the Originial Philly Cheesesteak and loved it! I'd recommend splitting it though-- it is huge! Only one thing, don't get the milkshake from Cafe R-- It is just ice milk The fries and sandwich were amazing though!
You won't regret staying here-- It is beautiful, clean, has a great mid-town location, convenient to public transportation, and is super comfortable!!! It is not a super large room but was plenty spacious for our needs (hubby and wife sharing a room for a weekend getaway). Really loved this gem and the great service we received during our stay! We will be back!!!

I travel with my wife and 3 sons and this was our first time in NYC. We spend 6 nights here (june 28 to july 4) and we liked this hotel very much. Lobby service was great. everybody was happy and friendly and helpful. Breakfast was excellent but mayby little bit pricey, but everything was fresh and the chef who made omelettes and pancakes and the staff was so friendly! (big thanks to pregnant lady who worked there). Location was great also. You could walk to central park in 10 minutes and to time square in about 15 minutes or just take the subway which is just next to the hotel. BIG thanks to the staff.

I had had bad experiences with Holiday Inn years ago (make that decades ago...) and was a little reluctant to book into one again for a conference I was attending in New York. Holiday Inn Soho redeemed the brand in my eyes. It was clean, well organized, with well appointed and sized rooms and friendly, helpful staff. Hallways were well lit and clean. It was stinking hot in New York when we were there (95F by 11:00 in the morning) and the little touch of having an ice-filled urn of iced tea in the lobby was greatly appreciated...a small thing, but indicative of attention to detail. The only complaint I had was that the air conditioner in my room had trouble keeping up with the heat, but I did notice when I left that the maintenance crews were at work first thing in the morning, working their way up floor by floor, making adjustments to the AC units. Location was great - one block away from stations on Canal St for the yellow and green subway lines and just a few blocks more to the red and blue. The World Trade Center area was within easy walking distance. Traffic on some of the streets down in that area can get a little plugged up at times - especially in evenings, so walking can be quicker than taxi. We would take the subway out of the area and then catch a taxi later if need be. All in all, would definitely stay there again.

Next to Ditka's restaurant and a quick walk to the Tempo and Tower Place- a great location to see the sites and enjoy great food nearby. The hotel is old and needs updating. Our room was small and clean. The elevator was being worked on so we had to walk up a smelly staircase to get to the service elevator. Also, due to the drastic change in weather- it had been in the 80's the prior week and dipped into the 40's while we were there- the 'one pipe' system had been switched from heat to a/c. So we did not have any heat the first two nights- we did have heat the last two nghts. In fact, the lobby felt like a sauna! The staff was nice and friendly. However, when we mentioned the inconveniences- like our room being under 60 degrees- they replied "Hey, this is Chicago! Want a blanket?"

title_masked: From Air Force Bunker to 5 star Hotel
text_masked: Our stay at this hotel was excellent. Staff were courteous and quick with check in. Rooms were clean, spacious and well stocked with toiletries. The bed was a king bed with a down comforter. The only think bad about the room was the remote control to the TV was slow to respond. We had the buffet breakfast in the hotel restaurant in the mornings which was delicious and our lunch and evening meals were catered by the hotel. I would say the dining was good, but mostly quality hotel style dining. I believe the room rates were very moderate as compared to other hotels down town.

My group of 4 enjoyed our stay here. Usually I'm not big on sharing rooms but in NYC as a group of 4 we decided to do just that to save some money. Boy are prices high for rooms in NYC! I couldn't be more than pleased with the large room size at this hotel. We booked a standard room with two queen beds and I was worried about space. No need to be concerned, it was quite roomy!
The free breakfast was good. Nothing super spectacular but good nonetheless. Saved us a little more money not having to pay $20 for pancaked down the street. The have apples, coffee, and hot chocolate available 24/7. 
Overall a nice stay. Its close to Central Park, Times Square, and the great food in Hells Kitchen.

We stayed here for 8 nights in April. The hotel looked very welcoming on our arrival late at night. We had asked for a ground floor room as we had seen that there was no lift and we were allocated the room next to the reception desk which was extremely convenient for the coffee which was available in reception at all times! The room was very comfortable and spotlessly clean with a walk in closet, good bathroom and kitchenette. There was a cooker and a micro wave oven and plenty of plates and cutlery. They even put a small bottle of washing up liquid in the kitchen. The bed was really comfortable. Fluffy towels ( changed every day) and lovely toiletries ( replenished daily) were an added bonus. There was free wifi in the room. There is a laundry room downstairs with washing machines and tumble dryers for a small fee.
The staff on the Reception desk were very helpful and although we had a problem with the amount at check in this was rectified by the end of our stay and we paid what we were expecting to pay.
The hotel was conveniently located, a short walk to the Space Needle, close to the bus stop and within a short walk of both supermarket and restaurants. We walked from the hotel to Pike Place Market one day.
I would definitely recommend this hotel and should we go to Seattle again I would certainly stay here. It was very reasonably priced for such a lovely hotel and we got a good rate for staying more than a week. It was the best hotel on our trip to the US this time!

title_masked: THE place to stay in New York City
text_masked:
BWHH was recommended by a friend who has stayed there several times. We stayed for 17 days and could not have been happier with the accommodation. It is so handy to everything: subway, buses, Broadway, Rockefeller Centre/Plaza and Times Square. The apartments are huge, with separate kitchen, living room, bedroom and bathroom. 
All of the staff were friendly and helpful, especially Sam the Man, and the delightful Mayran who manages the breakfast room. Yes, the breakfast room can be a little tight during busy periods, but we sometimes used the quaint outdoor patio which was secluded and tranquil. We never had the need to take a breakfast tray back to our room. The freshly-made waffles were a real treat, as were the munchkin donuts!
BWHH is one of the most comfortable, friendly and well-located places that I have ever stayed.

title_masked: Stay here, you'll love it as much as we did!
text_masked:
My 94 year old father and I recently fled from being in the path of Hurricane Isaac to this wonderful property, where we felt like family.
The staff was such a blessing to us, by helping us get settled and ensuring we were their family. They constantly supported us as we worried about our home and our friends back home. The staff was helpful, reassuring and caring.
The property itself is gorgeous, and I have lived in apartments much smaller than my room. 
Best of all, my cat was welcomed there with open arms!
The location was great! Just down the road was everything I could ever want. I loved that we were so close to everything. 
The on-site laundry room was cleaner than if I cleaned it myself. 
Even though we were displaced for a week, it was more than a pleasure to stay at this lovely property with these caring, kind people. 
Thanks to everyone who helped us out!

title_masked: Great hotel, great W staff, horrible valet service
text_masked: I recently stayed at the W for business a couple of days ago. Upon driving up to the hotel, the valet service just stared at me in the car. Watched me unload the car and walk around and not until I begin to walk in the front doors offered me a valet ticket. In addition, the valet person couldn't event speak english and struggled for about 2-3 minutes to spell my last name (my last name only has 7 words and is of english origin). For $55 a night, I would expect a better level of service. In addition, upon returning to my car the other days, I received the same level of smug service. This is the only reason I am giving them 4 stars. The staff in the actual hotel was wonderful from the front desk to the restuarant and maid staff. The room was great and as a platinum guest I arrived to my room with a very nice welcome gift of prosecco and chocolate. This hotel is good but they should look to improve the welcome guests receive upon entering their establishment. Perhaps they should look for guidance from the W at Lake Shore as their valet service is great.

first stay in NY, great hotel, great location, newly refurbished rooms and friendly staff.
i had emailed to tell them this trip was for both mine and my husbands birthdays and our wedding anniversary and asked if we could have a room on the higher floors as trip advisor users stated these were quieter, when we arrived a very helpful polite young man called [NAME] told us they were happy to give us an up grade to a suite for free on the 25th floor-WOW-lovely room, good size rooms and 2 bathrooms-THANKS AFFINIA !
We found the hotel to have a great central location,great staff and lovely rooms, we would also like to say thanks to Vanessa, who always seemed to be there when we needed to know something and who was friendly and helpful.
If we are ever lucky enough to go back to NY we wouldn't stay anywhere but the Affinia Manhattan.

My husband and I stayed 3 nights beginning July 12. The room was teeny tiny... We brought back food to the room the first morning for breakfast and had to eat sitting on the bed! The hotel was far from immaculate - the furniture in the lobby looked old and kind of dirty... There was an off smell in the hallway next to the sushi restaurant. We got the room for $165/night on hotwire and it was good enough for the value. The location was great - only a few blocks from Time Square and pretty well walking distance to everything. Only a block from 50th Street subway station. I'd go back if I had no other reasonably priced option but would likely try somewhere else if I could get a similar price. The front desk staff and doormen were super friendly! The air conditioner was really loud...but not loud enough to drown out the street noise.

title_masked: Great Deal for New Years Weekend
text_masked: Great location, great service, great price and clean room. The only down fall is the parking which is 2 blocks from the hotel which cost $$ but that is the way it is in SF, not the hotels fault!

Sales Manager Karen Liston and front desk guest services personnel Lisa Adams, Muneit O'Brien and Tessa Simmons were awesome! They made us feel like family by providing exceptional service and hospitality, coupled with warm greetings and beautiful smiles. Other hotel staff members were also courteous and helpful whenever assistance was needed. SBCC is clean and beds very comfortable, which provided the rest we needed to sustain our long days and nights. I highly recommend SBCC to anyone reading this review and look forward to staying again myself!

We spent our anniversary weekend at the NYLO Dallas South Side. What a great hotel. The loft like rooms are unique with great views. The combination of historic and modern architecture creates an atmoshere that is very enjoyable. 
The staff was great. The location is central, but not right in the middle of a crowded downtown.
I would absolutely recommend the NYLO for a weekend get away.

title_masked: Location, caring staff, historic atmosphere, good food.
text_masked: Yes, the construction is real and present. Ignore it as much as possible and this is a good place to stay. One half of the the hotel is walled off and under construction. There is a six-storey building being built on the south side of the hotel. If you don't mind the daytime noise because you will be out exploring the city, get a room on the south side (even numbers) and the sunshine warms your room. If the noise bothers you, get a room on the north side (odd numbers). This is such a great, old hotel. Balboa Park is right across the street. Beds are very comfortable. Breakfast (not fancy; just simple food) on the roof is fabulous - food and view. The restaurant piano bar in the basement is excellent - food, service and music. The staff are wonderful. They do everything within their power to minimize the inconvenience of the renos. They have a tough job right now - trying to make everyone happy with so much going on. Be kind to them. We had such fun and will definitely stay here again.

title_masked: Great location, price, amenities and staff !
text_masked: I received great info from Trip Advisor regarding this Courtyard Marriott San Diego near the airport. The place was very convenient to the airport. It was all that I needed and more- clean, very attractively landscaped and offered walking trails right off the property, typically comfortable Marriott room and the great mattresses! The staff had wonderful info on the city and suggestions on routes to the SD Zoo. The hotel is located within an upscale neighborhood with various restaurants within walking distance. This is a great choice for business or families.

This motel was the worst i have ever seen seriously they should not operate this place in the condition that it is in. When we checked into the room the garbage was full and they place it in the closet, the cloth that they use to wash or try to wash the bathroom with was hanging up in the bathroom. the bathroom was very dirty from previous user the shampoo bottle that they uused was still in the bathroom with the left over soap. title_masked: ok for a nite or two
text_masked: Older hotel good location for what i needed. Down side had to get my key redone every night and was not asked a name or for id for the room they just asked what room and that was it so i guess anybody could just go into any room with a key. Older tv and lot of the channels didn't come in. WiFI was good

After reading a number of not-so-good reviews on this hotel, I was unsure of what to expect. On top of that, I had booked using "SPG Cash and Points" at a Category 4 rate, but checked before the trip and found out that this property had been downgraded to a Category 3 this year. I suspect that is because of the complaints that were received? I could be wrong. Thankfully I was able to re-book at the Cat3 rate.
Check-in and room thoughts:
All my fears were taken away though, right from the get-go. My son and I were offered a high floor, Marina facing room. Check-in was fast, efficient and very friendly! As an SPG Gold, I chose the free in-room Internet option and we were on our way up to the 10th floor. The room itself was average size. We were there just for the weekend and it suited our needs just right. The real treat was the view from the balcony!! Overlooking the large, beautiful pool area, over to the marina and out over the water. Really a nice view late morning until sunset. The airport was off to the right, but we were not bothered by noise from aircraft. It was fun for my son to watch the early morning departures anyway. Bathroom was small, but again, no big deal. It was showing some signs of wear and tear, but everything was clean. 
The only problem we had with our room was the A/C. There are sensors on the sliding glass balcony door and the room door that trigger the A/C to go on or off. The first night, I was roasting because the A/C did not appear to be working. No matter how I adjusted it, the room would not cool off. I call the next day to have it fixed. When we returned to the room later that evening, it appeared fine, but the next morning, it was back to "not working". Long story short, the batteries needed to be replaced in the door sensors. Every time we opened the sliding door to the balcony, it tripped the A/C off, but never went back on when we shut the door. The last night, we slept comfortably. **COMPLIMENT TO THE STAFF: Hotel Services was very nice and very apologetic. The second time we called, we were immediately offered a complimentary breakfast for 2 the next morning at the Harbor View restaurant (see my review below on that).
Pool / Hot Tub Thoughts:
We loved the awesome heated pool and equally awesome hot tub! It was a great way to relax at the end of the day before heading out for dinner. Everything was clean, fresh towels and wonderfully laid out. The size and shape of the pool was really cool and the large hot tub allowed multiple families to share and enjoy! Nice work on that, Sheraton!
Harbor View Breakfast Thoughts:
We ate here twice for breakfast and once at Starbucks for a quick on-the-run breakfast (full size, real deal Starbucks at the hotel). The buffet was very nice, food was excellent and tasty!! Lots of fresh fruit, your normal (but tasty) eggs, bacon, sausage selection, cereals, muffins, etc, etc. $22 per adult, $11 per kid, so it is not cheap, but again, if you are looking for a hearty breakfast, this is the way to go! The real compliments go to the staff who waited on us. They made an extra effort both days to make sure we were comfortable, enjoying ourselves and were genuinely happy and helpful!
**side note: Since this was my first experience at this hotel, I can't comment on previous experiences, but if there truly were customer service issues, I think management is definitely making an effort to ensure their customers are well taken care of. Maybe it is a result of being bumped down a category and there is a effort to bring it back up, maybe not. I can only comment on my experience and try and relate to what others have had. 
Bar Thoughts:
I did grab a drink at night and the bartenders both nights were very friendly, personable and made you feel welcome. I didn't hang around for long, but just enough to notice that.
Negative Thoughts:
Ok, one area that people have complained about that I agree with is the parking. I knew I was going to pay $22 a night or whatever it was, so I wasn't shocked. Still, there really was no reason other than to make money for charging that amount. At busy times, we had to park far from the entrance. One evening (over the weekend), there was an event (Wedding?). This absolutely killed the parking situation and was my only frustration point. The Wedding guests (driving the likes of Ferraris, Porsches, Maserati's, etc) were all crammed into the Valet parking area and spilling over into the regular parking areas. We were relegated to the back, dusty, dirt lot with a long walk back. $22 for that night?? Meh....I don't think so....I guess my rental Nissan wasn't good enough for asphalt. Ha! 
Another "issue" that was resolved very quickly was that apparently our rebooking at the Category 3 rate did not make it's way to the hotel. We received our bill and saw the Cash and Points Cat.4 rate listed. This was quickly corrected by the front desk, but an unsuspecting, early-o-clock departure person may not have caught that. 
Final words. Keep doing what you are doing, Sheraton SD. If you can keep up the great customer service and continue to improve on what you already have, I'm sure the reviews will turn around in your favor. Maybe you guys should ditch the other building down the road from you, or add additional amenities to it. It is a bit of a hike for people staying there and, while I didn't personally check it out, it seems a little strange and definitely (obviously) disconnected to have as a part of the main hotel.

title_masked: Not worth what I paid, but nice
text_masked:
I stayed here with a few friends for the 2012 Ohayocon. It was convenient that they had a shuttle running from the hotel to the convention center and back, however, I don't think that this was planned by the hotel, and it was at the furthest possible corner of the hotel away from everyone else. I got the distinct impression that they were trying to hide all the anime nerds away from the rest of the hotel.
Our trip was in February and it was very very cold, so waiting outside of a locked outside far away back door was not convenient at all, when the shuttle could have pulled into the drive through right near the lobby and it would've been much nicer.
Having said that, the beds were nice but we were placed in a single instead of a double room (though I called before to guarantee it was a double) and we were given a cot because they could not move us out of the room.
For close to $250 bucks a night, I expected at least free breakfast, but their 3 egg omelets were $12 dollars! I've had much more for a fraction of the price.
The staff was considerate and helped us out a lot, I know a lot of the circumstances that we were put in could not have been solved at that point in time by the front desk staff.
Overall, I would say this hotel was not a good value for the amount of money I paid for it.

title_masked: Don't say I didn't warn you....
text_masked: The staff do try and make up for poor facilities, inadequate staffing levels, tired rooms, long waiting at the reception, inadequate training, exclusion from facilities for private functions, over-pricing etc.

Hotel lobby was like grand central station but without the beautiful architecture! Far too many conference guests, so you are jostled about whenever in the lobby or lifts.
Corridors are maze like as hotel is so big with so many rooms. Decor is bland, outdated & in need of an overhaul. Feels grubby & unloved.
Rooms are large & comfortable. Again decor is lacking & furniture looks ancient. Bed very comfortable though which is really the only good point.
Decent location being only a couple of blocks from union square & the shops & sightseeing. Walking distance to pretty much everything though should you need to get a cab to the airport then leave plenty of time as the queue at the taxi rank outside hotel was very long. Again this is probably due to the sheer number of guests it accommodates.
All in all not too bad but wouldn't want to spend my own money staying here!

2 adults + 2 children, stayed 4 nights.
Room was beautiful, spacious, comfortable and clean. Bathroom was very nice with an amazing shower!
Very very nice, kind and helpfull staff, especially Darren in the front desk, who gave us some excellent recommendations.

What a great hotel to stay in the Big Apple. The representatives were quite helpful and resourceful. If you do consider staying at the Park Central hotel, please ask for Elizabeth. She just makes your day, from customer service to sense of humor. I will definitely come back to this hotel in the future.

A giant hotel just off Mission Street that is frequented by conventioners. The rooms could use a bit of facelift, however, you can't beat this place for its location. The View lounge upstairs offers stunning views, good cocktails and OK food.
More on my trip to San Francisco:
http://www.traveladdicts.net/2012/07/san-francisco-california.html

I rented two rooms during the Maryland primary elections, one for my wife and one for two other people that were from out of state to work the elections. I had gotted an email from choice hotels to get a discounted room upgrade to which I took for my wife and I. Our room had a wirlpool tub. Our first day there I used it and it did not work, so the next day when my work crew showed up i mentioned it to the manager and asked if we could get a room that had one that work. I was told no that I got the room at a discounted rate, and he also refused to get it repaired while we were there. When I complained to choicehotel.com the contacted the hotel to find out what happend and told me that they should have an answer for me in 24 to 48 hours. I called back and they had not heard from him but gave me extra points for my problems

We recently had our annual Sales Managers Meeting at the Warwick in Dallas. I must say that in my 30 years of planning meetings, this was the best experience I have ever had. This exquisitly maintained/rennovated property built in 1924 has a unique charm and character. The service was above the top on every level. The Sales Manager, Deanna, was extremely accomodating from beginning to end. The Director of Catering, Cynthia, was simply unbelievable. I am extremely picky when it comes to my corporate meetings. She exceeded my expectations on every level, which has never happened. The quality of food as well as the presentation was out of this world. The rooms are so beautiful and beds are top of the line. Eeryone in the hotel bends over backwards to help you and always with a smile. My managers were so impressed with everything. Out of my group of 35 I did not have one complaint. Even the invoice was a breeze being easy to read and very organized and detailed. The location is perfect being 5 minutes away from tons of upscale clubs and restaurants in the prestigious Uptown area. I highly recommend this little Oasis for business meetings, family or a romantic getaway.

title_masked: Many thoughtful touches and enormous rooms
text_masked:
My family - two teens, my husband and I spent three nights at the Affinia Hotel. It is a leisurely 20 minute walk from Penn Station and located in Murray Hill. There are plenty of dining options around: Dunkin Donuts, the Murry Hill Diner, McDonalds, Vietnamese, Thai and Indian restaurants, and small grocery stores. 
The lobby is small and doesn't really give you an idea of how nice the rooms are. We have stayed at 3 other boutique hotels in NYC and the rooms here large - they even have a proper closet - not a clothes rack wedged between the bed and the wall, but real closet. The views are fantastic too. Our rooms looked out to the East River and beyond. There are only 7 rooms per floor and the rooms are very quiet. No noise from the hallway or the room next door. The housekeeping carts are kept next to the elevators so you can grab a towel or toiletries anytime you need. The elevators are quick to arrive and there is a sign on each floor that says you can call the desk if the elevators are slow and they will send one up for you. We didn't have to use that feature, but it was nice to know you wouldn't be waiting and waiting for an elevator. Our room had a kitchenette with a full size apartment refrigerator, mini microwave, 4 burner stove with oven, dishes and a couple of pans. They even included wine glasses and a corkscrew. The only con to the hotel - and this is very nit picky and minor- is the bathrooms could use some touch ups and minor repairs - cracked grout, paint peeling in some places, but not enough to deter anyone from staying here - just cosmetic blemishes that do not diminish the many great things about this hotel. 
Pros:
Huge rooms with gorgeous views
extremely comfortable bed
real closet
choice of pillows 
nice (Philosphy brand) toiletries
apartment sized fridge
Friendly staff
water cooler in the lobby
fast elevators
good shower pressure
Cons:
bathrooms could use some touch ups
We would definitely stay here again.
Took a flyer on hotwire. Stayed one night and wished for a week. 2 bedroom suite, patios, and pools are amazing. Slow on check-in service but they were training someone new.
The room was very nice and clean. There wasn't a mirror over the sink in the bathroom in which was a little strange.

My family and I stayed here for more than a week, the price was very affordable. Clay, Josie and all the housekeepers were very friendly and pay attention to our needs. Parking lot is big and it's free. Easy access on public transportation. I recommend this motel to anyone who's looking for a clean and very affordable place to stay in.

This hotel was the standard Hilton quality you expect to find. The rooms were very clean and we had a great view of the small pond area from our window. The pond area was nice to walk around as there were some shops and restaurants. The staff was friendly and for the most part helpful. I would say the bathroom was smaller than other Hilton's we have stayed at however we truly enjoyed our stay.

We booked this hotel on hotwire while taking our son and nephew visiting colleges. The "deal" on hotwire was only $5 cheaper than the online price, Both which were quite reasonable. The hotel let us upgrade to a 2 bed separate bedroom room for $40 more. Some issues: holes in walls patched but still obvious; floor squishy and uneven under carpet; holes in the towels and blankets; chipped paint, ripped carpet on the stairs, coffee pot didn't work and the mattress on the sofabed springs were sticking out. The whole place could have used a good scrubbing especially the walls. Our key didn't work and twice we had to run back to the front desk (downstairs and outside in a different building) before they moved us rooms where we had to take all stuff downstairs and outside again. There were no logs available at the front desk for purchase but we did pick up some wood at Giant Eagle and enjoyed a fire. The good: price, location to the highway, quiet, very comfortable beds, and good breakfast. There was a pretty substantial snowfall overnight and the walkways and stairs were not shoveled by time we left at 9:00 am.

More things were found to be wrong with the room the longer we were in it. Two of the lights were not working. The standard non flat TV had poor cable reception with approximately half the channels showing a snowy picture. Every time, yes every time the toilet was flushed it kept running and we had to lift the back off to manually put the flapper down. The refrigerator wasn't keeping our things cool and had the control knob removed. The refrigerator made so much noise at night my wife had to unplug it to get any sleep. A little skimpy on the number of towels. Tried to get some ice in the morning and there was none to be had out of their machine. Continental breakfast looked uninviting and decided to go to IHop. Management was unwilling to reduce the inflated rate due to NASCAR event even though there were plenty of vacancies that night.

Great location, amazing staff provides great service. Location is ideal. Have stayed here several times and the hotel is consistent in the fantastic service they provide. I will continue to be loyal and would recommend to anyone traveling to NYC.

title_masked: Nice hotel close to Denver airport
text_masked: We stayed at this hotel after our flight direct to Denver. It was handily placed about 3 miles from the airport, Check in was smooth, staff were very pleasant. The room was large, clean and modern. Breakfast was good. Thoroughly nice place to start our road trip.

The room was spacious along with a view of the lake. The spa has excellent jets; most relaxing. The hotel is located at the river. Restaurants and shops a short walk away. Bus service and "L" transportation close. Overall a very good experience.

We stayed there for one night after traveling from Boston. Very easy drive from the airport, private parking and very good location : a couple blocks to downtown. Room was clean and comfortable and the staff very nice. The breakfast is relatively poor but it is included with the room. So good place to stay in phoenix, we even came back in this hotel after hiking a couple days in the Grand canyon.

title_masked: Seattle Top Hotel Recommend, close to Convention Center and offers Self Service Laundry on-site
text_masked: This was my first stay at this Seattle SpingHill Suites and it was amazing from the moment I arrived. The staff was friendly and eager to help me find my way around the city and get to and from the Seattle Convention Center for my convention; including their free hourly shuttle to various sites. The morning breakfast buffet offered plenty of popular hot food choices and there is also plenty of sitting areas for just sitting back and relaxing with your morning cup of Java or tea. Having the self service laundry on-site was a real time and money saver! The hotel even provides dryer laundry sheets for you if requested. The restaurant and bar were worth staying on property for, well at least for some of your nights. Obviously you want to explore as much of Seattle dining and wining as you can while in the city. I highly recommend this hotel for business or pleasure, with or without families. I definitely recommend and will return to this hotel. Hope you enjoy it as much as I did.

Put it like this - i only joined tripadvisor to review this hotel. That is how bad it is.
Massively overpriced, we paid $179 plus taxes per night.
Shabby and must have been due a refit even 20 years ago. That said, to be fair it wasn't dirty per se, but when taps are rusted etc it certainly "feels" dirty.
Location is on main drag into city but not a nice area - there are so many other nice places in the city, don't choose this one. We found it hard to get a hotel online in the city due to an Oracle exhibition and America's Cup sailing, but reality is there are loads of hotels and motels not listed on expedia hotels.com etc so don't make the mistake I did and be lazy re researching!
No one likes to feel taken advantage of, so don't stay here.
Like other reviewers, lots of homeless and unsavories in the area and we were woken up at 5am with an argument outside. It is very sad, of course, that there were so many homeless around the whole city, but i think this is representitive of US cities currently - and that's whole another discussion!

nothing like a standard Holiday Inn, The beverley Garland has a style of its own. We travelled with two teange boys and had a family room with a seperate bunk area for the boys. Really good with their own playstation. The pool was welcome in the heat we had there and was even full for the films played on the screen their in the evening. The bed and room were great, clean and comfortable. The pool was welcome and very clean. The shuttle to the park was excellent and even returned to pick up passengers when the bus was full! 
the friendly staff offered us a free drink in the bar which felt very decadent when travelling on a budget, and we had a great breakfast (provided as a bonus by the friendly staff otherwise the prices for breakfast are quite high).
All in all very impressed and had a great stay. Drove all around the city which was easy to access from the hotel.

I stayed here for a convention in the Moscone Center in late August. It is a 10 minute walk through a nice area (across Market St.). I was in room 810, which wasn't big, but sufficent. New flat screen, desk, coffee maker, safe, nice comfortable kingsize bed and pillows, good size bath room, smallish tub, great WiFi coverage although somewhat slow at times. Carpets, paint etc. all lookd fine although the cupboard looked a little worn to me. Only drawback in the room was that it was a little on the dark side (just one, relatively, small window), and the fact that it had a door to an adjoining room, which meant you quite clearly could hear the neighbours. It didn't bother me, as they weren't noisy. The gym is very small and only has one treadmill, one bike, one cross trainer, weights and one of those multi-functional-thingies. All new and in good condition, but if you want more, there's a real gym on the same block, which you can buy day-passes for at the reception for 12USD. The receptionists were nice and helpful. They have a wine-tasting in the afternoons, but if you really appreciate wine, you will probably be disappointed :-/ But I guess it is some sort of attempt of compensating for not having a bar, and as such I like the idea. They don't have any restaurant either, but there is a Japanese/Mexican restaurant next door (weird combination) which they recommended. It must open quite late as I never saw it open in the mornings (before 8AM when I left. Next to the hotel there is "Bread and Cocoa" which is coffee shop where I had my breakfasts, which were great. There is also a Starbucks up the street. 
If you enjoy a run, it is less than 1km to the sea/piers, where you can get some nice long and very beatiful runs uninterrupted by traffic. As I was in town for a big conference, prices were very high (for all the hotels I checked) and I paid around 400USD per day. If I come back, and the prices aren't jacked up due to big events, I would stay here again, but at any other time of the year, I would never pay that much for a 3,5 star hotel. Supply and demand, I guess.

title_masked: Classy hotel, but only if you are on an EXPENSE ACCOUNT
text_masked: Very nice downtown hotel and in a good neighborhood. But unless you are on an expense account, don't expect anything. Breakfast buffet was $19 each and did NOT include coffee ($5.50) nor juice ($3.50). no complimentary coffee anywhere. no complimentary internet. again, a very nice hotel, but not for the family. I was staying overnight to visit my granddaughter after an Alaskan cruise.. Very disappointed in the extra expenses after paying $200 for a night's sleep.

Great location between Chinatown and Union Square. I was very sceptical at first because of the price; however, at the end of my stay, I didn't regret my decision to stay here. Even though the room is very small, it was very clean. The wifi worked great! Only one out of the 4 nights we stayed there, the wifi connection didn't work. You don't need a car to go around the city since they have the hop on and hop off bus that stops nearby the hotel. Overall, we really enjoyed our trip.

Spent three nights and four days in NYC with wife and 2 kids. The Eastgate was more than satisfactory. We went shopping, saw a show, visiting landmarks and had dinner at fun places. The key value to this place is the location. If you don't need luxury, then this is your place to stay for lodging with 2 bedrooms and 2 bathrooms. Kids were fine. The area is very safe. Quiet at night. Overall, we would stay again.

title_masked: Outstanding Value - Awful Water Savers in Bathroom
text_masked: This hotel is exceptionally clean. The entire hotel is VERY family and pet friendly. The food at breakfast is okay but not exceptional in fact it is always cool to cold but free is allowed to be cool to cold. The two worst attributes are the too-soft beds and the terribile water pressure in the shower. If I had traveled with a pair of pliars and a small flat blade screw driver I would have popped that water saver out of the shower head. Is it possible that Embassy Suites fails to understand that guests will use what ever volume of water is necessary to wash themselves? If there is no water saver in the shower head I am rinsed and done in 3 minutes. If there is a water saver I am rinsed and done in 15 minutes. I think that the math speaks for itself. Other than that, the room is terrific and the hotel is very close to everything I need to visit. I'll stay here again but with a pair of pliars the next time.

title_masked: Excellent place in Seattle, close to the city centre
text_masked:
We really enjoyed our stay at the Loyal Inn. It is only about 2 blocks away from the more expensive Executive Inn. Close to most of the city attractions, all the transit options and easy walk to anything, including the Market.
We found the hotel to work well for our needs in Seattle. The included breakfast was great each morning and got us going. The room itself was nothing special but worked.
Overall it was a good stay for the location and for the money. I would recommend this place to anyone staying in Seattle and would go there again.
Great location to the convention center with awesome opportunities for night entertainment. The free breakfast and social hour in the evening was outstanding!

Our first time staying at the Belvedere. What a great location! Just a short walk to many theatres, Time Sq. & Central Park. Also liked the fact that our room had a microwave, small fridge & coffee maker. Staff were always pleasant, helpful, and attentive. We stayed in one of the executive rooms which looked newly renovated - furnishings were lovely - very cosy. Of course, the room was fairly small - but that is to be expected. Beds were very comfortable. Had a problem with the air conditioning upon our arrival -- the problem was promptly taken care of - always appreciate such good service! Makes your vacation that much more enjoyable. Will definitely return here!

title_masked: Great location, good spa, amazing bed!
text_masked:
Stayed at the Surrey for 3 days in January, had a wonderful stay. I was really jet-lagged and an ultra-comfortable bed made all the difference. Needless to say, its perfect location as Madison Ave is around the corner etc.
I would also like to thank Phil at the Spa for the most wonderful back massage - he is truly a professional!
The only downside was the bathroom - did not like the toiletries (things like that make a difference to me) and the bathroom feels a bit old and used.
Otherwise loved it!

Booked this hotel to attend the TEDxMidAtlantic conference. Brought the family since my 8year old was attending with me and thought the rest would enjoy the sights. The location was really convenient (5-10 min walk) to the Sidney Harmon Theater (next to Convention Center), but it wasn't through the nicest of areas. We planned all our outings strategically so we'd be back before dark or drove where we needed to go.
The hotel was newly remodeled and looked very nice. The kids loved the breakfast calling i the "best breakfast ever" several mornings in a row. Only issue was the room next to us decided it was a good idea to party until 4am the one night (and broke the hotel's no smoking policy).
