If I had a need to be in the area again I definitely would consider this hotel, especially for business travel.
BTW, the concierge/hotel staff is great. They helped with everything and even got us some bananas and breakfast bags when we checked out. The personal service and touches are why Hilton hotels are the best.

title_masked: charlotte hotel - great place - great staff
text_masked: safe, clean, great breakfast and DINNER mon-thurs evenings. nice pool and workout room, very convenient to downtown charlotte and 2 nice malls. free access to a nearby gym with all the workout equipment. lots of well lit, safe parking.

title_masked: Westin San Diego Gaslamp gets 4 stars
text_masked: It is nice to get off of a long flight and get good service from a staff that wants to help. That has not always been the case many years ago. My stay was a 4 star. What more can say. Steve Elisberg

I stayed at the Colonnade for a friends wedding and it was full because the wedding happened to be during graduation time. They were fully staffed and prepared and I never felt neglected. Jerry at the consierge desk called to get me tickets for the harbor cruise but they were so busy that he went on line and booked it for me! After the cruise and the walk I came back and stopped at the bar and both of the guys bartending were happy, friendly and very accommodating! There was a rude lady that was never satisfied, yet the bartender kept trying until she walked away happy and he never once got impatient with her. One night there was a ragging party next to my room and I finally called at 11:30 and security was there within 2 min. and not only did they ask them to quiet it down, they waited in the hall for a few minutes and when I got loud again,the made it stop and were VERY calm, kind and respectful in doing so. They even offered to move me to a different room, but I didn't feel the need but truly appreciated the offer
Now to the wedding....it was at the hotel, on the roof top and was by far the most organized and well run wedding I've every been to in my many years on this earth!!! It was fantastic in every aspect, from the amazing and perfect appetizers, meal, cake and drinks to the perfect timing with cutting the cake and serving it seamlessly. I truly was impressed and the wedding planner (I believe her name was [NAME]) never missed a things and never showed any signs of stress. 
The location is perfect for anything you may want to do in Boston and I would highly recommend this hotel for any type of stay - singles, family, business and definitly for a wedding!
Thank you for the perfect trip!

title_masked: location great! but don't bring a car!
text_masked:
We stayed in the middle of July of 2012. We were only passing through so we only stayed one night. We got in from the airport at about 10:30 and were surprised to find out that there was only valet parking for $22/day. The only available parking was street parking that started ticketing at 8am or a parking garage that was about a 7 minute walk. We actually found a parking lot that was about 10 minute walk that was half the price of the garage. 
The hotel lobby was beautiful and the staff helpful.
The hotel room was nice and well appointed except for a lack of electrical outlets by the bed. Bring a power strip! When we moved the mattress to get to the outlet, there was hair behind the mattress. The carpet needed to be deep cleaned. The toilet handle was broken. But this room was average for the price. Also I found it disappointing that the hotel had a van but doesn't offer airport service to their guests.
Kind of a disappointing Doubletree.

The hotel is well located, the rooms are clean, cosy and well designed, the service is good. The strong point of the hotel is undoubtedly the dining room (where breakfast is served, but it transforms itself into the restaurant "Americano" for dinner) : it is splendid and airy (facing the Ferry Building), the food is innovative and the waiters and waitresses are pleasant and helpful. Drawbacks of the hotel : laundry is expensive ; there's no swimming pool.

My GF and I just spent 5 nights at this hotel during the month of June and found it to be excellent. The staff was friendly and helpful. The rooms were extremely clean and spacious. The beds were super comfortable and our view of Beale Street was great. I would stay there again in a heartbeat.

Clean place... I was not familiar with the Red Lion chain - since I am on the East Coast. Hotel was in a GREAT location. 1 - 2 blocks from all the big shopping names - Nordstroms, Banana Republic, Macy's, etc. Also only about 3 blocks from Pike Place Market. As I said - hotel was clean - and about on the same scale as a remodeled Hampton Inn.

Sanctuary is on 47th, one block from Marquis Theatre ,where we saw "Evita." Hotel location was great! Rooms are not spacious, but the room space is optimized by a layout that works well. Modern decor & clean rooms. Nice shower, no tub. Separate, private toilet with sink allowed me to use the second sink, closest to shower, when toilet was occupied; I like that! Continental breakfast was very nice & the lovely lady in charge of breakfast was kind, helpful. Very comfortable beds! We slept well. Nice bedding, also. I would have preferred sheers in addition to the blackout blinds. They have black out blinds & fabric Roman shades, so if you want natural light, you don't get any privacy. Sheers would be a great addition. Doormen are very courteous. Front desk staff friendly. Assistant Manager, "Kimberly" was attentive & conscientious & lovely!

title_masked: Great hotel and helpful staff. Not much in the area
text_masked: This is a great business/conference hotel, don't expect anything much in the surrounding area. Huge rooms and bathrooms, executive lounge is a long way from some of the executive rooms. Hilton need to get with the times and stop charging for wifi access.

A coworker found this hotel online as our usual hotel was sold out. Soooo happy to have stayed here instead and this is my new hotel of choice when in NYC on business. I was in room 1406, and was shocked at how large the room was by NYC standards. In addition to the usual bed and desk (larger than usual), there is a small closet, a mini-refrigerator (not stocked with impulse-buy items--an actual fridge to store your own drinks!), and a shelving unit to lay your suitcase on. Sweet! The room also contained a Keurig coffee maker, making a trip to Starbucks unnecessary.
The breakfast buffet was delicious every day, and the staff here is unbelievably nice (from front desk, restaurant, housekeeping, engineers... every single person encountered was welcoming). Happy hour each night offers reduced priced drinks, a nice oasis after an exhausting day at work.
Overall, I'd give Tryp my highest recommendation as a great place to stay while in NYC.

Do not let the name or the outside fool you. This is a completely modern, updated Inn! Gorgeous color schemes and perfectly situated next to the highway. Continental breakfast in the a.m. friendly staff. Only downfall I would have to say is some tight parking.

I stay here whenever I come to Austin. I've tried a few other places and found that this is a nicer place to stay than some of the big name luxury hotels near downtown/UT. It was updated about 5yrs ago. The common areas are showing a little wear and this is an older hotel but not to the point that I find it displeasing. I always get a room with a lovely lake view. Not only is the view nice but it keeps you away from the noise of the interstate. The luxury hotels downtown don't have this advantage; I found them noisy and difficult at which to sleep. I really have enjoyed this Holiday Inn and would recommend it.

We stayed at this hotel for my niece's wedding in August and it was just beautiful. The service staff is very attentive and the food is very good. Our room was on the harbor side making our view spectacular! The rooms are good size and the beds are so comfy. The only complaint I would have with the room was the air vent that blew on the bed. I wish there was a way to shift the vents so the blow would go towards the wall. It was also a little noisy because of the hallway noise but nothing too bad. All in all, a lovely hotel with an incredible harbor view, especially at night.

Went to Washington DC for Springbreak. Definitely worth staying.
The cost per night is very reasonable and we had booked quite late. 
The staff is friendly and very helpful. 
There is free wifi in the hotel.
The hotel is recently renovated. Room is clean and tidy.
Free breakfast in the morning.
We travel to DC from Baltimore airport. Hotel staff arranged for transport back to Baltimore airport at reasonable price.
Transportation to the museums and monuments is easy.
Went to Lincoln Memorial for dawn.

staff is friendly. rooms are getting a little bit dated and showing some signs of wear. overall the property was clean though which can overshaddow other small wear issues. some examples of wearing include frayed carpet between bedroom and bathroom in room 231 and cabinetry in bathroom were a bit dated and worn. again, place was spotless and staff was friendly.

i am not one to complain or even write a review, but I felt like there has to be an honest review posted.. for families that are planning a visit to Houston .. requested. kingsize bed, nonsmoking room was given 2 full size room .. cigarette burns on fridge and tub.. went in for shower and looked to left side and pub hairs on wall.. along with mold on shower curtain, I really wanted to go complain to management. but husband advised. me to just step out while he cleaned tub for myself and him, as if things couldn't. get worst later that night we had cars with system's. driving around, people hanging around outside. and nieghbor having visitors. late at night with loud banging on doors, and I swear room was infested with bed bugs

After reading all the negative reviews of this hotel, I was really nervous about staying there, but I'm so glad I did! The hotel has a great location, just a few short blocks from Union Square. We were even able to pick our rental car up directly across the street. The staff was super nice. My boyfriend and I are both HHonors members and had each booked one night of our two night stay with our points. The man at the front desk was kind enough to combine our reservation, so we didn't have to switch rooms, and upgrade us to a balcony room! We also got the free Starbucks breakfast both mornings, which was a really nice touch. Although the hotel does touch on a bad area of town, my boyfriend and I never felt unsafe. I'd say avoid turning left on O'Farrell St. when you leave the lobby and you'll be just fine!

Stayed here for 1 night. Leaving our car for valet parking was a nightmare - cars stacked up blocking the road when we arrived. Gentleman on check in was very helpful, offering us complimentary cold water. When he discovered we were leaving at 4:30 am he offered us vouchers for room service breakfast which was a nice touch. Room was clean and more nicely appointed than a regular Hilton room, but wasn't really anything special. Separate shower and bathtub was nice. We had a couple of glasses of wine in the hotel bar 'Tastings' - there was a bad singer and little ambiance, but the wine tasting idea was neat and allowed us to try a glass of more expensive wine than we would normally buy. Room service breakfast arrived at the beginning of the delivery window, and while expensive as expected in this kind of hotel, was fresh and plentiful with the biggest pancakes I have ever seen. When we left at 4:30am the lady on check in had our car waiting for us, and took us out herself, also giving us more complimentary water. While I wouldn't pay the Conrad premium over Hilton for the room, I would for the service we received at this Conrad.

We had a river view and it was a great hotel stay. Very clean, everyone was very friendly and helpful. We were looking for a bar to watch the Packer game at, and we were directed to a great place. Take the elevator town to the river level, and we were right were the action was. Walked everywhere for dinner and just had a great time.

title_masked: I recommend the New Yorker Hotel!
text_masked: I stayed there with my mom for a week. Perfect location, nearest subway stop just a few steps away. Easy access from JFK by subway as well. Tic Tock diner on the ground floor, wonderful breakfast place. Blueberry pancakes <3 The staff very helpful and friendly. Asked for a upgraded room, as it was my graduation trip. Got it, high up and a great view towards Madison square garden. Safety boxes were easy to use and visit in the reception area. Room were refurbished, bathroom dated but clean, had everything we needed. Small rooms but a closet for clother+bagage, and well, we didn´t need that much of a space for sleeping :) Didn't hear any noise up there! Good value for your money, and a perfect base for your vacation in the big apple!

My family and I stayed two nights here.I liked the central location,we walked to downtown,the next morning we took a $6 cab ride to Pike Place,which actually was cheaper than if we took the bus.The staff was very friendly and helpfull,especially the young man that checked us in on Thursday evening.We loved the continental buffet breakfast included with our stay,it offers a huge varriety of choices,from fresh waffles,fruit,yogurt,to eggs & ham.My wife and I find this very convienant,and our children love the choices.

What a nice hotel! This provided much more value than I expected it to do (and I didn't have low expectations). Was here for a conference and stayed for three nights and here is a summary of +/-
Location : fabulous on Michigan Av and actually has lake view from some rooms (incl 803). Situated just opposite Ralph Lauren and the RL Grill (which was great as well).
Hotel itself : good mix between modern and classic. Standards and cleanliness was very good. Good roomy lounge area downstairs.
Conference facilities : very good and the catering was excellent as well.
Rooms : much larger than expected. Huge bathroom with window across the bedroom for a lakeview (room 803) which was very impressive and nice. The room itself was also very large, great bed, excellent work desk and had all the facilities you might need (excl coffee maker). Very nicely decorated, high standards and very clean. 
Fitness room : pretty big, well equipped and connected with the SPA (incl changing rooms). All in all it felt modern and a good place for a nice workout.
Bar / Restaurant : NoMi lounge, bar and restaurant on the 7th floor. Interesting menu with good tasting food. Pretty well stocked wine list and good selection of international and local beers. Service was great and always with a smile (not the least from Stefan).
Service : Excellent, not one bad experience. Everyone very curteous, friendly and professional. A well run team I think. 
All in all, this is an excellent hotel that I would recommend to anyone, whether going there on business, for shopping or just a trip away with the family.

title_masked: Cheap but in a bad area of town
text_masked:
I was going to a trade show and needed a room - i could have stayed at the W, St. Regis or Palace for $400 - $500 a night....or USE HOTWIRE and paid $69 bucks for the Whitcomb.....so, i stayed at the Whitcomb. It's a very old hotel and all in all just fine. The downside is the location is in a rough part of town. I had no issue with anyone and experienced no issues. The Gym is very poor so i went outside and ran up and down the subway stairs. ....felt a little like Rocky :) 
The internet is very slow, but they do have an okay Starbucks downstairs. To get into the city jump on the subway / bart for 1 stop or get on the bus.....take 5-10min.
Again, okay place....saved a ton of money....but don't expect the Ritz ;)

IT is a really good solution for "low budget" traveller, for NYC it could be considered cheap. the position it is really good, mid Manhattan, nearby Union Sq, but in a secondary street, it results also a good place for rest..not so much noise. the room was internal, there was no view, but the space between the two adiacent building, but who cares, the view it is outside! the bathroom is common, but was always clean, also in the nights, I think there is somebody dedicate 24/7. on the other hand nobody enter in the room room for clean it, I stay only 4 days and I don't know if for longer stay they will come and clean, but I suppose so, and in any case they are so kind that if you ask, maybe they will do it . in case..I would come back

title_masked: Big Room For Family - Nice Service
text_masked:
We checked into the Ritz Carlton after taking an Amtrak Train Ride through Colorado, Utah and Nevada. After sleeping in a sleeper on board, the Ritz Carlton's fantastic bedding was a welcome change. I am never disappointed with the comfort of their beds. I slept with my daughter in a queen and I felt like I was sleeping on a cloud. 
Our Junior Suite is really just a larger room so don't get too excited over it unless you have kids. If so, it accommodates a roll away queen bed just fine. There is no separate area in the room to watch TV or anything like that...just one big room. 
Housekeeping if fabulous. These ladies really work hard. Our souvenir hide-away room was nicely cleaned each day. 
Being an American Express platinum card member gave us a $60 credit each day for breakfast. Don't get too excited about this because on our first day, our breakfast was $110 with tip. We since cut down and only ordered granola and and pastries to keep the bill within the limits! 
Lunch was delicious as the 37 restaurant. My husband and I ordered a pulled pork sandwich which was amazing. Kids can order off a separate menu which is good as well.
The concierge desk set up all day trips to Sausalito and Miur Woods and gave us tips about restaurants in Chinatown which is just a walk down the block. 
Warning: Do not use yellow and black cab out of Emeryville and Berkeley. [TEL]. Besides the driver being the meanest man I've ever seen and a crummy, aggressive driver, my son's cellphone slipped out of his pocket. When we called them, the driver said he didn't have it. it was a lie because my son used it on the cab. We lost service and could not get the phone traced after awhile. The phone is $800 to replace. He's accepted the fact that it's gone but I feel the cab company could have done more.
The hotel is a great place to stay, the gym is wonderful, but there is no hot tub or pool for the kids. No Ritz Kids as this is no a resort. 
 Our room rate was $539 a night with the 4th night free. Be careful, WIFI is NOT included and it's expensive! Luckily with AMEX Platinum travel, it's included. However, with our included rate, we were not offered a room upgrade and this hotel does not looked fully booked.

Everything was great from the front desk staff to the comfort of the bed. Would definetly reccomend this hotel for vacation, business, or just have an early flight at Indy airport. Also have a great hot breakfast! Also great Godfathers pizza available for delivery at a reasonable cost! Thanks for making the start of my trip to Maui so relaxing. Carol F. and Donny B.

This hotel was ok but not worth the money it had a great location and a very friendly front desk staff but that is about as far as it goes. I stayed on the executive floor and with the exception of a extra desk space and tea and coffee available all day there was nothing special about paying the extra price for staying on this floor,no separate check in or lounge. Two days out of my stay I had to complain to house keeping that my towels were dirty and needed to be replaced and it took most of the day to remove trays discarded from the rooms out of the hallway. Over all the experience wasn't terrible but for the service I will go with a little less expensive hotel next time or something a little more exclusive.

First off, i always search this site before i travel and find it really helpful, so i hope this will be as helpful to others. The new yorker is in a perfect location, it is within walking distance of times square, empire state buliding etc. On arrival the front desk were inpolite and seemed like they couldnt wait to get us out the way. Our room was clean and the bed was extermely comfy, the bathroom could do with an update and was really small. We had a view of a brick wall so i would defo advise to book a room with a view (my mistake). We both slept really well though. the tick-tock diner was ok, a bit pricey for waht it was, but ok for a quick breakfast and the milkshakes are delicious. We had a lovely lunch in the hotel restaurant before departure. The conceige was quite helpful although kept trying to sell thearte tickets when we were trying to book transport to the airport. We found the hotel shop really good for last minute souveniers. Overall our stay in New York was incredible and i would stay at this hotel again (if you don't mind the front desk staffs rudeness). Everything i tried to ask them, i had one word answers etc and they were talking between themselves alot, while i was stood waiting to speak to them. The hotel is lovely though and i would recommend it just for the location.

I stayed at the Holiday Inn Express Fisherman's Wharf for several days in July 2012, and it was a wonderful experience, again. The staff were above par in their willingness to accommodate early check-in and with other needs I had (Joseph at the front desk is a seasoned employee who knows the ropes and gets results). The rooms are comfortable and nicely appointed, though the inner rooms lack any view of anything other than the opposing rooms across small "courtyards". The cleaning staff were amiable and efficient in cleaning the room though on one day this was not completed until around 5 PM, which I found curious. I also thought a microwave in the breakfast area, for general use in the evening (for popcorn snacks, etc.) would have been nice but sadly is not available. Complementary WiFi worked just fine and the breakfast was excellent, though long lines formed to access the breakfast bar. The usual Holiday Inn offerings were available, and in ample quantities. Again, there were times when long lines formed to access the food, and table seating was sometimes at a premium. 
The location of the hotel is superb, about 4 blocks from Pier 39. I also utilized BART to travel to the Embarcadero station and then caught a trolley to within a block of the hotel. For seniors this is an economical alternative to shuttles from the airport or rental cars. My total out of pocket cost was approximately $9 one way. Public transportation in San Francisco is safe, efficient, and doable, though some of the bus drivers have poor attitudes. 
I would highly recommend this hotel, primarily based on its location, its comfort, and on the fact that the staff go way beyond the call of duty. They seem to enjoy their work and they are very accommodating. I also met the General Manager and I can see where the staff receive their inspiration from.

have stayed for 2 weeks beginning of November and found the stay very comfortable. location is great by the galleria, very convenient with lots of things to do after conference. rooms not luxurious but very spacious suites and clean. could not fault the service. breakfast included in the rate is fine. will be back if visiting Houston again.

title_masked: Excellent stay at Hotel metro again.
text_masked: Second year at Hotel metro for girls weekend away with my daughter and sister. family room looking right up at Empire State Building. The staff there could not be nicer, even concierge with very dry affect.

Great hotel and service. The staff at this hotel will go out of their way to deliver service that exceeds your expectations. Would definitely stay again, again and again. The night before my departure, my husband called to ask if he could get something special (chocolate) sent to my room with a note. The staff member stated he would take care of and don't worry about it. My husband asked how can I pay you and he responded "no problem" for he will take care of it. He ended up buying a bag of M&M's (my favorite) that made my night so special. 
Wow, what customer service. The conversation and action by the team at the hotel has made it to a life long impression that I will to tell everybody how wonderful the team at the Dallas Forth Worth Holiday Inn was.

I stayed here on vacation. The outside of the hotel is not impressive and looks like a bog standard hotel, inside I found all the members of staff very friendly on reception and helpful at 4am when I had jet lag and an issue with the free wifi not working.
I thoroughly enjoyed our 2 night stay. The metro was so close by, with a Starbucks just by the entrance (what more could you need?) The beds and pillows were very comfortable and although we were driven by price and wanted a 3 star hotel but did not want to break the bank, we had good nights sleep, there were 3 available computers in the foyer and there were ample towels in the bathroom. The room was completely clean.
I recommend this hotel. Yes, it was a standard Days Inn with no frills, but as a base for some hard core sight seeing it was perfect.

Just spent the weekend in Boston visiting my son. Although I have stayed at many Four Seasons properties, I have never stayed at this property in Boston. After three nights, I can honestly say without hesitation, that the experience at the Four Seasons Boston was truly outstanding. The location, condition of the hotel, amenities, and service provided by all staff members was absolutely perfect. Although expensive, you do indeed get what you pay for. Rest assured, at the end of the day--you will be extremely satisfied with your decision to stay at the Four Seasons !!

We booked this hotel for my birthday trip. Since we travelled with a 6 & 8 year old, we requested a double queen room. Reviews I had read did not lie. This hotel was lovely! A nice change from the huge chain hotels we have booked in the past. The rooms were very spacious. Most importantly, the bathrooms were large as well. Concierge service was nice and the included continental breakfast was just enough for us. We even received a bottle of champagne as a birthday gift. Our room was on the front of the building. The Book of Mormon was playing just steps away, yet we did not have any street noise. I highly recommend this hotel, and will stay here on my next visit.

I heart Nine Zero. Very boutique-y format. Happy hour every night. And the front desk greets you with a glass of wine if you miss the happy hour -- which is likely if you (like me) are in Boston for work. Make sure you join the loyalty program. You get $10 in minibar credits with each stay!
Love the bathrobe. Love the toiletries. Love the room service menu and how quickly the food comes. Love the chenille footie socks (hate the price). Love the customer service; I had an issue with room service and the front desk comped my entire meal, not just the part of the meal that was troublesome. It says a lot that the hotel empowers its staff to rectify service issues on the spot without management intervention.
Kimpton has definitely gotten it right, you'll be very pleased.

Arriving at around 11pm, we checked in to our room and quickly sought something to eat. Luckily, the Thai restaurant across the road is open til 1am every day so we really enjoyed some Pad Thai and satays in our room. The guy that the desk told us about another Thai restaurant nearby which he recommended so we tried that one the next night and weren't disappointed. Our room was quite basic but not a bad size, nice and clean and even had a small kitchenette. The tv worked well and we quite enjoy old buildings with character so the fact that it is dated doesn't matter to us. Basic breakfast, coffee, tea, croissants etc are included in the tariff as well as afternoon wine and cheese in the lounge area which was a lovely touch, almost like a b&b feeling. The only hiccup we had was that we couldnt connect to the free wifi from our room. we had to go out to the landing and sit on the steps. This hotel is very reasonably priced being so close to Union Square and I wouldn't hesitate recommending to anyone.

This property is a tourists dream. It is adjacent to the Alamo and across the street from the Paseo del Alamo which is a beautifully landscaped series of terraced steps with waterfalls that takes you from the street level to the river level. In front of this area, you find relics from the original outer walls of the Alamo Compound and it gives you a true sense of the actual size of the compound. The Menger Hotel takes you back in time to a period of charm and grace but, it does not eliminate any of the modern ammenities.
Their service is unparalled. Enjoy your stay!!

Have stayed at this great, vintage, first class hotel many times over the years. Restaurants are simply outstanding !! Learned of a turn-of-century underground passage way to a historic and renovated building across street which was at times in the past ( all the way back to gold rush period to the 1930's) a bordello, speakeasy,gambling den and mens club.........now the passage is closed, and the building renovation is excellent. A must experience for the traveller seeking a "historic" experience.

title_masked: Good neighborhood, rooms are less 'stylish' than customary
text_masked: A nice mid-town location, good neighborhood. The older-style room was not quite the usual stylish W room. The shower curtain was hung so high that it barely reached the tub and eventually it would extend over the edge if you brushed it and dump the shower water onto the floor. Very little shelf space in the bathroom. No side chair, room too small for that. I had an upgraded corner room with windows on two sides. Nothing special would not do again. Got free internet with my Gold upgrade. Had breakfast twice. Nothing special, sausage was not fully cooked. Go for the cereal. Took the free Acura test ride to the train station. Very good experience. Recommended.

Average hotel. Nothing bad, but nothing great. The typical decent hotel you would find on the side of an expressway.
Definately can't find anything within walking distance but if you have a car, Austin's South Congress neighborhood is fairly close, maybe 10 mintues, another 10 mintues up and you're downtown. They have a gym but it's lacking at best. I ended up asking is there was a trail or sidewalk to run and the front desk sent me to a path behind the Best Buy down the street (not a good idea).
I stayed here for about a week and did not have any problems, however my colleague's whole reservation was moved, then canceled. He ended up telling them not to bother getting him a room and he stayed at a friend's in town.
The rooms were good, average, and decently clean. Mine had a bad smell for the first couple days but you run in to that every now and then.

title_masked: Loved this place! Work or fun!
text_masked:
I travel to Chicago often, but I don't often review the hotels because let's face it - Most Chicago hotels have small rooms, dark hallways and that "musty" building smell. 
The Radisson Blue Aqua was NONE of these things. My city-view room actually had a view of the city! The rooms were large and comfortable with a great desk space, VERY comfortable bed with superior linens and love the squishy pillows. The wonderful lighting options in the room were a great benefit. The furnishings were modern without giving an "Ikea modern" vibe. The bathroom was fabulous with a chic glass door walk-in shower that I now depserately want in my own home. :-) There was also great light in the hallways which are lined with fun wall art. Best of all? It was quiet. Peope were coming and going, but the solidly built room ensured those noises didn't impact me. 
I arrived early for check-in and they greeted me promptly, they found me a room and even escorted me to the elevators. My room service lunch was delicious and the concierge recommened Asian cuisine was a divine (and delivered!) dinner. 
I attended an on-site conference the second day. The food at the conference FAR surpassed that which has been provided at other conference sites (hotels & clubs) in the city. The servers at our conference also far surpassed the typical service. They were attentive, helpful, respectful and friendly. 
And when I left something behind? They Fed-Exed it to me next day!
I have a new favorite work hotel and I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone wanting an exciting night on the town - just for fun. They have really done a great job here. Go check them out!

We stayed at this hotel for 10 nights in February 2012, so I think I can give a very good review. We were from out of state visiting family in the area.
First the good - Very comfortable beds. Some hotel beds are so hard you can't stay in one position for very long. These were wonderful beds, even "heavenly". Only problem was the woven blanket between the triple sheeting was a little stiff and scratchy. Softer blankets would be nice. Maybe they are very new and need to break in a little.
Room was comfortable with nice furniture setup. Never felt cramped. Loved the free WIFI!
Hotel grounds are immaculate! You could not find any chipped paint or beat up things anywhere. Very well maintained with beautiful landscaping. Excellent location to everything.
Staff was very helpful and friendly.
Price was excellent through Priceline. Try it!!!
Not so good - Being close to freeway (good and bad) can be noisy. Get in the tower suite area. Much quieter. Also parking can be difficult. We came back every evening after 10 and had difficulty finding parking spots. 
Try to get top floor. Several nights we heard people running around till almost midnight above us. Also shower has one of those saver heads. It was also positioned so high on the wall, it was a trickle by the time it hit you. And we are tall.
Several times we smelled cigarette smoke. Finally last time, my husband went outside and found a guy smoking on top floor balcony, flicking his butts off to right near our air conditioning. Nice little pile was building up. Wasn't hotel's fault but irksome, nevertheless. Made our room stink.
Overall a great place to stay.

title_masked: Great location by City Hall, good for business travelers
text_masked: I stay at this property often when on business at City Hall. The location can't be beat, and the staff are accommodating and friendly. The hotel restaurant is above-average in terms of quality for a hotel, I think, and the prices are not bad. I prefer it to the Residence Inn next door. While the Residence Inn has larger rooms, I think the rooms in the Courtyard are a bit nicer and more updated. The Executive Suite with the separate desk and sofa area are great for spreading out when you have work to do. My only complaint would be that the gym is small, (a few treadmills, 2 bikes, and 3 ellipticals and some weight equipment) and sometimes you have to wait for a machine in the morning. I have not visited the pool and can't comment on that.

title_masked: One of the worst rooms I stayed in
text_masked:
During my last visit I stayed in a hotel next to Union Square and was looking for the same location. This was the only available hotel for my dates. I stayed in the mystic junior room on the 3rd floor. Granted, it had some recent renovation and does not look old... but that's it.
To start with some good things: 
* Bar on the 2nd floor is amazing 
* You have a brick wall in the room that looks fancy 
* Free breakfast
To go on with the rest: 
* Cardboard walls 
* Ongoing renovation works (go nice with cardboard walls) 
* Windows of the room on 3rd floor that are not transparent - for a reason. They are overlooking a sidewalk and a dumpster right in front of them. It's not 3rd but the ground floor on this side of the building. 
* A garbage truck comes at 6:30 every morning to pick up the trash cans with lots of bottles in it, right next to your window. OTOH, it's a nice wake up call for the morning meetings 
* Room 309 has emergency exit right behind the cardboard wall next to bed - people are carrying and dropping pianos or something equally heavy and noisy within 20 cm from your head while you're trying to sleep 
* Rough and ragged towels - they are actually falling apart and have threads hanging from the fringe 
* Very poor room cleaning service 
* Lack of desk or drawer
* Safe is just a box next to the window (on the ground level, remember), not bolted or attached to anything - it looks very easy to break in, grab it and go away.
Maybe rooms on the floors 4 and up are better. If you're looking for a good location in the shopping area and a decent bar, it might work for you. If you're looking for a place to actually rest and sleep - it's the wrong place, at least in the junior type of room.

No this isn't the Hilton which is located nearby if you want to pay for it, otherwise why complain?
The staff here is great. This is a long term stay place so you do get neighbors of all sorts, just like real life- we have to get along with others. I felt safe. Anything that needed done got done quickly. Everything you need is in walking distance and I met some people in my couple of months there that I will remember forever.

title_masked: Fab, cute hotel in central Manhatten
text_masked:
This is GREAT hotel! Definitely one of the cheapest we could find in Manhatten and it's a brilliant find. The staff are super friendly (And their uniforms are amazing!) and there are quirky little details throughout the hotel.
We stayed in the bunk bed room and whilst it is TINY it really doesn't matter, you won't be spending a lot of time in your room whilst in NYC! Both bunks have their own Tvs and reading lights. The Jane also have free wifi which is great.
The cafe at the front of the hotel is also really great with good service, but there are also fab places to eat and drink at around the West Village/Chelsea/Bleeker Street.
The hotel is about a 5/10 min walk from the 14th Street/8th Ave Subway station and perfect for exploring NYC. The aircon in the rooms isn't amazing but it did us fine and we were there in the heatwave so should be fine during the normal summer months!
Absolutely loved this hotel and the added extra of robes and slippers is great!

My family and I (6 in total) booked 2 one bedroom suites for 3 nights and loved this hotel. It may not be the most swish hotel I've stayed in but we felt so at home here and it worked very well for a family as we could all relax together. The pool was lovely and the service second to none - there was nothing they couldn't do for us and they were sooo friendly and helpful. It was ideally located, just round the corner from the Walk of Fame and all the tour buses started here. We loved all the snacks too! So kind, I would definitely stay here again and recommend it to anyone. It was nice not to be in a high rise hotel too.

title_masked: Um, didn't mention the renovations until I arrived
text_masked: I'm a Marriott person (those of you who are fellow Marriott people know what I'm talking about). So I try to stay at Marriott hotels whenever I can. But - bad Marriott! I would like to know ahead of time if the hotel I am booking is undergoing major renovations! The lobby is a disaster zone. Ice machines are out of order. The fitness center is closed (but you can use the one at the Courtyard that is nearby - I did, and I left wishing I was staying at the Courtyard). I recommend waiting a few months before staying here. It will probably be fine once the renovations are done but ugh for the meantime.

title_masked: Great Place...Check-In was a disaster, but Otherwise Great
text_masked:
I'm just going to break it down piece by piece...
Arriving at the hotel: The hotel entrance is kinda weird. You can only enter from the side street. There is a huge empty parking lot on Broadway. I pulled into this parking lot because it looks like it goes right up to the front doors of the hotel. Wrong. You have to turn onto Gulfmart Street then take a left into the actual hotel parking. You can park in the huge parking lot since it's just a few steps from the entrance, but it's not the hotel's, so there were some construction vehicles parked in there. Either way, your preference.
Check-In: This was great (at first). A gentleman welcomed me and asked my name, etc.. I handed him the hotel's paperwork to verify that the card to be charged was not mine personally, but a corporate company card. He took it, all was good, and I got my key. 5 minutes into walking into my room, the room phone rang and it was the front desk telling me that my corporate card declined and I needed to come back to the front desk. I'm not sure how other company cards are, but usually the limits are high enough to charge a room to. I went back downstairs and a female at the front desk informed that it was declined and they needed another card. (Did I mention she was too busy to help me at first because she was talking to her son standing at her desk?) Especially with the way she said it as if I was someone off the street trying to scam the hotel. I was so embarrassed, especially since there were other guests standing there watching. Extremely annoyed and embarrassed, I told her I was going to go back to my room and get another card. While I was going to my room, one of my co-workers were trying to order from the bar and the bartender informed them that the credit card machines are working properly so he needed to pay cash. Really?!?! Your credit card machine wasn't working?!?! So basically the female on duty that embarrassed me in front of other people regarding my "declined" credit card, was wrong! How the hell does a bartender know the credit card machine isn't working but the front desk clerk doesn't?? Normally they would know before anyone else. At the end the room was charged. So all this unnecessary drama left me aggravated, embarrassed, and a sour taste towards the hotel service.
Room: The room was great! The bathroom has the designer sinks, amenities, hair dryer, etc.. There is a mini living room area with a love seat, ottoman, chair, and a flat screen on the wall. Next to the tv is a nice sized desk with a hard-wire internet access (although they give you a wifi password as well). (If you have an iphone, after you go to general settings to choose the hotel's wifi, you have to go to "safari" and log-in there with the hotel's username & password in order to get wifi on your phone.) There was a full length framed mirror, which was a nice addition. In front of the desk was a frosted window-type opening that you can open and close. I'm assuming that is for when someone is sleeping while another person is at the desk working??? On the other side of the window is the bed, small closet with a safe (in the wall), dresser with a flat screen tv, night stands, and a bench. There was also a console with a mini-fridge and microwave. Make sure you turn the fridge's settings when you put your stuff in there. I thought it was already on, so later when I go to get a drink, it was all warm. On top is a mini coffee maker with coffee, tea, etc..
Continental Breakfast: A great addition to staying here is the free breakfast. There were eggs, bacon, potatoes, bagels, mini-muffins, oatmeal, cold cereal, canned fruit, toast, and a belgian waffle maker. Plus apple, cranberry, and orange juice. 
Bar: Bar drinks were good. Little pricey, but you expect that with a hotel bar.
So all and all I liked the hotel. I give it 4 stars only because of the drama during check-in.

Not a bad hotel for a 1 night stay. Wouldn't stay there more than that. Hotel was filled with families and kids screaming all over the place. Of course that's because it's close to Sea World. The room was clean, only had and issue with the A/C, but it really doesn't get hot in San Diego so it wasn't a big concern. Also the person doing the hotel laundry laundry may want to wear a hair net, i had towels covered in long black hairs, but honestly you can't catch anything from a strain of hair. Just one word of advice DO NOT STAY IN ROOM # 119! Right next to the elevator and the hotel cleaning staff will wake you up bright and early while they try work.

Really enjoyed this for a business conference. SO close to Seaport Village, 10 minutes from Sea World. Better than average gym, cool rooftop pool and firepits. 40th-floor bar was nice and the food at the conference was good. The area was much improved over what I remember for San Diego (5-10 years ago) and there were a lot of people out running and enjoying the area. The hotel is dog friendly. Lots of good places to sit and have mini-meetings, and seemed like lots of good dinner/breakfast places in Seaport Village. As a side note, my family came down the last night and some of the casual dining places in Seaport Village are very pricey (too high for the quality) BUT the carousel is a good deal, open late, and gives kids things to do. A fair amount of places to walk/jog in the area.

title_masked: Great hotel and easy access to LAX
text_masked: I am a big fan of this hotel, not to mention its close proximity to the rental car lots and LAX. The staff is very professional and helpful, Mr [NAME] always greets me upon my arrival. The lobby lounge has great food and drink along with friendly service from the staff, especially Carlos. The rooms are very clean and have a fresh clean odor when entering and the bedding is fantastic; other Marriott brands could learn from this hotel on the proper way to prepare a bed. The VIP lounge is always great with delicious food, friendly service and a wonderful view of LAX.

Extrodinary: Thank you to the staff. Especially Bonney Eberts, for the concern for our needs for 3 rooms. She is an Extrodinary Professional, she really treated us with respect and dignity. She made the trip from New Mexico and the stay extremely enjoyable and worry free for my team. I asked her to quit you and come to work for me. She is an asset to your company, she is bright, concerned, very interested in our disposition, and actually came out to meet me and my team. With service and attention to detail, she alone made the trip worth while. Thank you, Bonney and your staff for the treatment that you rendered to us. Bonney is exceptional and with her there, anytime that I and my tear are in Phoenix, we will look forward to staying at the InnPlace Hotel Phoenix. If I am ever in Phoenix again I will plan on staying there. I was the best experience that I have ever had staying in any Hotel I have ever been in. It was the friendly staff at this business that will keep us coming back. Thank you again, Bonney Eberts!!

The staff is very friendly and helpful. I love the lobby fireplace, wine hour and fresh baked cookies! I had stayed here a few years ago and remember enjoying my visit so I decided to stay again with my daughter for our mother/daughter get away! I am looking forward to our next visit at the Hotel Triton! Also a great location, a few blocks from cable car, shopping, next to Chinatown.

On a trip to support my daughter in a beauty pageant several weeks ago, I stayed in the Sheraton Universal where I had a very bad experience. To make a long story short, a waiter got our check mixed up with another check. The problem, mistakes happen, the problem was, the other person's card had already been entered, and my bill charged to their account. The other patron had complained, how they didn't have a lot of money, because my check bill was 4 times what they should have paid. The problem was the Manager, Mr [NAME], insulted the other patron, by telling them they were poor...and something to the fact, they shouldn't be eating here at the Sheraton.
This was very uncalled for and insulted the other patron. I believe managers should have more respect for customers.
I will return to the Sheraton, however; I hope that Manager receives some Management Training.

title_masked: Don't book here!! There is better around !
text_masked:
I called the lobby around 8 pm to get a fork and they didn't have one 
Forgot to clean my room till i got back and called them to do it .
Very noisy - Construction all around

I didn't have high expectation on this hotel since I've read the reviews on tripadvisor before I went. but I am still very disapointed.. not because of the small room without fridge and hair drier, but the poor service..
The first night finding out there was no hair drier in the room.. I called the front desk and the guy said he would send someone to bring us one. but after 20 mins, no one was coming.. I went to the reception by myself to take it, but the guy at the reception said he didn't have one there, he had to call someone to get it.. and he didn't even sounds friendly.. I went back and started watching a movie, and after one hour, still no one came.. I called again and the guy said sorry, he'll send someone right away, then another 10mins, again, no one came.. 
I called again, and being ignored this time.. so disappointed.. if you cant find one, can you just say sorry and tell me that?.. 
other than that, the location is great, very close to little Italy, where you can find a lot of good places to eat and hang out. the roof resteraunt has a good view too.
but.. I'll never come back..

title_masked: You are not recognizing my rewards partnership
text_masked: Everytime I book this hotel (which has been 4 times this year alone), I do not get credited with my rewards points or recognized as a reward member. This time they gave me my rewards number which does not look like the number I remember receiving when we signed up. This is very frustrating.

title_masked: Expensive but tolerable for a conference stay.
text_masked:
Standard room, nothing special, but all the amenities were available (soap, toothpaste, plenty of towels, an empty refridgerater and coffee). Housekeeping did a great job keeping the place tidy. Bed was comfortable for us. We paid a special group rate of $229 for a conference but there was an extra $40 plus worth of tax each night. Rooms although comfortable definitely needs a remodel for the price they charge. 15 minute walk to chinatown/financial district. Close to the BART stops. Lots of places to eat around the restaurant--the Embarcardero market is right in front of the hotel--of course everything is tourisy expensive. We stayed in room 336 and unfortunately, it was right above the lobby's open restaurant, so we can most definitely hear the noise up till 1-2am (especially on Friday night)--better insulation is needed. 
TIP on PARKING: valet only if through the hotel, $57 each night with in/out privileges (but it'll take them FOREVER to get your car--call them 15minutes ahead of time). ALTERNATIVE: park in the parking structure on DRUMM, between Sacramento and CLAY, it's $32 per 24hours (although no in/out privileges). It's a VERY short walk to the hotel, and the funny thing is the hotel uses them also--and they just upcharge their hotel customers $25 for valet. 
Probably wouldn't stay here if it was just for leisure.

My husband and I recently stayed at the beautiful, luxurious Fairmont Hotel in Downtown Boston at Copley Plaza. This hotel is conveniently located to the best shopping and dining in Boston. We felt like we were right in the heart of the city and the subway was right across from the hotel. We had a few issues with our room but the Hotel GM made sure that we had everything we needed for our stay. GM Paul Tormley is an excellent asset to the Hotel Business and we will happily recommend this hotel to our friends and colleagues in the future.

I recently lodged and attended a conference at the Westin Riverwalk. I was very impressed with my room, the physical structure of the hotel, the high degree of professionalism and customer service exhibited by the staff and the quality of the food served in the restaurant. Particularly noteworthy was the service I received at Starbucks. Lorraine is very friendly and makes the best white moca I have ever tasted!
Two thumbs up for The Westin Riverwalk!! I highly recommend this hotel.

When arriving to hotel, I left my briefcase with i-pad, kindle, and next day meeting notes in cab. Located using i-pad locator, but it was moving around. Hotel manager worked with me and police for several hours to trace it down and recover it. Had my notes in time for the meeting. Well done!

title_masked: friendly and customer service oriented staff make the difference
text_masked: Stayed April 29 to May 5 with family for one week vacation in New York. Had read the previous reviews on Tripadvisor which were very good. Did not disappoint. Stayed on the 12th floor. Upon check in, we had two queens that were too soft ( have a bad back) and front desk kindly moved us to another room, where beds were more firm. Hotel is very well managed, have committed staff, and this is why they consistently are rated very well. Location is very central to theatres, times square, walkable to central park ( 15 min), empire state building (15 min). Grayline sight seeing bus across the street, as well as Bikram Yoga NYC. Restaurants in times square are so so, but concierge was very helpful in guiding you to restaurants in Hell's Kitchen and nearby. Would come back again.

title_masked: NO returned calls by the Accounting Dept.
text_masked: Accounting Dept. does not return phone calls after complaints made. I stayed at the hotel on February the 4th and after finding out that the billing had been charged to my credit card instead of charging the bill to the promotional company, I called the hotel on February the 9th., and was told by guest services that I'd have to contact the Accounting Dept. for reimbursement. I called the Accounting Dept. and left a mesage and the recorder states that they will get back with you right away...not really! I called again today February the 13th and had to leave another message that they call me back today. Will I have to leave another messsage or will I have to take a trip to San Antonio and demand service?

Stayed two nights for the Irish Dance Competition in July. Very short walk from the train station so it is conveniently located. Check in was quick--they had a room available at 11AM when we arrived so we were allowed to check in early which was wonderful since the heat wave was well under way at that point! The staff is efficient, friendly and helpful. The room was clean and spacious (Single room, King sized bed) and had a fabulous view (room 1472) especially at night! Loved the food at Daddy O and the coffee at the express counter. The food was a bit pricey at the restaurant on the 1st floor--but it was tasty!

title_masked: Lockheed Martin Rate Great For this hotel
text_masked: We had to stay in the San Jose area due to sunnyvale area was sold out. They offered us a great Lockheed Martin Rate of $106. Great Breakfast, and Dinner in the Island Grill was very good. Will stay here next time and just only about 10mins away to Lockheed.

We stayed at this hotel 3 days (2 separate bookings) over a 10 day period and found it to be very nice. We got a terrific deal on priceline - $85 per night. I noticed a comment about no hair dryer in another review - it's in the cabinet with the iron/board. Beds were very comfortable and furnishings were tasteful. The hotel is located just off I -93 and is behind South Bay Center which has a Target, BestBuy, Home Depot, supermarket, TGI Fridays, Olive Garden, etc. There's a liquor store just south of the shopping center and a gas station 8 blocks east of that. The subway is about 3 blocks away (next to Dunkin' Donuts) and the hotel offers a free shuttle through the slightly sketchy neighborhood. Hotel has a laundry ($2 wash/$2 dry) and offers free soap/dryer sheets. Breakfast was too spendy, but not bad. Hotel pub closes early; 10 pm. Pool and hot tub nice, gym reasonably equipped. Overall a very nice place, convenient to the airport and downtown, and reasonably priced if you book it right.

The hotel was great, but I have to say the location is the best part. Very central to sightseeing, shopping and transportation. Also, because it's right on the river it was really easy to find your way back, you just had to find the river. We had booked two rooms and both were great. The room with the two queen beds was huge, including a huge bathroom. The room with the king bed was quite a bit smaller, bathroom as well, but it had an amazing view up the river. Loved the view! Rooms were kept clean and were comfortable. Staff at the front desk were great. Very friendly and very helpful.
Negatives would have to be: very noisy from the hall. Could hear doors closing all the time. Did not hear anyone in the rooms beside, only hallway noise. Bathtub/shower very slow to drain. Also the toilet in the one room kept running, very annoying noise. Personally pillows were far to soft for my liking (this is personal preference). 
I would definitely recommend this hotel.

I agree with the superlatives others have offered. New. Contemporary. Stylish. But the mattress was the worst ever in the US. I got a terrible night's sleep, woke up frequently and finally with an aching back (very unusual for me). Even my wife thought it was painfully soft. For an equally soft, unsupportive mattress you have to go to the UK. And $10 for a breakfast only a little better than Holiday In Express. Avoid.

I stayed there on business and will not go back. My room was on the second floor, facing canal street, and even with earplugs it was impossible to sleep. Innaddition, the rooms are so tiny that they won't even fit a closet, so you can't hang your clothes anywhere.
The laundry service failed to pick up my clothes on time even though I called them a good hour before the deadline for same day return. Wen I got back to my room in the evening, my clothes weren't back and the front desk told me they would be back by 10am the next day. Unfortunately I had to check out at 7am. The front desk clerk was very helpful and arranged to have it delivered during the night at 2am so that I could get it there upon checkout.
In fact, the front desk staff is the redeeming feature about this place. All the receptionists I had to deal with were polite and helful. The other one good point is that my room and bathroom were spotless. Finally the location is perfect for downtown.

The room was very clean and the bed was very comfortable.This hotel was located in walking distance for restaurants and a Movie Theater which was very convienient. Hotel was very nice and the staff was very friendly. I would definitely stay here again.

Well this hotel is in two parts, i opted what appears to be the more older part, the Bay tower. i say older as the decor appears to show this. But the Bay Tower has larger rooms and accomodated the gymnasts i took away. I had 5 in one room, we paid an extra fee for a roll-a-way bed. I had a double bed in a room looking over the Marina and the airport beyond this. I have to say the bed was incredibly comfy. Pillows were as well. Its not often i can stay in a hotel bed without aches etc as we all like our own bed. But this hotel was the best ever. the planes landing and taking off did not bother me and also the Marina side you get to see the fireworks every night from the distant Sea world. But i wanted to see the other view out at sea so asked to change, so they moved e from floor 9 to floor 10 with no fuss at all, they also gave me an additional fridge in both rooms free of charge. They get very irritated if you use the fridge with their drinks to house yours stuff, and will charge you too if you do it. Anyway the Sea view was in my view better, great view of the bridge and the city town town...stunning at night. So for me this was the better side....but both are really nice. The bathroom was dated in my view, about 3 star basic stuff to be honest, kind of lets the rooms down which are lovely. Great to have an ironing board and iron and also in room safe....the usual coffee machine, USA hotels really need to consider the English, i took my travel kettle so i could have a nice cup of tea, took about ten minutes mind you, maybe longer to boil. Towels were great no issues there, room cleaned daily but if you opt out you get 5 dollars voucher which can be taken off breakfast. rates don't include breakfast unless booked via a holiday company. Breakfast is 22 dollars an adult under 10 free and over tens ( ie kids) is 11 dollars. Have to say their breakfast was the best i have ever had in USA. You have great choice in fruit, blue berries, black berries, strawberries, pineapple melons, wicked choice, cereals, cakes and of course hot cooked food as well...a stunning breakfast and great service...for me a 9 out of 10 and a 4 star easily. Now where the hotel pissed me off was when i found it was 22 dollars to park your car each day, i had two cars due to gymnasts so it cost me $440 to park two cars....this i found was too expensive and has put me off staying there again as i hate being ripped off. Also if you want internet its free in the lobby, but if you want it in your room its 11 dollars a day or 18 if you want it to be fast!!!..they are losing the plot here for me, how unfriendly is that..If i as running a hotel nearby it would be free. again it was not too friendly and its a shame. The hotel is a nice place to stay, rooms good, views great, food good, service good, parking and internet a total rip off. Swimming pool is good and you can walk in 4 minutes to the other main hotel and use their pools as well. You need a car to get about or use taxis, airport is across the road so take minutes to get there, they have a shuttle which takes you there too. I loved staying at the hotel, but if you have a budget it can catch you out...overall i would give it a thumbs up. You need a good bed lets be honest and they have that right, in both rooms i used. bathroom as i said dated and basic, did the job. One last thing if you use the room service for food and stuff, expect it to be not cheap...but again good service. All outside areas which includes the whole town is very clean... i like San Diego been 3 times now going back in Oct 2012 for just two days but at 850 dollars without breakfast and without parking rights for two rooms for just two nights...i wont be at the Sheraton....shame as i liked it!

We stayed at the hotel just two weeks ago and I'm still so impressed. 
From the moment we walked into the clean and accommodating lobby, to the check in process, room (more on that in a moment!), and most importantly - a most professional, helpful and awesome staff.
We were blown away. I've stayed in Manhattan more times than I can count - this is by FAR the best hotel experience I've had (sorry Ritz.)
We were upgraded to the Penthouse level (yay Hyatt rewards program!). Oh-em-gee .... a roof patio! The room was gigantic - especially by NY standards. The lounge is awesome and I'm in love with their espresso machine. The concierge was very helpful and we had a few ideas where we wanted to dine the last night and Eataly was great experience. She suggested it for a unique experience over the hotel restaurant. 
Most of all - the staff went above and beyond. Jordan was so awesome - he handled our check in (room wasn't quite ready, so he had us relax in the lounge while he handled check in) and he risked life and limb during an epic thunderstorm on our 2nd day to score us a taxi to get to an appointment on time. 
I will not think twice when booking my next hotel in NYC - Hyatt 48 Lex is terrific hotel and excellent value. Yes, you can find cheaper hotels. But I found it to be terrific value for NYC and we enjoyed the amenities. Wow. Such an outstanding experience and I can't wait to return.

We stayed one night to go to an event at Staples center, as it is a short walk. It was on the small side, but that's the way downtown hotels tend to be. Room was clean and modern, comfortable bed and small frig. The complimentary breakfast (bagels, pastries, coffee, tea, juice, fruit) wouldn't be enough for someone with a big appetite, but sufficient as a continental breakfast. The pastries were very good. We were worried that the room might be noisy since we faced the street side, but it wasn't. We parked in the parking garage right next door ($12).
Great time staying there for sure! Steve Richardson was the man! Very friendly and a great help while enjoying my visit :)

We chose this hotel to celebrate our 20th anniversary. We live less than an hour away but hadn't stayed over at this hotel for over 16 years. From arrival to departure, an outstanding experience with no exceptions. We were upgraded to a harbor suite which only made our stay that much more enjoyable and memorable. The view, accomodations, amenities, location and restaurants were all first class. The 5-star package was the key to a great stay with nothing left to chance or think about except to relax and enjoy.

title_masked: Great service and all the Staff are just wonderful!!!
text_masked:
This is the first time that I have have a great experience at this hotel. Great service and all the Staff was so friendly and always with a smile! The room was exceptionally clean and the bed very comfortable. Something that I really loved was the fact that you can bring your dog and the hotel will provide your pet with a doggy bed, 2 bowls for water and food with a mat, I just loved it!!!!!
I will rated with AAA+++ Highly recommended!!!!!!!

Nice hotel. Friendly staff. They genuinely treated me well and were helpful in terms of telling me where I needed to go to downtown. The hotel is conveniently located to points of interest downtown. You can get a ride to Rendevous and be there within minutes. The lobby is clean and has a professional appearance.

Positive-
Clean, easy to get to, close to Madison square garden, short walk to time square and surrounding area. 
Downside-
Rooms were very small. 
hotel has no fitness facility. You had to pay I believe $15 to use another locations workout facility.

title_masked: Thank goodness the company was paying...
text_masked:
I can honestly say that in all my travels including hotels and hostels across the developed and developing worlds, that this is one of the worst places that I have stayed in terms of value. At over $250 a night, I would have expected more than surly staff, terrible breakfasts and tired decor but that is all that I received. 
I was travelling on business. The location was good. My stay started badly when I discretely told them that I was pregnant but that I didn't want my colleague to know. I told them because I was hoping that they could find me a room before I had to head off to the office so that I could shower after our flight from the UK. They did find me a room but not before saying loudly in front of my colleague that it was "only because I was pregnant". I was horrified!
The room was really old and badly laid out. Limited power sockets and a tiny bathroom. I don't need a TV in the bathroom - I would just prefer a hair dryer with a power lead that could make it to the power socket! Evening turn down apparently included but did not happen every night.
The breakfast was a joke. They included American Breakfast in the price of the room but you could not order off the menu. You could either have a fry-up or cereal. Not both. No pancakes or waffles (apparently those aren't part of an American Breakfast). The toast was stale and cold, the portions were small. It was the first time in all my years of travel that I have ever gone and bought breakfast when it was included in the price of my room - that was how much I couldn't face it on my second morning there!
The bill was wrong at the end - a bunch of costs I never made. When trying to get them to sort the bill, I nearly lost the will to live. I am still waiting for my credit card bill to see how much I paid as they were unable to produce me a full correct invoice. The girl at the desk rolled her eyes at me - I asked her not to do it again - she said that it was her face! It wasn't... 
My colleagues had similar problems and we all decided it was one of the worst places we had ever stayed. I really don't say this lightly - my reviews show that I travel in all sorts of different ways with varying degrees of accommodation but this fell well below my expectations.
Go find yourself anywhere else to stay - it will be better than this overpriced, rudely staffed hole... These people don't listen and thus they will never learn...

title_masked: Room was clean, service was good but the heat/air condtitioning was not good.
text_masked: The location was perfect for where we were going. Got into our room and the fire alarm was going off. Maintance was wonderful came right in and changed battery. Went to dinner came back it was going off again. Called front desk and with a few minutes maintaince was there to replace the alarm. Great! Then it was cold so we turned the heat up. Then when it got too warm the air conditoning unit kicked in. It was hot/cold all night long. Blankets on then off. I have a bad back so by the time I got up I was in alot of pain. I have stayed at Ramada before and always rated them high. This one not so good. Staff members had coats on, they must have been cold too.

My company choose this hotel for employees. 
Good points ... 
Very clean room
Mega comfortable bed 
Central location in Phillie
Bad points
The staff servicing the rooms appear to have no concept of noise ... They happily on several occasions, were happy to allows guest room doors to slam from fully open to shut. I had room 1227 that was close to the banging door of the service area. The room maids were gathered on several occasions loudly chatting. This spoilt what should be a great experience. 
The only other point in regards to room service .. There is a $ 3.50 tray charge added. Then after the cost of food is applied , a 20% service charge. ... $17 food ,$8 worth of service charge ... Whilst the foo was good and tasty, I will be using the wok Chinese resturant about 2 mins away in the future.

title_masked: Excellent hotel. Very clean. Courteous staff.
text_masked: We stayed here December 7-9 2012. Had a double room. Room was very spacious. Room, lobby and breakfast area all very clean. Breakfast was the standard continental-eggs, waffles, bagels, donuts. Staff was helpful and friendly. Convenient location.

I stayed here with my mum back in July and we had a fantastic time.The sheets were spanking new, and the pillows were so comfy and had that delicous wiff of duck feathers. We absolutley loved the exciting bold decoration everywhere and enjoyed chilling after a day out in the lounge. This had a constant supply of freezing cold water, usually flavoured with floating fruits (lovely touch), and teas, coffees and hot chocolate.
Every staff member we saw would always greet us with a friendly smile, and the petite girl with dark hair (sorry I forget her name!) was particulary helpful. She even went out her way to find the nearest place where we could by a kindle and other shops we wanted to peruse. They were also happy for me to use the lounge after I'd checked out for the day, with their speedy wifi.
The hotel itself is in a great location - close to subway stops, and wasn't far from Central Park either. We also were happy to find that Carnegie's Delhi (think man v's food) was round the corner.
I'd definatley stay here again in a heart beat...if only to sleep in that bed again!

I have stayed at this Times Square location for several years. It is a great location for theater attendees and the action of the Square itself. The rooms are ok and have been refurbished from time to time. As far as I can tell, the concierge lounge has not, and it is woefully short of the usual Marriott standards. We stayed three nights in the middle of April, and the lounge was packed each time we tried to go in. It was a joke, and we ended up giving up! It desperately needs expansion and a make over. Other than the location, one might consider staying elsewhere for awhile.

We arrived at the front desk with four of us -- two adults and two teenage kids to find out that our single room with a king bed wouldn't accommodate a roll-away. The young lady at the front desk looked puzzled briefly, but then very courteously said "let me see what I can do here" and managed to get us a room with twin double beds -- perfect! It saved me from having to get two rooms and we have a great view of the DuPont Circle Park.
Room service is pricey, but the food is quite good and the service is excellent. The rooms are nice appointed and very clean, but quite small. It's a bit tight with four of us, but not unexpected given the locale and desirability of this area. The decor is modern but not sparse like you might find in a European hotel. The fixtures are bold but with muted colors - they fit the decor and add to the ambience. 
The vibe that we get here is that there are "big things" going on -- the clientele are well dressed and appear to be quite driven. I must admit that I accidentally eavesdropped on some nearby visitors and found the conversation interesting! It sounded like they had some aggressive growth plans for their business.
The DuPont Circle Metro stop is a couple of blocks away and there are plenty of places to get a bite to eat or a snack/coffee/tea along the streets surrounding this hotel. It's just a few stops in any direction to get to the better attractions in DC. We like the location.
The restaurants span the price spectrum from $, $$, to $$$. I personally liked the looks of ShopHouse Asian Cafe - I'm headed there tomorrow and I'll review it after I test it out.
Internet service is complimentary and the connection is solid. 
Overall, the experience has been great and we would certainly both recommend this hotel as well as visit again on a future stop in DC.
Happy Travels!

title_masked: Caught Scabbies from the Hotel Bed
text_masked: The hotel is very old and in the homeless section of Indianapolis. The rooms are dirty and not cleaned very well. Although they do wash the sheets occansionaly, the bedspreads, pillows, mattress cover, and comforter are not washed. After staying at the hotel for four days, I broke out in a rash over 80% of my body. I went to the doctor and found out that I caught Scabbies from the Hotel. I have had to put pesticide lotion on my body head to toe once every 7 days. Most of the rash is gone except my feet where the scabbies had bittin me the most.

title_masked: Great location in Times Square and great staff
text_masked: We have stayed at the Edison three times and have enjoyed our stay each time. The staff is committed to being as helpful as possible and always ready to listen. One thing that stands out is that when the housekeeper saw that the bath oil bottle was completely empty (I love my long hot bubble baths.) she left me extra bottles so I would have enough. This may be a small item to some people, but to me, it was a very considerate thing to do. Some of the rooms are dated, but who doesn't like the retro look. I like the Edison for its location, friendly staff, and atmosphere.

Have stayed at several Hampton Inn's over the years and always leave satisfied, the pricing is fair, room very clean and comfortable. The staff always greets you with a smile and very helpfull with knowledge of the local area. Stayed here on business, so did not have time to enjoy the facilities. They do have valet parking for 35 or park yourself for 25, both off site at the end of the block. It's next to the Convention center, so you can leave your car and walk. The breakfast buffet is very convenient or if in a rush grab a bag on the way out. if back in Philly would stay again.

title_masked: Gorgeous Art Deco Hotel, Central to everything
text_masked: My family and I stayed here for 11 days and absolutely loved it. The New Yorker is central to everything. Macys is only a block away, Madison Square Garden is across the road, the Empire State Building is close by... the subway station is directly next to the hotel. This hotel is perfect for any New York stay. Great diner 'Tick Tock Diner' downstairs that is open 24 hours - and cheap for New York. There are also plenty of great places to eat nearby and a great pizza place across the road - Famiglias. The hotel reflects Art Deco style and boasts a gorgeous big foyer. The hotel also offers complimentary wireless internet, a gym and much more. Rooms and bathrooms are a little small - but overall we didn't spend much time in our rooms. Staff were warm and friendly. This hotel is excellent value for money and a great place to stay. This hotel is a safe comfortable choice for New York and you can't go wrong! Loved it!!!

title_masked: Glad we got to try the Renaissance
text_masked:
Glad I got to try the Renaissance! Really enjoyed it and it has to be on my top 5 list now of Hotels in Seattle. 
Parking-I didn’t park with the hotel. If you don’t need your car and just need a place to park there is the Madison garage (self-park) one block down. Total cost was $24 for 24 hours instead of about $36 with the hotel.
Check In-was a breeze with friendly staff. We had arrived early but they had a room ready. 
Room-We had a nice corner King Room with great views. Room was clean and showed very little wear (the bedroom had a small hole in the wall) but other than that, flawless. I really enjoyed having a living space and a separate bedroom. Room had a safe, mini fridge, and great TV’s. It also included a small coffee maker, great closet space, and everything you needed in a room. Bathroom was spacious as well.
As far as noise from Freeway and/or city, you’re in the city people so you get noise at any hotel. We were on 22nd floor and could still hear sirens, city noise, etc. But that’s part of the city so not sure why so many people complain about that. I do recommend asking for high floor if you can get one for the views.Bed was very comfortable and we had a great night’s sleep.
Location- About a $5-8 cab ride anywhere you need to be in the city. Yes, this hotel is on top of the hill on 6th Ave, but if you walk North to south and then down the hills, it’s not as bad.
We did utilize the lobby bar for a night cap. Liquor prices expensive as expected for any nice hotel. It was nice they had daily drink and beer specials though. We also used this area in the morning as they convert it into their coffee area. Staff was friendly and prices were fair.
Overall, I was impressed with the hotel and staff was very friendly every time we interacted with them. I would stay here again.

I stayed for 2 nights at this hotel after getting a good rate from priceline.com. The guest service is poor, they forgot to give the wake up call, luckily we had got up earlier. Never came across a hotel where they forgot to give the wake up call. They had advertised free shuttle to Sea World, but it is at specific hours only, and they wont tell you anything about it unless you keep on asking. The guest service lady acted funny when I requested for shuttle to old town (which was part of their service). She told me sheepishly that I could just walk up there, its not too far, or you could take a cab etc. The hotel room was ok, if you go to front desk and ask for creamers for the coffee maker, they are not very pleased to give extra ones. If you call guest services from your room, their answers are too abrupt.
