I requested for a shuttle back to the hotel from Sea World, and the guy rudely replied that I ll have to take the one which they send at 6 PM (which was 2 hrs later). The "continental breakfast" which was offered free, gives you bread, bagels, cheese horns and cup cakes, along with some juice and coffee. If you want pancake or eggs, you have to pay and eat at another break fast bar. I would never stay at this hotel again.

We booked this hotel purely based on the great tripadvisor reviews and we were not disappointed. We visited NYC to celebrate my husbands 40th birthday and after getting in touch with Connie Wang we were upgraded to a beautiful room overlooking the library (just what I had asked for) but not only that, the next day we were sent a complimentary bottle of bubbly on ice as a birthday gift. The staff were unobtrusive but helpfeul when needed (just how we like it). The room was spacious and the bathroom amazing with double sinks, robes, state of the art three way shower. The free snack and soft drinks in the room were a great touch. The location (only 10minutes walk from Times Square) was perfect for us. I cannot recommend this hotel highly enough and would definitely book again for my next trip.

title_masked: Different from the other luxury hotels!
text_masked:
The Edgewater is a luxury hotel for sure. The rooms are spacious and well appointed. We had rooms on the water, as requested. Each of our 3 rooms had a fireplace with two club chairs and a bear foot rest in front of the chairs. The king bed was comfortable, the sheets and pillowcases were very nice. There's a refrigerator that's very well stocked, but if you had anything you wanted to store in it, it was very crowded. Our room and bath were spotless.
The bath is large. There's a claw-footed tub and a separate glass surrounded shower. The bath floor is a little distracting as it's stone and concrete. The shower floor is the same.
Our view across the water included the downtown waterfront and we had a cruise ship dock right in front of us one day. After that ship unloaded and restocked for a new cruise another cruise ship docked in the same spot the next morning. Fascinating to watch.
We would certainly stay here again. It's an absolutely amazing change from the big box luxury hotels and is northwestern throughout.

The staff is awesome! You know them by name at the end of your stay. The rooms are nicely decorated & modern; the photos are accurate. Honestly,l splept better in their beds than any hotel I've stayed. Yes they are small, but very accommodating – not the ideal room for storing a lot of luggage or strollers, but we managed with a wheelchair and luggage for a 2 week vacation. Very close to Times Square & surrounding areas. We ended up needing a wheelchair & the concierge overheard us talking & arranged a discount rental through a pharmacy service they contract with – how unexpected & so easy. The service took the request over the phone & dropped off the chair at the hotel.

The lobby of the hotel may look nice but don't look too closely. The room was a disaster. It was loud, you can hear everything from garbage trucks to horns from thr cars downstirs (5 floors down as though the indow was wide open), it had a distinct odor and to top it all off, the toilet was broken. We were given another, quiter room but that was still a non-renovated room. There was a remote control for an air-con, but don't bother because there was only a ceiling fan/light, no air-con.
It is an old hotel. You might get one of those refurbished rooms, but I wouldn't try your luck.

title_masked: A treasure in New York City
text_masked:
I recently stayed at the Paramount Hotel for 7 days (4-23-12 to 4-30-12) and it was a wonderful experience! I chose the Paramount because of it’s proximity to the venue I was going to be spending most of my time in New York, as well as as for the reasonable cost. 
Right from the start, the Paramount showed themselves to be aggressive in providing the best possible experience from the patron. I had originally booked the hotel, then changed my mind and canceled it. A few days later I received an email offering me a 20% discount if I’d rebook my stay with them. That made the cost lower than anywhere else I’d been looking at, and so I did rebook. And it was definitely the right decision.
My one concern about the hotel, from reading all the reports here, was the size of the rooms. Yes, the smallest rooms are incredibly small, but they actually don’t have very many of those rooms. All you have to do is ask and you will get upgraded (at no additional charge, in my experience) to a Queen. This size room is perfectly adequate. The biggest problem is that there is very little in the way of practical furnishings in the room. I can see that that’s how the designers wanted it – they wanted to give the rooms a clean, spare look. They sacrificed functionality for the aesthetic. But all you have to do is ask and you can get extra luggage racks and a rolling table. There is plenty of space in the room for these, so even with their addition you won’t be cramped.
Initially I was given an room on the 8th floor. It would have been fine, except the design of the bathroom was such that the only way you could use the toilet was to sit sideways. There was almost no clearance between the side of the toilet and the wall, and there was a large heating unit in front of it. When I returned from my evening’s activities the night I checked in, I went to the front desk and mentioned this. The two lovely people behind the desk just about fell all over themselves to get me a better room. In particular, the lady knew exactly what I was talking about and said she knew just which rooms elsewhere in the hotel had bathrooms that were laid out better. They were very apologetic that they couldn’t change my room then and there, but assured me I would have a different and better room the very next day.
And they fulfilled this promise in a spectacular way. I was moved to room 1528 the next afternoon. It was the same size (Queen) as the first room, but the bathroom was laid out much more comfortably. The trade-off was the shower was just a stall instead of a full bathtub/shower unit, but it was perfectly fine. I asked for a second luggage rack, and a rolling table and was able to set up my room very comfortably. And as my room was on the 15th floor and at the front of the hotel, I had a wonderful view of the city from my window.
The hotel is amazingly soundproof. It was built in 1928 and they built buildings to be rock solid back then. No paper thin walls here! I never heard my neighbor’s tv or any other noise unless I was passing in front of their door. And even then it was very faint.
A special shout out to Anthony, the hotel’s IT manager. I had a problem with the wireless at the start, and Anthony came to my room and spent a considerable amount of time trying to solve it. As it turned out, it was more my equipment’s problem than the hotel’s. The wireless actually works quite well, and they’ve installed repeaters on every other floor so there’s no longer an issue with a weak signal on the upper floors. And the wireless in the lobby and on the 2nd floor (where the Library bar is located) is free!
Another shout-out to the lovely people at the concierge desk. I was always greeted with a cheerful welcome and they were unfailingly pleasant and happy to help me, no matter how much I pestered them with questions. Every suggestion they made for restaurants or sightseeing or transportation was excellent.
The housekeeping staff in the hotel is to be commended, too. Anything you ask for is brought to your room promptly, and with a smile. I asked for additional bath towels the first day, and every day after that the housekeeper replenished the same amount of towels that she took out. You’d think this would be a no-brainer, but I anywhere else I’ve stayed I always have to ask for extra towels every day. 
The thoughtfulness and care and attention to detail are very evident in everything the hotel does for it’s patrons. I would stay again at the Paramount in a heartbeat, and I will be recommending it to everyone I know who will be traveling to New York. Just remember to ask for a room upgrade and you will not be disappointed.

I enjoyed my stay at the Ramada Central. My proximity to UT was great, the rooms were clean and management was courteous and efficient. The daily breakfast was also very good. Thanks for a very pleasant stay!

We were pleasantly surprised with this hotel which was clean, roomy, and more upmarket than expected. Good downtown location close to Union Square, but as we were only there 2 nights we found ourselves having to travel down to the Wharf area 'where the action is' quite a bit, so if we went again to SFO on a short stay again I would stay in the Wharf area and not downtown. However this does not deter from the hotel. I just have 2 little niggles - firstly if you try to contact the hotel by email, it seems to go via the Kempton website and I never even got an acknowledgement despite sending 2 emails. Secondly, coffee is provided free in the lounge in the morning, but the cost of the coffee in the bar at night was way over priced and was only provided from a flask - not even fresh. Despite that we enjoyed our stay at this hotel.

I have to admit, midtown is not my favorite area of NYC so I wasn't so sure about this but my experience was really great. 
First, major points for having a room available for a very early check in. I took a red-eye in so I figured I'd have to drop my bags off and wait several hours before I got a room, but nope, the Marriott had one ready for me. That made my whole day. The front desk staff was super polite and helpful every time I needed them. Same goes for the bellman, concierge etc. Customer service here was top notch the entire time, not one complaint. Also, no surprise fees or charges, everything here was above board. 
The room itself was nice, I know some others have said small - but for NYC I thought it was actually pretty good sized. Cleaning staff did a great job and room was always in good shape when we returned to it. My only complaints are that the bed was not very comfortable and our room was NOISY. I think it was because we were right next to the maid closet but we could hear door slamming, a hammering noise etc. Also, I recommend requesting a higher floor if you are bothered by traffic noise. I'm a city mouse so it actually helps me sleep, but it was definitely audible from our 6th Fl room. 
If you want to stay in Midtown - this is a great option. They take good care of you.

The room at the Paramount that I stayed in with my sister was an okay size. We had shared a queen bed which was clean and very comfy. The bathroom was tidy and well stocked with toiletries. The card key was hard to use at first, you have to figure out which way it needs to be swiped. It took a few tries to open the door but we got it down to an art on the last night. The check in time given was 3pm and check out time was 12pm. The hotel overall was dark and hip, great for all ages and the ipads were always available for use. It is in a great location and very easy to find.

title_masked: Nice but I would not go barefoot in room
text_masked: I did like the friendly reception once we arrived and the bar area was very nice. However the rooms were a bit dated and not very clean. The couch and flooring were stained and the bathroom had not been updated for many many years. The price was good, but I would have preferred to spend more in order to get more. The workout facility was nice, large and always empty.

title_masked: Don't stay here if you want a good night's sleep
text_masked:
After reading all the reviews on this site I decided that this would be a great Residence Inn to stop at on the way home from our family trip. Unfortunately; I noticed right after arriving in our room that the walls were paper thin. There was a lot of activity going on in the room above ours. It finally settled down around midnight and I went to sleep. And surprise! The person above us decided to vacuum his room at 1:30 am. I called the front desk and all they could offer was that the above person worked nights and they were sure he'd be done soon. Really??? He was a busy beaver up there until about 3am. I think that this Residence Inn is really suited for long term guests not someone who needs a good night's rest before heading on the road.
Also there is no free wifi, you have to plug in. And I could not make it work. The breakfast wasn't the best either. I stay at a lot of Residence Inns because it suits my family, but I'll be skipping this one on my next trip to Florida.

title_masked: Near good food and free parking!
text_masked:
Our family of 4 (with two boys age 7 &10) stayed here for two nights.
Here's what we thought:
Positives:
-free parking, free wifi
-clean
-close to restaurants (Gino's East is right around the corner)
-the parking attendants were more than helpful and offered their opinions and suggestions for getting around to some of the attractions.
Negatives:
-uncomfortable beds
-small
-when we checked in, we found the man who checked us in to be somewhat rude (the only strange encounter really, and I think he was trying to be funny. It was just a rather awkward encounter)
If we drove to Chicago again, we would consider this hotel. The free parking alone seems worth it.

This was our first time staying at a W hotel. Our party of 6 loved the convenient location...how great to be able to walk out the hotel door and be at Navy Pier in 5 minutes. Amazing restaurants and shopping venues were within walking distance and Union Station was just a $10 cab ride away.
The hotel itself is fun and upbeat. We loved the rooms overlooking the lake...a sense of calm in the frenetic city. Rooms are small but make great use of the space. The products, robes, bedding and Tv/audio systems are of superior quality. We had cocktails and food service in Whiskey Sky and the lobby restaurant...everything was delicious and the service was prompt and friendly.
And the service is amazing! The concierge staff is available from early (7am!) until late evening. They were so helpful in finding great dining and nearby pastry shop for an amazing birthday cake. Showing the concierge business card brought us special attention as we tried to order from an Indian menu that was unfamiliar to many of us. Wow, what a spectacular meal! (Check out the review under restaurants; Indian Garden.)
We hope to return to W soon.

title_masked: Will stay there again and again
text_masked: I just returned yesterday from a four night stay at the Embassy Suites Lakefront Downtown Chicago, Il, hotel. The staff is so wonderful, it's worth going there alone for that. We loved "Shirley" at the breakfast every morning and loved the wonderful greeting we received each time we returned or left the hotel. The breakfast was great and we loved the managers reception everyday at 5:30. Great location, within walking distance to "The Magnificent Mile." We had a lakefront room on the 17th floor and the view was fabulous. We were 2 blocks from the Navy Pier and we saw the Fireworks on the 4th of July and on Saturday. Loved all the places we could buy food in the area such as grocery stores and walgreens for personal items. Made our trip wonderful!

The Red Lion at SeaTac is everything you would expect from a hotel in its class. It was clean, the staff friendly, etc. The furniture layout in the lobby looks like they are trying to fill a space that was made for something else at one point in time... However, what was really fantastic was the comfort of the beds - firm, but with a cushion-y layer on top. Very nice.

title_masked: Great remodeled hotel! Bonus next to trader joes!
text_masked: This is a great business hotel. I stay many weeks a year here. It's great to walk to restaurants and shops! Plus trader joes in same plaza. Nice employees too! I enjoy staying here. Free parking. I will continue to return here.

We stayed at this hotel in August 2012. We had Room 420, which was a small room (for America) and the hotel is a bit of a rabbit warren – lots of corridors. However, the room was quiet – but no view – just a wall.
There was not much room for storage, however, there was a safe. There was a coffee machine.
The bathroom was clean, but the shaving mirror was positioned over the toilet – not very accessible.
Breakfast is in the Daily Grill (next door) - it is waiter service - there is a choice of main course – choice of coffee or orange juice - but no choice of cereals/fruit. Food is good though.
Hotel service good - extra coffee & whitener were provided very quickly. The Concierge was knowledgeable and helpful.
The room key-card can be used to get 10% off most purchases in Macy’s.
Overall, we thought it was a reasonable hotel for San Francisco, conveniently located for most places and access to public transport.
Big Tip: We stayed in August and experienced fairly large fluctuations in temperature – it was cool in the morning, especially if the fog was down, hot in the middle of the day and cool in the evening. We went over Golden Gate bridge twice and it was extremely cold and blowing a gale. So – take layers of clothes.

title_masked: Nice hotel, but there were a few issues
text_masked:
The hotel was nice, for the most part, but there were several annoyances that prevented me from giving it a top rating:
-No hair dryer in the room. I had to call to get one.
-The in-room safe wasn't working, so I had to call for the engineers to fix it.
-After the first day, the maid didn't replace the bath mat, so I had to call to get a new one.
-The thermostat was very frustrating. I had to push the button about 10 times to change the temperature 1/2 degree.
-One night, there was no cold water (hot water when I used the cold spout).
-One morning, there was an issue with the hot water.
-There was a motion sensor for the lights in the bathroom. Nice when going in (didn't have to look for a switch), but another person in another room told me that the lights went out when he was showering!
-The closet was a nice size, but there were only two usable drawers to store clothes. It was OK since I was by myself, but that could be an issue for couples or families.
Other than these, the room was nice, and there was a mini-fridge which was nice to store refrigerated items.

Stayed Aug. 4th. Loews is in a great Hollywood location, upscale hotel that will be better after more remodeling. Room we had was very nice with two queen beds for four people. We had a great view of the Hollywood sign and the hills. Room was clean, plenty of room. The bathroom was big and offered privacy. We called at 1:00pm when we landed at LAX to see if the room would be ready. We were told it wasn't ready yet but would be by the time we arrived. We made a couple of stops along the way, and arrived at 3:00pm. When we checked in we were told the room wasn't ready. It would be another hour and a long wait in the lobby before the room was ready. Normally, the wait wouldn't bother me, we would drop off our bags and find something else to do. However, I was having a gallbladdder attack and just wanted to get to a more comfotable place.
 I do want to thank Steve Layton for his assistance with the original reservation.

This was my second time staying at a Wingate. It turned out to be as pleasurable and satisfying as my first Wyngate stay in Houston. i will definately be on the lookout for a Wyngate in my dfuture travels.

My family had a reservation at this hotel for a non-smoking room. When my husband made the reservation he made it clear that we would be arriving after midnight after flying into Phoenix. When we arrived at 1:30am we were told that our room was a smoking room and was the only room left in the hotel. It smelled like a casino and there was no way we could stay with my husband and daughter having a headache from traveling all day, me being very sensitive to smells and my other daughter had a cold. The front desk clerk had offered to spray something in the room but had no idea of how long it would take to work. We inquired about other hotels in the area but she said they were all full. We decided to leave and drive the 2 hour trip home in the middle of the night. What an inconvenience!
My family was in the hotel business for forty years, and I have a feeling I know what happened. Someone else checked into the smoking room that did not have a non-smoking room reserved. After they complained, the front desk staff decided to rent our room to them and let the night auditor deal with us when we arrived much later. Why didn't the housekeeping staff try to get the room smelling better during the day or anyone else once they realized they would have to place a non-smoking reservation in a smoking room? I left my contact information and asked for the general manager to call us but never heard from her.
I think this property is poorly managed. Before leaving I used the restroom off the lobby. It was a mess. I do not recommend this property and will not try staying here again.

I stayed here for 5 nights as I was attending a class. I totally agree with others when they say the people working here are very friendly and helpful. They appear genuine. The hotel is really not close (like within walking distance) to anything but I had a car and most places are not too far away. The rooms are big, clean and quiet. There is a pool on the roof and a workout room next to it. I didn't eat at the hotel so I can't judge their food. The highway, 35e, is right out the door so you can go anywhere. I would recommend this hotel.

title_masked: Great location, peaceful, spacious room, quiet street
text_masked: We arrived at the crowded lobby of the wellington hotel since we had a reservation, but we were told that we should change hotel due to no room availability. We had to walk half block to the Blakely hotel (a partner boutique hotel). It was really nice, clean, the breakfast was at a charming restaurant named abbocado. The location was excellent and the street really quiet, one block away from subway, 2 blocks from central park. The last day, they kept our luggage for the rest of the day, the staff was really nice. A peaceful and quiet hotel. We were glad about the change.

We stayed for an in-town staycation. We enjoyed the Friday night grill. Nice variety and great food. The room was a regular room. The room was nice but certainly not worth the price. We were expecting a lot more from a Ritz Carlton. The location was near a lot of restaurants and shopping. Great location.

Don't like to write bad reviews, but felt I had to...I was told a check in we could get a roll in bed since we brought the kids double beds are kinda small....Find out later (after we chose our room) thats against fire code...OK..I get it....Things happen..Thought with an extra blanket I would hit the floor and momma and the kids would be drama free..till 1am found that the heater was blowing cold air..only 62 degrees in the room..Seriously considered going to the parking garage and sleeping in the suv..the floor is concrete my beanie and jacket wasn't working and the blanket ( too short) only covered me in fetal position and my heat escaped when i rolled over from shoulder to shoulder the only thin sleeping....now back at home in az and all the kids have fevers..but they were sorry and offered us a continental breakfast....save your money..motels are on one floor..you park in front of your room..(not a huge parking garage that you pay a ton of fees and walk a mile to get to..) they are bigger and cleaner..and usually closer to the beach..not to mention half the price and all the service..Troy in az..Have a blessed day..

When we arrived, we were early and new that our room would probably not be ready, so we were prepared to have our baggage minded and return. We did not expect such a rude and snobby welcoming. I had booked a large room with a bay or city view and a king bed. On arrival the man at reception told me that because I had booked on line and not directly through them, that my booking was not accurate and instead we had the smallest room in the Hotel and no view and were told to go and come back when they called us. Whilst away I checked my details and returned at 3:00PM as we had not had a phone call. On return I requested that what I had booked and prepaid for was what we should be getting. After much deliberation we finally got the room that I had booked. The room was absolutely georgous! The bar was great! Walking distance to Little Italy and Quincy Market, but out of the way of crowds. They need to improve there reception staff that's for sure.

title_masked: Absolutely LOVED the Doubletree Times Square!
text_masked: I returned yesterday from a 3-night business trip to NYC for a convention and was booked at the Doubletree Suites. This place is fantastic. While the bathroom is not as elegant as a Ritz Carlton bathroom, as far as fixtures and marble, etc., it is quite large. The bed was incredibly comfortable, as were the linens. And my coworkers and I checked our mattresses, no signs of bed bugs, which was a huge concern to us. There was a microwave and coffee pot, a bar sink, and an empty mini-fridge, as well as a stocked mini bar. My view was directly over Times Square, on the 26th Floor. I had no problem being in Room 2602, which was in close proximity to the elevators, I didn't hear any noise. The TV's were large and equipped with some high definition channels. I did not eat at the hotel, but I had a most pleasant experience in my 3 nights. Would highly recommend for business travelers, families, anyone really.

We used to go to this hotel when it was an Embassy Suites and we liked it then, and still do as a Conrad! The rooms are elegant and so new that there is still a slight odor of fresh paint! The beds are comfortable, the bathrooms are equipped with the latest fixtures, two big fluffy bathrobes, huge soft towels and beautifully tiled floors. Everything is state of the art. Our room had a jacuzzi bath tub as well as a large tile walk in shower. 
As Hilton Honors Gold members we were afforded some perks and a room upgrade that may not come with lower level membership, so I am only speaking from my experience. Here's a break down of what I did and didn't like, just to give a rounded perspective:
Likes:
1)The large walk-in bathroom with a shower head that you can adjust the temperature of the water on a seperate dial.
2)The bed and bedding is really comfortable.
3)The rooms are state of the art with up to date fixtures and a nice big couch.
4)Greeted promptly by the reception staff and they are extremely helpful in assisting with any needs or wants you may have. I was even taken personally to the gym when I asked where it was located.
5)If you've forgotten anything, and they have it and will deliver it to your room promptly.
6)Very quiet. A nice respite from the noisiness and bustle of downtown New York. You can really relax here.
7)The location! It's within walking distance of the World Trade Center and subway stops, as well as shopping (Century 21) and restaurants. You can walk across the street to Battary Park and have a view of the Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island on a clear day while eating a meal in the outside terrace area or just drinking a cup of coffee..
Dislikes:
1)The rooftop bar! It was very over rated! There is very limited space, glasses are left sitting around on tables from any previous occupant and finding a waitress is an effort in futility. When my husband went to the bar to get drinks they said they were out of pretty much everything and it was early on a Friday evening, so I hate to think what it's like later in the weekend.
2)Internet access is NOT free. 
3)The set-up for the check-in is a little confusing because you come into a large unoccupied lobby and have to go up an escalator to find the reception area. They need to put a sign up directing patrons to the location of the reception area.
4)Lack of assistance when arriving or departing with luggage. Half of the time there wasn't a doorman in attendance.
5)It's expensive. Very expensive. But this is New York, so I expect that.

Nice relaxing stay, just perfect for my business trip. 
Hotel provides everything I required. Especially the Lady attending the concierge lounge;
She got out of her way fixing the broken printer and even delivering the pending business
Papers I needed for the next day, wile I was out for dinner!
Great responsive welcoming Staff, which does makes a difference on such trips.

title_masked: A great place to stay in D.C.
text_masked:
We had 2 rooms, one at the front of the hotel and one on the side. Both were quiet, this is not on a very busy street. The beds were very comfortable and the rooms felt high quality. 
The hotel is very close to the Capitol, and from there a longer walk down the Mall to the other sites. The area the hotel is in is not busy like downtown, which suited my family. The Dubliner, around the corner, serves good food but there is not too much else nearby. DC is not a big city so you can get around easily.
The rooftop pool was the icing on the cake, especially since we were here in July when the temperatures were 90+. 
I have already recommended this place to some friends.

I stayed at the Rittenhouse in Oct. 2012 for three nights. It is lovely and they have a nice breakfast. My room was very nice and comfortable. The staff is great. It is homey and quiet.
They DO have bed bugs. I had one one me and brushed it off.

Excellent location right on the Metro line. Had a wonderful view on the 15th floor of the Capitol, Washington and Jefferson Monument. Room seemed "worn" and could have used some updating. Had dinner in the restaurant and it was tasty and reasonable.

We stayed at the Hilton in the Fisherman's Wharf area for 2 days before we left for a driving trip to some of the National Parks. Being in this area of the city was fantastic for our first trip.. So easy to get around the city from here. Hotel parking was expensive but we had great service and the room was well appointed.

We were stunned when they upgraded us to the Presidential suite. All we really wanted was a room that had a working air conditioner. We booked here for one night because the hotel is in the historic PSFS building – the first true skyscraper in Philadelphia, and so the views towards city hall and the sunset are pretty remarkable. We had requested a grand luxury room because they are all corner rooms on high floors. When we checked in, our room on the 26th floor did indeed have great views both south and west, but it was struggling to keep cool. We closed the curtains and went to visit the Fabric Workshop – expecting things to improve. When we returned two hours later, we were met by two things: an even warmer room and a rancid fruit-cheese plate addressed to a guest not in our party or in our room. When we requested a room change, we got a technician, who pretty much confirmed, as he rattled around in the air-conditioner, that things were not going to improve. A second request brought both the removal of the cheese plate and the news that there were no other rooms to be had (!) to which we responded that we were more than happy to check-out and move to the Four Seasons as we did not intend to pay several hundred dollars for a bad nights sleep. Next thing we knew, we were in the so-called [NAME] suite on the 31st floor! Now this suite is pretty grand, with a dining room, living room, guest bath, master bath with a shower big enough for five and a bath tub big enough for three. The view is north, west AND east, no complaints there – we basically slept with William Penn in our room! That said (and thank you management I really do appreciate the grand gesture and I do believe you were full-up that weekend) I wish I could report that the rest of our stay was presidential and perfect….Sadly, both of the flat screen TVs malfunctioned, and after an attempted repair by that same technician at 9:30 pm, the cable box fell out of the wall. Two technicians were still futzing with it at 10:30 when we finally asked them to leave us alone. Which seemed to surprise them??!! Add to that: the door to the master bath has no latch and you can hear EVERYTHING from the room next door. I hope the White House travel desk is reading this….

I have stayed at this hotel before and I will continue to return for my stays!! The entire place is clean, inviting and the staff is extremely friendly. The food is fresh, delicious and outstanding! I met the VP of Sales as I was checking in and he was gracious enough to briefly show me around and even made excellent recommendations for places to shop and eat around the area. Thank you, Mr [NAME]!

title_masked: This is why we are LaQuinta fans
text_masked: We are LaQuinta rewards members for good reason and that is that they seldom disappoint. This location was no exception. Tastefully decorated, comfortable bedding, generous sized double bed room . Good location near the SoCo district and other attractions. Above average breakfast which was included . Our only complaint was the walls were not well insulated as far as sound goes. We could hear EVERYTHING in the room next door , as though the conversation was occurring in OUR room. The receptionist dispatched their security person to ask that the guests keep the noise level down which they tried to do but at that point we realized, it was just the walls were "thin". Staff were all pleasant and competent. Ask to be away from other occupied guest rooms of that is at all possible.

title_masked: Nice hotel very well located in NYC
text_masked:
We stayed there for some days in New York and I must say the quality of service in this hotel is very good. At first, we had a room next to the elevators, and we found it a bit noisy. They offered us another room with an excellent view but it appears that the door was not working properly. Within 30 mins, we have been offered a new room, as good as the previous one.
All details are superbly considered and you feel everything is very good.
What we also lover was the great location of the hotel: close to several metro stations, next to Time Square, 10 mins from Central Park. We will certainly go back there!

I went to this hotel on Easter with my Family and everything was absolutely fantastic!
Check in very quick and we were given all the information that we needed. 
Beautiful room (Toshi Corner Suit) clean but a bit noisy in the night. In the bathroom there was tv on the mirror so while you wash your theeth you watch the news :) confy bed, a/c, but small wadrobe!Free internet connection bar with music every night!
The location is also very good just in the middle of Manhattan so if you like to walk you can really go almost everywhere by foo. Of couse there is a starbucks just in front the hotel!
A special thanks to Reginaldo the receptionist, he was really nice and professional!

Very very clean big rooms & comfy beds. The property seemed full but very quiet. Excellent friendly & helpful staff. Very nice indoor pool. Restaurant very hand and good. Bar very nice also. Will definitely stay again!!!!

Nice hotel, close to everything. The hotel was very quiet at night to sleep and loved looking at the New York skyline while lying in bed. The deli across the street was excellent... and not too expensive.

title_masked: Great service! Best room service cheese steak!
text_masked:
The overall quality of the hotel is very good. 
I received great service during the 5 days I stayed.
I decided one night to order a cheese steak with the room service. I think it was if not better, at the same level of Geno's (of course, I'm not an expert).

We've stayed at the Carlton at 88 Madison several times for weddings and business trips, and though it is worth considering for the price (one of the more affordable hotels in the city) the service is terrible. The staff is generally friendly during check-in, but when we've needed further assistance with room keys, non-feather pillows or other service amenities, the concierge is often resistant to assisting us.... or they claim someone will come to our room shortly to deliver what we need, and then never show up. I'm not sure if the staff is simply forgetful or just unprofessional, but to me, it is worth paying an extra $20-40 a night to get efficient, hospitable service. Also, the waitstaff at Carlton's restaurant is awful -- as though they feel too good to work in a service profession. (And if that's the case, perhaps they should look for a job that's not in a hotel.) Overall, if you're just in for a quick, bare-bones NYC weekend, the Carlton is fine. But if you're looking for a weekend getaway within this price range, I would recommend the W hotel.

My wife adn I have unusual dietary needs--not only were they met with superior food, the personal concern of sous chef Eugene Sclaff was exceptional. Don't miss eating there. The hotel is one of our favorites too, very comfortable, great staff, and the location is on the Riverwalk yet a bit removed from the congestion.

title_masked: Good hotel, but extra charge for in-room Internet service
text_masked:
Clean and comfortable hotel and room.
Slow check-in and extra charge for in-room Internet service.

Another good stay at the Hampton Inn. No complaints about the hotel itself but if you are on AT&T for your cell service and rely on that while traveling, this is not the place to stay. Two of us in the room had AT&T and got very poor reception inside the hotel - the moment we walked outside it was fine. The wireless internet access was not all that great either.

The Hilton Chicago is a gorgeous historic hotel that was recently renovated and in a great location! Our bed, bedding and room were extremely comfortable, and we had a great view of Lake Michigan and Grant Park. We loved having Chicago's largest park across from the hotel and enjoyed a run and/or walk in the Park right on the lake. It was bustling with activity, but not crowded, and really gorgeous. I also noticed a bike rental shop a block away for those interested. The location was great with the Art Institute, Field Museum, Aquarium, Planetarium and Symphony close by. Shopping on State Street was close and the Magnificent Mile an lovely 15- 20 minute walk. I'd also recommend getting a room with the Executive Level access. for the concierge, breakfast, snacks, beverages and wifi. Starbucks in the lobby was too bad either! Lovely hotel and location.

I spent three nights here for a long weekend in San Francisco for shopping, food, and fun. The location is perfect for walking around and shopping. When you're in SF be prepared to do a lot of walking! We also purchased the three day pass for unlimited use of the cable cars, muni, and street cars. The hotel itself is very large and we had a long walk from the lobby to the room on the sixth floor. The check in staff was very helpful and let us have a late check out. We also talked to the concierge for some activities we wanted to do and he was also very helpful. The room was clean and spacious. Be careful with the mini bar and snacks in the room! They automatically charge you for moving any of the items off the tray/ mini fridge. We wanted to put our own beverage in the fridge to keep cold and moved a soda out of the way. Luckily we did not get charged and put the soda back in it's place, but just be aware and careful of this! The beds were comfortable, but there were big fat pillows that were a little too fat and fluffy to be comfortable to sleep on. The bathroom was OK with great smelling shampoo, conditioner and lotion. The shower pressure was great with hot water just how I like it. Don't forget to put the shower curtain inside the tub before you turn the water on! Twice we forgot to do this and had water all over the floor! The other thing that I did not like was the shower curtain would billow out while I was showering and touch me while I was showering. Other than that, we enjoyed this hotel and got a good deal on the cost. I would definitely stay here again if I got a good price. San Francisco is a great place to visit for site seeing, eating, shopping and so much more!

title_masked: Front desk was more than helpful.
text_masked:
This was our first time staying at the Renaissance and all went well. The front desk staff was gracious and helpful. I am a gold elite member with Marriott and was hopful to get a room upgrade from our regular sized room. We arrived on a Saturday night with a guitar festivile going on close by and all rooms were booked. We did however receive a double upgrade for Sunday and Monday nights thanks to the help of Elizabeth Oliva who was working the front desk on Sunday. We brought my parents along and while they do not travel alot were also impressed by this hotel. It is a short trip to downtown but in all centrally located on the northwest side of Dallas. We went to a Yankees vs Rangers game and it took about 20-25 minutes to get to the stadium. 
We ended up on the 24th floor looking toward the medical district after the fisrt nights view of downtown. We saw virtually no children during our stay. Noise levels were very low except for the train that is near the hotel. We ordered room service for breakfast (really good) and it arrived on time still hot.
Over all a great stay, we will definatly stay here again.

Overall: Great stay, good value for the room size and location.
Rooms: My room was large, especially considering New York standards. We had four people in a queen double room, and there was more than enough space for all of us and our luggage. The rooms were very clean and non-carpeted. The bathroom was small, but bright. I loved the look of the hotel - modern and a little trendy - but not over the top. 
Service: Great service. I came in on a redeye at 6am, and they were able to check me into my room early. 
Convenience: TRYP hotel really wins on this point. Its close to the subway, and only 2 blocks from Penn station. If you are coming or going via Amtrak, its a very close walk.

Convenient location,beautiful bright, clean suites with full kitchen, lovely pool in courtyard. Staff was outstanding! Friendly, knowledgeable, helpful with tips about local activities and festivals, printed out directions for us to a festival, etc. Breakfast buffet had a wide variety of fresh and delicious items--way above average! Would definitely stay there again if in Dallas area!

title_masked: Unique historic hotel, conveniently located in downtown loop near trains
text_masked:
I have stayed at The Silversmith many times and always enjoy it. Each room/suite seems to have its own unique layout ... this is not a cookie-cutter hotel setup. The rooms are generally large. The hotel is located right in the business loop with convenient access to the trains right outside the front door (the trains can be a bit noisy, but after the first night it kind of lulls me to sleep ... however, some people will likely find the train noise to be an annoyance ... an interior room on a lower floor may provide the best noise reduction). One other noise issue is the sound of doors closing in the hallway (the doors are solid and they slam closed if people don't slow them down ... it would be a nice courtesy to others for you to help the door close slowly & quietly).
If you enjoy shopping, this is a great location. The State Street shopping district is just two blocks west. There are many food choices within a few blocks as well (Elephant & Castle is recommended). It is about a half mile walk to the Magnificent Mile shopping on the other side of the Chicago River ... an easy and enjoyable walk, in my opinion. And Grant Park is one block east from the hotel. The location definitely minimizes the need for taxis ... just walk or jump on the train.
The staff at The Silversmith are very pleasant and helpful. There is always a doorman/bellman at the entrance to greet you with a friendly smile and hello. The lobby is on the 2nd floor directly off the elevator (and the lobby is huge and historically beautiful, including a grand piano and lots of seating). On this particular trip I was hoping to check-in early, and the very nice lady at the front desk worked to find me an available room (which turned out to be an upgrade to a one bedroom suite ... she recognized my name from previous stays, which really made me feel valued and special). For added safety, access to the room level floors requires you to insert your room key inside the elevator before pressing the button for your floor.
Room amenities: large floor safe, iron, ironing board, hair dryer, coffee maker, small refridgerator, large flat screen tv (2 in suites), shampoo, conditioner, lotion.
For location, space, price and uniqueness, I highly recommend The Silversmith Hotel.

Let me start by explaining how bad the overall experience was. I flew in late and needed a room, so, I pricelined a room. I got the Microtel by Denver Internation Airport which I thought couldn't be too bad but in fact it was the worse experience ever.
First, the shuttle van driver had friends riding along that forced actual paying customers to to sit in the back. 
Secondly, the driver kept getting honked at because she kept weaving, I assume she was either drunk or sleepy. Also, she didn't help with the luggage nor did she open the back door for my bags. 
Thirdly, the front office was terribly dirty and the carpet was duct taped. 
Fourth, I had the A/C set on 60 degrees but they have it rigged so it doesn't get colder than 75 degrees. 
Fifth, the room had stains on virtually everything in the room and they gave me a smoking room. The clerk told me that I requested a smoking room, and even argued with me that I ordered a smoking room, but offered me a $15 discount if I called priceline. 
I travel a lot and made sure I didn't forget to write a review so you can avoid a terrible experience. Avoid Microtel as a chain and specifically the Denver location. AVOID AT ALL COST! PAY A LITTLE MORE!

We were booked at the De Anza for business and were very pleased. The room was very comfortable and updated. The location is perfect for walking around downtown San Jose. Many restaurants close by. No complaints here.

The most recent negative reviews could have been prevented if those folks had done their research. The parking fee is clearly stated on their website. Their is no other parking option but it is on a pier . . . . so that's to be expected. I always map out my hotel to see if trains are nearby - especially in a port city like Seattle. We paid for a waterside room with a balcony because the trains run on the other side of the hotel. (You get what you pay for!) The gas fireplaces are wonderful! And the bathroom was fantastic . . . great walk-in shower. I wanted to take the bed home with me.
The staff were admittedly not superstars . . . but they weren't rude either. Extra pillows were delivered quickly . . . the bar overlooking Puget Sound was VERY nice. It's within quick walking distance of the Seattle Aquarium which is one of the best I've ever visited. I would definitely return to the Edgewater Hotel.

title_masked: Was just ok. Not as near the Stadiums as I had hoped.
text_masked: The name implied to me that this hotel would be within walking distance to both the football and baseball stadiums. It really is not. Technically you could walk there, but it is not close and the neighborhood you walk through does not feel safe. The shuttle was only leaving every hour, and did not want to let us our when we got the Ball Park! It seems there are designated stops, but we did not want to sit in traffic another 10 minutes when the park was right next to us. The rooms were clean and the staff was friendly enough. The hot complimentary breakfast was just ok. The conveyor belt pancakes were not something I had ever seen before, but it broke down a few people after us and was not repaired. The rest of the food was just standard cafeteria and boxed bakery stuff. I would choose a hotel much closer to the actual stadium next time I go.

I loved The Sofia. Friendly service, great location, excellent facilities.I had a very stylish room, a lot is said about the rooms here being small and a bit dark but I found no prombles with either,. Easy walk to the Lamplight Quarter, a lively section with lots of excellent restaurants. The only slight glitch was an IT problem which ment no room charges from the Bar and Resturant but Im sure that will be addressed

I was very pleased with my decision to stay at this location. My actual destination was very close to this inn and my budget was very limited. Choosing a motel by lowest room rates can be a big mistake.
Not with Red Roof Inn- especially this location.
I was very impressed with my room and amenities featured.
The room was spotless as though I were the first guest to have ever been there.
I have stayed in many other higher priced name motels on many,many business trips in the past with my husband. 
I can honestly say those establishments have something to worry about.
I would highly recommend this Red Roof Inn to any one needing a place to stay while in this area of Jacksonville Florida..

Perfect location, gorgeous, well appointed room. Friendly, professional staff. Near EVERYTHING, and the best shopping. A short cab ride to North Beach. Really nothing negative to say. We were in #1917 and the bed was just like home (clean and fluffy), and there was a discretely hidden stocked fridge, and coffeemaker in the bathroom to tide us over until we went up the complimentary breakfast in the am. A five minute walk to the BART to take you back to SFO. Our room was super quiet, but shopping, walking, and enjoying the nightlife kept us tired.

This hotel was old, the rooms were decked out in vintage furniture. While the rate was reasonable, and we were only staying there one night (flying out next day), decided well it is likely do'able so we started to settle in. While unpacking, my husband stepped in puke that was in the carpet beside the bed!!!! We immediately packed up, and went to see what could be done. The clerk gave us another room to review, which was in just as horrible shape so we checked out. In order to check out however, we had to wait 20 minutes to have a manager come on site to refund our money since the credit card had already been run through. The manager did offer to give us a 40% discount to stay in another room!! ha ha, no way! craziness! 
Besides, nothing was good about our experience here. When we checked in, the key didn't work had to go back and get that fixed. Additionally the clerk said that the machine to run the credit card wasn't working so he made a photo copy of my credit card. My husband spoke up and the clerk shredded it, but goodness, how awful!

My boyfriend, Ken, and I were in NYC to cover the 9/11 Memorial (11th anniversary). He was speaking at the Voices of September 11th conference and I was taking photographs. We were able to set up at the top of the hotel to do a Skype interview with the UT TV San Diego with the World Trade Center in the background. The staff was unbelievable. The rooms are wonderful. Their restaurant is delightful. Great view and delicious.

we enjoyed our stay here the staff was very friendly. it is a older hotel but it was stll nice had a wonderful view of the bay. we left our sliding door open at night and early mornings we could here the sea lions it was really cool. our bartender John was awesome great memory. not a big place thats what made it more personal. would stay here again

title_masked: Awesome view, great service, great staff & accomodations!!!
text_masked:
This is a hidden gem....decided to try out Pacific Beach area...when first came into town sounded like college days...lol...wondered what we had gotten ourselves into...however, upon arrival at our hotel we realized much more to this area...our hotel "Pacific Terrace" was upscale, gorgeous rooms, incredible view, and some of the friendliest staff we have come across in our travels...Pacific Beach has some great shopping and dining experiences...
Our adventure started with help from Dan Thomas....for a bell/valet staff he was one of...sorry the most helpful hotel staff we have come across in all our hotel stays....not only did he help us with our bags, he got us our complimentary drinks...gave us good suggestions for dinner...so helpful & friendly...he needs a promotion...best service ever...this hotel has some great ideas for making visitors feel at home...you can get a package (with my AAA card!!!) that gives you complimentary wine...a photo...and a 1 pm checkout...best idea yet...other hotels could learn from this...now lets talk about the view...
get an ocean front room and you will not be disappointed...we had a junior suite and it was adorable...it looks even better than the on line site...when does that happen...we will definitely go back when we are in the area....love it!

title_masked: Executes everything well, one of my favourite hotels ever
text_masked:
I am not generally a fan of high-end hotels and I was all ready to hate the JW. I generally feel that value for money just isn't there and prefer to stay in Courtyard-level hotels. The JW Chicago proved me wrong.
This hotel just executes well in all of the details that I personally value.
The room - nice high ceilings give the feeling of space, tastefully decorated but not over the top in any way. Comfortable bed, lovely bathroom, great shower. The air conditioning (one of my pet peeves in a hotel) covers the spectrum of needs from silent to good solid white noise when the fan is set to high. Plugs everywhere I needed them. Nice flatscreen TV with high definition content.
Internet - A common failing of the larger hotels is internet, not so with the JW Chicago. Internet was solid and fast, allowing me to join in a meeting back at the office via video conference.
Lobby - Staff available just to help, fast and friendly check-in, and helpful concierge.
Lobby bar - nice selection of local beers on tap, lots of activity, good service including a friendly lounge attendant who was just there to make sure everything was going well for customers.
Meetings - I was here for a small conference, and even there they executed above and beyond. Staff were always checking in to see if we needed anything, requests were handled quickly, even the security head came to say hello and let me know what to do if there was an emergency.
Marble lobbies and wood-panelled elevators aren't usually my thing. But the JW was so much more, and is the model for what a downtown business hotel should be. A new bar has been set for me, I feel sorry for the next hotel that I stay at because they will never match up.

title_masked: Very adequate hotel, convenient for the airport
text_masked:
After our long flight from London we were satisfied with what this motel-style hotel offered. We were not expecting five star comfort for the two star prices charged, but we nevertheless found everything to be satisfactory. The neighbourhood is somewhat run down, and there are no shops or bars within walking distance but, then again, few places are withing walking distance of each other in Phoenix!
The room was comfortable, with a TV, fridge and very comfortable beds, and we saw no bugs or dirt. The shower in particular was excellent, with plenty of hot water, and the room had a bright and well-appointed bathroom too. The air conditioning was fairly noisy but, as it was 28°C/ 82°F through the night, it had to work hard to keep the room cool.
Breakfast in the morning was served from a conveniently early hour. It was self service, basic but very adequate, and with excellent coffee and make-your-own pancakes.
A highlight for us was that after my wife left her handbag, which contained all our passports, money and credit cards, in the breakfast room, only realising this an hour or so later, we were delighted to find that the duty staff member had found it and kept it for us at reception. A massive bouquet for honesty, sir! 
If I had to find fault with anything, I suppose the pool was a bit of joke, small, uninviting and deserted but, really, this hotel offers excellent value for money and, after our experience with my wife's handbag being returned, we would not hesitate to use this hotel again if we return to Phoenix.

We have just stayed at the Conrad for 3 nights between the 15th & 18th November and I have to say I was uber impressed. The service was near perfect, the rooms where a great size and very very comfortable. We used the Conrad as a base for exploring the lower and mid town area of Manhattan and couldnt have chosen better. 
The location was perfect for the 911 Memorial and the Financial District. Statue of Liberty, Staten Island Ferry etc etc. We had a suite on the 15th floor overlooking the Hudson. It had a great bed, excellent walk in wet room and seperate restroom. Living area had good furniture with a great TV and then same again in the bedroom. Its not often I find hotel bedroom matresses up to scratch but this really was like being at home for quality. 
All in all 5* and worth every penny...would definately use again

title_masked: Stiff robotic front desk staff that does not greet you as you walk by
text_masked: The spectacular room $250 and the regular rooms $189 are exactly the same except the spectacular is on a higher floor, the view is nothing special. Rooms are very average. Be prepared to have a hold of $250.00 on your credit card for incidental charges. Valet parking is a ridiculous $37 per day, plus tax. comes out to be about $45 a night, with that kind of charge you will have no interest in tipping the valet staff. You can walk through the lobby pass the front desk and hear a pin drop, no greeting and eye contact, everyone's eyes are on a computer screen. I think the only greeting i got was from the guy in the lobby marketing Acura SUVs. FYI lots of homeless folks in the downtown area. I you are reading this and you are the General Manager......the take away is pay attention to customer service.

We just returned from a week's stay at the Eventi. We have been to NYC many times with our kids, but have never experienced a hotel like this one. You really feel like the staff cares about you. If you forget a toothbrush or need a razor, just call the front desk and they'll send one up. I broke a nail on my last morning, and they brought me an emery board. The wine and cheese reception every day from 5 - 6 is a wonderful way to end a busy afternoon in NYC. And our room was modern, clean and quiet. We were four people in a room with two Queen beds and with a bit of imagination, we found enough room to unpack our things. If you stay here, be sure to check out the banquet floors. The decor is sleek and there are fresh flowers and other little surprises sprinkled throughout. This was also a new location for us and while it's south of Times Square, it was an easy walk to any where we wanted to go. I have absolutely no problem recommending this hotel to others. And I will look for other Kimpton hotels in other cities. Thank you to everyone at the Eventi for making our stay so memorable.

I stayed here last week and had an outstanding experience. The property is attractive, the room was well appointed and very comfortable, the bed was amazing, and the rate I paid was very fair. But what really made the experience was the employees. Every person I encountered was friendly and seemed genuinely eager to be helpful, even, as other reviewers have mentioned, to the point of anticipating my needs. I don't know that I've ever had that experience in a hotel before. I stayed only one night and my time in Philadelphia was very busy, so I did not get to enjoy all of the hotel's amenities, but I would gladly return and recommend this hotel to others.

The Mandarin is a lovely hotel. The service is amazing. Everyone is helpful and extremely conscientious. We were celebrating two special occasions. I really wanted our celebration to be special and the hotel was amazing. We were upgraded and our room was huge. It was located next to the elevator which I normally do not like, but the room is so well laid out that I did not hear any noise from the elevator. The bathroom was absolutely gorgeous! It might be the best bathroom I have ever encountered. I would definitely stay again.
I scheduled several spa treatments and everyone at the spa was remarkable. All our treatments were excellent and the spa is fantastic. I would definitely go again and would encourage everyone I know to go to the Mandarin Spa. It would be perfect if there was a coed waiting room. 
I really think that the only shortcoming is Asana. The food is only okay. For dinner, the presentation was unimpressive and the food was only okay. Though our allergies were listed, they were ignored and I was served a course that included one of the listed ingredients. The service and food at breakfast was sorely lacking.

Nice hotel in the center of the teater-district. Clean, friendly and not in the highest price-group.Breakfast is a boufee, reliatively high priced, so we ate breakfast at the Edison hotel, where you can take the menue. There is one thing with the Belvedere: the aircondition-system is so noicy that we had to turn it off at night, Then it can be too hot in bed at night.

I enjoyed my nine nights at this La Quinta. The location was excellent with easy access to MO PAC and HWY 183. The staff was so helpful and friendly. I booked the king suite for plenty of room for visiting family members during the day. There are plenty of food and shopping options nearby. The bed was so comfortable. I also loved the two flat panel TV's.

Wow! What a place. A bit out of the way, but a beautful resort. While there were tons of families with kids, I was trying to have a quiet stay, which I was able to accomplish by going to the spa and fitness center, which were spectacular and included in your high resort fee (but if you're going to utilize the spa, it's actually a great deal). The rooms were modern and well appointed, the sports bar is spectacular, and if you have kids, the water slides and lazy river are loads of fun. Really nice spot.

The hotel had no hot water during my entire 3 day stay, and I only found out after asking another guest in the elevator that the hot water had been out for an entire week BEFORE I arrived. How could they say nothing to me? In the morning, I called early and asked them to move me to another room because the rug was wet and there was an odd smell in the room. I was told that they couldn't do anything at that time because guests hadn't yet checked out, but they would move me during the day. I get back to the hotel at 9pm (I told them I would be back late), and they said they couldn't move me and hadn't heard anything about it. Really?? Unbelievable. Front desk night manager wasn't helpful at all--no apology, no nothing. As if that wasn't enough, I go downstairs to go in the jacuzzi to warm up ahead of my cold shower--the jacuzzi wasn't hot--probably around 95 degrees! Just an all around poor hotel with poor management.

The night auditor was completely rude and unwilling to work with me on the room price at all even though I am an employee, and had an employee voucher. The last 2 times I've stayed there everyone was really nice and helpful. I work the night shift sometimes too, but there's still no reason to act like your night auditor did. Especially to another employee.

title_masked: Great location and staff; some drawbacks.
text_masked: This property is convenient to the beach and within walking distance of bars, shops and restaurants, and the canals. We even walked the two miles each way to Santa Monica pier. That was the best part. The staff is extremely polite, helpful and friendly. They directed us to excellent local restaurants and it was nice to get free use of beach chairs so we didn't have to bring our own. They also have a keurig so you can get yummy coffee in the office from 9:00 to 9:00 when they are on-site. We were glad to have coffee maker and coffee in the room. And yes, there were a few downers. The advertised "unloading" zone really isn't one at all. It's actually a commercial alley really busy and narrow - beware the hotel has no driveway or roundabout - you are at the back steps of the hotel in a strictly signed "no-parking zone". Although the hotel advertises being a member of the local chamber of commerce, the local authorities apparently cut him no slack to allow his customers to check in and out. We had two people and he was adamant that one person stay with the vehicle at all times or we would risk being ticketed. Seriously it seems like no way to welcome tourists to me. The other person has to carry all the bags in to the room and/or the office if your room is not ready. Then you have to fight for street parking which is also limited particularly on Monday and Tuesday mornings where street cleaning is done - we arrived on Monday and didn't know this. It's best not to arrive before 1:00 p.m. because that's when the street cleaning is done and more parking opens up. Not knowing about any of this and arriving on a Monday it was very stressful. Took us nearly an hour to unload, check in and drive around to find a spot. They also advertise maid service as "available" on the website. Upon arrival we learned that this is an extra fee. It wasn't that big of a deal but we thought it was a bit unclear. We had to take our own trash out each day and gather up our towels and exchange at the office, sweep the sand up and make the bed. This hotel is not inexpensive so a bit more service in the room would have been nice. Then there is an envelope in the room implying guests should leave a tip. That's a bit over the top when I'm servicing my own room. That said, the hotel's common areas are constantly being cleaned and maintained. Also, we didn't mind that the hotel doesn't have air conditioning...but if you leave the windows open which feels great, the blinds make noise all night banging on the window frame. Hotel has charm, but also drawbacks. Also the bathroom window has no screen so if you open it for ventilation in there flies come in.

title_masked: A little old - Some service issues
text_masked: I stayed at the Ritz San Francisco on business in October. The hotel itself was fine, but not spectacular. The common areas seemed a little old and in need of an update. The room was small. Despite a request for a room with one bed, I was given a room with two small beds (I was traveling alone) The woman who checked me in was surprisingly churlish and didn't react well when I highlighted that I wanted a room with one large bed rather than two small beds. I was quite surprised to encounter this attitude at a Ritz. Overall, an average hotel with average service.

title_masked: Most enjoyable stay at the Willows
text_masked: We just returned from a short break in Chicago where we enjoyed summer weather in March! The Willows is a great choice to be away from downtown while able to get into within 15 minutes on the bus. Old style smallish hotel with very comfortable rooms and modern bathrooms. Fridge in the room with very affordable drinks and snacks. Absolutely fantastic staff, so friendly and always happy to help. Great neighbourhood. Only downside for us was the fact that the very decent continental style breakfast was served in the lobby which is not properly set up for that but you can take your tray to your room if you prefer. Will definitely use again and highly recommend!

I was recently in town for a wedding that was a while's away, but opted for this quaint hotel with no regrets! Great location and wonderful staff who even acknowledged me by name. I arrived at 8am and the front desk greeted me with their signature warm cookie and great news that one of my rooms was available at no additional charge. Having booked 2 rooms, the front desk didn't need for me to request the rooms to be adjoining/connecting but took it upon themselves to arrange a connecting room, which was perfect! The rooms were a classic design, which I adored. They have the cutest "sweet dreams" pillow on each bed and anything and everything I requested was delivered promptly within minutes of hanging up. If you dare, as a girlfriend and I did...visit Viktor at the lobby bar for a dangerous yet delicious Absinthe cocktail. Who knew absinthe and champagne equaled "Death in the Afternoon?" Viktor was a sweetheart and did an impressive presentation! I'll definitely be back to Seattle and definitely back to the Arctic Club! They should be very proud to be hanging their 4-diamond plaque at the reception desk for it is well deserved!

I stayed at this hotel during a weekend college visit for my daughter. The room was clean, quiet, attractive and very comfortable. The hotel is located among various businesses, but had a good amount of green space. The parking area was somewhat small but I was able to get a spot close to the entrance. It was convenient to have a refrigerator and microwave as most of my time was spent working and not sight-seeing. The breakfast buffet was terrific - omelets, pancakes, waffles, sausage in addition to the normal buffet items. Also, as a non-coffee drinker, the buffet offered fountain soft drinks - an unexpected treat. Breakfast time in the eating area was busy, though, and spots at the tables were difficult to come by. The nightly rate was very reasonable. I would definitely stay here again.

We stayed at this hotel with a soccer group for a tournament. We were greeted by very efficient and friendly staff at the front desk in a very classy, modern lobby. Then we went to our room. The bed was very uncomfortable and the sofa bed was horrible. The carpeting very badly needed to be vacuumed. The nifty dispensers in the bathroom for shampoo, conditioner and shower gel were empty. The shower curtain was too short to tuck inthe tub to keep a lake from forming on the floor. We set the air on a comfortable temperature and it went there...and then reverted back to the original hot temperature we found it on. And it was very loud. On the plus side, the breakfast that was provided in a meeting room for our group was very decent and the young man who kept it stocked was very pleasant. The rooms were well soundproofed so we didnt hear noise from the other guests or the traffic we could see on the highway that was very close by. And when I asked for more towels, they brought me a huge stack within minutes. Also, there is a Cracker Barrel restaurant across the parking lot.

title_masked: Cab it if you have a conference at the convention center
text_masked: I booked this hotel because of its proximity to the conference center. However when I arrived, I was told my king bed was not available due to my booking through a 3rd party. What does that mean? I booked through Expedia as most people do. The person at the front desk had no customer skills to keep the customer happy. They offered nothing for the inconvenience. Once I got to my room, it was dingy and obviously needed to be renovated. The closet was a drape hung across the closet. This is a how many star hotel? At this price, I expected a better room. Please do yourself a favor and don’t make the mistake I made. Book at another hotel along the Miracle Mile and cab it to the convention site. For food, you're stuck with the hotel bar and an overpriced restaurant .There is absolutely nothing in the area. Chicago's a great city - unfortunately I didn't see much of it until I transferred to another hotel after my convention. Next time I'll get a more central hotel and take a taxi.

title_masked: Excellent hospitality and fantastic business/conference location.
text_masked: The hotel staff was excellent, especially April in the restaurant and Henry from the front desk. They were genuinely eager to help, and went out of their way to greet me and make me feel at home. This is the kind fo service that generates repeat customers. Great job!

I was responsible for arranging a 3 day business meeting for <50 Team Members
The Meeting Group did an excellent job, overcame a small challenge with the third party internet service not working at times.
Would recommend the Sheraton to anyone needing a quality meeting location.

I was unsure what to expect after reading some of the reviews here, but the price was right and location was exactly where I needed to be. I was pleasantly surprised. My room was clean, warm, and QUIET. I had a restful night. The staff was quite nice too. I had some work in Baltimore and would need a fax later in the day. The staff said that sure i could come back and use their business center and fax machine. The only glitch i experienced was the stairs. I have bad knees and had slow going on the stairs. An elevator would have been nice, the staff did offer to move me, but for safety sake I didn't want a ground floor. The receptionist also recommended a nice close by restaurant with GREAT crab-cakes... a treat for a former Marylander.

Kona Kai resort can boast a near-perfect location along San Diego Bay, but the rooms leave a great deal to be desired. The carpet, upholstery and bed covers are dated and, in some cases, threadbare, but the biggest drawback is the ventilation. Our room had a balcony looking out onto the esplanade, but in order to have any fresh air, we had to leave the door wide open, which flooded the room with bright light from the parking lot all night long. When we closed the door, the woefully inadequate wall unit sounded like a jet from the nearby Navy base taking off every time the air conditioner kicked in.

We have stayed here numerous times. The rooms are large by any standard for any large city. We were able to reserve a king room with a Central Park view - Fabulous! Continental breakfast was included in the rate and was satisfying - wish that there would be some yogurt available. Restaurant staff were attentive, and not overbearing. All hotel staff were friendly and courteous. Location across from Central Park is very convenient to the park and is just several blocks from museums and Times Square.

We loved the location of this hotel in relation to the subway, shopping and the city in general. Our room was big, and the property was modern and clean.
The gentlemen who helped us with our bags, Robert, was extremely friendly and helpful! If only all hotel staff were so pleasant to work with.
We will definitely be back.

This was my first stay at the Trump in Chicago..............the Peninsula Hotel is were I have stayed the last four previous visits. I really enjoyed my stay at the Trump. I loved the location of the hotel. At first I was apprehensive but it is a great central location. The facilities are beautiful and the room accomodations over the top. The building is a 92 story tower with hotel and residential condominiums. The hotel is located on 1 -27 floors with accommodations on level 14-27. Most of the rooms are suites so there is a very good chance you will receive an upgrade. What I liked most - the one bedroom suite with 10 ft ceilings, floor to ceiling windows with fantastic views of the river and Lake Michigan, the beautiful furnishings, bathroom, room service and extremely friendly and professional staff. What I didn't like that was annoying but no big deal - first two nights no turndown service and one morning room service breakfast arrived one hour after being ordered.............but smaill things that were corrected. Bottom line: we loved the Trump and will return which says alot since there are great hotel choices in Chicago

title_masked: this hotel can do much better with improvements.
text_masked: If you are a light sleeper, do not choose to stay here. I booked for two nights and let me tell you I didn't sleep at all! I tried, but being on the 4th floor where their restaurant was located was awful. I heard footsteps through out the night, trash cans being dragged out, people talking, showers running, airplanes landing (since it was very close to SD airport), and drills going off (building next door was being renovated). The service at the hotel was good, front of the building and lobby was nice, and their Glass door restaurant was cute with a nice view of the harbor from afar. I wished they took more time in improving the decor when you walk out of the elevator to your room since it felt and looked like a motel after (I suggest more plants and flowers). Also, they should replace their toilet seat since it was worn out obviously and they had an old school ac/heater that stuck out of the wall that was all dusty. Turning the ac/heater on made me feel like I just had dust blew all over me at night while sleeping since it was directed right onto the bed.

My daughter and I spent a couple of nights in NYC to see a Broadway show etc. Once again, I decided to stay at the Hotel Iroquois. As always, the accommodations were absolutely wonderful and the staff catered to our every need. The rooms were impeccably clean and the beds were so comfortable. The location is perfect if you only have a couple of days in NYC as the hotel is in close proximity to many of the attractions. I’m looking forward to spending some more time in NYC and I will surely be staying at the Hotel Iroquois.

My expectations were exceeded at this moderately priced property. The rooms were spacious and nicely appointed. Comparable to rooms at more expensive hotels. The owner and staff were very gracious and accommodating. I would definitely stay there again!

Had a girls trip to this property. The service everywhere (except Roys) was absolutely the best. Every employee was excited to work there and excited that we were there. Or at least that's the impression they gave. The Griffin Club was worth every penny! All the restaurants (exept Roys) were fantastic. Food was Very good. Waitstaff was very friendly. 
The spa was also spot on....... the spa pool is a bit on the boring side. If you want to hang out & relax in quiet, this is the place to go! The food & service here was also very nice! 
The only thing that would make this resort better......... replacre Roy's! The manager Gina Powers should learn how to talk to & treat customers. Her attitude spilled over onto the waitstaff. It's obvious they are not part of the JW Marriott. I

I stayed at the nyma for five nights on my first trip to New York City. The room was comfortable, clean and spacious with a king bed, LCD TV, phone, iPod dock, clock radio and coffee making facilities. My room was on the 13th floor with a view of the Empire State Building. The bathroom had a bathtub and shower and came with ample supply of towels. Every day the room was cleaned and bed made, with toiletries and coffee supplies replaced. Free breakfast was provided, which consisted of continental style breakfast and fresh fruit, coffee and tea. On the mezzanine floor there is a coffee machine and water fountain for guests use, which was a great place to sit after a long day of shopping and sightseeing. In the lobby there are two computers for guests use as well as a concierge and tour desk service. Location of the hotel is perfect as it is very close to Times Square, Broadway, Maceys and other shops and heaps of restaurants and the subway. As a solo traveller in New York City, the nyma was perfect and an enjoyable place to stay.
