I have been to the Ritz Toronto a few times, loved it and wanted to give this SF location a try. Well it is like comparing apples to pears: Toronto Ritz is brand new, walking into the room it smells sooo good, and everything is luxurious and new, from carpet to marble bathroom. 
Although the SF Ritz is a beautiful historical building, and conveniently located, to my opinion this is all it could offer. Walking into my 532 room in SF on June 27th, I smelled old coffee and saw old, tired carpet. The room is very standard, nothing to be "wow". Restaurant food is overpriced and substandard. I ordered a salmon and although I explained to the waitress that I want it tender and juicy inside, it came overcooked. They did bring me another piece which was better but it clearly tasted de-frosted salmon and not fresh. 
I did like the complimentary shoeshine service offered every evening.

I stayed 2 nights at the hotel, the bar area was great, plenty of beer and spirits varieties. 
I was on the 34th floor corner room, views where great, 
shower could have been better, iron did not work, and the maids knocked at my door at 8:15 am
parking is not comped for Platinum Ambassadors.
Pretty pricey for the room
The facilities were great and the staff were very helpful, especially the front-desk clerk George who helped us out with a few mishaps. I would definitely come here again.

Just returned from 6 nights at this hotel and found the room to be extremely comfortable. We found check-in to be quick and easy and the location is great for downtown/financial district, but if you want the more touristy areas (ie. Times Square/Uptown) i would maybe consider another hotel. We required this location and when we wanted to go Uptown we had no problem getting a cab with help from the hotel doormen. The views are really the selling point here, with stunning views of Ground Zero (now called 9/11 Memorial Site) you find yourself just watching the workman and being amazed at the scale of the project. I am a very light sleeper, yet the construction noise didn't bother me at all and we were on the 20th floor. Lots of drawer space but quite a small wardrobe, while the bathroom was clean and a good size with really nice toiletries. We didn't use either the bar or restaurant during our stay but found a great bakery across the street for a fresh, cheap breakfast. Would love to stay here again...

title_masked: Good location but where is the smile and extra comfort?
text_masked:
I have multiple stays at the Barclays over the last years when in New York on business. It is a classic NY hotel with a very good location close to the Grand Central, Fifth Ave and Central Park. It got all the expected "service ingrediences", but as always in NY it is unfortunately never delivered with a smile... There is always a lot of people waiting for breakefast to start at 7am - why not start earlier as many of the guests may have jetlag or have an early flight to catch? For people on business in NY 7am is not very early....
I was surpriced that they now have WiFi in all rooms! A vital upgrade from the previously "WiFi in the reception area only". The average room is small and somewhat worn out (need a general facelift), but compared to peers like the Roosevelt (terrible) rooms at Intercontinental Barclay are ok. Nice firm beds, but almost no water preassure in the shower.

title_masked: You may want to consider another hotel.
text_masked: Just spent 5 days at the Flatotel in NYC. This is really a 2 star hotel and not a 3 star. The hotel is in shabby condition and really needs to be refurbished. The rugs and walls are quite dirty and the tile floor and countertops in the bathrooms are cracked, chipped and dirty. The maids did a very poor job cleaning our room and always forgot something like wash cloths or towells. They had the old style of ac/heater unit in the wall that had to run all night to make the room bearable for sleeping. Everytime we used the toilet we had to flush it several times. No flat screen TV's just big old clunkers that seem to have a lot of static. The staff was nice and got us another room when the first one turned out to be a smoking room and it really stunk. The elevators can be real slow. They want $14.95 a day for wifi. We were with another couple and they had all the same problems as us. Although the rooms are large and the hotel is in a very convient location I wish we had stayed at some other hotel. My wife and I are not picky people and we are not complainers so it must have been pretty bad for us to feel this way.

title_masked: Brentwood Inn is a pleasant place to stay in LA
text_masked: This inn is fabulous. A Brazilian architect updated the inn, which is a classic, and I like the charm of it. The staff is friendly and helpful. The rooms are immaculately clean and comfortably furnished. The bed was comfortable. For those who prefer more room to cozy, try the deluxe room which is larger and has it's own private patio; they even lit a candle for us when we stayed there. We were fine in the regular rooms, and perhaps others will find the bathroom too tight. I have to admit I am partial to the deluxe room. Some reviewers did not prefer the feather pillows--I honestly didn't notice since I use my Bucky pillow. The location is convenient for walking to Brentwood Village (10 minutes) or St. Vicente Boulevard (15 minutes) for a variety of cafes and restaurants. The neighborhood is pretty and feels safe. The staff will help you with reservations and detailed directions if you ask. For a reasonable drive you can go to Santa Monica, Venice Beach, the Getty, Getty Villa, Mullholland Drive, and West Hollywood. The breakfast is a light, continental style breakfast. The terrace, just outside reception, is pleasant and you can eat there or in the lobby. Available for breakfast are: juices, coffee, tea, oatmeal, fruit, danish, muffins, and whole fruit. WIFI is free. Parking is free. We usually don't have a car.They can arrange transport to and from the airport. There is a laptop in the reception area if you didn't bring one and want to Google the LA scene. I recommend this inn.

The pool was what sold me, and it was disappointing. Great views and pool, but managed poorly. It's smaller, maybe they have 6 to 8 actual lounge chairs. It appeared they let anyone use it. It was very crowed with 30% of the people being actual guests. I asked if they let locals in to and they said, we TRY to keep them out. Ummm, you have to walk right by the front desk and you need a key to the pool, and it's your hotel, maybe instead of try, just do. The pool furniture needs to be replaced as well, several broken legs that were barely holding on. Nice hotel, but don't let the pool sell you.

The room was clean and well kept. The staff was very nice and accommodating. The shuttle driver took us to the local mart for supplies. There is a restaurant and bar onsite but we chose to order out and delivery didn't take long. The shuttle service starts running at 5:30am, get there early for a seat. Great airline employee discount.

Stayed overnight with my daughter and arrived early. When we arrived, the front desk was very busy checking out people but was surprised to see others checking in around noon. Was prepared to store our luggage but they were able to get us a room. Beds were comfortable but the room was oddly shaped. Had breakfast at a little cafe about a block from the hotel. We went to the 8 PM Mary Poppins Show. Seems like all shows were letting out about the same time. Not being familiar with which streets were safest to walk and cabs were not moving due to all the people even on the street, we opted for a pedicab (bicycle carts) to take us back to the hotel. It was $52! I was shocked-no fault of the hotel just wanted you all to be aware of the price from Times Square area to the hotel. Would stay here again.

title_masked: Great Hotel, Great Location, Clean, GREAT WIFI!
text_masked:
Pod 51 is exactly how I pictured it to be based Yelp reviews and pictures from their website. On my recent trip to New York, I was able to book a room at Pod 51 for a five night stay. Since I took the red-eye to New York, my flight landed super early so the hotel was able to store my luggage while I went about to explore the city.
The room I had was clean with clean floor, bed, shower, toilet, and sink area. It was very well organized with great use of space, NO BED BUGS, and most important - GREAT WIFI! Most reviews would say the rooms were small, but I didn’t find it too much of a problem or I imagined it would be smaller based on what everyone had said so I was pleasantly surprised.
I liked this hotel because of its GREAT LOCATION. It is right next to the 6, E, and M subway station as well as being within walking distance to a TON of great spots to eat (places I bookmarked to try) It’s right next to: Madison Restaurant, Choux Factory, Ess-A-Bagel, and Tsushima. And about 10 blocks from Serendipity 3! If that’s not enough, the location is nice enough that you can take the subway to more places like the 53rd and 6th Halal Cart. Also, the hotel is a short subway ride to the LOVE sculpture, and it is right next door to Greenacre Park. 
Regarding the beds, it was more towards the firm side. The air condition in the room worked perfectly, and the water was strong vs. some hotels where you only get a trickle. (BTW I was on the fourth floor). The room I had gave me a view of the streets right in front of the hotel… it was an okay view. But if that’s not good enough, check out the view on their rooftop patio! 
Another great factor in choosing this hotel is that it was in a super safe area and there were always lots of people walking around at all hours of the day. Customer service was good! BTW if you’re going to book a room here, you would be better off booking ONLINE. I received a totally different (HIGHER) price for the same room when trying to call vs. what the price online was showing.
One last thing, there are ipads in the lobby so you are able to print out your boarding tickets down there for free. Also, visit the concierge if you’re going to be touring the city, they’ll be able to hook you up with deals for example VIP access to the Empire State Building, plus a free gift.
I would definitely be booking a stay at Pod 51 the next time I'm in New York, or I'd try out Pod 39 their sister hotel for cheaper!

We stayed here for a vacation. The room was larger than we expected for New York. Most of the room was clean except the carpet which looked old. Our window faced the alley which made for a more quiet experience. There is an air conditioner in the window which works well, but can get noisy at times. The bathroom was small, but we expected this in New York and it was clean. The hotel is on 7th Ave and 28th street which is a good location and we were able to walk to Penn Station and Time Square. However, there is also a metro station very close to the hotel. The breakfast is included with the room and the staff at the breakfast were very helpful and asked us if we wanted more food before they closed. Overall, it was a good experience and we would stay here again.

We booked thru a third party site and got a great price for this property. I thought the service ranged from excellent to good. The front desk service was satisfactory, but not anything special. However, Rick who helped us with our luggage and stopped to say hello and give recommendations throughout our stay was awesome. The valet staff was also courteous and attentive.
We had a king room overlooking the river. We found the room to be quite spacious and fairly clean. However the bathroom needs better ventilation. There was some possible mold growing on the ceiling above the shower, because it gets so damp when you take a shower. 
Ordered room service and found it to be prompt and priced as expected (expensive) for a downtown hotel. We also had breakfast at the restaurant and a drink a t the bar one evening and all were satisfactory. 
I would probably stay in Jax Beach next time, but have stayed at other downtown Jax hotels previously and found this to be the best overall.

I stayed at the Hyatt Regency in May 2012 to attend a conference that was also held in the hotel. My check-in and check-out were effortless. In my limited interaction with the staff, I found them competent, helpful and friendly. My room was spotlessly clean and very comfortable. The location is great for a visit to Chicago--close to the Loop, the river, Miracle Mile, John Hancock Tower. This is a huge hotel. Some might like to stay in something a little more cozy, but I enjoyed my stay very much.

Stayed here for five nights. Had never heard of the hotel or CityCentre which is not anywhere near downtown Houston. Turned out to be a modern, well appointed hotel with some lovely features including crisp, cleanly designed, well maintained, fairly large guestrooms and lovely public spaces. Breakfast is an upscale cold buffet of quality fresh fruit, croissants and other pastries, boxed cereals, yogurt, juice and coffee, all served in a beautiful lobby seating area. Walk to all sorts of restaurant and shops that are right outside the hotel door. Self park in a nearby covered garage is convenient. Only drawbacks - the hotel promised transportation within a 5 mile radius and then seemed to favor business groups over individuals. Also no real concierge on staff.

I stayed in this hotel with my friend for two nights. Although I called very short notice the same day to ask if the they could change the bed type to two beds it was "not a problem". The room was huge (I'm used to New York rooms). Everything was clean and very tastefully designed. I loved the shower. We didn't spend a whole lot of time in the room. But the little time we had was comfortable and we enjoyed it. The Front Desk staff was very helpful with all our questions and roomservice and amenity orders were promptly delivered.A very good choice.

Location is good for travelling around Manhattan. However, the street is noisy and the rooms are small and nothing special. The breakfast had muffins/baked goods only. No fresh fruit or anything else. Non-smoking rooms still smelled of smoke. The men at the front desk were off-standish; barely mumbled an answer when we had a question about restaurants. The women were friendlier.

title_masked: Almost don't want to give this one away
text_masked:
Amazing price for this great place. I can see why perhaps the prices are not high: the bathroom is really, really tiny. And the view is 4 feet across to another room or brick wall. But to me that was part of the charm. Maybe I like a good value too much. But in that really small bathroom were great space-saving fixtures, great towels, real clean. Old fashioned small tiles that you know were actually there for the last 90 years plus. 
The desk was great. Nice pillows. Very clean and neat. 
Front desk staff great. 
And here's a little story that shows the kind of staff that works there: I took my phone off the hook so that the wake-up call wouldn't wake up my neighbors while I was in the shower. And guess what? The hotel staff came up just to make sure I was awake about 5 minutes after the scheduled wake up call. Wow! That is caring service. 
Feels very home-y. I loved the place. Great location of course.

title_masked: Good location, clean, quiet and safe area.
text_masked: My partner and I stayed at Morningside Inn in September last year. We were very happy with the location as it was only a short walk to the subway and central park. We stayed in a double room with use of shared bathroom and kitchen. Facilities were basic (no pots, pans or cutlery in the kitchen) and we could only get internet connection downstairs in the lobby. We stayed for 4 nights and got a great nights kip every night as hotel is located off the main road in a quiet road. Perfect for travellers who like a bargain, a great location and peace and quiet. Food, shops and atm within 5 minutes walking distance.

title_masked: Why would you stay anywhere else!
text_masked: Pleasant greeting from valet, friendly & quick check-in at front desk, clean spacious room with exceptionally comfortable bed, convenient location close to theater, shopping and arts, very nice breakfast buffet and fine dining for evening meals on site Checking out was a breeze, car was out front waiting for us. Responsive and helpful staff. Left an item in the room, called on the way home and had a tracking number within an hour. Thank you! Already made a reservation for a return trip to Philadelphia!

The hotel is beautiful, the location is not Ideal!!! It is far from everything, best to stay at their other location "Mark hopkins" This hotel is more for business men wanting to stay close to the convention center. The service however was exquisite. The staff is more than helpful and they even brought me a new scale because the one in the room was not working. The fitness center is nice, however the food is not to my liking. Overall a good stay.

The hotel is beautiful and is located in an excellent and accessible to central Boston area. The location really encourages walking and touring. The hotel has everything you could desire especially on the Gold floor level. The meals and snacks are fantastic and the service is always superior. Though costly, the stay is worth every cent. The stay really makes you feel like you are someone special.

title_masked: Best Hotel in the Theatre District
text_masked: If your travels call for Theatre, there is no better place to stay than the Chatwal. Amazing friendly and spot on service, the rooms are extremely modern. Truly a home away from home.

The room was big and everything was in order! I loved the breakfast bar especially Paulette! She is a loving person and her smiles radiates her energy. She loves people and serving the people. Her cooking is outstanding! I loved the hospitality they have! Thank you Paulette for my awesome experience, I felt right at home.

The last time I stayed here was in 1992. It is still as good as it was then. The location is good, close to time square and the theatre district and close to major bus and underground stations/ connections. The bed was comfy and large as was the bathroom, products of good quality. 
The staff are ok, but seem to be fishing for tips. The bar is expensive and lacks any warmth. Breakfast was good, but again I would go down the road to the diner.
Best rates for this hotel are to be found on comparison. Overall a clean and good stay, with a good sleep.

title_masked: Staying at the St. Gregory Hotel & Suites in Washington, DC
text_masked:
My husband and I love staying at the St. Gregory when we are visiting Washington, DC. The service has always been excellent and so it was again. The hotel is always clean and attractive. 
The staff, front desk and bell staff have always been friendly, helpful, and courteous. The rooms, Jr. suites have always been clean and attractive. We love the AAA package which includes free parking.
